description: Takes the value of one if a facility received a fine of $10,000 or more in a given year, and zero otherwise. The $10,000 cutoff is used because fines below that threshold are typically imposed for administrative violations to which the theoretical argument does not apply. About 2% of facilities in the sample are fined in a given year.

The logged total amount spent on lobbying the EPA in the prior 3 years by all other firms that have the same SIC-4 code, with 1 added before taking the log. Lobbying targeted at the EPA is calculated by dividing a company's total reported expenditure in a disclosure filing by the number of agencies it lobbied. In a given year, about 10% of firms in the sample that engage in lobbying contacted the EPA, spending an average of about $15,000.

Total amount of chemical byproduct (released and recycled/disposed) of a facility, combined with the EPA's Risk-Screening Environmental Indicators so that chemicals are standardized by hazardousness by exposure type. Toxicity from inhalation is multiplied by the amount of air releases and toxicity from ingestion by the amount of water releases; the two products are summed for chemical-level toxicity, and the sum of all chemicals' toxicity in a facility-year is logged. The measure is lagged by 1 year.

Binary moderator based on facilities' geographic location and the distance to the closest facility owned by an industry competitor that has a lobbying relationship with the EPA. High values indicate facilities with a lobbying competitor closer than 50 km; low values indicate a closest lobbying competitor farther than 50 km.

Quantifies how unique the inputs of each facility are in terms of the chemicals it uses in production compared to the rest of the industry, following the procedure outlined in Diestre and Rajagopalan (2011). Separate coefficients are estimated for facilities above and below the median standardization.

Measured with changes in industry-level imports, which are associated with an influx of low-cost competition into the US market, matched to firms at the SIC-4 level. The level of competitive aggression within the US is the change in net imports for the industry from 5 years prior; facilities are split at the median change in net imports.

Follows Greve (2003) in using Compustat information on the Returns on Assets (ROA) of a firm relative to the SIC-4 level average. Separate coefficients are estimated for facilities with an above and below median industry-relative ROA.

Sum of SMO-initiated conflict against the focal firm, including protests, boycotts, or lawsuits. Measured yearly over a 10-year period, 5 years pre-acquisition and 5 years post-acquisition: pre-acquisition it is the yearly sum of the acquirer's and target's conflict, post-acquisition it is the combined firm's annual conflict. The dependent variable is logged (one plus the count) to estimate linear models.
scale: count (logged as one plus the count)
time_window: yearly over 10 years (5 years pre- and 5 years post-acquisition completion)

description: Number of offsetting stakeholder relationships brought by the acquirer and target, using the minimum of the acquirer's and target's opposing-valence pairs under the assumption that each relationship of negative valence must be offset by a relationship of positive valence (the equation block itself is unreadable in the payload). Summed over the 3-year window before acquisition completion. Used as the baseline in the field fragmentation models.
time_window: 3-year window before acquisition completion (t-3 to t-1)

description: Count of the subset of total offsetting relationships that pertain to similar issues. Offsetting relationships are classified as involving similar issues if the two stakeholders interact with the acquirer and target on the exact same issue or if the issues pertain to the same underlying environmental problem (e.g., climate change). The issues pertaining to each firm-SMO relationship were hand coded using the Comparative Agendas Project (CAP) topics codebook.
time_window: 3-year window before acquisition completion (t-3 to t-1)

description: Count of the subset of total offsetting relationships whose issues do not match, used as the unaligned comparison. In the example given, cooperation on recycling offset by conflict on drinking water safety is an offset on dissimilar issues.
time_window: 3-year window before acquisition completion (t-3 to t-1)

description: Count of the subset of offsetting relationships in which the stakeholders involved have a cooperative tie with one another, based on the concept of relational embeddedness; cases in which the offsetting relationships involve the exact same stakeholder also count as proximate (direct proximity). A tie between SMOs was counted if they interact in a meaningful way, such as co-filing a lawsuit or co-organizing a rally or a conference, hand coded from documents mentioning two or more SMOs.
time_window: 3-year window before acquisition completion (t-3 to t-1)

description: Count of the subset of offsetting relationships involving stakeholders that do not have a cooperative tie with one another (socially distant stakeholders), used as the unaligned comparison to socially proximate offsets.
time_window: 3-year window before acquisition completion (t-3 to t-1)

description: Binary variable equal to one when there are no ties between SMOs who cooperate with firms and those who do not, and zero otherwise. To determine if a stakeholder field is fragmented pre-acquisition, the authors first identify SMOs in the field that never cooperate with firms and those that do, based on each SMO's conflictual and cooperative relationships with the 670 sampled firms in the preceding 3 years. It is a network characteristic, not an ego-network characteristic, and is based on the network of ties among stakeholders.

Big Five agreeableness score generated by the open-language machine learning program developed by Harrison et al. (2019) applied to transcripts of quarterly earnings conference calls; the program's best performing regression model for each trait generates scores on a seven-point scale (1-7). Transcripts from the 2 years preceding each observation were used, obtained from the Thomson Reuters StreetEvents database. Personality variables were standardized prior to estimation.

Big Five conscientiousness score generated by the open-language machine learning program developed by Harrison et al. (2019) applied to transcripts of quarterly earnings conference calls; scores are on a seven-point scale (1-7). Transcripts from the 2 years preceding each observation were used, obtained from the Thomson Reuters StreetEvents database. Personality variables were standardized prior to estimation.

Big Five neuroticism score generated by the open-language machine learning program developed by Harrison et al. (2019) applied to transcripts of quarterly earnings conference calls; scores are on a seven-point scale (1-7). Transcripts from the 2 years preceding each observation were used, obtained from the Thomson Reuters StreetEvents database. Personality variables were standardized prior to estimation.

The entropy measure of unrelated diversification, defined as a weighted average of a firm's revenue shares across unrelated industries, with the weight being the logarithm of the inverse of each industry's revenue share. P_j is the share of a firm's total sales in the jth industry, categorized using two-digit SIC codes; industries under different two-digit SIC codes are considered unrelated. The printed formula is garbled in the text.

Three indicators are used: return on assets (ROA), an accounting-based measure; and annual stock returns and market-to-book ratio, both market-based measures. All performance indicators were adjusted by industry averages at the two-digit SIC level. A principal component analysis was conducted to create a composite measure, which was standardized because it was used in interaction terms.

CEO total compensation (variable tdc1 from ExecuComp) used as the dependent variable, with pay for performance examined through interaction effects. The natural logarithm of CEO total compensation is used in the analysis to address the high skewness in its distribution.

A binary variable equal to one if the company has only one founder, and zero if the company has more than one founder. Founders were identified from the Y Combinator website, and supplemented with LinkedIn data on individuals who listed themselves as a founder or co-founder of the company; this multi-step process produced a comprehensive list of all founders.

A binary variable equal to one if financial data from Pitchbook indicated that the startup achieved a successful exit (IPO or acquisition), and zero otherwise. Of the 3010 ventures in the sample, 397 experienced successful exits. The authors describe exit as a robust measure of success in entrepreneurship widely used in prior studies.

Measured by coding the work and educational histories of each lead entrepreneur from LinkedIn. Keyword lists corresponding to nine functional categories (general management/strategy, operations/supply chain, marketing/sales, finance/accounting, HR, legal/compliance, software development, science/R&D, and medical) were applied to prior job titles; a founder was coded as having experience in an area if a prior job title included a keyword associated with that area. The measure counts the number of distinct functional areas in which the founder had prior experience, ranging from 0 to 9, with higher values reflecting broader functional experience.

Calculated from the same keyword-based coding of LinkedIn work histories. For each founder the total years of experience in each of the nine functional areas were computed, and depth is the maximum number of years the founder spent in any one area, reflecting their deepest specialization. Because the measure is highly skewed, the natural log of one plus this measure is taken.
scale: natural log of one plus years in the deepest area

description: A binary variable equal to one if the individual has experience in more than three functional categories and has more than 5 years of experience in one single functional category, and zero otherwise. The authors note that they experiment with different cutoffs and find similar results, and that this measure is used alongside the triple interaction between Solo Founder, Broad Experience, and Deep Experience.

Measured using the same approach as in Study 1: a binary variable equal to one if the company has only one founder and zero if it has more than one. Founder lists were extracted from Crunchbase and supplemented by scraping LinkedIn for individuals who had ever held a job title containing 'founder' or 'co-founder' at companies in the sample, and the lead entrepreneur was identified as the first founder to hold the CEO title or, absent that, the first entrepreneur to join the company.

Measured using the same approach as in Study 1: a binary indicator of whether the venture achieved a successful exit (IPO or acquisition). Ventures with identifiable founder information had higher exit rates than those without, which the authors interpret as their sample capturing the more serious entrepreneurial ventures.

Measured using the same approach as in Study 1, based on information on each lead entrepreneur's education and work experience collected from LinkedIn profiles and coded into functional categories. In selecting the nine functional categories the authors inductively examined the top 1000 most common job titles in the data and used three subject-matter experts to validate the lists.

Measured using the same approach as in Study 1: the maximum number of years the lead entrepreneur spent in any one of the nine functional areas, based on keyword-coded LinkedIn work histories, logged as the natural log of one plus the measure.
scale: natural log of one plus years in the deepest area

description: Measured using the same approach as in Study 1: a binary variable equal to one if the individual has experience in more than three functional categories and more than 5 years of experience in one single functional category. In Study 2 the interaction between Solo Founder and this binary measure is positive, the authors report.

variable_name: Industry relatedness of founding team human capital
description: Built from directional employee mobility flows between NAICS-4 high-technology industries in the LEHD: the human capital relatedness of industries j and i is the number of employees moving from employment in industry j into industry i during the year divided by the total number of employees in high-technology industry i who change employers that year. The startup-level measure weights each prior industry j by the share of the founding team's pre-entry wages earned in industry j in the four quarters prior to startup formation, so that industries in which founding team members earned more wages immediately before founding are weighted more heavily. Founding team members are identified as individuals who receive earnings from the startup during the first quarter of business operation. The equation mapping the industry-dyad measure to the firm was not readable in this payload.
time_window: four quarters prior to startup formation

description: Startup failure is a dummy variable equal to 1 if all establishments affiliated with the startup's firm identifier no longer appear in the data or contain any employment in the following year. Possible recodes, mergers, and acquisitions are removed by identifying situations where more than 75% of the startup's employees join the same firm following startup dissolution.

The primary growth measure is the DHS growth rate, based on Davis et al. (1998), computed from the startup's employment as calculated using headcount information on all establishments from the LBD, aggregated across all establishments affiliated with the startup's firm identifier. The text states that the measure mitigates bias from regression to the mean and is a second-order approximation of the log difference for growth rates around zero; the explicit formula was not readable in this payload.

Startup size is measured as the log of the startup's employee headcount across all establishments affiliated with the startup's firm identifier, used as the dependent variable in the firm size models.

A binary variable that takes the value of 1 if the startup firm is acquired in the following year. To minimize false positives, the authors require that the acquirer was present in the LBD prior to the acquisition and that the startup and the acquirer have different tax identifiers.

Measured at the NAICS-4 industry level as the number of hires from inside the industry divided by the number of total new hires in the industry, using worker mobility data in the LEHD. The variable ranges in theory from 0 to 1.

The dependent variable is measured using the firm's published score in the annual Fortune 'Most Admired Companies' survey. Fortune annually asks thousands of securities analysts, executives, and directors to rate the 10 largest companies in their industry on a 0-10 scale across eight attributes (e.g., management quality, financial soundness, and innovativeness). The eight item scores are averaged to generate each firm's overall reputation score.

Indicator variable coded as one if the CEO departed for poor job performance (173 cases) or undisclosed personal issues (27 cases), and zero otherwise. Information on succession events and the reasons for CEO departure came from the database compiled by Gentry et al. (2021) who identified and categorized reasons for succession events. Unforced succession firm-years are controlled for separately.

The total number of awards that the firm's current CEO has won within 3 years (t-3 to t-1) prior to the succession year. Awards were taken from the CEO of the Year competitions of Financial World (first-stage 'bronze' medals, following Wade et al.), Business Week (Best Managers and Repeat Performers categories), and Barron's (the editors' annual list of approximately 30 top CEOs). An interaction term with the CEO award measure and forced succession was constructed when testing Hypothesis 2.

The total number of articles about a CEO in a 3-year time window from 2 years prior (t-2) through to the succession year (t), from leading business publications and daily newspapers available from Factiva (Wall Street Journal, New York Times, Washington Post, Business Week, Forbes, and Fortune). Only articles where CEO presence was prominent, as indicated by mention in the headline or leading paragraph and at least three mentions in total, were included. Overall, 36,504 media articles were collected and analyzed.

Measured as the mean change (in fractional terms) in the market value of equity during the three prior years. The measure is lagged by a year so that it runs from year t-3 to t-1, to avoid overlapping with the control variable for contemporaneous firm performance. It is used in the interaction term testing Hypothesis 4.

Post-DST is a dummy variable that is a deterministic function of the running variable Days, which measures the number of days before and after a daylight saving time change in the fall or spring. In the fall panel the US regions shift their clocks 1 h backward, increasing temporal distance between the United States and India; in the spring panel they shift 1 h forward, decreasing temporal distance. The coefficient of interest indicates the discontinuity in user interactions following the DST change.

Absolute Time Difference measures the number of hours separating one region from the other in terms of time zone. Temporal distance differs naturally across each poster-region and voter-region pair, and the analysis tests whether the slope relating votes to temporal distance changes after the feature release.
time_window: 15 days before and after the design change

description: Number of unique views a post received on a given day, aggregated to the region-region-day level for the dyad formed by a poster region and a recipient region. Views can be conceptualized as a type of knowledge seeking. Region-region dyads with zero views are preserved in the balanced panel.
time_window: daily, ±15 days around each DST shift, 2015-2018

description: Number of unique votes a post received on a given day, aggregated within a region-region dyad formed by a poster region and a recipient region. Votes can be conceptualized as a type of knowledge engagement or curation. Region-region dyads with zero votes are preserved in the balanced panel.
time_window: daily, ±15 days around each DST shift, 2015-2018

description: The authors rank the tags associated with all questions posted on StackOverflow between 2015 and 2018 by the number of questions carrying that programming-language tag. Popular categories are posts with the five most popular tags; niche categories are tags associated with no more than 200 posts. The PPML specification is replicated separately for popular and niche categories and the coefficients are compared.

The interaction between the absolute time difference (hours) between a poster region and a voter region and Post-Update, an indicator for whether the voting activity occurs before or after the April 15, 2014 design change. On that date StackOverflow began labelling featured homepage questions as 'asked', 'answered', or 'modified', shuffling content representation. The interaction coefficient estimates how the relationship between votes and temporal distance changed after the feature release.
time_window: 15 days before and after the design change

description: Cross-sectional data obtained by aggregating daily votes to the question-region level for questions from the United States, the United Kingdom, Germany, France and India in the design-change window. Only question-region pairs with at least one vote from users in the selected country regions are observed.
time_window: daily, 15 days before and after the design change

description: For each firm i in year t the authors build a rolling-window co-invention network by taking an undirected one-mode projection of the inventor-patent bipartite graph, connecting two inventors if they co-author at least one patent filed by firm i during the interval. Ethnic integration is quantified with the External-Internal (EI) index of Krackhardt and Stern (1988), where E is the number of edges connecting inventors from different ethnic groups ('external' ties) and I is the number of same-ethnicity ('internal') ties; by construction -1 <= EI <= +1, with EI = -1 when all ties are internal and EI = +1 when all ties are external. The observed EI is compared to a null distribution of 1000 degree-preserving randomized networks generated with an edge-swap algorithm (BiRewire) and standardized; the focal variable is the resulting z-score, where positive values indicate more cross-ethnic ties than expected by chance.
scale: EI ranges from -1 to +1; the focal variable is a standardized z-score

description: Ethnic diversity over the five-year window is measured with the fractionalization index, computed from the share of inventors in firm i belonging to each ethnic group. The index captures the probability that two randomly selected inventors have different ethnic backgrounds: it equals 0 when all inventors share the same ethnicity and increases toward 1 as diversity rises.

Firm i's innovation performance in year t is the total real economic value of patents whose application dates fall in that year, summed over all granted patents belonging to firm i with an application date in year t. Each patent's private value is drawn from Kogan et al. (2017): the abnormal stock return around the grant date is scaled by the patent's ex ante probability of grant to filter out noise and then multiplied by the firm's market capitalization just prior to grant, deflated to 1982 dollars. The dependent variable used in the models is the logarithm of this total real dollar value.
time_window: patents with application dates in year t; value measured around the grant date

variable_name: Innovation complexity (Shannon entropy of subclass shares)
description: A global USPTO-subclass co-occurrence network is built over the five-year window, with an undirected edge between two subclasses if at least one patent in the window is co-classified in both, weighted by the number of such co-classifications. The Leiden community-detection algorithm partitions this graph into clusters treated as global technology domains, and each subclass is assigned to a unique cluster. For each firm-year the authors extract the subgraph induced by the subclasses in which the firm patented over the same window, compute the share of the firm's subclasses falling in each cluster, and take the Shannon entropy of these shares.

Binary measure that takes a value of 1 if the private partner is primarily compensated through user charges and so bears a substantial share of demand risk, and 0 if it receives regular payments from the government that are largely insulated from realized demand. A project is classified as user-pay when the private partner holds the right to collect and retain user fees as its main source of compensation, even if tariffs are regulated and some ancillary public support is present; all other projects are coded as government-pay.

Dummy variable indicating whether there was a PPP-specific law in force at the time of the project announcement. Enactment dates of laws and their amendments were taken from the PPPLRC and the Benchmarking Infrastructure Development report, and compared with the announcement date of each project.

Legal specificity is measured as the number of provisions contained in each PPP law, coded from the full text of the law in force at the project's announcement. The sample median number of provisions is used to classify projects governed by a PPP law as operating under high- versus low-specificity regimes, which enables split-sample tests.
level: project (law version in force at announcement)

description: Binary indicator equal to one when a law's number of provisions exceeds the sample median, and zero otherwise. The unit of observation is the country-law-year corresponding to the initial enactment or subsequent amendment of a PPP-specific law, and the variable is the dependent variable of the law-level cross-sectional model.

The POLCON variable developed by Henisz (2002) quantifies the extent of institutional constraints on government by analyzing the number of independent veto points within the political system (executive, legislative, and judicial branches) and the distribution of political preferences both across and within these branches. The index ranges from 0 to 1, with higher values indicating higher institutional constraints on government, and the pre-adoption value is used in the law-level model.
time_window: measured prior to the enactment or amendment of the law

description: A formative index built from the 1940 census records of the CEOs' parents. Parental education is the total number of years of education achieved by the parental breadwinner; parental occupation is the breadwinning parent's occupation mapped onto Duncan's Socioeconomic Index scores; parental income is the sum of the annual incomes of both parents. Each of the three components was standardized and then averaged to attain the index, which ranges from -2 to 2, with higher values indicating a higher-class background and lower values a lower-class background.

Measured using the TDC1 variable from Execucomp, which consists of salary, bonus, restricted stock, other income, and stock options (using the Black-Scholes option pricing model) paid to a CEO in a given year. The variable was natural log-transformed to correct for skewness.
Measured after the initial year also using the logged TDC1 variable from Execucomp, consistent with much of the research on CEO compensation.
time_window: after the initial year of tenure

description: Total shareholder return calculated as the total compounded return to shareholders, then adjusted by the industry median TSR based on the focal firm's four-digit global industry classification standard (GICS). Firm performance was winsorized at the 1% level to minimize the impact of extreme values.

Data on dismissals were obtained from Gentry et al.'s (2021) dataset of CEO departures in S&P 1500 firms, which categorizes eight distinct reasons for CEO turnover. Dismissal was coded as 1 only in the cases when dismissal occurred for performance reasons, excluding other extraneous reasons such as fraud and criminal conduct.

In supplementary two-stage least squares analyses, social class background was instrumented with the average home value of the county and the average social class of the county in which the parents resided in the 1940 Census, collected from the IPUMS USA database.

The interaction of a treated-group dummy with a post-event dummy used as the independent variable in the difference-in-differences analysis. Firms are assigned to the treated group (treat = 1) if their holding institutional investors were involved in investor-level M&As that made them become ESG investors, and to the control group (treat = 0); treated firms represent 17.5% of the total observations. Post equals 1 if the observation is in a year after the event and 0 if it is before the event; a two-year or three-year window is assigned for each event.
time_window: two-year or three-year window around the event

description: The cumulative proportion of ownership by ESG investors, where ESG investors are those that joined the UN PRI before the current holding year. The authors use a fuzzy name-matching approach to identify 1114 ESG investors that became PRI signatories between 2006 and 2019 in the FactSet Ownership database. The average proportion of ESG ownership in the sample is 12%.
ESG ownership aggregated at the firm level, exactly as in the main firm-year analysis, while the dependent variable is measured at the individual supplier level.

The natural logarithm of a firm's Scope 3 upstream emissions, led by one year (t + 1). Scope 3 upstream emissions refer to GHG emissions caused by activities of the firm but that stem from the firm's suppliers. This is the main dependent variable of the difference-in-differences analysis.

The natural logarithm of a firm's Scope 1 direct emissions, led by one year (t + 1). Scope 1 direct emissions refer to GHG emissions directly controlled by the firm, generated directly by its production activities.

The natural logarithm of the sum of Scope 3 upstream emissions and Scope 1 direct emissions, led by one year (t + 1). Scope 2 emissions are not included because they arise from purchased energy and may vary for reasons unrelated to pollution outsourcing.

A dummy variable capturing a firm's access to green technologies, equal to one if the percentage of its total ESG ownership held by green-technology-intensive ESG investors is greater than the median, and zero otherwise. An ESG investor is classified as green-technology-intensive if its portfolio firms aggregately hold an above-the-median number of green patents, identified with the USPTO 'Green Patent' classification. A dummy is used because M&A events change the ownership structure of firms.

The number of suppliers in which a firm's ESG investors invest while also having ownership in the focal firm, dichotomized because the variable is highly skewed (mean = 7.11, median = 1). It equals 1 if the number of a firm's suppliers who are also invested in by the firm's ESG investors is above the median, and 0 otherwise.

The natural logarithm of a firm's Scope 3 upstream emissions, led by one year (t + 1). Scope 3 upstream emissions refer to GHG emissions caused by activities of the firm but that stem from the firm's suppliers, and the variable measures firms' pollution outsourcing behavior.

The natural logarithm of a firm's Scope 1 direct emissions, led by one year (t + 1). Scope 1 direct emissions refer to GHG emissions directly controlled by the firm, generated directly by its production activities.

The natural logarithm of the sum of Scope 3 upstream emissions and Scope 1 direct emissions, led by one year (t + 1). Scope 2 emissions are excluded from the total because they arise from the energy firms purchase and use and can vary with factors unrelated to pollution outsourcing.

A dummy variable equal to one if the ratio of the cumulative ownership by ESG investors who are also intensive in green technology investment to total ESG ownership is above the median, and zero otherwise. Green-technology-intensive investors are those whose portfolio firms aggregately hold an above-the-median number of green patents, classified with the USPTO 'Green Patent' classification.

The number of a firm's suppliers that are also invested in by the firm's ESG investors, dichotomized because the variable is highly skewed (mean = 7.11, median = 1). It equals 1 if that number is above the median and 0 otherwise.

The natural logarithm of the sum of Scope 1 and Scope 3 emissions measured at the individual supplier level, led by one year (t + 1). The authors use the sum at the supplier level because firms may outsource production to suppliers who themselves continue outsourcing to lower-tier suppliers.

variable_name: Perceived ability to deal with challenges
description: Simple average of nine items measuring entrepreneurs' perceived ability to deal with specific challenges in Tanzania, each ranked on a scale from 1 (not able at all) to 7 (very able) as of the day the survey was completed. The nine items were presented in randomized order in each survey. The average of the items forms a general measure of perceived ability to deal with challenges; pooled across all six data collection points the Cronbach alpha for internal consistency is 0.77.
time_window: as of the day of each survey; six data collection points from April 2021 to July 2022

description: Simple average of the four project-related items of the perceived ability scale: identifying the right customers/market, knowing what customers want, knowing who competitors are, and developing the business strategy. The authors report a Cronbach alpha of 0.82 for this indicator; entrepreneurs were unaware of this categorization when completing the surveys.
time_window: six data collection points from April 2021 to July 2022

description: Simple average of the five environmental items of the perceived ability scale: accessing inputs, government policies and regulation, accessing reliable infrastructure, accessing financial capital, and accessing workforce. The authors report a Cronbach alpha of 0.70 for this indicator; entrepreneurs were unaware of this categorization when completing the surveys.
time_window: six data collection points from April 2021 to July 2022

description: Dummy variable indicating the experimental training condition, set to 1 when entrepreneurs are in the theory-and-evidence-based condition. In the difference-in-differences models this variable is interacted with a Prepost dummy that indicates whether an observation has been collected at or after the baseline; Table 3 instead estimates the effect of each experimental condition separately over time with respect to baseline values.

The main independent variable of interest is the triple interaction between being assigned to the private insurance ward, arriving in the months between July and October, and arriving in 2022. The dashboard was installed in the private insurance ward in the third week of June 2022, with physician training completed by early July, so July 2022 is defined as the start of the treatment period; the regular ward never received the technology.

The log-transformed number of laboratory tests ordered during the episode; tests include blood counts, metabolic panels, urinalyses and many others performed in-house. The main tables report results with the continuous and count measures log-transformed to minimize the impact of outliers.

A test is classified as generic if its category appears in 50,000 or more episodes—corresponding to the 99th percentile of the distribution of laboratory tests—and as targeted otherwise, using all episodes from 2016 to 2022. Separate regressions are estimated on the log number of generic tests and of targeted tests ordered; Complete Blood Count and Urinalysis are given as examples of generic tests and the Angiotensin Converting Enzyme test as a targeted one.
time_window: during the episode; classification based on 2016–2022 episodes

description: The log of the amount in Colombian Pesos (COP) charged by the hospital to the payer for each episode. Charges include all billed items between ER admission and discharge: tests, drugs, consumables and physician fees.

Log-transformed patient length of stay in the Emergency Department, used as a proxy for decision speed for non-critical patients, for whom exit from the ED is primarily determined by the physician's discharge or hospital admission decision. The baseline specification includes all triage levels and does not winsorize the length of stay distribution.

A dummy that equals one if the patient is hospitalized rather than being discharged home. Admission to the hospital represents an acknowledgment that the patient has not improved sufficiently during her stay at the Emergency ward.
A dummy that takes the value of 1 if the patient returns to the Emergency Department within a 30-day period.

variable_name: Patient satisfaction (attitude, compliance, answering questions, average)
description: Based on a survey sent to a randomly-selected subset of patients, using three responses: whether the patient thought the medical staff displayed the right attitude in the provision of care, whether the patient thought the physician complied with good medical practices, and whether the patient believed the physician was good at answering questions and addressing potential concerns. The average of the three questions is also used as a dependent variable. These results are only available for 2022 and for fewer than two thousand observations, so the specification is a difference-in-differences model with coarser time effects.

The proportion of orders undertaken by nurses (who have less authority than providers) to total orders on a care team for a specific patient encounter. The care team includes all providers and nurses who enter at least one order for a patient during the stay. For example, a 50-order patient encounter of which 10 orders were performed by nurses would be calculated as 0.2 (10/50).
time_window: over the entire patient encounter (admission to discharge)

description: An indicator variable treatment hospital takes a value of 1 for Hospital A (which receives the new system) and 0 otherwise; an indicator variable post-EHR treatment takes a value of 1 from July 1 onward and 0 otherwise. The interaction of the two multiplies the EHR and the hospital variables, and its coefficient represents the effect of the new system on decentralization in the care team for patient encounters in Hospital A.

Captures how often, on average, particular providers and nurses have worked together on patient encounters in the past. For each provider-nurse dyad in a patient encounter, the authors sum the number of times that particular dyad has appeared on other encounters in the same study period (pre- vs. post-), then divide this sum by the total number of potential provider-nurse dyads on the care team to normalize by care team size.
time_window: same study period (pre- vs. post-EHR implementation)

description: An indicator variable identifying encounters in which two or more providers matriculated from the same medical school within 10 years of each other. Among doctors, common training reflects attendance at the same educational institution; the variable received the value of 1 if two or more providers attended the same medical school in a 10-year window and 0 otherwise.

Care teams' self-reported reliance on notes for intra-team communication (versus other messages sent through the EHR system, such as orders), which is an item from the pre-implementation survey that was averaged at the level of the care team. The authors use this approach because medical privacy concerns do not allow them to observe individual clinical notes at the encounter level.

Number of new add-ons introduced in each category in a given month, corresponding to new product introductions in a given market. The authors also estimate models on the logarithm of this count (Log. new add-ons introduced).

variable_name: New add-ons introduced by new developers
description: Number of new add-ons introduced in each category in a given month by new developers, that is, developers who had not introduced any add-ons before. It is analyzed both for the sample of new developers and in models comparing new developers with existing developers.

Number of add-on updates in a given month, used as a proxy for tracking generational innovation, analyzed at the add-on-month level. The authors also employ a dummy variable (Updated), assigned a value of one if an update occurs in a given month and zero otherwise.

Average number of categories that newly introduced add-ons span in a given month, used to measure the scope of knowledge domains that original software products draw on. The taxonomy of categories used by Firefox does not change, so the variable reflects a wider functional scope per product rather than a proliferation of categories.

Latent Semantic Indexing (LSI) similarity scores for the textual descriptions of newly introduced add-ons, used to assess whether add-ons differ from previously introduced ones; higher values mean greater similarity to previous products, that is, lower novelty. A second version uses the neutralized description text, adjusted to reduce potential style differences resulting from GAI-assisted text generation.

Availability of generative AI assistance is proxied by the introduction of ChatGPT in November 2022. Post x Treatment equals one for observations after the introduction of ChatGPT (treatment-year months from November 2022 to May 2023) and zero otherwise, compared with the same calendar months of the prior year as the control period in a panel-differences design.

Dummy variable equal to 1 if the state in which the firm is headquartered has enacted an anti-SLAPP law by year t, and 0 otherwise. Historical headquarters information is used to assign firms to states, and during the sample period 169 of 3488 firms (4.8%) relocated their headquarters. The treatment variable is not lagged.

Additive score of CSP strengths minus CSP concerns in the MSCI (formerly KLD) Community, Environment, and Human Rights categories. The Corporate Governance category is excluded because it reflects engagement with shareholders rather than broader stakeholders, and the three retained domains involve stakeholders such as local communities and society at large who generally do not engage in regular economic exchange with firms. A higher score indicates more socially responsible performance.

Count of news articles mentioning a firm's CSI each year, following Kölbel et al. (2017), using data from the RepRisk database. Only environmental and social dimensions are counted, to align with stakeholder rather than shareholder activism, and all articles are included regardless of severity or reach. The variable is standardized prior to analysis and is lagged by one year.

Built from pair-wise results similarity scores based on the list of patent families involved in patent infringement lawsuits in both countries prior to the focal year. For each country a vector is generated indicating the litigation outcomes of the shared patent families: 1 if the patentee wins, 0 if tied or split win, and -1 if the alleged infringer wins; the cosine of the angle between the two country vectors, ranging from -1 to 1, gives the pair-wise similarity. The firm-level measure averages the pair-wise similarity scores for all the countries in the firm's choice set. Because both the choice set and historical records change over time, the aggregated variable changes over time.
scale: -1 to 1 (cosine of the angle between outcome vectors)
time_window: litigation prior to the focal year; first focal year is 2010

description: At the firm-country level, results similarity is measured by averaging the pair-wise similarity scores between the focal country and each of the remaining countries in the choice set. The pair-wise scores are built from the outcomes of patent families litigated in both countries prior to the focal year, coded 1 for a patentee win, 0 for a tied or split win, and -1 for an alleged infringer win, with the cosine of the angle between the two country outcome vectors ranging from -1 to 1. The aggregated value changes over time as the choice set and historical records change.
scale: -1 to 1 (cosine of the angle between outcome vectors)
time_window: litigation prior to the focal year

description: The Herfindahl index calculated from the number of patent infringement cases litigated by the focal firm and its subsidiaries across countries. To capture litigation trends over time, the count of cases in the previous 5 years is used to calculate the level of concentration (e.g., 2013-2017 if the focal year is 2017). Higher values indicate more geographic concentration.
The number of cases that each corporate family files in that country-year; the count dependent variable of the firm-country level analysis.

Calculated as the focal firm's assets in the focal country divided by its total assets 1 year before the focal year. The authors use a firm's logged amount of assets in the focal country as an alternative measure of firm-country assets.

The top five industries (SIC 2 digits) in which the focal firm's entities (headquarters and subsidiaries) are primarily engaged are identified; the variable then counts the number of Fortune Global 500 entities that in the preceding year operate in these same industries and have a presence (themselves or their subsidiaries) in the same focal country. Entities may not be equally important, so the number of entities in each industry is also weighted by the size category of the entities to identify each firm's top 5 industries.

Measured in a two-step procedure: first, CEO returns were calculated as the percentage change in CEO firm-related wealth during the fiscal year, where the numerator includes salary adjustments, bonus payments, restricted stock grants, LTIP payouts, value of exercised stock options, value of stock sold, and changes in the CEO's equity portfolio value, and the denominator is the beginning-of-year value of all CEO long-term equity holdings plus salary; the measure was transformed with the inverse hyperbolic sine function. Second, differences between CEO returns and shareholder returns were calculated for each fiscal year, and the resulting difference scores were used as the dependent variable.

variable_name: External board social capital (board eigenvector centrality)
description: Operationalized as the board's eigenvector centrality within the board interlock network, capturing the board's structural network position in the network as a whole and taking into account the connectedness of the focal board's neighbors. The normalized eigenvector centrality was calculated with UCINET 6 based on yearly symmetrized board interlock matrices.

variable_name: Independent director shared networking (director networking experience)
description: Operationalized as the independent directors' history of networking experience within the focal board, captured as the overlap in the board tenure of independent directors. The sum of the shared or overlapping board tenure is divided by the number of pairwise comparisons; inside directors are not included in this measure.

A composite measure built from three proxies: the total number of directors who joined the board under the leadership of the current CEO, CEO tenure in years since the CEO took office, and CEO duality, a dummy equal to 1 if the CEO is simultaneously chairman of the board and 0 otherwise. The three power dimensions were standardized and summed, with each component weighted equally.

Measured as the percentage of total year-end shares owned by the top five institutional investors. The five largest institutional investors in any given firm year were identified and their absolute ownership divided by total shares outstanding; the five percentage values were then summed.
A dummy variable indicating that the firm is a lateral diversifier, with prior activities in another industry. It enters the models in either the age-independent or the age-dependent vector.

The rate of mortality at the organizational level is defined as the probability of mortality in an infinitesimally small interval, and regression-like effects of covariates on the rate are estimated. Mortality collapses all ending events that resulted in the demise of a unique organization, including cessation of production, bankruptcy and acquisition by another firm; spells are split at least every year to update covariates.
Years the firm has spent in automobile production, updated as spells are split.

A dummy variable indicating that a de novo firm engaged in observable preproduction activities. The activities consist of building a car, incorporating as a car manufacturer, or listing the concern in an industry directory.

Contemporaneous organizational population density, indicating the total number of producer organizations in the population in a year, divided by 100 for reporting; the square of this variable divided by 10,000 is also used. Density variables are lagged one year to ensure exogeneity.

variable_name: industry origin dummy variables (Bicycle Producer, Carriage Manufacturer, Dealer, Other motor vehicles, Components, Other industries)
description: For de alio firms, dummy variables indicating prior activities in bicycle manufacturing, carriage manufacturing, automobile dealing, other motor vehicle manufacturing, components supply, and other industries. In the comparison models engine manufacturing is the omitted category, so the coefficients express the advantage of each origin relative to engine manufacturers.

The authors recorded whether businesses shut down in a given record year. The variable took a value of 0 if a business continued to participate at a given record year and 1 if it shut down during the year. Exits include cases in which a parent company sold a business to another company, and 233 business divestitures were treated as right-censored cases, that is, nonexits, in the analysis of business dissolution.

Dummy variables noting that a partner shut down its hospital software systems business during the current year or that a partner was dissolved during the 4-year lag period. Contemporaneous dissolution is defined as dissolution during the same calendar year, and dissolution lags are examined during the subsequent 4 years.

variable_name: Partner adds partner, same type, year 0, years 1-4
description: Dummy variables denoting cases in which a partner operating in the software systems industry added a new partner of the same type (marketing-oriented or development-oriented) as the existing agreement. The variables are recorded for the current record year and for the cumulative 4-year lag period.

variable_name: Partner adds partner, different type, year 0, years 1-4
description: Dummy variables denoting cases in which a partner operating in the hospital software systems industry added a new partner of a different type (marketing-oriented or development-oriented) from the existing agreement. The variables are recorded for the current record year and for the cumulative 4-year lag period.

variable_name: Business adds partner after partner dissolution, years 0-4
description: Dummy variable denoting cases in which a business added a new partner after a partner shut down, measured over the current year and the 4-year lag period. Including this variable allows the authors to distinguish between the effects of differential response to partner failure and new partnerships.

variable_name: Business adds partner after partner adds partner, years 0-4
description: Dummy variable denoting cases in which a business added a new partner after a partner added a new partner, measured over the current year and the 4-year lag period. Including this variable allows the authors to distinguish between the effects of differential response to partner failure and new partnerships.
Dummy variables noting that a partner sold its hospital software systems business during the current year or that a partner was divested during the 4-year lag period.

For each rival k, organization j's recent-experience clock TRik ticks until it reaches 10 years and then maintains that value until the sample period ends or either j or k fails or otherwise disappears. Means were then constructed for each organization for this recent-experience clock (Mr).

After 10 years, the distant-experience clock begins to tick, recording with each additional year the number of years of competitive experience between j and k before the 10-year window. Means were then constructed for each organization for this distant-experience clock (Mo).
Rivals' experience measures were created using the 10-year window to measure recent experience, giving for each organization j the competitive experience of its rivals (MR).
Rivals' experience measures were created using the 10-year window to measure distant experience, giving for each organization j the distant competitive experience of its rivals (MD).
The variance in the durations of an organization's competitive relationships, computed from the distribution of its Tik over all rivals k. The printed formula is not readable in the extracted text.

Viability is operationalized as the organizational failure rate, estimated in terms of the instantaneous hazard rate with a piecewise exponential model. Failures include bank closures that occurred because of actual or impending insolvency, whether or not the closure was managed by regulators; failures eventually resolved by restructuring and reopening were recorded as failures. Mergers and acquisitions not associated with a bank failure were treated as a competing risk.

Fund family size is the natural logarithm of the sum of the net assets in the family's funds. It is measured for each month in the time series and used both as a variable in the vector autoregression and, in its updated value, as a predictor of the hazard rate.

Product-line breadth is the number of funds in a fund family, measured for each month in the time series and used both as a variable in the vector autoregression and, in its updated value, as a predictor of the hazard rate.

Fund family subsidization of fund expenses is the proportion of the fund family's net assets that are subsidized, measured for each month in the time series and used both as a variable in the vector autoregression and, in its updated value, as a predictor of the hazard rate.

For each fund in the family, the deviation of the fund's yield from the average yield of the fund's category for that month is calculated; the fund's yield deviation is weighted by the ratio of the fund's net assets to the total net assets of the fund family; the weighted yield deviations for all funds in the family are averaged to arrive at the family's overall product performance. It is measured monthly and used both in the vector autoregression and, in its updated value, as a predictor of the hazard rate.

The time-varying coefficients of the fund family's four-equation vector autoregression, estimated with the Kalman filter. Each coefficient is estimated as a function of its value in the prior time period plus a time-varying factor that is a linear function of the forecast error; the coefficients are continuously updated each period and represent the outcome of the search process.

The search component of the forecast error, the change in the variables of the growth system net of the lagged error term, is normalized in each period and cumulated over time for each growth system equation and each fund family. This cumulative sum reflects the cumulative contribution of search behavior to changes in the growth system coefficients, independent of error in the growth system.
time_window: cumulated over the fund family's history through each month

description: The dependent variable of the hazard model is the risk of failure of a fund family. The authors use a log-linear specification for the hazard model and include an age parameter in logarithm form to assess age dependence. Of the 233 fund families in the data, 50 exited the industry.

A (0,1) dummy for traditional relatedness: those firms classified as Related or Dominant take the value of 1, while firms classified as Unrelated take the value of 0. Classification follows Rumelt's (1974) diversification categories, using data from the TRINET tapes as well as the firms' annual reports.

variable_name: A/V FEWCUST, A/V HSERV, A/V CHANNEL, A/V TORDER, A/V SKILL
description: Five structural indicators of strategic relatedness, three of which were available for the main classes of strategic assets: customer assets (FEWCUST, HSERV), channel assets (CHANNEL) and process experience assets (TORDER, SKILL). Each indicator K is expressed as the weighted average of the indicator across the businesses in the firm's portfolio divided by the weighted variance of the indicator across those businesses, so that firms whose businesses differ on the dimension are discounted. FEWCUST is the percentage of product lines for which there were less than 1000 customer accounts at the manufacturer level; HSERV the percentage of product lines requiring a 'moderate to high' degree of after sales or technical service; CHANNEL the percentage of products which pass through an intermediary before reaching the final user; TORDER the percentage of product lines made to order based on customer specifications; SKILL the proportion of 'high-skilled' jobs in the industry as a percentage of total employment.

The profitability of the sample firms, measured as return on sales. The authors state that they use return on sales rather than return on assets because, depending on the accounting method used for an acquisition (pooling of interest vs purchase accounting), profitability measures such as ROA end up systematically smaller under purchase accounting than under pooling of interest accounting.

The central independent variable is an LBO dummy variable that equals one if the firm underwent an LBO and zero otherwise. LBOs were identified from the ADP/MLR Publishing M&A Data Base, augmented with lists supplied by other authors, and characteristics were coded from a search of the Wall Street Journal for a 3-year period before and after the LBO announcement.

The main dependent variable, R&D/sales, is derived from the NSF R&D data and is defined as company sponsored R&D plus contract R&D divided by company sales. We focus on R&D intensity in the 3 years before the buyout; for the pre- and postperiods, simple averages of R&D/sales were calculated for the 1, 2, or 3 observations in the period.

The change in R&D intensity from the 3 years before the buyout to the 3 years after the buyout. The firm had to have at least one observation in the t-3, t-2 or t-1 period and at least one observation in the t+1, t+2 or t+3 period, and simple averages of R&D/sales were calculated for the 1, 2 or 3 observations in each period.
time_window: from 3 years before to 3 years after the buyout

description: Size is measured as the natural log of company sales. Sales figures are taken from the QFR data.

Our proxy for diversification is a dummy variable which equals one if the firm operates in five or more 4-digit SIC industries and zero otherwise. The ADP/MLR Publishing M&A Data Base contains a list of up to 11 SIC codes for each LBO; for LBOs not in that data base, SIC codes were obtained from Standard and Poors.

Divestiture activity was measured by a dummy variable that equals one if the firm sells off 10 percent or more of its assets in the three post-LBO years and zero otherwise. Restructuring or divestiture activity information came from the M&A Data base and from a search of the Wall Street Journal for the three post-LBO years.

If we found any evidence that the pre-LBO management took an equity stake in the buyout (i.e., the LBO was a management buyout [MBO]), we set the MBO dummy variable equal to one. Information on management participation was found by searching the Wall Street Journal.

If we found evidence of hostile threats in the 3 years before the buyout, the hostile takeover dummy variable was set equal to one. Information on hostile takeover activity was found by searching the Wall Street Journal.

Performance is measured by the change in cash flow divided by sales, where cash flow is defined as operating income before depreciation and is derived from the QFR data. The short-run measure calculates the change in cash flow/sales from the year before the buyout to the year after the buyout; the long-run measure computes the change from the year before the buyout to the average of the third to fifth postbuyout years. When relating cash flow/sales to R&D, R&D is added back into cash flow.
time_window: year before to year after the buyout; year before to the average of years t+3 to t+5

description: Each restructuring firm was dummy coded such that years prior to restructuring were coded '0' while years subsequent to restructuring were coded '1'. The years in which firm restructuring activity was occurring were coded as missing so as not to confound the transition period of restructuring with the pre- and postrestructuring periods.

Restructuring firms were placed into one of four categories by use of median splits on DU and DR following Palepu's (1985) categorization. In addition, three variables—the specialization ratio (sales of the largest segment divided by total firm sales), DR and DU—were clustered to form the four corporate strategy types in the pre- and postrestructuring periods. Chi-square and sign tests of pre- and postrestructuring strategy types were conducted.

The level of total diversification was calculated using the entropy measure of diversification, formed by adding the related diversification (DR) and unrelated diversification (DU) components, and calculated for each firm for each year of the study. It was used to control for preexisting and concurrent levels of diversification.

Three dummy coded variables were created using the entropy measure of total diversification to measure the difference between prerestructuring and postrestructuring level of diversification. Firms decreasing their total diversified scope ('down') were coded '1' in the postrestructuring period and '0' in the prerestructuring period, with all nonchange firms coded '0' in the postrestructuring period; firms increasing their total diversified scope ('up') were coded '1' in the postrestructuring period and '0' in the prerestructuring period, with all nonchange firms coded '0' in the postrestructuring period. Strategy change dummies were likewise created for firms that changed category down, changed category up, and did not change.

R&D intensity is the firm's reported spending on R&D per $1000 of sales. It is the dependent variable in the pooled cross-sectional time series regressions and was measured 2 years pre- and 2 years postrestructuring.

The initial division of equity share between partners at the start of the venture, indicated by three types of ownership structure: highly unequal ownership share (maj/min or min/maj), somewhat unequal ownership share (51%-49% or 49%-51%), and equal ownership share (50%-50%). In the original model the variables UNEQ and EQ distinguish the majority-minority group and the 50%-50% group from the 51%-49%/49%-51% baseline; in the reduced model the 50%-50% and 51%-49%/49%-51% contracts are merged into a single baseline group.
time_window: at the start of the venture

description: A dummy variable that classified the host country as either 'restrictive' or 'nonrestrictive,' depending on the country investment policies reported in two publications designed for U.S. investors. Countries were classified as 'restrictive' if local ownership was specifically mandated, either with respect to sector or with respect to the amount of equity, or by the presence of any limits on foreign ownership; no distinctions were made concerning the amount of mandated local ownership. When host government policies changed during the time frame of the study, values for the 'restrictiveness' variable were modified accordingly.
level: host country of the joint venture contract
time_window: modified when host government policies changed during the study period

description: The existence of prior renegotiations was represented by two variables. One indicated the occurrence of a single previous renegotiation; the other indicated the occurrence of two or more. These variables also correct for problems of assuming independence in a sample that may include several intervals in the life of a single joint venture contract.

variable_name: change in the ownership structure of the joint venture (years to contract change)
description: The dependent variable for this test is an indicator of change in the ownership structure of the joint venture. The measure indicates the number of years that passed before equity division changed, a change being taken to mean any shift greater than 0.5 percent; this includes buy-ups of the venture to create a wholly owned subsidiary as well as smaller shifts in the division of ownership of an ongoing joint venture. Possible values were whole numbers between 1 and 15, and a dummy variable indicated contracts that survived to the end of the study period without being renegotiated (censored).

Bank presidents categorized their bank's planning efforts for the previous five years according to the degree to which sophisticated written documentation emanated from the planning effort, checking one of three statements. Of the 50 responses to question set I, 38 banks categorized their preceding five-year planning as category 1, 11 as category 2, and one as category 3. The banks were then divided into two groups: non-formal planners (category 1, N=38) and formal planners (categories 2 and 3, N=12).

All South Carolina banks were divided into three groups based on total dollar deposits; within each group all banks were ranked on each performance measure and the ranking was converted into a percentile for each performance measure during each year. Performance data were obtained for three years (1977-1979) on profit margin, return on assets, loan growth and return on equity. The analysis compared the mean percentile rankings of formal and non-formal planners on each of the four measures.

variable_name: degree of emphasis on strategic decision-making dimensions
description: Regardless of the formality of the planning process, bank presidents identified the degree of emphasis their bank's strategic decision-making placed on each of six dimensions of strategic management, responding to a set of questions adapted from the conclusions of Bourgeois' (1980b) review. A mean emphasis score was computed for each dimension for formal and non-formal planners and compared with t-tests.

When all of the subscale scores are combined into a single index, the Item Score is obtained; it reflects the overall positive versus negative trend of the responses to the 35 scorable items and thus provides a measure of the extent to which an individual is motivated to fulfil the role requirements specified in the theory of managerial effectiveness. The authors state a numerical range for this score, but the printed range is garbled.

A second comprehensive measure developed in accordance with the theory of projective test interpretation to minimize social desirability or conformity effects. Responses are compared against frequencies obtained from a normative group to determine if a rare pattern (one occurring 5 per cent of the time or less) is present; if responses on a particular subscale match one or more rare patterns, a +1 or -1 is given. The normative group used contained managers drawn from a wide range of functional areas.

The MSCS Form H contains 40 items, only 35 of which are scored, and each individual response is scored as positive, neutral or negative. Subscale scores are obtained by subtracting the total number of negatively scored responses within each set of five items from the number that have been scored positively. The authors state a numerical range for the subscale scores, but the printed range is garbled.

Extensive interviews with the entrepreneurs provided information used to classify the entrepreneurs along the craftsman-opportunistic dimension in accordance with the working definitions. Scoring -1 for a craftsman classification and +1 for an opportunistic classification, the type of entrepreneur score could vary from -14 to +14; the actual range was from -12 to +14. Sufficiently complete information to permit classification was obtained for 30 individuals.

Interviews provided the information used to classify the firms along the rigid-adaptive dimension in accordance with the working definitions. A -1 was given for a rigid classification and a +1 for an adaptive classification, and the potential total range was from -6 to +6; this same range was reflected in the actual scores.

Group comparison. The entrepreneurial sample consists of 38 founders still associated with their Oregon firms, and its Miner Sentence Completion Scale scores are compared with scores of six samples of managers (first-line supervisors and middle managers) from large business firms.

Word-embedding models are trained repeatedly over firm- and industry-specific text; the measure is the semantic closeness (using cosine similarity of word vectors) of words that most commonly refer to employees to words that capture the firm's strategic orientation. Models are run at the two-digit industry-year, three-digit industry-year, and firm-four-year levels, and the level of aggregation is chosen based on the nature of the independent variable.

For each three-digit industry and year, the ratio of labor share in output to capital share in output is calculated, used as a proxy for human capital-intensive industries because labor's share in output should be higher compared with capital across such industries. The authors also examine the contribution of labor composition and R&D intensity to labor productivity; both relate directly to the workforce.

Industry-level employment data from the Bureau of Labor Statistics are used to calculate the vacancy-to-unemployment ratio at the two-digit industry level and year, as a measure of tightness of the labor market.

Data on the nature of institutional investors from Brian Bushee's website are merged with 13-F holdings data for institutional investors from Thomson/Refinitiv to derive a measure of a firm's transient investor holding. Two variables are used as a measure of transient investor holding: the proportion of institutional holding that is transient, and the total transient institutional holding as a percentage of the firm's total stock; the firm's total institutional investor holding is controlled for.

Product-market-fluidity data for firms are taken from the Hoberg and Phillips data library; the variable enumerates the competitive threat for a particular firm and the risk of changes in its product market.
time_window: firm-year measures averaged across four-year periods

description: A dependent variable constructed as the opposite of herding: the absolute difference between a recommendation and 'market consensus,' where market consensus is the average of all active recommendations before the focal recommendation is made. Recommendations are coded '1' for strong buy, '2' for buy, '3' for hold, '4' for underperform, and '5' for sell. Higher deviation means less herding. Values are analyzed at the analyst-stock-recommendation level.

Winning the StarMine Top Stock Pickers award is used as an exogenous increase in reputation for the winners. A dummy (Win) indicates whether the analyst is a winner of the StarMine award in the year and industry in which the stock is classified, and PostAward indicates whether the StarMine award winners have been announced in that year; their interaction is the coefficient of interest. A control group of runners-up with similar simulated performance covering the same industries is constructed following StarMine's methodology.
time_window: 120-day window around the award announcement (60 days before and after)

description: A measure of the transparency of the competitive landscape built on the industry disparity measure of Hoberg and Phillips (2018), taking (1 - disparity). Firm-level signal correlation equals the ratio of total sales of peers in the intersection of TNIC and GICS competitors divided by the total combined sales of competitors in the union of the TNIC and GICS groups. The firm-level values are then aggregated to the GICS industry level, and the industry-level measure is used in the regressions.

The 18-month buy-and-hold abnormal returns associated with firms' product introduction announcements. BHARs are a long-run abnormal financial return that capture the stock market performance of a firm over a certain period, adjusted by the average increase for firms of a similar size. They are described as an established measure of long-term performance used to determine whether corporate acquisitions are value enhancing or destroying.
time_window: 18 months following the product introduction announcement

description: A binary variable equal to 1 if the manager increased their stock holdings in the firm prior to the focal product introduction announcement and 0 otherwise. The underlying net purchase volume adds the dollar value of purchases in the six months prior to the announcement to the deviation in sales in that same six-month period relative to the previous six-month period (number of shares sold multiplied by the transaction price). The authors state that the mathematical computation is given in an equation block; the equation itself is not readable in the text. Stock Trading is coded 1 when net purchases were positive and 0 otherwise.
time_window: six months prior to the product introduction announcement, benchmarked against the preceding six-month period for sales

description: Teachman's entropy index calculated over the proportion of time (based on the number of years) the manager spent in each industry, using the firm's primary fourth-level Standard Industry Classification code (SIC-4). A higher value of the index represents broader experience.

Teachman's entropy index calculated over the proportion of time (based on the number of years) the manager spent in each firm, as reported in BoardEx. A higher value of the index represents broader firm experience.

Teachman's entropy index calculated over the proportion of time (based on the number of years) the manager spent in each functional category, as reported in BoardEx. A higher value of the index represents broader functional experience.

The Chicago Board Options Exchange Volatility Index (VIX), described as measuring the market's overall expectation regarding the evolution of near-term aggregate volatility and as based on S&P 500 index options' implied volatilities. The authors compute the rolling average VIX over the corresponding six months of each manager's stock trading prior to the product announcement, and split the sample into high and low uncertainty according to the mean value.
time_window: rolling six months prior to the product announcement

description: Distance in kilometers between the residential addresses of the two inventors in a pair. Addresses are geocoded from residential address information in the USPTO Image File Wrapper and geographic coordinates are entered into the Vincenty formula, which returns the Euclidean distance over the surface of the earth. The inventors' contemporary address is used for each patent year. The median distance between within-firm pairs is 28 km and distances range from 0 to 208.6 km.
time_window: contemporary address in the patent application year

description: Indicator equal to one if the two inventors in a pair are coinventors on the focal patent application and zero otherwise. Pairs are constructed from the application-specific risk set of individuals who might lead to patenting at the assignee that year. Patents with more than two inventors generate the set of pairs that underlie the collaboration.

Indicator that takes the value of one if a pair of inventors is in the same division and zero otherwise. Divisional affiliation is estimated from patent text: abstracts and claims are categorized into treatment areas using key terms and then mapped to the companies' divisions, and patent applications with more than one division indicator are coded to both divisions. Inventors are matched to divisions by their maximum division indicators on the patents they file.

Indicator equal to one when the pair is same gender (male/male or female/female) and zero for across-gender (female/male) pairs. Each inventor is hand-coded as male or female based on first names, cross-referenced with LinkedIn when available.
Logged count of citations from the focal patent to the assignee firm's patents. It is regressed on the patent-level average residential distance between local inventors.
Calculated as (renewal years paid)/(the statutory term of that patent); it indicates the proportion of the life of the patent that has been maintained and has not been abandoned.

One of the OECD patent quality metrics (Squicciarini et al. 2013) used as a dependent variable in the patent-level OLS regressions on average inventor distance; the paper does not describe its construction further.

One of the OECD patent quality metrics (Squicciarini et al. 2013) used as a dependent variable in the patent-level OLS regressions on average inventor distance; the paper does not describe its construction further.

Experimental condition indicator. In the time constraints condition, limits were set for the evaluation of each startup (including watching the videos), the decision on which startup would be more successful, and the estimation of the likelihood of success for both startups; the time available for each evaluation was three minutes, 20 seconds for the decision, and 40 seconds for the likelihood estimations. In the no time constraints condition participants could take unlimited time. The time limits were derived by subtracting one standard deviation from the baseline duration based on a pretest with 35 participants.

Experimental condition indicator. In the LLM condition, participants were provided with an LLM chatbot based on gpt-4o-2024-11-20 integrated into the study interface, accompanied by a system prompt designed for each startup evaluation. Participants in the LLM condition were asked to use the LLM provided during startup evaluation.

Measured as the number of distinct categories in participants' mental representations. The authors analyzed participants' pros and cons lists for both startups and assigned all pros and cons to one of 10 strategic categories: industry structure, market size, imitability and time to market, costs, operations, value to customer, nonmarket, marketing, business model, and funding. For example, if a participant's list of pros and cons included items categorized as value to customer and funding, breadth was two.

Measured as the average number of items per category by dividing the total number of pros and cons by breadth. Depth indicates how much detail a participant provided within each category; for instance, a participant listing two customer items and one industry structure item had a depth of 1.5.

Measured as the Manhattan distance of the individual's 20-dimensional category vector (representation of 10 categories per startup) to the centroid, that is, the average vector of all participants. To ensure that higher values reflected greater consensus, the Manhattan distances were multiplied by −1, so that a value of, for example, −1.3 indicated closer agreement with the crowd than a value of −2.0.

A binary variable based on which of the two startups participants expected to be more successful. The authors assigned 1 to participants who selected Vitaloop as the more successful startup and 0 to participants who selected Tidee.

Predicted market reaction to a transaction, generated by the random forest model, which the authors select because it yields the highest R2 in both the training set and the test set among the candidate ML models. The model is trained on 10,590 transactions completed between January 1, 1976, and May 18, 2012, and used to predict reactions for the 2,647 transactions completed between May 19, 2012, and December 31, 2022, using a time series split to avoid information leakage. Predictions are built from 286 input variables grouped into five categories: deal-specific attributes, acquirer and target characteristics and accounting performance, acquirer prior acquisition activity and performance, recent market-wide acquisition activity and performance, and macroeconomic factors.
