Cumulative abnormal return to the acquirer's stock surrounding the acquisition announcement, computed over an event window of (-1, +1) days with t = 0 the announcement date. The expected return had the acquisition not been announced is estimated using the Fama-French three-factor model over an estimation window of (-250, -50) days relative to the announcement date. Stock price data are obtained from the Center for Research in Security Prices database.

The absolute difference between the actual CAR and the Predicted CAR generated by the trained ML model for a given transaction. It represents the prediction error or surprise associated with the transaction and encompasses both positive and negative deviations. It is used as the independent variable in the regressions of deal completion time.

The logarithm of one plus the number of days between the public announcement date of an intended transaction and its completion date, using data from the Refinitiv database. In the testing sample the average deal completion time is 59 days.

variable_name: Predicted CAR of actual versus alternative transactions
description: Deal selection is assessed by comparing the random forest Predicted CAR of the transactions managers actually executed with the Predicted CAR of five hypothetical alternative targets per deal (randomly drawn, or the most similar by cosine similarity of 30 firm and industry variables) in a paired t-test. It is also assessed by the counterfactual value created if only deals with positive predicted reactions were pursued and those with negative predicted reactions forgone.

Binary variable capturing the temporal shift in divestiture behavior following deal termination. In the first-difference model, it equals one from the year following deal termination (t+1) onward, enabling within-firm comparisons of divestiture activity before and after the termination event. In the difference-in-differences model, it represents the interaction between the post-termination period and treatment group for terminated deals, equaling one only when the firm experienced deal termination and the observation is from the post-termination period; zero otherwise.

Binary outcome indicating whether the focal firm undertakes divestitures in a given year in industries/sectors related to the intended target firm, measured by two-digit SIC code. For example, if the intended target firm operates in four-digit SIC code 2833 (medicinal chemicals), the measure captures the number of divestitures the focal firm makes of businesses with the broader two-digit SIC code of 28 (chemicals and allied products) after deal termination. Divestitures include sell-offs and spin-offs.

Binary variable equal to one if the deal is motivated by leveraging complementarity between the bidder's existing resources and the target's resources, and zero otherwise. Three types of complementarity motives are distinguished: economies of scale or scope; innovation and new product development; and explicit mentions of complementary assets. Coded from deal descriptions.

Binary variable equal to one if the bidder firm was unable to complete the acquisition due to target-related resistance, and zero otherwise. Coded as target rejection when the target firm was directly involved in terminating the deal, including target management or board rejection, target shareholder rejection, disagreement on transaction price, or inability to agree on management terms. Identified through systematic reviews of documentation released on or around the deal termination date.

Difference between three-year moving averages of primary market growth rates (acquirer minus target). Yearly growth rates for each primary market are computed using WRDS Compustat sales data, then the three-year moving average growth trend is calculated as (YGt−1 + YGt + YGt+1)/3. Higher values indicate greater opportunity costs for resources devoted to target-related activities. Primary markets are defined using industry classifications from the Refinitiv data set.

Constructed as three resource distance measures. Distance to Acquisition Target (Technological Asset-Based) is one minus cosine similarity of two companies' patent portfolios, based on patents filed during the five years before deal announcement. Distance to Acquisition Target (Tangible Asset-Based) is one minus cosine similarity of tangible resources between bidder and target primary businesses, using the 1997 BEA capital flow table. Distance to Acquisition Target (Human Capital-Based) is one minus cosine similarity of human capital used between bidder and target primary businesses, using the BLS occupational profile table.
time_window: five years before deal announcement for patent portfolios; preannouncement for other measures

description: Japan is a dummy that equals one if the car is made by a Japanese manufacturer. Tsunami is a dummy variable that equals one if the sale took place between March 15, 2011, and September 15, 2011. The interaction of the two identifies the post-tsunami demand surge for used Japanese cars, since the shortage of new Japanese vehicles induced prospective buyers of Japanese cars to consider used autos instead.

The price paid by a dealer for a used car, that is, the price at which the dealership could sell the vehicle in the national wholesale market. The average vehicle in the sample has a wholesale value of $13,424.
The selling price of the vehicle at the time of sale, realized by the dealer. The average retail price is $17,266.

Dealer profit margin is measured as retail price minus wholesale price divided by retail price, and averages about 36% in the sample. A decline of 2.3 percentage points relative to this average represents a drop of 6.6%.

The difference between the retail and wholesale value of the vehicle, which gives rise to the per vehicle gross profit. The measure is also aggregated to the level of aggregate profits earned each month by every dealer, accounting separately for Japanese and non-Japanese used car sales.
time_window: at the time of sale; aggregated monthly and quarterly

description: The total new car sales of that make-model in the year preceding the tsunami (2010); vehicles with greater previous year new car sales trade in thicker markets. The 2010 new vehicle sales in the United States for each make and model are provided by Automotive News, and make-model sales data are also aggregated by goodcarbadcar.net.

The fraction of total used car sales in January-February 2011 (the two months preceding the tsunami) that were generated by a given make-model; this is a direct measure of the pre-tsunami used car market thickness of each vehicle. These data were supplied by IHS Markit.
An indicator for vehicles that were discontinued by their manufacturers. Discontinued vehicles are less desirable and trade in less liquid markets.

The age of the vehicle at the time of sale, used to distinguish young used cars (age less than or equal to three years) from old cars (more than three years). The used cars in the sample are quite young, with a median age of three years.
Equal to one if the dealer is selling a used vehicle of its own make and zero otherwise; for example, Dealer-Make Match = 1 if Karl Malone Toyota is selling a used Toyota.

Intermediary dispensability is proxied by market thickness of the vehicle make-model, since in thick markets buyers and sellers can find each other and dealers are less essential. Three proxies are used: 2010 new-car sales of the make-model, its share of used car sales in January-February 2011, and a model discontinuation indicator (thin market).
scale: continuous sales and share; discontinuation dummy

variable_name: Japanese Dealers x Tsunami on dealer profits from non-Japanese cars; vehicle age triple interaction
description: Reallocation is tested in two ways. First, aggregate dealer profits are computed separately for Japanese and non-Japanese used car sales, and the Japanese Dealers x Tsunami coefficient in the non-Japanese profit regression (Table 11, dealer-quarter data) shows whether Japanese dealers shifted activity to non-Japanese used cars after the tsunami. Second, the age of the vehicle sold is regressed on the triple interaction of Tsunami, Dealer-Make Match and Japanese dealer to see whether same-make Japanese dealers shifted to older cars.
scale: dollars of aggregate dealer profit; years of vehicle age
time_window: 2010 to 2012, tsunami period March 15 to September 15, 2011

description: Time variable indicating whether the observation is in a year after the acquisition event. It is coded one if the year is sometime after the acquisition year and zero if it is in the acquisition year or any year prior. It is interacted with the independent variable of interest and individual fixed effects are included to estimate the outcome for the same inventor before and after the acquisition.
time_window: seven years before to seven years after the acquisition

description: Measured as the meaningful innovation performance of inventors, focusing on the quality (i.e., impact) of inventions by observing forward citations. It is the three-year forward citation count for an inventor's patents generated in year t. Applied patents are used for all measures.
time_window: three-year forward citation window for patents generated in year t

description: Measured each year based on the cumulative patents the inventor holds. Knowledge specialization is calculated for each year on the entire base of patents held by an inventor until the year prior to the focal year (t-1), defined by the Herfindahl index (concentration ratio) of applied patents' patent classes, where the patent class is obtained by the IPC code. Specialization is the sum of the squares of the proportion of patents in each patent class; breadth is one minus the specialization value, a fraction between zero and one.
time_window: cumulative patents until year t-1 for observation year t

description: Preacquisition distance between the acquirer inventor's knowledge and the knowledge brought in by the acquired firm, measured at the dyad level prior to the acquisition but calculated at the dyad-year level so it varies each year before and after the acquisition. For both the inventor and the target firm, a class experience vector is constructed from the proportion of total patents in each technology class in each year; the angular distance (Jaffe 1986) is the inverse of the cosine similarity of the two vectors and ranges from zero (complete overlap) to one (no overlap in any technology class that year).
time_window: each year before and after the acquisition

description: Binary variable used to do a split-sample analysis. The knowledge distance between the acquiring and target firms is first calculated using the cosine similarity measure; if the distance between the acquirer and the target firm is higher than the sum of the average and standard deviation of the knowledge distance across the sample the variable is coded one, and if it is equal to or lower than that it is coded zero.

Dummy based on whether the acquiring firm inventor who patented for the firm prior to the acquisition continued to patent for the firm after the acquisition or not. It is estimated on the cross-section of inventors, with all variables calculated cumulatively for the year prior to the acquisition.
time_window: from the year prior to the acquisition to after the acquisition

description: The inventor's knowledge breadth for the cross-sectional logit estimation, calculated cumulatively for the year prior to the acquisition. It is entered both alone and interacted with the proportion of patents in new classes. The text states that a purely generalist inventor has a diversification score of one (specialization score of zero) and a pure specialist has a specialization of one.
time_window: cumulative to the year prior to the acquisition

description: Calculated as the proportion of patents in classes where the acquiring firm did not patent prior to the acquisition but did so after the acquisition. It is entered in the continuation logit and interacted with inventor breadth.

Number of extreme heat-related events (heatwaves, wildfires, and drought) and, separately, number of extreme cold weather events (cold waves, extreme unseasonal wintry conditions, and winter storms) in a country in T-1, reported by EM-DAT as abnormal or deviant relative to the country's typical seasonality, temperature, and precipitation. Only extreme weather events that affected more than one region in a country are counted. This is the independent variable used to predict demand.

variable_name: BEV demand predicted on weather events
description: The predicted sales (in standardized form) for BEVs in a country based on the effect of extreme weather events, taken from the first-stage model; the authors refer to this predicted demand as the 'demand shock.' It serves as the endogenous regressor in the IV probit entry models.

variable_name: PHEV demand predicted on weather events
description: The predicted sales (in standardized form) for PHEVs in a country based on the effect of extreme weather events, taken from the first-stage model, and included as an additional endogenous regressor in the firm entry models.

Sales of electric vehicles in a country in a year, separately measured for BEVs, PHEVs, and HEVs, proxying demand for these alternative electric vehicle technologies. The dependent variables for Hypothesis 1 are scaled as z-scores to enable comparability across EV technologies, and are interpreted as standard deviations from the mean.
scale: z-score standardized (raw sales in thousands of units)

description: Sales of plug-in hybrid electric vehicles in a country in a year, used alongside BEV and HEV sales to proxy demand for the alternative electric vehicle technologies. Scaled as z-scores for comparability across EV technologies.
scale: z-score standardized (raw sales in thousands of units)

description: Sales of nonplugin hybrid electric vehicles in a country in a year, used alongside BEV and PHEV sales to proxy demand for the alternative electric vehicle technologies. Scaled as z-scores for comparability across EV technologies.
scale: z-score standardized (raw sales in thousands of units)

variable_name: firm entry into a country's electric vehicles market
description: Set to one if a firm enters a country in a year and zero otherwise. Firms are at risk for entering a country from the start of the study period until they enter or are right-censored; entry of a new brand of a firm already present in a country does not count as an entry.

The pre-existing number of fast-charging stations in a country, in log form, with one-year lags. High-voltage fast charging outlets allow EVs to be charged rapidly, making the charging experience more convenient and resolving range anxiety; this measure was only available for a limited set (about 10%) of countries and years, and no missing data were imputed.

The number of upstream complement providers - electric auto parts manufacturing and service firms present in the country market in the previous year - gathered from ORBIS. Such firms are likely to retool from electric parts and instrumentation to make components such as coils and circuitry for EVs; about 90% were independent firms rather than OEM-owned.

The number of EV-related startups in a country market in the previous year, gathered from Crunchbase. This includes makers of control systems, battery cell arrays, subassembly makers, charging infrastructure installation and maintenance, cooling components for EVs, and app makers providing consumer-end software for EV makers.

variable_name: overlap between firm's global portfolio and country product market characteristics
description: A measure of product market overlap based on the electric vehicle model segments (and subsegments) that the firm has experience producing and the segments and subsegments that are commercially available in a country, measured before entry. The lower the overlap, the larger the bottleneck a firm experiences with commercializing products; a value of zero indicates a complete lack of product market overlap and a value of six indicates perfect overlap in all six EV segments.
scale: 0 (no overlap) to 6 (perfect overlap across six EV segments)

variable_name: years since entering the local electric autos market
description: The number of years since a firm entered a country's EV market; for example, a firm that entered the EV market in Germany in 2010 has time since entry set to zero in 2010 and updated by one in every subsequent year.

variable_name: proportion of hybrids in firm's local electrics portfolio
description: The proportion of hybrids among a firm's portfolio of all electric vehicles sold in a country in a year, computed as (HEV + PHEV)/(HEV + PHEV + BEV), conditional on the firm having entered the market with any electric vehicle. A lower proportion of hybrids indicates a greater shift toward the radical (BEV) technology.

variable_name: number of complementor acquisitions by firm in country
description: The number of complementor firm acquisitions (which proxies for investments in the technology ecosystem) by firms in a focal country in a year, based on SDC Platinum M&A data. Acquisitions are recorded in the year they were announced and include complement providers such as electric vehicle parts makers, parts subassemblers, EV instrumentation, and control system software companies.

variable_name: local operating revenue of firm in fossil fuel autos
description: The local operating revenue of the firm in the country in a year in fossil fuel autos, used as a measure of the firm's legacy market position in the old technology.

variable_name: local number of employees in fossil fuel auto operations
description: The number of employees of the firm in the country in a year in fossil fuel autos, used as a measure of the firm's local human capital in the legacy technology.

Monthly count of aircraft stored by the airline, aggregated from the day-level timing of events in the database. Storage is a unilateral action that reduces cash outlays from operating aircraft with little or no passenger traffic but has some cost and a risk of slow return to service.

Monthly count of aircraft retired (scrapped) by the airline, aggregated from the day-level timing of events in the database. Retirement is a unilateral and irreversible action that reduces financial constraints at the cost of constraining strategic options.

Monthly count of aircraft sold to another operator, aggregated from the day-level timing of events in the database. Sales are irreversible but bring in payment, and unlike storage and scrapping they require a buyer.

Policy stringency of the airline headquarter nation, a factor calculated based on the strictness of state lockdown policies that restrict people's mobility. It is updated monthly and interacted with the airline experience variables to measure how responsive each airline is to the environmental changes.

Indicator variable set to one for U.S. airlines that were in operation on September 11, 2001, and zero otherwise. It is interacted with state stringency to test Hypothesis 1a; the main effect is factored out by the firm fixed effects.

Indicator variable set to one for airlines headquartered in high-GDP-per-capita nations (as defined by the World Bank) that were in operation on January 1, 2008, and zero otherwise. It is interacted with state stringency to test Hypothesis 1b; the main effect is factored out by the firm fixed effects.

variable_name: Region [action] (e.g., Region storage, Region retirement, Region sales)
description: Sum of aircraft subject to the same action in the same region (using the World Bank regions) in the previous month, for example the number of aircraft stored in Europe in May 2020. A one-month lag is used because airlines announce these actions as soon as the decision is made.
Average stringency in nations in the same region in the previous month. A one-month lag is used because airlines regularly monitor peers, especially during a crisis.

variable_name: Wedge between control and cash-flow rights
description: The control rights of a parent in a subsidiary are the percentage of a subsidiary's voting rights that are directly and indirectly controlled by its parent. The parent's cash-flow rights are the fraction of the dividend paid by the subsidiary that can eventually be received by the parent, calculated through capital held at each stage of the ownership chain linking the parent to the subsidiary. The wedge is the difference between control and cash-flow rights (multiplied by 100 for demonstration of coefficients).
time_window: at the time the subsidiary joins the firm

description: Relatedness is inferred from resource flows: relatedness of any two subsidiaries increases with the degree of overlap in the mix of their inputs, following Lemelin (1982). The importance of each market (at the NAF700 level, roughly equivalent to four-digit SICs) is weighted by the percentage of total sales of the firm in that market. The relatedness of a subsidiary to its firm is thus a function of the input similarity between its business and the firm's other businesses and how prominent each of these businesses is for the firm.

Multimarket contact is calculated as the percentage of sales from markets (i.e., industries) in which the firm faces multimarket rivals, following Feinberg (1984), Sohn (2001), and Sengul and Gimeno (2013). The measure is greater if a firm has significant sales in markets in which many incumbent firms are also in the focal market; the importance of a given market increases with the firm's sales in that market and with the number of multimarket rivals also operating there, and decreases with the number of active firms in that market and with the firm's overall sales volume. The authors state that the formula block in the text is unreadable as extracted and specify it in prose in the surrounding text.

Measured at the unique title level, takes the value of one, two, or three, representing single-homing, sequential multihoming, and simultaneous multihoming, respectively. A title is considered simultaneously multihomed if it was released across two or more platforms (consoles and PCs) within 30 days; it is considered sequentially multihomed if it was released across two or more platforms with a separation of more than 30 days; if neither, it is coded as a single-homed title.
The number of unique consoles (i.e., other than PCs) for which the developer released a title in the previous five years.
The number of titles released for a PC by the developer in the previous five years divided by the total number of unique titles released by the developer.
The number of titles released as single- or sequential homing console titles in the previous five years divided by the total number of unique titles released for consoles by the developer.
A dummy variable that takes the value of one for games based on a movie or franchise license (e.g., Harry Potter or the NFL) and zero otherwise.

The number of titles released in the cult game genres (strategy, role-playing, adventure, family entertainment, children's entertainment, and arcade) by the developer in the previous five years, divided by the total number of unique titles released by the developer.

Binary variable that equals one if the annual royalty fee increased from one year to the next and zero if it decreased or remained unchanged. The authors use a dummy rather than a continuous measure because royalty fees are calculated in many different ways across systems (percentages of net or gross sales, absolute amounts paid weekly or monthly, scaled systems with tiers, and combinations of these).
time_window: annual change, one year to the next

description: Dummy variable that equals one in the first and second year after acquisition and zero otherwise. It is the main independent variable capturing possible increases in the dependent variable in the initial years after acquisition compared with the years before acquisition.
time_window: first and second year after acquisition

description: Dummy variable taking the value of one if the system offers area development agreements in a given year and zero if it does not. The variable is a proxy for a franchise system's strategic intent regarding multiunit franchising; data on the number or sizes of area development agreements are not available in FDDs.

The number of franchise outlets opened in the previous three years plus the number of transfers in the previous three years, divided by the total number of franchised units in the focal year. New outlets opened and transferred outlets are combined because in both cases the franchisee signs a new contract with the franchisor.

A binary measure of inventor CEO status built by matching individuals' names, assignee names, and filed dates from the PatentsView database to CEOs' employment history in Execucomp and BoardEx. A CEO is identified as an inventor when the inventor name, the assignee names of the patents, and the patent filing years match the CEO name, the CEO's employers' names, and the CEO's employment years. One represents a CEO with a patent and zero a CEO without a patent; only firm-years after the grant year of the inventor CEO's first patent were assigned a value of one.
time_window: firm-years after the grant year of the first patent

description: A composite measure based on six dimensions: advertising intensity, inventory level, plant and equipment newness, R&D intensity, nonproduction overhead, and financial leverage. Each dimension was winsorized by 0.5%, the year-on-year difference along each dimension was calculated, each difference was standardized by SIC three-digit industry and year by subtracting the mean and dividing by the standard deviation, and the absolute value of each standardized difference was taken. The sum of the absolute standardized values of the six measures is the composite measure of strategic change, capturing changes in resource allocation from time t to t + 1.
time_window: change from time t to t + 1

description: Generated from records of CEOs' personal political donations, using four indicators: the number of donations to the Democratic Party divided by the number of donations to both parties; the dollar amount donated to the Democratic Party divided by the amount donated to both parties; the number of years the CEO donated to Democrats over the number of years donations were made to either party; and the number of distinct Democratic recipients over the total number of distinct recipients of both parties. Following Chin et al. (2013), 0.1 was added to the numerators and 0.2 to the denominators to account for zero values, and the mean of the four indicators is the measure of CEO liberalism.

An index built from CEO experience in different functional areas, firms, and industries. The sum of the number of distinct functional areas, firms, and industries in which the CEO had worked before the focal year is divided by the total years of work experience. Functional areas were categorized into eight areas: accounting/finance, law, management/administration, marketing/sales, personnel/labor relations, production/operations, R&D/engineering, and others.

The sum of industry sales was regressed against the year between year t and year t - 4, and the standard error of the regression coefficient was used to capture industry dynamism. A larger standard error of the regression coefficient means that industry sales were more dynamic and unpredictable over time.

The number of Protestant sects (Haveman 2016) during the state's founding period, that is, when the state was admitted to the Union. The count is a time-invariant state-level attribute merged into firm observations by the firm's headquarters location.
time_window: at state founding (state admission to the Union)

description: The number of women senior leaders, hand-collected from proxy statements available through EDGAR and coded by research assistants by name, job title, and gender; proxy statements have been consistently available since 2001. The manually coded data exhibit a significant overlap with the data from Execucomp. Financial information is sourced from Compustat.

Calculated as the difference between the number of words addressing suffrage, initiative, and representation (categories 1-3) and those addressing state powers and executive authority (categories 4-5), divided by the total number of words in a state constitution. The data, drawn from Clouse (2019), include the initial and subsequent versions of state constitutions issued by state legislatures, governments, and general assemblies.

The average number of immigrants from countries with predominantly Catholic populations (e.g., France, Ireland, Italy, Poland, and Spain), computed from U.S. Census data available from 1850 onward in decennial intervals. Immigrant origins are identified by country and cross-referenced with the Correlates of War's World Religion Project and other historical sources; countries with balanced Catholic and Protestant populations, such as Germany and the United Kingdom, are excluded. Immigration variables are adjusted using historical GDP data from the Maddison Project Database.

The number of Protestant sects during the state's founding period, using the annual Haveman (2016) data, used as the independent variable in the state-level regressions of the constitutional focus on equality.
time_window: at state founding (state admission to the Union)

description: The difference between the number of words addressing suffrage, initiative, and representation (categories 1-3) and those addressing state powers and executive authority (categories 4-5), divided by the total number of words in the state constitution; both the initial and future constitutions are measured.

The average number of immigrants from predominantly Catholic countries based on U.S. Census/IPUMS decennial data, used as the counter-imprinting variable in the state-level discussion of institutional persistence.

Indicator of competing against higher-ability opponents. It equals one for contestants assigned to the upper division, that is, contestants with an ability rating at or above the division threshold, and zero for contestants just below the threshold in the lower division.

The contestant's point score in the competition, net of challenge points. The final point score is the sum of points earned from submitted solutions across the three problems plus points earned during the challenge phase; the authors use the point score net of challenge points because challenge points are not comparable across rooms. The points earned from submitted solutions are comparable across rooms because all solutions had to pass the same set of tests.

The declared primary interest for signing up for Topcoder. A primary interest in 'technology competitions' and in 'creative competitions' is categorized as indicative of achievement-based motives, whereas an interest in 'cash' or 'employment' is categorized as economic-based motives. On Topcoder these categories are mutually exclusive.
time_window: at first registration on the platform

description: Indicator for female coders, used to interact gender with the treatment effect. The authors report that 97% of the contestants in the sample are male.

The number of prior competitions in both divisions, which the authors define as their measure of experience. In the classification used for the interaction, coders in the top quartile of prior competitions are referred to as 'experienced coders', whereas those in the bottom three quartiles are considered less experienced.
time_window: counted prior to the focal contest

description: Indicator equal to one if the coder's performance ranks in the top 5% of all coders in the same SRM, and zero otherwise. The dependent variable uses the same regression model as the main performance equation, estimated with local and global polynomial controls.

Topcoder's ability rating, standardized and centered at the division threshold, used as the running variable in the regression discontinuity design. Contestants with a negative rating compete in the lower division, whereas contestants with a positive rating compete in the upper division. A polynomial function of the rating, allowed to differ below and above the threshold, controls for the smooth dependence of performance on ability rating.

For each firm in a given year, industry effects are estimated in a subsample comprising all observations related to the industries in which the firm is active in that year. The measure divides the between-industry variance of business performance by the sum of that variance and the average within-industry variance of business performance in those industries, using the Intraclass Correlation Coefficient to estimate the proportion of total variation attributable to industry effects. The between-industry variance is the variance of mean industry ROA across the industries in which the firm operates, and the within-industry variance is the dispersion of individual business unit ROA within each industry. The within- and between-industry variance components are meaningful only in relative terms, with no absolute thresholds, and a firm's value is interpretable only in comparison with other firms in the sample.

The dependent variable is constructed following a similar approach to the Relative Value Added by Allocation (AVA) variable introduced by Rajan et al. (2000), measuring the extent to which a firm's capital allocation across its business units aligns with an industry-based benchmark. Investment for a segment is based on the segment's capital expenditure and beginning-of-period assets relative to the median asset-scaled capital expenditure of single-business firms in its industry, weighted by the segment's assets divided by firm total assets. The variable q is the segment's industry Tobin's q mean-centered across the segment's parent's portfolio to capture the segment's industry investment opportunities relative to its sister businesses. Because the match (mismatch) between the signs of q and Investment reveals conformity to (or deviation from) industry investment trends at the segment level, the firm-year variable provides a measure of the sensitivity of the firm's capital allocations to industries' Tobin's q. The formula blocks for this variable were not readable in the source text.

A dummy variable equal to one if the worker in the acquiring firm is hired through a startup acquisition, and zero if the worker is organically hired. Acquisitions are identified in the LBD based on firm ownership changes, validated using preacquisition establishment names and employer identification numbers.

A binary outcome equal to one if the worker is no longer employed at the acquiring firm in year t since the acquisition and is employed at another firm for higher wages, and zero otherwise. The postmobility wage-increase restriction is used so the measure can be interpreted more closely as voluntary turnover. Departures are measured for the first, second, and third years following the year of joining.
time_window: first, second, and third years after the acquisition year

description: The number of quarters that the individual was employed in her prior employer before joining the acquirer, based on the prior employer, which is the target firm for acquired workers and simply the previous employer for regular hires. The variable is interacted with whether the person is an acquired or a regular hire.

A binary variable equaling one if all the founders remain employed with the acquirer in the year prior to the focal year. Because the variable is relevant only to acquired workers, the analysis splits the sample by whether the founders are retained.
time_window: year prior to the dependent variable's time window

description: A dummy variable equaling one if the acquired establishment remains as a stand-alone entity in its preacquisition location three years after the acquisition. It equals zero (integration) if the acquired establishment is moved to the location of, or simply absorbed by, the acquirer's headquarters establishment during the three years. The measurement of employee turnover is independent from this measure.

Coded one when a SPAC's attempt to go public resulted in a successful IPO completion, and zero when the attempt failed. It captures the likelihood of successfully raising capital through an IPO and is one key measure scholars have used to assess the success of a firm's financing efforts.
The average age of a firm's founders, used as an indicator of the founders' general experience and expertise.
The number of founders with Ivy League degrees.

variable_name: Founders with top management team (TMT) experience
description: The number of founders who had top management experience in publicly listed firms.
The number of founders with experience in private equity (PE) and venture capital (VC).
The sum of media articles mentioning all founders in a focal SPAC in leading U.S. business media in the year before the Form S-1 was filed.
time_window: the year before the Form S-1 was filed

description: The number of founders in a focal SPAC who had been involved in at least one other SPAC in the past that successfully acquired a target.
The dollar amount of the founders' investment in the SPAC, taken as a signal of the founders' own assessment of the venture and of alignment of their interests with other investors.

The number of uncertainty-related words within the management team section divided by the total number of words in that section, using Loughran and McDonald's (2011, 2013) uncertain word list of 297 words that denote uncertainty (e.g., may, could, believe, possible, anticipate, depending, might, likelihood), accounting for all conjugations. The management team section lists the names, ages, and positions of executive officers and directors and provides brief biographies together with their relevant skills, executive compensation, and possible conflicts of interest.
scale: percentage of words in the section

variable_name: Uncertain language - S1 acquisition of a target
description: The number of uncertainty-related words within the proposed business section divided by the total number of words in that section, using Loughran and McDonald's (2011, 2013) uncertain word list. This section contains information about the acquisition of a target, including the search process and the risks associated with finding a target, valuing it, conducting due diligence, securing shareholder approval, and the negotiation, drafting, and execution of relevant agreements.
scale: percentage of words in the section

description: The number of uncertainty-related words within the risk factors section divided by the total number of words in that section, using Loughran and McDonald's (2011, 2013) uncertain word list. This section contains information and broader concerns about investing in SPACs as an emergent vehicle itself, including risks associated with SPACs as blank check companies, dilution of shareholders, SEC rules, and the uncertain regulatory environment.
scale: percentage of words in the section

description: Following Souder and Bromiley (2012), asset durability captures the horizons of firms' new capital investments each year, that is, the expected life of only newly purchased capital. It is based on gross PP&E (the total value of all property, plant, and equipment a firm owns without accumulated depreciation), CAPEX (funds used each year for new additions to gross PP&E, excluding amounts from acquisitions), and depreciation rate and expense. Higher depreciation rates and expenses and lower capital expenditures decrease firms' investment horizons, so a lower value signals that a firm is making fewer investments in long-term capital. The value is restricted to a feasible range (1 to 40 years) for the depreciable life of capital expenditures using straight-line depreciation; the equation itself was not readable in the provided text.
time_window: dependent variable measured in year t+1

description: The ratio of the number of industry peers sued in SCA litigation in the prior three years over the total number of industry peers, based on the FIC-200 industry classification. Industry peers are identified using fixed industry classification (FIC) identifiers from Hoberg and Phillips, which are generated from a clustering algorithm applied to product similarity scores derived from a textual analysis of firms' product descriptions in 10-K filings, using the set of 200 classifications. A three-year period is used because managers' assessment of their litigation risk is likely to extend beyond one year.
time_window: prior three years, measured in year t

description: Investors' horizons are measured from their portfolio churn ratio, which captures how frequently an investor reshuffles its portfolio; investors who churn their portfolios quickly are seen as having short investment horizons. Investor-level churn ratios are weighted by the stock ownership of a given investor to obtain a firm-level value in a year-quarter, and the annual average of year-quarter firm-level churn ratios is multiplied by −1, so that a larger value indicates that a firm's investors, on average, have longer horizons. The churn-ratio formula was not readable in the provided text.
time_window: year-quarter churn ratios averaged annually; measured in year t

description: The number of future focus words included in the Linguistic Inquiry and Word Count (LIWC) future focus dictionary, scaled by the total number of words in the question and answer (Q&A) sections of earnings call transcripts. Consistent with DesJardine and Shi (2021), only CEOs' language in the Q&A sections is used because language in the prepared remarks section is more easily subject to impression management.
time_window: earnings call transcripts; measured in year t

description: Equals one for each quarter after Google Maps has formally entered a given country and zero otherwise. It captures whether the OpenStreetMap community in a given country is in competition with Google Maps, and is used both in the contributor-quarter specification for pre-entry contributors and in the country-quarter specification for newly recruited contributors.
level: country-quarter (applied to contributor-quarter observations as well)

description: The number of contributions made by contributor i in quarter t, contingent on contributor i having contributed before 2009; each contribution is an uploaded changeset placed within a country using its average latitude and longitude. If a contributor contributes to multiple countries, each contributor-country combination is treated as a unique contributor. In the estimation the variable is logged after being inflated by one.
scale: count (log of count plus one in the regressions)

description: The total number of contributions in country c in quarter t from newly recruited contributors, that is, the sum of contributions across all individuals contributing for the first time in a given country-quarter; individuals are not counted again once they are no longer newly recruited. In the estimation the variable is logged after being inflated by one.
scale: count (log of count plus one in the regressions)

description: Equals one if the contributor belongs to a country with above-median GitHub contributions or above-median Firefox market share. The political proxies are country-level: the average number of contributions ('pushes') per capita to GitHub, an open-source platform, and the market share of the crowdsourced browser Mozilla Firefox; both capture macro-level differences among countries in their orientation toward open source.

Equals one if a contributor belongs to a community with a mailing list or has hosted a mapping event. Both are country-level measures of real investments made by country communities to foster social interaction within OpenStreetMap, collected from official OpenStreetMap sources as of 2014.

Equals one if a contributor ranks in the top five by contributions or has made more than 10 contributions in her community before Google Maps entry. Rank captures the very top contributors in each country, whereas the 10-contribution threshold distinguishes those who had made sufficient investments in the community to deserve a basic level of respect from other members.

Measured by content analysis of press items mentioning the CEO in the past five years (year t-4 to year t). A customized dictionary of 72 risk-proneness and risk-aversion words (selected out of 120 by two senior scholars rating each keyword from one = high risk aversion to seven = high risk proneness, retaining words scoring five and higher and three and lower) was developed. A Python algorithm counted risk-proneness and risk-aversion words appearing within 15 words after the CEO's name, and the authors report that most relevant risk-propensity words appeared after rather than before the CEO's name while only 2.119% of coded words were suspected of reversed meaning. Risk propensity is a ratio of risk-proneness words to risk-aversion words, each adjusted by the count of press items containing such words; the printed formula is garbled in the OCR text, but a high value of the measure indicates the CEO's risk proneness.

A single continuous variable capturing the proportion of new products that the firm introduced in a given year out of its total number of new products and versions of existing products. Products were classified using a software product typology encompassing four product classes, 54 product segments, and 464 product functions, developed with industry experts and the Software & Information Industry Association. A product was coded as new if it incorporated completely new functionality and was substantially distinct from the firm's prior products; two trained coders classified products based on name, version number, and distinct functionality, with interrater reliability of 84.570%. The variable is measured at year t+1, with all independent variables, moderators, and controls lagged by one year.
Measured as the number of years the individual served as the firm's CEO. Updated annually and lagged by one year relative to the dependent variable.
Indicates whether the CEO also served as the chairperson of the board in a given year, coded one and zero otherwise.

Distinguishes an outsider who was employed by another firm prior to the appointment as the CEO in the firm (coded zero) from an insider who spent at least two years in the firm in another position before being appointed as CEO (coded one).

Measured as the ratio of the accumulated number of new products to the total number of products that a firm introduced (excluding year t, which precedes the year in which the dependent variable is measured), weighted by a memory decay rate of r = 10%. The printed measure sums, from year t-1 back to the year of first product introduction, the count of new products introduced in a given year divided by the count of all products introduced that year, each weighted by the decay factor.
time_window: up to year t-1, with 10% memory decay

description: Measured by counting the number of other firms in the sample that introduced software products in the past three years whose functionality overlaps with at least one of the firm's products during that period; the three-year period is in line with the observed average product life cycle in the sample.

Similarity between every pair of films in the studio's portfolio was estimated as the number of matching genres divided by the average number of genres used to classify the two movies, giving a value scaled between 0 (two movies have no genres in common) and 1 (all genres in each movie appear in the other movie). The measure is decade-specific and captures the average of these similarity coefficients over all pairs of movies in the studio portfolio leading to the release of the focal movie, so it varies with the release date of each movie. Genre descriptors come from IMDb classification of movies into nonexclusive genres.
level: movie (firm-level focus computed at each movie's release)
time_window: average over all pairs of movies in the studio portfolio leading to the release of the focal movie

description: Similarity between every pair of films in the distributor's portfolio was estimated as the number of matching genres divided by the average number of genres used to classify the two movies, giving a value scaled between 0 (two movies have no genres in common) and 1 (all genres in each movie appear in the other movie). The measure is decade-specific and captures the average of these similarity coefficients over all pairs of movies in the distributor portfolio leading to the release of the focal movie. Genre descriptors come from IMDb classification of movies into nonexclusive genres.
level: movie (firm-level focus computed at each movie's release)
time_window: average over all pairs of movies in the distributor portfolio leading to the release of the focal movie

description: ROI is calculated as the ratio of domestic box office revenues minus production costs divided by production costs. Because the distribution of movie profitability is highly skewed, the Profit variable was calculated by adding 1 to the raw profitability score and taking the natural log of the result, so that the logarithm is identified across the entire range of return values.

variable_name: Production Studio Focus and Distributor Focus
description: Strategic focus is operationalized by two portfolio-similarity measures: Production Studio Focus and Distributor Focus. Each is the average pairwise genre similarity (Sorensen-Dice coefficient from IMDb genre labels, scaled 0 to 1) of the films in the firm's portfolio up to the release of the focal movie. Higher values mean a more focused portfolio.

variable_name: Degree of MPC in product marketsijt
description: Adapted from the dyadic measure of Baum and Korn (1999); the specification is given as a formula whose OCR rendering is unreadable in the payload. In prose, m denotes a given product market in the set of markets Mit or Mjt in which focal firm i and rival j were each present in year t, Pimt and Pjmt are the proportion of sales firm i and rival j had in product market m, and Dimt and Djmt are dummy variables indicating whether firm i and rival j were present in product market m in year t. A squared term of Degree of MPC in product marketsijt was further constructed to test the curvilinear effect.

variable_name: Degree of firm i's expansion into rival j's technological areas
description: Ratio of the number of rival j's patent classes entered by firm i in year t+1 over the number of rival j's patent classes in which firm i did not have patents in the five years prior to year t+1 (year t-4 to year t). For example, if the number of rival j's patent classes in which firm i did not have patents is 50 in the five years prior to year t+1 and 15 of these were entered in year t+1, the variable is coded 0.3. Patent classes are three-digit U.S. patent classes used as a proxy for an area of technological focus.
time_window: year t+1 outcome, five-year prior window (year t-4 to t)

description: Firm i's market share minus rival j's market share, where a firm's market share is the ratio of the firm's total sales over the industry's total sales in a given year. A higher value suggests that firm i has a larger market share than rival j. Interaction terms with the linear and squared multipoint contact terms were constructed to test the moderation.

Firm i's Euclidean normalized eigenvector centrality at year t minus rival j's Euclidean normalized eigenvector centrality in year t. Centrality is obtained from a comprehensive patent citation network constructed for each five-year window of patent activity among all firms in Dataquest that had patent applications, using UCINET 6.21; normalization accounts for changes in network size across years. Interaction terms with the linear and squared multipoint contact terms were constructed to test the moderation.

A Herfindahl-Hirschman index of the industries in which the VC firms in the syndicate have previously invested, considering only the experience of the last 15 years. The maximum specialization across the VC firms in the syndicate is used, reflecting that different investors add different types of value. The measure varies from zero to one, approaching zero when all VC firms in the syndicate are generalists and one when at least one VC is highly specialized in an industry.

The event variable for the Cox regression models, coded as one if the start-up applies for a patent after VC investment and zero otherwise. Patents were hand-collected from the USPTO website with hand-matching of the name of the company, location, and scientists. Following the standard in the literature, patents that are eventually granted are considered at the time of application.

variable_name: Time to first patent after VC investment
description: The duration variable, measured as the number of days between VC investment and patent application. Measuring in days reduces ties and improves the estimation power of hazard models. There is one observation per start-up, and the data are right-censored.

The level of development of the country research environment of a start-up, measured as a discounted stock of patents in biotech in a given country. All biotech patents for each country-year were gathered directly from the USPTO, following the OECD definitions of biotech codes within the International Patent Classification. The sample is split by the median of this measure.

Calculated following the same process as the country measure but for each U.S. state (and Washington, DC), to account for heterogeneity within the U.S. subsample (the high research environment subsample).

variable_name: Number of universities founded in the incumbent's category (t-1)
description: Count of organizations founded in the incumbent's own identity category. The classification of new entrants into categories relies on the cluster analysis performed on annual data. The variable is lagged by one year; because each founding requires government approval, a one-year lag in practice corresponds to incumbents having several years to respond.

variable_name: Number of universities founded in other categories (t-1)
description: Count of organizations founded in identity categories other than the incumbent's own category. The classification of new entrants into categories relies on the cluster analysis performed on annual data, and the variable is lagged by one year.

variable_name: Number of universities founded in other ancestral categories (t-1)
description: For the test of Hypothesis 4, entries into other categories are divided into the number of organizations founded in other ancestral identity categories and the number of organizations founded outside ancestral identity categories. The variable is lagged by one year.

variable_name: Number of universities founded outside ancestral categories (t-1)
description: Count of organizations founded outside the ancestral identity categories. Universities that exhibit characteristics of multiple ancestral categories are classified as being outside them, which leads to a more liberal interpretation of what constitutes a deviation from ancestral templates. The variable is lagged by one year.

variable_name: Classical: number of programs per faculty
description: For Classical universities, identity-deepening actions are measured as the average number of programs they offer across their faculties; offering a greater variety of degree programs constitutes an identity deepening action for this category. Estimated with OLS on an unbalanced university-year panel.

variable_name: American: number of students going on exchange
description: For incumbents in the American category, investments in exchange programs with foreign universities are used as the identity-deepening measure. Lacking data on the number of exchange programs, the authors rely on the number of students that participate in these programs, which is driven by the university's focus on its exchange operations and the funding it secures and allocates for these operations. Estimated with a negative binomial model.

variable_name: Orientation to quality in teaching: faculty members to students (ratio)
description: Orientation to quality in teaching is measured with the faculty-student ratio, which informants mentioned as a mark of quality in teaching. The measure is correlated highly with the ratio of associate or full professors to students and gives the same results in analyses. Estimated with a fractional logit model.

variable_name: Orientation to research: proportion of PhD students
description: Research orientation is measured with the proportion of doctoral students among all students; the size of graduate programs is widely seen as a sign of research orientation. Estimated with a fractional logit model.

A second measure of research orientation is applications to the various grant programs that were started by The Scientific and Technological Research Council of Turkey (TUBITAK) in 2003. The authors use applications for grants rather than approvals or subsequent publications because this likely captures early stages of orientation to research better. Estimated with a negative binomial model.

variable_name: Classical: disciplinary range of all faculties
description: For Classical universities, identity-affirming actions are measured by the degree to which universities manifest the distinguishing feature of their category, disciplinary range, i.e. the number of disciplines represented among the 12 that are officially recognized by the Interuniversity Assembly. Estimated with a negative binomial model.

variable_name: Technical: proportion of faculties in technical faculties
description: For the Technical category, identity-affirming actions are measured by the focus on technical faculties, i.e. the proportion of faculties in engineering and architecture fields, which is the distinguishing feature of that category. Estimated with a fractional logit model.

variable_name: American: number of programs with instruction in English
description: For the American-modeled category, identity-affirming actions are measured by the degree to which universities manifest their distinguishing feature, programs taught in English. Estimated with a negative binomial model.

Based on the Osgood Semantic Dimensions list implemented in the LIWC software, the LIWC software identified the level of positive emotions in the text of each beer name by measuring the percentage of words in a name that are positively charged. The variable counts the number of words in the beer name identified as positively charged and divides the count by the total number of words in the name. The variable is time invariant.
scale: proportion of positively charged words in the name (0 to 1)

description: Based on the Osgood Semantic Dimensions list implemented in the LIWC software, the LIWC software identified the level of negative emotions in the text of each beer name by measuring the percentage of words in a name that are negatively charged. The variable counts the number of words in the beer name identified as negatively charged and divides the count by the total number of words in the name. The variable is time invariant.
scale: proportion of negatively charged words in the name (0 to 1)

description: Each reviewer evaluates a beer on a scale from one to five in increments of 0.25 on the dimensions of look, smell, taste, and feel; the authors first generated the mean of these four scores for each review of a given beer and then calculated the average score of all reviews of a given beer in a given year. The resulting measure is a time-varying continuous variable ranging from one to five.

Texts of beer reviews were analyzed with the natural language processing software Linguistic Inquiry and Word Count (LIWC) using a dictionary of authenticity words created by Kovacs et al. (2014, table 1); the number of words communicating a sentiment of authenticity in each review was counted and each word was weighted by its score in that dictionary. The count of weighted words was aggregated to the beer-year level, producing a time-varying yearly authenticity score for each beer across all its reviews.

variable_name: Beer perceived authenticity (lagged control in appeal models)
description: The same authenticity-weighted word count from all reviews of a given beer in a given year, lagged by one year, is included as a control in the models predicting beer appeal.

variable_name: Haessel's R2 (fit to true values) and the change in fit, Δ(R2)
description: Haessel's R2 is a measure of statistical fit that assesses the extent to which valuations match the true value of an asset, ranging from zero to one; the higher its value, the better the fit. It was used ex ante by calculating the fit between the responses in the Valuation Questionnaire and true values, and ex post by calculating the fit between market prices and true values. The dependent variable capturing change in accuracy is the difference between the ex post and the ex ante fit, so that a negative value means that participants exhibited worse valuation in trading than in the questionnaire.
level: market (ex ante responses aggregated for each market)
time_window: ex ante (before trading) and ex post (during trading)

variable_name: Common error component of the total average valuation error
description: The total average valuation error was decomposed into two components following the economics and finance literature (Hommes et al.). The first term is the average dispersion error, the squared distance between a price in a specific transaction and the average price for such transactions in the same period, averaged across transactions and periods, which measures the similarity of prices. The second term is the average common error, the squared distance between the average price in a period and the true value for that period, averaged over periods, which measures how similar valuation errors are across market participants. The common component was divided by the overall error to derive the average percentage of the common component in overall error per period across markets.
time_window: each of the 10 trading periods of every experimental market

description: To assess the presence and magnitude of bubbles the authors used three measures from the economics literature. The most common is Haessel's R2, a measure of statistical fit that assesses the extent to which market prices match the true value of an asset, with higher values indicating a better fit. The two additional measures are normalized absolute price deviation, the absolute deviation between mean prices and true values summed for each period and divided by the number of shares outstanding, and price amplitude, the highest minus the lowest discrepancy between true value and prices divided by 100. Bubbles were defined as persistent deviations above 0.10 on a scale of 0.00-1.00.

variable_name: Bubble magnitude (change from ex ante valuations to market prices)
description: The same three bubble measures (Haessel's R2, normalized absolute price deviation, and price amplitude) were computed in Study 2, and the average change in valuations from ex ante to ex post was compared between the higher-ambiguity condition (Study 1) and the lower-ambiguity condition (Study 2).

variable_name: Ambiguity-reduction manipulation (feedback score on valuation technique)
description: After participants returned their Valuation Questionnaires, the authors reviewed the responses, summed the number of answers within ±10 ECUs of the correct answers, and handed each participant a sheet showing that number as a single-digit score. The feedback did not indicate which responses were wrong, provide the correct answers, or guide how to value assets. It was designed to reduce social/subjective ambiguity by providing an external validation of the technique the participant had been using to value assets.
time_window: after the Valuation Questionnaire, before trading

description: Each experimental session consisted of 10 trading periods in which participants could post bids and asks, accept others' offers, or avoid trading and earn dividends from holding assets. All bids, asks, and prices from concluded transactions were visible to everyone on a public digital board. The sequence of periods indexes how long participants observe others and interact in the market.

Piloted denotes whether FilmLA recorded that the program was piloted, regardless of whether it was later ordered to series. The authors state that Piloted therefore represents whether the program was experimented on prior to broadcast. It is available for the entire data set of 1,505 programs and is the dependent variable in the H1a test.

One Hour is an indicator encoding each show's runtime as marked by FilmLA. Half-hour shows are situational comedies where the cast remains consistent across episodes and plots are usually self-contained within each episode; hour-long programs are classified as dramas because cast members often change between episodes through plotlines that span episodes. The authors use One Hour programs to represent low-type projects, where the information generated by the pilot is limited.

Series Ordered is an indicator of whether the program was ordered to series, that is, whether it passed the pilot stage. It is the dependent variable for the H1b test, which restricts observations to piloted shows because the prediction is conditional on piloting. Piloted programs that were not ordered to series were terminated after the experimental stage.

Veteran Actor denotes whether any of the main actors associated with a program are listed as the first actor credit on a prior program. Each cast member listed for each program in the FilmLA data set is matched against IMDb's television program history for each actor, which includes cast lists for all programs since about 1950. Receiving first actor credit implies that the actor was the most prominent actor in a program. The authors use it as a proxy for the level of resources allocated to a program, since actors are cast after the program receives either a straight-to-series or pilot order.

IMDb Rating is the average user rating for a program on IMDb, measured for the first season of a program, and is the primary outcome variable. The authors view it as a general proxy for program outcomes, noting it correlates with financial metrics and with other television measures. It is available for 759 observations, because IMDb variables are valid only for programs that were ordered to series and were successfully matched to IMDb.

The authors argue that Veteran Actor meets the superstar criterion, because the positive relationship between star actors and film performance is well documented and should also matter to a similar medium like television. They also argue it satisfies the requirement of being allocated subsequently, since networks base their piloting decisions on the background of a program's main writer and the script without knowledge of which actors will play which parts.

variable_name: custom estimator of the treatment effect of piloting
description: For H3a and H3b the authors use a custom estimator, described as inverse-propensity-score-based weighting over a region of 10th to 90th percentile common support that applies a bias adjustment to point estimates and standard errors, because networks and creators select programs into piloting or straight-to-series orders. It is compared against standard OLS estimates. The estimator is built from the Overlap sample of piloted programs before 2013 with a high propensity of being ordered straight to series and straight-to-series programs after 2013 with a low propensity of being ordered straight to series.

Scientist Mobility is a dichotomous measure that takes on the value of one if a scientist mobility event occurred between the two firms in a dyad during the period of five years from t-5 to t-1, where t is the year of a focal alliance deal, and zero otherwise. A mobility event was identified when a scientist was listed as an inventor in patents granted to two different firms, and its year was calculated as the halfway point between the last patenting date at the originating firm and the first patenting date at the destination firm. The sample is based on unique dyads, so the variable also accounts for scientists' movements in either of the two possible directions in a dyad.

R&D Alliance Formation is dyadic and dichotomous and equals one for realized alliances and zero for unrealized alliances between two ventures in year t. Realized alliance deals come from the alliance database, and for each realized deal the authors constructed the set of potential yet unrealized deals from all biotech ventures meeting the same screening criteria.

Absence of Ties takes on a value of one if the firms in a dyad have no direct or indirect (i.e., shared third-party) interfirm alliances during the five years before the focal R&D alliance and zero otherwise.
time_window: five years before the focal R&D alliance

description: Absence of Colocation is a binary indicator variable that takes on a value of one if the headquarters of both prospective R&D alliance partners are not located in the same state of the United States and zero otherwise.

Built from Crunchbase category labels. A proximity score Pij is computed for each pair of categories from the frequency with which the two categories coincide at any finance company prior to the startup's founding, relative to the number of times each category appears. Category spanning is one minus the average of the proximity scores of each pair of categories listed by the startup, where N is the total number of category pairs. In the main analysis the continuous measure is discretized at its median into category spanning versus not category spanning.

The percentage of shared industry categories between the incumbent and the startup, calculated as a metric ranged 0 to 1. It is used to determine whether each startup was related to each incumbent; in the main analysis a startup is considered related to an incumbent if the relatedness metric was at or above 0.4.

The market-adjusted firm returns on the three-day window following a startup funding announcement, the window including the day of the announcement and the following two days. Market-adjusted returns are calculated as the firm return (CRSP holding period return) minus the return on the CRSP value-weighted index. In the reported models the dependent variable is winsorized at the 1% level.
time_window: three-day window (day of announcement and following two days)

description: For each firm-year, the authors first obtain an average categorical CSR score for each of eight CSR categories and, analogously, an average score for each category across all firms in the firm's two-digit SIC industry in that year. They then compute the squared difference between the firm's categorical score and the industry average for each category and add up these squared differences across all eight categories. A high value means the firm's cross-category pattern of CSR performance differs from the industry average pattern, and a low value means it resembles it.

Calculated by aggregating the firm's categorical scores across all eight CSR categories observed in the data set in each year. It proxies for the overall CSR performance (overall stakeholder orientation) of the firm and is included as a control in the market value regressions.
Calculated as the market value of common stocks (i.e., number of stocks outstanding times stock price) plus the total debt outstanding. It is the dependent variable of the main regressions.

Built in two steps. First, using SASB data, the authors match the issues SASB classifies as material for each of its 79 industries with the issues covered by the eight CSR categories of the ASSET4 database; a category is considered material for an industry if at least one SASB-material issue for that industry is related to it. Second, they count the number of CSR categories considered material for each industry. Because SASB has a single materiality classification, the variable is a time-invariant proxy for materiality.

The same cross-category uniqueness construct used in the main analysis (summed squared differences between the firm's categorical CSR scores and its industry's average categorical scores), here used as the dependent variable of the difference-in-differences models around the oil spill.
time_window: one fiscal year before and one fiscal year after April 20, 2010

description: A decomposition of CSR Uniqueness in which the squared differences for the CSR categories more directly affected by the oil spill are added up. The categories are resource use reduction, emissions reduction, employee health and safety, employee relations, and community.
time_window: one fiscal year before and one fiscal year after April 20, 2010

description: Analogous to Material Uniqueness but calculated by adding up the squared differences for the other three CSR categories in the data, which were arguably less affected by the Deepwater Horizon disaster.
time_window: one fiscal year before and one fiscal year after April 20, 2010

description: A dummy that equals one for firms with SIC equal to 13 and zero otherwise; it indicates treated industries, i.e., extractive industries closely related to oil. It is omitted in models that include industry fixed effects because of collinearity.
time_window: one fiscal year before and one fiscal year after April 20, 2010

description: A dummy that equals one for the first fiscal year ending after April 20, 2010 (the day the Deepwater Horizon rig exploded) and zero for the last fiscal year ending before that date.
time_window: one fiscal year before and one fiscal year after April 20, 2010

description: A composite variable built from two data points, the firm's patent portfolio and its camera portfolio. Each is operationalized for each firm-year as the proportion of analog patents (or models) over analog plus digital patents (or models). Confirmatory factor analysis using structural equation modeling was used to develop the composite, computed as the weighted sum of the product of both measures and their standardized factor loadings, and expressed as an overall percentile. The variable was lagged by one year.

Coded one if a firm made a new technology acquisition in a year and zero otherwise. A new technology acquisition is one where a firm acquired a target possessing digital photography resources and products as per SDC. Alliances, acquisitions and legacy divestitures were identified from SDC Platinum and augmented with Lexis-Nexis and other archival sources.

Coded one if a firm divested legacy technology resources or unit(s) in a year and zero otherwise. The divested units or assets had to be based on the legacy analog (silver-halide based) photography technology.

The cumulative number of alliances made by a firm for technological or product-related knowledge sharing with partners, or joint development of technology- or product-related resources, linked to digital photography. Alliances coded as R&D alliances or new technology-based product development alliances in SDC. The variable was lagged by one year.

For each firm-year when an acquisition was made, the choice of integration approach was coded as one for full integration or full autonomy and two for partial integration; years when a firm did not make an acquisition were coded zero. Full integration was coded when the target was fully absorbed; full autonomy when the acquirer bought a majority stake but ceded operational control by retaining the target's identity as a separate business unit; partial when some target resources were absorbed and residual resources were granted autonomy.
scale: 0 = no acquisition, 1 = full integration or full autonomy, 2 = partial integration

description: Coded one in the year when a firm exited the digital camera product market and zero otherwise, so that a higher value indicates exit rather than survival. Exit was assessed using the multidimensional conceptualization of Josefy et al. (2017): discontinued production of digital cameras (operations failure), acquisition and an end to operational autonomy (ownership failure), or dissolution or bankruptcy (solvency failure). Firms remaining were treated as right censored.

variable_name: Negative status contrast of new CEO
description: A spline variable computed as old CEO status minus new CEO status when the new CEO's status is below the old CEO's status, and zero when the new CEO's status is greater than or equal to the old CEO's status. Status is a fortune rank weighted index of the CEO's external board memberships counted during the year of transition. It ranged from 0 to 15.8 with a mean of 0.72 and a standard deviation of 1.56.

variable_name: Positive status contrast of new CEO
description: A spline variable computed as new CEO status minus old CEO status when the new CEO's status exceeds the old CEO's status, and zero when the new CEO's status is less than or equal to the old CEO's status. Status is a fortune rank weighted index of the CEO's external board memberships counted during the year of transition. It ranged from 0 to 15.5 with a mean of 0.76 and a standard deviation of 1.62.

A fortune rank weighted measure of CEO status combining the count and the status of the boards the CEO sits on: full credit for a Fortune 100 board membership and half credit for a non-Fortune board. Boards were categorized into six types based on fortune ranking and weighted accordingly.

An event history in which a new CEO is at risk of making an acquisition announcement each day after the CEO's appointment, so that each CEO can make multiple acquisition announcements. Each new CEO's acquisition activities were observed for a maximum of three years (1,096 days) from the date of appointment, and Cox hazard rate models based on interarrival time estimate the rate of transition from the Kth acquisition to the K+1th acquisition.
time_window: maximum of three years (1,096 days) from appointment date

description: A separate hazard rate analysis estimated the hazard rate of a focal CEO acquiring an unrelated target at any given time during the observation window. Acquisitions were classified into diversifying and related acquisitions based on Securities Data Company's proprietary classification system; a deal was classified as a diversifying acquisition when the acquirer and target were from different midindustry.
time_window: observation window (maximum three years from appointment)

description: A separate hazard rate analysis estimated a new CEO's hazard rate of making a big acquisition announcement. Big acquisitions were first identified as those reported to be over 100 million USD in transaction value; when the exact transaction value was not disclosed in SDC, other news sources were searched to identify if the deal was valued above 100 million.
time_window: observation window (maximum three years from appointment)

variable_name: Market reaction to new CEO announcement
