description: Cumulative abnormal returns computed from deviations in actual returns from predicted returns following the event, where the predicted return on a firm's stock is a function of a firm-specific intercept, a firm-specific regression coefficient (systematic risk) and the market return for the day. A window of 10 days before the event and 10 days after the event was used to compute the cumulative abnormal returns.
time_window: 10 days before and 10 days after the event

description: The coefficient of media favorableness computed from content analysis of news items published under the 'Major World Publications' category during the one month before and after the announcement date, coded as positively worded, negatively worded, neutral, or irrelevant. The value of this measure ranges from -1 to 1, where 1 indicates all positive coverage, -1 indicates all negative coverage, and 0 indicates a balance between the two during the observation period.
time_window: one month before and after the announcement date

description: Participants were randomly assigned to a low or high epistemic motivation condition. Those in the high condition were told before commencing the problem formulation activity that the study was not an exam, that there were no right or wrong answers, that only their thought process would be evaluated, and that a thorough process of problem analysis would require them to reflect on, summarize, and develop their own thoughts; participants in the low condition did not receive this statement. The manipulation was checked with three items ('I felt accountable for the quality of the process by which I analyzed the problem,' 'I thought carefully about what the core issues are,' and 'I tried to understand my problem better') rated on a five-point scale from Strongly Disagree to Strongly Agree and averaged (Cronbach's alpha equals 0.83).
scale: high vs. low experimental condition; manipulation check items on a five-point response scale

description: Participants were randomly assigned to a low or high construal level condition and answered a series of either why or how questions. After reading an example (why or how to attain life happiness), participants followed the same process of asking themselves why or how they would accomplish two goals, achieving success and gaining more knowledge, providing successively more abstract reasons in the high condition or successively more concrete means in the low condition. The manipulation was strengthened by embedding construal level-related language in the task instructions: the high condition was asked why they thought the problem exists and what the underlying causes are, and the low condition was asked how the problem occurred and what kinds of contexts and factors created it.

Comprehensiveness is the number of alternative and relevant causes of a problem. Two expert coders who were familiar with the agricultural industry in China and who were blind to the hypotheses counted the number of nonredundant and relevant causes that participants identified. The two coders converged in the number of causes they counted, with an ICC(1) estimate of agreement of 0.82 and an ICC(2) estimate of reliability of 0.90, and the ratings were averaged to create the measure.

Half of the participants were randomly asked to be accountable for their process of analysis. They were told that the study was curious about their thought process, that they should not feel pressure to find the right answers, and that a professor might contact them via a short phone call to learn about the rationales behind their answers and their thought processes, and were asked to indicate times for contact in the following week; participants in the low condition received only the definition and symptoms of medical noncompliance. During debriefing, participants in the process accountability condition were told that they would not be contacted and that the instruction was part of the experimental manipulation. The manipulation was checked with four items rated on a seven-point scale from Strongly Disagree to Strongly Agree (Cronbach's alpha equals 0.83).
scale: high vs. low experimental condition; manipulation check items on a seven-point response scale

description: As in Study 1, construal levels were manipulated by asking participants a series of either why or how questions. After reading an example (why or how to attain life happiness), participants read one of three prompts and then answered why or how they would accomplish each goal four times; all participants responded to the three prompts, with the order of the prompts randomized. Three prompts were used rather than two to strengthen the manipulation because participants were not as time constrained as the executives in Study 1.

Comprehensiveness was again measured via the number of nonredundant and relevant causes of medical noncompliance identified by participants. To derive a list of the causes, the authors reviewed relevant literature and public health websites, conducted five rounds of pilot studies, each with nine participants, and had six master's degree students from the school of social work and two medical doctors review the coding scheme. Two trained coders blind to the hypotheses reviewed each participant's analysis and coded the number of nonredundant, relevant causes; the ICC(1) and ICC(2) estimates of interrater agreement and reliability were 0.82 and 0.90, and the number of causes identified was averaged across the two coders.

Binary variable indicating whether the song was produced by a multigroup agency, the authors' measure of strategic differences in social exposure. A multigroup agency is one that has managed more than one idol group as of a given point in time, whereas a single-group agency has managed only one idol group up to that point.
time_window: updated at the beginning of each one-week segment

description: Binary variable denoting whether the song is the title track of an album, a measure of product visibility. The authors argue these songs receive greater social exposure through music videos, marketing around the song, and televised performances.
time_window: updated at the beginning of each one-week segment

description: Continuous count of the number of top-100 ranked songs that the song's group had prior to time t, used to capture group reputation as a source of social exposure.
time_window: count of hits prior to time t, updated over weekly segments

variable_name: Transition to popularity (ranking in the top 100 weekly charts)
description: Dependent variable of the popularity models: the event of a song becoming popular, operationalized as occurring on the day when song i first ranked in the top 100 weekly charts. Songs entered the risk set on the day they were released; songs were allowed to remain at risk for becoming popular for a calendar year (or until the end of the study period if that occurred first).
time_window: from song release until ranking, censored at one calendar year

variable_name: Extinction (delisting from the top 100 weekly charts)
description: Dependent variable of the extinction models: the event of a popular song falling into obscurity, operationalized as occurring on the day when song i fell off the weekly charts. The risk set was defined as all idol songs that were on the top 100 weekly charts on a given day, with duration measured since first entering the top 100.
time_window: from first entering the top 100 ranking until delisting

description: Count of popularity-ranked (top 100) rival K-pop songs, N_pj, lagged by one week so that it measures the number of rival ranked songs at the start of a given one-week time segment. Rival songs are songs by groups other than the group that released the focal song.

The count of lagged rival ranked songs restricted to songs produced by single-group agencies, i.e., agencies that up until that point had managed only one idol group, so that competition coming from and felt by different organizational types can be distinguished.

The count of lagged rival ranked songs restricted to songs produced by multigroup agencies, i.e., agencies that had managed more than one idol group as of a given point in time, used to see whether songs of the strategically capable agencies generate stronger competition.

A separate term counting ranked rival songs by other groups managed by the same multigroup agency as the focal song, created in the most complete model to isolate within-agency competition (cannibalization) from between-agency competition among multigroup agencies' songs.

Employees who choose routine projects in round 2 receive a value of zero on this measure, whereas employees who choose the innovation project receive a value of one. In round 2 all participants are given a choice between continuing with more routine projects or opting for a more innovative project, with 10 minutes available for problem solving regardless of choice.

After completing round 1, employees place themselves on the skill distribution of colleagues and each employee identifies a percentile in which the employee believes to rank, expressing efficacy relative to others. Belief reporting is unincentivized to avoid hedging, and employees are told that their answers are for future study and have no impact on the focal experiment. Belief reporting precedes the innovation choice and employees receive no information about how well their colleagues perform the box-moving task.
scale: percentile on the skill distribution of colleagues
time_window: after round 1, before the innovation choice

description: Each experimental session populates both tunnel- and funnel-firm treatments; the experimental software randomly allocates each session participant as an employee to one of these two firms (alternating assignment by order of entry). All procedures are identical across firms except for the process of selecting innovators in round 2: a tunnel firm selects a maximum of 50% of all its employees once, whereas the funnel firm selects a maximum of 60% of all its employees at its initial selection point before reducing this to 40% at the second selection stage.

A continuous index operationalizing three components of enabling technology. Pervasiveness is measured by the breadth of technical fields (three-digit U.S. patent classes) in which the focal patent is subsequently cited, using a Herfindahl index from zero to one. Novelty is measured by the breadth of technical fields of the patent's backward citations, also a Herfindahl index from zero to one. Complementarity is the ratio of forward citations that uniquely cite the originating patent and not its predecessors, calculated at 15 years after grant, ranging from -1 to 1. The three factors are loaded onto a single factor using factor analysis (varimax with oblique rotation, eigenvalue > 1, Cronbach's alpha > 0.7); the resulting ETI is mean centered at zero.
time_window: citations within 15 years of the patent's grant date

description: Coded from the mandatory federal interest statement in private firms' U.S. patents: a tie between a public agency and a for-profit firm existed to exchange resources and to create a mutually desired R&D outcome. Private-firm-only efforts are the omitted category.
Binary variable that takes a value of one if the patented technology was the result of a grant-based relationship, coded from the details provided in the federal interest statement.

Binary variable that takes a value of one if the technology was the result of a procurement contract, coded from the details provided in the federal interest statement and supplemented with federal contract information.
Binary variable that takes a value of one if the technology was the result of a cooperative agreement, coded from the details provided in the federal interest statement.
Binary variable that takes a value of one if the patented technology was a result of a relationship with the DOD or NASA, coded from the details provided in the federal interest statement.
Binary variable that takes a value of one if the patented technology was a result of a relationship with the NIH, NSF, or NIST, coded from the details provided in the federal interest statement.

The fraction of the overall acetaminophen sales volume attributed to the regulated acetaminophen 500-mg submarket, computed for each firm in each region in each month. A decline in this fraction indicates repositioning away from the regulated submarket toward the unregulated 650-mg submarket. In the price equation it is complemented by the fraction of 500-mg sales by revenue in the descriptive evidence.

The price of a tablet per 500-mg dose, obtained by normalizing product prices to a price per 500-mg tablet so that prices of products containing 500-mg and 650-mg dosage strengths can be compared. The authors state that the variable uses the strength (either 500 or 650 mg), the product price of a stock-keeping unit (SKU) and the number of tablets contained in a SKU, but the formula itself is not readable in the text provided.

Investment in demand shifting measured as the ratio of marketing expenses to sales, computed annually for firms in the CMIE Prowess database. It is used as the proxy for a firm's ability to shift demand in favor of its branded products. Because financial information is available only for publicly listed firms, this variable is available only for the CMIE subsample.

Four period dummies that divide the timeline covering the design and implementation of the 2013 DPCO. Period 1 runs from March 2007 to September 2009, before the public consultation for defining essential medicines; period 2 from October 2009 to June 2011, after the consultation but before the announcement of the list of essential medicines in 2011; period 3 from July 2011 to December 2012, between the announcement of essential medicines and the public notification that these medicines will be price-controlled under the 2013 DPCO; and period 4 from January 2013 to June 2015, after the implementation of the 2013 DPCO. Period 1 is the reference period and period 4 captures the implemented regulation.
level: firm-region-month (and firm-product-region-month in the price equation)

description: A dummy variable for the unregulated acetaminophen 650-mg submarket, which enters the price equation on its own and interacted with the period dummies (and with marketing intensity in the triple interactions), so that the regulated 500-mg submarket is the reference category.

Improvement of the target's return on assets from one year before to one year after the acquisition. The variable is calculated as (target's ROA in year t+1 - average industry ROA in year t+1) - (target's ROA in year t-1 - average industry ROA in year t-1), where t is the year in which the acquisition occurred.
time_window: from one year before to one year after the acquisition (t-1 to t+1)

description: The authors first calculated the farmland ratio devoted to wheat and rice in a province from the beginning of the sample to the most recent available year and then constructed a continuous value from 0% to 100% with zero indicating all-wheat cultivation and 100% indicating all-rice cultivation. They also discretely labelled cultures with a rice farmland ratio between 50% and 100% as one, indicating rice culture, with the remaining provinces (0% to 50%) labelled as zero, indicating wheat culture. Three northeast provinces with recent rice expansion (Liaoning, Jilin, Heilongjiang) were defined as wheat culture following Talhelm et al. (2014).

variable_name: Cultural similarity (one as rice-rice; zero as wheat-wheat)
description: Dummy variable created to test the differential impact of cultural similarity: rice culture similarity versus wheat culture similarity. The variable equals one for transactions with rice culture targets and rice culture acquirers and zero for transactions with wheat culture targets and wheat culture acquirers.

variable_name: Cultural difference (one as rice target + wheat acquirer; zero as wheat target + rice acquirer)
description: Dummy variable for the two types of cross-cultural acquisitions, created to test the potential asymmetry of the impact of cultural difference. The variable equals one for transactions with rice culture targets and wheat culture acquirers and zero for transactions with wheat culture targets and rice culture acquirers.

variable_name: Prior experience with wheat target for wheat acquirer
description: For each acquirer, wheat target experience was measured as the number of transactions with wheat culture targets before the focal transaction. The variable used in the models is the wheat-target experience of wheat acquirers, one of the four experience variables created to capture the cultural interaction between wheat and rice cultures.

variable_name: Prior experience with rice target for rice acquirer
description: For each acquirer, rice target experience was measured as the number of acquisitions with targets in a rice culture before a focal transaction. The variable used in the models is the rice-target experience of rice acquirers, one of the four experience variables created to capture the cultural interaction between wheat and rice cultures.

variable_name: Prior experience with rice target for wheat acquirer
description: For each acquirer, rice target experience was measured as the number of acquisitions with targets in a rice culture before a focal transaction. The variable used in the models is the rice-target experience of wheat acquirers, one of the four experience variables created to capture the cultural interaction between wheat and rice cultures.

variable_name: Prior experience with wheat target for rice acquirer
description: For each acquirer, wheat target experience was measured as the number of transactions with wheat culture targets before the focal transaction. The variable used in the models is the wheat-target experience of rice acquirers, one of the four experience variables created to capture the cultural interaction between wheat and rice cultures.

Time-to-build is regressed on a set of systematic determinants of time-to-build (project type, region and project capacity, with industry, region and year dummies) using non-LNG oil and gas projects, and the residual is used as the measure of idiosyncratic firm speed. The residual is standardized, averaged for each firm across projects for a particular year and collapsed to the firm-year level. Positive values indicate an intrinsically slow firm; the lower the value, the greater the intrinsic speed capabilities of the firm. The regression equation is not readable in the supplied text.

Dummy variable capturing whether the firm decides to partner with another firm in the LNG project through a joint venture or to go it alone. JV equals one if the firm initiates an LNG project via a joint venture, and zero if the firm elects to go it alone and pursue autonomous development.

Categorical variable taking three values that capture whether the focal firm partners with a fast partner, partners with a slow partner, or opts for autonomous project development as the baseline category. Partner firms are categorized as fast or slow based on their realized values of Slowness, where a positive value indicates a slow partner firm and a negative value indicates a fast partner firm; where there is more than one partner firm, the average of the partner firms' Slowness values is used.
scale: three categories (Fast Partner, Slow Partner, go it alone)

description: A proxy for valuable complementary assets, constructed as a count of the number of LNG tankers that a firm possesses. Data come from Tusiani and Shearer (2007) and the 2016 World LNG Report of the International Gas Union.

Total medical expenditure per patient for the departments that are most vulnerable to malpractice lawsuits (drug prescription and dispersion, intensive care units, operating rooms, and emergency departments). For each vulnerable department the measure includes major medical expenditures reflecting investments in new equipment, staffing, and training (e.g., nursing school, interns and residence programs, paramedical education). Two control groups of expenditures are used: nonmedical expenditure per patient in vulnerable departments and medical expenditure per patient in nonvulnerable departments.

The total malpractice awards paid by health insurance firms for all healthcare providers in state s and year (t-1). The greater the total awards, the greater the potential loss from future malpractice lawsuits and the more future lawsuits will be encouraged by these awards, so a larger amount is associated with a higher risk of future malpractice liability.

A dummy variable that takes the value of 1 if state s had imposed by year (t-1) a cap on the size of awards that can be paid to plaintiffs in a medical malpractice lawsuit and 0 otherwise. The cap limits the loss for hospitals and physicians and discourages future malpractice lawsuits, and is therefore expected to reduce the risk of future malpractice liability.

A dummy variable that takes the value of 1 if a hospital is a private nonprofit hospital and 0 if it is a private for-profit hospital. Public and government-owned hospitals were excluded from the sample.

A dummy variable that indicates whether a hospital is highly reputable based on third-party rankings. Two widely publicized rankings were combined: the 'America's Best Hospital' ranking published in 1996 by U.S. News & World Report and the 'Hospital Compare' ranking published by CMS based on quality measures such as mortality, safety of care, and readmission (the 2005 CMS ranking, used because the rankings were stable across 2005-2011). A hospital is defined as highly reputable if it was ranked as one of the 500 best hospitals by either ranking.

Indicator for whether an MFI received the Family and Community Empowerment (FCE) badge of Kiva's social performance badging program, introduced on December 11, 2011. Thirty-seven MFIs in the estimation sample received the FCE badge in Q4 2011 (the treatment group) and the remaining 33 MFIs did not (the control group). The badge is awarded by an internal team at Kiva based on an MFI's score on Kiva's internal social performance scorecard and is featured on the MFI's profile page.

Ratio of female borrowers to all borrowers (female and male). Because the FCE badge has a strong focus on promoting loans by female borrowers, adjusting the loan portfolio toward this dimension is the observable form of portfolio reorientation. The number of female borrowers in the group of borrowers requesting a loan is traceable in the data and is aggregated to the MFI-quarter level; the authors include the number of borrowers at the MFI-quarter level to control for variation in the denominator and capture the relative change in female borrowers.

Indicates that an MFI received any of the other six social performance badges in addition to the FCE badge. Twenty-seven of the control group MFIs received one or more of the remaining six badges, while six received no badge at all.

Measures the degree that MFIs' loan portfolios are concentrated by industry sector, using the concentration ratio, or CR4: the combined share of an MFI's four largest industry sectors each quarter. A higher CR4 implies that an MFI's loans are more strongly clustered in the four largest sectors, whereas a lower CR4 means that its loans are more diffuse and spread across multiple sectors. Loans are classified into one of 15 predefined industry sectors.

The number of forward citations received within a four-year postapplication window to the firm's patents in the focal firm-year. Forward citations act as a proxy for the economic value created by the patented innovations; a fixed citation window facilitates meaningful comparisons across observation years.

The concentration of a firm's forward citations among its patents in a focal year, calculated using the standard Herfindahl index formula. Each patent's share is the forward citations to the patent divided by the total forward citations to all of the firm's patents in the focal year; the sum of the squared shares gives the firm-year measure. It ranges from 0 to 1, with a lower value indicating citations come from a broad base of patents and a higher value a more limited set of patents.

The count of backward citations by the firm's patents in the focal firm-year that do not cite patents by one of the citing patent team's inventors but are firm-level self-cites, divided by the total number of backward citations in the focal firm-year. The numerator captures the volume of knowledge flowing inside the firm from one team to another distinct team, and the denominator adjusts for the total volume of knowledge the firm builds on in the firm-year.

An intermediate index built from inventors' career patenting experience, measured as a class experience vector of the stock count of each inventor's patents in each primary USPTO patent class through the focal year. All possible dyads of inventors on a production team are formed, the cosine diversity (1 minus the cosine similarity of the class experience vectors) is calculated for each dyad and averaged for the team, and the measure is aggregated to the firm-year level by averaging over the firm's patents. It ranges from 0 to 1, where 1 is completely diverse.
level: firm-year (aggregated from inventor dyads within teams)
time_window: inventor's entire career history through the focal year

description: An intermediate index built by summing the class experience vectors of the inventors on a team to create an aggregate class experience vector per production team, forming all possible dyads among the firm's teams in a year, calculating the cosine diversity among teams based on their aggregate vectors, and averaging over all dyads of patents in the firm-year. It captures the degree to which production teams within the firm differ from one another with respect to each team's aggregate knowledge.
time_window: inventor's entire career history through the focal year

description: An indicator (0/1) for firm-years where within-team knowledge diversity is above the 75th percentile of the sample and across-team diversity is below the 75th percentile. The intermediate measures are dichotomized at the 75th percentile of their underlying distributions to capture the meaningful variation in the data. All coefficients are estimated relative to the excluded baseline case of low within low across diversity.

An indicator (0/1) for firm-years where within-team knowledge diversity is below the 75th percentile of the sample and across-team diversity is above the 75th percentile. The intermediate measures are dichotomized at the 75th percentile of their underlying distributions. All coefficients are estimated relative to the excluded baseline case of low within low across diversity.

An indicator (0/1) for firm-years where within-team knowledge diversity is above the 75th percentile and across-team diversity is above the 75th percentile. It is one of the three main independent variables included in all models, with the excluded baseline case being low within low across diversity.

A measure of lowered within-team coordination costs: prior within-team collaborative experience between different inventors on a team. For any two inventors, joint experience at time t is the stock count of patents for which both inventors were on the same patent team at any point in their career through time t. The measure averages the joint experience among all dyads of inventors on the same patent team, then averages over all patent teams in a firm-year.
level: firm-year (averaged from inventor dyads on teams)

description: The largest number of unique three-digit zip code prefixes among inventors on a production team, across the production teams patenting in the focal firm-year. The first three digits of a five-digit U.S. Postal Service zip code represent a broader geographic region than the full five digits; higher team geographic dispersion would make across-team consultation more difficult.
scale: count of three-digit zip code prefixes

description: Count of invention patent applications filed by a listed firm (including its subsidiaries) in a given year. Patents in the SIPO database were matched to the listed firm and its subsidiaries by stem-name matching.

Count of granted invention patents filed by a listed firm in a given year. Because patent examination and grant is a government certification process by which innovative activities can be qualified, granted patents generally have higher quality than nongranted ones.

The aggregate number of claims in the invention patents of a focal firm divided by the number of invention patents filed by the firm in a given year. Patent claims indicate the value and quality of a patent by defining novel features in the patented invention and delineating the scope of intellectual property rights.

Reform is a dummy variable that equals one in years after the focal firm adopted the reform and zero otherwise. SOE is a dummy variable that equals one if the focal firm is majority-owned or ultimately controlled by the Chinese government (at the central or local government level) and zero otherwise. The interaction term Reform × SOE is added in the regressions to identify the effect of privatization on innovation.
time_window: years after the focal firm adopted the reform

description: The percentage of equity owned by the top management team. Information on the percentage of shares owned by the top management team is available from the CSMAR database.

Intercorporate loans divided by sales revenue of a listed firm in a given year. Such loans from the focal firm to its controlling shareholders or their affiliates indicate value expropriation against minority shareholders, reflecting conflicts between controlling and minority shareholders. The variable is an inverse proxy of interest alignment: the greater its value, the more poorly aligned are the interests of controlling and minority shareholders.

Using the strategy method in the ultimatum game, respondents indicated a minimum acceptable offer between 0 INR and 500 INR before knowing what was actually being offered, while offerors reported their proposed offers before knowing the respondents' MAOs. If the MAO was equal to or less than the offer, the respondent received the offer and the offeror the remainder; if the MAO was greater than the offer, both parties received nothing. Each respondent played the same role with the same counterpart for 10 rounds and one round was chosen at random for payment.

variable_name: experimental condition (UG, PUG unaware, PUG aware)
description: Participants were randomly assigned to one of three conditions. In UG there was no peer. In PUG unaware only the offerors knew that they were engaging two respondents simultaneously, so from the respondent's perspective there was no difference from UG. In PUG aware both respondents were aware that the offeror was simultaneously engaging another respondent, but not the magnitude of the offer to that respondent.

variable_name: PUG secrecy versus PUG transparent condition
description: Participants were randomly assigned to a PUG secrecy condition or a PUG transparent condition. In the secrecy condition they were not informed of the salary offered to a peer candidate but were aware of the peer's presence; in the transparency condition they were informed that an equal monthly salary was offered to a peer candidate from the same organization for a similar position.

variable_name: likelihood of accepting the job offer
description: After reading the scenario, participants indicated on a five-point Likert scale how likely they would be to accept the job offer, anchored 1 = definitely not to 5 = definitely yes.

variable_name: uncertainty condition (full secrecy, partial secrecy, risk, transparent)
description: Uncertainty about the offer amount to the peer respondent was manipulated in four ways: full secrecy (no information about the offer to the peer), partial secrecy (information on the offeror's past offers to past respondents, specifically whether they were equal or unequal), risk (information about the exact range of possible offer amounts to the peer) and transparent (information about the exact offer amount to the peer). Four of the 24 logical conditions were omitted because under full secrecy inequity relative to a peer is undefined.

After reading the information about the scenario, participants reported their willingness to accept the offer on a seven-point Likert scale, anchored 1 = not at all to 7 = definitely. The measure was collected before the fairness question to prevent demand effects.

Respondents reported their perceived fairness of the amount offered to them on a seven-point Likert scale, anchored 1 = extremely unfair to 7 = extremely fair. The authors state that the central process in EDS is an escalated perception of what is considered a fair allocation to oneself, and measured this subjective sense of fairness in addition to willingness to accept.

Takes a value of 1 when the focal firm divests a subsidiary from a different two-digit NAICS industry code after it experiences a data breach, and 0 when the firm does not engage in any divestiture within a given year. A broader two-digit NAICS code was chosen to ensure that the technologies, data, and management processes of both the parent firm and its subsidiary were sufficiently distinct. Divestitures resulting from parent firm death, tracking stock issuances, financial buyers and non-U.S. subsidiaries were excluded. Divestiture data were obtained from SDC Platinum.

Takes a value of 1 if the focal firm replaced or laid off its CTO in a given year, and 0 otherwise. It is derived from a yearly dummy that indicates whether the CTO, or an executive officer that performs a similar role, retained the position from the previous year. Data were obtained from Form 10-K annual reports and Form DEF 14A proxy statements; a search dictionary of 78 possible designations was used and role descriptions were examined to identify officers fulfilling the CTO responsibility.

Binary variable that equals 1 if a firm experienced a data breach in a given year, and 0 otherwise. Breach events were obtained from the Privacy Rights Clearinghouse archives, focusing on cyberhacking-related breaches classified as 'hacking or malware' and 'insider'. The operationalization reflects the bimodal distribution of firms that experience breaches, wherein the majority of breached firms had up to two breaches.

Binary variable that equals 1 if a firm experienced a data breach in a given year, and 0 otherwise. Breach events were obtained from the Privacy Rights Clearinghouse archives, focusing on cyberhacking-related breaches classified as 'hacking or malware' and 'insider'. The operationalization reflects the bimodal distribution of firms that experience breaches.

Spline variable that equals the historical performance gap (the firm's EPS in the current year minus its historical aspiration level, the average EPS in the three years prior to the current year) for observations in which the firm's performance is greater than its aspiration level, and 0 for all observations in which performance is less than its aspiration. It is one of the two variables created by splitting the historical performance gap above and below the aspiration level.
time_window: current year relative to the three prior years

description: Spline variable that equals the absolute value of the historical performance gap (the firm's EPS in the current year minus the average EPS in the three years prior to the current year) for observations in which the firm's performance is less than its aspiration level, and 0 for all observations in which performance is greater than its aspiration. Absolute values are used for negative performance gaps for ease of interpretation.
time_window: current year relative to the three prior years

description: Spline variable that equals the social performance gap (the firm's EPS in the current year minus industry average performance in the same year) for observations in which the firm's performance is greater than its social aspiration level, and 0 for all observations in which performance is less than its aspiration.

Spline variable that equals the absolute value of the social performance gap (the firm's EPS in the current year minus industry average performance in the same year) for observations in which the firm's performance is less than its social aspiration level, and 0 for all observations in which performance is greater than its aspiration.

Spline variable that equals the historical performance gap (the firm's EPS in the current year minus its historical aspiration level, the average EPS in the three years prior to the current year) for observations in which the firm's performance is greater than its aspiration level, and 0 otherwise.
time_window: current year relative to the three prior years

description: Spline variable that equals the absolute value of the historical performance gap for observations in which the firm's performance is less than its historical aspiration level, and 0 otherwise; absolute values are used for negative performance gaps.
time_window: current year relative to the three prior years

description: Spline variable that equals the firm's EPS in the current year minus industry average EPS in the same year for observations in which performance is greater than the social aspiration level, and 0 otherwise.

Spline variable that equals the absolute value of the firm's EPS in the current year minus industry average EPS in the same year for observations in which performance is less than the social aspiration level, and 0 otherwise.

The number of HBR articles in the focal year that are assigned the focal keyword. It is the dependent variable in the count models, and its one-year lagged, logged version is also used as the moderator and as a control.
time_window: year t (lagged to year t - 1 for the predictor version)

description: The sum of the popularity of the keywords with which the focal keyword is mentioned (listed together as a keyword in a given article) in period t - 1. For example, if keyword A appears with B in one article and with C in another in 1984, the value for A in 1985 is the sum of the counts of mentions of B and C in 1984. The standardized version is used in the regressions.

Computed as the sum over keywords j of sim(i, j) times Pj, where Pj is the popularity of keyword j and the sum only includes keywords that were used together with i in year t - 1. Similarity is the Jaccard similarity of the two keywords, the proportion of the overlap and union of the articles to which the two keywords are associated. The standardized version is used in the regressions.
scale: Jaccard similarity ranges from 0 to 1; the composite is standardized

description: The average Jaccard similarity between the focal keyword i and all the keywords with which i is ever mentioned. A high value implies that the keyword is frequently used with a few other keywords, whereas a low value implies that it is mentioned with keywords that are seldom combined. The standardized version is used in the regressions.
scale: Jaccard similarity ranges from 0 to 1; the composite is standardized
time_window: computed using data from all years and then lagged by one year

description: Every city of origin in the data set was assigned to one of six regions: the Netherlands, Germany, Scandinavia, France, England, and others. The Simpson index for a ship in a given year is computed from the proportion of individuals from each region and is then subtracted from one, so that increasing values point to greater national diversity. The authors note that this measure is often labeled the Blau index.
scale: 1/6 to 1 for the Simpson index; 0 to 5/6 after subtracting it from one
time_window: measured for each ship in a given year of the voyage

variable_name: Average experience of the whole crew
description: The authors tracked the career of each of the half-million seafarers in the VOC database and counted the number of times each had travelled to Asia before the current trip. They summed the individual number of trips of the crew members and divided the result by the number of crew members, creating a measure of the average experience of the whole crew.
time_window: prior trips (T-1) before the current voyage

description: The number of days between the date of departure from the Netherlands and the date of arrival in Batavia for each ship. Because of the presence of a few outliers, the authors logged this variable.

variable_name: Periods of increasing versus decreasing standardization
description: The authors distinguish two periods: increasing standardization from 1700 to 1755 and decreasing standardization and local experimentation from 1756 to 1796, and they estimate models separately for each period. Models also include dummies for the 1700-1741 and 1742-1755 periods (van Imhoff's era).

Strategic change was measured using four dimensions: financial leverage (debt/equity), overhead efficiency (SGA/sales), R&D intensity (R&D expenses/sales), and advertising intensity (advertising expenses/sales). The absolute difference (without regard to direction) in values between the previous year and present year was computed for each dimension. Each dimension was standardized over all observations (mean = 0; standard deviation = 1) as z scores, and the four standardized indicators were summed into a single composite index. Higher scores reflect greater resource reallocation.

variable_name: ROA below historical aspiration / ROA above historical aspiration
description: Performance was measured using accounting-based return on assets (ROA). Historical aspiration was computed as the focal firm's performance in the previous year. Slopes for below and above historical aspiration were evaluated using spline functions: an indicator was assigned the value one if current performance of the firm dropped under the aspiration benchmark, and the performance below aspiration variable was the product of the continuous variable (ROA - ASP) and the dummy-coded indicator; the performance above aspiration variable was the product of (ROA - ASP) and (indicator - 1).
time_window: aspiration measured at t - 1, performance at t

variable_name: ROA below social aspiration / ROA above social aspiration
description: Social aspiration was constructed using a matching technique to identify the k most proximal matches of similarly sized firms (based on the firm's total assets), with Mahalanobis distance measuring the distance between social peers and the focal firm with respect to firm size; results are reported with peer group size of k = 5. Below- and above-aspiration slopes were evaluated with spline functions in the same way as for historical aspiration.
time_window: aspiration measured at t - 1, performance at t

description: Measured using the entropy measure defined as the sum over product segments of P sub i times the natural logarithm of 1 over P sub i, where P represents the proportion of sales (in U.S. dollars) of the i-th product segment and the logarithm of the inverse sales is the natural logarithm.

Measured with an entropy measure weighted by firm sales across four geographic markets: domestic (the United States), Europe, Asia Pacific, and others. Entropy was defined as the sum over markets of P sub i times the natural logarithm of 1 over P sub i, where P denotes the proportion of sales of the i-th global regional market.

Measured as the greatest percentage increase in sales for a product line among the firm's portfolio of product segments. For example, within Armor Holdings Inc.'s product portfolio the product bright spot was the highest percentage increase in sales of a product line among its product mix. The variable suffers from kurtosis and skewed distribution, and outliers were removed using the outlier labeling rule of Tukey (1977).
time_window: one-year percentage change in segment sales

description: Measured similarly to product bright spot except that geographic segments were used in lieu of product segments; it is the highest percentage increase in regional market sales among the firm's geographic mix. The variable suffers from kurtosis and skewed distribution, and outliers were removed using the outlier labeling rule of Tukey (1977).
time_window: one-year percentage change in regional market sales

description: Dummy variable indicating the treatment group; it takes the value of 1 for firms that had at least one of their licenses cancelled by the Supreme Court order and 0 otherwise. Approximately 48% of the sample has a value of 1 for this variable.

Ratio of calls terminated unwillingly to all call attempts, in percent, reported at the firm-region level for each quarter and obtained from the TRAI quarterly reports of telecom services performance indicators. Lower values indicate better network performance for this measure; the TRAI benchmark value is at or below 2%.

Connections with good voice quality, in percent, reported at the firm-region level for each quarter and obtained from the TRAI quarterly reports of telecom services performance indicators. Higher values indicate better network performance; the TRAI benchmark value is at or above 95%.

Ratio of established calls to call attempts, in percent, reported at the firm-region level for each quarter and obtained from the TRAI quarterly reports of telecom services performance indicators. Higher values indicate better network performance; the TRAI benchmark value is at or above 95%.

Content analysis of 20,458 quarterly earnings-call transcripts downloaded from ThomsonOne and split into cover, presentation and Q&A sections, with only the presentation section of senior executives used. A dictionary of 40 words and phrases judged patriotic (score of 6 or more) or unpatriotic (score of 2 or lower) by nine academic subject experts was applied to the text. The measure is the ratio of the number of patriotic words divided by the sum of patriotic and unpatriotic words, with all words aggregated from the presentation section of the quarterly earnings calls to the year level.

Content analysis of 12,260 press releases that the sample firms published between January 2002 and December 2015, downloaded from Factiva and analysed with Linguistic Inquiry and Word Count software. The same validated list of 40 patriotic and unpatriotic words and phrases was used as for the earnings calls. The measure is the ratio of the number of patriotic words divided by the sum of patriotic and unpatriotic words in the press releases.

Measured using text analysis of all congressional and presidential documents and media reports, capturing how often words emphasizing the own nation (e.g., the United States) were used in documents published by the U.S. Government Publishing Office and in political media reports of The New York Times, The Washington Post and The Wall Street Journal. The variable is the mean of the two standardized variables, computed on a yearly basis.

Following prior research into the multinationality of firms and its performance effects, the involvement of firms in overseas markets is measured using the mean of the standardized ratio of foreign sales to total sales and the standardized ratio of foreign assets to total assets.

Following prior research, firm performance is measured using the firm's return on assets in a given year. Specifically, the return on assets was calculated as the net income of a company in a given year divided by its total assets.

Indicator coded one when a clause was revised as a result of business input gathered through the VCCI consultation initiative (one of eight VCCI clauses) and zero when the clause was revised only on the advice of chemical safety experts (one of six placebo clauses). It is the key independent variable of the clause-selection models.

Randomized indicator of whether the respondent was told that the revised version was based on suggestions from 'over 400 small and medium enterprises' (T4 = 1) rather than from 'chemical and labor safety experts' (T3 = 0).

Coded one if the respondent chose the revised version of a clause and zero if the original version was chosen, regardless of whether the revised version appeared in the left or right column. Each of the 14 clause answers forms its own observation, so the data are indexed at both the clause and respondent levels.

variable_name: Clause selection under the business-performance prime (T1 = 1, T2 = 0)
description: The clause-selection dependent variable for respondents assigned to the purpose experiment condition that asked which version was 'most suitable for successful business operations' (T1). Selection of the revised clause over the original in this condition is treated as the firm's view that the change is positive for business performance.

variable_name: Clause selection under the worker-safety prime (T2 = 1, T1 = 0)
description: The clause-selection dependent variable for respondents assigned to the purpose experiment condition that asked which version 'provides the greatest protection to your employees' (T2). Selection of the revised clause over the original in this condition is treated as the firm's view that the change is positive for worker safety.

Agreement with the statement 'Bureaucrats use compliance with local regulations to extract informal fees from business', answered on a four-point scale from one (strongly disagree) to four (strongly agree), so a higher score implies a more negative evaluation of the intentions behind state regulation. 'Don't know' answers were imputed from firm size, sector, type and gender of entrepreneur; a dichotomous version equals one when the respondent agreed (reg_intention = 3 or 4).

Treatment of Israel on an international airline's online route map, categorized as an Israel denier, avoider, or embracer. Plausible and intentional embracers are consolidated into a single embracer category and plausible and intentional deniers into a single denier category; the avoider category lies between the other two in a three-level ordinal ranking.
Whether an international airline's in-flight menu lists kosher meal options at its company website or at wanderbat.com. Airlines are categorized as either including such kosher meal options or not.
scale: 0-1 categorical (1 = kosher meal options listed, 0 = not)

description: A weighted average of the ADL anti-Semitism index across the countries where an airline's likely customers are located. Google search index values for the airline name by country are weighted by country GDP to build the customer distribution, which is then used to weight the ADL anti-Semitism index; the measure varies across airlines in the same country when their customers are distributed differently. Values range from 0 to 100 on the ADL scale, with higher values indicating greater anti-Semitism.
time_window: Google search-term use from 2004 to the first quarter of 2016; GDP weights from 2010

description: Search intensity on the use of the word 'kosher' by country, weighted for each airline by the GDP-weighted search intensities on the respective airline names. Values run from 0 to 100, with higher values indicating greater kosher interest among an airline's likely customers.

A categorical measure indicating whether an airline is majority state-owned by a country not recognizing Israel. Data on majority state ownership come from airline websites and the International Civil Aviation Organization, and diplomatic recognition of Israel is ascertained from Wikipedia.
scale: 0-1 categorical (1 = majority state-owned by a country not recognizing Israel, 0 = otherwise)

description: Whether an international airline is listed as a member of either the Star, OneWorld, or SkyTeam alliances, based on airline websites, the websites of prominent U.S. carriers leading major alliances, and alliance websites. Code sharing with alliance members is not required.
scale: 0-1 categorical (1 = member of one of the three alliances, 0 = not)

description: The OECD employment dismissal protection index for the 2003-2010 period, taken as the measure of a country's employment protection law rigidity. The index measures cross-country differences in the difficulty of dismissing workers and is computed as the average of five equally weighted dimensions, each ranging from 0 to 6. Higher values indicate that employment protection is more strict, i.e. less flexible labor.

Industry-level estimates of the substitutability of labor and capital from Chirinko and Mallick (2017), who use a low-pass filter to isolate long-run components of the data described in Jorgenson et al. (2000). The authors proxy the model's alpha with these measures of factor substitutability at the industry level, preferring them because of the recency of the data and the superior industry coverage.

For each publication year of Orbis, firms whose date of incorporation equals the publication year are coded as entrants and all other firms as incumbents. The dependent variable is the natural log of 1 plus the number of firms incorporated in each year-country-industry; the authors also distinguish stand-alone entrants from entrants affiliated with corporate groups.

Entrants affiliated with corporate groups are separated from stand-alones with no equity ties to other firms using data from the ownership section of Orbis. In Orbis this is operationalized by defining firms as affiliates if their independence score is a C or D; stand-alones are firms with no equity ties to other firms or with missing ownership information. The authors note the operationalization is conservative and biases against finding results.

Capital intensity is calculated as the log ratio of assets over employees; the firm-level analysis uses each firm's own ratio, with the entry-year sample used to look at capital-labor ratios at entry. The industry-level version of the measure is computed as the log ratio of assets over employees averaged at the four-digit NAICS level from Amadeus.
time_window: entry year and firm life cycle, 2003-2010

description: The uncertainty measure is the media Economic Policy Uncertainty Index from Baker et al. (2016), computed as a function of the number of terms in local newspapers that indicate economic policy uncertainty. The sample is divided by level of media uncertainty (highest versus lowest quartile).

Firm age measures how long a firm has been in existence and is interacted with industry elasticity of substitution to show how capital intensity changes as firms mature. The life-cycle sample includes only firms incorporated in the first year of the sample and tracks them over time, so that new firms can be observed as they grow.

In the capital-intensity analysis the firm-year sample is divided into stand-alone and group-affiliated firms, using the same Orbis ownership-based definition of corporate group affiliation. The authors compare sample averages and the elasticity-of-substitution x age coefficient across the two subsamples.

An indicator that is equal to one if the applicant was recommended by the platform's machine learning algorithm, that is, if the applicant's undisclosed algorithm score was 0.50 or above at the time of application. Applicants are never made aware of their recommendation statuses nor their exact algorithm scores.
An indicator for whether the employer viewed the applicant's detailed application. It is the dependent variable in Model 2 of the main regression discontinuity estimations.

An indicator for whether the applicant was interviewed, conditioning on the applicant having been viewed by the employer. An applicant is 'interviewed' if the employer sent a message to the applicant. It is the dependent variable in Model 3 of the estimations.
An indicator that applicant i, to job posting j, was hired by the employer. It is the dependent variable in Model 1 of the estimations, estimated on all applicants.
An indicator for whether the applicant was hired, conditioning on the applicant having been interviewed by the employer. It is the dependent variable in Model 4 of the estimations.

Market size is calculated as the number of job postings in the submarket, where the 12 submarkets are the occupation categories chosen by the employer when posting the job. Market size is measured as a z-score indicating standard deviations from the mean submarket demand.

variable_name: number of previous jobs the employer has filled on the platform
description: Firm experience is measured as the number of previous jobs the employer has filled on the platform, chosen because it more accurately represents exposure to the platform than tenure. The distribution is highly skewed; the sample is split at four prior filled job postings, with zero to three prior filled jobs defining low-experience firms and 4+ prior filled jobs defining more experienced firms.
time_window: prior to the focal job posting

description: A normalized Herfindahl index of the shares of firm i's accumulated production as of time t recognized as conforming with each logic k among the n logics available in the industry. The variable ranges from zero, when a firm's products are evenly spread across logics, to one when the firm has released products consistently conforming to one logic. In the two-logic French film industry the index simplifies to one minus the sum of the squared shares of production conforming to the professional logic and to the market logic. Film producer Fidélité, involved in 45 films of which 20 were Art and Essay films, has a value of 0.012, while Sunday Morning Productions, with 10 Art and Essay films and one mainstream film, has a value of 0.669.
time_window: cumulated film production as of time t (time varying)

description: Differences in survival rates are modeled as the log of latent survival time T as a function of firm characteristics at time j, with T distributed as Weibull. Firms enter the risk set at the date they sign their first contract and are assumed to have failed when they have been inactive for at least three years, consistent with prior studies of the industry. Firms still active in the last three years of observations are assumed to have survived and are coded as right censored, and exit is interpreted as failure.
time_window: 1994-2008, with complementary contract data going back to 1987 to identify birth dates

description: The proportion of firms in the industry that are fully institutionally specialized as of year t, i.e., either fully focused on Art and Essay films or fully focused on mainstream films. The authors reason that the more firms embrace two institutional logics, the lower the contrast between the logics at the industry level. The proportion of observations where firms are institutionally 'pure' decreases from 82.9% in 1994 to 48.7% in 2008.

Derived from the VC firm fixed effects estimated in a Poisson model of the number of financing rounds the VC invests in a venture, controlling for venture, dyad and market characteristics; the fixed effects are taken from the failed-venture model and their sign is reversed so that the measure takes a larger value for firms with higher termination capability. Each value is weighted by the inverse of the standard error on the fixed effect. A VC firm's TC is inferred from the number of rounds it has invested in each failing venture, with fewer rounds indicating higher TC.

A parallel fixed-effect measure derived from the number of rounds the VC firm invests in the subsample of successful ventures, analogous to the termination capability measure for failed ventures. It is used to test whether a general tendency to invest fewer rounds across the board explains performance differences.

The number of ventures invested relative to the number of VC professionals employed in the VC firm. When each partner has more ventures to manage, their attention will be more divided, resulting in suboptimal continuation or termination decisions. In Step 2 the variable is calculated as an average over the study period; in the VC-venture model it is time varying.

The number of support members in the VC firm relative to the GPs. Members with the authority to 'write a check' (partner, founder, vice president, principal, managing director, chair) are designated high-level, and all other members (such as analysts, associates and administrative staff) are designated support. A larger number of support members relative to higher-level members indicates that VC partners allocate more of their time and attention to decision making.

The total number of ventures in which the VC firm invested in the study period. In the VC-venture model the measure is cumulative from 1980 until the year of the VC firm's first investment in the venture.

A concentration measure akin to the Herfindahl-Hirshman index of the VC firm's investments across industry groups over the study period; it takes a higher value when a firm is more specialized. The formula is not readable in the text.

The VC firm's level of experience in its area of specialization, calculated as the maximum number of the VC firm's ventures in any industry group. In the VC-venture model the measure is cumulative from 1980 until the year of first investment by the VC firm in the venture.

The total count of IPOs divided by the total number of ventures in which the VC invested in the study period; only investments in which the focal VC was the lead investor are used. Only IPOs are considered unequivocal successes.
The measure recalculated as the sum of the counts of IPOs and acquisitions over the total number of ventures invested, used as an alternative performance measure in the reported models.

Fund-level internal rates of return; for VC firms that have multiple funds, an average IRR variable weighted by the size of each fund is calculated. The variable is available for a small subset of the firms in the sample, n equal to 131.

An organization's knowledge-space proximity to other microcomputer organizations is calculated by observing every patent issued to organization A and measuring each patent's maximum similarity to all patents issued by organization B, where similarity is based on citation overlap. The organization's proximity to every organization B that uses a CPU is summed and divided by the total number of patents issued to A in the given year. Past similarity to this CPU is taken into account by summing past proximities and discounting by the square root of time. The equations for these sums are given as formula blocks that are not extractable from the text.
time_window: current year, plus discounted past years

description: Knowledge consistency is measured using the same logic for comparing two organizations, but instead compares an organization's patent portfolio in the current year to its portfolio in previous years, based on citation-overlap similarity between patents. To take account of consistency in previous years, past consistencies are summed, discounting for time. The equation for consistency and for the summed past consistencies is given as formula blocks that are not extractable from the text.
time_window: current year, plus time-discounted previous years

description: Knowledge generalism (versus specialism) is constructed by computing A's knowledge-space proximity to every organization C that uses a CPU other than the target CPU. Past similarity to other CPUs is taken into account by summing past proximities and discounting by time. The equations are given as formula blocks that are not extractable from the text.
time_window: current year, plus time-discounted previous years

variable_name: adopting a CPU from a different supplier
description: The event is the adoption by an organization in a dyad of the target CPU, where the target CPU comes from a supplier the manufacturer does not already use. Dyads enter the risk set when there is a new microcomputer manufacturer or a new CPU, and the hazard rate is estimated from the time from dyad entry to adoption of the target CPU. All independent variables are measured as of the beginning of each time period.
A dummy variable that equals 1 for the years after Craigslist enters the newspaper's local market and 0 otherwise. The relevant market is defined as the county in which the newspaper is based.

Editor job titles for each newspaper are categorized into 11 content types and, for each newspaper-year, a vector indicates whether the newspaper has an editor for each of the 11 types. The distance between newspaper i and competitor j is the angle distance (in radians) between their product-location vectors, normalized by 2, where competitors are newspapers that circulate in the same ZIP Code and do not have the same parent. The differentiation measure for a newspaper is the minimum of the distances between it and its competitors in that year; the exact formulas are unreadable in the text provided. The distance measure is between 0 and 1, equal to 0 when two newspapers have identical sets of editor types and to 1 when there is no overlap.

variable_name: ad representative; no. of news services; no. of names/no. of positions
description: Three proxies for newspaper-level cost-cutting on both sides of the market. Ad representative is 1 for each year in which the newspaper uses an advertising representative to sell advertising space and 0 otherwise. No. of news services counts the number of news services the newspaper uses in the year. No. of positions counts the number of editor types the newspaper employs, no. of names counts the number of unique names associated with those positions, and the ratio of names to positions captures reliance on the same editor to cover more content areas; a drop in the ratio indicates more such reliance.

Constructed from U.S. Census Bureau data on the fraction of the population that is Black in the market for the year 2000, using a procedure similar to the construction of political heterogeneity; reader heterogeneity increases as the variable increases in value.

Constructed from U.S. Census Bureau data on the fraction of the population that is Hispanic in the market for the year 2000, using a procedure similar to the construction of political heterogeneity; reader heterogeneity increases as the variable increases in value.

Computed from the percent of voters in a market who voted for George W. Bush in 2000 (pct conservative) and pct liberal, which is 1 minus pct conservative; political heterogeneity is computed as 1 minus the sum of the squared liberal and conservative shares, so the higher its value, the greater the political heterogeneity of the market.

Equals 1 when a newspaper that experiences Craigslist's entry in year t has one or more sister firms that had already faced Craigslist's entry prior to year t, and 0 otherwise. Parents and sister firms of newspaper firms in each year are identified from ABC and E&P data.

Residuals are computed for each differentiation and cost-cutting model of Table 3 (except the models on the numerator and denominator of the ratio) and averaged across all years after Craigslist's entry for each affected newspaper. The variable is 1 if a newspaper is in the bottom decile of all newspapers based on how responsive it is to Craigslist's entry, in terms of both differentiation and cost-cutting, and 0 otherwise. A companion variable, outlier (high response), is 1 for the top decile.
time_window: average across study years after entry

description: Equals 1 if the newspaper firm continues to offer daily editions in 2014 and 0 otherwise. A second variable, survival (newspaper), measures whether a newspaper still exists at all as of 2014. Both are built from the 2014 online edition of E&P and verified by checking individual newspaper websites.

variable_name: Number of entries in the Pho forum per month
description: The number of entries (by month) in the digital music forum Pho, counted by the author and used as the operationalization of the level of discourse surrounding metacompetition. Pho was invitation-only, allowed users to exchange ideas in discussion strings sent and received through email, and saw surges in activity when big issues in the debate erupted.

The observed change in size of an organization following a strategy from time t to time t+1, derived from the partial adjustment model with size specified in the natural logarithm as a Gibrat process. Organizational size is measured by Alexa rank, which ranks websites according to the frequency of visits and page views by Internet users with an Alexa toolbar; ranks vary inversely to size, so a very low rank implies an extremely large service and negative coefficients mean a variable increases the growth rate.

Websites featuring music downloading were categorized according to which of three strategies they followed: free music sharing, commercial music download, and commercial music subscription. In the growth models the strategies enter through indicator variables for pay downloading websites and subscription downloading websites, with the free downloading website as the left-out category.

A dichotomous time-varying firm-level variable, REFOCUS_jt = BAN_t x MULTI_j, where BAN is equal to one in all periods following the mackerel ban, and zero before the ban, and MULTI is equal to one if firm j had at least one boat that fished for mackerel for fishmeal before the ban, and is zero otherwise. It captures whether the ban on mackerel fishing forced a firm to reduce the scope of its operations in week t.

variable_name: Log Y_it = Log(tons of anchovy caught by ship i in week t)
description: The dependent variable is the log of tons of fish (anchovy) caught per week by ship, which is reported directly to the ministry. It is measured only during the weeks of the government-determined anchovy fishing season, when anchovy represents more than 95% of all catches by weight.

A firm-level indicator equal to one if firm j had at least one boat that fished for mackerel for fishmeal before the ban, and is zero otherwise; it identifies the firms whose anchovy extraction was interdependent with mackerel fishing.

Categorical variables for each of the seven anchovy fishing seasons from the date of the ban (September 2002) until the end of 2005, where seasons are defined by the Peruvian fishing authority, interacted with REFOCUS to capture the marginal effect of the ban on productivity over time by season. By construction, the REFOCUS x SEASON dummies capture the time path of organizational rigidity and adaptation after the ban; the main effects of the season dummies are absorbed by the week fixed effects.

variable_name: SW installed base IB SW j 1 1 t [100 millions]
description: Installed base of games for the compatible parent console, expressed in hundreds of millions of units. It is built from the software data of all available titles for each console, whose associated console is reported. As in prior work, the installed base is depreciated with 5% annually.
scale: hundreds of millions of game units

variable_name: Market share s jt of console j relative to market potential (dependent variable ln(s jt) - ln(s 0t))
description: Market shares are calculated by dividing monthly unit sales of console j by total units sold in a given month. Potential market size is proxied by the number of TV households; from this the authors derive s jt, a console's market share of market potential, and s 0t, the market share of the outside good, i.e., the share of potential consumers that do not have a console and do not buy one in the given time period.

For every platform the authors count the number of game titles with positive sales to obtain Njt, so Njt can decline over time if game titles are no longer sold. The variable is expressed in hundreds of titles.
Age of the console in months, counted from the console's U.S. launch date. Older consoles are expected to be less attractive to the remaining nonadopters.

Percentage improvement of the CPU speed of the new console compared to the CPU speed of the compatible parent generation. Because the data span a long period of rapid technological progress, CPU speed is normalized by calculating yearly mean values and standard deviation and constructing a z-score for each console-month before the relative improvement is derived. The variable is set to zero if there is no active parent console.

Indicator that takes the value of one for labels the authors classified as major. Using the label classification in Thomson (2009) as well as Wikipedia, they classified 481 labels as major, including smaller labels owned by the three major music conglomerates. In some specifications an alternative designation combines verified major labels with high-volume 'unknown' labels that released more than 40 albums during the study period.

Indicator that takes the value of one for labels the authors classified as independents; 1,625 labels were classified as independents. A larger category of 'nonmajors' combines known independents and the unclassified 'unknown' labels, which release an average of 2.6 albums per label over 1990-2010, in contrast with 9.5 for the classified independent labels and 25.5 for the classified major labels.

variable_name: share of a label's releases presenting an artist who previously appeared in the Billboard 200
description: For each label and year, the share of the label's new releases that are albums by artists with prior chart success, measured by whether the artist's albums have previously appeared on the weekly Billboard top 200 or top 50 charts. The measure is further broken down into releases of artists whose prior success occurred on the same label ('internal') and on other labels ('external'). Releases are classified using Discogs data back to 1980 in order to identify artists' first releases, and compilations and rereleases are excluded.
time_window: annual (label-year), with Discogs data back to 1980 used to date first releases

description: The number of albums released by a music organization, by year and by label type. The regressions use the log of the number of releases; some specifications use the aggregate number of releases by label type and year, others use the log of the number of releases at the individual label in a year.
level: label-year (and label type-year in aggregate specifications)

variable_name: share of a label's current releases that appear in the Billboard 200
description: For each label and year, the share of a label's current releases that achieve a ranking in the weekly Billboard top 200 (or top 50) during the year of the release. The data are collected for each week from 1985 to 2010, aggregated by year and recording artist, and matched to the Discogs artists by exact mapping plus hand matching by research assistants. The authors also construct an index of estimated revenue from the rankings, weighting the reciprocal of each album's weekly rank by the aggregate real value of overall U.S. sales in the year; the index's time pattern approximates the organization's sales pattern.

Seven items from Kreutzer et al.'s (2015) validated scale covering both formal behavior control and formal outcome control, answered on a scale from 1 (strongly disagree) to 7 (strongly agree) with question wording in the past tense. The seven items load on two factors that clearly separate formal behavior control (alpha 0.77) from formal outcome control (alpha 0.86); the overall scale has a Cronbach alpha of 0.84. Items were answered by the informant about top management's control of the growth initiative team.
time_window: Items worded in the past tense

description: Four newly developed items (from an original set of six, two of which were dropped after cross-loading) covering informal behavior control and informal outcome control, answered on a scale from 1 (strongly disagree) to 7 (strongly agree) with question wording in the past tense. The four items together have an alpha of 0.75; informal behavior control and informal outcome control items load on two factors with alphas of 0.69 and 0.82.
time_window: Items worded in the past tense

description: McGrath's (2001) nine-item measure, of which two items cross-loaded on other variables and were eliminated; the remaining items were aggregated into a single construct with an alpha of 0.76 and loaded onto two factors (four items oriented externally toward new markets and customers, alpha 0.74; three items oriented internally toward new products incorporating technology, alpha 0.66). Respondents rated the extent to which listed characteristics or factors of their growth initiatives were new to the company.
scale: 1-7 (1 = to no extent; 7 = to a very great extent)

description: An 11-item measure adapted from prior research (Lechner et al. 2010, McGrath 2001), in which items reflect the extent to which a number of goals and objectives were achieved on a seven-point scale from 1 ('very unsuccessful') to 7 ('very successful'). The authors added 'meeting revenue parameters' to the original 10 items, and report that results remain the same with and without this item; the 11-item scale has an alpha of 0.88. Only 57% of the strategic initiative teams in the sample were rated as successful (above 4).
time_window: Performance of the growth initiative up to now (retrospective)

description: Indicator variable taking the value one if a segment-year observation pertains to one of the treated parent firms that was matched by the propensity score matching model, and zero if the observation pertains to one of the control firms. Parent firms are the Fortune 500 companies identified through SDC Platinum as having undertaken the sample spin-offs; control firms are the five nearest neighbors matched to each parent firm-year observation in the year prior to treatment based on propensity scores from a first-stage probit on total assets, total sales, net income, and market capitalization.

The dependent variable in the main models, defined as the capital expenditures made by a business segment in a given year, scaled by its total assets. It is constructed from the Compustat Segments File for the retained business segments of parent firms and for the segments of the matched control firms.
time_window: segment-year, three years pre- to three years post-spin-off

description: Defined as the median Tobin's q of all of the single-segment firms operating in the same industry (identified by its three-digit SIC code) as a given business segment in a given year. The authors state that this variable measures the investment opportunities available to the individual business units operated by the firms in the sample, and that its coefficient measures the sensitivity of segment capital expenditures to segment investment opportunities.
level: three-digit SIC industry-year, matched to a business segment-year
time_window: segment-year, three years pre- to three years post-spin-off

variable_name: After x Median Segment Industry q x Treated
description: The three-way interaction term used to represent the prediction of a pre- to post-spin-off improvement in the efficiency of capital allocation decisions among the parent firms that undertook spin-offs, relative to the control group. The authors explain that the two-way interaction After x Median Segment Industry q represents, for both parent and control firms, the improvement in the efficiency of capital allocation decisions in the post-spin-off period relative to pre-spin-off levels, so the three-way term captures that improvement for parent firms relative to control firms.
