A firm-level value is then obtained by aggregating the complementarity coefficient of each secondary segment with the primary segment using the segment's sales weight. This variable measures the commonality between segments on the input and the output side.

Related diversification is measured using the entropy measures of Palepu (1985). It captures the extent to which a firm's output is distributed within industry groups in the same two-digit NAICS code.
Unrelated diversification is measured using the entropy measures of Palepu (1985). It captures the extent to which a firm's output is distributed across unrelated industry groups.
Physical capital is measured by the firm's plant, property, and equipment divided by sales.

R&D capital is measured by the firm's R&D stock divided by sales. R&D stock is assessed as the average R&D expenditure over the past five years. Firms with missing advertising and R&D expenditures were replaced with industry means.
time_window: average over the past five years

description: Relational capital refers to a firm's reputation and its relationships with customers and suppliers, and is measured as advertising stock divided by sales. Advertising stock is assessed as the average advertising expenditure over the past five years. Firms with missing advertising and R&D expenditures were replaced with industry means.
time_window: average over the past five years

description: Organizational capital is measured in a three-stage process. First, the difference between a firm's market value and book value as a proportion of the book value of total assets is calculated, which is essentially equivalent to a firm's Tobin's q. Second, a regression of firms' Tobin's q against their corresponding industry-average Tobin's q is run and the regression residual is taken as a measure of firm-specific intangible value. Third, from that residual the variance caused by R&D capital, relational capital, and IT capital is removed, and the resulting residual is used as the measure of organizational capital.
Firm performance is measured using return on assets, or pretax income divided by total assets.

Computed from a weight and a distance: the weight is the logged number of nanotechnology patents awarded to firm j at time t and the distance is the Euclidean distance between firm i and firm j, obtained from the latitude and longitude of the centroid of the zip code in which each firm was then located. The measure effectively represents the average distance between firm i and all other firms at time t, weighted by other firms' patent productivity; firms in San Jose have values at the high end and firms in Manhattan, Kansas at the low end of the distribution.

The citation-weighted sum of nanotechnology patents applied for by firm i at times t+1 and t+2. Each patent is weighted by the number of citations it received from future patents in the first five years after issue. Only patents produced by an inventor associated with the firm's main research facility are counted.

The sum of nanotechnology patents applied for by firm i at t+1 and t+2 that bridge previously uncombined technological domains. To identify new combinations the author counted how many times the set of USPTO subclasses used to classify a patent had been used previously between its issue date and 1790; patents that were first to fall into a particular combination of subclasses were given a score of 1 and those using an existing combination a score of 0.

Measured for each firm i at time t as the ratio of triangles (closed triads) to triples (open triads) in the firm's network of inventors; the raw coefficient ranges from 0 to 1, with larger values signalling higher cohesion. Because the collaboration network is a unipartite projection of a bipartite inventor-patent network, the observed clustering coefficient is scaled by the clustering coefficient of a simulated random network with an identical bipartite degree distribution; values at or below 1 imply that clustering is largely an artifact of the projection and values greater than 1 indicate clustering that results from collaborations spanning teams. Ties were dropped after five years and only collaborations involving an inventor from the firm's main research facility were included.
scale: ratio, 0 to 1 before scaling to a random-network benchmark
time_window: five-year tie window; measured at t

description: Measured as the average length of the paths in each firm i's network of nanotechnology inventors at time t; networks with longer characteristic path lengths have more intermediaries separating nodes and information spreads more slowly and less accurately as path length increases. Because paths across disconnected components are undefined, only paths within connected components were considered, and the measure is scaled relative to the expected path length of a random network. Ties were dropped after five years.
time_window: five-year tie window; measured at t

description: The sum of distinct industry sectors, distinct firms, and distinct functional areas the individual had worked in prior to becoming CEO of the focal firm, divided by the number of years the person had worked prior to becoming CEO. Industry sectors were identified with a firm's two-digit Global Industry Classification Standard code; every employing firm was allocated a single industry sector code. A firm was coded as distinct only if the individual joined it as an outsider, and each function was counted only once.
time_window: full employment history since completing formal education, up to becoming CEO

description: The year-on-year absolute change in six strategic choice variables: advertising intensity (advertising expenditure/sales), R&D intensity (R&D expenditure/sales), overhead efficiency (selling, general, and administrative expenses/sales), capital intensity (fixed assets/total employees), plant and equipment newness (net plant and equipment/gross plant and equipment), and financial leverage (total debt/shareholder's equity). For each variable the authors took the absolute difference from the prior year to the focal year, took the log, converted the six logged measures to z-scores, and summed them into a single standardized index for each year. All firm-year dependent variables were Winsorized at the 2% level.
time_window: year-on-year change, calculated for each of the first five years of a CEO's tenure

description: The year-on-year change in diversification, where diversification was measured with the entropy measure reflecting the number, importance, and relatedness of a firm's business units. For each firm-year the authors calculated the absolute percentage change in the entropy measure from the prior year, then logged and standardized this value. Because data for some firm-years were unavailable, the sample size for this dependent variable was 475 firm-years.
time_window: year-on-year change, first five years of a CEO's tenure

description: For each year the authors used the same six resource allocation variables as for the resource reallocation measure, took each variable and calculated the standardized absolute difference between the firm's score and the industry mean, then took the log of each and summed the six individual variables to create an overall strategic distinctiveness index for the firm in that year.
time_window: annual, first five years of a CEO's tenure

description: The annual sum of additions and deletions to the TMT in a year, divided by the number of members in the previous year. A firm's TMT in a given year was defined as all senior executives identified in the firm's annual 10-K report, excluding the CEO.
time_window: annual, first five years of a CEO's tenure

description: Four annual measures of TMT heterogeneity were generated: age, tenure, educational background, and gender. Age and tenure heterogeneity were operationalized using the coefficient of variation (standard deviation divided by the mean, multiplied by 100), with tenure coded as the number of years the individual had continuously been a member of the firm. Educational background was coded according to Wiersema and Bantel's five-category scheme (arts, science, engineering, business and economics, law); gender was coded as a 1/0 binary variable. Education and gender heterogeneity were operationalized via the Herfindahl-Blauf index, calculated as 1 - sum of squared category proportions, where higher scores indicate greater heterogeneity.
time_window: annual, first five years of a CEO's tenure

description: Eigenvector centrality of the venture's VC investors in the field-level formal co-investment network. Ties are placed between two VC investors if they co-invested during the five-year window ending in the year prior to the round, using all investors active during that window. Centrality scores for all past VC investors of the venture are calculated and the maximum score is taken as the measure; each year's centralities are scaled between 0 and 1, and ventures without connected VC investors are assigned a centrality of 0.
time_window: five-year window ending in the year prior to the round

description: Inverse of the shortest geographical distance between the venture and any of its VC investors in any past round. Distance in miles is calculated using longitudes and latitudes determined from the zip codes of the firms' headquarters. Low values approaching 0 indicate distant VC investors; high values indicate local VC investors. Ventures without VC investors from any past round are assigned a value of 0.

Count of corporate venture investors that participated in a given round of a young firm's funding. An investor is coded as corporate if it was a nonfinancial firm that purchased private equity, excluding loans and public offerings; subsidiaries of banks and insurance companies are excluded. Corporate VC investors were coded using company directories, annual reports, and databases on public companies such as Compustat and Worldscope.

Strength of trade secret defenses in the venture's industry, measured as the percentage of product inventions for which surveyed R&D managers in an industry believed trade secrets to be effective at preventing appropriation. Industries are matched at the three-digit SIC code level at which the Carnegie Mellon Survey of Industrial R&D was conducted.

Investment round number (first, second, etc.) of the focal funding round, logged to reduce skew. Investment round reflects the technology and customer-development milestones that the venture has reached.

Defined as the number of industries in which a group is involved, with industries defined at the two-digit NIC level. Data were compiled from the Prowess database for groups present there; for groups not in Prowess, internet and media searches were used to calculate diversification. The variable is lagged by one period relative to the dependent variable.
time_window: lagged by one period (t, dependent variable at t+1)

variable_name: International sales of a business group
description: Defined as the sum of international sales (in ten million rupees) of all firms that belong to the same group, not including the focal firm. For business groups without a single firm in Prowess the authors state it was impossible to calculate international sales. The variable is lagged by one period relative to the dependent variable.
time_window: lagged by one period (t, dependent variable at t+1)

description: A count of the number of industries that a firm serves in each year, taken from the industries (verticals) each firm lists in the Nasscom directories. Because data on firm sales in each industry segment are not reported, an entropy measure could not be used. Operated as a count variable in a negative binomial model.

Constructed by counting the number of foreign regions that a firm serves, using the United Nations Statistics Division classification of geographical regions to categorize the countries firms name in the Nasscom directories. Firms were classified by region rather than individual country; only 2 percent of observations involve countries in India's own region. Operated as a count variable in a negative binomial model.

International sales in millions of rupees, taken directly from firm entries in the Nasscom directories, where firms report both total sales and export (or international) sales. International sales were used rather than export intensity because in the latter case the numerator and denominator are endogenous. Estimated with a dynamic fixed-effects panel estimator.

Sales per employee, calculated by dividing total sales by the total number of firm employees, described as revenue per employee (productivity). Because Indian software companies mainly provide software development to clients rather than selling packaged products, sales per employee reflects how much a firm can charge its clients and thus its relative profitability.

A dummy variable that takes the value 1 after 1999 and 0 otherwise, used to separate observations from before and after the deregulation of internet access and international bandwidth. The sample is also split into observations occurring prior to the reforms (1994-95, 1996-97, 1998-99) and afterward (1999-2000, 2000-01, 2001-02).

For each dyad in which i is the focal firm and j is the existing or potential firm linked via an interlock, the measure counts the number of ties firm j has to firms operating in the same industry as firm i. Rivals are defined as firms operating in the same industry based on their primary six-digit GICS code. The authors illustrate it with IWKA (machinery), whose partner Dyckerhoff generates two indirect competitor links. This measure was used to test Hypotheses 1 and 2 at the dyad level.

Ego-network measure used to test Hypothesis 3, built by summing across all of the focal firm's partners the indirect links to the focal firm's competitors created by each partner, weighted by the number of direct interlocks that partner has (ties_j). The authors state the intuition that the more others to which a partner can disclose information, the more that partner compounds the baseline risk of leakage for the focal firm. The formula as displayed in the text is not readable.

The logged number of countries in which firm i had engaged in foreign direct investment as of year t. Entries into specific countries are not double counted, so firms with higher values have entered many different countries and possess a broader picture of operating in transition economies. Logging gives more weight to earlier experiences because those are the most formative sources of strategic knowledge.
time_window: as of year t; lagged one year in the models

description: Coded 1 if firm i and j cease having a board tie in year t, and 0 otherwise. Ties had to be discontinued for two years or more to be considered terminated, because a one-year interruption did not clearly signal the intent to end the relationship. Each pair of firms with a board tie was observed from 1990 or the year of inception until termination.
Coded 1 if firm i and j create a new board tie in year t, and 0 otherwise. Only cases in which a pair of firms established a tie for at least two continuous years were counted as additions.

Burt's (1992) measure of constraint, which captures the extent to which firm i's direct ties to its partners are redundant given the number of direct ties between firm i's partners. The variable ranges from 0 to 1, with increasing values indicating higher closure.
time_window: annual, 1990-2003; lagged dependent variable included; predictors lagged one year

description: The dependent variable tracks the average risk-adjusted mortality rate across CABG surgeries performed at the hospital during each two-year period, with higher values reflecting a worse patient survival rate. The risk-adjusted rate, rather than an ordinary rate, is used so that the measure reflects hospital quality rather than patient deaths due to preexisting conditions. Each hospital's failure rate is weighted by a factor relating to the preoperative conditions of the CABG patients treated by that hospital during the period, with hospitals handling more complex cases receiving a larger risk-adjustment weight.

An index of entropy for patient deaths across surgeons within each hospital-period observation, where P is the proportion of the hospital's patient deaths that result from surgeries performed by each surgeon i who operates at the hospital during the period. As the entropy index takes higher values when events are more evenly distributed across categories, the index is reverse-scored to arrive at a measure that increases when failures are more concentrated for particular surgeons at the hospital.

A count of the number of surgeons that performed CABG surgery at the hospital during the period, since this measure directly corresponds with the number of locations (individuals) where failures could potentially arise. To examine the moderating effect of size, the interaction between this variable and the measure of failure concentration was constructed, and variables were centered prior to constructing the interaction to reduce multicollinearity.

variable_name: Percentage of surgeons with above-average performance
description: The percentage of the hospital's surgery staff who received an above-average rating from the regulatory agency during the period, after adjusting for each individual surgeon's patient case mix; the agency discloses the number of surgeons at each hospital who performed better than the statewide average for surgical mortality using the risk-adjusted rate. The variable measures the discrepancy from the published aspiration level when performance exceeds it, and its interaction with failure concentration was constructed with variables centered beforehand.

variable_name: Percentage of surgeons with worst performance
description: The percentage of the hospital's surgery staff who received a below-average rating from the regulatory agency during the period, after adjusting for each individual surgeon's patient case mix; the agency discloses the number of surgeons at each hospital who performed worse than the statewide average for surgical mortality using the risk-adjusted rate. The variable measures the discrepancy when performance falls below the aspiration level, and its interaction with failure concentration was constructed with variables centered beforehand.

variable_name: hazard rate of making a subsequent acquisition
description: The dependent variable is the hazard rate of a bank making a subsequent acquisition following the focal acquisition. The event indicator was coded '1' if a bank made an acquisition during a given spell, and '0' otherwise. The data were transformed into yearly spells so that the analysis incorporates the time the bank took to make the acquisition.

Acquisition performance is measured by the cumulative abnormal return (CAR), the sum of daily abnormal returns for a security over the event window. Returns of the bank's security were assessed against the return of the market portfolio in a market model. The CAR was computed from one trading day before to one trading day after the announcement of an acquisition.
time_window: one trading day before to one trading day after the acquisition announcement

description: An exponentially weighted moving average of the CARs of prior acquisitions. The acquirer market returns of the most recent acquisition update the aspiration level set by all prior acquisitions, with a weight of 0.3 assigned to the most recent acquisition. When a bank entered the sample without a prior acquisition record, its historical aspiration level was set to 0.

The average acquirer market returns of all acquisitions made by all other banks in the state in which the focal bank derives the largest amount of deposits, measured during the year prior to the focal acquisition. The core state (the state from which the bank derives the largest portion of its deposits) is used as the boundary of social comparison.
time_window: year prior to the focal acquisition

variable_name: Acquirer Market Returns below Historical Aspiration
description: Set to 0 when the acquirer market returns of the focal acquisition is above the historical aspiration level. Equals the difference between the acquirer market returns of the focal acquisition and the historical aspiration level when the acquirer market returns of the focal acquisition is below the historical aspiration level.
time_window: focal acquisition relative to prior aspirations

variable_name: Acquirer Market Returns above Historical Aspiration
description: Set to 0 when the acquirer market returns of the focal acquisition is below the historical aspiration level. Equals the difference between the acquirer market returns of the focal acquisition and the historical aspiration level when the acquirer market returns of the focal acquisition is above the historical aspiration level.
time_window: focal acquisition relative to prior aspirations

variable_name: Acquirer Market Returns below Social Aspiration
description: Set to 0 when the acquirer market returns of the focal acquisition is above the social aspiration level, and equal to the difference between the acquirer market returns of the focal acquisition and the social aspiration level when the acquirer market returns is below the social aspiration level. Created using the same spline method as the relative historical performance measures.
time_window: focal acquisition relative to the social aspiration level

variable_name: Acquirer Market Returns above Social Aspiration
description: Set to 0 when the acquirer market returns of the focal acquisition is below the social aspiration level, and equal to the difference between the acquirer market returns of the focal acquisition and the social aspiration level when the acquirer market returns is above the social aspiration level. Created using the same spline method as the relative historical performance measures.
time_window: focal acquisition relative to the social aspiration level

description: Measured by the standard deviation of the acquirer market returns of all the acquisitions that a bank made prior to the focal acquisition since 1988. The variable was measured as of 1988 to reflect the major deregulation in the banking industry. It was set to 0 when a bank did not have any prior acquisition record.

variable_name: acquirer market returns below and above historical and social aspiration
description: Acquisition performance relative to aspiration was entered as a spline, splitting the acquirer market returns of the focal acquisition into a below-aspiration and an above-aspiration variable. This was done separately for historical and social aspiration levels.
Binary variable equal to 1 if the boat leading at the start of the upwind leg was the first to round the windward mark, and equal to 0 if the follower rounded the windward mark first.

Correlation between the compass headings of the leading and following boats, with the heading of the leading boat lagged by 1 second. The variable takes the value of 1 if the leader's lagged changes in heading over the upwind leg match exactly those of the follower, a value of -1 if they are opposite, and a value of 0 if there is no relationship between them.

The absolute value of the difference between the leader's and follower's average positions with respect to course boundaries over the leg, with the negative of this absolute difference taken as the measure. The average position of each boat is calculated from its average distance to the boundary on its right and left sides. The variable takes a value of 0 if both boats have the same average course position during the upwind leg, and decreases with any difference in average positioning.

A GARCH (1,1) model of wind direction, augmented with an autoregressive dependent variable term capturing wind direction in the previous second, is used to forecast wind direction. The uncertainty measure is the absolute percentage difference between the model's forecast of wind direction and the true wind direction, averaged over the upwind leg, then multiplied by 1,000 to make its range comparable to that of other explanatory variables.
time_window: upwind leg; per-second wind direction readings

description: The distance that the leader is ahead of the follower when the follower has rounded the leeward mark, calculated as the distance between the rival boats with respect to the direction from which the wind is blowing.
time_window: start of upwind leg (leeward mark rounding)

description: Calculated as the difference in average velocity made good (VMG), normalized by the wind speed, of both competitors over all previous upwind legs of events in which both participated. An increase in this efficiency score indicates an increase of capability advantage of the follower over the leader, while a negative score indicates that it is the leading boat that has a capability advantage.
time_window: all previous upwind legs of events in which both competitors participated

description: A bank's status was measured with Bonacich's (1987) centrality score, which computes an actor's power in its network by taking into account not only the actor's centrality but also the centrality of those connected with it. The network used was an affiliation network based on the preferred banker relationships of the 500 largest firms listed on the BSE, in which banks intersect when they jointly service a corporate client that lists them as preferred. Each bank's Bonacich centrality score was computed in each year.
time_window: computed each year, observed between 2004 and 2008

variable_name: number of loan recovery harassment complaints
description: Corporate illegality for each bank in each year was quantified as the number of harassment complaints against the bank, as reported by the Banking Ombudsman. The data were coded from the Banking Ombudsman's annual reports, which categorize the complaints lodged against each bank, using the loan recovery harassment category that the RBI clarifies pertains to non-observance of Reserve Bank guidelines on engagement of recovery agents by banks.

variable_name: decline in historically referenced reputation for quality
description: Financial asset quality was coded as the NPA percentage in the bank's loan portfolio, where higher values indicated poorer financial asset quality. The difference in NPA percentage between year t and year t-1 was computed for each bank-year; values above 0 indicated deterioration and values below 0 improvement. The decline variable was set to the difference when NPA percentage in year t exceeded NPA percentage in year t-1, and to 0 otherwise. The printed formulas for the spline variables are garbled in the text.

variable_name: decline in socially referenced reputation for quality
description: The annual change in NPA was computed for each bank-year, and the mean annual change in NPA of peers was computed as the average of the annual changes in NPA of all other banks in a focal bank's peer group, where peers are the banks that jointly serve the same BSE500 clients as preferred bankers. The decline variable was set to the difference between the focal bank's annual change in NPA and the mean annual change in NPA of its peers when the focal bank's change exceeded that of its peers, and to 0 otherwise. The printed formulas for the spline variables are garbled in the text.
time_window: annual change in the focal year

variable_name: reputation for integrity expectations of associates
description: The reputations for integrity of all BSE500 firms that disclosed their preferred bankers were coded using the Karmayog data, whose ratings are based on the mandatory sustainability reporting each BSE500 firm includes in its annual report. The mean Karmayog score of all of a bank's BSE500 associates was divided by the standard deviation of the scores to construct the variable, so that larger values indicated higher integrity expectations and greater agreement among a bank's BSE500 associates.

variable_name: number of bars in the municipality appearing on the member list of the SSB
description: Based on the membership files of the SSB foundation at the end of 2008, which contained the names and addresses of pubs and bars that openly stated that they were against the smoking ban and in almost all cases allowed smoking on their premises. Address information was used to determine the municipality in which bars were located, and the number of bars per municipality was counted. The measure was validated against the number of fines per municipality for 2008-2009, with a correlation of 0.83.

Measured based on (a) the number of people entering a community through residential moves relative to the number of inhabitants and (b) the number of people leaving a community through residential moves relative to the number of inhabitants, each calculated for 2007, the year prior to the measurement of the dependent variable. The resulting variables were standardized and then inverted so that high scores reflect high levels of residential stability; because the two variables were highly correlated (0.84), they were averaged. Only residential moves within the Netherlands are taken into account.

Measured using information from the National Housing Survey from 2008, in which a sample of 78,071 respondents designed to be representative at the municipal level answered numerous questions about their living environment. The authors adopted the measure developed by Goudriaan, Wittebrood, and Nieuwbeerta (2006) based on nine items from this survey, each answered on a seven-point Likert scale; the measure is the average answer over the nine items, with a reliability of 0.83 in the data. To arrive at the community-level measure, individual scores were averaged within each municipality.

variable_name: spatial lag of the dependent variable
description: Calculated on the basis of the dependent variable using spatial econometrics: the spatially lagged variable of the dependent variable based on an exponential distance decay function, capturing the level of resistance in the communities surrounding the focal community, with the weight of neighboring municipalities exponentially diminishing with distance from the focal municipality. The distance is the geographical distance as the crow flies between the centroids of the municipalities.

Core knowledge employees reported their own experienced performance-oriented HR systems rather than an overall assessment of their firm's HR systems, using Gong, Law, et al.'s (2009) 36-item performance-oriented HR systems measure. A sample item was 'I regularly receive development-focused performance appraisals in my firm.' Cronbach's alpha was 0.91. Rwg(j) was 0.55, below the conventional aggregation cutoff of 0.70, so the experiences were not aggregated to the firm level.

Core knowledge employees rated their own experienced maintenance-oriented HR systems in line with Gong, Law, et al.'s (2009) 12-item maintenance-oriented HR systems measure. A representative item was 'my firm has offered me a pledge of employment security.' Cronbach's alpha was 0.82. Rwg(j) was 0.57, below the conventional aggregation cutoff of 0.70, so the experiences were not aggregated to the firm level.
Firm ownership was coded as a dichotomous variable with 0 = POE and 1 = SOE.

Youndt et al.'s (2004) five-item scale was used to measure core knowledge employees' skills in their job/specialty areas. Employees rated items such as 'I am highly skilled in my job/specialty area.' Cronbach's alpha was 0.80. Convergent validity was checked against the technical levels of 87 surveyed engineers from 15 firms.

Supervisors rated core knowledge employees' creativity using the 13-item scale from Zhou and George (2001). A sample item was 'this employee suggests new ways to achieve goals or objectives.' Cronbach's alpha was 0.90. Within each firm the key R&D personnel were under the same supervisor.

In line with an additive composition model, aggregate employee creativity in a firm was operationalized as the mean of the firm's core knowledge employees' creativity evaluations done by their supervisor. Because it reflects the average rather than the shared level of creativity, empirical justifications such as Rwg do not apply.

Firm innovation was measured as the number of new products introduced into the existing line of products of a firm in the year following the phase 3 data collection. The surveyed companies' R&D managers indicated that it was appropriate to use this measure to capture the companies' innovation levels.
time_window: the year following phase 3 data collection

description: The annual change (year t-1 to t) in a firm's published Fortune rating. The published rating is the average of eight survey items. A change measure is employed to remain consistent with the paper's focus on how earnings misses cause reputational evaluations to shift in their wake.

A count of the (up to four) quarterly earnings estimates that the firm failed to meet during the focal year. Whether a firm missed earnings in a given quarter was assessed by comparing its actual earnings to analysts' last median earnings estimate (as provided by IBES) before the firm announced its earnings for the quarter. Misses are counted for the four quarters prior to the mailing of the Fortune survey rather than for the prior calendar year itself.
time_window: four quarters prior to the survey mailing

description: The number of quarters in which a firm made its earnings estimates in the three years prior to the focal year. To isolate the effect of an individual firm's history from trends in firms' overall propensities to meet earnings estimates, the raw count was reexpressed as a deviation from the overall sample mean in each year. The reexpression also centered the variable to facilitate interpretation of interaction terms.
time_window: three years prior to the focal year

description: A dichotomous measure set to one if First Call data show that the focal firm provided public and explicit earnings guidance in the given year, and zero otherwise.

A count of articles in the Wall Street Journal Abstracts that referenced the firm in the focal year. The abstract search returns only articles in which the firm is prominently featured. The raw count is reexpressed as a deviation from the overall sample mean in each year, which centers the variable and takes account of long-term shifts in media coverage.

The fraction of other surveyed firms within the firm's Fortune industry that made all of their quarterly earnings estimates in the focal year. The raw fraction is reexpressed as a deviation from the overall sample mean in each year.

A simple time trend measure which is the count of years minus 1995 (the study period's temporal center). Used to test the prediction that broad shifts in the institutional context led to earnings misses causing more reputational damage later in the study period; it is described as a broad measure.

Participants completed objective assessments of whether the board engaged in 13 CEO succession planning related activities. A parallel analysis suggested a single-factor solution and an exploratory factor analysis identified 10 items with factor loadings greater than .40; the three items with loadings below .40 were excluded. The final measure is the count of the number of formalized succession processes that the board uses in its succession planning. The measure exhibited acceptable reliability (Cronbach's alpha = .74).

Respondents were asked, 'When it comes to the reality of choosing the CEO's successor, how much influence will the CEO have versus the board?' Response categories ranged from '100% board/0% CEO' to '0% board/100% CEO' in 10% increments, treated as interval variables with values from 0 (0% CEO/100% board control) to 10 (100% CEO control/0% board control).

Respondents were asked, 'Approximately how many executives in the total executive population currently would be considered potential successors to the CEO?' Responses were coded 0 if one or fewer candidates were being considered and 1 if there were at least two candidates under consideration, because the authors anticipated a qualitative difference between firms that consider just one candidate and those that consider more than one. In 2015 two questions about insiders and external candidates were combined to create a comparable measure.

Respondents were asked, 'If your CEO were to step down or leave today, how confident are you that his/her permanent successor would immediately be an internal direct report (i.e., immediate promotion without an 'interim' CEO)?' The scale for this item ranged from 0% to 100%, in 10-unit intervals. The item assesses the quality of succession planning by evaluating the expectation that the organization could name an internal successor.

Respondents were asked, 'If your CEO were to step down or leave today, how long do you think it would take to have a permanent successor in place?' The six response options ranged from 'less than one week' to 'six months or more'; smaller values indicate a shorter timeframe.
scale: six response options from 'less than one week' to 'six months or more'

description: Respondents were asked, 'Are you using external/third party help in CEO succession?' coded as 1 if companies indicated use external help and 0 otherwise.

variable_name: count of new LEED-certified buildings in an MSA-year
description: A count of new LEED-certified buildings in an MSA-year. Zip code-level information on building locations was aggregated to the MSA level using a spatial concordance file.

A factor composed of six items capturing the strength of the market logic in each MSA-year, extracted with principal component factor analysis (eigenvalue of 2.25; alpha of 0.66). The six items are the ideology of each MSA's political leaders on a liberal-conservative continuum (state-level measure weighted to the MSA by population), the political ideology of citizens based on state-level election results, the percentage of voters in an MSA who voted Republican in national elections, the ratio of contributions to Republican candidates relative to total donations in each MSA, the local tax burden for businesses (reverse coded so that a lower tax burden means a stronger market logic), and the density of registered labor unions in an MSA (reverse coded so that lower union density means a stronger market logic).
time_window: MSA-year; social capital and contribution data interpolated or biennial as available

description: Regional strength of a community logic measured with an established measure of community social capital from the regional economics literature. The data were available at county level for the years 1990, 1997, 2005, 2009, and 2014; the authors interpolated data for missing years for each county and then aggregated to the MSA level.

A count variable constructed from the number of green building economic incentive policies by MSA-year, including policies enacted at a city or county level matched to appropriate MSAs, gathered from a USGBC online database and cross-validated with the Database of State Incentives for Renewables and Efficiency. Because the variable is strongly right-skewed, its logged value was used in models.

To create an annual measure of TSMO activity, the authors obtained the addresses and joining dates of USGBC members. The count was normalized by MSA population and multiplied by 100,000 to scale appropriately for model coefficients.

The number of LEED Accredited Professionals in each MSA for a given year, obtained at zip code level from the Green Building Certification Institute, aggregated to the MSA level, normalized by population, and scaled for interpretation of coefficients. APs are not certifiers; their role is purely advisory.

A log-transformed count of new companies listed in the GreenSpec directory of green building product suppliers for each MSA-year. GreenSpec is not advertising based and firms do not pay to be listed; entrepreneurial entrants (founded no earlier than 1994) were separated from incumbents.

variable_name: economic distance (lower economic distance; higher economic distance)
description: Economic distance was measured as the difference, in U.S. dollars, in the real per capita GDP between Singapore and a host country in the first year of an FDI. The natural logarithmic difference was used: ln(ys) minus ln(y) for less developed host countries and ln(y) minus ln(ys) for more developed host countries, where ys and y represent the real GDPs per capita in U.S. dollars of Singapore and the host country. The variable was partitioned into two parts, one measure for distance from more developed economies and the other for distance from less developed economies. The text does not name the source of the GDP figures.
level: home country-host country pair per FDI

description: The dependent variable was the hazard rate of an FDI, modelled with the logarithm of the hazard rate as the dependent variable and estimated in discrete time. A censoring dummy took the value 1 if the FDI survived until the end of the study period or exited the survey for reasons other than failure (e.g., it was sold for a profit), and 0 otherwise; the PHREG procedure adjusted for the censored observations.
time_window: from FDI establishment until termination or the end of the 1980-2000 observation period

description: Two dummies were coded on the mode of entry. Acquisition was coded 1 if a venture was acquired and 0 if it was not. Greenfield was coded 1 if a venture was a newly established operation and 0 if it was not.

A dummy variable coded '1' for a founder CEO with one or more start-up experiences throughout his or her prior career and '0' for a founder CEO with the focal firm as his or her only start-up experience. The authors investigated the entire careers of the 448 founder CEOs and distinguished start-up experience from other involvements such as academic, political, and other business careers. The absence of other new venture experiences indicates that the focal firm is this person's only creation.

A continuous variable that equals the total number of founders at a firm's inception. The authors state that the higher the total number of founders, the less organizational identification the founder CEO is deemed to have.

Coded '1' if the founder CEO was the initial founding CEO (had been CEO from the firm's inception) and '0' in all other cases. The authors follow Wasserman (2017) in using initial CEO status to define core founders.

variable_name: time as a private firm (private-year ratio)
description: The relative length of time as a private firm, calculated by taking the number of years between the firm founding and the IPO as the numerator divided by the total age of the firm. A higher private-year ratio is expected to indicate a higher level of founder CEO organizational identification. The authors also ran models using the absolute number of years the firm existed before going public, with consistent results; only the private-year ratio measure is reported in the tables.

An event indicator coded '1' in the year in which the founder CEO departed voluntarily and '0' otherwise. A voluntary succession was defined as: resignation with retention of another position within the firm for more than a year; succession by a family member; retirement due to age; or acceptance of an equivalent or better position at another organization. The authors tracked CEO status from each firm's IPO year to 2013; 134 firms that ceased to exist independent of founder CEO succession and the 191 firms whose founder CEOs remained in office until 2013 were censored, leaving 123 succession events of which 88 were voluntary.

Measured by the percentage of negative words captured in the media coverage of the acquisition, using the Linguistic Inquiry and Word Count (LIWC) content-analysis software with its pre-validated dictionary of negative emotion words. Articles were collected over a 21-day window starting three days before and going 17 days after the acquisition announcement, from four national business news outlets (Forbes, Wall Street Journal, Bloomberg BusinessWeek, Barron's) and three news services (Associated Press Newswires, Dow Jones Newswires, Gannett News Service). Articles not directly about the focal company and focal acquisition, duplicates and exact reprints of company press releases were manually removed. The higher the value, the more negative the media coverage.
time_window: 21-day window from three days before to 17 days after the acquisition announcement

description: The total value of all large acquisitions announced during the 365 days following the focal acquisition. It is used instead of the number of acquisitions because it is continuous and captures the nuance of acquisition behavior, such as the number of deals and the size of targets pursued. The variable was log-transformed due to skewness.

Content analysis of the CEO's letter to the shareholders with LIWC's dictionary of 145 past focus words. The value is the number of words the past-focus dictionary captured from the letter to the shareholders from the year prior to the acquisition announcement, divided by the total number of words in the letter. The measure captures past focus as an independent construct rather than the relative strength of past versus future focus.
time_window: letter from the year prior to the acquisition announcement

description: Content analysis of the CEO's letter to the shareholders with LIWC's dictionary of 48 future focus words. The value is the number of words the future-focus dictionary captured from the letter to the shareholders from the year prior to the acquisition announcement, divided by the total number of words in the letter. The measure captures future focus as an independent construct rather than the relative strength of future versus past focus.
time_window: letter from the year prior to the acquisition announcement

description: Count of female executives who represent new additions to the TMT in a given year. New TMT members were identified from annual reports, with demographic and job-related information retrieved from BoardEx; TMT membership is defined as having the rank of vice president or holding a board executive directorship.
Count of male executives who represent new additions to the TMT in a given year, identified in the same way as female appointments.

Percentage of words in the firm's letter to shareholders capturing the construct of change orientation (e.g., create, transform), counted with Linguistic Inquiry and Word Count (LIWC) software using a dictionary compiled and validated for this purpose by McClelland, Liang, and Barker (2010). The variable is transformed by taking the first difference (from year t-1 to t) to capture changes in TMT cognitions, and censored at zero if the letters used none of the dictionary words.
time_window: first difference from t-1 to t

description: Percentage of words in the firm's letter to shareholders capturing the construct of risk taking (e.g., audacious, precarious), counted with Linguistic Inquiry and Word Count (LIWC) software using a dictionary compiled and validated for this purpose by Short, Broberg, Cogliser, and Brigham (2010). The variable is transformed by taking the first difference (from year t-1 to t) to capture changes in TMT cognitions, and censored at zero if the letters used none of the dictionary words.
time_window: first difference from t-1 to t

description: The total number of women on a TMT, lagged by one year (i.e., in a year preceding the year in which a new appointment occurred). For the threshold tests, dummy variables take the value of 1 if no woman, exactly one, exactly two, exactly three, or four or more women were on the TMT prior to the female TMT appointment.

variable_name: Relative size of the cohort of incoming TMT appointees
description: The total number of male and female new TMT appointments during a year divided by the number of TMT members in the previous year. A relative small cohort corresponds to adding one or two new executives and a large cohort means adding two to four new executives, depending on the size of the TMT; the sample mean used to split subsamples is 0.14.
time_window: appointments in year relative to TMT size in previous year

description: The yearly growth of the focal firm's R&D stock beyond replenishment and depreciation. R&D expenditures reported in balance sheets comprise both new and replacement R&D; the knowledge capital produced by R&D investments is constructed with the perpetual inventory method using a single depreciation rate of 15%.
For each focal firm, the first difference (from t to t+1) of the annual count of technology-based M&A, that is, acquisitions of target firms with patent activities.
time_window: first difference from t to t+1

variable_name: Number of founders with variety of experiences
description: Within-founder experience variety aggregated at the team level: the count of founders who, in the five years before joining their startups, worked in at least two firms and did not transition from the same industry incumbent as the other founding members. Only workers who entered the data at least five years before being employed by the startup are included, to avoid comparing workers who had the chance to change jobs with those who did not. Founders whose earnings decreased when they changed jobs, or whose average yearly earnings over the five years were below $10,000, are excluded.
time_window: five years before joining the startup

variable_name: Shared experience of founders transitioning from the same industry incumbent
description: The number of years the team worked together in the same incumbent firm right before creating the startup. The four-digit level NAICS is used to establish that the incumbent firm and the startup belong to the same industry. The largest set of team members who came from the same incumbent is identified and the time they worked together is measured; in case of a tie between multiple sets, the set with the highest earnings the year before the startup's creation is used.

Coded 0 in any year the startup is alive and 1 the year the startup fails. If the startups were acquired, the last year observed as an independent firm is coded 0 and the following years are not included. The yearly failure rate is 5%, and 27% of all the startups failed during the period from 2000 to 2008.
time_window: each year of survival and one year of failure, if any

description: The difference between the number of hours of actual sunshine realized on a Demo Day and that on the previous day. It is calculated from historical weather data with a precision of up to a quarter of an hour (15 minutes). The weather data were validated against the National Oceanic & Atmospheric Administration wherever available.
time_window: Demo Day and the preceding day

description: Takes a value of 1 if a startup secures a Demo Day funding round and 0 otherwise. Following past practice, any financing round recorded within a 90-day period of the Demo Day date is considered a Demo Day round.
time_window: within 90 days of the Demo Day date

description: The time elapsed, in months, between the startup's founding date and its Demo Day date. It is a continuous variable at the startup level, described as a proxy of startup maturity; the authors also refer to it as Venture age (months) in the results.

Each founder scored 1 if they had prior entrepreneurial experience, held a master's degree or higher, and 0 otherwise. The variable Human capital is the overall score calculated as the mean value across a startup's founders; it is a startup-level continuous variable taking values between 0 and 1.

Measures investment attractiveness using a 7-item Likert scale, where the value 1 denotes a highly unattractive opportunity and 7 stands for a highly attractive opportunity. It captures the extent to which participants viewed the startup as a viable and attractive investment opportunity.
Equals the natural log of the intended investment plus 1. Respondents were asked to report the intended investment amount using a sliding scale with dollar amounts ranging from $0 to over $20,000.

A binary variable that equals 1 for the scenario where the day was described to be sunnier than the previous day, and 0 otherwise. The manipulation consisted of visual and textual weather cues presented on the opening page of the survey instrument, randomly assigning participants across a sunny and a cloudy scenario.

Reports mood valence based on participants' scores on the PANAS-SF instrument, the 10-question short-form version of the Positive And Negative Affect Schedule. It was deployed immediately after the manipulation but before showing the pitch.

All identifiable work experiences of each current TMT member up to that point in his or her career were aggregated on a firm-year basis. Industries were defined by NAICS boundaries, with a NAICS code (fidelity up to six digits) assigned to each experience using the primary NAICS code of the firm or division the individual worked at that year. A Shannon entropy index of the different NAICS codes present was then computed, capturing the number and spread of qualitatively different experiences, normalized such that a value of one equated to the theoretical maximum of ln(249).
time_window: career histories up to the focal firm-year

description: Repertoire complexity was first measured as a Shannon entropy index of the action types employed by a firm in a specific year, normalized by the theoretical maximum ln(10) so that the maximum value equals unity. A time-varying external variety standard was constructed from the complexity of the top three firms by sales volume each year, using the linear trend of their repertoire complexity. The firm's achieved complexity was subtracted from that standard, the difference partitioned into magnitude and sign, and the deviation magnitude subtracted from one, so the measure is maximum when there is no difference between the firm's repertoire and the calibration standard.

Repertoire consistency was computed using a normalized displacement vector incorporating the magnitude and direction of the year-to-year change in a firm's competitive repertoire in 10-dimensional space versus actions taken in prior years; a fully consistent repertoire takes a value of unity and a completely inconsistent repertoire takes a value of zero. The external variety standard was the consistency of the top three firms by sales volume, modeled with linear, quadratic, and cubic orthogonal polynomial trend terms. The firm's achieved consistency was subtracted from the standard, and the deviation magnitude subtracted from one to obtain the calibration measure.

Firm performance was measured using return on assets. In the performance analyses the authors controlled for return on assets in the prior year to mitigate reverse causality, and the prior year's ROA was verified not to be a significant predictor of calibrated repertoire complexity or consistency.
time_window: focal year, with prior-year ROA as a control

description: An approximation of Tobin's Q calculated as the sum of the market value of common stock, the book value of preferred stock, and total debt, divided by total assets. The authors chose this forward-looking market-based measure rather than backward-looking accounting-based measures.
time_window: predictor measured one year before the appointment event

description: Measured using expert ratings of companies from the 'Korea's Most Admired Companies' list, the South Korean equivalent of Fortune's 'Most Admired Corporations' list. The list relies on survey ratings by business executives, financial analysts, and consumers in six areas: social value, shareholder value, employee value, customer value, image value, and innovation, and includes overall top 30 'all-star companies' as well as industry top-ranking firms. The binary variable was coded as 1 if the firm was included on the list.
time_window: annual list; predictor measured one year before the appointment event

description: Measured as the degree centrality within the intragroup board interlock network. Specifically, it is the total number of board positions that board members in a focal firm held at other firms within the business group. The logarithm of this variable was taken before its inclusion in the empirical models.
time_window: predictor measured one year before the appointment event

description: A dummy variable equal to 1 if net income was negative in the year prior to the appointment event. The authors note that firms under financial distress are subject to a higher risk of bankruptcy.
time_window: year prior to the appointment event

description: Measured as the count of existing family members serving on a focal firm's board. Because the empirical models always control for the total number of board members, the variable assesses the impact of the number of existing family directors scaled by board size.

Binary dependent variable in the pooled probit models, taking the value of 0 for the appointment of nonfamily inside directors and 1 for the appointment of family directors. Nonfamily inside directors were used as the baseline comparison group rather than outside directors because they are more comparable to family directors in terms of potential to be groomed for leadership. Appointment events were measured one year after the predictors.
time_window: appointment event at t+1 relative to predictors

variable_name: Later- versus earlier-generation family member appointment
description: Categorical dependent variable in the pooled multinomial probit models, taking the value of 0 for the appointment of nonfamily inside directors, 1 for earlier-generation family members, and 2 for later-generation family members. Consistent with prior research, the first and second generations of the family were treated as the 'earlier generation,' while family members beyond the second generation were classified as part of the 'later generation.'
time_window: appointment event at t+1 relative to predictors

description: The authors obtained personal data on controlling family members, including names, dates of birth, generation, and total number of family members, from books on chaebol families supplemented with media reports and internet searches. Three family director appointees who joined the family through marriage were included in the sample.

Measured by first observing whether any VC partners coinvested in at least one other firm within the five years prior to a given date. For each coinvestment tie between a start-up's VCs, the authors count the number of companies in which VCs A and B invested prior to time t, and for each such company observe the number of investors other than A and B; the tie-strength score of a coinvestment via company i is 1/(Ni-1), where Ni is the total number of investors in that company. The weight of the coinvestment tie between A and B is the sum of these scores, and the sum of the weights of all coinvestment ties among a given firm's investors is the measure of VC joint collaboration experience. It is calculated for first-round VC investors and standardized in some estimation models.
time_window: five years prior to a given date (time-varying)

description: Indicator of whether a venture-backed start-up experiences an acquisition exit, which the authors treat as a focused success. A start-up enters the risk set at its first round of VC investment and leaves when it goes public, is acquired, or fails, so acquisition is modeled as one of three competing exit events. Of the 10,879 U.S.-based VC-backed start-ups analyzed, 1,689 (15.5%) experienced an acquisition exit, with mean time-to-exit of 1,237 days.
time_window: from first round of VC investment until exit or right-censoring on July 1, 2014

description: Indicator of whether a venture-backed start-up experiences an IPO exit, which the authors treat as a broadcast success. Of the 10,879 U.S.-based VC-backed start-ups analyzed, 317 (2.9%) experienced an IPO exit, with mean time-to-exit of 1,658 days. IPO is modeled as one of three competing exit events in the hazard models.
time_window: from first round of VC investment until exit or right-censoring on July 1, 2014

description: The CEO's political ideology was measured with the validated CEO liberalism index based on the executive's contribution records for the 10 years before becoming CEO, manually checked against Federal Election Commission filings. Four indicators were computed (donations to Democrats over donations to both parties in number and dollar amount, years in which donations went to Democrats over years donations were made to either party, and distinct Democratic recipients over all distinct recipients), .1 was added to all numerators and .2 to all denominators to handle 0 values, and the average of the four indicators was taken; the index ranges from 0 (intensely conservative) to 1 (intensely liberal). The national political climate was coded 1 if the president was a Democrat and 0 if not, and divergence is the absolute difference between the two measures.
time_window: Donation records cover the 10 years before the executive became CEO; divergence is measured at t-1

description: R&D intensity is measured by R&D spending divided by firm sales, following Chen and Miller (2007), and the examination is limited to firms with R&D intensity less than 1. It is measured at time t, with independent, moderating and control variables lagged at t-1, and the data were obtained from Compustat.

Retention of earnings was measured by the amount of retained earnings depicted in the firm's annual report. The variable is measured at time t, with independent, moderating and control variables lagged at t-1, and the data were obtained from Compustat.
The moderator is calculated as the vested (i.e., unexercised but exercisable) option value taken from the ExecuComp database, logged to normalize its distribution.
A dummy variable reflecting a regulated industry, coded 1 if an industry belongs to one of the 10 most highly regulated industries according to McLaughlin and Sherouse's (2016) categories.

Index of executive job demands formed from five causal indicators. Environment dynamism was measured with a 3-item survey scale on a 6-point Likert scale (1 = strongly disagree to 6 = strongly agree). Hostile suppliers and buyers (8 items) and hostile competitors (3 items) were reverse-coded because higher values represented friendlier environments, then averaged from standardized scores. Performance challenge was the percentage of sales growth from 2013 to 2014 minus the average sales growth rate of firms in the same industry in the same period, reverse-coded so that higher values correspond to lower relative sales growth. Executive aspirations were measured with the CEO's need for achievement (18 items), reverse-coded and summed as standardized scores. The index is the sum of the standardized scores of these measures.
time_window: environment dynamism assessed over the past three years; performance challenge uses 2013-2014 sales growth; survey in 2015

description: The 12-item scale developed and validated by Jansen et al. (2006), which includes six items measuring exploratory innovations and six items measuring exploitative innovations in all major areas of business operations. Executives rated responses on a 7-point Likert scale ranging from 1 (strongly disagree) to 7 (strongly agree). A firm's overall innovation is the simple average of the 12 items.
scale: 7-point Likert scale (1 = strongly disagree to 7 = strongly agree)

description: Six items from the 12-item scale of Jansen et al. (2006) measuring exploratory innovations in all major areas of business operations, rated by executives on a 7-point Likert scale ranging from 1 (strongly disagree) to 7 (strongly agree).
scale: 7-point Likert scale (1 = strongly disagree to 7 = strongly agree)

description: Six items from the 12-item scale of Jansen et al. (2006) measuring exploitative innovations in all major areas of business operations, rated by executives on a 7-point Likert scale ranging from 1 (strongly disagree) to 7 (strongly agree).
scale: 7-point Likert scale (1 = strongly disagree to 7 = strongly agree)

description: Following existing studies, the share of exploratory innovations is calculated as exploratory innovations divided by the sum of exploratory and exploitative innovations after standardization.

variable_name: variety in executives' gender, age, and tenure
description: The sum of the standardized scores of variety in gender, age, and tenure. Variety in gender was measured using Blau's index, calculated as 1 minus the sum of squared percentages of executives in each gender category. Variety in age and tenure were each measured by the ratio of the standard deviation to the mean.
Measured using the survey questionnaire developed and validated by Tsui et al. (2006), with four items in the scale.
Measured using the survey questionnaire developed and validated by Tsui et al. (2006), with four items in the scale.
Measured using the percentage of employees with at least a bachelor's degree.

Social conservatism was measured with five items capturing beliefs and preferences for relevant traditional norms in Iran: collectivism, environmental protection, and concerns about diversity. Items were compiled from previous studies and reviewed by Iranian scholars for appropriateness to the Iranian context. Responses used a 5-point Likert scale from 1 = strongly disagree to 5 = strongly agree. The scale was reported by CEOs at T1 and had a reliability alpha of .88.
scale: 5-point Likert (1 = strongly disagree to 5 = strongly agree)

description: Economic conservatism was measured with six items capturing beliefs about cooperation in society and economic inequality. Items were compiled from previous studies and reviewed for appropriateness to the Iranian context. Responses used a 5-point Likert scale from 1 = strongly disagree to 5 = strongly agree. The scale was reported by CEOs at T1 and had a reliability alpha of .91.
scale: 5-point Likert (1 = strongly disagree to 5 = strongly agree)

description: A four-item validated scale capturing intuitive strategic decision-making. Responses were given by CEOs and TMT members at T2 and aggregated to the TMT level, with aggregation justified by ICC(1) = .20, ICC(2) = .49, and rWG(J) = .62 and a reliability alpha of .91. Items include reliance on experience-based intuition rather than quantitative analysis and the influence of industry experience and lessons learned over formal research.

A validated 5-item scale capturing the essence of cooperative decision-making, the extent to which members perceived rewards or goals in their team as interdependent. Responses were given by CEOs and TMT members at T2 and aggregated to the TMT level, with aggregation justified by ICC(1) = .23, ICC(2) = .55, and rWG(J) = .69 and a reliability alpha of .94.

CE was reported by CEOs and TMT members at T3 using a 15-item formative scale with three underlying dimensions: innovation, corporate venturing, and strategic renewal. CE was modeled as a second-order factor subsuming the three first-order factors, and the authors averaged the z-scores of the three factors to derive CE (alpha = .91). Within-TMT agreement for the aggregated CE measure was acceptable (ICC(1) = .20, ICC(2) = .51, rWG(J) = .87).
scale: Likert-type items (1 = strongly disagree, 5 = strongly agree)

description: The measure compares the focal developer's ranking with those of the publisher's other developers. Ranking uses review scores assigned to a developer's games (including non-PS2 games), normalized on a scale of 1 to 100 and averaged over the three years prior to year t, with an average updating procedure giving more weight to developers who more consistently developed high-quality games. The focal developer's score is compared with the other developers in the publisher's portfolio by counting the number of 'inferior' developers and dividing by the total number of developers affiliated with the publisher. In cases in which there were no other developers, the variable was set to 1.
time_window: three years prior to year t

description: Measured by the number of reviews the games released by the publisher received. Operationally, the authors counted the average number of reviews (in hundreds) received by a publisher's games in the three years prior to the focal year t, dividing the number of reviews by the number of games published, and took a logarithm to reduce skew.
time_window: three years prior to year t

description: Measured by a developer's product experience: the number of games launched by the developer in prior years, including non-PS2 games. High values indicate high external resource needs.

Measured by the anticipated count of PS2 games likely to overlap with the games of the focal developer in a year. To compute overlap, the population developers' games were compared with each of the focal developer's games using genre categories; the authors counted all published games in the focal developer's genres over the last three years and took an average.

A dummy variable coded 1 if a developer and a publisher formed a tie to develop one or more PS2 games in year t and 0 otherwise. The game release year was used as the year of collaboration; for collaborations that were initiated but fundamentally repurposed or subsequently discontinued, the year when this change occurred was used.

A CAR is the sum of the daily abnormal returns for a security over a period, capturing the influence of events during that period. Stock returns were assessed against the return of the market portfolio, with CAR[-1,0] calculated based on estimates of the model's constant and stock-specific slope during a 250-day window that runs from 295 to 45 days before the focal acquisition. For Hypothesis 1a and Hypothesis 1b, the absolute value of negative CAR[-1,0] was used in the models.
time_window: event window [-1,0]; estimation window from day -295 to day -45

description: Strategic noise was coded as present if three criteria were met at the time of an M&A: (a) a firm announced a confounding event within [-1, +1] day of the M&A announcement, (b) the confounding event was completely under the control of the firm, and (c) the event was not intended to clarify or be causally related to the M&A. Since the focus is reactive IM, strategic noise was measured as the count of strategic noise events that occurred on Day +1 after an M&A announcement (on Day 0). Clearly positive releases were coded as positive strategic noise; in the case of ambiguous releases, additional information was used, with earnings increases relative to estimations treated as positive, estimation confirmations as neutral, and decreases as negative news.

Strategic noise was coded as present if three criteria were met at the time of an M&A: (a) a firm announced a confounding event within [-1, +1] day of the M&A announcement, (b) the confounding event was completely under the control of the firm, and (c) the event was not intended to clarify or be causally related to the M&A. Reactive negative strategic noise was measured as the count of negative strategic noise items released on Day +1. Clearly negative releases were coded as negative strategic noise; in the case of ambiguous releases, additional information was used, with earnings decreases relative to estimations treated as negative news.

Two independent judges blind to the research objectives read the Kickstarter campaigns and coded the basis for cofounder-relation initiation: friendship, family ties or romantic ties (interpersonal attraction), or professional, entrepreneurial and educational background (resource-seeking); Cohen's kappa was .91. The bases were classified as interpersonal attraction, resource-seeking, or dual strategy (a combination of more than one type across strategies), and two dummy variables were created with interpersonal attraction as the omitted referent.

Early entrepreneurial success was measured as the funding amount in United States dollars; non-USD currencies were converted to USD using the respective average exchange rates in 2014 and amounts are presented in units of $1,000 ($K).
time_window: at the end of the campaign (April to December 2014)

description: As in Study 1, two independent judges blind to the research objectives were trained and read the competition applications to code the basis for cofounder-relation initiation; Cohen's kappa was .87. Relations were classified as interpersonal attraction, resource-seeking, or dual strategy, and two dummy variables were created with interpersonal attraction as the omitted referent.

Measured with 12 items from the scale developed by Lewis (2003) on a 7-point scale ranging from 1 = 'strongly disagree' to 7 = 'strongly agree' (alpha = .93). Items formed a single score per individual and were then aggregated to the team level using average scores of members per team; intermember agreement (median rwg(j) = .95) and intermember reliability (ICC(1) = .43, ICC(2) = .60) justified aggregation.
scale: 7-point Likert scale (1 = strongly disagree, 7 = strongly agree)
time_window: last week of the e-school phase

description: Early entrepreneurial success was measured in terms of advancement to different phases of the competition, including whether teams were selected to the competition (i.e., entered the e-school phase); a dummy variable was coded as 1 for entering the competition and 0 otherwise. Selection is highly competitive, with only 25% of applicants entering the e-school.

Survival was measured through the number of months teams continued to participate in the competition; failure events for assessing the hazard rate were coded 1 if the team was eliminated from the competition and 0 otherwise.

variable_name: Formation strategy conditions (interpersonal attraction high/low; resource-seeking high/low)
description: Interpersonal attraction was manipulated based on a network-assessment task: founders were paired with students they had a strong relationship with (higher interpersonal attraction; at least three members who knew each other and had an above-median closeness score) or whom they did not know (lower interpersonal attraction). Resource-seeking was manipulated from coders' ratings of resumes in four skill domains (general management, marketing and sales, finance, technical); founders were paired with students who possessed different dominant skills (high resource-seeking, complementary skills) or the same dominant skill (low resource-seeking, overlapping skill).
time_window: team assignment at the start of the course

description: As in Study 2, measured with 12 items from the scale developed by Lewis (2003) (alpha = .92). Items formed a single score per individual and were then aggregated to the team level using average scores of members per team; intermember agreement (median rwg(j) = .96) and intermember reliability (ICC(1) = .25, ICC(2) = .49) justified aggregation.
time_window: after three weeks of team work

description: Entrepreneurial success was measured using the team profits in USD. Teams sold a minimum viable product (a version of a product aimed at satisfying early customers and providing feedback for future development) for a predefined period.

Measured by the number of overall investments the VC firm made in the five years prior to the round following the filing of the venture lawsuit. The five-year window reflects the VC investment cycle and the authors' expectation that events prior to that window would be less influential on VC decision-making. The variable was mean centered.
time_window: five years prior to the round following the filing of the venture lawsuit

description: A count of the rounds that a particular VC firm invested in a particular venture before the round following the filing of the venture lawsuit. The measure is intended to capture the length of time and repeated interactions between the VC and the focal venture. The variable was mean centered.
time_window: prior to the round following the filing of the venture lawsuit

description: For each VC firm, the authors took the number of the firm's lawsuits in each of the years preceding the venture lawsuit, depreciated that number at a rate of 15% per year, and then summed the depreciated number of lawsuits for the five years prior to the venture lawsuit. The five-year window reflects the VCs' organizational memory. The variable was mean centered.
time_window: five years prior to the venture lawsuit

description: A contrast-coded, dichotomous variable coded as 0.5 if the VC firm had defendant experience within five years of the filing of the venture lawsuit and as -0.5 if it did not.
time_window: within five years of the filing of the venture lawsuit

description: A contrast-coded, dichotomous variable coded as 0.5 if the VC firm settled a lawsuit within five years of the filing of the venture lawsuit and as -0.5 if it did not.
time_window: within five years of the filing of the venture lawsuit

description: A dichotomous variable coded as one if the VC firm invested in the first round following the filing of the first venture lawsuit and zero if the VC firm did not invest in that round.
time_window: first round following the filing of the first venture lawsuit

description: Dummy variable coded 1 if a focal firm i is accused of infringing a patent in therapeutic class j in year t − 5, and 0 otherwise. A rolling window approach (one to eight years) was used to identify the optimal lag, and a five-year lag was identified as yielding the strongest coefficient for the litigation event dummy.

The number of a firm's novel drugs in a given therapeutic class approved by the FDA subsequent to the litigation event; for every firm i the authors count the number of drugs in therapeutic class j in year t. The measure accounts only for novel drugs, that is, drugs using new molecular entities or new combinations of existing molecular entities offering significantly better treatment or much lower side effects.
time_window: subsequent to the litigation event (five-year lag)

description: Applied to all patents in therapeutic class j that are litigated against firm i in year t − 5, using the formula in Heeley and Jacobson (2008): the average age of patents cited by the litigated patent in technology class j in year t is compared with the average age of citations by all patents in technology class j in year t, divided by the standard deviation. Because the firm score is subtracted from the average technology class score, litigated patents using relatively newer technological inputs have more positive scores. Only cited patents whose recency is in the top 10th percentile of all cited patents are included.

An entropy index over the distribution of secondary therapeutic classes in litigated patents, applied to all patents in therapeutic class j litigated against firm i in year t − 5. While a patent is assigned to one primary therapeutic class, it can also have connections to other secondary therapeutic classes, with 13 possible therapeutic classes; the measure takes higher values when more therapeutic classes are associated with litigated patents and lower values when fewer classes are involved.
