The log of the number of claims in the litigated patents for firm i in therapeutic class j and year t − 5. Each claim identifies fundamental and distinct features of the new art, and the number of claims reflects the scope of the patent.

Operationalized as the average industry-adjusted ROA during the first three years following the CEO appointment. For each of the three years following the appointment, the median ROA of firms operating in the firm's primary two-digit SIC was subtracted from the firm's own ROA, and the resulting difference was averaged across these three years.
time_window: first three years following the CEO appointment

description: The accumulated number of months spent in executive positions prior to the CEO appointment in the firm. Tenure in a position counted toward executive experience if the job title indicated a high-level managerial position such as CEO, executive chairman, vice president, executive vice president, senior vice president, managing director, or head of a division, or if the word chief was indicated.
The number of firms in which the CEO had held executive positions prior to the CEO appointment in the firm.

The misfit between the appointing firm's characteristics and the characteristics of the firms in which the CEO had held executive positions, based on the firms' primary industry (four-digit SIC), firm size (number of employees), and firm age at the time the CEO left that firm. Separate indicators of corporate misfit with respect to industry, size, and age were calculated; the formulas for the industry, size, and age misfit indicators are not legible in the text, but each is described as a weighted average of the discrepancy between the CEO's career-history firm and the appointing firm, weighted by the proportion of the CEO's executive career length spent in each firm or industry. Each indicator was normalized to a 0-1 scale and the three misfit indicators were averaged to obtain the measure.
time_window: CEO's career prior to the appointment

description: Measured using textual analysis of media coverage around the announcement of CEO succession. LexisNexis was searched for press items published from three months prior to three months after the announced appointment, considering all press items that simultaneously mentioned the names of the CEO and the appointing firm. A textual analysis algorithm in Python counted instances in which a word from the Harvard IV-4 dictionary of negative words appeared in the press item within a 10-word distance from the name of the CEO, accounting for words appearing both before and after the CEO's name and dropping counts relating to the prior CEO when both were mentioned. The measure divides the total number of negative sentiment words by the number of press items identified for each appointment.
time_window: three months prior to three months after the announced appointment

description: A dummy variable that took a value of 1 if the newly appointed CEO was not employed by the firm prior to the appointment as CEO and a value of 0 otherwise.
Binary variable indicating whether a firm's board chair is a CCP member, coded 1 for yes and 0 for no. Party membership of board chairs was hand-collected from annual reports of listed firms.

The total number of invention, utility, and design patent applications submitted by the firm. SIPO specifies the three patent types: invention patents for new technical solutions related to a product, process, or improvement; utility patents for new technical solutions regarding shape or structure; and design patents for new designs for aesthetic purposes.

Dummy variable coded 1 if the firm experienced a patent infringement lawsuit as the defendant in a given year that resulted in conviction, and 0 otherwise. The database contains all patent infringement litigation documents published by the courts in China; the filing date was used to identify the year of patent infringement, and defendant names were matched with those of the listed companies.
Age was reverse-coded as 100 minus the actual age of a board chair, so a larger value indicates a younger chair.
Categorical variable of the board chair's educational attainment, coded 1 = high school, 2 = community college, 3 = bachelor's degree, 4 = master's degree, and 5 = doctoral degree.

Percentage of older Party-member corporate directors out of the total number of Party-member directors of all listed firms in the province where a focal firm is headquartered. Older Party members are those who reached age 18 before 1978, i.e., born before 1960.

Alliance performance below the aspiration level. A spline function was used to construct the alliance performance above and below the aspiration level. It was measured by the CAR of the focal alliance minus the social aspiration level if the CAR of the focal alliance was below the aspiration level; it equals 0 if the CAR was higher than the aspiration level.
time_window: event window [-1,+1] for the focal alliance; aspiration based on the year prior to the focal alliance

description: Alliance performance above the aspiration level. It was measured by the CAR of the focal alliance minus the aspiration level if the CAR of the focal alliance exceeded the aspiration, while it equals 0 if CAR was lower than the aspiration level. The social aspiration level of a firm is measured by the average of CAR of every alliance made by all other firms in the same industry during the year prior to the focal alliance.
time_window: event window [-1,+1] for the focal alliance; aspiration based on the year prior to the focal alliance

variable_name: change from an alliance to an acquisition
description: The dependent variable is the unobserved hazard rate for a firm that used an alliance at t to change to an acquisition at t+1. The dependent variable equals 1 if the first event that a firm made at t+1 was an acquisition, and 0 otherwise.
Alliance partner number represents the total number of partners that participated in the focal alliance, and was measured accordingly.

Partner alliance experience represents the perceived alliance capabilities of the partners in an alliance and was measured by the average of the total number of alliances that were completed by each partner during a five-year period prior to the focal alliance.
time_window: five years prior to the focal alliance

description: Alliance performance variability represents the degree to which a focal firm's past alliance performances fluctuated, and was measured by the standard deviation of the performance of all the alliances that a firm made during the five-year period prior to the focal alliance.
time_window: five years prior to the focal alliance

description: Fuzzy-set calibrated score based on 13 items measuring the novelty of the business model design, following Zott and Amit's scales. Items were assessed on Likert scales and aggregated; the construct was then calibrated with thresholds at 0.75, 0.50, and 0.25 when the scale was 0-1 or at 4, 3, and 2 when the scale was 1-5.
scale: calibrated fuzzy set 0-1 from 13 Likert-scale items

description: Fuzzy-set calibrated score based on 13 items measuring the novelty of the business model design, following Zott and Amit's scales. Items were assessed on Likert scales and aggregated; the construct was then calibrated with thresholds at 0.75, 0.50, and 0.25 when the scale was 0-1 or at 4, 3, and 2 when the scale was 1-5.
scale: calibrated fuzzy set 0-1 from 13 Likert-scale items

description: Fuzzy-set calibrated score based on 11 items measuring the efficiency of the business model design, following Zott and Amit's scales. Items were assessed on Likert scales and aggregated; calibration thresholds were 0.75, 0.50, and 0.25 for 0-1 scales or 4, 3, and 2 for 1-5 scales.
scale: calibrated fuzzy set 0-1 from 11 Likert-scale items

description: Fuzzy-set calibrated score based on 11 items measuring the efficiency of the business model design, following Zott and Amit's scales. Items were assessed on Likert scales and aggregated; calibration thresholds were 0.75, 0.50, and 0.25 for 0-1 scales or 4, 3, and 2 for 1-5 scales.
scale: calibrated fuzzy set 0-1 from 11 Likert-scale items

description: Fuzzy-set calibrated score based on 11 items measuring lock-in in the business model design, following Zott and Amit's scales. Items were assessed on Likert scales and aggregated; calibration thresholds were 0.75, 0.50, and 0.25 for 0-1 scales or 4, 3, and 2 for 1-5 scales.
scale: calibrated fuzzy set 0-1 from 11 Likert-scale items

description: Fuzzy-set calibrated score based on 11 items measuring lock-in in the business model design, following Zott and Amit's scales. Items were assessed on Likert scales and aggregated; calibration thresholds were 0.75, 0.50, and 0.25 for 0-1 scales or 4, 3, and 2 for 1-5 scales.
scale: calibrated fuzzy set 0-1 from 11 Likert-scale items

description: Fuzzy-set calibrated score based on nine items measuring complementarity in the business model design, following Zott and Amit's scales. Items were assessed on Likert scales and aggregated; calibration thresholds were 0.75, 0.50, and 0.25 for 0-1 scales or 4, 3, and 2 for 1-5 scales.
scale: calibrated fuzzy set 0-1 from nine Likert-scale items

description: Fuzzy-set calibrated score based on nine items measuring complementarity in the business model design, following Zott and Amit's scales. Items were assessed on Likert scales and aggregated; calibration thresholds were 0.75, 0.50, and 0.25 for 0-1 scales or 4, 3, and 2 for 1-5 scales.
scale: calibrated fuzzy set 0-1 from nine Likert-scale items

description: Fuzzy-set calibrated score based on three items measuring differentiation strategy, following Zott and Amit's scales. Items were assessed on Likert scales and aggregated; calibration thresholds were 0.75, 0.50, and 0.25 for 0-1 scales or 4, 3, and 2 for 1-5 scales.
scale: calibrated fuzzy set 0-1 from three Likert-scale items

description: Fuzzy-set calibrated score based on three items measuring differentiation strategy, following Zott and Amit's scales. Items were assessed on Likert scales and aggregated; calibration thresholds were 0.75, 0.50, and 0.25 for 0-1 scales or 4, 3, and 2 for 1-5 scales.
scale: calibrated fuzzy set 0-1 from three Likert-scale items

description: Fuzzy-set calibrated score based on four items measuring low-cost strategy, following Zott and Amit's scales. Items were assessed on Likert scales and aggregated; calibration thresholds were 0.75, 0.50, and 0.25 for 0-1 scales or 4, 3, and 2 for 1-5 scales.
scale: calibrated fuzzy set 0-1 from four Likert-scale items

description: Fuzzy-set calibrated score based on four items measuring low-cost strategy, following Zott and Amit's scales. Items were assessed on Likert scales and aggregated; calibration thresholds were 0.75, 0.50, and 0.25 for 0-1 scales or 4, 3, and 2 for 1-5 scales.
scale: calibrated fuzzy set 0-1 from four Likert-scale items

description: Fuzzy-set calibrated score based on four items measuring the degree of competition, developed by the authors from existing literature. Items were assessed on Likert scales and aggregated; calibration thresholds were 0.75, 0.50, and 0.25 for 0-1 scales or 4, 3, and 2 for 1-5 scales.
scale: calibrated fuzzy set 0-1 from four Likert-scale items

description: Fuzzy-set calibrated score based on four items measuring the degree of competition, developed by the authors from existing literature. Items were assessed on Likert scales and aggregated; calibration thresholds were 0.75, 0.50, and 0.25 for 0-1 scales or 4, 3, and 2 for 1-5 scales.
scale: calibrated fuzzy set 0-1 from four Likert-scale items

description: Firm size calibrated using the number of employees. The crossover point was set at 250, the lower threshold for fully out of the set of large firms at 50, and the threshold for fully in at 1,000.
scale: calibrated fuzzy set 0-1 from number of employees

description: Firm size calibrated using the number of employees. The crossover point was set at 250, the lower threshold for fully out of the set of large firms at 50, and the threshold for fully in at 1,000.
scale: calibrated fuzzy set 0-1 from number of employees

description: Firm performance measured as Tobin's Q, the ratio of a firm's market value to its total assets. For high performance, the crossover point was set at 1, the lower threshold at 0.70, and the upper threshold at 2; for very high performance, the thresholds were 2 for fully out, 3.5 for the crossover, and 5 for fully in.
scale: calibrated fuzzy set 0-1 from Tobin's Q

description: Firm performance measured as Tobin's Q, the ratio of a firm's market value to its total assets. For high performance, the crossover point was set at 1, the lower threshold at 0.70, and the upper threshold at 2; for very high performance, the thresholds were 2 for fully out, 3.5 for the crossover, and 5 for fully in.
scale: calibrated fuzzy set 0-1 from Tobin's Q

description: Operationalized as the number of design elements in a high-performing configuration. The authors define complexity here as the number of elements in the configurations because all design elements interact with each other; it is used to compare small and large firms in mature versus new technological environments.

Operationalized as the number of design elements in a high-performing configuration. The authors define complexity here as the number of elements in the configurations because all design elements interact with each other; it is used to compare small and large firms in mature versus new technological environments.

A count of newly certified B Corps in each state-year. Each B Corp was assigned to its home state and certifications were aggregated by year. The outcome is a nonnegative count and is modeled with firm count as the exposure term.

An indicator that equals 1 in the years when BCL was in effect in a state, and 0 otherwise, coded from public legislative records. It compares initial B Corp certifications in states that have enacted weak sustainability legislation with those in states that have not.

Each state's BCL was coded as either Model-style or Delaware-style. Model-style BCL was drafted by a legal team working with B Lab (n = 28); Delaware-style BCL follows legislation first enacted in Delaware in 2013 and is notably more flexible and less stringent (n = 7). The two variables are mutually exclusive indicators.

Region-level counts of ESG concerns for publicly traded firms from the MSCI ESG KLD STATS, focused on 'concerns' (negative indicators of ESG performance). Each firm was assigned to one of nine U.S. Census divisions based on headquarters location; counts were normalized by year and reversed so that higher scores indicate 'cleaner' corporate sustainability norms.

A continuous measure built from a list of 24 criteria that states have specified in their benefit corporation legislation; legislation is broader in scope when it addresses more of these criteria. Two of the authors manually reviewed and coded each BCL text along each dimension and summed them. Values were assigned to certifications within two years of BCL passage in a state as well as to certification spells that followed BCL enactment.

The firm-level data were transformed into a survival panel in which firms 'survive' until a decertification event or the end of the observation window, whichever comes first; 'certification spells' coinciding with each certification or recertification are used as survival time. Firms must actively recertify to maintain their B Corp status, and the model estimates the hazard of decertification (lower hazard indicating greater recertification).

The same MSCI-based moderator is used at the firm level: the reversed, normalized count of ESG concerns attributable to public companies headquartered within each Census division, where higher scores indicate 'cleaner' corporate sustainability norms.

Indicator variable set to 1 only if the focal business unit experienced any adverse event within the preceding three years (including the focal year) in the focal product market. Product failure is measured using adverse events reported to the FDA; an adverse event involves a malfunction of a medical device due to technical or user errors. The authors use a binary measure because, according to their interviews with managers at medical device firms, it is the first occurrence of an adverse event that triggers internal search efforts. Exits that did not involve a product failure are considered market-related exits and serve as the base category in the analyses.
time_window: preceding three years including the focal year

description: Binary variable set to 1 for the year that a business unit reenters the focal product market, and 0 otherwise. Reentry was determined from the MDR and recorded whenever a business unit offered a product in a market where it did not offer a product in the previous year but did have offerings in prior years.

Composite measure of the proximity of headquarters to the business unit built from hierarchical, geographic, and cognitive proximity, each of which was standardized via z-scores and then added together. Hierarchical proximity is the number of hierarchical layers between the focal business unit and its corporate office, reverse-coded from distance (which varies from 0 to 4) by subtracting it from the sample maximum. Geographic proximity is the natural logarithm of the 'great circle' distance in miles between unit and headquarters, reverse-coded by subtracting it from the sample maximum. Cognitive proximity is built from corporate similar product experience (correlation across shares of products in 19 medical specialty areas) and corporate product failure experience. Higher values indicate greater proximity to the corporate office.

Operationalized as the age of the product market based on the FDA Premarket Notifications and Premarket Approval databases. The FDA classifies medical devices into product categories of similar purposes or functions and assigns each a unique product code. The variable is the time elapsed since the product market was first introduced; for example, replacement heart valves (code DYE) were first introduced in 1983, so the variable takes a value of 10 for this product market in 1993.

Cause of the product failure identified from the FDA Medical Device Reporting database. Coded as technical error-driven if the cause was solely attributable to the medical device itself (i.e., fault in the product) or as user error-driven if it was precipitated by a user error.

Severity measured using the FDA categorization of severity, which distinguishes adverse events according to whether they were associated with a malfunction, serious injury, or death. Coded as severe (value of 1) when the failure was associated with a serious injury or death of a patient, and as nonsevere (0) if it only involved a malfunction.

This variable captures entrepreneurial entry by aggregating all new distilleries founded each year in a given county. Founding and failure dates for all known distilleries come primarily from Hume and Moss (2000), complemented by other whisky industry records.

STL member proportion is measured annually by taking the total membership of the STL in each county. To account for differences in population size across Scottish counties, this figure is divided by the number of inhabitants in a county. The variable was lagged by one year.

A count variable at the county level capturing the SPBTA local elite members, identified from the professions listed in the membership records. At the local level the SPBTA sought to bring in elite members who occupied a position on municipal and administrative councils as well as those in authority in enforcing the observance of the licensing laws.
A count of the number of SPBTA members who were Members of Parliament, capturing the SPBTA's ability to attract support at the level of national politics by recruiting MPs into its ranks.

A count of all distilleries founded between 1680 and 1823 which failed before the relaxation of constraints to obtain distilling licenses came to pass. Larger ancestral populations are expected to locally endow whisky distilling with a higher level of cognitive legitimacy.

SLTDA membership by county, measured as a count of the number of local organizations that were a member of the SLTDA. This organization came into existence in 1879 and represented the interests of the alcohol producing and distributing industries more broadly, including publicans, brewers, distillers, and others in the licensed trade such as grocers.

A count variable tracking the number of Scottish Whisky Associations active in each county. Various associations were established over time, mostly regionally but acting nationally, starting with the Scotch Distillers' Association in 1865 and ending with the Scotch Whisky Association in 1917.

A first-stage ordinary least squares regression at the project well level regresses the firm's drilling rate for the well (total depth of the well divided by the total number of drilling days needed to complete that well) on well type (vertical vs. directional), project size (total depth), contract type (footage, day rate, or turnkey), field demand, and field and year dummies. The residual represents the firm-specific idiosyncratic component of drilling rate associated with the firm's capabilities. The residuals are standardized within each field and year subgroup and then averaged for the firm each year and collapsed to the firm-year level. A positive value indicates the driller was intrinsically faster in drilling than the systematic expected average across projects in a given year.

The proportion of the focal driller's total number of its rigs that are idled, or 'stacked', relative to its total rig fleet in year t. For a driller that has a fleet of 10 rigs in operation and 5 rigs stacked in a given year, the variable takes the value 0.5.
A binary indicator that takes the value '1' if the driller 'stacks' a given rig in month t by suspending its drilling operations and releasing its associated rig crew members, and '0' otherwise.

Monthly measures of U.S. oil demand (millions of bbl) are run through a generalized autoregressive conditional heteroscedasticity (GARCH) model on the time series of demand for the sample period of 2001-2018, controlling for heteroscedasticity in the time series. Demand uncertainty is estimated as the market forecast error, which is the absolute percentage difference between the value of industry output predicted by the regression at period t and the observed level of demand at t. This approximates unique time-varying estimates of demand uncertainty for the industry.

A dummy variable capturing whether the focal rig being considered for idling is the traditional type that is fully human operated, taking the value of '1', as opposed to automated, taking the value of '0'. The different degrees of automation (semi-automated or fully automated) could not be observed in the data, so a dummy was used.

The firm's capabilities in a given period, based on the driller's intrinsic speed capabilities of drilling wells as defined for the capability erosion analysis (residual-based firm-year measure constructed from the project-level drilling-rate regression). It is used as a moderator of the effect of demand uncertainty on the likelihood of idling.

The difference between actual ROA and a firm's aspirations if the firm's ROA was lower than or equal to its aspirations and zero otherwise; constructed as a negative value and the absolute value was then taken for ease of interpretation. ROA is the ratio of net income to total assets in a specific fiscal year. Aspirations are weighted sums of historical aspirations (based on a firm's own performance history) and social aspirations (based on the average ROA of a peer group of five members), with a1 set to 0.70 and a2 set to 0.75 by a grid search.
The ratio of R&D expenditures to sales. Consistent with prior literature, firms in industries where the majority of constituents do not invest substantially in R&D were excluded from the analysis.
time_window: contemporaneous dependent variable, with predictors lagged one year

description: The ratio of a firm's philanthropic expenses to sales, rescaled by multiplying the ratio by 100. Donations are restricted to direct cash or product contributions to nonprofit organizations that operate independently of the firm; expenditures for hospital or school construction in poverty-stricken areas and post-disaster reconstruction by the firm itself were also included, while monetary donations to employees and support for for-profit activities were excluded.
time_window: contemporaneous dependent variable, with predictors lagged one year

description: The number of causal sentences linking R&D and performance in a given MD&A document, with the logarithm taken to avoid skewness. A two-step procedure was used: two trained graduate student coders constructed keywords for '(R&D) causes' (21 keywords) and '(performance) effects' (39 keywords), and a heuristic NLP algorithm then scored each sentence by the ratio of the number of keyword pairs for 'R&D-performance' in the sentence to the total number of words in that sentence, with sentences above a threshold of 0.0689 selected as target sentences.

The number of causal sentences linking CSR and performance in a given MD&A document, with the logarithm taken to avoid skewness. Keywords for '(CSR) causes' (64 keywords) and '(performance) effects' (78 keywords) were constructed by coders, and a heuristic NLP algorithm scored sentences by the ratio of keyword pairs for 'CSR-performance' to total sentence words, with a threshold of 0.069 used to select target sentences.
Three-year rolling correlations between R&D intensity at time t and ROA at time t+1 computed from the firm's own past.

Three-year rolling correlations between R&D intensity at time t and ROA at time t+1 within the firm-specific peer group of five similar firms, selected using the Mahalanobis distance between the focal firm and other firms within each industry-year based on revenues and total assets.
Three-year rolling correlations between CSR ratings at time t and ROA at time t+1 computed from the firm's own past.
Three-year rolling correlations between CSR ratings at time t and ROA at time t+1 within the firm-specific peer group of five similar firms.

The authors used source-verb-target triplets, which identify directionality in each interaction, to calculate the percentage of triplets in which the source is the firm out of the total triplets involving a specific firm-stakeholder pair; this percentage captures the continuum from reactive stances (low) to proactive approaches (high). The dummy variable is coded 1 if the continuous measure is more than half a standard deviation above the mean of this variable, and 0 otherwise, so it captures highly proactive stances in firm-stakeholder dialogue.

variable_name: improvements in a stakeholder's evaluation of a firm
description: Built from the stakeholder-initiated events, on the assumption that a stakeholder's actions toward a firm or statements about it reflect the stakeholder's evaluation of the firm. For multiple events reported on the same date, the verb scores were averaged across all events initiated by the same stakeholder toward the same firm. The dependent variable takes the value 1 if a stakeholder's evaluation of a firm improved from the first to the second observation time and 0 otherwise, where the two observations are the conflict-cooperation scores for that stakeholder and firm.

Measured from the authors' data set of all publicly available English-language media reports about the firms in the sample. It is the count of media reports published about the mine before the date on which a stakeholder's evaluation is measured, divided by the total number of media reports published about that mine over the period for which stakeholder evaluations were observed. The measure ranges from 0 to 1 and accounts for the possibility that the overall number of media reports differs across firms.

Automated thematic content coding scored each of 22,229 articles on 11 distinct themes, including three environmental issues, seven social issues, and one governance issue. The Python tool EMPATH, which leverages deep learning via neural embedding, analyzed the text against lexical categories. The scores across the 11 themes were added to obtain an aggregate measure of media focus on ESG topics in a given article, and when multiple articles were published on the same date the average of the combined ESG score was taken across all articles.

Country-level measure obtained from the V-dem project that captures the level of government censorship of the media. Low values indicate that the government routinely and directly censors the media; high values indicate that government attempts to censor the media are very rare and that, when discovered, are severely punished.

Mean Jensen-Shannon divergence (JSD) between the topic distributions of all unordered pairs of campaigns that ended in a focal category during the 90 days preceding a given day (t-90 to t-1). The value equals 0 when a pair of campaigns is identical and grows toward 1 as campaigns diverge. Topic weights come from a structural topic model with 750 topics estimated on the 'Story' section of campaign narratives.

Mean Jensen-Shannon divergence (JSD) between the topic distributions of all unordered pairs of campaigns, comparing campaigns that ended in a focal category with those that ended in related categories during the 90 days preceding a given day (t-90 to t-1). The JSD equals 0 when the compared campaigns are identical and grows toward 1 as they diverge. Topic weights come from the same structural topic model used for heterogeneity.

Daily number of campaign launches over a 30-day period starting from any given day (t to t+29) in any given category. Only campaigns that received the support of at least five backers are counted; the measure equals 0 when no campaign launched within the 30-day period garnered the support of five backers, and grows with the number of campaigns that did.

variable_name: Gender composition of entrepreneurial units (proportion of women entrepreneurs)
description: Operationalized as the proportion of women entrepreneurs in the entrepreneurial unit. This was applied to ventures led by individuals and by teams. Supplementary analyses used a subsample of single-gender entrepreneurial units.

Measured with one item taken from Amason et al. (2006) and Zott and Amit (2007); raters coded the extent to which each shark commented that the venture was novel. Scores coded by each rater across all sharks evaluating the same venture were aggregated, and the aggregated scores from the pair of raters who rated the same venture were averaged to compute the final score.
scale: 1 = not at all to 5 = to a very large extent

description: A separate panel of raters coded the extent to which each shark questioned whether the venture corresponded with the normative practices of relevant businesses. Ratings of one rater on all sharks were first aggregated and then averaged across the pair of raters who rated the same venture.
scale: 1 = not at all to 5 = to a very large extent

description: A dichotomous measure indicating whether entrepreneurial units received any investment from sharks.
Calculated by dividing the amount of investment by the share of equity that sharks invested. Reported in million USD.

Manipulated through the audio recording of a female or male entrepreneur pitching an otherwise identical venture project, paired with the gender-typed name and the corresponding silhouette gender icon. Recordings were generated with Amazon Polly and differed only in the gender of the speaker; 'Emily' and 'Greg' were the female- and male-typed names.

Manipulated using two ventures selected in pretests: the Hoodie Pillow, an inflatable neck pillow embedded in a hoodie, represented the high-novelty venture, and the Home T, state-themed T-shirts, represented the low-novelty venture. Both were in the apparel manufacturing industry and did not differ in gender type or venture profitability. A three-item manipulation check confirmed the intended effects.
Measured with three items developed for this study from prior research. Funders rated their agreement with each item.

Assessed with three items adapted from Mueller et al. (2018). Funders rated their agreement with each statement, for example that they expect the venture to receive endorsement from other funders on the crowdfunding platform.
Funders rated how likely they would be to fund the venture.
Funders indicated the intended funding amount using a sliding scale with dollar amounts ranging from 0 USD to over 175,000 USD.

Manipulated, as in Study 2A, with a combination of voice, image, and name; additionally, gendered cartoon characters were presented in the pitch animation in the respective gender condition. Facial expressions, body movements, and progression of the videos remained the same between the two gender conditions.

Manipulated using ventures selected in pretests: LIFTiD Neuro, a device worn on the forehead that helps people focus through brain-stimulating currents, and Bridal Buddy, an attachment to wedding gowns that helps brides to use the bathroom, were the high-novelty ventures; Real Investor, an app providing real estate information, and Natural Heal, a first-aid ointment, were the low-novelty ventures. A three-item manipulation check verified the intended effects.

Based on pretest results, Bridal Buddy and Natural Heal were used as female-typed ventures and LIFTiD Neuro and Real Investor as male-typed ventures. Ventures were screened using the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics gender percentage data across industries as a reference for industries with either men or women as dominant workforces.
Measured with the same three items from Study 2A, with the industry name varying by venture.
Measured with the same three items from Study 2A.
Funders rated how likely they would be to fund the venture, the first measure of funding support.

The intended funding amount was indicated on a sliding scale ranging from 0 USD to the asking amount; because asking amounts varied between male- and female-dominant industries, funding proportion (the investment amount divided by the asking amount) was used as the other measure of funding support.

Founders possess general human capital if they have obtained a general education degree and have work experience that does not include industry-specific experience, that is, experience in the domain in which they created their business. The measures combine founder education type (vocational vs. general, chosen in Greece upon completion of lower secondary schooling) with prior work experience. Two dummies, specific human capital and other human capital, are entered in the models; general human capital is the omitted category against which the specific human capital coefficient is read.
time_window: prior to firm creation (education and work experience)

description: Founders possess specific human capital if they have (a) knowledge obtained from vocational education and work experience, both specific to the domain in which their firm was founded, or (b) knowledge obtained from general education and work experience, both specific to the domain in which their firm is founded. Because vocationally trained founders typically obtain work experience through internships during schooling, the measure includes them even without post-schooling related work experience. It is entered as a dummy whose coefficient reflects differences relative to the omitted general human capital category.
time_window: prior to firm creation (education and work experience)

description: The dependent measure is the yearly sales revenues generated by a new firm, built from respondents' reports of the total revenues (in EUR) generated by their firms in a given year. Firms contribute one observation per year of existence, up to a maximum of three years based on the date of firm creation. It is analyzed with OLS on the firm-year panel.
time_window: each year of firm existence, up to three years after founding

description: A dichotomous measure capturing whether the new firm's industry was among the most favorable in terms of demand conditions, based on the number of observations in the sample in the 15 industries observed and taking into account that firms could be founded in 2008 or 2009. The cutoff point was equivalent to one standard deviation above the mean level of industry growth, which coincided with being in roughly the top 10th percentile of industry growth.
level: industry (NACE Rev. 2 letter-level), matched to firm
time_window: year in which the new firm was created (2008 or 2009)

description: A dichotomous measure capturing whether the new firm's industry was among the most unfavorable in terms of demand conditions, based on the number of observations in the sample in the 15 industries observed and taking into account that firms could be founded in 2008 or 2009. The cutoff point was equivalent to one standard deviation below the mean level of industry decline, which coincided with being in roughly the bottom 10th percentile in industry decline.
level: industry (NACE Rev. 2 letter-level), matched to firm
time_window: year in which the new firm was created (2008 or 2009)

description: Average dissimilarity of all possible combinations of ideas in each crowd at each period. Dissimilarity between ideas i and j is one minus the cosine similarity of their vectorized texts and is normalized into the range [0, 1]. The variable is log-transformed.
Average cosine similarity of all possible pairs of selected ideas in each crowd at each period. A lagged variable is used for selection consistency to account for reverse causality.

Proportion of newcomers for each crowd-period observation. A newcomer is an external contributor who first contributed to a crowd at a given period. When all contributors are newcomers (returnees), Churn Newcomer is set to 1 (0).

Departures of established contributors whose last submissions were made during that period, divided by the number of active established contributors in that period. Established contributors are contributors who submitted at least one idea before that period.

Network density of a contributor-commenter network (who comments on whom) for each period. Density is measured as 2m/(n(n-1)), where n is the number of users and m is the number of contributor-commenter ties. The variable is log-transformed and lagged due to reverse causality.

Whether a contributor contributes again. The self-selection analysis uses pooled ordinary least squares regression while keeping crowd fixed effects and limits focus to the subsample of unselected contributors.

Dissimilarity between a focal idea and its closest selected idea. For the self-selection analysis, it is the distance from organizational selection for unselected contributors. For the self-adjustment analysis, the dependent variable is the dissimilarity between the submitted idea and its closest selection in the previous period.
Number of submissions made by a contributor. The variable is log-transformed in the self-adjustment analysis.

Categorical variable coded 1 for private–private collaboration, where both partners are for-profit businesses, and coded 2 for public–private collaboration, where one partner is a for-profit business and the other is an organization with a public mission. The baseline is solo development, coded 0. In the case of multipartner collaboration, mixed partner types are coded as a public–private collaboration.

Coded 1 if the drug moved from a given phase to the next (e.g., from discovery to preclinical, or from phase 1 to phase 2 clinical) for the respective indication, and coded 0 for drugs that are either under development at the end of the observation period, or withdrawn, suspended, or discontinued without progressing to the next stage.
time_window: from the focal stage to the next stage of development

description: Measured by the number of days it takes for a drug to proceed from one development stage to the next, with time treated as the valuable resource allocated for drug development.
time_window: from the focal stage to the next stage of development

description: Categorical variable for discovery, preclinical, and clinical phases 1, 2, and 3, coded from 0 to 4 respectively, included as fixed effects in all models. The authors also use the distinction between early (including discovery and preclinical stages) and clinical-stage (including clinical phase 1, 2, and 3) development to create two subsamples, on the basis of field experts' report that the highest uncertainty is experienced in the discovery and preclinical stages.

Measured by counting the number of times the same target mechanism of action has been explored for antimicrobial development by any organization in the industry before the start of the focal drug-development task; a lower count indicates higher levels of technology novelty, and vice versa. The sample is divided into two subsamples by the median, the group below the median being labelled the 'new mechanism' subsample and the one above the median 'existing mechanism'.
time_window: before the start of the focal drug-development task

description: Community-specific cumulative number of provisional spaces from 1896 to a given year, counting all provisional spaces, whether highbrow or lowbrow. Coded as the number of new provisional spaces in community i in year t plus the prior cumulative number depreciated by 25% per year so that recent values weigh more heavily than past ones. The measure is lagged by one year.
time_window: cumulative from 1896 to year t, lagged one year

variable_name: cumulative number of highbrow provisional spaces
description: Community-specific cumulative number of highbrow provisional spaces from 1896 to a given year, discounted by 25% per year and lagged one year. Venues coded highbrow include all legitimate theaters, concert halls, symphony orchestra halls, resort centers, and playhouses, as well as opera houses that showed opera and high-class vaudeville theaters. Coding of cultural status used the type of a venue's shows as the main criterion, complemented with advertised ticket price, architectural value, and operating philosophy.
time_window: cumulative from 1896 to year t, lagged one year

variable_name: cumulative number of lowbrow provisional spaces
description: Community-specific cumulative number of lowbrow provisional spaces from 1896 to a given year, discounted by 25% per year and lagged one year. Venues coded lowbrow include all airdomes, burlesque houses, penny arcades, storefronts, dime museums, and dance halls, as well as community-gathering 'opera houses' and tawdry vaudeville theaters.
time_window: cumulative from 1896 to year t, lagged one year

variable_name: founding rate of the first movie theater of any kind
description: Instantaneous rate at which a community experiences the founding of its first movie theater of any form since 1896, estimated in continuous time with the community as the unit at risk. Communities that had not experienced any movie theater founding by 1927 are treated as censored.

variable_name: founding rate of the first movie house or palace
description: Instantaneous rate at which a community experiences the founding of its first highbrow movie theater, combining the first founding of a movie house or a movie palace. Movie palaces and movie houses are combined because there were few movie palaces and both forms were more highbrow than nickelodeons.

variable_name: founding rate of the first nickelodeon
description: Instantaneous rate at which a community experiences the founding of its first lowbrow movie theater, the nickelodeon. Nickelodeons are movie theaters whose admission prices were only a nickel.

A dummy variable set to 1 if a VC firm is affiliated with at least one network community in a given period and 0 otherwise. Communities are detected with the clique percolation method (clique size k = 4) on one-mode VC-to-VC syndication projections built from trailing n-year windows (n = 1 and n = 3). With n = 1, the average of Insider is 0.313.

A continuous variable that measures the total number of network communities with which a VC firm is affiliated in the given period, based on community detection via the clique percolation method. With n = 1 it ranges from 0 to 22; because affiliations for 99% of observations fall between 0 and 4, the variable is winsorized at the 99th percentile, and the same procedure is used for n = 3.

The proportion of a VC firm's portfolio companies that exit via IPOs or M&A transactions. VC firms usually make profits via these exits, and the ratio of successful exits serves as an appropriate measure of VC firm performance; the average exit rate in the data is 0.37. An alternative operationalization using IPO rate is reported in additional analyses.
time_window: exits tracked until the end of 2018

description: The marketization index, constructed annually by the National Economic Research Institute, measures the development of local institutions where the VC firms are headquartered. For each of the 31 provincial-level administrative divisions it contains a general index of marketization progress, five major categories (subindices), and dozens of basic indices; the general index and subindices are computed as the weighted average of the basic indices using principal component analysis, and the general index is used to measure institutional development. The general index typically ranges from 0 to 10 but in some years can go below 0 or above 10.

The Euclidean distance between the predecessor's and successor's experiential attributes (eight categories in total), including functional background (marketing, finance, law, and other), military experience, international experience, outside board experience, and whether the CEO is the founder of the firm. Both CEOs were coded on each metric as a binary variable, coded 1 if the CEO had experience in the area and 0 otherwise. The successor's value was subtracted from the predecessor's and the resulting differences were squared, summed, and square-rooted. A higher value represents a greater difference between predecessor and successor with respect to their professional experience.
A binary variable coded as 1 if the new CEO worked in the firm for at least two years before being promoted to that role and 0 otherwise.
A binary variable coded as 1 if the outgoing CEO remained on the board as the chair for any period of time in the year following the succession and 0 if not.

The total number of competitive attacks in the post-succession year in which the focal firm was the intended target, so the variable is a count of attacks in the year after the succession event to ensure temporality. A competitive attack is only coded as such if the focal action can be classified into one of the eight types of competitive actions established in prior studies (mergers and acquisitions, strategic alliances, new market entries, new facilities, product launches, pricing adjustments, legal proceedings, and marketing activities). RavenPack's coding of co-mentions between firms was used to identify the intended target and the attacking firm, and article content was manually reviewed.

Polarity score from sentiment analysis of textual documents about the deal, retrieved using the acquirer's firm name, the target entity name, and the main figures and event process in the SDC synopsis field. Documents were identified within three months before the deal announcement up to the last day of the month in which the deal was announced, extended two days after announcement for deals announced at the end of a month. A lexicon approach was used, with the Loughran-McDonald Master Dictionary merged with SentiWordNet, Stanford CoreNLP, and customized Java codes. Sentiment values were decomposed by 20% so that more recent periods received higher weights, and the weighted document polarities were aggregated for each deal.
time_window: three months before announcement to the last day of the announcement month (plus two days for end-of-month announcements)

description: Polarity score from sentiment analysis of documents about the acquiring firm retrieved over a three-year window, following prior studies on public perception toward firms because opinions or perceptions about a company are usually formed over a longer period of time. Sentiment toward the acquirer was calculated at a monthly interval using the machine learning approach with Stanford CoreNLP's pre-trained model trained with the Recursive Neural Tensor Network on the Stanford Sentiment Treebank.
time_window: three years, measured at monthly intervals

variable_name: host country sentiments toward inward investments from China
description: Polarity score from sentiment analysis of documents about inward investments from China, using the same three-month time frame as sentiments toward the deal and the same weekly intervals, with the machine learning approach and Stanford CoreNLP's pre-trained model.
time_window: three months, measured at weekly intervals

description: Measured as the standard deviation of differences in the average sentiment values between adjoining weeks, capturing the temporal changes of sentiments toward the deal at a weekly level for a three-month duration; a larger value reflects greater volatility.
Measured as the standard deviation of differences in average sentiment values between adjoining months for a three-year period.

variable_name: sentiment volatility toward inward investments from China
description: Measured as the standard deviation of differences in average sentiment values between adjoining weeks for a three-month duration.

Wave peaks were first identified for each acquisition deal, each peak meeting the requirement that the sentiment value in the focal time t is larger than the sentiment values in both time t-1 and t+1. Sentiment wavelength was then calculated as the mean value of the time distances between adjoining peaks.
The same peak-identification and mean-distance-between-adjoining-peaks approach applied to the sentiment series for the acquirer.

variable_name: sentiment wavelength toward inward investments from China
description: The same peak-identification and mean-distance-between-adjoining-peaks approach applied to the sentiment series for inward investments from China.

variable_name: sentiment augmentation between acquirer and deal
description: Operationalized using cross-lag correlation, measured as the cross-lag correlation of sentiments toward the acquirer in the closest period prior to t and sentiments toward the deal in time t, with the lag k set to 1.

variable_name: sentiment augmentation between inward investments from China and deal
description: Operationalized using cross-lag correlation, measured as the cross-lag correlation of sentiments toward inward investments from China in the closest period prior to t and sentiments toward the deal in time t, with the lag k set to 1.
Following past studies, a completed acquisition deal is coded as '1,' and '0' otherwise. In the final sample, 66.4% of the deals are completed.

Complexity of a serious accident was measured with an entropy-based index built on the heterogeneity of accident causes, following Haunschild and Sullivan (2002), where the 21 different categories of accident causes are the sections of MSHA regulations relevant to the accident. The index was calculated for each serious accident and averaged for a firm-year when a firm experienced more than one serious accident in a year. To estimate the effect of complexity on the rate of depreciation, an indicator variable, 'high complexity,' took a value of 1 for each past year in which complexity was above its median and 0 when below, calculated separately for each prior year between year t-1 and year t-5.
scale: complexity scores ranged from 0 to 2.74; the indicator is 0 or 1

description: MSHA inspectors rate the degree to which negligence on the part of the firm operating the mine contributed to an accident, on a 5-point scale from 1 (no negligence) to 5 (reckless). The culpability rating is the average negligence score assigned to serious accidents occurring at a firm's mines during a given past year; it ranged from 1 to 5. An indicator variable, 'high culpability,' took a value of 1 for each past year in which culpability was above its median and 0 when below, calculated separately for each prior year between year t-1 and year t-5.
scale: 5-point negligence scale (1 = no negligence to 5 = reckless); the indicator is 0 or 1

description: Mines in the sample fell into two broad types, underground mines and surface mines, and some firms operated both types. The routine relatedness variable was a simple indicator that took a value of 1 when an accident had occurred in a mine of the same type as the majority of the mines operated by the firm and 0 when it did not. The indicator 'high routine relatedness' took a value of 1 for each past year in which accidents occurred that were related to the firm's core routines and 0 for years in which no such accident occurred, separately for each prior year t-1 through t-5.

The depreciation parameter indicates the fraction of organizational knowledge gained from past experience that is retained from one time period to the next and may range from 0 to 1, where 1 indicates that knowledge does not depreciate at all and 0 represents no retention. Experience from a past year is multiplied by the depreciation parameter raised to the power of the age of that experience, and the parameter is estimated within the primary models using fixed effect maximum likelihood nonlinear regression rather than by an external grid search, so that separate depreciation parameters (with standard errors) can be estimated for different types of experience.

Safety performance was tracked using a count of the number of employee days that a firm's employees missed work due to mining injuries during a year, as MSHA requires mines to report. Because some injuries result in death or permanent disability, MSHA assigns lost days to each such injury according to severity: a fatal injury is assigned 6,000 lost work days and a permanent injury between 5 and 4,500 lost work days. Summing the actual lost work days with these assigned lost work days gives the overall index of mine safety performance, which is logged prior to inclusion in the analysis.

Counts of a firm's prior experience with serious accidents (accidents resulting in at least one fatality or permanent disability), constructed by counting the number of fatalities and permanent disabilities that resulted from all accidents at a firm's mines during a given year, so that each fatality or permanent disability is treated as a separate unit of accident experience. Counts were created for each prior year from year t-1 through year t-5 and are referred to as 'all accident experience.'

The weighted average of the CVC firm's QS industry holdings. For each QS j, the industry holding percentage in each CVC venture's industry i is the shareholder's value-weighted relative holding percentage in the industry each year. Total QS holdings are then computed using the weighted average of the firm's QS industry holdings, where the weight is the percentage of QS j's shares relative to total shares outstanding.

A CVC firm's funding in a venture was coded as terminated if the firm did not invest in any subsequent rounds. If a firm funded a venture until an exit event (e.g., initial public offering or acquisition) or a failure (e.g., bankruptcy or not receiving funding from any investor for multiple years), it was not a termination. The sample was limited to CVC ventures that received initial funding between 2000 and 2014 so that five years of subsequent funding could be examined up to 2019.
time_window: five years of subsequent funding, with initial funding between 2000 and 2014 and follow-up up to 2019

description: Each QS's industry investment concentration was calculated using a Herfindahl-Hirschman index based on its holding percentages in all the industries; the measure is normalized to account for the overall size of the QS. QSs were classified as high concentration or low concentration based on the median value of industry concentration of all QSs. Concentrated QS industry holdings and dispersed QS industry holdings were each calculated as weighted sums and then orthonormalized using the modified Gram-Schmidt procedure.

Market heat reflects the market conditions for each industry in which a CVC-funded venture competes. It is measured as the number of successful exit events (i.e., IPOs or acquisitions) within the venture's industry in the prior year, using its natural logarithm to address skewness.

Industry-specific knowledge is operationalized using supply-chain industry experience: the number of a CVC firm's customers and suppliers in the industry where a venture competes divided by the number of the CVC firm's total customers and suppliers in industries where they do not yet compete but do have CVC funding. It does not include customers and suppliers in industries where the firm already competes or in industries where the firm does not have CVC funding.

variable_name: Vigilance of CEO Attention to Exploration
description: The frequency of exploration-related keywords is counted in the CEO presentation section of each quarterly earnings call and divided by the sum of the frequencies of exploration and exploitation keywords, giving the quarter-level amount of CEO attention to exploration. The standard deviation of the four quarter-level amounts within a year is calculated to capture the vigilance of CEO attention at the firm-year level, so that high standard deviations indicate fluctuating attention and low standard deviations suggest attentional stability; the standard deviation score is then reversed so that a high value indicates a high level of vigilance.

variable_name: number of explorative (brand new) product introductions
description: The annual number of brand new software products with no prior versions introduced by a focal firm, which signify exploration by tapping into new knowledge and targeting new customers. Products are identified from press release and industry publication articles about product launches, and extended versions of existing products are treated as exploitation rather than exploration. The variable is a count measure.

A spline function of the discrepancy between the return on assets (ROA) and aspiration levels, created as two variables: ROA - Aspiration Level > 0 and ROA - Aspiration Level < 0. The historical aspiration level is measured as the firm's ROA in the previous year and the social aspiration level as the average ROA of other firms in the same industry; the weights of the two aspiration levels are estimated (0.3 for the historical and 0.7 for the social aspiration level). The negative discrepancy variable, which indicates firms with financial performance below aspiration levels, is the moderator.

The average of satisfaction ratings (on a 5-point scale) posted on Glassdoor at the firm-year level, restricted to reviews written by employees in explorative (R&D) units. R&D employees are identified first by self-reported R&D job functions and, for reviews without a reported job function, by a textual analysis that classifies reviews containing at least one exploration keyword as R&D-specific.

A content-analytic measure built from CEO speech in earnings call transcripts. The percentage of words utilized by each CEO in each earnings call representative of each underlying component was calculated; these percentages were then averaged by call year and the subcomponent yearly averages were summed to obtain a yearly measure of CEO paranoia. The word lists for the six components were developed deductively from a thesaurus and WordNet and validated by raters.

Following prior research, the authors standardize and sum both the number of agencies and pieces of legislation a firm targeted with lobbying expenditures. This provides an indication of the amount of unique governmental entities targeted for lobbying influence and thus information provision. The variable is left-censored since not all firms engage in lobbying activity.

Measured using RavenPack as the count of the number of competitive actions taken by a firm in a year, using eight major types of competitive actions identified by prior research. Fewer actions indicate more avoidance and more actions indicate engaging with external entities with aggressive actions.
Captures the result and severity of a regulatory process exacted on a firm using the penalty amount, in millions of U.S. dollars, for assessed rulings; values are from goodjobsfirst.org.
Captures the number of competitive actions in RavenPack with the caveat that the focal CEO or firm is the target of the action rather than the initiator of the action.

Video content from all 68 board meetings was converted into 145,370 individual static images and run through Microsoft Azure Computer Vision REST Application Program Interface (Face API), which outputs weights ranging from 0 to 1.0 for eight emotions for every static image. The measure of anger was derived from the intensity of the facial expressions of anger. Each board member-agenda item contains a set of images; for each set the maximum score of displayed anger was taken.

Static facial images from the board meeting videos were processed by the Face API, which outputs intensity weights from 0 to 1.0 for eight emotions, including happiness. The measure was derived from the intensity of the facial expressions of happiness, and for each board member-agenda item set of images the maximum happiness score was taken.
Captured by summing the total frames of speaking TMT and board members per agenda item.
A dummy variable, per director-agenda item, that indicates when, in response to the director's statement, the top manager responds with a promise or commitment to alter the original proposal.
A dummy variable indicating that the director's change initiative received majority support.

Degree of CEO abusive behaviors measured with the five-item measure developed by Mitchell and Ambrose (2007), as rated by CMOs. Example items are 'My leader tells me my thoughts or feelings are stupid' and 'My leader makes negative comments about me to others.' All scales were assessed using 5-point Likert scales (1 = strongly disagree, 5 = strongly agree) unless otherwise noted. Cronbach's alpha was .95.

The same five-item measure as in Study 1, rated by TMT members at Time 1 and aggregated at the team level; interrater agreement (mean rwg(j) = .96; ICC[2] = .56) justified the aggregation of TMT member ratings. A 7-point Likert scale (1 = strongly disagree, 7 = strongly agree) was used. Cronbach's alpha was .97.
level: team (TMT ratings aggregated to the firm)

description: Assessed by CEOs using Simsek et al.'s (2005) 9-item measure. Sample items include 'The TMT members are willing to help each other with complex jobs and meeting deadlines' and 'The TMT members let each other know when their actions affect another team member's work.' Answers used a 5-point Likert scale. Cronbach's alpha was .91.

The same 9-item measure as in Study 1, assessed by TMT members at Time 2 and aggregated at the team level; interrater agreement (mean rwg(j) = .98; ICC[2] = .75) justified aggregation. A 7-point Likert scale was used. Cronbach's alpha was .96.
level: team (TMT ratings aggregated to the firm)

description: Measured using Homburg et al.'s (2013) 4-item measure, based on the version created by Carroll (1991), with ratings provided by the COOs to reduce single-source and CEOs' subjective self-assessment biases. Sample items are 'Our company gives back to the communities in which it does business' and 'Our company integrates charitable contributions into its business activities.' Answers used a 5-point Likert scale. Cronbach's alpha was .88.
The same 4-item measure as in Study 1, obtained from CEOs at Time 1. A 7-point Likert scale was used. Cronbach's alpha was .96.

variable_name: Percentage of sales generated from new products (PSGNP)
description: The percentage of sales generated from new products in the survey year. The percentage of sales from new products introduced was calculated as sales from new products introduced divided by total sales. These objective indicators were obtained from the collaborating agency one year after the survey data collection.
time_window: One year after the survey data collection

variable_name: Percentage of sales generated from new products
description: Consistent with Study 1, organizational innovation was measured using the percentage of sales generated from new products, reported by CEOs in the Time 3 follow-up survey over the past six months.
time_window: Past six months (Time 3, approximately six months after Time 1)

variable_name: ROA adjusted by the industry average
description: Organizational performance was assessed by the percentage of ROA of the survey year, which was adjusted by the industry average. ROA was operationalized by dividing net income by total assets over the year. These data were obtained from the collaborating agency one year after the survey data collection.
time_window: One year after the survey data collection

description: Consistent with Study 1, ROA was used to measure organizational performance. ROA was operationalized by dividing net income by total assets over the past six months, reported by CEOs in the Time 3 follow-up survey.
time_window: Past six months (Time 3, approximately six months after Time 1)

description: The KLD database provides binary scores for different dimensions of CSR strengths and concerns; CSR is operationalized as the sum of the standardized strength scores on five dimensions: community, diversity, employee relations, environment, and product. Because the partners in the dyads are indistinguishable, the measure is operationalized at the dyadic level by summing both partners' CSR scores, and is labeled partners' CSR.

CSI is operationalized as the sum of the standardized concern scores on the same five KLD dimensions used for CSR. Because the partners in the dyads are indistinguishable, a dyad-level CSI measure, labeled partners' CSI, is constructed by summing both partners' CSI scores.

A dichotomous variable that takes the value of '1' if an alliance is realized in a given year, and '0' otherwise. The authors focus on contractual alliances and equity joint ventures, which involve substantive information asymmetry and interactions between partners, and exclude unilateral alliances such as simple cash-for-technology licensing deals.
A dichotomous variable that is coded as '1' if the headquarters of the two firms are located in the same core-based statistical area (CBSA), and '0' otherwise.

Media coverage is measured by counting the number of unique articles in which a firm is mentioned in a given year, searched in the Factiva database for articles published in major news outlets (e.g., Financial Times, New York Times, USA Today, Washington Post, Wall Street Journal, Forbes, Fortune). A dyad-level measure of partners' media coverage is created by summing the media coverage of two firms and dividing it by 100 for ease of interpretation.

Common institutional ownership among a target firm's industry rivals and MSCI. The authors retained investors owning more than 1% of outstanding shares in each firm. For each firm j's rival-MSCI pairs, they calculated the total ownership held by common owners in the rival and in MSCI and computed the product; they then averaged the product measure among all rivals.

MSCI divides industry-adjusted scores (0-10) into seven equal parts corresponding to letter grades AAA to CCC. The authors assigned integer scores of 6 to 0 from AAA to CCC and measured MSCI ESG rating as the average integer score in a year.

The average value of ESG media controversies among rivals with common institutional ownership with MSCI. For each firm-date observation, RepRisk reports raw incident counts for each issue and scores each incident's severity and reach as high, medium, or low, scored 3, 2, and 1. The authors measured ESG media controversies as the natural logarithm of 1 plus the number of ESG risk incidents weighted by severity and reach in each firm-year.

The natural logarithm of 1 plus the number of ESG risk incidents weighted by severity and reach in each firm-year for the target firm. RepRisk reports raw incident counts for each issue and scores each incident's severity and reach as high, medium, or low, scored 3, 2, and 1.

The percentage of rivals with common ownership with MSCI that received at least one ESG award in a year. ASSET4 reports whether a firm received an external award for its social, ethical, community, or environmental activities in a year.

Equals 1 if a target firm received at least one ESG award in a year, and 0 otherwise. ASSET4 reports whether a firm received an external award for its social, ethical, community, or environmental activities in a year.

Counts the number of Board Game Geek users who indicate ownership of a board game, two years after the board game's release. Users on Board Game Geek can indicate which board games they own and these indications are time-stamped. The natural logarithm of the count is taken to account for skewness; the variance of owners is used to test the baseline hypothesis.

Dummy variable that takes the value of 1 if a board game has any collectible components (i.e., it is a CNG) and 0 otherwise. Within the subsample of 225 CNGs, most board games include trading cards (199), while the other 26 come with either miniatures (19) or collectible dice (7).

Each board game is assigned a value of 1 or 0 per gameplay mechanic depending on whether it lists that mechanic, and these 182 binary codes are concatenated into a single vector. The market average vector for each game is computed from all board games released five years prior that share at least one genre with the focal game. Novelty is the cosine distance between the game's gameplay vector and the board-game-specific market average, so a higher value corresponds with a more novel product design.

Takes the value of 1 when a board game was funded via a successful Kickstarter campaign and 0 otherwise. A project is successfully funded only if it reaches its funding goal within the time set for the campaign. Kickstarter allows designers to showcase their board games before release and lets fans support their development by providing feedback and pledging funds.

Counts the number of board games released within the same genre as the focal game from three months before to three months after its release, divided by the count of genres in case it competes in more than one genre. It thus captures the mean competition a board game faces across its genres within a six-month rolling window of its launch.

Dummy variable that takes the value of 1 when a board game competes against a game with an ownership share of 15% or more (calculated excluding the focal game) released within the same six-month rolling window used for competition intensity, and 0 otherwise. All board games released in the same period are considered rather than restricting the measure at the genre level.

Products are classified into three fashionability categories: basic, new-basic or semi-trendy, and trendy. Basic products are steady sellers with minor modifications, while trendy products are new designs aimed at revitalizing the brand's image; in the regressions, Basic is the omitted control case and Semi-Trendy and Trendy are indicator variables.

Realized sales performance is used as an ex post proxy of failure risk. Miss is a binary variable equal to one if a product sold less than 75% of the produced quantities; the percentage sold is the continuous percentage of total products sold.

Binary variable set to one if a product was produced via contract manufacturing, and zero if it was produced through CMT, the make alternative. The buy vs. make decision occurs shortly after the design team approves individual designs.
Binary variable set to one if the average percentage of products sold for the category during the sample period is above 80%, representing approximately 10% of each brand's overall product portfolio.
Binary variable set to one for pants and shorts. Bottoms are treated as less critical to a brand's image than tops; for men's brands bottoms tend to be more important than for women's brands.

Recorded as the number of all enforcements taken against the company in Good Jobs First's Violations Tracker database, which collects information from over 400 federal, state, and local regulatory agencies and includes only resolved cases and settlements that resulted in a monetary penalty of $5,000 or more; the seven recorded types relate to competition, consumer protection, employment, environment, financial reporting, government contracting, and workplace health and safety. Firms in the Violations Tracker were matched to Fortune 500 firms with a Jaro-Winkler algorithm at a score of 0.90 or greater. Because violations and penalties are observed only at the time of enforcement and not necessarily at the time of misconduct, the analyses model a one-year and a three-year lag on corporate misconduct.

Derived as the squared term of the CEO political ideology index, thereby capturing the deviation from political moderates, because identification with political and ideological groups strengthens as one moves in either direction along the political spectrum. To simplify calculation of the squared index score, 0.5 was deducted from all ideology scores, so that political moderatism equals 0, conservative-leaning CEOs score on the negative ideology axis, and liberal-leaning CEOs score on the positive axis.

The Chin et al. (2013) multi-item index of political ideology, computed from political donations, which takes a simple average of four ratios to place a CEO on the political spectrum, with scores ranging from 0 to 1; a score closer to 0 indicates a highly conservative CEO, while a score closer to 1 indicates a highly liberal CEO. The authors observe a Cronbach's alpha of .94, find the data to be normally distributed, and find the within-CEO political ideology score to be highly stable across all years. It is controlled in all models for the underlying CEO political ideology.

Measured through the CEOs' use of first-person singular pronouns (i.e., I, me, my, mine, and myself) in the Q&A portions of quarterly earnings call transcripts, applying an inverse document frequency analysis that discounts commonly used words. To ease interpretation, the measure was reversed by multiplying it by -1, so that high values indicate higher perspective taking.
time_window: four quarterly earnings calls aggregated each year, cumulative moving sample

description: Captured by an inverse document frequency analysis of the moral foundations dictionary created by Graham et al. (2009), composed of 41 terms including noble, ideal, commendable, and righteous, applied to the CEO speeches in the Q&A portions of quarterly earnings calls. These words are associated with moral concepts such as sanctity, loyalty, and authority, which are important to those with a strong sense of morality.
time_window: four quarterly earnings calls aggregated each year, cumulative moving sample

description: The natural logarithm (after adding 1) of the venture's number of patents, gathered from Orbis IP. The measure is mean-centered to facilitate interpretation of regression coefficients, so a venture at the sample mean of patent stock has a value of zero.

Ventures' self-descriptions (collected by Beauhurst from their websites) were analyzed with a latent Dirichlet allocation topic model with 60 topics, producing a 60-dimensional vector per narrative. For each five-digit SIC industry, a vector of mean topic probabilities across all ventures in that industry (including those excluded from the regression sample) was computed to infer the prototypical narrative. Narrative distinctiveness is the sum of absolute distances between the topics in the given narrative and the prototypical narrative in its industry, multiplied by 100 to ease coefficient comparison.

The collective amount of equity fundings (in pounds sterling) that UK ventures in a given industry had collectively raised between 2017 and 2021, i.e. in the previous five years, identified from all equity funding rounds of UK ventures including those not in the regression sample. The natural logarithm (after adding 1) is applied to mitigate skewness and the measure is mean-centered.

An inverse Herfindahl index relating to the diversity of technological patent classes (International Patent Classification codes) of the forward citations of the venture's patents. Following Argyres and Silverman (2004), a correction procedure is applied to adjust for differences in the number of citations, and the measure is set to zero if a venture has fewer than three forward citations. The measure is mean-centered.

The total number of live patents across all UK-based companies (not only new entrepreneurial ventures) in a given industry, created by merging Orbis IP (all patents held by UK-based companies) with Companies House data (industry of each patent-holding company). The measure is log-transformed (natural logarithm after adding 1) and mean-centered.

Modeled in RSiena through a geometrically weighted dyad-wise shared partner ('GWDSP') term. The term captures the prior period's effect of shared third-party network connections on the likelihood of tie formation between two given network actors, using a geometrically decaying multiplier for each additional shared partner.

Modeled with a mixed 'WW5.X closure' term in RSiena. It is similar to a triadic closure term in a univariate network, but involves the presence of multiplex ties in the alternate technology network (e.g., two firms having small-molecule technology alliances with a common third party and subsequently forming a direct alliance in mAbs).

Tested in RSiena using a 'jumpWWClosure' model term based on mAbs patent expertise. The term examines the tendency for mAbs alliance ties to form when the focal actor does not have prior emergent technology experience in terms of patented inventions in mAbs technology, the alter firm does have such expertise exhibited through prior mAbs technology patents, and the two firms are indirectly connected through an intermediary with which they share prior alliance ties in the incumbent (small molecule) technology. The mAbs patent expertise measure is based on the patents using the primary CPC codes associated with mAbs technology.

variable_name: Tie formation in the emergent technology network (mAbs)
description: The emergent technology network was constructed using interorganizational ties from cancer therapy alliances based on mAbs, isolated as those deals in which 'monoclonals' appears in the 'technologies' field of the database. Ties are directional and point from the client firm seeking technology to the R&D firm providing it. The dependent variable is modeled as tie formation in the mAbs network, with alliance ties considered dissolved after three years.
