Differences between actual and expected earnings per share, using a formula adapted from Brown and Rozeff; expected rather than actual EPS was used in the denominator because the authors were interested in actual results in relation to predictions. A positive value denotes performance greater than analysts' predictions, a negative value represents performance less than predictions, and zero denotes performance identical to predictions. The estimate made six months prior to the earnings announcement was used. To prevent outliers from driving the results, all values beyond positive and negative 300 percent were truncated.
scale: percentage difference from expectations, truncated at plus/minus 300 percent
time_window: 1982, with a one-year lag constructed from 1981 data

description: Indicates the incidence of turnover of CEOs in 1983, coded 0 if no turnover occurred and 1 if turnover occurred. Turnover was inferred from the Forbes report of a CEO having one year of tenure in 1984, checked against the prior year's issue of Forbes for the name of the CEO, and proxy statements filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission were used to fill in missing turnover data.

Cumulative abnormal returns were calculated for the 250 trading days in 1982, following a procedure similar to Reinganum (1985); abnormal returns are the actual return minus the normal or predicted return from a market model estimated prior to corporate year end. Abnormal security returns are typically not adjusted for industry. A positive abnormal return reflects performance that exceeds the market's expectations, and a negative abnormal return reflects performance that fails to meet expectations.
time_window: 250 trading days in 1982, with a one-year lag using 1981 data

description: One of four accounting ratios used as a surrogate for selectively determined accounting-based bonus plans, obtained from Compustat. Most recent performance was calculated as the change in the ratio from 1981 to 1982 compared with the industry; a five-year average was calculated from 1978 to 1982. For each ratio the firm's performance was evaluated relative to its industry counterparts, grouped by 2-digit SIC code. Each ratio was entered into the equations separately to compare with previous studies.

One of four accounting ratios used as a surrogate for selectively determined accounting-based bonus plans, obtained from Compustat. Most recent performance was calculated as the change in the ratio from 1981 to 1982 compared with the industry; a five-year average was calculated from 1978 to 1982. For each ratio the firm's performance was evaluated relative to its industry counterparts, grouped by 2-digit SIC code. Each ratio was entered into the equations separately to compare with previous studies.

One of four accounting ratios used as a surrogate for selectively determined accounting-based bonus plans, obtained from Compustat. Most recent performance was calculated as the change in the ratio from 1981 to 1982 compared with the industry; a five-year average was calculated from 1978 to 1982. For each ratio the firm's performance was evaluated relative to its industry counterparts, grouped by 2-digit SIC code. Each ratio was entered into the equations separately to compare with previous studies.

The mechanical accounting measure of earnings per share, obtained from IBES, which compares current EPS with the prior year. Most recent performance was calculated as the change in the ratio from 1981 to 1982 compared with the industry; a five-year average was calculated from 1978 to 1982. For each ratio the firm's performance was evaluated relative to its industry counterparts, grouped by 2-digit SIC code.

Brand change is treated as a repeatable event; it takes a value of 1 in years in which a winery adds or withdraws one or more brands and 0 in all other years. In the disbanding analyses the effects of brand-increase and brand-decrease events are estimated separately, each variable taking the value 0 until the first such event and 1 thereafter. The existing number of brands in the current brand portfolio is controlled.

The coding of the product-line variables is identical to the coding of the brand-portfolio variables: a repeatable event taking the value 1 in years in which the product line changes and 0 otherwise. There are seven product categories, and product-line increases and decreases are estimated separately in the disbanding analyses.

Takes a value of 1 in years in which a non-vineyard-owning winery acquires land or a vineyard-owning winery divests itself completely of land, and 0 otherwise; it is treated as a repeatable event. In the disbanding analyses, separate variables distinguish wineries that have experienced any land acquisition or any land divestment (0 until the first event, then 1).
Organizational size is measured as storage capacity expressed in thousands of gallons.
Organizational age is measured as the number of years of continuous existence and is specified in terms of its natural logarithm.

variable_name: number of preceding changes of the same kind
description: For brand and product changes the variable is initially set at 0, takes a value of 1 in the year following the first change, 2 in the year following the second change of the same kind, and so on. For land-status changes the variable is constructed so that there cannot be more than one episode of land acquisition unless there is an intervening episode of land divestment, capturing a tendency to vacillate on land issues or to speculate on real estate.

variable_name: log duration since the last event of the same kind
description: The variable is initially set at 0, set to 1 in the first year when a change of a particular kind occurs, and measures time in annual increments until the same kind of change occurs again, at which point it is reset to 0. It is entered as a natural logarithm.

variable_name: uncertainty, frequency, and amplitude of change in wine consumption
description: Uncertainty is measured as the coefficient of alienation (1 - R^2) for the level of wine consumption in the current year regressed on the same for the five preceding years. Frequency of change is the number of slope reversals in the preceding five years divided by four, the maximum number of reversals possible. Amplitude of change is the absolute deviation of the current year's growth from the mean growth rate in wine consumption during the preceding five years.
time_window: current year with five preceding years

description: The dependent variable in the second part of the analyses is defined as an organization-specific instantaneous transition rate for winery disbanding, which is modelled as a nonrepeatable event. Each organization's life span is divided into annual spells and the values of covariates are updated at the beginning of each spell, all covariates being lagged by one year.

The dependent variable is the total number of CEO turnovers occurring at a given hospital during the 1980-1988 period. Changes in the hospital CEO were determined by comparing hospital CEO names in consecutive years of the AHA Annual Survey of Hospitals, so that no more than one CEO turnover per year can be detected, which may yield a somewhat conservative estimate. The measure does not distinguish between voluntary and involuntary exits.

A factor-score index created from six governing-board measures by principal components factor analysis with varimax rotation. This factor was defined by the three variables pertaining to CEO influence and participation on the governing board. Its alpha coefficient was .79.
A discrete indicator of whether or not hospital boards maintained a formal, written employment contract with the CEO. It is a dummy variable coded 0 for no written contract and 1 for a contract.

A factor-score index formed by principal components factor analysis with varimax rotation, defined by governing board size, diffusion of board member selection responsibility, and occupational heterogeneity of board members. Its alpha coefficient was .66.

The number of board members occupationally classified as corporate executives. Proportional representation by corporate executives was assessed by controlling for board size in the multivariate model.

The number of board members who are physicians with active staff privileges at the hospital. As with corporate representation, proportional representation was assessed by controlling for board size in the multivariate model.

Hospitals were placed in one of four mutually exclusive stage categories for the period 1980-1984: decline, growth, stability, or instability. Stages were determined by patterns of adjusted admissions compared with nine industry comparison groups formed by ownership category and bed size; growers showed increases in adjusted admissions of more than 5 percent above the average change for their comparison group for at least three of four consecutive-year pairs, decliners decreases of more than 5 percent below, unstable hospitals at least one year pair of growth and one of decline greater than 5 percent with respect to their comparison groups, and all remaining hospitals were classified as stable. Stability is the suppressed category in the regressions.

The dependent variable in the first analysis was all transitions from an origin format including Easy Listening to a destination format not including Easy Listening. Abandonments were modeled as an event history, so the quantity estimated is the hazard rate of abandoning the format. Ninety point two percent of the abandonments had Easy Listening as the sole origin format.

The contagion effect is the sum, over stations that have previously abandoned the format, of the influence of each previous abandonment on the hazard rate of stations still using the format. The influence is specified as additive rather than multiplicative, so each successive event has the same incremental effect rather than an accelerating one.

One of three disjoint reference groups coded for each station, consisting of the other stations in the same corporation. Abandonments by members of the group were categorized as proximate by setting the relevant social proximity variable to one, so the coefficient estimates whether abandonment by a member of the group is more (positive) or less (negative) contagious than abandonment by an organization outside the reference group.

One of three disjoint reference groups coded for each station, consisting of the market contacts outside the focal market. Abandonments by members of the group were categorized as proximate by setting the relevant social proximity variable to one, so the coefficient estimates whether abandonment by a member of the group is more or less contagious than abandonment by an organization outside the reference group.

variable_name: direct competitor (market contacts in the focal market)
description: One of three disjoint reference groups coded for each station, consisting of the market contacts in the focal market, i.e., the direct competitors. Abandonments by members of the group were categorized as proximate by setting the relevant social proximity variable to one, so the coefficient estimates whether abandonment by a direct competitor is more or less contagious than abandonment by an organization outside the reference group.

The size of the corporation was coded as the number of radio stations it owned. For the limited attention argument the number of stations indicates the load of decision-relevant information generated within the corporation; for the inertia argument it measures the administrative complexity faced by the corporate center.

Two indicator variables for market rank measure market size: one for the top ten markets and the other for the next fifteen. Hypothesis 3 predicts a positive sign for both coefficients and a larger coefficient for the top-ten variable.

Reference-group indicator coded as a social proximity matrix in which members of the group are indicated by a 1 and nonmembers by a 0; a station is a corporate contact of the focal station when it belongs to the same corporation. The indicator is permanent, because the model specifies that an adoption remains influential even if the station later abandons the format. Spells are split when a station is sold so that the reference groups can be updated.

Reference-group indicator coded as a social proximity matrix in which members of the group are indicated by a 1 and nonmembers by a 0. A corporation that owns a station in the focal market has its stations outside that market coded as market contacts, so those stations receive information about the actions of the competitors of the corporation's sister organization.

Reference-group indicator coded as a social proximity matrix in which members of the group are indicated by a 1 and nonmembers by a 0; each adopter of Soft AC in the focal market is coded as a member of the group. It remains in the reference group permanently, even if it abandons the format, while it is removed from Soft AC density on abandonment.

Entry into Soft AC is counted as an event; entry into any other format, going off the air, or the end of the study is counted as a censored observation. Stations are at risk from founding or the start of the study, whichever occurs last, until the end of the study, so there are no fatal events.

Indicator variable set to one after the station is sold. When a station is sold the spell is split so that the reference-group indicators can be updated, and hypothesis 2a predicts a positive coefficient for this variable.

Indicator variable set to one for the first year of a new spell after a station changes its format; spells are split at each format change. Because it is not possible to see whether stations had a recent format change in the first year of the study, spell segments in 1984 were given weight zero.
time_window: first year after a format change

variable_name: Adult Contemporary origin and News/Talk/Religion origin
description: Two indicator variables used to test hypothesis 2c, updated when the station changes its format. A station changing from Adult Contemporary to Soft AC can use the current knowledge of its sales staff because the same advertisers are sought, so this indicator was expected to have a positive coefficient. Nonmusic formats such as News, Talk, and Religion do not use music selection procedures and need to acquire competence in music selection, so this indicator was expected to have a negative coefficient.

variable_name: overall measure of board control over management
description: The five indicators of board control (outsider ratio, board leadership structure, diversification, total compensation, and compensation contingency) were standardized and summed for each board in the sample. The measure was calculated as the average value over a moving three-year period (year t-2 to year t) to avoid measurement error from temporary fluctuations. Boards were then divided into high- and low-control groups by taking the median split of this measure, separately for each year.

The outsider ratio was first measured each year as the number of nonemployee directors divided by the total number of board members. Participation in increased outsider ratio was then calculated as the number of boards on which the focal individual sits that increased the ratio of outside to inside directors from year t-1 to year t. Each change was treated as a dichotomous event and counted across boards.

A parallel measure to participation in increased outsider ratio, gauging prior participation in reduced board independence. It counts the boards on which the focal individual sits that decreased the ratio of outside to inside directors from year t-1 to year t.

Board leadership structure was measured dichotomously, coded 1 if the CEO and board chair positions are separate in a given year and 0 otherwise. Participation in CEO/board chair separation was calculated as the number of boards on which the focal individual sits with a combined CEO-board chair position in year t-1 and separated positions in year t.

A parallel measure gauging prior participation in reduced board independence through board leadership structure. It counts the boards on which the focal individual sits that moved from separated to combined CEO-board chair positions from year t-1 to year t.

Diversification was measured with Palepu's (1985) entropy measure, which takes into account the number of segments in which a firm operates and weights each segment according to its contribution to total sales; the text prints the formula in symbols that are not fully readable. Reduced diversification was calculated as a decrease in the entropy measure exceeding one standard deviation of the change in diversification from year t-1 to year t. Participation in reduced diversification was then measured as the number of firms where the focal individual serves as director that decreased diversification from the prior year to the current year.

A parallel measure gauging prior participation in reduced board independence through corporate strategy. It counts the firms where the focal individual serves as director that increased diversification from the prior year to the current year, using the same entropy measure and change thresholds.

variable_name: participation in reduced total CEO compensation
description: Participation in reduced total CEO compensation was calculated as the number of firms where the focal individual serves as director that reduced CEO total direct compensation from the prior year to the current year. Total direct compensation includes salary, short-term bonus, and the total value of long-term incentive grants, with all compensation values adjusted for inflation to 1990 constant dollars.

A measure of prior participation in reduced board independence through CEO pay. A positive change in the CEO's total direct compensation exceeding one standard deviation was used, to capture relatively distinctive and noticeable changes, since a large portion of companies increased total compensation in any given year.

variable_name: participation in increased CEO compensation contingency
description: Compensation contingency was first calculated for each year as the total value of long-term incentive grants divided by total direct compensation; short-term bonuses were excluded but stock options were included. Stock options were valued with the Black-Scholes (1973) method and other grants (restricted stock, performance shares, etc.) were valued at market price at date of grant, with values adjusted for inflation. Participation in greater CEO compensation contingency was calculated as the number of firms where the focal individual serves as director that increased compensation contingency from the prior year to the current year.

A parallel measure gauging prior participation in reduced board independence through the incentive structure of CEO pay. It counts the firms where the focal individual serves as director that reduced compensation contingency from the prior year to the current year, using the ratio of long-term incentive grants to total direct compensation.

variable_name: additions/subtractions in appointments to boards with low control over management
description: Change in appointments to low-control boards was calculated as the number of appointments to boards with low control in year t+2 minus the number of such appointments in year t. From this overall change measure four count variables were created indicating the net increase or decrease in appointments; the models analyze additions and subtractions separately. Low-control boards were those below the median on the combined board control measure in each year.

variable_name: additions/subtractions in appointments to boards with high control over management
description: Change in appointments to high-control boards was calculated as the number of appointments to boards with high control in year t+2 minus the number of such appointments in year t. From this overall change measure four count variables were created indicating the net increase or decrease in appointments, with additions and subtractions analyzed separately. High-control boards were those above the median on the combined board control measure in each year.

Heterogeneity of top management team members' functional backgrounds, computed as a Herfindahl-Hirschman index in which p is the percentage of top management team members in each of 16 functional background categories. Where an executive had substantial experience in more than one category, the primary category selected was the one in which the executive spent the most time. Coding was based on each year's Dun and Bradstreet Directory of Corporate Management.

Heterogeneity of top management team members' educational backgrounds, computed as a Herfindahl-Hirschman index over eight different disciplines. For executives with graduate degrees the corresponding graduate discipline was coded; for those without graduate degrees, their undergraduate discipline was coded. Coding was based on each year's Dun and Bradstreet Directory of Corporate Management.

Heterogeneity of top management team members' company tenure, calculated as the standard deviation of the number of years the executives on the top management team had spent in the firm. The coefficient of variation was not used because one control variable was the team's mean company tenure.
Calculated as the total number of actions a firm launched in a given year. Actions were identified from an extensive review of every issue of Aviation Daily and classified into 21 types.

Measured as the number of strategic actions the firm took in a year divided by its total number of actions. Three raters working independently classified actions as strategic (e.g., mergers and acquisitions, hub creations) or tactical (e.g., price cuts), with total agreement among the raters.

Measured by the amount of industry attention accorded a move, counted as the number of lines Aviation Daily devoted to reporting the action. Because press attention differs inherently by type of move, scores were standardized for each of the 21 types over all years and all airlines to have a mean of zero and standard deviation of one.

Measured as the proportion of the firm's revenue base potentially affected by the action. After identifying the airports affected by a firm's action, the firm's annual number of passengers at these airports was divided by the firm's total number of passengers in that year.

The amount of time a firm took to execute an announced action, measured as the time between the date the firm publicly announced or acknowledged the intended action and the date that action began to be executed, as reported in Aviation Daily. The time lag was standardized across all years and firms to a mean of zero and standard deviation of one, and the signs were reversed so that a large value indicates great speed.

Measured by the total number of responses a firm executed in a year, given that it was identified as a competitor affected by an action. Response opportunities were defined by first identifying all airports affected by the initial action and defining the airlines competing via those airports as potential responders; response propensity was then calculated as the percentage of response opportunities that the firm actually took in each year.

Measured by the number of lines Aviation Daily devoted to the response, standardized for each type of response. The authors assume that Aviation Daily allocates space in proportion to newsworthiness and that items commanding more attention are viewed as relatively innovative, bold, unexpected, or complex.
Measured as the percentage of the firm's revenue base affected by its response.

Measured as the amount of time a firm took to generate a response, calculated from Aviation Daily reports as the time lag between the day that a competitor announced its initial action and the day that the focal firm announced its response. The lag was standardized by response type and reverse-scored to indicate speed.

The amount of time a firm took to execute an announced response. Because response execution speed depends on the type of initial action and other features, response execution time was regressed on type of action and action execution time for all years and airlines, and the average residual scores across all the responses made by an airline in a given year were used as its response execution time for that year. The signs of the scores were reversed so that a large value implies great speed.

The firm's market share change during the year, calculated as the percentage change from the previous year in market share in those markets in which the airline was present (this year's market share minus last year's, divided by last year's).
time_window: one year, change from previous year

description: The firm's change in profits during the year, calculated as the percentage change in dollar profits between this year and the previous year.
time_window: one year, change from previous year

description: The number of outside directors currently also serving as chief executive at another Fortune or Forbes 500 company, divided by the total number of outsiders on the board. Separate analyses operationalized the presence of CEO-directors as the absolute number of such directors on the board, with substantively unchanged results; the proportional measure was used in the final models.
scale: proportion of outsiders on the board
time_window: lagged one year in the models

description: Dichotomous variable coded 1 in a given year if the CEO and board chair positions were separate in that year but not in the prior year, and 0 otherwise. All three varieties of separation experience were combined: losing both positions, losing only the CEO position while remaining board chair, and losing only the board chair position while remaining CEO.
Dichotomous measure coded 1 if the ratio of outside to inside directors was greater in the current year than in the prior year, and 0 otherwise.

Dichotomous measure of increased demographic distance, coded 1 if CEO-board similarity decreased across all three dimensions, and 0 otherwise. Functional background and education similarity were measured with a variant of Blau's index of heterogeneity over CEO-board member dyads, and age similarity with an analog of the coefficient of variation converted to an indicator of similarity by subtracting each firm's coefficient from the highest value in the sample. Degree type was coded as the highest university degree obtained in five categories: arts, sciences, engineering, management or economics, and law.

Compensation contingency was calculated for each year as the total value of long-term incentive grants divided by total direct compensation, with stock options valued by the Black-Scholes method and other grants valued at market price at date of grant, all adjusted for inflation to 1990 constant dollars. The dichotomous measure is coded 1 in a particular year if compensation contingency increased from the prior year, and 0 otherwise.

Unrelated diversification measured with Palepu's entropy measure, which takes into account the number of segments in which a firm operates and weights each segment according to its contribution to total sales. Reduced diversification was operationalized as an absolute decrease in the entropy measure of .10 or more, to capture relatively significant change and exclude change reflecting random alterations in segment sales levels.
scale: 0/1 (decrease of .10 or more in the entropy measure)

variable_name: proportion of CEO-directors who experienced separation at home
description: Number of outside CEO-directors serving as CEO at another Fortune or Forbes 500 company who have also experienced a separation of the CEO and board chair positions at their home company within the past two years, divided by the total number of outsiders on the board.
scale: proportion of outsiders on the board

variable_name: proportion of CEO-directors who experienced an increased outsider ratio at home
description: Number of outside CEO-directors serving as CEO at another Fortune or Forbes 500 company who have also experienced an increase in the ratio of outside to inside directors at their home company within the past two years, divided by the total number of outsiders on the board.
scale: proportion of outsiders on the board

variable_name: proportion of CEO-directors who experienced increased dissimilarity at home
description: Number of outside CEO-directors serving as CEO at another Fortune or Forbes 500 company who have also experienced an increase in demographic distance from the board at their home company within the past two years, divided by the total number of outsiders on the board.
scale: proportion of outsiders on the board

variable_name: proportion of CEO-directors who experienced a diversification reduction at home
description: Number of outside CEO-directors serving as CEO at another Fortune or Forbes 500 company who have also experienced a reduction in unrelated diversification at their home company within the past two years, divided by the total number of outsiders on the board.
scale: proportion of outsiders on the board

variable_name: proportion of CEO-directors who experienced an increase in compensation contingency at home
description: Number of outside CEO-directors serving as CEO at another Fortune or Forbes 500 company who have also experienced an increase in compensation contingency at their home company within the past two years, divided by the total number of outsiders on the board.
scale: proportion of outsiders on the board

description: A symbolic LTIP adoption is one in which firms adopted an LTIP in a particular year but did not announce grants of any of the incentive vehicles included under the plan. The authors checked proxies before and after the LTIP adoption date to confirm the newness and uniqueness of coded LTIP adoptions, and checked for grants from the year of adoption to the end of the time period studied. Dummy variables were created to isolate the effects of symbolic and substantive LTIP adoptions, with no LTIP adoption as the base case.

A substantive LTIP adoption is one in which firms adopted and also announced grants under the plan. LTIP grants ranged from 2 percent of total compensation to 93 percent, with a mean of 26 percent. The two categories of adoption (symbolic or substantive) were used to create subgroups in the stock market analyses and to create dummy variables in the analyses of other governance changes.

A basic content analysis of proxy statements in the year of adoption was used to determine the presence or absence of agency explanations for new LTIPs. Coders were given a summary description of the agency perspective and asked to determine whether an agency explanation was present anywhere in the proxy, so the recording unit is the entire proxy statement. Pre-negotiation intercoder reliabilities were very high, with Pearson correlation coefficients ranging from .903 to .972 and an intercoder agreement rate of 95 percent; forty-nine percent of the proxy statements included an agency explanation. The categorization was used to create subgroups in the stock market analyses and dummy variables in the analyses predicting governance changes.

Excess stock returns are the cumulative difference between a firm's observed return and its expected return during a specified period surrounding adoption. Excess returns were observed from the proxy mailing date, and returns were cumulated over four time intervals: 2 days, 11 days, 31 days, and the subsequent 390-day period. Average cumulative excess returns were calculated for all adopting firms and for subgroups defined by symbolic versus substantive adoption and by the presence or absence of an agency explanation.
time_window: 2 days, 11 days, 31 days, and 390 days around adoption

description: A dichotomous variable created for each year, coded as 1 if the CEO and board chair positions were separate in the subsequent year, t+1, but not in the current year, and 0 otherwise. The model examines the likelihood of the first event during the time period, removing the firm from the risk set following change.

Increases in the ratio of outside to inside directors were measured by subtracting the ratio in the current year from the ratio in the subsequent year. The prior ratio of outside to inside directors was also used as an indicator of prior board control.

Measured as equity held by pension funds, banks and trust companies, savings and loans, mutual fund managers, and labor union funds divided by total common stock. The variable was used in interaction terms with the LTIP adoption and LTIP explanation variables.

A composite of four formative indicators of change in structural board independence. Three indicators were measured with archival data: change in the outsider ratio, computed as the ratio of non-employee directors to total board members in the current year minus the value in year t-2; CEO/board chairman split, a binary variable coded 1 if different individuals occupied the CEO and board chair positions in the current year while the same individual held both positions in year t-2; and CEO-board demographic distance. Demographic distance was a composite of the z-scores of three similarity variables (age similarity, measured with an analog of the euclidean distance measure, and functional background and educational degree type similarity, measured as the squared proportion of CEO-board member dyads sharing the same category), summed and subtracted from the highest value in the sample so that higher values indicate greater demographic distance; change was the current value minus the value in year t-2. The fourth indicator, change in CEO/board friendship ties, was measured with survey data as the current number of perceived friendships divided by the total number of board members minus the value in year t-2.

A multi-item scale measuring the frequency of CEO ingratiation attempts toward board members, with items adapted from Kumar and Beyerlein's (1991) 'Measure of Ingratiatory Behaviors in Organizational Settings'. The phrasing of each item is taken from the CEO survey and most items were altered appropriately for the director survey; four of the eight ingratiation items were not included in the director survey. When multiple outside directors responded for the same company, director responses were averaged. Interrater reliability was assessed with kappa coefficients for the items used in both surveys.

Two survey items measuring the frequency of CEO persuasion attempts toward the board. The items were developed from available qualitative research on how top managers and directors describe their interactions, as well as feedback from the pilot interviews, and were included in both the CEO and director surveys.

The entropy measure of diversification, which takes into account the number of segments in which a firm operates and weights each segment according to its contribution to total sales; P is the sales attributed to segment i and the logarithm of the inverse of its sales is the weight for each segment. This measure captures not only the extent of diversity across a firm's activities but also the relatedness of that diversity, and it was adjusted for industry differences in each year by subtracting the average value for the firm's primary industry. Change in diversification was calculated as the absolute (raw) change in this measure over the subsequent two-year period (year t to year t+2); when CEO succession occurred before the end of the time period, change was measured to the year of departure.

Total compensation includes base salary, short-term bonus awards, and the total value of long-term incentives granted in a given year. Stock options were valued using the Black-Scholes (1973) method, which estimates option value based on the historical price volatility of the underlying security, and other grants (e.g., restricted stock, performance shares) were valued according to the market price at date of grant. The compensation variables were adjusted for industry differences by subtracting the average value for the firm's primary industry. Change in total compensation was calculated as the logarithm of compensation in year t+2 minus the same measure in the current year.

Compensation contingency was calculated as the total value of long-term incentive grants divided by total compensation; short-term bonuses were not included in this measure because they have been shown to be susceptible to manipulation. The compensation variables were adjusted for industry differences by subtracting the average value for the firm's primary industry. Change in compensation contingency was calculated as contingency in year t+2 minus the same measure in the current year.

Binary variable set to 1 if a supplier established its first manufacturing plant in the United States or Canada in a given calendar year and set to 0 otherwise. It describes whether the supplier expanded into the host location. The event of interest is the establishment of the supplier's first plant in the United States or Canada during a given year.

A count variable measuring how many current buyers of a given supplier had expanded as of a given year. To model the nonlinear effect, the count was logarithmically transformed after adding 1 to the initial count to avoid undefined logarithmic values. A current buyer was defined as one for which the supplier manufactured at least one component for direct sale in Japan.
time_window: cumulative as of a given year

description: A count of how many potential buyers of a given supplier had expanded as of a given year, logarithmically transformed after adding 1 to the initial count. Potential buyers included those buyers that purchased no component from the supplier in Japan.
time_window: cumulative as of a given year

description: A time-varying count of previous entries by competitors, entered as the initial count together with a squared term to capture the predicted nonmonotonic effect. Two suppliers were coded as competitors if the lists of components they manufactured contained at least one component in common out of the 136 components covered.
time_window: cumulative as of a given year

description: A logarithmic transformation of the initial count of prior entries by non-competing suppliers, after adding 1 to the initial count. Suppliers were coded as non-competing if there was no overlap between the lines of components they manufactured.
time_window: cumulative as of a given year

variable_name: time since at least one current buyer entered
description: A clock variable measuring how many years had elapsed since the earliest entrant among a supplier's current buyers established its first plant in the United States or Canada. The clock is set to zero until the first entry by an organization in the relevant set. The inverted-U prediction was tested by including a squared term for this clock.
time_window: years elapsed, measured as of a given year

variable_name: time since at least one potential buyer entered
description: A clock variable measuring the number of years since the first potential buyer of the supplier expanded into the United States or Canada, set to zero until that first entry. A squared term for this clock was included to test the inverted-U prediction.
time_window: years elapsed, measured as of a given year

variable_name: time since at least one competitor entered
description: A clock variable measuring the time since the first competing supplier of the focal supplier expanded into the United States or Canada, recorded in years and set to zero until the first such entry. A squared term for this clock was included to test the inverted-U prediction.
time_window: years elapsed, measured as of a given year

variable_name: time since at least one non-competing supplier entered
description: A clock variable measuring the time since the first non-competing supplier of the focal supplier expanded into the United States or Canada, recorded in years and set to zero until the first such entry. A squared term for this clock was included to test the inverted-U prediction.
time_window: years elapsed, measured as of a given year

description: A composite score formed by summing the firm's dyadic technological overlap scores over all firms in the industry. The dyadic overlap a_ijt is the proportion of firm i's patent citations that firm j also made, where patents are treated as technologically similar to the degree that they are structurally equivalent (cite the same antecedent patents) in the patent citation network. The composite was computed over a five-year moving window from t-5 to t-1, chosen because five years approximated the product life cycle in the semiconductor industry. Firms without patents have realizations of 0 and are identified with a no-patent dummy until they secure a patent.
time_window: previous five years (t-5 to t-1), moving window

description: The proportion of all patent citations made during the interval that were to patents assigned to the focal firm, with self-citations excluded. The denominator adjusts for changes over time in the total volume of citations accruing to the sampled firms, so the variable is a proportion with a time-invariant interpretation. Computed over five-year moving windows: for example, Intel's prestige in 1991 was the number of patent citations received from patents with application dates between 1986 and 1990 divided by the total number of patent citations received by all firms in the sample in the same interval.

A count of the number of technology alliances formed by each organization in the sample during each year in the observation window. Only horizontal, reciprocal technology alliances qualified: both firms had to be semiconductor producers and the deal had to be to exchange or develop technology. Vertical partnerships, marketing agreements, and one-way technology licensing alliances were excluded; the qualifying coalitions were joint product development agreements, joint ventures, and technology exchanges.

A symmetrical dyadic measure formed by summing the two asymmetric alpha coefficients for the firms in a dyad. Two firms occupied overlapping technological positions when their patent portfolios cited the same antecedent patents, i.e., when they were structurally equivalent in the citation network. Covariates describe a dyad and are lagged by one year.
time_window: previous five years, lagged by one year

variable_name: prestige of the most prestigious firm in the dyad
description: The technological prestige score of the most prestigious of the two firms in the dyad, included on the assumption that the likelihood of an alliance in a dyad is higher when at least one of the two firms has high prestige because the gains from association are greater when a high-status actor is involved.
time_window: previous five years, lagged by one year

description: An indicator denoting the presence (= 1) or absence (= 0) of an alliance in each dyad-year, built from annual, symmetric firm-by-firm alliance matrices in which the ijth cell is 1 if there was an alliance in the ijth pair of firms in year t; one triangle of each annual matrix was pooled across years.

variable_name: number of acquisitions completed by the focal firm
description: The number of 'traditional' acquisitions completed by the focal firm during the sampled year, in which one existing firm buys a controlling interest in another existing firm; other types of acquisitions such as LBOs were excluded and the purchase price had to exceed one million dollars. The variable ranged from zero to nine.

The number of acquisitions completed by the focal firm's interlock partners in the sampled year and the three years before the sampled year. Directorship lists came from the focal firm's proxy statements; the acquisitions by partners of inside directors (sent ties) and by firms with which outside directors were principally affiliated (received ties) were each influential and were combined into a single variable, while neutral ties were not influential.
time_window: sampled year and the three years before

description: Sales of the focal firm at the end of the year prior to the sampled year, log-transformed to correct for skew before entering the analyses. An interaction of size with the number of acquisitions by the interlocked firms was created.
time_window: end of the year prior to the sampled year

description: Network degree centrality was calculated as the number of sent ties, minus any duplicated ties, i.e., when two directors from the focal firm sit on the same outside board; also called outdegree centrality. It captures the number of other firms the focal firm's inside directors could get information from through board ties, and an interaction with the number of acquisitions by the interlocked firms was created.

variable_name: CEO membership in Business Council or Business Roundtable
description: Coded one if the CEO of the focal firm was a member of the Business Council and/or Business Roundtable and zero otherwise. Business Council membership was obtained from membership lists for four years during the 1980-1990 period; for firms sampled in 1986-1990 a 1989 roundtable listing was used and for those sampled in 1981-1985 a 1983 listing was used. An interaction between the acquisitions of the interlock partners and focal CEO membership was created.

The combined number of articles dealing with mergers and acquisitions in Business Week, Fortune, and Forbes during the three years prior to the sampled year for each firm, obtained from periodical indexes. Wall Street Journal articles were not used so that articles would not simply proxy for the number of acquisitions, and an interaction of the number of acquisitions by interlock partners and the number of business press articles was created.
time_window: three years prior to the sampled year

description: Degree of similarity between the focal firm and its interlock partners, for which higher values indicated more similarity. Firms sharing the same 2-digit SIC code were coded four; firms sharing the same 1-digit but not the same 2-digit SIC were coded three; firms sharing the same general SIC category of manufacturing and mining, wholesaling, or service were coded two; and firms sharing none of these were coded one. An interaction of the acquisitions by interlock partners and industry similarity was created.

The number of new administrative rule documents born in a given year in each administrative subpopulation. The analysis pools time series for six administrative rule subpopulations, with the subpopulation-specific birth rate as the dependent variable. The number of administrative rule births was 257 before being reduced to 177 due to missing values of covariates and exclusion of the founding version of the Administrative Guide.

The number of new academic rule documents born in a given year in each academic subpopulation. The analysis pools time series for four academic rule subpopulations that combine rule-making body and problem area. A total of 344 academic rule births is analyzed.

Global density is the number of administrative rules in force in year t-1. Local density is the number of rules in force in year t-1 in a given administrative subpopulation. Joint local density pools the six local densities, while separate local density allows each subpopulation its own slope.

Global density is the number of academic rules in force in year t-1. Intermediate density aggregates academic rules across rule-making body or across problem area. Local density is the number of rules in force in year t-1 in a given academic subpopulation. Joint and separate local density variables are also defined.

Global suspensions are the number of administrative rules suspended in year t; local suspensions are the number suspended in year t in a given administrative subpopulation. Suspension variables are not lagged because recycling is treated as occurring more or less instantaneously. Joint and separate suspension variables are also defined.

Global suspensions are the number of academic rules suspended in year t; intermediate and local suspensions are also defined. Suspension variables are not lagged because recycling is treated as occurring more or less instantaneously. Joint and separate suspension variables are also defined.

Differences in problem supply across rule areas were captured by dummy variables for the administrative rule subpopulations (procurement rules as the reference category, five dummies added), letting the baseline rule birth rate differ by area. Differences in the intercepts were then read as differences in problem supply.

For each state, the authors computed the number of state-level prohibitions in adjacent states, calling it the number of local prohibitions. A dichotomous measure of prohibition onset is used for each state prohibition, assuming that effects did not vary across time or jurisdictions.

The authors calculated the total number of state-level prohibitions in force each year and subtracted the number of local prohibitions for each focal state, creating the nonlocal prohibition variable. A squared term for this variable is also used in the founding analysis.

The dependent variable is the number of brewery foundings in each state in each year; observations were not recorded for states while a state-level prohibition was in force. To test hypothesis 4a, counts of foundings in rural areas, large cities, and very large cities were treated as separate outcomes in three data sets.

Each brewery's life-history was broken into annual spells with all but the last spell censored on the right; because only the year of failure is known, failure is assumed to occur at the midpoint of the year. A dummy variable indicates left-censoring for breweries alive before 1845, and time-varying covariates were updated at the beginning of each year.

variable_name: large city and very large city dummies
description: Foundings were differentiated by city size into rural areas (cities of less than 250,000), large cities (250,000 to 500,000 people), and very large cities (greater than 500,000 people). For mortality, two organization-level dummy variables indicate whether a brewery was located in a large city or a very large city.
level: state-year for foundings; organization-year for mortality

variable_name: change in prohibition status of an adjacent state
description: A dummy variable equals one (and remains one thereafter) once an adjacent state enacted a prohibition. A clock denotes the elapsed time since a change in the prohibition status of any adjacent state, allowing the immediate disruptive effect and its decline over time to be modeled.

variable_name: clock denoting elapsed time since a change in prohibition status
description: A clock denoting the elapsed time since a change in the prohibition status (enacting or repealing a prohibition) of any adjacent state, used together with the change dummy to model the immediate and long-term effects of environmental reversals.

variable_name: age of the firm at the time of the last change in the prohibition status of an adjacent state
description: A variable took the value of the age of the firm at the time of the last change in the prohibition status of an adjacent state; if no adjacent states experienced prohibition, the variable remained zero. A separate measure counts the cumulative number of adjacent state prohibition changes a firm had experienced.

Two coders reviewed each NTSB accident or incident report and classified its causes into one of 23 cause categories (Cohen's kappa .87 for all accident causes; discrepancies resolved by discussion). Heterogeneity was computed with an entropy-based diversity index, Diversity = -[P(lnP)] for i = 1...23, where P is the proportion of causes in each category; higher scores mean more heterogeneous underlying causes. The within-event measure was constructed at the accident level, discounted by the age of experience (prior year weighted 3/3, the year before 2/3, the year before that 1/3) and averaged over the prior three years.

Heterogeneity was measured across all of an airline's accidents and incidents for a given year, discounted by the age of experience, and the prior three years' measures were summed rather than averaged because across-accident heterogeneity means the prior three years' experience essentially should count as one accident with multiple causes. It uses the same entropy-based diversity index over the 23 cause categories.

The number of accidents plus incidents per 100,000 departures, calculated for each airline and updated annually; the rate per departure is used because most accidents occur on takeoff and landing. Analyses were run on accident rates and incident rates both separately and together as event rates.

The dependent variable is the number of pilot errors reported for each airline for each year, estimated with a random-effects negative binomial model because the dependent variable is a count and the specification controls for nonindependence among observations. Additional analyses examined ground-crew, flight-attendant, maintenance, supervisory, external-factor and equipment errors.

variable_name: number of prior causes of each type
description: The number of each of the 23 cause categories an airline experienced in a given year, used as a function of the number of prior causes of each type experienced by that airline, with C = cause 1...23, A = airline 1...310 and Y = year 1984...1997. Estimated with a random-effects negative binomial model on the full sample and then on single-cause accidents only.

variable_name: number of subsequent causes of each type
description: The dependent variable of the repetition analysis: the number of each of the 23 cause categories an airline experienced in a given year, modeled on the number of prior causes of each type that the airline experienced. Models were run on the full sample of accidents and incidents and on single-cause accidents only.

Fleet diversity was used as the airline industry standard for measuring level of specialization and was calculated with the same entropy formula as causal heterogeneity: Diversity = -[P(lnP)] for i = 1...n, where P is the proportion of planes in each type (e.g., 727s, 737s, MD80s). Higher scores mean the airline has a more heterogeneous fleet (a generalist); an airline with only one type of plane has a score of zero (highly specialized). Airlines were classified into specialists and generalists using this measure together with the Official Airline Guide, U.S. edition, and FAA and NTSB data; size was controlled separately because size and generalism are correlated at .594.

Constructed by estimating Nickerson and Silverman's (2003) two-sided Tobit model of the proportion of a firm's total miles driven by company drivers for observations in 1991, applying the resulting coefficients to each year in the sample, and setting Driver Misalign equal to the absolute value of the residual for each firm-year. It ranges between 0, which occurs when the proportion of a firm's total miles driven by company drivers conforms perfectly to the predicted proportion, and 1, which occurs when reliance on company drivers is diametrically opposite that predicted.

Annual return on assets for each carrier i in year t, calculated by dividing annual earnings before interest, taxes, and depreciation expense by total assets. Tobin's q was not used because many of the firms in the database are private, which precludes calculating it.

variable_name: Adjustment in Driver Misalign (partial-adjustment dependent variable)
description: Dependent variable of the partial-adjustment equation, capturing the rate and amount of adjustment in Driver Misalign between time t and time t+1 as a function of a carrier's attributes at time t. If adaptation is unconstrained the coefficient for Driver Misalign would equal 0 (perfect alignment in t+1); if adaptation is highly constrained it would equal 1 (a carrier remains as misaligned at t+1 as at t).

Measured as the proportion of carrier i's annual revenue derived from less-than-truckload (LTL) carriage. In the short run LTL Share is treated as a constraint on employment mode choice because LTL carriage requires investment in idiosyncratic assets.

A categorical variable equal to 1 if carrier i contributes money to a union pension plan in year t, and 0 otherwise. Unionization is interpreted as an example of formal contractual commitment; because very few firms changed union status during the sample period, the variable was used to divide the sample into unionized and non-unionized subsamples.

Overinteg is a categorical variable equal to 1 if carrier i's level of integration is greater than that prescribed by transaction cost economics, and 0 otherwise. Underinteg is a categorical variable equal to 1 if the level of integration is less than prescribed, and 0 otherwise. Overintegration is interpreted as generating a higher level of contractual commitment than underintegration; the variables were used to construct over- and underintegrated subsamples.

variable_name: number of kibbutzim founded in a region in a year
description: The dependent variable is the count of kibbutzim founded in a region in a year. Regions are ten-by-ten kilometer squares of the map-grid used in maps of mandatory Palestine and Israel; the authors note that an earlier analysis with a different grid gave comparable results. Regions were included in years in which they were part of Palestine, Israel, or occupied by Israel.

Counts of corporations, available only in aggregate for the society as a whole, following the argument that competition between kibbutzim and corporations is society-wide. Like all time-changing variables in the analysis, it was updated at the beginning of each year.
time_window: annual, updated at the beginning of each year

description: Because moshavim and development towns compete with kibbutzim for suitable land on which to settle, their densities were operationalized at the local level as the count in a given region, updated at the beginning of each year.
time_window: annual, updated at the beginning of each year

description: Because development towns compete with kibbutzim for suitable land on which to settle, their density was operationalized at the local level as the count in a given region, updated at the beginning of each year.
time_window: annual, updated at the beginning of each year

variable_name: percentage of immigrants from Africa and Asia
description: A moving average of the percentage of Jewish immigrants over the preceding five years who were from Asia and Africa, used to test the Sephardic dimension of community influence.
The number of Jews in the country at the start of a given year, representing the opportunity to provide absorption.

An indicator variable coded 1 in years of significant political violence or tension between the Jewish population and surrounding Arab populations. For the mandate period the coding follows Haganah (1954), which designated the first and second Arab revolts, World War II in the Middle East, and the years from the end of World War II to the end of the 1948 war; for the Israel period it designates the Sinai War, the Six-Day War, the 1973 War, the Lebanon War, and the first Palestinian Intifada.

A coding by region based on two conditions. First, proximity to a border contested by an Arab population: a region spanning a contested border is coded 3, within 5 kilometers is coded 2, and within 10 kilometers is coded 1. Second, if the region qualifies as contested it must have some non-kibbutz Jewish settlement; if it does not, the contention code is set to 0.

A count of the number of state bureaucrats and police divided by 100,000 and logged for scaling. The authors tested for a differential impact of institutional capacity between the British Mandate and the State of Israel and found no difference.
A dichotomous variable coded 1 in years after the formation of the Israeli state, used to capture the delegitimation campaign the new state launched on the kibbutzim.

variable_name: early establishment (number of incorporated firms in 1905)
description: The number of incorporated firms in each city in 1905, taken from the Census of Manufacturers for each state in 1905, the closest measurement to 1910 of this concept the author could find. The variable has a mean of 300 incorporated firms per community and ranges from 2,797 incorporated firms in New York down to the bottom seven communities, which were not included in these volumes and received a value of 0 (cities with populations of less than 8,000 were not included). Because of extreme values, this variable was logged (+1).

variable_name: early establishment (number of incorporated firms in 1905)
description: The community-level count of incorporated firms in 1905 from the Census of Manufacturers for each state in 1905, logged (+1) because of extreme values, entered in the organizational-level models as a community characteristic.
level: community (assigned to firms by headquarters location)

description: The number of direct connections between local companies compared with the total number of direct network connections, including neutral as well as received and sent ties. In the illustration given, there are two fully local direct connections and eight total connections in the network, so the proportion of local connections is .25. The author notes that this is not a standard network measure but was used because standard measures do not capture how locally focused a network is in relation to total network connections and because it allows neutral ties to be included.

The count of the total received local ties for each firm, following Kono et al. (1998) in focusing only on local connections created by directional ties, which are consciously managed by firms. Received ties are those in which officers of other corporations sit on the board of the focal firm; sent ties, in which an officer of the focal firm sits on another board, are excluded, as are neutral ties, which are more difficult to assess at the organizational level.

A dummy variable indicating whether a community had an upper-class club, based on the upper-class social club list established by Domhoff (1998), which represents the most exclusive upper-class clubs and the most exclusive meeting grounds of the elite. Of the 51 cities in the sample, 23 have at least one upper-class club and 28 do not have an upper-class club.

A dummy variable indicating whether the firm's community had at least one upper-class club, based on Domhoff's (1998) list of the most exclusive upper-class clubs, entered in the organizational-level models as a community characteristic.
level: community (assigned to firms by headquarters location)

description: The total number of banks in each community was tabulated and included in the analysis, based on Standard Industrial Classification codes associated with the organization in the Compact D/SEC database, including 2-digit SIC codes 60, 61, and 67. In 1986, the average number of banks was 3.86, ranging from 0 (Dayton, OH; Ventura, CA; Nassau Suffolk, NY) to 12 (New York); in 2000, the average was 3.67, ranging from 0 (Stamford, CT; Richmond, VA; Ventura, CA; San Diego; Denver) to 16 (New York). Because of extreme values, this variable was logged (+1).

The community-level count of banks headquartered in the community, based on 2-digit SIC codes 60, 61, and 67 in the Compact D/SEC database and logged (+1) because of extreme values, entered in the organizational-level models.
level: community (assigned to firms by headquarters location)

description: For each community, the total number of arts and culture nonprofit organizations with more than $10,000,000 in assets, where examples are museums, symphonies, and operas; the asset cutoff results from data limitations at the source, the National Center for Charitable Statistics at the Urban Institute. In 1986, the mean number of these organizations was 1.7, ranging from New York with 19 down to 19 communities with none; in 2000, the mean was 6.4, 10 cities had more than 10, New York had the most with 54, and five cities had none. Because of extreme values, this variable was logged (+1).

The community-level count of arts and culture nonprofit organizations with more than $10,000,000 in assets, from the National Center for Charitable Statistics at the Urban Institute and logged (+1), entered in the organizational-level models.
level: community (assigned to firms by headquarters location)

description: A variable measuring the percentage of local received connections held by prominent firms, operationalizing prominent firms as those at the 75th percentile and higher of firms in each community based on firm sales, i.e., the largest 25 percent of firms in each community. To calculate the measure for this group in each community, the author summed the total number of received connections and divided this value by the total number of received connections, producing a community-level profile of the propensity of prominent firms to create local connections. Because it was used only in analyses of newly founded firms between 1987 and 2000, it was measured in 1986 only; it has a mean of 33 percent, ranging from 58 percent in Milwaukee to eight communities whose prominent firms had no local connections (Oakland, CA; Miami, FL; Ventura, CA; Tampa, FL; Salt Lake City, UT; Middlesex, NJ; Wilmington, DE; and Newark, NJ).

Connectivity is built on Krackhardt's (1994) measure of connectedness, which counts the number of pairs of nodes that are connected to one another. Given a matrix R in which r_ij = 1 if i can reach j and 0 otherwise, the measure is the proportion of mutually reachable pairs over the total number of reachable pairs in a fully connected network. It ranges from 0 to 1, with 0 equal to no connectivity in the network and 1 equal to maximum connectivity, and is computed on the yearly valued biadjacency matrices of producer and distributor organizations.
time_window: three-year moving window for ties; yearly values

description: Repeated ties were calculated for each producer organization in each year by counting the average number of times the organization worked with a distributor in the three-year window. These values were summed and divided by the total number of connected pairs in the network. The independent variable used in the analysis is the log of the average number of times producer organizations repeated collaborations with the same distributors during the window period.

Audience turnover was measured as the heterogeneity of audience members by analyzing the tenure distribution, using the standard deviation of distributor tenure as the measure of heterogeneity. Because a single measure like the coefficient of variation may confound two distinct characteristics of demographic distributions, a variable measuring the mean organizational tenure of distributor organizations was included when estimating the effect of tenure heterogeneity.

The dependent variable is the exit rate of feature film producer organizations from the market. Exit was modeled using r(t), the instantaneous risk of exiting, defined as the limiting probability of exiting between t and t + delta t given that the organization was operating at t. Producer organizations enter the population with the release of their first film and exit it the first day following the release date of their last film; life histories of each production company were broken into one-year spells to incorporate time-varying covariates.

Measured as equity held by public pension funds, mutual funds, endowments, and foundations, divided by total common stock. In further modeling, the authors also operationalized the construct as equity held by the top five institutional owners divided by total common stock.

Six-item scale capturing other-enhancement, opinion conformity, and favor rendering. Respondents answered separately for each representative of an institutional investor with whom they had communicated during the previous twelve months; for firm-level analyses responses were summed across alters and factor scores generated. Interitem reliability alpha was .87.

Multi-item scale measuring persuasion attempts toward representatives of institutional investors. Respondents answered separately for each representative with whom they had communicated; for firm-level analyses responses were summed across alters and factor scores generated. Interitem reliability alpha was .88.

Measured as the number of directors who were not full-time employees divided by the total number of board members. Hypothesized effects on change in the outsider ratio were tested using simultaneous equations estimating change in the number of outside directors and change in the number of inside directors separately.
Dichotomous variable coded one if the board-chair position was reallocated from the CEO to an independent director during the two-year period after the time of the survey.

variable_name: creation of an independent board nominating committee
description: Dichotomous variable coded one if the board had a nominating committee composed exclusively of outsiders two years after the time of the survey and either did not have a nominating committee in the previous year or had a committee that included one or more insiders.

Measured as annual total direct compensation, including CEO salary, short-term bonus, and the value of long-term incentive grants made in a particular year. The natural log transformation of total direct compensation was used in the models. Stock option grants were valued using the Black-Scholes method, and other long-term grants were valued at the market price on the date of grant.
Measured as the proportion of total direct compensation consisting of long-term incentive pay.
Measured with the entropy measure of corporate diversification, which the authors note has been shown to have good construct validity relative to alternative measures.

The extent of the connections that the focal actor maintains with partners that, in turn, have some level of interconnectedness, built from Burt's (1992) constraint indicator. Higher constraint values indicate higher interconnectedness in the firm's partner network, i.e., absence of structural holes. The variable is reverse-coded for ease of interpretation, so higher values of structural holes indicate greater nonredundancy (greater structural holes) and lower values indicate greater redundancy.
time_window: network constructed over two-year moving periods (1992-93, 1993-94, ...), with each bank's network position measured in the second year of each period

description: Banks' eigenvector centrality, used following Podolny (2001) and Benjamin and Podolny (1999). The indicator belongs to the Bonacich (1987) family of prestige measures and captures not only the connectedness of the focal actor but also the connectedness of its partners. It is usually computed using valued sociomatrices; banks obtain higher eigenvector centrality by being connected to a group of partners that have many well-connected, powerful partners of their own.
time_window: network position measured in the second year of each two-year moving period

description: The dollar value of the M&A deals an investment bank advised on, used as an indicator of revenue-generation ability. The dollar value of each offering during a year is allocated among the members of the syndicate that advised on the deal: a bank advising alone receives 100 percent of the offering's dollar value, while deals involving multiple investment banks in an advisory team are split equally among team members, which interviewees indicated was the general rule for distributing advisory fees and league table credit. A log of deal values was taken to smooth the distribution of the variable.
time_window: annual, per year of deal activity

description: Binary variable that equals one if a new firm receives a corporate investment in a funding round and zero if it does not. Investment partners were coded as corporate if they provide equity (loans and public offerings excluded) and are non-financial firms; subsidiaries of banks and insurance companies were excluded. Both U.S. and foreign corporate investments were captured.

The new firm's financial resource need was measured by the funding round amount in thousands of U.S. dollars, adjusted for inflation with the producer price index and then logged to mitigate skewness. Entrepreneurs determine the size of a funding round by trading off capital requirements against unnecessary ownership dilution.

Manufacturing resource need was measured by the capital intensity of the industry, because new firms in highly capital-intensive industries are likely to require greater manufacturing assets to commercialize their products. The measure is the average ratio of fixed assets to sales in each industry yearly, collected from Compustat at the 4-digit SIC level.

Marketing resource need was measured by the advertising intensity of each industry, because high advertising intensity implies that product commercialization is marketing-intensive and requires the joint exploitation of marketing resources and new technology. The measure is the average ratio of advertising expenditures to sales in each industry yearly, collected from Compustat at the 4-digit SIC level.

The percentage of product inventions for which patents are considered an effective protection mechanism in a particular industry, taken from the Carnegie Mellon Survey of industrial R&D. The survey data are time-invariant and measured at the three-digit SIC level; three-digit values were used for the corresponding four-digit sublevels of each venture.

The percentage of product inventions for which trade secrets are considered an effective protection mechanism in a particular industry, taken from the Carnegie Mellon Survey of industrial R&D. The survey data are time-invariant and measured at the three-digit SIC level; three-digit values were used for the corresponding four-digit sublevels of each venture.

Timing defense was measured by the investment round (e.g., first, second, etc.), logged to reduce skewness. Investment round reflects the venture's maturity and the commercial and technical progress that determines its ability to advance to the next round.

variable_name: Manufacturing and marketing resource need (industry capital intensity and advertising intensity)
description: Complementary resource need was measured with two industry-level variables: capital intensity (average fixed assets to sales in the industry year) for manufacturing need, and advertising intensity for marketing need. Alliance intensity measures from SDC data were used as alternative measures.

A modification of the clustering coefficient that takes into account the strength of ties between technology classes. For each node the sub-network of its ties and the ties between its neighbors is identified, and integration with neighboring nodes outside its cluster is calculated as the ties that involve out-of-cluster nodes divided by the maximum possible number of ties. The level of decomposability for the entire network is then measured as one minus the weighted sum of the integration for each node, with the percentage of patents that belong to each node as the weight. Couplings between technology classes are computed with Jaccard's coefficient from the firm's patents in years t-3 to t-1.

The number of citations that the firm's patents in year t received in subsequent years until 2002. The frequency with which a patent is cited is treated as a proxy of its usefulness in driving technical change, and the date of application rather than the date of grant is used.

The coupling matrix for each firm at time t is compared with the coupling matrix at time t + 3, ensuring no common patents between the two matrices. Change in structure is the weighted number of technology class pairs that had a significant change in coupling between the two periods, where a significant change is a change in coupling that exceeded one quartile (e.g., from the first quartile to the third or fourth, or from the second to the fourth). The weight equals (pi + pj)/2 + (pi' + pj')/2, where pi and pj are the percentages of patents in classes i and j at time t and pi' and pj' at t + 3. The variable was logged.

A dummy variable indicating whether a new winery had founders with non-local wine industry pre-founding experience, i.e., prior formal winemaking education or wine industry employment in a foreign country. Information was supplied by Daniel Rogov, corroborated with archival sources, and checked against the accounts of 32 founders.

A dummy variable indicating whether a new winery had founders with prior wine industry employment in Israel. Sources of local experience distinguish employment in local kosher wineries, employment in local non-kosher wineries, and experience as grape growers. It was built from Rogov's information, corroborated with archival sources and founder accounts.

An indicator variable set to one when a winery was established as a non-kosher wine producer, based on Rogov's annual directories, which indicate whether a winery produces kosher or non-kosher wines; the two states of the dependent variable are non-kosher and kosher at founding.

The natural logarithm of the number of bottles produced in each year's vintage, as reported by Rogov (2004, 2005, 2006, 2007). Each directory reports systematic current-vintage size information as well as sporadic prior-vintage size information.

A producer-level quality rating that ranges from one to five stars, where five stars denote 'a world class winery, regularly producing excellent wines' and one star indicates that a producer's wines are 'hard to recommend.' The ratings come from Rogov's annual directories and rest on more than 4,000 wine reviews conducted, whenever possible, in blind tastings.

variable_name: lead VC–potential syndicate partner geographic distance (i–j link)
description: Logged distance in miles between the lead venture capitalist and the potential syndicate partner. Venture capitalists were assigned to precise locations by the latitudes and longitudes of the zip codes of their mailing addresses; for firms operating more than one office, the office closest to the target company was assigned as the location for that deal. Distances were calculated using spherical geometry to account for the curvature of the surface of the planet.

variable_name: lead VC–potential syndicate partner industry distance (i–j link)
description: Distance between the investment profiles of the lead VC and the potential syndicate partner, computed as the sum of squared deviations between the proportions of investments each firm made over the preceding five years across ten venture capital investing categories. The resulting measure ranges from zero, for two VC firms with identical investment patterns, to two, for firms with no overlap in their investing patterns.

variable_name: co-investment tie (lead VC i–syndicate partner j in target company z)
description: Binary dependent variable for the presence or absence of the ijth link in target company z, that is, whether lead VC firm i chose syndicate partner j to participate in the setting.
