The variable was highly correlated with membership in an exclusive social club, and there was a high level of agreement (93 percent) with a survey question on class background.

Survey scale gauging the extent to which the outside director engaged in flattery toward a fellow director during the prior twelve months, adapted from Westphal and Stern (2006, 2007). Some items ask directly about ingratiatory intent and others gauge intent indirectly through exaggerated or overstated compliments. Factor analysis with promax rotation produced two factors as expected, with an alpha of .89 for the flattery scale, and factor scores were estimated using the Bartlett method.

Survey scale gauging the extent to which the outside director expressed agreement with a fellow director in an attempt to gain favor during the prior twelve months, adapted from Westphal and Stern (2006, 2007). Items include direct questions about intent and questions about expressing agreement in ways that exaggerate the respondent's opinion. Factor analysis with promax rotation produced two factors, with an alpha of .91 for the opinion conformity scale, and factor scores were estimated using the Bartlett method.

Multi-item survey scales assessing the extent to which the outside director engaged in each of the sophisticated forms of flattery toward a fellow director during the prior twelve months. Scales included a variety of response formats and some counted the number of times a behavior occurred. Confirmatory factor analysis showed items loading on the same factor as expected, with alphas ranging from .87 to .95, and factor scores were estimated using the Bartlett method.

Multi-item survey scales assessing the extent to which the outside director engaged in each of the sophisticated forms of opinion conformity toward a fellow director during the prior twelve months. Each scale used a variety of response formats, and some items asked for counts of occurrences. Confirmatory factor analysis showed items loading on the same factor as expected, with alphas ranging from .87 to .95, and factor scores were estimated using the Bartlett method.

Dichotomous measure indicating whether the focal outside director was appointed to a particular board where a fellow director served on the nominating committee at the time of the survey. Appointments were examined at the 2500 largest U.S. industrial and service firms for which data were available and over the two-year period following the survey.

A set of dichotomous variables operationalizing the outside director's background: one variable coded 1 if the individual had previously held a position in sales, a second coded 1 if the individual had previously been employed as a lawyer, and a third coded 1 if the individual had previously held an elected office at the state or federal levels. The measures were developed from archival data sources and agreed closely with survey responses about vocational background.

A dummy variable coded 1 if the individual was listed in the Social Register and/or attended an exclusive preparatory ('prep') school, with exclusivity designations taken from prior research. The variable was highly correlated with membership in an exclusive social club, and there was a high level of agreement (93 percent) with a survey question on class background.

Measured as the amount of overlap between the fund vector and the hypothetical average, or central tendency vector, for the fund's primary style category. Each fund is represented as a vector of 33 binary indicators corresponding to its strategic focus and investment approach attributes, and the hypothetical fund is generated by averaging across the funds of a given primary style in a given quarter. Similarity is computed with a Dice coefficient, where p equals the number of attributes present for both the focal fund and the average fund, and a and b equal the number of attributes present in one but not the other. The resulting value is bounded by zero and one and is treated as dynamic, responding to the entry and exit of other funds in the reference style.

Raw, net-of-fees percentage returns of the fund in the preceding quarter. Following convention, R is split into two variables: in the positive returns variable, observations having negative returns are set to zero; in the negative returns variable, observations having positive returns are set to zero. This adjustment accounts for the potential nonlinear association between returns and capital flows around the point of zero returns, and positive coefficient estimates are expected for both returns variables.

Increases, by way of additional investment, and decreases, by way of capital redemption or divestment, in the amount of invested capital in a fund. Calculated as the intertemporal change in total net assets (TNA) above and beyond what can be attributed to returns (R); flows are assumed by construction to be realized at the end of each period, and periods are quarters. FLOW has a theoretical lower bound of -100 percent, corresponding to all investors redeeming all capital allocated to the fund.

The annual purchase cost of raw material divided by the volume of grapes, for each house in a given year. The authors use it as a proxy for the average price of grapes because houses do not report grape costs separately and other raw materials are commodities that do not vary in price between houses.

Binary variable coded 1 if the CEO is a descendant of the founder by either blood or marriage, and 0 otherwise. Data were obtained from firms' corporate websites and cross-checked with the French Who's Who and the Guide Curien de la Champagne.
The number of Champagne houses in the village relative to the village's population (measured in hundreds). Location data for each house were collected from the Guide Curien de la Champagne.
Coded 0 if the house was founded before 1960; otherwise, the variable takes the value of year of entry minus 1960. The cut-off point reflects the time when the industry took its present form.

Binary variable coded 1 if the house belongs to a larger corporate group and 0 if it operates independently. Data were tracked using DIANE and the French Registry of Trade & Companies, with cross-checks against corporate websites.
Binary variable coded 1 if the group that owns the house is listed on the Paris stock exchange and 0 otherwise. Data were tracked using DIANE and the French Registry of Trade & Companies.

For each house-year, the total number of supermarket brands the house supplied in that year; the authors took the natural logarithm of this variable because its influence on price is not expected to be entirely linear.

The cumulative increase in the number of winemaking subsidiaries a house owned outside of France between 1998 and 2007. Only subsidiaries dedicated to production, not mere distribution, were included.

The cumulative number of hectares of vineyard purchased by each house in Champagne during the sample period (1998-2007). The measure excludes vineyards owned for historical reasons, as recent purchases are the norm violation.

variable_name: norm violations by buyer (set of characteristics and actions)
description: Local norm violations were measured as a set of house characteristics and actions that growers viewed as violations, identified through 43 industry interviews: not family-run (family CEO), location outside traditional villages (village density), relative newcomer, ownership by a corporate group, ownership by a listed group, supplying supermarket brands, foreign winemaking subsidiaries, and vineyard acquisition. Each was entered as a separate variable.
scale: set of binary and count variables

variable_name: niche width (natural log of number of genres)
description: Niche width is the total number of distinct genres under which each film was classified across IMDB, RottenTomatoes and Showbizdata. Genres not recognized by all three sources and not clear subgenres were excluded, leaving 17 common genres. The natural log of this term is used because its distribution is skewed to the right-hand side.

variable_name: number of reviews by professional critics (ln)
description: Audience size at the professional critic level is the number of reviews published in major media outlets, gathered from RottenTomatoes.com. Analyses predicting the number of reviews focused on critics whose reviews included numerical ratings of the film's quality. The natural log of the number of critics who reviewed each film is estimated by tobit regression, with the possible range left-censored at zero.

The number of film aficionados who rated a film is treated as a proxy for the size of the consumer audience each film attracted. Registration at IMDB is free of charge and registered users can enter ratings for any of the films listed. Because of high skewness in values, the natural log of the count of votes is modeled.
time_window: any time during the film's exhibition

variable_name: total U.S. box office gross receipts
description: Total U.S. box office gross receipts are treated as a proxy for the size of the consumer audience each film attracted. Information on box office grosses was gathered through the paid subscription area of IMDB.

Professional critics provide numerical ratings of films on a 0-10 scale; the overall appeal of each film to critics is assessed through the average of its ratings among critics. The variable is estimated by tobit regression and is both left- and right-censored, varying from 0 to 10.

Ratings among IMDB voters are on a 1-10 scale, and the overall appeal of each film to this audience is assessed through the average of its ratings among IMDB voters. The variable is estimated by tobit regression and is both left- and right-censored, varying from 1 to 10.
time_window: any time during the film's exhibition

variable_name: audience consensus on fit (genre consensus score)
description: Consensus on a film's fit with targeted genres is measured as the average pairwise similarity between each archival source that listed the film. Similarity is measured with Jaccard's coefficient, the proportion of binary classifications that match between two sources, excluding classifications missing from both. For films listed in only two sources the measure is the pairwise similarity between those two sources, and films listed in only one source are assigned a value of 0. For the 949 films the consensus scores range from 0 to 1, with a mean of 0.619.

Composite external individualism percentage score. For each externally relevant measure a percentage was computed as the number of individualistic codes divided by the total number of responses on that measure, and the composite sums these percentages across measures so that each measure is given equal weight. When a response received more than one orientation code each code was weighted equally, and responses not coded for identity orientation remained in the denominator.

Composite internal individualism percentage score, computed as the number of internal individualistic codes divided by the total number of responses on each internally relevant measure and summed across measures with equal weight per measure. Responses not coded for identity orientation are kept in the denominator and multiple codes on one response are weighted equally.

Composite external relational identity orientation percentage score, computed as the number of relational codes divided by the total number of responses on each externally relevant measure and summed across measures with equal weight per measure. Responses not coded for identity orientation are kept in the denominator and multiple codes on one response are weighted equally.

Composite internal relational identity orientation percentage score, computed as the number of relational codes divided by the total number of responses on each internally relevant measure and summed across measures with equal weight per measure. Responses not coded for identity orientation are kept in the denominator and multiple codes on one response are weighted equally.

Composite external collectivistic percentage score, computed as the number of collectivistic codes divided by the total number of responses on each externally relevant measure and summed across measures with equal weight per measure. Responses not coded for identity orientation are kept in the denominator and multiple codes on one response are weighted equally.

Composite internal collectivistic percentage score, computed as the number of collectivistic codes divided by the total number of responses on each internally relevant measure and summed across measures with equal weight per measure. Responses not coded for identity orientation are kept in the denominator and multiple codes on one response are weighted equally.

Industry dummy distinguishing legal services firms, the professional service context, from non-alcoholic beverage companies, the production-based context. Legal services was chosen because of the array of client types to which law firms cater, and non-alcoholic beverages because many companies specialize in agricultural products, some organized as supplier-owned co-ops.

Classification of law firms by the type of clients they primarily serve, distinguishing firms serving businesses, those serving individuals and families, those serving nonprofits, public agencies, and citizens' groups, and firms serving multiple client types. Client type was entered as dummy variables and planned contrast analyses were performed using dichotomous predictor variables for each contrast.

Dummy distinguishing production-based beverage companies structured as cooperatives from those structured as non-cooperatives. Only three co-ops were in the sample, so the authors caution that all co-op-related results should be viewed with caution.

A purity score was first created for each external and internal identity orientation from the composite percentage scores; possible values ranged from 0, where the corresponding orientation received the maximum possible composite percentage score while the other two received the lowest possible score, to 300, where it received the lowest score while the other two received the maximum, with lower values indicating greater purity on a given orientation. Purity z scores were then calculated for each identity orientation, and the lowest of the three external z scores and the lowest of the three internal z scores were taken as indices of external and internal purity. The printed formula is garbled and cannot be reproduced exactly.

The price of the admission fee charged for a regular adult who wishes to visit a temple. The ticket price was coded as zero if the temple did not sell tickets at all; otherwise prices were found on three online crowd-sourced review websites and triangulated using other online sources, official price statements, or a call to the temple's box office. During the observation period, admission fees ranged from zero to U 233 at the 141 temples studied.

A dummy variable indicating substantial increases in admission fees that rise 25 percent or more over those of the previous year or in which the absolute growth level exceeds U 15. A panel of ten informants agreed that such a change can be regarded as substantial.
A dummy variable indicating substantial decreases in admission fees that drop 25 percent or more below those of the previous year or in which the absolute decrease in price exceeds U 15.
A dummy variable indicating that a temple has no admission fee in a year. Being free to the public is described as the ultimate goal of the Free Entrance Movement.

A dummy variable indicating that a previous fee-collecting temple abandoned the admission fee in a year. The authors model the abandonment of admission fees with survival analysis using a risk set that included all temples that had charged admission in the previous year.

variable_name: first principal component of non-admission-fee-related indicators (PC1)
description: A principal component analysis of six non-admission-fee-related indicators of temple commercialization; the first principal component explains 47 percent of the total variance and is used as the measure of commercialization. Its correlation with the admission ticket price is .74.

variable_name: ranking of the GDP growth rate
description: The ranking of the GDP growth rate in the county (or equivalent unit of jurisdiction) in which a temple was located in the previous year. The GDP growth rate was calculated as the change in GDP per capita from the previous year; the county's growth rate was then standardized by subtracting the mean value of all county-level jurisdiction units within the same prefecture city in the previous year and dividing the difference by the standard deviation.

variable_name: strength of the Free Entrance Movement
description: Measured as the number of nationally prominent temples that did not charge admission fees in the previous year in the province where a focal temple was located.

variable_name: political ties to the central government
description: A dummy variable that equals 1 if a temple's abbot was a member of the NPC or CPPCC at the central government level in the previous year. The data were coded from temple and Buddhist websites as well as websites dedicated to individual temples.
Measured as the percentage of people in a prefecture city's total population that had used the Internet in the previous year, collected from the China City Statistical Yearbook.

A compound measure created from the full RGB and five-cluster color information of each cover image. Its first component, Weighted saturation, is the average color saturation of the image's clusters weighted by their pixel size; its second component, Color entropy, is a Shannon-type measure of the proportion of occurrences of each RGB vector in the image. The measure is a linear combination of the two components and simultaneously captures the intensity and distribution of colors in the cover image.

variable_name: Median non-black metal image colorfulness per year (lag)
description: The median cover image colorfulness per year for non-black metal bands, lagged two years to allow time for cover images to diffuse and influence the production of subsequent releases. These variables measure the extent to which past choices of the reference group influenced the current aesthetic choices of black metal bands.

The measure takes the average of the two darkest clusters and the average of the two brightest clusters of the image and calculates the degree of difference on luminance between them. Group-based contrast controls for the size of different clusters by aggregating small clusters with larger ones on the basis of proximate luminance levels.

variable_name: Median non-black metal image contrast per year (lag)
description: The median cover image contrast per year for non-black metal bands, lagged two years to allow time for cover images to diffuse and influence the production of subsequent releases.

variable_name: News articles stigmatizing Norwegian black metal per year (lag)
description: The measure counts the number of major news articles per year denouncing black metal during the observation period in Norway. To ensure the measure reflects the public outcry and social pressure on the genre, the search results were filtered using the keywords 'Satanist,' 'arson,' and 'black metal' together; the variable is lagged.

variable_name: Number of commercial Norwegian black metal releases per year (lag)
description: A measure of the number of commercial Norwegian black metal releases per year, used as an indicator of the degree to which a genre is becoming acceptable or prevalent in the record industry and in heavy metal. It captures two processes at the same time: increasing legitimacy and sales and increasing competition; the variable is lagged.

An indicator that distinguishes bands that draw on different genres in their music from those that perform what is perceived as pure black metal. It was calculated from user-generated classifications of bands and takes the value of 1 if the band is a pure black metal band and 0 if it is a hybrid.

Funded ideas are classified according to whether they were developed by LU studies or by other, more traditional divisional processes. All LU teams employed an identical LU process taught with identical coaching materials, while non-LU teams used informal internal methods and never reported collecting information from lead users.

variable_name: LU vs. non-LU method of major product line development
description: Major product lines are classified by whether they were generated by LU methods or by non-LU methods. During the 1997-2000 period the divisions studied produced five major product lines using LU methods and two using non-LU methods; the 1950-2000 comparison sample of non-LU major product lines contains 21 cases.

variable_name: New Product Idea Description Form items (projected annual sales in Year 5 and related idea attributes)
description: A New Product Idea Description Form was built from measures used in previous academic research (novelty of ideas, originality/newness of customer needs, potential for proliferating into an entire product line; company sales/market share in year 5 and probability of business success; global market potential) supplemented with items in general use within 3M, and was pretested with 3M staff. All projected sales data were deflated by a 25% sales-forecast deflator chosen in consultation with 3M management. LU ideas averaged $146 million in projected Year 5 annual sales versus $18 million for non-LU ideas.

variable_name: Sales in Year 5 of the major product line
description: For major product lines commercialized in 1994 or later (five LU and two non-LU major product lines) five-year sales forecasts were deflated by 25% in line with 3M historical forecast error experience; for major product lines commercialized before 1994 the figure is actual historical sales. All sales data were converted to 1999 dollars using the Consumer Price Index. Average Year 5 sales were $146m for LU major product lines (n = 5) and $62m for non-LU major product lines (n = 16).

variable_name: rate of major product line generation per four-year period
description: The number of major new product lines introduced by the divisions studied is counted on a four-year rolling basis across 1950-2000. The average rate over the half-century was 1.64 major product lines per four-year period; the highest rate achieved was seven major product lines in the 1997-2000 period during which the LU process was implemented, five of them generated by LU methods.
level: four-year period in the divisions studied

variable_name: quality of fit items (distribution channels, manufacturing capabilities, divisional strategic plans)
description: The last three items in Table 1 address organizational fit: the quality of fit of the idea with existing divisional distribution channels, with divisional manufacturing capabilities, and with divisional strategic plans. The authors report no statistical difference between LU and non-LU ideas on these items. The text does not state the response scale of these items.

variable_name: organizational 'fit' dimensions of major product lines
description: The last three rows of Table 4 compare LU and non-LU major product lines on dimensions of organizational fit, using items noted in the table as measured on a 10-point rating scale where 10 = high and 1 = low. The authors reject the hypothesis of a significant difference between LU and non-LU major product lines on these dimensions.

variable_name: protectability by patent or other intellectual property protection
description: A single item is used to test whether ideas generated by the LU method are less protectable by patents or other means of intellectual property protection than ideas generated by other methods. The authors report they cannot reject the null hypothesis of equality.

variable_name: protectability of major product line ideas by patent or other intellectual property protection
description: Table 4 is used for an additional test of whether ideas for major product lines generated by LU methods are significantly less protectable by patent or other means of intellectual property protection than those generated by non-LU methods; the authors reject this hypothesis.

variable_name: person days and total cost per funded project
description: An audit of idea development time shows that generation of a funded LU idea consumed 154 (sd = 82) person days on average versus 60 (sd = 43) person days for an average non-LU idea. Using internal 3M data for average costs of professional development personnel, total cost was approximately $100,000 per funded LU project (including LU training costs) versus $30,000 for non-LU projects; after accounting for the different probability of success, 3M pays about $80,000 more on average for a successful LU project.

The annual percentage of new entrants is the ratio of the number of entrants (net of exits) to the total number of competitors in any year. New Firm Entry between commercialization and the year prior to sales takeoff is computed as the average of the annual values during that period; values for other periods are defined similarly.
time_window: commercialization to the year prior to sales takeoff

description: An exponential time trend is fitted to the annual price series for each innovation, and the measure of changes in Price is the estimated exponential coefficient theta, which is independent of takeoff times. Annual prices were deflated by the Consumer Price Index for consumer products and the Producer Price Index for industrial products to correct for inflation.

Takeoff times are identified with a statistical procedure based on a generalized version of discriminant analysis, which partitions the annual percentage change in sales into three categories (pre-takeoff, in-between, post-takeoff) and optimally classifies the in-between years on the basis of mean values. The calculated takeoff times were validated against published histories of the product innovations.

Total number of citations a patent receives from the time it is granted till the end of 1996, used as an indicator of impact on future knowledge creation. These citations are received from the entire universe of patents that includes the sample of 15,345 patents used in the paper.
time_window: from grant date to the end of 1996

description: A recency measure computed from the prior art cited on the front page of the patent. The median age is the median difference between the grant date of the patent and that of the U.S. patents referenced in the patent; this median age was then transformed by subtracting it from 100 so that the minimum value of 0 years represents the oldest possible knowledge and the maximum value of 100 years represents the most recent knowledge.
time_window: grant date of the patent and of the cited U.S. patents

description: A time spread measure based on the patents cited, measured as the interquartile range of knowledge used in a patent. It is computed as the difference between the grant dates of the lower quartile and the upper quartile of the age distribution of the cited patents.
time_window: grant dates of the cited patents

description: The dependent variable is the incidence rate of new firm formation per patent-year. Firm formation was defined as occurring in a given year if the invention was licensed to a for-profit firm that did not exist as a legal entity in the previous year; only the initial start-up patents were counted as leading to firm formation, so a later license by an already existing start-up was not counted. Each patent was observed from its year of issue through 1996, and the 1,397 patents led to 401 firm formation licensing efforts.
time_window: each patent observed from its year of issue through 1996

description: Measured as the natural log of the number of years since the USPTO established the three-digit patent class.

Measured by the Levin et al. (1987) item 'designing products for specific market segment' under the heading 'to what extent have the following technological activities been engaged in consistently and repeatedly in this line of business?' The item is measured on a Likert scale ranging from one to seven, with one equal to 'of no importance in this line of business' and seven equal to 'very important in this line of business.' Line of business mean scores were used.

A four-item, evenly weighted scale derived from Levin et al. (1987). Two items concern production processes ('patents to prevent competitors from duplicating the process' and 'patents to secure royalty income') and two concern products ('patents to prevent competitors from duplicating the product' and 'patents to secure royalty income'). All four items were measured on a seven-point Likert scale from one equals 'not at all effective' to seven equals 'very effective.' Across the 129 lines of business for which scores were available the scale had a Cronbach's alpha of 0.78.

A two-item, evenly weighted scale derived from Levin et al. (1987): 'superior sales or service efforts' as a means of capturing and protecting the competitive advantages of new or improved production processes, and the same item for new or improved products. Both items were measured on a seven-point Likert scale from one equals 'not at all effective' to seven equals 'very effective.' Across the 129 lines of business for which scores were available the scale had a Cronbach's alpha of 0.65.
Measured with the subconstruct of hierarchy of authority, a five-item scale found to be reliable and valid; Cronbach's alpha is 0.71. Items were measured on a seven-point scale.
scale: seven-point scale (1 = strongly disagree to 7 = strongly agree)

description: Measured with a five-item formalization scale; Cronbach's alpha is 0.74. Items were measured on a seven-point scale. The appendix lists four of the items.
scale: seven-point scale (1 = strongly disagree to 7 = strongly agree)

description: Measured with a five-item scale adapted from Jaworski and Kohli (1993) that measured the extent to which employees were networked to various levels of the hierarchy in their organizational unit; Cronbach's alpha is 0.78. Items were measured on a seven-point scale, and one item is reversed.
scale: seven-point scale (1 = strongly disagree to 7 = strongly agree)

description: Six-item measure capturing the extent to which units depart from existing knowledge and pursue innovations for emerging customers or markets; Cronbach's alpha is 0.86. Items were measured on a seven-point scale.
scale: seven-point scale (1 = strongly disagree to 7 = strongly agree)
time_window: measured in the 2003 survey, approximately 10 months after the first survey

description: Six-item measure capturing the extent to which units build on existing knowledge and meet the needs of existing customers; Cronbach's alpha is 0.80. Items were measured on a seven-point scale.
scale: seven-point scale (1 = strongly disagree to 7 = strongly agree)
time_window: measured in the 2003 survey, approximately 10 months after the first survey

description: A unit's profitability divided by its target profitability, both ascertained through internal corporate records. The profitability-achieved rate was averaged over a one-year period to guard against random fluctuations in the data.
time_window: 2003 up to one year after the measurement of exploratory and exploitative innovation

description: A five-item measure that tapped into the rate of change and the instability of the external environment; Cronbach's alpha is 0.87. Items were measured on a seven-point scale. The appendix lists four of the items.
scale: seven-point scale (1 = strongly disagree to 7 = strongly agree)

description: A four-item scale measuring the extent to which a unit's external environment is characterized by intense competition reflected in the number of competitors and the number of areas in which there is competition; Cronbach's alpha is 0.86. Items were measured on a seven-point scale.
scale: seven-point scale (1 = strongly disagree to 7 = strongly agree)

description: Four measures: a set of commonly used categories of service offered to customers, a set of commonly used categories of customer effort, an estimate of the time the salesperson spends with the typical customer who makes a purchase, and an estimate of the length of the training period. Service increases with each category of service and of customer effort, so higher values indicate a less programmable job. The informants' answers to the same question were averaged to produce the four measures for each store, and a single measure for the construct was computed from the first factor score of a common factor model.

Measured by the physical limitations on the observation of salespeople by management: selling space square footage of the store, total number of store employees, and number of salespeople per store supervisor (managers and assistant managers). A single measure for the construct was computed from the first factor score of a common factor model.

Measured by the number of stores in the store chain and by a dichotomous ownership variable, private/family owned vs. public corporation. Both are size measures because, in this setting, outcome based control is commissions, which require extra administration, a particularly burdensome cost in small organizations.

Three secondary source measures: the number of competitors in the San Francisco SMSA by merchandise category, and the failure rates in 1975 and in 1979 respectively by merchandise category. The competition measure captures a major source of uncertainty in retailing; the failure rate measures are more directly tied to the variance in the outcome distribution and to perceptions of risk within the industry.

variable_name: control strategy (behavior based vs. outcome based reward)
description: A dichotomous measure of short-term monetary compensation. Outcome based rewards are pay plans in which at least a portion of the compensation is based upon outcomes, generally sales, for which the employee is personally responsible: commission, commission against draw, and salary plus commission; in this sample most outcome based plans are salary plus commission and the commission contribution is at least 30% of total pay in all cases. Behavior based rewards are those pay plans in which pay is salary or hourly rate.

Return on assets, chosen as one of the most commonly used performance measures in strategic management research; the ratio's inclusion of the venture's asset base effectively measures the income generated for each dollar of asset, so possible size effects are reduced. ROA is preferred to ROE since it controls for the effects of differing amounts of financial leverage. Financial data were either collected directly from the financial statements included in the IPO documents or calculated from them.

Compounded average sales growth over the three years prior to the IPO, used because measures such as ROA are less applicable for new businesses; growth in revenues, especially sustained high growth, is often indicative of technical quality, market acceptance, and the perception of differentiated advantages. Financial data were either collected directly from the financial statements included in the IPO documents or calculated from them.
time_window: three years prior to the IPO

description: Year of incorporation, used to indicate early or late market entry; it was coded from the description of the business sections of the IPO statements. Lower values represent earlier entry into the industry.

Dichotomous variable capturing the strategic advantage pursued: 0 = cost leadership, 1 = differentiation. It was coded from the IPO statements using key phrases; phrases such as offers of superior features identified firms pursuing differentiation, while phrases mentioning cost or price as major competitive factors identified firms pursuing a cost leadership strategic advantage.

Dichotomous variable coded from phrases in the IPO statements describing the target of the firm's marketing, distinguishing firms pursuing a narrow strategic target from those pursuing a broad strategic target. The text does not state which value is assigned to narrow versus broad.

Dichotomous variable for whether cooperative business strategies such as joint ventures, exclusive distributer arrangements, supplier arrangements, etc. were used (0 = no, 1 = yes), coded from phrases in the IPO statements. The definition of cooperative arrangements included collaborative agreements with distributors; technology-related arrangements were coded separately.

Dichotomous variable for whether cooperative technology arrangements, such as R&D contracted externally by sub-contracting firms, joint R&D ventures, cooperative R&D with competitors, or cooperative R&D with key customers or suppliers, were used (0 = no, 1 = yes). Coded from the IPO statements by the two researchers.
Average relative R&D spending, calculated as the ratio of the most recent three year average R&D spending to average sales.

Scale for design-based AMT investment, which focuses on the design of products and processes. It is the average of the investment in the individual technologies included in the scale, and is based on Boyer et al. (1996). Each technology is rated on a scale whose highest possible rating is 7.

Scale for manufacturing-based AMT investment, which focuses on the actual manufacturing and physical transformation of the product. It is the average of the investment in the individual technologies included in the scale, and is based on Boyer et al. (1996). Each technology is rated on a scale whose highest possible rating is 7.

Scale for administrative-based AMT investment, which is used primarily to track operations inputs and outputs. It is the average of the investment in the individual technologies included in the scale, and is based on Boyer et al. (1996). Each technology is rated on a scale whose highest possible rating is 7.

Scale drawn from Ward et al. (1994) that assesses manufacturing involvement in the strategic processes of the business unit. It is computed as the average of five items shown in the Appendix. The scale is used to evaluate whether more proactive manufacturing functions are more likely to invest in AMTs.

Average of two questions on market share growth and sales growth drawn from Swamidass and Newell (1987). Respondents rate their plant's position with respect to competitors on a seven-point Likert scale ranging from 1 = significantly lower to 7 = significantly higher.

Average of three questions drawn from Vickery et al. (1993) that ask respondents to rate their plant's position relative to competitors in terms of return on investment, growth in ROI, and return on sales. Each question uses a seven-point Likert scale ranging from 1 = significantly lower to 7 = significantly higher.

variable_name: two-year lag between 1994 AMT investment and 1996 performance
description: Time lag was operationalized by comparing the relationship of 1994 AMT investment with 1994 performance (no lag) to its relationship with 1996 performance (two-year lag), using the 1994 and 1996 survey waves.
scale: comparison of contemporaneous and lagged models

description: The proportion of founders holding a Ph.D. on a firm's founding team, computed from biographical sketches of founders, scientific advisors and senior executives coded from the IPO prospectuses. About 70% of the founders can be identified from the IPO-prospectus documents and the remaining 30% were identified via search over the Internet. The variable ranges from 0 to 100% of the founding team.

Count of research papers published in ISI-indexed scientific journals by the firm by the fifth year after it was founded, used as an outcome-based indicator of a firm's adoption of the open-science strategy. The advantage of relying on the outcome is that it captures what a firm has actually done, as opposed to symbolic adoptions, though it may be confounded with firms' ability to implement the strategy.
time_window: by the fifth year after founding

description: For each firm, the number of other firms competing in the firm's main technological niche at the time of founding. A firm's main technological niche is the area in which it has the largest number of clinical trials; the density count includes not only the 512 public biotech firms in the data set but also the pharmaceutical and private biotechnology firms in the United States and abroad (a total of 3,728 biotech and pharmaceutical firms).

A structural-equivalence-based measure of the pressure for adopting open science in a firm's institutional environment, computed as a weighted sum over rival firms of an indicator coded 1 if the competitor had already started publishing by the focal firm's founding year. The weight captures structural equivalence between two firms, measured as a Euclidean distance between their shares of clinical trial cases across 34 technological areas, converted into a structural proximity weight.

Measured in terms of an offensive team's choice of play on a fourth down. Coded as a binary variable, 0 for no risk taking (the team punted or attempted a field goal on fourth down) and 1 for risk taking (the team attempted a fourth down conversion by 'going for it').

variable_name: Performance at or below the aspiration level (P_AL)
description: Measured as the difference between the offensive team's score and the aspiration level (the opponent's score plus one point), using a spline function following prior research convention. Equals 0 when performance is above the aspiration level and equals performance minus the aspiration when performance is at or below it. An indicator variable (1 if P_AL and 0 if P_>AL) allowed the curve to jump at the aspiration level rather than forcing the functions on either side to intersect at the same point.

Measured as the difference between the offensive team's score and the aspiration level (the opponent's score plus one point), using a spline function. Equals 0 when performance is at or below the aspiration level and equals performance minus the aspiration when performance is above it.
The aspiration level is the opponent's score plus one point, i.e., the number of points needed to win the game.

Measured in terms of whether the offensive team was experiencing positive momentum in the game at hand (gains through scoring points against its opponent) and the magnitude of that momentum in terms of number of points scored. Momentum was considered to 'start' after two unanswered scoring episodes, such that the magnitude is the number of points earned during the second scoring episode plus all points earned in subsequent scoring episodes of the same trend. Took on a value equal to the magnitude of the momentum when the team was experiencing positive momentum and a value of 0 otherwise; values were log transformed after adding 1.

Measured in terms of whether the offensive team was experiencing negative momentum in the game at hand (losses through its opponent scoring points) and the magnitude of that momentum in terms of number of points lost. Momentum was considered to 'start' after two unanswered scoring episodes, such that the magnitude is the number of points lost during the second scoring episode plus all points lost in subsequent scoring episodes of the same trend. Took on a value equal to the magnitude of the momentum when the team was experiencing negative momentum and a value of 0 otherwise; values were log transformed after adding 1.

Measured in terms of whether the offensive team was experiencing a series of wins upon entering the game at hand and how many games had been won consecutively. Momentum was considered to 'start' after the second win in a row, such that the magnitude indicates the total number of consecutive games won starting with the second game plus all subsequent games of the same trend. Took on a value equal to the number of wins when the team was experiencing a winning streak and a value of 0 otherwise; values were log transformed after adding 1.
time_window: prior games upon entering the game at hand

description: Measured in terms of whether the offensive team was experiencing a series of losses upon entering the game at hand and how many games had been lost consecutively. Momentum was considered to 'start' after the second loss in a row, such that the magnitude indicates the total number of consecutive games lost starting with the second game plus all subsequent games of the same trend. Took on a value equal to the number of losses when the team was experiencing a losing streak and a value of 0 otherwise; values were log transformed after adding 1.
time_window: prior games upon entering the game at hand

description: Measured in terms of whether or not either team had scored any points in the game thus far. Coded as a binary variable, 1 if some points had been scored and 0 if no points had been scored (0-0 score).

variable_name: degree of adoption of the change initiative
description: Degree to which the organization had adopted the change initiative after 12 months of implementation, from a three-item scale in the telephone survey administered to change agents after one year. The first item asked, on a scale of one to five, how far the change agent had progressed toward completing the change project, where one is defining the project for the clinical strategists program and five is institutionalizing the implemented change as part of standard practice in the organization. The second item, 'in my view, the change is now part of the standard operating practice of the organization,' and the third item, 'in my view, the change was not adopted in the organization,' were assessed on a five-point scale from one (strongly disagree) to five (strongly agree), and the third item was reverse coded. Cronbach's alpha for the scale was 0.60, and the research team's joint assessment on the same scale correlated 0.98 with the change agents' responses.
time_window: 12 months after the start of implementation

description: Ego-network name-generator data. Change agents listed alters whose endorsement of the project would significantly increase its chance of success and alters whose active resistance could derail it; alters listed in response to both questions (47% of alters) were coded as potentially influential fence-sitters, and alters listed only in response to one question were coded as endorsers or resistors respectively. Tie strength was measured with the survey item 'How close would you say you are with this person?' on a seven-point scale ranging from 'especially close' to 'very distant,' with four as the neutral point. The measure is the average tie closeness with members of the fence-sitter subgroup. Mean tie strength to endorsers is used as a control variable.
time_window: during the first week of the executive program, prior to implementation

description: Ego-network name-generator data. Alters listed by the change agent only in response to the survey item about individuals whose active resistance to the implementation of the project can derail it were coded as potentially influential resistors. Tie strength was measured with the survey item 'How close would you say you are with this person?' on a seven-point scale ranging from 'especially close' to 'very distant,' with four as the neutral point. The measure is the average tie closeness with members of the resistor subgroup.
time_window: during the first week of the executive program, prior to implementation

description: Two scales developed by Battilana (2011) were used to measure divergence from the institutionalized model of medical professionalism in the NHS. Scale 1 (four items) measures divergence from the institutionalized model of role division among professionals; scale 2 (six items) measures divergence from the institutionalized model of role division among organizations. Each of the ten items was assessed on a three-point rank ordered scale ranging from one (no extent) to two (some extent) to three (great extent). Two independent raters blind to the study's hypotheses coded the change project descriptions collected three months after the start of implementation (kappa 0.90), discrepancies were resolved by consensus, and each project was assigned a score on each scale corresponding to the average of its items. The degree of change divergence is the unweighted average of the two ratings.
time_window: change project descriptions collected three months after the start of implementation

description: Dummy variable that equals one if the bank opens a new branch in the target postal area in the period. Months are used as spells over which entry decisions are examined, and only branch openings in markets where the focal bank does not have a branch are analyzed. Title changes due to acquisitions or mergers of banks are disregarded.

variable_name: MMC with banks in postal area (lagged)
description: Multimarket contact density is computed for each bank-target postal area-month triplet by summing the multimarket contact (number of postal areas the bank comes into contact with outside the target market) of the focal firm with each incumbent in the target market, scaled by the number of incumbents in the target market. To test H1B, the measure is calculated separately for competitors in different strategic groups. A squared term of the measure is also included in the models.

variable_name: Big Four bank branches in postal area
description: The density variable is separated into the component densities of the three strategic groups; the Big Four bank branch count is the number of branches of the large universal banks in the target postal area. Its squared term is also included in the models.

variable_name: own strategic group bank branch density in postal area
description: Density counts are separated by strategic group, so that for each bank the number of branches of banks in its own strategic group in the target postal area is counted separately from the density of other incumbents. The squared density term of each strategic group is also included. Estimates are reported separately for Big Four, Islamic, and Other banks.

variable_name: Islamic bank branches in postal area
description: Number of branches of incumbent Islamic banks operating in the target postal area, used to estimate Islamic banks' hazard of subsequent entry and interacted with the Islamist town dummy in Model 4.5.

Nonstate conventional banks are separated into strategic groups using cluster analytic methods on annual balance sheet data. The variables used are the ratio of credits to total assets, the ratio of consumer credits to all credits, and branch network size, suggested by interviews with bank executives. Hierarchical clustering with average linkage on standardized variables yields three groups: foreign-owned wholesale banks, the four big universal banks, and the remaining small and medium-sized banks; Islamic banks are classified into a separate group.

Dummy indicating that the focal bank is an Islamic bank, used in Model 4.4 in interaction with Big Four bank branch density in the postal area. Islamic and Other bank samples are combined to test whether Islamic banks follow Big Four banks more than Other banks do.

Minimum of the geodesic distances between the target postal area and all other postal areas in which the bank operated a branch in a given month. Each postal area's latitude and longitude were obtained and Vincenty's formula was used to calculate pairwise distances.

variable_name: Share of town in national GDP
description: Centrality of a target market in the resource space is proxied by the share of its town in national gross domestic product. GDP data are available at the level of 81 provinces for 2001 and 2006; the authors extrapolated the ratios to the remaining years and adjusted by the ratio of town to province population.
time_window: annual, extrapolated to all study years

description: Dummy variable coding towns that consistently voted for Islamic political parties. Election outcomes of all municipal government elections held from 1994 to 2009 are used, and towns are coded as Islamist where the total votes received by political parties with a religious message exceeded 20% in all elections. One hundred sixty-seven towns are marked as Islamist.

The number of writing credits the writer has obtained in the previous five years for movies that are produced or distributed by a major studio (major writing credits). Whenever there is more than one writer, the maximum of the writers' credits is taken as that of the team. The raw measure ranges from 0 to 7, and writers with more than four credits are grouped at four.

A dummy indicating that a sale is a spec (that is, a later-stage sale of a complete script) rather than a pitch; 54% of the sales in the analysis sample are specs. Because not all sales indicate whether they are specs or pitches, the information is completed for about 70% of the sales using two complementary sources.

U.S. box office revenues of a movie that is eventually released, available for released movies; the regressions report the performance difference between specs and pitches for different values of the writer's observable quality.
Worldwide box office revenues of a released movie, used as an alternative measure of movie performance in the same regressions as U.S. box office revenues.

The ratio between U.S. box office revenues and the production budget of a released movie, used as an alternative measure of movie performance. Twenty-six movies lack production budget information, and regressions are run including and excluding them.
A variable indicating the writer's association with one of the five biggest agencies in Hollywood. Approximately 40% of the sales are through these five agencies.

A dummy variable indicating whether the movie is released, defined as theatrically released in the United States with positive box office revenue; movies released at film festivals with zero recorded box office revenue are categorized as not released. Overall, 12% of the sales are released, and the release likelihood is significantly higher for specs for all values of the writer's observable quality.

The amount of the front-end payment, the part of the reported price that is roughly the price for two drafts and a polish. Price data are observed for only 56% of the sales; many sales report only the sum of the front-end payment and the credit bonus, often in rough ranges.

Primary measure of the density of patent thickets in a technology area a, based on the count of 'triples' in which three firms own mutually blocking patents. Pairs are established if firm A is on firm B's list of critical references and firm B is on firm A's list; triples are formed if A and B, A and C, and B and C all form mutually blocking pairs in the same period. Critical references are the X- and Y-type references in EPO search reports; the area-year measure is lagged by two periods because patents younger than 18 months are not published.
time_window: current and two preceding years (t-2 to t), lagged by two periods

variable_name: Own (insider) triples Tr_i and rivals' triples Tr_o
description: The count of triples at the level of a technology area is split into a firm level count of the number of triples in which the focal firm itself is involved (insider triples, Tr_i) and the count of triples present in the technology area without the involvement of the focal firm (rivals' triples, Tr_o). Both measures are lagged by two periods.

For each applicant the authors compute the natural logarithm of the cumulative number of patent applications filed at the EPO by the year in which the focal patent is granted, as a proxy for the size of the applicant's patent portfolio.
time_window: cumulative up to the grant year of the focal patent

description: Herfindahl index of the concentration of rivals' granted patents in a technology area a, computed for the patents applied for in the same year ta as the focal patent. It distinguishes 30 technology areas according to the OST-INPI/FhG-ISI technology classification. The firm-area-year level variable measures the strength of the public good effect and is calculated on the basis of the application year rather than the grant year.
time_window: application year of the focal patent

description: Indicator of whether an opposition was filed against the focal granted patent within the statutory period of nine months after the grant date. The reference year is the year in which the patent is granted by the EPO, and technology and firm level measures are calculated relative to this grant year.
time_window: nine months after the grant date

description: Cumulative number of comments customers have left on a project page up to period t. Used directly in the panel models and as the cumulative number of comments up to the period in which a project reaches its funding goal in the cross-sectional IV models. Customers can only comment on projects that they have invested in.
time_window: cumulative up to period t (or up to tF in the IV models)

description: Binary variable that indicates whether a project's final funding amount is greater than or equal to its goal; it equals 1 if the condition is true. The authors use it instead of the continuous ratio of funding to goal because projects tend to be either just successful or completely unsuccessful.
time_window: at the time a project reaches its funding goal or fails (tF)

variable_name: new funding since the previous period (ΔFi,t)
description: The difference between cumulative funding levels in periods t and t-1, that is, the new amount of funding generated since the previous period. It is the dependent variable in all panel models.

Equals 1 if the majority of personal pronouns used in the project description are singular ('I' and 'me'); equals 0 if the majority are plural ('we' and 'us'). Of the projects in the sample, 40% (8,531) were created by individuals.

The number of changes creators make to project descriptions, identified by observing the update timestamp in the HTML code for the project pages; each time the update timestamp moves forward, the description has been changed. Because the timestamp is observed once every 12 hours, it is a lower bound for the number of changes. Used as the cumulative number of changes up to tF in the IV models and as the difference since the last period (0 or 1) in the panel models.
scale: count (cumulative) and binary difference in the panel models
time_window: cumulative up to tF (IV models); since the last 12-hour period (panel models)

description: Weighted distance of commenting customers based on funding experience. For each commenting customer, proximal funding experience is the number of previous investments in the same category as the focal project, divided by the customer's total funding experience; this share is weighted by the customer's share of all comments on the project, funding experience is measured at the time of the customer's last comment, and the weighted proximal experiences of a project's commenting customers are summed and subtracted from 1.
time_window: measured at the time of the customer's last comment on the project, up to period t

description: A dummy variable equal to one for companies that participated in one of the 13 accelerators in the sample and zero for the matched non-accelerator companies. It is the main explanatory variable in the closure, funding, and performance regressions.

Closed is a binary variable with 1 indicating that a company is no longer active and 0 indicating that a company is still operational. A company is coded as inactive if it is indicated as 'closed' on any of the data sources, if the company website cannot be found, or if the company social media accounts or any traces of presence on the internet have not been updated in a year. All other companies are coded as active, including companies that have been acquired.
scale: binary (1 = no longer active, 0 = still operational)

description: For companies with explicit closing dates reported in any of the databases, time-to-close is calculated as the company age when it goes out of business. It is used to estimate how quickly companies go out of business in the Cox proportional hazards model.

The log of the funding amount for company i, used in the ordinary least squares regression estimated only on companies that shut down. Funding is the external funding obtained by the company in U.S. dollars as disclosed on company websites, Crunchbase, or through press releases, and when no funding information is found it is assumed the company has not raised any money.

The funding ratio is defined as the average funding of companies that closed divided by the average funding of companies that were acquired. It indicates whether companies that eventually succeed receive more funding than companies that eventually shut down; a small ratio (<1) means better investments. It is calculated directly for the matched sample.

The patient's main DRG code (DX1) is mapped onto the USNWR specialties using the USNWR crosswalk, and the hospital-specialty is then matched to the USNWR rankings based on the month of admission; because USNWR releases annual rankings in July, the ranking of a specialty is the previous year's ranking for the first half of the year and the focal year's ranking for the second half. The rank is converted to a rank score so that an increase corresponds to an improvement in position, with the top-ranked specialty receiving a value of 50 and the specialty ranked 50th receiving a value of 1.
time_window: ranking matched by month of admission; previous-year ranking before July, focal-year ranking after July

description: The procedure code DRG is mapped onto the USNWR specialties in a similar manner to the main diagnosis, and the hospital-specialty is matched to the USNWR rankings by month of admission. As with the diagnosis rank, the rank is converted to a rank score so that a higher value corresponds to an improvement in position.
time_window: ranking matched by month of admission; previous-year ranking before July, focal-year ranking after July

description: Binary indicator of a bipartite (two-mode) tie between two specialties within a hospital. For a patient with a main diagnosis in a given specialty, the variable is coded 1 for each procedure specialty (excluding the diagnosis specialty) in which the patient had a procedure performed and 0 for the specialties where no procedure was recorded. Up to a maximum of 15 procedures undergone during the patient stay are recorded in the data.

Specialties are split into three groups by rank: those in the top 10, those ranked from 11 to 30, and those ranked from 31 to 50. In the rank category analysis, buckets of ranks are scored with the top bucket (rank 1-10) receiving a score of 4, the next bucket (11-30) a score of 3, the lowest ranked bucket (31-50) a score of 2, and unranked specialties a score of 1.

Specialties are split into high-prestige and low-prestige groups. Cancer, cardiovascular, endocrinology, gastroenterology, and orthopedics are treated as high prestige because they have been consistently found to be above average in both prestige surveys of physicians and average compensation, while gynecology, nephrology, neurology, otolaryngology, pulmonology, and urology are considered low-prestige specialties.

Dummy variable that equals 1 if a candidate was assigned to receive the treatment email emphasizing an extrinsic reward (Cash or Support). The Social treatment, which repeats the intrinsic reward cue that is standard in the agency's outreach materials, serves as the control group. Separate dummies identify the Cash cue (θ1) and the Support cue (θ2) in the regressions estimating each reward form's effect.

Dummy variable indicating that the individual submitted a full application in the second round of the grant competition. It is the dependent variable in the sorting regressions and is interacted with ex ante characteristics from the EOI (Equation (3)) to estimate differential opt-in and opt-out across treatment groups.

Number of money words (e.g., cash, bill, revenue) in the applicant's response to the EOI question 'Explain your venture and what is unique about it', generated with the LIWC software program, which searches over 4,500 words or word stems categorized into over 70 linguistic dimensions. The measure captures the candidate's orientation prior to the intervention.

Prosocial references in the EOI text field captured with the DICTION text analysis software, whose thematic dictionaries contain over 10,000 words; the authors focus on the word lists for 'collectives,' 'cooperation,' and 'exclusion.' The count of 'collectives' words is used as the proxy for social orientation, measured before the intervention.

Dummy variable indicating whether the target beneficiaries belong to a disadvantaged group such as minority groups or persons with disabilities, coded from the full application (as opposed to more general groups such as adults and/or children). In addition, the applicant's main challenge in the next 12 months was coded from a text response as a 'money,' 'support,' or 'social' challenge.

Several proxy measures taken from the full application and from the reviewers' rejection reasons: word count of the responses to two open-ended questions (nonfinancial support/prior recognition received, and main challenges and how support will benefit the venture); readability scores of those two fields (reported for Flesch Reading Ease); the number of days before the deadline the application was submitted, where the deadline was typically 30 days after receipt of the email; whether the application was rejected for being incomplete; and the amount of funding requested from the agency.
time_window: second application round, up to 30 days after the invitation email

variable_name: words on prior nonfinancial support and recognition
description: Word count of the applicant's response to the open-ended full-application question on nonfinancial support received and prior recognition of the candidate's work (for example, having won a prize), used as the measure of self-promoting behavior. Requesting a smaller amount of money than the grant amount is described as one example of attempting to please the evaluators.

Dummy variable indicating whether the full application was successful in obtaining a grant, ascertained from the archival records of the partner organization. The committee of grant managers that reviewed the full applications was blinded to the experiment and applied a standard set of evaluation criteria; 95 of the 431 EOI candidates ultimately received the grant.

variable_name: end-of-grant performance and social impact measures
description: Self-reported measures from the end-of-grant survey administered 12 months after grantees receive the initial grant, covering the economic performance and social impact of the grantee's venture over the prior 12 months. Most questions use Likert-scale response anchors; the response rate was 67%, with 64 of the 95 grantees completing the survey.
time_window: 12 months after receiving the initial grant

description: The main independent variable is the interaction between two dummies: postpublication, equal to one after the publication of the Guide and zero before, and treated, equal to one for restaurants included in the Guide and zero for control restaurants. The interaction coefficient captures how treated restaurants reacted to Michelin's entry compared with control restaurants.
time_window: pre- and post-publication of the Guide (2016 and 2017)

description: A restaurant in the treated group received a prior standing score of one if it appeared at least once in any of the identified prominent local rankings and awards in 2015 or 2016, and zero otherwise. This identified 45 treated restaurants with high prior standing and 38 with low prior standing.

Level of detail provided in menus, measured as the number of words used in the menu divided by the number of dishes in the menu, to facilitate comparison across menus. It is one of the descriptive attributes of menus.

Emphasis on portion sizes, measured as the number of words, divided by the number of dishes, used to characterize the size of portions, using the list compiled by Jurafsky (2014). It is a descriptive attribute of menus.

Mastery of skills, measured as the number of words, divided by the number of dishes, related to cooking techniques, using the list compiled by 'The Professional Chef' from The Culinary Institute of America. It is an authenticity attribute of menus.

Focus on raw materials, measured as the number of words, divided by the number of dishes, related to the provenance and origin of food, using the list compiled by Jurafsky (2014). It is an authenticity attribute of menus.

The average of all dish prices listed as 'main dishes' (or equivalent) in the menu, where changes could potentially imply changes in the restaurant's operations. Because some menus did not include price information, value variables are available for 71 of the 83 treated restaurants and 133 of the 143 restaurants in control 1.

The minimum of all dish prices in the main dishes (or equivalent) section of the menu, where changes are expected to mostly capture signaling behaviors. Available for 71 of the 83 treated restaurants and 133 of the 143 restaurants in control 1.

Dummy equal to one if the firm has experienced a PHA either in year t or within three years prior to it, and zero otherwise, at the firm level; at the firm-therapeutic area level, PHA_ICD equals one if the firm has experienced a PHA in that ICD in year t or in the three years prior to it. Only the first occurrence of a PHA at the indication level is used because the strategy rests on the events being unanticipated.
time_window: year t or within the three years prior to t

description: Dummy equal to one if the firm acquires at least one drug project from other firms in year t and zero otherwise, estimated at the firm-year level and at the firm-therapeutic area (ICD)-year level. The authors focus on whole-project drug acquisitions as replacements for existing products; the additional acquisitions tend to be in the later phases of development (phase II trials and above).

variable_name: InitNum, Suspend Rate, Hold Rate, Late Trial
description: Internal pipeline outcomes at the firm level and the firm-therapeutic area level: InitNum is the number of new projects initiated by the firm in the year; Suspend Rate is the number of suspended projects divided by the total number of active projects in t-1; Hold Rate is the number of temporarily held projects divided by active projects in t-1; Late Trial is the number of new trials initiated for phase II and later projects within a firm's therapeutic area.

R&D expenditures scaled by total assets at the firm-year level, and, in an alternative specification, R&D expenditures scaled by market capitalization. Financial variables are matched from Compustat to the firms in the BMT sample and are winsorized at the 1% level.

Treated firms are split by the portion of company sales affected by the PHA, using drug sales data: HSales denotes affected-drug sales above the median of all treated firms and LSales below it. A second proxy uses whether the affected firm has other recently approved, unaffected products in the PHA-shocked therapeutic area (OtherDrugs) rather than none (OnlyDrug), capturing the ability to partially reallocate slack commercialization capital.

Treated firms are split by the number of active phase III trials the affected firm has at the time of the PHA, with LowP3 denoting firms with relatively weak internal pipelines. As an alternative to the number of phase III trials, the authors build a firm-level score of recent pipeline development performance: the number of new drug launches and of projects that progressed from phase II to phase III over the prior two years, less recent phase II and III failures; a treated firm is classified as winning (losing) if its score is above (below) the median at the time of the PHA.
time_window: prior two years for the performance score; at the time of the PHA

description: Each physician's total monthly payments from drugs in a group k, aggregated from company-to-physician payments for each referenced drug at monthly frequency. Drugs are categorized into three groups: PHA-affected drugs, unaffected drugs from the PHA-affected firm (the 'reallocation group'), and unaffected drugs from unaffected firms (the 'clean group'); the sample is restricted to payments from public companies in the sample to physicians with a long-term promotional relationship tied to an eventual-PHA-affected drug.

Dummy variable equal to one for having participated in a group that received the social skills treatment and zero for being in the control group. Treatment was assigned by randomly selecting half of the participating cohorts of entrepreneurs into the social skills condition.

Entrepreneurs were asked to think about the interactions they had had during the two days of the training program and were given a sheet with a grid of 24 words, half related to collaboration (such as help, trust, friendship, sharing, alliance) and half related to competition (such as grow, dominate, adversarial, beat), and asked to circle five words that best represented these interactions. The measure is a count of the total number of collaborative words selected.
time_window: during the two days of the training program

description: At a structured networking event at the end of the training program each entrepreneur was successively paired with three randomly selected discussion partners and given pen and paper. The handwritten notes from the discussions were scanned, and the total number of words each participant wrote during the three discussions is used as a measure of information exchange.
time_window: during the networking event at the end of the training program

description: In the six-week follow-up survey all participants were asked whether they had spoken over the phone or met in person with any other participants from the same training group after the program had ended, and to name those individuals. The number of relationships formed is the total number of people the entrepreneur had kept in touch with.
time_window: six weeks after the training program

description: Participants were asked to describe the most pressing issue in their business and to select which of five categories it fell into: firm financing, marketing, stock and inventory management, accounting and record keeping, or planning for the future. In parallel, each participant was coded according to whether they used best practices in those five categories using the World Bank list of business best practices. A dyad-level indicator equals one if participant j showed evidence of expertise in the domain in which participant i indicated they wanted to improve. The individual-level measure sums the number of relationships with skill complementarity that each entrepreneur formed.
time_window: six weeks after the training program; pretreatment survey for best practices

description: Using pretreatment data on each entrepreneur's ethnicity, the ethnic concentration of the newly formed relationships is calculated with Herfindahl indexes, a common approach for measuring diversity in egocentric portfolios of relationships. The index ranges between a minimum of 1/N, where N is the number of possible categories represented in the sample, and 1. The minimum value indicates that all relationships were equally distributed among the ethnicities, and the maximum value (1) indicates that all relationships formed were concentrated in one ethnicity. There are five ethnic groups, making the minimum value of the index 0.20.
time_window: six weeks after the training program; pretreatment ethnicity data

description: In each of four surveys (a pretreatment survey at the beginning of the training and three posttreatment surveys at six weeks, six months, and one year after the training) participants were asked about their businesses' profits in the month previous to the survey. Log monthly profit is used as the performance measure; baseline log monthly profits are controlled for in the specification without entrepreneur fixed effects.
time_window: month previous to each survey; baseline, six weeks, six months, and one year after training

description: Citation-weighted patent counts for firm i in industry j at year t. Each one of a firm's patents receives a score equal to one plus the ratio of that patent's citations over the average number of patent citations in the same year and industry, and the citation-weighted patent count is the sum of these patent scores for each firm.

Competition in licensee product markets associated with innovator industry j in year t, constructed in two steps. For each four-digit SIC licensee industry k, the degree of competition is measured from the Lerner index, computed as one minus the average Lerner index of the firms in that industry, where the Lerner index is operating profits net of depreciation divided by sales. The measure is then the weighted average of this degree of competition across licensee product markets associated with innovator industry j, weighted by the fraction of licensing deals made that year between innovator industry j and each licensee product market k. The squared term, Licensee PMC squared, is included in the regression.

The same measure of licensee product market competition as in the innovation analysis, used as the independent variable of interest when explaining the choice between targeted and market-wide licensing and when interacted with targeted licensing in the innovation regressions.

A firm-level dummy variable equal to one under targeted licensing and zero under market-wide licensing for firms that enter just one licensing agreement as licensor in a given year. In the event that a firm enters more than one licensing agreement as licensor in a given year, the variable is the average of these values.

Citation-weighted patent counts for innovator i in industry j and year t, used as the dependent variable when the interaction of licensee product market competition and targeted licensing is examined.

The degree of competition in the innovator product market, measured based on the Lerner index, where the Lerner index is the difference between operating profits net of depreciation, divided by sales. It is included as a control variable in the innovation regressions.

An exploratory factor analysis of the Trust Index employee survey yields four factors; the factor that includes beliefs about the meaning and impact of work and about management clarity is labelled Purpose-Clarity. The firm-year measure is the average of this factor across all survey respondents within a firm-year. The factors are based on a rotated loading matrix that orthogonalizes the measures, so the factor does not capture overall job satisfaction or perceptions of overall management quality.

Indicator variable that takes the value of one if the firm is publicly listed; the omitted group is private firms. Public firms are identified by whether they have a corresponding record in Compustat North America, crosschecked with an indicator within the GPTW survey of the public or private status of the firm.
