The percentage of outstanding shares held by hedge funds, identified by merging the sample with Factset and Thomson Reuters investor identity information.

Calculated for each firm-year as the difference between the percentage of shares held by voting dedicated and transient investors, using the classification of institutional investors of Bushee (1998, 2001). A larger percentage corresponds to greater commitment to the firm.
Indicator equal to one for firms with private equity owners. A firm is coded as PE owned if a private equity firm is identified as an owner in Capital IQ.
Indicator variable for whether the CEO was internally promoted from the lower ranks of the organization; created from GPTW data.
The natural logarithm of the CEO's tenure in the organization; created from GPTW data.

variable_name: Pay gap relative to salaried ranks
description: The ratio of CEO compensation to that of the median salaried worker in the firm.
The total compensation reported for the CEO, taken from Institutional Shareholder Services data.
The number of incentive provisions explicitly tied to margin (cost or profit margin) metrics as reported to the Incentive Laboratory.
The number of incentive provisions explicitly tied to nonmargin metrics, such as sales, growth, or nonfinancial measures, as reported to the Incentive Laboratory.
A composite index of employee benefits provided to the company, calculated from GPTW data.
Indicator variable of whether the company offers an employee stock ownership plan, from GPTW data.
The percentage of total compensation that is variable for salaried employees, from GPTW data.

variable_name: Three proxies of owner commitment (hedge fund ownership, dedicated minus transient institutional ownership, private equity ownership)
description: Owner commitment was proxied by three variables, each entered as its own variable in the purpose regressions: the percentage of shares held by hedge funds (lower commitment), the difference between the percentage of shares held by dedicated and by transient institutional investors under the Bushee classification (higher commitment), and an indicator for private equity ownership among private firms from Capital IQ (lower commitment).

The authors use book synopses to calculate the extent to which an author attempts to reposition. They first calculate each book's predicted position in label space based on its synopsis, then calculate the sum of squared distance of the focal book's synopsis from that of each previous book in the predicted label space and average these pairwise distances. The most common pattern is high similarity to previous books, but a large number of authors also reposition substantially.

Calculated as the mean squared distance between the observed label vector assigned by readers and the label vector predicted based on the producer's synopsis for each book. In the attention and appeal analyses the variable is split at the median into a binary indicator of high versus low label mismatch.

variable_name: audience attention (total count of users who rate a book)
description: Measured as the count of users who rate a book; readers who review a book need not like it but typically have enough awareness and familiarity with the book to evaluate it. The book-level dependent variable in the matched sample models is the logged total count of users who rated each book.
The numerical ratings users assign to books, on a one to five integer star rating scale, aggregated to the mean rating of a book. The mean star rating assigned is 4.09.
The logged count of five-star ratings a book receives, examined alongside the mean rating because this measure distinguishes books with a relatively rare level of positive appeal.

The proportion of a focal book's readers who have had prior experience with the author. For each reader the authors examine whether the reader has completed a book by that same author prior to the focal book; books read earlier do not have to be books published earlier, because the measure focuses on the timing of a user's prior interaction with the author. Approximately 82% of the interactions are from users completely new to the author.

Using the geographic coordinates of entrepreneurs' businesses, the authors calculate the straight-line distance in kilometers between each dyad of participants and convert distance into proximity with an exponential distance decay function, so that the measure ranges from one for peers located at a distance of 0 km and tends toward zero as distance increases. To create a single measure for each entrepreneur they take the average of the proximities of the three assigned discussion peers. The authors also construct a set of alternative measures counting the number of assigned discussion peers whose businesses are located within radii of 1, 2, 3, and 4 km.

A dyad-level variable, defined for each pair of entrepreneurs who were assigned to talk during the networking event. It is equal to one if the entrepreneurs spoke on the phone or met in person since the previous survey and zero otherwise. The variable is defined only for the three posttraining time periods.
time_window: the three posttraining survey waves (six weeks, six months, and one year after the program)

description: The proportion of 27 managerial best practices, defined by McKenzie and Woodruff (2017), that an entrepreneur uses. Following McKenzie and Woodruff (2017), the best practices were operationalized as a series of binary questions, one for each practice, covering the areas of marketing, finance, planning, and stock management.
time_window: baseline and three posttraining survey waves

description: Surveyors asked entrepreneurs for their estimated profits from the previous month. To increase the precision of reported profits, the surveyors also asked them to estimate monthly expenses and sales, which helped triangulate their profits.
time_window: previous month, measured at baseline and each follow-up survey

description: The average of several standardized variables indicative of performance: log sales last month, log sales last month winsorized at the 1st and 99th percentiles, log sales last week, log clients last month, log clients last month winsorized at the 1st and 99th percentiles, log clients last week, and number of loans received from a bank or microfinance institution.
time_window: baseline and three posttraining survey waves

description: Measures the share of a major m's outsourced flights at airport a that are assigned to regional r in the first quarter of 2017. Majors update their flight outsourcing decisions at the beginning of each quarter, so SPC reflects the level of supply portfolio concentration that airline partners took into account in their February 2017 cooperation decisions. The measure varies at the airport level within each major-regional relationship.

Counts the number of slot exchange packages submitted at destination airport a on GDP day d in which regional r reschedules at least one of its flights to make a slot available to major m. It can be thought of as an extensive margin measure of cooperation. The variable is a log(1 + x) transformation of the actual number of cooperation episodes.

Counts the number of flights operated by regional r that are rescheduled in favor of major m as part of slot exchange packages submitted at destination airport a on GDP day d. It measures the intensive margin of cooperation. The variable is a log(1 + x) transformation of the actual number of cooperation episodes.

Counts the number of slot exchange packages in which major m reschedules at least one of its flights to make a slot available to regional r at destination airport a on GDP day d. It can be thought of as an extensive margin measure of cooperation. The variable is a log(1 + x) transformation of the actual number of cooperation episodes.

Counts the number of flights operated by major m that are rescheduled in favor of regional r as part of slot exchange packages submitted at destination airport a on GDP day d. It measures the intensive margin of cooperation. The variable is a log(1 + x) transformation of the actual number of cooperation episodes.

Using DB1B quarterly ticket and coupon data, the authors identify all one-way and roundtrip tickets with one or two layovers on either or both legs of the ticket and keep connecting flight tickets, dropping tickets that begin a passenger's journey. They count the number of connecting tickets per flight sold by each major that were outsourced to each regional partner and departed from each airport. For each major-airport combination, the measure is the difference between the total number of connecting flight tickets the major outsourced to all regionals and the number outsourced to the focal regional r.

variable_name: Patent-Based IUC Dummy and Patent-Based IUC Count
description: Patent-Based IUC Dummy equals one if the focal firm has an IUC patent filed in years t-4 to t and zero otherwise; Patent-Based IUC Count denotes the number of IUC patents filed by the focal firm in years t-4 to t. IUC patents are defined as patents coassigned to both a firm and a university.

variable_name: Paper-Based IUC Dummy and Paper-Based IUC Count
description: Paper-Based IUC Dummy equals one if the focal firm has an IUC paper published in years t-4 to t and zero otherwise; Paper-Based IUC Count denotes the number of IUC papers published with affiliation to the focal firm in years t-4 to t. IUC papers are defined as Chinese publications coauthored by a firm employee and a university staff member.

The output value of new products (revenue from new products) in million RMB in year t+1, entered in natural logarithm form. New products are defined by the NBS as products introduced to the market for the first time in a fiscal year or products recognized as new products by relevant government departments.

The number of product-oriented patents solely applied by the focal firm in year t+1, entered in natural logarithm form; patents also granted to coassignees are excluded. A patent is product-oriented if its title and abstract specify a new product rather than a new process.

The average number of forward five-year citations of product-oriented patents solely applied by the focal firm in year t+1, entered in natural logarithm form (plus one). Forward citations are taken from the Item 56 references listed on the front page of each patent issuance document.

The ratio of a firm's R&D expenditure divided by total assets across all historical years up to year t, used as the primary measure of absorptive capacity. Firm-year observations are split into high and low groups by the sample median, with High Group equal to one if the measure is above the median.
time_window: all historical years up to t

variable_name: Ratio of Backward Citations to Academic Papers
description: The industry-level ratio of patents' backward citations to academic papers divided by total backward citations across all historical years up to year t, used as the primary measure of science dependence; observations are split into high and low groups by the sample median.
time_window: all historical years up to t

description: The weighted average of dummy variables indicating whether universities that have a collaborative relationship with the focal firm up to year t are within a 100-km distance; observations are split into high and low groups by the sample median.

variable_name: Ratio of Commonly Cited Technology Classes
description: A firm's ratio of commonly cited technology class pairs divided by total technology class pairs in the previous five years (from t-4 to t). A technology class X of firm F and class Y of the firm's collaborating university U are commonly cited if they are included in two different patents that are cited by at least one other patent; observations are split into high and low groups by the sample median.
Equals one if the focal firm has an IUC patent filed in years t-4 to t and zero otherwise, as stated in the table notes describing the independent variables used in the moderation tests.

In the Endogenous Bonus treatment, entrepreneurs chose whether to offer a refund bonus after they learned the quality of their project. A project offering a refund bonus, prominently displayed on the investors' decision screens, paid a $1 bonus to a sole investor (who also received back their $1 investment). In the Random Bonus treatment each project was randomly assigned a refund bonus with equal likelihood, independent of the project's quality.

Mean successful funding rate across sessions, where funding success occurs when both investors choose to invest in the project. Reported separately for good and bad quality projects and for the EB and RB treatments.

Each project was either good or bad quality. If both investors invested in a good quality project they earned a $3 return on their $1 investment; if both invested in a bad quality project they each lost their $1 investment. When a project was bad quality, investors received an independent signal that it was definitely bad quality with a one-quarter (25%) likelihood, described as a 'negative report'; for good quality projects they never received any kind of report.

Frequency with which investors chose to invest in a project rather than the outside option; each round an investor made two binary investment decisions, one for each of two projects. The indicated investment frequency excludes the cases where an investor received a negative report that a project was definitely bad quality.

Cumulative number of plays garnered by the songs on a newly released album j by artist i in the 52 weeks since its release on radio station k, where j identifies the chronological position of the album in the artist's career. The variable is normalized to adjust for average time-varying effects, following Deshmane and Martínez-de-Albéniz (2023), and is separated between focal and past plays. The underlying BMAT log of plays is compiled at the artist-week level.

Score given by critic k to artist i's album j upon its release, presented on a 0–100 scale. Album of the Year aggregates critics' responses and ratings from major outlets such as Rolling Stone, Billboard, and Entertainment Weekly; web scrapers collected data on albums reviewed by 75 music-reviewing outlets.

Product differentiation of the focal product from the past profile of the artist in sonic attributes, estimated with the cosine dissimilarity index between the album's attributes and the within-artist reference level R_WithinArtist_ij = θR_ij−1 + (1 − θ)X_ij−1, where θ is a factor of memory decay. Setting θ = 1 gives the best fit for the model with focal album plays and θ = 0.8 for ratings.
Genre-based differentiation of album j from the past profile of artist i; it takes a value between 0 and 1 based on genre overlap between albums j and j − 1 by artist i.

Product differentiation of the focal product from albums released in the year prior and displaying the same genre affiliation as the focal album. Out of this pool the three peer albums that performed best in the market are identified (plays for radio stations, mean ratings for critics), and the average values of their sonic attributes serve as the reference level.
time_window: one year prior to focal album release

description: Sonic-attribute differentiation of the focal product from the dominant design, identified as the three albums with the highest number of plays (or, for ratings, the highest reviewer ratings) released within a year prior to the focal album, regardless of genre. The average values of the artistic attributes of these three albums serve as the reference level.
time_window: one year prior to focal album release

description: Genre-based distinction between the focal album and the dominant design, taking values of 0, 1/3, 2/3, or 1 based on genre overlap between the corresponding albums.
The chronological number of album j in the career of artist i; used to capture the career age of the artist and as a moderator of the differentiation relationships.

variable_name: product differentiation metrics (Delta X_ij) from reference sets
description: Product differentiation was the deviation of a new album's sonic attributes (Spotify audio features) from three audience reference sets, computed as cosine dissimilarity: the artist's own past profile, proximal peers' best-performing albums, and the dominant design of the top albums. Genre-based versions were computed from genre overlap in Deezer data.

Logged value of monthly revenue (in domestic currency units plus one) of firm f in market m for month t. Estimated at the firm-market-month level for all vaccine markets from January 2005 to December 2016.

Logged value of the number of SKUs (plus one) offered by firm f in market m for month t. Product variety is measured objectively using the number of stock-keeping unit (SKU) types a firm offers in the vaccine market; SKUs can differ in dimensions such as vaccine technology (e.g., inactivated vaccine and live attenuated vaccine) or the segment for which a product has been developed (e.g., pediatric versus adult vaccines).

Binary variable set to one for the vaccine markets that witnessed a sudden reduction in supply from the public sector (the markets in which the three suspended PSUs produced vaccines, e.g., BCG, tetanus, polio) and zero for other vaccine markets (e.g., typhoid, influenza). Time periods are demarcated by PreShock (January 2005 to December 2007), DuringShock (January 2008 to February 2010) and AfterShock (March 2010 to December 2016); the main coefficient of interest is the interaction term DuringShock x Treated.

Indicator identifying domestic firms operating in the Indian vaccine markets, with ForeignFirm identifying foreign firms. Equation (1) is estimated separately for the subsamples of domestic and foreign firms.

Firms are classified by the location of their headquarters into politically aligned and not-aligned states, where politically not-aligned refers to states in which the political affiliation of the state government (where the firm is located) differs from that of the federal government. The three-way interaction Treated x DuringShock x DomesticFirm is estimated separately for firms from politically not-aligned and politically aligned states.
time_window: pre- and during-shock periods, and including the aftershock period until December 2010

description: Number of products of a publisher in a market segment in a given release year; the publisher is taken as the focal producer making product portfolio decisions and the measure is restricted to one year to reflect short-lived product cycles. Aggregated to the publisher–segment–year level by taking averages and inverse hyperbolic sine transformed in the baseline regressions.

Retention is proxied by the number of updates to a video game on Steam, because users who own a game are alerted about updates: updates can be downloaded automatically and are prominently shown in the 'what's new' section of a user's game library, whereas users not having the game are not actively made aware of them. Aggregated to the publisher–segment–year level by taking averages and inverse hyperbolic sine transformed.

Segment value is approximated by the price of the game, because prices should be higher in more valuable segments and equilibrium prices increase in the value of the market. Segment-specific prices are averaged to the publisher–segment–year level; the squared term is included to capture the predicted inverted U shape, and both are inverse hyperbolic sine transformed.

variable_name: Share of games without the segment's most popular tag
description: Heterogeneity is measured from user-defined game tags: the authors first determine the most popular tag in each segment-year, excluding the segment itself, and then define heterogeneity as the share of games within a segment-year not having the most popular tag among its first five (most important) user-defined tags. The variable is inverse hyperbolic sine transformed in the baseline regressions.

Frequency of self-inclusive, first-person plural pronouns (we, ours, us) used by the CEO in the presentation and Q&A sections of quarterly earnings conference calls. The count is normalized by the total number of words spoken and averaged across all earnings calls in a given year; the authors use the average from years t and t−1.

Word-embedding measure created by calculating the cosine similarity of word vectors representing the terms 'employee' and 'fair' within a firm's 10-Ks and DEF-14A filings each year. The proximity of the terms employee and fairness in a 300-dimensional vector space is used as a proxy for managerial prosociality.

Indicator that a CEO is external, where a CEO is identified as external if their first year as a CEO is the year that they joined the firm; internally promoted managers are expected to possess stronger prosocial preferences for current employees. External CEOs represent approximately 40% of firm-year observations.

Percentage share of charitable organizations among all of the CEO's external activities. The authors first identify the CEO's involvement in all outside organizations from their 'other activities' listed in BoardEx and then identify whether each organization is categorized by the IRS as a 'Charitable Organization'.

Proxy for exit based on a firm being delisted from Compustat, which indicates that its securities are no longer publicly traded. The authors use the variable dlrsn in Compustat ('Research Co Reason for Deletion') to identify specific reasons for exits; the mean value of Exit in the baseline sample is 3.58%.

Number of divestitures reported in the SDC Platinum database, used as a proxy for partial exits. Divestiture counts exhibit an extreme right skew, so the variable is winsorized at the 99th percentile.

For each four-digit SIC code, the change in imports from China from the previous year divided by initial absorption, where initial absorption is the sum of U.S. industry shipments and Chinese imports minus U.S. exports. The authors follow Acemoglu et al. (2016) but calculate the measure for each year rather than at five-year intervals; the annual median value is 0.28% and the mean value is 14.47%.
time_window: annual change from the previous year

description: Random assignment to one of three between-subject conditions using picture priming with five pictures shown in each condition: high prosociality (pictures conveying high prosocial value), low prosociality (pictures conveying a focus on the self or financial interest), and neutral (pictures unrelated to any specific values or beliefs). The manipulation check used four items adapted from the scale developed by Caprara et al. (2005).

One-shot Dictator Game in which participants divide a pie of $100 between themselves and an anonymous recipient; a person who allocates a greater sum to another is considered to be more prosocial. The game was measured before the manipulation and provides an alternative trait-based proxy of prosocial preferences.
The minimum revenue participants would accept to continue operating a store, asked after the prosociality manipulation in the vignette.

Coded one if the participant chose Location A and zero if they chose Location B for a new store. Location A has revenue of about $70k-$90k with a lower expected revenue ($80k versus $90k) but eliminates the risk of falling below the average exit threshold ($55k) and corresponds to a max-min option; Location B has revenue of about $50k-$130k and corresponds to both max-mean and max-max options.

Extent to which participants expected to feel six guilt-related emotions for employees' loss if they stopped operating the store, rated 1 = 'not at all' to 7 = 'extremely'. The six items draw from the Positive and Negative Affect Schedule-Expanded Form (PANAS-X).
Random assignment to one of two conditions, high prosociality or low prosociality, using the same picture priming as in Experiment 1.A.
The minimum revenue participants would accept to continue operating a store; the short survey measured only the exit threshold.
Participants' expected feelings of guilt for employees' loss if they stopped operating the store, measured as in Experiment 1.A.

Three between-subject conditions varying the harm to employees from stopping operating a store. In the high harm condition all employees of the store would be laid off and no longer covered by company-sponsored medical insurance; in the low harm condition laid-off employees continue to have medical insurance coverage for the next six months or until finding a new job; in the no harm condition the ownership of the store is handed over to another company and all employees are kept without any layoffs. Participants rated how negatively employees would be affected to check the manipulation.
The minimum revenue participants would accept to continue operating a store, asked in the vignette after the harm manipulation.
Participants' expected feelings of guilt from closing the store, measured with the same guilt items used in Experiment 1.

Direct manipulation of prosocial preferences following Hu and Liden (2015). In the high prosociality condition participants were told that they consider employee welfare and financial performance to be equally important and would think about employees' welfare when making tough decisions; in the control condition they were told that they consider financial performance to be the most important and think about their company's financial performance when making tough decisions.

Direct manipulation of the severity of harm: participants were told that once they stop operating a store the ownership would be handed over to another company, with 'all employees will be laid off' in the high-harm condition and 'all employees will be kept without any layoffs' in the no-harm (control) condition. Perceived harm was checked by asking the extent to which employees would be negatively affected (1 = 'not at all', 7 = 'a great deal').
The minimum revenue participants would accept to continue operating a store, measured after both manipulations in the 2 × 2 design.
Choice of the conservative investment option (location with lower expected revenue but no risk of falling below the exit threshold), coded as in Experiment 1.
Participants' expected feelings of guilt for employees' loss if they stopped operating a store, measured as in the earlier experiments.

Completed is a dummy variable that takes a value of 1 for a completed vertical M&A and 0 for an uncompleted vertical M&A. After is a dummy variable that takes a value of 1 for the M&A event year and subsequent years and 0 for the years before the event year. The interaction term Completed x After is used to identify the treatment effect of vertical M&As on measures of innovation as proposed in the hypotheses.
time_window: event year t and subsequent years (After) versus years before the event year

description: The number of truncation-adjusted (eventually granted) patent applications by a firm in a focal year, matched to the acquirer and the target in a vertical M&A by year to generate a measure of patent counts at the acquirer-target-year level. Because of its skewness, the measure is log transformed to create the dependent variable Patent Counts.
time_window: focal year, panel from t-5 to t+5 relative to the M&A event year

description: The number of truncation-adjusted patent forward citations received by all patents of a firm in a focal year, matched to the acquirer and the target in a vertical M&A by year to generate a measure at the acquirer-target-year level. This measure is weighted by the patent counts of the acquirer and the target in the focal year to adjust for differences in the size of their patent portfolios, generating a continuous measure. The weighted measure is then log transformed to reduce its skewedness.
time_window: focal year, panel from t-5 to t+5 relative to the M&A event year

description: Based on Kauffman's NK framework and on patent subclass data following Fleming and Sorenson and Ganco, a patent subclass level measure captures the overall interdependency between a focal knowledge subcomponent and other subcomponents, and a patent level measure captures a patent's average interdependency of its subcomponents adjusted by the number of required knowledge subcomponents. The patent level measure is aggregated to the firm-year level by averaging over all patents of a firm in a given year. The acquirer-target-year level dependent variable is the average of the firm-year measure for the acquirer and the target, weighted by their patent counts in the focal year.
time_window: focal year, panel from t-5 to t+5 relative to the M&A event year

description: Constructed by directly following Katila and Ahuja (2002), the measure is the share of citations in a firm's focal year's citations that could not be found in the previous five years' list of patents and citations by the firm, that is, new citations. The firm-year level share of new citations is matched to the acquirer and the target in a vertical M&A by year to generate a measure at the acquirer-target-year level. This measure is weighted by the patent counts of the acquirer and the target in the focal year to adjust for differences in the size of their patent portfolios.
time_window: focal year with a previous five years' citation look-back, panel from t-5 to t+5 relative to the M&A event year

description: Following Hall et al. (2001), a patent level generality measure is calculated where the percentage of forward citations received by a patent that belongs to each patent technology class j, out of n patent technology classes, enters the calculation. This patent level measure is aggregated to the firm-year level by averaging the measure for all patents of a firm in a given year. The acquirer-target-year level dependent variable averages the firm-year measure for the acquirer and the target, weighted by their patent counts in the focal year.
time_window: focal year, panel from t-5 to t+5 relative to the M&A event year

description: Drawing on Claussen et al. (2015) and Jung and Lee (2016), a pool of distinct technology subclasses is created for each patent from the technology subclass information of all prior arts cited by the patent, and all possible pairwise links of subclasses are obtained. The number of subclass pairs with both subclasses from the same technology class is the measure of component interdependency, and the number of subclass pairs with subclasses from different technology classes is the measure of interface interdependency. Component interdependency divided by the sum of component interdependency and interface interdependency gives a percentage measure between 0 and 1, where a higher share means more autonomous innovation in a patent; the patent level measure is aggregated to the firm and then the deal level following the same weighting procedure as the other dependent variables.
time_window: focal year, panel from t-5 to t+5 relative to the M&A event year

description: For absorbed slack, managers were asked to provide an assessment on a seven-point scale on whether the firm has been operating below engineered capacity. The measure was entered in the regressions on profitability and on market position.

variable_name: retained earnings, discretionary fund, debt financing
description: For unabsorbed slack, managers were probed, based on a seven-point scale, on (1) whether the firm's retained earnings have been sufficient for market expansion; (2) whether it has a pool of financial resources that can be used on a discretionary basis; and (3) whether it is able to secure necessary bank loans. These three measures were entered separately in the regressions as retained earnings, discretionary fund, and debt financing.

Managers were asked to identify their firms' relative performance, as compared with close competitors, based on (1) profitability (after-tax return on assets) and (2) market position, on a five-point scale. Profitability and market position were used as separate dependent variables in the regressions.

variable_name: major repair fund, inventory fund, accounts payable
description: Three measures of slack were considered to be absorbed: major repair fund, designated for repairs of large equipment, typically has little alternative use other than its designated purpose; inventory fund, which has little alternative use; and accounts payables, which managers often use as a way of delaying payments, buying time but not leading to other purposes. Each was obtained from firms' audited accounting statements and entered separately in the regressions on performance. In the curvilinear analysis absorbed slack was entered as a standardized z-score together with a squared term created from that z-score.

variable_name: depreciation fund, reserve fund, loans, sales expenses, retained earnings
description: Five measures of unabsorbed slack were identified: depreciation fund, which in practice is often used to cover various unanticipated needs; reserve fund, specifically designated for daily operation and the most liquid resources managers can utilize; loans, which can be used for discretionary purposes; sales expenses, a major source through which managers cover various payments; and retained earnings, over which firms have a great deal of discretion. Each was taken from firms' audited accounting statements and entered separately in the regressions on performance. In the curvilinear analysis unabsorbed slack was entered as a standardized z-score together with a squared term created from that z-score.

Firms' 1992 total pre-tax profits were used as an objective performance measure. Pre-tax profits, instead of after-tax profits, were used because different industries in China have different taxation rates and using after-tax profits might distort the actual profitability.

Slack was measured on two dimensions. In Study 1, absorbed slack was a manager-rated seven-point item on operating below engineered capacity and unabsorbed slack was a set of manager-rated items on retained earnings, discretionary funds and debt financing. In Study 2, absorbed slack was based on archival accounts (major repair fund, inventory fund, accounts payable) and unabsorbed slack on five archival accounts (depreciation fund, reserve fund, loans, sales expenses, retained earnings).

R&D intensity is computed for every business segment listed in Compustat II from 1980 to 1999 by dividing segment-level R&D spending by segment sales; a missing R&D figure was assumed to equal zero. Each segment's R&D intensity is compared to all business segments competing in the same industry (the segment's primary 3-digit SIC code) and assigned a percentile score. For single-segment firms this percentile score is the firm-level value; for multi-segment firms the firm-level value is the weighted average (by segment assets) of the segment percentile scores. Higher scores indicate that a firm invests more heavily in R&D than its industry rivals and is thus more likely to be attempting to compete on the basis of innovativeness.
level: firm-year (segment scores aggregated to the firm)

description: Computed by dividing the book value of debt by the total market value of the firm, where the total market value of the firm is the book value of debt plus the market value of equity plus the carrying value of preferred stock. A small constant (0.1) was added to make all values positive, and a Box-Cox procedure indicated that a transformation approximately equivalent to the natural log maximized model fit, so the variable was log-transformed. Independent variables in the leverage models were lagged one year.
time_window: annual, lagged one year relative to the dependent variable

description: The firm's market-to-book ratio, calculated by dividing the market value of the firm by the book value of total assets; the authors treat it as a holistic proxy for performance that corresponds closely to Tobin's q. A Box-Cox procedure showed that a transformation approximately equivalent to the natural log maximized model fit, so the variable was log-transformed. Independent variables in the performance model were contemporaneous measures.
time_window: annual, contemporaneous with the dependent variable

description: Firm-level accounting profitability measured by return on assets: operating income before depreciation divided by the book value of assets. It enters the leverage models as a control and as the focal variable in the predicted interaction with Innovation.
time_window: annual, lagged one year in the leverage models

description: Measured by the percentage difference between the actual price paid to a target firm and the market price of the target before the acquisition event. To avoid stock price distortions caused by information leakage surrounding the acquisition announcement, the SDC calculated the premium as the percentage difference between the final price per target share paid by the acquiring firm and the target's stock price several weeks before the announcement date. In the primary analysis, premiums calculated four weeks prior to the announcement dates were used.
time_window: four weeks prior to the announcement date

description: Calculated as the grand mean of all premiums experienced by a focal board of directors across all boards, including the focal board, during the prior 48-month period (month t-48 to t-1, inclusive). The grand mean is simply the mean of individual-level average prior premiums. Observations were dropped when data for over a quarter of directors' prior premium experience were missing.

Measured on five demographic characteristics shown to be salient bases for promoting interpersonal trust and open communication among top executives: gender, industry of employment, highest degree (PhD, Masters, Bachelors, or lower), Ivy League educational background, and functional background. Homogeneity on each characteristic was calculated using a variant of Blau's index, defined as the sum of squared proportions of directors in each category. The primary measure was an index calculated as the sum of standard scores of the five measures of demographic homogeneity.

Calculated as the average number of acquisitions experienced by minority viewpoint directors 48 months prior to the focal decision divided by the average number of acquisitions experienced by the majority in the same period. Minority viewpoint directors were identified relative to a post hoc revealed reference point of 36 percent: if more than 50 percent of directors on the focal board experienced average premiums higher (or lower) than 36 percent, a director whose average prior premium was lower (or higher) than 36 percent was labeled a minority viewpoint director.
time_window: 48 months prior to the focal decision

description: Measured based on four variables widely used to measure outside directors' influence on strategic decisions: the total tenure of outside directors on the focal board, the total number of board appointments held by all outside directors, the proportion of outside directors on the board, and the structure of the board in terms of the separation of CEO and board chair positions. The sum of standard scores of these four variables was used as the primary measure of board influence.

Based on total compensation, the vertical pay gap is measured as the difference between the CEO's pay and the average pay of the other four highest-paid members of the TMT. All observations are monotonically transformed by taking the natural log of the difference to measure the vertical pay gap. In a robustness measure the authors also used the coefficient of variation of total pay among the top five executives including the CEO.

variable_name: filing of a class action lawsuit
description: The dependent variable is filing of a class action lawsuit. To help rule out false targeting, the authors excluded lawsuits that were later dismissed by court, examining only lawsuits that led to a settlement in court. No firm was subject to more than one settled lawsuit in a year, so the dependent variable is binary, receiving a value of '1' if the focal firm is sued and '0' otherwise.

An entropy index is used to measure unrelated diversification, an objective categorical measure that reflects both the number of fundamentally different businesses in which a firm operates and the extent to which sales are evenly distributed among those types. Unrelated diversification arises from operating between two-digit SIC industry groups, with total firm sales as reference; Pj is the share of sales in each unrelated segment j and ln(1/P) is the weight for each segment j. Two-digit SIC codes indicate unrelated businesses because the first two digits indicate the major industry group. The equation itself is not readable in the supplied text.

A composite index of dynamism and complexity. Dynamism was measured following Dess and Beard (1984) and Boyd (1995) by creating a regression with total industry sales based on four-digit SIC codes as the dependent variable and time as a predictor, based on five years of data immediately preceding the focal year; dynamism is the standard error of the slope of the regression coefficient of time divided by the mean value of total industry sales over the five preceding years, an annual, industry-level variable. Complexity follows Boyd (1990, 1995) and uses a Herfindahl index, summing the squares of the sales market shares of all firms in each four-digit SIC industry in Compustat, and is then one minus this Herfindahl index so that low values correspond with low levels of complexity. Dynamism and complexity were standardized and combined into a composite index of environmental uncertainty.
time_window: five years immediately preceding the focal year

description: For each company in each country the authors obtained the group (if any) with which the company is affiliated, gathering affiliation data from local and, in many cases, multiple sources and merging them with financial and industry information. Firms are coded as members of a group or as unaffiliated, with each group captured by a dummy variable in the estimation; groups are delineated within each country, and group affiliation is assumed not to be a choice variable in the short run.

Profitability is operating profit divided by total net assets. Operating profit is used rather than net profit because it is not directly distorted by taxation rules, which differ dramatically across countries, and because a consistent measure of operating profit is available in more countries. In India, data constraints force a slight variant: (net income plus interest expense divided by one minus the tax rate) divided by total net assets.

variable_name: within-group versus beyond-group similarity of profit rates
description: The first approach computes each firm's average profitability over time, then averages the absolute difference in profit rates over every within-group pair of firms and over every pair of firms that spans a group boundary, and compares the two averages. The second approach estimates the dummy-variable model by OLS, adding year, industry, group and firm effects in turn, and examines the incremental contribution to R-squared and the joint significance of the group dummy variables, which indicates whether within-group profit means are distinct from one another.
time_window: firm averages over time for the dyad comparison

description: The calendar year in which a firm was established, as recorded in the NBS database. It enters the productivity and exit models both on its own and interacted with the marketization index, so that higher values indicate more recent entrants.

A multilateral productivity index developed by Caves, Christensen, and Diewert (1982) and later modified by Aw, Chung, and Roberts (2003). Output and inputs (labor input, material input, and capital stock) are expressed as deviations from a hypothetical firm operating for each 3-digit SIC industry in the base year 1998, using the industry average for input shares, inputs, and output. Input shares are the ratio of labor costs to output for labor, the ratio of material costs to output for material, and one minus labor share and material share for capital. The equation itself is unreadable in the source and is not reconstructed; both tails of the index were winsorized by 0.1 percent.

A dichotomous variable that records the exit event when a given firm identifier at time t does not reappear in the database at time t + 1. Because a firm may have been removed from the annual industrial survey when its sales dipped below 5 million RMB, exit is recorded only when the disappearing firm does not reappear in the 2004 economy-wide census; roughly 1.3 percent of firms that disappear from the annual survey still exist in the census. Exit can therefore be defined only during the 1998-2004 period.

The marketization index constructed annually from 1998 to 2007 by the National Economic Research Institute (NERI), covering each of the 31 provinces in each year. It contains five major fields capturing the progress of marketization: the relation between the government and the market, the development of the nonstate sector, the development of the product market, the development of the factor market, and the development of market intermediaries and the legal environment. Each major category contains several subindices, totaling 23 subindices, built from National Bureau of Statistics of China data and surveys conducted by NERI. A higher degree of marketization reflects fewer institutional barriers.

The number of manufacturing alliances in which the focal firm is involved. Because the impact of an alliance may not be immediately felt on performance measures, the variable is the cumulative number of manufacturing alliances the focal firm entered into in the three years prior to the year in question. Only alliances that have manufacturing identified in their scope of activities are counted.
time_window: cumulative three years prior to the year in question

description: For each firm in the sample a list of all divisions, subsidiaries, and joint ventures was prepared, and each firm's history was traced to account for name and division changes, divestments, acquisitions, and joint ventures; the patent count was computed for each firm-year by assigning all patents issued solely to the firm or all of its subsidiaries. Because using number of patents assumes all innovations are equal, a weighted measure is used that assigns an impact factor to each patent in the firm's portfolio of granted patents for each year, the impact being the number of forward citations the patent receives from other patents. To avoid truncation bias, a window of five years from the patent's application date is used to measure citations.
time_window: patents filed in year t; five-year forward citation window from the patent's application date

description: Financial performance is measured as the firm's net income, chosen on the basis of past accounting literature suggesting net income as a reliable indicator of the performance of the firm. It is the dependent variable in the financial performance models.
time_window: firm-year, contemporaneous with the dependent variable year

description: A dummy variable that takes a value of 0 if the firm engages in design only and a value of 1 if the firm engages in both design and manufacturing (referred to as fabrication in the industry). Firm boundary data were obtained from a cross-sectional survey administered to all firms in the semiconductor industry by the Global Semiconductor Alliance and supplemented with 10-K reports to account for changes in firm boundaries over time.
scale: 0/1 dummy (0 = design only, 1 = design and manufacturing)

description: Coefficient of variation (the standard deviation divided by the mean) of total pay, where total pay is the sum of base pay and short- and long-term incentives and the monetary value of stock-based compensation is calculated using the Black-Scholes model. The database categorized R&D employee positions into five job levels; the CV was first calculated for each of the five job levels and then averaged across the five job levels to represent the pay dispersion of the firm's R&D group. The resulting measure was scaled by dividing it by 100.

The annual number of successful patent applications by a firm, collected from the U.S. Patent and Trademark Office website. Patent counts are used as a proxy for innovation because the measure correlates well with other innovation indices, such as the number of new products. A one-year lag was taken for the dependent variable.

The market-to-book ratio, calculated as the ratio of a firm's market value to its book value. Because a firm's share price reflects the stock market's evaluation of the firm's future returns, higher market-to-book ratios indicate that investors expect higher firm growth. The variable was mean-centered in the regression analysis.
Current assets divided by current liabilities; higher financial slack indicates that the firm has greater financial resources. The variable was mean-centered in the regression analysis.

HR slack is built from an equation whose rendering in this payload is unreadable; the authors state that the first term of the measure captures the ratio of workers to plant size for a focal plant i in year t, while the second term represents that same ratio for industry j in year t. To measure codified HR slack, the authors substitute the total number of plant employees in that equation with the number of line workers in a plant. Line workers perform manual labor of different types across work stations of highly fragmented production lines, and instructions for replicating their tasks are mostly contained in easy-to-follow manuals.

Following the computational logic of the HR slack equation, the authors substitute plant workers with the number of plant technicians. Plant technicians install, configure, and maintain the machinery and tools used by line workers; their tasks require tacit knowledge such as engineering principles, the workings of machinery/tools, and computers and programming languages, which can be applied to solve problems in a variety of settings.

Following the computational logic of the HR slack equation, the authors substitute plant workers with the number of plant managers. Maquiladora managers' tasks require deep knowledge of every aspect of plant facilities, their adjacent value chain (suppliers and customers), and relevant stakeholders, knowledge that is extremely difficult (impossible) to codify and much of which is only relevant in the context of a given maquiladora.

The dependent variable is performance at the plant level, computed as gross profits, the residual value appropriated by a manufacturing plant after netting all expenses except taxes. To account for the left-skewed distribution of gross profits in the sample, the authors rescale the variable logarithmically (natural logarithm). Variables measured in Mexican pesos, including profits, are transformed into U.S. dollars using the average monthly exchange rate published by Mexico's Central Bank.

A time-variant index built on concepts from the international trade literature: SI jt = [dCH jt - dMX jt] + [cCH jt / cMX jt], where j refers to products at the level of four-digit HS Codes, t equals years, dCH and dMX are U.S. ad valorem duties levied on Chinese and Mexican imports, and cCH and cMX are the dollar cost of shipping a 40-foot container to the United States from China and Mexico. The index is rescaled so that the smallest markup constitutes the highest value on the scale and the largest markup equals zero; higher values point to potentially high threats of Chinese substitution and thus high competitive pressures. The variable takes the value of zero in the years between 1999 and 2001.

A time-invariant dummy variable that takes a value of one if a maquiladora focuses on manufacturing its own products and zero if it offers customized manufacturing services. Contract plants provide bespoke manufacturing services to a number of customers, while the stability in the client/product portfolios of focused plants allows the developing of more standardized procedures. The coding relied on business descriptions contained in mainstream industry directories, directories of trade associations, and corporate websites, and it is negatively correlated with the number of different products a plant produces.

Takes the value of 1 in the year that the (parent) firm exits under at least one of the following conditions: bankruptcy or receivership, retirement from business, acquisition by another party because of severe financial problems, merging with a larger party because of financial difficulties or inadequate scale, and reorganizations because of financial constraints or state of receivership; it equals 0 for the years that the firm remains alive. Upon exit, the focal firm is removed from the risk set. The authors interpret the inverse, the survival probability, as the parent's performance, so a negative coefficient on a predictor implies a lower failure risk.

Takes the value of 1 in the year that the spinout was incorporated at the corresponding parent-year pair. A firm was classified as a spinout whenever at least one of its founders originated from (either worked for, founded, or both) an incumbent firm in the industry before the establishment of the spinout and the spinout firm was established within a maximum of one year after the founder left the parent. Where multiple parents could be identified, each was endowed with a spinout event in the year of the spinout's incorporation.

The log of the Euclidean distance between the characteristics of the most advanced automobile model at the parent in the spinout year and the characteristics of the first automobile model that the spinout introduced upon founding. The measure is based on three automobile characteristics: the number of cylinders, the engine's horsepower, and the wheelbase width of the car.
time_window: spinout year and first year of spinout production

description: Takes the value of 1 for every spinout event whereby the spinout-parent distance is above the median distance. The complementary category, spinout-parent distance below median, is the omitted category in the specifications. To avoid confounding the instances where the spinout and the parent overlapped with instances where no spinout event took place, the sample is completed by a no spinout event variable that takes the value of 1 for all parent-year pairs that did not experience a spinout event.
time_window: spinout year and first year of spinout production

description: Takes the value of 1 for all the spinout events that were classified as cases of severe disagreement at the parent. All instances of spinout events were read and coded independently by a research assistant and the author, and disagreements about coding were resolved by joint rereading and discussion. The authors describe this as the unconditional effect of conflict resolution via a spinout.

variable_name: hierarchical role of the exiting employee
description: The job title of the exiting employee at the parent as described in the Standard Catalog of American Cars, grouped into three categories: employee (entry level up to but excluding managerial level), manager (sales, production, and marketing managers and titles including the term manager, except general manager), and top executive (from general manager to the founders). Because there was only one instance of a spinout event initiated by a manager following a disagreement, that category was merged with the employee category, so the empirical analysis distinguishes between employee and top executive only. Spinout types are entered both as base effects and interacted with the presence of a disagreement at founding.

Searchers (D = 1) are executives who agree to share their résumés and be interviewed by the search consultant for a position; stayers (D = 0) are those that turn down the invitation. The classification follows the search firm's own internal classification of candidates, which is based on the most recent type of contact that it had with the executive. The response is reported by the search firm rather than self-reported by the executive.

Reputation is the sum of two variables: Best employer and Most admired employer. Best employer (0-10) measures the perception of the executives' employer in the business world as obtained from Fortune magazine's 100 Best Companies to Work For rankings; Most admired employer (0-10) was obtained from the organization's score on Fortune's America's Most Admired Companies and Global Most Admired Companies rankings.

The authors do not have information on the pay of each executive in the sample; as a proxy they use the total annual compensation received by the chief executive officer in the company as reported by Compustat, available only for publicly held companies. They measure the extent to which executives in each company are paid above or below prevailing levels by constructing a standard wage equation in which industry, organization size, and financial performance are regressed against the logarithm of annual total compensation, and include the residuals as an independent variable. Positive residuals indicate that the organization pays a premium.

Financial performance of one's employer is measured by its return on equity. This information is only available for publicly held companies, so models with financial data cover only the publicly held part of the sample.

Tenure since employer change represents the number of years one has been with the current employer; greater tenure is taken to be associated with better information and greater certainty about future prospects. Because the data set records the current and the previous jobs of each executive, and given that 32% of the individuals did not change employers between these jobs, the analyses control for Employer change observed.

The binary variable M&A indicates the employers that were involved in a merger or acquisition in the past two years. Mergers and acquisitions are used as a clear measure of exogenous shocks that affect uncertainty regarding future career prospects, because prior research shows that M&As break implicit contracts for executives and lead to net job cuts, with consequences that take years to play out.

Career breadth is the simple sum of four items: Change in job function (0/1), which indicates whether the current job represents a change in job functions from the previous job; Change in industry (0/1), representing moves across industries; Change in industry segment (0/1), representing moves across different industry segments within the financial services industry; and International assignments (0/1), identifying whether executives have had a work assignment outside the United States in their current or previous job. To test hypothesis 3A the authors look at the relationship between Career breadth and Job search in a split sample that included only moves within the same employer.

Following Snow and Hrebiniak (1980), self-typing of textual descriptions of strategy was used in this study. The two top executives in each enterprise evaluated their organization's strategic type as Defender, Prospector, Analyzer or Reactor, using textual descriptions of strategies.

Mintzberg's three strategy-making modes were operationalized for self-typing of textual descriptions, and pre-tested. The analysis uses the degree to which the organizations conformed to the Entrepreneurial mode of strategy making, as evaluated by the General Manager and, separately, by the Kibbutz Secretary.

Mintzberg's three strategy-making modes were operationalized for self-typing of textual descriptions, and pre-tested. The analysis uses the degree to which the organizations conformed to the Adaptive mode of strategy making, as evaluated by the General Manager and, separately, by the Kibbutz Secretary.

Mintzberg's three strategy-making modes were operationalized for self-typing of textual descriptions, and pre-tested. The analysis uses the degree to which the organizations conformed to the Planning mode of strategy making, as evaluated by the General Manager and, separately, by the Kibbutz Secretary.

Level of performance was operationalized by several measures. The two executives' evaluations of performance, for which the data are more complete, were used as surrogates for all performance measures. Correlations are reported separately for the General Managers' evaluations and for the Kibbutz Secretaries' evaluations; the analysis focuses on the evaluation of the general managers.

Firm size was operationalized as the total sales in 1986 dollars. The data base also included assets and number of employees as possible size variables, but these variables were highly correlated with sales.

Profit center size was operationalized as the total sales in 1986 dollars. Firm and profit center size were measured in the same way, and the data base also included assets and number of employees as possible size variables, which were highly correlated with sales.

This variable was operationalized as the ratio of profit center size and firm size in sales dollars. The authors argue that a relatively larger profit center may be considered more important and have more power than a relatively smaller profit center.

Following previous research (O'Reilly et al., 1988; Finkelstein and Hambrick, 1989), ROE was selected as the measure of corporate performance. The authors note that the effect of firm ROE on a PCM's compensation had not been previously addressed.

Cash compensation is defined as salary and bonus. The paper addresses salary, bonus and total cash compensation, with total cash compensation being the sum of base salary and bonus. Since the sample spans a number of years, all compensation and other dollar measures were inflated by the Consumer Price Index to 1986 dollars.

The bonus as a percentage of cash (total) compensation, which the authors also describe as the ratio of bonus to salary. Salary is typically fixed at the beginning of the year and cannot easily be changed during the year, while bonus is incentive based and may depend on current performance.

Firm tenure was operationalized as the number of years in the firm. Firm tenure, job tenure and age were highly correlated, and the authors report that these three variables were not included in the same regression.

Job tenure was operationalized as the number of years as the PCM of that particular profit center. The authors argue that a longer period of time allows the PCM to achieve a 'track record' and to build political power and expertise.
Age was measured as chronological age. Age is highly correlated with job tenure and firm tenure.
Education was measured as the number of years completed in school. Education is the one variable that does not vary from year to year in the sample.

The instantaneous rate of occurrence of a CVC investment by the corporate investor in the focal partner, in dyads who have not yet experienced a CVC. It is estimated in the competing risks model where the hazard of a CVC depends on the investor not having previously established a CVC and on whether an alternative MFT transaction such as licensing, majority ownership acquisition, or R&D alliance has occurred.

The ratio of the number of scientific papers published by corporate investor employees, scaled to one thousand, to the number of employees. It is used to estimate the investor's scientific capability, following the literature that measures the ability to select and evaluate external knowledge with scientific publications authored by firm employees.

An indicator variable that equals one if a partner firm has a patent in areas that are new to the corporate investor, and zero otherwise. It is constructed using the 3-digit patent classifications listed on each firm's patents, using all patents obtained by the corporate investors and partner firms and all the listed 3-digit technological classes.
scale: 0/1 indicator (1 = partner has a patent in areas new to the investor)

description: Within a corporate investor's research pipeline, the number of drugs in the early stages of development (preclinical and Phase 1) divided by the sum of the investor's total number of drugs in all stages of development (preclinical and Phase 1-3). A larger value indicates a greater proportion of early-stage drugs; a smaller value indicates a portfolio more heavily weighted toward late-stage technologies.

The implied partner valuation obtained from its financing history in the ReCap CVC database, which includes the expected future cash flows from the partner's technology. Because this measure is only available for years when the company obtained VC or CVC financing, the average implied valuation across years is used as a firm-specific measure that does not vary over time.
time_window: time invariant (average across years with financing)

description: Using PharmaProjects, the authors first compute the average empirical probability of successful launch of a drug in the pipeline by biotech firms operating in similar technological subfields as that of the focal biotech partner. They then use one minus the probability of successful launch as a proxy for exogenous technological uncertainty.

The instantaneous rate of occurrence of a license post-CVC in dyads who have not yet experienced a license post-CVC, examined from the year of the CVC investment. Each yearly spell is treated as right censored unless a license after the CVC investment or a competing event is observed; the only observed alternative (or competing event) to a license in the sample post-CVC is an R&D alliance.
time_window: from the year of the CVC investment

description: The ratio of the number of scientific papers published by corporate investor employees, scaled to one thousand, to the number of employees. It is used to estimate the investor's scientific capability, following the literature that measures the ability to select and evaluate external knowledge with scientific publications authored by firm employees.

An indicator variable that equals one if a partner firm has a patent in areas that are new to the corporate investor, and zero otherwise, built from the 3-digit patent classifications listed on each firm's patents. It is included in the post-CVC licensing models to capture whether the technology is distant from the investor's knowledge base.
scale: 0/1 indicator (1 = partner has a patent in areas new to the investor)

description: The number of drugs in the early stages of development (preclinical and Phase 1) within a corporate investor's research pipeline divided by the sum of its total number of drugs in all stages of development (preclinical and Phase 1-3). A larger value indicates a greater proportion of early-stage drugs.

The implied partner valuation obtained from its financing history in the ReCap CVC database, which includes the expected future cash flows from the partner's technology. Because the measure is only available in years when the company obtained VC or CVC financing, the average implied valuation across years is used as a firm-specific measure that does not vary over time.
time_window: time invariant (average across years with financing)

description: One minus the average empirical probability of successful launch of a drug in the pipeline by biotech firms operating in similar technological subfields as that of the focal biotech partner, computed from PharmaProjects, used as a proxy for exogenous technological uncertainty. In the second stage it enters the model interacted with the value of the partner's technology.

Nonmandatory technological upgrades, i.e., those executed in addition to compliance with compulsory FIA demands, gauged by examining teams' car blueprints and technical releases. Components based on unexplored industry-level knowledge belong to the explorative category, so the measure captures the level of firm exploration relative to expected baseline industry behavior. Because every team's two cars are essentially identical, the variable is team-specific and its value applies to both team cars.

The best rank classification attained by either of a team's two drivers in each race represents the team's performance in that race, and these scores are averaged across all races in the season, so that teams with lower averages outperform those with higher averages. To assign higher values to better performers, the team's season performance was set as the denominator and that of the winning team as the numerator, so the index indicates the winner as 1 and gives all other teams values less than 1 but greater than 0. The metric thus captures the average distance by which each team lags behind the winner in each season.
time_window: season t, averaged across all races in the season

description: The magnitude of the environmental regulatory change reflects variations in the FIA technical rules across six core technology areas. The three coders analyzed every regulatory release, assigning each a value ranging from 0 (no change) to 3 (radical change) in each of these six areas, with intermediate scores of 1 or 2 where rules altered the status quo in a limited way. The scores were triangulated with commentaries in the specialist press, and the six scores were averaged to obtain a single overall rating for the magnitude of each year's regulatory change.
scale: 0 (no change) to 3 (radical change) per area, averaged across six areas
time_window: annual FIA regulatory release for season t

description: Tracks the operator's accident rate through accident costs per mile, using the total damage costs due to accidents involving the operator's pipeline during the observation year, scaled by the number of miles in the operator's pipeline network. Accident costs rather than a count of accidents are used because property and environmental damage varies considerably across incidents. This measure was logged to reduce skewness.

Reflects actual organizational investments related to the pipeline operator's compliance with regulatory mandates, specifically the number of pipeline segment miles actually assessed by an operator during the year. Although statutes mandate that operators conform to integrity management requirements, the underlying law requires inspection of each relevant segment at a minimum of once every seven years and leaves significant discretion to individual operators regarding exact timing and frequency, making this a discretionary and sensitive measure of compliance-oriented investments.

The dollar amount of fines (in thousands) levied against the operator by the regulatory agency during the year. This measure accounts for the severity as well as frequency of enforcement actions against a particular operator, since monetary penalties vary according to the severity of each infringement. Variables were centered prior to constructing the interaction with the regulatory conferences measure.

The count of conferences in which the focal operator's representatives participated in a significantly material fashion (for example, through delivering a presentation, hosting a session, or facilitating a formal discussion) during the observation year. Measuring collaborations through significant participation rather than general attendance was considered beneficial because materially participating operators are more likely to exchange details about their own operations, query regulators and other organizations, and field follow-up contact. This count was used to test Hypotheses 1a and 1b.

A binary variable reflecting whether the operator materially participated in any regulatory conferences during the year. It was used to predict an operator's likelihood of engaging in any of these collaborations, as required by Hypotheses 2-4, since the crucial decision faced by executives is whether to participate in any collaborations at all.
The number of on-site inspections conducted by regulatory agents at that operator during the year, used as the measure of the operator's regulatory visibility.

The percent of an operator's overall system mileage that crosses through high consequence areas (HCAs). Companies that operate in these highly populated areas must interact more frequently with a diverse array of stakeholder groups, such as communities, advocacy organizations, business representatives, and civic leaders, and their operations are more visible as a result of this exposure.
The operator's lobbying expenditures, measured in millions of dollars, used as the measure of political engagement.

variable_name: MODE (100% cutoff), MODE (95% cutoff), MODE (80% cutoff)
description: The dependent variable is a dummy coded 0 for a wholly owned subsidiary and 1 for a joint venture. Because the distinction between the two forms is controversial, the authors used 100%, 95%, and 80% equity ownership as alternative cutoff points to differentiate wholly owned subsidiaries from joint ventures, giving three versions of the dependent variable. The results table is described as having the dependent variable coded 0 for wholly owned subsidiary and 1 for joint venture.

R&D intensity, the parent firm's research and development expenditure as a percentage of total annual sales, is used to measure the parent's firm- and product-specific knowledge as a proxy for asset specificity.

Parent experience in the host country is measured by the number of years since the establishment of the Japanese parents' first subsidiary in a host country. The same measure has been used in previous studies on mode of foreign entry.
level: parent firm in a host country

description: State influence is measured in terms of the extent to which local regulative forces influence foreign firms' activities in a host country, based on seven items from the 1995 World Competitiveness Report. Because the items were found to be highly correlated with correlation coefficients greater than 0.60, the authors used the mean score of the items. The original 0-10 rating scale was reversed in the study so that a higher score represents a higher value of institutional restrictiveness.
scale: mean of seven items on a 0-10 scale

description: Ethnocentricity was measured using two items from the 1995 World Competitiveness Report. Since the scores of these items were found to be highly correlated, ethnocentricity was measured by the mean score of the two items.

Cultural distance is defined as the difference between the national culture of Japan and those of the host countries in which the subsidiaries are located, following Kogut and Singh's (1988) measure as it has been most frequently used in past studies. The specification note states that the term stands for the cultural difference between countries j and k, that one term is the score for parent country j, i.e., Japan, on the ith cultural dimension, another is the score for subsidiary host country k on the ith cultural dimension, and that the variance of the index for the ith cultural dimension is also used. The formula itself was not readable in the extracted text, so the exact aggregation is not recoverable from this payload.

Mimetic entry was measured by the rate of joint venture over wholly owned subsidiary established by the other Japanese competitors in the sample in the same host country at the time of the focal multinational enterprise's entry. The variable was calculated separately for each industry in order to control for possible industry effects on the mimetic investment behavior of the parent firms. Only this frequency-based measure was used because of the limited information in the dataset.
time_window: at the time of the focal entry

description: Historical norm is measured by the rate of joint venture over wholly owned subsidiary established by the same parent firm in the same host country at the time of entry. The greater the value of the measure, the more frequently a firm follows the momentum of having formed joint ventures in the past.
level: parent firm in a host country

description: Calculated in two steps. First, for each patent granted at the USPTO over the observation period, the proportion of its subclass assignments belonging to the patent's original class is computed as the patent's typicality; this value equals one when all of a patent's subclass assignments fall within the patent's original class and approaches zero as the proportion of subclasses outside the original class increases. Second, the category contrast of technology class i at time t is the average typicality of all patents classified in technology class i in the previous five years.

A binary dependent variable set to one for the realized organization-technology class entry events, which constitute the case sample, and set to zero for the organization-technology class unrealized pairs, which constitute the control group. The case sample includes the first patent granted to organization i in technology class j; because the consideration set of organizations cannot be observed, control technology classes were selected through coarsened exact matching.

The number of citations received by each entry patent until the end of 2008. Forward citations are used as an indicator that innovation research has found to be correlated with patents' technological impact and economic value.

An indicator variable capturing whether the entrant is de novo or de alio. De novo entrants satisfy two conditions: they had no prior patenting history between 1963 and 1976, and their historical profiles revealed no previous business activity in sectors with low patenting propensity. Only the first entry event of an organization satisfying these requirements counts as a de novo entry event; all entries following the first one are classified as de alio.

The 17-level ordinal rating on long-term foreign currency-denominated debt published by agency r for country i on December 31st of year t. The scale runs from AAA = 16 through C = 0, with intermediate grades such as AA+ = 15, A = 11 and BBB− = 7. Higher values indicate assessments of less risk associated with lending and investment; lower values indicate the opposite.

A 0-1 indicator variable for ratings occurring during the years of crisis-induced turbulence, 1997-1998, coded 1 for those years and 0 otherwise. The authors choose 1997 as the starting year following previous academic, policy, and industry consensus that mid-1997 saw the first financial crisis in Thailand, and place the end of the turbulence in late 1998.

A 0-1 indicator for industry incumbency, taking the value of 1 for ratings published by Moody's or S&P, the two agencies active in the emerging-market sovereign rating business at the beginning of the period in 1987, and 0 otherwise.

Agency regional focus measured as the number of sovereigns i from one of the geographic regions the authors enumerate (North America-Caribbean, Latin America, Western Europe, Central-Eastern Europe, Africa-Middle East, and Asia — described in the text as five regions) relative to the total number of sovereigns i rated by agency r in year t.
The number of agencies publishing a rating for sovereign i in year t, measured as a 1-5 integer variable.

variable_name: absolute percentage change in the entropy measure of corporate diversification
description: Strategic change was measured by the absolute percentage change in diversification strategy over the period 1980-83.
