The variable relies on the Euclidean distance between potential partner firms' portfolios of three-digit technology classes, weighted by the number of patents in individual technology classes, and taking the natural log. Technology classes are identified as the main three-digit technology class under which inventions were categorized by the USPTO, information provided on the patent's front page. The measure is based on the past five years of patenting activity and captures how dissimilar the technological resources of the design and partner firm are.
time_window: past five years of patenting activity

description: A publication is coded 1 if its average team distance falls within 50 miles; these are referred to as 'colocated teams'. The average team distance of a paper is the mean distance between all dyads of coauthoring organizations, computed from the longitude and latitude of each organization (from zip codes, or city names when zip codes were not given). Only distances between different coauthoring institutions are used, so each institution is counted once even when multiple authors are listed at that site. The 50-mile mark is used as the boundary because the density of papers thins out dramatically after that point and 50 miles is a natural commuting distance; additional segments of 50-800, 800-2,000, 2,000-3,200 and greater than 3,200 miles are used in expanded models.

This variable takes a value of 1 if one or more of the coauthoring institutions (not including the firm) listed on the paper is one of the highly cited institutions, as indicated in the ISI institutional rankings in molecular biology and genetics. The ISI identifies 37 institutions whose papers in those fields received the most citations over the period 1992-2002.

Captures citations to the in-house research of the firm appearing as an author on a paper, constructed as the average number of paper citations to a firm's set of noncollaborative papers (papers listing an outside coauthor are excluded from the calculation). Because there are strong age effects in the citation rate, yearly citation counts are normalized by subtracting the average number of citations received by all sample firms in year t and dividing by the standard deviation, then summed through the year in which the focal paper was published and divided by the number of firm-only papers. The equations for these steps are not readable in the text. Firms were also coded as high prestige in the descriptive analysis if their average citations to firm-only papers were at least one standard deviation above the mean, which yields 15 companies classified as high-prestige firms.
level: firm (by publication year, attached to papers)

description: A count of citations made by the patents of the same firm that is listed as an author on the paper. Whenever a patent is issued, inventors and patent examiners identify prior art references, which can include nonpatent references such as published sources, and the paper is therefore counted when it is cited by a firm patent. The patent-to-paper citations were manually collected by professional searchers at Thompson/Derwent. The models are estimated on a subsample of 154 collaborative articles constructed to oversample on the dependent variable, pairing highly cited papers with randomly sampled papers from the same year.

A count of citations received by a paper from other scientific papers. It is estimated for the full set of coauthored papers, and captures the impact of research in wider scientific communities. Publication year and journal ranking are included as controls in these models.

Dichotomous variables indicating ownership structure, reported by the respondent. Company-owned establishments were affiliated with a brand and owned by the brand itself; franchisee-owned establishments were affiliated with a brand but owned by a franchisee; independently owned establishments were not affiliated with a brand or chain. Analyses include models with both independently owned and franchisee-owned establishments as the baseline.

An additive index combining employee selection and initial training into the skill-enhancing dimension of the HR system. The index was formed by standardizing and averaging the scores of the individual HR practices in the index. The overall score for each HR practice was obtained by weighting the scores of FOH and BOH employees by the proportion of employees in each group; in 15% of cases the overall HR practice reported by the respondent was used instead of a weighted average.

Assessed the extent to which restaurants use formal testing or other assessment methods to determine the suitability of job candidates, from 1, 'not at all,' to 5, 'to a great extent.' A higher score indicates a higher level of selectivity.
scale: 1 'not at all' to 5 'to a great extent'

description: The number of training hours that nonmanagerial workers typically receive in their first year, including orientation and job-related training.

An additive index combining relative hourly wage, employee benefits, job security, and internal promotions into the motivation-enhancing dimension of the HR system. The index was formed by standardizing and averaging the scores of the individual HR practices in the index. The overall score for each HR practice was obtained by weighting the scores of FOH and BOH employees by the proportion of employees in each group; in 15% of cases the overall HR practice reported by the respondent was used instead of a weighted average.

The typical average hourly wage of FOH and BOH employees relative to foodservice workers in the metropolitan area where the restaurant is located. The measure captures how competitive pay is compared with local alternatives; service tips were excluded.

The sum of benefits that the restaurant offers: subsidized health insurance, paid vacation, paid time off, paid sick leave, and other benefits such as free meals. The value of this variable ranges from zero to five.

Measured by the percentage of full-time employees in the restaurant, defined by the Bureau of Labor Statistics as employees who work more than 35 hours per week. Full-time work provides implicit employment security and indicates the firm's long-term commitment to employees.

Evaluated by the extent to which respondents agreed with the statement that the restaurant prioritizes promoting staff from within the restaurant rather than bringing in applicants from outside the restaurant, from 1, 'strongly disagree,' to 5, 'strongly agree.'

An additive index for employee discretion over work, calculated as the weighted average of FOH and BOH discretion in each restaurant. For FOH employees a four-item scale adapted from Batt and Colvin (2011) was used; BOH employee discretion was assessed with items on discretion over work methods and handling issues or problems that arise in the kitchen. The index was formed by standardizing and averaging the scores of the individual HR practices.

Respondents evaluated the extent to which FOH employees have discretion over work methods, what they say to customers, handling customer requests, and handling customer complaints (alpha equals 0.67). BOH employee discretion was assessed by the extent to which employees have discretion over work methods and handling issues or problems that arise in the kitchen (alpha equals 0.58). The overall measure was the weighted average of FOH and BOH discretion in each restaurant.

The GINI estimate of film production concentration among generalists during a given year, calculated after generalist film production was determined for each year. The GINI measures concentration by assessing the variability in the distribution of firms with respect to film production in a given year. The text states that G is the absolute mean difference in film production for all pairs of generalists in a given year and u is the mean of film production in that same year, but the printed formula is not readable in the available text.
time_window: annual, in the same year as the monthly founding counts

description: The GINI estimate of film distribution concentration among generalists during a given year, calculated after generalist film distribution was determined separately for each year. It assesses the variability in the distribution of firms with respect to film distribution in a given year, using the absolute mean difference in film distribution for all pairs of generalists and the annual mean of film distribution.
time_window: annual, in the same year as the monthly founding counts

description: The number of new firms founded as specialist producers in the population during a given month, tabulated for each month starting in January of 1914 to December of 1929. A specialist producer is a firm that only engaged in activities resulting in the creation of feature films in a given year.

The number of new firms founded as specialist distributors in the population during a given month, tabulated for each month starting in January of 1914 to December of 1929. A specialist distributor is a firm that only engaged in activities to ensure that the films were available to potential exhibitors in a given year.

Firms in the population were categorized into three mutually exclusive and exhaustive categories according to their activities in a given year: generalist producer-distributors, which were involved in both production and distribution; specialist producers, which only produced feature films; and specialist distributors, which only distributed films. Documented mergers and acquisitions were used to build company histories, and 15 firms that began as subsidiaries were removed and their film counts added to their parent company's totals.

variable_name: Specialist proportion of films produced within a new genre
description: For each year that a new genre emerged, variables equal to the counts of films produced by specialist firms within the genre and in the population as a whole were used to compute proportions. The proportion of films produced by specialists within the genre was compared with the proportion of all films produced by specialists in the population during the same year; the difference between these two proportions was tested with the sign test and the Mann-Whitney-Wilcoxon test.
time_window: first year the genre appeared among feature-length films (second year for genres beginning in 1912)

variable_name: Specialist proportion of films distributed within a new genre
description: For each year that a new genre emerged, variables equal to the counts of films distributed by specialist firms within the genre and in the population as a whole were used to compute proportions. The proportion of films distributed by specialists within the genre was compared with the proportion of all films distributed by specialists in the population during the same year, and the difference was tested with the sign test and the Mann-Whitney-Wilcoxon test.
time_window: first year the genre appeared among feature-length films (second year for genres beginning in 1912)

description: Assessed from the text of the project description the manager wrote at the initiation of the project, using the Linguistic Category Model: adjectives are weighted four, state verbs three, interpretive action verbs two, and descriptive action verbs one, that is (ADJ*4 + SV*3 + IAV*2 + DAV*1), and the score is divided by the total number of adjectives, verbs, and nouns. A computer-based algorithm using the Stanford Part-Of-Speech tagger picked up the nouns, adjectives, and verbs from each text, transformed verbs into their root form, and assigned them to LCM categories; words missing from the dictionary were categorized by coders. More abstract construal level is indicated by higher numbers.
time_window: project description written at project initiation

description: Survey questions about a specific project the respondent had managed and completed within the last two years, answered on a five-point Likert scale ranging from one (strongly disagree) to five (strongly agree). From a set of six items, confirmatory factor analysis indicated that the last four items hung together the best and these were used in the final analysis; Cronbach's alpha is 0.84. Higher levels reflect greater reliance on outcome controls, lower levels greater reliance on process controls, and mid ranges a combined approach.
time_window: post-completion survey (project completed within the prior two years)

description: Survey items asking the manager to indicate the nature of knowledge search used by the employees for the project, answered on a five-point Likert scale ranging from one (strongly disagree) to five (strongly agree). Exploratory learning was assessed with the extent to which knowledge sought addressed unique or unusual needs of the client, new ideas were developed specifically for the project, and knowledge was sought to develop a new framework for the project. Cronbach's alpha for these items is 0.91.
time_window: post-completion survey (project completed within the prior two years)

description: Assessed through reliance on knowledge drawn from other projects in the firm, with survey items answered on a five-point Likert scale ranging from one (strongly disagree) to five (strongly agree). The items captured the extent to which components taken from another project were modified, ideas from other projects were combined, and little time was spent adapting aspects of another project to make them work in the new context. Cronbach's alpha for these items is 0.73.
time_window: post-completion survey (project completed within the prior two years)

description: A multifaceted measure, collected by the firm's evaluation unit, of the quality of the solution obtained for the project and delivered to the client, assessing the degree to which the problem is solved and project goals are achieved. The unit surveys the client firm about its satisfaction with the solution and collects evidence on the impact of the solution on key outcomes for the client (e.g., changes in productivity, market share, sales or profitability), then gives one of nine possible ratings, from excellent to highly unsuccessful. These results are operationalized as a one to nine scale, with higher numbers reflecting higher effectiveness ratings, and the measure is typically collected between 6 months and 2 years after completion.
time_window: 6 months to 2 years after project completion

description: Assessed by the degree to which a project stays within its assigned schedule and allocated resources, based on the budget and timeline the frontline manager developed at the initial stage of the project. Within six months after completion, the evaluation unit examines whether the project stayed within budget and was completed within the planned time period; the percentage of time and money spent over or under the original timeline and budget is calculated and a predetermined formula establishes ratings of excellent, satisfactory, partly unsatisfactory, or unsatisfactory. These results are operationalized as a one to four scale, with higher numbers reflecting higher efficiency ratings.

A person-by-distribution-list two-mode matrix is converted into a one-mode matrix of overlapping distribution lists between actors. The crowding measure counts the number of email lists shared between actor i and a given alter j, conditional on both reporting to a common supervisor, weights this by the sum of distribution lists to which i and j each belong, sums across all alters, and weights the result by the number of alters with whom i shares a supervisor. The equation itself is not readable in the text, so the construction is taken from the authors' prose translation. The variable is an indicator set to 1 for people in the top quartile of the crowding distribution and 0 otherwise.
time_window: Lists and HR records from the same cross-section; HR data from the year after the list data

description: The same construction as at ISCO: a person-by-list two-mode matrix is converted into a one-mode overlap matrix, and competitive crowding counts lists shared with alters who report to the same supervisor, weighted by the number of lists each actor belongs to and by the number of alters sharing the supervisor. The underlying equation is not readable in the text. The variable is an indicator set to 1 for people in the top quartile of the crowding distribution and 0 otherwise.
time_window: Lists and HR records from the same cross-section; HR data from the year after the list data

description: Niche status is based on an individual's exposure, through list comemberships, to high-ranking colleagues, who were all in well-compensated senior management or executive positions. At ISCO a high-ranking employee was defined as someone in an executive-level salary band, representing the top 5% of employees. For each list the proportion of high-ranking members is calculated, and the status of an actor's niche is the mean proportion of high-ranking colleagues across all lists to which the actor belongs. The variable is an indicator set to 1 for people in the top quartile of this distribution and 0 otherwise.
time_window: Lists and HR records from the same cross-section; HR data from the year after the list data

description: As at ISCO, niche status is the mean proportion of high-ranking colleagues across all lists to which the actor belongs, computed from list comemberships. At BTCO a high-ranking employee was defined as a laboratory head; 9% of BTCO employees were in these roles. The variable is an indicator set to 1 for people in the top quartile of this distribution and 0 otherwise.
time_window: Lists and HR records from the same cross-section; HR data from the year after the list data

description: The measure is based on the Blau index of heterogeneity. For each distribution list, the proportion of members across all organizational units is computed, the squares of those proportions are summed and subtracted from one, and the resulting quantity is divided by the size of the distribution list. The mean of this list-level value is then computed across all lists of which the person was a member. The variable is an indicator set to 1 for people in the top quartile of this distribution and 0 otherwise.
time_window: Lists and HR records from the same cross-section; HR data from the year after the list data

description: Same construction as at ISCO: for each list the Blau index of heterogeneity across organizational units is computed from members' unit affiliations, subtracted from one, and divided by the size of the list; the average across the person's lists is then taken. The variable is an indicator set to 1 for people in the top quartile of this distribution and 0 otherwise.
time_window: Lists and HR records from the same cross-section; HR data from the year after the list data

description: A second diversity measure replaces organizational units with hierarchical levels: for each distribution list the Blau index of heterogeneity across hierarchical levels is computed, subtracted from one, and divided by the size of the list, and the mean across the person's lists is taken. The variable is an indicator set to 1 for people in the top quartile of this distribution and 0 otherwise.
time_window: Lists and HR records from the same cross-section; HR data from the year after the list data

description: Same construction as at ISCO but with hierarchical levels rather than organizational units: the list-level Blau index of heterogeneity across levels is divided by list size and averaged across the person's lists. The variable is an indicator set to 1 for people in the top quartile of this distribution and 0 otherwise.
time_window: Lists and HR records from the same cross-section; HR data from the year after the list data

description: Attainment at ISCO is based on the performance rating given to an employee by his or her supervisor, which ranges from 1 (does not meet expectations) to 5 (exceeds all expectations). The authors created an indicator, high performance, set to 1 for employees receiving a 4 or 5 rating, which was 48% of employees in the sample.
time_window: Rating for the prior year of service, collected in the year after the list data

variable_name: annual bonus (ratio of actual bonus to target bonus)
description: At BTCO the authors obtained both performance ratings and bonuses and chose annual bonus as the dependent variable because it is more directly tied to individual attainment. Under the compensation plan the HR department used a formula to provide supervisors with a target bonus for each direct report, and supervisors had discretion to adjust this target based on their evaluation of the employee's prior-year performance. The reported variable is the ratio of actual bonus divided by target bonus, which is formulaically centered near one.
time_window: Bonus paid in the year after the list data, reflecting prior-year contributions

description: Distance between the acquirer and the target in each M&A transaction, calculated from the zip codes of both firms' headquarters. Zip codes were used to determine the latitude and longitude of each firm, and the Great Circle distance formula was applied, with latitude and longitude values converted into radians by means of a division by 180/pi. The authors report an average distance between acquirers and targets of 1,121 miles.
time_window: at the time of the focal M&A transaction

description: Indicator variable that assumes a value of one if a venture capitalist was involved with the target firm at the time of the IPO, and zero otherwise. Data on this variable were provided by the new issues module of the SDC database.
time_window: at the time of the IPO

description: Measure based on the Carter and Manaster (1990) and Carter et al. (1998) scales, which are constructed from underwriters' positions in tombstone announcements, as well as on the addenda to these rankings by Loughran and Ritter (2004); final scores lie on a scale of one to nine, with nine representing the most prestigious underwriters. The variable was operationalized first by assigning a value of one to the most prestigious lead underwriters (a score of nine) and zero to those of intermediate or low reputation, and second by modeling the raw reputation scores of issuing firms' lead underwriters. The 1992-2000 rankings were used.
scale: reputation score of one to nine, dichotomized as 1 for a score of nine and 0 otherwise
time_window: at the time of the IPO (1992-2000 rankings)

description: Calculated as the first-day return of the equity offering, i.e., the extent to which the shares of the IPO firm were issued at a price less than their market value at the end of their first day of trading. Following prior work in financial economics, the authors computed this as the difference between the IPO's offer price and the stock's closing price on the first day of trading (the printed formula block is unreadable in the text provided). The authors state that the higher this first-day return, the higher the opportunity costs of going public. Data for this variable were obtained from the SDC database.

Defined as the mean geographic distance between alternative acquirers and the IPO target less the geographic distance between the actual acquirer and the IPO target. Alternative acquirers were identified as firms that had conducted acquisitions during the time frame three years prior to the focal transaction to three years after, had total assets in the range of 50-150 percent of the actual acquirer's total assets, and had their primary operations in the same industry as the actual acquirer at the two-digit SIC level.
time_window: three years before to three years after the focal transaction for identifying alternative acquirers

description: Premoney valuation from the most recent VC-backed funding round, used to represent a privately held digital startup's value because market-based valuation measures are not applicable. The authors describe it as a professional and comprehensive evaluation of the perceived net present value of the company before the latest round of funding. The dependent variable is the startup's value 12 months ahead of the current period (t + 12), and the measure is log transformed in the regressions.
time_window: t+12 (12 months ahead of the current period)

description: The total number of public repositories the digital startup has on GitHub, used to represent overall OSC. The measure is numeric and log transformed in the regressions because the distributions of the measures are very skewed.

The number of public repositories forked by the startup on GitHub, used to represent inbound OSC, i.e. knowledge flowing outside-in. The measure is numeric and log transformed in the regressions because the distributions of the measures are very skewed.

The number of public repositories created by the startup on GitHub, used to represent outbound OSC, i.e. knowledge flowing inside-out. The measure is numeric and log transformed in the regressions because the distributions of the measures are very skewed.

Venture stage is the moderator for digital startup maturity and uses the first three stages of Kazanjian's stage-of-growth model. Stage 1 (conception) indicates that the startups have not yet received any funding from angel investors or VC firms. Startups progress to stage 2 (commercialization) when they obtain angel investment or seed or series A funding from a VC firm. Startups are categorized as stage 3 (growth) once they raise a series B or later round from VC firms.

Blau index of the educational categories of the founding team's members, built from panel data on the number and types of advanced degrees held by individual team members. In the index p is the proportion of members in the jth educational category and N is the number of team members; the index accounts for team size because it increases for teams with fewer members. The index formula itself is not readable in the provided text.

Number of founding team members who were involved in founding other biotechnology firms. Information from BioScan and Knowledge Express was used to locate instances in which a founding team member was listed as part of another founding team prior to founding the focal firm.
Indicator variable coded as 1 when the CEO's name matched that of the founding team listed in BioScan and 0 otherwise. It is used to assess the CEO's structural power.

Binary variable where 1 indicates a breakthrough innovation and 0 otherwise, based on patented inventions in the top 1% of patents in terms of forward citations. To analyze the probability of breakthrough inventions the authors estimated hazard rate models with the marginal intensity function as the dependent variable, i.e., the limit of the probability that a breakthrough innovation will occur at time t given the past.

Classification of each firm into a startup stage and a growth stage that are mutually exclusive, with the size of the venture at the end of the startup stage used as the baseline. The startup stage is the period in which the main problems are to create innovations and secure funding, and all sample firms had secured financing and applied for at least one patent in the first seven years since incorporation. The growth stage is the period in which the firm experiences at least 10% growth in the number of employees as reported in BioScan; firms that grew but did not receive external funding and/or apply for at least one patent were not considered to be in the growth stage.

Same binary outcome as in the main study, coded 1 for a breakthrough innovation (patented invention in the top 1% of patents by forward citations) and 0 otherwise, modeled as the marginal intensity function in hazard rate models estimated separately for the startup-stage and growth-stage subsamples.

An indicator variable that indicates 1 if the firm had an approved 510(k) application that was not predicated on the firm's existing devices in a given year and 0 otherwise. Novel innovations were predicated on a competitor's devices. The authors use an indicator variable because very few firms have more than one novel innovation per year.

An indicator variable that indicates 1 if the firm had an approved 510(k) application that was predicated on a firm's devices and 0 otherwise. A firm in the sample is likely to introduce an incremental innovation every 5.6 years.

The log of the cumulative number of adverse events that occurred in the periods after a novel innovation. An adverse event is a product-caused event that leads to serious injury or death and proxies failure because it indicates if a device has technological problems. Firms have 51 adverse events with each novel innovation.
time_window: one-year lag of the independent variables

description: The log of the cumulative number of adverse events in a product line in the periods after the introduction of an incremental innovation. An adverse event is a product-caused event that leads to serious injury or death and proxies failure because it indicates if a device has technological problems. Firms have 34 adverse events with each incremental innovation.
time_window: one-year lag of the independent variables

description: Each firm's center of gravity was identified using Moody's corporate histories, supplemented by other sources, and assigned to one of four vertical chain stages, as was each business in which the firm had sales of at least 1%. A managerial relatedness score was computed for each firm by calculating the combined distance between the value stage of a firm's original center of gravity and the stages of the businesses into which it had diversified. Firms which stayed closer to their original center of gravity stage received lower combined distance scores; the specific formulae used are available from the authors.

The degree of input, distribution, and technological similarity between a diversified firm's businesses, operationalized with the constrained product relatedness measure used in prior empirical studies, which the authors elsewhere refer to as the entropy ratio. The authors state that this variable has been widely operationalized and tested in prior empirical studies and they do not report its formula here.

variable_name: return on sales and return on assets
description: For dependent variables, both return on sales and return on assets were used to assure comparability with previous studies. Because the only acceptable industry return variable available over the 1981-85 time frame at a four-digit SIC industry level was return on sales, industry performance was not controlled in the models using return on assets as the dependent variable. The regressions on return on sales and return on assets yielded similar results, so only the return on sales regressions are reported.

Each firm's center of gravity was identified using Moody's corporate histories, supplemented by other sources. Once identified, the center of gravity was assigned to one of four vertical chain stages: raw materials, commodity manufacturing, finished goods manufacturing, and wholesaling and retailing. The classification process was standardized by assigning each code in the Department of Commerce Input/Output Tables to one of the four basic vertical stages.

Strategy was viewed as implied from behavior rather than stated by management, and only the two extreme strategies, Prospector and Defender, were examined. A two-variable criterion set (marketing expenditure/sales and research and development expenditure/sales) was summed, firms were arrayed in ascending order, and a median split was used: the top 25 per cent were denoted Prospectors and the bottom 25 per cent Defenders, resulting in two sets of 56 firms each. The data for the strategy measures were obtained from Company Annual Reports and Form 10-K's; three further measures (net sales per employee, total number of product lines and number of new products) were used as a hold-out set to validate the classification.

variable_name: Degree of correspondence to the ideal executive profile (Euclidean distance metric)
description: The degree of correspondence between the ideal executive profile and the CEO profile of any given firm was computed with a Euclidean distance metric in which the score for the ideal profile on each executive characteristic is compared with the score for the firm on that characteristic. The indicator measures the distance between the CEO profile of a firm and the corresponding ideal profile in Euclidean space, so larger values mean greater misalignment. This distance was then correlated with the appropriate performance indicator; as distance from the ideal profile increases, performance should decline.

The managerial characteristics construct was operationalized with demographic variables obtained for each CEO. Separate ideal profiles for the CEOs of Prospector and Defender firms (Profile P and Profile D) were derived by ranking firms in each strategy group on the appropriate performance criterion and using the top 10 per cent of firms to derive standardized mean scores on the executive characteristics.
This variable was operationalized by counting the number of years that the executive had served in the organization.

This variable was operationalized by counting the number of years that the executive had served in the position. Only CEOs who had been in their position for a minimum of two years at the time of measurement of strategy and performance were retained.
Age was measured as the chronological age of the CEO.
A coding scheme was devised whereby each year of college education was added to a base score of 12 (for example, bachelor's degree = 12+4=16, masters degree = 12+6=18, etc.).

Functional background was coded as a categorical variable to reflect output or throughput experience. Output experience included backgrounds such as marketing and product research and development; throughput experience included backgrounds in finance, engineering and manufacturing. The area where the CEO spent the longest amount of time was used to determine his or her functional background.

Because no single measure effectively captures the performance outcomes of different strategic types, financial measures were used in conjunction with market based measures: return on investment was the primary measure of performance for the Defender firms in the sample and market share was the more appropriate indicator for the Prospector firms.

This indicator evaluates the rate of return on total assets utilized in the company and is described as a measure of management efficiency in resource deployments. ROI was used as the primary measure of performance for the Defender firms in the sample.

This measure captures the effectiveness of an organization's strategy, described as the success of a business's products and programs in relationship to those of its competitors in the market. Market share was used as the more appropriate performance indicator for the Prospector firms in the sample.

Annual return on investment used as the total return series for each corporate-level firm. Book value of assets in period t-1 is used in the denominator of ROI, so that only 19 years of data are available from the 20 years of observations. The analysis assumes that the behavior of total return approximates the behavior of abnormal returns.

An unsystematic return measure is calculated as the difference between total return and the expected return as indicated by economy-wide conditions and the beta of the firm. The beta is an accounting beta reflecting the association of a firm's return with the market return, measured as the average ROI for the sample of Compustat firms. An AR(1) model is estimated for the unsystematic return series in parallel with the model for total return.

Stock price information matched to the Compustat firms. The authors search for the autoregressive coefficient that produces the residual ROI series (unanticipated ROI) with the highest correlation with stock return, and compare it with the coefficient indicated by the time-series modeling process.

variable_name: autoregressive coefficient of the ROI series
description: Persistence is captured by the estimated autoregressive coefficient(s) of the ROI series: the closer any of the roots are to 1.00 the more persistent the abnormal profits, and a unit root would mean that abnormal returns do not dissipate completely. The aggregate estimate comes from an AR(1) model estimated on pooled time-series and cross-sectional data, and individual AR(1) models are estimated for each firm so that a Chow test can be used to test whether all parameters are the same across firms.

Return on investment of the business unit, the dependent variable of the model that allows the autoregressive coefficient to vary with strategic/market conditions. The model includes lagged ROI, lagged ROI interacted with quintile dummies for each factor, the factors themselves, and entry and exit dummy variables, so that slope and intercept effects are not confused.

variable_name: high and low market share quintile dummies
description: Dummy variables indicate whether the SBU is in the top or bottom quintile of the distribution of market share. Their interaction with lagged ROI shows whether the autoregressive coefficient is higher, lower or inconsequentially different for top- or bottom-quintile firms relative to firms in the middle of the distribution. Market share is also entered on its own so that its direct effect on the level of ROI is not confused with its effect on persistence.

variable_name: high and low served market concentration quintile dummies
description: Dummy variables indicate whether the SBU is in the top or bottom quintile of the distribution of served market concentration. Their interaction with lagged ROI shows whether the autoregressive coefficient is higher, lower or inconsequentially different relative to firms in the middle of the distribution. Served market concentration is also entered on its own to capture any direct effect on ROI.

variable_name: high and low vertical integration quintile dummies
description: Dummy variables indicate whether the SBU is in the top or bottom quintile of the distribution of vertical integration. Their interaction with lagged ROI shows whether the autoregressive coefficient is higher, lower or inconsequentially different relative to firms in the middle of the distribution. Vertical integration is also entered directly so that its effect on the level of ROI is separated from its effect on persistence.

variable_name: high and low marketing expenditure intensity quintile dummies
description: Dummy variables indicate whether the SBU is in the top or bottom quintile of the distribution of marketing expenditure intensity. Their interaction with lagged ROI shows whether the autoregressive coefficient is higher, lower or inconsequentially different relative to firms in the middle of the distribution. Marketing expenditure intensity is also entered directly to capture its effect on the level of ROI.

Dummy variable indicating that market entry has occurred in a previous period; the entry/exit variables reported in the PIMS data base occur prior to the ROI observation. It is entered on its own and interacted with lagged ROI to show whether the autoregressive coefficient is higher, lower or inconsequentially different when entry has occurred.

Dummy variable indicating that market exit has occurred in a previous period; the entry/exit variables reported in the PIMS data base occur prior to the ROI observation. It is entered on its own and interacted with lagged ROI to show whether the autoregressive coefficient is higher, lower or inconsequentially different when exit has occurred.

variable_name: high and low lagged ROI quintile dummies
description: Dummy variables indicate whether lagged ROI in period t-1 is in the upper or lower quintile of the distribution. Interacted with lagged ROI they allow the autoregressive coefficient to differ with the level of prior return, so that differing convergence patterns based on the level of return can be detected.

Persistence of return at the SBU level is captured by the coefficient on lagged ROI when it is allowed to differ with the strategic/market factors through their interaction with lagged ROI. Positive coefficients mean that the convergence process is slowed and negative coefficients indicate that the process is accelerated.

variable_name: Quintile dummies of concentration, market share, vertical integration, marketing intensity and lagged ROI, plus entry and exit dummies, interacted with lagged ROI
description: Strategic and market factors were measured on PIMS business units: served market concentration, market share, vertical integration (value added over sales), marketing expenditure intensity (marketing expenditure over sales) and lagged ROI, each entered as dummies for the top and bottom quintile of its distribution, plus dummies for whether market entry or exit occurred. The dummies were interacted with lagged ROI to test whether the autoregressive coefficient changed.

variable_name: Local partner contributions in management, marketing, and technology
description: In the absence of a continuous measure of knowledge mastery, local partner contributions in management, marketing, and technology were coded as binary variables; for instance, the local partner's contribution in management skills was coded as '1' if the local partner could contribute management skills to the venture and '0' otherwise. The contributions were coded from reports of the local companies, and the authors advise caution because of this data limitation.

variable_name: Search for management skills, marketing skills, or technology
description: A binary dependent variable was used to express the knowledge seeking decisions by local companies, coded '1' if the local partner was seeking transfer of a specific type of knowledge (management, marketing, or technology) from a foreign partner and '0' otherwise. Separate logistic regressions estimated the propensity to seek transfer of management, marketing, and technology knowledge.

Management skills are taken to represent tacit or embedded knowledge: they are not highly codified, cannot be readily reduced to written formulas, require vicarious or social learning, and are firm-specific, complex and not imitable, unlike technology, which can be codified. The variable used is the binary indicator of whether the local partner was seeking transfer of management skills from a foreign partner.

A binary variable was used to codify the governance mode of the firm, coded as '1' for an equity joint venture and '0' for a contractual venture. A cross-tabulation of the different CV modes with skill search did not reveal a significant difference, permitting their treatment as a single group.

The dependent variable in all the regression equations, referred to as SBU effectiveness or performance. The paper states that the measurement procedures and the reliability and validity of this variable are reported in Govindarajan (1988); no further details are given in the main text.

SBU competitive strategy operationalized in terms of Porter's (1980) low cost-differentiation framework and used as the moderator variable (X2) in the regression equations. The paper states that the measurement procedures and the reliability and validity of this variable are reported in Govindarajan (1988); no further details are given in the main text.

variable_name: Years of experience in research and development
description: Each respondent was asked to indicate the total years of experience accumulated in research and development, counting all jobs; it is one of a set of questions covering five functional areas. In this sample, 24 of the general managers had some prior experience in research and development.

Each respondent was asked to indicate the total years of experience accumulated in marketing/sales, counting all jobs; it is one of a set of questions covering five functional areas. In this sample, 72 of the general managers had some prior experience in marketing/sales.

Each respondent was asked to indicate the total years of experience accumulated in production/engineering, counting all jobs; it is one of a set of questions covering five functional areas. In this sample, 61 of the general managers had some prior experience in production/engineering. The hypotheses refer to this variable as experience in manufacturing or in production.

Each respondent was asked to indicate the total years of experience accumulated in finance/accounting, counting all jobs; it is one of a set of questions covering five functional areas. In this sample, 20 of the general managers had some prior experience in finance and accounting.

variable_name: Years of experience in general management
description: Each respondent was asked to indicate the total years of experience accumulated in general management, counting all jobs; it is one of a set of questions covering five functional areas.
Each respondent was asked to indicate the length of experience in current and closely related industries, counting all jobs.

The SBU general manager's locus of control, used as X1 in the regressions for Hypothesis 7 and taken from Rotter's internal-external control of reinforcement dimension. The paper states that the measurement procedures and the reliability and validity of this variable are reported in Govindarajan (1988); no further details are given in the main text.

Constructed from responses to a shortened version of Form F of the Meyers-Briggs Problem-solving Styles Indicator. The short form contains 17 forced-choice questions divided into two parts: Part I consists of nine questions instructing the respondent which answer comes closest to how he or she usually feels or acts, and Part II consists of eight pairs of words. Responses to the 17 items were used to construct two continuous measures; this one indicates whether the manager's perception was accomplished through sensing or intuition, where higher values of the variable indicated intuitive types.

Constructed from responses to a shortened version of Form F of the Meyers-Briggs Problem-solving Styles Indicator. The short form contains 17 forced-choice questions divided into two parts: Part I consists of nine questions instructing the respondent which answer comes closest to how he or she usually feels or acts, and Part II consists of eight pairs of words. Responses to the 17 items were used to construct two continuous measures; this one indicates whether the manager's judging was accomplished through feeling or thinking, where higher values of the variable indicated thinking types.

The firm's reported return on total sales in the baseline year (1978 or 1983). The authors note that ideally they would measure business unit profitability for the multi-business corporations in the dataset, but business line profitability data do not exist; corporate profitability is used because corporate-wide profits provide resources that can be used to maintain any business unit within the company.

Reported medical sector sales revenue in the baseline year, expressed in thousands of 1982 dollars based on the Producer Price Index. The natural log is taken in order to constrain the effect of outliers.

The natural log of the number of medical sector product lines that the business offered in the baseline year. The number of lines ranged as high as 56, but almost 60 percent of the businesses had only one or two lines: 223 single-line businesses (36%), 145 two-line businesses (23%), and 250 businesses with three or more lines (41%).

The number of medical sub-sectors in which a firm operates, treated as an alternative measure of scope; on average, firms in the sample are active in two sub-sectors. Product lines may be grouped according to product sub-sectors within an industrial sector to provide this measure of scope.

The dependent variable measures how long a business survived after the baseline year in which the firm entered the dataset. Firms that remained in the dataset in 1995 and firms that were acquired during the study period were treated as right-censored cases, because acquisition is a conceptually different outcome from business failure. Within the 618 cases, 212 (34%) continued in 1995, 199 (32%) shut down before 1995, and 207 (33%) were acquired before 1995.

The number of countries in which a firm had foreign subsidiaries, following Caves and Mehra (1986) and Kogut and Singh (1988). Because the count measure had significant positive skew, multinationality was defined as the logarithm of 1 plus the number of countries. Foreign subsidiary data came from the 1990 edition of the Directory of International Affiliations, and the variable was lagged in the models.
time_window: 1990 edition; entered lagged (t-1) relative to downside risk

description: The logarithm of 1 plus the number of equity joint ventures formed abroad or with a foreign partner during 1985-89, counted from public announcements. Announcements of preliminary discussions or venture negotiations were excluded so that the counts included only agreements that were actually consummated; the focus was on equity joint ventures rather than other alliance types.

A second-order root lower partial moment of a firm's annual return on assets (ROA) relative to a target level that changed over time, where the mean ROA for the firm's two-digit SIC industry in the preceding year was the proxy for the target. The squared difference term was summed over all years in the period 1990-94 in which the firm's ROA fell short of its target. Accounting data were obtained from COMPUSTAT.

The same second-order root lower partial moment specification as the ROA-based measure, calculated using return on equity (ROE) data instead, to reflect bankruptcy risk and creditors' interests; the lagged industry-average ROE served as the target. Miller and Reuer's factor analysis showed that this measure loads on the same factor as Altman's Z, an indicator of bankruptcy risk.

A mean lower partial moment CAPM beta measure calculated to consider shareholders' interests in firms' systematic risk. A firm-specific market model was estimated over the 1990-94 period for all months in which the market return fell short of the U.S. Treasury Bill rate. Stock returns data were acquired from CRSP, and interest rate data were obtained from the International Financial Statistics database.

For embedded firm dyads, the similarity of the two firms' network positions is the ratio of the smaller to the larger of the two firms' Bonacich (1987) eigenvector centrality scores. The eigenvector measure accounts for both direct and indirect ties, and each firm's score is computed for each year and normalized so that the eigenvector score of the most central firm in any year equals one. The variable ranges from zero to one, with higher scores representing higher similarity in network position between the firms.
time_window: each year, based on alliances accumulated over the previous five years

description: For dyads where at least one member is not in the main component, the variable represents the normalized Bonacich (1987) eigenvector measure of network centrality for the firm embedded in the main component. If neither firm of the dyad is a member of the main component, this score is set to zero.
time_window: each year, based on alliances accumulated over the previous five years

description: An event history was constructed for each dyad spanning the years 1993 to 2002; for each dyad-year record a dichotomous dependent variable indicates whether the pair of firms formed an alliance in the given year. Alliances reported among more than two firms are represented as alliance formation dyads among each of the firms included, and reverse-ordered dyads are discarded. This risk set consists of ties formed among members of the main component in different clusters, so that a positive outcome indicates shortcut formation.

The same dichotomous dyad-year dependent variable indicating whether the pair of firms formed an alliance in the given year. This risk set consists of dyads where one or both members are not embedded in the main component, capturing alliances by nonembedded firms with embedded firms and with each other. Multifirm alliances are represented as dyads among each of the firms included, and reverse-ordered dyads are discarded.

Number of partners represented in each alliance formed, used at the deal level of analysis. The authors examine the determinants of both the full risk set of deals and the subset of embedded deals formed solely within the main component.
time_window: deals formed 1994-2002, predictors lagged one year

description: For deal-level analyses, a binary variable that is set to one for alliances among embedded firms that have been formed with members of more than one cluster as indicated by CONCOR. The variable is set to zero if all the members of the embedded deal are members of the same CONCOR cluster.

For the full set of alliance deals, a binary variable that is set to one for alliances that include nonembedded firms. The variable is set to zero if all the members of the deal are already members of the main component.

Second-order construct measured with the items of the coordination, communication, and bonding dimensions. In the analysis the authors use a mean-based composite indicator of these items. The second-order three-factor model fits the data well and better than a one-factor or a constrained three-factor solution, and the first-order dimensions load highly on the second-order factor. The correlations between the first-order dimensions are high.
scale: seven-point Likert scale (1 = strongly disagree, 7 = strongly agree)
level: service provider's relationship with a particular vendor

description: Four items operationalize this dimension of alliance management capability. The items represent the establishment of processes that involve coordination of relationship-related activities across the relationship boundary, a firm's adaptation to its partner's work processes, and the adaptation of its incentive structures. The items were selected from organization theory and alliance research. The scale is used as a mean-based composite indicator in the regressions.
scale: seven-point Likert scale (1 = strongly disagree, 7 = strongly agree)
level: service provider's relationship with a particular vendor

description: Five items measure this dimension of alliance management capability. They reflect a firm's abilities to convey information that enables a partner to understand its market position, competencies, organizational features, and value proposition. The items were based on extant research that emphasizes the importance of communication in alliances. The scale is used as a mean-based composite indicator in the regressions.
scale: seven-point Likert scale (1 = strongly disagree, 7 = strongly agree)
level: service provider's relationship with a particular vendor

description: Six items measure this dimension of alliance management capability. They reflect a firm's attentive, considerate, and supportive behavior toward the partner, such as unconditional readiness for dialogue, willingness to stand by the partner in difficult times, and concern for the partner's viewpoint. The items were selected on the basis of prior alliance research and organizational literature on caregiving and organizational justice. The scale is used as a mean-based composite indicator in the regressions.
scale: seven-point Likert scale (1 = strongly disagree, 7 = strongly agree)
level: service provider's relationship with a particular vendor

description: The extent of joint action was measured by assessing how closely partners work together to accomplish various tasks or activities, using five activities where joint action of both parties was typical in the setting. In addition, respondents were asked what percentage of their marketing/promotional events per year are conducted together with their partner, what percentage of all project proposals per year are worked on together with their partner, and how many days per year employees from different functional areas attend training conducted by the partner. These additional measures correlated significantly with the measure for joint action. The multiple-item scale is used as a mean-based composite indicator.
scale: seven-point Likert scale for the five activity items (1 = strongly disagree, 7 = strongly agree); the additional measures are percentages and days per year
level: service provider's relationship with a particular vendor

description: Goal fulfillment was first captured by asking key informants in each company about the extent to which their firm had received valuable customer knowledge from the partner. Two items were used to collect this information, following prior research. The scale is used as a mean-based composite indicator.
scale: seven-point Likert scale (1 = strongly disagree, 7 = strongly agree)
level: service provider's relationship with a particular vendor

description: Respondents reported how well their firm had performed during the last three years relative to other partner firms of that vendor in terms of sales growth, profitability, return on investment, and ability to build customer loyalty. Similar indirect measures of firm performance have been used in prior alliance literature. The scale is used as a mean-based composite indicator.
level: service provider's relationship with a particular vendor

description: In 2005 the authors collected secondary information on the status conferred by a vendor on the focal firm from vendors' online partner directories that are updated annually. Partner status varies between 1 (no formal status) to 4 (highly preferred partner), so higher values indicate a higher status granted by the vendor.
level: service provider's relationship with a particular vendor

variable_name: customer knowledge, firm performance and partner status
description: Goal fulfillment is measured by three outcomes: customer knowledge received from the partner (two survey items), firm performance relative to other partners of the vendor over the last three years (survey), and the status conferred by the vendor on the focal firm (1 to 4, from online partner directories). Each is a separate dependent variable.

The yearly net change in the number of a chain's components that shared a name that identified them with each other and the chain. Net change was computed based on existing components' name changes and the names given to newly founded or acquired components during a year, thus capturing the chain's overall increase or decrease in common naming. A positive value indicates a net increase in the number of components sharing a common name, a negative value a net decrease.
scale: net count change, positive or negative
time_window: yearly net change in the current year

description: The proportion of a chain's components that did not share a common name in the prior year. Own local name concentration ranges from zero, indicating all components are commonly named, to one, indicating all components are locally named. It was included in the models to control for the main effect of organizational momentum and to obtain unbiased coefficients for the interactions.

The focal chain's number of commonly named component failures, weighted by the number of beds in each component. Thus, the value of the variable is equal to the total number of beds in the failed components. Support for H1a requires a negative coefficient.

The focal chain's number of locally named component failures, weighted by the number of beds in each component. The value of the variable is equal to the total number of beds in the failed components. Support for H1b requires a positive coefficient.

The number of commonly named component failures experienced by chains other than the focal chain, weighted by the number of beds in each failed component. The value of the variable is thus equivalent to the total number of beds in other chains' failed components; the size weighting is consistent with research on trait-based imitation.

The number of locally named component failures experienced by chains other than the focal chain, weighted by the number of beds in each failed component. The value of the variable is thus equivalent to the total number of beds in other chains' failed components.

For each industry the authors aggregated its chemical portfolio by measuring the distribution of emissions across all regulated chemicals in each year, producing a 347-dimension vector per industry. Chemical relatedness between a home industry and a target industry is computed as the similarity between the two industries' distributions of chemical emissions, following Sampson (2007); the algebraic formula given in the text is not legible in this payload. The measure varies between 0 and 1, where 1 represents the greatest similarity between two industries' distributions of chemical emissions. Because a company may be active in different home industries, the authors created a company-level measure as a weighted average using size (number of employees) in each home industry, then averaged the annual values over 1995-97.

Total value of environmental fines in target manufacturing industries (four-digit SICs) obtained from the IRRC. Because the dollar value of fines is likely to vary with industry size, the authors divided the industry fines measure by the number of firms in an industry to obtain an average value of fines per firm in each industry. This annual measure was then averaged over 1995-97. The operational formula given in the text is not legible in this payload.

Derived from the EPA database, which provides information about the ownership and industry (four-digit SIC) of every facility, so that every industry in which each sampled company had operations up to 1997 and every new industry entered during 1998-2003 could be identified. All manufacturing industries in which firms have to report toxic emissions formed the list of 384 potential target industries. For each firm-industry dyad that did not exist up to 1997, the variable was coded 1 if the combination was realized during the 1998-2003 period and 0 otherwise, making the unit of analysis a firm-industry dyad.

R&D investments in millions of U.S. dollars divided by the firm's annual sales, following similar prior studies. The authors focused on firms with R&D intensity of 1.0 or less because the original mean and standard deviation were high; a deletion of 42 firm-year observations left 2,004 firm-year observations in the final sample. All variables were standardized prior to being entered into the models.

The restricted stock value relative to the reference point was derived by computing CEO restricted stock value received in the previous year at year t - 2 and then subtracting this value from the current CEO restricted stock value at year t - 1. An indicator variable for restricted stock values comprises one where the previous restricted stock values at firm i drop below the reference point; this variable captures the below-reference-point deviation. The authors expect a negative coefficient because it indicates that, as deviation becomes more negative, R&D intensity increases.

The complementary portion (1 - I1) of the restricted stock deviation, corresponding to restricted stock values in firm i that either equal or exceed the reference point. The authors predict and find a significant negative coefficient, indicating that R&D intensity decreases as positive deviation increases.

The aggregate market value of restricted stock held by the CEO at fiscal year end, collected from ExecuComp. The variable is entered as the absolute level of CEO restricted stock to serve as a baseline against the relative pay model.
time_window: fiscal year end, lagged at t - 1

description: Dummy-coded 1 if the CEO also holds the position of board chairperson, and 0 otherwise.

The board vigilance measurement considers both the proportion of outside directors and their ownership stakes. The ratio of outsiders, the ratio of outside director shares to the firm's outstanding shares, and the ratio of outside director options to the options granted were standardized and then summed.

A binary variable equal to 1 if a possible provider-problem match was realized (that is, if provider i posted a response to problem j), or 0 if that possible match was not realized. Realized dyads are identified from the forum message logs and compared with nonrealized dyads drawn by choice-based sampling. It is the dependent variable in the rare-event logit models.

Our measure of expertise matching was constructed by capturing how similar the keywords in the provider's expertise description were to the keywords in the focal problem, using a keyword similarity approach. A list of 574 keywords derived from the 3,948 expertise descriptions in the company's expert yellow pages was used to construct a keyword-by-keyword similarity matrix, with the Salton cosine formula applied to keyword co-occurrence; the exact formula was not readable in the text. The provider-by-keyword matrix was multiplied by the keyword similarity matrix and then by the transposed problem-by-keyword matrix, and each cell was divided by the product of the total number of keywords in the expertise description and in the problem to restrict the indicator to between 0 and 1. Problems that addressed areas of expertise more similar to the expertise of the potential knowledge provider have a higher value.
Measured by counting the number of words in each problem posted to the forum. The squared term of this variable is used to test the predicted inverse U-shaped relationship with attention allocation.

Computed as the extent to which there was variety in the domains of expertise addressed in the problem. A hierarchical clustering analysis on the keyword-by-keyword matrix (Ward method with Euclidean distances; stopping rule of Duda and Hart) produced 19 clusters representing different domains of expertise inside the company, and the keywords appearing in each problem were classified into one or more of these domains; the formula itself was not readable in the text. The measure uses Teachman's entropy index, where pi is the proportion of keywords in domain i, so that problems whose keywords are spread more evenly across a higher number of expertise domains have a higher value.

Captures how different the focal problem is from problems previously posted to the forum, again using a keyword similarity approach. The problem-by-keyword matrix was multiplied by the keyword similarity matrix and then by the transposed problem-by-keyword matrix to generate a problem-by-problem matrix; each cell was divided by the product of the total number of keywords in the two problems, and the measure is the inverse of the average similarity between problem i and all other problems previously posted on the forum (problems posted after the focal problem are excluded). A problem containing keyword combinations that differ from those in previously posted problems scores highly; the formula itself was not readable in the text. Month and year dummies are included in the models because problems posted earlier in the observation period tend to display lower values on this measure.
time_window: all problems previously posted prior to the focal problem

description: Equal to the number of problems posted on the forum in the three working days prior to the focal problem being posted. The three-working-day window was chosen because close to 90% of the problems in the dataset were answered within this time frame. The squared term of this variable is used to test the predicted inverse U-shaped relationship with attention allocation.
time_window: three working days prior to the focal problem

description: The letter(s) sent by the activist to the target firm's management and board were content-analyzed with the Linguistic Inquiry and Word Count (LIWC) software after formatting to exclude headers, footers, page numbers, addresses, tables and exhibits. Confidence in tone is measured with LIWC's summary variable clout; greater clout is indicated by more we-words and social words and fewer I-words, negations, and swear words. LIWC's standard is to adjust the clout score for varying text lengths, and in the 203 campaigns with more than one letter the clout scores of the letters were averaged. The measure ranges from 0.23 to 0.99, with a mean of 0.78.

To identify the demands in each campaign and their outcomes the authors relied on Thomson Reuters ASSET4 ESG, which lists all demands issued by the activist in a campaign and reports the outcome for each demand. Campaign success is measured as the number of demands that the target firm agreed to divided by the total number of demands issued by the activist. If an activist is successful in achieving all demands, campaign success is coded as 100%; when they achieve none, it is coded as 0%.

Prior campaign success includes all campaigns launched in the previous three years. In line with the dependent variable, it is operationalized as the number of demands met divided by the total number of demands made. For activist investors that engaged in multiple campaigns during the three-year period, campaign success scores are averaged across these campaigns. If an activist did not launch any campaigns in the preceding three years, activist campaign success is coded as 0%.

The authors operationalize multiple activists as a continuous measure. For the sample of 475 campaigns, 83% are single-activist campaigns, 13% involve two activists, and 4% involve three or more activists.

Binary measure coded 0 or 1, with 1 indicating an exit from the bank in the two years prior to the failure and 0 otherwise. Ship jumpers were identified by examining year-end reports for the names of each bank's chairman, president, CEO, and executive vice presidents who were not on the initial list in each of the two years preceding the failure; this also established a benchmark for 'normal' employment mobility and retirement among the control firms.

Binary outcome measure coded 0 or 1, with 1 indicating that the title held after the failure is lower than the one held prior to the failure. The titles of all executives prior to the failure were coded into one of three groups (in order of importance): chairman/CEO; president; or executive vice president; a movement downward from one group to another constitutes a demotion. The measure exists only for executives who are found reemployed in Texas banking.
time_window: title as of July 1993 relative to the pre-failure title

description: Binary outcome measure coded 1 if the executive is employed in a different city than in his or her previous job and 0 otherwise. Leaving a community where relationships with clients and the community have been forged represents a significant cost to the affected executive. The measure exists only for executives who are found reemployed in Texas banking.
time_window: employment location as of July 1993 relative to the previous job

description: Dichotomous key independent variable identifying failed banks and matching non-failed banks. The sample comprised 437 public and private Texas banks that received FDIC intervention between 1 January 1985 and 31 December 1990; for each failed bank a matching non-failed bank that operated continuously from 1 January 1985 through 31 December 1990 was identified based upon geographic proximity and bank asset size.

Coded from a survey question that asked whether, after the focal patent by the incumbent firm, the inventor became self-employed within three years of the patent application date. Coded as 1 if the focal inventor transitioned to self-employment and 0 if the inventor continued to work at the same company after the focal patent. Relying on a self-employment indicator as a proxy for starting up a business is consistent with prior studies on knowledge workers; a further survey question on the year the business was started was used to eliminate cases in which self-employment does not refer to a start-up.
time_window: within three years of the patent application date

variable_name: Patent value as assessed by the inventor (top 50%)
description: Constructed from a survey question: 'In comparison with other patents in your industry or technological field, how would you rate the economic and strategic value of this patent?' Respondents ranked their patent as being in the top 10%, between the top 25% and top 10%, between the top 50% and top 25%, or the bottom 50%. In the regressions the authors examined both the individual categories and a dummy for whether the assessed value of the patent is higher or lower than the industry median, and about 57% of sample inventors believe their patent is in the top 50% relative to patents in the same technological domain. The measure captures the value of patented knowledge as perceived by the focal inventor.
scale: four ordinal categories (top 10%, top 25-10%, top 50-25%, bottom 50%); dummy coded 1 if above the industry median

variable_name: Patent value as assessed by the firm (top 50%, conditional)
description: The number of patent jurisdictions as shown in the EPO record in which the parent firm filed the patent, used as a proxy of value as assessed by the parent firm; overall costs increase linearly with the number of registered countries. To facilitate analysis and interpretation, the variable is dichotomized as 1 if the number of patent jurisdictions is above the median and 0 otherwise. Because the test of H2 proposes that the effect is conditional on a high valuation by the inventor, the measure is coded as 1 in instances when the valuation by both the inventor and the firm is in the top 50th percentile.
scale: count of patent jurisdictions; dummy coded 1 if above the median

description: Coded as 1 if the inventor declared that the firm 'used the patent for commercial purposes' and 0 otherwise. Approximately 67% of the patents in the sample were used for commercial purposes. The authors note that the variable may partially overlap with the licensing variable.
scale: binary (1 = used internally for commercial purposes)

description: Coded as 1 if the patent was licensed to a third party and 0 otherwise (only granted patents can be licensed), as reported by the inventor. Only licenses that occurred before the inventor exits the firm were counted. In the sample, 14% of the patents were licensed, which is similar to data used in prior work.
scale: binary (1 = licensed to a third party)
time_window: licenses occurring before the inventor exits the firm

description: Based on a survey question that asked inventors whether the focal patent belonged to a group of patents that 'crucially depend on each other in terms of their value, or in a technical way.' The dummy variable is coded as 1 if the patent was interdependent and 0 otherwise; in the sample, 47% of the patents were designated as interdependent with other patents. A version using the number of interdependent patents did not add explanatory power, so the dummy variable was reported.

variable_name: Patent number of technological domains (no. of IPC4 classes of the focal patent)
description: The number of IPC four-digit (IPC4) classes for the focal patent, where a higher number of classes means a less specialized patent. A median patent in the sample referred to one IPC4 four-digit class, with a maximum of four classes, and the sample includes patents classified in 142 IPC four-digit classes. The patent's technological classification is assigned by EPO examiners and based on the International Patent Classification.
scale: count of IPC4 classes (median of one, maximum of four in the sample)

description: Survey respondents indicated whether their firms either (1) 'introduced new products or services' and/or (2) 'upgraded an existing product line or service' over the last 36 months. Because each of these activities represents some level of newness in the firm's offerings relative to continuing to sell existing products, both activities were considered to qualify as new product development. The authors code a dichotomous dependent variable as '1' if the firm has either developed a new product or upgraded an existing product and '0' otherwise (i.e., the firm continues selling existing products/services).
scale: dichotomous (1 = new or upgraded product/service, 0 = neither)

description: Respondents were asked, 'Are practices of competitors in the informal sector no obstacle (0), a minor obstacle (1), a moderate obstacle (2), major obstacle (3), or a very severe obstacle (4) to the current operations of this establishment?' The authors also considered an alternative measure in robustness testing that simply asked whether the establishment competes against unregistered or informal firms.
Measured with a survey question asking respondents to rate the obstacle level presented by formal competitors, using the same scale as the informal competition measure.
scale: same scale as the informal competition measure (0 to 4 obstacle rating)

description: Drawn from a survey question asking respondents to indicate whether 'It is common for firms in my line of business to have to pay some irregular "additional payments or gifts" to get things done with regard to customs, taxes, licenses, regulations, services etc.' Answers were provided on a six-point scale from 'Never' to 'Always'; 'Don't Know' responses were included in the 'Never' category.

A regulatory obstacle index was first calculated by averaging respondent answers across seven categories of regulatory issues (alpha = 0.75). This index was then regressed against a set of industry and country dummies from the data along with a measure of the amount of time senior managers spend dealing with regulations. The residuals from that regression were used as the measure of regulatory optimism, coded such that individuals who score higher rate the regulatory environment more optimistically than predicted by industry, country, and amount of time dedicated to addressing regulations.

The number of hierarchical levels between a given ideator and a given evaluator is used as a proxy for perceived hierarchical similarity. The variable captures the inverse of the absolute difference between the ideator's and the evaluator's number of levels to the CEO (absolute difference × (−1)); it ranges from −7 (most dissimilar) to 0 (most similar, i.e., same hierarchical level). The organizational code displayed next to the ideator's name on the crowdfunding platform was used and verified against the organizational charts.
Main dependent variable of the field study, capturing whether or not an evaluator invested any money into a given idea.
scale: binary (whether or not money was invested)

description: The horizontal proximity between any given creator–evaluator pair, measured as Reitzig and Sorenson (2013) did. From smaller to larger units, the organization was structured into departments, business units, and divisions. Creator–evaluator pairs were coded as laterally close if they were in the same business unit or closer, and as laterally distant if they were in the same division or more distant; the variable is depicted as 1 = close and 0 = distant.

Content distance between the proposed idea and previous innovation projects at Alpha.
