The textual description of each idea is compared to the descriptions of 12,000 projects implemented by the organization in the previous 4 years; word descriptions were stemmed, converted to lowercase, and stripped of punctuation, numbers, blank spaces, and stop-words, then transformed into word vectors in a bag-of-words approach. The cosine similarity between each idea vector and the vector representing all projects from the project database is deducted from 1, using a weighting strategy that emphasizes unique words.
time_window: previous 4 years for the reference projects

description: Participants were randomly assigned to one of three hierarchical levels (top vs. medium vs. low level) and were shown their position in an organizational chart. Within subjects, three ideas were presented, each associated with a creator's hierarchical level, and hierarchical similarity between the evaluator's and the creator's hierarchical level is the predictor in the replication analysis.
The experiment's dependent variable, reported as Idea selection, based on the participants' evaluations of the three ideas they were asked to read and evaluate.

Participants saw the last idea they had rated again and answered the authors' measure of Hierarchy-based homophily, using an adapted scale (see Greenberg & Mollick, 2017). It was used to test the indirect effect of hierarchical similarity on idea selection.

For each year examined the sample was divided into two ownership groups. A firm was designated externally-controlled if at least 5 percent of the stock was controlled by a single individual or organization not involved in management of the company, and management-controlled when no single party controlled 5 percent or more of the stock. Firms where top managers themselves held 5 percent or more of the stock were eliminated from the sample. In the moderated regressions a dummy variable represented the externally-controlled category, so management-controlled firms are the omitted comparison category.

Compensation was measured as the sum of cash pay (salary, bonus, and miscellaneous fringe benefits) plus the value of stock options granted during the year, with stock options valued by a modified version of the Black-Scholes option valuation model. Compensation, along with other monetary variables, was expressed in 1983 dollars to adjust for CPI inflation. Change in pay for year t - 1 to t was calculated by dividing the increase (or decrease) in CEO compensation from year t - 1 to t by the level of pay for the year t - 1. Results were essentially the same when change in cash pay (without options) was used as the dependent variable.
time_window: year t - 1 to t, over the 1978-1982 data period

description: Change in sales in year t (using net revenues as reported in COMPUSTAT) was calculated by dividing the increase (or decrease) in sales from year t - 1 to t by firm sales for the year t - 1.

Profitability was assessed as return on equity (ROE). Because ROE could be negative, change in ROE could not be computed as a proportion; hence, the increase (or decrease) in ROE from year t - 1 to t served as the measure.

Shareholder returns were computed by dividing the sum of the change in stock price and dividends paid during the year by the stock price at the beginning of the year. As with ROE, because this measure could be negative the increase (or decrease) from year t - 1 to t was used to compute change scores.

Industry pay was determined by averaging the pay of all CEOs in each respective industry sample each year. Change in industry pay was calculated by dividing the increase (or decrease) in industry pay from year t - 1 to t by the level of industry pay for the year t - 1.

Tenure as CEO was measured as the number of years an individual had been chief executive as of year t, obtained from the Dun and Bradstreet Reference Book of Corporate Management and proxy reports. It was the only variable in the analysis not assessed as a change score.
A dummy variable for CEOs for whom year t was their first year in the position, but not in the firm.
A dummy variable for CEOs who were new to the firm entirely in year t.

variable_name: percent of stock held by the single largest nonofficer shareholder
description: A continuous measure of external stock concentration used in place of the categoric ownership dummy in a replication of the moderated regression. It is described as most analogous to the categoric scheme, simply without a cutoff.

Binary dependent variable for each carrier-route combination. It takes the value zero as long as the airline has not yet entered the market and the value one in the month of market entry; observations for all months following the first entry are excluded from the sample. Only the first time an airline enters a market is considered, because re-entries after exits likely follow a different logic.

Count of unique aircraft types operated by an airline, the authors' preferred flexibility measure. It is measured in the month preceding the entry decision and tells how many different aircraft types could theoretically be used on a new route to adjust to the demand patterns of this route. A carrier's flexibility increases with the number of aircraft types it operates because each will usually have a different number of seats, which allows for a more precise matching of capacity and demand.
time_window: last month (month preceding the entry decision)

description: Coefficient of variation in total industry demand of a given market across the five years prior to each entry decision, that is, the standard deviation of passengers transported on a route divided by the mean number of passengers transported on that route. The coefficient of variation is used because routes serving a larger number of passengers would otherwise mechanically produce higher levels of absolute demand variation.
time_window: five years prior to each entry decision

description: Total Route Variation multiplied by the R-squared of a regression of average demand (across carriers) on a constant, calendar-month fixed effects and a linear time trend, estimated for each route and each month on the demand of the five preceding years. It captures the part of the demand variation that can be explained by those factors; the exact regression equation is not readable in the text. It distinguishes markets with the same level of demand variation but different levels of predictability, and lower values mean demand variation that is harder to predict.

Total Route Variation multiplied by (1 - R-squared) of the same route-level regression of average demand on a constant, calendar-month fixed effects and a linear time trend over the five preceding years. It captures the part of the demand variation that cannot be explained by those factors, so higher values mean variation that is more difficult to predict.

Subscale of the 18-item imaginativeness survey measure developed for this study, administered to the sample of 506 participants. Items were rated on a seven-point Likert-type scale ranging from 1 (strongly disagree) to 7 (strongly agree). The measure demonstrated strong convergent and discriminant validity, and reliability of 0.93 for creative imaginativeness.

Subscale of the 18-item imaginativeness survey measure developed for this study, administered to the sample of 506 participants. Items were rated on a seven-point Likert-type scale ranging from 1 (strongly disagree) to 7 (strongly agree). The measure demonstrated strong convergent and discriminant validity, and reliability of 0.92 for social imaginativeness.

Subscale of the 18-item imaginativeness survey measure developed for this study, administered to the sample of 506 participants. Items were rated on a seven-point Likert-type scale ranging from 1 (strongly disagree) to 7 (strongly agree). The measure demonstrated strong convergent and discriminant validity, and reliability of 0.89 for practical imaginativeness.

The number of new venture ideas a participant generated in Part I of the study, based on a description and diagram of facial recognition technology, after being asked to generate as many potential business ideas as possible. Two expert raters independently scored the quantity (number) of ideas generated. This measure served as one of the dependent variables.

The rated quality of the single best idea each participant selected and described in Part II of the study, scored independently by two expert raters. Idea quality was viewed as the combination of originality and feasibility. Originality was operationalized using Dean and colleagues' (2006) four-point originality scale ranging from 1 (common, mundane, or boring business idea) to 4 (rare, unusual, ingenious, imaginative, or surprising business idea), and feasibility using a three-point scale ranging from 1 (low feasibility) to 3 (high feasibility). The overall interrater reliability of the idea quality measure was acceptable (ICC = 0.92).

CEOs reported their own FWC over the past year using six items from the measure of FWC of Carlson et al. (2000), limited to the time-based and strain-based items; the three behavior-based items were excluded based on feedback from the conference planning committee. Sample items include 'The time I spent on family responsibilities often interfered with my work responsibilities' and 'Because I was often stressed from family responsibilities, I had a hard time concentrating on my work.' The six items were on a five-point Likert scale ranging from 1 = 'strongly disagree' to 5 = 'strongly agree,' and the FWC score is the mean across items.
time_window: past year, measured at Time 2 (three months after Time 1)

description: CFOs evaluated their CEOs' decision-making comprehensiveness over the past year using the five-item scale of Miller et al. (1998), recently used and validated by Souitaris and Maestro (2010). Sample items include 'When faced with an immediate, important, non-routine threat or opportunity, the CEO usually develops many alternative responses' and 'The CEO considers many different criteria and issues when deciding the course of action to take.' Items were on a five-point Likert scale ranging from 1 = 'strongly disagree' to 5 = 'strongly agree,' and the score is the mean across items.

CEOs rated their level of job engagement over the past year using the 18-item scale of Rich et al. (2010). Example items include 'I have felt energetic in my job' and 'I have been interested in my job' (emotional engagement), 'At work, I have focused a great deal of attention on my job' and 'At work, I have concentrated on my job' (cognitive engagement), and 'I have exerted my full effort to my job' and 'I have tried my hardest to perform well on my job' (physical engagement). CEOs responded on a five-point Likert scale, and the 18 items were averaged to obtain the score.

Objective data on firm financial performance was obtained from the consortium in the form of return on assets. In line with prior recommendations, the authors calculated an average ROA over two quarters after survey data collection to reduce bias caused by single-quarter outliers.
time_window: two quarters after survey data collection (Time 4)

description: My measure of performance is missedscan, calculated weekly for each store as the sum of all of the missed scans during restocking. A missedscan is generated when an error occurs in the end-of-night reconciliation portion of the new restocking practice: the store computer lists an item as out-of-stock but its corresponding shelf placement is not scanned in the end-of-night process. Higher values indicate worse performance, so the variable runs opposite to the construct as named.

Captures the district pilot store's prior performance in missedscan errors. It is disclosed at the beginning of the week along with all the other district stores' missedscans, before any restocking has occurred. Higher values mean worse pilot performance, so the variable runs opposite to the construct as named.

Captures the extent to which a store's prior week restocking performance can be used to predict this week's performance. Since the prior week's performance is known at the start of the new week, before any restocking has occurred, the restocking supervisor can use it to inform decisions for the new week. The authors note that capturing learning from own experience has traditionally relied on quantifying repetitions of the new practice, but past performance may also predict current performance to the extent that learning is motivated by performance improvement aims; higher values mean worse own performance.

Indicator variable equal to 1 if the focal store's restocking performance is better - that is, fewer missedscan errors - than that of its pilot, and equals 0 otherwise. This indicator is interacted with prior performance of both the focal store and its pilot to measure the extent of imitative learning under conditions in which the pilot has superior and inferior performance.
scale: binary (1 = focal store performed better than its pilot)

description: A time-varying count of the number of de novo firms in the disk array market in a given year, measured at t-1 in the entry models and at t in the exit models. De novo status was determined from the source materials and recorded with a dummy variable indicating de novo status.
time_window: annual, lagged one year in entry models

variable_name: Density of Boston area firms / Density of California firms / Density of Bay Area firms
description: Time-varying counts of the number of array producers located in each of the three geographic areas where producers agglomerated and a place identity was operative in the market: the Boston Area (Route 128), California, and the Bay Area in Northern California. Densities were grouped by geographic area rather than by continuous distance because the theoretical distinction is categorical.
time_window: annual, lagged one year in entry models

variable_name: Density of California de novo firms / Density of Bay Area de novo firms / Density of Boston area de novo firms
description: Time-varying counts of de novo producers within specific geographical areas, for example California de novo producers and, most narrowly, Bay Area de novo producers. These narrowest counts were used to test the hypotheses about geographically agglomerated de novo producers.
time_window: annual, lagged one year in entry models

description: A time-varying count of the total number of products of a particular kind on the market in a given year, constructed from information on firms' annual product counts. A narrower count was also built for the non-captive array market of OEM, PCM, reseller and distributor products.
time_window: annual, lagged one year in entry models

description: The array market is the unit at risk; entry models use quarterly counts of array producers entering the array market, with covariates updated every quarter except annual measures of industry revenue and venture capital array funding. A firm's first date of product shipment signified its entry into the array market.

The dependent variable was disbanding/exit to another industry, defined to include events of unknown type; firms known to have ended by merger or acquisition were treated as censored on the right at the times of these events. Tenure in the disk array market was calculated from quarterly entry and exit data, and the duration scale was broken at 2.0 and 4.0 years.

variable_name: Founding and disbanding/exit rates of array producers (vital rates)
description: Establishment of the form is not scored as its own variable. The paper states that the empirical test of the proposition consists of relating the focused-identity density counts to the vital rates of the population, so the construct is operationalized as the dependent variables of the entry and exit models: quarterly counts of array producers entering the market, and the disbanding/exit-to-another-industry rate of producers. Rising founding rates and falling mortality rates with initial increases in density are read as legitimation of the form.
scale: quarterly entry counts (negative binomial) and instantaneous disbanding/exit rate
level: market (entry, quarterly) and firm (exit, annual spells)

description: In structured interviews each unit manager evaluated each dyadic interface between their unit and the other 19 units. With the aid of graphic diagrams of Thompson's (1967) typology of interdependence, managers recorded their perceptions of interunit interdependence for each dyadic interface ranging from no interdependence to pooled, sequential, and reciprocal. The recording was conducted without any input from the researcher and revealed each unit manager's operational assumptions on interunit task interdependence.
scale: ordinal: no interdependence, pooled, sequential, reciprocal

description: In interviews with the division managers, theoretically possible types of interdependence based on Thompson's (1967) typology were critically assessed in light of task constraints, and division managers and the researcher collaboratively specified 'the type of interdependence that should be assumed as the basis for coordination' for each divisional unit dyadic interface. The determination was not simply the division managers' perceptions but a detailed critical analysis of each interface in which the researcher presented his observations.
scale: ordinal: no interdependence, pooled, sequential, reciprocal

description: The various modes of integration for each dyadic unit interface were ascertained in structured interviews with the division managers and unit managers, who were presented with the prescribed set of modes of integration based on previous research rather than being asked for an open narrative response. Data were coded as nominal level (0/1) and were based on the Guttman-type sequence with higher level modes inclusive of lower level modes, corroborated by the researcher's observations during the four-month period. In the analysis five successive modes are specified, each inclusive of the preceding modes.
scale: ordinal sequence of five cumulative modes

description: Based on earlier work, theoretically predicted (optimal) modes of integration were identified for each dyadic unit interface based on the interdependence levels for that interface. In dyads where predictions resulted in ties, the tie breaking criterion was lower versus higher information processing requirements. The optimal modes were predicted from prior theory and also tested in the study.

The levels of interdependence were operationalized as ordinal scales, so the deviation between the perceived and the latent interdependence could assume positive or negative values and its magnitude was the number of levels deviating. The authors report that in 24.5% of the cases perceived interdependence is one level lower than latent interdependence, in 10.0% two levels lower, and in 0.5% three levels lower, while in only 0.7% of the cases the perceptual error is in the opposite direction.
scale: number of ordinal levels deviating, positive or negative

description: The deviation between the theoretically predicted (optimal) mode of integration and the actual observed mode of integration for each dyadic unit interface, computed on the ordinal sequence of modes of integration so that the magnitude is the number of levels deviating. The authors report that in 19.7% of the cases the deviation is one level, in 10.5% two levels, and in 2.6% three levels.

A five-item scale, with each item ranging from 1 to 5, completed by the focal unit managers for each dyadic unit interface and summed across the five items. Scale development included standard psychometric procedures including principal component analysis for discriminant validity, and a coefficient alpha of 0.93 was obtained. The scale includes items examining the extent to which the focal unit a had an effective working relationship with unit j, the extent to which unit j fulfilled its responsibilities to unit a, the extent to which unit a fulfilled its responsibilities to unit j, the extent to which the coordination was satisfactory, and the positive or negative effect on productivity as a result of the coordination.
scale: sum of five items each rated 1 to 5

description: Dyadic openness is simply the number of individuals in focal unit a communicating for purposes of coordination to unit j. It is useful for determining the degree to which a focal unit is open versus restricted to external information flow.

Calculated as the sum of the incoming communications for purposes of coordination from unit j to focal unit a, divided by the sum of the number of staff in unit j plus the number of staff in unit a. In the notation given, F jai is the sum of the communications from respondent i in unit j incoming to focal unit a, nj is the number of staff in unit j, and na is the number of staff in unit a.

Calculated as the ratio of outward communications for purposes of coordination from the respondent in focal unit a who exhibits the largest number of communications to unit j, divided by the sum of the outward communications from unit a to unit j. Centrality addresses the centralization of information flow.

Calculated as the ratio of the observed number of communication links in the focal unit a-unit j dyad to the number of potential communication links in the dyad; the formula reduces to twice the total observed communication links divided by the sum of the staff in the two units minus one. Dyadic connectivity has utility in ascertaining the level of communication.

Calculated as the ratio of total outward communications for purposes of coordination to total incoming communication between unit a and unit j. Dyadic reciprocity has been utilized to examine the degree to which information flow is asymmetric.
scale: ratio of outward to inward communications

description: Calculated as the proportion of staff in focal unit a initiating communications for coordination purposes to unit j plus the proportion of staff in unit j initiating communications to focal unit a. Multiplexity is useful in observing the proportion of staff interacting across units.

A network isolate measure calculated as the proportion of staff in unit a that did not initiate (i.e., send) communications for purposes of coordination with unit j. The isolate proportion is used in the network literature because of its utility in identifying isolation from communication.

Technology closeness of submarket j to all submarkets in the industry at time t, computed as the average of the pairwise closeness between submarket j and every other submarket using the submarket-level analog of Jaffe's uncentered correlation approach. Technology profiles were built by decomposing the technology words recorded for fabs into single words, cleaning them, and counting the most frequently appearing technologies for each submarket-year. The pairwise correlation runs from 0 (orthogonal profiles) to 1 (perfectly coinciding profiles), and the average closeness denotes how close a submarket is to the industry average with regard to the technologies it uses. The authors include the measure to exploit its variation over time, where increasing closeness means convergence.

Market closeness of submarket j to all submarkets in the industry at time t, computed as the average of the pairwise closeness between submarket j and every other submarket from the products fabs produce, using the same uncentered correlation approach applied at the submarket level. Product profiles were built by counting the most frequently appearing product words for each submarket-year, and the pairwise correlation runs from 0 to 1. The measure denotes how close a submarket is to the industry average with regard to the key functionalities of the products it produces, with increasing closeness meaning convergence.

A multilevel categorical variable equal to one if firm l stops operating fab i in submarket j at time t and zero otherwise; it is the failure event in the event-history models of the likelihood to exit or reposition through fab closure. Fabs drop out of the WFW dataset only when they are no longer in operation, i.e. shut down by the company, and even when fabs are acquired, sold, spun off or renamed they remain in the dataset under the same assigned record identifier. Continued fab operations in a submarket are treated as the success of entrants and incumbents.

Coded one if firm l has more than one fab at time t and zero otherwise, and also coded one for single-fab firms that have been active in the industry for more than eight years. The coding ties incumbent inertia to both firm size and age, while firms with one fab are treated as more flexible to changes. Fabs of entrants that were acquired by an industry incumbent were recoded thereafter as incumbent fabs, and fabs that entrants bought from an incumbent were recoded thereafter as entrant fabs.

An n-dimensional technology vector whose elements are the counts of submarket j's most-used technologies at time t, constructed by decomposing the technology words recorded in the fab data into single words, cleaning them, and counting the most frequently appearing technologies for each submarket-year. It denotes the underlying technological knowledge base of a submarket and is the input to the technology closeness measure.

An m-dimensional market profile vector whose elements are the counts of submarket j's most-used products at time t, constructed by counting the most frequently appearing product words for each submarket-year. It denotes the product characteristics and key functionalities that provide customer benefits in a submarket and is the input to the market closeness measure.

A continuous measure of the stated performance target minus the realized performance. An earnings target above the realized value is treated as an upward-striven, aggressive target and one below as conservative. For firms that provide a range instead of a specific EPS target, the target is taken as the midpoint of the stated range, and the measure is trimmed at the 99th and 1st percentiles.
time_window: t+1 (target disclosed during the fiscal year, realized earnings revealed two to three months after the fiscal period end)

description: Debt ratio is debt in current liability divided by the total asset. The authors also report analyses splitting debt into short-term and long-term components.

The sum of institutional shares with less than five percent of a firm's outstanding shares. Because institutional ownership fluctuates over the course of the year, the maximum value of the quarterly data is used.
time_window: t (maximum of the four quarterly values)

description: The total percentage of firm shares owned by investors with more than five percent of a firm's outstanding shares. The maximum value over the four quarters of the year is used because institutional ownership fluctuates over the course of the year.
time_window: t (maximum of the four quarterly values)

description: Tie strength was measured with the three-item scale developed and validated by Levin and Cross (2004), capturing the closeness and interaction frequency of a relationship between two parties. Respondents reported the strength of the interpersonal ties with each of the advisors they listed. An overall tie strength score for each respondent was computed as the average of the values of tie strength with each of the advisors listed.

Bridging ties were gauged by nonredundancy using an ego-centered network instrument. Respondents identified the five most important sources, internal or external to the firm, from whom they sought business-related information and advice regarding new product and market opportunities, and reported the extent of the presence of ties among these five sources. A nonredundancy score was computed as (potential ties - actual ties)/number of advisors, where potential ties and actual ties range from zero to 10 and the number of advisors equals the total number of advisors listed (zero to five). Values range from zero to two, with high scores indicating a network rich in bridging ties.

A composite IC score was made based on the original scores for Taiwan and the United States from the GLOBE scale (House et al., 2004). The measure is defined at the national level and is used to contrast the two cultural contexts.

This dependent variable was measured by a three-item scale adapted from Ozgen and Baron (2007) and Singh et al. (1999b). The scale gauges both the ability to recognize opportunities and the alertness to opportunities when they appear to exist.

Following Litov et al. (2012), the authors create a vector reflecting the sales distribution of a focal firm across all its segments and an industry benchmark vector (centroid) reflecting the benchmark strategy in the focal firm's primary industry, using three-digit SIC industries. The raw uniqueness measure is the product of the difference between these vectors. As the raw measure is left-skewed, the authors multiplied it by 100 and used a natural log-transformation for the final measure of strategy uniqueness.

The authors follow Bushee's (1998) institutional investor classification, which is based on the portfolio turnover and holding concentrations of institutional investors, and merge it with ownership information from Thomson One Banker. The measure considers all of the shareholdings of dedicated institutional investors and subtracts the shareholdings of transient institutional investors.

The measure combines three analyst-related variables: analysts' forecast errors, measured as the absolute difference between actual earnings per share and the consensus of analysts' EPS forecasts scaled by the stock price at the beginning of the year; analysts' forecast dispersion, the standard deviation of analysts' EPS forecasts scaled by the stock price at the beginning of the year; and analysts' forecast variability, the volatility (standard deviation divided by the mean) of the consensus forecasts over a three-year period. Z-scores of the three individual measures are added up into a single composite hard-to-value measure. The hard-to-value industry variable is then the industry average of this measure based on a three-digit SIC industry classification, excluding the focal firm.
level: firm-year (industry average assigned to the firm)

description: Sustainalytics' proprietary aggregate score for the firm's relations with capital providers, reported annually on a 0 to 100 scale, used as a surrogate measure of investment in this stakeholder group. For the set-theoretic analysis the score is transformed into a fuzzy set with the indirect method, using percentile-based crossover points (the 25th percentile for the minimum set, the 50th for the median set and the 75th for the maximum set).

Sustainalytics' proprietary aggregate score for the firm's relations with employees, reported annually on a 0 to 100 scale, used as a surrogate measure of investment in this stakeholder group. The score is calibrated into fuzzy sets using the same percentile-based crossover points as the other stakeholder groups.

Sustainalytics' proprietary aggregate score for the firm's relations with suppliers, reported annually on a 0 to 100 scale, used as a surrogate measure of investment in this stakeholder group. The score is calibrated into fuzzy sets using the same percentile-based crossover points as the other stakeholder groups.

Sustainalytics' proprietary aggregate score for the firm's relations with customers, reported annually on a 0 to 100 scale, used as a surrogate measure of investment in this stakeholder group. The score is calibrated into fuzzy sets using the same percentile-based crossover points as the other stakeholder groups.

Sustainalytics' proprietary aggregate score for the firm's relations with environmental groups, a secondary stakeholder group, reported annually on a 0 to 100 scale. The score is calibrated into fuzzy sets using the same percentile-based crossover points as the other stakeholder groups.

Sustainalytics' proprietary aggregate score for the firm's relations with local communities, a secondary stakeholder group, reported annually on a 0 to 100 scale. The score is calibrated into fuzzy sets using the same percentile-based crossover points as the other stakeholder groups.

Fuzzy set of high performance built from the industry-adjusted ROE lagged one year, defined as net income over total firm equity. It is calibrated with the indirect method using the 25th, 50th and 75th percentiles of the ROEaj distribution as full non-membership, crossover point and full membership respectively.

Fuzzy set of very high performance built from the same industry-adjusted ROE lagged one year, calibrated with the indirect method using the 50th (full non-membership), 75th (crossover) and 99th (full membership) percentiles of the same distribution. It serves as the alternative operationalization of the outcome alongside high performance.

Industry advertising expenses-to-sales ratios and budgets published annually by Schonfeld & Associates are used as a surrogate measure of industry differentiation. A total of 56 six-digit GICS industries were considered, with a median advertising-to-sales ratio of 1.6 percent, which is used as the crossover point to classify industries into high and low differentiation.

R&D intensity, defined as R&D expenses over total sales for each firm, is used to distinguish innovative from non-innovative firms in the population. The median of the R&D intensity distribution, 1.7 percent in the sample, is the crossover point used to separate low innovation from high innovation groups.
scale: R&D expenses over total sales, in percent

description: Firms are split into European firms, which the authors assume to be affected by stronger CSR regulation, and U.S. firms, assumed to operate under softer CSR regulation. The two groups are analysed separately, with high and very high performance calibrated within each group's own ROEaj distribution.

Coded 1 if the subject is in the treatment with high exchange value uncertainty and 0 otherwise. Exchange value uncertainty is operationalized as the extent to which the costs each seller will face to deliver high quality to each buyer vary from period to period; in the high treatment costs are randomly drawn from a discrete uniform distribution of integers between 0 and 100, and in the low treatment from a discrete uniform distribution between 45 and 55, so that the expected cost (50 points) is the same in both treatments and only the dispersion of costs changes. Costs are private information: neither buyers nor sellers are informed about the exact costs of other sellers, though both are informed that seller costs can vary from period to period.

The difference between the price offered by the incumbent seller and the minimum price offered to the same buyer by any other seller in a particular period. Its lower bound is zero, which occurs when the incumbent seller is offering the lowest price on the market in a particular round. It is, on average, significantly higher in the high exchange value uncertainty treatment and thus essentially captures the hypothesized effect of exchange value uncertainty on buyers' inclination to move out of ongoing relationships.

Dependent variable coded 1 if the buyer accepted an offer from a seller other than the incumbent (i.e., the seller with whom the buyer transacted in the previous period), and 0 otherwise. Instances where the buyer has not accepted any offer are omitted. The decision is observed in each experimental round as a discrete-time event history procedure.

For a particular seller, the overall number of transactions performed in previous periods by each buyer who accepted the seller's offer in a given period is first computed; Commitment is then the proportion of that buyer's transactions that were made with that particular seller up to the current period. It ranges from 0 (the buyer has never transacted with that seller) to 1 (the buyer has only transacted with that seller), with intermediate values indicating intermittent exchange.

Dependent variable coded 1 if the seller delivers high quality to the buyer who accepted his or her offer in a given period, and 0 if the seller delivers low quality. Only observations where both the buyer and the seller have not exited (i.e., when they have agreed on a certain price) are used.

Treatment variable coded 1 when contracts are available and 0 otherwise. In the treatment where contract enforcement is possible, buyers choose whether to offer a contract simultaneously with their acceptance of a particular seller offer, and sellers are informed about the existence of a contract; in the other treatment contract enforcement is neither allowed nor mentioned. The contract forces sellers to deliver high quality whenever they choose low quality and is enforced with 50% probability; using a contract costs buyers five experimental points in every round.

Dichotomous measure coded 1 if the buyer offered a contract to the seller from whom he or she accepted a price offer, and 0 otherwise; it is computable only for the treatment where buyers were given the contract option. Unlike the treatment variable Contract, it is both time varying and buyer specific.

Sum of the scores for items 1, 2, 3 (reverse scored), and 6 of the trust questionnaire, collected at the end of each experimental session on a seven-point Likert scale measuring buyers' agreement with statements about people in general (Cronbach alpha = 0.822). Items 4 and 5 were dropped because they did not display a clear pattern of loading in the two-factor model, and the final measure is standardized to facilitate comparison.
scale: sum of four seven-point Likert items (standardized)

description: Sum of the scores for all four corresponding questionnaire items, where item 2 is reverse scored, collected at the end of each experimental session on a seven-point Likert scale (Cronbach alpha = 0.851). The final measure is standardized to facilitate comparison.
scale: sum of four seven-point Likert items (standardized)

description: Measured as the sum of the number of toys recalled by the focal firm in a given quarter. Recall data for 1998 to 2007 come from the Consumer Product Safety Commission, the independent federal regulatory agency charged with protecting the public from unreasonable risks from consumer products. The authors report that the 21 firms that recalled toys collectively experienced recalls of over 56 million toys.

Measured as the sum of all toys recalled in a given quarter, excluding a focal firm's toys. It thus captures the level of recall activity by the focal firm's competitors in the same industry and quarter.

Articles published in the 50 largest U.S. newspapers by circulation and blogs were identified with the Lexis-Nexis database from the first quarter of 1998 through the first quarter of 2008, resulting in approximately 37,500 articles and blog postings. The content of the articles and blogs about each firm in a given quarter was analyzed with Linguistic Inquiry and Word Count (LIWC) software and coded as positive if its total affective content was at least 66 percent positive and as negative if its total content was at least 66 percent negative. The measure is the difference between the number of positive and the number of negative articles and blog posts published about a firm, measured in the quarter of each recall and the following quarter to account for the effect of the recall as well as the firm's information subsidies.
time_window: quarter of each recall and the following quarter

description: Coded through structured content analysis of more than 5,500 firm press releases disseminated via the Business Wire and PR Newswire databases (Krippendorff's alpha of 0.90 for technical actions). Because some companies made several announcements about the same action while others made only one, each action type was coded 1 for a quarter in which a firm announced the action and 0 otherwise, and the binary measures of the action types belonging to the technical category were summed. Actions are measured in the quarter following the measure of wrongdoing to ensure they occurred after wrongdoing.
time_window: quarter following the measure of wrongdoing

description: Coded through structured content analysis of firm press releases disseminated via the Business Wire and PR Newswire databases (Krippendorff's alpha of 0.86 for ceremonial actions). Each action type was coded 1 for a quarter in which a firm announced the action and 0 otherwise, and the binary measures of the action types belonging to the ceremonial category were summed. Actions are measured in the quarter following the measure of wrongdoing.
time_window: quarter following the measure of wrongdoing

description: The dichotomous measure found is equal to 1 if the individual founded a firm in that year and zero otherwise. The pooled logit models predict the likelihood that an individual will become an entrepreneur, taking into account the right-side censoring effect. The time interval for the pooled logistic regression is one year.
time_window: annual observations from the individual's graduation year through the survey

description: Barriers to growth are operationalized through two time-period dummies for the two constitutional reforms. To test the impact of moderately lowering barriers to growth, time period 1 is defined as a 1 for observation periods after the 1988 reform (1989-1999) and 0 otherwise. Time period 2 is defined as a 1 for observation periods after the 1999 reform, which substantially lowered barriers to growth, and 0 otherwise. Time period 0 (1978-1988) is the excluded baseline.

Human capital is measured with an index built from multiple measures capturing ways individuals could acquire higher productivity skills. The index includes education level (master's and doctorate degrees compared to bachelor's degree only), promotion (an indicator for whether the individual has been promoted to general manager or technical manager), and student leader (an indicator for leadership experience as a leader in a student government). These variables loaded onto a single factor (varimax with oblique rotation, eigenvalue > 1), and the human capital index is mean centered at 0.

Firm size is measured by latest employees, the number of employees in the most recent year the firm was still in operation, logged to reduce skew. Failed firms are included, and so there is no survival bias. It is the dependent variable in the Heckman regressions, with the initial firm size controlled so that the analysis focuses on firm growth.
time_window: most recent year the firm was in operation before the 2007 survey

description: Survey item in which respondents were asked to indicate the level of growth in their industry sector, as shown in Question I of the Appendix. The item was used, together with strategic breadth, to sort ventures into the four industry growth/strategic breadth categories. The text does not describe the scale or the aggregation beyond this.

Five survey items were used to measure the strategic breadth of each venture: range of products, broadness of markets, number of market segments, number of customers, and number of distribution channels. The coefficient alpha of the five items was 0.63, which the authors judge an acceptable level of reliability. An individual venture's strategic breadth score was computed as its mean score on the five strategic breadth items.

Return on sales, one of two objective measures used in the study. The authors chose it because profitability measures have been widely used in studies of small firm and new venture financial performance. The text does not describe how the measure was computed.

Sales growth, one of two objective measures used in the study. The authors note that 'changes in sales' was overwhelmingly the most popular operationalization of new venture performance in the reviewed studies. The text does not describe how the measure was computed.

One of fourteen strategic variables describing a firm's competitive philosophy and practice, measured with a questionnaire item in the same format as those for industry growth and strategic breadth. Respondents indicated the emphasis their venture placed on entering on a large, aggressive scale when compared to other firms in their industry.

One of fourteen strategic variables describing a firm's competitive philosophy and practice, measured with a questionnaire item in the same format as those for industry growth and strategic breadth. Respondents indicated the emphasis their venture placed on attracting capital from outside investors when compared to other firms in their industry.

One of fourteen strategic variables describing a firm's competitive philosophy and practice, measured with a questionnaire item in the same format as those for industry growth and strategic breadth. Respondents indicated the emphasis their venture placed on new product development when compared to other firms in their industry.

variable_name: Ownership of patents or proprietary processes
description: One of fourteen strategic variables describing a firm's competitive philosophy and practice, measured with a questionnaire item in the same format as those for industry growth and strategic breadth. Respondents indicated the emphasis their venture placed on the ownership of patents or other proprietary knowledge when compared to other firms in their industry.

One of fourteen strategic variables describing a firm's competitive philosophy and practice, measured with a questionnaire item in the same format as those for industry growth and strategic breadth. Respondents indicated the emphasis their venture placed on innovation in manufacturing processes when compared to other firms in their industry.

One of fourteen strategic variables describing a firm's competitive philosophy and practice, measured with a questionnaire item in the same format as those for industry growth and strategic breadth. Respondents indicated the emphasis their venture placed on specialty products when compared to other firms in their industry.

One of fourteen strategic variables describing a firm's competitive philosophy and practice, measured with a questionnaire item in the same format as those for industry growth and strategic breadth. Respondents indicated the emphasis their venture placed on customer service when compared to other firms in their industry.

One of fourteen strategic variables describing a firm's competitive philosophy and practice, measured with a questionnaire item in the same format as those for industry growth and strategic breadth. Respondents indicated the emphasis their venture placed on premium pricing when compared to other firms in their industry.

One of fourteen strategic variables describing a firm's competitive philosophy and practice, measured with a questionnaire item in the same format as those for industry growth and strategic breadth. Respondents indicated the emphasis their venture placed on low cost when compared to other firms in their industry.

One of fourteen strategic variables describing a firm's competitive philosophy and practice, measured with a questionnaire item in the same format as those for industry growth and strategic breadth. Respondents indicated the emphasis their venture placed on advertising and promotion expense when compared to other firms in their industry.

One of fourteen strategic variables describing a firm's competitive philosophy and practice, measured with a questionnaire item in the same format as those for industry growth and strategic breadth. Respondents indicated the emphasis their venture placed on the dominance of marketing expertise in its top management team when compared to other firms in their industry.

One of fourteen strategic variables describing a firm's competitive philosophy and practice, measured with a questionnaire item in the same format as those for industry growth and strategic breadth. Respondents indicated the emphasis their venture placed on developing new channels of distribution when compared to other firms in their industry.

One of fourteen strategic variables describing a firm's competitive philosophy and practice, measured with a questionnaire item in the same format as those for industry growth and strategic breadth. Respondents indicated the emphasis their venture placed on brand identification and name recognition when compared to other firms in their industry.

One of fourteen strategic variables describing a firm's competitive philosophy and practice, measured with a questionnaire item in the same format as those for industry growth and strategic breadth. Respondents indicated the emphasis their venture placed on forward integration when compared to other firms in their industry.

A dichotomous variable reflecting the presence of the control orientation in the passage of the firm's proxy statement devoted to explaining and justifying its board leadership structure. A value of 1 indicates that the orientation was conveyed in the proxy statement, and a value of 0 indicates it was not; a value of 0 for one orientation does not indicate anything about the other orientation. Two human coders (including the author) independently identified the presence or absence of the orientation, with discrepancies resolved by the author, and inter-rater reliability was sufficient (kappa = 0.73).

A dichotomous variable reflecting the presence of the collaboration orientation in the passage of the firm's proxy statement devoted to explaining and justifying its board leadership structure. A value of 1 indicates that the orientation was conveyed in the proxy statement, and a value of 0 indicates it was not; a value of 0 for one orientation does not indicate anything about the other orientation. Two human coders (including the author) independently identified the presence or absence of the orientation, with discrepancies resolved by the author, and inter-rater reliability was sufficient (kappa = 0.75).

The lagged return-on-assets term, where ROA is calculated as net income divided by total firm assets. The lagged term is included in the appropriate models as a control and moderator variable, and it was standardized prior to analysis to avoid multicollinearity.

The lagged return-on-sales term, where ROS is calculated as net income divided by total firm revenues. The lagged term is included in the appropriate models as a control and moderator variable, and it was standardized prior to analysis to avoid multicollinearity.

Growth in return-on-assets. ROA is calculated as net income divided by total firm assets, and the growth measure consists of the difference between the profitability measure in year t and the profitability measure in year t-1.

Growth in return-on-sales. ROS is calculated as net income divided by total firm revenues, and the growth measure consists of the difference between the profitability measure in year t and the profitability measure in year t-1.

Financial resources are captured by the size of the production budget that is allocated to each film and within which it must be completed. This budget represents one of the most critical inputs into production. The variable was measured in millions of U.S. dollars and logged to reduce the influence of skew.

Sequels were used as the indicator of an established brand resource available to producers. Because they build on a prior movie, sequels are easily identifiable for audiences and can offer the advantages of a brand. A dummy variable (0/1) indicated whether or not a film was a sequel to a previous film; 87 movies in the sample were sequels.

The director was used to measure human resources because the producer works closely with the director throughout the entire process of development and production of the film. Talent of this human resource was assessed through the professional recognition the director had received for previous work: a dummy variable indicates whether the director had ever been nominated by the Director's Guild of America (DGA) for a major professional award (0/1). Using nominations rather than wins avoided being overly restrictive; 18 percent of directors in the sample had received a nomination.

A count of the number of previous films the producers working on a focal film had cumulatively produced prior to the current film. The data was gathered from the work histories of each producer as listed on IMDB.com. Groups of producers ranged in experience from 0 to 67 prior films produced with a mean of 6.5 films.

The total box office revenue generated from the U.S. release of each film served as the indicator of financial performance. Although this does not include revenues from other sources, the U.S. box office revenue is the most widely used indicator of financial success for a film in Hollywood. The variable was measured in millions of U.S. dollars and logged to address the skew in box office figures.

The probability p with which the Manager observes each task position independently, fixed by treatment at 0.2, 0.5, 0.8 or 0.9 for the whole session and known ex ante by all agents. The authors focus on values of p below the information threshold of 0.82 computed from the benchmark model, so that lower values of p correspond to higher environmental uncertainty.

In each round the Manager chooses Worker θ1 and θ2 by assigning each a 'placement' between 0 and 100, and the distance between the two selected positions measures team heterogeneity. The authors also compute the deviation of the selected positions from the optimal positions predicted by the benchmark model and use that deviation as the dependent variable in their moderating analyses.

In the Selector stage the Manager decides at the start of each round whether she or the Workers will complete the switch task, that is, whether the round is played in a Centralized or a Decentralized environment. The authors measure the percentage of rounds in which each Manager delegated task allocation to the Workers, and also compute the proportion of rounds in which the Manager chose the organizational structure predicted by the benchmark model.

Score on the cognitive reflection test, the number of correct answers to three questions designed to measure deliberative thinking and resistance to impulsive choices; the test was unincentivized. The authors pool scores above zero and compare less reflective (CRT = 0) with more reflective (CRT > 0) Managers.
An incentivized risk elicitation measure completed after the Selector stage. The authors classify Managers as more risk averse (EG ≤ 4) or more risk tolerant (EG > 4).

In each organization, project performance was measured by interviewing managers who were at least one hierarchical level above the project and functional managers and asking them to indicate on a 5-point Likert-type scale whether a project team was performing above, below, or at the level expected of it, given the particular technical activities on which it was working. Managers evaluated only projects they were personally familiar with and knowledgeable about, and evaluations were made independently and submitted confidentially. On the average, between four and five managers evaluated each project, and their ratings were averaged to yield project performance scores. To clarify the distinction between high and low project performance, performance measures were converted to normalized scores with a mean of 0.
scale: 5-point Likert-type scale; then normalized scores with a mean of 0

variable_name: influence over technical details of project work
description: Respondents in matrix structures indicated on 7-point Likert-type scales the degree to which their project and functional managers influenced the technical details of their project work. Scale responses ranged from 1 for "my project manager dominates" to 7 for "my functional manager dominates"; the middle point, 4, indicated that influence was balanced between the two. Individual member responses were averaged to calculate an overall project score.
scale: 7-point Likert-type scale (1 = project manager dominates, 4 = balanced, 7 = functional manager dominates)

variable_name: influence over salary increases and promotions
description: Respondents in matrix structures indicated on 7-point Likert-type scales the degree to which their project and functional managers influenced their salary increases and promotions. Scale responses ranged from 1 for "my project manager dominates" to 7 for "my functional manager dominates"; the middle point, 4, indicated that influence was balanced between the two. Individual member responses were averaged to calculate an overall project score.
scale: 7-point Likert-type scale (1 = project manager dominates, 4 = balanced, 7 = functional manager dominates)

variable_name: influence over having been selected to work on the project
description: Respondents in matrix structures indicated on 7-point Likert-type scales the degree to which their project and functional managers influenced their having been selected to work on the project. Scale responses ranged from 1 for "my project manager dominates" to 7 for "my functional manager dominates"; the middle point, 4, indicated that influence was balanced between the two. Individual member responses were averaged to calculate an overall project score.
scale: 7-point Likert-type scale (1 = project manager dominates, 4 = balanced, 7 = functional manager dominates)

variable_name: influence over the overall conduct of the organization
description: Respondents in matrix structures indicated on 7-point Likert-type scales the degree to which their project and functional managers influenced the overall conduct of the organization. Scale responses ranged from 1 for "my project manager dominates" to 7 for "my functional manager dominates"; the middle point, 4, indicated that influence was balanced between the two. Individual member responses were averaged to calculate an overall project score.
scale: 7-point Likert-type scale (1 = project manager dominates, 4 = balanced, 7 = functional manager dominates)

description: The dependent variable is constructed by comparing a firm's industry portfolio at year t and t+3 based on the U.S. 2-digit SIC code and counting the number of industries that were present at t+3 but not at t. Business segment descriptions reported in Chinese were manually matched with the U.S. 2-digit SIC code system because the detail of segment reporting varied across firms. The three-year window was chosen as a reasonable time span for the activities and procedures involved in an acquisition. The number of new industries entered ranges from 0 to 9, with an average of 0.99.

Measured as the logged number of laid-off workers from the SOEs that went bankrupt in a given year in a province, collected at the provincial level from statistics yearbooks. Provincial-level variables were assigned to a firm based on the province where it was headquartered.
scale: logged count (actual range of the logged value in the data was from 0 to 13)
time_window: each year, measured at time t

description: Coded 1 if the governor could serve only one existent political term in a given year before the next Communist Party Congress (i.e., is on one's last political term), 0 otherwise. It is a time-varying variable that changes from 0 to 1 for a relatively young leader who could serve multiple terms; political terms depend on how many Congresses a leader can experience before reaching the age of 65.
time_window: each year, measured at time t (2001-2008)

description: Coded in the same way as the retiring governor: 1 if the provincial party secretary could serve only one existent political term in a given year before the next Communist Party Congress, 0 otherwise. Information was collected from the résumés of provincial party secretaries serving between 2001 and 2011.
time_window: each year, measured at time t (2001-2008)

description: Coded as the number of instances of labor protests and strikes that took place in the focal province each year, obtained from the website called ''China Strikes,'' which maintains records of publicly reported workers' strikes across China by province. Because the data on collective actions were available only after 2003, the value in each province in 2003 was used for 2001 and 2002.
time_window: each year; 2003-2012 source coverage, with 2003 values imputed to 2001 and 2002

description: Measured as the number of years between 1990 and the year a firm had an IPO, then reverse coded so that the greater the value of the variable, the stronger the socialist imprint. The variable was dropped as a main effect due to its lack of variability over time, but its interaction terms remained.
time_window: years between 1990 and the firm's IPO year

description: Coded 1 if a firm's main industry was in one of the regulated industries and 0 otherwise. Prior studies have considered finance, banking, electricity, water, oil and gas, petroleum, telecommunication, and pharmaceutical industries as regulated, and studies in the Chinese context suggest that real estate is regulated as well. The variable was dropped as a main effect due to its lack of variability over time, but its interaction terms remained.

Firm performance is measured using Tobin's q, estimated as the ratio of the sum of the market value of equity and the book value of debt to the book value of a firm's assets. Values above 1 reflect the value created by firms through the effective management of resources, while values below 1 reflect the value lost through the mismanagement of resources. The measure is taken in the same period as strategic change.
scale: ratio; above 1 reflects value created and below 1 value lost

description: HR slack is operationalized as the difference between a firm's employees-to-sales ratio and the average employees-to-sales ratio across other firms in the industry. Because the interest is in measuring slack resources, negative values (which reflect relative resource deficits and thus indicate an absence of slack) were set equal to 0.

Financial slack is measured as the difference between a firm's current ratio, computed as the ratio of current assets to current liabilities, and the current ratio of other firms in the industry. Negative values of this measure were set equal to 0 to reflect the absence of slack.

Banks' strategies are assessed based on relative client mix, which refers to the ratio of business loans to consumer loans. Historical trends in the client mix of each bank were constructed by setting a bank's historical strategy equal to a two-year moving average estimated using an autoregressive moving average approach; deviations from this moving average reflect a change in strategy and were converted into z-scores to capture the magnitude of the strategic change, and the absolute value of the z-score was used. Banks with a z-score greater than 1 were categorized as having engaged in strategic change and those with a z-score less than 1 as not having engaged in strategic change in a given period, and all analyses were run separately for these two groups.
scale: z-score (absolute value); categorized as greater than 1 versus less than 1

description: Human capital investment is captured as the ratio of the financial resources that a firm directs to salaries, bonuses, and training over the total number of employees in the firm. The measure of change in human capital investment represents the year-over-year difference in this value. A focus on the change in, rather than the absolute value of, a firm's human capital investment is used because the interest is in a firm's new allocations to human capital in a given year.

Each respondent rated every department's influence on each strategic decision as well as the importance of each decision to the success and destiny of the organization, using a five-point Likert-type interval scale (reliability measures of the instrument ranged from a = 0.89 to a = 0.98). INFLUENCE was determined by first averaging all respondents' scores for a particular department and decision; every department's scores were then weighted for each decision's importance and averaged over all the strategic decisions of the organization.

Respondents were asked to allocate 100 points for each department in their organization among the five categories that would best describe each department's influence on the important decisions of the organization. For each organization, the scores for each department on each power base were then averaged across all the respondents.

The measure of each department's activity with respect to a specific boundary spanning role was determined by factor analysing the responses to the boundary spanning instrument. This procedure yielded three factors which are the three boundary spanning roles used here, with reliability a = 0.89. The measure of a department's relative activity with respect to a specific boundary spanning role is the department's factor score on that role.

Three industries were selected to correspond to each of Thompson's technologies, using two bases of classification: the degree to which internal activities are standardized (and are therefore structured, predictable, and repetitive) and the degree to which internal activities are sequentially synchronized (and therefore require co-ordination and scheduling). Food processors represent long-linked technology, financial institutions mediating technology, and general hospitals intensive technology.

System openness is operationalized by the industry group, ordered from more closed to more open. Food processors (long-linked technology) represent the more closed system, financial institutions the middle, and general hospitals (intensive technology) the more open system. The tests compare the influence results across the three industries.
scale: three industry groups ordered by openness

description: The firm-specific, time-varying coefficient on log fund family size from the risk-adjusted gross yield equation, estimated separately for each fund family and each month using only data from the prior 24 months. It captures scale economies that operate through portfolio selection ability. Larger values represent higher economies of scale.
time_window: prior 24 months for each fund family-month

description: The firm-specific, time-varying coefficient on log fund family size from the weighted-average expense ratio equation, estimated separately for each fund family and each month using only data from the prior 24 months. The sign on this measure is reversed because lower costs, like higher gross yields, are better, so that larger values represent higher economies of scale.
time_window: prior 24 months for each fund family-month

description: A fund family's market share is the sum of the total net assets of all of its MMMFs, expressed as a percentage of the total industry-wide TNA. Relative market share is the difference between its market share and the industry-wide average market share of all fund families at the same point in time; taking advantage of the fact that all market shares sum to 100 percent, this relative measure automatically controls for the number of competitors in the market.

Family Age appears in the second-step model predicting relative market share both as a main effect and interacted with portfolio selection scale economies and with expense scale economies. The paper does not describe how it is computed.

The percentage of board members counted as independent outsiders. Board members were counted as independent outsiders only if they were not current or former employees, family members of firm executives, or otherwise affiliated with the firm. The variable is measured annually in the year prior to the quarter in which the institutional investor first buys stock.
time_window: annual, measured in the year prior to the quarter in which the institutional investor first buys stock

description: Coded 1 if the CEO is not the chair of the board, following previous research. The variable is measured annually in the year prior to the quarter in which the institutional investor first buys stock.
time_window: annual, measured in the year prior to the quarter in which the institutional investor first buys stock

description: A Boolean variable where a value of 1 indicates that a particular institutional owner added a particular semiconductor firm to its portfolio in a particular quarter. Each quarter, dyads were created of each institutional owner matched with all of the semiconductor firms that it did not already own; an investor was included in a quarter only if it added a new semiconductor firm to its portfolio that quarter.

A factor derived from Bushee's measures of the dimensions of trading strategy, based on eight variables that capture the trading history of an institutional owner; principal factor analysis revealed that the eight variables load onto two factors, one of which is block-holding, the sizes of stakes institutional investors typically take. The measures are based on the entire portfolio of every institutional investor; the variables were computed for each institution each quarter and a moving average of each variable over the previous four quarters was calculated. The sample was split at the median value for block-holding.
time_window: moving average over the previous four quarters

description: A factor derived from Bushee's measures of the dimensions of trading strategy, based on eight variables that capture the trading history of an institutional owner; principal factor analysis revealed that the eight variables load onto two factors, one of which is turnover, how long institutional investors hold stock. The measures are based on the entire portfolio of every institutional investor; the variables were computed for each institution each quarter and a moving average of each variable over the previous four quarters was calculated. The sample was split at the median value for turnover.
time_window: moving average over the previous four quarters

description: The Thomson-Reuters Institutional Holdings (13F) database classifies each institutional investor into one of five categories: banks, insurance companies, mutual funds, investment funds, and foundations. To test Hypotheses 3a and 3b the authors created one subsample for mutual funds and another for all other types of institutional investors. The authors analyzed trading behavior within each legal type and found that legal type is not a proxy for trading strategy.

Performance above historical aspirations is the difference between actual performance and aspiration levels when performance exceeds aspirations and is '0' otherwise, constructed with spline functions. The historical performance aspiration level is a function of the firm's prior performance (ROA at time t-1) and the aspiration level at year t-1, which equals ROA in t-2; the weight of past performance against past performance aspirations (the adaptation rate) is set at alpha equal to 0.7, the value that provided the best model fit. The aspiration formula itself is not readable in the extracted text. The variable is lagged by 1 year.

Performance above social aspirations is the difference between actual performance and the social aspiration level when performance exceeds aspirations and is '0' otherwise, constructed with spline functions. The social aspiration level of a focal firm in year t is based on the ROA of other firms sharing the same 4-digit SIC code as the focal firm in year t. The variable is lagged by 1 year.

Composite of four non-obtrusive indicators of narcissistic tendencies: (1) prominence of the CEO's photograph in the annual report, coded on a five-point scale from '1' if there was no photograph of the CEO to '5' if the CEO was photographed alone and the photo occupied more than half a page; (2) CEO prominence in company press releases, the number of times the CEO was mentioned by name divided by the total number of press releases in a year; (3) the CEO's relative cash pay, total cash compensation (salary and bonus) divided by the second highest paid executive's cash compensation; and (4) the CEO's relative noncash pay, the sum of the CEO's deferred income, stock grants, and stock options divided by the sum of these same items for the second highest paid executive. A two-year moving average of each indicator was computed, each indicator was then standardized, and the mean value of the standardized scores across the four indicators is the measure of CEO narcissism.
time_window: two-year moving average of each indicator

description: The dependent variable is the number of acquisitions made by a firm in a given year, counting acquisitions that led to a majority ownership of the target firm, consistent with Kuusela et al. (2017). It is a non-negative count variable.

Counts the number of forward citations received in the six years following the grant year of the focal patent. Self-citations are not excluded from this dependent variable, following Fleming (2001), although self-citations are also included as a control. The six-year window is chosen because most of the information available in forward citations appears in the first five years.
time_window: six years following the grant year

description: Constructed at the patent level and captures the number of USPTO categories (three-digit primary patent classes) being recombined by the focal patent, as indicated by the patent class listed on each patent that the focal patent cites, i.e., based on its backward citations. All sample patents recombine at least two different primary classes. For example, the value for patent 5,845,166 is 6.
time_window: application year of the focal patent

description: Defined at the organization level as the number of previous patents filed by the focal organization that featured the exact same combination of USPTO classes as the focal patent, counted until the year prior to the year in which the focal patent was filed. The natural logarithm of this count is taken to account for the marginally declining effect of experience. A quadratic specification of experience was also examined in robustness checks.
time_window: until the year prior to the focal patent's application year

description: Constructed at the organization level as a Herfindahl index, computed as the sum of the squares of the shares of each distinct recombination of USPC patent classes filed by the organization during the focal year. A low value indicates dispersion of the organization's inventive activity among various combinations in a given year, whereas a high value indicates focus (higher concentration of search). For example, Agfa's 19 patents across 15 distinct combinations in 1993 produced a low value, while its five patents across two recombination types in 1987, one accounting for 80% of the total, produced a high value.
time_window: focal year (contemporaneous with the focal patent)

description: Conventionality is measured by the number of times each opera has been produced by all the opera companies in the population in the previous three years. The observed market identity order is the sum of the conventionality differences between adjacent operas in the observed repertoire, and the minimum market identity order is the same sum computed with the operas arranged by conventionality in ascending or descending order. The market identity order is the difference between the observed order and the minimum order divided by the minimum order and repertoire size; higher values indicate more interspersion. The algebraic specification is printed as a formula whose rendering is unreadable in the available text.
time_window: conventionality based on the previous three years; statistical analyses start in 1998

description: Conventionality is measured by the number of times each opera has been produced by all the opera companies in the population in the previous three years. The observed market identity order is the sum of the conventionality differences between adjacent operas in the observed repertoire, and the minimum market identity order is the same sum computed with the operas arranged by conventionality in ascending or descending order. The market identity order is the difference between the observed order and the minimum order divided by the minimum order and repertoire size; higher values indicate more interspersion. The algebraic specification is printed as a formula whose rendering is unreadable in the available text.
time_window: conventionality based on the previous three years; statistical analyses start in 1998

description: The percentage of available tickets that are sold as season tickets. It is the dependent variable in the season-ticket analysis, where the relevant product for season-ticket buyers is the entire yearly repertoire. The variable is also included lagged by one year in the change model.

A binary variable coded one if a particular opera performed by a particular opera company in a particular year gets critical attention from any of the nine most prominent newspapers covering classical music, and zero otherwise. The nine newspapers are the New York Times, the Los Angeles Times, the Washington Post, the San Francisco Chronicle, the Boston Globe, the Wall Street Journal, the Houston Chronicle, the Dallas Morning News, and the Chicago Tribune.

Binary variable identifying the onset of the treatment, which equals zero for the years before enactment of the law (2003-2007) and one for the years after enactment of the law (2008-2012). Its interaction with Private, Property law × Private, captures the differential effect of the property law on private firms compared with SOEs.

Binary treated-group variable that equals one if a firm is majority owned or ultimately controlled by private entities or individuals and zero if majority owned or ultimately controlled by the government (at the central or local level) or its agencies. Data on ownership and ultimate controller are available in CSMAR.

Ratio of intangible assets to total assets. The measure 'intangible assets' in the database, according to China's accounting standards, includes patents, nonpatent technologies, trademarks, copyrights, franchises, and so on; goodwill (business reputation) is not included in this measure.

Ratio of fixed assets to total assets. According to China's accounting standards, fixed assets include buildings, machines, machinery, transportation vehicles, other equipment and instruments, and tools that firms can use for more than one year and are related to firms' production and operation.

Ratio of long-term debt to total assets, used to capture the role of debt financing as a mediator. The authors focus on long-term debt because firms' short-term debt (less than one year) is used for firms' temporary financial needs rather than resource investment purposes.

Ratio of external equity to total assets, used to capture the role of equity financing as a mediator. The numerator, external equity, is calculated as total equity minus capital reserve and minus retained earnings for firm i in year t.

variable_name: intangible assets and fixed assets ratios
description: Resource investment is measured by two ratios to total assets. Intangible assets is the ratio of intangible assets (patents, nonpatent technologies, trademarks, copyrights, franchises, excluding goodwill) to total assets. Fixed assets is the ratio of fixed assets to total assets. A robustness check combines them into Aggregated assets.
