Markets where i was dominant were paired with markets where j was dominant and these markets were counted as reciprocal. Measured in the year prior to the observation year, using counts rather than ratios to limit collinearity with the nonreciprocal variable.
time_window: t-1 (year prior to the observation year)

description: The shared markets remaining after markets where partner i was dominant were paired with markets where partner j was dominant were counted as nonreciprocal. Measured in the year prior to the observation year, using counts rather than ratios to limit collinearity with the reciprocal variable.
time_window: t-1 (year prior to the observation year)

description: A binary variable indicating whether an alliance was terminated ('1') or survived ('0') during that year. Because SDC did not report termination dates, the authors tracked each alliance across its lifetime using archival sources and a multistep approach, treating dissolution, discontinuation, spinoff or acquisition dates, or the date of last reported activity as termination.

Following Jaffe's uncentered correlation approach, each firm's technological portfolio served as a proxy for its technological resource base and was constructed as a vector of the distribution of its patents across technology groups, using CPC coding of technology groups. Technological overlap is the uncentered correlation between the two partners' vectors; the coefficient ranges from zero to one, increasing with greater overlap between partners' technological portfolios.
Information from SDC Platinum, verified using archival sources, indicates whether an alliance involved R&D activities. SDC's notation 'RDS' was coded '1' and all other alliances were coded '0'.

Total scheduled passenger traffic (sum of individual billion RPKs) of constellation Cj at year t. To avoid a spurious correlation with the size of a carrier's individual customer base, the carrier's own total passenger traffic is excluded from the variable. The variable is measured twice, considering the composition of the carrier's constellation as defined both implicitly and explicitly.

Average distance between the main hubs of all carrier-pairs within constellation Cj at year t, in thousands of kilometers. The main hub of a carrier is the city with the highest number of departing connections to other cities for that carrier, as evidenced by the Traffic by Flight Stage database. The value is largest when carriers' headquarters are scattered around the globe and small when carriers are closely situated.
Ratio of carrier i's available seat capacity (ASK) to the total seat capacity of its constellation Cj at year t. It indicates the carrier's relative size within its constellation.

Sum over all cities k in the constellation's route network of the standardized betweenness centrality of city k, w_kt(Cj), multiplied by p_ikt, the proportion of all carrier-routes from city k serviced by carrier i at year t. Betweenness centrality is computed with UCINET from a matrix of global city-pairs for each year, where each entry is coded 1 if at least one member of constellation Cj offers a flight from one city to another at year t. The measure indicates a carrier's dominance of traffic involving cities in the constellation's network, weighted by the criticality of those cities.

Proportion of constellation Cj's passenger traffic (RPK) that comes from members to which carrier i is bilaterally tied at year t; the ratio of traffic coming from those members to the total traffic of the constellation excluding carrier i's own traffic. It measures the extent to which the carrier is connected with members controlling large traffic flows.

Carrier i's passenger load factor at year t: the ratio of the carrier's total traffic, measured in revenue passenger kilometers (RPK), to its overall seat capacity, measured in available seat kilometers (ASK), expressed in percent. It is a simple and standard industry metric of airline operational performance.

Dummy variable equal to 1 if carrier i belongs to some explicit constellation at year t, and 0 otherwise. Membership is based on public announcements of carriers' membership in airline constellations and their departure from those groups, as recorded in Airline Business and other sources obtained through Nexis-Lexis. A carrier is assumed to be a member in a given year if it announced its association with the group in the first half of that year.

Each article was analyzed using the negative emotion dictionary in the LIWC (Language Inquiry Word Count) program; LIWC measures a construct by counting the number of words from a particular dictionary that appear in a given text and produces a score for each article based on the percentage of words from that content category. Articles about the sample firms were extracted from Factiva from the Wall Street Journal, Business Week, Forbes, Fortune, the New York Times, and the Washington Post, excluding articles that did not mention the firm in the title or lead paragraph, had fewer than 50 words, or mentioned more than four other firms. Article-level scores were averaged for all articles in a given firm-year to represent the overall evaluation of the firm in that year.
time_window: Articles published 2001-2005; variable lagged one year relative to the dependent variable

description: Data on six dimensions of strategy were collected from Compustat to form the measure of strategic change. For each ratio the value in the prior year was subtracted from the current year's value and the absolute value of that difference was taken; these values were then standardized and the average of the six dimensions was used to represent the extent of strategic change. Large changes to these ratios from one year to the next represent important changes to a firm's resource allocations, whereas a lack of change represents persistence.

Board independence was measured as the proportion of outside directors sitting on the firm's board of directors. Only nonaffiliated directors were included in this measure, meaning that directors did not have employment, family, or business ties with the focal firm.
Firm performance was measured as the total stock returns in a given year. This market-based measure was used to test the hypothesized moderating effect in Model 3.
time_window: Given year; independent variables lagged one year

description: The authors also used an efficiency-based measure of performance, return on assets (ROA), shown in Model 4. They adjusted for industry differences in ROA by subtracting the industry mean performance.
time_window: Given year; independent variables lagged one year

description: Acquisition is defined as a binary variable, coded as 1 for the actual acquisitions and 0 for potential, unrealized acquisitions. The analyses are run on 6,638 acquirer-target pairs, including 79 actual acquisitions and 6,559 potential but unrealized acquisitions, formed by the potential acquirer-actual target pairing approach.
scale: binary (1 = actual acquisition, 0 = potential, unrealized acquisition)

variable_name: Acquiring firm's connection to focal provincial government
description: Coded as 1 if the CEO has previous or current service experience as (a) an official in the provincial government of the focal province where the target firm is located, (b) a representative in the provincial Congress or Conference of the focal province, or (c) a representative of the focal province in the National Congress, and 0 otherwise.

variable_name: Acquiring firm's connection to rival provincial government
description: Coded as 1 if the CEO has previous or current service experience as (a) an official in the provincial government of another province outside the focal province, (b) a representative in the provincial Congress or Conference of another province, or (c) a representative representing another province in the National Congress, and 0 otherwise.

variable_name: Acquiring firm's direct connection to central government
description: Coded as 1 if the CEO has previous or current service experience as (a) an official in the central government, or (b) a representative in the National Congress or Conference, and 0 otherwise.

variable_name: Acquiring firm's indirect connection to central government
description: A continuous variable defined as the sum of percentages indicating birthplace ties, school ties, and workplace ties between central officials and provincial officials. Birthplace ties are calculated as the percentage of Politburo members born in the same province as the provincial government's party secretary and governor, respectively, summed; school ties are calculated the same way using alma mater; workplace ties are the percentage of Politburo members who served as chief administrators in the provincial government before being promoted to the central government.
scale: percentage points, summed across three tie types

description: The difference in age and the difference in tenure of party membership between party secretaries and between governors are first calculated; these differences are then summed for party secretary and governor, respectively. Provincial official similarity is the reverse code of the sum of age and party tenure differences between both party secretaries and governors.
The difference of GDP size between the focal and rival provinces, reverse coded.

Coded as 1 if the focal and rival provincial governments are in the same greater administrative area, and 0 otherwise. China's 33 provincial-level divisions can be grouped into six greater administrative areas: North China, Northeast China, East China, Central and South China, Northwest China, and Southwest China.

A dummy variable indicating a Qualified LID, coded as one when the LID has all four qualities from the quad model and zero otherwise. The authors measure it as a dummy because Hambrick and colleagues suggest that if a director is missing any of these qualities he or she is much less likely to be an effective corporate overseer. The four underlying indicators are prior appointment relative to the CEO, three or more prior board appointments, no other full-time position, and pay more than 30% above average board pay.

The primary measure is a sum of the number of misconduct-related reports in the media across eight categories: fraud, corruption, embezzlement, patent infringement, copyright infringement, discrimination, corporate espionage, and antitrust lawsuits. Only RavenPack events with a relevance score of at least 80 and in which the focal firm is identified as the defendant are used. Media reports categorized as legal issues are excluded from this broad measure.

A narrower measure of misconduct that includes only the number of acts of fraud in which the focal firm is coded as the defendant for a fraud-related report in the RavenPack dataset. It is presented as a more closely aligned measure of likely misconduct.

A dummy variable with a value of 1 if there was at least one news story related to the eight misconduct components in which the focal firm was identified as the defendant, and 0 if no incidents of misconduct were reported. The authors note that only 8% of observations had at least one such event.

Proposals made by shareholders to the firm are collected from the ISS and Audit Analytics databases, and following past literature the authors create a dummy variable to indicate when a shareholder proposal is tendered.

Publicly traded firms report the number of board meetings held in a fiscal year and the percentage of directors that attended more than 75% of board meetings; these data are obtained from the ISS database. Board meeting attendance is measured as the percentage of directors that attended more than 75% of all board meetings.
A dummy variable equaling one if the LID was appointed to the board before the CEO and a zero otherwise.
A dummy variable equaling one if the LID had three or more prior board appointments and a zero otherwise.
A dummy variable equaling one if the LID does not hold a different full-time position and a zero otherwise.
A dummy variable equaling one if the LID was paid over 30% more than average board pay and a zero otherwise.

A composite proxy for PAE intermediation in technology class j in year t − x built from three indicators based on PAE litigation: the count of PAE infringement lawsuits filed on behalf of patents in the class, the count of unique patents represented in PAE infringement lawsuits for the class, and the count of PAE infringement events for the class, where an infringement event occurs when a focal defendant is alleged to have infringed on a focal patent and the number of events for a lawsuit is the number of defendants multiplied by the number of patents allegedly infringed on. Each of the three indicators was standardized and combined to create a composite score (Cronbach's alpha = .93). The lag x ranged from 1 to 2 years.

The composite measure described above, based on PAE litigation activity in class j in year t − x. It combines standardized counts of PAE infringement lawsuits, unique patents represented in lawsuits, and PAE infringement events for the class-year. The measure is entered both as a first-order term and interacted with the focused inventor dummy.

The composite PAE litigation-based measure described above, varying by technology class and application year for each patented invention. It is the main covariate and is entered together with the interaction PAE intermediationj,t-x × focused inventori.

The count of focused inventors who applied for patents (and were subsequently granted) in class j for the first time in their history in year t. To establish whether an inventor active in class j in year t was a focused inventor, all patents applied for by these inventors who were flagged in the Patent Fee Maintenance file as assigned to small entities and eligible for a reduced filing fee were assigned 1, and 0 otherwise; these values were averaged across all patents applied for by each inventor for each year, and an inventor was designated focused for year t if this value was greater than 0.5, and commercializing otherwise. To establish new entrant status, the inventor's entire patenting history dating back to 1976 was observed, and an inventor who had not previously patented in any class was designated a new entrant.

A dummy variable that categorizes inventor i as either a focused or commercializing inventor, based on data from the Patent Fee Maintenance file and the methodology described for determining focused inventor new entrants. The variable was coded as 1 if inventor i was deemed a focused inventor, and 0 otherwise. Of the 21,294 inventors, 7,689 were designated as focused inventors and the remaining 16,506 as commercializing inventors.

A dummy variable categorizing inventor i as a focused or commercializing inventor, coded as 1 if inventor i was deemed a focused inventor and 0 otherwise, using the Patent Fee Maintenance file and the methodology described above. It is entered in the interaction PAE intermediationj,t-x × focused inventori.

The number of patents applied for (and subsequently granted) by inventor i in patent class j in year t. An inventor enters the panel when the inventor applies for a patent in any of the USPTO technology classes and remains in the panel until the final year the inventor applies for patents; focal inventor-technology class dyads with no patented inventions during the time window were removed.

A binary variable indicating whether patent p applied for (and subsequently granted) by inventing entity i within technology class j in year t is incremental in nature. The incremental nature of every patent was computed with a Herfindahl-Hirschman Index that assesses the dispersion of a patent's backward citations across technology classes, where j is the number of unique classes counted across the focal patent's backward citations, Nj is the number of backward citations in the jth class, and N is the total number of backward citations; the formula itself was not readable in the extracted text. Patents with an HHI score over 0.2 were classified as pursuing incremental improvements and those below 0.2 as pursuing novel inventions; the threshold classified 355,389 patents as incremental, 82% of the final sample.

The number of patents generated by each inventor in the previous two years minus the average number of patents generated by all the inventors specializing in the hard disk drive industry over the same period. The authors focus on the previous two years because time has to elapse for performance to influence an inventor's creativity and because R&D lags between 10 and 18 months from project inception to completion in the computer industry.

The dependent variable in the event history analysis is whether and when an inventor generates a new creative idea, indicated by a patent. The authors model the length of time in days until a new creative idea is generated and focus on patent application dates rather than patent issue dates because the time employed by the U.S. Patent Office to process an application is largely outside inventors' control.

The number of new subclasses in which a patent is classified that are new to the inventor. Patents are classified according to classes and subclasses: classes reflect broad technological areas, whereas subclasses reflect specific technological components within a given technological area; patents about hard disk drives and their components fall into three classes, which together comprise more than 1,000 subclasses.

Citations to patents that were not previously cited in the inventor's patents; citations, also known as prior art, are the references a patent document makes to the patents on which the invention builds. The authors exclude citations to the inventor's own patents even when these are made for the first time, and also exclude citations to the organization's own patents.

The inventor's proportion of patents in which he/she is the sole inventor. The authors describe this as a necessary control variable because inventors who collaborate less should be less likely to patent, and they also expect an interaction with success.

variable_name: Organization's proportion of patents entering new subclasses
description: An organization's proportion of patents that enter new subclasses over the past two years, used to measure the extent to which organizations embrace norms for exploration.

variable_name: Organization's proportion of patents making new citations
description: An organization's proportion of patents that make new citations over the past two years, the second indicator of the extent to which organizations embrace norms for exploration.

The number of citations a patent receives after it is granted, excluding self-citations, which would reflect inventors' tendency to build on their own work rather than other inventors' recognition of the importance of a patent. In contrast to the number of citations made, this measure uses citations received from subsequent patents.

Measured by calculating the weighted average of the aggregate market shares held by the nearby rivals in the focal product markets (i.e., therapeutic classes) of the R&D alliance, where the weight is the importance of that market to the focal firm, as indicated by the percentage of overall firm revenue derived from sales in that product market. Competing pharmaceutical firms were considered nearby rivals if they were co-located with the partner and had sales in the product markets corresponding to therapeutic areas of the R&D alliance; rivals were drawn from the list of the 1,000 largest pharmaceutical companies in 2007 and were defined to be co-located if their headquarters are located within the same geographic cluster (MSA) as the partner. The written formula for the measure could not be read in the text.

A dichotomous variable coded one if a focal R&D alliance between a focal firm and a partner is equity-based, and zero otherwise. Out of the 639 R&D alliances, 595 (93.11%) were non-equity alliances while the remaining 44 (6.89%) were equity-based alliances.

A categorical variable taking the value of one when a focal alliance involves manufacturing and/or marketing activities in addition to collaborative R&D, and zero otherwise (i.e., pure R&D). Out of the 639 R&D alliances in our sample, 543 (84.98%) were pure R&D alliances while the remaining 96 (15.02%) included manufacturing and/or marketing activities.

A binary variable that distinguishes the level of task independence between a focal firm and a partner, following the approach of Reuer and Devarakonda (2016), coded as one if a focal R&D alliance is classified as 'Collaboration' or 'Co-Development' in Recap and zero otherwise. Recap assigns an R&D agreement to one of these categories when both parties jointly participate in the research and development, implying reciprocal input-output relationships; agreements coded 'Research' or 'Development', in which only the biotechnology venture performs research or development, fall into sequential interdependence. Out of the 639 R&D alliances, 295 (46.17%) involved reciprocal interdependence and the remaining 344 (53.83%) sequential interdependence.

Measured on a monthly basis as the number of full-time equivalent front-line employees per supervisor, across the five core station functions: gate, ticketing, ramp, baggage, and operations. The calculations were made from monthly staffing records produced by each site for the purpose of reporting to headquarters. Lead agents were counted as front-line employees rather than supervisors because they were not responsible for providing discipline, coaching or feedback.

A measure of group process that includes a communication component (frequency and timeliness of communication) and a relational component (problem solving, helping, mutual respect, shared goals, shared knowledge). Respondents answered seven questions about each of the 12 functions involved in flight departures, with communication with their own function dropped, yielding 77 scores per respondent. Each dimension was measured as the percent of connections within the group that were reported to be strong, i.e., 4 or 5 on a 5-point scale. All items were recoded so that a high value corresponded to high frequency, timeliness, and so on, and each survey response was weighted by the relative size of the respondent's function within the group.
scale: percent of connections rated 4 or 5 on a 5-point scale
time_window: surveys administered on a single day per group

description: An equally weighted index of five performance measures with a Cronbach's alpha of 0.806: three quality measures (customer complaints, baggage handling, late arrivals) and two efficiency measures (gate time per departure and staff time per passenger). All components of the index were reverse-signed to indicate that better performance was a function of shorter gate times, fewer staff per passenger, fewer customer complaints, fewer late arrivals, and fewer lost bags. The performance measures were collected monthly and are therefore available at the group/month level of analysis.

variable_name: Count of dissolved accounts with client
description: The dependent variable is the count of accounts dissolved in the advertising firm–client parent firm relationship when no offsetting additions of accounts occurred in the same year. An account is counted as dissolved in the first year when the advertising firm no longer lists the client account in its Redbooks record. The variable is 0 if an account is also added in the same year.

variable_name: Client tied to both agencies premerger
description: Indicator variable set to 1 if both merging agencies had relationships with the client prior to the merger, and 0 otherwise. This variable was interacted with the client resource endowment, agency status, agency status difference, and relationship duration variables to examine the moderation effects.

Clients were ranked based on their total selling, general, and administrative expenses (SGA), which include advertising expenditures and therefore indicate the resource endowment of a client firm most relevant to advertising firms. The main analysis uses the logarithm of the rank of the firm based on SGA, reverse coded. Missing SGA data were filled with predicted values from a regression of SGA on sales, and an indicator for missing SGA was entered as a control variable.

Indicator set to 1 if each of the merging firms had won more than 10 CLIO Awards in the five years prior to the merger, and 0 otherwise. The number of CLIO Awards each agency won was gathered as the status measure; the indicator approach matches the highly skewed distribution of the awards.

Indicator variable set to 1 if there was a difference of 10 awards or more between the two merging agencies before the merger, and 0 otherwise. It is tested using the same awards data as the joint status measure.
time_window: five years prior to the merger

description: Measure of the average duration of the accounts in the client relationship at the time of the merger. Each advertising agency's listings were consulted for the 20 years before a merger and the start year for each account was coded as the first year in which it listed the client account in its Redbooks record. When the start year could not be determined (17% of observations), it was set to the first year in which client data were available, and a left truncation indicator was included as a control; the natural logarithm of average account duration was entered into the regression.

Factor score generated from an exploratory factor analysis of six board chair-level proxy variables, using principal axis factor extraction with a minimum eigenvalue of 1. The two retained factors explained 92.1 percent of the variance; the two traditional human capital proxies loaded very highly on one factor, which the authors identified as reflective of human capital without any form of rotation. Factor scores were generated for the variable Chair Human Capital.

Factor score generated from the same exploratory factor analysis of six board chair-level proxy variables, using principal axis factor extraction with a minimum eigenvalue of 1. The two traditional social capital proxies loaded very highly on the second retained factor, which the authors identified as reflective of social capital, and the two ambiguous proxies loaded highly on both factors. Factor scores were generated for the variable Chair Social Capital.

Dichotomous coding of whether the board views its chair as a resource, obtained by content-analyzing the legally mandated passage in proxy statements devoted to explaining and justifying the firm's choice of board leadership. Three human coders (two MBA students and the lead author) read each passage and identified the presence or absence of the resource-based view of the board chair; a value of 1 indicated the presence of a resource-based justification for the firm's choice of board chair and a value of 0 the absence of such a justification. Inter-rater agreement was at acceptable levels (Cohen's kappa = 0.7) and disputed ratings were resolved by the authors with deference to the majority opinion.

Ratio of common ownership to total ownership between the two firms in a dyad, where Cij is the total number of common institutional owners between firms i and j, Dij is the total number of disjoint institutional owners between them, and COH and DOH are common ownership holdings in percentage and disjoint ownership holdings in percentage, respectively. The number can range from 0 (no common institutional ownership) to 1 (complete overlap of institutional ownership between rival firms). For the main analysis the authors imposed a value of zero on common ownership for all non-rival pairs, so the measure captures intra-industry common ownership. The published equation could not be read from the text provided.

Euclidean distance between firm i's and firm j's competitive action repertoires, where the competitive action portfolio vector P specifies the count of actions in each of seven behavior classes for every firm and p_ikt is the number of actions made by firm i in class k during year t. The measure equals zero if firm i's competitive portfolio is exactly identical to j's portfolio. Actions are counts of news events matched to event categories, limited to the first story reporting a categorized event, in seven categories of competitive actions. The published equation could not be read from the text provided.
The sum of competitive actions for both firms in an intraindustry dyad. Action counts are assembled from the seven categories of competitive actions identified in the news data.

Return on assets (ROA), described as the most common measure of accounting performance in the strategy literature. Joint performance of the rivals is calculated by summing the ROAs of both firms in the dyad: JROA_ijt = ROA_it + ROA_jt.
The performance disparity between the rivals is calculated as the absolute difference of the ROAs of the two firms in the dyad: DROA_ijt = |ROA_it - ROA_jt|.

Profitability was measured using both accounting and operating-based measures: return on assets (ROA), return on equity (ROE), return on sales (ROS), and sales growth (SG). Averages were used to reduce variability in the data. Each of the four profitability measurements was regressed separately on the explanatory variables in Models I to IV. The paper reports that the models accounted for 19-25 percent of the variability in the profitability measurements.

Innovator position (IP) is measured by R&D expenditures, which are the average of the reporting business's annual expenditures on R&D expenses, divided by revenues. A 3-year average over the 1995 through 1997 period was used for the variable.

Market awareness (MA) is measured by advertising expenditures, which are the average of the reporting business's annual expenditures on advertising expenses, divided by revenues. The authors note that existing studies regard advertising as an important means to create market awareness, as advertising promotes brand name, reputation, and consumer goodwill.

Product scope (PS) is determined by an entropy measure based on SIC classification. Products belonging to different 4-digit SIC industries within the same 2-digit industry group are treated as related, and products from different 2-digit SIC industry groups are defined as unrelated. The authors treat operations in related products as tantamount to operations in narrow niches and operations in unrelated products as equal to operations in broad product segments.

Internationalization (INT) is determined as the extent to which a firm is involved in foreign activities. It is measured by multinationality, that is, the proportion of total revenues earned overseas.

Treatment equaled 1 for firms that experienced an anti-corruption shock and 0 for all other firms; a firm experienced a shock if it had connections with prosecuted officials. Connections were identified as hometown connections (birth in the same city) and alumni connections (graduation from the same university) between the firm's chair or CEO and politicians, matched conservatively to firms in the politician's city, province, or nationwide for central-government politicians. Post was a dummy variable coded as 1 for years after an anti-corruption event and 0 for all other years. The interaction term Treat × Post captures the effect of connection loss.

The number of invention patent applications the firm applied for in year t. The authors focused on invention patents as a better representation of knowledge creation than utility or design patents. Because patent application counts are integers, the variable was log-transformed to address nonlinearity and reduce skewness.

Constructed as a combination of the 16 sources of knowledge or information for innovation listed in the survey. As a starting point, each of the 16 sources is coded as a binary variable, 0 being no use and 1 being use of the given knowledge source; the 16 sources are then simply added up, so that each firm gets a 0 when no knowledge sources are used and a value of 16 when all knowledge sources are used. Firms that use higher numbers of sources are assumed to be more open with respect to search breadth.

Constructed using the same 16 sources of knowledge as BREADTH. Each of the 16 sources is coded 1 when the firm reports that it uses the source to a high degree and 0 in the case of no, low, or medium use of the given source; the 16 sources are then added up so that each firm gets a score of 0 when no knowledge sources are used to a high degree and a value of 16 when all knowledge sources are used to a high degree. Firms that use higher numbers of sources are assumed to be more open with respect to search depth.

A variable aimed at indicating the ability of the firm to produce radical innovations, measured as the fraction of the firm's turnover relating to products new to the world market. It is one of three proxies for innovative performance used as dependent variables.

A proxy for incremental innovation expressing the fraction of the firm's turnover pertaining to products new to the firm. This variable is mutually exclusive with INNIMP since they, together with unchanged or only marginally modified products, add up to 100 percent.

A proxy for incremental innovation expressing the fraction of the firm's turnover pertaining to products significantly improved. This variable is mutually exclusive with INNFIRM since they, together with unchanged or only marginally modified products, add up to 100 percent.

A measure of R&D intensity, measured as firm R&D expenditure divided by firm sales. The numerator is taken from the U.K. innovation survey, while the denominator, firm turnover or sales, is based on Office of National Statistics register data supplied with the survey data. It is included both as a control for the effect of R&D on innovative performance and to test the hypothesis about complementarity with openness.

variable_name: INNWORLD, INNFIRM and INNIMP (share of turnover by degree of novelty)
description: Degree of novelty of innovation was read from the survey's innovation-type sales shares. INNWORLD, the fraction of turnover from products new to the world market, stands for radical innovation, while INNFIRM (products new to the firm) and INNIMP (significantly improved products) stand for incremental innovation. The moderation was tested by comparing the breadth and depth coefficients across the three models.

An index of the change in the interpretation of patent law in circuit c due to the CAFC, constructed by Hou et al. (2022). The outcome variable of the underlying regression takes the values of 0, 1, and 2 increasing in the order of patent litigation outcomes of invalid, valid but not infringed, and valid and infringed; the right-hand side comprises circuit fixed effects before and after the CAFC together with patent, litigation, and year controls. The coefficient λc measures the CAFC index used for the analyses and represents the change in patent law due to the CAFC. The index is matched to businesses by circuit and year.

Count of patents assigned to each business by circuit and year that are based on continuing patent applications, which are filed during the pendency of an original application and comprise continuation, divisional, and continuation-in-part applications. The numbers of conventional and strategic patents assigned to each business by circuit in the pre- and post-CAFC years are compiled from the Patent Examination Research Dataset (Public PAIR).

Count of patents assigned to each business by circuit and year that are not subject to any continuations, that is, stand-alone patent applications. The numbers of conventional and strategic patents are compiled from the Patent Examination Research Dataset (Public PAIR) for the sample of USPTO patent applications.

Following Cohen et al. (2000), the sample is divided into complex and discrete technology industries, and the effect of the CAFC on conventional and strategic patents is estimated separately in each group.

Following Ziedonis (2004), for every business-circuit-year, the dispersion of the ownership of the backward citations by the focal business in each circuit and year, normalized by the proportion of backward citations by that business of backward citations by all other businesses in that circuit and year. In the summary statistics the measure is multiplied by 1,000 as the raw number is very small.

Measured by the ratio of gross investments in property, plant and equipment to sales revenue in the two-digit SIC. Estimates compare sub-samples split by the level of investments in manufacturing assets.

The degree of local, technological competition, represented by the geographical concentration of forward citations made by other businesses to patents assigned to any focal business for each circuit and year. Other businesses with technologies built upon the incumbent's technologies are more likely to compete for patentable 'facets' in similar technological fields.

The number of employees of the parent company in the two-digit SIC, used to split the sample into above- and below-median size groups. Company employment is also entered as a size control in the patenting regressions.

Entry is defined as occurring when another business patented in the focal business's patented technological class and home circuit for the first time. The count of entrants is the dependent variable in the entry estimates.

The number of prior strategic alliances concluded between the dyad partners in the past. Prior alliances were counted in a moving window: for the 62 (29.0%) strategic alliances for which termination information was available they counted until termination, and for the others a life span of no more than five years was assumed. These prior ties are indicators of how well the two firms know each other and of the extent to which information asymmetry and indigestibility problems may be alleviated.
time_window: prior to each year, moving window

description: The shortest path between two firms in the network of prior strategic alliances, calculated with the distance routine in UCINET based on the number of edges in the geodesic. The authors took the natural logarithm of this measure because a change in distance matters more when distance is small and to mitigate the distance value for firms not indirectly linked by any path. As network distance is an inverse metric of the strength of indirect ties, a positive coefficient is expected.

Dummy variable indicating that allies or acquirer and acquired firms are both ASIC producers of which the (major) ASIC sales come from a different segment, e.g., a gate array producer and a PLD producer. The default category is a dyad including an ASIC producer and a company that belongs to another industry.

Dummy variable indicating that both firms realize (the largest share of) their ASIC sales in the same segment, e.g., two PLD producers. The default category is a dyad including an ASIC producer and a company that belongs to another industry.

Dummy variable indicating that the strategic alliance or acquisition took place between two firms from different economic blocks (Europe, America, Asia), as opposed to intratriad ties. A negative sign is expected, indicating that companies from different economic blocks prefer strategic alliances compared to firms that belong to the same block.

The number of past strategic alliances entered by each firm in the dyad prior to the given year. Because this is a firm characteristic there are two values per dyad: alliance history 1 refers to the acquired firm and alliance history 2 to the acquiring firm in the case of an acquisition; for (nondirectional) strategic alliances allies were randomly assigned to either of the two variables so that mean and variance were the same for both variables.

Betweenness centrality, measuring the potential control of a firm over other firms that have no direct ties to each other; betweenness refers to the number of times an actor is located on the shortest geodesic path between two other actors in the prior strategic alliance network. Normalized centrality measures were used, controlling for overall network size, to make centrality measures comparable across years. Two values per dyad: firm 1 refers to the acquired firm and firm 2 to the acquiring firm in the case of an acquisition.

Binary choice variable indicating whether the pair of firms entered a strategic alliance or an acquisition in a particular year. A strategic alliance was coded 0 and an acquisition 1. It is the dependent variable of the random-effects probit models.

variable_name: Acquired firm (firm 1) versus acquiring firm (firm 2) position in the dyad
description: Acquisition role was coded by the position of each firm in the acquisition dyad. For an acquisition, the firm 1 values of alliance history and network centrality refer to the acquired firm and the firm 2 values refer to the acquiring firm, so the effects of the firm 1 and firm 2 coefficients show who becomes the acquirer.

variable_name: actual quality management scores (Z1, Z3,..., Z8)
description: Each manager rated 78 quality management items twice, once for current practice ('Is') and once for ideal practice ('Should be'), on a scale running from Very Low to Very High. For each quality management factor, the actual level perceived by a manager is the average of the manager's actual ratings of that factor's measurement items, so each manager generated eight actual quality management scores (Z1 to Z8). Because none of the ten service companies in the sample had a quality department, the quality-department variables were not used in the analysis, leaving seven variables (Z1, Z3 to Z8).

variable_name: ideal quality management scores (Y1, Y3,..., Y8)
description: For each quality management factor, the ideal level is the average of the manager's ideal-practice ratings of the factor's measurement items, yielding eight ideal quality management scores (Y1 to Y8). As with actual quality management, the quality-department variables were not used in the analysis, leaving seven ideal quality management variables. Reliability coefficients (Cronbach's alpha) for the eight measures of ideal quality management ranged from 0.7 to 0.9.

variable_name: organizational quality context variables (X1 to X11)
description: Each manager assessed 26 items (Appendix A) covering managerial knowledge, corporate support for quality, marketplace environment, product/process environment, and past quality performance, rated from Very High to Very Low. The 26 items were factor analyzed and four distinct varimax rotated factors were identified; 19 of the original items were reduced to four factors and the seven items that did not load on any single factor were treated as separate variables, giving the eleven context variables X1 to X11. Reliability coefficients (Cronbach's alpha) for managerial knowledge and corporate support for quality were 0.84 and 0.91 after eliminating one item from each set.

Entries were categorized according to the number of businesses the parent firm had that were related to the new business entered: no related business, one related business, two to four related businesses, and five or more related businesses. Following the approach of Jaffe (1986), relatedness is assessed with a similarity index, and for the tables two products (businesses) are categorized as related if they appear together in the product portfolios of multiple firms in the CorpTech directory. The authors expect the potential for redeployment to increase as one moves down these categories.
scale: four ordered categories (none; one; two to four; five or more)
level: entry (product code within firm), aggregated into categories

description: For each category of relatedness the authors report the percentage of exits that occurred within two, three, four, and five years of the date of entry, contingent on eventual exit. Entry is defined as the appearance of a new product code that persists in the directory for at least two years, and exit is identified when that product code stops being listed in the firm's product portfolio for two consecutive years.
level: entry (product code within firm), aggregated by relatedness category
time_window: two, three, four, and five years after entry

variable_name: fraction of entries reversed via exit
description: The number of subsequent exits divided by the number of entries in a category of relatedness, that is, the fraction of entries that were reversed via exit. Exit is identified when a product code stops being listed in the firm's product portfolio for two consecutive years.
level: entry (product code within firm), aggregated by relatedness category

description: Potential for redeployment was proxied by the number of businesses the parent firm had that were related to the new business entered (none, one, two to four, five or more), with relatedness assessed by a similarity index from product portfolios in the CorpTech directory. The potential for redeployment is expected to increase with the number of related businesses.

A Herfindahl-Hirschman Index (HHI)-based measure built from the percentage of a firm's sales to its major customers. The authors write that Salesij represents supplier (focal firm) i's sales to major customer j and Salesi represents supplier i's total sales. The variable ranged between 0 and 1, with high values representing a more concentrated customer base; it equaled 0 if a firm did not disclose its sales to any major customer, and 1 if it relied on a single major customer for all of its annual revenues. The printed formula itself is unreadable in the available text.

Measured by calculating the average frequency with which previously referenced patents cited by a focal firm in a given year were repeatedly cited during the previous five years (i.e., repeated citations), which proxies for the accumulated search experience. The printed equation is unreadable in the available text. Patent activities proxy for firm search behavior.
time_window: five-year look-back; dependent variable in year t+1

description: Measured as the share of the total citations of a focal firm's patents in a given year that cannot be found in the firm's lists of patent citations from the previous five years (i.e., new citations). The printed equation is unreadable in the available text.
time_window: five-year look-back; dependent variable in year t+1

description: Top executives' existing-oriented attention for each firm was measured by the word count in a given letter to shareholders or earnings conference call according to a dictionary of existing-oriented attention words. The count was normalized by the total number of words in the document, and the measure was then calculated as the ratio of existing-oriented attention to the sum of existing- and future-oriented attention. The dictionary was built in five steps from synonyms of the seed keywords 'existing' and 'future', validated by three content experts rating words from 1 (definitely existing-oriented attention) to 7 (definitely future-oriented attention) and retaining words scoring 1 or 2. Full coverage of letters to shareholders and earnings conference calls was obtained for about 14.6% of the full sample (2,783 observations).
scale: ratio of existing-oriented words to the sum of existing- and future-oriented words

description: Top executives' future-oriented attention for each firm was measured by the word count in a given letter to shareholders or earnings conference call according to the corresponding dictionary, normalized by the total number of words in the document. Words scoring 6 or 7 on the experts' scale from 1 (definitely existing-oriented attention) to 7 (definitely future-oriented attention) were retained.
scale: word count normalized by total words in the document

description: Measured as the patent citations received by a focal firm in year t minus the median number of patent citations of its peers (three-digit SIC industry code) in the same year. Innovation performance metrics such as patent citations were used because usual profitability measures are too general for studying innovation search.
Measured as the firm's patent citations in year t minus its own historical performance, an average of the previous two years' patent citations.
time_window: year t; previous two years for own historical performance

description: Calculated as minus one times the TNIC HHI provided in Hoberg and Phillips's (2010) database; it is a continuous variable in which a larger number indicates a high degree of competition. The TNIC measure was constructed by combining web crawling and text parsing algorithms to analyze the text of product descriptions of firms' 10-K filing statements, calculating firm-by-firm pairwise similarity scores as a Hotelling-like product location space, and updating the calculation of product similarity for each firm every year.
scale: continuous; larger values indicate more competition

description: The authors counted each candidate's cumulative number of employers at each year of experience, then assigned a z-score to each person-year observation describing the candidate's position in the distribution of the cumulative number of employers for that particular number of years of experience. The z-score from the search year is used, so the measure represents prior mobility relative to other workers with the same level of experience.
time_window: career up to the search year

description: The function of each role on the resume was coded into 22 categories based on functions described in the top management team literature and supplemented with SearchCo's internal rubric. The authors counted the cumulative number of unique functional areas a candidate had worked in at each year of experience and calculated a z-score for people with that many years of experience; the z-score from the search year is used as the measure.
time_window: career up to the search year

description: Industries were categorized into sectors using their 2-digit NAICS code. As with mobility, the authors counted the cumulative number of unique industries the candidate had worked in at each year of experience and calculated a z-score for people with that many years of experience, using the z-score from the search year as the measure.
time_window: career up to the search year

description: Tenure was calculated by subtracting the year that the candidate started work at their current employer from the search year.
time_window: search year minus start year at current employer

description: Dependent variable taking the value of one if a candidate was given an offer by the hiring firm at the final stage of the selection process and zero otherwise.
time_window: final stage of the selection process

description: Yearly change in profitability, where profitability is measured by operating income to avoid noncomparabilities due to differences in depreciation, pension pay and tax laws. Years are divided into growth and decline years defined by the sign of the annual profitability change at the firm level; years without any change in profitability are not included.

Yearly change in sales volume; sales volume time series are corrected for in-house supplies. Years are classified by whether sales increased or decreased. The data are divided into growth and decline years as defined by the sign of the annual profitability change.

Ranking of ethylene cracker units from high (1) to low (32) efficiency in 1982, where efficiency is measured in terms of total cost in US dollars per ton. Lower cost per ton indicates higher efficiency; the ranking is from high to low efficiency. Data on 1992 ranking are also available.

Status of each ethylene cracker in 1992 in terms of exit from or stay in the market. In the 1982-1992 period, 10 crackers were withdrawn from the marketplace; the crackers that exited are indicated in the ranking.

Summed number of creativity points that a house obtained from the JdT evaluators annually, where each buyer (one of around 70 per season), from leading retailers around the world, can give up to 20 points to a house that presented a fashion collection in the major annual fashion shows. The evaluation is conducted bi-annually by the Paris-based trade publication Journal du Textile and the points are summed over a calendar year, which contains two fashion seasons, giving a theoretical maximum of 2,800 points. The dependent variable is evaluated in the regressions with a 1 year forward lead.

Dummy coded equal to 1 if a fashion house becomes affiliated with a fashion conglomerate during the sample period, and zero otherwise. In the regressions, Affiliated is entered on its own to capture the baseline effect of affiliation and interacted with the quartile splines of initial and concurrent conglomerate creativity; fashion houses affiliated with non-fashion business groups such as banks or private equity firms are excluded from the treatment and potential control groups.

Average number of JdT points that the other houses inside the same fashion conglomerate had in the year when the focal house became affiliated, excluding the focal fashion house. This value is carried forward to the future observations of the same house while it stays within the same fashion conglomerate and is updated if the house is sold to another fashion conglomerate. In the regressions the continuous measure is partitioned into a spline in quartiles computed using the full sample, with a 'missing' category used as the excluded reference group for independent firms.
time_window: year of affiliation, carried forward to later observations of the same house

description: Average number of JdT points that the other houses inside the same fashion conglomerate had in a specific year, excluding the focal fashion house, and updated annually to capture concurrent effects. In the regressions the continuous measure is partitioned into a spline in quartiles computed using the full sample, with a 'missing' category used as the excluded reference group for independent firms.

Event variable that takes the value of 0 for all years the firm division uses external sales, and a value of 1 if and when it integrates sales. Firm divisions are dropped from the analytical sample for the years after integration because they are no longer at risk. Firm divisions that never integrate sales are 0 for all years they remain in the sample until either firm exit or the end of the observation window.
time_window: event in the year following the predictors

description: Length of time is used as a proxy measure for relational capital, measured as years using external sales in 2-year bands: 1-2 years (reference category), 3-4 years, 5-6 years, and 7 or more years. The authors expect time using external sales to be negatively related to integration for firms that maintain the same focal downstream market.

The change in the count of innovative products sold by the firm division. Products that entered the market during the first approval year for their respective FDA product category are categorized as innovative products. The measure represents changes in the need for the development and sharing of new, relationship-specific knowledge.

Indicates that the firm division changes its main specialty, which is the medical specialty within which the firm has the most products in each year. A change in the firm's focal downstream market is defined as a change in its focal medical specialty (e.g., from Cardiovascular to General Surgery).

Innovative product introductions counted separately for innovations inside the firm's existing focal downstream market, that is, in its focal medical specialty. The authors separate innovative products into within versus outside specialty to test Hypotheses 3a and 3b.

Innovative product introductions counted separately for innovations outside the firm's existing focal downstream market, that is, outside its focal medical specialty. The authors separate innovative products into within versus outside specialty to test Hypotheses 3a and 3b.

Collaboration is measured as the average number of authors on a scientist's publications in a given year. The number of coauthors on a project is obtained by counting the number of names in the author field of each publication (the coauthorship index). At the scientist-year level the variable is the mean of this count across the year's publications.

Quality is the average number of citations received by a scientist for all the papers published in a given year. Citations are counted as the number of citations received by 2008 for each paper, and the scientist-year value is the average of this count across that year's publications.

NPubs is the number of papers the scientist published in a given year, holding the input constant at a scientist-year. The authors note that publication data are only a proxy for the number of projects the scientist is involved with, since projects that lead to no publication are not counted.

Frac_Pubs is the sum of the 'paper shares' directly attributed to the scientist. For each paper published in the year the scientist's share is its number of authors divided into one, and these shares are summed over the year's papers; the authors describe this as the simplest functional form of fractional counting, corresponding to (N) = 1/N.

Attributed citations for a scientist-year are computed by summing the citations attributed to the author for every paper published in that year. Attribution uses a credit-sharing function (N) of the number of authors N; the paper examines (N) = 1, (N) = 1/N, (N) = 1/N and, for the whole sample, (N) = N^b for values of b between 0 and 1. If (N) = 1 each author claims the entire credit for a coauthored paper, while if (N) = 1/N credit is split so that shares sum to one.
Measured by responses to a question asking CEOs to indicate the percentage of the shares of the firm owned by the CEO's family. The same measure was used in both samples.
Measured by responses to a question asking CEOs to indicate the percentage of the shares of the firm owned by the CEO's family. The same measure was used in both samples.

variable_name: Duration of family ownership / firm age
description: Measured by an open-ended question about the age of the family firm. The authors state this was appropriate because in all cases the founding families were still in control of the firms in the samples, and that age of the firm is also a useful proxy for the generation of the family in control.

variable_name: Duration of family ownership / firm age
description: Measured by an open-ended question about the age of the family firm. The authors state this was appropriate because in all cases the founding families were still in control of the firms in the samples, and that age of the firm is also a useful proxy for the generation of the family in control.
Two items measured on a seven-point Likert-type scale to capture opportunity/feasibility and desire. The items were added and the sum divided by the number of items to obtain the final variable used.
Two items measured on a seven-point Likert-type scale to capture opportunity/feasibility and desire. The items were added and the sum divided by the number of items to obtain the final variable used.

The dependent variable is the family firm owner-CEO's total perceived value of the family firm, measured at the owner level of analysis with a single-item question: 'What is the minimum acceptable sales price at which you are willing to sell 100% of your company's equity to a nonfamily member?' The question made it clear that the value sought was (1) the value of the firm's equity (2) when selling the entire firm (3) to parties outside the family. The variable was characterized by high positive skewness and kurtosis, so the logarithm of total perceived value was used in the analysis. Figures for this sample are in Swiss francs.

The dependent variable is the family firm owner-CEO's total perceived value of the family firm, measured at the owner level of analysis with a single-item question: 'What is the minimum acceptable sales price at which you are willing to sell 100% of your company's equity to a nonfamily member?' The question made it clear that the value sought was (1) the value of the firm's equity (2) when selling the entire firm (3) to parties outside the family. The variable was characterized by high positive skewness and kurtosis, so the logarithm of total perceived value was used in the analysis. Figures for this sample are in euros.

Executives rated each of the production/operations activities on a seven-point Likert-type response mode ranging from 'greatest strategic significance' to 'completely strategically insignificant'. The ratings were grouped by function and summed to determine the relative importance of the production/operations activities.
scale: seven-point Likert-type ratings summed across the function's activities

description: Executives rated each of the marketing activities on a seven-point Likert-type response mode ranging from 'greatest strategic significance' to 'completely strategically insignificant'. The ratings were grouped by function and summed to determine the relative importance of the marketing activities.
scale: seven-point Likert-type ratings summed across the function's activities

description: Executives rated each of the finance activities on a seven-point Likert-type response mode ranging from 'greatest strategic significance' to 'completely strategically insignificant'. The ratings were grouped by function and summed to determine the relative importance of the finance activities.
scale: seven-point Likert-type ratings summed across the function's activities

variable_name: engineering, research and development distinctive competence score
description: Executives rated each of the engineering, research and development activities on a seven-point Likert-type response mode ranging from 'greatest strategic significance' to 'completely strategically insignificant'. The ratings were grouped by function and summed to determine the relative importance of these activities.
scale: seven-point Likert-type ratings summed across the function's activities

description: Executives rated each of the general administration activities on a seven-point Likert-type response mode ranging from 'greatest strategic significance' to 'completely strategically insignificant'. The ratings were grouped by function and summed to determine the relative importance of the general administration activities.
scale: seven-point Likert-type ratings summed across the function's activities

description: Executives rated each of the personnel activities on a seven-point Likert-type response mode ranging from 'greatest strategic significance' to 'completely strategically insignificant'. The ratings were grouped by function and summed to determine the relative importance of the personnel activities.
scale: seven-point Likert-type ratings summed across the function's activities

variable_name: public and governmental relations distinctive competence score
description: Executives rated each of the public and governmental relations activities on a seven-point Likert-type response mode ranging from 'greatest strategic significance' to 'completely strategically insignificant'. The ratings were grouped by function and summed to determine the relative importance of these activities.
scale: seven-point Likert-type ratings summed across the function's activities

description: Data on daily market returns for firms' securities were obtained from CRSP tapes; a maximum of five years of data were used to calculate the geometric mean annual return. The geometric annual risk-free rate was computed from the average selling prices at the weekly three-month treasury bill auction, obtained from the Federal Reserve Bulletin. The variable was defined as MR = (GMRi - RFRk)/B, where B is the beta measure of systematic risk taken from the Value Line Investment Survey and calculated for a period of five years matching the market returns data.

Grand strategy type was measured on a nominal scale with four strategy classifications. The CEO was instructed to denote the firm's grand strategy; the classifications are stability (similar operating levels to pursue similar objectives with only incremental performance improvements), internal growth (growth through internal development), external acquisitive growth (growth through acquisition, merger and/or joint ventures) and retrenchment (reduction of level or scope of product/market objectives).

Executives noted their firm's principal industry, defined as the one in which the largest percentage of sales is earned. Industry type was measured on a nominal scale using four normative classifications: consumer durable (goods purchased for personal gratification that last for long periods of time), consumer non-durable (goods purchased for personal gratification that last only a limited time period), capital (goods that are buildings) and producer (goods used as raw material to produce consumer or capital goods).

Corporate-level distinctive competence was measured through executives' ratings of the strategic significance of 55 functional activities, grouped into seven functional scores (production/operations, marketing, finance, engineering/R&D, general administration, personnel, public and governmental relations). The seven scores were related to performance within each grand strategy and industry type.

The number of partners the prime contractor used on the most recent previous job (repeated partners) divided by the total number of partners on the current job. For example, if a prime contractor used three partners, two of whom were also used on the last job, this value would be 2/3. Values range from 0 to 1, indicating that all partners on the current job are new or that all current partners were also on the last job.
time_window: most recent previous job relative to the current project

description: Calculated as the sum of deep relationships for that project's partnership group by summing the number of times the prime contractor has used repeated partners over its last five projects. In the authors' example, a prime contractor with three partners scores Partner C, which is new, as zero, Partner A, used on each of the five previous jobs, as 5, and Partner B, used three times within the previous five jobs, as 3, giving a project-level value of 5 + 3 + 0, or 8.

A binary measure (1, 0) that indicates whether a prime contractor won the bid, meaning that its cost proposal was the lowest among all bids for a particular project. Because federal regulations only award bids to the lowest-cost proposal, revenue is only generated when a prime contractor submits the lowest bid, and no new business is awarded for second place.

A continuous measure of the percentage change between the final approved bid cost and actual authorized construction costs, measuring the relative profitability of each winning bid. ODOT scrutinizes the bid and approves the final approved bid cost, and following construction the construction authorization reflects the actual cost of construction. If a prime contractor has an approved bid of $10 million and the final cost of the project is $9 million, the difference between the two numbers favors the prime contractor and adds to profitability.

Each of the three informants in each organization assessed the statement 'Plant management is not included in the formal strategic planning process. It is conducted at higher levels in the corporation' on a 1-5 Likert scale. The scale was reversed so that a high value indicates a high degree of plant management participation. Estimates for the participation construct were obtained by computing factor scores from a confirmatory factor analysis of the participation and communication constructs, using the regression method.

The same three informants were asked to assess the statement 'Our business strategy is translated into manufacturing terms' on a 1-5 Likert scale. Estimates for the communication construct were obtained by computing factor scores from a confirmatory factor analysis of the participation and communication constructs, using the regression method.

Three middle-level managers - the plant superintendent, the plant manager, and the plant research coordinator - were asked to assess the importance of eight specific dimensions of operational performance on a 1-8 scale (1 = most important, 8 = least important). Four operational-goals variables - volume flexibility, design flexibility, fast delivery, and short cycle time - were selected for MTMM analysis because they exhibited the highest average within-plant variance. A CFA multitrait-multimethod model with four traits and three methods was estimated with AMOS, and factor scores of the method factors were estimated with the regression method; each informant receives a method factor score that measures whether he or she is over- or underemphasizing the traits. The average bias is calculated for each plant as the arithmetic average of the three individual position bias scores.
scale: 1-8 ranking scale for the item ratings
level: informant within plant; plant-level arithmetic average

description: The competition score for each unique partner pair is the cosine similarity between the three-year patent technology subclass vectors of the two firms in the pair, computed from four-character CPC subclass codes. Overall portfolio competition is the average of the pairwise competition scores among all partner pairs in a given year. To isolate competition arising from partners' independent strategic choices, only the stable portion of the portfolio is used: partners present in both t-2 and t-1, with competition data taken from year t-1.
time_window: t-1, using three-year patent technology subclass vectors

description: For every focal firm-partner pair the authors first count the technology subclasses in which the focal firm is a leader but the partner is not, where a firm is a leader in a subclass if it ranks in the top decile of patenting firms and holds at least 5% of all patents in that subclass in a given year. Second, they count the subclasses in which the partner is the sole leader within the firm's portfolio. Third, they subtract the second count from the first. Finally, they compute a weighted average of these values across all firm-partner pairs, weighting each pair by the pairwise cosine similarity between the partner's technology subclass vector and those of other partners in the portfolio. The variable is natural log transformed and lagged by one year.

Disconnectedness is the proportion of inventor pairs that lack a direct or indirect path between them in the intrafirm coinvention network: V is the number of inventor-pairs with no connecting path and N is the total number of inventors in the firm. A fully disconnected network (comprised entirely of isolates) yields a value of one, whereas a fully connected network yields a value of zero. The measure captures both direct and indirect (i.e., via mutual collaborators) limitations on knowledge exchange within the firm. The printed formula is not readable in the available text.

The cumulative number of forward citations received by a firm's patents within 10 years of their application. The fixed citation window mitigates temporal bias, as older patents tend to accumulate more citations, and the 10-year window aligns with the typical 8- to 9-year technology cycle in the pharmaceutical industry.

The number of forward self-citations received by a firm's patents within 10 years of application. This measure captures the firm's ability to generate follow-on innovation and retain value from its existing knowledge base.

A Herfindahl-type index measuring the extent to which a firm's pattern of actions carried out in a given quarter consisted of a broad or narrow range of action types. The authors first calculated the ratio of actions in each of the eight action categories to total actions, squared each action-type proportion, and summed the squared proportions. Simplicity ranges from zero to 1.0; a score near 1.0 indicates a simple sequence, whereas a score nearer to zero indicates a complex one.
time_window: each quarter in which the firm was public

description: The Levenshtein distance score from optimal matching analysis, capturing the extent to which a firm's sequence of actions was similar to or dissimilar from its sequences in other quarters. The score is calculated as the proportion of INDEL costs to the total number of elements in the referent sequence and ranges from zero to 1.0; a low distance score indicates continuity and predictability from one period to the next. In the analysis the authors reversed the directionality of the scores (multiplying by -1.0) so that a high score indicates a more predictable pattern of action sequences.
time_window: quarter-to-quarter comparison; one observation quarter lost to establish the initial comparison point

description: The separation score from gamma analysis, which captures the extent to which an action of a given type occurred in close ordinal proximity to each other type of action. Separation scores range from zero to 1.0, with low average scores indicating that actions are typically carried out in close ordinal proximity and high scores indicating that actions are carried out in relative isolation. To capture grouping for the entire sequence the authors calculated the mean of the separation scores across all action types and reversed the direction of the scores (multiplying by -1.0) so that higher scores indicate higher levels of grouping.
time_window: each quarter in which the firm was public

description: The variance of the averages in the pair-wise precedence scores across all action types, capturing the ordinal specificity and stability of elements in a sequence. Low variance scores indicate that a sequence exhibited a particular order among its elements, whereas high variance indicates that actions of any type had an equal or random chance of being early or late in the sequence. The authors reverse-scored this measure to better reflect the motif construct.
time_window: each quarter in which the firm was public

description: The standard deviation in quarterly earnings-per-share forecasts issued by the set of analysts covering each firm, coded for each firm-quarter as either above or below the median level of the standard deviation. Firms were treated as associated with a low or high level of ambiguity based on whether their analyst EPS forecasts were more often in the high-variance or the low-variance group; the two firms whose forecasts were evenly split were assigned to the low-ambiguity condition. On average, 8.3 analysts' forecasts were obtained per firm-quarter.
scale: above or below the median standard deviation of EPS forecasts
level: firm-quarter forecasts aggregated to a firm-level high/low classification
time_window: each quarter in which the firm was public

description: Market value was collected from the Compustat database and operationalized as share price multiplied by the number of outstanding shares on the last date of each quarter for which competitive actions were tracked. The analysis uses quarter differences of this variable expressed as percentage differences, calculated as [(MVt - MVt-1)/MVt-1].

variable_name: Price (Zone P0, Zone P3, Zone P5)
description: A price was assigned to each of the three study zones: 0 (free), 3 Kwatcha, or 5 Kwatcha, corresponding to a free, a deep discount, and a moderate discount pricing strategy. The zones were labeled Zone P0, Zone P3, and Zone P5. Prior to the study and/or outside the study zones, the standard retail price for the packets was 5 Kw, and retailers were directed to keep the price at the fixed level during the study.
time_window: fixed for the duration of the study in each zone

description: Calculated as the number of empty packets (EMPTY_PKTS) plus the number of packets respondents had used and discarded (DISCARDED_PKTS). During the follow-up survey the team recorded empty packets, unopened packets remaining from the initial purchase, and unmarked packets obtained after the initial survey, and asked how many packets respondents had obtained from retailers since the initial survey. In the free condition the number of discarded packets was recorded on the voucher, while in the other conditions it was reported by respondents.
time_window: cumulative over the approximately six weeks between the baseline and follow-up surveys

description: Households were identified as repeat consumers if they used more than three units of the product, which was the median for usage. The share classified as repeat consumers was then compared across the free, deep discount, and moderate discount zones.
scale: binary (used more than three units or not)
time_window: over the period of the study

description: Performance was measured in each production trial by counting the number of sailboats made during the trial, so performance development is the increase or decrease in total boats produced from one trial to the next. Performance change from Trials 2 to 3 and from Trials 3 to 4 was used to predict adoption decisions, and performance change from Trials 3 to 4 was used in the mediation analysis.
scale: count of boats produced (one point for each sailboat that met product specifications)
time_window: trial-to-trial change (Trials 2 to 3 and Trials 3 to 4)

description: The primary dependent measure was whether the team adopted the new routine in Trials 4 or 5. In Trial 4 (A1), teams could either adopt the new routine for the first time (1) or continue with the old routine (0). In Trial 5 (A2) there were four possible situations: adopting the new routine for the first time (01), not adopting it again in this second option period (00), continuing with the new routine first adopted in Trial 4 (11), or returning to the old routine (10). Our measure of routine change was determined objectively.

Participants' emotions were measured as self-assessments on a questionnaire that included 28 emotional items designed to measure Russell's (1980) circumplex model of emotions. Each item was rated on a five-point Likert scale (1 = very slightly or not at all; 2 = a little; 3 = moderately; 4 = quite a bit; 5 = extremely). The questionnaire was administered three times: immediately after the baseline (Q1), immediately after the first three production trials (Q2) and after the fifth production trial (Q3).
scale: five-point Likert scale (1 = very slightly or not at all to 5 = extremely)
time_window: Q1 (after baseline), Q2 (after Trial 3), Q3 (after Trial 5)

description: Electromyographic measures of participants' facial muscle activity were used to capture valence. Participants had electrodes attached on the forehead to capture activity in the currogator supercilii (frown) muscle and on the cheek to capture activity in the zygomaticus major (smile) muscle. A baseline measure, which lasted five minutes, was obtained for each participant, and activity was recorded during each four-minute trial.
time_window: baseline (PP1, PP2) and each of the five four-minute trials

description: Firm size measured using the (logged) number of employees in the focal year. The primary data sources are the Directory of Corporate Affiliations and Compustat historical databases.
