The same indicators for the focal latent constructs were used in Study 2 as in Study 1. A measurement error covariance between two entrepreneurial behaviors indicators (EB2 and EB3) was freed.

Measured with the Covin and Slevin (1989) entrepreneurial orientation scale and the Anderson et al. (2015) measurement model, retaining two indicators for managerial attitude toward risk after four EO indicators were eliminated for poor loading or cross-loading.
The same indicators for the focal latent constructs were used in Study 2 as in Study 1.

Measured as the percentage return on assets (ROA) of the acquired unit minus the mean ROA of the unit's 2-digit SIC industry, to control for potential industry effects. It was measured annually over the years from the acquisition to the divestiture. Data came from the COMPUSTAT Segment Tapes; the segment whose 4-digit SIC code matched that of the acquired firm was identified by its time of appearance and disappearance, and its sales were compared with the acquired unit's sales prior to acquisition to avoid misspecification. The authors note that they use business 'segments' rather than 'acquired units' and that unit performance was measured relative to overall firm performance in an additional check.
scale: percentage (ROA of the unit minus industry mean ROA)
time_window: annually from the year of acquisition to the year of divestiture

description: A dummy variable for the arrival of a new CEO from outside of the acquiring company, covering the year of acquisition through the year prior to the divestiture. It was coded new CEO = 1 and no = 0.
time_window: from the year of acquisition through the year prior to the divestiture

description: Following Bergh and Lawless (1998) and Keats and Hitt (1988), a variable designated for each year was regressed on net industry sales (2-digit SIC) using 5 years of data; for example, net industry sales values from 1990 through 1994 were used to predict volatility in 1995. The basic equation was yt = b0 + b1t + a, where y = industry sales, t = year, and a = residual. Industry stability is the standard error of the regression slope coefficient divided by the mean of sales. The lower the number of this variable, the more stable the industry. The raw data were collected from COMPUSTAT.
scale: ratio (standard error of the regression slope coefficient divided by mean sales; lower value = more stable industry)
time_window: 5 years of annual industry sales data per prediction year

description: Slack was measured with accounting data (Singh, 1986); the measure of absorbed slack is the debt to equity ratio, which reflects the healthiness of the balance sheet and borrowing capacity. The variable was reverse signed such that a negative sign indicates a low amount of slack and a positive sign indicates a high amount of slack. The authors also examined the effects of change of the divesting firm's slack in an additional analysis.
Measured as the percentage of ROA of the acquiring firm relative to the industry average ROA, operationalized as the firm's ROA minus the 2-digit SIC industry average ROA (Bergh, 1997).
scale: percentage (firm ROA minus 2-digit SIC industry average ROA)

description: The dependent variable is dummy coded in each spell (divested = 1, not divested = 0) to indicate whether the divestiture had occurred or not at the last date of each spell, with right-censoring for acquisitions not divested by 1998. The time between the announcement dates of the acquisition and the divestiture was used to measure the time between the two events, and this time was split into spells corresponding to the fiscal year of each sample or control firm. The data were obtained from the SDC Database.
time_window: annually over the years from acquisition to divestiture, 1988-1998

description: Ordinal measure of IEJV financial profitability with three levels (loss, break-even, gain), based on a perceptual assessment of venture performance rendered by the IEJV's general manager in the TK data. It was used as an independent variable for the effect of prior performance at time t-1 on initial ownership change at time t, and as a dependent variable for the effect of ownership change at time t on short-term performance at time t+1. The performance variables were lagged by one year.
time_window: t-1 for the change model; t+1 for the performance model

variable_name: Changes in IEJV ownership structure (event of ownership change)
description: Changes in the relative ownership levels of existing partners, operationalized as an ordered and repeatable event variable; events are ordered, multiple, and have a natural sequence, and a subject can only experience one event at any given time. The Cik event variable denotes event time for the kth event for IEJV i, with Cik equal to or greater than Cik-1. Change characteristics such as direction, magnitude, or destination were not included.

variable_name: state-dependent covariate Z(t) / stage of ownership changes (number of prior changes)
description: State-dependent covariate of the number of prior ownership changes: 0 if t is at or before the time of the first ownership change; 1 if t is after the first change and at or before the second; 2 if after the second and at or before the third; 3 if after the third and at or before the fourth; and 4 if after the fourth change and at or before the fifth. The state-dependent effects of multiple and sequential ownership changes were tested by jointly modeling transitions from one state to another, and the stage is entered as separate indicators for one, two, three, and four prior ownership changes.
scale: count of prior ownership changes (0-4 states)

description: Entropy-based measure of the extent to which equity ownership is shared between/among IEJV partners, adapted from Raghunathan's refined entropy measure of diversification to the IEJV context. It is computed from the number of IEJV partners and the distribution of equity ownership among partner groups, incorporating related and unrelated aspects based on nationality and corporate affiliation, where Japanese partner groups follow Makino and Beamish's classification. The value originates at 0 (100% ownership control by a single parent firm) and the maximum value is 1 (completely even distribution of equity ownership between/among partners); a higher value indicates a higher extent of shared equity ownership. The equation itself is unreadable in the extracted text.

Nonrepeatable event of IEJV relationship termination: the dependent variable Tit equaled 1 if IEJV i was terminated by time t and 0 otherwise. Observations were right-censored in 2003 if the indicator variable Tit = 0 in every year for IEJV i.

Analyst coverage is the number of financial analysts issuing reports for the firm, taken as the number of analysts included in the earnings forecast consensus in December of each year; if no earnings forecast consensus is available, coverage is zero for that year. Analyst coverage is regressed cross-sectionally each year on firm size, stock return, ROA, and return volatility, and the residuals of that model are taken and standardized to measure each firm's status.
time_window: the year just before the takeover announcement

description: The acquiring firm's status minus the target firm's status, where firm status is the firm's standardized residual of analyst coverage in the year just before the takeover announcement.
time_window: the year just before the takeover announcement

description: The three-day percentage abnormal return for the acquiring firm for the time window [-1 day, +1 day] around the takeover announcement.
time_window: [-1 day, +1 day] around the takeover announcement

description: The three-day percentage abnormal return for the target firm for the time window [-1 day, +1 day] around the takeover announcement.
time_window: [-1 day, +1 day] around the takeover announcement

description: A dummy variable that takes the value of '1' if the deal announced was successfully completed and '0' otherwise.
time_window: from announcement to completion or failure

description: ROA is income before extraordinary items scaled by average total assets. Post_ROA_Adj is the acquirer's post-acquisition ROA in the kth year after deal completion minus the median ROA of the corresponding two-digit SIC industry; only completed deals are included and k can take the value of 1, 2, or 3.
time_window: t+1 to t+3 after deal completion

description: MTB is the market value of equity plus book value of liabilities divided by total assets. Post_MTB_Adj is the acquirer's post-acquisition MTB in the kth year after deal completion minus the median MTB of the corresponding two-digit SIC industry; only completed deals are included and k can take the value of 1, 2, or 3.
time_window: t+1 to t+3 after deal completion

description: The ratio of shares held by all institutions to the total number of shares outstanding, based on Section 13(f) filings provided by the Compact Disclosure data base. Ownership was measured for 1989.

The number of new products developed by the firm, calculated as the total number of new product announcements in the 1990-92 period. Data were obtained from Dialog's PTS New Product Announcements (PTS NPA) data base, which provides the full text of news releases issued by firms; these announcements include new products and services, new processes, new technologies, and other similar events.

The proportion of a firm's equity in 1989 owned by pressure-resistant institutions, i.e., public pension funds, mutual funds, and endowments and foundations owning at least 1 percent of the firm's equity. For each category, the proportion of ownership in 1989 was determined. Institutions were classified following the procedure described in Brickley et al. (1988); institutional type was identified using the Money Market Directory and cross-verified with Moody's Bank and Finance Manual and Nelson's Directory of Investment Managers.

The proportion of a firm's equity in 1989 owned by pressure-sensitive institutions, i.e., insurance companies, banks, and nonbank trusts owning at least 1 percent of the firm's equity. For each category, the proportion of ownership in 1989 was determined. Institutions were classified following the procedure described in Brickley et al. (1988); institutional type was identified using the Money Market Directory and cross-verified with Moody's Bank and Finance Manual and Nelson's Directory of Investment Managers.

Count of prior adoptions of the L-1011 by airlines headquartered in the same nation as the focal airline. It is updated whenever an adoption occurs, and the update is effective the day after an adoption so that simultaneous adoptions do not influence each other in the model estimates. The variable was orthogonalized together with the other adoption and abandonment variables using Stata's orthog command, in the order adoptions in nation, abandonments in nation, adoption of the competing type, size-weighted adoption, size-weighted abandonment.

Count of prior abandonments of the L-1011 by airlines headquartered in the same nation as the focal airline; a full abandonment is when an airline sells all of its planes of the focal design. It is updated whenever an abandonment occurs, effective the day after the event. The variable was orthogonalized together with the adoption variables.

Count of prior adoptions of the competing aircraft (the DC-10) by airlines headquartered in the same nation as the focal airline, entered in the L-1011 adoption model. It is updated whenever an adoption of the competing aircraft occurs, effective the day after the event, and was orthogonalized with the other diffusion variables after adoptions in nation and abandonments in nation.
time_window: cumulative prior adoptions of the competing aircraft, updated daily

description: The dependent variable is the event of placing an order for an innovative aircraft design; in this analysis the event is an L-1011 adoption. Adoption dates are the time of delivery, accurate to the day, because order dates are not available for all aircraft. Firm observations are split annually to update covariates and split again within the year whenever needed to update the diffusion covariates.

Count of prior adoptions of the DC-10 by airlines headquartered in the same nation as the focal airline. It is updated whenever an adoption occurs, effective the day after the event. The variable was orthogonalized together with the other adoption and abandonment variables using Stata's orthog command.

Count of prior abandonments of the DC-10 by airlines headquartered in the same nation as the focal airline; a full abandonment is when an airline sells all of its planes of the focal design. It is updated whenever an abandonment occurs, effective the day after the event. The variable was orthogonalized together with the adoption variables.

Count of prior adoptions of the competing aircraft (the L-1011) by airlines headquartered in the same nation as the focal airline, entered in the DC-10 adoption model. It is updated whenever an adoption of the competing aircraft occurs, effective the day after the event, and was orthogonalized with the other diffusion variables.
time_window: cumulative prior adoptions of the competing aircraft, updated daily

description: The dependent variable is the event of placing an order for an innovative aircraft design; in this analysis the event is a DC-10 adoption. Adoption dates are the time of delivery, accurate to the day, because order dates are not available for all aircraft. Firm observations are split annually to update covariates and split again within the year whenever needed to update the diffusion covariates.

For each focal patent assigned to an original firm, the authors isolate each forward citation made to that patent by other (external) firms during the five years following its application date (Group 1). They then examine the forward citations made to those citing patents during the five years following their application dates; reabsorption is said to occur if any of those citations are owned by the original firm (Group 2). The variable is measured as the number of patents in Group 1 that are cited by the originating firm, i.e., the number of spilled patents that are reabsorbed by the firm.
time_window: forward citations observed in the five years following each patent's application date, and in the five years following the citing patent's application date

description: A count of the number of patents in Group 2, which represents the number of times that spilled knowledge (Group 1) is reabsorbed by the firm. It captures how many times spilled knowledge is used in the firm's subsequent patents.
time_window: five-year window following the application date of the citing external patent

description: Measured at the patent level in two steps. First, for each subclass appearing on the focal patent, the ease of recombining that subclass is measured as the number of distinct subclasses that appeared with the focal subclass in all USPTO patents featuring that subclass divided by the number of patents featuring that subclass. Next, the focal patent's complexity is calculated as the total number of distinct subclasses listed on that patent divided by their cumulative ease of combination. The equations themselves are not readable in the supplied text.

A firm-level variable. Units are defined by the geographical region of the inventors listed on a patent, where a region is a state if the inventor was from the United States and a country otherwise; interdependencies between units occur if inventors on a patent are from different regions. For each firm, the patents applied for during the three years preceding the application date of the focal patent are isolated, coupling between each pair of units is computed from the overlap of patents across units, and firm coupling is the average coupling between all pairs of units in the firm. The equation itself is not readable in the supplied text.
time_window: three years preceding the application date of the focal patent

variable_name: Time and effort to coordinate with a partner
description: Single-item perceptual measure: the architects reported to what degree they had to spend a significant amount of time and effort to coordinate with their alliance partner. Responses are ordered ordinal, based on a 7-point Likert scale running from strongly disagree to strongly agree. The item was used as the dependent variable in the ordinal regression analysis.
scale: 7-point Likert scale (strongly disagree to strongly agree)

description: The log value of the project cost was used as a proxy for joint task complexity. The authors argue that the costing of these projects is largely based on their technical and logistic complexity, which requires more extensive project management, and that larger projects require greater interaction between architects and contractors. The measure is a single item and is treated as a continuous variable.

The average response of two highly correlated questionnaire items (r = 0.50, p < 0.001) on the compatibility of the two firms' goals and of their organizational processes, both reverse coded, with a reliability of 0.75. Interpartner diversity increased to the extent that the architect indicated that the goals as well as the objectives and organizational processes of the two organizations were not compatible.

Single-item measure of mutual adaptation in work styles, estimated by the degree to which the architects perceived both partners as having changed their ways of working to suit the specific needs of the other. The item is reverse coded, so higher values indicate a lack of mutual adaptation. The authors argue the construct is unidimensional, clear to respondents and narrow, which supports the use of a single item.

Single-item measure of the perception of equity in the problem-solving process: when problems arose, the extent to which the architect and the contractor cooperated with each other, for example by fully complying with the request of the other partner even at the expense of their own short-term interests. The item is reverse coded, so higher values indicate a lack of cooperative problem solving.

Single-item measure of the architect's opinion that the contractor would take advantage of opportunities to profit at the architect's expense, following Parkhe (1993). The authors note that, although the measure does not specify why a contractor may be able to hold up the architect, its advantage is that it is a direct measure of a manager's perception of that threat.

A subjective measure of asset specificity in the context of a specific relationship: architects estimate the degree to which they feel they would lose non-recoverable investments (drawings, equipment, etc.) if the project were discontinued.

Single-item measure of the degree to which an architect believes that their contact person in the contractor firm will look out for the architect's interests even when it is costly to do so. The authors state that this corresponds to 'personal trust' in Williamson's (1993) typology.

The architects indicated the number of prior projects on which they had worked with the contractor: none, one to three, four to six, or more than six projects. The variable is measured on a 4-point scale, in contrast to the 7-point Likert scales used for the other variables.
scale: 4-point scale (none; one to three; four to six; more than six prior projects)

variable_name: Joint task complexity and interpartner diversity
description: Cooperation costs were represented by their two direct sources: joint task complexity (log of project cost) and interpartner diversity (average of two reverse-coded items on compatibility of goals and organizational processes). Lack of mutual adaptation and lack of cooperative problem solving were also measured as related items.

The gap was calculated by summing the scores for each scale item to create an overall measure for both customers and employees for each business unit and then subtracting the total average employee score from the total average customer score; scores for the 'ruthlessness' items were reverse scored. The text's stated order of subtraction is ambiguous relative to the definition of a positive gap as employee perceptions exceeding those of customers. The scale proved reliable with a Cronbach alpha for customers of 0.83 and for employees of 0.86.
time_window: at the time of the survey

description: Employee perception of the company's reputation was measured with the Corporate Character Scale, a generic inventory of traits used to distinguish between organizations and to define how a respondent believes an organization will behave. Respondents are asked to imagine that the target organization 'has come to life' as a human being and to assess its personality, with each item measured on a five-point Likert-type scale labeled from strongly disagree to strongly agree. The item scores were summed to create an overall measure for employees of each business unit.
scale: five-point Likert-type items summed to an overall score
time_window: at the time of the survey

description: Customer perception of the company's reputation was measured with the same Corporate Character Scale used for employees, an inventory of traits on which the respondent assesses the organization as if it were a person. Each item is measured on a five-point Likert-type scale labeled from strongly disagree to strongly agree, and the item scores were summed to create an overall measure for the customers of each business unit.
scale: five-point Likert-type items summed to an overall score
time_window: at the time of the survey

description: Annual sales revenue was obtained at the time when the survey was conducted and for a point in time one year later; the dependent variable is the percentage change in sales between the two points. The measure is used as an equally relevant and comparable outcome across the businesses in the sample.
time_window: survey year and one year later

description: Experimental cue manipulated in the written scenarios at two levels (0 = low, 1 = high). The wording was developed with an expert panel and relied on Rousseau et al. (1998), R. C. Mayer et al. (1995) and Zaheer et al. (1998), with the goal of creating a sense of accepted vulnerability and positive behavioral expectations on the side of the respondents.

Experimental cue manipulated in the written scenarios at two levels (0 = low, 1 = high). The wording relied on the definitions by Feldman and Pentland (2003) and Becker (2004) and described how partner-specific alliance experience did or did not result in stable patterns of interaction, for example with regard to communication, conflict resolution, and decision-making.

Experimental cue manipulated in the written scenarios at two levels (0 = low, 1 = high). The levels were based on Balakrishnan and Koza's (1993) ideas but adapted to the context so that they described whether or not the focal firm was able to gain exclusive insights into the partner firm (e.g., processes, business practices, capabilities, and technologies) by means of partner-specific alliance experience.

For each scenario respondents indicated whether the resources offered by the partner firm were best accessed via an alliance or an acquisition, and could also indicate that under the given circumstances neither form of future cooperation was suitable. The resulting three-category variable is analysed with alliances and acquisitions contrasted against the no-decision category.
scale: three categories: no decision, alliance, acquisition

description: The same three-category governance choice variable is used for the comparative contrast between the two forms of future cooperation, i.e. the equation contrasting a subsequent alliance with a subsequent acquisition with the former partner firm.

Scale calculated by taking the average of all significant items loading on the factor identified in the factor analysis. Seven items loaded on the first factor and describe executives' perceptions of the merger announcement. Items were answered on a five-point Likert scale (5 = strongly agree, 1 = strongly disagree).
scale: 5-point Likert scale (5 = strongly agree, 1 = strongly disagree)

description: Scale calculated by taking the average of all significant items loading on the factor identified in the factor analysis. The second factor describes executives' interactions with acquiring company top managers following the merger. Items were answered on a five-point Likert scale (5 = strongly agree, 1 = strongly disagree).
scale: 5-point Likert scale (5 = strongly agree, 1 = strongly disagree)

description: Scale calculated by taking the average of all significant items loading on the factor identified in the factor analysis. Six items loaded on the third factor and describe executives' perceptions of the long-term effects of the merger. Items were answered on a five-point Likert scale (5 = strongly agree, 1 = strongly disagree).
scale: 5-point Likert scale (5 = strongly agree, 1 = strongly disagree)

description: Dependent variable in the logistic regression, coded 0 = left and 1 = stayed. The employment status of each manager was followed in the Register for 6 years following the acquisition; managers still employed 6 years later were coded as 'stayers' and managers no longer employed were coded as 'leavers.' Departed executives were also asked to list their reasons for leaving and were labeled as voluntary or involuntary leavers.

Dummy variable coded 1 if Target proposed to open a store in a census place in a year. Proposals were compiled through a media search of Lexis-Nexis, America's News, and Sprawl-Busters from 1998 to 2008 and matched with a list of Target store openings from 1998 to 2010; for an opened store whose proposal date could not be identified, the proposal time was estimated as the average construction time for a Target store before the opening date. It is estimated with a probit equation within the four-equation CMP model.

Count of protests against Walmart's new store opening proposals within a 15-mile radius of the center of a place in the past three years that were not spearheaded by protest-prone activists. Protests led by local residents, merchants, or politicians were coded as protests not spearheaded by protest-prone activists against a first mover. Two trained research assistants independently coded the explanatory variables from reports of anti-Walmart protests (average Cohen's kappa 0.91).

Count of protests against Walmart's new store opening proposals that were backed by unions within a 15-mile radius of the center of a place in the past three years. A protest was coded as being union-led if the sources reported that at least one protest activity was backed by unions; the authors used union-led protests as a proxy for protests spearheaded by protest-prone activists belonging to a national organization and measured this variable for comparison purposes.

Number of protests with Walmart-specific claims only within a 15-mile radius of the center of a place in the past three years. These specific concerns include the lack of retail diversity due to too many Walmart stores nearby, problems with a particular location that Walmart chose, a poor proposal and planning process that Walmart made, neighbors' concerns over the design of a Walmart store, and public subsidy to a Walmart project. If a protest made both Walmart-specific and big-box-store-general claims, it was counted as a protest with general claims but not as one with Walmart-specific claims only.

Number of protests that made general claims against big-box retailers within a 15-mile radius of the center of a place in the past three years. General concerns include the disruption by the presence of a big retailing chain to the identity of a small town or historical district, the impact on local business, the poor labor conditions, the antiunion attitude, the reliance on imported goods from overseas, the store size, or too many other big-box stores (such as Target and Home Depot) nearby.

Number of protests that attempted to introduce store-cap legislation within a 15-mile radius of the center of a place in the past three years. Store-size-cap rules that limit the square footage of any new store are described as a severe measure to wipe out big-box stores.

The percentage of protests from which Walmart withdrew its store opening proposals within a 15-mile radius of the center of a place in the past three years. Its inclusion restricts the estimation to places with at least one anti-Walmart protest and is used in the Target proposal equation of the CMP model.

Dummy variable indicating whether Target lacks local knowledge in a place, coded 1 if Target neither had a store nor made any proposal within 15 miles in the past three years. Interactions between this variable and the six independent variables measuring specific types of protests were created.

Firm participation in one (or both) of the core CSR conferences held each year for companies interested in CSR-related practices: the Committee Encouraging Corporate Philanthropy (CECP) and the Boston College Center for Corporate Citizenship (BCCCC) annual conferences. The authors obtained the list of firms that participated in these conferences during the time of the survey and matched these to the firms in their sample, using conference participation as a robust and clear objective indicator of firms' involvement in the network.
time_window: during the time of the survey

description: The percentage of organizations within the firm's two-digit standard industrial classification (SIC) code that adopted the same practice, calculated for each of the three dependent variables (EVP, DOS, SBV). SIC codes were identified using the North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) online database. The measure was mean-centered to mitigate potential multicollinearity.

A four-item scale (Cronbach's alpha = 0.72) asking respondents whether they had written processes and standards in place for employees to contribute to CSR activities, for nonprofit board involvement, for managing asset allocation to nonprofits, and for facilitating agreements with nonprofits. Responses to each item were coded 1 (yes) or 0 (no) and then summed to index the extent to which the organizational infrastructure was ready to implement EVP practices.

Responses to a behaviorally based survey item asking whether at least 30% of individuals in the top two levels of the company (chief executive and direct reports) had publicly participated in a company-sponsored CSR event within the last year. Responses were coded 1 for agreement, 0 otherwise.

Participation in the Global Reporting Initiative (GRI), coded 1 for GRI reporting firms and 0 otherwise, based on the online list of all companies that adopted the GRI. The authors describe GRI adoption as a corporate identity strategy demonstrating belongingness to socially responsible organizations, and note that completing a GRI report requires substantial resources, operational changes and third-party audit verification.
Coded 1 if the firm was a member of the Fortune 100 (F100) in 2008, the time of the survey, and 0 otherwise, using the Fortune online database.
Dummy variable, coding adoption as 1 and 0 otherwise, reflecting the adoption of any type of employee volunteering program practice.
Dummy variable, coding adoption as 1 and 0 otherwise, reflecting the adoption of a day of service practice, the turnkey practice variant.
Dummy variable, coding adoption as 1 and 0 otherwise, reflecting the adoption of a skills-based volunteering practice, the tailored practice variant.

Net cash inflows into all funds offered by a provider, measured in millions of dollars. The measure captures the change in assets under management from year to year, adjusted for the appreciation (or depreciation) of the fund's investments, summing over each of the firm's mutual funds the change in assets minus the fund's return times average assets. Fund provider profits are, to a first approximation, increasing in the amount of assets they manage.

A decaying stock of the firm's prior new product experience consisting of new funds created in domains new to the firm that performed below social aspirations. Each new fund is assigned to exactly one of four experience categories based on its initial launch conditions; a domain is new if the firm has no prior experience in that category, and a fund is negatively performing if its second-year cash inflows are below the median cash inflow of all other funds in the same category that year. The annual experience values are aggregated to the firm-year level and decayed by 15% each year.

A decaying stock of the firm's prior new product experience consisting of new funds created in domains in which the firm already operated at least one fund and that performed below social aspirations. New funds are categorized by their initial launch conditions and a fund is negatively performing if its second-year cash inflows fall below the median cash inflow of all other funds in the same category that year. The annual experience values are aggregated to the firm-year level and decayed by 15% each year.

A decaying stock of the firm's prior new product experience consisting of new funds created in domains new to the firm that generated cash inflows greater than the median cash inflow of all other funds in the same category during the same year. The annual experience values are aggregated to the firm-year level and decayed by 15% each year.

A decaying stock of the firm's prior new product experience consisting of new funds created in domains in which the firm already operated at least one fund and that generated cash inflows greater than the median cash inflow of all other funds in the same category during the same year. The annual experience values are aggregated to the firm-year level and decayed by 15% each year.

variable_name: negative feedback in a new domain (dummy)
description: Indicator for the focal new fund having been created in a category new to the firm and having performed below social aspirations in its second year. The fund-level models use a set of dummies for each of the four types of experience, with negative feedback in experienced domains as the omitted category.
time_window: categorization based on the fund's first two years of existence

variable_name: negative feedback in an experienced domain (omitted category)
description: Indicator for the focal new fund having been created in a category in which the firm had prior experience and having performed below social aspirations in its second year. This category is the omitted category in all fund-level models.
time_window: categorization based on the fund's first two years of existence

variable_name: positive feedback in a new domain (dummy)
description: Indicator for the focal new fund having been created in a category new to the firm and having generated cash inflows above the median cash inflow of other funds in the same category in its second year. Included as one of the four experience-type dummies in the fund-level models.
time_window: categorization based on the fund's first two years of existence

variable_name: positive feedback in an experienced domain (dummy)
description: Indicator for the focal new fund having been created in a category in which the firm had prior experience and having generated cash inflows above the median cash inflow of other funds in the same category in its second year. Included as one of the four experience-type dummies in the fund-level models.
time_window: categorization based on the fund's first two years of existence

variable_name: number of new funds created in the same category as the focal fund
description: A count of how many new funds the firm creates in the year after the focal fund is categorized as performing above or below aspirations, counted within the focal fund's category. It is one of three counts of new funds created by domain relative to the focal fund, and the dependent variable is highly overdispersed count data.
time_window: one-year period after the focal fund is categorized

variable_name: number of new funds created in completely new categories for the firm
description: A count of how many new funds the firm creates in the year after the focal fund is categorized as performing above or below aspirations, counted for categories that are completely new to the firm. It is one of three counts of new funds created by domain relative to the focal fund.
time_window: one-year period after the focal fund is categorized

variable_name: number of new funds created in other categories in which the firm has prior experience
description: A count of how many new funds the firm creates in the year after the focal fund is categorized as performing above or below aspirations, counted for other categories in which the firm already has prior experience. It is one of three counts of new funds created by domain relative to the focal fund.
time_window: one-year period after the focal fund is categorized

variable_name: net new cash flow in third year (for new funds)
description: The focal new fund's net new cash flow in its third year, where the fund is categorized as existing in a new versus experienced domain in year one and as above versus below aspirations in year two. The dependent variable is unbounded (net new cash flows are continuous and can be positive or negative) and is estimated with an OLS model that includes a fund-level lagged dependent variable and the category-level average flow into each fund in the category in the current year.

variable_name: net new cash inflow in each year (four plus) for existing funds
description: The dependent variable in the spillover analysis is the net new cash inflow of an existing fund (a fund at least four years old) in each year. The independent variables are counts of new funds lagged one year that were categorized as performing positively or negatively in the same category as the focal fund, in another category in which the firm had prior experience, or in a completely new category for the firm; a second model uses decaying stock values of these same independent variables.
time_window: annual, from the fund's fourth year onwards

description: A dummy variable set equal to 1 if the firm reports providing customization services for a product in a market in a year, and 0 otherwise. It comes from the survey item in which firms indicate, for each of their products, whether they provide customization services to meet user needs; the measures of production activity in the survey are not mutually exclusive, so a firm may report more than one activity.
time_window: annual, 1997-2009, with one-period lagged explanatory variables

description: The fraction of firms in product market j in year t-1 that undertake product customization services. It is entered lagged by one period in the product-market-level count models of entrants and exits, and is interacted with the laser industry dummy.

A dummy variable set equal to 1 if firm i exits product market j in year t, and 0 otherwise. The variable is set equal to 0 for the last year in the data, 2009, since firm exits are not observed for that year.

A dummy set equal to 1 for the laser industry and 0 otherwise, used as the measure of submarket potential. The authors argue that the upstream laser industry has greater submarket potential because it features a general-purpose technology with wide-ranging applications; the measure is interacted with the customization measures.

Count of the number of entrants in a product market in a year, estimated with negative binomial regressions at the product market level. The explanatory variables, including the fractions of firms undertaking stock, custom, design and distribution activity, are one-period lagged values.

Count of the number of exits in a product market in a year, estimated with negative binomial regressions at the product market level. All explanatory variables, including the lagged fractions of firms undertaking stock, custom, design and distribution activity, are lagged by one period.

Emissions of each chemical reported to the Toxics Release Inventory were divided by the EPA reportable quantity for that chemical and aggregated across the chemicals released at a facility to produce a 'toxics release index.' Emissions of chemical i to air, land, and water count where they are above the reporting threshold, and 0 otherwise, across the chemicals tracked by the TRI. Because the data were skewed, the index was log-transformed after adding 1. Where releases of none of the chemicals exceed threshold levels the index is a missing value, because no report to the TRI is necessary. The formula shown in the paper was not readable in the source text, so this description follows the authors' prose.
scale: log-transformed index (log of the toxicity-weighted sum plus 1)
time_window: 2000 (lagged emissions from the prior reporting period)

description: A variable derived from the survey data, coded 1 if the environmental quality manager reported directly to the plant manager and 0 otherwise.

variable_name: plant manager compensation tied to environmental performance
description: A survey variable coded 1 if the plant manager had a portion of salary tied to environmental performance, and 0 otherwise.

variable_name: environmental manager compensation tied to environmental performance
description: A survey variable coded 1 if the environmental quality manager had a portion of salary tied to environmental performance, and 0 otherwise.

A composite variable created by adding responses from three survey questions asking the extent of agreement, on a five-point scale on which 1 indicated strong disagreement and 5 indicated strong agreement, with statements about the inclusiveness of strategic processes. The three statements concern the inclusion of environmental quality managers in discussions about the choices of equipment to be installed at the facility, about fundamental design issues impacting the facility, and about potential process modifications. The composite had a reported reliability of .88 and ran from 3 to 15.

Abnormal returns earned by corporate blockholders, computed with the market-adjusted return model with size-based decile indices: an abnormal return equals the difference between a firm's total return and an index return computed by averaging the total return of a decile of similar-sized firms for a common time interval. Daily abnormal returns were compounded into holding period performance measures. Each holding period began on Day = -1, the trading day preceding the Form 13D filing, and included a fixed number of ex post trading days (63 days = 3 months; 148 days = 7 months; 233 days = 11 months; and 317 days = 15 months).
time_window: Day = -1 through 3, 7, 11 and 15 months after the Form 13D filing

description: Coded 1 if the surveyed target's financial executive reported the target was a supplier or customer of the blockholder and coded 0 otherwise.
Coded 1 if the surveyed target financial executive reported the target made a cross-investment (not necessarily of 5 percent) into the blockholder's equity securities and coded 0 otherwise.

Computed by multiplying the fraction of blockholder ownership times the ex ante value of the target and then dividing that product by the ex ante value of the blockholder. The percentage of blockholder ownership was taken from target proxies dated approximately 18 months after the initial Form 13D filing to allow the blockholder to adjust the extent of its holding to a level sufficient to obtain private benefits. Firm value measurements were computed as of the day preceding the initial Form 13D filing by multiplying a firm's closing stock price by the number of its common shares outstanding. A log transformation of the variable was made to adjust for positive skewness.
time_window: ownership from proxies approximately 18 months after the initial Form 13D filing; firm values as of the day preceding the initial Form 13D filing

description: Firm bio value-chain employment in an economic area the year before the expansion: the sum of the firm's employment in all firm activities (four-digit SIC codes) that map into the bio value chain (SIC codes 8731, 2830 and 5120) in that EA. Entered in the models in natural log form.

Firm employment in non-bio value chains in the economic area the year before the expansion, i.e., employment in non-bio R&D (SIC codes 8732-8734), non-bio manufacturing (SIC codes 2000-3900, except 2830) and non-bio sales (SIC codes 5000-5900, except 5120). Entered in the models in natural log form.

Firm employment in support activities in the economic area the year before the expansion; support covers any SIC code outside the bio and non-bio value chains, mainly business services such as headquarters, medical labs, and financial, insurance and real estate services such as holding companies. Entered in the models in natural log form.

Firm bio R&D (SIC code 8731) employment in the economic area the year before the expansion, a component of firm bio value-chain employment used to examine within- and across-activity collocation. Entered in the models in natural log form.

Firm bio manufacturing (SIC code 2830) employment in the economic area the year before the expansion, a component of firm bio value-chain employment used to examine within- and across-activity collocation. Entered in the models in natural log form.

Firm bio sales (SIC code 5120) employment in the economic area the year before the expansion, a component of firm bio value-chain employment used to examine within- and across-activity collocation. Entered in the models in natural log form.

The specialization of the region in biopharmaceuticals, computed as the employment location quotient: the share of regional (EA) employment in biopharmaceuticals compared with the share of U.S. employment in biopharmaceuticals, excluding the focal firm's own biopharmaceutical employment at the region level. A value greater than 1 indicates that biopharmaceuticals was overrepresented in terms of employment in the EA. Entered in the models in natural log form.

Dummy equal to 1 if firm f chooses economic area r to open a new establishment in focal bio activity i at time t. This is the dependent variable of the conditional logit location choice models, where within a firm-activity-year group the firm chooses among 134 EAs.

The focal activity of the new establishment in the bio value chain, identified from the establishment's SIC code: R&D (SIC code 8731), manufacturing (SIC code 2830), or sales (SIC code 5120). Separate location choice models are estimated for each activity.
The number of years in which the CEO has served in his or her current position. CEO tenure data were collected from the information provided through the office of the Corporate Secretary.

A composite of two variables: the number of international assignments and total years in such assignments. The index distinguishes an officer with a single international assignment of fifteen years from another officer with fifteen years of international experience spread over three separate venues. Because the distribution of international experience for this sample was not normal, this variable was transformed. The data were collected from the information provided through the office of the Corporate Secretary.

A multi-item construct including: (1) foreign sales as a percentage of total sales, (2) foreign assets as a percentage of total assets, (3) the number of foreign subsidiaries relative to the company's total number of distinct operating units, and (4) the dispersion of the subsidiaries of a firm among ten psychic zones of the world identified by Ronen and Shenkar (1985). A confirmatory factor analysis indicates that the four-item construct constitutes a robust construct, with a reliability coefficient (Cronbach's alpha) of 0.93. Data were collected from Compact Disclosure/Worldscope Global, 1996 and the Directory of Corporate Affiliations.

Refers to whether the current CEO was employed by the focal firm immediately prior to his or her promotion to CEO (inside succession) or by another firm (outside succession). The data were collected from the information provided through the office of the Corporate Secretary.

An accounting measure of firm performance; ROA is described as an appropriate performance measure due to the relative inability of firm management to manipulate it and as particularly useful for examining performance for firms with international exposure. All performance measures are computed as three-year averages, and all performance data are collected from Compact Disclosure/Worldscope Global for the years 1994-1996. Where CEOs have not been in office for the entire period, only the years for which they have held the position of CEO are relied on.

An accounting measure of firm performance; based on an extensive analysis of performance data, Woo and Willard (1983) concluded that ROI provides the most comprehensive measure of firm performance. All performance measures are computed as three-year averages, and all performance data are collected from Compact Disclosure/Worldscope Global for the years 1994-1996. Where CEOs have not been in office for the entire period, only the years for which they have held the position of CEO are relied on.

The market-based measure of firm performance; whereas accounting-based measures reflect past and present firm performance, a market measure such as market-to-book ratio provides an indication of the firm's future performance potential, reflecting the firm's ability to exceed expected returns in the future. All performance measures are computed as three-year averages, and all performance data are collected from Compact Disclosure/Worldscope Global for the years 1994-1996. Where CEOs have not been in office for the entire period, only the years for which they have held the position of CEO are relied on.
CSR score estimated as a net score (strengths minus concerns) of the six dimensions in KLD: community, diversity, employee relations, environment, product, and human rights.
CSR strengths score, part of the net CSR score (strengths minus concerns) of the six KLD dimensions.
CSR concerns score, part of the net CSR score (strengths minus concerns) of the six KLD dimensions.
CSR actions toward stakeholders that directly transact with the firm: employee, product, human rights, and diversity dimensions.
CSR actions toward other stakeholders: community and environment dimensions.
Change in the CSR score (Δ CSR) used as the variable of interest in the short-interest regression for pilot firms during the Reg SHO period.
Average monthly scaled short interest during the year. Scaled short interest is monthly short interest divided by shares outstanding times 100.
Indicator variable equal to one for pilot firms and zero for nonpilot firms.
Indicator variable equal to one if a firm's total assets fall into the bottom quartile, denoting small firms.

Team members reported their years of previous work experience in each of nine functional areas. The dominant function of each team member was determined as the functional area in which he or she had spent the greater part of his or her career, and the heterogeneity index proposed by Blau (1977) was then computed. Following Teachman (1980), the measure was normed so that its values range from 0 (low diversity) to 1 (high diversity). The formula itself is not readable in the available text.

An intrapersonal functional diversity score was first computed for each team member (see Walsh, 1988) and then the average of these scores was computed within each team (see Burke & Steensma, 1998). The score is based on the percentage of a manager's total years of experience spent in each functional area and assesses the central tendency in the distribution of intrapersonal functional diversity scores within a team. The measure was normed (Teachman, 1980) so that values range from 0 (low diversity) to 1 (high diversity); the formula itself is not readable in the available text.

Each team member evaluated the extent to which (1) information used to make key decisions was freely shared among the members of the team, (2) team members worked hard to keep one another up to date on their activities, and (3) team members were kept 'in the loop' about key issues affecting the business unit. The response set for all items ranged from 1, 'very strongly disagree,' to 7, 'very strongly agree,' and the three-item scale had a Cronbach's alpha of .89. Responses were averaged across all of the managers on a team to create a group-level index.
scale: 1 = very strongly disagree to 7 = very strongly agree
level: individual responses aggregated to the team

description: Performance was measured as a management team's actual profitability relative to its targeted profitability for the survey year, multiplied by 100 to simplify the interpretation of results. Profitability was defined in terms of net operating profit before tax (NOPBT), and targets were developed under the supervision of corporate management and intended to be stretch goals. Performance data were collected from corporate records; financial target achievement for the teams in the sample ranged from 70 to 113.
time_window: survey year (about one year after survey administration)

description: Informants indicated on a seven-point Likert scale the extent to which they would use the information cues in a scenario to clarify and define the strategic issues identified in the applicable case. The scale consisted of all 16 information cues in each scenario; the Cronbach alpha was .88. Statistics were calculated on the basis of averaged responses for each of the variables from both cases.

Items were constructed from the information in the case scenario and focused on whether the information was external to the hospital or internal. Ten items consisting of five external and five internal information cues from each scenario were used initially; one item for the second scenario had a negative interitem correlation and was dropped. Items were scaled so that high scores indicated high use of external information for interpretation, and the Cronbach alpha was .73.

Ten items adapted from the questionnaire used by Jackson and Dutton (1988) assessed the positive-gain dimension of interpretation, for example asking to what extent respondents would label the situation as something positive. The continua were scaled so that high ratings indicated that respondents labeled the case situation as positive; the Cronbach alpha was .91. All 15 items were repeated after each scenario was presented.

Five questions assessed the extent to which a CEO would use the controllable label to describe the two case scenarios, adapted from the questionnaire used by Jackson and Dutton (1988). Items asked, for instance, whether the hospital could manage the situation instead of the situation managing it, and the continua were scaled so that high ratings indicated that respondents labeled the case situation as controllable. The Cronbach alpha was .72.

Profiles of product-service offerings were constructed for each hospital for 1987 and 1989 from the 54 product-service or facility categories reported in the American Hospital Association's Annual Guide Book. The weighted-differences method used by Hambrick (1981) assigned a weight of three to a service added in 1989 that one-third or fewer of the hospitals offered in 1987, two to one added by 1989 that existed in between one-third and two-thirds of the hospitals in 1987, and one to one added by 1989 that existed in two-thirds or more of the hospitals in 1987. The difference between the number of services offered in 1987 and the summed weights of the products and services offered in 1989 indicated the extent of growth in offerings.

Hospital inpatient days divided by the total number of days beds were available. Values were averaged over performance data from 1989 and 1990 to guard against one-year outlier performance, and the measure came from the Healthcare Financial Management Association's Medicare Cost Report data base. Occupancy is an efficiency measure.

Net inpatient revenue minus inpatient cost divided by total discharges. Values were averaged over performance data from 1989 and 1990, and the measure came from the Healthcare Financial Management Association's Medicare Cost Report data base. Profit is used here as an indicator of financial viability.

The number of admissions divided by total beds to standardize for size. Values were averaged over performance data from 1989 and 1990, and the data were obtained from the American Hospital Association's Annual Guide Book. Admissions is treated as an efficiency measure.

Directors' ideologies were measured by assessing the ideological emphases of their donations to the two major political parties in the United States, using political donation data from the DIME database over the period 1980-2014. Bonica's ideal point estimates were first rescaled to range from 0 to 1, with higher (lower) values representing greater conservatism (liberalism), and then an adapted version of the four-item index developed by Chin et al. (2013) was computed. Given that these items cohered strongly (alpha = .95), they were averaged to create a composite index ranging from 0 (highly liberal) to 1 (highly conservative). Directors with no donation records (around 30% of those in the sample) were classified as moderate and assigned a score corresponding to the sample mean (0.56).

Built from the same composite index of director conservatism based on political donation records from the DIME database, which rescaled Bonica's ideal point estimates to range from 0 to 1 and averaged four donation-based items (alpha = .95). For ease of interpretation, in models predicting adoption of CEO-chair separation the variable was reversed to reflect director liberalism by subtracting the variable from 1. Directors with no donation records (around 30% of those in the sample) were classified as moderate.

variable_name: Prior adoptions by interlock partners / conservatism-weighted adoptions
description: A variable equaling the count of all prior adoptions of lone-insider structures in the focal firm's network (the diffusion 'intercept') was entered in the contagiousness vector to account for the expected baseline diffusion effect. To test the hypotheses, all prior adoption events in the network were individually multiplied by the corresponding interlocking director's conservatism and then aggregated at the level of each firm-year observation and entered alongside the baseline count. In the rare instances where a firm was connected to prior adopters by multiple directors, the adoption was weighted by the average conservatism of those interlocking directors.

variable_name: Prior adoptions by interlock partners / liberalism-weighted adoptions
description: A variable equaling the count of all prior adoptions of split CEO-chair structures in the focal firm's network (the diffusion 'intercept') was entered in the contagiousness vector to account for the expected baseline diffusion effect. For the hypothesis tests, all prior adoption events in the network were individually multiplied by the corresponding interlocking director's liberalism and aggregated at the level of each firm-year observation, entered alongside the baseline count. Where a firm was connected to prior adopters by multiple directors, the adoption was weighted by the average ideology of those interlocking directors.

variable_name: Adoption of a lone-insider board structure
description: Binary measure that took a value of 1 when the focal firm transitioned from having two or more inside directors to having the CEO as the lone inside director. This variable was assessed annually from 1997 to 2016. Following Joseph et al. (2014), an adoption event was coded as occurring when the focal firm moved to and subsequently retained a lone-insider board structure for at least two consecutive years. The authors observed 510 adoption events during the 20-year study window.

variable_name: Adoption of a split CEO-chair board structure
description: Coded similarly to the lone-insider measure: the variable took the value of 1 when the focal firm transitioned from having the same individual holding the CEO and board chair titles to having the two roles occupied by distinct individuals. It was assessed on an annual basis and updated from 0 to 1 when a firm adopted a split CEO-chair structure and retained it for at least two consecutive years. In the sample of 444 firms that had not adopted the practice as of 1996, 124 adoptions were observed during the study window.

Measured as the number of governance-related proxy proposals submitted by the focal firm's shareholders in the prior year. Data on governance proxy proposals were obtained from the Ethvest database, which contains information on shareholder resolutions. Unless otherwise noted, all control variables were lagged by 1 year.

Measured as the number of governance-related proxy proposals submitted by the focal firm's shareholders in the prior year. Data on governance proxy proposals were obtained from the Ethvest database, which contains information on shareholder resolutions. Unless otherwise noted, all control variables were lagged by 1 year.
To distinguish pre- and post-SOX time periods, the authors created a binary variable that took a value of '1' for the years 2002 and onward and '0' for all years prior.
To distinguish pre- and post-SOX time periods, the authors created a binary variable that took a value of '1' for the years 2002 and onward and '0' for all years prior.

Return on Equity in percent, calculated for each year as the measure of return. End-of-period measures were used for those parts of the analysis conducted for comparison with previous studies, while the statistics for the tests of Hypotheses 1 and 2 were computed with both end-of-period and beginning-of-period measures.

The absolute difference between ROE at time t and ROE at time t − 1, used as the measure of risk at time t − 1. It does not depend on the estimation of a mean and allows risk taking to be examined in relation to lagged returns within a firm's time series.
time_window: t − 1 relative to the return difference

description: The mean of quadratic differences of ROE over the time period, formed as the sum of the squared year-to-year differences multiplied by 1/(T − 1). Because it does not depend on the estimation of a mean, it equals twice the variance of a time series for a white noise process and leads to meaningful results also in nonstationary series.

Variance of returns was calculated in addition, for comparison with previous results. In the negative association ratio analysis it is the second risk measure beside the mean of quadratic differences.

Each industry was divided at its median ROE into below and above median firms. The split is used for the two-by-two contingency tables of negative association ratios and to compare the correlations between estimated reference points and average returns of firms below and above the industry median.

A firm's individual reference level, taken to be the level of minimal risk. A regression on absolute differences in ROE at time t with quadratic and linear ROE at time t − 1 as independent variables provides a firm-specific estimator (REFr); this posterior estimator is combined with the industry median (IM) as prior in a shrinkage estimator that weights the two by the adjusted proportion of explained variance, REFw = R²·REFr + (1 − R²)·IM. If the fit of the regression is low, or if the estimated term does not indicate a minimum, the industry median is accepted as the estimator.

variable_name: median ROE in the time series
description: The median of a firm's ROE time series, used as the measure of the firm's average return. It was chosen to minimize the influence of outliers in short time series.

Average Return on Equity for a firm within a time period, used as the dependent variable. The whole equation is divided by the standard deviation of returns as a correction for heteroscedasticity, so that average ROE divided by its standard deviation is the dependent variable.
time_window: within each of three time periods, 1971-1982

description: Standard deviation of ROE within a time period, used as the independent variable in the generalized least squares regressions and as the divisor that standardizes the model.

A dummy variable assigned the value 1 if a firm had returns above its estimated reference point at time t and zero otherwise, averaged over the time period. In Model II this variable is multiplied with the standard deviation of returns and added as a multiplicative construct, so that in the standardized form of the model it is entered in its original form.

The total gain associated with the announcement to acquire the target is the difference between the value of the combined firm given the acquisition announcement and the sum of the value of the individual firms if the announcement had not been made. To compute the percentage total gain (TOTGAIN), the value of the combined firm at day t* + 10 is compared with its value in the absence of a takeover, where PREVAL is the value of the acquirer and target firms on day - 11 and k is the proportion of the target's shares purchased by the acquirer. The equations themselves appear in formula blocks that are not readable in the extracted text.

Cumulative abnormal returns to the acquirer estimated with the market model, with market model parameters estimated using return data from day - 70 to day - 11. For single-bid transactions abnormal returns for bidders are cumulated from day - 10 to day + 10; for multiple-bid transactions acquirer CARs are computed over day t' - 10 to day t* + 10, where t' is the day of the first bid by the ultimately successful bidder and t* is the day of announcement of the winning bid.
time_window: day - 70 to day - 11 (estimation); day - 10 to day + 10 or day t' - 10 to day t* + 10 (event window)

description: Proxy for the reverse internalization hypothesis, expected to capture the presence and magnitude of intangible assets in the target firm that are of value in combination with the assets of the bidding firm. The authors state that it is measured as a formula, but the formula appears in a block that is not readable in the extracted text; the source of the underlying accounting data is not stated in prose.

Relative size of the target to the bidder, used in the synergistic acquisitions regression as the measure of the potential to realize gains from asset sharing, i.e., gains from economies of scale and scope. The annual sales of the firms are as reported for the last full financial year prior to the announcement of the acquisition. The defining formula appears in a block that is not readable in the extracted text.
time_window: last full financial year prior to the announcement

description: The same relative size of the target to the bidder variable used in the managerialism subsample, where it acts as a proxy for growth-seeking at the expense of profits and empire building. The authors expected a negative relationship between this variable and both total gains and bidder gains in that subsample.
time_window: last full financial year prior to the announcement

description: Proxy for the market-seeking motive, based on RELGDP, the ratio of the real GDP growth rate in the United States to that in the home country of the acquiring firm. The variable is constructed to allow a slope shift for values of RELGDP below 1 (when the real GDP growth rate in the United States is lower than in the acquirer's home country) versus values above 1 (when growth in the United States is higher and market development may be relevant as a source of value creation). The defining formulas appear in blocks that are not readable in the extracted text.
level: country pair (acquirer home country versus United States)

description: Measure of the financial diversification benefit, computed as the reduction in the variability of returns from combining the two firms: the difference between the variance of the firm after the merger, based on the standard deviations of the U.S. target's and the foreign bidder's stock returns, their market-value weights and the correlation coefficient between their returns, and the variance of the combined firm when the correlation equals one. The absolute value of REDVAR is used in the regressions. The equations appear in blocks that are not readable in the extracted text.

The same measure of the reduction in the variability of the combined firm's returns (the difference between the variance of the merged firm and the variance when the correlation between bidder and target returns equals one), used in the managerialism subsample as the proxy for risk reduction driven by managerial motives. The absolute value of REDVAR is used in the regressions, and the authors predict a negative relationship between this variable and both total gains and bidder gains in that subsample.

variable_name: Project size (dollar amount raised in an equity underwriting)
description: The dollar amount raised in an equity underwriting, taken from SDC reports of the total dollar amount of each underwriting including both the book proceeds and the total value of any overallotment shares sold. Nominal dollar amounts were converted to a constant real value normalizing to 1977 dollars using the consumer price index. Deals are segmented by inflation-discounted dollar volume, with the learning models estimated on all deals in one category and then on increasingly fine equal-sized percentile groups (median split, terciles, quartiles, quintiles).
level: deal, aggregated to bank-year size segments
time_window: 1992-2005 deals, entered with a one-year lag

description: Client evaluations from Greenwich Associates' annual survey of investment banking clients: only those who had worked with a bank in the prior 12 months were asked to evaluate that bank, multiple respondents were surveyed, and each bank was ranked by a minimum of 20 respondents in any given year. Interviewees ranked banks' equity underwriting capabilities on a scale ranging from 1 (poor) to 5 (excellent). Greenwich Associates weights responses (100 for 'excellent', 50 for 'above average', 25 for 'average', 12.5 for 'fair', and 0 for 'poor') and averages them into a composite score for each bank-year ranging from 0 to 100.

Estimated from the gap-closing model rather than observed: the rate is the negative of the regression coefficient on the interaction between the bank's lagged deal volume in a size segment and its lagged capability. It tells the fraction of the gap between a firm's current and potential capabilities that will be closed each time it does a deal in that segment, and is estimated separately for each deal-size segment.

Estimated from the ratio of the coefficient on lagged deal volume in a size segment to the negative of the interaction coefficient between that experience and lagged capability (Cmax = -b1/b2). It tells the maximum amount that continued experience with deals in a particular segment could add to the firm's base capabilities, and is estimated separately for each deal-size segment.

The bank's experience with equity underwriting in a given year, entered lagged, measured as the inflation-discounted dollar volume of deals completed in the prior year and split into size segments (all deals in Model 1, then segments divided at the median and into terciles, quartiles and quintiles). Each size segment's lagged experience enters the model separately, along with its interaction with lagged capability.

PAC receipts collected in the 1979-80 election period by firms that appeared in the Fortune 1,000 industrial and 300 nonindustrial listings for 1980. The source of PAC receipt data was a U.S. Federal Election Commission report on corporate and labor PAC finances.
An index of the amounts of goods, measured in percentages, purchased by the federal government from the outputs of firms' industries. The index came from the Survey of Current Business.

A five-category industrial classification variable used as a proxy for degrees of exposure to governmental regulation. The categories were metals, manufacturing, and mining; construction and housing; food, leisure, and service; finance; and transportation, energy, and communications. Corporations were grouped into industrial classifications on the basis of the Business Week industry classification. Dummy variables were included for all categories except transportation, energy, and communications, which was the omitted industry group.
Assets in 1979, a continuous, firm-specific measure. Forbes (1980) provided data on corporate assets.

A dummy variable with 1 assigned to firms in an industry with a four-firm concentration ratio greater than 50 percent, 0 otherwise. Market concentration information for manufacturing industries came from the 1977 Census of Manufacturers. Because the Department of Commerce only calculates such a measure for manufacturing industries, nonmanufacturing concentration ratios were approximated by comparing the assets and sales of the largest nonmanufacturing Fortune firms to the total assets and sales of all Fortune firms in the corresponding nonmanufacturing industries.
The percent of unionization in firms' industries. Data came from Freeman and Medoff's study estimating private-sector unionism.

A dummy variable that denotes that a CEO was awarded celebrity status, coded 1 or 0 otherwise; the authors describe it as the full sample of award winners. Award data were collected from the comprehensive list in the 'CEO of the year' publication in Financial World magazine between 1986 and 1995. In all cases the acquisition occurred after celebrity had been awarded.
A dummy variable where 1 denotes that the acquisition occurred during the year after the medal was awarded or 0 otherwise. It represents recent award winners, i.e., CEOs with more recent celebrity.
time_window: acquisition year relative to award year

variable_name: Medal in five years prior to acquisition
description: A dummy variable representing longer-term celebrity status where 1 denotes that a CEO had won celebrity status over the previous five years or 0 otherwise. Higher values therefore indicate celebrity status attained less recently.
time_window: five years prior to the acquisition

description: The authors used the announcement-day premium, calculated as the offer price divided by the target's stock price one day before the acquisition public announcement date. Using the announcement-day premium reduces the impact of distracting events without excluding preannouncement anticipation.
time_window: one day before the public announcement date

description: Measured by using buy-and-hold abnormal returns: the individual firm's six-month returns estimated with CRSP minus the industry's returns, computed by summing the monthly returns of the matching Fama and French (1997) 38 industry portfolio for the six months prior to the acquisition announcement. The firm's financial performance relative to aspirations is the individual firm's returns minus the portfolio index returns, and a squared term is used to capture the curvilinear relationship.
time_window: six months prior to the acquisition announcement

description: Sectors and fields of technology in the data bank are grouped according to their technology (R&D) intensity, distinguishing so-called high-tech sectors from medium and low-tech sectors. In the sectoral setting used in the paper, 11 (sub-)fields qualify as high-tech sectors. The authors expect a positive T/M ratio for high-tech industries and a negative sign for the other sectors.

The technology-market ratio is the logarithm base 10 of the ratio between the total number of prevailing research inclined strategic linkages and the total number of predominantly market-related strategic linkages of an alliance category. Zero is a neutral score indicating equal weight for the technology and the market aspects of strategic cooperation; positive values mark an inclination towards 'pure' technology cooperation and negative scores indicate market dominance.
level: sector / field of technology and mode of cooperation (aggregated alliance counts)

description: Each alliance is classified by its organizational mode of cooperation. The authors contrast complex interorganizational modes of cooperation with relatively strong governance — joint ventures, research corporations and minority investment — with contractual arrangements such as joint R&D agreements, technology exchange agreements, customer-supplier relationships and one-directional technology flows.

For each agreement the motives were interpreted with a list of catch words, an extensive inventory based on motives found in the literature and in previous research. 'Perform basic research' is one of these motives and is recorded when performing basic research is indicated as a reason for the cooperative agreement.

Using patent records, each participant firm's specific learning capability was measured as the focal Firm A's citations to partner Firm B's patents divided by the total citations that Firm B received, excluding Firm B's self-citations, in a five-year moving window. Citation data were standardized by the average citation value for all patents in each technical class granted in the same year, then summed over the five years. The authors note that the measure can also be read as the focal firm's share of the partner's knowledge spillovers, or its understanding of the partner's knowledge structure. The final aggregation is presented only as an equation whose rendering is not legible in the text.

After deriving the value of SLC for each firm, the authors took the difference between the focal firm's SLC and the partner's SLC to obtain the SLCG. A positive value indicates that the focal firm's specific learning capability exceeds its partner's.

CAR was calculated with the market model, with the event date set at t = 0 for the alliance announcement date. The market model was estimated from a 255 trading-day estimation period ending 46 trading days before the event date, with the equal-weighted S&P 500 as the market return. Daily firm-level abnormal returns are the difference between actual returns and predicted returns, and CAR sums these abnormal returns over the two-day event window [-1, 0].
time_window: two-day event window [-1, 0]; 255 trading-day estimation period ending 46 trading days before the event

description: Alliances between two firms vary from non-equity-based alliances, in which each firm contributes resources but not investment, to minority-equity alliances and joint ventures where each participant firm claims residual value from its investment. To capture this difference the authors created a continuous variable reflecting the actual percentage of equity in each alliance.
scale: actual percentage of equity in the alliance

description: The authors compared the four-digit SIC codes of the focal firm and its alliance partner to capture how related the two firms are in a similar product domain. Market similarity was coded as '1' when the two firms had exactly the same four SIC codes, as '.75' if the first three SIC codes were the same, as '.5' if the first two codes were the same, as '.25' if the first codes were the same, and as '0' if all four codes differ.
