A dummy variable set to 1 if the firm has two or more alliances, and 0 otherwise. Because its correlation with the count of alliances is very high, it is never included together with that variable in the same model; the estimate reported is for its lagged value.

The running sum of the total number of alliances in which a firm is active, entered together with a squared term to estimate the quadratic relationship. The average number of alliance partnerships across observations is 0.08, with an accumulative count ranging from 0 to 19.

A binary dependent variable capturing the hazard of undergoing a liquidity event, that is, an IPO or an acquisition, in a given firm-year. Because the authors focus on the first outcome event experienced by young firms, there is no potential for repeated hazards; firms without an outcome event by the end of 2002 are right censored and all firms enter the risk pool at founding.

A binary dependent variable capturing the hazard of undergoing an IPO versus an acquisition, estimated on the subsample of firms that experienced a liquidity event. The rate parameter from the prior estimation of having a liquidity event is included to control for selection bias.

The running sum, per year, of the amount of capital raised prior to an IPO, an acquisition, or another outcome event, measured in millions of dollars. It is used as a control and, in Hypothesis 3, interacted with the alliance portfolio dummy; a cumulative mean of capital investment is reported in the text.

A running sum of the number of functional domains (including marketing, manufacturing, and R&D) covered by the alliances in a firm's portfolio; the variable ranges from 0 to 3. Because it correlates highly with the multi-function combination variables, it is not included together with them in any model.

The running average across years of the firm's heterogeneity in distribution of functional alliances, where each year's heterogeneity is the sum of three products; each product consists of one functional type's proportion within the alliance portfolio multiplied by the log of the inverse of that functional type's proportion. Higher values denote greater heterogeneity in distribution of functional alliances.

The running sum of the number of years in which the firm has had a multi-function alliance, equivalent to keeping a running sum of the dummy for multi-function alliances in each year. The average cumulative number of years of having a combo alliance in the sample is 0.02.
The running sum of the actual number of multi-function alliances in each year. The actual average number of these combo alliances in the sample is only 0.03.

The running sum of the number of total functional relationships, regardless of whether they are in single-function or multi-function alliances; its square, Functional relationships (count) squared, is used to estimate the quadratic relationship. In the test of competing Hypotheses 5a and 5b, this variable is interacted with the number of alliances. The average cumulative number of functional relationships held by firms is 0.13.

variable_name: Parenting rate by rank; progeny founder rank
description: In the parent-failure models, the volume of the parent-progeny transfer was captured by the proportion of name partners, regular partners and associates who left to found an offspring firm in a particular year, along with dummy variables for whether a name partner, regular partner or associate left to start a new firm. In the progeny-failure models, it was measured with dummy variables indicating whether the offspring was founded by a former name partner or regular partner, with associate progeny as the reference group. Progeny was defined as a firm with a founder who had been a name partner, partner or associate at another Silicon Valley law firm within the three years prior to founding.
time_window: year of parenting event; founder affiliation within three years prior to founding

description: Four dummy variables captured overlap between the progeny's and parent's practice areas: practicing in up to 25 percent, more than 25 up to 50 percent, more than 50 up to 75 percent, and 75 to 100 percent of the parent firm's practice areas.
The number of years since the occurrence of the most recent parenting event.

variable_name: Proportion of founders with Silicon Valley parents
description: A continuous variable giving the proportion of the founding team with Silicon Valley parents.
Age of the law firm, with the first year listed in the Martindale-Hubbell Law Directory considered the firm's first year.

Size of the parent firm in the progeny-failure models. Firm size was operationalized in two ways: the total number of full-time partners and the total number of full-time associates; because the distribution of firm sizes was log-normal, the log of each size variable was coded.
Age of the parent firm, based on the year in which the firm was first listed in the directory.
A dummy variable coded one if the offspring had more than one Silicon Valley parent, and zero otherwise. Of the 137 progeny, 19 had more than one Silicon Valley parent.

A dichotomous variable coded one in the year the firm was no longer listed or had only one attorney (no longer a partnership); firms had to remain failed for three years to be coded as failed, and at failure the firm was removed from the risk set. In the progeny models, a parent failure dummy was coded one if the parent firm failed within three years preceding the founding of the offspring.
time_window: year of failure; parent failure within three years preceding offspring founding

description: A dichotomous variable coded one in the year the progeny firm was no longer listed or had only one attorney; firms had to remain failed for three years to be coded as failed, and failed firms were removed from the risk set.

Count of years since a firm went public, marked by the year a firm's stock price was first quoted on a U.S. exchange. The square of Public Tenure was also included; all models show a positive effect for public tenure and a negative effect for public tenure squared. Observed ranges of public tenure were 1-40 years for ABSS and 1-38 years for LASS.
time_window: updated annually from the year of going public

description: Coded as 1/(Public Tenure^3). It has its maximum at Public Tenure = 1 and declines quickly thereafter, producing a narrow spike. Results were unchanged using either 1/(Public Tenure^2) or a dummy that identified a firm's first public year.
time_window: updated annually from the year of going public

description: Equaled 1 if a firm's average ROA in years t to t + tau - 1 exceeded a performance benchmark and 0 otherwise. Window widths and benchmarks were set so that a run of high performance was unlikely to arise from randomness, with tau ranging from 7 years in the most dynamic settings to 16 years in the most stable. In these analyses, 15,192 firms were observed for 134,374 firm-years, and 384 firms achieved ABSS.
time_window: forward-looking window of t to t + tau - 1 years

description: Equaled 1 if a firm performed above its industry median in all years from t to t + tau - 1. The tau values needed to rule out above-median randomness ranged from 11 years in the most dynamic settings to 15 years in the most stable. In these analyses, 14,970 firms were observed for 120,022 firm-years, and 1,159 achieved LASS.
time_window: forward-looking window of t to t + tau - 1 years

description: Performance was measured by return on assets (ROA) and return on invested capital (ROIC). In one set of analyses raw values were used and in others deviations from industry-year medians; results were identical in each case, and results reported are for ROA relative to industry-year medians, which reveal relative advantage. Annual ROA is also the dependent variable in the generalized least-squares models of performance inside superior windows.

A time invariant dummy that equaled 1 if a superior window began in the same year a firm went public; it equaled 0 otherwise. Results were unchanged when this dummy identified the first two or the first three years after going public.
time_window: time invariant over a firm's observation period

description: Started at 1 when a firm initially achieved ABSS and increased by 1 each year of a firm's tau-year window. Annual ROA was estimated on the superior window clock, fast superiority and their interaction.

variable_name: Creation matrix (creation field and creation complexity)
description: A firm's creation efforts were modeled using a two-dimensional matrix of 1s and 0s, which recorded how the firm allocated its creation budgets over time. Each column identified a potential creation, and the count of columns equaled the firm's creation field, set by a one-time draw from a Poisson distribution. Within a column, each row identified an actor who needed to cospecialize; creation complexity equaled the number of rows and was constant within an experiment, with experiments run at complexity 3, 4, 6, and 8. If all actors in a column cospecialized (a column of 1s), an opportunity was endogenously created.
time_window: each simulated period, with prepublic cells initialized before t = 1

variable_name: Discovery matrix (discovery field and discovery shock rate)
description: Each simulated firm had a two-row discovery matrix of 1s and 0s, with each column identifying a potential discovery. A cell in the top row was set to 1 when an environmental shock made a discovery technically feasible, and a cell in the bottom row was set to 1 when the firm became alert to that area of its environment; a discovery was activated when both cells in a column equaled 1. The breadth of a firm's discovery field, the count of columns, was set by a Poisson draw, and the discovery shock rate was operationalized as a Poisson draw each year determining how many shocks took place in the firm's discovery field.
time_window: each simulated period, with prepublic columns initialized before t = 1

description: The dependent variable is the number of outside directors without any direct or indirect relationship with the firm, that is, excluding former employees, interlocks, and family members of a director or executive. It is a count of nonnegative integers, which is why a negative binomial model is employed.

Pilot is an indicator variable equal to one for pilot firms and zero for control firms. During denotes the during Reg SHO pilot program period, equal to one for the during Reg SHO period and zero otherwise. The interaction of the two is the difference-in-differences estimator, representing the difference in the number of outside directors between the pilot and control groups in the during Reg SHO period relative to the pre-Reg SHO period.

Measured by the logarithm of the average number of first-degree connections of outside directors through employment, education, and other activities. Because director connections are driven by firm factors, the logged mean of outside directors' connections was regressed on firm size, board size, and firm performance and the residual values were used, following Akbas et al. (2016). The sample was split into two groups using the median value of the variable in 2004.

Measured by the ratio of the number of busy outside directors over the total number of outside directors. An outside director is considered busy if he or she serves on three or more boards, following prior literature. The sample was split into two groups using the median value of the variable in 2004.
Equal to one for CEO chairman duality and zero otherwise. The sample was split into two groups using the median value of the variable in 2004.
Measured as the ratio of executive directors and gray directors on the nomination committee. The sample was split into two groups using the median value of the variable in 2004.

variable_name: CEO Internal Attributions of Positive Firm Performance (CEO Internal Attributions)
description: Coded from the CEO's interview quotes in published news articles during the 3-day window around the firm's quarterly earnings announcement date, when the firm experienced a positive earnings surprise. The authors counted the frequency of words corresponding to each signifier category of internal versus external attributions and computed a variant of the Janis-Fadner coefficient of imbalance, first taking the natural logarithm of the total keyword counts to address skewness in the frequency distribution. The measure is the cumulative sum of CEO internal attributions from the start of a CEO's first year in office to the current quarter t, where ICEO is the total number of internal attribution signifiers and ECEO the equivalent for external attribution signifiers. Positive Earnings Surprise is a dichotomous variable coded as one when the announced earnings exceeded the analyst consensus forecast for the respective quarter or year. The equation itself is not readable in the text.
time_window: 3-day window around the quarterly earnings announcement date; cumulative from the CEO's first year in office to quarter t

variable_name: Analyst Internal Attributions of Negative Firm Performance (Analyst Internal Attributions)
description: Coded from the same corpus of performance attributions, counting the frequency of words corresponding to each signifier category indicating internal versus external attributions in analyst comments captured during the 3-day window of the earnings announcement date. The measure captures the relative degrees of the analysts' internal attributions for negative earnings surprise events throughout the CEO's organizational tenure up to the subsequent quarter t + 1, where IAN is the total number of internal attribution signifiers in the analysts' records and EAN the equivalent for external attribution signifiers. Negative Earnings Surprise is a dichotomous variable coded as one when the earnings fall short of the analyst consensus forecast for the respective quarter or year. The equation itself is not readable in the text.
time_window: 3-day window around the quarterly earnings announcement date; cumulative through quarter t + 1

description: Dichotomous variable coded as one if the CEO was discharged from the leadership position involuntarily in the corresponding company-quarter. Turnover events were first identified from EXECUCOMP and their nature confirmed in multiple news media sources at FACTIVA. Turnover cases were excluded when due to the CEO's sudden death (five cases), when CEOs took a similar position at another firm (five cases), or when the focal firm was acquired (three cases). CEOs older than 64 upon leaving were attributed to retirement, while CEOs under age 64 who did not remain on the board after the succession were classified as dismissals; this coding resulted in 94 CEO dismissal cases out of 255 CEO succession events.

Calendar year-end market value per share divided by calendar year-end book value per share. Calendar year-end book values per share were obtained from Value Line and the corresponding calendar year-end market values per share were drawn from the CRSP data files. The ratio was computed for each firm for the 1978 and 1983 study years.

The difference between Value Line's 5-year-ahead forecast of return on equity and the cost of equity capital. The cost of equity, ke, was estimated from the capital asset pricing model using the Value Line estimate of a firm's beta, the T-bill rate for the year, and the average market risk premium from 1926 to 1981 obtained from Ibbotson (1984).

Value Line's 5-year-ahead forecast of earnings per share growth for each firm. Forecasts were used rather than historical data because both ROE and g in the model denote expected future return on equity and earnings growth rates, respectively.

An index of how likely a covenant not to compete is to be enforced by courts in a state. It is developed in Starr (2016), which applies factor analysis to seven dimensions of enforceability quantified by Bishara (2011) to weight each dimension by how important it is for overall enforceability; the authors state that relative to other indices it is more finely coded and less subjectively weighted. The index is normalized to be mean 0 with a standard deviation of 1, and the 1991 index is used.
scale: continuous index, mean 0 and standard deviation 1

description: A dummy for firm j being a WSO. Spinouts are identified from LEHD employee movements as founding clusters of one or more employees moving from a predecessor establishment to a successor establishment within the same state during a one-year period. Clusters are retained if they have fewer than 20 employees, if the cluster size is at most 50% of employment at the predecessor establishment and at least 75% of employment at the successor establishment, and if the successor establishment is no more than one year old. Firms whose four-digit NAICS code matches that of their parent are WSOs; those with a different code are out-of-industry spinouts, and all remaining firms are other new firms, with the last two groups together called non-WSOs.

The number of new firms of each type (all new firms, WSOs, and other entrants) divided by the number of firms in the state-industry-year. The data are aggregated to the state-industry-year level for these regressions.

variable_name: log of employment in the first year
description: The log of firm employment in the first year of the firm's life (year 0 employment), used as the dependent variable in the initial size regressions. To examine the tails of the distribution, the data are aggregated to the state, year, industry, and new firm type level and the log of the 25th and 75th percentiles of the initial size distribution in each cell are used as dependent variables.
level: firm; state-industry-year-new firm type cell for the percentile regressions

variable_name: log of employment at years 3, 5, and 7
description: The log of firm employment three, five, and seven years after formation, estimated on the sample of firms that survived to those years. A variant of the specification adds log initial employment as a control to compare the growth of firms that start at the same size.

variable_name: survive 1 year / survive 2 years / survive 3 years
description: Dummies for whether the firm survived one, two, and three years, used as dependent variables in the survival regressions, both without and with a control for log initial firm size.

variable_name: mean founder earnings at parent; mean relative earnings
description: Mean earnings of the founders at their parent firm, taken from LEHD earnings records, used as an indicator of founder human capital. The authors also report mean relative earnings, the mean of founder earnings relative to average earnings at the parent in the year-quarter of leaving. The sample for these regressions includes only WSOs and OSOs, i.e., firms for which parent data exist.

Parent firm size is measured in three ways: the log establishment size of the parent, the log number of establishments of the parent, and the size of the founding cluster relative to the parent. The predecessor establishment from which the founding cluster moved is defined as the parent; when there are multiple parent firms the parent is chosen by industry match, cluster size, earliest observation and parent size.
scale: log employment, log count, and a ratio

description: Characteristics of all employees hired between quarters 5 and 12 of the firm's life, collected from the LEHD: age, imputed education, industry experience, and prior earnings. Separate regressions are estimated with each characteristic as the dependent variable, using the authors' preferred specification without initial size controls.
time_window: quarters 5 to 12 of the firm's life

description: A reflective measure of market orientation drawn from extant research, composed as a summated index of the items that constitute the scale, with equal weights given to each item. The construct comprises three dimensional scales: customer orientation, competitor orientation and interfunctional coordination. It was assessed by a marketing executive in each firm as part of the survey.

A reflective summated scale composed of three dimensional scales: information generation, information dissemination and shared interpretation. All reflective measures of market orientation and MIP were drawn from extant research except for the shared interpretation scale, which was developed based primarily on Huber (1991). Each scale was composed as a summated index of its items with equal weights, and responses came from a marketing executive in each firm.

A reflective measure of the firm's propensity to act based on knowledge gained, composed as a summated index of the items that constitute the scale with equal weights given to each item. It is one of the latent constructs in the measurement model and was assessed by a marketing executive in each firm.

Three objective formative indicators (ROI, ROA, and ROE) obtained via Compustat and annual reports were used to assess performance in time t + 1. These measures were taken 1 year after the survey. The same indicators measured in time period t are included as a control variable.
time_window: time period t + 1 (one year after the survey)

description: Density of communication ties within each firm's block of employees, calculated at four-month intervals for the acquiring firm and the target firm separately. For the dichotomized data, the density for each block equals the number of actual ties divided by the number of potential ties; for the continuous-valued data, block density equals the average cell value within that block.
time_window: June 2002 to February 2005, at four-month intervals

description: Density of communication ties between the acquiring firm's block of employees and the target firm's block of employees, calculated at four-month intervals. For the dichotomized data, density for each block equals the number of actual ties divided by the number of potential ties; for the continuous-valued data, block density equals the average cell value within that block.
time_window: June 2002 to February 2005, at four-month intervals

description: The dependent variable in the dyadic QAP regressions is the natural log of one plus the number of e-mails exchanged between a pair of workers in a given time period; the relevant data for the e-mail matrices were log transformed. The analysis covers 83,232 potential dyadic interactions per month (diagonals ignored). The equation blocks printed in the text are partially unreadable in this rendering.
time_window: each four-month time period from t0 + 3 to t0 + 35

description: Time equals t0 + n, where t0 is the month in which the acquisition was announced and n equals the number of months after the acquisition. The individual-level models regress each centrality measure on the time period and on the square of the time period; a second specification uses the natural log of the time period, but the rendered equation for it is unreadable in the text.

Betweenness represents the number of times that a worker is positioned along the shortest path (geodesic) between other pairs of workers; each geodesic is weighted by the inverse of the number of geodesics connecting the pair. Isolates were removed from the networks before the measures were calculated and the centrality measures were normalized to account for differences in network size. Average centrality measures for acquiring and target workers were plotted over time and then modeled with random- and fixed-effects models.

Communication efficiency is measured by closeness centrality and reach centrality. A worker's farness is the sum of the geodesic distances to or from all other workers and a worker's closeness is the sum of the reciprocated distances, so a worker who is close to others can communicate in fewer steps. Reach centrality (step = n) represents the percentage of workers that the focal worker can reach in n steps, with step = 1 expressing the worker's number of direct connections as a percentage of possible direct connections. Isolates were removed and the measures were normalized for network size before the models were estimated.

Common knowledge base was operationalized as those workers with the same job title; workers with the same job title (e.g., chemist, accountant) likely come from the same profession or occupational community and have been through similar training. In the dyadic QAP regressions the key term is being in a different firm interacted with having the same job title. Job titles for target firm employees were assigned by the acquiring firm.

Task interdependence was operationalized as those workers in the same job group. Job groups are classifications determined by firm management but are not part of management's hierarchical structure; they are not departments or divisions and tend to include workers with different job titles. The nature of work within job groups at the sample firm tended to be reciprocally interdependent, and the key term in the QAP regressions interacts being in a different firm with being in the same job group.

An indicator in the dyadic QAP regressions for whether the two workers in a pair belong to different firms — one employee from the acquiring firm and one from the target firm. The authors describe the key variable as being in a different firm but in the same job group and compare it with being in the same firm, which also leads to more communication.

variable_name: proportion of insiders appointed before the CEO
description: The proportion of inside directors other than the CEO who obtained their board seats at any time prior to the current CEO's arrival. Insider status was coded from Standard & Poor's Register of Corporations, Directors, and Executives based on the publication's indication of insider status, and family members were also considered to be insiders. All independent variables and controls are lagged.
time_window: lagged relative to the outcome year

description: Binary variable coded '1' if a CEO is also the board chair and '0' otherwise. It is one of three measures the authors use to capture CEO power, and it is described as one of the most widely used measures of CEO power, alleged to increase the CEO's ability to control board agendas.
time_window: lagged relative to the outcome year

description: Relative measure of CEO stock ownership calculated as the number of outstanding shares held by the CEO divided by the total number of outstanding shares held by all board members. A relative measure is used because stock is also an important source of power for directors, and high levels of CEO stock ownership directly afford CEOs power through enhanced voting rights.
time_window: lagged relative to the outcome year

description: Binary variable coded '1' if a CEO had a background in finance and '0' otherwise, determined using Forbes' annual CEO Compensation survey. It is used as a measure of CEO power because financial expertise is particularly critical for evaluation of firm performance.
time_window: lagged relative to the outcome year

description: Dichotomous variable coded '1' in a given year if the number of inside directors decreased from two or more insiders to only one insider (the CEO) and '0' otherwise. Transitions to the CEO-only insider structure were considered from 1981 to 2007 and coded from Standard & Poor's Register of Corporations, Directors, and Executives, and family members were also considered insiders. To avoid short-term perturbations, a firm was considered as having a CEO-only structure only if that structure lasted for more than two years. Firms are at risk of adopting the structure only if they have at least one insider on the board in addition to the CEO for at least one year, and the measure was treated as a repeatable event; 144 events were observed within the 2,918 firm-years.

Binary period variable coded '1' for the years 2003 and thereafter and '0' for the years predating SOX, after the law came into force. To test the elaboration of SOX, the authors include a variable interacting the SOX variable with the functional (finance) background of the CEO.
Coded as the difference in the firm's industry-adjusted return on assets (ROA) in the two prior years. The authors include interactions between this variable and each of their three power indicators.

A binary variable equal to 1 if (1) year is greater or equal to 1996, (2) the company has a staggered board, and (3) the company is incorporated in Delaware; and 0 otherwise. 1996 indicates the watershed year when Delaware-based companies experienced enhanced legal protection from takeovers. The state of incorporation and the presence of staggered board provisions are determined via Gompers, Ishii, and Metrick (2003) measures constructed using the Investor Responsibility Research Center (IRRC) data on corporate governance.

The main dependent variable measures overall corporate attention to stakeholders and is constructed by aggregating the strengths across the five selected KLD dimensions (community, minorities, employees, the natural environment, and customers) to obtain a score of total strengths. Because 53 percent of the scores take the value of 0 or 1, the variable is binary, equal to 1 if the firm has been rated as having at least one strength across the five dimensions considered, and 0 otherwise.

The measure of overall corporate attention to stakeholders is disaggregated into five additional dependent variables, each measuring corporate attention to a different stakeholder. For each stakeholder, a binary dependent variable is used, equal to 1 if the score is greater or equal to 1, and 0 otherwise.

The measure of overall corporate attention to stakeholders is disaggregated into five additional dependent variables, each measuring corporate attention to a different stakeholder. For each stakeholder, a binary dependent variable is used, equal to 1 if the score is greater or equal to 1, and 0 otherwise.

The measure of overall corporate attention to stakeholders is disaggregated into five additional dependent variables, each measuring corporate attention to a different stakeholder. For each stakeholder, a binary dependent variable is used, equal to 1 if the score is greater or equal to 1, and 0 otherwise.

The measure of overall corporate attention to stakeholders is disaggregated into five additional dependent variables, each measuring corporate attention to a different stakeholder. For each stakeholder, a binary dependent variable is used, equal to 1 if the score is greater or equal to 1, and 0 otherwise.

The measure of overall corporate attention to stakeholders is disaggregated into five additional dependent variables, each measuring corporate attention to a different stakeholder. For each stakeholder, a binary dependent variable is used, equal to 1 if the score is greater or equal to 1, and 0 otherwise.

M/B is measured as the sum of market value of equity and book value of debt divided by the book value of assets. The measure equals the ratio of the firm's market value (equity plus debt) to the replacement cost of its physical assets (book value of assets), and is high when the firm has valuable intangible assets in addition to physical capital. It is used to calculate shareholder value in the short term (one year into the future: MBt+1) and in the long term (two and three years into the future: MBt+2, and MBt+3).
time_window: one, two and three years into the future (t+1, t+2, t+3)

description: Measured using the Open Language Chief Executive Personality Tool (OLCPT), which applies open-language machine learning to CEOs' spoken language in the question-and-answer portion of quarterly earnings calls with equity analysts. Scores estimate the CEO's observed FFM conscientiousness on a 7-point scale, where 1 corresponds to low values and 7 corresponds to high values of the trait.
time_window: Sample period 1993-2015; multiple Q&A sessions consolidated

description: Measured using the Open Language Chief Executive Personality Tool (OLCPT), which applies open-language machine learning to CEOs' spoken language in the question-and-answer portion of quarterly earnings calls with equity analysts. Scores estimate the CEO's observed FFM neuroticism on a 7-point scale, where 1 corresponds to low values and 7 corresponds to high values of the trait.
time_window: Sample period 1993-2015; multiple Q&A sessions consolidated

description: Measured using the Open Language Chief Executive Personality Tool (OLCPT), which applies open-language machine learning to CEOs' spoken language in the question-and-answer portion of quarterly earnings calls with equity analysts. Scores estimate the CEO's observed FFM extraversion on a 7-point scale, where 1 corresponds to low values and 7 corresponds to high values of the trait.
time_window: Sample period 1993-2015; multiple Q&A sessions consolidated

description: Systematic risk, βi, estimated from the formula Rit = α + βiRmt + eit, where Rit is the rate of return for stock i during period t and Rmt is the market rate of return during the same period. The formula was estimated using one year of daily stock return data.
time_window: one year of daily stock return data

description: Calculated as the change in share price from the beginning to the end of the fiscal year plus dividends, divided by the beginning share price.

Firm i's sales in industry j, averaged over the time period under analysis. All size measures are logged in order to test the linear relationship between size and flexibility, and the size measures are adjusted for inflation using the Consumer Price Index. In the appendix the variable is described as the log of sales of firm i in industry j.

Fluctuation in firm output is defined as the standard deviation of annual sales during the time period under analysis. SVij is the standard deviation of sales (log sales in the appendix description) for firm i in industry j. The authors note that other measures of flexibility could be used, such as the sales deviation from a trend line, but limited year points persuaded them to use simply standard deviation.

Return on assets divided by risk, where risk is measured as the variance of returns during the investigated time period, to create a risk-adjusted measure of return. Firm size, output flexibility and their interaction are regressed on this risk-adjusted performance measure within each of the eighty-three industries.

Return on sales divided by risk, where risk is measured as the variance of returns during the investigated time period, to create a risk-adjusted measure of return. Together with risk-adjusted ROA it is one of the two performance measures on which firm size, output flexibility and their interaction are regressed within each industry.

Industry volatility is operationalized as the standard deviation of total industry annual sales during the time period under analysis, denoted ISVj for industry j. It is used as an explanatory variable for the industry-level slope coefficient bj of the firm size-output fluctuation regression.
Capital intensity for industry j was calculated as the ratio of assets over sales. It is used as an explanatory variable for the industry-level slope coefficient bj.
Industry average profit was calculated as the ratio of return over sales. It is used as an explanatory variable for the industry-level slope coefficient bj.

Binary variable coded 1 for a breakthrough innovation. Built from the patents citing the original patent, excluding self-citations, within 10 years of the original patent's application date, so that every original patent has an equal citation window. Original patents were sorted by the number of citations received and the top 2 percent of the sample were identified as breakthrough innovations.
time_window: 10 years from the original patent's application date

variable_name: technologically distant knowledge of national origin
description: Number of cited patents of the original patent that (a) were assigned to a technology class outside the five classes comprising the biotechnology industry, reflecting technological distance, and (b) whose inventor location was the United States, pointing to national origin. Information on inventor location and technology class was taken from the patent document. Self-citations were excluded.

variable_name: technologically proximate knowledge of international origin
description: Number of cited patents of the original patent that (a) were assigned to a technology class within the biotechnology industry, reflecting technological proximity, and (b) whose inventor location was outside the United States, indicating international origin. Self-citations were excluded.

variable_name: technologically distant knowledge of international origin
description: Number of cited patents of the original patent that (a) were assigned to a technology class outside the five classes comprising the biotechnology industry, reflecting technological distance, and (b) whose inventor location was outside the United States, pointing to international origin. Self-citations were excluded.

Standardized cumulative abnormal returns for the 3-day event window, calculated with the market model using the CRSP equally weighted market index to represent the market return for each day in the estimation and event periods. The triggering event is the first trading day following shipment of the magazines, and the event window extends through 3 trading days. Firms with potentially confounding stories published in the Wall Street Journal were deleted for the day the article was published as well as the prior day and subsequent day.

Firms were classified according to whether their boards were listed among the 25 'best' or the 25 'worst' boards of directors of publicly traded U.S. corporations in Business Week's 1996 and 1997 cover stories. The lists were based on a Board Performance Poll sent to governance experts and a Governance Guideline Analysis using aggregated data from publicly available data sources, combined into an overall rating of the board from which ordered rankings were derived. Complete data were available for 50 of the 'best' and 49 of the 'worst' listings included in the two reports.

variable_name: Mean Survey Score (mean of the expert rating variables)
description: Raters, primarily professional investors who managed portfolios worth $1.6 trillion in 1996 and $2 trillion in 1997, identified the public corporations whose boards they considered most and least effective and graded the boards on a scale of 0 (poor) to 10 (excellent) for four categories: accountability to shareholders, quality of directors, independence, and corporate performance. The scores were then aggregated into an overall Survey Score. To correct for the multicollinearity present among the expert ratings variables, the mean of the variables was used as an overall subjective rating of the board, and a regression using the shareholder accountability rating as the expert rating was also reported.

variable_name: Mean Governance Analysis Score (mean of the Business Week objective scores)
description: Objective ratings created from indicators of 'best practices' articulated by a group of governance experts, in three measures corresponding to three of the survey categories: Independence (inside directors; insiders on audit, nominating or compensation committees; outside directors with consulting or legal contracts with the company; board interlocks), Board Quality (directors' total board memberships; at least one outsider with experience in the firm's core business; at least one CEO of a firm of similar stature), and Accountability to Shareholders (director stock ownership; no director pension plan; unclassified board). Objective scores were combined into a summary Governance Guideline Score; because information necessary to decompose the scores was not made available in the articles, the authors also collected all directors' insider status, tenure, and total number of boards from the listed firms' proxy statements.

The authors measured geographic distribution using the Blau index of diversity (Blau, 1977), where p is the proportion of a firm's patents granted in the previous year to inventors at location i and N is the number of locations of the firm; the equation block itself is not readable in the available text. Locations were identified at the regional level in the United States and at the country level elsewhere, and R&D, pilot, and manufacturing fabrication facility locations from SEMI were cross-checked against R&D activity locations derived from individual researcher addresses in the USPTO data. The measure was computed for year t when the dependent variable was measured for year t + 1, and its value is contingent on the number of locations.
time_window: year t, with the dependent variable measured at t + 1

description: The authors measured the Blau index for technology diversity as one minus the sum of the squares of the proportion of a firm's innovative activities across i technology domains for a given year. Technology domains were taken from the main three-digit technology domain the USPTO assigned to the invention on the front page of each patent. A value of 0.05 indicated a high level of technological focus and a value of 0.95 indicated a high level of technological diversity. Technological diversity was measured for year t when the dependent variable was measured for year t + 1.
time_window: year t, with the dependent variable measured at t + 1

description: Measured as the fraction of a firm's patents that were coauthored by scientists from different locations of the firm in year t, thus capturing the degree to which active researchers in the firm's overall population had ties across locations. Researcher location was the inventor's home address, measured at the regional level in the United States and the country level elsewhere, and duplicate observations (patents coauthored by the exact same set of scientists at the same locations) were dropped. The measure takes values between 0 and 1: 0 indicates that a firm's active researchers have worked independently and formed no ties outside their own locations, and 1 indicates that all active researchers are engaged in interlocation collaboration and have at least one tie with another individual in a distant unit.
time_window: year t, with knowledge transfer between units in year t + 1

description: Quality of innovation is the impact of the firm's innovation output, measured as the sum of the number of citations that each of the firm's patents had received; it is a firm-year variable measuring the number of granted patents applied for in a particular year weighted by the number of citations each patent received. Weighting each firm patent by its citations allows different values to be placed on different patents in a firm's patent portfolio. To avoid truncation bias the authors chose a window of five years from the application date for a patent. Data were drawn from the first page of patents, which records the prior art on which the patent built.
time_window: five years from the patent application date; firm year t + 1

description: A dyadic measure that takes on a value of 1 if a VC firm invested in both firms within the three years prior to the date of the focal alliance, and 0 otherwise. Because firms might share more than one VC, the authors also measured the variable using the count of the VCs the two firms shared at the time of the partner selection decision.
time_window: three years prior to the focal alliance

description: Takes on a value of 1 for realized alliances and zero for dyads of nonrealized transactions. Nonrealized dyads were constructed for a given realized alliance dyad by considering all firms from the universe of VC-backed firms present in the biopharmaceutical industry at the time of the focal realized alliance dyad.

A dummy variable that is equal to 1 if there is at least one drug application approved by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration agency for the focal firm at the time of the R&D collaboration, and 0 otherwise. Given that firms' products reflect their progress in product development, the variable captures the firm's stage of product development.

A dummy variable that is equal to 1 if there is at least one drug application approved by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration agency for the partner firm at the time of the R&D collaboration, and 0 otherwise. Given that firms' products reflect their progress in product development, the variable captures the partner's stage of product development.
The number of alliances between the firms during the five years prior to the focal alliance. The authors also measured this variable for different time windows such as three years and seven years.
time_window: five years prior to the focal alliance

description: The number of patent cross-citations between a firm and its potential partner during the five years prior to the date of the focal alliance. The authors also measured this variable for different time windows such as three years and seven years.
time_window: five years prior to the focal alliance

description: The cosine of the angular separation in firms' patents across patent classes. Following Jaffe (1986), the authors calculated this measure as the normalized scalar product of the patent class distribution vectors of firms in a dyad during the last five years prior to the focal alliance; they also measured it for different time windows such as three years and seven years.
time_window: last five years prior to the focal alliance

description: For each inventor–patent observation, the authors retrieve the three-digit technology classes of all prior patents of the focal inventor and identify whether there is any overlap with the three-digit technology classes of the focal patent. Exploring new fields is a binary indicator that equals one in the absence of any overlapping class between all prior patents and the focal patent. All classes assigned to a patent are used rather than just the primary class.

The logarithmic transformation of one plus the number of pairwise subclass combinations of a patent that appear for the first time in the U.S. patent database. Each pairwise combination of subclasses is compared with all pairwise combinations of all prior U.S. patents. This is the authors' measure for the novelty of the patent.
scale: count, natural logarithm after adding one

description: The logarithmic transformation of one plus the number of times a patent is referenced as prior art within 10 years. Forward citations are positively correlated with the private economic value of a patent, maintenance fee payments, and the market value of the assigned company. This is the authors' measure for the value of the patent.
scale: count, natural logarithm after adding one

description: For each inventor–patent observation, the authors identify whether there is any overlap between the three-digit technology classes of the focal patent and the three-digit technology classes linked to all prior patents of the coinventors on the patent, excluding the focal inventor. Expert team is a binary indicator that equals one if at least one of the coinventors has a prior patent in the same class(es) as the focal patent. The measure is used as a moderator in the value models.

Science is a binary indicator that equals one if the focal patent cites nonpatent prior art, which are typically scientific publications. The authors rely on a supervised machine-learning approach to identify citations to scientific publications. Such citations indicate an awareness of the inventor of the cited articles; the measure is used as a moderator in the value models.

The same binary indicator, equal to one in the absence of any overlapping three-digit technology class between all prior patents of the focal inventor and the focal patent, calculated for the first patent of an inventor after moving between two firms within the same state. It is the endogenous variable instrumented by the interaction of Michigan residence and post-MARA timing in the 2SLS models.

The logarithmic transformation of one plus the number of pairwise subclass combinations of a patent that appear for the first time in the U.S. patent database, used as the novelty outcome in the MARA sample. Each pairwise combination of subclasses is compared with all pairwise combinations of all prior U.S. patents.
scale: count, natural logarithm after adding one

description: The logarithmic transformation of one plus the number of times a patent is referenced as prior art within 10 years, used as the value outcome in the MARA sample. Forward citations are positively correlated with the private economic value of a patent.
scale: count, natural logarithm after adding one

description: Binary indicator equal to one if at least one coinventor on the focal patent has a prior patent in the same three-digit technology class(es) as the focal patent, used as a moderator in the value models estimated on the MARA sample.

Binary indicator equal to one if the focal patent cites nonpatent prior art, typically scientific publications, identified with a supervised machine-learning approach, used as a moderator in the value models estimated on the MARA sample.

variable_name: managerial ownership (percentage of equity owned by the top management team)
description: The percentage of equity owned by the top management team. The percentage of shares owned by each member of the top management team for each year was obtained from Execucomp, and these were summed by year to form a total measure of TMT managerial ownership.

International diversification is measured using the entropy measure, which captures both the number of geographic segments as well as the weight of each segment relative to the firm's sales. Data for the diversification measures were obtained from the Compustat Segments database.
Business diversification is measured using the entropy measure over business segments. Data for the diversification measures were obtained from the Compustat Segments database.

A continuous variable measured as the inverse of a normalized Herfindahl index capturing the diversity of unique patent classes at year t based on patents applied for in the past five years. Sr is the share of patent class r in firm i's patent classes and N is the number of distinct patent classes; the measure ranges between 0 and 1. Observations with fewer than two patents were assumed to be balanced and assigned a value of 0.5. Patent classes (rather than subclasses) are used to ensure that the knowledge domains entered are new to the firm.
time_window: patents applied for in the five years ending at year t

description: An inverse Herfindahl index capturing the annual diversity of patent classes of the firm's alliance partners, considering all the patents applied for by each partner in the past five years ending at year t − 1. The index is averaged across the firm's partners that formed an alliance with the firm during this five-year window, and records are pooled across all alliances in a firm-year.
time_window: past five years ending at year t − 1

description: An inverse Herfindahl index relating to the average annual diversity of patent classes of the firm's five primary competitors with the highest Jaffe score for patent class overlap in year t − 1. Records are pooled across the firm's five primary competitors.

Measured as the difference between the standardized monthly volatility of the firm's stock price and the average standardized monthly volatility in the stock prices of all sampled firms that year, so that only uncertainty idiosyncratic to the firm is captured. Volatility is the standard deviation in monthly closing stock price divided by its mean value, where piT is firm i's stock closing price at the end of month T (January to December) and pmT is the average closing price of the sampled firms' stocks at the end of month T.
Measured in year t − 1 by calculating the variance in the partner exploration variable, thus capturing the variance in the exploration tendencies of the firm's alliance partners.
Measured in year t − 1 by calculating the variance in the competitor exploration variable, thus capturing the variance in the exploration tendencies of the firm's five primary competitors.

Measured with the Jaffe (1986) proximity measure, where Fi and Fj are vectors representing the knowledge domains of firm i and partner j based on classes of patents applied for during a five-year window. To compute the technological proximity to partners, this measure is averaged across the firm's partners in each year.
Calculated using the average Jaffe (1986) proximity measure corresponding to the firm's five primary competitors, based on vectors of the patent classes they applied for during a five-year window.

The average value of the six Worldwide Governance Indicators developed by the World Bank Group for the subsidiary's host country in a given year. The six indicators are highly correlated, so their average value is used to measure a country's overall quality of institutions. The indicators are reported annually and many countries show significant governance changes over time.

A dummy variable that equals 1 if a subsidiary is supervised by a supervisory unit in the same host country as opposed to a supervisory unit in a different country. For each subsidiary the supervisory unit was identified based on the corporate hierarchy reported in DCA, which describes reporting/supervision relationships to the seventh level of corporate linkage. Because the construct is cross-border supervision, higher values of this variable indicate lower cross-border supervision.

For each subsidiary, the number of same-MNC subsidiaries (in or outside the United States) whose primary segments have significant input-output flows to and from the focal subsidiary's primary segment, divided by the number of all subsidiaries of the same MNC parent. For each MNC-year an N x N task matrix is constructed in which entries are set to one when two subsidiaries' primary segments on average contribute more than 1% of the input to one another according to the BEA input-output tables; task centrality is the number of such entries in the subsidiary's row divided by N.
time_window: subsidiary-year within the MNC-year task matrix

variable_name: Alliance portfolio concentration across geographic units
description: Operationalized with the Gini coefficient, which measures inequality among values of a frequency distribution. The measure only includes subsidiaries with operational alliances. A value of 0 means alliances are equally dispersed across the subsidiaries that engage in alliance activities, whereas a value of 1 indicates that alliances are concentrated in one subsidiary.

Measured as the sum of all operational alliances of the firm. Because the distribution of the number of alliances is highly skewed, a logarithmic transformation is applied. Alliances are linked to the subsidiary that formed them and counted per subsidiary per year, with alliances of acquired subsidiaries added to the total number of alliances of the firm.

Calculated by dividing the income before extraordinary items by the total sales. Net profit margin is analyzed at t + 1, while all explanatory variables are lagged 1 year (i.e., at time t). A financial performance indicator was chosen instead of an innovation performance indicator because the authors aim to highlight knowledge as a strategically significant resource and include manufacturing, marketing, and R&D alliances.

Recipients were asked whether the marketing and production process skills they possessed matched those required to produce and sell the product for which know-how was being sourced and whether they required marketing, management, and other technical assistance to implement the technology contributed by the transferor. Factor analysis with orthogonal rotation yielded one factor with an eigenvalue greater than 1 accounting for 86% of total variance; the last three of the five items loaded above 0.50 and were retained for the main analyses. The ordinal alpha for the three items was 0.81.

Recipients indicated the size of investment that was made specifically to implement the know-how and, thus, could not be easily redeployed for other uses. The variable was coded in five bands: 1 for specific investments of less than 10 million U.S. dollars, 2 for investments between 10 and 45 million, 3 for investments between 45 and 110 million, 4 for investments between 110 and 220 million, and 5 for those above 220 million.

Two five-point Likert-type items ranging from strongly disagree to strongly agree, adapted from Simonin (1999), capturing the extent of overlap in the transferor's and recipient's organizational routines and culture. The scale has an ordinal alpha of 0.93 and both standardized item loadings exceeded 0.80.
scale: five-point Likert-type (strongly disagree to strongly agree)

description: A binary variable representing the mode of know-how transfer; it took the value 1 when know-how was transferred via joint venture and 0 when it was through a licensing agreement. The authors note it picks up whether the know-how transfer was within-firm or to an unaffiliated party.

variable_name: Alter Firm Alignment to Focal Firm Core Technology Trajectory
description: For each focal firm-year, the core technology area is the primary USPC that appears most frequently on patent applications submitted by the firm in the observation year. A vector measure of the global technology trajectory of this patent classification is calculated by observing all patents listing this USPC and identifying all other USPC codes co-listed with it, with magnitudes given by the count of patents combining each code with the focal technology. For each alter firm, its trajectory in the focal firm's core technology is constructed from how it combines other knowledge elements with that technology. The Euclidean distance between the alter firm's trajectory and the global trajectory is calculated, and a linear transformation turns this distance into a relatedness measure ranging from 1 to 0.
time_window: one-year lag (e.g., observed in 2003 for firm A's core technology in 2004)

variable_name: Alter Firm Patent Assertions in Focal Firm Core Technology Area
description: The number of court cases filed by the alter firm that reference a patent with its primary USPC code matching the core technology area of the focal firm. A one-year lag is used, with litigation filed in year t-1 observed to impact interlock formation in year t.

Interlock tie formation is the selection of a new director to the board of the focal firm who holds a previously established position as a director on the board of the alter firm. The measure observes new ties formed during 2002-2006, controlling for interlock ties that existed in the prior year, and requires that the new director maintains his or her membership on the alter firm's board. In tests of downstream outcomes, board interlocks present at time t-1 predict litigation or alliance ties at time t.
scale: binary (1 if interlock tie formed/exists, 0 otherwise)

description: A network-based variable constructed for each observation year as a sociomatrix in which the firm listed in the jth column is the potential plaintiff and the firm listed in the ith row is the potential defendant. The xij location is coded 1 for years in which a U.S. Federal Court patent infringement case was filed corresponding to this plaintiff-defendant pair, and 0 otherwise. Board interlocks present at time t-1 predict the formation of these litigation ties at time t.
time_window: each observation year 2002-2006; t-1 predictor for interlock

description: The count of R&D alliances announced between sample firms in the year of observation, drawn from SDC Platinum. In the dyad-year panel analysis, the outcome is treated as a binary measure equaling 1 if the dyad firms form an alliance in the observation year and 0 otherwise.

A four-item scale developed for this study, not included in the q-sorting exercise but resulting from discussions with a sourcing expert. The items specifically represent the extent to which the service provider's compensation and business opportunities are tied to performance against contractual service level agreements, and are worded in a vernacular familiar to respondents; all items relate to the SLAs that exist within the contract between the two organizations. Measured from the provider's survey.

A composite of four items reflecting the reliance upon committed and cooperative relations to govern the commercial exchange, drawing on multiple previously validated scales. Validity and reliability were assessed in the provider confirmatory factor analysis. Measured from the provider's survey.

Modeled as a meta-construct (higher order construct) reflecting two first-order constructs, shirking and poaching. The second-order structure was empirically validated by strong second-order factor loadings and a Marsh and Hocevar target coefficient equaling 0.994. The opportunism questions were measured from the service provider's own respondents using an indirect questioning technique to mitigate social desirability bias.

A newly developed four-item scale measuring the extent to which the provider deliberately underperforms or withholds resources when the customer is unable to detect the action. Items were developed and refined through a multiround q-sorting exercise involving academic peers and experienced sourcing professionals, with each item matched with its intended construct at an acceptable rate by the final round. Measured from the provider's survey.

A newly developed three-item scale measuring the degree to which the provider is inclined to utilize information obtained through the relationship for its own unauthorized benefit. Items were developed and refined through the same multiround q-sorting exercise as the shirking items. Measured from the provider's survey.

Based on Hofstede's individualism-collectivism cultural dimension scores, obtained from geerthofstede.nl in December 2011. The questionnaire presented the respondent with a listing of countries and asked him/her to indicate all countries where the provider had operations servicing the focal relationship; this information was combined with the culture score for each country to arrive at an average relationship score. The scores are with respect to the location of the service provider's operations.
level: outsourcing relationship (average of provider country scores)

description: Based on Hofstede's uncertainty avoidance cultural dimension scores, obtained from geerthofstede.nl in December 2011. Respondents were asked to indicate all countries where the provider had operations servicing the focal relationship, and this information was combined with the culture score for each country to arrive at an average relationship score. The scores are with respect to the location of the service provider's operations.
level: outsourcing relationship (average of provider country scores)

description: Composite questionnaire scale measuring the use of rational processes in the focal strategic decision, answered by an executive closely involved in making the decision. The measures were reoperationalized on the basis of the first stage so as to be more applicable to the Egyptian context, and were checked for reliability and validity. Alpha coefficients for all scales range between 0.72 and 0.92, and the instruments met the convergent and discriminant validity criteria. Individual items are not reported; the authors state that details of operationalization and original sources are available from the first author.

Composite questionnaire scale measuring the use of intuition in the focal strategic decision. The authors state that the present study assessed intuition through Khatri and Ng's measures, reoperationalized for the Egyptian context after the first stage. Alpha coefficients for all scales range between 0.72 and 0.92.

Composite questionnaire scale measuring political behavior in the focal strategic decision. On the basis of previous research and the first-stage interviews, the item 'openness about interests' - which loaded significantly on both political behavior and rationality - was included in the composite measure of political behavior. Alpha coefficients for all scales range between 0.72 and 0.92.

Perceptual questionnaire measure of the effectiveness of the focal strategic decision, answered by an executive closely involved in making the decision. The strategic decision, not the organization, is the unit of analysis, which provides a close link between the decision-making process and its outcome. The authors acknowledge that the perceptual measures employed may not truly reflect the phenomenon of interest, so the results should be interpreted with caution.

Composite questionnaire scale for the importance of the focal decision; its alpha coefficient was 0.63, the only scale outside the 0.72 to 0.92 range. The item 'time pressure', which should theoretically load on decision motive, loaded significantly on decision importance instead. The authors note that the high average level of importance of the decisions in the study may have limited the variation available.

Composite questionnaire scale for the uncertainty attaching to the specific strategic decision. The items 'confidence in making the right choice' and 'clarity of goals', which should in theory load on decision uncertainty, actually loaded significantly on decision motive. The authors suggest this unexpected result may be due to the effect of culture and requires more research.

Composite questionnaire scale capturing whether the decision was framed by decision makers as a crisis or as an opportunity. The items 'confidence in making the right choice' and 'clarity of goals' loaded significantly on this factor although they were expected to load on decision uncertainty. Alpha coefficients for all scales range between 0.72 and 0.92.

Composite questionnaire scale for uncertainty in the firm's external environment, entered as one of the broader contextual variables in the models. Alpha coefficients for all scales range between 0.72 and 0.92. Individual items are not reported; operationalization details are available from the first author.

Composite questionnaire scale for environmental hostility versus munificence, entered in the moderated regression models as the environmental hostility variable. For the subsample analysis the sample was median split into low- and high-munificence groups and correlations with strategic decision effectiveness were compared. The Egyptian economy during the study period was described as a hostile environment.

Perceptual questionnaire measure of how the firm performs in comparison to companies similar in size and industry, covering financial as well as nonfinancial indicators. It was entered as one of the broader contextual variables and as a moderator; for the subsample analysis the sample was median split into high- and low-performance groups.

Company size as reported in the questionnaire, entered as one of the broader contextual variables and examined as a moderator of the process-effectiveness relationships. All firms in the target population employed more than 100 people. The paper does not report the specific items used; operationalization details are available from the first author.

variable_name: four-year moving average of at-large invitations
description: The number of times a school had been invited to participate in the NCAA postseason tournament in the previous four years, calculated as a four-year moving average. The authors used the variable to capture historical legacy as a cumulative status benefit that is independent of current-year performance.

A dichotomous measure, with 1 indicating that the school had received an at-large invitation to the NCAA postseason tournament in the most recent prior year and 0 otherwise. It captures a more recent historical legacy than the four-year moving average.

The number of games a team played against teams that had been invited to the prior year's NCAA postseason tournament; the variable ranged from 0 to 17 games. The authors view opponents' prior invitation histories as capturing status rather than quality because opponents' win/lose records were controlled in all analyses, and the measure excludes invitations guaranteed by performance, such as placing first in one's conference.

variable_name: winning percentage against prior-year NCAA-invited teams
description: The focal team's winning percentage in games played against teams that had been invited to the prior-year NCAA tournament, ranging from 0 to 100 percent. The authors created it to parallel the games-against-prior-year-invited-teams variable and to ensure the separation of status effects from performance effects.

The number of games against non-Division I teams that a school played in a current year. The authors did not control for winning percentage against these teams because historically it was over 90 percent.

A dichotomous measure, with 1 indicating that a college was selected to participate in a current year's NCAA postseason basketball tournament and 0 otherwise. Teams that received automatic bids were excluded from the analysis, leaving 1,871 colleges competing for 217 invitations over the study period.

Function exploration is the average value of an alliance agreement indicator across all alliances formed by the firm in year t: the indicator is coded 1 for a knowledge-generating R&D agreement, 0 for another type of agreement based on existing knowledge (joint marketing and service, OEM/VAR, licensing, production, or supply), and 0.5 for a combination of R&D and other agreements. Values range from 0 to 1, with high values indicating function exploration and low values indicating function exploitation. Balance within the function domain is tested with the linear and the squared term of this variable: a negative linear term together with a positive quadratic term, i.e., a U-shaped curve, supports the negative performance implications of balance.
time_window: year t, lagged one year relative to the dependent variable

description: For each alliance formed by the firm, an indicator received a value of 1 if the firm had no joint prior alliances with its partner and 0 if such alliances existed. Structure exploration is the average value of this indicator across all alliances formed by the firm in year t; values range from 0 to 1, with high values indicating structure exploration and low values indicating structure exploitation. Firm-year observations corresponding to years in which firms formed their first and only alliance were excluded. Balance within the structure domain is tested with the linear and the squared term of this variable.
time_window: year t, lagged one year relative to the dependent variable

variable_name: Linear interaction of function exploration and structure exploration
description: Balance across domains is tested by introducing a linear interaction of function exploration and structure exploration. Positive main effects of the two exploration variables combined with a negative interaction effect suggest that performance improves when exploration is extensive in one domain and limited in the other, and declines when exploration increases in both domains simultaneously.
time_window: year t, lagged one year relative to the dependent variable

description: Market value was calculated by multiplying the firm's stock price by the number of common shares outstanding. Because of the high volatility of this measure, the annual market value was calculated by averaging the 12 end-of-month daily values of the relevant calendar year. Market value serves as the long-term performance measure.

Net profit is used as a short-term, accounting measure of financial performance and was extracted on an annual basis from Compustat. It serves as the second dependent variable alongside firm market value.

Firm size was measured as the value of total assets reported in Compustat and served as a moderator of the relationship between exploration/exploitation and firm performance. The measure was highly correlated with alternative measures based on firm revenues and firm equity.
time_window: year t, lagged one year relative to the dependent variable

description: Dummy variable identifying whether the model change involved a new platform, which is considered a major update; it is coded 1 if a major platform design occurred during the period and 0 otherwise. Redesign data identify when and how an automobile manufacturer redesigned or introduced a new model, and the individual contract data identify the date on which the first vehicle of a new model or model update was sold.

Ex post measures of reliability for 14 vehicle characteristics, written on a five-point scale, used to proxy for realized depreciation. A high reliability rating of five indicates that very few respondents reported problems, while a rating of one represents a high problem report rate; the measures are constructed from the number of necessary repairs reported by survey respondents.

The ratio of captive leases to total production for the model, capturing how heavily manufacturer-owned captive lessors are involved in leasing that vehicle. Captive lessors represent core manufacturers vertically integrating into the complementary leasing market.

variable_name: MarkShare x CapPen / DealProf x CapPen
description: Captive subsidization is measured by interacting model-specific captive leasing penetration with one of two measures of low demand: vehicle segment market share (the average model family market share in its vehicle segment) and dealer profitability (the average dealer profit margin for this model). Low dealer profit indicates low demand relative to supply, suggesting the potential need for manufacturer lease and loan subsidization.

Straight percentage error calculated as (r - v)/c, where r is the contracted residual value, v is the lease-end market value and c is the capitalized cost, or original value of the new car. Positive values reflect an overestimation and negative values reflect either an underestimation or conservative contracting; because winning a lease while underestimating the residual value is a good thing, the authors treat this as the more appropriate measure.
time_window: lease-end values from January 2000 to January 2004

description: The absolute value of the percentage difference between the forecasted and realized values, computed as the absolute value of (r - v)/c. Under this measure, overestimating and underestimating by equivalent amounts are treated as equal forecasting performance.
time_window: lease-end values from January 2000 to January 2004

description: Duration of a specific lessor in a model-specific market, estimated with a semi-parametric Cox proportional hazard model; the data identify the day of each market entry and exit. Because the data are left truncated, all firm/market pairs where entry occurs within the first 300 days of the data are eliminated, and failures within 300 days before the January 2002 right truncation are treated as right-hand censored.

Cultural spawning measures to what extent each treated spawn startup's culture is more similar to its parent organization's culture than the matched twin's culture is to the same parent in a given year. The cultural distance of two organizations is measured with the Jensen-Shannon distance, the square root of the Jensen-Shannon divergence, which equals zero when the two distributions are identical and increases up to one as they diverge. The cultural distance between a spawned startup and its parent is subtracted from the cultural distance between its matched twin startup and the same parent and divided by the cultural distance between the matched startup and the parent. A larger value means a stronger cultural spawning effect.

The reverse-coded value of the Jensen-Shannon distance between the cultural topic vectors of a focal startup and its parent organization. Because the Jensen-Shannon distance equals zero when the two distributions are identical and increases up to one as they diverge, reverse coding gives a measure of cultural similarity. This is the dependent variable of the analysis comparing spawned startups with matched twin startups.

Years worked at the parent organization, measured by counting from the first year that an individual founder appeared as working in the firm. It captures the time the founder had to learn the parent organization's culture.

The extent to which the parent organization's cultural elements are semantically coherent. A word embedding model (Word2Vec) was applied to measure the semantic similarity between words, and the pairwise cosine similarity between the 50 highest-probability words of each topic was calculated and aggregated into the similarity of topics. Organizational cultural congruency is measured from these topic similarities together with the probability weights of the topics, and the parent's cultural congruency is the average yearly cultural congruency of all the years when a founder worked for the parent.
time_window: average over the years the founder worked for the parent

description: The Jensen-Shannon distance of each organization's cultural topic vector from the yearly average cultural topic vectors of all companies within the same product category, calculated for each year. Companies were clustered into 14 product categories from binary vectors of the 740 distinct product categories in Crunchbase using K-means. The parent's cultural atypicality is the average Jensen-Shannon distance of all the years that a founder worked for the parent.
time_window: average over the years the founder worked for the parent

description: A startup is a spawn when its founder had previously worked at another technology company; the parent was the company where the founder worked immediately before establishing the startup, set to the CEO founder's previous employer when more than one cofounder's profile was identified. In the matching analysis spawned startups were the treated group and nonspawned startups the control group, with one twin nonspawned startup found for each treated startup. The variable is coded one for a spawned startup and zero for a matched nonspawned twin startup.

Employee review texts from Glassdoor were used to assess organizational culture, and latent Dirichlet allocation (LDA) was applied to identify common cultural topics in reviews of technology companies; 30 topics were identified and are the cultural elements in the sample. Each review is transformed into a 30-dimensional probability vector whose elements sum to one. For a given year, an organization's cultural topic vector is the centroid of the vectors of all employee reviews for that company/year; a parent's cultural topic vector is measured the same way, and a founder's cultural learning from a parent is measured as the centroid of topic vectors of all the years in which the founder worked for the parent.
scale: probability vector over 30 topics, each between 0 and 1 and summing to 1

description: An indicator for whether partners set up a steering committee for an alliance. Steering committee equals 1 when the contract establishes this committee, and 0 otherwise. Because this dependent variable is binary, the authors specify probit models.
