Follow-up visits were identified by evaluating whether the patient returned to the referred-to specialist for follow-up care within 365 days following the first visit. The authors view the outcome as a measure of patient confidence in a specialist: a patient who trusts the specialist will be more likely to return for follow-up care.
time_window: within 365 days following the first visit

description: Captures the extent to which a provider specializes in treating the patient's diagnosis. To compute the measure, the authors counted the number of patients the specialist saw in the prior 12 months with the same diagnosis as the focal patient and divided this number by the total number of patients the specialist treated in that time window. The variable was constructed as a fraction rather than a count, to be consistent with most prior research on physician specialization and health outcomes.

An index of the perceived effectiveness of strategic responses constructed from the aggregated responses of all respondents within each firm to four questions on the perceived effectiveness of pricing, sourcing, plant siting and international capacity loading responses (Cronbach's alpha = 0.93). The effectiveness measures were thus not just one individual's perception but the perception of a cross-functional group of senior managers about the effectiveness of each firm's strategic responses.

Index combining the two variables that loaded together as expected in the factor analysis of the treasurer's questionnaire: how important are the goals of 'minimizing the impact of FX on current year's profits relative to plan' and 'the goal of minimizing balance sheet translation exposure'. The authors report a Cronbach's alpha of 0.55 and note that alpha is highly dependent on the number of variables in an index, arguing that the two variables substantively reflect two aspects of a corporate-finance orientation towards managing the impact of currency movements.

Index of the importance the Treasury manager attaches to two goals that loaded together as expected in the factor analysis of the treasurer's questionnaire: 'assisting divisions in identifying exchange-rate impacts' and 'assisting divisions in maximizing profits when faced with exchange-rate fluctuations' (Cronbach's alpha = 0.91).

A variable measured in months, constructed from three questions on the extent of use of hedging with forwards up to 12 months (HDGTO12), of hedging with forwards from 12 to 24 months (HDGTO24) and of hedging with forwards beyond 24 months (HDGGT24), as TIMEFRAME = HDGTO12*6 + HDGTO24*18 + HDGGT24*36 (Cronbach's alpha = 0.63).

Index of the existence of disincentives to Treasury cooperation with operations or involvement in hedging competitive exposures, created from three statements capturing the disincentives to cooperation most often mentioned in the interviews (Cronbach's alpha = 0.63). On a 7-point Likert-type scale, the response 'Strongly agree' was coded as 1 and 'Strongly disagree' as 7, and the scale was reversed so that high values indicated a high level of disincentives to cooperation.
scale: 7-point Likert-type scale (1 = Strongly agree to 7 = Strongly disagree), reversed

description: Indicator of the firm's commitment to cross-functional integration through multiple processes, built from a set of seven variables capturing the existence or otherwise of seven cross-functional integrating mechanisms identified in the authors' first-phase interviews, ranging from the existence of cross-functional teams to entrepreneurial 'internal consultants' who acted as boundary-spanners and systematic information dissemination on exchange rates through the companies' management information systems. The seven variables were added together and averaged across all respondents in each firm. The construct makes the simple assumption that more integrative processes can lead to better cross-functional integration.

Index of four variables covering the extent to which alternative exchange-rate scenarios and assessment of foreign-exchange exposures were used in the medium and long-term planning processes of the firm (Cronbach's alpha = 0.90), capturing the flexibility or rigidity of the firm's budgeting and planning processes.

A dummy variable indicating whether a CEO has a private pilot license, equal to one if the CEO holds a pilot license and zero otherwise. The main data source is Cain and McKeon (2016), who first collected a sample of CEO names from the ExecuComp database and then searched extensively for the CEO names in the Federal Aviation Administration's Airmen Certification Database. If a name could not be found, the CEO was assumed not to be a pilot; for every name with at least one match, additional information such as birth date, home address, and other personal information extracted from LexisNexis, Bloomberg, and other public records was collected to confirm the match.

The drawn all-in spread in basis points (plus any annual fee and up-front/maturity fee) in excess of the benchmark rate (LIBOR), which equals the loan interest rate minus LIBOR. It represents the risk premium lenders charge based on the risk profile of each borrower and reflects the level of default risk of a loan as far as lenders are concerned. In essence, it is the interest cost of a bank loan.
scale: basis points (the unit of Loan Spread is 100 basis points)

description: A binary variable that is equal to one if the bank loan is collateralized and zero otherwise. Lenders may require collateral assets to protect their financial interests and minimize potential losses from loan defaults.

The number of general and financial covenants specified in a loan contract. These covenants often limit managers' operating, investing, and financing activities, and more covenants imply greater constraints imposed on borrowers.

A Herfindahl index calculated from the respective contributions of the lead bank and syndicate banks to the loan. The higher the syndicate concentration, the higher the proportion of the total loan that the lead bank would be responsible for; involving more lenders means a less concentrated ownership and helps reduce the credit risk borne by any single lender.

An indicator variable equal to one if the CEO lists his or her firm as the sole beneficiary in the corporate-owned life insurance and zero otherwise. In the event that the CEO dies, the firm receives the face value of the insurance policy; purchasing such insurance reflects the importance of the CEO to the firm.

Minus one times the percentage of independent outside directors on a board, where that percentage is the number of independent outside directors divided by the board size. Higher values therefore indicate a less independent board.

Experimental treatment in which the experts, after evaluating the investments individually in their assigned scenario, viewed the videos of all scenarios, watched representatives of each scenario present their evaluations and rationale, and discussed the evaluations across all scenarios. The posttest (Posttest B) was administered after this treatment.

Experimental treatment in which the experts, after evaluating the investments individually in their assigned scenario, viewed the videos of all scenarios, watched representatives of each scenario present their evaluations and rationale, and discussed the evaluations across all scenarios. The posttest (Posttest B) was administered after this treatment.

Experimental treatment in which the experts, after recommending investment strategies in their assigned scenario, viewed the videos of all scenarios, watched and discussed the evaluations of each scenario, and discussed the evaluations across all scenarios. The posttest (Posttest B) was administered after this treatment.
level: individual expert recommending a strategy for a segment

description: Experimental treatment consisting of reading the assigned scenario, immersion in the scenario (identifying its key features and viewing a custom-designed video), discussion of the scenario's implications, and individual evaluation of the investments using the voting procedure. Posttest A was administered after this treatment.

Experimental treatment consisting of reading the assigned scenario, immersion in the scenario (identifying its key features and viewing a custom-designed video), discussion of the scenario's implications, and individual evaluation of the investments using the voting procedure. Posttest A was administered after this treatment.

Confidence in the recommendation about whether the planning agency should make the investment, recorded on a four-point scale ranging from highly certain to highly uncertain alongside a yes/no/do not know investment recommendation. The questionnaires used in the pretest and the posttests of the study were identical, so confidence was recorded before any scenario and after the single-scenario (Posttest A) and multiple-scenario (Posttest B) evaluations.
scale: four-point scale ranging from highly certain to highly uncertain

description: Confidence in a forced yes/no investment recommendation, recorded using a finer seven-point ratio scale. The scale permits calculation of average confidence as a sum of the products of proportion of votes and average value of the confidence interval. Confidence was recorded in the pretest and after the single-scenario (Posttest A) and multiple-scenario (Posttest B) evaluations.

A judgment was designated to have become more favorable if the change in expert vote from pretest to Posttest A was one of three types: changed recommendation from opposing the investment to supporting it, remained opposed to making the investment but with lower confidence, or remained supportive of the investment and with higher confidence; the criterion for designating a judgment less favorable was symmetric. Change from the pretest to Posttest B was recorded when an expert who answered either yes or no in both waves changed his/her judgment, i.e., the investment advice and/or the confidence in it.
scale: more favorable / less favorable / no change
time_window: pretest to Posttest A and pretest to Posttest B

description: A judgment was designated to have become more favorable if the change in expert vote from pretest to Posttest A was one of three types: changed recommendation from opposing the investment to supporting it, remained opposed to making the investment but with lower confidence, or remained supportive of the investment and with higher confidence; the criterion for designating a judgment less favorable was symmetric. Study II yielded 404 pairs of judgment where an expert evaluated a given investment in both pretest and Posttest A.
scale: more favorable / less favorable / no change

description: Using the group vote from the particular scenario, each investment was classified as useful, wasteful, or neither for that scenario. If n investments were assessed in a workshop, an investment was denoted useful for Scenario X if it received a minimum of 1/n points in Scenario X and its proportion of points was at least three times higher than its proportion of vetoes in that scenario. The authors note that this parameterization is somewhat arbitrary, but that sensitivity tests show the results hold over a wide range of parameter values.
time_window: workshop evaluation of the assigned scenario

description: Using the group vote from the particular scenario, each investment was classified as useful, wasteful, or neither for that scenario. The criteria for wasteful investments is symmetric to those for useful investments: an investment received a minimum of 1/n vetoes and the proportion of vetoes was at least three times that of points in that scenario. The authors note that this parameterization is somewhat arbitrary, but that sensitivity tests show the results hold over a wide range of parameter values.
time_window: workshop evaluation of the assigned scenario

description: For each of the transportation infrastructure segments, four generic strategies were specified, ranging from the least flexible to the most flexible; experts were asked in the pretest and Posttest B to recommend an investment strategy for each type of segment. The questionnaire noted the variation in flexibility of the four strategies.
scale: four ordered strategy options from least to most flexible
level: individual expert recommending a strategy for a segment

description: Estimated with a cross-classified multilevel model as the Level-3 between-corporate parent residual in subsidiary ROA, which captures all first-order corporate-level differences consequential to subsidiary performance, including the quantity and quality of resources and their interactions. The output provides point estimates and standard errors for each effect class, which the authors use to calculate percentages of variance explained in subsidiary performance.
level: corporate parent (Level 3 of the multilevel model)

description: Net income divided by total assets, used as the measure of subsidiary performance. Observations below the 1st percentile and above the 99th percentile are winsorized to avoid estimation bias due to outliers; the authors note that this gives a more conservative measure of the effect.

The number of subsidiaries within a given corporate portfolio for each corporate year. All units directly linked to the corporate parent under the corporate umbrella are counted, even those for which performance is not analyzed, and a parent must directly own at least 1% equity in an active subsidiary to be included in the count. The 50th percentile is used to categorize subsidiaries according to their corporate parents' subsidiary portfolio size.

Computed by matching the NAICS codes of each corporate parent and subsidiary pair with a multistep weighting system: a two-digit match of primary codes is coded '2' and a four-digit match '4', a subsidiary primary code matching a parent secondary code at two digits is coded '2' and at four digits '3', other combinations are coded '2' or '1', and non-matches are coded '0'. The summed scores range from '0' to '9'; a score of '0' denotes that the subsidiary and parent share neither a primary nor secondary NAICS code, while '9' reflects a four-digit match of primary and secondary codes. Subsidiaries coded '0' or '1' are treated as unrelated and the remaining codes as related.

Measured by matching home and host country pairs to the World Governance Indicators database. All six WGI dimensions are included; because the six dimensions are highly correlated and one factor explains 97% of the variance, the absolute difference of each dimension is averaged into one overall score for each country pair. The measure reflects differences in formal institutions such as regulatory quality, rule of law, and government effectiveness; because it is continuous, the 50th percentile distinguishes low- from high-distance corporate parent-subsidiary pairs.

The executives of interest were the top executives of acquired firms before their acquisition, defined as officers holding a title above the rank of vice president, or a board directorship, or both, identified from annual reports or SEC 10K forms filed immediately prior to the acquisition. Dates of departure were obtained from the postacquisition firm, by telephone for 78 firms and in writing for 31 of the remaining firms. The event of interest was the executive's departure, modeled as the instantaneous rate of transition from the retained state to the departed state during the observation window.
time_window: first four years (1,460 days) following an acquisition

description: Return on common equity was used as the preacquisition performance measure. ROE was preferred over return on assets because the data set included both manufacturing and service firms with widely differing asset configurations, and it is a well-understood measure that is somewhat comparable across firms and industries. For acquired firms, ROE was assessed as a three-year average covering the last full preacquisition fiscal year and the two preceding ones; ROEs were calculated from COMPUSTAT data.
time_window: three-year average covering the last full preacquisition fiscal year and the two preceding ones

description: The three-year average ROE of an acquiring firm minus the three-year average ROE of the acquired firm, included because of the authors' interest in the standing of acquired executives relative to that of acquiring executives. Higher values therefore indicate a larger performance advantage of the acquirer over the acquired firm.
time_window: three-year average covering the last full preacquisition fiscal year and the two preceding ones

description: The relative size of an acquired firm was calculated by dividing its sales in the year preceding the acquisition by the sales of the acquiring firm. The authors report that this measure was highly correlated with the chief alternative measures using assets and employees.

Each acquisition was placed into one of three categories: mutually negotiated unions, uncontested tender offers, or contested tender offers. To separate mergers from tender offers, the authors searched Wall Street Journal reports for indications of either type; for acquisitions involving tender offers they searched for statements from management regarding support of or opposition to the offers, and any statement of opposition by target management led to classifying the acquisition as contested. Announcements of the acquisitions in Mergers and Acquisitions provided a check on the validity of the Wall Street Journal reports, and in no case did the evidence from the two sources conflict.

The autonomy of acquired firms was assessed by expert informants: for each acquisition the authors identified six acquiring firm officers who were employees of the acquiring firm when the acquisition occurred and six security analysts who specialised in the acquiring firm's securities at that time. Respondents rated on a seven-point scale the extent to which an acquired firm was operated autonomously (1) or closely integrated with its acquiring firm (7). Of the 1,065 instruments sent in 1989, 353 (33%) were returned, averaging 3.2 per acquisition, with an intraclass correlation coefficient of .72.
scale: 1 = operated autonomously to 7 = closely integrated with the acquiring firm

description: Coded 1 when an acquired executive became an officer or director in a postacquisition firm and 0 otherwise, as indicated in the first SEC filing of the acquiring firm following the acquisition event. The measure reveals only titular status; the status embodied in actual managerial responsibilities goes unmeasured.
time_window: first SEC filing of the acquiring firm following the acquisition

description: A variable coded 1 when at least one member of the acquired top team, but not the executive under consideration, became an officer or director in the postacquisition firm, and 0 otherwise.
time_window: first SEC filing of the acquiring firm following the acquisition

description: Each employee's job title is categorized into one of 12 levels - Owner, President, VP, CEO, C-Suite, Head, Director, Manager, Producer, Lead, Supervisor, and Other - by applying Rules 1-12 in ascending order until a match is found, and the number of unique levels with at least one employee is then counted. The list of relevant terms includes abbreviations and typographical errors that frequently appear in the MobyGames database.
scale: count of hierarchical levels, up to 12
time_window: at the release of the start-up's first game

description: GameRankings aggregates over 240,000 critics' review ratings from both offline and online sources and computes their average in terms of percentages, which is used as a measure for creative success. The rating is on a scale from 0 to 100 and, to a large extent, reflects novelty, as terms such as 'novel,' 'creative,' 'unique,' 'groundbreaking,' 'new,' and 'original' appear disproportionately in the reviews with above-60 ratings.
time_window: at the release of the first game

variable_name: Commercial success (units sold globally in millions)
description: VGChartz documents the global sales figures for games that sold more than 10,000 units, which are used to measure commercial success; the measure is comparable to the typical measure of commercial success (i.e., attendance) in studies of the movie industry. Information on profit, revenue, or return on investment is unavailable, so task-level characteristics are added to account for development costs, and the natural logarithm is applied to account for right skewness.

At the individual level, IndBreadth is the diversity across all functional domains in terms of 1 - HHI, where HHI stands for Herfindahl-Hirschman Index; these individual-level characteristics are then averaged to the firm level as Breadth.

A collaboration network is constructed in a given year, where two individuals have a tie if they collaborated within the previous 5 years. For each start-up, its employees' pairwise shortest path lengths are measured; because the shortest path length to an isolate is infinite, the inverse of pairwise shortest path lengths is calculated and averaged, and this average is considered a measure of social capital.

Khandwalla's (1974) measure of formal control, using 7-point scales to indicate reliance on a comprehensive management and control system, cost centers for cost control, quality control techniques, and formal appraisal of personnel. The scale was selected because it is not reliant on the term formalization, which can carry very different meanings for U.S. versus Chinese managers.

Using the Miller and Dröge (1986) format, decentralization was assessed by the level with authority for making decisions in four domains, on 7-point scales. Higher scores indicate that decision authority rests lower in the organization.

Three 7-point scales were used to measure customer product knowledge utilization. On the survey, knowledge was defined as 'understanding some phenomenon.' SOE managers assessed applied knowledge in terms of product quality as driven by information gleaned by customer expectations, joint product co-design with customers, and how customers use their goods/component parts.

variable_name: growth performance relative to the industry
description: Growth performance relative to the industry was measured by three items (Miller, 1991). Managers rated performance over the past 3 years on 7-point scales with endpoints of 'well below industry average' and 'well above industry average.'

Created from the secondary data source: industry foreign funded enterprise sales were divided by industry sales revenue, using 1999 data. Foreign funded enterprises include equity joint ventures, contractual joint ventures, and foreign wholly owned subsidiaries. Industry sales revenue refers to sales by all state-owned and non-state enterprises with annual sales over 5 million Yuan.

Technological turbulence was measured by four 7-point semantic differential items indicating dynamism in products and processes (Celly and Frazier, 1996). Respondents were instructed to consider the stability of the SOE's environment and were asked to rate their primary industry.
Production technology routineness was measured by mass output orientation (Khandwalla, 1974). The construct is defined as the level of repetitiveness in transforming inputs into outputs.
The number of employees and annual sales, both measured on open-ended scales, are the indicators of size. Logarithmic transformations, which normalized the variables, were applied.

The dependent variable is the logged value of total contract dollars, that is, the log transformation of a firm's yearly performance in contract dollars. The semi-log form gives the interaction terms the interpretation of a percentage change in output for the same firm before and after the shock.

variable_name: High inter- and high intraproduct coordination; high inter- and low intraproduct coordination; low inter- and high intraproduct coordination
description: Categorical versions of the two coordination measures, constructed from a matrix of four quadrants that arise from the firm being higher versus lower than the median on either dimension. Three dummy variables are used across the specifications, with the fourth (low inter- and low intraproduct coordination) serving as the baseline category. The authors' main theoretical concern is with the asymmetric quadrants in which the firm is high on one dimension and low on the other.

Measured by calculating, for each product the firm sells in the five-year preshock period, the number of other products to which the focal product is connected via a common customer; the variable is the average of this value across all products of the firm. A link between a product area and a customer exists when a contract granted to the firm shows the firm selling that product to that customer.

Measured by counting the number of customers to which each product of the firm is connected in the five-year preshock period, then averaging across all products of the firm. Together with interproduct coordination it gives preshock measures of the firm's locus of coordination at the firm level.

Measures the degree of overlap between the inputs and outputs (based on SIC codes) of a firm's products, following Fan and Lang (2000), and is built in two stages. First, for each SIC a vector is formed whose elements are the percentage of inputs arising from each intermediate SIC other than the two focal SICs, the correlation between the two vectors is calculated, the process is repeated for outputs, and the value of complementarity is the average of the input and output correlations. Second, all possible unique pairs of the firm's SIC codes are formed, each pair is assigned the complementarity value calculated in the first stage, and the average across pairs gives the firm-level value.

Represents the degree of scope for each firm unit, preshock, measured as the inverse of the number of distinct organizational units within the firm. Each firm has one or more distinct subunits under which contracts can be granted; using the inverse number of such units facilitates the interpretation of the interaction term as the degree of interdependence per organizational unit.

variable_name: bank closure tie minimum, mean, and maximum age
description: The age of a tie between two banks was set to one in the first year they appeared as syndicate partners in the four-year adjacency matrices, and thereafter was set equal to the number of years since that first syndicate as long as the two banks partnered in at least one syndicate in the following four years; ties that lapsed for more than four years were treated as terminated and their age was restarted. Closure ties were identified by inventorying the triads in each bank's ego network, defined as those comprising closure triads in which the focal bank A is a syndicate partner with banks B and C and B and C are also partners; the 'Simmelian' tie BC was included when computing the closure tie age measures. The minimum, mean, and maximum ages of a bank's closure ties were used to test hypotheses H1, H2A, and H2B.
time_window: four-year moving windows ending in year t

variable_name: bank bridging tie minimum, mean, and maximum age
description: Tie age was set to one in the first year two banks appeared as syndicate partners in the four-year adjacency matrices and thereafter to the number of years since that first syndicate as long as the two banks partnered again within the following four years; ties that lapsed longer were treated as terminated and their age restarted. Bridging ties were identified by inventorying the triads in each bank's ego network, defined as those comprising bridging triads in which the focal bank A is a syndicate partner with banks B and C but B and C are disconnected. The minimum, mean, and maximum ages of a bank's bridging ties were used to test hypotheses H1, H2A, and H2B.
time_window: four-year moving windows ending in year t

description: To measure a bank's market share at time t, the inflation-adjusted dollar value of each offering made during the previous year was allocated among the members of the syndicate that underwrote the deal. For deals involving a lead manager only, the bank was assigned 100% of the offering's dollar value; for deals involving multiple syndicate members, the lead bank was assigned 50% of the underwriting value and the remaining value was split equally among other members, based on norms identified in interviews with investment bank managers. Each bank's deal values were then divided by the total value of public offerings at time t, and the resulting market share was logged.
time_window: t, based on offerings made during the previous year

variable_name: maximum closure tie age divided by minimum bridging tie age; maximum closure tie age multiplied by maximum bridging tie age
description: For hypothesis H3A, predicting the hybrid effect of old closure ties and young bridging ties, a bank's maximum closure tie age was divided by its minimum bridging tie age; for hypothesis H3B, regarding the hybrid effect of old closure ties and old bridging ties, a bank's maximum closure tie age was multiplied by its maximum bridging tie age. The ratio variable is largest when maximum closure tie age is high and minimum bridging tie age is low, whereas the multiplicative interaction is largest when maximum closure tie age and maximum bridging tie age are both high.
time_window: four-year moving windows ending in year t

description: Cumulative related operating experience measured by the past three years of parent food service sales (all revenue from domestic restaurant operations and franchise revenue), discounted by age. The variable is computed as current-year sales plus half of prior-year sales plus one third of sales from two years earlier. It is specific to the chain's industry and measured at the parent level rather than at the unit or chain level.
time_window: current year plus the previous two years

description: Binary variable created from parent and business unit headquarters data published in the NRN. It is coded 1 when the chain and parent share the same city and state headquarters and 0 otherwise.

Governance mode of the chain, franchising versus company ownership, treated as a discrete choice rather than a continuum. In the data 55 percent of the chains use franchising while the rest operate all outlets through company ownership, and the second-stage models are estimated separately for franchised and company-owned chains.

Sales growth of the chain compared to the prior year, calculated from the NRN Top 200 lists as (Sales t - Sales t-1) / Sales t-1. Growth is used because it is the goal of many chains and may be more appropriate than profitability in this mature, competitive context.

Unit growth of the chain compared to the prior year, calculated from the NRN Top 200 lists in the same way as sales growth. Growth is used rather than profitability because it is the goal of many chains in this mature, competitive context.

Reader score from the Consumer Reports survey of roughly 70,000 readers, which it conducts for restaurants approximately every three years, reflecting overall satisfaction. Each chain must have at least 250 visits to be included in the results.
time_window: survey conducted approximately every three years

description: Informants rated their satisfaction with the supplier on three seven-point items: 'We are satisfied with the relationship that we have with supplier'; 'We are displeased with our relationship with supplier' (reversed); and 'Our relationship with supplier has more than fulfilled our expectations.' Items were anchored by 'strongly disagree' and 'strongly agree,' and the reliability of the scale was 0.87. The measure is based on Ruekert and Churchill (1984).
scale: seven-point scale anchored by 'strongly disagree' and 'strongly agree'

description: A single item asked 'How attractive is supplier compared to your next best alternative manufacturer in terms of generating profits?' on a seven-point scale anchored by 'much less attractive' and 'much more attractive.' Informants were asked to consider their economic payoffs (profits) from the supplier in question relative to alternative supplier relationships.
scale: seven-point scale anchored by 'much less attractive' and 'much more attractive'

description: The standard deviation of the economic payoffs measure within a given territory; a higher standard deviation for the territory-level indicator reflects inconsistency across resellers in terms of resellers' perceptions of economic payoffs. The measure was computed for territories with a minimum number of observations (at least five questionnaires from different resellers). It is not captured directly from the individual respondents but constructed from the data of all respondents within a territory.

The number of years that the focal reseller had been working with the supplier, collected with the item 'How long have your worked with supplier? (in terms of number of years).' A logarithmic form was adopted for the time measure.

variable_name: Dummy for whether economic payoffs below average in territory
description: A dummy variable coded 1 if the buyer's perception of the level of economic payoffs for the reseller in the territory is below the average level for the same variable across resellers in that territory, and 0 otherwise. It was used both as a main effect and to moderate the effect of inconsistency on satisfaction.

variable_name: Consistency between formal authority network and informal network
description: Measured as the structural equivalence of each organizational member across the informal advice and information network and the formal authority network. The authors used the CONCOR algorithm of the structural equivalence procedure in UCINET VI, joining the two matrices and adding the transpose of the second matrix to account for tie directionality, and computed a correlation between node profiles bounded between the (-1, 1) interval.
time_window: roughly 10 months prior to the 2005 performance evaluation

variable_name: Inconsistency between reciprocal interdependent formal workflow and informal networks
description: Measured as the inverse of structural equivalence of each organizational member across the informal advice and information network and the reciprocally interdependent formal workflow network. The authors used the CONCOR algorithm of the structural equivalence procedure in UCINET VI, joining the two matrices and adding the transpose of the second matrix to account for tie directionality.
time_window: roughly 10 months prior to the 2005 performance evaluation

variable_name: Inconsistency between sequential interdependent formal workflow and informal networks
description: Measured as the inverse of structural equivalence of each organizational member across the informal advice and information network and the sequentially interdependent formal workflow network. The authors used the CONCOR algorithm of the structural equivalence procedure in UCINET VI, joining the two matrices and adding the transpose of the second matrix to account for tie directionality.
time_window: roughly 10 months prior to the 2005 performance evaluation

description: Operationalized as the log of the sum of three performance components from the company's formal evaluation system: knowledge growth, task performance, and contextual performance. Task performance is based on goal achievement, performance time, and error rate. Contextual performance includes activities such as spontaneously helping coworkers, volunteering, defending organizational goals, and following its rules, measured with the Borman and Motowidlo scale. Individuals are evaluated by their direct superiors.

For each patent team the authors identified the geographic location of each inventor and, for each cluster, built a technological vector from the percentage of patents assigned to each of 37 two-digit technology classes by all organizations in the cluster, using cumulative patent data from 1981 up to the focal year and updating the vector each year. The measure is the angular distance in radians between the technology vectors of the clusters represented on the team; when inventors are in more than two clusters the authors take the average angular distance among the clusters. The measure has a theoretical range of zero to 1.57, taking zero for clusters with identical technological vectors and 1.57 when no technological overlap exists. The formula for the angle is presented only as an unreadable formula block, so the specification is recorded from the surrounding prose.
time_window: cumulative patent data from 1981 up to the focal year

description: A patent is coded ''1'' if it is in the top 5 percent of the count of future citations, net of self-citations, up to 2010, compared with the population of U.S. nanotechnology patents of the same application year assigned to all organizations, and ''0'' otherwise. Citation rates are compared among patents from the same application year because average citations received have been increasing over time. The authors' sample contained 74 breakthrough inventions.
time_window: future citations up to 2010; sample period 1995-2004

description: Computed as the average number of prior collaborations among team members in the same geographic clusters. For each pair of collocated scientists on a patent team, the authors counted the number of times since 1981 that the pair had been listed as collocated co-inventors on a patent, not including the current patent (variable WRKwi). The summed value across pairs is divided by the total possible number of collocated pairs on the team, given by N(N-1)/2, where N is the number of collocated inventors on the team. A higher score indicates a team in which collocated members have many prior collocated collaborations.
time_window: prior collaborations since 1981, excluding the current patent

description: Computed as the average amount of prior collaborations occurring between members in different geographic clusters, including collaborations at other organizations. For each pair of scientists on a patent team who are not in the same location, the authors counted the number of times that pair had been listed as dispersed co-inventors on a patent since 1981, not including the current patent (variable BRKbw). The summed value across pairs is divided by the total possible number of dispersed pairs on the team, given by N(N-1)/2, where N is the number of dispersed inventors on the team. A higher score indicates that team members have worked with members in other clusters many times in the past.
time_window: prior collaborations since 1981, excluding the current patent

description: Relatedness is measured by comparing the primary Standard Industrial Classification (SIC) codes of the partner firm and the focal partnership. Increase in partnership relatedness is measured with a decrease in the distance between the primary SIC codes (at the two-digit level) of the partner firm and the focal partnership, calculated by subtracting the distance between SIC codes at time t from the distance at time t-1. The covariate is updated annually.
time_window: updated annually; change from t-1 to t

description: Partner firm marketing resources were measured with sales, general, and administrative expenditure, used as a proxy for the resources firms spend on market research, sales efforts, and other marketing related activities. Any increase in firm resources was calculated by subtracting the value of resources at time t-1 from the value at time t. The covariate is updated annually.
time_window: updated annually; change from t-1 to t

description: Partner firm R&D resources were measured with R&D expenditure. Any increase in firm resources was calculated by subtracting the value of resources at time t-1 from the value at time t. The covariate is updated annually.
time_window: updated annually; change from t-1 to t

description: M&A event was measured with the number of M&A events that occurred to the partner firm (either the partner firm acquiring another firm or being acquired by or merged with another firm) where the acquired or acquiring/merging firm is in the same industry as the focal partnership. If the partner firm did not experience such an event, it was coded as zero. The covariate is updated annually.

Formation of competing partnerships was measured with the number of partnerships formed by the focal partner firm in the same industry as the focal partnership to carry out the same type of activities (i.e., manufacturing, marketing, or R&D) as the focal partnership. If no such partnership was formed, it was coded as zero. The covariate is updated monthly.

Formation of multiple partnerships was measured with the number of partnerships formed by the focal partner firm with its current partner after the formation of the focal partnership. If no such partnership was formed, it was coded as zero. The covariate is updated monthly.

variable_name: Decrease in the availability of alternative partners
description: The availability of alternative partners is measured indirectly: for the focal firm, the availability of alternative partners decreases when firms in the current partner's industry form partnerships in the focal partnership's industry to carry out the same activities as the focal partnership. The variable is the number of partnerships formed by firms in the same industry as the focal partner firm's current partner, in the same industry as the focal partnership, to carry out the same types of activities as the focal partnership. If no such partnership was formed, it was coded as zero. The covariate is updated monthly.

Competitor imitative activities was measured with the number of partnerships formed in the same industry as the focal partnership by firms in the same industry as the focal partner firm. If no such partnership was formed, it was coded as zero. The covariate is updated monthly.

Termination information was coded at month level, that is, whether the event of termination occurred at each month after the JV was formed until its termination or end of observation (2004). A JV can be terminated through dissolution or acquisition; acquisition by a third party was not included in termination events, and for JVs with prespecified duration only terminations prior to contract expiration were considered. Termination information was gathered from SDC Platinum, Corporate Affiliations and Factiva, and by contacting partner companies directly by e-mail and phone for JVs whose termination information was missing.
time_window: monthly from JV formation until termination or end of observation in 2004

description: Change in organizational performance is operationalized by the change in percentage of games won compared with the prior season. During the regular season each major league club received performance feedback as it played a relatively stable number of about 22 games against seven league competitors. Because the farm-team practice focuses on player development, field performance is treated as the appropriate source of feedback information.
time_window: change from season t-1 to season t

variable_name: Difference in population mean network size (DPMj,t)
description: Subtracting the size of a team's farm network from the population's average network size results in the difference in population-level mean network size. The population of referent organizations consists of the other second-mover organizations currently executing the farm-team practice; the first mover (St. Louis Cardinals) is excluded from the calculation of relevant population means.

variable_name: Change in FT size next season (Yj,t+1)
description: Change in FT size next season is the dependent variable in all models. FT size is operationalized based on the number of affiliated minor league teams a club has. The analyses pertain only to observations of organizations with farm teams, as only those organizations could adjust FT size.

FT size is operationalized based on the number of affiliated minor league teams a club has; in the estimation sample the mean was 7.49 and the standard deviation 3.70. Teams' affiliations are identified based on the Baseball Bluebook (1917-1940), the Minor League Digest (1936-1940), and an unpublished detailed list of farm-team systems generated by a member of the Society of Baseball Research, Jerry Jackson.

Successful campaigns that raised beyond 150% of their funding goals are coded as blockbuster successes. For each of the 165 subordinate categories and each of the 2,080 days of the study, the authors calculated the average number of campaigns in this group that ended during the 90 days preceding a focal campaign's start date.
level: subordinate category-day, matched to a focal campaign
time_window: 90 days preceding the focal campaign's start date

description: Successful campaigns that raised between 100% and 150% of their funding goals are coded as unsung successes. For each of the 165 subordinate categories and each of the 2,080 days of the study, the authors calculated the average number of campaigns in this group that ended during the 90 days preceding a focal campaign's start date.
level: subordinate category-day, matched to a focal campaign
time_window: 90 days preceding the focal campaign's start date

description: Failed campaigns that raised more than 20% but ultimately fell short of their funding goal are coded as path breaking failures; the 20% cut point corresponds to the first inflection point in the distribution. For each of the 165 subordinate categories and each of the 2,080 days of the study, the authors calculated the average number of campaigns in this group that ended during the 90 days preceding a focal campaign's start date.
level: subordinate category-day, matched to a focal campaign
time_window: 90 days preceding the focal campaign's start date

description: Failed campaigns that raised between 0% and 20% of their funding goals are coded as broken path failures. For each of the 165 subordinate categories and each of the 2,080 days of the study, the authors calculated the average number of campaigns in this group that ended during the 90 days preceding a focal campaign's start date.
level: subordinate category-day, matched to a focal campaign
time_window: 90 days preceding the focal campaign's start date

description: The authors used the amount of funds pledged to a campaign as their dependent variable and calculated the log of these values to linearize the relationship with its predictors; they treat resource acquisition as a fundamental and measurable proxy for legitimacy in this setting. Because Kickstarter operates under an all-or-nothing model, pledges are collected only if an endeavor meets its funding goal. Funds raised in foreign currencies were converted to U.S. dollars using average exchange rates.

A count of firm i's patents in years t-5 to t-1 in which it used graphene. Graphene was assumed to be a fundamental component of a patent when the term 'graphene' was present in the title, abstract, or claims and was not nested within a list of other materials. Patents were counted in their application year. The formal equation for the variable is not readable in the available text.

The percentage of patents in a target patent class that employed graphene as a component, computed as the number of graphene-incorporating patents relative to the total number of utility patents in the class in years t-5 to t-1. The proportions for the classes in firm i's set of distant graphene-linked target classes in year t were averaged, and the resulting variable was scaled by a factor of 100 so that it can be read as percentages. It is a firm-level measure constructed from a firm-specific subset of sample-level information about the percentage of graphene patents in a patent class. The formal equation for the variable is not readable in the available text.

The maximum value of all shortest-path knowledge distances in year t between a focal firm's unfamiliar graphene-linked patent classes and the firm's prior knowledge base; a class was unfamiliar to the firm if the firm had not patented in the class before year t. Between-class knowledge distance was generated with the cosine similarity measure for classes i and j, transformed by subtracting the similarity from one so that one is the most distant, over the 434 USPTO patent classes. The shortest knowledge path is the lowest distance between any class in the firm's knowledge base in years t-5 to t-1 and the target class. The variable is a proportion bounded [0,1] and is log transformed in all models. The formal equations for the measure are not readable in the available text.
time_window: t, with distances computed over t-5 to t-1 and a 2002-2012 calculation window

description: For each firm-year, the set of graphene-linked patent classes j that were distant to firm i's knowledge base and into which firm i patented in years t to t+2, where a class was identified as distant if the distance of its shortest path to the focal firm's knowledge base was above the median of all between-class distances. The number of firm i's patents in each distant class was summed and divided by the number of classes in the set, giving the firm's average number of patents in distant graphene-linked classes in years t to t+2. The variable is log transformed in all models. The formal equation for the variable is not readable in the available text.
Respondents rated the degree to which their firm had engaged in seven types of outward international activities. The items were averaged to create the score for the construct.

To test H4 the authors categorized outward activities into high-risk and low-risk groups based on the resource commitment and risk that each activity may involve, and entered the two groups as separate dependent variables.
Respondents indicated the degree to which their firm was involved in various types of inward activities. The items were averaged to create the score for the construct.

Respondents indicated the degree to which their firm had benefited from inward activities compared with competitors along five dimensions. The items were averaged to create the score for the construct.

Respondents indicated the degree to which their firm's resources could be easily applicable to cross-border deployment, on six dimensions. The items were averaged to create the score for the construct, which enters the structural model as a single latent variable in the H1 test.

Formed from the resource fungibility dimensions covering a firm's organization-related resources and capabilities, namely organizational structure, organizational culture, and human resource management system. It enters the model as a separate latent variable in the H2 test.

Formed from the resource fungibility dimensions covering a firm's technological resources and capabilities, namely product manufacturing technologies and product development technologies. It enters the model as a separate latent variable in the H2 test.

Respondents indicated the degree to which their firm favoured risk-taking, using two items. The authors calculated the sum of the two items after reverse-coding the second one and divided the sample into two groups (high-risk vs. low-risk propensity firms) based on this variable's sample median value. It was not used as a latent construct in the measurement model.
Spinout captures inventors' affiliation at any moment in time. It takes a value of 1 if the patents awarded to inventor i at time t are assigned to a spinout and 0 otherwise.

The number of claims contained in the patents applied for by inventor i in year t that belong to a new patent class, i.e., a class in which the inventor has never patented before. If the patents fall into multiple new classes, the first class listed in the patent document is used. The measure combines the number of claims and the novelty of technological classes to appraise whether the inventor's output is new with respect to his or her personal prior experience and to the state of the art.

The proportion of citations to prior patents assigned to Xerox contained in the patents each inventor applies for in any given year. It is computed as the proportion of the focal inventor's citations to Xerox's patents divided by the total number of backward citations. It proxies the extent to which the inventor builds on the originating parent's organizational knowledge.

Tenure in Xerox is measured with a 'tenure clock' that captures the amount of time, in years, elapsed since the first patent the inventor applied for with the parent organization. This clock stops with mobility events and reports a maximum value thereafter. The variable is centered on its mean when entered in the interaction terms.

Experience in Xerox's core technologies captures the extent to which inventors' prior innovations fit with Xerox's core areas. Xerox's core classes are identified as USPC classes with a frequency greater than 3% in a five-year moving window (from t-5 to t-1), yielding 12 time-variant core USPC classes per year. For all inventor-year observations, the measure is coded as the proportion of patents applied for by inventor i in Xerox's core classes from his or her first year in Xerox up to year t-1; for all inventor-year observations after spinout events, the proportion of patents observed in the inventor's last year with Xerox is reported.

A seven-item scale adapted from the conceptualization of Selnes and Sallis (2003), tapping the exchange of information between the buyer and the supplier regarding end-user needs and preferences, market structures and acquisitions, technologies of products, strategies and finances of partners, and unexpected problems. It was part of a 17-item relational learning scale developed through a review of the organizational learning literature and through 26 in-depth interviews with informants from both sides of 13 customer-supplier dyads. Identically worded, multiple-item Likert-type items were administered to buyers and suppliers in two versions of the questionnaire. Indicator weights of the formative measurement model were estimated by bootstrapping and all weights were significant at the five percent level.

A scale for joint sensemaking activities, whose mechanisms include information sharing forums, meetings, and cross-functional teams designed to create learning arenas between organizations. It is part of the 17-item relational learning scale following Selnes and Sallis (2003), administered in identically worded, multiple-item Likert-type items to both buyers and suppliers. Indicator weights were estimated by bootstrapping and all weights were significant at the five percent level.

A scale capturing the idiosyncratic routines and relationship-specific memories (organizational beliefs, behavioral routines and physical artifacts such as documents and electronic databases) that partners develop for how they do things in the specific relationship. It is part of the 17-item relational learning scale following Selnes and Sallis (2003), completed by buyers and suppliers on identically worded, multiple-item Likert-type items. Indicator weights were estimated by bootstrapping and all weights were significant at the five percent level.

Performance was operationalized as a construct with multidimensional formative indicators, constructing an index rather than a scale, because specific performance indicators may conflict and need not be correlated. Four indicators capture how the relationship with the supplier/buyer has helped improve product quality, on-time delivery of orders, the ability to develop successful new products for the marketplace, and reduce costs. Respondents evaluated their partners' or the partnership's performance rather than their own performance over time. Indicator weights of the formative measurement model were estimated by bootstrapping and all weights were significant at the five percent level.

Following Kogut and Singh (1988), the authors used Hofstede's cultural indices to form a composite index for cultural distance based upon the deviation along each of the four cultural dimensions (power distance, uncertainty avoidance, masculinity/femininity, and individualism) between the two countries in which the buyer's and supplier's facilities were located. The fifth dimension (long/short-term orientation) could not be used because 41 percent of the countries in the study have not been assigned an index on that dimension. Scores range from 0 to 5 and were dichotomized into low cultural distance (0 to 2) and high cultural distance (3 to 5) groups.
scale: index ranging from 0 to 5, dichotomized into low (0-2) and high (3-5)

description: Executives were classified by hierarchical level as chief executives, second-level executives, and third-level executives. The chief executives were asked to identify upper-level executives to participate, including all second-level executives and a sample of (or all) third-level executives, up to a maximum of 12 executives per organization.
scale: three categories: chief executive, second-level, third-level

description: EXTGAP is the absolute value of the difference between the external measure of realized strategy, converted to the 7-point scale, and an executive's perception of strategy on the 7-point scale. For example, an organization externally measured as a Prospector is given a strategy score of seven, and an executive who perceives the strategy as five has an EXTGAP score of two. Higher values indicate a larger gap, that is, less awareness.
scale: absolute difference between two 7-point scale scores

description: INTGAP is the absolute value of the difference between the chief executive's perception of strategy and the focal executive's perception, both on the 7-point scale. For example, if the chief executive perceives the organization's strategy as six and the focal executive rates it five, the INTGAP score is one. Higher values indicate a larger gap, that is, less agreement with the chief executive.
scale: absolute difference between two 7-point scale scores

description: Organizations' realized strategies were identified with the Miles and Snow typology by combining quantified published data on recent product/market additions with expert panel assessments, selecting only organizations whose strategies were at the extremes (Prospectors and Defenders). Interviews with the chief executives were then used to check the currency of these measures and organizations whose current strategic behaviour had moved were reclassified. For the awareness measures the external classification was converted to the 7-point scale, with a Prospector given a strategy score of seven on the rationale that organizations with very extreme realized strategies had been selected.
scale: 7-point scale after conversion (Prospector scored seven; low end for Defender). Direction: higher = more prospector (defender to prospector scale)
time_window: reflects the organizations' strategies up to about 12 or 18 months before the interviews

description: Each executive rated the organization's strategy on a 7-point scale representing the Miles and Snow typology (1 = Defender; 4 = Analyser; 7 = Prospector); the Miles and Snow labels were not used on the questionnaire. The instrument was not forced-choice: respondents could indicate that their organization did not consistently pursue a strategy on the continuum, and 14 such responses reduced the usable responses to 195.
scale: 7-point scale (1 = Defender, 4 = Analyser, 7 = Prospector). Direction: higher = more prospector (defender to prospector scale)

description: Organizations were classified as having recently changed or as unchanged on the basis of the interviews with chief executives, which indicated that several organizations had more recently engaged in strategic behaviours that warranted their reclassification, that is, they had changed or were changing their realized strategies. In the analysis, organizations were compared as unchanged versus recently changed.

variable_name: Receptivity to public affairs information (breadth and depth)
description: Receptivity was captured with two dimensions from the forest products executive survey. Breadth was measured as the number of outside stakeholder groups with whom executives claimed to be in contact for more than one hour a week, and depth was measured as the average length of time generally spent on any particular public affairs issue. Individual executive responses were aggregated at the company level, so the analysis uses company-level means for the six participating firms.

variable_name: Receptivity to public affairs information (breadth and depth)
description: Receptivity was captured with two dimensions from the insurance executive survey. Breadth was measured as the number of outside stakeholder groups with whom company executives claimed to spend at least one day a month, and depth was measured as the average length of time generally spent on any particular public affairs issue. Responses were aggregated at the company level for the seven participating insurers.

The executive survey measured the degree of integration of public affairs information by asking about the frequency of use of task forces and about how well established steering committees in public affairs were in the organization. Both items were scored on a 5-point Likert scale, and there was a moderate positive correlation between the two dimensions. Company-level means were used in the analysis.

The insurance executive survey measured the degree of integration of public affairs information by asking about the frequency of use of task forces and about how well established steering committees in public affairs were in the organization. Both items were scored on a 5-point Likert scale, and there was a moderate positive correlation between the two dimensions. Company-level means were used in the analysis.

The executive survey measured the influence of public affairs through the importance of public affairs in terms of the time and attention of the CEO, in terms of the time and attention of the board of directors, and for the respondents' career advancement potential. In addition, the authors computed a total influence score, an average of the importance of public affairs in terms of decision making in different parts of the company, which also included the annual planning process, performance appraisals, career paths, and training programs. Each influence item was rated on a 5-point Likert-type scale ranging from not very important to extremely important, and the items were well correlated with each other.
scale: 5-point Likert-type scale (not very important to extremely important)

description: The insurance executive survey measured the influence of public affairs through the importance of public affairs in terms of the time and attention of the CEO, in terms of the time and attention of the board of directors, and for the respondents' career advancement potential. In addition, the authors computed a total influence score, an average of the importance of public affairs in terms of decision making in different parts of the company, which also included the annual planning process, performance appraisals, career paths, and training programs. Each influence item was rated on a 5-point Likert-type scale ranging from not very important to extremely important, and the items were well correlated with each other.
scale: 5-point Likert-type scale (not very important to extremely important)

description: Stakeholder respondents rated the six participating forest products firms along with the 20 largest firms in the industry on a general question of social responsiveness, on a 5-point Likert-type scale ranging from 1 = poor to 5 = excellent. The general measure was highly correlated with seven other, more precise components of corporate social performance and with the average of those component dimensions. Company ratings were formed from the stakeholder questionnaires returned by the panel of 150 forest-industry stakeholders.

In the survey, insurance commissioners picked, from a list of the 25 largest insurance corporations, the firms they considered to be the industry's 'five best' and 'five worst' social performers. Social performance scores were computed by expressing the number of commissioners who nominated each company in each category as a percentage of the total number of responding commissioners and taking the difference between the percentage of best-five nominations and the percentage of worst-five nominations. Questionnaires were received from 34 of the commissioners surveyed.

The primary dependent variable, referring to the source of IS services a bank adopts. Banks usually choose one of six major sources of IS services, plus an 'other' category; all but in-house computer operations and an IS subsidiary at the parent bank were classified as IS outsourcing, and use of in-house IS services was considered insourcing. In the logistic model the dependent variable is the probability of choosing to outsource IS services in preference to insourcing. Responses from banks that relied on their parent banks or bank holding companies for IS services were discarded.

Institutional influence arising from peer banks, assessed by the informant for his or her bank. Items were measured on 7-point Likert scales, factor analysis confirmed a single-factor structure, and the items were summed into a total-score measure for the construct.

Institutional influence arising from federal examiners, such as the Federal Reserve Bank and the Office of the Comptroller of Currency, assessed by the informant for his or her bank. Items were measured on 7-point Likert scales, factor analysis confirmed a single-factor structure, and the items were summed into a total-score measure for the construct.

The degree to which an external service provider is perceived to have an advantage in production cost economies over internal bureaucratic management of IS services. Production cost was operationalized as hardware costs, software costs, and personnel costs. Items were measured on 7-point Likert scales and summed into a total-score measure after confirming a single-factor structure.

The level of working capital, measured as the amount of financial resources available for IS relative to past years' resources and peer banks' resources allocated for IS. Items were measured on 7-point Likert scales and summed into a total-score measure.

The degree to which investments in IS yielded unique value to any single firm. The construct was operationalized as the level of investment in specialized equipment, the level of specialized technical skills specific to the needs of a particular bank, and the level of specific business skills and knowledge pertaining to a particular bank; items were measured on 7-point Likert scales and summed into a total-score measure.

The rapid and unexpected change in IT developments. It was operationalized as the degree to which a bank can forecast accurately its technical requirements as well as the degree to which a bank can anticipate IT obsolescence; items were measured on 7-point Likert scales and summed into a total-score measure.

The degree of formal structural differentiation within the organization, in the context of the IS function. It was operationalized as an overall assessment of the degree of complexity in managing IS operations, the number of hardware platforms and systems configurations, and the degree of sophistication of the software portfolio; items were measured on 7-point Likert scales and summed into a total-score measure.

The availability of reputable and trustworthy external IT service providers in the market. It was operationalized by the perceived presence of adequate service providers and the ability to find comparable providers to replace the services of a current one; items were measured on 7-point Likert scales and summed into a total-score measure.

Size is represented by a dichotomous variable, zero for small banks and one for large banks. Small banks are those with assets less than $1 billion and large banks are those with assets of at least $1 billion. Banks with more than $1 billion in assets were reclassified as large banks and those with less than $1 billion as small banks.

Dummy variable equal to one if a Japanese parent owned more than 5% but less than 95% of the subsidiary equity (i.e., if it had a joint venture stake), and equal to zero otherwise (a wholly-owned stake). Information on this variable was collected from secondary sources and phone surveys.

variable_name: duration (in years) of a Japanese parent stake
description: The dependent variable is the duration (in years) of a Japanese parent stake in a U.S. subsidiary. For exit cases, the duration is the difference between the ending (exit) year and the starting (establishment) year; for censored cases it is the number of years between establishment in the United States and 1991, the cutoff point. The first model analyzes the determinants of gross terminations, defined as withdrawals from the United States due to liquidation/bankruptcy and selloffs.

Two types of exits are recorded, liquidations and sales; liquidation means that subsidiaries were closed, liquidated, or went bankrupt. In the second, competing risk model the dependent variable is termination through liquidation, while selloffs are treated as censored.

A stake that is sold to either the partnering firm or a third party is recorded as a sale. In the third, competing risk model the dependent variable is selloff, while liquidations are treated as censored.

It is the log of EXP, the number of years elapsed between a Japanese parent's first entry into the United States and the year of establishment of a particular subsidiary. EXP is expressed in logs because the authors assume that an additional year of U.S. market experience has a diminishing impact on affiliate survival.
time_window: at time of establishment of the affiliate

description: Dummy variable equal to one if the products manufactured by the subsidiary were different from those of the parent, and equal to zero otherwise. Data was obtained from various Japanese company directories.
time_window: at time of establishment of the affiliate

description: Dummy variable equal to one if the affiliate was established through an acquisition, and equal to zero in the case of greenfield investment.
time_window: at time of establishment of the affiliate

description: Annual growth rate of shipments of the U.S. 4 digit SIC industry entered by Japanese affiliates from 1980 to the year of status change or the censoring year in the case of no change. Following Kogut (1991), it is the percentage growth rate of shipments between year t and year t - 1. The variable was entered as a time-varying covariate with a one-year lag.
time_window: 1980 to year of status change or censoring, one-year lag

description: Number of employees of the parent company at the time of its establishment of its U.S. affiliate. Data was obtained from the Nikkei database and other Japanese company directories.
time_window: at time of establishment of the affiliate

description: Age of the affiliate in 1980 when it became at risk.

Binary variable equal to one if the firm is classified as having pre-entry experience, and zero if the firm is a startup. Pre-entry experience was determined by matching each firm in the IDC database with its corresponding information in the Thomas Register: if a firm was listed in the index volumes of the Thomas Register for the year preceding its entry into personal computers, it was classified as a diversifying entrant. Firms that did not appear in these sources before their inclusion in the IDC database were classified as startups (almost 75% of the firms in the sample).

variable_name: Only Technical Exp., Only Market Exp., Technical & Market Exp., Other Exp.
description: A set of mutually exclusive binary variables classifying the pre-entry experience of diversifying entrants using Thomas Register information on the primary line of business. Firms with only technical experience are those in related product markets and/or technology markets (13% of the firms in the sample); firms with only market experience have knowledge of the potential customers for personal computers (6%); firms with both technical and market experience (5%) include IBM, NCR and Everex Systems.

Dependent variable is the timing of firm exit from the personal computer industry. A firm is considered to have exited in year t if its unit sales for years t+1 to 1994 were zero; otherwise the firm exit date was coded as a right-censored observation. The few multibusiness corporations that exited were treated as failures, and acquisitions were infrequent and left the acquired firm operating as a distinct entity.
A firm's entry time into the personal computer industry, defined to be the year in which the firm first sold a personal computer (less 1973). Higher values indicate later entry.

Equal to one if the firm ever introduced a personal computer with a microprocessor involving the Intel x86 architecture, and zero otherwise. Used to capture whether or not a firm offers products incorporating the technology standard during its tenure in the industry.
time_window: during firm tenure in the industry

variable_name: Cumulative Time in Market Without Intel x86
description: The cumulative number of years (up to the prior year) a firm does not offer a personal computer with the Intel x86 CPU. It equals zero for time periods before 1979 when the Intel x86 technology was unavailable and for time periods after the firm introduces a product with the Intel x86 technology, or if the firm never introduces the technology.

variable_name: Startup Entering With Intel x86 / Diversifying Entrant Entering With Intel x86 / Startup Not Entering With Intel x86
description: A mutually exclusive set of binary variables involving pre-entry experience and whether the firm entered with the Intel x86 technology. The baseline category is diversifying entrants not entering with the Intel x86 technology. These variables are used to test the hypotheses about early entrants.

Equal to one if the firm ever introduced a personal computer using the newest (most advanced) microprocessor technology at the time, and zero otherwise. The definition of 'newest technology' changes dynamically as successive generations become available.
time_window: during firm tenure in the industry

variable_name: Cumulative Number of Newest Product Technology Generations Ever Offered
description: The cumulative number, up to the prior year, of the newest technology generations offered by the firm, used to capture dynamic experience effects of offering the latest technology.

variable_name: Startup Entering With Newest Technology / Diversifying Entrant Entering With Newest Technology / Diversifying Entrant Not Entering With Newest Technology
description: A mutually exclusive set of binary variables involving pre-entry experience and whether the firm entered with the newest technology. The baseline category is startups not entering with the newest technology. These variables are used to test the hypotheses about later entrants.

Binary indicator for the exploration treatment group: subjects are told they will be paid 50% of the profits they make during the last 10 periods of the 20-period experiment. The exploration contract combines tolerance for early failure in the first 10 periods with reward for long-term success in the last 10 periods.
Binary indicator for the fixed-wage treatment group: subjects are told they will be paid a fixed wage of 50 francs per period, independently of the profits they produce.

Binary indicator for the pay-for-performance treatment group: subjects are told they will be paid 50% of the profits they make during the 20 periods of the experiment, so compensation depends on performance from the very first period.

Binary indicator for the termination treatment group: subjects receive the exploration contract and are told that if the profits they make during the first 10 periods are below 800 francs the experiment will end after 10 periods.

Binary indicator for the golden parachute treatment group: subjects receive the exploration contract and are told that if their profits during the first 10 periods are below 800 francs the experiment will end early and they will receive a payment of 250 francs.

After subjects completed the experiment their degree of risk aversion was elicited in a separate experiment. For the statistical analysis subjects are split into a less and a more risk-averse group based on the median observation for each measure in the sample.

Binary dependent variable that takes the value 1 if the subject's final location choice is the school, which is the highest-profit location in the experiment, and 0 otherwise. The authors compare the proportion of subjects choosing the school in the final period across contracts, and also assess how close subjects come to the optimal strategy using the maximum per-period profit achieved by a subject and final-period profit.

variable_name: location choice other than the default location
description: Exploration is measured by whether a subject chooses a location other than the default location (the business district) in a period; the authors report the proportion of such choices in the first and the last 10 periods. They also use the subject-specific standard deviation of the three continuous choice variables (sugar content, lemon content, price) and the hazard rate of ending an explorative phase, which begins when a subject first chooses a location other than the default location and ends when the subject makes only small changes to strategy choices or switches back to the default.
scale: proportion of period choices; standard deviation of strategy choices

variable_name: time spent on the decision screen
description: Effort is measured by the time a subject spends on the decision screen, where subjects enter their strategy choices, and by the effort of recording previous choices and outcomes in the table provided in the instructions. The authors report whether subjects fill out half or more of the fields in the decision record table.
scale: seconds; proportion of subjects completing more than half of the fields
time_window: over the entire experiment and in subperiods

description: Overall performance is measured by the average profit a subject earns per period in the lemonade stand game, expressed in francs. The authors also report the maximum per-period profit achieved by a subject and the subject's final-period profit.

Entropy measure proposed by Jacquemin and Berry (1979). DT is calculated as the sum over industries i of Pi ln(1/Pi), where Pi is the proportion of a firm's sales in industry i at the four-digit Standard Industrial Classification (SIC) level.
Related diversification is equal to total diversification minus unrelated diversification (DR = DT minus DU), where unrelated diversification is computed from sales at the two-digit SIC level.
Entropy measure calculated as the sum over industries i of Pi ln(1/Pi), where Pi is the proportion of a firm's sales in industry i at the two-digit SIC level.

Diversity of nonprofit organizations to which a firm donates, drawing on the concept of heterogeneity.
