It is calculated using Blau's (1977) index of heterogeneity, 1 minus the sum over categories j of Kj squared, where K represents the proportion of types of nonprofits within a category of secondary stakeholders and j is the number of different secondary stakeholder categories with which firms associate. The authors illustrate that a value close to 0 implies firms mainly associate with only a few categories, while a high value implies association with a broad range of nonprofits evenly.

Ratio of earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization (EBITDA) to total assets. The authors followed Kacperczyk (2009) and controlled for the tax effect because the study involves philanthropic donations and the tax deduction for donations could bias a firm's net income.

Three items taken from the threat subscale of Thomas and McDaniel's (1990) larger 15-item threat-opportunity scale, selected on the basis of face validity as the most characteristic items from the positive-negative, loss-gain, and controllable-uncontrollable portions of that scale. Scale values were the item average. Collected in the first questionnaire.

Three items taken from the opportunity subscale of Thomas and McDaniel's (1990) larger 15-item threat-opportunity scale, selected on the basis of face validity as the most characteristic items from the positive-negative, loss-gain, and controllable-uncontrollable portions of that scale. Scale values were the item average. Collected in the first questionnaire.

A three-item measure constructed as a subscale of three items drawn from two sources, Ginsberg and Venkatraman (1995) and Denison et al. (1996), with items selected on content and face validity logic as the ones most characteristic of the construct. Scale values were the item average. Collected in the first questionnaire.

A two-item measure drawn from Dutton et al. (1990), with the items judged most characteristic of urgency selected for inclusion. Scale values were the item average. Collected in the first questionnaire.

One of three factors emerging from a principal-components factor analysis with oblimin rotation of the 12 threat-opportunity and feasibility-urgency interpretation items, using a factor loading cut-off of 0.50. The factor consists of two opportunity items, positive and gain, and is interpreted as the extent to which a firm's response to a strategic issue will result in a positive gain. Scale values were the item average.

One of three factors emerging from a principal-components factor analysis with oblimin rotation of the 12 threat-opportunity and feasibility-urgency interpretation items, using a factor loading cut-off of 0.50. The factor contains the three feasibility items and two items concerning controllability, and is interpreted as the perceived capacity of the organization to respond to a strategic issue. Scale values were the item average.

variable_name: Intended external and intended internal response
description: Informants reported the extent to which firm executives intended to make changes in each area, adapting the measure of response originally employed by Glick et al. (1990) and later used by Chattopadhyay et al. (2001). Five items measure responses of an external nature and eight items measure responses of an internal nature. Scale values were the item average. Collected in the first questionnaire.

variable_name: Actual external and actual internal response
description: The same 13 items used for intended response, administered in the second survey mailed four months after the first, asking about the degree to which firms actually responded to the issue of economic uncertainty rather than what they intended to do. Five items cover external responses and eight items internal responses; scale values were the item average.
time_window: second questionnaire, mailed 4 months after the first

description: The response variables are reported in the descriptive statistics table with their means, standard deviations, reliabilities and zero-order correlations with the other study variables and the controls.

The integrated structure is assessed by a principal components factor analysis with oblimin rotation (loading cut-off 0.50) of the 12 threat-opportunity and feasibility-urgency interpretation items. Three factors emerged (influence, urgency, favorability) and are matched to the three expectancy-instrumentality-valence components.

An index based on responses to three hypothetical occupational income gambles, following Barsky, Juster, Kimball, and Shapiro (1997). Participants were asked the income gamble questions in the 1993, 2002, 2004, and 2006 surveys, and the authors constructed a time-varying measure: responses from the 1993 survey were used from 1994 to 2002, the 2002 responses until 2004, the 2004 responses until 2006, and the 2006 responses until 2008. The index is calculated as the degree to which the expected value of the payoff must be greater than the value of the absolute certain payoff in order for the respondent to accept the gamble.
time_window: time-varying; 1993, 2002, 2004 and 2006 survey responses applied through 2008

description: Measured with 12 questions from the NLSY79, following Judge and Hurst (2007, 2008). Because the NLSY79 does not include a measure of CSE, these questions were selected because they reflect the 12 items on the CSE scale developed by Judge et al. (2003). The authors state the measure demonstrates high construct validity, content validity, discriminant validity, and reliability. CSE is time invariant.

Event indicator in the competing-risks model for the transition from a paid job into hybrid entrepreneurship. By comparing job start and stop dates, the authors determine whether any participant held two jobs simultaneously (i.e., if a new job begins before an existing job ends), which allows them to identify true hybrids. Participants who remained at their paid job at the end of the survey window, exited their paid job to take another paid job, or entered unemployment were treated as right censored.

Event indicator in the competing-risks model for the transition from a paid job directly into full-time self-employment. Participants who started a self-employed business within a three-month window of exiting their paid job were treated as entering full-time self-employment, and the authors report that results are robust to shorter and longer windows. Participants who remained at their paid job, exited to another paid job, or entered unemployment were treated as right censored.

A dummy variable indicating whether a participant transitioned into full-time self-employment from hybrid entrepreneurship ('1' = transition occurred). Participants who transitioned to full-time self-employment directly from paid work (i.e., direct entry) were coded as '0'.

For those who entered full-time self-employment from hybrid entrepreneurship (i.e., staged entry = '1'), the amount of time, measured in years, each participant spent in hybrid entrepreneurship immediately prior to transitioning into full-time self-employment. Participants who transitioned to full-time self-employment directly from paid work were coded as '0'.

The amount of time a participant survives in a full-time self-employed job before exit. For participants who transitioned into full-time self-employment from hybrid entrepreneurship, survival time does not include the time spent as a hybrid entrepreneur. Because entrepreneurs who hold a secondary paid job are able to persist for longer periods in self-employment, participants who began a secondary paid job were treated as if they exited full-time self-employment, and participants who remained in their self-employed job at the end of the survey window were treated as right censored.

Measured with the Armed Forces Qualifications Test (AFQT), which measures quantitative and verbal skills. Prior studies have demonstrated the AFQT to be a reliable measure (alpha > .9), correlating highly (.95 or higher) with the g factor, an alternative measure of cognitive ability, and stable over time. Cognitive ability is time invariant.

The cumulative number of businesses started as a full-time self-employed entrepreneur, following recent research (e.g., Eesley & Roberts, 2012; Toft-Kehler et al., 2014). The authors followed Folta et al. (2010) and differentiated between full-time self-employment experience and experience as a hybrid entrepreneur.

The cumulative number of businesses started as a hybrid entrepreneur, that is, while also holding a paid job. This variable was constructed by differentiating hybrid entrepreneurship experience from full-time self-employment experience, following Folta et al. (2010).

The duration of the participant's most recent prior full-time self-employment spell. It was used together with the count of prior businesses started as an alternative measure of entrepreneurial experience.

The duration of the participant's most recent prior hybrid entrepreneurship spell. It was used together with the count of prior hybrid businesses started as an alternative measure of hybrid entrepreneurship experience.

Firms indicated the stage of companies they primarily targeted in their investments using five gradations that, in increasing order of investment maturity, are seed stage, early stage, expansion stage, mezzanine stage, and late stage. The variable takes integer values from 1 to 5, with 1 indicating the earliest-stage companies and 5 indicating late-stage (mature prepublic) companies.

For the performance model the stage variable was captured by two dummy variables rather than the linear stage variable. The early stage dummy variable had a value of 1 for firms that focused on the seed or early stages, and the later stage dummy had a value of 1 for firms that focused on the expansion, mezzanine, or late stages.

The ratio of the number of principals to the number of GPs (P/GP), used as the main dependent variable. Firms that had no principals have a P/GP ratio of 0, so the variable was analysed as the logarithm of (P/GP) + 1 in the core model and as the square root of P/GP in an alternative model. An alternative dependent variable, PA/GP, uses the ratio of the numbers of principals and associates to the number of GPs.

variable_name: Leverage × early stage and Leverage × later stage
description: To test whether counter-pyramidal early-stage firms outperformed pyramidal firms, a leverage × early-stage variable was created, the coefficient of which was expected to be negative. To test whether pyramidal later-stage firms outperformed counter-pyramidal firms, a leverage × later-stage variable was created, the coefficient of which was expected to be positive.
time_window: lagged one and two years relative to the structure data

description: The internal rate of return reported for each fund, used as the dependent variable in the performance models. Because performance data tend to be erratic and overly negative during VC funds' early years, performance data were used only for funds that were at least five years old, and were lagged by one and two years relative to the data on firm structure.
time_window: lagged one and two years relative to the structure data

description: Ownership share (votes) of the largest owner, taken from the 1990 ownership database. The authors report that on average the largest owner controls 39 percent of the votes and that shares of the largest owner are fairly evenly distributed over the 0-100 percent scale. Ownership structure is assumed to be stable over the sample period.

Categorical variable recording the identity of the largest owner, distinguishing the five ownership categories identified in the theory section: banks, institutional investors, (other nonfinancial) companies, personal/family, and government.

Market-to-book value of equity, one of three performance measures used in the study. The authors note that market-to-book values are only available for companies with quoted shares, and that stock prices give the stock market expectation of the long-term effects on profitability.
Return on assets, which the authors describe as measuring current accounting profitability more than expected future earnings. It is one of the three performance measures used in the study.
Growth of sales (turnover), one of the three performance measures used in the study.
Company performance is measured by three variables: market-to-book value of equity, return on assets, and sales growth. Each is used as a separate dependent variable in the ownership share models.

The percentage of segment pairs in firm i's portfolio in year t-1 that supplied significant inputs to one another. The flow of inputs between two industries is defined as significant if they, on average, contribute more than one percent of the inputs to one another; one percent was used in the main analyses. It is constructed from the BEA Input-Output 'Use' Tables, converted to SIC industries through an IO-SIC concordance, and is lagged by one year.

The degree to which firm i's primary industry, j, shares inputs with a target industry, k, following Fan and Lang (2000). It is calculated as the correlation coefficient across industry input structures between the amounts of intermediate inputs that two industries directly require per dollar of their respective output. A large correlation coefficient suggests a significant overlap in inputs required by the two industries.
time_window: 1992 IO Tables, held constant across the sample period

description: Equals 1 when firm i diversified from its primary industry j into industry k in year t, and 0 otherwise. Any industry k in which firm i did not operate in the previous year (t-1) was treated as a potential target destination industry in the current year (t); among the target industries, those that firm i did operate in year t were entries and coded as 1.

Each hospital's cumulative prior experience performing PTCA, calculated on a quarterly basis dating back to January 1999 and lagged one quarter relative to the quarter in which the current patient's procedure was performed. For example, for a patient receiving PTCA in a New Jersey hospital in March 2004, Experience equals the total number of PTCAs performed by the hospital from January 1999 through December 2003. Lagging captures the hospital's experience prior to the focal quarter.
time_window: counts from January 1999 onward; lagged one quarter

description: A patient-level indicator equals one if a patient required a rework procedure while in the hospital, where procedures were classified as rework if the patient required a coronary artery bypass graft following PTCA or received a repeat PTCA procedure on a subsequent day. Predicted values from a logistic regression of this indicator on patient risk factors (demographics, severity proxies, and Elixhauser comorbidity indicators) are averaged within hospital-quarter to create a predicted rework rate, which is combined with the hospital's observed rework rate (total rework cases divided by total PTCA patients in the period). The average rework rate across all hospitals during the study period is used to normalize and center the risk-adjusted rate; the exact algebraic form is not readable in the text extraction. Lower values indicate better performance.

A categorical variable with three levels constructed from classifications in the AHA annual survey: no academic affiliation (Academic0), non-COTH medical school affiliation (Academic1), and COTH membership, i.e., academic medical centers (Academic2). In the models, these variables are lagged by one year to improve causal identification.

The number of interns (observational training during medical school) and residents (supervised, hands-on, post-medical school training) per hospital bed, derived from the AHA annual survey. The authors state that this variable is commonly used in the medical and health services research fields to capture teaching intensity in hospitals and captures the extent to which each organization is engaged in coaching and mentoring in regular work settings; it is lagged by one year.

Ownership was measured as the stock owned by the CEO divided by total common shares outstanding as reported in 1992; because stock options granted to CEOs may also contribute to the degree of insider ownership, the stock options to CEOs were incorporated into the measure. The focus was on the CEO because most of the agency theory literature treats this individual as the primary source of agency problems. CEO stock ownership and the industry dummy were transformed by subtracting their respective mean values, and the interaction term was obtained from the transformed variables.

A dummy variable coded 1 for higher dynamism firms and 0 for lower dynamism firms. Industry dynamism was assessed by regressing values of industry shipments against time over 5 years and dividing the standard error of the beta coefficient of the time dummy by the average value of shipments for that industry, producing standardized indices of environmental dynamism for 42 4-digit SIC code industries; industry segments were then aggregated at the 2-digit SIC level to produce an adequate sample size. Firms were drawn from the food and beverage industry and the computer and electronics industry, which were found to differ significantly on the dynamism indices.

One of four return-related performance variables selected because the research concerned ways to align the interests of owners and managers. Return on assets is widely used in strategic management and financial management studies examining the relationship between owners and managers. The measure was averaged over the four years between 1990 and 1993.

One of four return-related performance variables selected because the research concerned ways to align the interests of owners and managers. Return on equity is widely used in strategic management and financial management studies examining the relationship between owners and managers. The measure was averaged over the four years between 1990 and 1993.

One of four return-related performance variables selected because the research concerned ways to align the interests of owners and managers. Return on investment is widely used in strategic management and financial management studies examining the relationship between owners and managers. The measure was averaged over the four years between 1990 and 1993.

The measure was developed by Barton (1988) and is operating income divided by the book value of a firm's total assets. As constructed for this study it was a control for systematic risk and monopoly power; it taps earnings before debt charges and their tax effects, allowing examination of managerial contribution to firm performance without the confounding effects of a firm's leverage and the impact of debt holders. The measure was averaged over the four years between 1990 and 1993.

Number of corporate officers who were also board members in each firm for each year. Firms with only one inside board member were excluded because power distribution measures are not meaningful in such organizations. The average size of the top management teams so defined was 3.39, with a standard deviation of 1.46.

An overall index of power created by averaging the standardized coefficients of variation for each of ten indicators of power over all top team members in each firm in each year. When the coefficient of variation is high, power is unevenly concentrated in a firm's CEO, so CEO dominance is high; when it is low, the distribution of power is balanced. The percentage-with-higher-titles item was reversed in computing the index.

Composite measure of firm performance created by standardizing and averaging three indicators: return on assets, return on sales, and return on equity. Correlations among these performance measures ranged from .75 to .89, and the global measure yielded a Cronbach alpha of .93.

Dummy variable coding firms in the computer industry as 1 and firms in the natural gas distribution industry as 0. The computer industry was classified as the turbulent environment because it is characterized by continuous product innovation, high growth rates, and high product differentiation, and the natural gas distribution industry as the stable environment because it is governed by regulations controlling pricing and capital acquisition. The classification was confirmed by comparing indicators of turbulence-stability, performance risk and demand instability, both of which were significantly greater in the computer industry.

Dummy variable coding firms in the computer industry as 1 (the high-discretion environment) and firms in the natural gas distribution industry as 0 (the low-discretion environment). An index of five environmental discretion indicators from Hambrick and Finkelstein (1987) — average advertising intensity, average R&D intensity, average annual sales growth, the standard deviation of annual sales growth, and the degree of regulation — was standardized and averaged, with the regulation indicator reverse-scored, yielding a Cronbach alpha of .80. The index scored .54 in the computer industry and -.63 in the gas industry, supporting the classification of the two industries.

Coded as '1' if the firm experiences a CEO dismissal in a given year, and as '0' for firms with no CEO succession events or a routine CEO succession event in a given year. CEO succession events were identified from Booz Allen and Hamilton annual surveys and Wall Street Journal 'Who's News' listings and verified through company announcements in the business press. Each succession was classified with a detailed investigative method that examined the company's succession announcement and news articles on the company up to one year prior to the event, so that direct firings as well as forced resignations are captured. Coding was validated by comparing the date the departure was announced, the date the new CEO was appointed and the date the new CEO took office, with dismissals showing a substantial gap (three months, on average) between departure and the announcement of a replacement.

The mean analyst recommendation for all investment analysts who cover a firm in the six-month period, built from monthly mean recommendations from I/B/E/S. On the I/B/E/S five-point scale a higher score means a lower recommendation (1 = strong buy, 5 = sell), so the monthly mean recommendation was reverse coded by subtracting it from six so that a higher score means a higher recommendation. Because the number of analysts covering a firm varies over time, the monthly mean recommendations were weighted by the number of analysts providing coverage in each month to form a weighted average. The measure ranges from 2.18 to 5 with a mean of 3.76 in the sample. The analysis uses the residual from a regression of this measure on firm size, industry-adjusted ROA and prior industry-adjusted stock return as the proxy.

Measured as the difference between the average analyst recommendation in the six-month period immediately prior to the month in which CEO succession occurred (t-1 to t-6) and the average analyst recommendation in the six-month period seven months prior to that month (t-7 to t-12). Because the recommendations were reverse coded so that a higher score means a higher recommendation, a negative value indicates a downgrade, a zero indicates no change, and a positive value indicates an upgrade. The measure ranges from -2 to 1.5 with a mean of -0.04 in the sample. The residual from the first-stage regression is used as the proxy in the analysis.
time_window: six-month periods t-1 to t-6 versus t-7 to t-12

description: Measured as the weighted average percentage of analyst recommendations in the six-month period that are rated either as underperform (4) or sell (5) on the I/B/E/S scale. The monthly percentages of sell recommendations were weighted by the number of analysts who provide firm coverage in each of the six months. The measure ranges from 0 to 0.66 with a mean of 0.05 in the sample. The residual from the first-stage regression is used as the proxy in the analysis.

Measured as a firm's return on assets in the prior year minus the median firm ROA (excluding the focal firm) in the firm's core industry (two-digit Standard Industrial Classification code) in the prior year. Data for this variable were gathered from COMPUSTAT.

Measured by the firm's total return to shareholders minus the median stock return (excluding the focal firm) of firms in the focal firm's core two-digit industry. The industry-adjusted stock return was measured for the same six-month period as that used to calculate the analyst recommendation measures. Data used to calculate this variable were gathered from the Center for Research in Security Prices.
time_window: six months (the same period as the analyst recommendation measures)

description: Each analyst recommendation measure was split into two variables: a pre-litigation measure capturing the value of the specific analyst measure for the years 2000-2002 and a value of '0' otherwise, and a post-litigation measure capturing the value for the years 2003-2005 and a value of '0' otherwise. The imposition of a $100 million fine on Merrill Lynch in May of 2002 is used as the point in time that captures the shift in investment analyst credibility in the financial community. The coefficients for the pre-litigation and post-litigation analyst measures were compared using the Wald chi-square test statistic.

A time-varying dichotomous outcome measure coded 1 in a year in which a new CEO was dismissed and 0 otherwise. Two research assistants collected all news reports on each newly appointed CEO from the year of succession to three years after the succession from the Dow Jones databases; these reports and annual corporate proxy statements were used to check whether the CEO was still in office three years after succession and to date departures. Circumstances of departure were classified as dismissal or voluntary turnover using an approach adapted from Shen and Cannella (2002a), yielding 26 new CEO dismissals; a CEO was dropped from the sample after leaving office.
time_window: from the year of succession to three years after the succession

description: Coded 1 for new CEOs who had firm tenure of less than two years when assuming office and 0 otherwise. The primary data sources for new CEO origin were the Dun & Bradstreet Reference Book of Corporate Management, annual corporate proxy statements, and news reports.
time_window: at the time of assuming office

description: A dummy variable coded 1 for firms with an independent nominating committee on which the number of outside directors was larger than that of inside directors, and 0 otherwise. Whether the firm had a nominating committee was checked from the corporate proxy statements in the year prior to succession. The coefficient represents the comparison of this group of firms with firms that had no nominating committee.

A dummy variable coded 1 for firms with a nonindependent nominating committee on which the number of outside directors was equal to or less than the number of inside directors, and 0 otherwise. The coefficient represents the comparison of this group of firms with firms that had no nominating committee.

variable_name: Nominating committee with more external directorships
description: Coded 1 if the firm had a nominating committee on which the average number of external directorships of the outside directors was larger than the sample median (1.75, excluding the focal firm's board) and 0 otherwise. The coefficient represents the comparison of this group of firms with firms that had no nominating committee.

variable_name: Nominating committee with fewer external directorships
description: Coded 1 if the firm had a nominating committee on which the average number of external directorships of the outside directors was equal to or smaller than the sample median and 0 otherwise. The coefficient represents the comparison of this group of firms with firms that had no nominating committee.

Coded 1 if the predecessor CEO was dismissed and 0 otherwise. The circumstance in which the predecessor CEO left office was identified following a procedure similar to the one used to identify new CEO dismissals.

Dichotomous variable produced by the partitioning around medoids clustering (pamk function) of each participant's 49 variables: 7 percentages of thinking time spent in each of the seven problem-solving phases and 42 normalized between-phase transitions. It assigns each participant to one of two clusters; the clustering grouped 28 participants into the problem-focused strategy and 20 into the solution-focused strategy. In the analyses it is coded −1 for the problem-focused strategy and 1 for the solution-focused strategy.

Dichotomous variable produced by the partitioning around medoids clustering (pamk function) of each participant's 49 variables: 7 percentages of thinking time spent in each of the seven problem-solving phases and 42 normalized between-phase transitions. It assigns each participant to one of two clusters; 20 participants were grouped into the solution-focused strategy and 28 into the problem-focused strategy. In the analyses it is coded 1 for the solution-focused strategy and −1 for the problem-focused strategy.

Indicator for the treatment condition in which participants were asked, after the winter survival task and before the NASA survival task, to analyze the problem by recalling the available information, empathizing to identify with the situation, and developing hypotheses or assumptions to understand the problem. The manipulation was shown as text in a red font, and the description of the mental activities was taken directly from the coding scheme used in Study 1. The control condition forms the baseline, and dichotomous variables are stored with contrast coding (1 and −1).
scale: contrast coded (1 = framing disposition condition, −1 = control)

description: Indicator for the treatment condition in which participants were asked to design a sequence of actions that could unfold during the solution of the problem, anticipate how events would evolve, and evaluate the feasibility of the solution. The manipulation was shown as text in a red font, and the description of the mental activities was taken directly from the coding scheme used in Study 1. The control condition forms the baseline, and dichotomous variables are stored with contrast coding (1 and −1).
scale: contrast coded (1 = implementation disposition condition, −1 = control)

variable_name: Change in number of moves, s.d.
description: Number of drag-and-drop moves the participant made, used as a proxy for the number of thoughts engaged in during problem solving; the NASA survival problem imposes a lower bound of 15 moves and the winter survival problem 12 moves. The change score is the standardized value of a participant in the NASA survival task minus the standardized value in the winter survival task, with standardization in units of standard deviation from the mean of the control condition after the manipulation.
time_window: change from the winter survival task (before manipulation) to the NASA survival task (after manipulation)

variable_name: Change in time per move, s.d.
description: Time per move is the time between the first and last moves divided by the number of moves and measures the amount of deliberation involved in each thought. The change score is the standardized value of a participant in the NASA survival task minus the standardized value in the winter survival task, with standardization in units of standard deviation from the mean of the control condition after the manipulation.
time_window: change from the winter survival task (before manipulation) to the NASA survival task (after manipulation)

description: Total time spent on the task, which reflects the total effort and attention participants put into the task as it includes both the time spent reading the task and moving the items to create a ranking. The change score is the standardized value of a participant in the NASA survival task minus the standardized value in the winter survival task, with standardization in units of standard deviation from the mean of the control condition after the manipulation.
time_window: change from the winter survival task (before manipulation) to the NASA survival task (after manipulation)

description: Indicator for the treatment condition in which participants were asked, after the winter survival task and before the NASA survival task, to analyze the problem by recalling the available information, empathizing to identify with the situation, and developing hypotheses or assumptions to understand the problem. Study 3 replicated Study 2 with the same tasks, manipulations, measures, and analyses, and added preregistration and pandemic control variables. The control condition forms the baseline.
scale: contrast coded (1 = framing disposition condition, −1 = control)

description: Indicator for the treatment condition in which participants were asked to design a sequence of actions that could unfold during the solution of the problem, anticipate how events would evolve, and evaluate the feasibility of the solution. Study 3 replicated Study 2 with the same tasks, manipulations, measures, and analyses, and added preregistration and pandemic control variables. The control condition forms the baseline.
scale: contrast coded (1 = implementation disposition condition, −1 = control)

variable_name: Change in number of moves, s.d.
description: Number of drag-and-drop moves the participant made, used as a proxy for the number of thoughts engaged in during problem solving; the NASA survival problem imposes a lower bound of 15 moves and the winter survival problem 12 moves. The change score is the standardized value of a participant in the NASA survival task minus the standardized value in the winter survival task, with standardization in units of standard deviation from the mean of the control condition after the manipulation, and it is regressed on the treatments plus demographic and pandemic controls.
time_window: change from the winter survival task (before manipulation) to the NASA survival task (after manipulation)

variable_name: Change in time per move, s.d.
description: Time per move is the time between the first and last moves divided by the number of moves and measures the amount of deliberation involved in each thought. The change score is the standardized value of a participant in the NASA survival task minus the standardized value in the winter survival task, with standardization in units of standard deviation from the mean of the control condition after the manipulation, and it is regressed on the treatments plus demographic and pandemic controls.
time_window: change from the winter survival task (before manipulation) to the NASA survival task (after manipulation)

description: Measured in terms of an offensive team's choice of play on a fourth down and coded as a binary variable: 0 = no risk taking (the team punted or attempted a field goal on the fourth down) and 1 = risk taking (the team attempted a fourth-down conversion). Punting and kicking the ball were treated equally as less risky alternatives because the choice between the two alternatives is primarily determined by field location rather than performance and because it was unclear whether one of the two alternatives is riskier than the other.

Built from performance, measured as the difference between the focal team's score and the opposing team's score plus one point. A spline function was created: performance at or below the aspiration level equals 0 when performance is above the aspiration level and equals performance minus aspiration when performance is at or below it. A squared term was also included to allow for the proposed curvilinear nature of the performance-risk relationship, together with an indicator variable allowing the curve to jump at the aspiration level.

Equals 0 when performance is at or below the aspiration level and equals performance minus aspiration when performance is above it; performance is measured as the difference between the focal team's score and the opposing team's score plus one point.

Measured as the number of minutes and seconds remaining to play the game at the time of each play. Each game lasts 60 minutes and consists of four 15-minute quarters. Higher values indicate more time left and therefore a less proximal deadline.
time_window: time remaining at the moment of each play within a 60-minute game

description: Four items measuring the outcome of the acquisition and the integration process. Respondents indicated how well the acquisition and the integration process had succeeded, and how the acquisition and the integration process had succeeded compared with expectations. The scale ranged from 1 = total failure to 7 = great success.

Respondents rated their perceptions of the extent to which management's actions had affected the outcome of the integration process and explained the overall success of the acquisition. The scale ranged from 1 = not at all to 7 = a great deal.
scale: 1 = not at all to 7 = a great deal

description: Respondents rated the extent to which they perceived that cultural differences had affected the outcome of the acquisition's integration process and explained the overall success of the acquisition. The scale ranged from 1 = not at all to 7 = a great deal.
scale: 1 = not at all to 7 = a great deal

description: A sum index combining the number of acquisitions in which the respondent had been personally involved on the acquiring firm side and the number in which the respondent had been personally involved on the acquired firm side. The index represents the person's combined prior experience of acquisitions.

Dummy variable that takes the value of one if the listing agent shares either the same ward or the same stake (church congregation) as the seller. Agent congregation boundaries are identified from the permanent mailing address agents provide to be licensed in Utah, and home congregation boundaries from publicly available congregation boundary records.

The number of homes an agent has helped consumers sell or buy at the time of the transaction, with dual agency transactions counting as two. The variable is coded as missing until an agent has bought or sold five homes, to allow burn-in. It is entered as log(total experience) in the models.

The applicability of an agent's previous experience to the current transaction, measured by dividing the total number of seller agent transactions by the total number of transactions for each agent. Higher values reflect increased human capital applicability, as the majority of the agent's previous transactions have been selling instead of buying. Coded as missing until an agent has bought or sold five homes.

The natural log of the final home sale price. After controlling for house and transaction characteristics, this variable reflects the price premium paid by the buyer to purchase the home, and higher values benefit sellers and agents.

variable_name: Sale price to predicted sale price
description: The final home sale price divided by its predicted sale price. The predicted sale price comes from a regression of the log of sale price on home observables, quality controls, transaction controls, time controls, and geographic controls. The variable is winsorized to 2.58 standard deviations above and below the mean; a value of 1 implies the sale price equals the predicted price and values above 1 indicate price premiums.
The number of days between initial listing and closing. Homes with days on market greater than two years are dropped to avoid uncommon situations such as complex short sales.

A dummy variable that takes the value of 1 if a home is sold. Sellers and agents typically enter into listing agreements that give agents the right to commissions if a home sells during a specific time period.

variable_name: Chosen (agent selected for the listing), conditional logit
description: Agent selection is a dummy variable, chosen, equal to one for the agent the seller selected to list the home and zero for the other agents in the choice set of alternative active agents. It is modeled with a conditional logit on agent affiliation, experience, applicability and their interactions, with standard errors clustered by listing.

Cognitive processing was manipulated through conceptual priming introduced only after the first round. Half of the participants were asked to write at least 600 characters recollecting a situation in which their intuition (type 1 processing) led to a positive outcome or their reflection (type 2 processing) led to a negative one, and half were asked to do the opposite, so valence was counterbalanced. The variable was modeled as a dichotomous variable indicating the treatment category in which 1 equals type 1 and 0 equals type 2 processing.
time_window: between the first and second rounds of the game

description: Ambiguity was manipulated by varying the degree to which decision makers had information about the meaning and implications of particular events or situations, through different dashboards. In the high-ambiguity condition participants had access to the hand number, the total elapsed time, and the number of moves made in the hand; in the low-ambiguity condition a hand index told them how far they were from the optimal solution, that is, the minimum number of moves required to solve that hand. The variable is modeled as a dichotomous variable indicating the treatment category, where 1 equals high and 0 equals low ambiguity.

variable_name: money gained by the groups in the second round
description: Organizational adaptation was measured by the money gained by the groups in the second round, after the discontinuous change. Remuneration is a function of one dollar per hand completed less 10 cents per move required to put the target card in the target position, so the measure reflects both the number of hands solved and the sophistication of moves. The authors describe it as a group measure of adaptive success that captures the modification of shared patterns of action after the change manipulation and is not subject to self-evaluation.

Deviance from the optimal solution is measured as the number of unnecessary moves used in each hand relative to the minimum number of moves required. The authors complement this with the original measure of overreliance on the UU*T sequence of moves, counting how often groups used that sequence.
time_window: second round, with the first round reported for comparison

description: Speed is examined by regressing the average move time per hand on the hand number, following Cohen and Bacdayan (1994). The authors also compare the time per move in the first five hands with the same hands repeated later in the game and report the total time groups took to complete the second round.
time_window: second round, with the first round reported for comparison

description: Routinization is captured by the degree to which the groups relied on specific patterns of behavior, operationalized as the average number of times each pattern was repeated to complete a hand during the second round. The authors also report the number of distinct patterns groups relied on during the first round for comparison.
time_window: second round, with the first round reported for comparison

description: Coordination efficiency is computed by regressing the number of moves on the hand number; a steeper reduction in the number of moves per hand indicates greater coordination efficiency. The authors also compare the number of moves used in the first five hands with the same hands repeated later in the game.
time_window: second round, with the first round reported for comparison

description: Dichotomous governance variable equal to one for firms with a dual governance structure (the CEO also serves as board chair) and equal to zero for firms with a non-dual governance structure. It is the dependent variable of the probit selection equation and enters the performance equations as an endogenous shift dummy. The sample is restricted to firms with no change in the duality structure over the sample period.

One-year total market return to shareholders, including the reinvestment of dividends. It is one of the four alternative performance measures used as the dependent variable of the performance equations.

Tobin's q calculated as the ratio of the sum of the market value of common equity and the book values of preferred equity and long-term debt to the book value of assets. It is one of the four alternative performance measures used as the dependent variable of the performance equations.

Return on assets defined as income before extraordinary items divided by total assets. It is one of the four alternative performance measures used as the dependent variable of the performance equations.
Earnings per share deflated by beginning-of-year stock price. It is one of the four alternative performance measures used as the dependent variable of the performance equations.

variable_name: (σ2u − σ1u), read from the row labeled ϕ
description: The estimate of the difference between the covariance terms of the performance and selection equations, which the authors require to be positive for selection under comparative advantage. It is obtained from the pooled performance equation estimated by least squares on the fitted standard normal density and cumulative distribution functions evaluated at the probit selection estimates.

The hazard variable, Ĥj, defined as the sum of the two inverse Mills ratios weighted by the governance structure indicator, constructed from the maximum likelihood estimates of the selection equation. It is included in the single-equation performance models to account for selection bias, and its estimated coefficient is the estimate of σ.

Three strategic factors were used to capture strategic variety, following Porter (1979) and Miles et al. (1993): a marketing factor measured by the ratio of advertising to sales, a capital intensity factor measured by the dollar value of plant, property and equipment per employee, and an R&D factor measured by the ratio of R&D expenditures to sales. The coefficient of variation (the standard deviation divided by the mean) was calculated for each strategic factor variable by industry, and the three heterogeneity measures were then summed within each industry to produce overall strategic variety. Data for these measures were taken from the COMPUSTAT tapes and averaged for the years 1983-87. The authors report that using the Miles et al. clustering method encountered a methodological problem that severely compromised its validity, so they adopted the coefficient of variation as the measure of heterogeneity.

Industry performance was measured as average ROI for all observations in each industry over the time period 1984-87. A one-year shorter time period than that used to calculate industry variety was deemed appropriate in order to capture any lag between firms' strategic decisions and industry performance outcomes.

Eight survey items were used to measure the degree of differentiation of the supplier of a component vis-a-vis the procurer, capturing both structural and behavioral elements. The items measure the difference between supplier and procurer organizations in terms of speed of decision making, flexibility, information systems, time horizon, formalization, bureaucratization, employee benefits, and pay scales. The Cronbach alpha measure for reliability for this construct is 0.78, and confirmatory factor analysis yielded an adjusted goodness of fit index of 0.94.

Five survey items captured the degree to which a state of cooperation and coordination existed between the supplying and procuring unit for each component and were used to compute a single scale for integration. The Cronbach alpha measure of reliability for this construct was 0.72, and the adjusted goodness of fit index from confirmatory factor analysis was 0.98.

The instability in exchange conditions associated with each component was broadly assessed in terms of demand and technological developments, encompassing measures of volume uncertainty and technological uncertainty. To construct the scale, four items were used. The reliability of the scale was satisfactory (alpha = 0.73) and the adjusted goodness of fit index from confirmatory factor analysis was 0.99.

A scale constructed from five items measures the nature of task interdependence between procurer and possible supplier for each component. The items assessed the degree to which simultaneous contributions from supplier and procurer are required to design and produce the component, as well as the need for extensive interactions between the two for the supplier to understand and meet the specific requirements of the buyer. The scale had satisfactory reliability (alpha = 0.71) and an adjusted goodness of fit index from confirmatory factor analysis of 0.97.

Objective data on exchange performance is considered confidential and hard to collect, so the measure uses items capturing multiple facets of the satisfaction of the procurers with the supplier in comparison with alternative suppliers, which the authors expect to be strongly correlated with exchange performance. Six measures rate supplier performance along the dimensions of price, innovativeness, flexibility, and quality. The Cronbach alpha for this scale was 0.89, and the adjusted goodness of fit index from confirmatory factor analysis is 0.91.

Respondents identified each of the two primary supply relationships for a component as falling into one of three categories defined in the questionnaire: market procurement (purchasing arrangement with external suppliers characterized by relatively shorter-term contracts and competitive bidding), vertical alliance (purchasing arrangement with external supplier characterized by relatively longer-term or open-ended contracts), and internal procurement (purchasing arrangement with an internal division of the company). The response was corroborated with two other survey items in which respondents indicated the percentage of the component sourced through each of the three types of arrangements and the expected duration of each relationship. Of the 222 exchanges in the sample, 21 were organized as internal procurement, 132 as vertical alliances, and 69 as market procurement.

Percentage of the population with at least a bachelor's degree, taken from the U.S. Census Bureau. The authors use higher education as the primary indicator of cultural omnivorism because it cultivates the aesthetic disposition to recognize artistry in both highbrow and lowbrow genres. The variable is measured at the city level for the cities in the sampling frame.

Blau index on race computed from Census data. There were seven racial categories, so the variable could range from 0.857 when the population was perfectly dispersed to zero when the population was homogenous.

Number of craft breweries per 100,000 people in a city, from Brewers Association data reflecting 2012 information. Craft breweries are treated as established organizations that emphasize the local, handcrafted, and unique rather than the mass-produced and standardized.

Number of farmers' markets per 100,000 people in a city, from U.S. Department of Agriculture data current to their download date in October 2013. Farmers' markets are treated alongside craft breweries as established organizations emphasizing local, handcrafted, and unique products.

Percentage of restaurants in a city that are steakhouse restaurants, derived from Demographics Now and downloaded in October 2013. The authors use steakhouses because Carroll and Wheaton (2009) identify this kind of restaurant as epitomizing conventional type authenticity. They expect the share of steakhouse and national chain restaurants to be stable over the time period.

Percentage of restaurants in a city that belonged to national chains, derived from Demographics Now and downloaded in October 2013. It is used to capture organizations that suppress authenticity concerns by representing values of efficiency and reliability.

Number of gourmet food trucks created by city-year, constructed from tweet records, with the start date of each truck taken as the first tweet reporting business operations. Truck locations were identified from self-reported location data on Twitter; in a minority of cases trucks reporting operation in a metropolitan region were counted for each city in the region, and trucks reporting suburbs were assigned to the central city. The count is taken over the 289 U.S. cities with populations greater than 100,000 in 2013.

Dichotomous dependent variable indicating whether the firm entered any alliances in the given year. A record was created for each firm in each year of the period covered in the study. In instances in which firms entered multiple alliances in a single year, the firm was recorded as having entered a tie; new alliances include those formed with any partner, both prior and new partners. Alliance was coded as 1 if the firm had formed an alliance in that year and 0 otherwise.

The number of cliques to which a firm belongs, also called clique overlap centrality. This was assessed within UCINET IV using the Bron and Kerbosch algorithm, which identifies all Luce and Perry cliques; the minimum clique size specified was three. The clique centrality of each firm was computed for each year and expressed relative to the most central firm in the network for that particular year.
time_window: network cumulative from 1970 until the prior year, lagged one year

description: Closeness centrality score for each firm across all its partners, constructed within UCINET IV, capturing how closely connected a firm is to the rest of the firms in the interfirm network, both directly and indirectly. It is computed by counting the number of firms that a focal firm must go through to reach other firms in the network. The centrality scores were normalized to the highest centrality score within each industry and for each year.
time_window: network cumulative from 1970 until the prior year, lagged one year

description: The number of past alliances a firm has formed; the variable counts all the prior alliances a focal firm has entered with any partners, new or old. It captures the extent of the alliance formation capabilities a firm may have developed from its prior experience, and is the cumulative total of alliances the firm has entered until the previous year.
time_window: cumulative to the previous year, lagged one year

description: Diversity of a firm's prior alliance experience, considered in terms of the kinds of governance structure used to formalize its prior alliances and the nationalities of its partners. The authors computed the reciprocal of the Herfindahl index for the nationalities of each firm's prior alliance partners and for the governance structure of its prior alliances, and also alternative variables using a specification akin to Blau's index of heterogeneity. The reported results for these measures are not presented in the paper.
time_window: prior alliances until the previous year

variable_name: Percentage of criteria that are prescribed
description: The number of prescribed criteria cited for a decision divided by the total number of criteria cited for that decision, multiplied by 100. Three coders (two researchers and one senior bank executive) independently coded each piece of information cited by loan officers as prescribed (falling into one of the eight categories on the risk-rating guide) or ad hoc; disagreements were resolved through discussion. The eight prescribed categories were cash flow, financeable assets, net income, liquidity, leverage, collateral, firm size, and sources of loan repayment. The percentage was transformed by subtracting the percentage value from a constant and then taking the log of that value, and the values were reverse scored in the presentation of results to preserve the low-to-high ordering.

A simple count of the number of prescribed criteria cited for each decision. The variable was transformed by subtracting the count from a constant and then taking the square root of this score, and the values were reverse scored in the presentation of results to preserve the low-to-high ordering.

variable_name: Number of ad hoc criteria cited
description: A simple count of the number of ad hoc criteria cited for each decision, where ad hoc criteria are pieces of information that did not fit into one of the eight standard categories. The variable was transformed by adding one to its value and then taking the log of that value.
Measured as the current size of the loan in millions of dollars; data were obtained from the loan review documents.

Assessed as the duration of the relationship between the bank and the borrower in terms of the number of years; data were obtained from the loan review documents, which recorded the date that the lending relationship was established.
time_window: years since the relationship was established

description: Measured using the average size of the commercial loan portfolio within the branch in millions of dollars. Calculated on an annual basis.
Assessed by calculating the percentage of the branch's commercial customers that were from manufacturing as opposed to service industries. Calculated on an annual basis.
Measured as the net income for lending divided by the total size of the branch's lending portfolio. Calculated on an annual basis.

A perceptual measure based on a short questionnaire completed by three senior managers who had been in top-level management roles throughout the study, assessing the degree of standardization by year across the entire bank. The measure consisted of four questions rated on a seven-point Likert-type scale: three items were adapted from Van de Ven and Ferry's (1980) measure of unit standardization, and the fourth question asked top managers to assess the degree of standardization across subunits (branches). The Cronbach's alpha across the four items was greater than 0.98 for each informant, and the intraclass correlation indicated significant agreement among the coders (r = 0.51). Responses were averaged across questions and informants to get an overall indication of the strength of standardization by year; the data indicated that the strength of standardization increased over the time period of the study.

The borrower's risk assessment was measured in both the prior (t-1) and the current year (T) using a seven-point rating scale, with a one being the lowest risk and a seven being the highest risk. An indicator variable was then created to measure whether the risk assessment of the borrower had remained the same or changed, indicating stability or instability in the decision assessment.

Whether a theater holds federal status. The authors describe theaters with federal status as the paragons of the Russian theater tradition, representing the highest degree of accumulated recognition, and use this variable to capture the institutional recognition attribute of respectability.

Theater age, used as a measure of sustained institutional prestige and heritage. The authors divide the theaters into seven age cohorts, each with approximately the same relative frequency of observations; the base cohort is theaters founded less than 10 years ago.

Celebrity status of the artistic director, operationalized as recognition as a popular culture figure who makes regular appearances in television shows, films, or TV series. It is a dichotomous variable (yes or no) indicating at least one appearance in the past two years, a horizon that accounts for the window of time between the promotion of a film or a TV series and its release.

The number of previous year nominations received by the theater's cast members for The Golden Mask, a national theater award established in 1993 and its associated professional festival of theatrical arts, described as the most prestigious of all in the Russian Federation and comparable to the Tony Awards in the United States.

Binary variable that indicates the presence or absence of corporate support in each theater each year. On average, approximately 36% of the theaters in the sample enjoy some form of corporate support.

Operationalized in two steps. The first step is a media analysis of the public political stances of the artistic directors in each given year, including press interviews, social media posts, political campaign participation announcements and other publicly accessible displays of political views (327 media outlet interviews, 217 Facebook posts and 123 popular press articles). The second step is a categorical variable with three levels: progovernment, neutral, and critical. Two independent coders coded the discourses, with an interrater reliability of 0.94 and a Cohen's kappa of 0.72.

The presence of a board of trustees in a given year, operationalized as a dichotomous variable coded as either one or zero, by consulting the official database of Russian theaters provided by the Ministry of Culture.

Respectability is constituted by institutional recognition and age. It is operationalized with the federal status of the theater and the theater's age cohort, which are the existing measures for those two attributes.

variable_name: Celebrity status of the artistic director and Golden Mask nominations of cast members
description: Reputability is captured by two indicators entered separately: a dichotomous variable for whether the artistic director is recognized as a popular culture figure with at least one appearance in television shows, films or TV series in the past two years, and the number of nominations of the theater's cast members for The Golden Mask national theater award received in the previous year.

Words spoken by the CEO and the CFO during the Q&A section of each conference call were extracted and analyzed separately with Linguistic Inquiry and Word Count (LIWC), which reports the percentage of total words in each of nine basic-level function word categories. The printed formula is unreadable in the available text; the authors state that preps CEO is the percentage of prepositions used by the CEO and preps CFO the percentage used by the CFO, that 0.001 is added to the denominator to prevent empty sets, and that the nine category-level language similarity scores are added to yield a composite LSM score, where a larger number represents a higher level of LSM. For the CFO-level analyses each transcript was weighted by the ratio of the total number of words spoken by the CEO and the CFO in that call to the total words they spoke in all conference calls in a CFO-year; for the firm-level analyses the transcripts were weighted analogously within a firm-year.
time_window: Conference calls during the fiscal year; measured at t-1 relative to the dependent variables

description: The natural logarithm of the CFO's total compensation, including salary, bonus, options granted, restricted stock, and other pay. The dependent variable is measured at t.

An indicator that receives a value of '1' in the year when a CFO becomes a board member of the focal firm and '0' otherwise. All the observations after a CFO becomes a board member of the focal firm are excluded in the event history analysis.

The total number of majority-ownership M&As announced in a year, which will have been completed subsequently, as reported in SDC data. The sample was constrained to deals with a transaction value of over $1 million and to deals classified as 'acquisition of majority interests,' 'acquisitions of assets,' 'acquisitions,' or 'mergers' based on SDC's classification. The natural logarithm of the number plus one was taken to address skewness; firm years with no M&As received a value of '0'.
The total transaction value of these M&As in a year. The natural logarithm of the value plus one was taken to address skewness, and firm years with no M&As received a value of '0'.
The percentage of cash (as opposed to stock) used to pay for the focal deal. It is the proposed mediating variable in the relationship between CEO-CFO LSM and investor reactions to M&A announcements.

Cumulative abnormal returns - the returns over the event window minus the normal returns - calculated with the standard event study methodology. The authors first computed abnormal returns for an M&A announcement and then accumulated them over a three-day window surrounding the announcement date [-1, +1], which incorporates the day before and the day after the announcement; a [-2, +2] window is also reported.
time_window: Three-day event window surrounding the M&A announcement date

description: A formative index consisting of five variables: (1) CEO tenure, (2) CEO duality, (3) board independence, (4) CEO equity ownership, and (5) percentage of directors appointed by CEOs. CEO tenure is the number of years that a CEO has been at the CEO position; CEO duality is '1' if the CEO holds the board chairman position; board independence is the ratio of non-executive directors to board size, reverse coded so that a larger value corresponds to greater CEO power; CEO equity ownership is the ratio of total shares owned by the CEO to total shares outstanding; and the percentage of directors appointed by the CEO is the ratio of the number of board members appointed after the CEO took office to board size. The five variables were standardized and combined into the index.

A dummy (treatment) variable that equals one for treated firms and zero for matched control firms. A firm is treated if it operates in a four-digit SIC industry that experiences a large tariff rate reduction and has coverage in Compustat and the KLD database at least one year before and one year after the reduction. A tariff rate reduction in a given industry-year is qualified as large if it is at least three times larger than the average annual (absolute) change in tariff rate in the same industry across all years; the baseline uses the 34 large tariff reductions that occurred as of 1992.
scale: dummy (1 = treated firm, 0 = matched control firm)

description: Composite KLD index constructed by summing up all strengths along the dimensions covered by the KLD database. The dependent variable is the difference between the firm's average KLD index in the three years following the tariff reduction and its average KLD index in the three years preceding the tariff reduction; where KLD data are not available for the full window, the respective average is computed on the basis of the nonmissing years.
time_window: three years before to three years after the tariff reduction

description: A dummy variable indicating whether a company operates in the business-to-consumer (B2C) sector, i.e., industries in which the purchasing decision is more sensitive to companies' CSR engagement. The classification of B2C industries is obtained from Lev et al. (2010: 188). In the auxiliary analysis the dummy is interacted with the tariff reduction dummy.

Number of patents or citations cumulated up to period t-1, where t is the year of tie formation; a patent with multiple inventors was counted as 1/N toward each inventor, and citation-weighted counts divide all citations made to each patent by the number of associated inventors. Both versions are entered in logged form.

Patent stock for past performance, both simple counts and citation-weighted counts cumulated up to t-1, team-size adjusted, with a patent credited as 1/N to each of its N inventors; all explanatory variables are lagged one year.

Network constraint (Burt 1992) computed from the inventor collaboration network over a five-year moving window beginning from 1976, then transformed by subtracting it from 2 so that higher values indicate higher brokerage; inventors without collaborators were assigned zero, and the measure was lagged one year.
time_window: five-year moving window, lagged one year

description: Network constraint (Burt 1992) measuring brokerage, transformed by subtracting it from 2 so that higher values indicate more extensive brokering; zero was assigned to inventors without collaborators, and all explanatory variables are lagged one year.
time_window: five-year moving window, lagged one year

description: Indicator of the type of collaboration tie at risk, equal to 1 when the tie is with an inventor new to everyone in the focal inventor's ego network; the repeating-tie dummy is the omitted baseline, so focal inventor attributes are interacted with the type dummies. The dependent variable of the model is the binary indicator of tie formation, with each realized tie matched to up to three controls that could have been realized but were not.
time_window: five-year window used to define network relationships

description: Simple patent counts and citation-weighted patent counts as measures of performance, both adjusted by team size (the number of inventors on each patent) and logged; the citation-weighted count divides all citations made to each patent by the number of associated inventors.

For each of the 43 questions in the scenario questionnaire (24 single-item and 19 multi-item), the standard deviation was calculated across the individual respondents of each firm. The mean of these 43 standard deviations was then calculated to determine a firm-level score, and each score was subtracted from a constant (i.e., two), so that higher scores represent more agreement and lower scores indicate less agreement. Four methods of calculating agreement were tested (standard deviations, coefficient of variation, Euclidean distances, and interrater reliability scores), all highly correlated and yielding the same pattern of results; the standard deviation measure is reported.

For the 43 questions in the scenario questionnaire a mean score was calculated across the individual respondents in each firm. The mean response for the 10 or 11 questions pertaining to each of the four hypothetical phases of the decision process (situation diagnosis, alternative generation, alternative evaluation, and decision integration) gave a firm-level score for each of the four steps. Each firm's overall measure of comprehensiveness was the mean of the four decision process steps.

Net income before extraordinary items divided by total assets, calculated as a 5-year average including the five consecutive years after and including the year that the first scenario-questionnaire instrument was administered (1979–83 for the forest products industry and 1981–85 for the paint and coatings industry). A market-based measure was not used because approximately 40 percent of the firms in the sample were privately held.

A 5-year average ROA including the five consecutive years prior to and including the year the scenario-questionnaire instrument was administered: 1975–79 for the forest products industry and 1977–81 for the paint and coatings industry for the original studies, and 1981–85 for the firms from the follow-up study.

Each firm's industry and its attendant environment was represented by a dichotomous variable coded 0 for forest products firms and 1 for paint and coatings firms. A variety of measures established that the environments of these industries were highly stable (paints and coatings) or highly unstable (forest products) during the study period.
The log of the total number of employees was used as the measure of organizational size, because most size measures (e.g., employees and assets) tend to be highly correlated.
The total number of executives, including the CEO, that had been identified to participate during discussions with the CEO.

The questionnaire asked each executive to specify the number of years that he or she had worked for the firm, and these data were used to compute three measures for each firm: the mean number of years service of TMT members, variance, and coefficient of variation in TMT tenure. Because average tenure, variance and the coefficient of variation produced the same pattern of results in all analyses, only average tenure is reported.

Dummy variable coded 1 in case of a CEO dismissal in a given year and 0 when there was either no CEO succession event or a routine succession event (voluntary turnover). The nature of the 119 CEO succession events was determined through a content analysis of press articles and official company announcements; each incident was classified independently by two coders as voluntary turnover or dismissal, and inconsistent classifications (8 out of 119) were discussed until agreement was reached. As a result of this two-step approach, 45 of the 119 turnover events were identified as dismissals.

variable_name: average change rate of total shareholder return (TSR)
description: Average change rate of total shareholder return from Year 3 to Year 1 before the dismissal event, interacted with the two independent variables. TSR was operationalized as the firm's total return to shareholders (i.e., stock price changes and dividends) adjusted for industry effects by subtracting the median value of the TSR for all firms in the sample belonging to the same industry as the focal firm. Industries are defined according to the industry classification of the Deutsche Boerse Group.
time_window: average change rate from Year 3 to Year 1 before the dismissal event

description: Number of outside directorships of the focal firm's CEO for each year under study relative to the number of outside board seats of the focal firm's COB. For both individuals, COB positions in other firms were counted with a weight of 2 whereas ordinary supervisory board memberships were counted with a weight of 1 each, reflecting German law (a COB position counts like two ordinary memberships and the COB vote counts twice in case of a tie). Network relationship data were updated for each sample firm on an annual basis from 2002 to 2011.
Proportion of the focal firm's supervisory board members who do not hold seats on other boards.

The number of individuals who left a store divided by the total number of employees in the store. Turnover information was provided by store managers using store records six months following the collection of the survey data. The average turnover rate for the six-month collection period was 46 percent and the range was 26 percent to 70 percent.

A ratio of the average in-role performance of leavers divided by the average in-role performance of all employees in a store, used to account for baseline performance differences among stores and to standardize the measure for cross-store comparison. Managers rated each employee on four items, with 11 response options and bipolar anchors; the internal consistency reliability of the measure was .94. Ratings were mean-aggregated to the store level for all employees in the store and for departed employees.

The average betweenness centrality of leavers divided by the average betweenness centrality in a store, a ratio used to standardize the measure for cross-store analyses. Freeman's (1979) betweenness centrality measures the extent to which individuals occupied structurally advantageous positions in a store's communication network, that is, bridged structural holes, and takes both direct and indirect ties into account. Communication matrices were symmetrized using the 'max-of' rule, so a pair was considered to have a tie if either member of the dyad indicated a tie; employees indicated whether they communicated with other employees 'at least several times a week.'

The number of communication ties in a network divided by n x (n - 1), where n is the number of employees in the network, following the formula provided by Scott (2000). Communication ties were derived from the employee sociometric forms.

Average quarterly sales for the four fiscal-year quarters following the turnover measurement divided by the number of employees in a store. Total employees was used as the denominator; the authors report that alternative measures of store size such as square feet per store were not available.
time_window: four fiscal-year quarters following the turnover measurement

description: Average quarterly sales per employee for the year following the turnover measurement minus average quarterly sales per employee in the year preceding the study.
time_window: year before versus year after the turnover measurement

description: The actual dollar change in sales between the year preceding the study and the year following the turnover measurement.
time_window: year before versus year after the turnover measurement

description: Participants were first encouraged to adopt an inside view of the project: they described the path along which they saw the Project proceeding and constructed the most probable future scenario, creating a timeline of key steps, milestones, and actions. They were then asked to state the expected rate of return for the Project. The inside and outside view conditions were carried out within subjects.

After the inside view instructions, participants stated the expected rate of return for the Project. After being encouraged to take an outside view, they estimated the average return of the projects in each of two self-generated categories and were asked whether they would be inclined to revise their expected rate of return for the current project up or down and, if so, what the revised estimate would be. The analysis compares initial estimates, reference category means, and revised estimates.

Moviegoers were shown a synopsis, lead actors, storyline, and theatrical poster for each target movie and rated its similarity to past movies; the global similarity ratings were made on a seven-point scale and individual respondents' similarities were aggregated using a robust mean similarity function. The number of cases entering the prediction, x, was endogenous, determined by hierarchical cluster analysis of the similarity judgments. The SBF prediction was arrived at by regressing the raw SBF predictor along with production budget, genre, sequel dummy, and star actor dummy variables against actual revenue.

Forecasting accuracy was measured by the mean absolute relative error summed over all previous cases, comparing each model's predicted revenue for the 19 target movies with actual box office revenue. MARE was computed for the regression model, for the regression model with interactions, and for the SBF model; a paired t-test used each movie as one item and the difference in accuracy of the SBF and regression prediction as one pair.

Dummy variable with a value of 1 if the venture was a start-up and 0 if it was an acquisition. It is the dependent variable in the binomial logit models of the choice between a start-up and an acquisition when the focal firm expanded overseas.
time_window: at the time of the expansion

description: The number of foreign countries that the firm had entered at the time of the expansion. The variable was not mean-centered so as to keep the comparison with the original study fair. Its squared term and its interaction with product diversity are entered in the models.
level: firm at the time of the expansion
time_window: at the time of the expansion

description: The number of three-digit SIC codes in which the firm was active at the time of expansion. It is entered together with its squared term and with the interaction terms with multinational diversity.
level: firm at the time of the expansion
time_window: at the time of the expansion

variable_name: horizontal, related, vertical, and unrelated expansion
