A time-invariant count of the number of international patent classes into which the USPTO assigns a patent. Because international patent classes are nested, the more classes to which a patent is assigned, the broader is its intellectual property protection.

Constructed from MIT Technology Licensing Office records of its licensees, which indicate the legal status of the licensee and its year of incorporation. The variable was coded 1 in the year that the patent was first licensed if it was licensed to an (unincorporated) individual or to a firm incorporated after the patent application was submitted, and 0 otherwise in that year. Patents never licensed and patents licensed to an already incorporated company are treated as censored.
time_window: 1980-1996, case-year observations until a firm is formed or the observation period ends

description: A firm is assigned a score of 1 if it conforms to the description of an assessment item and 0 otherwise, and the total assessment item score reflects the firm's overall level of CSR engagement. Because the number of KLD assessment items changed over the years, the raw KLD score and the industry average raw KLD score are each deflated by dividing them by the total KLD score in that year; the ratio between the two identifies how well the firm performs in its CSR activities compared with other firms in the same industry.

The measure is the average long-term CSR engagement of firm i in year t. The authors state that the specification assumes the effects of long-term CSR engagement are progressively reduced over a three-year period, with greater weight placed on more recent observations. The equation itself is unreadable in the available text, so the exact weights cannot be recovered from the prose.

Abnormal returns are estimated with an event study following Ball and Brown (1968) and Fama et al. (1969), using an estimation period of 120 days. The date on which the negative event was first reported in the Wall Street Journal is the start date of the event. The event period includes the three days before and after the negative event, and observations are winsorized at the 5th and 95th percentiles.
time_window: three days before to three days after the event

description: Cumulative abnormal returns are calculated so as to analyze the continuing influence of the event on stock prices throughout the event period, which includes the three days before and after the negative event. They are estimated with the same event study methodology as abnormal returns, using a 120-day estimation period, and are winsorized at the 5th and 95th percentiles.
time_window: three days before to three days after the event

description: Abnormal returns of bonds are computed with the same event study methodology as stock abnormal returns, using the daily floating rate note (FRN) prices of the sample firms collected from Bloomberg and a 120-day estimation period. The event period includes the three days before and after the negative event and observations are winsorized at the 5th and 95th percentiles.
time_window: three days before to three days after the event

description: Cumulative abnormal returns of bonds are calculated with the same event study methodology to analyze the continuing influence of the event on bond prices throughout the event period. Bond prices are the daily floating rate note (FRN) prices collected from Bloomberg, the estimation period is 120 days, and observations are winsorized at the 5th and 95th percentiles.
time_window: three days before to three days after the event

description: Negative events are classified by their order of occurrence for the firm, and the effect of short- and long-term CSR engagement on abnormal returns and cumulative abnormal returns is estimated separately for each occurrence group rather than pooled. The authors report that the results indicate a 'credibility cliff' rather than diminishing marginal returns.

CSR engagement is measured from the KLD 400 Social Index: a firm scores 1 on each assessment item it meets and 0 otherwise, and the total reflects overall CSR engagement, adjusted for the growth in the number of items over years. A short-term version (adjusted KLD score) and a long-term version (LAKLD, a decay-weighted average of past adjusted scores) are used.
scale: sum of binary items, industry/year adjusted

description: The dependent variable is the goodness of the idea that each survey participant proposed. All 107 ideas were given anonymously to the two senior VPs, who were asked 'if this idea were well-executed, how much could it contribute to the improvement of the company's software development and/or operation processes?' on a scale from 0 ('no contribution or too short or simple to rate') to 10 ('the highest contribution'). The indicator is the average of the two VPs' scores; the Spearman rank correlation between the two raters was 0.79. The most important criterion the VPs used was whether the idea contained feasible solutions.
time_window: idea thought about during the past year

description: An actor i's network constraint (Ci) was computed as the sum over contacts j of cij, where cij is a measure of i's dependence on contact j: cij = pij + the sum over q (q not equal to i or j) of piq·pqj. pij is the proportion of the tie strength that actor i directly devotes to colleague j relative to the sum of tie strengths of all other of i's contacts, and the sum of piq·pqj captures the proportion of i's relations that are indirectly invested in connection with colleague j through a third party q. Following the routine used in UCINet 6, the authors employed the immediate network, consisting of anyone the actor designated as a communication partner and anyone who cited him or her.

Attention allocation was computed with a Herfindahl measure of the extent to which a focal actor distributes his or her attention to information coming across all communication partners. It is built from eij, the proportion of actor i's attention to information from an alter j to the aggregation of attention that i allocates to information from all of his or her communication partners, where the raw attention score aij is the mean response to four seven-point Likert items on noticing, encoding, interpreting, and focusing of time and effort (Cronbach's alpha = 0.93; first principal component accounted for 84.5% of the variance). A high Herfindahl score indicates divided attention while a low score indicates focused attention; only communication partners cited by the focal actor were counted. (The equation as printed in the paper is not legible; this description follows the surrounding prose.)

Tie strength with each listed communication partner was measured with Hansen's (1999) two items, the degree of communication frequency and emotional closeness, as a proxy for tie strength between an actor and an alter. Each item was measured on a seven-point Likert scale, ranging from one (strongly disagree) to seven (strongly agree). The indicator was the mean of the two items; Cronbach's alpha was 0.78 and the first principal component accounted for 80.0% of the variance.

Dummy equal to one for firms that appoint a family CEO following the departure of a professional CEO, and zero for firms that continue with professional leadership, that is, appoint another professional CEO. It is interacted with the post-succession dummy in the difference-in-differences specification.

Ratio of earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization scaled by total assets, trimming 1% of observations in the extreme right and left tail of the distribution to reduce the risk of outliers. In the regression analyses the unadjusted ROA is the dependent variable, with industry trends accounted for by the interaction between industry and year dummies.

The logarithm of the volatility of industry revenues, used in a triple interaction with the Type-R succession dummy and the post-succession dummy to test whether the performance effect of Type-R successions is weaker in turbulent industry contexts.

Dummy equal to one if the firm reports any positive R&D/advertisement expense 1 year before the succession, and zero otherwise; it is apt to capture the reliance on innovative inputs (regarding new technological efforts or product developments) immediately before the CEO succession. It is interacted with the Type-R succession dummy and the post-succession dummy.

The average overall job satisfaction rating given to the firm by employees during the year, using employee-supplied scores from the website Glassdoor.com. Glassdoor measures these ratings on a five-point scale, with one as the lowest rating and five as the highest. A minimum of 25 ratings during the year is required to average out idiosyncratic views, and reviews from both current and former employees are included.

Measured as the natural logarithm of one plus the cash and non-equity bonuses provided to the CEO, in millions. The authors concentrate on bonuses paid to CEOs because research suggests that relative to equity-based compensation, nonfinancial performance metrics such as employee satisfaction ratings are most likely to be weighted in the CEO's contract through bonus payments.
scale: natural logarithm of one plus bonuses in millions

description: Equals one if the CEO was fired and zero otherwise. Dismissals were identified by evaluating CEO successions using news articles, which included eliminating instances in which CEOs had health problems or died, were interim CEOs, left due to a merger or acquisition, or the company ceased to exist; from the remaining successions, dismissals were identified when CEOs were reported to have stepped down for reasons related to job performance or were terminated for behavioral or policy-related problems.

Measured using an estimate of the compensation paid per employee. Compensation costs are measured at the industry level by averaging, for each two-digit SIC industry in the sample, the staff expense per employee among firms with available Compustat data. The variable is the average per-employee staff expense for the firm's industry in each fiscal year, and is standardized with a mean of zero and a standard deviation of one.

A count variable representing the number of unique board committees the firm has with a CSR-related keyword in the committee title. Board committee names were searched for the keyword-stems sustain*, responsib*, ethic*, employee, health, safety, divers*, inclusion, environment*, community, citizen, public, and charit*.

An indicator variable that equals one for firms listed in the top 25 of Fortune's Most Admired Companies list during the year and zero otherwise. The list is used as an independent and publicly available measure that appears to capture the construct 'corporate reputation'.
scale: indicator (1 = top 25 of the Most Admired list, 0 = otherwise)

description: Organizational size is measured as scale of operations, specifically the firm's annual production of automobiles, expressed in logarithmic form. Annual production is recorded for each firm in each year of the life-history spell file.

Technological niche width is the range of engine capacity in horsepower across all models produced by each firm in any given year. It is entered as a covariate in both the rate-of-change and the mortality models.

Market-center stability is a dummy variable that equals unity if the midpoint of the technological niches of the four largest firms in the market does not shift between two consecutive years. The market center itself covers the range of the niches of the four largest firms in the industry each year.

Absolute position change (niche-center change) refers to the difference in each firm's niche midpoint between two consecutive years, and is the type of change that by definition must be initiated by the focal firm. The authors modeled both dichotomous and continuous measures and report the models using the dummy specification.

Cumulative niche-center change sums the number of prior changes in a firm's niche center. The difference in the propensity to change between firms with and without prior change experience is what the authors call the relative momentum of change.

The rate of position change is the dependent variable of the rate-of-change analysis and is modeled as a piecewise-exponential function of tenure in the industry, with breakpoints at 1.0, 3.0, 7.0, and 15.0 years. The rate is specified as a function of tenure, industry age, size variables, other measured covariates, and niche characteristics.

The outcome event of interest is disbanding or exit to another industry, defined to include events of unknown type; exits of unknown type were treated as disbandings or exits to other industries. Firms known to have ended by merger, acquisition or other events were treated as noninformatively censored on the right at the times of these events.

For each firm-year the author constructs a task matrix of the firm's N business segments, whose entries (i,j) and (j,i) are set to xs if segments i and j on average contribute more than 1% of the input to one another according to the BEA input-output tables. Task complexity is the number of segment pairs in the firm's portfolio that are interdependent, that is, the number of xs in the task matrix. Because firms change their business portfolios over time, the measure varies both cross-sectionally and longitudinally.
time_window: firm-year, contemporaneous with the structure measure

description: The measure is built from the community structure of the firm's task network. A D value is computed as the difference between the observed and expected proportions of within-community edges for a separation of the network's nodes into communities, and the highest D value across all possible separations is the network decomposability; the D value is calculated with the Guimerà and Amaral (2005) algorithm for the largest component. Task decomposability is then defined as a function of this D value, the number of communities in the largest component, and the number of components in the task network, so that more components and more separable communities in the largest component mean a more decomposable network. Components of the network were identified with a breadth-first search algorithm. The equation rendering the exact formula is unreadable in the available text, so the precise functional form cannot be reproduced.
time_window: firm-year, contemporaneous with the structure measure

description: Divisionalization is measured from organization charts as the number of divisions and majority-owned subsidiaries that have no subordinate divisions or subsidiaries. These units represent the lowest level of profit-center responsibility and are therefore comparable across firms, and majority-owned subsidiaries are included to account for business units of a separate legal form that contribute significantly to the parent firm's revenue and coordination responsibilities.

Organizational hierarchy is measured from the number of layers in organization charts. To capture firms' aggregated capacity for hierarchical coordination, the author sums the number of supervisory units (departments, groups, etc.) on each layer that have at least one subordinate unit (another department, group, division, or subsidiary) and multiplies them by the rank of the layer in the hierarchy. With the same number of layers, firms with more supervisory units have a greater value of organizational hierarchy.

Firm capital structure measured by taking the equity amount and dividing it by firm sales as an adjustment for size. The text states that the GIPC provided measures of both equity and firm sales, though not of debt; low equity to sales indicates a relatively leveraged firm. Firm equity/sales is averaged over 1997-1998.

Calculated by running a regression analysis to predict sector turnover (sales) with time as the independent variable; the dynamism measure is the standard error of the regression divided by the average value of sector sales, which produces comparability across sectors. The measure is calculated over a three-year rather than a five-year window, and the dynamism measurement window temporally precedes the dependent variable, performance. Sectors follow the 12 GIPC categories, with manufacturing split into food and industrial.

Return on sales, used as a measure of firm profitability. Each firm's outcome on the variable is averaged over three years (1997-1999). Accounting-based rather than market-based measures are used because there are relatively few (only 12) publicly traded firms in the sample.

Profitability per employee, used to measure operational productivity; the average of each firm's outcomes on the variable over three years (1997-1999). It was chosen together with ROS to reflect two distinct dimensions of firm performance, because the GIPC data did not provide the wherewithal to calculate return on assets and return on investment.

Total debt, computed as long-term debt plus debt in current liabilities, divided by book value of total assets. All variables were winsorized at the 2.5% level unless otherwise specified. The numerator of this variable is used to construct DEBT_INCR.

The ratio of the total number of self-citations to the total number of outward citations. Rather than taking the self-citation ratio measured at one point in time, the authors construct a stock equivalent by averaging the measure over the three years between t-1 and t+1, which makes the measure less sensitive to short-term fluctuations. The formula block specifying the measure was not readable in the paper text.

variable_name: Δ Exploitation of own prior knowledge
description: Changes in the self-citation ratio used as the dependent variable in the second stage of the treatment effects model, with k ranging from 2 to 4, i.e., changes in self-citations measured in a period ranging from one to four years after time t. The authors note the lags take into consideration that there could be important gaps between the effects of debt in correcting the firm's innovation trajectory and the filing of patents that stem from that trajectory. The formula block specifying the change measure was not readable in the paper text.
time_window: one to four years after t

description: A binary variable that takes the value of one if a firm's patent stock normalized by firm size is greater than the industry median, but its ratio of self-citations is less than the industry median. The authors argue these firms, although having generated significant innovative output, have inefficiently utilized their prior stock of knowledge and technological capabilities, and hence are most likely in a state of suboptimal exploration compared to peers.

A binary variable denoting leverage increases between t-1 and t. Leverage increases were first measured as the difference in total book debt between time period t-1 and t normalized by assets at time t-1, and DEBT_INCR was then coded as one when the difference in debt levels as a percentage of assets was greater than 5%, a minimum cut off used to capture significant changes in debt levels.

Tobin's q, calculated as the market value of the firm divided by the book value of total assets. In the models for overexplore firms the authors use changes in the numerator of Q over various time periods as the market value measure.

Classification of the origin of the claim prompting action into internal, external, or both, coded by the researcher from the case summaries during repeated sorts. Claim origin was identified in 309 of the 352 cases, for an 88-percent classification rate; 10 percent of the decisions had both internal and external claims, 59 percent had internal, and 31 percent had external claims. Interrater reliability was checked by a colleague on a 20 percent sample of the cases.

Classification of the claim as performance, adaptation, innovation, or conflict, coded by the researcher from the case summaries by working back and forth between cases and classification categories. The classification success for claim type was 99 percent (351 of the 352 cases). Sorting was repeated to improve intrarater reliability and checked against a colleague's coding of a 20 percent sample.

Classification of the direction the decision maker set as vision, problem, goal, or justification, coded by the researcher from the case summaries. Strategic decision makers in all 352 of the cases were found to use one of the four types of direction, for a 100 percent classification rate. The categories were compared with those found by a colleague on a 20 percent sample, with more than 90 percent agreement.

A downstream indicator of use that adjusts the use rate by adding the ultimate adoptions and deleting the ultimate rejections. Decisions were followed for two years after the first implementation attempt to find the changes needed to construct the measure. The adoption measures are binary.
time_window: two years after the first implementation attempt

description: A downstream indicator of degree of use that treats all partial adoptions as failures. Decisions were followed for two years after the first implementation attempt to find the changes needed to construct the measure. The adoption measures are binary.
time_window: two years after the first implementation attempt

description: Subjective ratings of the intrinsic value of a decision provided by the two secondary informants, using an anchored rating scale with five anchors: 5 outstanding, 4 good, 3 adequate, 2 disappointing, 1 poor; informants checked anywhere along the rating scale. The estimate-reflect-estimate procedure was used, in which informants first filled out the questionnaire and then reviewed the average responses and reconsidered their initial ratings. An average of the informants' final ratings was used.

The duration of the strategic decision process, measured in months, covering the period from concern or need recognition to the completion of an acceptable plan to meet the need or deal with the concern. Obtained in the questionnaire filled out by the two secondary informants; recall was refined by a discussion of the initial time estimate using the estimate-reflect-estimate procedure, and the average time in months from the final estimate was used.

R&D investments are measured as R&D intensity, the ratio of R&D expenditures to total sales. The measure has been widely used in previous studies. In the sample the dependent variable covers 1999-2004, one year after the independent and control variables.
Financial slack is measured as the ratio of quick assets (cash and marketable securities) to liabilities. The variable covers the 1998-2003 period, one year before the dependent variable.
Family ownership is the sum of equity ownership by family members, including founders and descendants. It is computed from the ownership information reported in the KIS database for 1998-2003.

Affiliated ownership is the sum of equity ownership by firms and financial institutions that belong to the same business group as the focal firm. It is computed from ownership information in the KIS database for 1998-2003.

Domestic institutional ownership is the total percentage of equity ownership held by domestic institutional investors composed of insurance companies, securities firms, and merchant banks, which do not belong to the same group as the firm being examined. Domestic financial institutions belonging to the same group are excluded from this category.

Foreign ownership is measured as the percentage of equity ownership held by both foreign firms and foreign financial institutions, following Khanna and Palepu (2000). It is computed from ownership information in the KIS database for 1998-2003.

Firm exit captures for each time t any decrease in the number of firms with an ownership stake in the project compared to time t - 1. For example, a project formed in 2003 between three companies A, B, and C scores 0 if all three are again listed in 2004, and scores 1 for 2005 if only A and B remain affiliated with the project, capturing the exit of firm C. Firm exit was hand-coded for all 3,181 project-year observations.
scale: count of exits (98.8 percent of values were 0 or 1)

description: Firm entry captures for each time t the increase in the number of firms with an ownership stake in the project compared to time t - 1. For a project formed in 2003 by companies A, B, and C whose membership in 2004 is A, B, C, and D, this is an increase of 1 compared to 2003, reflecting the entry of firm D into the partnership. Firm entry was hand-coded for all 3,181 project-year observations.
scale: count of entries (98.8 percent of values were 0 or 1)

description: The variable Exit-Munificent Firm is a dummy variable that is coded as 1 for exit by a munificent firm, coded as 0 for exit by a nonmunificent firm, and coded as missing otherwise. A firm is considered munificent when it holds more financial assets than the mean of the financial assets of the other collaborating firms combined. This relative measure is specific to each alliance rather than an absolute measure of size.

Entry by a munificent firm occurs when an entering firm holds more financial assets than the mean of the financial assets of the other partnering firms. The variable Entry-Munificent Firm is a dummy variable coded as 1 for entry by a munificent firm, coded as 0 for entry by a nonmunificent firm, and coded as missing otherwise.

Environmental dynamism is a time-varying covariate that captures price trend variability over the preceding 12 months for each mineral explored by the focal project. Following Dess and Beard (1984) and Boyd (1990) the monthly price of different minerals was regressed against time, and a moving average of the standard error of the coefficient (beta) was taken. The mean dynamism score was taken for alliances involved in mining more than one mineral.

Unplanned project termination is an event coded 1 when a given joint exploration project present at time t no longer existed at time t + 1, and coded 0 otherwise. A termination was only coded as unplanned when the mineral exploration project was terminated during the exploration phase, before reaching the planned goal of becoming operational and turning a profit. Of the 1,025 interfirm mineral exploration projects in the sample, 379 experienced such an event during the nine-year period of observation.
Our independent variable, Female CEO, takes a value of 1 if the CEO is female and 0 if the CEO is male. It identifies the gender of the incoming CEO in a succession observation.

Dichotomous variable that takes a value of 1 if the firm's proxy statement exhibited the collaboration board chair orientation and 0 otherwise. Orientations were identified by extracting the portion of the proxy statement explaining the board's choice of leadership structure and manually content-analyzing it with coding instructions adopted from Krause (2017); four expert human coders first independently coded 70 proxy statements with sufficient inter-rater reliability (kappa = 0.906), after which one coder blind to the hypotheses coded the remaining 453 passages. The dependent variables are independent of each other and are not mutually exclusive; in the final sample 52% of firms exhibited a collaboration orientation.

Dichotomous variable that takes a value of 1 if the firm's proxy statement exhibited the control board chair orientation and 0 otherwise. Boards exhibiting the control orientation will often use the words 'oversight' and 'independence' or explain that a separate board chair facilitates holding the CEO and management accountable, evaluating the management, or introducing greater objectivity and integrity in board decision-making. Coding used the same procedure as the collaboration orientation, with inter-rater reliability kappa = 0.892; 35% of firms in the final sample exhibited a control orientation.
Our moderator variable, Female directors, is the percentage of non-CEO directors on the board who are female.

Subgroup membership in each board was identified with the average silhouette width (ASW) algorithm based on five characteristics: age, gender, race, directors' CEO experience, and director appointment after the CEO. Individual directors' power was computed using three indicators: director title, the number of external directorships, and director ownership (the number of outstanding shares). CEO subgroup power was computed as the weighted power of the CEO subgroup (excluding the CEO) divided by the weighted sum of the power of the other subgroups within the board, using subgroup size as a weight; the relative power measures for the three indicators were standardized and averaged into an index of CEO subgroup power.

CEO dismissal is a binary variable coded as one for dismissal and zero for non-dismissal departures. Press releases and news reports were manually examined to identify CEO dismissals between 1998 and 2013, and the sample was updated by appending an open-source database of CEO dismissals between 2014 and 2018 provided by Gentry et al. (2021).

Performance decline is coded as one if the firm experienced a decline in return on assets (ROA) in the past 2 years and zero otherwise. Interaction models additionally use 5% or more decline and 10% or more decline in ROA as cutoffs.

The two-year lagged sum of contentious interactions that a firm received from any sampled SMO on a specific climate issue. Contentious tactics include protests, boycotts, and lawsuits, and interactions were identified from media reports, press releases, and firms' financial filings and coded to environmental issues with the CAP topics codebook. In the difference-in-differences models the measure is dichotomized into an indicator that equals one if the firm was contentiously targeted on the climate issue (the treated firms).
scale: count; dichotomized in the DiD models

description: The two-year lagged sum of intensive collaborations that a firm had with any SMO on a specific climate issue. Collaborations are coded where organizations work together, commit resources, and pursue mutually relevant outcomes; intensive collaborations are those focused on internal corporate processes and product development, and arm's-length cooperative interactions are excluded. In the DiD models the measure is dichotomized into an indicator that equals one if the firm had an intensive collaboration on the climate issue.
scale: count; dichotomized in the DiD models

description: A dummy variable coded one if the climate issue is material to the firm according to the Sustainability Accounting Standards Board and zero otherwise, described by the authors as the common operationalization of issue materiality. SASB uses internal research and industry working groups to classify an issue as material to a given industry if the issue can affect either the operational or financial performance of firms within that industry, and the authors aligned their climate issues with SASB topics and coded materiality according to firms' industry codes.

The number of patents applied for by a firm on a given climate issue in a year, based on granted patents and their application year. Patents' primary technology classes are mapped to the climate issues using Amore and Bennedsen (2016) and the USPTO EST Concordance; when a patent belongs to multiple issues it is divided over the number of issues to which it belongs, and patents whose primary classes fall into air pollution and global warming, alternative and renewable energy, and energy conservation are used. The main models use the log of one plus the count.

The number of patents applied for by the focal firm each year on a climate issue, counting only patents whose combination of subclasses is new compared with all previous patents that have ever been granted until then. When a patent belongs to multiple climate issues it is divided over the number of issues to which it belongs, and the main models use the log of one plus the count.

Each individual-year observation is matched with the corresponding number of establishments reported in County Business Patterns using the respondent's county of residence and the sector code of the current or most recent job at the time of interview. Industry codes were concorded between the 1980 and 2002 census codes and the SIC and NAICS codes. The density that a respondent faces during a self-employment spell is therefore localized in terms of both industry type and geographic location. The measure enters the regressions in logarithmic form.

Class-of-worker status is collapsed into a binary indicator taking the value 1 if self-employed in a particular year and 0 otherwise; unpaid work in an own family farm or business is not counted as self-employment. The random-effects logit models of exit use this status to model leaving self-employment in the following period.

Earnings of the self-employed are measured as the sum of military income, wage and salary income, and business or farm income in the previous calendar year. All three sources are combined because more than half of the self-employed respondents who earn positive earnings do not report business income. Supplementary questions are used to impute amounts for respondents who do not know or refuse to report the exact amount, taking the midpoint of a reported range or the minimum/maximum amount conforming with the respondent's answers.

Earnings in the first year of the self-employment spell, constructed in the same way as current earnings from military income, wage and salary income, and business or farm income in the previous calendar year. Two specifications are estimated, the second of which adds a control for earnings in the year prior to business creation.
time_window: first year of the self-employment spell

description: The growth rate of self-employment earnings of surviving firms over the interval (t, t+τ) conditional on profit at time t. The regression relates this growth rate to the log of density, the log of earnings, and the interaction of log density and log earnings.

Earnings in the year after an entrepreneur has returned to the paid labor force, measured as the sum of military income, wage and salary income, and business or farm income in the previous calendar year. In the model this quantity corresponds to w, the return from wage employment that constitutes the opportunity cost of running the business.
time_window: year after return to paid employment

description: The percentage of a company's outstanding shares held by its five largest blockholders. The authors describe it as a measure of ownership concentration that does not distinguish shareholders' identities and state that it is identical to the primary measure used by Prowse (1992). This variable was used to evaluate Hypotheses 1a and 2a.

The percentage of a company's outstanding shares held by Japanese financial companies. It is one of two identity-based ownership variables used to evaluate Hypotheses 1b and 2b, alongside ownership by nonfinancial companies.

The percentage of a company's outstanding shares held by Japanese nonfinancial companies. It is one of two identity-based ownership variables used to evaluate Hypotheses 1b and 2b, alongside ownership by financial institutions.

The ratio of net income to total assets. The authors state that ROA is a commonly used measure of profitability that has been used by others in the Japanese context, and that accounting-based measures such as ROA are preferable in studies relating ownership structure to financial performance.

The firm's return on assets in the prior period, entered as the lagged dependent variable; the authors assumed a one-period lag, and one year (1986) was lost because of the lagged dependent variable. The coefficient on this term reflects the ability of Japanese firms to redistribute profits, with lower values indicating greater redistribution.

A summed 10-item scale on the Competitor Analysis Form combining six aggressiveness items and four intelligence items on seven-point bipolar scales, giving a range of 10 to 70. Items 1-3 under the aggressiveness factor are taken from Peabody and Goldberg's (1989) surgency factor and items 4-6 were developed by the first author; the four intelligence items are from Peabody and Goldberg's intellect factor. The two subscales are highly correlated and a 10-item credibility scale composed of the six aggressiveness and four intelligence items has an alpha of 0.95. In the deterrence regression the attacker's ratings of the defender are averaged across the attacker team's members; the form was handed in with team decisions for turns 3, 6, and 8.
level: individual rating summed to a team mean
time_window: current period (turns 3, 6, and 8), with antecedent regressions using the rating made at the beginning of a period

description: Coded 1 if a team reports attacking a given rival in the current period and 0 otherwise, taken from the open-ended Competitor Reaction Form questions on whether decisions were a reaction to competitors' previous moves and whether decisions were directed at particular competitors. Answers were transcribed with information indicating team and time period deleted and coded by three independent coders, with a mean interrater agreement of 71% on observed attacks and reactions and disagreements resolved by discussion; when agreement on nonattacks is included the mean agreement is 93%.

The sum of advertising and salesforce expenditures in the previous period for the team being rated, divided by the industry average for that sum in the corresponding period. The expenditures are based on market research reports available in the game, and 2% of total observations were excluded because teams did not order the necessary reports.
time_window: previous period, relative to the corresponding period industry average

variable_name: Relative Number of Product Introductions and Modifications
description: The number of product introductions and modifications in the previous period by the team being rated, divided by the average number in that same period. Each period firms may introduce modified or entirely new brands, and these product changes are reported in all game outputs to teams.
time_window: previous period, relative to the same period average

description: For the team being rated, the mean period-to-period change in relative expenditures on advertising and salesforce over the history of the game to that point; for example, consistency in expense in period 5 for Team 1 is the mean period-to-period change in relative expense for periods 1 through 5. This measure is then reverse scored to make it a consistency measure.
time_window: whole game history up to the period being rated

variable_name: Consistency in Product Introductions and Modifications
description: For the team being rated, the mean period-to-period change in the relative number of product introductions and modifications over the history of the game to this point. The measure is calculated in the same manner as for Consistency in Expense, including the reverse scoring to make it a consistency measure.
time_window: whole game history up to the period being rated

description: A summed two-item scale composed of standardized observations on previous period rank in net marketing contribution, a profit measure, and previous period total unit market share. These were the success measures commonly used over the course of the game; the Cronbach alpha for Success is 0.88.

variable_name: Degree of adjustment in resource allocation to SBUs
description: Four-digit SIC codes are used to define SBUs, so the measure captures a firm's change in its resource allocation across its four-digit SIC businesses. In a three-step procedure, the authors first compute industry-adjusted SBU-level capital expenditure ratios by dividing the total capital expenditure allocated to the SBU by its total assets, minus the average investment ratio for the SBU's industry. Second, they calculate the absolute annual percentage point change in the capital expenditure ratio for each SBU. Third, they calculate the weighted average of annual changes in the capital expenditure ratios across all SBUs, using each SBU's share of the firm's total assets as weight, and the overall firm-level degree of adjustment is the sum of the weighted individual changes for all SBUs of the firm.
time_window: annual change between year t and t + 1

description: A firm's level of unrelated diversification is measured using the entropy measure (Arrfelt et al., 2015; Palepu, 1985). The formula block is not readable in the supplied text. The prose states that Pj is the percentage of firm sales in two-digit SIC code i for a company with M different two-digit SIC industry groups.

Operationalized by the volatility of industry sales over a 5-year period. Following Misangyi et al. (2006), the authors calculated environmental dynamism for each four-digit SIC code by regressing total industry sales over 5 years, with the focal year as a midpoint, on the year variable, and then divided the standard error of the slope coefficient by the mean of total industry sales for the 5-year period. Given the diversified nature of the firms, each firm's environmental dynamism is the average of the dynamism values for each four-digit industry in which the firm operated, weighted by relative SBU size (percentage of total firm assets).
time_window: 5-year window with the focal year as midpoint

description: The Herfindahl index is used to calculate the level of industry competitiveness, computed as the sum of the squared market shares of all companies operating in a particular four-digit SIC industry, which accounts for both the number of firms in the industry and their relative market power. The overall index is a weighted average based on SBU size (percentage of total firm assets) as the weight. The resulting index was multiplied by (−1) so that higher values serve as a proxy for higher levels of competitive activity.
Measured as the average number of new industries (based on four-digit SIC codes) entered in the past 5 years. This captures experience gained through recent new market entries.

A firm's debt-to-equity ratio relative to industry norms, that is, the focal firm's deviation from the industry average. The debt-to-equity ratio was deducted from one to ensure that higher values indicate greater slack.

The employees-to-sales ratio is used as an indicator of HR slack. As with financial slack, a firm's employees-to-sales ratio is considered relative to industry norms, that is, the focal firm's deviation from the industry average.

A dummy variable indicating whether or not a firm maintains a CSO position in each year. All senior managers and executives reported by the sample firms were retrieved from BoardEx, and managers whose job titles contained the word 'sustainability,' 'sustainable,' 'responsibility,' 'ethics,' or 'environment' were identified as CSOs; the role descriptions of those managers were then manually scrutinized to ensure validity. Firm-year observations with a CSO were coded as 1 and those without as 0.

Measured across five dimensions: community, diversity, employee relations, environment, and product issues. For each dimension KLD covers strengths and concerns and assigns a 1 or a 0 to each specific strength or concern; the standardized number of strengths was summed across the five dimensions to generate the CSR performance variable. The value was further standardized to make it comparable with CSiR, so the variable has a mean of zero and a SD of one. CSR was measured at year t + 1 to alleviate the concern of reverse causality.

Measured across five dimensions: community, diversity, employee relations, environment, and product issues. The total number of standardized concerns across the five dimensions was used to measure CSiR performance. The value was further standardized to make it comparable with CSR, so the variable has a mean of zero and a SD of one. CSiR was measured at year t + 1 to alleviate the concern of reverse causality.

A dummy variable indicating whether the firm had a specialized board committee on related issues in each year, coded as 1. The names of all board committees of a firm in the BoardEx database were reviewed, and committees having the word 'sustainability,' 'sustainable,' 'responsibility,' 'ethics,' or 'environment' in their names were coded as sustainability committees.

Firms operating in the tobacco, arms, natural resources, and alcohol industries were first identified based on SIC codes; firms that received a rating of 1 for the items related to 'tobacco,' 'firearms,' 'military,' 'alcohol,' or 'gambling' in the KLD database were then highlighted. The variable was coded as 1 if the observation met either of the two conditions, and 0 otherwise.

Whether the individual top executive departs from his or her current firm, established by examining whether the individual previously listed as a corporate executive is present on the list of corporate executives from the Execucomp database and company proxy statements in the subsequent three years. To ensure the individual had in fact departed, the firm's later list of top executives in Execucomp and the executive profile in BoardEx were examined. Departures within the three-year window were coded '1'; executives still employed by the firm but no longer reported among the top-five compensated executives were treated as right censored and coded '0'.
time_window: three years following the last reported year in Execucomp

description: A binary variable coded '1' if the newly appointed CEO was considered an outsider at the time of appointment and '0' if considered an insider. Outsider status was proxied by examining the successor's tenure at the focal firm: outside successors were newly appointed CEOs who had been at the focal firm for less than two years, whereas inside successors had at least two years of experience at the focal firm prior to becoming CEO.
time_window: at the time of CEO appointment

description: An indicator of the number of TMT members exiting the firm that year. All TMT members listed in Execucomp for a given year were examined to see whether they reappeared in the database in the subsequent three years; non-CEO executives who did not reappear were coded as exiting the focal firm. The exits were then summed, excluding the CEO and the focal top executive, for a given firm.
time_window: the focal year, with a three-year reappearance window

description: A count of Schedule 13D shareholder concern filings within the prior year, derived from the AuditAnalytics Shareholder Activism database, which provides information about Section 13(d) shareholder activism filings in which a shareholder indicates interest in influencing firm management. All Schedule 13D filings classified as shareholder concerns regarding management activities were examined.

A count of the legal cases in which the focal firm is listed as a lead defendant in a court case in the prior year, taken from the AuditAnalytics Legal Case and Legal Parties database, which provides information about civil cases filed in federal district courts.

Executive pay disparity was measured by dividing the focal executive's total current compensation by the average compensation of the other TMT members. Given the focus on top executives, the focal executive's compensation is measured relative to the other non-CEO members of the TMT.

Dummy variable that took a value of 1 if the later mover had survived the initial 4-year period in the new product category and 0 if it had dropped out of the market. The exit of each late entrant was verified through a combination of archival records and company interviews.
level: late entrant in a new product category

description: Market share in the third, fourth and fifth years after entry, used to compute an average market share for this 3-year period, and then log (base 10) transformed to reduce problems with heteroscedasticity. Market share figures were obtained for specific product categories from a variety of trade publications.
level: late entrant in a new product category

description: The number of significant competitors present in the market, reflecting the degree of competition that had already developed. It was obtained from the product reports published in Consumer Reports, which include all of the firms that have achieved sufficient national distribution, and was assessed for each late entrant in the year that it actually made its entry.

Extent of market saturation as indicated by the percentage of U.S. households that already owned the product at the time of the late mover's entry. The measure was obtained from various industry publications such as Appliance and Merchandising and assessed in the year of entry.
Size of the firm at the time of its entry, measured by the log transformation of its total annual sales. Sales were determined for the full year in which the late mover made its entry.

Dummy variable which was given a value of 1 if the late entrant had already operated for at least 3 years within the broadly defined 4-digit industry grouping as the new product category. It was determined on the basis of the firm's background within the same 4-digit industry grouping.

Relative price for each late mover's product, reported as a percentage of the average price calculated from the products of all significant competitors reported in the same Consumer Reports survey. The product reviews for a late entrant generally appeared between 2 and 3 years after entry.

Relative quality on key performance characteristics of each late mover's product, assessed as a percentage of the average quality calculated from the products of all significant competitors reported in the same Consumer Reports survey. Measures of product quality were based on the five-point ordinal scale that Consumer Reports uses to rate product performance on various characteristics.
scale: percentage, built from a five-point ordinal quality scale

description: Degree of innovation for each late mover's product, measured by a count of new product features listed under advantages in the Consumer Reports surveys. A relative measure was then derived by dividing the number of new product features for each late mover by the maximum number of new product features that were listed for other competitors covered in the same survey.
scale: ratio of new features to maximum number of new features

description: Dichotomous variable set to zero if the incumbent firm has a decentralized R&D unit and one if it has a centralized R&D unit. It is developed in four steps from top management team data in 10-K/20-F/DEF 14A SEC filings and annual reports, coding roles with the categorization of Guadalupe, Li, and Wulf (2014) and identifying all roles pertaining to R&D; for diversified firms only pharmaceutical R&D units are considered. The variable is set to 1 if the firm has a single integrated pharmaceutical R&D group and 0 if multiple R&D groups report to separate heads within the TMT covering different pharmaceutical domains or to leads of business units. The measure was validated through review of organizational descriptions and press releases and through interviews with managers from all incumbent firms in the sample.

The count of new drugs belonging to the entrepreneurial firm that enter phase 1 of clinical trials. The authors use the log of one plus the number of new drugs that enter phase 1 clinical trials for the entrepreneurial firm in the 3 years after the focal year. Entering phase 1 requires FDA Investigational New Drug approval and is treated as a signal of validation for the startup's technology.

This measure captures the diversification of the incumbent firm's drug development portfolio across therapeutic classes. Pharmaprojects classifies drugs into one or more of 18 classes based on therapeutic application. The measure is the sum of the squared proportions of drug candidates in each therapeutic class in the incumbent firm's overall clinical development portfolio, subtracted from 1, so higher values indicate a more diverse portfolio.

Measured analogously to Therapeutic Diversity Incumbent but using the therapeutic classes of drug candidates in the startup's development portfolio at the pre-clinical stage. The measure captures the breadth of the application areas to which startups are attempting to direct their technologies, with a higher value indicating that a startup's pre-clinical portfolio is spread over a wider range of therapeutic areas.

For each incumbent firm-year, the number of insiders in the CVC division of the incumbent firm. CVC managers were classified as 'insiders' if they had at least 3 years of prior experience within the incumbent firm in non-CVC roles. Manager identities were obtained from the Greyhouse and Galante Venture Capital directories and archived company web pages, and their career histories from linkedin.com and archive.org.

Equal to 1 if the startup's and the incumbent firm's headquarters are located in the same 2 digit zip code, which roughly encompasses metropolitan areas in the US. Information on the incumbent firm's headquarters comes from their annual reports and on startup headquarters from Venture Xpert.

Team-level TMT turnover was measured by analyzing the rate of executive departure across a three-year time period; all executives, including the CEO, were included in the turnover calculations. The number of executives who left the TMT within a three-year period were summed and divided by the total number of executives employed by the firm during the same three-year time span to yield an average turnover percentage for each firm. Each executive who left the TMT was coded as a turnover event, regardless of the reason for the departure reported in the ExecuComp database, because many turnover events list no reason and forced departures are often not reported as involuntary.

Firm performance was assessed using a rolling three-year average of return on assets (ROA), an average used to smooth yearly fluctuations in performance. The lag structure has one year of overlap between the averages for the independent/control variables and the dependent variable: average turnover rates from 1995 to 1997 are used to predict average firm performance from 1997 to 1999. This lag structure was selected to allow proximal chronological sequencing without capitalizing on short-term performance drops resulting from TMT changes.

Operationalized as the average organizational tenure of executives within the TMT for a given year. Tenure data were extracted from the ExecuComp database when available and supplemented by reviewing company 10-K filings when ExecuComp data were missing. All firms without complete tenure information on at least 60% of the reported executives were removed from the sample, and an average was taken of the executives with tenure information for each firm-year.

Following Keats and Hitt (1988), industry instability was measured by regressing sales across five years of time for each four-digit industry. The antilog of the standard error of each regression was used as the instability measure for each firm.

Industry munificence was measured using the same regression equation of sales across time, reflecting the overall growth in an industry, where greater growth is taken to indicate greater munificence. The antilog of the regression slope coefficient from this regression equation was used as the measure of munificence.

Industry complexity was measured using the same measure employed by Keats and Hitt (1988), which looks at firm market share to understand the concentration of a given industry, where greater concentration is said to reduce complexity. It is essentially a regression of terminal-year market shares of all firms in a given industry upon their shares in the initial year; the resulting regression coefficient suggests increasing or decreasing monopoly power in the industry.
time_window: initial- to terminal-year industry market shares

description: Firm financial strength was measured with statistics from Standard & Poor's Industry Surveys: return on equity (ROE), debt/equity ratio (DE) and dividends paid as a percentage of earnings (DIVPAY). Each firm's position was compared both with the average of its competitor group and with its own financial record over the three prior years; the year preceding the divestment decision is the focal year. Hypotheses H1 and H2 were tested with these measures.
time_window: year preceding the divestment decision; three prior years for the firm's own record

description: Unit strength was assessed from the interview data and covers both unit financial strength and unit competitive strength. The measures are the unit's performance compared with other units of the firm, with its planned performance and with performance expected from the firm's alternative resource uses, its profit and sales growth rates compared with those of its firm, its contribution to firm profits, its projected resource needs, its competitive position as a major or minor factor in its industry, and its autonomy relative to other units.
time_window: year before the divestment decision (three years for performance compared with planned performance)

description: Interdependency was measured from the personal interviews with firms' managers. The measures are the transfer of technology from the unit to other units of its firm, the proportion of plant and equipment shared with other units, the proportion of the unit's sales to customers of the firm's other units, and the proportions of the unit's interfirm sales and interfirm purchases.

The general external economic conditions at the time of each divestment decision were classified by the researcher as expansion or contraction according to guidelines of the National Bureau of Economic Research. The variable reflects the conditions within which the firm and its units were operating at the time of the divestment decision.

A unit-specific measure of the degree and nature of the relationship between the divestment decision-maker and the unit that is a divestment candidate, taken from the personal interviews. The manager whose attachment to the unit is of most interest is the Chief Executive Officer (CEO).

The observation is the firm's decision to divest a whole business unit, taken from the divestments made (or in progress) by the participating firms during the study period that the interviewee felt most familiar with. The hypotheses were tested by comparing the distributions of units' and firms' classifications on the factors with expected frequencies using non-parametric tests.

Count of the different types of innovation partners with which the plant was working, built from the plant's binary responses to eight questions about the types of external partners used as part of product or process development. Values range from 0 to 8. Linkages to other group companies were asked about in the questionnaire but excluded from this measure.

Dummy variable which takes value 1 if the plant was engaged in openness prior to the current period (i.e., used any external linkages in either of the two previous surveys) and zero otherwise; it is used to partition the current breadth measure. In further estimations the prior dummy is set to 1 if the plant had at least one, two, three, four, five, or six knowledge linkages during at least one of the two previous periods, in order to establish what extent of previous breadth is required for learning effects.
time_window: either of the two previous survey periods

description: The proportion of the plant's total sales (at the end of each three-year reference period) derived from products newly introduced or improved during the previous three years. It reflects units' ability to introduce innovative products to the market as well as their short-term commercial success. Around 60 percent of plants reported introducing such new or improved products over the sample.
time_window: previous three years, measured at the end of each three-year reference period

description: A measure of the total sales revenue derived from new and improved products introduced over the previous three years, used in logarithmic form. It measures the value of sales of innovative products, as opposed to their importance in the unit's portfolio.

Binary variable coded '1' for the first year a politician connected to a lobbyist is selected to be a chair of a congressional committee or is assigned to one of the powerful committees in Congress, and '0' otherwise. The authors use appointments to committee chair and assignments to the four most powerful committees in Congress to capture connected politicians' power changes in the legislative process, treating these power changes as plausibly exogenous conditional on observables.
time_window: measured at t (the period before mobility)

description: Binary dependent variable coded '1' if a lobbyist's primary employer had changed since the previous period and '0' otherwise. Mobility variables are measured at t + 1 and the rest of the variables are calculated at t, which for movers is the period prior to mobility. Among the 1,108 revolving door lobbyists in the sample, the total number of exits is 555 in the 10-year sample period.

Binary dependent variable coded '1' if a lobbyist either creates or joins a start-up after leaving a firm in the lobbying data in the previous period, and '0' otherwise. Entrepreneurship is identified when an employee joins a firm in the first period that the firm is observed in the data. Among the 555 exits, 156 are entrepreneurship.

The paper distinguishes mobility to established firms from employee entrepreneurship and runs the same models with the likelihood of mobility to established firms as the dependent variable, using the same approach as for entrepreneurship. In the sample of employee exits (555 observations) the likelihood of spin-out conditional on exit is modelled, so entrepreneurship is contrasted with mobility to an established firm.

A weighted measure of employee-firm distance in the knowledge space, based on the assumption that the knowledge distance between the firm and the employee, measured in terms of overlap of lobbying issues, is proportional to knowledge-relatedness among issues; it captures both the overlap of issues central to the firm and joint use between issues central to the firm and those covered by the lobbyist. A knowledge-relatedness matrix among the 78 issues predefined in Congress is built from issue co-occurrence in lobbying reports, and the distance between firm m and employee n is calculated as the angular separation of the firm's and employee's issue revenue-share vectors weighted by that matrix (following Jaffe 1986 and Bloom et al. 2013). The authors set the distance variable at its mean and take only observations with an unchanged unweighted angular separation measure, so that remaining variability comes from yearly shifts in the knowledge-relatedness matrix.
time_window: yearly variation in the knowledge-relatedness matrix; measured at t

description: Instances of audiences' stigmatizing labels aimed at arms producers, identified by searching media articles for each firm's name together with keywords such as critic*, attack*, under pressure* and condemn*, and then content-coded by the authors. Events were dropped when other significant activities occurred in a (-3, +3) window around the event, when the firm was not publicly traded, when no stock market information was available during the estimation period, and when multiple actors criticized the firm on the same day. The final sample is 534 events targeting 113 firms.

A stigmatizing label was coded as illegality content when it accused the arms producer of rule violations, fraud, bribery, or the leaking of secrets, using illegality-related keywords; of the 534 events, 196 concerned allegations of illegal behavior. In the regressions a dummy variable takes the value of 1 when political actors shamed the arms producer's behavior as illegal and 0 when other actors did the same.

A stigmatizing label was coded as harm content when it highlighted the physical and social harm caused by the arms producer, emphasizing death, killing, damage, torture, the promotion of conflict, and global insecurity and instability, using harm-related keywords such as kill*, harm*, tortur* and war crime*. Of the 534 events, 168 were allegations of harmful behavior. In the regressions a dummy variable takes the value of 1 when civil society actors shamed the arms producer's behavior as harmful and 0 when other actors did the same.

Labels aimed at the economic exchange relationship between an arms producer and a third party (e.g., investing in, working for, or being sponsored by an arms producer) and problematizing the affiliation as inappropriate and unethical, using keywords such as unethical, immoral, illegitimate together with deal*, invest*, tie*, sponsor* or contribut*. Of the 534 events, 170 were levied at affiliates by association. In the regressions a dummy variable takes the value of 1 when financial actors shamed affiliations with third parties as inappropriate and 0 when other actors did the same.

Audience coding of who articulated the stigmatizing label, derived from the content analysis of the media articles; political actors are politicians and elected officials and political parties. A dummy variable takes the value of 1 when the stigmatizing label shaming the firm's behavior as illegal was enacted by political actors and 0 when it was enacted by the remaining audiences.

Audience coding of who articulated the stigmatizing label, derived from the content analysis of the media articles; civil society actors are journalists, activists and religious organizations, who are the quintessential moral entrepreneurs evaluating firms with respect to the overall well-being of society. A dummy variable takes the value of 1 when the stigmatizing label shaming the firm's behavior as harmful was enacted by civil society actors and 0 when it was enacted by the remaining audiences.

Audience coding of who articulated the stigmatizing label, derived from the content analysis of the media articles; financial actors are market actors such as current investors, financial analysts and potential investors or customers. A dummy variable takes the value of 1 when the stigmatizing label shaming affiliations with third parties as inappropriate was enacted by financial actors and 0 when it was enacted by the remaining audiences.

Cumulative abnormal return computed with the market model: the abnormal daily return is the stock's actual return minus its expected return, and CARs are the sum of abnormal returns within the event window. Market model coefficients are estimated by ordinary least squares over the period t = -250 to t = -50 relative to the event, using the equally weighted CRSP (or Compustat Capital IQ-Global) market portfolio, and the publication date of the article is day 0; the primary window is the two-day (0,1) window. The mean CAR for (0,1) is -0.35%.

The TMT was defined as those executives identified by their firms as strategically important and included in the firm's Form 10-Ks and proxy statements. These documents were manually searched for CSOs using the terms 'strategy/strategic,' 'development,' or 'planning' in titles as a starting point, and all TMT members' titles and, where necessary, their role descriptions were analyzed for completeness. Firms with a CSO were coded as 1 and those without as 0. Because the exact appointment date could sometimes not be determined, CSO presence was determined at the end of each year.
scale: 1 = firm with a CSO in its TMT; 0 = firm without a CSO

description: An accounting-based performance measure, extensively used in prior TMT research, used to analyze the performance consequences of CSO presence.
A market-based measure of firm performance reflecting the stockholders' premium placed on the firm's equity and indicating the stockholders' expectations regarding the firm's future prospects.

Palepu's (1985) entropy measure of diversification, which considers the degrees of related, unrelated, and total diversification of a firm's business portfolio. The reported results are for total diversification; measures of related and unrelated diversification were also initially used. The variable is lagged by one year.
The logarithm of the average number of acquisitions over the past three years. The variable is lagged by one year.
time_window: average over the past three years, lagged by one year

description: The logarithm of the average number of new alliances over the past three years. The variable is lagged by one year.
time_window: average over the past three years, lagged by one year

description: Computed as the logarithm of the firm's total sales. The variable is lagged by one year.
Blau's (1977) heterogeneity index based on six functional categories of the TMT members' titles. The variable is lagged by one year.

Each member was asked to rank all members on the level of leadership shown, so that in a five-member team the rankings ranged from 1 to 5, with the person ranked 1 showing the highest leadership level. A team was considered to have a distinct leader when all members ranked the same member as 1. These teams were coded 1 and teams with no distinct leaders were coded 0. In the sample, 28 (55%) teams had distinct leaders.

Educational background diversity was calculated with the Teachman Index, chosen over the Blau Index because the Blau Index is sensitive to the underlying frequency distribution. The prose states only that the index was calculated from Pi, the fraction of members in each category; the explicit formula is not available in the text. Educational background was coded into 10 areas, including computer science, engineering, science, and business administration, based on members' highest educational level, and records submitted to the competition organizers were used for members who did not respond to the questionnaires.

A four-item, 7-point instrument developed by Stokes (1983), with alpha of 0.65. Sample items included 'There are certain topics which my group avoids talking about' (reverse coded) and 'My group is very straight-forward with me'. Individual scores were aggregated to team scores based on within-team agreement; average rwg was 0.85, with 43 estimates exceeding 0.70.

A nine-item, 7-point scale developed by Smith et al. (1994), with a scale alpha of 0.69; the original nine-item scale was retained because the reliability increase from dropping the first item was marginal. Sample items included 'The members of the team are quick to defend each other from criticism by outsiders', 'The success of other members of the team help me achieve my own objectives', and 'Everyone's input is incorporated into most important company decisions'. Individual ratings were aggregated to the team level after checking agreement (mean rwg of 0.89), and the authors averaged the scores for each team.

A seven-item, 7-point Likert scale instrument developed by Hackman (1988), with alpha of 0.75. Sample items included 'Members of the team care a lot about it, and work together to make it one of the best', 'Working with members of the team is an energizing and uplifting experience', and 'As a team, this work group shows signs of falling apart' (reverse coded). Individual responses were aggregated to the team level; mean rwg was 0.89 with 47 out of 51 estimates above 0.70.

A three-item instrument on a 7-point scale developed by Hackman (1988), with alpha of 0.71. The items were 'Generally speaking I am very satisfied with the team', 'I frequently wish I could quit the team', and 'I am generally satisfied with the work I do on the team'. Individual scores were aggregated to team level; average rwg value was 0.94 with 49 out of 51 estimates above 0.70.

Normalized betweenness centrality computed on the inventor's copatenting with respect to all of the firm's copatenting in (t-4, t). For each year the authors considered all patents the firm filed in (t-4, t) and built a collaboration graph linking inventors who coauthored at least one patent, weighting links by the Jaccard coefficient. Node betweenness was computed on the weighted network, with shortest paths minimizing the cost of connecting inventors assumed inversely proportional to interaction strength, and then normalized using the minimum and maximum realized values of node betweenness in the network. Whenever an inventor was unproductive in (t-4, t), the inventor's collaboration centrality was multiplied by a 15% yearly decaying component.
scale: zero to a theoretical maximum of one

description: Normalized betweenness centrality computed on the inventor's USPC combinations with respect to the firm's USPC combinations in (t-4, t). The authors counted how often two three-digit USPC classes co-occurred in the firm's patents in (t-4, t) and standardized the co-occurrence count with a Jaccard coefficient, computed normalized node betweenness for each USPC class in the resulting technology network, and then computed for each inventor the weighted value of the betweenness centrality of the three-digit USPC classes in which the inventor was active. The weight is the share of the inventor's patents in (t-4, t) classified in each technology.

A binary indicator set to one when the focal inventor leaves the firm to join another employment context and zero otherwise. If the LinkedIn profile of the inventor shows two consecutive jobs, first with the firm and then with a different firm, and the time gap is no more than one year, the authors suppose the inventor left the firm in the starting year of the record. During the time frame of the study, 1,429 inventors left the firm to join 801 other incumbent firms and 128 inventors left to start 77 new ventures.

A binary indicator set to one when the focal inventor is recruited by another firm and zero otherwise. The authors distinguished mobility events using the LinkedIn profile: if it cites 'founder' as the inventor's job title at another employer the move was classified as entrepreneurship, otherwise as a move to another employer.

A binary indicator set to one when the focal inventor leaves the firm to either start or join the founding team of a new venture and zero otherwise. The classification is based on the LinkedIn profile citing 'founder' as the inventor's job title at another employer. The authors also searched public information on each detected new venture and excluded self-employment (freelance consultants) and misspecifications in LinkedIn profiles.

For each unit-month, the number of nurses in a unit who voluntarily left the organization in a given month as a proportion of the number of nurses in the unit at the beginning of that month. Involuntary separations were not examined. The percentage values of turnover rates were transformed by the inverse hyperbolic sine function.
scale: percentage of unit (transformed by the inverse hyperbolic sine function)

description: For each unit-month, the number of new nurses hired from outside the organization into a unit within a given month relative to the number of nurses in the unit at the beginning of the month. Percentage values were transformed by the inverse hyperbolic sine function.
scale: percentage of unit (transformed by the inverse hyperbolic sine function)

description: For each unit-month, the monthly number of nurses transferred out of a unit relative to the number of nurses in the unit at the beginning of the month. Percentage values were transformed by the inverse hyperbolic sine function.
scale: percentage of unit (transformed by the inverse hyperbolic sine function)

description: For each unit-month, the monthly number of nurses transferred into a unit relative to the number of nurses in the unit at the beginning of the month. Percentage values were transformed by the inverse hyperbolic sine function.
scale: percentage of unit (transformed by the inverse hyperbolic sine function)

description: Calculated by dividing monthly-adjusted patient-days by the number of nurses employed by the unit in that month. The result captures the intensity of activity an average nurse would experience at work.

Measured through a questionnaire administered to patients immediately following their hospital stay, using six of 27 items from the Hospital Consumer Assessment of Healthcare Providers and Systems (HCAHPS) survey that focused on nursing services. Scores were aggregated to the unit level to arrive at monthly unit-level patient satisfaction scores. Scores theoretically ranged from zero to 100, but the observed range was narrower (64.5-98.5).

The absolute value of the difference between the firm's current performance and its current historical aspiration level; historical aspiration is built with the classic recursive measure At = alpha Pt-1 + (1 - alpha) At-1, where the aspiration level adjusts to prior performance and prior aspirations. A fixed value of alpha of 0.75 was chosen, and the first-year aspiration is defined solely by the performance of the first year in the data. Current performance is measured with return on assets.
time_window: performance at t-1, aspiration and shortfall at t

description: The absolute value of the difference between the focal firm's actual performance and the average performance of its peer group. Peer groups were identified by exact matching on year and three-digit SIC industry and then selecting the five closest peers by Mahalanobis distance on revenue and total assets, after which the average peer performance was subtracted from the focal firm's actual performance. Current performance is measured with return on assets.
time_window: performance at t-1, aspiration and shortfall at t

description: The annual acquisition rate was measured as the number of majority acquisitions announced each calendar year. A frequency-based measure was used because focal companies frequently undertook multiple transactions within a year and because transaction values are not published for most deals. Acquisition frequency is a measure of organizational change in the performance feedback literature.

The annual divestment rate was measured as the number of divestments announced each calendar year. A frequency-based measure was used because focal companies frequently undertook multiple transactions within a year and because transaction values are not published for most deals.

Financial slack was based on leverage and measured using the equity-to-debt ratio, chosen over the more commonly used debt-to-equity ratio to make the results easier to interpret: large equity-to-debt values indicate large financial slack. The ratio between equity and debt is commonly used as the measure for 'potential slack'. The time horizon of acquisitions was considered long enough for firms to arrange financing if required and available.

This dummy variable took a value of 1 when the CEO belonged to the family that controlled the firm as per the authors' definition of family ties (n = 148). It took a value of 0 when the CEO was not a member of the family (n = 105).

Total compensation for the 1995-98 period, the sum of salary, bonuses, and long-term income (LTI). The cash compensation components (salary and bonuses) were valued in U.S. dollars. Following previous work, the value of stock options was calculated as the number of options granted to a CEO multiplied by 25 percent of the exercise price.

Long-term income for the 1995-98 period.
