Total compensation (TDC1) from Execucomp, the sum of the CEO's salary, bonuses, other annual compensation, total value of restricted stocks granted, total value of stock options granted (using the Black-Scholes formula), long-term incentive payouts, and all other total compensation. Because the distribution of compensation is highly skewed, one was added to TDC1 and the natural log was taken. The dependent variable is measured in the year following the media appearance.
The natural log of the total assets of the firm, taken from the accounting information merged into the sample.
The holding period return over the 12 months until the end of the fiscal year, computed from the stock price and return data merged into the sample.
time_window: 12 months until the end of fiscal year t

description: A dummy variable indicating whether the CEO is a founder of the company, constructed by hand-collecting information about the CEO using various sources including Forbes, Fortune, Factiva, Google, and the company website. The authors tracked the history of the company and identified the names of the founders, and identified the CEO as a founder if his or her full name was the same as one of the founders.

A dummy variable identifying CEOs who had more than 5% equity ownership of their company, following Jenter and Kanaan (2015). The authors used a threshold rather than a continuous variable of CEO equity ownership because equity ownership may meaningfully affect a CEO's decision and behavior only beyond a certain level of ownership.

The first factor produced by a principal components analysis with varimax rotation performed on items tied to financial, operational, and effectiveness dimensions; it explained 37.7 percent of the variation in the data and had an eigenvalue of 5.77. The scale was based on 16 items from Contractor and Lorange (1988). It represents the logic that when very important strategic needs are being met very well, an alliance can be said to be performing well.

The second factor from the same principal components analysis, explaining an additional 20.7 percent of the total variation and having an eigenvalue of 3.19. It captures other critical dimensions of alliance performance.

The payoff structure was completed by the respondents using a four-cell matrix in which one cell, mutual cooperation, served as the anchor; respondents estimated their own payoffs under the other behavioral combinations. The measure exhibited a high test-retest reliability (.91) in a pilot test on executives participating in the pretest interviews over the suggested two-week interval. The payoff structure is captured by the payoff residuals UD - MC, MC - MD, and UD - UC.

Estimated by respondents in the same four-cell payoff matrix, as the payoff to the respondent's firm in the combination where its own firm cooperates and the partner firm behaves opportunistically. Mutual cooperation served as the anchor cell against which the other payoffs were stated.

An additive model was postulated to represent behavioral transparency: transparency = information source + information accuracy + time lag. Speed was measured on a scale specifying four ranges ("over 1 month" to "within 1 day") and reverse-scored. Reliability was measured by asking about the source and accuracy of information regarding a partner's behavior, with a choice of sources typically used (own firm's employees, alliance itself, partner firm) and a four-point range of accuracy ("never" to "always").
Assessed with two items, one asking the number of senior executive meetings occurring annually and the other assessing lower-level interactions. The two components were weighted equally.
Measured as the product of two items, the intended duration of an alliance and the perceived likelihood of the alliance lasting through the intended duration.
Respondents were asked to describe the potential for their partner's behaving opportunistically using John's (1984) six-item scale, which similar studies have also employed.

The level of ex post deterrent use was assessed with a list of contractual safeguards developed from a computer-aided search of the relevant legal literature and corroborated by the senior executives participating in pretest interviews. The safeguards were arranged in a presumed order of increasing stringency and assigned their corresponding values, for example the first safeguard had a value of 1, the fourth, 4. A composite index of ex post deterrents was computed as the safeguards used divided by 36, where the denominator is the summation of all eight safeguards.
The level of ex ante deterrents was gauged as the degree of potential loss that would occur through nonrecoverable investments in the event of alliance dissolution.

If there were no prior alliances between two partners, the variable was equal to zero; otherwise, its value was the product of the number of alliances the two firms had participated in and the number of years the two firms had been partners.

variable_name: Transparency, frequency of interaction and time horizon
description: The shadow of the future is measured by three survey indicators treated as a set: behavioral transparency, frequency of interaction, and length of time horizons. They are entered together as one variable set in the canonical analysis of performance and in the safeguards models.

variable_name: Exchange history (number of prior exchanges, all deals)
description: The number of all transactions prior to the focal deal in which the acquirer hired the same advisor for intermediary services. The count is taken over a five-year moving window preceding the focal deal date; in the 9% of deals in which acquirers hired multiple advisors, the maximum value of the measure was used, assuming that the advisor with the most extensive exchange history played a representative role. The count was transformed by taking the log of 1 + x.
time_window: five-year moving window preceding the focal deal

description: A dummy variable equal to 1 if the target is privately held or a nonlisted division of a public firm and 0 otherwise. It is used as an indicator of information uncertainty about the target: less information is likely to be available to the acquirer if the target is not a listed firm.

The aggregated forecasting errors of individual stock returns in the target's industry, indicating how volatile or unpredictable stock prices are in that industry. The author first computed the volatility of stock returns for all firms in Compustat by using the single-factor model, then computed the log of the mean volatility of each industry as defined by its three-digit SIC code, and finally assigned to each target the volatility measure of its industry.

The acquirer's propensity to rehire the same investment bank in subsequent M&A transactions, computed as the number of advisors the acquirer hired in more than one deal up to the focal deal date divided by the total number of advisors hired by the acquirer for M&As during the same period. Both counts treat each deal-bank pair as a separate instance, so the same advisor hired for two different deals is counted twice, and all M&A transactions in the seven years preceding the focal deal are included. Acquirers with no prior transactions were assigned the mean propensity of all other acquirers in the corresponding year.
time_window: seven years preceding the focal deal

description: The difference between the observed returns on an acquirer's stock and the expected returns, accumulated over the three days surrounding the date on which the transaction was publicly announced. Expected returns were estimated with the market model using return data over the period between 250 days and 41 days before the event; the abnormal return is the difference between the actual and the predicted return, and the CAR is the sum of the abnormal returns over the event window. A negative reaction suggests that investors perceived the acquisition price to be higher than the target value, which the author interprets as overpayment.

KLD STATS classifies its CSR-related items into controversial business areas and qualitative issue areas, and gives a binary (1/0) rating for a set of strengths and concerns in each qualitative issue area. The authors use only CSR strengths, not strengths minus concerns, and omit corporate governance and product characteristics, so the score is built from the community, diversity, employee relations, environment and human rights areas. Data for the individual underlying indicators are not available, so the indicators cannot be classified according to the tacit or codified knowledge they embody. Separate regressions replace the aggregate score with the score of each issue area.

The measure adapts an indicator developed by Sorenson and Audia and is a weighted density of CSR engagement around the focal firm: i refers to the focal firm at time t and j refers to all other firms, CSRjt is the CSR engagement score for firm j at time t, and d is the distance between firm i and firm j. The exact functional form is not readable in the text available. The measure increases if the number of nearby firms engaged in CSR increases or if the level of engagement increases, and the authors state it is superior to density measures based on simple counts of firms within a jurisdiction.

Distance is the log of the distance from the corporate headquarters to the center of the nearest financial center measured in kilometers, computed with the Great Circle Distance Formula. The six financial centers are Boston, Chicago, Los Angeles, New York, Philadelphia and San Francisco, isolated for having the largest number of financial intermediaries. In the alternative models the measure is replaced by dummy variables: Distance < 100 km equals 1 if the firm is headquartered within 100 km of the center of the nearest financial center and 0 otherwise, and Distance < 250 miles equals 1 if the firm is situated within 250 miles of that center and 0 otherwise.

The ex-ante cost of equity capital is backed out of current stock prices and analyst forecasts of earnings using four practical implementations of the dividend discount model, following Hail and Leuz: the Ohlson and Juettner-Nauroth (KOJN), Easton (KMPEG), Claus and Thomas (KCT) and Gebhardt, Lee and Swaminathan (KGLS) approaches. The 10-year U.S. Treasury bond yield is subtracted from the estimated cost of equity of each model, and the average estimate obtained from the four models (KAVG) is retained as the dependent variable.
time_window: forecasts as of June of year t; 10-year Treasury yield

description: In the first stage of the two-stage estimation procedure, CSR engagement is predicted for each firm-year using the model regressing CSR engagement on CSR density, distance and the control variables (Model 1 of Table 3). The fitted score of CSR engagement is then used in the second stage, both on its own and interacted with CSR density, to explain the cost of equity capital.

The dependent variable, a developer's choice to release a game title for a given console, defined as categorical and time-varying. yij,t equaled 1 if developer i on date t released a game title for console j, where j was a console in the developer's choice set, J it; for the remaining consoles in the developer's choice set, yij,t equaled 0. The choice set was not constant: consoles for which the title had already been released were excluded, obsolete consoles were permanently removed, and the introduction of a new console increased the number of consoles in the choice set.

Overlap density (Baum & Singh, 1994) measuring the potential competition faced by developers in the platform j niche. The term pij,t denotes the proportion of titles that developer i released to platform j, and pik,t the proportion of titles developer i released to platform k; wkj,t is the degree of overlap between the niches of platforms k and j, defined on the interval 0 to 1, where 0 means two disjoint sets of developers and 1 means developers released titles for both platforms. Because the Euclidean metric is symmetric while the overlap weight is in general asymmetric, the authors used Sohn's (2001) overlap metric; the equation itself is not readable in the text.

Platform embeddedness using Uzzi's (1996) second-order coupling: Pji,t denotes the proportion of platform j's video games released by developer i on date t for platform j, and platform embeddedness is the sum over i of the squared values of Pji,t. It varies between 0 and 1; a value close to 1.0 meant that a platform was tightly embedded with (supported by) a few developers, and a value close to 0 meant a platform was loosely embedded with (supported by) many developers.

Platform j's dominance on date t is the number of titles released by all developers for the platform divided by the total number of titles in the network. The authors state that the range of platform dominance is from 0.0 to 1.0.

Platform age in months on the release date t of a game title, defined as the difference between that date and console j's launch date. A developer was predicted to be more likely to release a title for a newer platform, that is, the odds of releasing a title decrease for higher values of the difference between the title's launch date and the platform's launch date.

Count of citations made by firm i's optical disk patents in year t that were traced to patents assigned to the same firm (self-citations). Because self-citations and nonself-citations sum to total citations, which is included in the model, the coefficient on self-citation represents the difference between the effects of self-citation and nonself-citation on impact.

Count of citations made by firm i's optical disk patents in year t that were traced to built-upon patents classified in one of the optical disk technology classes. Because disk citations and nondisk citations sum to total citations, which is included in the model, the coefficient on disk citation represents the difference between the effects of disk citation and nondisk citation on impact.

Count of the firm's citations in year t that are in the optical disk area and were filed by the firm itself (self-citations that are also disk citations). This type of exploration spans neither the organizational nor the technological boundary. In Model 3 the four exploration measures sum to the total number of citations, so the total citations term is implicitly controlled for even though it is omitted from the regression.

Count of the firm's citations in year t that are in the optical disk area but were not filed by the firm itself (nonself-citations that are disk citations). This type of exploration spans the organizational boundary but not the technological boundary. In Model 3 the four exploration measures sum to the total number of citations, so the total citations term is implicitly controlled for even though it is omitted from the regression.

Count of the firm's citations in year t that are not in the optical disk area but were filed by the firm itself (self-citations that are not disk citations). This type of exploration spans the technological boundary but not the organizational boundary. In Model 3 the four exploration measures sum to the total number of citations, so the total citations term is implicitly controlled for even though it is omitted from the regression.

Count of the firm's citations in year t that are not in the optical disk area and were not filed by the firm itself (nonself-citations that are not disk citations). This type of exploration spans both the organizational and the technological boundary. In Model 3 the four exploration measures sum to the total number of citations, so the total citations term is implicitly controlled for even though it is omitted from the regression.

Number of citations from optical disk patents (citing patents classified in the optical disk subclasses) received by firm i's patents granted in year t. For this measure self-citations were excluded. Year dummies are included to control for the greater citation risk of patents granted in earlier years.
time_window: citations received after the focal patents were granted

description: Total number of citations from nonoptical disk patents received by firm i's patents granted in year t. For this measure self-citations were excluded. Year dummies are included to control for the greater citation risk of patents granted in earlier years.
time_window: citations received after the focal patents were granted

description: The absolute value of the average cumulative abnormal returns to the firm's prior acquisition deals. It is the measure of prior investor reaction used in the logit models of whether the focal deal is an acquisition, and it is reported to enter those models with a negative sign.

The absolute value of the average cumulative abnormal returns to the firm's prior alliance deals. It is the measure of prior investor reaction used in the logit models of whether the focal deal is an alliance, and it is reported to enter those models with a positive sign.

The portion of all of the firm's prior deals that are acquisitions. It measures the firm's concentrated experience with acquisitions and is used in the models of the change in CARs and as a control in the deal-type logit models.
time_window: all prior deals up to the focal deal

description: The portion of all of the firm's prior deals that are alliances. It measures the firm's concentrated experience with alliances and is used in the models of the change in CARs and as a control in the deal-type logit models.
time_window: all prior deals up to the focal deal

description: The squared portion of all prior deals as acquisitions, included to capture nonlinear, diminishing, or enhanced effects of prior acquisition experience.
time_window: all prior deals up to the focal deal

description: The squared portion of all prior deals as alliances, included to capture nonlinear, diminishing, or enhanced effects of prior alliance experience.
time_window: all prior deals up to the focal deal

description: The difference between the absolute value of the cumulative abnormal return to the focal acquisition and the average absolute value of the cumulative abnormal returns to the firm's prior acquisition deals. It represents the change in the stock market response between the focal deal and the firm's prior acquisition deals.
time_window: focal deal relative to prior acquisition deals

description: The difference between the absolute value of the cumulative abnormal return to the focal alliance and the average absolute value of the cumulative abnormal returns to the firm's prior alliance deals. It represents the change in the stock market response between the focal deal and the firm's prior alliance deals.
time_window: focal deal relative to prior alliance deals

description: Indicator dependent variable that takes the value of one if the focal deal is an acquisition. It is used in the logit models that test whether the incidence of a deal type depends on prior investor reactions.

Indicator dependent variable that takes the value of one if the focal deal is an alliance. It is used in the logit models that test whether the incidence of a deal type depends on prior investor reactions.

Scale of three items developed from the line employee and supervisor interviews: 'I follow standard operating procedures for safety, quality, and production', 'My job is repetitive, but I stay alert so I don't get hurt or make poor quality products', and 'I follow standard operating procedures to get my work done'. All variables were measured with a seven-point Likert scale (strongly disagree/strongly agree). Coefficient alpha for the scale was 0.62.
scale: seven-point Likert scale (strongly disagree to strongly agree)

description: Scale of three items: 'I make suggestions for new procedures to improve safety and quality', 'I think of new ways to solve problems', and 'I suggest new ideas to improve quality, safety, and production procedures'. Items were rated on a seven-point Likert scale (strongly disagree/strongly agree). Coefficient alpha for the scale was 0.78.
scale: seven-point Likert scale (strongly disagree to strongly agree)

description: Scale of three items: 'I discover new ways of making new products', 'I create new products and processes', and 'I figure out what to make and how to make it'. Items were rated on a seven-point Likert scale. Coefficient alpha for the scale was 0.75. The authors used this measure to contrast improvement activities measured as continuous improvement with the same activities measured as innovation.

Scale of four items: 'It's the supervisor's job to come up with ways to improve things, not mine', 'I fill out the control charts. Someone else checks them and tells me if there's a problem', 'When my control chart goes out of specifications, I call over my supervisor or maintenance', and 'I have enough to do with production. Someone else should come up with ideas on how to improve things'. Items were rated on a seven-point Likert scale. Coefficient alpha for the scale was 0.60. For plant-level percentages the authors counted line employees scoring 3.95 and above as using avoidance.

Scale of five items: 'When my control chart goes out of specifications, I immediately try to figure out what is causing the problem', 'While doing production, I come up with new ideas to improve my work', 'I figure out how to improve my work not only in total quality meetings, but also while doing production', 'At my workstation, I brainstorm with others to solve problems or improve the work that I do', and 'When my products are not up to quality standards, I try to solve the problem at once'. Items were rated on a seven-point Likert scale. Coefficient alpha for the scale was 0.71. For plant-level analyses the authors took the median scores and calculated the percentage of line employees whose scores were 5 and above.
level: line employee (individual); aggregated to the plant

description: Five items from Rizzo et al.'s (1970) scale were selected as indicators of role conflict in a manufacturing context and were reworded to reflect the language of the participants. The appendix lists four of these items, such as 'I am asked to do things that do not help me get the job done' and 'One person wants me to do my job one way, and another person wants me to do it another way'. Items were rated on a seven-point Likert scale. Coefficient alpha for the scale was 0.68.

Scale of four items: 'I'm unable to do production as well as I used to because I also have to do total quality', 'It's difficult to do production and total quality at the same time', 'It's harder to keep my productivity up, because now I have to think of total quality', and 'Keeping up with production is harder, since I also have to do total quality'. Items were rated on a seven-point Likert scale. Coefficient alpha for the scale was 0.76.

Scale of three measures, satisfaction with the job, the work, and the coworkers: 'Overall, I am satisfied with my job', 'I like the work I do', and 'I like working with the people who work here'. Items were rated on a seven-point Likert scale. Coefficient alpha for the scale was 0.72.

Plant performance was measured via classifications of TQM performance (high, medium, and low) for each plant, as judged by eight senior managers (two from each division) and by two to six relevant peer managers from other plants. These data were augmented by longitudinal archival performance data from a five-year period (1988-1992). The ranking was based on the average TQM performance evaluations for each plant.
scale: high, medium, and low performance classifications

description: Using the data from the qualitative analysis, the plants were sorted into three broad categories, superficial, moderate, and full implementations; the variable ranged from 1 to 3, with 3 reflecting full implementation. Five plants were observed to be at a superficial degree of implementation, two were classified as moderate, and three were classified as fully implementing TQM. The assessments were made by the researchers prior to the collection of any employee-level data and did not rely on the data concerning the use of switching in the plant.

variable_name: Standardized production plus continuous improvement work
description: The dual TQM role is described through the combination of two line-employee survey scales, standardized production work and continuous improvement work, supported by interview profiles of the line employee job. Both are reported as present together in the TQM job.

Total number of pieces of financial (semantic) information the participant selected through Search Monitor, regardless of the category the information originated in, measured for each of the four cases. The financial information available consisted of 33 pieces in six categories. Each financial measure also included industry ratios for comparison purposes.

Total number of pieces of strategic (episodic) information the participant selected through Search Monitor, regardless of the category the information originated in, measured for each of the four cases. The strategic information available consisted of 10 pieces in four categories.

Total amount of financial (semantic) information acquired by each auditor, traced with the same Search Monitor procedure used in study 1, now over six cases. Responses on the like cases within each problem setting were averaged before across-problem-setting comparisons were made.

Total amount of strategic (episodic) information acquired by each auditor over the six cases, traced with the same Search Monitor procedure used in study 1. Responses on the like cases within each problem setting were averaged before across-problem-setting comparisons were made.

Two rigidity measures were computed for each lender, one for financial information and one for strategic information, by subtracting the amount acquired in structured problem settings from the amount acquired in ill-structured settings. The rigidity construct itself was tested by contrasting the information acquired in the structured and ill-structured settings.
Rigidity measures for the auditors were computed in the same way as in study 1, contrasting the information acquired in structured and ill-structured problem settings.

Two-level within-subject factor defined by the match between the case and the analyst's experience base: given the venture capital lenders' work experience, the loan decisions concerning the start-up companies represented structured problem settings and those concerning the mature companies represented ill-structured settings, and for the commercial lenders the reverse pattern held. Each subject was presented with four hypothetical loan cases, two concerning mature companies and two concerning recent start-up companies.

variable_name: problem setting (relatively structured vs. relatively ill-structured)
description: For the auditors a hierarchy of problem-setting familiarity was inferred, in which mature, prosperous firms represent the most familiar, or structured, problem setting and start-up, prosperous firms represent the least familiar, or ill-structured, problem setting; mature near-bankrupt and start-up near-bankrupt firms represent midrange levels of familiarity. The contrast between a structured and an ill-structured problem setting in study 2 was therefore one of degree.
scale: relative degrees of structure (most to least familiar)

description: Six cases were used, three mature and three start-up. The cases were not hypothetical but were based on data from public documents produced by actual companies, with fictitious names used for each company and its managers. One of the start-up cases was near bankrupt, as were two of the mature companies.

Participants were classified by their professional setting into 23 commercial lenders and 19 venture capital lenders. The two groups perform the same general lending task but in different problem settings: venture capitalists typically encounter recently founded companies that lack meaningful financial information, whereas commercial lenders deal with mature companies that have long track records of financial performance.
scale: two groups: commercial lender, venture capital lender

description: Survey measure of the extent to which product knowledge is common and applicable across business units rather than unique and specific to each business unit, covering both internal product knowledge and external product knowledge acquired from the R&D and manufacturing alliances of individual businesses. Respondents rated each item on a five-point scale (1 = unique in all or almost all of the business units, 2 = unique in a majority of the business units, 3 = unique in about half of the business units, common across the other half, 4 = common across a majority of the business units, 5 = common across all or almost all of the business units). The scale was designed to capture the actual, realized knowledge relatedness of a business portfolio rather than potential relatedness. The items formed first-order factors in the confirmatory factor model.

Survey measure of the extent to which customer knowledge is common and applicable across business units rather than unique and specific to each business unit, including customer knowledge acquired through the marketing and distribution alliances of the business units. Respondents rated each item on the same five-point scale running from knowledge that is unique in all or almost all business units to knowledge that is common across all or almost all business units. The items formed a first-order factor in the confirmatory factor model.

Survey measure of the extent to which the managerial knowledge embedded in the firm's corporate-level processes is common and applicable across business units rather than unique and specific to each business unit. Respondents rated each item on the same five-point scale running from knowledge that is unique in all or almost all business units to knowledge that is common across all or almost all business units. The items formed two first-order factors in the confirmatory factor model.

Second-order factor in the LISREL measurement model that captures patterns of interactions and covariance among the first-order knowledge relatedness factors, representing the super-additive value synergies arising from the complementarity of the three types of knowledge relatedness. The five first-order knowledge relatedness factors serve as its indicators. The target coefficient for the second-order knowledge synergy construct is 0.83, and all second-order factor loadings are highly significant.

Computed as the ratio of the market value of a firm to the replacement cost of its assets, using basic financial and accounting data from COMPUSTAT (Chung and Pruitt, 1994). It is a market-based, forward-looking measure of firm performance and was measured with year 2001 financial data, one year after the knowledge synergy measures.

Return on assets, adopted as one of three widely used objective measures of firm performance in the diversification literature and used as a dependent variable. It was measured with year 2001 financial data, one year after the knowledge synergy measures. The text reports no further computational detail for this variable.

Return on equity, adopted as one of three widely used objective measures of firm performance in the diversification literature and used as a dependent variable. It was measured with year 2001 financial data, one year after the knowledge synergy measures. The text reports no further computational detail for this variable.

variable_name: top management team heterogeneity (composite heterogeneity index)
description: The top management team is defined as the chairman, vice chairmen, CEO, president, and chief financial and operating officers, plus the next highest level identified in the Dun & Bradstreet Reference Book of Corporate Managements. Three measures of team heterogeneity were calculated: educational background heterogeneity and functional background heterogeneity using Blau's index, and industry tenure heterogeneity using a coefficient of variation (the standard deviation divided by the mean for the team's years of experience in the focal industry). The composite heterogeneity index is the sum of the three standardized individual heterogeneity measures; high scores indicate that a top management team possesses, overall, a diverse set of experiences, cognitive perspectives, and backgrounds.
Each company's annual return on assets (ROA), lagged one year, was used as the measure of past performance for each year of the time panel.
Organizational slack was measured as unabsorbed slack using the quick ratio, the ratio of current assets less inventory to current liabilities.
A composite measure of each industry's barriers to entry, calculated as the sum of the year-by-year pooled industry means for investments in R&D, selling activities, and total assets.
time_window: year by year over the seven-year panel

description: A simple growth rate calculated for each industry-year (year t) as the percentage change in industry gross sales between the study year and the previous year (year t-1) for each four-digit SIC industry.
A Herfindahl index of industry concentration for each four-digit SIC industry for each year over the seven-year time panel.
time_window: each year over the seven-year panel

description: Measured as the average number of competitive action events composing each of a focal firm's competitive attacks in a given year (for example, the annual average of a first attack of six action events and a second attack of four action events). Higher attack volume scores indicate that a firm typically carries out attacks comprised of many actions; the measure accounts for periods of relative competitive activity and inactivity within the year.
time_window: within each year of the seven-year panel

description: The duration of a particular competitive attack is measured as the number of days elapsed from the first action in a given attack to the last action of the attack. For the analyses, attack duration was calculated as the average duration of all a firm's competitive attacks carried out in a given year. High scores indicate that firms typically sustain competitive attacks against rivals, and low scores that firms typically carry out only short bursts of competitive activity.
time_window: within each year of the seven-year panel

description: Attack complexity uses Ferrier et al.'s Herfindahl-type index of competitive simplicity, which accounts for the weighted diversity among all six action types: the ratio of actions in each of the six action categories to total actions was calculated, each proportion was squared, and the squared proportions were summed. For the analyses the annual average of attack complexity was calculated. The authors state that firms with low scores carry out competitive attacks that typically consist of a broad range of action types, while high scores indicate that a firm typically carries out attacks with just a few action types.
time_window: within each year of the seven-year panel

description: Optimal matching analysis was used to measure the extent to which a firm's sequence of actions carried out in a given time period was or was not similar to that carried out in the preceding time period, accounting for the costs of insertions, deletions, and substitutions (INDEL costs) among all action types needed to transform one action sequence to match another, based on a matrix of INDEL costs across all action types. The procedure calculated the (dis)similarity between the focal firm's entire sequence of competitive actions carried out in year t and that carried out in year t-1. A high optimal matching score indicates that the firm is strategically unpredictable; a low score indicates that the firm's sequence changes little from year to year.

Market share gain was calculated as the positive year-to-year change in the percentage of total sales in the focal firm's primary industry that its own sales represent. The measure also accounts for market share erosion, measured as the negative annual change in market share.

variable_name: Individual constraint (staffings in last six months)
description: The number of mandates a particular partner has been staffed on in the past 180 days, used as the partner's current utilization of the capacity constraint. The authors note that they do not observe when a mandate begins but only when it ends, that is, when the acquisition is announced, which introduces measurement error.

variable_name: Staffing (partner being staffed on a new deal)
description: Indicator variable that takes a value of 1 if the partner has been staffed on the project and 0 otherwise, with the unit of analysis being the partner-project pair. The risk set includes all staffed partners and nonstaffed partners working for the mandated law firm who had been staffed at least once on a corporate acquisition mandate during 1997-2005, from the moment they were listed as partner.

Firm-specific capital is defined as how long a partner has been partner at the respective law firm minus the average time the partners of the firm have been partner at the respective law firm in the sample. The adjustment for the firm average captures the relative difference in firm-specific human capital among the partners who are at risk of being staffed. The uninteracted partner firm-specific human capital variable is also included as a control.

Dummy variable that takes a value of 1 when a firm uses a firm-performance-based compensation system which shares law firm's profits based on the seniority of the partner (Lockstep) and 0 if it is using a merit-based compensation system. Firms do not change compensation systems during the period of the study; the 2004 edition of the Lawyer 100 is the only year in which such information was provided.

Average Euclidean squared distance among members of the top management team. Distance begins with the calculation of distances between each pair of individuals within a designated group; for a dyad, distance is measured by summing the squared differences between individual responses to an identified set of questions, and a team score is derived by summing the distances between each unique dyad within a team and dividing by the number of unique dyads. A high distance score regarding competencies implies high linkage ambiguity among members of that organization. Distances were derived from all competency factor scores for that industry (seven in the hospital industry and eight in the textile industry), and ambiguity was assessed relative to other organizations in the industry at two levels: among top managers and among middle managers.

Average Euclidean squared distance among middle managers of a firm. Distance begins with the calculation of distances between each pair of individuals within a designated group; for a dyad, distance is measured by summing the squared differences between individual responses to an identified set of questions, and a team score is derived by summing the distances between each unique dyad within a team and dividing by the number of unique dyads. A high distance score regarding competencies implies high linkage ambiguity among members of that organization. Distances were derived from all competency factor scores for that industry (seven in the hospital industry and eight in the textile industry), and ambiguity was assessed relative to other organizations in the industry.

Managers assessed four statements about the competency in question, modified from Zander and Kogut (1995), on a 7-point scale. Principal component analysis of the four items revealed two stable two-item factors consistent with Winter's (1987) dimensions of tacitness: the first factor represents managers' perceptions that the competency has been articulated and the second factor represents perceptions that the competency is articulable. Each manager answered the questions regarding the competency that he or she considered most important to the firm's current success and regarding the competency of 'cost containment' (hospital industry) or 'managing costs' (textile industry). Assessments were analysed separately for top managers and for middle managers.
level: manager; analysed separately for the TMT and middle managers

description: Managers answered a forced-choice question based on Leonard-Barton's (1995) framework, allocating 100 points among four locations where the competitive advantage might reside. All responses were divided by 25 so that each respondent's mean score was one. Assessments were analysed separately for top managers and for middle managers.
level: manager; analysed separately for the TMT and middle managers

description: Each executive indicated, on a scale from -3 to +3, whether his or her organization was at an advantage or disadvantage with respect to its competition for each competency. Average responses for each individual competency (36 in the textile industry, 30 in the hospital industry) were calculated by managerial level in each organization. High scores indicate that managers believe this competency provides their firm superior competitive advantage; low scores indicate that managers believe that the firm's competency is competitively inferior.
level: individual competency within firm, by managerial level

description: The dependent variable in the model is firm performance, measured as return on assets based on financial data from secondary sources. The authors argue that ROA provides superior relative year-to-year stability relative to other measures and that it continues to be accepted in multiple industry studies involving the hospital and textile industries.

Characteristic ambiguity is measured from manager responses on two features of the most important competency: tacitness (four statements modified from Zander and Kogut 1995, seven-point agreement scale) and culture location (a forced allocation of 100 points across four options, based on Leonard-Barton 1995).

variable_name: Average proportion of TMT incentive pay
description: The sum of TMT members' granted and held incentive-based compensation forms divided by their total compensation. Three forms of incentive pay are included: stock options (new and previously awarded), restricted stock, and long-term performance plans. New option grants are valued with the Black-Scholes formula; previously awarded exercisable and unexercisable options by the number of held options times the difference between exercise price and fiscal year-end stock price; restricted stock by the number of shares held times the year-end stock price; and long-term performance plans as the expected future target payout reported in the proxy statement. For each firm-year, the value of stock options, restricted stock, and long-term performance plans is summed for the top five managers, a total pay variable sums each manager's salary, bonus, and incentive-based pay, and aggregate TMT incentive pay is divided by aggregate TMT total pay.

The gini coefficient of the proportion of TMT incentive-based pay in the portfolios of each TMT member (the top five managers). The gini coefficient ranges from zero, indicating 'complete agreement,' to one, indicating 'complete disparity.' The reported equation is unreadable in the payload; per the prose, it uses the incentive structure of each individual TMT member of firm j arranged in decreasing order of size, the mean incentive structure for the TMT, and the number of TMT members.
scale: gini coefficient ranging from zero to one

description: The annual investment in majority public and private (51% or greater) acquisition transactions each firm announced and subsequently completed, in which the individual acquisition value was greater than $10 million as reported in the SDC database. Firms in the sample announced and subsequently closed 16,543 acquisitions that met these restrictions.

Short-term cumulative abnormal returns as reported in the Eventus database, computed as the unanticipated returns on a security over the given period, i.e., the difference between the observed return and the expected return. The measure sums the daily unanticipated returns over the event window and averages all individual CARs around the focal firm's acquisitions in the focal year; for firms announcing multiple acquisitions in the focal year the surrounding CARs are averaged to obtain an annualized measure. The reported equation is unreadable in the payload, but the prose states that it uses the stock return for day t, the market portfolio return for day t, a constant, the stock's beta, and the first and final day of the event window. Results use a window of three days before to three days after acquisition announcements [-3,3].
time_window: event window [-3,3] around acquisition announcements, averaged within the focal year; lagged one year in the models

variable_name: themes discovered by common factor analysis
description: Common factor analysis was iterated on progressively smaller sets of the most frequent nonstructural words, culling words that failed the Kaiser-Meyer-Olkin measure of sampling adequacy, with scree plots used to decide the number of themes present. After a VARIMAX rotation the outcome was a set of five themes, each composed of four to six words with high factor loadings, which the authors labeled R&D, Marketing, Governance, Finance and Management. MANOVA showed that governance, financial and management themes were statistically identical across the whole data base and discriminated neither companies nor years, so only the R&D and marketing themes were used. Their loadings are listed in Table 5.

Frequency values for the future tense sentences from the 'R&D' and 'marketing' sentence lists were entered into separate cluster analyses, and cluster analysis placed each of the 426 annual reports into a cognitive strategic group. K-means cluster analysis was used, with six clusters for the cross-sectional portion of the study and three for the longitudinal portion. Initial cluster centers were selected by SPSS and iterated until the Euclidean distance between centroids changed less than 2 percent; ANOVA tables confirmed there was no significant probability (p = 0.000, alpha = 0.05) that the observed clusters occurred by chance.

For the cross-sectional test, performance strategic group membership was taken from Cool and Schendel's (1987) six strategic groups, which were operationalized by 15 measures of strategic scope and strategic resources. For the longitudinal test, present and past tense sentence counts from the R&D and marketing themes were clustered by K-means cluster analysis into three performance strategic groups in each year of the study, based on reports of achievement in the present and near past.
time_window: 1963-1982; two- to five-year lags in the longitudinal analysis

description: Every sentence that contained a word from a theme was catalogued based on its tense, with future tense representing strategic intent and present/past tense representing current or past performance. Sentences from the two factors showing the most discriminatory power (R&D and marketing) were separated by tense and entered into separate data bases. Frequency counts of future tense statements formed the cognitive group data base used to identify cognitive strategic groups.

Sentences containing words from the R&D and marketing themes written in the present or past tense report current and past achievements, such as sales already made. Frequency counts of these present and past tense statements formed the strategic group data base used for the longitudinal analysis of performance-based strategic groups.
time_window: two to five years after the intent statements in each year of the study

description: Indicator of foreign ownership of a defense contractor, built by identifying the global ultimate owner of each contractor and matching company identifiers across databases. The variable takes a value of 1 if the firm is included in the set of foreign firms and 0 otherwise. Because the binary variable does not vary within firms, it is dropped in the firm fixed-effects equations and included in the random-effects models.

Annual outside-lobbying spending on defense-related issues by each defense contractor, constructed from lobbying transaction reports. Because only the aggregate activities of each lobbying subject are known, expenditure is allocated evenly across the congressional issues addressed on a report, and the defense-related portion is kept; of the 79 distinct congressional issues listed in a standardized lobbying report, Appropriations (BUD), Defense (DEF), and Homeland Security (HOM) are classified as defense-related.

The average number of years that an outside lobbyist is employed by a lobbying firm-lobbying client. It is used as the moderator in the three-way interaction among foreignness, outside lobbying expense, and the duration of the lobbying contract.

The logged dollar amount of U.S. defense weapons-system contracts awarded to a given firm in a given year, aggregated by defense contractor annually. Weapons procurement covers all contracts coded A1 through A6 (except A4B, Noncombat Vehicles) in section B12B (DoD Claimant Program code) of the Individual Contracting Action Report (DD Form 350), including airframes and spares, aircraft engines and spares, other aircraft equipment, missiles and space systems, ships, combat vehicles, weapons, and ammunition.

Dummy variable for Gujarati hotel ownership used to test whether owners of low-resource establishments belong to the immigrant entrepreneur group. Membership is determined from the owner surname: two Gujaratis designated the surnames Patel, Bhakta, Desai, Amin, Gandhi, Mistry, Thakor, Jallab, Shah, Govind, Zaveri, Rama, Rana, Mehta, Nathu, and Dalwad as Gujarati. Because owners are often listed as corporations, the Texas incorporation file was used and any hotel that is incorporated and has a partner with a Gujarati surname is considered Gujarati-owned. Due to ownership changes, the same hotel may be Gujarati-owned in some periods but not in others.

variable_name: Proximate branded hotels owned by Gujaratis
description: Count of branded-chain hotels among the 10 closest hotels to the establishment under observation, measured from the hotel's latitude and longitude coordinates. The counts are separated into hotels owned by Gujaratis and hotels owned by others, and they do not include other hotels belonging to the same owner as the hotel under observation. The count enters the models as a main effect and is interacted with the Gujarati owner dummy.

variable_name: Proximate branded hotels owned by non-Gujaratis
description: Count of branded-chain hotels among the 10 closest hotels to the establishment under observation that are owned by non-Gujaratis. The count is computed from latitude and longitude coordinates, excludes other hotels belonging to the same owner as the hotel under observation, and is interacted with the Gujarati owner dummy.

variable_name: Proximate unbranded motels owned by Gujaratis
description: Count of unbranded motels among the 10 closest hotels to the establishment under observation that are owned by Gujaratis. Unbranded motels are hotels with the words 'motel' or 'motor hotel' or 'motor inn' or 'motor lodge' in the business name that are not affiliated with any franchised chain. The count excludes other hotels belonging to the same owner and is interacted with the Gujarati owner dummy.

variable_name: Proximate unbranded motels owned by non-Gujaratis
description: Count of unbranded motels among the 10 closest hotels to the establishment under observation that are owned by non-Gujaratis. The count excludes other hotels of the same owner and is interacted with the Gujarati owner dummy.

Dependent variable of the event history analysis: motels are considered survivors as long as they remain open for business and are at risk of failure until they have permanently closed down. Changes of ownership or of 'doing business as' name are not treated as failure. Because all covariates of theoretical interest change over time, life histories are split into yearly spells and covariates are set at their values at the beginning of each year; the models estimate the hazard of failure, so positive coefficients indicate greater likelihood of failure.

Dummy variable identifying Gujarati ownership, used in the conditional logit as a main effect and interacted with the proximate-hotel counts to test whether Gujaratis are attracted to particular locations. Membership is determined from a list of Gujarati surnames and from Texas incorporation records for hotels owned by corporations with a Gujarati partner.

variable_name: Proximate branded hotels owned by Gujaratis
description: Count of branded-chain hotels among the 10 closest hotels to each zip code's centroid, because the actual hotel had not yet been built. The count is separated by Gujarati and non-Gujarati ownership and is interacted with the Gujarati owner dummy in the location choice model.

variable_name: Proximate branded hotels owned by non-Gujaratis
description: Count of branded-chain hotels among the 10 closest hotels to each zip code's centroid that are owned by non-Gujaratis. The count is interacted with the Gujarati owner dummy in the location choice model.

variable_name: Proximate unbranded motels owned by Gujaratis
description: Count of unbranded motels among the 10 closest hotels to each zip code's centroid that are owned by Gujaratis. Unbranded motels are those with 'motel', 'motor hotel', or 'motor inn' in the name and no franchised chain affiliation. The count is interacted with the Gujarati owner dummy.

variable_name: Proximate unbranded motels owned by non-Gujaratis
description: Count of unbranded motels among the 10 closest hotels to each zip code's centroid that are owned by non-Gujaratis. The count is interacted with the Gujarati owner dummy.

Observed dependent variable of the conditional logit: Yij equals 1 if zip code j is chosen and 0 for the 577 zip codes not chosen. The alternatives are the 578 zip codes in Texas with at least one hotel present, so each observation has 578 rows of data. Positive coefficients imply that zip codes with high values of the associated variable have a higher probability of being chosen, and negative coefficients imply lower probabilities.

Cumulative production refers to cumulative workstation sales in 1996 U.S. dollars gleaned from the IDC Processor Survey. In the estimated models the term labeled experience captures the baseline learning rate, and time-varying integration is accommodated by multiplying the degree of integration for a period by the logged ratio of cumulative production at the end of the period to the beginning of the period. The analysis excluded cases that lacked sales information.

Counts the number of components the company produces internally, coding information on eight components: CPU, logic board, memory, storage media, networking components, monitor, operating system, and applications software. An organization that produces all of these components internally receives a score of eight, the maximum degree of vertical integration, and one that does nothing beyond assembling and selling systems receives a score of zero. Organizations employing tapered integration are considered integrated into that component, and quasi integration is not captured.

Based on the input side of environmental volatility, it is the combined Herfindahl indexes of processors and operating systems, inverted so that higher values indicate more uncertainty, where pr and os represent the proportion of all products on the market that use a particular processor or operating system. It is computed using information on all 1,276 individual workstations (product-level data); the lack of convergence on a set of technological standards provides this measure.

Measured as the correlation in same-product sales from period t-1 to period t, using vectors of workstation model sales for a given year; the resulting correlation is inverted so that increasing values indicate greater volatility rather than greater stability. Using the correlation in sales eliminates the influence of industrywide growth and decline.

Pooled logistic regression estimates the likelihood of firm exit, where market exit occurs when a company no longer markets a workstation product, or is acquired; the probability of exit over the interval is written as a function of covariates and estimated by maximum likelihood. In models of firm exit, negative coefficient estimates indicate those factors that promote learning-by-doing, while positive coefficient estimates correspond to slower learning.

Estimated with the proportionate growth model, which assumes organizations expand and contract at a random rate drawn independent of organizational size; the coefficient on lagged size equals one when growth occurs independent of size, and logging provides a function suitable for OLS estimation. The growth models are estimated with firm fixed effects and include the inverse Mills ratio as a control for selection effects due to firm exit. Positive coefficients point to factors that accelerate learning and negative coefficients to factors that retard learning.

variable_name: Ruling Party Has a Parliamentary Majority
description: Indicator of whether the ruling party possessed a parliamentary majority in a given year, used as the primary predictor in the bribery analyses. The authors argue that a parliamentary majority secures dominance because it gives agenda-setting and law-passing power, so a value of one indicates less political competition.

variable_name: Opposition Distance to Taking Majority Power in Parliament
description: Constructed by subtracting 50 from the percentage of parliamentary seats held by the ruling party in each year (Definition 1). Lower values indicate more political competition, as the opposition moves toward the threshold of 50% plus one seat that carries agenda-setting and law-passing power. This is the measure used in the charity analyses because ruling-party majority status was time-invariant during 1981-1987.

Yearly bribery amounts paid by each of 45 business groups during 1980-1992, in KRW billion. The amounts are hand-collected from the Seoul District Court verdict (1996), which disclosed how much each business paid to whom, how often, and when.

variable_name: Business Group Gave a Bribe in This Year
description: Indicator of whether each business group made a positive nonzero bribery payment during 1980-1992, coded one when the business group gave a bribe in that year and zero otherwise. It is the dependent variable of the probit analyses of bribery incidence.

One-year lagged amount of bribery paid by the business group, used as the predictor of current-year contributions to politically connected charities in the rechanneling analysis. The models also interact this lagged bribery amount with business group financial characteristics.

variable_name: Sum of Contributions Given to Any of the Three Charities
description: Yearly total amounts contributed by each business group to any of the three quasi-foundations established by Chun and his spouse (Il-hae Foundation, New Generation Education Foundation and New Generation Heart Foundation) during 1981-1987, in KRW billion. The amounts are taken from the National Assembly's special investigative report (1990).

variable_name: Business Group Gave Positive Nonzero Amount to Any of the Three Charities in This Year
description: Indicator of whether the business group made a nonzero contribution to any of the three quasi-foundations during 1981-1987, coded one for years with a positive contribution. It is the dependent variable of the probit analyses of charity contribution incidence.

CAR is defined as the sum of daily abnormal returns within an event window; abnormal returns are a firm's actual returns minus its expected returns. Expected returns are estimated with a market model using the CRSP value-weighted index as the market return over a 180-trading-day estimation window ending 14 days before the event date. The event dates are the publication dates of the Fortune issues announcing the rankings, and the window is the event date and the day before (t-1, t0). CAR values are expressed as percentages.
time_window: two-day event window (t-1, t0) around the ranking publication date

description: A Fall took a positive value equal to the absolute difference in a firm's rank between two consecutive years if the firm's rank dropped, and a value of 0 if the firm's rank rose or remained unchanged; the variable was log-transformed. As an alternative categorical measure, falls were classified as none (baseline), small (a fall of 15 or fewer positions) and large (a fall of 16 or more positions).

A Rise took a positive value equal to the absolute difference in a firm's rank between two consecutive years if the firm's rank rose, and a value of 0 if it fell or remained unchanged; the variable was log-transformed. As an alternative categorical measure, rises were coded as small (a rise of 19 or fewer positions) or large (a rise of 20 or more positions).

The total number of media articles mentioning a firm during the full calendar year prior to the announcement of the rankings, searched in Factiva on the basis of firm names, with company filters used when available to exclude articles unrelated to the firm. A value of 0 was assigned if the firm received no media coverage during a particular year, and a natural logarithm was applied to account for skewness.
time_window: full calendar year prior to the ranking announcement

description: The sum of unique earnings estimates by financial analysts during the calendar year prior to the publication of the rankings, measured for each firm annually using the IBES database. A value of 0 was assigned if the firm received no analyst coverage during a particular year, and a natural logarithm was applied to account for skewness.
time_window: calendar year prior to the ranking publication

description: The total ratio of the number of a firm's stock shares owned by institutional investors to the total number of shares outstanding in each year the ranking was announced, taken from the Thomson Reuters database; for example, 100 of 1,000 outstanding shares gives a value of 0.10. Where data for a firm were not available for a year, the firm's most recent available value was used, values reported above 100 percent were capped at 100 percent, and a natural logarithm was applied.
time_window: each year the ranking was announced

description: Two distinct metrics assess a firm's Previous rank. The first grouped firms into three tiers based on their previous ranking, high (1-166), medium (167-333), and low (334-500), assigned values of 2, 1, and 0, with larger numbers corresponding to higher-ranking groups. The second, more fine-grained measure was defined as 500 minus the previous year's rank, so that a firm ranked fifth in the prior year takes a value of 495.

The main independent variable in the natural experiment. The author projected the hypothetical rank of Fortune 500 firms assuming Fortune had not changed its ranking methodology in 1994, creating a hypothetical list of the 500 largest manufacturing firms based on 1994 revenue from the 1994 Fortune 1000 and Compustat databases, and then calculated the difference between this hypothetical rank and the actual rank in the 1994 Fortune 1000. The variable took either a positive value or 0; firms that failed to appear even on the Fortune 1000 list were assigned an actual rank of 1,001 so that their fall could be calculated.

Cumulative abnormal returns computed as in the main analysis: the sum of daily abnormal returns over the two-day window ending on the publication date of the Fortune ranking, where abnormal returns subtract expected returns estimated with a market model over a 180-trading-day window ending 14 days before the event date.
time_window: two-day event window (t-1, t0) around the ranking publication date

description: Media coverage as used in the main analysis: the total number of media articles mentioning a firm during the full calendar year prior to the announcement of the rankings, log-transformed. The authors state that the regression specification of the natural experiment largely follows the main analyses.
time_window: full calendar year prior to the ranking announcement

description: Analyst coverage as used in the main analysis: the sum of unique earnings estimates by financial analysts during the calendar year prior to the publication of the rankings, log-transformed. The authors state that the regression specification of the natural experiment largely follows the main analyses.
time_window: calendar year prior to the ranking publication

description: Institutional ownership as used in the main analysis: the ratio of shares owned by institutional investors to total shares outstanding in the year the ranking was announced, log-transformed. The authors state that the regression specification of the natural experiment largely follows the main analyses.
time_window: the year the ranking was announced

description: A firm's previous ranking position as used in the main analysis, entered both as the categorical tier measure and as the continuous measure (500 minus the previous year's rank). The authors state that the regression specification of the natural experiment largely follows the main analyses.

Binary variable equal to 1 if a firm had at least one independent director who issued a dissenting opinion in a given year. It is hand-coded from independent directors' joint opinion reports, which state which director(s) agreed and which director(s) dissented or abstained. The authors report that results are robust to defining dissent as a combination of dissent and abstention.

Binary variable equal to 1 if a specific independent director dissented in an opinion report. It is coded from the multiple director-opinion pairs contained in each joint opinion report, which state which director(s) agreed and which dissented or abstained.

Binary variable equal to 1 if all independent directors sitting on the board in a particular year are appointed by the board chair. Independent directors are defined as appointed by a board chair if they joined the board after the chair assumed office.
Continuous variable defined as the percentage of independent directors appointed by the board chair. Appointment is defined by joining the board after the chair assumed office.

Dummy variable equal to 1 if the appointing chair left the board during an independent director's tenure. In the estimation it captures the pre-treatment (unobserved) systematic difference between independent directors who experienced departure of the board chair and those who did not.

Binary variable equal to 1 if an opinion was issued after the appointing chair left the board. Together with chairperson departure it forms a difference-in-differences specification that takes care of the difference in voting behavior before and after departure of the appointing chair.
time_window: votes occurring after the appointing chair's departure

description: Binary variable equal to 1 if the opinion is issued in less than 60 days before one of three events: the director left the board before reaching the six-year term limit (director midterm departure); the current board chair left the board, irrespective of whether the chair appointed the director (chairperson departure); or the director left the board upon reaching the six-year term limit (director term limit).

The total number of patents law firm i filed on behalf of company j in year t. Patent filings are used as a proxy for the amount of new business obtained by patent law firms and for the revenue generated, accounted for at the time the business is generated. Data on each company's patents came from the USPTO PATSIC database, and the corporate family of each Fortune 500 company was compiled from the Directory of Corporate Affiliates so as to include patents filed by all subsidiaries, divisions, and affiliates; the law firm on each patent was handcoded from the 'Attorney, Agent or Firm' field. All outsourced patents going to the focal law firms were used to compute the variable.

A dummy variable coded 1 if an attorney joined law firm i from (potential) client company j in the previous year, and 0 otherwise. Attorney employment in a given year and attorney movements over time were tracked from the USPTO OED patent attorney roster using each attorney's unique registration number. Independent and control variables were lagged by one year to guard against reverse causation.

Using the unique registration number of each patent attorney, a dummy variable coded 1 if an attorney joined (potential) client company j from law firm i in the previous year, and 0 otherwise. The variable was lagged one year relative to the dependent variable.

A dummy variable coded 1 if an attorney joined law firm i from any competitor law firm that had prior business ties to (potential) client company j, and 0 otherwise. Prior client ties were defined as the outsourcing of at least one patent from a Fortune 500 company to a competitor law firm in the previous two years. The variable was lagged one year relative to the dependent variable.

The logarithm of the total number of attorneys lost from law firm i to any competitor law firm in the previous year. Because the number of such moves varied between 0 and 18, this variable was not dummied. For all variables that could take the value 0, 1 was added before taking the log; logs were required because of the exponentiation of independent variables in count-data models.

The company's status with regard to product development was captured via a dichotomous indicator of whether the initial product had begun shipping and a time clock that tracked the amount of time since product shipment had begun. The time clock is logarithmically transformed because the time distribution since initial product shipping was lognormal; both variables are time-varying across company-months. Survey responses for product shipping dates were checked against company websites, press releases, and press articles.

Financing rounds are well-defined events that are accurate down to the month in which they occurred, and every round date was checked against the Venture One database and against company press releases. A time clock was calculated for the time since the last round of financing, for company-months after the first financing round, and is logarithmically transformed because the distribution was lognormal. The models also include a time clock for the time until the next round of financing.

The amount of money raised by the company in its latest round of financing, measured in millions of dollars and logarithmically transformed. It is a time-varying variable that changes with each financing round.

The number of new venture capitalists participating in the latest round of financing. To test the hypotheses about the effect of having new investors, data from Venture One were used on the rounds in which each venture capitalist began investing in each company. It is a time-varying variable that changes each financing round.

A variable indicating whether insiders own more than half of the equity of the company, in which case outside investors do not have equity control. It is a time-varying variable, since each round more equity is sold to outsiders, diluting insiders' equity holdings.

The dependent variable records whether a Founder-CEO succession event occurred at time point t; it was coded 1 at the time point when the Founder-CEO was replaced, and 0 otherwise. Firms where the Founder-CEO was still the company's CEO as of the end of the data collection period were treated as censored observations, as were cases where the company was acquired or went out of business before there was a Founder-CEO succession event.

The CEO's personal contributions to the Republican Party minus contributions to the Democratic Party divided by the total contribution to both parties, consistent with prior studies. This resulted in a continuous measure where +1 indicated that all contributions were made to the Republican Party and -1 indicated that all contributions were made to the Democratic Party. The measure was calculated for each CEO in each two-year election cycle, and the average of these values across all election cycles in which the CEO made contributions was used as the final measure. CEOs who did not make personal political contributions were not included in the analyses.
time_window: each two-year election cycle; averaged across all cycles with contributions

description: The ratio of performance pay to initial total pay in the year of the succession, consistent with Chen (2015). Performance pay is the sum of options (options_awards), stock and restricted stock (rstkgrnt), and bonuses (bonus). Initial total pay is the sum of options, stock and restricted stock, bonuses, and salary (salary). Options are the value of option-related awards including stock appreciation rights; stock is the value of stocks and restricted stocks granted during the year; bonuses are the value of earned bonuses during the fiscal year; and salary is the value of the base salary during the fiscal year.

variable_name: VC prominence in syndicate networks (VC prominence)
description: The centrality of each VC firm is first calculated as of year t using the Bonacich (1987) measure over all direct and indirect syndicate ties formed with other VC firms during the most recently past five years. Because typically more than one VC invests in a new venture, the authors take the maximum of the centralities of those VCs that had invested in the new venture by time t to represent the signaling benefits the new venture receives. The specification of the centrality formula is not readable in the text; only its components are described in prose.
level: venture capital firm-year, aggregated to new venture-year
time_window: five years prior to t (t - 5 to t)

variable_name: New venture's prominence in alliance networks (alliance prominence)
description: A new venture's alliance network centrality was calculated as its Bonacich (1987) centrality in networks of prior alliances using the new venture's alliance formation activity within the last five years. The relationship matrix shows the number of alliances formed between the new venture and each partner during the last five years, up to year t. The centrality measure was normalized so that the maximum centrality in a particular year is equal to 1. The specification of the centrality formula is not readable in the text; only its components are described in prose.
scale: normalized so that the maximum centrality in a particular year equals 1

description: The dependent variable is whether or not a particular new venture (i) and established company (j) form an R&D alliance in a given year (t), coded 1 = 'yes,' 0 = 'no.' The data set includes not only the realized alliances between the companies in these two sets, but also the nonrealized alliances. All independent and control variables enter the regressions with values lagged one year with respect to this dependent variable.
time_window: year t; independent variables lagged one year

description: The complexity of the inventor's prior patenting activities is used as a proxy for the complexity of the recipes the inventor acquired. The measure relies on classification of patents into subclasses and on the interaction matrix from Kauffman's NK model: the interdependence K of a focal component (subclass) is computed from co-occurrence frequencies of subclass combinations relative to the occurrence frequency of the focal subclass, and the total number of components N is operationalized by the number of patent subclasses. The complexity measure is obtained by dividing the number of interdependencies K by the number of components N, and the final measure for a given inventor in a given year is the average of K/N for all patents awarded to the inventor in that year. The formula blocks for the computation of Ki and of K are not readable in the provided text.
scale: K in the interval [0, N-1]; complexity measured as K/N
time_window: focal year (patents awarded in that year)

description: A binary indicator set to 1 if an employment spell in a source firm in a focal year was followed by a move to a different firm in the recipient sample, and 0 if the spell was followed by a further employment at the source firm. Mobility was observable only when an inventor patented at both a source and a recipient firm; the patenting and employment histories were reconstructed from patent data with a matching algorithm.

Coded as 1 if the inventor patented together with the same co-inventor within the parent firm and the recipient firm and 0 otherwise. This variable is estimated on the subsample with employee mobility = 1.

A binary variable set to 1 if founding a start-up followed an employment spell in a focal year and 0 if joining a rival firm or further employment with the same firm followed, depending on the comparison group. Founder status was defined stringently, requiring the word 'founder' or 'cofounder' to appear with the person's name on the archived corporate website or in early press releases or industry materials, and founder names were then matched with the source-firm pool of inventors.

Coded as 1 if the inventor patented together with another inventor within the parent firm and both were listed as start-up cofounders and 0 otherwise. This variable is estimated on the subsample with employee entrepreneurship = 1.

Measured from the SSA national data on given names between 1880 and 2016. Following prior research on uncommon names, the commonness of a CEO's given name was calculated as the frequency of its appearance (by gender) in the SSA data set, and the measure of name uncommonness is simply the negative value of the measure of name commonness. In the primary analysis, a CEO's name uncommonness was measured since the birth year of the oldest CEO in the sample.
time_window: since the birth year of the oldest CEO in the sample

description: Strategic distinctiveness was analyzed along six dimensions: advertising intensity (advertising expense/sales), inventory level (inventories/sales), plant and equipment newness (net plant and equipment/gross plant and equipment), R&D intensity (R&D expense/sales), nonproduction overhead (selling, general, and administrative expense/sales), and financial leverage (total debt/equity). Along each dimension the authors calculated the absolute difference between a firm and the average of all other firms in the same industry in each year. Each indicator of strategic distinctiveness was then standardized by industry and year, and the sum of these standardized scores is the composite measure.

Measured based on how a CEO exercises stock options, following prior research suggesting that a CEO who retains more unexercised exercisable options is more confident about the future of the firm. The authors measured CEO confidence by the annual value of the CEO's holdings of vested, in-the-money options divided by the CEO's total salary and bonus. Data were collected from the Execucomp database.
time_window: 1 year prior to the dependent variable
