Two coders with substantially different backgrounds independently assessed the articles; the intra-class correlation coefficient was 91 percent. The primary analysis included articles from the year preceding the measure of the dependent variable.
time_window: the year preceding the measure of the dependent variable

description: Factor score of three indicators of financial performance: return on assets (ROA) for an accounting-based measure, and market-to-book value of equity and total stock returns as market-based measures. Factor analysis showed that these indicators loaded on a single construct, and factor scores were obtained using the Bartlett method. The variable was lagged by one year in the primary analysis.
The value of common shares owned by a CEO divided by total common stock. The variable was lagged by one year in the primary analysis.

The total value of long-term incentives granted to the CEO in the particular year divided by total direct compensation, which includes annual salary, short-term bonus, and the value of long-term incentive grants. Stock option grants were valued using the Black-Scholes method; performance shares, restricted stock, and other long-term grants were valued at the market price on the date of grant. The variable was lagged by one year in the primary analysis.

Index combining four indicators of board independence using principal components analysis, which the authors describe as appropriate for combining causal (formative) indicators. The four indicators are the proportion of the board composed of outside directors not affiliated with the firm, whether the CEO and board chair positions are separate, the portion of outside directors whom the CEO considered to be personal friends, and the percentage of total common stock held by outside directors. Factor analysis showed that all four indicators loaded on the same factor with an eigenvalue greater than one. In the primary analyses CEO responses were used to measure friendship ties. The variable was lagged by one year in the primary analysis.
The equity held by public pension funds, mutual funds, endowments and foundations, divided by the total amount of common stock. The variable was lagged by one year in the primary analysis.

Binary dependent variable distinguishing firms that filed a Chapter X or XI petition in the Federal bankruptcy courts from their matched survivors. Bankruptcies used as legal strategies to void labor contracts, to fight hostile takeovers or to cope with product or antitrust liability suits were treated as intentional and dropped from the sample. The final sample comprises 57 bankrupt firms and 57 matched survivors.

The standardized sum of two standardized variables: (1) the percent of the top team who were former high government officials (holders of elected federal or state-wide offices, appointed cabinet level or judicial positions, or elected mayors of major cities), and (2) the percent of the top team who were formally partners in a big eight accounting firm or major law firm, defined as any of the 10 largest (number of attorneys) firms in a major city (largest 20 by population). All items were standardized (mean = 0, s.d. = 1) using the mean and standard deviation when all firms (N = 114) were pooled over the five-year period.
time_window: each of the five years preceding bankruptcy (T-5 to T-1); standardized on pooled five-year means

description: The (standardized) percent of the top management team that held officer rank in any branch of the U.S. military. This variable was not restricted to higher ranks because of the infrequency of very high ranks (e.g., generals) in the sample. It did not load on any factor, so it was treated as a single item.
time_window: each of the five years preceding bankruptcy (T-5 to T-1); standardized on pooled five-year means

description: The standardized sum of three standardized variables: (1) percent of the top team who graduated from ivy league undergraduate schools or a small number of ivy league equivalent research institutions, (2) percent of the top team who attended a graduate level program in business, economics or law at an ivy or ivy equivalent university, and (3) the average education level of the top team, based on a scale of 1 to 7 for each manager's educational history where 1 = high school drop out and 7 = Ph.D. Cronbach alpha = 0.69 in year T-1.
time_window: each of the five years preceding bankruptcy (T-5 to T-1); standardized on pooled five-year means

description: The standardized sum of four standardized variables: (1) the number of corporate boards (other than his own firm) that the CEO sits on, (2) the number of officers in the top team who sit on corporate boards (other than their own firm), (3) the total number of corporate boards (other than their own firm) that the officers serve on, and (4) the number of officers in the top team who serve as trustees of nonprofit institutions. The measure was designed to tap both the depth of the team involved in outside boards and the breadth of interorganizational connections of the team; absolute numbers rather than percentages were used because the number of any single firm's top managers who serve on outside boards is generally limited to a few officers. Cronbach alpha = 0.84 in year T-1.
time_window: each of the five years preceding bankruptcy (T-5 to T-1); standardized on pooled five-year means

description: The (standardized) percent of the top team who were formerly officers (vice president and up) in another corporation. Former officers in financial firms and partners in law and accounting firms were excluded because these were included in POLIT or FINLINKS. The variable does not distinguish between previous experience with prestigious and nonprestigious employers.
time_window: each of the five years preceding bankruptcy (T-5 to T-1); standardized on pooled five-year means

variable_name: Five status characteristics (POLIT, MILT, EDUC, BOARDS, PREVTITLES)
description: Top team prestige was measured with five status characteristics of the top management team (vice-presidents and above): political elite membership (POLIT), military officer rank (MILT), elite education (EDUC), board memberships (BOARDS) and previous officer titles in other corporations (PREVTITLES). Most were standardized multi-item scales built from a factor analysis of resume data, and each was tested separately against bankruptcy.
time_window: Years T-1 to T-5 before bankruptcy

variable_name: direction-external or internal-of an organization's action
description: All changes associated with an organization, as reported by its top executive, were coded by the interviewer into 1 of 12 categories and also coded by a trained M.B.A. student, with an interrater reliability of .67 (Cohen's k) and a third trained coder resolving disagreements. Two of the 12 categories were externally directed organizational actions and eight were internally directed organizational actions; these 10 categories captured all changes that were actions taken in response to changes in the external environment. For purposes of analysis the 284 organizational actions were dummy coded 1 for externally directed actions and 0 otherwise.
time_window: changes associated with the organization within the previous six-month period

description: Antecedent events recalled by the executive were first coded as environmental events or events and actions within the organization, and the environmental events were then coded on each of four threat/opportunity categories by two independent raters using standardized coding instructions (interrater reliabilities .70 and .67, Cohen's k). An event was coded as a control-reducing threat when an aspect of the environment became more controlling. Each category received an increment of 1 if an environmental event could be coded into it and 0 otherwise, and a variable equals the total number of such antecedents when an action was associated with more than one; 161 control-reducing events were coded.
scale: count of coded antecedents (0 or more)
time_window: events antecedent to each action, within the previous six-month period

description: The same coding of antecedent environmental events by two independent raters into the four theoretically relevant threat/opportunity categories. An event was coded as a control-enhancing opportunity when an aspect of the environment became less controlling. Each category received an increment of 1 if an environmental event could be coded into it and 0 otherwise, and the variable equals the total number of such antecedents when an action had more than one; 60 control-enhancing events were coded.
scale: count of coded antecedents (0 or more)
time_window: events antecedent to each action, within the previous six-month period

description: The same coding of antecedent environmental events by two independent raters. An event was coded as a threat of likely loss when the organization reporting it stood to lose resources as a result of the event. Each category received an increment of 1 if an environmental event could be coded into it and 0 otherwise, and the variable equals the total number of such antecedents for an action; 105 likely losses were coded.
scale: count of coded antecedents (0 or more)
time_window: events antecedent to each action, within the previous six-month period

description: The same coding of antecedent environmental events by two independent raters. An event was coded as an opportunity for likely gain when the organization stood to gain resources as a result of the event. Each category received an increment of 1 if an environmental event could be coded into it and 0 otherwise, and the variable equals the total number of such antecedents for an action; 80 likely gains were coded. Gains and losses were coded as separate variables, as were control-enhancing and control-reducing events.
scale: count of coded antecedents (0 or more)
time_window: events antecedent to each action, within the previous six-month period

description: The informants used a seven-point, five-item Likert-type scale to indicate the extent to which their organization emphasized a product-market development strategy rather than a domain defense strategy. Consistent with Thomas and McDaniel (1990) and Miles and Snow (1978), the items measure the extent to which organizations focus on developing market shares and offering new rather than low-cost products and services. The data were collected with a survey mailed one month after the third interview, with the top executive treated as a key informant.
scale: 7-point Likert (1 = 'not at all', 7 = 'to a great extent'). Direction: higher = more prospector (defender to prospector scale)

description: A two-item, seven-point Likert-type scale measuring slack resources focused on the extent to which an organization had easy access to resources. One item asks the extent to which the organization has difficulty obtaining sufficient funds to produce its products and/or services (reverse-coded) and the other the extent to which the organization has easy access to resources for growth and expansion. The scale was collected with the same mailed survey of top executives.

Following the method in Podolny et al. (1996), each newsgroup's monthly membership growth was measured by dividing the total number of active members in the current month by the total number of active members in the previous month. On the rare occasions when there was no activity, and thus no active members in a month, the growth rate in the following month was set to be equal to the number of active members in that following month. The calculated growth rate ranged from 0 to 316 and was highly skewed, so the natural log was taken. The authors also constructed an alternative measure counting core members (those who had posted at least 11 messages), which yielded similar results; the reported results use the growth rate of all members.
time_window: current month relative to previous month

description: Two newsgroups were considered as sharing a member if the member posted at least one unique message in both groups in a given month; individuals who only cross-posted and posters who participated in more than 150 groups in a month were excluded. For each focal group the authors identified all other newsgroups in the Netscan database that shared at least one member with it in a month, including newsgroups not in the sample, and counted the members shared with each. The degree of membership overlap between focal group i and another group j in month t was the number of shared members between the two groups divided by the total number of posters in the focal group in that month. Member overlap density was the sum of the degree of membership overlap between the focal group and each other group with which it shares members; the paper's formula block is unreadable in this text, but the prose gives the example of adding 10% and 15% overlap to obtain 0.25. The measure was computed at a monthly interval.

A newsgroup's size was measured as the total number of active members who posted at least one message to the group in a given month. People who read messages without posting were not considered members and were thus not counted in this measure.

Group age was measured as the number of years that have elapsed since a group's creation. For a group created in September 1999, its age was coded as 1 from September 2000, 2 from September 2001, and so on. For groups created prior to September 1999, the month when they first appeared in the Google Groups archive was used as the starting month.

Binary variable indicating whether the U.S. parent firm in the IJV holds the call option right. It is coded 1 if the call option right is assigned to the U.S. firm (i.e., the option right is not assigned to the local firm), and 0 otherwise (i.e., the option right is assigned to the local firm). Researchers identified the assignment of call option rights by searching the activity synopsis text provided by the SDC with the key words option, right, choice, and opportunity, and reading each synopsis to code whether the IJV contained a call option right to acquire and which partner held it. In the simultaneous models this variable also serves as an explanatory variable in the equity ownership equation.

Binary variable coded 1 if the U.S. firm has a majority equity position—defined as greater than 50 percent of the ownership—in the IJV (i.e., the local firm holds an ownership of less than 50%), and 0 otherwise (i.e., the local firm holds an ownership of 50% or higher). Data for firms' ownership positions were from the SDC. In the simultaneous models this variable also serves as an explanatory variable in the call option right equation.

The input-output (IO) tables from the Bureau of Economic Analysis were used to first measure the degree of complementarity between an IJV and each of its two parent firms. The variable relative complementarity was then calculated as the difference between the complementarity index of the U.S. parent and the IJV and that of the host country parent and the IJV. The authors note that this approach comes with the limitation associated with the industry codes in the IO tables and the SIC system.
level: U.S. parent versus host country parent dyad

description: Each parent firm's IJV experience was measured by counting the number of IJVs formed in all foreign countries during the five years prior to, but not including, the focal year in which the focal IJV was formed. IJV experience was then defined as the log of one plus the number of IJVs. Relative IJV experience was calculated by subtracting the local partner's IJV experience from the U.S. partner's IJV experience.
time_window: five years prior to, but not including, the focal year

description: Words associated with optics in general (such as fiber optics) as well as with specific optical technologies were selected from each letter to shareholders and counted. The count is normalized by dividing by the total number of words in the letter to produce a measure of attention relative to other themes, and each CEO attention variable is multiplied by 1,000 for the regressions. The variable is calculated as a lagged, three-year decaying stock, so a market entry in 1980 would be predicted by the stocks of attention from 1977 to 1979.
scale: share of words in the letter to shareholders, multiplied by 1,000 in regressions
time_window: lagged one year; three-year decaying stock (e.g., 1977-1979 for an entry in 1980)

description: Words mentioning a specific communications technology other than those associated with optics (such as handset, amplifier, or semiconductor) were selected from each letter to shareholders and counted. The count is normalized by dividing by the total number of words in the letter, and the variable is multiplied by 1,000 for the regressions. It is calculated as a lagged, three-year decaying stock.
scale: share of words in the letter to shareholders, multiplied by 1,000 in regressions
time_window: lagged one year; three-year decaying stock

description: Words related to the industry in general and its main business (such as telephony, communications, or WAN-wide area network) were selected from each letter to shareholders and counted. The count is normalized by dividing by the total number of words in the letter, and the variable is multiplied by 1,000 for the regressions. It is calculated as a lagged, three-year decaying stock.
scale: share of words in the letter to shareholders, multiplied by 1,000 in regressions
time_window: lagged one year; three-year decaying stock

description: The percentage of nonoptical communications-related patents the firm has in its patent portfolio, where patents are used as a proxy for the degree of investment in a particular technology and as an indicator of the direction of R&D in the firm. The patent categories are three-digit nonoptical telecom patent classes and the variable is measured at the date of application. Like the other orientation and attention variables it is calculated as a lagged, three-year decaying stock.
time_window: patent application date; lagged one year; three-year decaying stock

description: The percentage of the company's overall sales reported as coming from the general telecommunications sector. The higher the ratio of telecom sales, the more focused on and dependent on the telecommunications industry the firm is and the more likely it has developed industry-specific competencies or complementary assets. It is calculated as a lagged, three-year decaying stock.
time_window: lagged one year; three-year decaying stock

description: A dummy based on whether or not the firm introduced a product specifically for the fiber-optics product market in that year, either through internal development (15 of the 20 cases) or external activities such as acquisition, joint ventures, or licensing (5 of the 20 cases). Only the first introduction of a product is modelled, so the event is nonrepeating. Information on entry was obtained from company press releases, trade journal articles, and other available industry data sources, triangulated to ascertain that a product was actually launched rather than simply announced. The variable is estimated in a Cox proportional hazard model stratified on the smaller-firm dummy.

Based on two survey items measuring the percentage of times that respondents had paid tips, gifts, or bribes for two administrative transactions with the government that are related to environmental regulations: (i) obtaining permits to use and exploit natural resources, and (ii) government inspections to monitor toxic waste discharges and spills. The measure is constructed at the state level from the EDGE survey of private businesses.

Based on three survey items that gauge firms' perceptions about whether firms that are similar to them pay bribes to governmental officials to avoid compliance with any type of regulations at three levels of government: federal, state, and local. The items are measured on an eight-point scale, 0 being 'never' to 7 being 'very frequently,' and the measure is constructed at the state level.

Binary variable that takes the value of 1 if the facility was ISO 14001 certified by 2004 and 0 otherwise. Certification is granted at the facility level by private third-party auditors who perform on-site visits to verify facilities' compliance with ISO 14001 requirements. The certified facilities in the sample obtained initial certification between 1998 and 2004 and no facility lost certification in the study period.

Technological overlap is measured from patent data following Podolny, Stuart, and Hannan (1996). The authors first define the niche overlap between each pair of firms i and j as the intersection set of the number of patents the two firms cite in a given year, that is, the count of common back-cited patents for each pair of firms. They then aggregate this across all pairs formed by a firm with every other member firm. The formula for this aggregation is not readable in the source text.

Support during standards creation is measured from the text of the electronic mails sent by firm representatives to the committee's mailing list. The authors employed the Linguistic Inquiry Word Count (LIWC) software's positivity index, which checks each word against an internal dictionary and reports the percentage of total words in each linguistic category. The positivity index is constructed as the difference between the scores for positive category words and negative category words. Higher scores indicate greater positivity and a more collaborative than competitive outlook, while lower scores suggest greater competitive tensions; scores were aggregated at the firm-month level using the monthly average.

The certainty index is an alternate measure of a firm's interaction tone during standards creation, based on a reliable linguistic measure of the extent of confidence expressed in the discourse being analyzed. The authors state that what sets it apart from the positivity measure is that it captures the level of assurance or optimism independent of emotional content, evidenced by a low correlation of 0.13 with the positivity index.

Consensus is modeled from ballot-voting data; ballots are voted on by firms at specific milestones during the standard-setting process. Firms' votes fall in one of four categories: 'Yes,' 'Abstain,' 'Yes with comments,' and 'No.' The authors computed a Herfindahl-Hirschman index of these vote choices, with higher values indicating stronger agreement between firms and lower values indicating the persistence of divergent opinions; a value of 1 at the extreme indicates that all votes were in the same category.
scale: 0 to 1, with 1 indicating that all votes were in the same category

description: The authors computed an analogous product-market competitive position measure using the Corptech product data, using the product codes at the most granular (third) level. They first calculated the number of product overlaps between the focal firm and each member firm, productOverlapij. They then defined the downstream competition for firm i as the aggregate number over all dyadic i, j product overlaps. The exact formula is not readable in the source text.

Measured using a 5-year window of the count of the number of distinct product categories that the firm was classified into in Corptech. The higher the number of product categories a firm spans, the broader is the firm's array of complementary products.

The authors first constructed the member firms' multipartner alliance network, coding ties between firms if at least one common multipartner alliance was observed in a 5-year window preceding a focal ballot; this set of ties formed the adjacency matrix defining the network. Using this matrix they calculated an eigenvector centrality measure for each firm. Heterogeneity in relational influence for a ballot is the standard deviation of the centrality scores of all firms voting in that ballot (Gulati and Gargiulo's structural differentiation measure), with higher values indicating greater heterogeneity.

The authors first counted the number of multipartner alliances (MPA) that each firm on a focal ballot had been involved with in the five preceding years, and also the number of partners the firm had in each of those alliances. They then constructed the measure as the standard deviation of the average number of partners of the firms' prior MPAs, so that the measure weights firm experience by multipartner alliance size.

Operationalized as the number of functional titles divided by all titles coded in the top management team in this study. The top management team is defined as the reported senior management body in a firm's annual report that was clearly entrusted with executive decision-making discretion. Titles not related to any of the constructs discussed in the paper were excluded from the count of all titles. The measure is expressed as a ratio.

Coded as the absolute number of distinct subunits within a reported division on the immediate next level. If no subunits were described in the reports, the value 1 was assigned. Distinct structural subunits were identified from separate reporting details for such subunits, from explicit references to subunits and their business activities in the annual report and division review, and by cross-validating descriptions with the preceding and following years.

Operationalized as the number of executive titles representing a given division divided by all division titles in the top management team. All titles that reflected responsibility for the focal division as a whole or for a distinct subunit belonging to this division were counted; for example, a division with two coheads and a chairman was counted as 3. If a single individual assumed multiple roles related to the same division, the value 1 was assigned, and if an executive had multiple titles relating to multiple divisions, a 1 was assigned for each affected division. If there were no division-related titles in the entire company for a given year, the value was set to 0.

Operationalized as the subunit's top management team title representation as a percentage of the division's total representation in the top management team. The measure captures a division's internal asymmetry of sublevel to both top and sublevel titles, so a greater value reflects a greater proportion of subunit influence regarding all influence that a division may exert.

Coded 1 when a division ceased to exist in its current form, i.e., when it lost its identity as a business segment in its own right. Identification followed a two-step approach: the official segment reporting of the current year was compared with that of the previous year, and the operations of the previous business segment were traced to their assignment in the current year. A previous segment was coded as recombined if it was split into multiple new segments, merged with at least one existing segment, merged with one or multiple other segments to form a new segment, or merged with parts of other segments to form a new segment.

Defined as the total monetary value of loans issued at the end of 1994. The authors use it, together with the parallelism between firm size and geographical spread between 1992 and 1994, to delimit each group, so that two firms of similar size may yet belong to different size classes because they have different geographical scopes. The first group (GI) comprises the seven largest firms, the second group (GII) comprises 16 medium firms, and the third group (GIII) contains the 77 smallest firms. The benchmark firms are the largest firm in each group plus the smallest firm in the sample.
time_window: end of 1994, with group delimitation over 1992-1994

description: Conjectural variations reflect agents' adaptation of their expectations about a firm's strategic behavior as a function of past experience, and are estimated for responses to decisions of output (quantity) within and between each size-defined strategic group in the Spanish loans market. The conjectural variation is a strategic group's subjective estimation of the effect of increasing their offer by one percent over the amount offered by another group. A positive value of the conjectural variation reflects competition between firms, while a negative value reflects collusion, both in reference to the Cournot situation. The conjectures are specified parametrically only for the benchmark firms, and the conjectures of nonbenchmark firms are expressed as linear combinations of the benchmark conjectures weighted by output distances.
level: firm (benchmark firm of each strategic group)

description: The Lerner index of bank i in the loans market, measured as ((rli - r - Cmgi)/rli), i.e., the interest rate on loans granted by firm i minus the three-month interbank interest rate and the marginal operating cost, divided by the interest rate on loans. The marginal operating costs used in this expression come from the estimated translog operating cost function.

Measured indirectly. The first indicator is the number of employees per branch, which captures the quality of service that bank employees offer to their customers; the second is the number of branches per km2, which captures the quality of service a bank offers in the geographical area in which it operates. These two variables reflect characteristics of firm i and in combination represent the implicit interest rate paid by a customer who chooses this firm; service quality is a linear function of these dimensions. In the estimates the intercept and the employees-per-branch coefficient are positive and significant, while the branches-per-km2 coefficient is not significant.

Defined as the EPS as announced by management minus the analyst consensus forecast when EPS exceeded forecasts (i.e., (Earnings - Forecast) if (Earnings - Forecast) > 0), and zero otherwise. High values correspond to earnings far above forecasts; differences greater than $1 were excluded, and more than 95% of the above target differences were smaller than $0.15, with a mean difference of $0.03.

Defined as the analyst consensus forecast minus EPS as announced by management if the forecast exceeded EPS (i.e., (Forecast - Earnings) if (Earnings - Forecast) < 0), and zero otherwise. The reversal of variables as compared with above target allows for consistency in interpretations of coefficients; high values correspond to earnings far below forecasts, and differences greater than $1 were excluded.

Taken to equal unity if the firm provided point estimate forecasts, indicated an interval within which it expected future performance to lie, or made a material statement regarding an existing analyst forecast, and zero otherwise. Approximately 44% of observations of quarterly figures included a forecast guidance.

The natural logarithm of the total number of the firm's press releases in each period, used instead of the raw number because the distribution had an extremely long positive tail, with a mean of 37 and a maximum of 1,794. The number of press releases was hand-collected for a random sample of firms.

A count of conference calls between management and analysts. Conference calls are announced to the public, generally include statements by firm managers (either the CEO or COO or both), and management's responses to analyst questions; about three-quarters of conference calls occurred in conjunction with earnings announcements.

The mean analyst EPS as forecast for quarter t generated in quarter t-1, minus the mean analyst EPS as forecast for quarter t generated in quarter t-2. Forecasts were averaged in windows immediately following earnings announcements (2, 6, 15, and 90 days), and the change was then explained by influence activities between the announcements.
time_window: quarter t forecasts made in t-1 and t-2

description: C-TPAT validation was determined with the question 'Has your company received C-TPAT (Tier Two) Validation?' Responses were coded high investment = 1 and nominal investment = 0. Tier two status required a mandatory external assessment for validation of the firm's entire supply chain and significantly higher monetary and resource commitments, whereas tier one firms received their status through self-assessment.

variable_name: Timing of entry (early adopters versus late adopters)
description: The moderating effect of timing of entry was measured by dividing the sample into two groups: firms that adopted the C-TPAT program between its inception and 2004 (n = 262) and firms that adopted after 2004 until 2007 (n = 270).
scale: binary group split (early adopters vs. late adopters)

variable_name: Speed of goods through U.S. Customs (Speed1 through Speed4)
description: A four-item scale asking: 'In your company, how have the following factors been impacted as a result of participation in C-TPAT?' The items were the number of U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) inspections, disruptions to the supply chain, lead time, and time and cost of getting cargo processed and released by U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP). Responses were coded 'increased' = 0, 'stayed the same' = 1, 'decreased' = 2, and the scale displayed a Cronbach's alpha of 0.78.

Competitiveness was measured with a single five-point Likert scale item ranging from 'extremely unimportant' = 0 to 'extremely important' = 4. The questionnaire item asked the respondent to indicate the relative importance of C-TPAT in making 'your company more competitive.'
scale: 5-point Likert item (0 = extremely unimportant to 4 = extremely important)

description: The total monetary value of loans issued at the end of each year of the analyzed period. Three groups are delimited between 1992 and 1998 on the basis of the parallelism between company size and geographical spread: large firms with a national scope that lent more than 2.5 billion pesetas, medium firms with regional scope that lent between 600,000 million and 2.5 billion pesetas, and small firms with a local scope that lent less than 600,000 million pesetas for the year 1998.

Conjectural variations estimated within each of the three size-defined strategic groups from the first-order condition of an oligopolistic competition model with product differentiation. The parameter VCh = (∂rplj/∂rli) represents the conjectural variation of firm i when firm i belongs to strategic group h, that is, the expectation of firm i about its rivals' reactions to an initial change in its price. The sign indicates the strategic interaction pattern, with a positive coefficient indicating a collusive pattern and a negative coefficient a competitive pattern relative to Bertrand-Nash behavior; the magnitude indicates the size of the rivals' responses, and significance rejects the assumption of Nash behavior.

The Lerner index of bank i in the loans market, measured as ((rli - r - Cmgi)/rli), where rli is the interest rate for loans issued by bank i, r is the interbank interest rate for three-months operations, and Cmgi is the marginal operating cost for firm i. It is the relative margin suitable for analyzing the evolution of competition, because oligopolistic competition models determine an equilibrium relationship between this relative margin and the structural and competitive conditions of the market, and it is the best proxy for the social welfare loss suffered due to market power. Accounting measures such as return on equity and return on assets are not used because the focus is on the loans market.

Each subject received a one-paragraph description of the target firm on each of the three reputation dimensions, manipulated into a positive or negative condition. The manipulations were coded into one variable with eight states that represented all of the combinations of the three variables in two possible states. This variable was used to create an unsaturated logit model assessing the role of reputation in the decision to joint venture.

The target firm was described in one paragraph either as respected for the high quality of its products and services, with customers believing that its reputation for value, quality products at a reasonable price is among the best in the industry and with a reputation for developing innovative products, or as having products and services reputed to be below industry standards, among the worst in the industry, and without a reputation for developing innovative products.

The target firm was described in one paragraph either as known for the high quality of its top managers and their integrity, with executives displaying concern for their community, responsiveness to environmental concerns, and a reputation for attracting, developing and keeping talented people, or as having top managers whose quality and integrity is suspect, showing little concern for their community and known to be unresponsive to environmental issues.

The target firm was described in one paragraph either as known for its financial soundness, having consistently provided investors with excellent returns and proved to be a very valuable long-term investment, with a reputation for efficient and effective use of corporate assets, or as having suspect financial soundness, below-average returns and no such reputation.

variable_name: decision to proceed with the strategic alliance
description: The first question and principal dependent variable for analysis was a decision as to whether to form the venture or not. The question read: 'Based on the description, would you proceed with the strategic alliance? (Circle One) Yes No.' Fifty-five respondents indicated they would proceed with the alliance and the remaining 115 respondents indicated that they would not proceed.

Tolerance of ambiguity was measured using the 16-item scale developed and validated by Budner (1962). Scale reliability for this study was 0.7062. The simple correlation coefficient between tolerance of ambiguity and locus of control was 0.34.

Locus of control was measured using the 16-item scale developed and validated by Spector (1988); its items are directly relevant for work-related behavior, making it a more specific scale than the Rotter instrument. The reliability for this study was 0.8061. High values denote internals (high locus of control).

The scenario contained the sentence 'Niche has in the past been a strong competitor/supplier of Acme's in various markets,' with the competitor or supplier wording varied as the manipulation. The experimental design created two groups: one group was cast in the role of joint venturing with a competitor, and one group was cast in the role of joint venturing with a supplier.

A cumulative count of the failures of other Japanese subsidiaries in industry i in China prior to subsidiary x's entry at time t-1. A parent firm's own failures in the industry were excluded from the count. Industry was delimited at the two-digit SIC code to capture the peer group of predecessors from which a new entrant may learn, and a subsidiary was considered failed if its operations had ceased or it had been formally dissolved. The summation formula itself is not legible in the text.

The unobserved hazard rate for Japanese subsidiary x's cessation of its FDI activity in China at time t. Subsidiary cessations were coded as 1 and surviving subsidiaries as 0, and the duration of each investment was computed as the number of years from entry into China to the time of exit, or until the year 2000 for subsidiaries that had not exited. Exit years were determined by comparing successive editions of the Toyo Keizai directory.

A composite index in which three types of heterogeneity - size, ownership structure and location - were z-score-standardized and then summed. Size heterogeneity is the standard deviation of the employment of all failed Japanese subsidiaries in the target industry in China before a focal subsidiary's entry, divided by the mean size. Ownership structure heterogeneity is a Herfindahl index over the three ownership types (WOS, JV and acquisition), and location heterogeneity is a Herfindahl index computed across the 20 provinces and 3 municipalities in which Japanese subsidiaries demised.

The number of the firm's prior FDIs in China other than in the target industry, including both surviving and failed investments, with the natural logarithm taken. The authors note that foreign parents with direct experience in the host country but no direct experience in the target industry are more likely to benefit from the experience spillovers offered by earlier FDI failures.

variable_name: ownership ties with failed investors before entry
description: The number of jointly invested ventures a Japanese firm had created worldwide with other Japanese investors who had made failed investments in China, prior to launching a subsidiary in China. The authors first identified which other firms invested in each subsidiary with the primary parent firm and then traced how many of those connected Japanese firms had previously invested in China and failed. Early FDI investors were identified across all industries in China, not limited to the subsidiary's industry.

Social outreach intensity is measured as an MFO's poverty focus, proxied by average loan size (ALS, logged), following the convention in the microfinance literature. The logic is that the amount a person can afford to borrow varies with his or her wealth, so smaller ALS reflects a focus on poorer borrowers. The measure adjusts for inflation, is comparable across MFOs and nations, and is reverse coded so that higher values reflect greater social outreach intensity.

Operating revenue divided by the sum of financial expense, loan loss provision expense, and operating expenses. The variable excludes income not derived from an MFO's core business, such as external funding and donations. It was log-transformed to adjust for positive skewedness.

The value of loans over 30 days past due, divided by the value of an MFO's loan portfolio. The authors note that this measure is more reliable than 'default rate,' which can be manipulated by an MFO to portray a higher quality loan portfolio.
An MFO's operating cost divided by its gross loan portfolio, logged and reverse-coded.

Based on the most recent update of the World Values Survey, the authors constructed a variable from responses to questions about whether or not a respondent would welcome as their neighbor: people of a different race, immigrants/foreign workers, people of a different religion, and people who speak a different language. They calculated the portion of respondents in a nation who did not want to have members of each group as neighbors and performed exploratory factor analysis using the standardized transformation of each variable. A confirmatory factor analysis with maximum likelihood estimation was then used to calculate an overall discrimination score for each nation; higher values reflect stronger discrimination based on race, country of origin, religion, and language.
time_window: most recent World Values Survey update

description: The Heritage Foundation's Economic Freedom Index, which comprises data from the Economist Intelligence Unit, International Monetary Fund, and World Bank and scores nations on 10 market efficiency factors. Nations are graded from 0 to 100 on each factor, and the scores are averaged to create a composite index (rescaled to 0-1). Higher scores reflect strong property rights, an effective legal system, low corruption, a favorable investment climate, and efficient regulations.

Created by the Economist Intelligence Unit to assess a nation's microfinance business environment. The measure reflects the quality of regulatory frameworks and practices as well as sector-specific institutions that support client protection, dispute resolution, and competition. Nations are scored on a 0-100 scale and the scores are rescaled to 0-1, with higher values reflecting a stronger institutional environment for microfinance operation.

The index developed by Cobb et al. (2016), which combines MIX data about the quality of an MFO's financial reporting with data on its regulatory status (i.e., whether or not an MFO is regulated by a state banking authority). Both measures are thought to reflect MFO management quality.

A multiple-indicator latent measure of CEO outside directorships, adapted from the model developed in previous research and supported by confirmatory factor analysis; the reduced, four-indicator submodel fit the data well. The four indicators are the total number of outside directorships held by each CEO, a count of directorships with Fortune 1000 firms, the average net sales of outside firms on whose boards a CEO served, and the average profitability of those outside firms in 1987. Relevant data were obtained from several sources, including Compustat, Disclosure, Trinet, company annual report and 10-K documents, Moody's, and Ward's directories.

Measured using five-year averages (1987-91, inclusive) of return on assets (ROA) and return on sales (ROS). The two indicators were used as multiple indicators of subsequent performance in the structural model, where both loaded highly significantly and in the expected direction. Data for this variable were drawn from Compustat files.

Measured over a five-year period (1982-86) using a measure developed and validated by Dess and Beard: time was regressed against the value of shipments and the regression slope was divided by the mean value of shipments. Industries were identified by four-digit SIC codes and data were drawn from the U.S. Industrial Outlook. For firms competing in multiple businesses, a weighted average reflecting the composition of each firm's unique business portfolio was calculated.

Measured using the Herfindahl-Hirschman index, which incorporates both the number of firms in an industry and inequalities in their relative market shares. The index ranges from 0 (perfect competition) to 1 (monopoly) and is published by the Commerce Department at five-year intervals; the authors employed scores reported for calendar year 1987. For firms operating in multiple businesses, a weighted average based on business portfolios was computed.

Measured using Palepu's (1985) entropy measure, which the authors note has been found to possess superior reliability and validity over other diversification measures. Data for calendar 1987 were drawn from the Compustat Business Segment database and company 10-K reports.

Content analysis of quarterly earnings conference call transcripts using LIWC 2015. Six LIWC word categories were used: verbs, adjectives, numbers, nonspecific quantifiers, past-focused words and future-focused words. Each lexical category score was normalized, the normalized scores of concreteness (verbs, numbers and past-focused words) were summed, and the normalized scores of abstractness (adjectives, nonspecific quantifiers and future-focused words) were subtracted, producing a continuous concreteness-abstractness measure. The authors treat language concreteness as an aggregate (formative) measure.

Event study measure of investor reaction, where an abnormal return is the difference between the observed return for a security and the predicted or normal return for the same security. The market model parameters alpha and beta were estimated over a 255-day estimation period ending 46 days before the event date. The main analyses cumulated returns over a 2-day (0, 1) window capturing the immediate investor reaction to the earnings call event. The mathematical specification of the abnormal return equation was not extractable from the text.
time_window: 2-day (0, 1) event window around the earnings call

description: Quarterly standardized unexpected earnings, defined as the difference between actual earnings and expected earnings, scaled by the end of quarter stock price. The consensus expected estimates of earnings were measured as the median of all analysts' forecasts in the 90-day period prior to the earnings announcement.
time_window: 90-day period prior to the earnings announcement for analyst forecasts

description: The firm's financial risk profile was measured using the firm's debt-to-equity ratio. High debt-to-equity ratios raise downside risk concerns because highly leveraged firms have limited access to debt markets to fund strategic investments and must commit a large percentage of their cash flows to paying off debts.

Assessed as the number of stable dyads present in the organizational core over time: for each pair of core members (players who played an average of more than 26 minutes per game over the season, plus the head coach) the number of seasons they had played together over the previous 10 years, including past common experience at clubs where they had previously played together. Scores are accumulated at the beginning of each season, and a mean-centered quadratic term is also entered in the models.
time_window: previous 10 years, accumulated at the beginning of each season; explanatory variables lagged by one year

description: Calculated following the same logic used for core relational stability, except that any possible dyad that involves at least one peripheral player is considered, i.e. dyads composed of one core and one peripheral player or of two peripheral players. For each such pair the number of seasons played together over the previous 10 years is counted, including common experience at clubs where they had previously played together.
time_window: previous 10 years, accumulated at the beginning of each season; explanatory variables lagged by one year

description: An overall relational stability measure that captures the dyadic stability of teams' networks without differentiating for stable dyads' network positions, i.e. the total effect of relational stability irrespective of network location. A mean-centered quadratic term of this measure is also included in the models.
time_window: previous 10 years, accumulated at the beginning of each season

description: The players available to each team at the beginning of each season, averaging their Player Efficiency Rating (PER) for the previous season (t - 1). PER weights multiple individual statistics and standardizes for minutes played and the team 'paces' that result from more offensive or defensive team strategies. Rookies had no previous-season performance data, so their current-year efficiency was used as a proxy for their talent.

Each club's human capital separated into core and peripheral components, using the same procedure used to distinguish core and peripheral relational stability; the core component is the average prior-season Player Efficiency Rating of the players belonging to the organizational core. The interaction between this variable and core relational stability and between this variable and peripheral relational stability are entered in Model 6.

The peripheral component of each club's human capital, obtained by separating the club's human capital into core and peripheral components using the same procedure used to distinguish core and peripheral relational stability; it is the average prior-season Player Efficiency Rating of the players belonging to the organizational periphery. Its interactions with core and peripheral relational stability are entered in Model 6.

Measured as the percentage of games won during the regular season. Because the percentage of games won is a continuous variable bounded between 0 and 1, which could be problematic for regression analysis, the authors transformed the dependent variable using a logit link function.

A time-varying, dichotomous measure coded 1 in the year a VC is affected by the delisting of an IPO firm and 0 otherwise. It captures whether a firm is delisted within five years following its IPO, using delistings by the primary exchange on which the firm is traded with CRSP delisting codes between 500 and 587, which are associated with negative events. Acquisitions are not treated as delistings.
time_window: within five years following the IPO

variable_name: VC reputation index (modified LPJ VC Reputation Index)
description: A modified version of the LPJ VC Reputation Index, an objective, multi-item, time-varying index capturing the theoretical dimensions of visibility and firm quality, created by averaging five formative indicators of VC firm reputation. The measures were standardized and summed, and the total score was then converted to a 100-point scale comparable across years. VC firm age was excluded from the index in the main analysis. The dependent variable uses the VC firm's reputation index value in the year after the focal year (t+1), controlling for the index value in the focal year (t).

Operationalized as the difference between a firm's opening and closing stock prices on its first day of public trading (closing price minus opening price) divided by its opening stock price, multiplied by 100. The measure was transformed into its natural logarithm to reduce the effect of outliers, adding the positive equivalent of the minimum value plus one to avoid log transformation of negative values.

Each firm's annual ROA was adjusted for capital expenditures and calculated using a firm's operating income before taxes, depreciation, and special items, minus its capital expenditures, divided by the firm's total assets. Industry differences were taken into account by subtracting the IPO firm's ROA from the average ROA of all publicly listed companies in the firm's two-digit SIC code for the focal year. ROA was Winsorized by 5% in each tail.
time_window: each year following the IPO; rolling average of the prior three years

description: The MTB ratio was calculated annually as the ratio of market value (the annual number of shares outstanding multiplied by the firm's annual stock price) over total assets. Market value data come from CRSP and accounting data from COMPUSTAT. The ratio was transformed into its natural logarithm to reduce the effect of extreme values, and because ratio variables may fluctuate around the time of delisting, a rolling average of the prior three years was used; for companies delisted fewer than three years after IPO, all available information up to the current year was used.
time_window: each year following the IPO; rolling average of the prior three years

description: The number of years a newly public firm has survived after the IPO, calculated on an annual basis by subtracting the IPO year from the current year.
time_window: annual, from the IPO year onward

variable_name: Number of rackets with focal innovation
description: The count of new rackets with a particular design introduced by competitors of an innovating company in a year; rackets launched by the innovator itself are excluded so that the count captures imitation. For example, in counting the number of oversized rackets introduced in 1985, rackets launched by Prince, the innovator, are excluded.

The highest playability score received by a racket embodying the innovation. Playability was scored by World Tennis test panelists who played with a racket for at least an hour and gave a score from one to ten on intrinsic quality; the highest score among a design's rackets is used as the quality frontier for the design. This variable is centered and lagged by one year.

A count of the number of top professional players using a racket incorporating one of the eight new racket designs, constructed from Tennis, World Tennis, and other publications on tennis. Visible and prestigious users are those on the 'top ten players of the year' lists of the ATP (male players) and the WTA (female players), plus athletes who reached the semifinals at the four Grand Slam tournaments. This variable is centered and lagged by one year.

The total number of advertisement pages in Tennis promoting a specific racket design in the entire industry. A full one-page advertisement dedicated to one tennis racket counts as one; when multiple rackets appear on a single page advertisement, each racket is given the count of one over the number of all rackets advertised on the page. This variable is centered and lagged by one year.

The count of advertisement pages in Tennis promoting a specific racket design placed by the innovating firm. A full one-page advertisement dedicated to one racket counts as one, and a racket among several on a page gets one over the number of rackets advertised on that page. This variable is centered and lagged by one year.

The count of advertisement pages in Tennis promoting a specific racket design placed by competitors of the innovating firm, since a new technology also appears in competitors' advertisements for their own brands incorporating it. A full one-page advertisement dedicated to one racket counts as one, and a racket among several on a page gets one over the number of rackets advertised on that page. This variable is centered and lagged by one year.

The authors sum two centered ratios: the biotechnology firm's number of drugs in development, centered around the mean value for all biotechnology firms, and the pharmaceutical firm's selling, marketing and administrative (SM&A) expenses, centered around the SM&A mean for all pharmaceutical firms. Only drugs that have entered clinical trials are counted as products in development. A centered ratio of 1.0 implies that the firm matches the average of its group, so the sum proxies the magnitude of potential synergies realizable in the dyad. The text does not state separately which data source supplies each component.

A count of each pharma-biotech dyad's non-overlapping niches, used as a proxy for strategic interdependence. The authors coded each firm's participation or non-participation in 133 biotechnology subfields, which two industry experts independently collapsed into 54 distinct subfields; they then calculated the absolute overlap in subfields for each dyad and subtracted that value from the maximum level of overlap (54 subfields).

A dyad-level measure of the extent to which the pharmaceutical and biotechnology firm in each dyad cite each other's patents, proxying how important each partner's patents are in the other's external technology portfolio. The authors constructed the rate from the NBER patent database for the sample firms' patents.

A dyad-level measure of the degree to which the pharmaceutical and biotechnology firm in a dyad draw from the same external technology base. The authors constructed the rate from the NBER patent database for the sample firms' patents.

Each biotechnology and pharmaceutical firm's patenting propensity was centered by its respective industry average in the same way as the centered ratios of the complementarity index. For each dyad the authors took the absolute difference of the two centered patenting ratios to create a patenting distance measure, so that a distance score of zero reflects complete similarity in patenting propensity. They then subtracted this distance from its maximum value so that the resulting measure represents similarity instead of distance.

A binary variable for the event of alliance formation between an old and a new technology firm, proxied by the probability of an alliance being formed in any possible dyad opportunity set between a pharmaceutical and a biotechnology firm. It is coded 1 if the given dyad formed an alliance, and 0 otherwise.

A second dependent variable for the event of alliance formation, applied to address unobserved heterogeneity arising from including different alliance types. It is coded 1 if the given dyad formed a non-equity alliance, and 0 otherwise; non-equity alliances are contract-based cooperative agreements.

A count of the total number of alliances formed within a pharmaceutical and a biotechnology dyad over the observation window, proxying the intensity of alliance activity in the dyad. During the 4-year time window between 1998 and 2001, 508 dyads had an alliance event, and a total of 580 alliances were formed.
A count of the total number of non-equity alliances formed within a pharmaceutical and a biotechnology dyad, used in parallel with the count of all alliances to assess alliance intensity.

The biotechnology firm's age since founding, measured beginning at incorporation, used as the moderating variable; its direct effect is included in all regression models. The average biotechnology firm in the sample is 15 years old.

A formative index formed by counting the number of discrete CSR activities a firm pursued, as identified from the firm's signature Web site pages ('About Us,' 'History,' and 'Mission and Vision Statements'). Broad statements, statements indicating that the firm's core business fulfills a specific social or environmental need, and 'will do' statements of intention were excluded. For each firm, all its discrete CSR activities were added to form the index. The authors report that 138 CSR activities pursued by 47 new ventures were identified, categorized into five groups.

A four-item, seven-point scale that was validated in prior research (Miller and Friesen, 1982; Venkatraman, 1989). The four items ask whether the firm emphasizes long-term (over 5 years) goals and strategies when defining strategies, whether criteria for resource allocation reflect long-term considerations, whether the firm emphasizes basic research to build future competitive advantage, and whether the major concern when defining strategies is how to build future competitive advantage. The appendix anchors the low end of each item in short-term statements and the high end in long-term statements.

A nine-item, seven-point scale on which respondents evaluated their firm's performance in the last year, where 1 means the firm was much worse and 7 means it was much better than major competitors. The nine items are sales level, market share, sales growth, cash flow, ability to fund business growth from profits, return on assets, return on equity, return on sales, and overall firm performance/success. The scale was validated in prior research (Stam and Elfring, 2008).

Measure of breadth in the firm's product development experience based on the concentric diversification index, which sums over pairs of categories the product of each category's share of the firm's activity and the distance between the categories. Activity is the percent of all 83 Strategic Insight categories in which the fund provider offers funds, and distance is set to 0 for the same category, 1 within the same level 3 category, 2 within the same level 2 category, 3 within the same level 1 category, and 4 across level 1 categories. The variable uses all funds the firm controlled in the year prior to the launch of the focal new product, and is interacted with the old category dummy to test Hypotheses 1 and 2.
time_window: year prior to the launch of the focal new fund (t-1)

description: Constructed with the same concentric diversification formula as firm breadth, but the set of funds considered is limited to funds introduced by the firm in the current year, concurrent with the focal new fund. A negative and significant coefficient indicates that introducing new funds in a broad array of categories at the same time decreases new product quality, testing Hypothesis 3.
time_window: current year (concurrent with the focal fund)

description: Count of the funds the firm has created in the focal new category over its history, excluding the focal year. The count is logged to deal with overdispersion and is used to test Hypothesis 4.
time_window: firm's history before the focal year (t-1)

variable_name: firm's new funds in same category
description: Count of the number of funds created by the firm in the same year in the focal category. The count is logged to deal with overdispersion and is used to test Hypothesis 5.
time_window: current year (concurrent with the focal fund)

description: The percentage of the 36 months after launch in which the fund posted a better-than-median return versus the other funds (new and old) in its fund category, out of 83 possible categories. To account for funds that closed before 36 months, the percentage of months the fund was active (up to a maximum of 36) in which the fund posted median-positive returns is used. Because the variable is a percentage bounded at 0 and 1, a logit transformation was used to create an unbounded dependent variable tested with ordinary least squares.

Dummy noting whether the firm has ever created a new fund in the focal category. Sixty-six percent of the new funds in the sample were created in categories in which the firm had prior direct experience, while 34 percent were in new categories. The variable is used to interact with firm breadth in the tests of Hypotheses 1 and 2.
scale: dummy (1 = firm has prior experience in the category)
time_window: firm's full history before the focal fund

description: A binary variable measuring participation in community CSR that functions as the DID estimator. It takes the value 1 for forecasts made by TPA-participating brokerages on companies headquartered within a 300 km radius and within the same province as any county or district the brokerages were paired with, and 0 for forecasts of companies headquartered in different provinces, outside the 300 km radius, for forecasts made before the pairing occurred, as well as for forecasts made by brokerages that had not yet participated in TPA. The 300 km radius was chosen from survey responses of brokerage employees about how far their personnel traveled outside the formally assigned county or district.

Measured as negative forecast errors, so that larger values of the dependent variable indicate more accurate forecasts and better forecast performance. Forecast error is the absolute difference between the forecasted and actual earnings per share, scaled by the company's stock price at the beginning of the year, multiplied by 100 and expressed in percentage points; the equation given in the paper could not be read from the provided text. Only current-year forecasts, that is forecasts for companies' next-coming annual earnings, are used.
time_window: annual forecasts for the next-coming year's earnings, 2013-2019

description: A categorization of the brokerages' TPA activities into those that involved ground-level activities and those that did not. Ground-level activities were coded to include providing on-site financial training, consultation or financial services for local businesses, establishing poverty alleviation workstations, and assigning stationed personnel. The remaining initiatives, which did not involve ground-level activities (No ground-level activities), typically included donations and the purchase of local products. The specific activities are explained in brokerages' CSR reports, available for 75 of the 79 brokerages in the sample.

Following the operationalization of Chen et al. (2022), a variable describing whether being proximate to (as opposed to distant from) a company is important for accurately projecting its earnings. Brokerages were divided into close and distant to a focal company based on the sample median of the distance between a brokerage and the company. The variable equals 1 when, in the prior 3 years, a company's forecasts issued by the close brokerages were more accurate than those issued by the distant brokerages.

The percentage of local revenue a forecasted company derived from its headquarters province relative to its total revenue, obtained from the CSMAR database. In the sample, the most detailed publicly available revenue data was at the provincial level.

A binary variable indicating that a brokerage had already conducted site visits to a company by the start of the TPA program in 2016. The Shenzhen Stock Exchange requires listed companies to disclose the organizations that conduct site visits to them, so this analysis uses the sample of companies listed on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange and enters the variable as an interaction with Paired.
time_window: visits before the start of the TPA program in 2016

description: Forecasts made by brokerages on companies headquartered in the same province are excluded from the main sample and analyzed separately; the analysis is restricted to observations where brokerages and covered companies are located in the same province. Analysts typically belong to a research department based at the brokerage's headquarters location and are assumed to be familiar with their home province.

The proportion of quantitative content in each analyst report, calculated with the Linguistic Inquiry and Word Count (LIWC) software using the 2015 Chinese dictionary, as a proxy for easily codifiable, explicit information. Texts were first segmented into words and phrases with Python, and punctuation and special characters were removed before the LIWC analysis; the data cover part of the sample (139,628 reports) from CSMAR.

Status is measured with the Bonacich power centrality, which iterates a firm's own centrality and the prominence of its partners until a stable score is reached. The scaling constant was selected so that the maximum status for a given year equals 1, and b, the constant determining how much an actor's status is determined by its partners' status, was set at three-quarters of the inverse of the maximum eigenvalue. Status was calculated for each VC in each year based on the preceding five years of syndication activity.

A spline variable equal to the absolute value of the status asymmetry when the follower was of greater status than the lead, and equal to zero otherwise. Status asymmetry is the difference between the status of the lead and that of the follower, divided by their sum. This index measures the ability of lower-status leads to bring higher-status VCs into a syndicate.
time_window: focal investment round; status based on the preceding five years

description: A spline variable equal to the status asymmetry when the status of the lead was greater than that of the follower, and equal to zero otherwise. A positive coefficient on this variable indicates greater willingness to bring in VCs of lesser status, whereas a negative coefficient indicates greater aversion to bringing in VCs of lesser status.
time_window: focal investment round; status based on the preceding five years

description: The logged ratio between the pre-money valuation of the company in the focal round (before any of the focal round's investments were added to the company value) and its post-money valuation after the conclusion of the preceding funding round. The authors log the measure because unlogged valuation changes are asymmetric and exhibit lower variance on the downside than on the upside.
time_window: between the preceding funding round and the focal round

description: The number of distinct companies within the focal company's industry funded in the given year, divided by the average number of companies funded within the preceding three years. The ratio is logged to reduce skewness and ensure the symmetry of the measure.
time_window: focal year relative to the preceding three years

description: The dependent variable indicates whether the observation is the factual tie that formed rather than a counterfactual tie that did not. For each factual observation the preexisting syndicate, the lead VC, and the investment round were held fixed and only the identity of the follower was replaced with an alternative follower that had invested in a new venture in the same investment stage, the same industry, and the same U.S. state during the same year as the focal round; up to 10 counterfactuals were randomly selected per factual. The conditional logit uses only within-group variation to predict the probability that a given observation was factual rather than counterfactual.
level: lead–follower dyad within an investment round

description: The operationalization is based on the balance in two variables: local network efficiency and foreign network efficiency. Respondents reported whether one or more of five types of local and foreign partners were involved in the development of the innovation (customers, suppliers, subcontractors, universities, competitors) and rated the importance of collaboration for each (0 = not important; 1 = of minor importance; 2 = important; 3 = of great importance). Local and foreign network efficiency were measured as a Herfindahl-Hirschman Index based on the proportion of alliance partner rating relative to the highest possible rating. Geographic network balance is one minus the absolute difference in relative focus between local and foreign partners; a worked example yields 0.981, and higher values indicate greater balance in network efficiency.

The hazard of exporting an innovation during the period of observation, measured as the number of years between 'Innovation prototype development year' and 'Export year.' A venture could export a given product innovation during the observation period (coded as 1), or if the venture did not export its new product innovation, the observation is censored (coded as 0). Of the 407 product innovations, 153 were exported.

Assessment of innovation complexity by industry experts in SFINNO, distinguishing structural (artefactual) complexity and development complexity. Innovations were classified into high complexity; medium artefactual complexity/high developmental complexity; medium artefactual complexity/low developmental complexity; and low complexity, with high complexity being an innovation that is a system of several functional parts developed from several disciplines and low complexity a single coherent unit developed from one discipline. The items were reverse-coded so that higher values indicate increased complexity.

A reflective measure of (1) product clockspeed, (2) process clockspeed, and (3) organizational clockspeed, replicated to the Finnish context from Nadkarni and Narayanan (2007). Product clockspeed is the average time between the introduction of new products by all incumbents in the industry; process clockspeed is the average number of years for which firms in a four-digit NACE code depreciated their capital equipment; organizational clockspeed is the average time span between corporate strategic actions introduced by all firms in each industry. All three indicators load on a single factor (eigenvalue = 4.528) with factor loadings for product (0.89), process (0.95) and organizational clockspeed (0.87), and the reliability of the measure was 0.84.

The room capacity in hundreds of rooms added through entry in a focal hotel's zip code in the quarter in which entry occurred. In the case of multiple entrants in a particular market-period, the measure reflects the capacity of all entrants. A quadratic term (entrant size squared) and a log-transformed version (log entrant size) were also investigated to test alternative shapes of the relationship.

A hotel was classified as facing a high-quality entrant in a particular quarter if a new high-quality hotel opened in its zip code during the quarter. Hotels were defined as high quality if they operated in the Upscale, Upper Upscale, or Luxury segments, or were upscale independents whose average price over the life of the dataset fell within the range of average prices defining the branded high-quality segments.

The dependent variable is the average daily price of an individual hotel room, transformed using the natural logarithm because hotel prices tend to follow an approximately lognormal distribution. The measure is the hotel's average price over the particular quarter, so it does not capture intra-quarter variability. Price was used instead of revenue per available room because RevPAR is a function of both price and occupancy.
scale: natural logarithm of average daily rate in dollars

description: A count of the number of entries a particular hotel has faced since the beginning of the dataset, with values ranging from zero to 11. It is used both as a main effect and interacted with entrant size, entrant size squared, and facing high-quality entrant.
time_window: since the beginning of the dataset

description: RKS adapted the MSCI KLD 400 Social Index framework and the standards of the Global Reporting Initiative (GRI 3.0) to create a rating system of firms' CSR reports. All Chinese listed firms' reports are rated on more than 70 subdimensions that consider the range of CSR activities and the extent of the firms' engagement. The indicators fall into three major categories: social responsibility strategy and innovation (14 items), disclosure content (45 items), and technical sufficiency (11 items). Experts assess the firms along these indicators using an anchored scale of 0 to 4, with an interval of 0.5 points. The final RKS score is a weighted average of scores along the three categories, ranging from 0 to 100.
A dummy variable created based on the plan's policy change in 2011. It is coded '1' for the post-policy period (2011-2014) and '0' for the pre-policy period (2009-2010).

Measured as the governor's and the party secretary's prior political appointments, calculating the total number of different provinces in which they had served as governor or party secretary prior to their current positions in the focal province. The more provincial positions that officials have held, the more contestable they are in China's RDA political regime, and the more motivated they are to compete for promotion to the central government.

Measured as the average number of years before the governor and the party secretary would retire at age 68 under China's political system. The greater the number, the longer an official's career horizon. To test the curvilinear moderating effect, this variable was interacted with the Twelfth Five-Year Plan in its square term, while the first-order term was controlled for.

Coded as the total number of senior appointment positions a CEO was currently holding or had previously held in one of four key political organizations at the central level: the government, the Communist Party, the National People's Congress, and the Chinese People's Political Consultative Conference. CEO names were manually matched with those of officials collected from Chinese central governmental websites, and the names were crosschecked to identify current or previous interlocks between firm CEOs and central government officials or party leaders.
Measured as the total number of years since the CEO took the position. The measure is consistent with prior research on CEO tenure and firm CSR.

Clustering coefficient of the firm's intraorganizational collaboration network, calculated for each year. The network matrix was constructed annually from collaborative ties between scientists, measured as coauthoring relationships on patents with application dates in that year, and was dichotomized before calculating cohesion so that only the presence of a tie is captured. The clustering coefficient of an individual actor equals the density of its neighborhood, and the overall clustering coefficient of a network is the average of the densities of the neighborhoods of all of the actors. The measure was calculated using UCINET.

Density of the overall intraorganizational collaboration network, calculated as the proportion of all actual ties to the total number of all possible ties within the network. It captures the global degree of cohesion among all members of the network, and increasing values capture higher global density. The measure was calculated using UCINET.

Number of patents in each year of the observation period that led to a drug launch between 1984 and 2007.
