description: Measured by the target's sales growth over the 3 years preceding the year of a focal acquisition.
time_window: 3 years preceding the year of the focal acquisition

description: Cumulative abnormal returns associated with an acquisition announcement, calculated with standard event study methodology. An asset-pricing model is estimated using historical data from a 250-day period preceding the acquisition announcement, predicted returns are calculated over the 3-day event window (-1, 1), abnormal returns are actual returns minus predicted returns, and CAR is the sum of abnormal returns within the event window.

A content-analysis measure of the percentage of dividend-related words in an acquisition announcement. The dividend dictionary consisted of the words dividend, safe, stable, maintain, cash flow, steady, and all of their forms and derivatives. The percentage is calculated as the number of dividend words divided by the total number of words in the announcement, multiplied by 100.

A content-analysis measure of the percentage of growth-related words in an acquisition announcement. The growth dictionary consisted of the words grow, expand, innovate, rise, pioneer, dynamic, rapid, fast, and all of their forms and derivatives. The percentage is calculated as the number of growth words divided by the total number of words in the announcement, multiplied by 100.

Excess entry is the ratio of the mean number of entrants to known or expected market capacity c, and is also reported as the proportion of games producing more entrants than capacity (over-entry) versus fewer than capacity (under-entry). The authors give the ratio of entrants to known or expected market capacity, the ratio of entrants to the zero-profit industry equilibrium, and the average profit per round earned by entrants in each market.

Markets varied by size (market capacity c) and by volatility; the entrepreneurial market is the smallest risky market, whose capacity values were (0,1,2) and whose expected capacity was 1. It is compared with the smallest stable market (c = 1) and with larger stable and risky markets.

variable_name: Proportion of games with over-entry and under-entry
description: The proportion of games producing more entrants than market capacity c (over-entry) and fewer entrants than capacity c (under-entry), compared with the binomial model's predictions for the same conditions. The bias is evidenced where actual over-entry significantly exceeds, and actual under-entry significantly falls below, the unbiased predictions.

A statistical null model in which subjects are assumed to hold correct beliefs on average about their rank-orderings on the quiz and about the entry decisions of other players. For a given player facing a market with capacity c, this implies entering with probability c/7, and the expected number of entrants follows a binomial probability model with n = 7 and p = c/7; for markets with uncertain capacity the binomial probabilities were averaged over the three possible market capacities.

Confidence is the difference between a subject's entry choices in the first and second blocks of the experiment, with a positive value indicating overconfidence and a negative value indicating underconfidence. Less aggressive entry in the second block gave evidence that a subject held overconfident beliefs about their abilities during the first block, more aggressive entry gave evidence of underconfident beliefs, and no significant difference gave evidence of well-calibrated beliefs.

Entry is a binary variable coded 1 for entry and 0 for non-entry in each round of the market entry game. Subjects decided in each round whether or not to enter a market, and payoffs were determined by their performance on the quiz and by market capacity c in that round.

The independent variable size represented the known or expected market capacity c. In the known condition c was either 1, 2, 3, 4, or 5; in the risky condition c had expected values of 1, 2, 3, 4, or 5, with the corresponding realized values (0,1,2), (1,2,3), (1,3,5), (2,4,6) or (3,5,7).

Market volatility was coded 1 for risky markets and 0 for known markets. In the known condition players were confronted with known market capacities, and in the risky condition market capacities were subject to risk, with players knowing the distribution of possible market capacities.

An evenly weighted multi-item scale composed of three questions about direct ties between the investors and the venture team prior to the investment decision (Cronbach's alpha = 0.78). The items were: 'Prior to seeing the deal, I had a professional relationship with at least one venture team member'; 'Prior to seeing the deal, at least one member of the venture team was someone with whom I had engaged in informal social activity (e.g., playing tennis, going to the movies)'; 'Prior to seeing the deal, at least one member of the venture team was a personal friend'. Individuals responded to five-point Likert scale items ranging from 1 = strongly disagree to 5 = strongly agree, and each scale was calculated by adding together the values for the items that composed the scale and dividing by the number of items.

An evenly weighted multi-item scale composed of four questions about indirect ties between the investors and the venture team prior to the investment decision (Cronbach's alpha = 0.75). The items were: 'Someone whom I trust to discuss important confidential matters knew at least one member of the venture team'; 'A third party whose judgement I trust provided me with nonpublic information about the venture team'; 'I could obtain information about the venture team from my network of contacts faster than other investors could obtain the same information'; 'By calling people I know, I could obtain information about the venture team in a relatively inexpensive manner'. Responses were on five-point Likert scale items ranging from 1 = strongly disagree to 5 = strongly agree, and each scale was calculated by adding the item values and dividing by the number of items.

An evenly weighted multi-item scale composed of three questions about the members of the venture team's reputation as entrepreneurs (Cronbach's alpha = 0.71). The items were: 'Someone on the venture team had a reputation for successfully building public companies'; 'A third party I respected vouched for the team's ability to start a successful company'; 'At least one venture team member is viewed by other investors as giving the venture credibility'. The scale was based on individual responses to five-point Likert scale items ranging from 1 = strongly disagree to 5 = strongly agree.

The dependent variable was a binary variable of one if the investment was made and zero if the investment was not made. Respondents were randomly divided into two groups, one asked about the most recent seed-stage investment that they evaluated and made, and the other asked about the most recent seed-stage investment that they evaluated but did not make.
scale: binary: 1 = investment made, 0 = investment not made

description: The proportion of total pay comprised of stock options, calculated as the ex ante value of options granted (as reported by Execucomp) divided by total compensation (measured as TDC1 in Execucomp) in the same year. It is calculated as a two-year average of the prior two years to reflect that companies may grant options periodically rather than annually and that options are meant to motivate behavior over multiple years. Continuous variables were Winsorized at the one percent level and inflation-adjusted to 2010 dollars.

A binary (1/0) measure of whether a company experienced a recall in year t. Recalls are identified as all Class 1 and Class 2 product recalls occurring during the sample frame, i.e., instances where there is a reasonable probability that a product will cause serious harm or death (Class 1) or where exposure may cause temporary or medically reversible health consequences (Class 2); Class 3 recalls were not included.

A count of recalls in year t, ranging from 0 to 27 in the sample. Recalls are all Class 1 and Class 2 product recalls identified from the FDA's weekly Enforcement Reports; Class 3 recalls were not included.
Measured as the number of years since becoming CEO, natural log-transformed to correct for skew. It was included as a moderator and also as a control variable lagged by one year.
A binary indicator of whether the CEO was listed as the founder of the firm in S&P Capital IQ.

A player's reputation in a given season is measured with his average performance during the previous three seasons, adjusted by an annual decay function, so that performance in the previous year is divided by one, performance two years ago is divided by two, and so on. Performance in each season is measured by the player efficiency rating (PER), a per-minute rating of a player's performance, standardized for each year.
Reputation at the team level in a season is measured by the average reputation of the players on the team roster in that season.

An indicator variable coded 1 for high-status players and 0 for non-high-status players. To determine whether a player was of high status, the authors used information on awards and team-selection honors in the NBA; if a player was selected for any of these honors in the previous three seasons, he was coded as being of high status in the present season, and if not, he was considered non-high status.

Team status is measured by the average status of the players on the team roster in that season. Because the player status measure is dichotomous, this measure is equivalent to the proportion of high-status players on the team roster.

An ordered variable taking a value of 1 if the team did not qualify for the Playoffs, 2 if the team qualified for the Playoffs, 3 if the team advanced to the Conference Semifinals, 4 if the team advanced to the Conference Finals, 5 if the team advanced to the NBA Finals, and 6 if the team won the NBA Championship. This is the dependent variable used to test Hypothesis 1a.

variable_name: Number of wins during the regular season
description: To capture actual product quality in the mediation analysis, the authors used the number of wins during the regular season in the current season. The correlations confirm that the number of wins during the current season is positively and significantly associated with ticket income as well as with team status and team reputation.

The log-transformation of the total ticket income (gate receipts) for a team for that season, excluding corporate seats, because corporate seats are less sensitive to variation in team composition. This is the dependent variable used to test Hypotheses 1b and 2.

Performance relative to the teams' historical aspiration levels, defined as a moving average of past product quality, obtained with an updating parameter a that weights recent performance information; results are reported using a value of .50. To arrive at the final measure, a team's past product quality (product quality in the previous season) is subtracted from its historic aspiration level for product quality in the previous season. The formula for the aspiration level is not readable in the text provided.

A team's aspiration level for revenues is measured with historical aspirations as a moving average of past revenues, constructed in the same way as described for product quality aspirations. To arrive at the final measure, a team's past revenues (from the previous season) are subtracted from its historic aspiration level for revenues in the previous season.

A new player is someone who was playing for a different team in the previous season but is playing for the focal team in the current season. The reputation measure was dichotomized so that a player was coded as being of high reputation if he was above the 85th percentile in the performance distribution of the reputation measure in the current season. Indicator variables identify new pure high-reputation players (high reputation but not high status) and new pure high-status players (high status but not high reputation); the dependent variable is coded -1 if the team recruited more new pure high-reputation players than new pure high-status players, 0 if it recruited the same number in these two categories, and 1 if it recruited more new pure high-status players than new pure high-reputation players.
time_window: current season (relative to the previous season)

description: Yearly salary figures in US dollars, used to test Hypothesis 4. To reduce the skewness of the distribution, the authors used the natural logarithm of salaries.

The dependent variable was assessed using four items: the ratio of acquisitions to divestitures, the percentage of total sales due to acquisitions, the importance of acquisitions, and the importance of divestitures. The two importance-of-restructuring items were composites of different motivations for asset restructuring measured by seven-point Likert-type scales. The factor loadings for the four items were 0.65, 0.66, 0.70, and 0.74, and Cronbach's alpha for the combined measure was 0.70.

Change in country development was measured by the 5-year average of the Human Development Index (HDI). HDI is a composite of adjusted real GDP per capita (in purchasing power parity dollars), educational attainment (combined first-, second-, and third-level gross enrollment), adult literacy, and life expectancy. HDI indexes were collected from the United Nations Development Programme's Human Development Reports 1992-1996.

Competitive change was measured using three survey items: change in local competition, change in access to the local market by foreign competitors, and access to capital. Responses were made on seven-point Likert-type scales. The factor loadings were 0.86, 0.85, and 0.74, and Cronbach's alpha for the composite scale was 0.88.

Deregulation was assessed using four items: the number of government regulations with which the company must comply (reverse coded), liberalization in the government's attitude toward domestic acquisitions, changes in government policy regarding privatization, and export liberalization. These items were measured by seven-point Likert-type scales. The factor loadings of the four items were 0.72, 0.64, 0.61, and 0.63; the authors summed the four items and obtained a Cronbach's alpha of 0.71.

Group affiliation is a dummy variable based on three survey items: the importance of a commercial bank which has ownership in the firm, the importance of affiliated partner firms which have ownership interest in the firm, and the importance of other companies in which the firm has ownership interest. Responses were on seven-point Likert-type scales, with factor loadings of 0.72, 0.75, and 0.68 and a Cronbach's alpha of 0.72. The combined survey item was used to divide the sample into business group-affiliated firms and primarily independent firms, with a median split resulting in 92 business group-affiliated firms and 106 independent firms.

Count of the number of technical articles published in Solid State Technology that reported on technical challenges regarding the mask and resist for each of the new technology generations. Lithography-related articles published between 1961 and 2010 were identified with a list of keywords, and articles published five years after a generation was commercialized were excluded. Generations were categorized as High or Low according to whether the count was above or below the cross-generation average.
time_window: articles published 1961-2010, excluding those published five years after generation commercialization

description: Based on published technical specifications for lithography tools sold by every major tool manufacturer, including resolution, numerical aperture (NA) and wavelength, from which the value of k1 was derived for every tool model using the Rayleigh criterion. Extension opportunity is computed as the percentage increase in NA and the percentage decrease in k1 between the best old technology tool sold in the year that the new technology was introduced and the best old technology tool ever sold after that year.
time_window: tool specifications sold between 1973 and 2009; from the year of new technology introduction onward

description: The number of years from the year the new generation was commercialized to the year its annual market share surpassed that of the old generation. Market dominance is defined as the first year in which the new generation exceeds the annual market share of the old (previously dominant) generation. Generations that never achieved dominance are marked with a dash.
time_window: from commercialization of the new generation

description: The new technology generation's annual share of total industry sales (in dollars) during the period of technology transition; the higher the new generation's annual market share during this period, the faster it substitutes the old generation. The main analysis is performed for the first six years of sales for each of the new technology generations.
time_window: first six years of sales for each new technology generation

description: The authors first identify all M&A of firms in the sample, then for each firm at a given year T they calculate the sum of sales contributed by target firms up to year T. The measure captures the significance of each M&A transaction on overall firm size (measured by sales) and is more fine-grained than previously used dummy variables. Values are logged because the raw values display approximately lognormal distributions.
scale: log of sales contributed by target firms

description: Measured as the difference between firm sales at year T and the previously calculated M&A growth; the portion of sales not acquired via horizontal M&A is considered the result of organic growth. Values are logged because the raw values display approximately lognormal distributions. Twenty-six observations have raw values smaller than 0 and are excluded from the analysis.
scale: log of sales not acquired via M&A

description: The spread between the price paid by buyers and the price charged by suppliers (cost of goods sold), used to evaluate the bargaining power of the focal firm over both its customers and suppliers. Gross margin is calculated, according to the US GAAP guidelines, as the difference between sales and purchases, divided by sales. An increase following M&A may imply higher prices charged to customers or lower prices paid to suppliers, or a combination of both, and in either case reflects an increase in the firm's bargaining power.

Operating costs as a percentage of sales, used to assess operating efficiency; a firm enjoys higher operating efficiency if its operating cost/sales ratio is lower. Operating costs include depreciation, headquarter, logistics, labor, other sales, and general and administrative costs. Because higher values of the variable indicate lower operating efficiency, the measure is reverse-coded relative to the construct as named.

Return on Assets, described as a common measure of profitability in strategy research that helps compare the results to previous research. The authors note it is somewhat unreliable since it is affected by the choice of accounting methods and assumptions.

Operating profit as a percentage of sales, used as an alternative measure of overall firm performance. The authors state that, unlike ROA, it is not contaminated by choice of accounting rules for asset evaluation.

Takes the value 1 for firm-year observations if the firm is incorporated in a state that has passed the UD law by year t and 0 otherwise. Firms' state of incorporation in each year is identified from 10-K filing header information, and missing values are replaced with Compustat's current state of incorporation information. Because the corporate law of the state of incorporation governs shareholder derivative litigation, adoption of the law is treated as an exogenous reduction in shareholder litigation risk, so a value of 1 indicates lower litigation risk.

Sum of the total strengths across items in the five MSCI KLD STATS categories that are highly relevant to stakeholder initiatives: environment, community, human rights, diversity, and employee relations. The product category is excluded, as are items under the diversity category that are directly related to executives and directors of the firm. The total score is scaled by subtracting the average strength score of firms in a given year to account for structural changes in the KLD database.

Ratio of total shares owned by outside directors over total shares outstanding. Shareholding information of outside directors is collected from ISS Directors Data, and the director identification procedure proposed by Coles et al. (2014) is followed to match director shareholding information to the panel dataset. The variable is centered on its mean value for easier interpretation of the main effect of the independent variable.

Ratio of the number of shares owned by dedicated institutional investors over the total number of shares outstanding. Dedicated institutional investors are identified using Bushee's (1998, 2001) investor classification, which uses portfolio turnover and holding concentration to identify investors holding a focused (as opposed to diversified) portfolio for a longer period of time. The variable is centered on its mean value for easier interpretation of the main effect of the independent variable.

Operationalized as the sum of the six provisions in the Protection sub-index of the Gompers et al. (2003) Governance Index, which covers provisions aimed at providing insurance for directors and officers against job liabilities or offering special compensation upon changes in their responsibilities or termination (for example, golden parachutes). The variable is reverse coded so that a higher level indicates less protection for managers, and thus stronger governance. For missing years, the last available score is used; the variable is centered on its mean value.
time_window: last available score carried forward for missing years

description: Transparency International computes the CPI annually as a composite of a number of independent surveys whose target questions range from the frequency of corruption in various contexts (such as obtaining permits, avoiding taxes) to the common occurrence of bribery to politicians, senior civil servants, and judges. The surveys differ with respect to respondents and items but are strongly correlated, and in most cases sample designs are restricted to business practitioners who are local residents. The authors used Husted's (1999) transformation, inverting the 0 to 10 scale by subtracting each country's score from 10, so that 10 is the most corrupt country and 0 the least corrupt. Scores were taken for two years, 1999 and 2000.

Computed by taking the raw changes in FDI from one year to the next, i.e. the proportional change in FDI between 1998 and 1999. For example, FDI into Argentina changed from U.S. $6.670 billion in 1998 to $23.929 billion in 1999, so Argentina's FDI linear change took the value 2.59 [(23.929 - 6.670)/6.670]. The authors state that this variable captures their construct of developmental speed, with the opportunities for corruption that it presents, as employed in Hypothesis 1a.

Created by taking the absolute value of the FDI linear change variable, thus capturing both the positive and negative flow of FDI. The FDI figures for 1998 and 1999 were obtained from the World Bank statistical unit.
Created by squaring the FDI linear change variable. The FDI figures for 1998 and 1999 were obtained from the World Bank statistical unit.

Based on Hofstede's (1997) cultural dimension scores from an earlier multinational study of cultural values; the authors note that recent studies have upheld the theoretical and empirical value of his constructs and measures. As an earlier measure it is assumed to be constant, so no lag is applied to it.

Based on Hofstede's (1997) cultural dimension scores from an earlier multinational study of cultural values; the authors note that recent studies have upheld the theoretical and empirical value of his constructs and measures. As an earlier measure it is assumed to be constant, so no lag is applied to it.

A 0-1 variable indicating whether the alliance experienced significant contract alterations, major changes in the board or committee overseeing the alliance, or the introduction or formalization of monitoring mechanisms. To avoid counting minor changes, the survey questions were worded with qualifiers such as 'significant' and 'major.' Equation (1) was estimated using logistic regression, and separate binary logit models were also estimated for each of the three types of change.

The respondent was asked to indicate the number of prior agreements with any partner on similar subjects. Because the variable was positively skewed, it was redefined using the logarithmic transformation 'new variable' = log(1 + 'old variable'). Experience was measured for the responding firm only, not for both sides of the dyad.

The respondent was asked to indicate the number of prior agreements with the same partner as in the focal alliance. Because the variable was positively skewed, it was redefined using the logarithmic transformation 'new variable' = log(1 + 'old variable'). Experience was measured for the responding firm only.

The respondent was asked to indicate the number of prior agreements with any partner on any subject. Because the variable was positively skewed, it was redefined using the logarithmic transformation 'new variable' = log(1 + 'old variable'). Experience was measured for the responding firm only.

Respondents characterized the activities the collaboration comprises, choosing among six specific project activities: basic research, new product or process development, testing and obtaining regulatory approval, manufacturing, sales and marketing, and distribution. Alliance Scope was measured as the number of project activities encompassed by the alliance.

For each activity the collaboration involved, respondents allocated 100 percentage points across the collaborators to indicate partners' responsibilities for the task. Division of Labor is a continuous variable ranging from 0 to 1. When the variable takes on a value of zero, the collaborators share responsibility for every project activity equally; when it equals one, a partner is solely responsible for individual project activities, so larger values indicate a clearer division of labor. The equation block that specifies the computation is not readable in the paper text available.

Respondents were asked to describe the relevance of the alliance for the overall business of the parent firm in terms of the amount of available resources committed. The variable can take on values from 1 to 4, which correspond to 'marginal,' 'normal,' 'important,' and 'critical.'

Dependent variable equal to 1 if the focal firm failed in the period of observation. Failure is defined as exit from all submarkets in the ISM in which the focal start-up may have operated; a firm is termed as having failed if it ceases to exist or if it enters a 'distress sale,' and favorable acquisitions are treated as censored. The year of exit was identified as the year in which the focal firm's corporate Web site was last available on archive.org, and the date of acquisition was identified using the Zephyr database.
time_window: annually, from entry until 2004 or exit

description: The number of information security patents assigned to the start-up when it was formed, weighted by the number of forward citations received. Virtually all these patents are invented by members of the founding team, and thus represent a good signal of the technical capability of the start-up.

The number of sales executives that the start-up employed at the time of entry, based on the CorpTech directory, which lists the top 10 employees of the firm along with their principal function (e.g., finance, sales or marketing, engineering). Since the distribution of the number of sales executives is skewed, the authors use the log of one plus sales executives.

The number of university security patents relevant to the submarket, representing the stock of ISM patents held by universities and government agencies, lagged one year. All ISM patents held by universities and government agencies were collected and each patent assigned to an ISM submarket using a many-to-one USPTO subclass-ISM submarket mapping, so the measure varies not only between submarkets but also within a submarket over time.

For public firms the authors use return on assets from Compustat to estimate the relative performance variable on an annual basis; relative performance is the gap between firm performance and the average performance of all firms in the industries in which the firm operates. This measure is annual, whereas Chang (1996) used five-year averages of both the firm and the industry. Each firm-level variable is lagged one period from the entry/exit activity.

In the extensive search model, dissimilarity is the closest distance between the target industry and any industry in which the firm currently operates, computed as the minimum over those industries of the sum over the four human resource types of the absolute difference in percentages. The human resource percentages are at the three-digit SIC code level and come from the Occupational Employment Survey, where four human resource groups are defined: managerial, engineering, scientific, and marketing.

In the intensive search model and the exit model, the measure is the average distance of human resources between the focal industry and the other industries in which the firm operates, where the distance is the absolute difference in the percentages of each human resource type. Chang (1996) weighted the distances by sales to compute a weighted average distance; because CorpTech does not report sales by SIC code, the authors' average distance is unweighted.

variable_name: HRP dissimilarity with the firm's entries at time (t - 1)
description: In the sequential entry model the authors follow Chang (1996) and estimate HRP dissimilarity as the closest distance between the target industry and the industries that a firm entered in the previous period.

The dependent variable is a binomial variable that equals one if firm i enters manufacturing industry j at time t, and zero otherwise; for extensive search this is entry into a new three-digit SIC industry in which the firm did not previously operate. Nonentry events are generated considering all three-digit SIC manufacturing categories in which the focal firm does not operate but some sample firm operates in that year, following Chang's state-based sampling.

The dependent variable is a binomial variable that equals one if firm i enters an industry at time t, and zero otherwise; for intensive search this is entry into a new four-digit SIC in a three-digit SIC industry in which the firm is currently operating. Nonentry events follow the same state-based sampling scheme as for extensive entry. Because most sample firms had no intensive entry, the authors pool all observations that have the required lags rather than reporting results for each two-year period.

The exit models estimate the likelihood of exit from all markets in which a firm operates with a specification comparable to the Cox hazard model estimated by Chang (1996). The authors include the same control variables as Chang except for line-of-business characteristics, which are not available in CorpTech. Relative performance and the human resource profile dissimilarity measures and controls are lagged one period.

variable_name: Extensiveness of a firm's previous search activity
description: The ratio of the number of a firm's extensive search entries to the number of its total entries in the previous period. Because the authors have annual data, a one-period lag represents one year, whereas with Chang's biannual data a one-period lag represented two years.

Market entry is measured as a firm entering a new three-digit SIC manufacturing industry (extensive entry) or a new four-digit SIC within a three-digit SIC industry in which it already operates (intensive entry). Each is a binary dependent variable for a firm, industry and year.

Indicator coded one if the International Directory of Corporate Affiliations (1991) identifies the firm as having operations in Egypt, Iran, Iraq, Israel, Jordan, Kuwait, Lebanon, Saudi Arabia, Syria, Turkey, or Yemen in 1990, and zero otherwise. Control firms drawn from Compustat were checked in the same directory and only multinationals without Middle East operations were kept. In all but five cases sample firms had divisions or full ownership of the Middle East operation(s).

R&D expenditures divided by firm total assets; expenditures are scaled by total assets to control for potential heteroskedasticity. For each firm the values of each variable are averaged over the 1986 to 1990 time period. Used as a proxy for technological or production intangible assets.

Advertising expenditures divided by firm total assets; expenditures are scaled by total assets to control for potential heteroskedasticity. Values are averaged for each firm over the 1986 to 1990 period. Used as a proxy for marketing intangible assets.
Total firm sales, averaged for each firm over the 1986 to 1990 time period.

Sales from foreign sources divided by total firm sales; sales from foreign sources are gathered from the Compustat geographic segment file. Values are averaged for each firm over the 1986 to 1990 period.

Firm profitability measured as return on assets, consistent with the scaling of the intangible asset measures because all of these variables are scaled by total assets. Values are averaged for each firm over the 1986 to 1990 period.

The first stage uses patient-level data to regress ICU status and generate the predicted probability that a given patient would be in the ICU under normal conditions, and this estimation is used to compute expected ICU use by year at the center and industry levels. The second stage uses the deviation from predicted ICU use to measure patient misrepresentation. Three measures are used: Stat95, a binary variable with a value of one if the center's ICU use was above the 95th percentile confidence interval of the predicted value; Count deviation, the count difference between the actual number of patients and the predicted number of patients from the ICU; and Fraction deviation, the difference between the actual fraction and the predicted fraction of patients from the ICU. A 3-year window is used to calculate the measures, and the deviation is also used in first-differenced form as Δ deviation from predicted use.
time_window: 3-year window; first 3 years after entry for entering centers

description: A count, for each year and OPO, of the number of entrants that had begun misrepresenting patient status in a previous year. To determine when a center adopted the unethical strategy, a statistical threshold of having been above the 95% confidence interval of predicted ICU use for two consecutive years in a row is used, with the start date assigned to the first of the two years. A binary variable indicates whether a center begins misrepresenting, having the value of 0 until they begin and 1 afterwards, and once a center is identified as having adopted the strategy it is dropped from the sample so that only the initial adoption is captured.

In the ICU-use analysis, entrant is defined as a center that entered during the analysis time frame; an alternate definition is a center in the first 3 years after entering. As a further alternate measure of new entrants, the analysis is repeated looking at centers with cumulative volume either below or above 100 transplants. In the adoption analysis, any center that entered after 1990 was considered an entrant unless it was the first center in a given OPO.

Entry is a dummy variable at the transplant center level where entry equals 1 in the year of the first liver transplant and 0 for the previous years. The reported analysis is based on only the first entry point, and kidney transplant centers that are not performing liver transplants are considered the pool of potential entrants for that year. Because entry is a forward-looking decision, the announcement date of the new policy, July 16, 2001, was used as the before and after cutoff instead of March 1, 2002.

The change in the number of transplants a center performs from the previous year, used as the baseline performance metric that misrepresenting patient status could improve. It is regressed on the change in the deviation from the predicted ICU use compared to the previous year, Δ deviation from predicted use, in a first-difference estimator approach.

Exit is defined as occurring in any year where a firm has no transplants in the following year, and any year with no volume in the following year is considered an exit year, so exit is assumed to occur at the end of the year. For entering firms, exit events are captured through the end of the data set and classified as right censored at that time. A Cox proportional hazards model is used to estimate the hazard rate of exit for firms that entered before 2001, and for incumbents a model of the probability of exit in any given year is estimated.

The position on the Billboard chart that a label reaches in a specific month. If a label has more than one single in the chart, the average is used as the measure of chart position. Y is the position of firm i in month t; a lower position means a better chart performance.
time_window: monthly, 48 weeks before and 48 weeks after the change

description: The position on the Billboard chart that a certain artist, genre, or song reaches in a specific week; if an artist or genre has more than one single in the chart, the average is used. A lower position means a better chart performance.
time_window: weekly, 48 weeks before and 48 weeks after the change

description: Estimated with a probit equation in which entry is a dummy that takes a value of 1 if the artist i enters the chart in week t, and 0 otherwise. The model includes emerging artist, change, their interaction, week variables and artist controls.
time_window: weekly, 48 weeks before and 48 weeks after the change

description: A product space is built from Spotify product attributes of all the songs produced in the previous 12 months in the song's genre; a song's novelty is the Mahalanobis distance of the song from the centroid of this product space. Mahalanobis distance accounts for possible interdependence across product attributes.

A dummy variable that takes on value 1 if an artist has not had a single appearing in the top 50 of 'The Hot 100' chart nor an album in the top 50 of the 'Billboard 200' chart before the focal month. Artists are classified by cross-checking different sources.
A dummy that takes on value 1 if the genre is mainstream according to Discogs; the analyses compare the chart entry and performance of nonmainstream versus mainstream genres.
time_window: weekly, 48 weeks before and 48 weeks after the change

description: A dummy variable that takes the value of 1 following the introduction of streaming sales to the computation rule of the Billboard chart and 0 otherwise. The change went into effect on March 24, 2012, and the same dummy is used in the demand and supply analyses.
time_window: 48 weeks before and 48 weeks after the change

description: The average novelty of all the songs that firm i produces in month t. Each song's novelty is the Mahalanobis distance of the song from the centroid of a product space defined by the Spotify attributes of all the songs produced in the previous 12 months in the song's genre.
time_window: month t; novelty product space over the previous 12 months

description: The diversification of a firm i's product portfolio in different music genres, which represent niches in the music industry. Because genre is a categorical variable, the Blau index is used: BI = 1 - sum of p_igt squared, where p is the proportion of songs released by firm i in each of the g th genre during month t. The variable ranges from 0 (perfectly homogeneous) to 1 (perfectly heterogeneous).
The number of songs that firm i produced in the niche with the highest product density during month t.

The measure is based upon the concentration diversification index, computed from a firm's activity in genre g during month t and the distance between genres g and j; the full specification is given in a formula whose rendering in the text is unreadable. Distances between genres are set to 0 for g = j, 1 if the misclassification rate of g to j is higher than 3%, 2 if it is between 0.5% and 3%, and 3 if it is between 0.1% and 0.5%. EB is the sum of all the diversification indices in the 12 months preceding the focal month t, and since the measure is highly skewed the logarithm of (1 + breadth) is used.
time_window: 12 months preceding the focal month t

description: The approximate total monetary cost, in Euros, of the research that led to the surveyed patent, measured before the date of application. Reported by the inventors in the PatVal-EU survey and used as the endogenous core covariate, instrumented with GOVERNMENT FUNDS, SERENDIPITY and FIRM INTERESTS ON LIABILITIES. Entered in logarithms in the regressions.
level: research project leading to a patent
time_window: up to the patent application date

description: The depreciated patent stock of each NUTS3 region for the specific technology of the focal patent, over all the years available since 1978. It is computed as the number of patents in the same ISI-INPI-OST technological class as the focal patent, invented in the same NUTS3 region, up to the year in which the focal patent was applied for. The authors report a 0.3 depreciation rate and note that using different depreciation rates does not change the estimated results. Entered in logarithms in the regressions.
time_window: 1978 to the year before the focal patent application date

description: Built from the inventors' ratings, on a 0 (not used at all) to 5 (very important) scale, of the importance of interactions such as discussions, meetings, and sources of ideas with people belonging to the inventor organization including affiliates, and with people belonging to other unaffiliated organizations, during the research that led to the patented invention. The authors derive a standardized difference between the external and internal scores; the specification shown in the article's formula block is not readable in this text. The measure takes a lower weight and approaches zero if it derives from the intense use of both resources or if the difference between the scores is small, and it increases if the scores are low or their difference is high.
time_window: during the research leading to the patented invention

description: A dichotomous dependent variable that takes a value of 1 if inventors use internal knowledge sources, regardless of their importance, and 0 otherwise. It is estimated together with the EXTERNAL variable in a two-step bivariate probit model.
time_window: during the research leading to the patented invention

description: A dichotomous dependent variable that takes a value of 1 if the inventors use external sources, regardless of their importance, and 0 otherwise. It is estimated together with the INTERNAL variable in a two-step bivariate probit model.
time_window: during the research leading to the patented invention

description: An indicator reported directly by the inventors in the survey of the importance assigned to protecting the invention from imitation as a reason to patent. It is independent of the two factors that form the interaction term between research investment and regional absorptive capacity, which allows the authors to conduct a simple mediation test with three regressions.

The number of self-citations, that is, later patents by the same applicant citing the focal patent, counted in the five years following the application year, after controlling for the total number of forward citations received by the focal patent in the same period. It is used as a dependent variable to examine whether the interaction term affects future R&D trajectories.
time_window: five years after the application year

description: Coded as the year in which a firm was no longer listed in The Red Books. An agency was considered as surviving if the agency name remained the same or changed only slightly, or if the name changed to reflect a newly named partner. Where names were similar, the agency's address was used to verify that the same firm was being listed; if the name and address were different, the firm was coded as a new entry. To protect against spurious deletions, agencies were considered as failed if they remained unlisted for two consecutive observation periods, and departure events in which over 75 percent of the listed employees in one agency moved to another agency were treated as mergers/acquisitions and the departed firm was censored rather than failed.

Dummy variable created to indicate whether a firm lost an executive to another firm in the sample. If a firm was involved in a departure event, it was flagged as such for that firm year. The variable is time variant and was calculated for each observation period on the basis of the number of executives who were at the firm at that time; the firms from which executives depart are set to be under risk after a departure event takes place.
time_window: year of the observation period in which the departure occurred

variable_name: total top executive exits to competing firms
description: Count measure of the total number of top executives that a firm lost to competing firms, included to measure the quantity of executives that a firm loses to its competitors. It is time variant within the data set and was calculated for each observation period on the basis of the number of executives who were at the firm at that time. The measure records all departures even if they occur multiple times throughout the time period.
time_window: year of the observation period in which the departures occurred

description: Dummy variable indicating whether a firm gained a top executive from a competing firm. If a firm was involved in an entry event, it was flagged as such for that firm year. The variable is time variant and was calculated for each observation period on the basis of the number of executives who were at the firm at that time.
time_window: year of the observation period in which the entry occurred

variable_name: total top executive entry from competing firms
description: Count variable for the total number of top executives a firm added from competing firms, created alongside the top executive entry flag. It is time variant within the data set and was calculated for each observation period on the basis of the number of executives who were at the firm at that time.
time_window: year of the observation period in which the entries occurred

description: Category grouping the departures of production and administrative top executives, coded from qualitative data from interviews with current and former advertising executives and from the trade literature. Administrative top executives oversee the everyday operations of the agency, including treasury, human resources, facilities maintenance, and payroll, while production executives work to create the tangible advertisements. Coded for each observation period on the basis of the number of executives at the firm at that time and time variant within the data set; for example, if an agency loses a given executive position in 1944, that departure variable is set equal to 1 for that year but 0 for the next year in the sample.
time_window: year of the observation period in which the departure occurred

description: Category grouping the departures of creative, account, and media top executives, coded from qualitative data from interviews with current and former advertising executives and from the trade literature. Creative executives manage the advertising campaign for clients and devise text, visuals, and concepts; account executives acquire new clients and manage current client relationships; media executives manage the advertisement placement strategy and formulate media purchase plans. Coded for each observation period on the basis of the number of executives at the firm at that time and time variant within the data set.
time_window: year of the observation period in which the departure occurred

description: Experience was measured by cumulating all the prior cases that involved one or more IVF cycles using the patient's own fresh eggs. In line with prior research, the authors computed the natural log of experience. This assumes that the experiential difference between 100 and 200 cases is more influential than the difference between 10,000 and 10,100 cases.
time_window: cumulative prior to the year of observation

variable_name: Success rate for standard patient group (up to 35)
description: Success rate in standard cases, defined as the live-birth rate in the IVF patient group aged 35 and under involving the use of the patient's own fresh eggs. It is calculated as the number of live-birth events per number of female patients 35 and under who underwent one or more fresh IVF cycles in the year of observation.

We computed the proportion of older patients as the ratio of the number of IVF patients over the age of 35 to the total number of IVF patients treated each year by each clinic. Thirty-five years is used as the standard cutoff rate in the field because at around that age female fertility shows a rapid decline.

We proxy the proportion of patients who have received more than one IVF cycle by dividing the total number of IVF cycles by the total number of IVF patients treated at a clinic in the same year of observation. A history of prior IVF failure can signal a possible problematic underlying etiology.

The number of frozen cycles relative to the number of fresh IVF cycles performed at a clinic is treated by sector analysts as indicative of the proportion of good prognosis patients in the clinic's patient mix. To make the interpretation of this ratio consistent with the hypothesis, which refers to the effort expended by clinics to handle more demanding cases, the authors reverse coded this ratio to obtain a proxy for the number of poor prognosis patients.

CAR is calculated through the event study methodology for each firm. The event window is (0, +1), the day of the event and the next day, and the estimation window is (-210, -11), covering 200 trading days with at least 30 days of stock return data available. Abnormal returns are residuals from the standard market model specified in the paper; the equation itself is not readable in the text provided, so the exact specification is a gap. Cumulative abnormal returns for the portfolio between (0, +1) are calculated by summing abnormal returns, and CARs for non-host firms are computed the same way based on the host firms' visit dates.

A dummy variable that receives a value of 1 if a firm receives a visit, and 0 otherwise. It is used in the second-stage regressions together with a treatment correction calculated from the first-stage probit regression on whether a firm received a visit.
Return on assets (ROA) lagged one year prior to the visit, used to measure the firm's prior financial performance.
time_window: lagged one year prior to the visit

description: A dummy variable coded as 1 if a firm's controlling shareholder is not the Chinese central or local government, and 0 otherwise.

variable_name: Percentage of top managers with political connections
description: Measured as the percentage of top managers with political connections. A top manager is deemed to have political connections if he or she has worked in the government.

The level of institutional development of the province where the focal firm is headquartered, using data from the NERI Index (Fan and Wang, 2011). More institutionally developed provinces receive higher NERI Index scores.

Composite score of the average extent to which various resources are shared between the JV and the parent, weighted by the importance of the resource shared. The JV CEO assessed the importance (0 = none to 4 = very great) of each listed resource/skill/service to the ongoing operations and success of the JV and the extent (0 = none to 4 = very great) to which it was shared with each parent. The importance response was divided by its maximum value of 4 to obtain a perceived importance weight, so the composite can be interpreted on a 0-4 scale. The composite score correlated positively with a single-item overall measure of strategic interdependence (0.74).

Composite score of the average degree of environmental change associated with environmental factors, weighted by the importance of change in each factor. Keeping the past 5 years or the time period since JV formation in mind, the CEO assessed both the importance of change in the five environmental factors (0 = none to 4 = very great) and the extent of change in the factors faced by the JV (0 = none to 4 = very great); the importance response was divided by 4 to obtain a perceived importance weight. The composite correlated positively with a single-item overall measure of environmental uncertainty (0.53). In estimating the regressions the variable took the same value for each of the two dyadic relationships between the JV and its parents.
time_window: past 5 years or the time since JV formation

variable_name: Use and complexity of integrative mechanisms (COORD)
description: Weighted average of the frequency of use of four kinds of integrative mechanisms. JV top executives indicated the frequency of use of each mechanism in coordinating decisions made by JV managers and managers from each parent, on a 5-point scale ranging from 1 = rarely to 5 = very frequently. Each mechanism's frequency was weighted by its relative capacity for information processing: a rank of 1 was assigned to direct contact, 2 to liaison personnel, 3 to temporary task forces and 4 to permanent committees, and each rank was divided by the sum of the ranks (10) to obtain a weight.
scale: 5-point frequency scale (1 = rarely to 5 = very frequently)

description: The CEO of the JV was asked to indicate the involvement of board members from each parent in each of four board member roles, ranging from 0 = none to 4 = very great. The four roles concern participating in drawing up the strategic plan, approving budgets and short-term plans, monitoring operating performance, and coordinating JV and parent actions.

The external role of the board members was assessed on a one-item measure. The CEO of the JV was asked to indicate the involvement of board members in the role of facilitating legal or public/government relations of the JV, ranging from 0 = none to 4 = very great.

For each parent, a 'yes' response to three questions was used to construct the measure: whether there is a planned rotation of the JV's CEO back to the parent, whether either parent has planned rotation of JV top managers to and from duty with this JV, and whether JV top managers attend executive development programs and seminars conducted by either parent. The number of 'yes' responses was summed for each respondent, so that a score of 0 indicates that no socialization mechanisms were in use, whereas a score of 3 indicates that all three socialization mechanisms were in use.

variable_name: Incentive compensation based on a mix of JV plus parent performance (INMIX)
description: JV CEOs were asked to respond to the question: what percentage of the JV top management bonus is based on the performance of the JV alone, as opposed to being based on a mix of JV plus parent performance or some other criteria. The measure took the value of the numerical response to this question, which ranged from 0 to 100 percent. Because a higher value means bonus determination rests on the JV's own performance rather than on the parent's performance, the measure runs opposite to the construct as named.

variable_name: Proportion of board members from each parent on the JV board (RBOD)
description: Two questions were asked to assess the proportion of board members from each parent: the total number of members on the JV board, and how many of the total members represent each parent. The number of members representing a parent was divided by the total number of JV board members to compute the proportion of board members for that parent.

variable_name: Proportion of top management positions occupied by parent managers (RMGR)
description: The representation of managers from each parent in the JV is measured by the proportion of top management positions in the JV which are occupied by managers from each parent.

variable_name: Whether the top executive of the JV is from the parent (CEO)
description: A binary variable indicating whether the top executive (CEO) of the JV is from one of the parents.

Computational content analysis of independent director biographies. Keywords and stem-word variations are counted for four categories: monitor and control, material independence, resource provision, and service and strategic counsel. The counts for monitoring and controlling plus material independence form Monitoring Role, and the counts for resource provision plus service and strategic counsel form Resource Providing Role. The relative emphasis of the monitoring over the resource-providing role is then computed with the Janis-Fadner coefficient of imbalance, producing a company-level score.
scale: ratio bounded between zero and one

description: All undergraduate and higher levels of education that an individual director received in an Anglo-American country such as the United States, United Kingdom, Canada, or Australia were counted; foreign education in non-Anglo-American countries such as the former Soviet Union, Japan, Germany, and France was coded as zero. The total number of years of Anglo-American education for individual directors was aggregated per company board and standardized by the total number of directors per board.

Board interlocks with foreign companies were counted as the number of interlock ties with Anglo-American companies, that is, the United States, United Kingdom, Canada, and Australia, as indicated in the director biography and the BvD filing, and then aggregated at the company level.

Codes the share ownership percentages of non-Chinese institutional shareholders (5% block shareholders) in the focal company, based on the nationality of the majority shareholders and their share ownership as captured by BvD and 20F filings. The nationality of foreign institutional owners included the United States and other offshore incorporation countries such as the Cayman Islands and the British Virgin Islands.
A continuous variable indicating the number of years since the local incorporation year of the firm, obtained from the 20F and BvD database.

A continuous variable built by counting the total number of positions directors hold in the Chinese government, state-regulating authorities, or national committees such as the People's Congress (CPC) and the People's Political Consultative Conference. The current number of corresponding positions for individual directors as captured in the BvD database or the director biographies was then aggregated at the company level.

A PCA factor score combining two variables. The first is the total amount of institutional investor's investment as captured by 13F filings (logged), used as a measure of the investor community's attention to the listed company and funding success in the financial market. The second is the market-to-book ratio (shares outstanding multiplied by stock price over total asset size), a conventional measure of post-IPO financial performance. The eigenvalue of the first component was 1.01 and the two variables were loaded with factor scores of 0.70.

Based on the stock ownership report in the sample company's 20F filing, computed as the remaining stock ownership excluding the top three majority stock owners. Higher degrees of ownership dispersion under the principal-principal conflict indicate fragmentation among the minority shareholders and uninterrupted power of the majority shareholders, which constrains the capacity of an independent director's monitoring task.

Computerization in support functions (COMSUP) was measured by asking respondents to indicate on five-point scales the extent of computer usage in nine functional areas found in most manufacturing firms. Computerization of the technical core (COMCOR) used five-point scales to assess the degree of computerized equipment usage in 11 key manufacturing processes. Both variables were calculated by averaging responses to the appropriate scales.

Computer integration of support functions (INTSUP) was measured using four-point scales by asking the extent to which transactions between four pairs of subunits were accomplished using computers. Computer integration between support and core functions (INTBTN) was measured similarly, using four-point scales for four pairs of functions. Computer integration of the technical core (INTCOR) was measured by asking about computerized flows of materials between six pairs of production processes, using six-point scales. Scores were computed by averaging responses to the appropriate scales.

Respondents were asked which mode—automatic (2), semiautomatic (1), or manual (0)—best described data exchange among 66 pairs of functions. Measures of sophistication (SOPHSUP, SOPHTN, SOPHCOR) were derived by averaging appropriate subsets of this data. SOPHTN was deleted from the measurement model because it was highly correlated with SOPHCOR, leaving SOPHSUP and SOPHCOR in the final model.

Vertical differentiation (LEVELS) is the number of hierarchical levels in the organization. Functional specialization (SPECIAL) is the number of functional task areas in which there is at least one full-time specialist. Job specialization (JOB) is the number of job titles in the organization. Indicators of organization structure were drawn from the Aston battery of structural measurement, and the scales were slightly modified for phrasing.

Formalization is the extensiveness of written rules and procedures. The scale was drawn from the Aston battery of structural measurement and was slightly modified for better phrasing, with some items added and some deleted.

Decentralization of resource allocation decisions was represented by two items from the Aston scale, and decentralization of system design was captured by three items. The lower in the organization these decisions are made, the more decentralized is the organization. Major revision of the decentralization scales was necessary in order to distinguish among types of decisions.
Professionalization was operationalized as the proportion of employees who occupy jobs that require a college degree.

Advanced manufacturing technology is measured by three latent constructs from the plant survey: computerization (extent of computer use in individual functions), integration (computer integration between pairs of functions) and integration sophistication (automatic, semiautomatic or manual data exchange). Each is measured for support functions, the technical core and between them.

Dummy variable coded 1 if a subcontractor was involved in a given project and 0 if the project was completed using only in-house resources. Variable coding was based on an analysis of the records in the project file, which contained information regarding the use of subcontractors and, in some cases, subcontractor invoices. Data limitations prevented a finer-grained measure: the data indicate only whether a subcontractor was employed, not the percentage of the contract completed by any subcontractor or the number of subcontractors. When subcontracting, Compustar generally contracts out a significant portion of the work for a given project.

Coded 1 if a customer's personnel were directly involved in the project in such a way that Compustar had to depend on them to complete the task(s), and 0 otherwise. It serves as a proxy for hold-up derived from asset specificity and captures bilateral dependence between Compustar and its client; two Compustar engineers aided in coding the variable from the 'Deliverables and Responsibilities' sections of each contract.

Additional measure of asset specificity, defined as a dichotomous variable coded 1 if the contract stipulated that Compustar must complete a project by a specified date and 0 otherwise. This treatment of temporal specificity is consistent with the empirical TCE literature.

Dichotomous variable coded 1 if a project could shut down a 'significant portion' of a customer's data center and as 0 otherwise. It identifies projects with the potential to shut down a customer's data center, where mistakes can be especially costly to Compustar and a subcontractor could take advantage of its position to opportunistically renegotiate the terms of its contract.

An amalgamation of the variables interdependence, time specificity, and disrupt; a count variable taking values ranging from 0 to 3. The three hazards were grouped into one hold-up variable for a theoretical reason, that all three represented hold-up hazards, and a practical one, that the authors lacked sufficient variance to test them individually with interactions.

Captures whether the technology employed in a project made it difficult to determine the quality of the output generated by the project team. Coded 1 if the quality of the end product associated with a particular project was difficult to observe and 0 otherwise; Compustar engineers coded the data on the basis of whether a brief, inexpensive inspection could have determined the quality of the output.

Captures whether assets were at risk of misappropriation in a given project. Compustar engineers and managers generated a list of their proprietary technologies and coded the variable as 1 if any of these technologies or processes were to be used for a transaction and as 0 otherwise; projects requiring proprietary technologies subjected valuable knowledge to the risk of misappropriation by a subcontractor.

Dummy variable coded 1 if a project involved working on Compustar-manufactured hardware and 0 otherwise. The firm had superior (relative to competitors) internal capabilities in working on hardware that it manufactured, and employees with world-class capabilities in this area.

Coded 1 if a contract involved working on a mainframe computer and 0 otherwise. Compustar had been designing and manufacturing mainframes since the 1970s and had developed very strong capabilities in this area; external industry experts verified Compustar's capabilities in these areas.

Dichotomous variable that took the value 1 if a project primarily involved programming tasks and 0 otherwise. Programming capabilities are highly specialized, complex, and typically technology-specific, and were not historically part of Compustar's focus.

Dummy variable coded 1 if a project involved working on hardware from another vendor and 0 otherwise. Compustar's capabilities in working on these machines are not superior to those of several other firms in the industry.

An aggregate varying from 0 to 2, counting the number of individual capabilities that a particular project drew upon among the capabilities in which Compustar had an advantage (Compustar hardware and mainframe). Capabilities were aggregated because testing the interaction hypotheses with the individual capability terms would have resulted in twelve interaction terms.

An aggregate varying from 0 to 2, counting the number of individual capabilities that a particular project drew upon among the capabilities in which Compustar did not have an advantage (programming and other hardware). Capabilities were aggregated because testing the interaction hypotheses with the individual capability terms would have resulted in twelve interaction terms.

variable_name: hold-up, lack of observability, appropriability concerns
description: Contractual hazards are measured at the project level with five coded indicators from contract documents and manager interviews: interdependence, time specificity, disrupt (combined into a hold-up count), lack of observability, and appropriability concerns.

Return on assets was selected as the dependent variable because it is a well-understood and widely used accounting measure of operational performance in CEO succession research. Each firm's ROA was calculated as income before extraordinary items and discontinued operations divided by net assets as reported during each fiscal year. Postsuccession firm ROA was calculated as average firm ROA during the first three years following the year of CEO succession, to capture the succession effect and to smooth fluctuations in ROA specific to a given year.
time_window: first three years following the year of CEO succession

description: Coded 1 when an executive who was currently an officer of a firm was promoted to the CEO position and the departing CEO terminated his/her service as both the CEO and a director of the firm before the age of 64, and coded 0 otherwise. CEO turnovers due to sudden death, health issues, and taking a similar position at another firm were excluded from the analysis. Both CEO age and continued board membership were used to separate contenders from followers, and news reports were also examined to bolster identification of CEO dismissals.

Coded 1 when an executive who was not an employee of the focal firm was promoted to the CEO position, and coded 0 otherwise. CEO turnovers due to sudden death, health issues, and taking a similar position at another firm were excluded from the analysis.

Follower successors were the omitted category in the analysis and included all noncontender inside successors. They are inside executives promoted to CEO positions following their predecessors' ordinary retirements rather than dismissals.

Measured as the proportion of officer turnover during the first two years after CEO succession. Turnover was measured among all executives who were listed as officers in a firm's annual report to shareholders one year prior to the year of succession. A two-year period was selected to fully capture the succession effect on executive turnover and the period normally required for a new CEO to fully take charge in a new job.
time_window: first two years after CEO succession

description: Measured as the number of years an individual had served as the CEO of the firm from which he or she was departing. Departing CEO tenure squared was also included in the analysis to test for the hypothesized inverted U-shaped relationship.

All forms of taxable compensation that an employee received in a given calendar year; including salary, bonuses, and other reported income. The authors treat earnings as highly correlated with the employee's ability to generate value for the employer. Earnings appears in the mobility models in thousands of dollars.
A dummy variable coded 1 if an employee's dominant employer changed since the previous year and 0 otherwise. A dominant employer is the one at which the employee earned the most during the year.

A dummy coded 1 if an employee's dominant employer changed since the previous year and the new employer appeared in the data for the first time in that year. The authors note this measure of exit to spin-out is broader than the typical definition of a spin-out founder because it includes nonfounding employees who join a spin-out in its first year.

variable_name: Cumulative # of employees leaving to spin-outs
description: A count of the number of unique individuals who leave a firm to join a spin-out in each measurement year and the four years prior to it. The authors also count movers to spin-outs separately within employee earnings classes.
time_window: measurement year and the four prior years

variable_name: Cumulative # of employees leaving to established firms
description: A count of the number of unique individuals who leave a firm to join another established firm in each measurement year and the four years prior to it. The authors also count movers to established firms separately within employee earnings classes.
time_window: measurement year and the four prior years

description: Total firm revenues are constructed by aggregating the earnings of all employees inside a firm, which include partners, less noncompensation costs and set-asides for future years. To compare firms of different sizes, revenues are divided by the number of employees, including partners, associates, and staff, to obtain the average firm revenue generated per employee. Firm performance is measured at least one year after the measured mobility events and is therefore based on the earnings of the retained workforce and any individuals hired to replace the moving employees.
time_window: at least one year after the mobility events

description: Compound growth rate in sales for firm J in year T, computed as the log of the ratio of sales in year T to sales in year T-1. Sales growth is one of the firm-level variables taken from the annual COMPUSTAT corporate data tapes.

Operating income divided by corporate assets for firm J in year T. Operating return is profits before interest, taxes and depreciation. It is one of the two performance measures used because of the known problems with accounting returns.

Compound growth rate in stockholder returns for firm J in year T, based on market value per share and dividends per share relative to the prior year. The printed formula in Table 1 is partially unreadable in the extracted text. It is the second of the two performance measures.

Lagged operating income before depreciation minus total income taxes, minus the change in deferred taxes from the previous year, minus gross interest expense, minus the preferred dividend requirement, minus dividends declared on common stock, with the result divided by assets. The COMPUSTAT industrial item numbers identified in Table 1 are used to build the components; the formula is given in the table.

FCF is defined as QDumJ,T-1 * Cash FlowJ,T-1; it equals cash flow for firms with Tobin's Q below one and equals 0 for firms with Q above one since in theory they have profitable opportunities for investment. Tobin's Q is lagged market value divided by book value, following Lang, Stulz and Walkling (1991).

A firm is considered Owner-Managed when officers (not including directors) of the firm, or partnerships in which officers are principals, own 5% or more of the company's stock. Firms with company sponsored employee savings plans holding 5% or more of the stock are also categorized as Owner-Managed. The indicator equals one for such firms and zero otherwise.

Equals one when at least one outside blockholder (owner of 5% or more) is not a mutual fund or public pension fund, and zero otherwise. This modifies the Owner-Controlled definition of Tosi and Gomez-Mejia (1989) and O'Reilly et al. (1988) by separating non-fund outside block owners from fund owners.

Equals one when at least one outside blockholder (owner of 5% or more) is a mutual fund company, and zero otherwise. Outside owners listed as 'Security Advisers' in the Directory of Mutual Funds and Other Investment Companies are identified as mutual funds, and certain non-public funds such as university endowment funds and government pension funds are included with mutual fund companies.

Scientific diversity was measured as the number of specific scientific specialties represented in the R&D laboratory. R&D directors were asked to characterize the distribution of R&D knowledge by indicating the percentage of professionals/scientists working in each of ten general areas of scientific expertise, and were then asked to check all specific areas of scientific expertise that corresponded to each general expertise area. The number of specific specialties represented in R&D laboratories could range from 1 to 59. The number of specific scientific specialties represented in each R&D laboratory was used as the measure.

Professionalization was measured with four 7-point items (alpha = 0.91). The scale captured the propensity of R&D personnel to seek contact with professional colleagues and exposure to information external to the organization, including the extent to which the firm encouraged acquiring additional in-house educational/developmental training and requiring additional external/degree education.

Centralization was assessed as the extent to which decision-making authority was at lower levels of the R&D laboratory hierarchy, measured with nine 7-point items (alpha = 0.94). Items asked the extent to which the firm delegated decision-making authority to R&D project professionals/scientists concerning issues such as choosing R&D projects to work on, choosing employee assignments for projects, hiring R&D staff, the administrative system, and making major noncapital expenditures.

Formalization was assessed as the extent to which rules governing behavior were precisely and explicitly formulated, measured with five 7-point items (alpha = 0.82). Items concerned whether written rules and laboratory procedures existed, whether rules and procedures stated how to perform normal daily activities, whether written procedures existed for individual tasks, and whether there was strict enforcement of written rules and procedures.

Frequency of performance appraisals was assessed as the extent to which behavior was measured and evaluated, measured with three 7-point items (alpha = 0.85). Items asked how frequently managers evaluated R&D projects/outcomes and performance, the extent to which managers had the opportunity to frequently observe and informally evaluate R&D professionals, and the extent to which they provided frequent informal feedback concerning performance.

Goal specificity was assessed as the extent to which goals were explicit, clearly defined, and provided unambiguous criteria for selecting among alternatives. It was measured with three 7-point items (alpha = 0.90) concerning how specific R&D goals were with respect to overall R&D laboratory goals concerning drug indications and specific R&D project goals concerning drug indications.

A general measure captured the extent to which the quantity of outcomes was emphasized in performance appraisals and rewards, measured with six 7-point items (alpha = 0.94). Items concerned whether the quantity of new ideas submitted, new patents, publications, and new drugs produced was reflected in performance appraisals and in rewards received.

A measure examined whether professional forms of output was emphasized, based on the idea that in most university and many corporate research laboratories presentations and published papers are the primary outputs of research. It was measured with two 7-point items (alpha = 0.92) concerning the extent to which the firm encouraged R&D professionals to present papers and to publish in journals.

Rewards and recognition were assessed as the extent to which R&D professionals received public recognition for outstanding achievements, measured with three 7-point items (alpha = 0.74). Items concerned whether R&D professionals received personal mention in oral and written reports for excellent work, received financial rewards for good ideas/accomplishments, and received non-financial rewards for good ideas/accomplishments.
