Index of external CSR actions built from 120 Thomson Reuters (ASSET4) data points that the authors independently classified, using a working decision rule that classified as external those actions that are more externally oriented in terms of disclosure (e.g., reporting) and claims; the category includes claims that firms make and disclosures they issue. Questionable items and items with a majority of missing data were dropped, and items with negative coefficients in the Cronbach's alpha test were dropped, leaving an index with a Cronbach's alpha of 0.74 (inter-item covariance of 0.09). The index is normalized on a 0-1 scale and divided by total (logged) assets in the current year.

The joint effect of internal and external actions is operationalized as the sum of current external actions and one-year-lagged internal actions, CSR it = E it + I it-1. After calculating the sum of current external and prior internal actions, the authors divide it by total (logged) assets, following the derivation of the market-value equation, which yields the main independent variable Sum/assets.
time_window: external actions at t combined with internal actions at t-1

description: The undermining effect (the gap between external and internal actions) is operationalized as the absolute value of the difference between current external and one-year-lagged internal actions, CSR it = |E it - I it-1|; the authors take the absolute value of the gap to capture the misalignment in both directions. The gap is divided by total (logged) assets, giving Abs. value (gap/assets). The authors also estimate the market-value equation with the real value of the gap (Gap/assets).
time_window: external actions at t minus internal actions at t-1

description: Dummy variable that equals 1 if the licensee is a start-up and 0 otherwise. Start-ups are firms founded one year prior to or subsequent to the execution date of a license to commercialize a technology in the sample. They were identified through phone contacts and interviews of employees at licensee firms and the university Office of Technology Transfer, supplemented by secondary sources to verify the accuracy of interviews.

At the end of the observation period each license has one of three mutually exclusive outcomes; the license is commercialized when the firm has paid royalties to the university based on achieving product sales. Duration spells commence at the patent application or approval-to-file date, and the maximum survival time is 7,585 days. In the estimation of the hazard of commercialization, inventions that were terminated are coded as censored at 7,585 days so that they remain in the risk set.

One of the three mutually exclusive outcomes: the license contract was subsequently cancelled or ended prior to sales, signalling that the licensee discontinued development and commercialization of the technology. Termination occurs either when the university terminates the license for failure to comply with contractual provisions or, more commonly, when the licensee decides not to pursue the technology further. In the hazard of termination models, observations for which only minimum royalties were reported are censored on December 31, 2002.

variable_name: total royalties and fees paid to the university (natural log of payments to the university)
description: Tobit analysis of total royalties and fees paid to the university related to a commercialized invention; only commercialized technologies are included, excluding terminated and censored observations. Contracts typically specify payment of the minimum of either a fixed dollar amount (minimum royalty) or a percentage of total sales (earned royalty). Because the royalty distribution is truncated on the left at zero and skewed by a few inventions generating extreme positive values, the natural log of payments to the university is used as the dependent variable. Inventions generating a minimum royalty followed by an earned royalty are coded as commercialized on the earliest date of minimum royalty.
time_window: royalties reported gross of delayed or installment payments through July 2002

description: Multi-item scale measuring the manufacturer's efforts to verify contractor performance through supervision of production schedules and inspection of incoming orders. The scale jointly measures monitoring of contractor output and of production activity, and the response formats appear in Appendix S2.
Multi-item scale measuring the willingness of the parties to strive for joint benefits in the manufacturer-contractor relationship. The response formats appear in Appendix S2.

Dummy-coded as 1 if any (nonzero) percentage of the requirements was produced internally, and otherwise coded as 0 (no internal production). The authors also examined the robustness of the results to less stringent percentage cutoffs. Its scale format was purposely kept different from the opportunism measure.

Measure of the manufacturer's perception of whether the contractor engages in 'self-interest seeking with guile' vis-a-vis the focal manufacturer. Its scale format was purposely kept different from that of the sourcing dummy to limit common method artifacts. The response formats appear in Appendix S2.

Measure of the contractor's supply chain performance toward the focal manufacturer. The authors list delivery cycle time, proportion of shipments delivered on-time, quality of deliveries, and responsiveness to requests for change as the aspects covered. The response formats appear in Appendix S2.

The retailer's monitoring in the manufacturer relationship, collected from the retailers in a new survey. The measure was identical to the one used for the upstream relationship, with minor adaptations to suit the downstream context.

The retailer's solidarity norms in the manufacturer relationship, collected from the retailers in a new survey. The measure was identical to the one used for the upstream relationship, with minor adaptations to suit the downstream context.

The retailer's sourcing context (concurrent vs. singular), collected from the retailers in a new survey. The measure was identical to the one used for the upstream relationship, with minor adaptations to suit the downstream context.
The manufacturer's performance toward the retailer, collected as part of the manufacturer survey and used as the dependent variable in the replication study.

Calculated as the number of days between the NDA submission date and the approval date, and then taking the natural logarithm. The authors note that the median time the FDA took to approve NDAs in the sampled period was just over 1 year (366 days), with the fastest approval at about 3 months and the slowest at a little over 8 years.

Measured as the number of pharmacological classes to which the drug was assigned by the FDA during the revision process, since the number of assigned classes determines the range of diseases the drug is allowed to treat. Because the majority of drugs were assigned to either one or two pharmacological classes, the authors use a binary variable that takes the value of 1 if the drug was assigned to multiple classes and 0 if it was assigned to one single class.

Constructed by adding all lobbying expenditures on the issue 'medical research' to the FDA across the quarter the NDA was filed and the following two quarters (9 months), and then taking the natural logarithm to account for the skewed distribution. Only lobbying that targets the FDA and whose reported issue is 'medical research' is counted, since the FDA is responsible for many issues other than NDA reviews.
time_window: the quarter the NDA was filed and the following two quarters (9 months)

description: Measured as the natural logarithm of the total number of patents behind a given drug plus one. The patents behind each drug are identified from the FDA's Orange Book and are incorporated into each NDA submission.

Participants were classified by their current role in the circus arts: 177 creators, 120 managers, and 42 hybrids who occupied roles with both creator and manager duties, plus 150 laypeople recruited as a comparison group. Circus professionals had to have at least one year in their current role as a creator, manager, or hybrid. In the analyses, role was entered as dummy variables comparing managers, hybrids, and laypeople with creators.

Participants were randomly assigned to one of five conditions: creator, manager, creator-manager, manager-creator, and lay/control. In the creator condition participants spent ten minutes generating three different novel product ideas; in the manager condition they spent ten minutes describing three criteria for evaluating how successful novel product ideas will be; in the hybrid conditions they spent five minutes on each manipulation, in the order indicated by the condition name; in the lay/control condition participants did not perform either task.

After watching each video, participants made forecasts on a 0-100 percent scale using three items about liking, sharing, and going to see the performer(s). Estimation accuracy was scored by subtracting the actual percentage of audience members who shared each video from participants' predicted percentage. For placement accuracy, participants' predicted rankings were calculated by averaging their ratings on the three forecasting items for each video (alpha = .88), and the actual audience rankings were calculated by averaging the standardized liking, sharing, and financial scores across videos (alpha = .79); the predicted rank was subtracted from the actual rank for each video, where negative values represent false negatives and positive values represent false positives. Overall accuracy scores were calculated by subtracting the absolute value of each inaccuracy score from ten, so higher mean scores indicated greater accuracy.
scale: per-video accuracy scores from one to ten; participant means from five to ten

variable_name: Ranking of the four product ideas
description: Participants ranked a set of four product ideas according to how successful they predicted each one to be in the consumer marketplace (1 = most successful, 4 = least successful), with the order of ideas randomized. The four ideas were selected from a pretest such that there was a correct ranking according to the audience. Accuracy was examined by whether participants ranked the best idea first, thus ahead of the second-best idea and avoiding a false negative regarding the best idea.
scale: rank of one to four per idea

description: Three audience members who did not participate in the audience survey independently rated the 161 videos using the consensual assessment technique. Using a Likert-type scale (1 = 'Strongly Disagree' to 7 = 'Strongly Agree'), they rated each video on the item 'This video was novel.' The order of the videos was randomized for each rater, and raters watched 15 videos before starting to rate to establish a means of comparison. Ratings met standard cutoffs for interrater reliability (ICC2 = .78) and agreement (average deviation = 0.64).

Novelty of the 16 product ideas was measured in the pretest using three items adapted from the Creative Product Semantic Scale: 'This product is [novel, unique, original]' (alpha = .86). All items were rated on a Likert-type scale (1 = 'Strongly Disagree' to 7 = 'Strongly Agree').

The number of views each video had prior to the study was recorded; 157 of the 161 videos had publicly available view counts, and views ranged from one to 397,877 views (mean = 12,313, S.D. = 54,619).

Quality was measured as the percentage of respondents in the audience sample who shared each video. Because the videos were embedded in the survey and audience members did not know the number of times the video they watched had been viewed or shared by others, each video was given an approximately equal opportunity to be shared without external influences, isolating the intrinsic quality of the videos themselves.
scale: percentage of audience members who shared the video

description: For each creator who submitted a video and completed the forecasting survey, two sets of inaccuracy and overall accuracy scores were calculated: one without the creator's own video and one with his or her own video. The own-video scores were used to test whether creators place their own videos too high relative to others' videos.

Audience members watched and rated one randomly selected video. Liking was measured with three items adapted from Oliver and Bartsch's (2010) measure of audience appreciation ('I [liked, appreciated, enjoyed] this video'; alpha = .98) on a scale from 1 = 'Strongly Disagree' to 7 = 'Strongly Agree'. Sharing captured whether audience members actually shared the video via Facebook, Twitter, Google+, or e-mail. Financial success captured how much of a ten-cent bonus audience members gave to support the performer(s). The standardized scores for the three dimensions were averaged into a composite measure of success for each of the 161 videos (alpha = .79).

In the pretest, audience members' purchase intent was measured with three items: 'I want to own this product,' 'I am likely to buy this product,' and 'I would purchase this product if it was sold at a fair price' (alpha = .96), rated on a Likert-type scale (1 = 'Strongly Disagree' to 7 = 'Strongly Agree'). These ratings were used to determine the correct ranking of the four ideas used in the experiment.

Number of successful patent applications, or granted patents, for the acquiring firm i in year t. The granted patent carries the date of the original application, and this date is used to assign the patent to the year in which it was originally applied for. The patent count for the dependent variable is based on the patents of the acquiring firm obtained 1-4 years after the acquisition and is therefore different from the patents on which the independent variables are based.
time_window: patents obtained 1-4 years after the acquisition

description: Acquisitions were coded as technological if either the acquiring firm reported technology as a motivating factor or as part of the transferred assets, or the acquired firm had any patenting activity in the 5 years preceding the acquisition. Acquisitions that did not meet either criterion were coded as nontechnological acquisitions, and the variable is the number of such acquisitions in a year. Four lagged versions of this variable were used.

variable_name: Absolute size of acquired knowledge base
description: For each acquiring firm for each year, a list was prepared of the patents its acquisitions had obtained in the preceding 5 years. These patents were then combined with the patents cited by them, and all duplicates were removed so that a patent number appeared only once on the list. The acquired knowledge base was computed as the number of patents (i.e., knowledge elements) on this list. Four lagged versions of this variable were used.

variable_name: Relative size of acquired knowledge base
description: Obtained by dividing the absolute size of the acquired knowledge base by the size of the acquiring firm's knowledge base, which was computed using the same procedure as the size of the acquired firm's knowledge base. In the few cases where the acquired knowledge base was larger than the acquiring knowledge base, the larger number was used as the denominator, because a number greater than 1 is not meaningful. Four lagged versions of this variable were used.

The list of patent numbers that appeared in both the acquired firm's knowledge base and the acquiring firm's knowledge base was prepared, and the number of elements on this list was divided by the absolute size of the acquired knowledge base. The squared term of this variable, Relatedness of acquired knowledge base 2, is used to test the curvilinear effect. Four lagged versions of the variable were used.

A commingled patent is defined as one created by inventors coming together from the target and acquiring firms, and it can be assigned to the acquired or acquiring entity. Firm commingling intensity is calculated as the share of the acquired entity's cumulative patent stock invented by commingled teams as of a given firm-year. In the regressions a one-year lag of the measure is used. Commingling is present in 8.9% of the acquisition transactions analyzed.
time_window: cumulative as of a given firm-year; one-year lag in regressions

description: Following the methodology proposed by Arora et al. (2014), the variable is the three-year moving average representing the portion of newly created patents with acquired inventors' contributions but assigned to the acquiring entity out of the total number of patents contributed by the acquired entity inventors during the period. The variable is set to zero prior to the acquisition date. The authors note it is an imperfect yet scalable proxy for the delegation of authority or autonomy in R&D management and that it results in a one-period average lag to the outcome variables.

The cumulative number of patents assigned to a given target or invented by the target's employees and assigned to its acquirer after the acquisition, with priority dates before a certain year. The authors describe this as the measure of innovation quantity commonly used in the literature.

To measure innovation quality, the authors follow the convention in the innovation literature by weighting the patent grants by the number of forward patent citations over the following three years postpatent grant and calculating the stock.

Patents are labelled as invented in a commingled team with long-tenured acquirer inventors when there is at least one commingling acquirer inventor with documented patenting experience with the acquirer, and this is at least two years prior to the focal patent filing year. The variable is constructed as the share of commingled patents invented with long-tenured acquirer inventors in the target firm's patent stock. It sums with commingling with short-tenured acquirer inventors to firm commingling intensity.
time_window: two-year acquirer experience threshold; cumulative share

description: Defined as the share of commingled patents with only short-tenured acquirer inventors in the target firm's patent stock. Short-tenured acquirer inventors are those who lack documented patenting experience with the acquirer of at least two years prior to the focal patent filing year. Firm commingling intensity equals the sum of commingling with short- and long-tenured acquirer inventors.
time_window: two-year acquirer experience threshold; cumulative share

description: An SIC-based entropy index, a continuous measure computed as Sigma 1 Pi ln(1/Pi), where Pi is the sales attributed to segment i and ln(1/Pi) is the weight for each segment. Separate indices DR and DU are computed for related and unrelated diversification. Product segments were classified as related if they contained the same first three digits of the SSIC codes, indicating they belonged to the same industry subcategory; DR has a minimum value of zero and higher values indicate greater relatedness. Segment sales were gathered manually from annual reports for each company in each fiscal year.
scale: continuous entropy index, minimum value of zero

description: An SIC-based entropy index, a continuous measure computed as Sigma 1 Pi ln(1/Pi), where Pi is the sales attributed to segment i and ln(1/Pi) is the weight for each segment. Product segments were classified as unrelated if they did not contain the same first three digits of the SSIC codes; DU has a minimum value of zero and higher values indicate greater unrelatedness. Product segments were mapped into SSIC codes for each study year using information from three sources, and segment sales were gathered manually from annual reports.
scale: continuous entropy index, minimum value of zero

description: Firm leverage, or the level of debt financing, measured as the ratio of long-term debt to total capital. The debt financing variable was transformed into its natural logarithm to remove skewness, yielding an approximately normally distributed variable. All non-segment firm-level data were gathered from the Research Insight database and volumes of Financial Highlights of Companies on the Singapore Exchange.

Time-series data on the weekly levels of the Singapore Stock Exchange Straits Times Index (STI) were collected and averaged for each calendar year because the firm-level variables were collected yearly. Environment values were obtained using time-series analysis, and the mean squared error (MSE) from the AR(1) model for the environment variable was used in the PROC MIXED analyses. Separate models were estimated for a stable environment (1995-1997) and a dynamic environment (1998-2000).

Each year the League of Conservation Voters creates an index by counting the number of times each representative or senator in Congress votes favorably on an environmental agenda; the index ranges from zero to 100, with 100 representing a record of voting for the environmental agenda in all cases. The variable used is the average of the environmental scores of the U.S. representatives and U.S. senators of the states where each utility operated, weighted by the percentage of generation of each firm in each state for multistate utilities.
time_window: one-year lagged (1994-1998 data in the first stage)

description: The state's long-term commitment to the environment is measured through its investment in people as a ratio of the state's environmental agency employment to the total number of the state's employees. This method approximates the state's commitment to environmental protection and its institutional capacity to support its commitment.
time_window: one-year lagged (1994-1998 data in the first stage)

description: The annual amount of regulatory expenses paid by the firm, used as a proxy of regulatory agency pressure. The data report particulars of regulatory commission expenses incurred relating to prepared cases that were submitted to a regulatory body, or cases to which such a body was party, including fees paid to the FERC or the costs of dockets.
time_window: one-year lagged (1994-1998 data in the first stage)

description: An indicator in which a utility that is a member of the trade association takes the value one and zero otherwise. Membership is measured through the Edison Electric Institute, created in 1933 as the association of U.S. shareholder-owned electric companies.

A proxy for visibility noting whether a firm was among the top four sellers in a state in any of the residential, commercial, or industrial markets. For each year and state, the four big players in their states were identified using the retail sales reported on Form EIA861, assigning the value one when the firm was a big player and zero otherwise.

A measure of a firm's environmental efforts related to air pollution, reflecting investments undertaken for the reduction, prevention, or abatement of any adverse impact of an activity on the environment reported under the category of 'air pollution control facility'. The categories included are scrubbers, precipitators and tall smokestacks; changes necessary to accommodate use of environmentally clean fuels such as low ash or low sulfur fuels, including storage and handling equipment; monitoring equipment; and other.
time_window: prior to and during participation (1994-1998 in the first stage)

description: A categorical variable representing the type of participant within the Climate Challenge program. Early participants were those that enrolled during the official ceremony organized in March 1995 by the DOE, and late participants were those that enrolled at a later date (end of 1995 to end of 1998). Nonparticipants are coded one, late joiners two, and early joiners three; the variable is used as the dependent variable in the multinomial logit first-stage model.

A binary variable representing the decision of a firm to participate in the Climate Challenge program; it takes a value equal to one for the year of enrollment and the following years and zero otherwise. Participants and the year of their enrollment, as well as nonparticipants, were identified from the Climate Challenge participation agreements accessed through the DOE's Web site.

variable_name: CO2 emission per unit of electricity produced
description: The amount of CO2 emissions reported for each utility under the EPA Clean Air Market Program divided by the amount of net generation in megawatt hours reported on Form EIA906. It is used as the second-stage dependent variable assessing the outcome of the Climate Challenge program from 1996 through 2000; the variable is normally distributed, so pooled regression and random-effect GLS panel regression are used. Lower emissions per unit indicate substantive cooperation.

Media attention serves as the measure of frame salience and equals the sum over a state-year of article count times coherence times valence for articles coded to the agrarian frame. Articles were systematically collected from local newspapers in the Access World News database and coded by state and stakeholder group. Coherence is the frequency of frame-specific dictionary words per 1,000 words in an article, averaged across articles by state and year; valence comes from a full-text LIWC analysis using its positive and negative emotion dictionaries. All predictor variables in the models are lagged by one year.

Media attention serves as the measure of frame salience and equals the sum over a state-year of article count times coherence times valence for articles coded to the industry frame. Articles were systematically collected from local newspapers in the Access World News database and coded by state and stakeholder group. Coherence is the frequency of frame-specific dictionary words per 1,000 words in an article, averaged across articles by state and year; valence comes from a full-text LIWC analysis using its positive and negative emotion dictionaries. All predictor variables in the models are lagged by one year.

Media attention serves as the measure of frame salience and equals the sum over a state-year of article count times coherence times valence for articles coded to the environmental frame. Articles were systematically collected from local newspapers in the Access World News database and coded by state and stakeholder group. Coherence is the frequency of frame-specific dictionary words per 1,000 words in an article, averaged across articles by state and year; valence comes from a full-text LIWC analysis using its positive and negative emotion dictionaries. All predictor variables in the models are lagged by one year.

Annual count of organizations that entered the market in a state and used technologies that produced biodiesel only from oilseed feedstocks, as promoted by farm associations. Foundings were identified from quarterly reports generated by the National Biodiesel Board, the U.S. Department of Energy, and the archival reports of individual biodiesel producers. Cases in which founders were also members of a farm association were removed.

Annual count of firms that entered the market in a state and used technologies that produced biodiesel from a combination of oilseed, animal tallow, and WVO feedstocks. Foundings were identified from quarterly reports generated by the National Biodiesel Board, the U.S. Department of Energy, and the archival reports of individual biodiesel producers. Cases in which founders were also members of a farm association were removed.

Annual count of organizations that entered the market in a state and used technologies that produced biodiesel only from waste vegetable oil feedstocks, the only feedstock deemed acceptable by environmental organizations. Foundings were identified from quarterly reports generated by the National Biodiesel Board, the U.S. Department of Energy, and the archival reports of individual biodiesel producers. Cases in which founders were also members of a farm association were removed.

Size was measured by taking the common logarithm of the number of full-time students enrolled; this logarithmic transformation was employed because of the skewed size distribution of the responding schools. For the QAP analysis the variable was turned into a matrix of similarities between each institution and every other institution, computed as difference scores.

Type was coded in terms of the highest degree offered, with bachelors' degree equal to 1, masters' degree 2, and Ph.D. and beyond 3. Similarity between institutions was calculated as absolute difference scores for this categorical variable and entered as a matrix in the QAP multiple regression.

Ownership was coded as either public (1) or private (2). Similarity between institutions was calculated as absolute difference scores for this categorical variable and entered as a matrix in the QAP multiple regression.

Region was coded as Northeast (1), Midwest (2), South (3), and West (4). This coding scheme and the states representing these regions were based on the U.S. Department of Education's Digest of Educational Statistics. Similarity between institutions was calculated as absolute difference scores and entered as a matrix in the QAP multiple regression.

Church affiliation was coded as either yes (1) or no (0). Similarity between institutions was calculated as absolute difference scores for this categorical variable and entered as a matrix in the QAP multiple regression.

A 10-item scale (Cronbach's alpha = 0.90; IRA = 0.91) assessing how top managers thought members of peer institutions would rate their institution along various dimensions. Items used Likert-type scales from 1 (very low) to 7 (very high), and scores were aggregated to the university level by averaging the responses for universities with multiple informants. For the QAP regression a similarity matrix between institutions was computed from difference scores on this variable.

Desired future image was assessed using the same dimensions as the present image scale; top management members were asked about the extent to which they wished to emulate the universities they had identified earlier on each of the ten dimensions (Cronbach's alpha = 0.97; IRA = 0.90). Items used Likert-type scales from 1 (very low) to 7 (very high) and scores were aggregated to the university level by averaging across informants. For the QAP regression a between-institution similarity matrix was computed from difference scores.

The type of organizational identity as perceived by respondents was assessed with a 7-item scale (Cronbach's alpha = 0.69; IRA = 0.86) measuring whether the institution saw itself as more "utilitarian" (oriented toward economic factors) or more "normative" (oriented toward values and ideology). The scale was reverse-coded so that low scores indicated a more utilitarian identity while high scores reflected a more purely normative identity; an example item is whether there is a feeling that the institution should be actively engaged in marketing campaigns to attract students. For the QAP regression a between-institution similarity matrix was computed from difference scores.

Identity strength was assessed with a six-item scale adapted from Milliken (1990) that had been used in a higher-education research setting (Cronbach's alpha = 0.84; IRA = 0.84); higher scores indicated a stronger identity. An example item is the extent to which the institution has administrators, faculty, and students who identify strongly with the institution. For the QAP regression a between-institution similarity matrix was computed from difference scores.

Reputation was collected from the 1990 Gourman Report rather than from the questionnaire. For the QAP regression a between-institution similarity matrix was computed from difference scores on this variable.

Respondents were asked in an open-ended format to identify up to 3 higher-education institutions that they would like to emulate. For universities with multiple informants, emulation choices were aggregated at the university level by adding them together. The dependent-variable matrix is an asymmetric institution-by-institution matrix where 1 = want to emulate and 0 = do not want to emulate.
scale: 0 = do not want to emulate, 1 = want to emulate

description: A five-item scale based on Dess and Beard's (1984) conceptualization of an organization's task environment (Cronbach's alpha = 0.72; IRA = 0.82); higher scores indicated greater perceived environmental threat. An example item is the extent to which the environment can be described as turbulent or unstable. Scores were aggregated to the university level by averaging across informants, and the vectors were repeated to form a square matrix for the QAP correlation.

A four-item scale based on the quantitative study reported in Gioia and Thomas (1996) (Cronbach's alpha = 0.74; IRA = 0.81) asking top managers to report the extent to which their universities had changed along four dimensions over the past five years. Scores were aggregated to the university level by averaging across informants, and the vectors were repeated to form a square matrix for the QAP correlation.

variable_name: Difference in reputation between the emulated and emulating universities
description: A square matrix representing the difference in reputation between the emulating university and the emulated university, built for the QAP correlation. Positive values indicate that the emulated university has a higher reputation than the emulating university (upward comparison), negative values a lower reputation (downward comparison).

variable_name: Number of attributes on which emulated universities were similar
description: Derived from two separate QAP multiple regressions run on the low-threat and high-threat halves of a median split on perceived environmental threat, with all structural and identity-based similarity matrices as independent variables. The comparison is the number of the ten dimensions on which the emulated universities were similar in each half of the sample (six for low-threat universities and eight for higher-threat universities).

Cumulative abnormal return of each sample firm for each event, accumulated in an event window of length w. Abnormal returns are the differences between the realized daily return on a day in the window and the firm's constant expected return, which is the mean return of the stock computed in an estimation window of 100 days before the events (constant mean return model). Reported for the [-1,+1], [0,1], [0,3], [0,5] and [0,7] event windows.
time_window: 100-day estimation window before each event; event windows of [-1,+1] to [0,7]

description: The number of politicians supported through campaign donations in the 2010 election, using data from the Brazilian Superior Electoral Court. A campaign donation establishes a tacit contract between donors and recipients that facilitates access during the political actor's mandate (four years in this case).

The total number of NGOs supported via financial or in-kind gifts, as reported at the time of the events; the measure includes joint activities insofar as those activities require financial contributions or company time, goods, or services. Firms' 2013 annual reports (and those of their corporate foundations where applicable) were hand coded: NGOs mentioned in the same sentence as one of 26 material-contribution verbs (and 96 synonyms) were counted, and the resulting list of NGOs was cross-checked with the IPEA database.

The number of political connections held by board members in 2013. From the 5,489 resumes of all board members of sample firms collected using CVM data, political connections were counted where a member held or had held an elected or appointed office in local, state, or national government or occupied a managerial position in a state-owned company; the measure includes current and prior political experience.

The share of NGO connections among corporate board members in 2013, hand collected from publicly available information about board members' external board seats; each resume was manually reviewed to identify NGOs listed in the IPEA database. The measure incorporates current and past positions because board members rarely specify the time span of their involvement.
scale: share of NGO connections among board members

description: Measured by counting the other developers releasing games with the publisher in the same year as the focal developer. At the project level it is used for the game; at the year level, because some developers are involved in multiple projects in a year, the measures are averaged across the games with which the developer was involved in the focal year.
time_window: same year as the focal developer/game

description: The average review score that all games of developers working with the publisher received in the focal year, divided by the review score of the focal developer's game, so the variable is always positive; the higher the score, the more superior the other developers in the publisher's portfolio. The variable is set to zero if a developer is the only one working with a publisher, and it builds on game review scores by third-party sites as aggregated by MobyGames.

A game's revenues measured in millions of USD, based on revenues from the NPD data matched to the games in MobyGames. The authors focus on the revenues in the first 12 months after release to compare games released at different times.
The sum of the revenues of all games a developer released in the focal year, based on the NPD revenue data.

The revenue of the games with which the employee is affiliated, computed by adding the revenues of all games in which an employee participated in year t + 1. As some employees are involved in multiple projects in a year, the measures are averaged across all games with which the employee was involved in the focal year.

Multi-item, seven-point Likert-type scale drawn from established scales in the empirical literature, translated into German and reviewed by three bilingual researchers. Captures the buyer's transaction-specific investments in the relationship. Each procurement manager reported on the most important buyer–supplier relationship in its current state.
time_window: current state at the time of the survey

description: Multi-item, seven-point Likert-type scale drawn from established scales in the empirical literature, translated into German. Captures difficulties in foreseeing the technological developments and requirements in the relationship. Reported by the procurement manager for the most important buyer–supplier relationship.
time_window: current state at the time of the survey

description: Multi-item measure; the text discusses items such as whether the supplier provides a quality certificate and the ease of comparing components across suppliers. The authors treat it as a formative measure: the items jointly determine the construct, are not interchangeable (removing one alters the domain of the construct), and would not necessarily covary positively. Responses use the established seven-point Likert-type scale applied to all constructs.
time_window: current state at the time of the survey

description: Multi-item, seven-point Likert-type scale drawn from established scales in the empirical literature, translated into German. Captures how detailed the contract between the parties is and how wide a range of potential contingencies it addresses. Reported by the procurement manager for the most important buyer–supplier relationship.
time_window: current state at the time of the survey

description: Multi-item, seven-point Likert-type scale drawn from established scales in the empirical literature, translated into German. Captures depersonalized means of controlling and coordinating partner behavior and output, examples of which include budget plans, cost breakdown methods, and audit programs based on the evaluation of files, records, and reports. Reported by the procurement manager for the most important buyer–supplier relationship.
time_window: current state at the time of the survey

description: Multi-item, seven-point Likert-type scale drawn from established scales in the empirical literature, translated into German. Captures trust building and social identification through interaction of individuals from the partner organizations, examples of which are regular meetings and steering committees. Reported by the procurement manager for the most important buyer–supplier relationship.
time_window: current state at the time of the survey

description: Degree of opportunism experienced in the relationship, measured with an established multi-item, seven-point Likert-type scale. The dependent-variable questions were placed in part 5 of the questionnaire, separated from the governance and hazard questions (parts 2–4) to reduce common method bias. Reported by the procurement manager for the most important buyer–supplier relationship.
time_window: current state at the time of the survey

description: Indicator variable set to 1 for firms affiliated to a business group and 0 otherwise. The PROWESS database uniquely identifies a firm to an ownership group, which enables the authors to code this variable; firms in PROWESS are assigned to business groups based on a combination of individual company announcements about their group membership as well as assessments by informed insiders.
scale: 1 = affiliated to a business group; 0 = unaffiliated

variable_name: aspiration weights (attention to industry peers, business group peers, and own historical performance)
description: The focus of attention is captured through the weights in the aspiration level specification, which were estimated by a grid search over all parameter values in increments of 0.1, taking the combination giving the best model fit using a Wald test. For market search intensity, BG-affiliated firms are externally focused because historical performance has a weight of only 0.5, with industry median performance (0.3) and business group median performance (0.2) contributing half of the aspiration level in total, while unaffiliated firms are internally focused because historical performance has a weight of 1.0. In the R&D domain both organizational forms had an internal focus, differing only in the speed of adjusting to performance. Because the grid search models are nonnested, H1 is tested with a counterfactual variable that uses the optimal aspiration parameters of the other organizational form.

Performance is measured by ROA, the ratio of operating profits to capital used, chosen to minimize accounting distortions and because it is not affected by financial leverage. The aspiration level (A) is a mixture of external and internal (historical) influences: for business group affiliates the median performance of all other firms in the same industry and the median of all other firms in the business group, plus a historical aspiration that is an exponentially weighted average of previous performance levels of the same firm. For unaffiliated firms there is no group aspiration level, so only the industry and historical aspiration levels are used. The variable is entered lagged.

For each firm, advertising, marketing, and distribution expenses incurred during an accounting period were added and expressed as a percentage of sales revenues. Advertising expenses include costs incurred for advertising and sales promotion; marketing expenses include rebates, discounts, commissions paid to selling agents and all other marketing-related costs; distribution expenses reflect expenses incurred by firms on distribution of goods and services. The authors adopt a formative indicator approach; the three variables are moderately correlated in the data, with correlations of 0.41, 0.26, and 0.43. Firm-years where MKT is 0 are not included because the focal firm did not engage in market search.

Measured for each year as the ratio of total R&D expenses to revenues of the focal firm. The variable is coded in the same way as market search intensity, and observations with a value of zero are excluded from the search intensity model because those firms did not engage in R&D search.
scale: ratio of R&D expenses to revenues

description: The logarithm of millions of rupees of sales revenues for the business group during the year, where a group's revenues during a year is the total of the revenues of its constituent affiliate firms. For the contingency test, a business group was identified as large if it was among the top 50 business groups by revenue (approximately 90th percentile) in India either at the start of the study period (average of revenues in 1988 and 1989) or at the end (average of revenues in 2002 and 2003); this yielded 85 business groups coded as large out of a total of 537. Firms affiliated with a large business group were coded with a large BG-affiliated firm dummy and firms affiliated to the remaining business groups with a small BG-affiliated firm dummy. Lagged values of the time-varying independent variables were used.

The number of business groups managed was recorded for each conglomerate in each year of the study. This figure was averaged for all conglomerates in the sample each year and a standard error about the annual mean was calculated. Business groups are the level of aggregation used in the study, and a group can span more than one SIC line of business as defined by management.
level: firm-year, averaged to the annual sample mean

description: Each acquisition or divestiture event was categorized by type of business relatedness using management's description of the event: horizontal, vertical, complementary (product), supplementary (market) or unrelated. All related acquisitions (horizontal, vertical, complementary and supplementary) were summed for each year, as were all related divestitures; the restructuring index in a given year is the sum of all related acquisitions and all unrelated divestitures, less the sum of all unrelated acquisitions and all related divestitures. A positive index represents a net movement toward increased business-relatedness, a negative index a net movement away from it.
Dummy variable which takes the value 1 if entry is greenfield, 0 if entry is by acquisition. It refers to the conditions at the time of entry and is not time-varying.
Proportion of college graduates in the firm's work force. The variable is time-varying and measured annually.

Two dummy variables indicating the foreign ownership stake. Fully-Owned Subsidiaries equals 1 if foreign capital has a 100% stake, 0 otherwise. Majority Joint-Ventures equals 1 if the foreign capital's stake is greater than or equal to 50% but less than 100%, 0 otherwise. Minority holdings (foreign equity above 10% but below 50%) are the omitted category. The variables are time-varying and measured annually.
Dummy variable which takes the value 1 if the firm is a limited liability company, 0 otherwise. The variable is time-varying and measured annually.

The dependent variable in the closure equation is the hazard rate of firm closure. Closure is identified as the moment when the firm ceased to report to the survey. In the competing risks model, observations that end in divestiture are treated as censored in the closure equation.
time_window: entry until exit or end of survey

description: The dependent variable in the divestiture equation is the hazard rate of foreign capital divestiture. Divestiture is identified as the first year when the firm reported foreign participation below 10%. In the competing risks model, observations that end in closure are treated as censored in the divestiture equation.
time_window: entry until exit or end of survey

description: Dichotomous measure of whether an individual hotel establishment is closely held. Company-owned chain units are defined to be non-closely held, as the owners of these chains are not involved in day-to-day establishment-level management. Independent and franchised establishments are defined as closely held when the owner and the establishment are located in the same zip code, which allows owners to closely monitor and supervise their property. Overall, 1,799 (55%) of the hotels in operation at the midpoint of the data set were classified as closely held and 1,490 (45%) as non-closely held.

Average occupancy rate (the percentage of occupied rooms) across all hotels in a particular zip code, used as the measure of the economic attractiveness of the market. In the entry models the market-level measures were lagged four periods (one year) because entry decisions are made well in advance of the observed opening; in the exit and pricing models they were lagged one period.
time_window: lagged four quarters in the entry models; lagged one quarter in the exit and pricing models

description: Derived from a focal hotel's first appearance in the database and modeled as the choice of a particular market among a set of alternatives in a conditional logit. The definition of entry is restricted to the first appearance of an establishment and does not include cases such as the purchase of an existing establishment by a new owner nor a new branding of an existing establishment. Our sample includes a total of 1,081 entries.

Binary dependent variable coded 1 if the hotel exited during a particular quarter and 0 otherwise; only shutdowns are considered exits and not cases of sales to other owners or rebranding of hotels. To accommodate time variation in the covariates the data were divided into quarterly spells, resulting in 105,037 establishment-quarter observations in the total sample.

The dependent variable in the pricing analyses was the logged average daily price of an individual hotel room. Hotel-level fixed effects regression was used to control for potential unobserved sources of heterogeneity that might affect prices, and the sample includes 108,153 establishment-quarter observations.

The establishment's occupancy level in the prior quarter, used to capture responsiveness to recent performance; occupancy is a measure that is frequently used in the industry as a performance indicator. Occupancy is also used as the measure of market attractiveness when the average occupancy level in the zip code is used instead of the firm-level measure.

variable_name: asset durability of new capital expenditures
description: Estimated by partitioning a firm's depreciation expense into the portions attributable to assets carried forward and newly acquired. Depreciable assets carried forward equal gross PPE at the end of year t minus CAPX in year t; the carry-forward depreciation equals that figure times the firm's previous depreciation rate; depreciation on new CAPX equals total depreciation expense minus carry-forward depreciation. The average expected life assigned to CAPX acquired in year t is then CAPX divided by the depreciation expense attributable to the new assets. Values are restricted to the feasible range for the depreciable life of CAPX under straight-line depreciation, which is one to 40 years.
scale: years, restricted to one to 40 years

description: The average expected life in aggregate of all assets on the firm's books at the end of year t - 1, computed each year for each firm. The industry average expected life, computed from two-digit SIC code industries excluding the firm of interest, is subtracted from each firm's value in a given year. A firm with short-lived assets depreciates them rapidly, giving a relatively high amount of depreciation relative to PPE and a low value for historic temporal orientation.

Performance is measured as cash flow return on assets (CFROA), which equals 100 times a firm's earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization divided by the average of the firm's gross PPE at the beginning and end of its fiscal year. The social comparison is the mean CFROA in a firm's industry in the prior year and the historical aspiration is the firm's CFROA in the preceding year; the overall aspiration level is a weighted average of the two. The weight was estimated by inserting values and estimating the full model, and the best fit model had a weight of 0.5.

The proportion of total direct compensation (including salary, bonus, and stock compensation) for the five highest-paid members of the top management team that comprises restricted stock and the value of stock options granted, based on the Black-Scholes formula, in year t - 1. Using the proportion rather than the absolute dollar amount provides insight into within-firm signaling of the priorities implied by incentive compensation.
The value of the top management team's stock options exercisable in year t - 1 divided by total compensation in t - 1.

Each participant read two scenarios in which two firms come together to develop a new fuel cell car. In the same-function scenario both partners were car manufacturers who shared some of their R&D expertise; in the cross-function scenario one partner was an engineering firm with expertise in fuel cell technology and the other a car manufacturer with core capabilities in production and marketing. The terms same- and cross-function were never used, and the order of the two scenarios was rotated between participants.

Anchored on the statement that if both partners contributed 100% effort the likely performance would be 100%, participants rated the likely performance of an alliance for 24 other combinations of inputs in which at least one partner's input was less than 100% effort. Each participant rated the same set of input configurations for both alliance scenarios, so that the 25 scenarios per alliance type are compared within person.

Computed within each participant as the variance of the predicted performances across the 25 input configurations, separately for the cross-function and the same-function scenario. The average within-person variance of the cross-function alliances is 454, whereas the corresponding variance of the same-function alliances is 313; the two averages were tested for equality.
The same two alliance scenarios and procedure as in Survey 1, but with the clarification that firms have no opportunity to learn from alliance partners.

Same stimuli and procedure as Survey 1, with an added input combination in which one partner contributed nothing and the other contributed 100%. Ratings of likely performance were made on the same 100%-anchored scale for the same set of input configurations for both alliance types.

Type is a binary variable with zero indicating cross-function alliance and one indicating a same-function alliance, used to separate the two alliance types in the regression of the respondent's effort on the partner's effort level.

variable_name: percentage of effort contributed by the respondent (x1lk)
description: For each of the 15 exogenously given effort levels of the partnering firm, respondents indicated how much effort they would commit to a cross-function alliance and to a same-function alliance. The variable is the percentage of effort contributed by respondent k for the exogenously given effort level l of its partnering firm.

variable_name: effort level of the partnering firm (x2l)
description: Fifteen exogenously given levels of input by the partnering firm, held fixed for the respondent, for which the respondent stated the effort he or she would contribute.

variable_name: type of alliance (additive or conjunctive task)
description: Between-participants manipulation with two types of alliances. At the commencement of the session, participants were told how the resources of the partnering firms were pooled to determine the performance (utility) of the jointly developed product, namely whether the utility formulation was an additive or a multiplicative function. The utility formulation remained unchanged throughout the session.

Between-participants factor with two levels, n = 2 or n = 4 participants per alliance. The number of partners varied across experimental sessions but remained unchanged within a session, and each participant was informed of the number of partners in an alliance at the commencement of the session.

On each trial each participant was endowed with 24 francs, an amount that exceeded the optimal equilibrium investment, and had to decide how much capital to invest in the product jointly developed by his/her alliance, from zero up to the endowed capital. Each of the 128 participants made 120 investment decisions; for the analysis of variance the authors used each participant's mean individual investment.

After all participants made their investments privately and anonymously, the computer assessed the collective investments made by the competing alliances, i.e. the sum of the investments of the partners of an alliance on a trial. The mean collective investments per treatment are reported in parentheses alongside the mean individual investments.

A dummy variable set equal to 1 for link alliances and 0 for scale alliances. Each alliance was examined to determine whether to class it as a scale or link alliance according to the three categories of possible contributions: (i) research, technology development, and product design, (ii) manufacturing facilities and capabilities, and (iii) marketing and sales networks and capabilities. When, based on the three categories, all the contributions of the partners overlapped, the alliance was considered to be of the scale type; when, in at least one of the three categories, all contributions came from one partner, the alliance was considered to be of the link type. Two authors coded the variable independently, an industry expert independently classified a subset of alliances, and eleven ambiguous cases were dropped because of conflicting coding.

A 0-1 dummy variable that denoted whether an alliance underwent reorganization before the end of the study period. The authors first observed how the partners allocated the four functions (R&D, manufacturing, assembly, and marketing) at the beginning of the alliance, then considered any major subsequent change in this allocation, such as a partner beginning or ceasing to carry out manufacturing or marketing, to be a reorganization. Cases that first underwent reorganization and later underwent a second outcome event were classed as reorganizations.
time_window: before the end of the study period

description: A 0-1 dummy variable that denoted whether an alliance underwent takeover before the end of the study period. An alliance was considered to have been taken over when one of the partners exited the joint project altogether, thus terminating the partnership, while the other partner took on all the activities relating to the project in question. For those alliances that led to the creation of an equity joint venture that encompasses all collaborative activities, the acquisition of the joint venture is synonymous with the takeover of the alliance.
time_window: before the end of the study period

description: A 0-1 dummy variable that denoted whether an alliance continued until the end of the study period without reorganization or takeover.
time_window: until the end of the study period

description: A 0-1 dummy variable that denoted whether an alliance shut down without reorganization or takeover before the end of the study period.
time_window: before the end of the study period

description: A dependent variable that recorded the number of years between the formation of the alliance and the first of the four types of outcomes that took place. The four 0-1 outcome variables serve as right-censoring indicators for alliance duration before each type of outcome; that is, the outcome variables denote whether a particular type of outcome occurred at the end of the observed duration or whether some other form of outcome took place. If the organization of the partnership remains stable during the whole life of the alliance, the duration variable equals the length of the cooperation.
time_window: number of years between the formation of the alliance and the first of the four types of outcomes

description: GwG Adoption is a binary variable coded '1' in the first year between 2007 and 2012 in which, according to the JAAF's records, a plant successfully satisfied all criteria on core labor standards and became certified, and continues to be coded '1' as a code adopter for all subsequent years.
Absenteeism is the number of whole days of missed work per machine operator (MO) per year, reported by the plant's general manager for each year.
Voluntary Turnover is the log2 of the percentage of the total machine operator cadre that voluntarily quit working at the plant in a typical month in each year.

Efficiency is calculated as the number of earned minutes per day (total number of units produced per MO per day multiplied by Standard Minute Value) divided by the total number of minutes worked per day per MO, averaged over the calendar year, and log transformed prior to the analyses.
Productivity is calculated as the number of units produced per MO in a year, log transformed prior to the analyses.

Defect Rate is the percentage of finished garments produced during a day that was identified as being defective at the final end-line quality check, averaged over the year, and log transformed prior to the analyses.
On-time Delivery is the percentage of orders received throughout the year that were completed and delivered to retailers on time.
Sales Volume is the log of the volume of garments shipped/sold during the year, adjusted for work-in-progress and inventories of finished goods.
Average Selling Price is the log of the average price charged to retailers at point of shipping across all products manufactured and all orders fulfilled during a calendar year.

An accounting-based performance measure, the after-tax return on net worth, taken from archival financial data. The archival data for 1973, 1974, and 1975 were averaged. It is one of the observed measures of the latent performance construct.

An accounting-based performance measure, the after-tax return on total assets, taken from archival financial data. The archival data for 1973, 1974, and 1975 were averaged. It is one of the observed measures of the latent performance construct.

A 5-item scale that measured executives' subjective estimates about organizational performance; the scale asked them to rate how well their organizations were performing relative to competitors on profitability, employee satisfaction, public image, and goodwill. Ratings were aggregated over items and averaged over informants. The reliability of the instrument was 0.84, and the correlation between responses of multiple informants was 0.59.

Measured with financial data from annual reports by the levels of selling, general, and administrative expenses and working capital, after correcting for the volume of transactions as measured by sales in thousands of dollars. The ratio of selling, general, and administrative expenses to sales captures slack absorbed in salaries, overhead expenses, and various other administrative costs, and the ratio of working capital to sales captures absorption of slack related to capital utilization. The two indicators are observed measures of the absorbed slack latent variable, and the archival data for 1973, 1974, and 1975 were averaged.

Measured by the extent to which the sum of cash and marketable securities for the year covered current liability obligations, thus giving the amount of liquid resources uncommitted to liabilities in the near future; operationalized as the quick ratio, (cash + marketable securities)/current liabilities. The archival data for 1973, 1974, and 1975 were averaged.

An 8-item scale measuring the extent of delegation of authority; it asked executives to rate the extent of their delegated authority in key decision areas such as acquisitions, selection of large new investments, and raising long-term capital. Ratings were aggregated over items and averaged over informants; the reliability coefficient was 0.81 and the correlation between responses of multiple informants was 0.55.

A questionnaire measure using a 6-item scale that asked top executives to rate how much their organizations were oriented towards risk taking as demonstrated by decisions such as reliance on innovation, debt-financing, heavy R&D, and high risk-high return investments as opposed to low risk-moderate return investments. Ratings were aggregated over items and averaged over informants; the reliability coefficient was 0.53 and the correlation between responses of multiple informants was 0.58.

Industry-specific credit risk rating of the opportunity being exploited, created from detailed panel data obtained from the ZEW on the industry-specific credit ratings of new firms. The ZEW obtained individual credit rating information (derived from, e.g., the firm's payment behavior and solvency) for each of the new firms created in each year in Germany from CREDITREFORM and aggregated the individual credit rating information to the five-digit industry level. The measure captures the average risk across all start-ups at the detailed five-digit industry level that the founder faced when he/she created the firm, and in each of the following two years for firms that survived.
time_window: founding year and the following two years (2001-2003)

description: Measure of whether the founder had gathered management experience prior to engaging in start-up creation. Founders assessed their level of management experience at the time they founded their business on a five-point Likert-type scale ('very low' to 'very high'). The measure was standardized to facilitate hypothesis testing.
scale: five-point Likert-type scale ('very low' to 'very high')
time_window: at the time of firm founding

description: Degree to which the prior industry (industries) in which the founder worked matched the industry in which he/she founded the business. Coded 0 if the founder created the firm in an industry in which he/she had never worked previously, coded 1 if the firm was in the same industry as the one in which he/she previously worked (and if he/she had only worked in one industry previously), and coded 0.5 if the firm was in one of the two industries in which he/she had worked; the measure is based on same two-digit industry. The measure was standardized to facilitate hypothesis testing.

Respondents' reports of the total amount of revenues generated by their start-up firms in each year over the three-year period for which data are available (2001-2003). In order to ease interpretation of the findings, the nominal revenues in each year were converted from Euros into US dollars using the average conversion rate for each of the three years of the sample.

Developed 11 items addressing specific aspects of procedural justice concerning interparty exchange and cooperation and strategic decision making, measured on a seven-point Likert scale from 1 = not true at all to 7 = very true. The 11 items were averaged from the two surveys into a single score respectively (α = 0.89 for the first survey and α = 0.93 for the second), and these two scores from two boundary spanners were averaged into a single index, further weighted by James, Demaree, and Wolf's interobserver convergence rwg to measure the alliance's procedural justice as perceived by boundary spanners from both parties (average agreement level between first and second respondents: 0.83).

Financial outcome was defined as return on investment (%), obtained from the first survey. It was measured at the alliance level from the CEO's response in the first survey. The survey questions referred to the past three years.

Operational outcome was measured by the average of CEO responses (first survey) to the levels of labor productivity, manufacturing/quality control, technology development, customer service, and management efficiency, relative to major competitors in the industry. Responses used a five-point scale: 1 = lowest 20% in the industry, 2 = lower 20%, 3 = middle 20%, 4 = next 20%, 5 = top 20%. The informants were asked to refer to the past three years.

Interpersonal trust was measured using the first survey response, with items on a seven-point Likert scale from 1 = not true at all to 7 = very true. The items concern the boundary spanner's counterpart. Internal consistency and item appropriateness confirmed the reliability and validity of this construct. The informants were asked to refer to the past 3 years as the time frame.

Interorganizational trust was measured using the first survey response, with eight items on a seven-point Likert scale from 1 = not true at all to 7 = very true. Internal consistency was α = 0.80 and item appropriateness communality ≥ 0.83. Two items were reverse coded.

Cultural distance was measured by information from House et al.'s (2004) GLOBE project, which surveyed 61 nations' cultures in terms of nine dimensions. The distance measure was defined as 1/9 Σ [(Iia − Iic)² / Vi], where Vi is the variance of cultural dimension i and Iia and Iic are the scores of cultural dimension i for countries a and China, respectively. Country of origin was obtained from the Directory.

The information about governance form (1 if equity-based; 0 otherwise) was obtained from the Directory. It indicates whether the alliance is an equity joint venture or a non-equity based cooperative alliance.

Cooperation outcomes consist of financial outcome (alliance return on investment in percent, from the CEO in the first survey) and operational outcome (average CEO rating of labor productivity, quality control, technology development, customer service and management efficiency relative to competitors, 5-point scale).

The natural logarithm of the number of analysts initiating coverage of the focal firm in the previous year. The authors logged this variable because they anticipated that the pressure toward mimesis would increase at a decreasing rate, and the independent variables were lagged by a year.

variable_name: Logged recent adoptions weighted by status
description: Recent adoptions weighted by the status of the research department employing the analyst. Department status was derived from the 'All-America Research Team' rating issued by Institutional Investor magazine: the authors summed a research department's annual number of mentions in the four areas of stock picking, earnings estimates, written reports, and overall service and used the sum to weight the number of recent adoptions. Most research departments received a weighted score of zero; the variable was logged after adding one.

The event that an analyst initiated coverage of the focal NASDAQ firm, distinguished from new coverage initiation, in which an analyst added coverage of a firm when no other analyst in the same brokerage firm had dropped the firm. Each observation is a firm, with a duration from the time of the previous adoption to the next adoption or the data-censoring time, and spells were split annually to update covariates. A second model uses new coverage as the dependent variable; it treats analyst additions of a firm already covered by the brokerage as a censoring event.

variable_name: Logged number of adoptions at time of initiation of coverage
description: The natural logarithm of the number of analysts initiating coverage at the time the focal analyst first initiated coverage of the focal NASDAQ firm. It was included as a time-constant variable in the models predicting overestimation.
time_window: at the time the focal analyst first initiated coverage

variable_name: Logged status of adoptions at time of initiation of coverage
description: The natural logarithm of the number of analysts weighted by status initiating coverage at the time the focal analyst first initiated coverage of the focal NASDAQ firm. It was included as a time-constant variable in the models predicting overestimation.
time_window: at the time the focal analyst first initiated coverage

description: An indicator set to 1 when the analyst's overestimate was twice as large as the consensus overestimate, defined as the mean of all analyst estimates that were larger than the firm's actual earnings per share, and 0 otherwise. The authors used the last available forecast by the focal analyst and the last available consensus forecast in the focal year, and focused on such high errors because social salience leads to extreme evaluations.

variable_name: Logged number of adoptions at time of initiation of coverage
description: Recent adoptions at time of adoption were measured as in the analysis of overestimation errors: the natural logarithm of the number of analysts initiating coverage at the time the focal analyst first initiated coverage of the focal NASDAQ firm.
time_window: at the time the focal analyst first initiated coverage

variable_name: Logged status of adoptions at time of initiation of coverage
description: Recent adoptions weighted by status at time of adoption were measured as in the analysis of overestimation errors: the natural logarithm of the number of analysts weighted by status initiating coverage at the time the focal analyst first initiated coverage of the focal NASDAQ firm.
time_window: at the time the focal analyst first initiated coverage

description: Overestimation error was measured as in the analysis of overestimation errors and was lagged by a year: an indicator equal to 1 when the analyst's overestimate of the firm's earnings per share was twice as large as the consensus overestimate, and 0 otherwise.

An abandonment event was defined as an analyst stopping the issuing of an earnings estimate and recommendations for the focal NASDAQ firm; the IBES database flags these terminations of coverage. In the failure-time models the time from adding coverage to dropping coverage is the dependent variable, so a positive coefficient means longer duration and thus a lower hazard rate.
The natural logarithm of the number of analysts stopping coverage of the focal firm in the previous year, lagged by a year.

variable_name: Logged recent abandonments weighted by status
description: The natural logarithm of the number of analysts stopping coverage of the focal firm in the previous year, weighted by the status of the research department using the same weights as for adoptions, and lagged by a year.
Used as an annually updated control variable in the adoption analysis: the natural logarithm of the number of analysts stopping coverage in the previous year.

variable_name: Logged recent abandonments weighted by status
description: Used as an annually updated control variable in the adoption analysis: the natural logarithm of the number of analysts stopping coverage in the previous year, weighted by the status of the research department using the same weights as for adoptions.
Used as a control in the analyses of overestimation: the natural logarithm of the number of analysts initiating coverage of the focal firm in the previous year, lagged by a year.

variable_name: Logged recent adoptions weighted by status
description: Used as a control in the analyses of overestimation: the natural logarithm of the number of analysts initiating coverage in the previous year weighted by the status of the research department, lagged by a year.
Used as a control in the analyses of overestimation: the natural logarithm of the number of analysts stopping coverage in the previous year, lagged by a year.

variable_name: Logged recent abandonments weighted by status
description: Used as a control in the analyses of overestimation: the natural logarithm of the number of analysts stopping coverage in the previous year weighted by the status of the research department, lagged by a year.

The dependent variable is the length of time a firm in the industry offered products for sale up to 1994 or, in the event of a merger, the length of time products introduced by the acquired firm were offered for sale. If an exit was not recorded during the study period, the observation was coded as right censored, and the event-history method incorporates and weights the censored information.

For each firm the average rate of product introduction is measured over the study period. The measure is normalized to minimize correlation with its square, which is introduced to test the hypothesized curvilinear relationship.

For each firm the average life of products is measured over the study period. The measure is normalized to minimize correlation with its square, which is introduced to test the hypothesized curvilinear relationship.

To test hypotheses concerning strategy for managing product platforms and their derivatives, the rate of introduction of product platforms is calculated for each firm. A product platform was defined as a product whose design was zero-based, that is, a product whose design did not initially rely on existing architectures or components.
For each firm, the rate at which derivatives were generated from a platform is calculated. A family was defined as consisting of the platform and all its derivative designs.

variable_name: Family Life in Excess of Product Life
description: For each firm, the time by which platform life exceeded the life of the average of individual platform family members is calculated. Family life is the time from the introduction of the platform until the retirement of the last derivative product.

Dichotomous variable coded 0 in the years a dyad was intact and coded 1 in the year the tie dissolved. Dissolution was identified as occurring in calendar year t when an advertiser was listed as an agency's exchange partner, and an agency listed as an advertiser's advertising agency, in the respective Red Book directories in year t but not in year t + 1. When the two directories did not agree on the year of dissolution, the data reported in the Advertiser Red Book were used.

variable_name: Number of exits of advertiser executives
description: Count of the number of advertiser executives who exited the firm in a given year, formed by aggregating all individual exit events in a year to the executive level of the firm. Executives were identified by hierarchical level using job titles; only managers holding the titles Chairman, Chief Executive Officer, or President in advertisers were coded as executives. Exit was recorded in year t when an executive was listed as employed by the firm in year t but not in year t + 1.

variable_name: Number of exits of advertiser marketing managers
description: Count of the number of advertiser exchange managers who exited the firm in a given year, formed by aggregating all individual exit events in a year to the exchange manager level of the firm. Advertiser exchange managers were identified by functional category: managers with job titles indicating the marketing function were considered exchange managers because they are the primary point of contact between their firm and the advertising agency. Exit was recorded in year t when a manager was listed as employed by the firm in year t but not in year t + 1.

variable_name: Number of exits of agency executives
description: Count of the number of agency executives who exited the firm in a given year, formed by aggregating all individual exit events in a year to the executive level of the firm. Executives were identified by hierarchical level using job titles; only managers holding the titles Chairman, Chief Executive Officer, President, or Chief Creative Officer in agencies were coded as executives, omitting less relevant executive job titles such as Chief Financial Officer. Exit was recorded in year t when an executive was listed as employed by the firm in year t but not in year t + 1.
