variable_name: Number of exits of agency account services managers
description: Count of the number of agency account service managers who exited the firm in a given year, aggregated from individual exit events to the exchange manager level of the firm. Managers were coded as exchange managers if their job titles indicated they worked as account service managers, who are responsible for coordinating advertising campaigns and serve as the primary point of contact between the client and agency. Exit was recorded in year t when a manager was listed as employed by the firm in year t but not in year t + 1.

variable_name: Number of exits of agency creative managers
description: Count of the number of agency creative managers who exited the firm in a given year, aggregated from individual exit events to the exchange manager level of the firm. Managers were coded as exchange managers if their job titles indicated they worked as creative managers, who are responsible for conceiving, developing, and co-producing advertising through interactions with the client firm. Exit was recorded in year t when a manager was listed as employed by the firm in year t but not in year t + 1.

Change in the logarithm of the advertiser's gross revenue from time t to time t + 1. The log of advertiser gross revenue was used because the yearly revenue of firms in the sample was highly skewed. In the interaction plots the variable is interpreted as advertiser growth, with values below the mean indicating declining revenues from year to year and values above the mean indicating increasing revenues.
scale: change in log of gross revenue

description: Number of continuous years the advertiser and agency reported working with each other. Relationships were coded as beginning in the year prior to the first year an agency appeared as an advertiser's exchange partner. For relationships that already existed in 1986, duration was determined by following advertiser-agency relationships backward in time for a maximum of 10 years; relationships that began prior to 1976 were left censored and their duration clocks were assumed to start in 1975.

The DID estimator is the interaction of two variables, treated and post985. treated is coded as 1 if the respondent received his or her most advanced degree from a 985 university and 0 (control group) if he or she did not. For respondents in the treatment group, post985 indicates that the respondent received his or her most advanced degree after his or her university was affected by Project 985; for individuals in the control group, post985 indicates that the respondent received his or her most advanced degree after the matching 985 university was affected by the reform.

Measures, on a scale of 1 to 6, the importance that the respondents attribute to IP protection. IP importance was generated from the survey question asking respondents to rate on a scale of 1 to 6 the degree to which they believe that intellectual property is important.

R&D intensity is the ratio of R&D expenditure to total sales in the most recent year the firm was in operation, as reported on the survey. Because R&D intensity figures are skewed in their distribution, the authors took the natural logarithm of R&D intensity.
time_window: most recent year the firm was in operation

description: Reported revenues drawn from the firm in the most recent year the firm was in operation; if the firm failed or merged before the time of the survey, this is for the year prior to the failure or the merger. Because the distribution of revenues tends to be skewed, the authors took the natural log of the revenue figures.
time_window: most recent year the firm was in operation

description: Identifies whether an alliance has been terminated in the 5-year period between the two data collections, and before the end of the intended time period for cooperation. An alliance was classified as abruptly terminated when it was dissolved before the intended cooperation period was over, distinguishing preplanned termination from actual failure. Of the 34 terminated alliances, 25 had been abruptly terminated.

Measured as the perceived benefits at the first round of data collection (T1). The measure relies on a number of indicators, such as the net contribution from the alliance and the extent to which the alliance has resulted in firm growth, market growth, new products, new competencies, and new market entrances. It captures the partners' private goal fulfillment in the early stages of cooperation. All variables except size and cultural distance are standardized with scores ranging from 0 to 1.

Measured by the same indicators as short-term performance at the second round of data collection (T2). It reflects the benefits realized at later stages in the cooperation and captures the partners' private goal fulfillment over time. All variables except size and cultural distance are standardized with scores ranging from 0 to 1.

One of two variables used to measure specific investments, capturing specific investments in plant and equipment made in order to develop the alliance. Measured at T1 and at T2; the T1 value is used in the models of abrupt termination, short-term and long-term performance, and the T2 value in the T2 long-term performance model. All variables except size and cultural distance are standardized with scores ranging from 0 to 1.

One of two variables used to measure specific investments, capturing investments in human capital that have limited value outside the alliance. Measured at T1 and at T2; the T1 value is used in the models of abrupt termination, short-term and long-term performance, and the T2 value in the T2 long-term performance model. All variables except size and cultural distance are standardized with scores ranging from 0 to 1.

A scale capturing the degree of complementarity between the resources that each partner contributes to the alliance. Measured at T1 and at T2; the T1 value is used in the models of abrupt termination, short-term and long-term performance, and the T2 value in the T2 long-term performance model. All variables except size and cultural distance are standardized with scores ranging from 0 to 1.

A scale describing the strategic importance of the alliance for the future development of the firm. Measured at T1 and at T2; the T1 value is used in the models of abrupt termination, short-term and long-term performance, and the T2 value in the T2 long-term performance model. All variables except size and cultural distance are standardized with scores ranging from 0 to 1.

Measures growth or reduction in the scope of the alliance and whether the partners are more or less committed to the alliance. It is one of the two post-formation dynamics variables, which are related only to long-term performance. All variables except size and cultural distance are standardized with scores ranging from 0 to 1.

Captures whether the same company representatives in the respondent firm are responsible for the alliance in both surveys or if a great turnover of personnel has occurred. It is one of the two post-formation dynamics variables related to long-term performance. All variables except size and cultural distance are standardized with scores ranging from 0 to 1.

Captures whether the same company representatives in the partner firm are responsible for the alliance in both surveys or if a great turnover of personnel has occurred. It is one of the two post-formation dynamics variables related to long-term performance. All variables except size and cultural distance are standardized with scores ranging from 0 to 1.

The measure combines two indicators of service technology. The first, intensiveness of agency-client contact, was built from executive directors' reports of the percentage of their clients typically served in each of seven time periods, yielding one dimension for length of contact per day (ranging from extensive, half an hour or less, to intensive, more than 16 hours per day) and one for frequency of contact over the year (ranging from once a year to almost every day); these two dimensions correlate .61 and, after converting to Z-scores, were averaged. The second indicator is the number of service professionals per client, where service professionals are those engaged at least 50 percent of their time in service to clients rather than in administrative and supervisory duties. The two measures correlate .53 and were standardized and combined into a 2-item service technology scale; only this scale was used in subsequent analyses.

Each executive director was asked to approximate the number of hours over a typical month (200 hours) he or she spent "talking with the executive director of other agencies regarding agency concerns or problems."

variable_name: number of organizations in joint programs
description: The number of agencies and related organizations involved in the focal agency's joint programs, used as a measure of the extent of interagency contact through joint programs.
The percentage of total agency clients involved in the focal agency's joint programs, used as an indication of the extent to which joint programs pervade the agency's activities.

variable_name: referrals from other organizations (as a % of total clients)
description: The executive director of each agency reported the percentage of the agency's clients that were referrals from other agencies and related organizations. Referrals were measured as a proportion of total clients served rather than in absolute numbers, because absolute numbers tend to be a function of organization size.

variable_name: referrals to other organizations (as a % of total clients)
description: The executive director of each agency reported the percentage of the agency's clients that were referrals to other agencies and related organizations. Referrals were measured as a proportion of total clients served rather than in absolute numbers, because absolute numbers tend to be a function of organization size.

Respondents designated whether their last substantial innovation was developed internally or using an alliance for development, i.e., a partnership of one or more other firms explicitly formed for this project. Of the responding firms, 191 developed their last substantial innovation internally and 53 used an alliance, giving a data base of 264 firms. The hypotheses concerning the likelihood of forming an alliance are tested with a quantal choice logit model for whether an alliance was formed or not.
level: innovation project within the R&D director's division
time_window: the last substantial innovation developed (within the past 5 years)

description: A five-item scale with a coefficient alpha of 0.79. The scale assesses commitments in finance, plant, equipment, and marketing, and the extent to which the technology represents a core competence and a high degree of collective learning at the product category level. The product category level was selected in order to anchor the research as precisely as possible. Items were measured using 6-point Likert scales anchored by 'strongly disagree' and 'strongly agree'.

A scale measuring volatility, or the difficulty of predicting demand, with an alpha reliability coefficient of 0.64. The measure is not dissimilar to extant research measures, such as those of Walker and Weber (1984), John and Weitz (1988) and Klein et al. (1990). Items were measured using 6-point Likert scales anchored by 'strongly disagree' and 'strongly agree'.

Measured by six items relating to changes in technology in the product category. The scale has a coefficient alpha of 0.84. Items were measured using 6-point Likert scales anchored by 'strongly disagree' and 'strongly agree'.

A three-item measure concerning the specificity with which the performance of the innovation was established and monitored. The measure has a coefficient alpha of 0.68. Items were measured using 6-point Likert scales anchored by 'strongly disagree' and 'strongly agree'.

The number of alliances used by the division for technology development projects in the past 5 years. The experience of the firm with alliances is determined by the number of alliances already established by the firm.

A six-item scale evaluating past R&D alliances on different criteria, such as meeting objectives and market penetration levels achieved. The coefficient alpha is 0.93. Items were measured using 6-point Likert scales anchored by 'strongly disagree' and 'strongly agree'.

A four-item scale assessing demand growth at the product category level with a coefficient alpha of 0.83. Items were measured using 6-point Likert scales anchored by 'strongly disagree' and 'strongly agree'.

The percentage of stars in a research department is the ratio of ranked equity analysts, with analysts ranked in more than one subsector counted once, to total equity analysts in research department i in year t. Ranked analysts are those publicly ranked among the top four to six (first, second, third, and runners-up) analysts per subsector by Institutional Investor magazine each year. On average, 11.2% of analysts in a research department were ranked. Because proportions are bounded between 0 and 1, the authors used a logistic transformation of this variable.

Each analyst's specialization in the IBES database was classified into 12 major sectors (basic industries, capital goods, consumer durables, consumer nondurables, consumer services, energy, finance, health care, miscellaneous/undesignated, public utilities, technology, and transportation). The authors used Blau's heterogeneity index to measure the dispersion of analysts across sectors within each research department, which has larger scores when analysts are more dispersed across a large number of sectors. Expertise similarity is the reverse-coded Blau index (one minus the Blau index), so higher scores represent more clustering within sectors and thus higher similarity in expertise.
scale: one minus the Blau index, 0 to 1

description: Client-rated group effectiveness is the percentage of institutional clients who rated the research department as being one of the best ten research departments in year t. The ratings come from the Greenwich Associates Institutional Research Services poll, in which approximately 3,000 investment professionals are interviewed each year and asked to name the top 10 specific research departments that are their best sources for investment ideas. The average client-rated group effectiveness score in the sample was 0.136 (13.6%), with a standard deviation of 0.164.

A count of OFDI projects (i.e., foreign subsidiaries) established by a Chinese firm in a given year. It is a flow rather than a stock measure of OFDI projects: it is the number of annual FDI projects outside the firm's home country (China), and it captures how time-varying home-country dependence conditions may affect the subsequent establishment of OFDI projects. The measure was developed from a list of subsidiaries of the sampled firms compiled by WIND Data Services; a firm's OFDI was identified according to the names and/or locations of its subsidiaries, the foreign currency used to establish the OFDI, and information from the firm's Web site.

The concentration of FDI activities undertaken by foreign firms in the specific region of the home country in which the firm is located, where the firm's region is the province in which its corporate headquarters are located. Four measures were considered: revenue of foreign-owned enterprises divided by the total revenue of all enterprises in the province; assets of FOEs divided by the total assets of all enterprises in the province; number of FOEs divided by the total number of all enterprises in the province; and number of employees in the FOEs divided by the total number of employees in all enterprises in the province. FDI activities in any region where the FOE and the Chinese firm were in the same industry at the two-digit level were excluded from the four measures to avoid double-counting competitive interdependence, and the four measures were loaded on one factor and combined by taking the average.

The FDI activities undertaken by all foreign firms in the specific industry in which the firm competes, with industry defined by China's two-digit industry classification code. A combination (average) of four measures is used: revenue of foreign-owned enterprises divided by revenue of all enterprises in an industry; assets of FOEs divided by the total assets of all enterprises in an industry; number of FOEs divided by the number of all enterprises in an industry; and number of employees in all FOEs divided by the number of employees in all enterprises in an industry. Factor analysis indicated that the four measures loaded on one factor and the average of the four measures was used.

A count measure capturing EMF involvement in IJVs established with foreign firms in the home country, taking foreign IJV partner substitutability (embodied in multiple IJVs) into consideration. If a firm simultaneously engages in multiple IJVs in the same business activity, it proportionally reduces its dependence on any one IJV partner; for example, a Chinese firm with two IJVs producing the same product and a third producing a different product has only two nonsubstitutable IJVs. The measure is the cumulative number of nonsubstitutable IJVs that a firm has formed in China in a given year, logarithmically transformed. IJVs were identified according to the ownership level in the firm's subsidiaries (i.e., non-wholly owned domestic subsidiaries).
time_window: cumulative up to the given year, lagged one year

description: A three-step procedure was used. First, the ownership type of a listed company's Top 10 shareholders was identified. Second, if a shareholder's ownership type is an SOE, the state ownership was coded in terms of the proportion of shares held by that shareholder; if the shareholder's ownership type is not an SOE, its state ownership was coded as '0.' Third, all shareholders' proportions of SOE shares were summed. Information on ownership identity and the percentage of shares owned by different entities came from the CSMAR database.

For competing firms in a focal firm's state (private energy firms, IOUs, and publicly-owned utilities) the authors sum the total electricity generation from renewable resources (wind, sun, biomass, geothermal, and landfill gas) at the state level. The measure is the percentage of MW electricity generated from renewables to total MW operational at the state level; the formula block as printed is not readable in the provided text. The same measure was also calculated for wind only, for solar only, and for waste-to-energy (landfill gas) only.

A dummy variable that is 1 for states that have an RPS mandate in a respective year and zero otherwise, built from DSIRE information on the enactment date of the policy and the year in which the RPS took effect. States without RPS policies provide a natural control group.

The minimum targeted percentage of renewables in a utility's electricity portfolio mix in a respective state with an RPS mandate. States raise their RPS yearly goals over time as utilities as a group meet prior RPS targets, so higher yearly goals reflect a greater commitment to renewables; the variable only exists in states with RPS mandates.

variable_name: Investment in renewables (firm percentage of renewable electricity generation)
description: The percentage of a firm's MW operational from renewable resources relative to its total MW operational at time t + 1. Renewables comprise electricity generation from wind, sun, biomass, geothermal, and landfill gas, while hydroelectric power is excluded because it does not qualify toward meeting RPS targets in many states. The formula block as printed is not readable in the provided text.
A dependent variable whose value is 1 if a focal firm has invested in waste-to-energy (landfill gas) and zero otherwise, used in a random-effects Probit model.
A dependent variable whose value is 1 if a focal firm has invested in wind power and zero otherwise, used in a random-effects Probit model.
A dependent variable whose value is 1 if a focal firm has invested in solar power and zero otherwise, used in a random-effects Probit model.

The distance of a new resource's knowledge base from incumbents' established resource base is operationalized by comparing the three renewable types that qualify toward RPS requirements. Waste-to-energy is the most established renewable and is most similar to fossil technologies because it burns municipal waste in a combustion process to generate electricity; wind and solar do not burn a fuel source and are therefore more distant from the fossil-based knowledge base.

Normalized path length calculated as the average path length divided by the theoretical path length of a comparable fully connected regular graph of size (N) and mean degree (z), where N and z are determined empirically for the largest component for each period and region. The measure was inverted because the small-world measure requires path length in the denominator.

Individual clustering is the number of actual triples for an inventor divided by the number of potential triples, averaged across the largest component; inventors with one or zero ties receive a clustering score of zero. The average was normalized by dividing by the theoretical clustering of a fully connected regular graph.
Proportion of inventors within each region who had a collaborative tie within the largest component in the region.

Count of all utility patents granted to the region that had been applied for within the subsequent year, up to the end of the data in July 2002. The dependent variable is the number of successful patent applications in the year following the moving five-year window.
Small-world measure calculated as clustering multiplied by the inverse of path length after centering both variables; used to test the interaction of clustering and decreased path length.

Binary variable with a value of 1 when the incumbent CEO is replaced within the relevant time frame and 0 otherwise; the authors measured it within both one and two years of the restatement. Each occurrence of CEO replacement was verified with news downloaded from Lexis-Nexis covering a three-year window from one year prior to one year after the succession event, and with SEC filings in which the succession of the CEO was mentioned. Cases in which the CEO departure resulted from death, health issues, taking a CEO position in another firm, interim CEO status, a long-term retirement plan, or where the CEO continued to stay in the firm (typically as chairman) were removed.
time_window: within one year and within two years of the restatement

description: Binary variable that takes the value of 1 if a firm restates and 0 otherwise. The restatements examined are those reported by the U.S. GAO that involved the disclosure of earnings manipulation, specifically restatements related to revenue and expense recognitions that are downward revisions of previously inflated earnings. Each restating firm was matched with a nonrestating firm from the same four-digit SIC code, the same time period, and with similar total asset size.
scale: binary (1 = restating firm, 0 = nonrestating matching firm)

description: Measured as the proportion of non-CEO board members who are also executives of the firm.
time_window: year of the restatement (or year of the match for nonrestating firms)

variable_name: Proportion of board appointed by CEO
description: Measured as the proportion of board members appointed after the focal CEO was elected to the chief executive position.
time_window: year of the restatement (or year of the match for nonrestating firms)

description: Dummy variable that takes a value of 1 for the period after the passage of the Sarbanes-Oxley Act on July 30, 2002.

Rather than aggregating discretion variables into an index or treating them as separate variables in a regression, the authors used LISREL to represent discretion as a latent construct measured by multiple indicators. The indicators are market growth (a standardized growth coefficient based on 1982-86 sales), R&D intensity and advertising intensity (each a percentage of net sales, averaged over 1982-86), demand instability (the volatility of the sales growth rate from 1982 through 1986), capital intensity (total property, plant, and equipment standardized by number of employees, averaged over 1982-86), concentration (the Herfindahl index, weighted by business segment sales to create a composite level of concentration faced by each firm), and regulation (a dummy equal to one when at least one word formed from the base "regulat" appeared in a firm's annual letter to shareholders for 1982-86). Market growth, R&D intensity, advertising intensity, demand instability, concentration, and regulation were expected to load positively on discretion and capital intensity negatively. In the confirmatory factor analysis the demand instability indicator was not significant and was deleted and regulation was only marginally significant but retained, leaving a six-indicator model for the hypothesis tests, with the factor loading for concentration positive.

CEO compensation is modeled as a latent construct with two indicators, total cash compensation and long-term compensation. Total cash compensation is measured as the sum of salary and bonus; long-term compensation is measured as the number of shares multiplied by 25 percent of the exercise price. Data for both compensation measures were collected from proxy statements for 1987. In the measurement model the factor loading for cash compensation was set at 1.0 as the referent indicator and the loading for long-term compensation was significant, and both indicators were retained.

Subsequent performance was defined as a firm's average return on equity for the years 1987-91. To test the contingency hypothesis the sample was split at the median of subsequent performance and the LISREL model used for Hypothesis 1 was replicated in the high- and low-performance subgroups. The measure was not adjusted for industry norms.

The imitation variable describes the degree to which a firm introduces an offering based wholly or in part on an innovation by a competitor. The description of services for each mark was analyzed using key consulting terms combined with geographic terms and the 1987 SIC divisions, giving 252 unique terms; the key terms of a mark were then compared with the key terms of every other mark. The variable was obtained using network analysis by building an affiliation matrix with the Bonacich normalization routine, which evaluates the correlation between the use of key terms for mark i and the key terms for mark j. The displayed formula is not readable in the available text; the authors state that it yields a value between 0 and 1, with 0 indicating no words in common and 1 indicating that all words included in the description are common to both marks.

An order-of-entry variable registering the degree to which a mark filing used concepts and ideas introduced previously versus new concepts and ideas, based on the order of use of the same key management consulting terms used for the imitation variable. For each term, the competitor first to use it received a score of 1, the second received 1/2, and so forth, with a value of 0 when the term was not used to avoid a divide-by-zero error. The term scores were summed for each mark, divided by the number of words in the mark's description of services to normalize for description length, and the resulting weighted score was logged to normalize its distribution.

The collective innovative history of a firm's offerings, operationalized as the average of all prior offering innovativeness scores for a given competitor, producing an approximation of the competitor's past propensity to introduce innovative services over time, with higher values indicating greater innovativeness. If the firm had only one service mark, organizational innovativeness was set to zero.

Measured how closely related, or similar, the offerings of a competitor were to each other, constructed by taking the average imitation among the marks of the particular competitor. In other words, it measured the degree to which, on average, the services provided by a competitor were tightly clustered or diffuse. The calculation was similar to that used to create the dependent variable but measured within-firm rather than between-firm.

CDI is defined on the interorganizational dyad level as the extent to which a focal firm moves closer to or further away from a target firm in terms of strategic distance, defined as the ratio of the distance of the focal firm's position after the period from the target firm's position at time t to the distance between the two firms at time t. Strategic distance is measured by a Mahalanobis distance function over six dimensions of internal resource allocation: advertising intensity, plant and equipment newness, research and development intensity, overhead efficiency, financial leverage, and inventory rate. CDI is defined for all ordered combinations of a focal firm and a target firm, with the time lag set to two years. A positive value means the focal firm strategically converged toward the target firm over two years and a negative value means it diverged.
level: dyad-year (ordered pairing of a focal firm and a target firm)

description: Relative performance is defined as performance minus aspiration level, where performance is measured by ROA at time period t. The aspiration level is a mixture of social aspiration level, defined as the average performance of other firms in the industry, and historical aspiration level, defined as the firm's own performance at time t-1. A firm with performance greater than the social aspiration level has an aspiration level of 1.05 times its historical aspiration level, while a firm with performance below the social aspiration level has the social aspiration level as its aspiration. The variable is entered as a linear spline with a knot at zero, so that coefficients measure slopes separately for negative PRA (PRA-) and positive PRA (PRA+).

variable_name: Target firm's performance relative to focal firm's performance (TPFP)
description: TPFP is defined as the target firm's performance minus the focal firm's performance (TP - FP), where both firms' performance is measured by ROA. The variable is entered as a linear spline with a knot at zero, so that coefficients measure slopes separately for negative TPFP (TPFP-) and positive TPFP (TPFP+).

Equals one for coach-seasons occurring after the institution of NFL free agency in 1993 and zero for those occurring before that point. The variable captures the era in which market frictions for player human capital were significantly reduced; a positive coefficient would indicate a higher likelihood of coach dismissal in that era.

Dichotomous dependent variable that equals 1 if a team's head coach was terminated at the end of a given coach-season, and 0 otherwise. Dismissals occurring in the middle of a season end the corresponding coach-season.

The proportion of games won under a coach in a given coach-season. For example, a coach dismissed nine games into a season with a 1-8 record has a winning percentage of 0.11 for his portion of that season.

The quality of a team's opponents based on those teams' cumulative win-loss percentage during the current coach-season. The win/loss history of the focal team against its competitors was removed, so the variable captures the win-loss percentage of opponents against other teams in that coach-season.
A count of the number of players a team had in the Pro Bowl, the NFL's all-star game, in a given season. It serves as a measure of the quality of the team's production human capital.

A cumulative count of the number of Coach of the Year awards the coach won with the focal team prior to a given coach-season, that is, during the current coaching spell. Coach of the Year is awarded by journalists who cover the NFL and recognizes coaching accomplishment contingent on the competitive difficulties and advantages faced by a head coach in a given season.
time_window: prior to a given coach-season, within the current coaching spell

description: The number of seasons that a coach has been in his current coaching spell as of an observed coach-season.

The aggregate change in diversification profile between 1981 and 1985, used to determine if the firm became more or less diversified relative to its initial 1981 profile. The entropy index was computed for each firm at the initial and final point for the sample; the index is based on the fraction of the firm's sales that are in each industry, although the formula itself is not readable in the text. Large values of type imply that a firm was more unrelated in 1985 than it was in 1981. The authors state that the entropy measure is best suited for measuring continuous changes in diversification and has good convergent and discriminant validity.

The aggregate change in diversification profile between 1985 and 1989, computed from the entropy index of each firm at the initial (1985) and final (1989) point, exactly as for the first sample. Large values imply that a firm was more unrelated in 1989 than it was in 1985. The entropy formula is not readable in the text.

A continuous measure of the degree of emphasis on internal expansion across a series of diversification moves, defined as mode = $X/($X + $Y), where $X is the increase in sales due to internal expansions and $Y is the increase due to acquisitions between the two time periods. Higher values indicate greater dominance of internal expansion in the sales growth of a diversifying firm, and the variable ranges from 0 to 1. Trinet sales of businesses in individual SIC codes were used: the part of the sales of a SIC code in 1985 traceable to an acquisition made between 1981 and 1984 was marked as acquisitive expansion, and all other businesses were marked as internal expansion. Intermediate values do not represent joint ventures.

The same continuous measure of emphasis on internal expansion, constructed for the second sample's diversification moves, again as the share of sales growth due to internal expansion in total sales growth. Higher values indicate greater dominance of internal expansion, with the variable ranging from 0 to 1. The construction follows the Trinet-based tracing described for the first sample.

Ratio of long-term debt to market value in 1980, used as a standard measure of liquidity as a proxy for availability of internal capital. The authors note that low values of leverage imply availability of internal funds, or low default risk debt, or both.
Ratio of long-term debt to market value, measured in 1984 for the second sample. Low values imply availability of internal funds.

Ratio of current assets to current liabilities in 1980, used as a standard measure of liquidity as a proxy for availability of internal capital. High values imply availability of internal funds, or low default risk debt, or both.
Ratio of current assets to current liabilities, measured in 1984 for the second sample. High values imply availability of internal funds.

Average stock price in 1980-1984 divided by the average stock price in 1975-1979, used to measure the firm's ability to raise external capital; a high ratio means the market was willing to supply capital at a lower cost of capital than in the past, so high values indicate high availability of external funds. The authors used 1980-1984 rather than 1981-1985 on the premise that it takes roughly a year to translate expenditures into sales, and kept the time periods the same for all firms to correct for market variation in stock prices.

Belief about external capital availability for the second sample, measured with the same stock-price comparison logic as for the first sample; the paper does not restate the specific years used for the second sample. High values indicate high availability of external funds.
Ratio of R&D expenses to sales in 1980, used as a measure of innovative skills among knowledge-based resources.
Ratio of R&D expenses to sales, measured in 1984 for the second sample.
Ratio of advertising expenses to sales in 1980, used as a measure of marketing skills among knowledge-based resources.
Ratio of advertising expenses to sales, measured in 1984 for the second sample.

Ratio of the backlog of orders in 1980 to the three-year moving average backlog going back to 1974, used as a label for physical assets. Dividing by historical levels partially corrects for industry and persistent firm differences in average backlogs, and the moving average takes some account of different growth rates. The authors state that a firm with considerable excess plant and equipment was likely to have low backlogs, so high values on this variable indicate low excess capacity.
time_window: 1980, with a moving average back to 1974

description: For the second sample the years are 1984 and 1980; the variable is the backlog of orders relative to the historical backlog level as described for the first sample. High values indicate low excess capacity.

The change in the firm's average concentration ratio between 1981 and 1985, capturing the net concentration ratios of the markets the firm expanded into. The firm's average concentration ratio is computed from C4, the seller concentration ratio of the ith industry of the firm, weighted by p_i, the fraction of the firm's sales that were in industry i; the formula itself is not readable in the text. High-concentration markets are expected to be entered by acquisition.
The change in the firm's sales-weighted average industry concentration ratio between 1985 and 1989, computed as described for the first sample. The formula is not readable in the text.

The change in the firm's average sales growth rate between 1981 and 1985, capturing the net increase or decrease in the growth rate of the businesses the firm was involved in. The firm's average sales growth rate is computed from growth_i, the sales growth rate of the ith industry of the firm, weighted by p_i, the fraction of the firm's sales in industry i; the formula itself is not readable in the text.
The change in the firm's average sales growth rate between 1985 and 1989, computed as described for the first sample. The formula is not readable in the text.

Coded as 1 if the firm was founded in the wireless telecommunications industry, and 0 otherwise, i.e., 0 for diversifying firms that operated in another industry prior to entering wireless telecommunications. Among all the entrants, 25 percent were de novo firms.

The dependent variable is the natural logarithm of subscribers for firm i in year t, or ln(subscribersit). Growth is defined as the increase in firm size, measured in total subscribers, over two consecutive periods, and the lagged subscriber values are collected on the right-hand side of the growth model.

Computed as the natural logarithm of subscribers for the focal firm i in year t-1. In the growth model the lagged size terms are gathered on the right-hand side and the coefficient on lagged size is benchmarked at 1: a coefficient of 1 means no effect of size, greater than 1 means larger firms grow faster, and less than 1 means smaller firms grow faster.

Measured as the years a firm has been in operation in the wireless telecommunications industry, and equals the difference between time t and entry year. The authors define firm tenure as time in the focal industry, so that diversifying firms' clock is restarted for a better fit with focal industry conditions.

Coded as 1 if the firm entered the industry before 1991 and the year of observation is later than 1991, and zero otherwise; that is, coded as 1 if the firm entered during the analog era and is currently operating in the digital era, and 0 if the firm operates under the same technology regime in use when it entered (analog or digital). The analog regime is defined as ending in 1991, when the first digital service was introduced.

A dummy variable for businesses operating in TI industries. TI industries are those with average R&D expenditure-to-sales ratios in 1997 at least one standard deviation above the mean R&D expenditure-to-sales ratio for all industries in 1997, calculated from corporate-level Compustat data; the screen yields a subsample of 11,626 observations for 2,309 businesses in 31 four-digit industries.

A year counter ranging from 1 (in 1979) to 19 (in 1997) used to capture linear time trends in returns, market leadership loss, and mortality. In the industry dynamism models time is represented instead by dummies for three of the four five-year panels of the data (1978-1982, 1983-1987, and 1988-1992), with 1993-1997 omitted as the reference period.

The one-year lagged ROA of business j is entered in autoregressive models of current ROA together with the interaction ROA_jt-1 x YEAR_t, whose coefficient indicates whether the rate of decay of abnormal business returns trends over the study period, and with the interaction ROA_jt-1 x TECH_i in the cross-sectional model comparing TI and non-TI businesses. In the complementary analyses of high-performing businesses, durability is instead measured by a 0-1 variable identifying whether a business performing above its industry average ROA in a given year is still performing above that average in the following year, with a year counter or a TI industry dummy as the hypothesized predictor.

A 0-1 dependent variable identifying whether the business with the largest share of industry sales in a given year is no longer the industry sales leader in the following year; only annual industry leaders are used in estimation. The models include industry concentration (HHI_it) and either a year counter (YEAR_t) or a TI industry dummy (TECH_i) as the hypothesized variable.

A 0-1 dependent variable identifying whether a business does not survive in the following year, estimated with a proportional hazard rate model. The hypothesized predictors are a year counter (YEAR_t) in the longitudinal model and a TI industry dummy (TECH_i) in the cross-sectional model; controls are economic growth, M&A value, and industry density and its square.

For each four-digit industry in each of four five-year panels of the data (1978-1982, 1983-1987, 1988-1992, and 1993-1997), industry sales are regressed on 0-1 dummy variables representing years in the panel and the standard error of the regression is divided by the mean value of sales for that industry; the resulting value is the dynamism score. Dynamism scores are then regressed on industry dummies and time-period dummies, with a TI industry dummy (TECH_i) added in the cross-sectional model.

Coded as 1 when at least one of the existing VCs withdrew from the follow-on round of financing (did not participate in the follow-on round of investment) and 0 otherwise. Only withdrawal by independent VC firms was included. The withdrawing VC may retain its diluted equity in the venture or sell its equity in the secondary market, a distinction the data do not allow the authors to observe.
The pre-money valuation of the venture in the second round of funding, in millions of U.S. dollars applying 2012 values. The variable was logged to reduce skewness.

Binary variable indicating whether, in the second round, the development stage of the venture was Early stage (VentureXpert categories of 'Seed stage' and 'Early stage') or Late stage (VentureXpert categories of 'Expansion stage' and 'Late stage').

Binary variable equal to 1 when a new VC joins the second round and 0 otherwise. It captures whether the follow-on round is an outside round rather than an inside round composed of already existing investors, and serves as the mediator for the effect of VC withdrawal on valuation.

Eigenvector centrality in syndicate networks, used as a proxy for VC status: it measures the degree to which a focal actor is well connected to other well-connected actors. Adjacency matrices representing whether VCs had co-invested in a venture in the prior five years were constructed using all VCs in the database, not just the sample, and the largest eigenvector associated with the eigenvalue of the adjacency matrices was calculated. The measure used is the maximum eigenvector centrality of all joining VCs; if there was no joining VC, the value was replaced with zero.
level: VC firm (maximum across joining VCs, round level)

description: The total number of rounds in which a VC had invested in portfolio ventures over the five years prior to the focal round of investment, capturing the intensity of a VC's investment activity and its visibility. Used as the maximum VC general experience of all joining VCs; replaced with zero if there was no joining VC.
level: VC firm (maximum across joining VCs, round level)
time_window: five years prior to the focal round

description: The number of portfolio ventures a VC had taken public over the five years prior to the focal round, capturing the extent to which VCs select promising ventures and add value to achieve a successful exit. Used as the maximum VC IPO experience of all joining VCs; replaced with zero if there was no joining VC.
level: VC firm (maximum across joining VCs, round level)
time_window: five years prior to the focal round

variable_name: Aligned environment (Cell I) and partially aligned environment dummies
description: Entrants are classified into the four states of the innovative environment by crossing technology regime with technology intensity, as shown in Figure 1. In Model 1 two dummies represent these groups: T1 equals 1 for entrants into the aligned environment (Cell I, entrepreneurial regime with high technology intensity) and 0 otherwise, and T2 equals 1 for entrants into the partially aligned environments (Cell II or Cell III) and 0 otherwise. Entrants into the nonaligned environment (Cell IV) form the control group. Model 2 enters the two partially aligned environments separately, and the three-way model represents eight groups by seven dummy variables, with small entrants into the nonaligned environment as the control group.

Codes whether a firm entered during the entrepreneurial or the routinized regime of its industry. The entrepreneurial regime is defined as the period extending from the commercialization of an innovation to the significant reduction in entries, and the routinized regime as the period after that point. The delineating year between the two regimes is determined for each industry through a generalized discriminant analysis procedure applied to annual gross entry rates. The variable equals 1 if the firm entered in the entrepreneurial regime and 0 if the firm entered in the routinized regime.

Based on total (company, federal, and other) industrial R&D funds allotted as a percentage of sales, provided at the three-digit SIC level in the Survey of Industrial Research and Development. Industries above the average R&D intensity of all manufacturing industries in the United States, which was 4.7 percent for the 1987-97 period, are coded as high-technology-intensity industries and those below the average as low-technology-intensity industries. The measure does not vary over time across industries.

Firm size at the time of entry is measured by its asset size as listed by the Thomas Register in the year a firm entered the relevant market, converted to 1982 U.S. dollars to obtain a real dollar value. On the basis of their real adjusted values the firms were classified into five asset categories. Firms in the two lowest asset categories, with real value less than $5.5 million, are classified as small, and all other firms as large; small entrants accounted for approximately 68 percent of the firms operating in any given year.

Coded as 1 if a firm exited the focal industry in a given year and 0 otherwise; for example, for a firm that exited 3 years after entry the dependent variable took the value of 0 for the first 2 years and the value of 1 in the third year. For a firm that survived for 5 years after its entry, which is the survival period of interest in this study, the dependent variable is coded 0 for all five yearly observations. About 7 percent of firms exited in any given year.
time_window: yearly observations over the entry cohort's first years

description: Type of structure was first discovered during the interviews. The classification of organizational structure was done by either obtaining, or in some cases constructing with the help of organizational members, organization charts for each company. At least one hour was spent with organization members directly discussing the structure and how it worked. Companies were classified as international divisions, worldwide product divisions, area divisions, product division x area division matrix, or product division and area division mixed structures, and 34 companies had one of the structures covered by the Stopford and Wells Model.

Measured by the number of broad product lines a company offered for sale in two designated foreign countries; in all but a few cases one was the company's largest European subsidiary and the other was Brazil. The number of broad product lines in a subsidiary was measured during interviews with knowledgeable company executives, and products had to have either a different manufacturing technology or different customers and end uses, or both to count as a separate broad product line. The highest of the two measures was used to represent the company's foreign product diversity.

The percentage of a company's sales occurring outside of the parent country. In instances where a U.S. company's Canadian operations were organizationally treated as a part of U.S. operations and management for the two was integrated, Canadian sales were considered to be domestic sales.

Measured by dividing the value of foreign manufacturing (adjusted by the gross profit margin to make it equivalent to sales volume rather than cost of goods sold) by foreign sales. In a few instances where this information was not available, it was calculated by using foreign manufacturing assets to estimate the percentage of total company manufacturing occurring outside of the parent country, which was then divided by the percentage of foreign sales.

Density at founding is the count of automobile producers present in the population when the focal firm was founded, transformed into its natural logarithm and entered as a model covariate; a second-order polynomial specification adds the squared logged term. In this specification the simple term reflects the build-up of constitutive legitimacy and is expected to have a negative effect on the failure rate, while the squared term captures crowding and should increase the hazard. The logarithmic transformation is used because legitimation in this population occurred quickly and variance at very low counts had to be emphasized.

Estimated in event history format, where each record corresponds to a single firm-year spell of tenure in the automobile industry, with the initial year split into two half-year periods. The modeled event of interest is industry exit and includes exit to another industry, firm failure, and industry exit for an unknown reason. Merger and acquisition cases were coded as censored on the right, and the years of the Second World War were excluded from the data.

Organizational tenure in the industry, represented as a stochastic piecewise-exponential function whose pieces define tenure-specific baseline effects. The density-at-founding effects were also allowed to vary across tenure segments in order to test whether they persist over an organization's lifetime.
scale: years of tenure in the industry

description: The number of years elapsed since the inception of the automobile industry in 1885. It is used to interact with the density-at-founding terms to test whether those effects are confined to the formative years of the industry.

Percentage of individuals who said they felt 'somewhat' or 'strongly' that the war was worth fighting, based on ABC telephone surveys that asked whether, considering the costs to the United States versus the benefits to the United States, the war with Iraq is worth fighting. The sample of respondents was random and nationwide and typically had a 4.5-point error margin; the survey was conducted 38 times between March 2003 and December 2006 and usually had approximately 500 respondents. For months with missing values the authors used interpolated values.

variable_name: Combat performance (probability that any combat metric was mentioned)
description: Probability that any combat metric identified by the coders was included in a month's briefings, coded 1 if any speech during that month included a specific metric and 0 otherwise. Two research assistants unaware of the hypotheses coded the introductory section of each briefing, and when coders did not agree that a metric appeared, it was coded as not appearing. The authors estimate the probability of any of the 14 combat performance metrics being mentioned in the 46 months of the observation period.
The count of combat metrics released in a given month's press briefings, modeled with Poisson regression. Because this is a monthly model, the sample is 46 months.

variable_name: Reconstruction and rebuilding performance (probability that any reconstruction and rebuilding metric was mentioned)
description: Probability that any reconstruction and rebuilding performance metric (progress indicator) was included in a given month's press briefings, coded from the coded briefing transcripts. The sample size is 368, which results from estimating the probability of any of the eight reconstruction and rebuilding performance metrics being mentioned in the 46 months of the observation period.

variable_name: Count of reconstruction and rebuilding metrics
description: The count of reconstruction and rebuilding metrics mentioned in a given month's press briefings, modeled with Poisson regression. Because this is a monthly model, the sample is 46 months.

The cumulative number of U.S. troop deaths caused by car bombs, improvised explosive devices (IEDs), mortar attacks, and helicopter losses. The authors focus on IED deaths because they became associated with the guerrilla strategy pursued by the insurgents and because these deaths accounted for more than 50% of all U.S. deaths incurred in the Iraq War. Because this variable is a cumulative count of troops killed, higher values indicate more adverse outcomes. In supplemental analyses not reported in the paper the authors obtained the same results using U.S. troop deaths as a percentage of U.S. troops.

A change in the level of resources apportioned to the military budget; the DOD budget measures the total resources that go to military-related expenditures. The authors expect that an increase in the military budget would boost organizational members, thus increasing the extent to which they release information about war performance metrics in response to public support, so a higher increase in the budget suggests a lower degree of adversity.

The sum of the ranks of spokespersons in a given speech, based on manual coding of the ranks of all military officials who participated in press releases during the study period. Regular Army ranks range from O1 to O10, the lowest rank in the data set is O3, and each official was awarded a number analogous to that of their military rank; the Secretary of Defense was coded as 11. The authors obtained the same results when measuring this variable using the rank of the most powerful person involved in the speech.

Firms were coded into their Metropolitan Statistical Area based on the zip code of the firm's headquarters and compared with the twelve areas identified by Burrill and Lee as concentrations of biotechnology activity. The location variable is the percentage of the nation's total biotechnology firms located in the firm's specific MSA, and a '0' was recorded for firms not in one of the twelve geographical areas. Eight measures of scientific and technical activity in the firm's MSA were collected and normalized, factor analyzed into a single factor, and averaged into a single score measuring the munificence of a geographical area.
time_window: at the time of the IPO

description: This is a count of the number of active alliances the firm has with both non-profit and for profit research institutions and universities at the time of the IPO. This information was gathered from the prospectus.
time_window: at the time of the IPO

description: R&D intensity is measured as the average percentage of total expenditures spent on the R&D process during the last three years. The data were gathered from the IPO prospectus.
time_window: last three years prior to the IPO

description: In the business section of each prospectus the company reports the number of products under development or which have reached the market. None of the firms actually had products on the market at the time of their IPO, so the authors counted the number of products the firm had in preclinical trials, stage one, stage two, and stage three trials.
time_window: at the time of the IPO

description: From the offering firm's prospectus, a count of the total number of patents held by that firm was obtained. This includes both patents granted directly to the firm and patents in which the firm is the sole licensee.
time_window: at the time of the IPO

description: The names of all scientific personnel listed in the prospectus as well as top executives were compiled; only full time employees were included in the list in order to control for biases created by firms attempting to increase their visibility/legitimacy by hiring a long list of scientific advisors or consultants. The Science Citation Index was used to gather the total number of citations for each scientist in the firm during their career prior to the year in which the IPO was issued, and these citations were then totaled to create a measure of the quality of the scientific team employed by the biotechnology firm at the time of its initial public offering.
time_window: career prior to the year in which the IPO was issued

description: Market value is defined as the total market value of the offering firm's equity (1990 dollars) at the end of the first day of trading. A logarithmic transformation was used to control for the skewness of the distribution.
time_window: end of the first day of trading at the IPO

description: Factor score from a nonparametric principal component analysis (PCA) on 10 regional social capital variables, which derives eigenvalues from a cograduation matrix (Spearman's rho or rank-order correlation coefficients) aimed at minimizing the effect of outliers. Two principal components were extracted explaining 81.6% of the total variance; the first factor captures 'social interaction' and the second captures 'political participation'. The social interaction factor loads on participation in cultural associations, participation in voluntary associations, participation in nonvoluntary organizations, number of voluntary associations per region, meeting friends regularly, social meetings, and satisfaction as to relationships with friends.

A dummy variable that takes the value of 1 if the firm introduced a product innovation and 0 if it did not. It is based on responses to the question: 'Over the three-year period 2001-2003, did your firm introduce product innovation, by which we mean did the firm introduce at least one new (or a significantly improved) product?'
scale: dummy (1 = introduced a product innovation, 0 = did not)

description: A firm-level variable reflecting internal R&D efforts, measured by the percentage of sales revenue spent on R&D. Because the variable has a lower and an upper bound, predicted values from a first-stage fractional logit regression are used in place of the observed values in the second-stage equation. The instruments used in the first stage are current ratio, equity less noncurrent assets, and the gearing ratio.

Externally acquired R&D as a percentage of firm sales. Because the variable has a lower and an upper bound, predicted values from a first-stage fractional logit regression are used in place of the observed values in the second-stage equation. The instruments used in the first stage are membership of a commercial consortium, labor flexibility, and the gearing ratio.

Following Allison's (1978) recommendation on the measurement of inequality, the authors used the coefficient of variation (multiplied by 100 for ease of presentation) in the total compensation of the non-CEO top team members. Total compensation includes cash (salary, bonus, and other annual cash perquisites) and long-term components (stock options, restricted stock, and long-term accounting-based incentive plans). Options were valued with the modified Black-Scholes present value method computed by Execucomp, restricted stock at the current market value of the firm's common stock, and long-term accounting-based incentive plans at the expected payout reported by the firm.

Measured as the percentage of the CEO's top team who were on the board of directors. Because the authors hypothesize an inverse 'U' relationship, the main effect and its squared term were both included to test the hypothesis. Lagged one year.

Assessed using the coefficient of variation in the number of shares of common stock owned by each member of the CEO's top team. The coefficient of variation is described as the preferred measure when analyzing the variance of a continuous variable across a group of subjects. Lagged one year.

Because stock options may be considered a form of ownership, ownership variation was also gauged by measuring variation in unexercised stock options (options granted in previous years but not yet exercised) using the coefficient of variation in the number of unexercised stock options still owned by each such executive. Lagged one year.
Measured as the average organizational tenure (in years) of the CEO's top team members. Lagged one year.

Firm return on assets (ROA) was used as the indicator of firm performance in the models predicting performance. ROA was also included as a control for prior performance in the models predicting pay dispersion.
Measured using the modified Black-Scholes option pricing volatility parameter. In some models stock price volatility is also included as a control because it may affect how firms allocate pay.

The predicted level of pay dispersion for each firm generated by the fully specified model (i.e., with the control and independent variables) used in the first stage of the analysis. It was used in the second-stage models of firm performance in place of the original pay dispersion measure.

Measured as the difference between the actual levels of pay dispersion and expected dispersion. The authors' theory suggests that excess dispersion should be negatively associated with subsequent firm performance, while it makes no prediction about levels of dispersion that would be justifiably expected.

Dichotomous variable that takes a value of one in the first developer-platform-month in which a developer uses the focal platform, that is, writes code that calls on a platform's API, and zero if the developer has not yet used the platform (or ever). Because adoption is a nonrepeatable event, subsequent observations of that developer-platform pair are no longer included in the risk set. Adoption is identified by text mining the code of the developer's GitHub projects for unique platform-specific API keywords and dating the months in which the platform's technology was used.
time_window: developer time series from January 2012 (or first GitHub project) to November 2017

description: For each developer-platform pair, the variable takes the value of one for the month in which a developer attended a hackathon sponsored by the platform and all the months that follow, and zero otherwise. It is zero for platforms that do not sponsor the hackathon attended by the developer, and it considers only the first in-sample hackathon attended by a developer. Attendance is identified from Devpost by whether the developer submitted a project to the hackathon for judging.

In the month of the hackathon and the months that follow, Local Adoption Rate is the count of peer developers at a hackathon who have already adopted the platform divided by the total number of peer developers at the hackathon, independent of whether the platform sponsors the hackathon. In months prior to the hackathon, this variable is coded as zero. Prior adoption by peers is identified from their GitHub projects.
time_window: hackathon month through November 2017 (zero before the hackathon)

variable_name: Local Adoption > 25% / Local Adoption > 50% / Local Adoption > 75%
description: Three indicator variables for different adoption thresholds, used to test nonlinearity in perceptions of platform dominance across different levels of platform adoption. Local Adoption > 25% is set to one if a developer attends a hackathon where the proportion of developers who already adopted a focal platform exceeds 25%; the analogous indicators are set above 50 and 75%, respectively. The threshold indicators are defined using inequalities rather than mutually exclusive categories: when a higher threshold indicator is set to one, the lower threshold indicators are also set to one.

Each project that won an award at the hackathon attended by the focal developer was identified, and the set of platforms used in those projects was recorded. For each developer-platform pair, the dichotomous variable takes the value of one in the month of the hackathon and the months that follow for all the platforms used by the award-winning projects, and zero otherwise. Awards are recorded from Devpost and the platforms used in the winning projects are identified from project code.

variable_name: Hackathon Attendance (in the interaction Local Adoption Rate x Hackathon Attendance)
description: The Hackathon Attendance dummy in the developer-platform-month panel: one from the month a developer attended a hackathon sponsored by the focal platform and all months after, zero otherwise and zero for platforms that do not sponsor the hackathon the developer attended (Model 3.4, Local Adoption Rate x Hackathon Attendance).

The Treatment indicator variable takes a value of 1 if the founder/venture is in the treatment condition (103 observations), and it takes the value of 0 if the founder/venture is in the control group (78 observations) based on the randomization at the beginning of the study. Randomizing was performed using the 'runiform()' function in Stata. The main analysis uses the original assignment of the 181 founders, that is, the intention-to-treat.
time_window: assignment at the beginning of the study

description: A focal founder self-reported her venture's annual sales using a five-category, Likert-type scale. We assigned this variable the value of 1 if the sales were between SGD 0 and SGD 99,999; 2 if between SGD 100,000 and SGD 249,999; 3 if between SGD 250,000 and SGD 499,999; 4 if between SGD 500,000 and SGD 19,999,999; and 5 if above SGD 2,000,000. Sales was measured at both baseline (April 2017) and endline (February 2018).

Growth Goal measures the founder's expected sales revenues for the venture 12 months into the future, which was reported at the start of the study using the same five-category, Likert-type scale used for Sales. It is a time-invariant entrepreneur characteristic entering the models as a moderator.

An indicator variable that takes the value one in the months after the financial crisis (starting in July 2009) if a particular fund is the sister fund—another fund in the same firm—of a fund that was closed during the crisis (December 2007 to June 2009), and is zero otherwise. For all funds, CLOSED_CRISIS = 0 in the months before the crisis (through November 2007).
time_window: post-crisis months from July 2009; pre-crisis through November 2007

description: The information ratio is computed by dividing a fund's excess returns by the amount of risk taken on by the fund, relative to market benchmarks. For fund i at month t, excess returns are the sum of a time-invariant fund-specific alpha plus a mean-zero residual from a regression of raw returns on the risk-free rate and seven market risk factors; risk is the standard deviation of the residual. The measure captures real-time changes in the market value of the fund's portfolio.

Relatedness is computed as the pairwise correlation in excess returns between every pair of funds in a firm with at least 12 months of contemporaneous returns. It is used as an interaction with CLOSED_CRISIS; the interaction term equals zero for all control group observations and for all funds before the financial crisis. After the crisis, the interaction term takes values from -0.64 to 0.98 with a mean of 0.54 conditional on being treated.
time_window: monthly excess returns; at least 12 months of contemporaneous returns

description: To explore temporal dynamics, CLOSED_CRISIS is bifurcated into two variables that together span the post-crisis period: Years_0-2 corresponds to the first two years post-crisis, and Years_3-6 to the remaining years in the sample. These are interacted with CLOSED_CRISIS to capture temporary versus persistent refocusing costs.
time_window: post-crisis years; first two years versus third through sixth year

description: Organizational dormancy is measured as the rate of deviation from the prediction for the number of new branches established by a bank. Bank size (number of existing branches at t-1) and its squared term were first regressed on the number of new branches established by a bank in a negative binomial regression for the 10 years before the detrimental regulation (1971-1980), and the resulting estimates were used to predict how many new branches each bank should have opened each year during the period of regulation. The extent to which actual new branches deviated from these predicted values was then coded as a spline function, taking the positive deviation divided by the predicted value when the bank opened fewer branches than predicted, and zero otherwise. The lowest value is 0 (the bank expanded beyond the predicted level) and the highest value is 1 (the bank did not open a single branch in the year), and higher values mean a more dormant bank in a focal year.

Net dormancy compares the total number of branches a bank actually opened during the entire detrimental policy period (1981-1990) with the total number of branches predicted for that same period, using the same size-based prediction. The deviation of net actual from net predicted new branches was coded as a spline function, taking the positive deviation divided by net predicted new branches and zero otherwise. The greater the net dormancy, the more dormant the organization was during the period of the detrimental policy.

Political awareness was coded as 1 if a bank had an administrative office in the same zip code (110001) as the Indian Parliament, a prominent hub for the national government and its bureaucracies in New Delhi where the government quarters of India's national political elite are also located, and 0 otherwise. A nonbanking administrative office such as a zonal office or a regional office in this zip code is taken to indicate that a bank's managers are more politically aware. Direct links such as campaign contributions and board memberships were unavailable for the study period.

A politically plural state was first defined as one in which the state government had been formed by a political party different from the one controlling the national government. The variable was then coded as the ratio of the number of politically plural states in which a bank had a branch to the total number of states that were actually politically plural in a given year.

Organizational fitness was measured as the proportion of rural branches in a bank's portfolio of branches, on the logic that banks already active in rural areas required very little adaptation to remain fit when the restrictive rural branching policy was implemented. It is a proportion-based measure.

Organizational slack was measured as the amount of cash reserves and surplus a bank holds, a proxy often used in prior academic work. Because the data on cash reserves and surpluses of the sample banks were skewed, the variable was coded as the natural log of the amount of cash reserves and surplus maintained by a given bank in a given year.
scale: natural log of the amount of cash reserves and surplus

description: Financial performance was quantified as return on assets (ROA), the ratio of net income to total assets, because most banks in the sample were not listed on an Indian stock exchange and no market-based performance metric was available. It is the dependent variable in the postdetrimental period analysis.

The dependent variable is the expected acquisition performance of the acquirer, measured as the abnormal returns that accrue to the acquirer upon the acquisition announcement. The authors determined the unanticipated capital markets reaction by measuring the abnormal returns accruing to the acquirer in a two-day window around the acquisition announcement, calculating market-adjusted abnormal returns using the Eventus module of the WRDS database. The two-day window was chosen for the main results because shorter windows are more appropriate for event studies to reduce the effect of confounding events; three-day, five-day and two-week windows were used to check robustness. For the sample, the mean cumulative abnormal return was negative (-0.39%) but was not significantly different from zero.
time_window: two-day window around the acquisition announcement

variable_name: number of prior transactions with the advising investment bank
description: The ability of the firm's advising bank to transfer acquisition information to the acquirer is measured as the number of prior investment transactions that took place between those two parties during the 10-year period preceding the focal transaction. A previous investment transaction is defined as any investment transaction (debt or equity underwriting, acquisition advisory service, etc.) in which the firm retained the investment bank as either a book runner, a manager, or a lead financial advisor. Deals where the advisor role is classified solely as 'Fairness Opinion' by SDC are excluded. All independent variables except the dichotomous or dummy variables are mean-centered in the reported analysis.

variable_name: mean number of prior transactions with nonadvising banks
description: To measure the ability of 'nonadvising' banks to transfer relevant information to the focal acquirer, the authors counted the number of investment transactions the focal firm had with each bank in the 10 years prior to the focal transaction and then used the mean value of these counts. For instance, if the focal acquirer had retained three different banks for past investment transactions—none of which was retained as a lead advisor for the focal transaction—and the banks completed two, four, and nine prior transactions respectively, the measure is the mean value, which equals five. All independent variables except the dichotomous or dummy variables are mean-centered in the reported analysis.
time_window: 10 years prior to the focal transaction

variable_name: concentration of the advising investment bank (market share)
description: The concentration of the advising investment bank is operationalized as its market share in the acquirer's overall investment advisory business in the 10 years preceding the focal transaction. For instance, if the lead advisor in the focal transaction was retained for three prior deals in that 10-year period and the acquirer had completed 10 deals overall, the advisor's concentration measure is 0.3. Highly concentrated bank relationships correspond to a lower willingness of the investment banks to expend extra effort. All independent variables except the dichotomous or dummy variables are mean-centered in the reported analysis.

The Herfindahl index accounts for each nonadvising bank's share in proportion to the number of transactions with the acquirer, and is calculated as a Herfindahl-Hirschmann index for each transaction in the sample. In the specification, Di is the number of preceding deals in which the focal acquirer used the investment bank, i is either an advisor or a book runner, and D is the overall number of investment deals (acquisitions and underwritings) the acquirer has completed prior to the focal transaction; each underwriting and advisory assignment between the focal firm and investment banks was considered an equal contribution to their tie. The formula block itself is not readable in the supplied text, so the exact equation is not reproduced. All independent variables except the dichotomous or dummy variables are mean-centered in the reported analysis.
time_window: transactions prior to the focal transaction

description: In line with many existing acquisition studies, the authors used a SIC-based dummy variable that takes on value of 1 ('related acquisition') if in the first four-digit SIC code of the acquirer and the target there is at least one code common on the three-digit or on the two-digit level, zero otherwise. The results are reported using that dichotomous relatedness measure. For the split-sample tests, the sub-sample of related deals at the two-digit primary SIC code level and the sub-sample of unrelated deals were estimated separately.

Self-reported ratings of the firm on five performance measures, relative to the major competitors in its industry, on a seven-point scale ranging from 1 'much worse' to 7 'much better'. The performance information was collected from the head of the accounting and finance function in each firm, for the two-year periods 2001-2002 and 2004-2005. The correlation between the performance variables over the two time periods was 0.84. Objective measures of growth in sales and revenues, growth in net income/profits, return on assets, and return on sales obtained from the annual reports of 12 firms listed on the Ghana Stock Exchange correlated with the subjective measures at 0.70, 0.82, 0.79, and 0.86 respectively.
scale: seven-point scale ranging from 1 'much worse' to 7 'much better'

variable_name: social networking relationships with political leaders
description: Respondents assessed the extent to which top managers have developed and utilized personal and social networking relationships with government political leaders for the three-year periods 1998-2000 (data collected in 2002) and 2001-2003 (data collected in 2005), on a seven-point scale ranging from 1 'very little' to 7 'very extensive'. The measure was operationalized as the average responses to four items: relationships with city council politicians, district council politicians, regional government politicians, and national government politicians. The Cronbach alpha was 0.78.
scale: seven-point scale ranging from 1 'very little' to 7 'very extensive'

variable_name: social networking relationships with bureaucratic officials
description: Respondents assessed the extent to which top managers have developed and utilized personal and social networking relationships with government bureaucratic officials for the three-year periods 1998-2000 and 2001-2003, on a seven-point scale ranging from 1 'very little' to 7 'very extensive'.
