Engine size as reflected in horsepower, used as a second measure of product differentiation: cars with larger, more powerful engines tend to be more differentiated in other components as well, with the largest engine sizes found in highly differentiated luxury and sports car models and the smallest in the most basic economy cars (trucks were excluded). The square of horsepower was also included to account for possible nonlinearities in the effect of product differentiation on vertical integration.

The dependent variable is the firm's hazard of mortality, estimated with a Gompertz hazard rate model with maximum likelihood; nonparametric analyses suggested that the Gompertz specification shows superior goodness of fit relative to the Weibull and other specifications. The analysis is conducted at the level of the firm rather than at the level of the car model.

Two measures were used to capture complexity: comprehensiveness, measured by adding the total number of concepts in a causal map (Nc), and connectedness, measured by dividing the total number of linkages (Nl) in a causal map by the total number of concepts in that map (Nl/Nc). A composite measure of complexity was computed by averaging the two standardized individual measures.

Centrality was computed using a network-based measure of centrality: degree centrality, which focuses on direct and adjacent paths of a concept with other concepts in the network of concepts representing a map and is a measure of the overall centrality of the map. The text states that CD(Pk) equals the number of concepts connected to concept k, a(pi,pk) is the connection from Pi to Pk (either 0 or 1), and n is the number of concepts in the causal map; the formula itself was not extractable from the text provided.

Proactive logics were captured as strategy (action) to environment links in the causal map, using in-degree (links leading into the concept) and out-degree (links leading away from the concept) analysis of the causal links between environment and actions. The relative importance of the proactive causal links in the overall causal map is captured by the percentage of strategy to environment links. The final composite measure was obtained by averaging the z-scores of in-degree environment, out-degree of strategy, and percentage of strategy to environment links.
This variable was measured as yearly percentage change in industry gross sales. The growth rate for the year of IPO was computed as the percentage increase (decrease) in sales from the previous year.
time_window: year of IPO, relative to the previous year

description: Diversity was captured with Ferrier et al.'s (1999) Herfindhal-type index of competitive simplicity, computed as the sum over action categories of (Na/NT) squared, where Na/NT is the share or proportion of organizational actions in the ath category. Low scores represent firms that engage in highly diverse actions while high scores represent firms that engage in less diverse actions.
To capture frequency of new venture actions, the authors counted the number of different actions initiated by a firm during the year following the IPO.

Speed was measured as the amount of time elapsed between the announcement of the intent to undertake a given action and the date of its implementation, aggregated at the firm level by averaging the number of days between the date of the media announcement of actions and the date of their implementation as mentioned in subsequent announcements or in the firms' 10Ks. Only new product-related actions (371) allowed a relatively accurate measure of speed; 10 of the 104 firms did not undertake new product-related actions and these data are treated as missing during statistical analyses.

Events identified from Wall Street Journal articles retrieved through a Factiva keyword search (e.g., 'pollution,' 'recycling,' 'emission,' 'global warming'). Articles were read by at least two researchers and classified as 'eco-friendly events' or 'eco-harmful events'; articles reporting both types of behavior at the same time were excluded. In the final sample of 273 articles, 117 referred to eco-friendly events.

Events identified from Wall Street Journal articles retrieved through a Factiva keyword search and classified by the researchers as 'eco-harmful events' rather than 'eco-friendly events.' Articles reporting both types of behavior at the same time were excluded. In the final sample of 273 articles, 156 referred to eco-harmful events.

Cumulative abnormal return over the two-day event window (-1, 0), where day 0 is the publication date of the corresponding Wall Street Journal article and day -1 accounts for the possibility that the event happened on the previous trading day. Abnormal returns are computed with the market model, whose coefficients are estimated by ordinary least squares on the 200 trading days corresponding to the interval [-240, -41], using daily return data from CRSP and the equally weighted CRSP market portfolio as the market return. Cumulative abnormal returns are obtained by summing the abnormal returns within the event window, and are expressed as a percentage.

A linear time trend taking the value of the year of the event (trend = 1980, 1981, ..., 2009), estimated separately for eco-friendly and eco-harmful events. The coefficient on the trend measures how the stock market reaction evolved over time, and is the main proxy for external pressure to engage in environmental CSR.

Index of environmental strengths from the KLD database; it ranges from 0 to 7, adding one index point for each of seven possible strengths. The index is lagged by one year so that it is not affected by the events. KLD data are available as of 1991 and cover a subset of the companies in the sample, which reduces the sample to 55 eco-friendly and 47 eco-harmful events.
time_window: lagged by one year relative to the event

description: Index of environmental concerns from the KLD database; it ranges from 0 to 7, adding one index point for each potential concern. The index is lagged by one year so that it is not affected by the events. KLD data are available as of 1991 and cover a subset of the companies in the sample.
time_window: lagged by one year relative to the event

description: Bonacich's power centrality measure computed for the biotech (R&D) firm in the industry-wide network of alliances. Centrality for firm i as of year t is defined from the relationship matrix whose entry is the number of previous alliances between firms i and j within the past five years, with a weighting coefficient set to three-quarters of the reciprocal of the largest eigenvalue of that matrix. Centrality is scaled so that the maximum centrality for each year equals 1.
time_window: annual, with alliances in the past five years

description: Bonacich's power centrality measure computed for the pharmaceutical (client) firm in the industry-wide network of alliances. Centrality for firm i as of year t is defined from the relationship matrix whose entry is the number of previous alliances between firms i and j within the past five years, with a weighting coefficient set to three-quarters of the reciprocal of the largest eigenvalue of that matrix. Centrality is scaled so that the maximum centrality for each year equals 1.
time_window: annual, with alliances in the past five years

variable_name: net number of client's value capturing rights
description: The total number of value capturing rights assigned to the client minus the total number of value capturing rights assigned to the R&D firm. Rights are counted from a list developed from Lerner and Merges (1998) and Adegbesan and Higgins (2011), covering rights such as patents and intellectual property, licensing, manufacturing and marketing in the main collaboration area, and exclusive rights are assigned two points because they include basic rights. The authors count the number of value capturing rights rather than ranking them.

An ordinal measure of the rights to unexpected outcomes allocated to the client, constructed with attorneys in the field, with each contract placed into one of seven categories and given a corresponding score. The categories run from a score of 0 (the R&D firm is given all rights or the client firm is specifically not given any rights) through 1 (nothing is specified), 2 (client informed and given right of first negotiation or first offer without restrictions), 3 (client has right of first refusal or negotiation with restrictions on third-party offers), 4 (joint ownership of all rights), 5 (client given rights exercisable unilaterally) to 6 (client is given all rights). In the rare cases in which a client firm gets rights spanning multiple categories, the highest score is assigned.

For every month, the ratio of the number of biotech companies that went through an IPO in the previous six months to the total number of private biotech companies that have been operating during that period, multiplied by 1,000.

Breadth is calculated for each patent as per Gruber et al. (2013). A focal patent cites J prior patents; those references in turn cite work distributed across K different technological domains (four-digit IPC patent subclasses), with s_jk the share of domain k among j's references, and S the total number of references to technological domains by all of the focal patent's J citations. Summation is done recursively, first across patents within a technological domain and then across technological domains; the displayed equation for the measure is not readable in the text supplied here. Intuitively the measure tracks the focal patent's ties to prior bodies of knowledge and is down-weighted by how often those bodies of work reference one another. Breadth is bounded between zero and one.

Binary variable indicating whether an application was granted patent. Applications that were granted are coded 1; those that were rejected, withdrawn, or deemed withdrawn are coded 0. It is the dependent variable in the probit models of patent approval.
scale: 1 = granted; 0 = rejected, withdrawn, or deemed withdrawn

description: Count of the number of citations a patent received from subsequent patents (the focal patent's forward citation count) in the five years after the patent was filed. The count is modeled for patents that were granted, to maximize comparability with prior research that has focused on the impact of granted patents.
time_window: five years after the patent was filed

description: For each patent application the authors calculated the Jaccard index for each of its combinations of four-digit IPC classes, defined as the intersection of the two sets divided by their union, and then took the minimum Jaccard for each application. Lower minimum Jaccards reflect more atypical technological recombinations within an application, and higher values imply that combinations are more typical. The Jaccard is not defined for single-class patent applications, so models using it are estimated on the subsample of applications with citations to more than one technology class.

The study's sole dependent variable, professional program adoption, was inferred when a college granted, for the first time, a bachelor's degree in any one of five broad curricular areas: business, communications (such as journalism), public affairs (such as public administration), health fields (such as nursing), and computer science. These are typically defined as professional fields that lie outside the traditional domain of liberal arts colleges. An observation existed in the data if a college was at risk of adopting a particular program in a given year, and observations were dropped after a college adopted a professional program or exited the sample for other reasons.

Captured whether a college president had migrated from another school that already possessed the specific professional program that the focal college was at risk of adopting. The migration and all other independent variables were lagged four years, because the adoption of a program does not become evident in the data until the college first grants a degree, and the migration variables were allowed to operate for three years: the year a president entered a college and the two years following. In the authors' example, a college that in 1971 hires a president from a school that has previously adopted a business program is assigned a 1 on this variable for the years 1975, 1976, and 1977.
time_window: lagged four years, operating for three years

description: Captured whether a president had migrated from a nonliberal arts college, such as a state university or private research university. Like the other migration variables, it was lagged four years and allowed to operate for three years.
time_window: lagged four years, operating for three years

description: Inferred when a president had migrated from a college that was classified as 'not selective,' which was the lowest rank on Cass and Birnbaum's (1971) ordinal selectivity index. Colleges occupying the lowest position on this recognized ranking were presumed to be low in the field's status hierarchy and thus peripheral players. Like the other migration variables, it was lagged four years and allowed to operate for three years.
time_window: lagged four years, operating for three years

description: Included as a measure of external dependence (Hypothesis 4b). Colleges that are highly dependent on tuition will likely be more adaptive to changing student interests.

The percentage of part-time students, included with tuition dependence as a measure of external dependence (Hypothesis 4b). Colleges with more part-time students, who tend to have vocational interests, will likely be more adaptive to changing student interests.

One of two measures capturing financial pressures (Hypothesis 4c); it captures an organization's stock of financial resources. It was reverse-scored in the construction of the summary index of deinstitutionalizing pressures because it denotes lower pressures for institutional change.

The second measure capturing financial pressures (Hypothesis 4c), calculated as [total revenues — total expenditures]/total revenues. It is a 'flow' variable, capturing fluctuations in the organization's financial fortunes. It was reverse-scored in the construction of the summary index of deinstitutionalizing pressures because it denotes lower pressures for institutional change.
Included to capture the earlier adoption of institutional changes (Hypothesis 4d), a measure of the prior number of professional programs offered. This variable ranged from 0 to 5.

A measure capturing whether a college was located more toward the core or the periphery of the field (Hypothesis 4e), as determined by Cass and Birnbaum's (1971) six-point ordinal index. Lower prestige and a more peripheral position in the field are indicated by lower values on the index.

variable_name: index variable that captured other deinstitutionalizing pressures
description: A summary variable created by standardizing each of the six contextual variables described above and summing these standardized scores. Variables denoting lower pressures for institutional change (like endowment or operating margin) were reverse-scored. The migration variables were multiplied by this index to create multiplicative interaction terms.

Measured whether an immigrant president had held the position of president at his or her origin college. Boeker suggested that executive migrants with greater authority in their former organizations may have more influence as newcomers. This measure was interacted with the migration variables.

The enrollment of the origin college, the second measure of executive power. Boeker argued that executives migrating from larger organizations will have more power. This measure was interacted with the migration variables.

Executive migration is measured by three dummies based on the previous employer of an incoming college president: migration from a college that already had the focal professional program, migration from outside the liberal arts field, and migration from a peripheral (non-selective) college. Each is lagged four years and operates for three years.

The standard deviation of the securities analysts' forecasts of earnings per share for the year; the forecasts are taken from the last month of the previous fiscal year. Means and standard deviations of analysts' forecasts are available from IBES. The greater the variance in forecasts, the less predictable the income stream and the more risky.
time_window: forecasts from the last month of the previous fiscal year

description: Performance measured by return on total assets (ROA), return on equity (ROE) and return on sales (ROS). The model is estimated on each measure to test for differences across performance definitions.

Firm performance (ROA, ROE, and ROS) averaged over all the firms in a two-digit SIC-code industry for a given year. It measures the average profitability of firms in an industry and thus reflects an industry's competitiveness.

The difference between aspirations and expectations, following March and Simon; aspirations and expectations were normalized before their difference was calculated to compensate for differing sources of these two variables. Aspirations combine past performance and industry average performance: for firms with performance above the mean for their industry, aspirations are 1.05 times past performance (measured as ROA); for firms performing below their industry mean performance, aspirations are set equal to the industry mean performance. Expectations are measured by the mean of the earnings forecasts produced by securities analysts, originally in earnings per share and converted to ROA by multiplying by shares divided by total assets from the previous year.

Organizational decline is measured with fractional change in firm assets. Fractional change measures of assets control for size differences across firms and make the measure commensurate with other variables in the model, all of which are ratios, and reduce the likelihood of heteroskedasticity.
Fractional change in assets used as the dependent variable in the post hoc model of change in organization size.

Recoverable slack represented by selling, general and administrative expenses divided by sales. It is also described as a measure of excess expenses, and interpreted as a measure of inefficiency or of agency costs.

Potential slack represented by the debt to equity ratio (a negative relation to potential slack) and the interest coverage ratio (the ratio of income before taxes and interest charges to interest charges).
Available slack represented by the current ratio, current assets divided by current liabilities.

Measured with four items drawn from Miller (1987), reflecting the degree of price, product, technological, and competitive change perceived in the venture's principal industry. Respondents rated how well each statement described their principal industry over the last 3 years.
time_window: 3 years (or since founding for ventures less than 3 years old)

description: Measured with five newly developed items reflecting the role of government in providing financial, technology information, and manufacturing support to the ventures. One item was deleted because of its lower level of factor loading.

Measured by three items drawn from the work of McDougall et al. (1994) reflecting the growth in demand and attractiveness of the industry, rated for the principal industry over the last 3 years or since founding.
Measured as the number of full-time employees. The measure was transformed by natural log because the effect of size was expected to increase at a diminishing rate.

variable_name: R&D expenditure as percentage of sales
description: Measured by the average percentage of sales spent on R&D over the past 3 years or since founding if the venture was less than 3 years old.

Measured by six items based on the work of Bucklin and Sengupta (1993) and Magrath (1992) and the authors' field interviews. The items assessed the focal venture's cooperation with other firms in the new product development process including designing, manufacturing and marketing of new products, rated relative to competitors over the last 3 years.

The respondent indicated whether his/her firm was currently involved in any business as an agent for a foreign firm. The construct was dummy coded (0 = No and 1 = Yes). A crosscheck showed that in all 45 cases with two informants the two informants were consistent in indicating their firms' adoption of agency business activity.
Measured by the average percentage of the firm's total sales attributable to the agency business for the past 3 years or since its inception if the venture was less than 3 years old.

Measured with four market-related indicators: sales growth rate, market share growth, cash flow from market operations, and the firm's overall reputation. Respondents indicated how successfully their venture had achieved these goals relative to its established goals over the past 3 years on 5-point Likert scales.

Measured with four items drawn from Miller (1987) and Zahra and Covin (1993). The respondent was asked to compare his/her venture with its major competitors and then indicate the extent to which the venture engaged in developing and launching its own new products.

Seller-type indicator used in the OLS models on prices; artisan sellers are the sellers who independently design, produce and sell handmade products and who identify strongly with their work, while traders sell the same products without being involved in the creative production process and treat work instrumentally. In the regressions the artisan main effect is omitted and captured by the three mutually exclusive Artisan sellers x buyer category interaction terms.

Three categories of buyers role-played by six auditors: Indian-baseline buyers (non-discerning, dressed like locals), Indian-craft buyers (discerning, given handwoven cotton clothes, terracotta earrings, a handcrafted metal necklace and a handmade bag) and international buyers (discerning, foreign tourists transacting in English). The auditors' differing look, or material presentation, constituted the key aspect of the experiment treatment, and buyers were randomly assigned to sellers.

The price first quoted to a buyer before bargaining begins, recorded for each of the 455 sales transactions in the field experiment. The authors focus primarily on it because it captures the monetary value sought by a seller based simply on his appraisal of a buyer, and they call it a conservative measure because it is independent of the way in which bargaining proceeds.

The price at which the product is eventually purchased after auditors engage in up to three rounds of standardized bargaining, indicating the final economic compensation obtained for the product. It is used in models 4-6 replicating the analyses on initial price.

The mean initial price charged by traders to each buyer category in the experiment, used as the market-price benchmark against which artisans' initial and final prices are compared. The authors state that traders' initial prices are in line with each buyer category's perceived willingness to pay, with higher market prices charged to international buyers than to Indian-baseline or Indian-craft buyers.

The number of stages of production that an individual artisan engaged in himself, one of the two indicators of product attachment. Producing artisanal products involves nine distinct processes, so this variable has a range of 1 to 9; the survey showed a mean of 6.40 (standard deviation: 2.25).

A binary variable for whether artisans engaged in the color-related two stages of production that offered the most scope for creative expression, lacquering and painting. It is coded 0 for low creative engagement, when artisans do not engage in lacquering or painting, and 1 for high creative engagement, when artisans do their own lacquering and painting; the mean was .31 (standard deviation: .47).

The dependent variable, acquisition performance, is captured in the acquirer's stock price reaction to the acquisition, as measured by the cumulative abnormal return (CAR) over a specific window surrounding the event announcement. Abnormal returns are calculated using residual analysis of the market model: the baseline market model is estimated over the 241-day period [-260, -20] using the CRSP value-weighted index as the market return, and the cumulative abnormal return is the sum of daily abnormal returns over the event window. The authors obtained returns over several short and medium windows and report their findings using the 11-day [-5, +5] window.

We created the binary variable Prior Alliance, coded as 1 if the acquirer had a prior alliance with the target preceding the acquisition and 0 otherwise. Alliances represent relationships in which the firms reached a formal agreement to exchange or commit resources; if the acquirer had more than one prior alliance with the target, the earliest alliance between the partners is chosen as the focal alliance.

The binary variable Foreign Target is coded as 1 if the acquirer had a prior alliance with an international firm preceding the acquisition and 0 otherwise; because all acquirers in the study are headquartered in the United States, international targets consist of non-U.S. companies. The control-variable description states that the indicator Foreign Target is coded as 1 if the target firm is not from the United States and 0 otherwise.

We identified five types of prior alliances: R&D, marketing, supplier, licensing, and equity only, determining the type through text analysis of the press release announcing the formation of the partnership. We assigned each kind of tie an increasing strength score: 1 for equity-only, 2 for licensing, 3 for supplier, and 4 for marketing or R&D. Where firms had more than one type of alliance, we coded the alliance type that was strongest in terms of interaction between the partners.

Network churn is the percentage of the focal firm's alliance partners that change (are added or lost) from one year to the next: the number of (1) new ties formed and (2) old ties dissolved between one year and the next forms the numerator, and the total number of unique ties the focal firm had during the period is the denominator. Stability is the transformation 1 minus churn, i.e., the percentage of ties that stay the same from one year to the next. When the focal firm enters the sample for the first time, a stability score of 1 is assigned.

variable_name: Citation-weighted patent count net of self-citations
description: The focal firm i's innovation output for year t is the citation-weighted patent count of granted patents applied for in a five-year window, where each patent is weighted by its total number of citations net of self-citations. Patents are identified as pharmaceutical by converting four-digit SIC codes to technology classes using the OTAF 283 concordance, and are aggregated at the parent firm level after adjusting for name changes and mergers and acquisitions. Because the count is limited, discrete, and 15% of the count data are 0, the variable is not log transformed.
time_window: patents applied for in a five-year window (t+1 to t+5)

description: Access to structural holes is measured in three stages: first the dyadic constraint is computed using Burt's (1992) formula, then the aggregate constraint faced by the focal firm is calculated, and finally Zaheer and Bell's (2005) transformation is applied. A high score indicates exclusive access to alter firms and the measure differentiates between closed and open triads in the focal firm's ego network. The variable is mean-centered in the analysis.

The Herfindahl-Hirschman Index of the focal firm's inventive activities, calculated for each year from inventor location data on the focal firm's patents as the sum of squared fractions of the firm's patents in each country in which its inventors are present. An index value of 1 indicates that the research is concentrated in a single country; firms with missing inventor locations were assigned a score of 1, assuming no international presence. The variable is mean-centered in the analysis.

Ownership concentration was measured as the percentage of total outstanding common voting shares held by owners of 5 percent or more of each firm's common shares. These owners, known as blockholders, represent ownership concentration because they have financial incentives to monitor and control managerial actions. Blockholders were external owners only, and did not include managers, owner-directors, other insiders, or institutional holders. The percentage amount of stock held by blockholders one year prior to each sell-off was computed.
time_window: one year prior to each sell-off

description: Outsiders on the board of directors were those members with no personal or professional relationship with the firm, other than in their capacity as directors. Their equity holdings were measured as a percentage of total outstanding common voting shares. Outside director equity one year prior to each sell-off was computed.
time_window: one year prior to each sell-off

description: Corporate strategy was measured with two measures, entropy and specialization, then clustered into five strategy types. Entropy is a weighted function of the number and relative size of business segments and yields related diversification (DR), unrelated diversification (DU), and total diversification (DT); specialization was the sales of the largest 4-digit segment divided by total firm sales. Cluster analyses of these measures resulted in five corporate strategy types: single business, dominant business, related-constrained, related-linked, and unrelated businesses. The strategy types were coded in ascending order from 1 for single business to 5 for unrelated business, all data as of one year prior to each sell-off.
time_window: one year prior to each sell-off

description: The relatedness of each unit sold was determined by comparing the unit's primary business and the parent's core business at the 2-digit SIC level. Unrelated units were those whose primary business did not match the parent's core business at the 2-digit SIC level. Relatedness was represented by a dummy variable coded 1 for related units and 0 for unrelated units. Data for determining the primary industries were found in annual reports and COMPUSTAT Business Segment Tapes.
level: unit sold relative to parent firm

description: Each unit sold was measured as a percentage of the parent company's assets. This variable was computed as the total assets of the unit sold divided by the parent's total assets one year before the sell-off. Data for determining the size of units sold were found in the segment tapes of COMPUSTAT II.
level: unit sold relative to parent firm
time_window: total assets one year before the sell-off

description: Performance after the sell-off was measured as the seller's post-sell-off return on assets (ROA). This variable was computed for each of 2 years after the year of the sell-off. The 2 years were then averaged to minimize the effects of fluctuations. The seller's post-sell-off ROA data were found in COMPUSTAT II.
time_window: 2 years after the year of the sell-off, averaged

description: Environmental uncertainty and diversity were measured using scales developed by Khandwalla (1977) and refined by Miller (1988). It is a multi-item scale, and uncertainty scores run along a seven-point scale. The questions on environment were answered by the most senior vice president or general manager rather than by the CEO, in interviews in which the interviewers explained any possible ambiguities in the scales.

Environmental diversity was measured using scales developed by Khandwalla (1977) and refined by Miller (1988). It is a multi-item scale. The questions on environment were answered by the most senior vice president or general manager rather than by the CEO, in interviews in which the interviewers explained any possible ambiguities in the scales.

variable_name: Index of fit with environmental uncertainty
description: Each component of misfit is the squared difference between the standardized scores of a pair of environmental and structural variables specified by one of the fit relationships of Proposition 1. Whenever an inverse relationship was hypothesized, the original seven-point scale of the structural variable was inverted before standardization so that 1 became 7 and 2 became 6. All misfit components of Proposition 1 were summed to give a total misfit index for each firm, which was made negative to yield the index of fit, and all variables were standardized to have mean 0 and standard deviation 1. The formula block itself is not readable in the available text.

variable_name: Index of fit with environmental diversity
description: The index of fit for environmental diversity was calculated in the same way as that for uncertainty, substituting the relationships and variables of Proposition 5 for those of Proposition 1. The sample was split according to the median score for this index.

variable_name: correlations among structure and process variables
description: Internal and environmental fit are assessed using correlations among the variables of Propositions 1 to 5; internal fit is captured by the number of significant predicted relationships and by the average correlation among the structure and process variables within a group of firms. Correlation matrices were supplemented by multiple regressions that take each variable in turn as dependent and all others as independent, controlling for the linear relationships among the independent variables. The authors note that internal fit cannot be summarized in a single index because its components would be too many and too highly correlated.

Controls were assessed using the scales of Miller (1987). It is a multi-item scale, and the questions on structure were answered by the most senior vice president or general manager rather than by the CEO, in interviews.

Formalization was gauged using the abbreviated Aston scales defined by Inkson (1970). It is a multi-item scale, and the questions on structure were answered by the most senior vice president or general manager rather than by the CEO, in interviews.

Specialization was gauged using the abbreviated Aston scales defined by Inkson (1970). It is a multi-item scale, and the questions on structure were answered by the most senior vice president or general manager rather than by the CEO, in interviews.

Centralization was gauged using the abbreviated Aston scales defined by Inkson (1970), a multi-item scale answered by the most senior vice president or general manager rather than by the CEO. Centralization is not part of the structure-and-process relationships of Propositions 2 to 4; it enters the fit indices for Propositions 1 and 5, and where an inverse relationship was hypothesized its scale was inverted before standardization.

Integrative liaison devices were assessed using the scales of Miller (1987). It is a multi-item scale, and the questions on structure were answered by the most senior vice president or general manager rather than by the CEO, in interviews.

Scanning was measured using the scales of Miller (1987) and is one of the four variables reflecting the intended rationality of the decision-making process. It is a multi-item scale, and the CEO always responded to the process scales.

Analysis was measured using the scales of Miller (1987) and is one of the four variables reflecting the intended rationality of the decision-making process. It is a multi-item scale, and the CEO always responded to the process scales.

Planning was measured using the scales of Miller (1987) and is one of the four variables reflecting the intended rationality of the decision-making process. It is a multi-item scale, and the CEO always responded to the process scales.

Codification of strategy was measured using the scales of Miller (1987) and is one of the four variables reflecting the intended rationality of the decision-making process. It is a multi-item scale, and the CEO always responded to the process scales.

Dummy variable for whether a money market banker was among the firm's outside directors' principal affiliations. Representation on a firm's board was determined by tracing outside directors' principal affiliations, and the variable was coded yes if a financial institution was represented on a board in either the year borrowing took place or the preceding year.
time_window: the year borrowing took place or the preceding year

description: Dummy variable for whether an investment banker was among the firm's outside directors' principal affiliations. Representation on a firm's board was determined by tracing outside directors' principal affiliations, and the variable was coded yes if a financial institution was represented on a board in either the year borrowing took place or the preceding year.
time_window: the year borrowing took place or the preceding year

description: Dummy variable for whether a life insurance company executive was among the firm's outside directors' principal affiliations. Representation on a firm's board was determined by tracing outside directors' principal affiliations, and the variable was coded yes if a financial institution was represented on a board in either the year borrowing took place or the preceding year.
time_window: the year borrowing took place or the preceding year

description: Measured as current liabilities, or debt due in one year, divided by total assets to control for corporate size. The authors used current liabilities rather than bank notes because the former provided the only consistent data for short-term debt between firms and within firms across time, and because current liabilities include bank notes, commercial paper, bond and tax anticipation notes, warrants, and trade debt, its use provides a more conservative estimate of the hypothesized effects. The ratio was transformed to a logit to prevent out-of-range predicted values; the formula is printed as L = log_e[(d/a)/(1 - (d/a))] + 1, where d is the level of debt and a the level of assets, with the constant 1 added because the logarithm of zero is impossible (the printed formula is partly garbled in the text).
scale: logit of a ratio between 0 and 1

description: Amount of long-term public bonds issued, which are listed separately in Moody's with the date of a bond's issue and its amount. The amount was divided by total assets to control for corporate size and then transformed to a logit using the same formula as the other borrowing variables.

To calculate the amount of long-term private debt incurred in a given year, the authors subtracted the amount of long-term debt outstanding in the prior year and any new public bond issues in that year from the amount of long-term debt outstanding in the year. The result was divided by total assets to control for corporate size and transformed to a logit.
time_window: year of borrowing, with long-term debt outstanding measured in the preceding year

description: A firm's long-term debt plus current liabilities, divided by total assets. Because the numerator for the current year is a component of the dependent variables, the debt ratio was measured with a one-year lag; the other variables were measured contemporaneously.

variable_name: Money market banker, investment banker and insurance executive dummies
description: Financial institution board representation is measured by three dummies for whether a money market banker, an investment banker or a life insurance executive is among the firm's outside directors, based on directors' principal affiliations. Coded yes if represented in the borrowing year or the year before.

variable_name: Short-term borrowing, long-term public bonds and long-term private debt
description: Corporate borrowing is measured by three debt variables, each divided by total assets and transformed to a logit: short-term borrowing (current liabilities), long-term public bonds issued in the year, and new long-term private debt in the year.

Director gender is coded based on biographies of the film's first-listed director in the StudioSystem database, as well as follow-up searches of IMDb.com and Google. The variable distinguishes the female-directed films in the sample from the male-directed ones; the data include 1,343 male-directed films and 71 female-directed films.

Operationalized based on the similarity between the focal film and prior films with respect to the combination of both primary and secondary genre descriptors. A similarity score divides the number of prior films with the same primary-secondary genre combination by the total films released in the industry, which yielded a range of 0 to 8.6% conventionality; this measure was then inverted by subtracting all values from 1 to generate a measure of unconventionality, which was standardized to aid interpretation in the moderation tests.
scale: standardized; original conventionality score ranged 0 to 8.6%
time_window: prior films released in the industry up to the focal film's release

description: Audience ratings from IMDb.com (the Internet Movie Database) employed as a measure of mass market appeal. The measure ranges from 0 to 10.
Metacritic.com's Metascore, which aggregates and weights critic ratings from an array of reputable sources. The measure ranges from 0 to 100.
The total number of a film's award nominations and 'wins' for all award contests listed in StudioSystem's database, used as a measure of peer certifications.

Indicator of whether a given firm in the Korea Labor Institute sample was a majority-owned multinational affiliate. The authors contrasted it with a variable representing Korean-controlled firms whose cash-flow rights were largely owned by foreigners, which isolates the importance of foreign managerial control.

Percentage of women among chajangs (deputy general managers), an upper-middle-management position in which women had recently begun to make significant inroads. The authors also use an indicator for whether the firm had at least one female chajang and the percentage of women in the more mid-level gwajang position; women are rare in more senior management positions.

Firm-level indicators of whether the firm had implemented maternity leave, opened a workplace childcare facility, and provided two forms of financial support for childcare by 2005. The Korea Labor Institute data also record whether health-care coverage exceeded the legal requirement, whether the firm subsidized cultural, athletic, and recreational expenses, whether it provided a work leisure program, and whether it subsidized commuting expenses.

Return on assets, defined as operating profit divided by total assets, and winsorized at the 1st and 99th percentiles. It is the main dependent variable in the profitability models, which include company fixed effects.

Indicator distinguishing foreign-owned companies from non-foreign-owned companies using the ownership categories specified by KWDI. As in the Korea Labor Institute data, the foreign-owned companies were managerially controlled affiliates of foreign multinationals.

Representation of women among bujangs (general managers), the level of upper-middle management at which the firms in the KWDI sample differentiate themselves, whereas the Korea Labor Institute data differentiate firms at the chajang level. Every firm in the KWDI sample had at least one female manager.
Indicator of whether the firm had implemented a nursing holiday, which the authors describe as regular time off for new mothers.

Return on assets, defined as the ratio of operating profit to total assets, winsorized at the 1st and 99th percentiles to deal with a few extreme cases. An alternative dependent variable was operating margin, defined as operating profit divided by total sales and multiplied by 100, winsorized at the same percentiles.

Count of prior transparent OPEB curtailments among firms in the focal firm's proximity network, updated over time as prior adopters of that format accumulate. A transparent adoption is a cut, i.e., the ceasing of benefit provision for some or all of the company's current or future retirees. Separate counts were constructed for each network: proximal competitors (firms sharing the focal firm's employment region and/or two-digit SIC industry), firms connected by board interlocks, and firms retaining the same benefits consulting firm.
time_window: cumulative prior adoptions; time-varying variables lagged one year

description: Count of prior opaque OPEB curtailments among firms in the focal firm's proximity network, updated over time as prior adopters of that format accumulate. An opaque adoption is a cap, i.e., an announced ceiling on the dollar contribution of the firm (usually per retiree) paid toward retiree benefits, above which retirees are responsible for paying the difference. Separate counts were constructed for proximal competitors, firms connected by board interlocks, and firms retaining the same benefits consulting firm.
time_window: cumulative prior adoptions; time-varying variables lagged one year

description: The company's initial decision to adopt OPEB curtailment, coded 1 in the year of the first recorded OPEB event and 0 otherwise; competing-risks models predict transparent and opaque adoption separately. Candidate events were identified by searching full-text annual financial statements for actuarial keywords near OPEB terms, by using a proprietary database to find years with large curtailment gains and unrecognized prior service costs, and by searching a full-text news database for articles in which retiree benefits were being reduced or eliminated. Events were then verified and coded for year and type by reading the relevant SEC filing footnote text.

Total newspaper article count for a company's OPEB curtailment event, based on a full-text news database covering national and local newspapers. To be counted, the article had to make specific mention of the OPEB event in connection with that company, and the overall focus of the article had to be on retiree benefits. Each company was assigned a total article count if media coverage was found, and 0 otherwise.

Each company was coded 1 if a retiree interest group existed, or 0 otherwise. Groups were identified from the National Retiree Legal Network, supplemented by an online search for websites of retirees from each company in the sample, which yielded few additional groups.

Links between each company in the sample and each of the ten largest advisory services firms providing benefits consulting, based on payment for services related to employee or retiree health benefits reported in ERISA 5500 Large Plan Schedule C filings; where a company had more than one plan, payment relating to any of those plans counted as a connection. These linkages formed the basis for a set of proximity ties among companies that shared the same consulting firm. Ties were obtained for three years and applied to surrounding periods.

The BEA collects information on product transfers to and from both parents and affiliates, including both intermediate and final products, and the author aggregated product inflows and outflows to and from affiliated operations in other countries and scaled the measure by total subsidiary sales. More specifically, the measure is the ratio of the sum of total exports to the parent firm, plus total imports from the parent firm, plus total exports to other third-country affiliates, divided by the total sales of the foreign operation. The measure is lagged one year.

Binary dependent variable at the foreign operation level indicating whether the foreign operation has new multicountry collaborative patents. Multicountry collaborative patents are foreign patents granted to U.S. MNCs that have inventors from more than one country; patents that are not categorized as collaborative may include more than one inventor but have all inventors from the same country. The outcome equation is estimated jointly with a first-stage equation whose dependent variable is whether the foreign operation does foreign R&D, to limit selection bias.

Dependent variable at the foreign patent level with three categories based on the proportion of country inventors on each firm patent: (1) noncollaborative single country foreign patents; (2) collaborative multicountry patents with U.S. inventors (parent-subsidiary collaborations); and (3) collaborative multicountry patents with no U.S. inventors (subsidiary-subsidiary collaborations). Noncollaborative single country foreign inventor patents occur most frequently and are the base category.

Hall et al.'s (2001) measure of originality, essentially a measure of technological diversity considering backward patent citations; the defining formula is not readable in this text. The measure is based on the proportion of citations made to patents in each technology class, so higher values indicate more diffuse backward citations of technology classes and a wider array of technologies used in the innovation. The author weighted this measure by the average originality measure for all patents in the same primary technology class.

The author examined the ratio of forward self-citations to total citations for each foreign patent. Cited patents are a technological antecedent of the citing patent, and future MNC patents that cite the focal patent are considered to be extending and further developing this firm knowledge.

Four questionnaire items on a 7-point Likert scale asked whether one of the company's objectives of forming the joint venture was to learn specific skills and competencies held by the Chinese partner, to learn more about how to do business in China, to learn or improve the skills of inter-firm cooperation in a joint venture setting, and to learn or improve the skills of managing overseas operations. The first indicator was dropped from further analysis because its loading did not exceed 0.7, so the measure used in the structural model consists of the remaining three items. The construct was modelled with reflective indicators and its internal consistency and Cronbach's alpha were above 0.8.

Four questionnaire items on a 7-point Likert scale asked whether one of the company's objectives of forming the joint venture was to learn specific skills and competencies held by the Chinese partner, to learn more about how to do business in China, to learn or improve the skills of inter-firm cooperation in a joint venture setting, and to learn or improve the skills of managing overseas operations. The first indicator was dropped from further analysis because its loading did not exceed 0.7, so the measure used in the structural model consists of the remaining three items. The construct was modelled with reflective indicators and its internal consistency and Cronbach's alpha were above 0.8.

A joint venture's sales revenue, profit, strategic position and product market potential were used as indicators of its strategic importance, supplemented by one item asking the respondent to assess the overall importance of the venture. All five items were answered on a 7-point Likert scale. The construct was modelled with reflective indicators.

A joint venture's sales revenue, profit, strategic position and product market potential were used as indicators of its strategic importance, supplemented by one item asking the respondent to assess the overall importance of the venture. All five items were answered on a 7-point Likert scale. The construct was modelled with reflective indicators.

Five indicators measured on a 7-point Likert scale. The first two concern the amount of executive time and attention committed by the parent to the joint venture and the attention paid by the parent to evaluating the written operational reports submitted by the venture. The next two concern the frequency of visits to the venture by senior management and the frequency of communication between the venture and the parent, similar to the two items used by Inkpen (1992). The last item assesses whether staff assigned to the venture are encouraged to share their experience with colleagues in the parent. The construct was modelled with reflective indicators.

Five indicators measured on a 7-point Likert scale. The first two concern the amount of executive time and attention committed by the parent to the joint venture and the attention paid by the parent to evaluating the written operational reports submitted by the venture. The next two concern the frequency of visits to the venture by senior management and the frequency of communication between the venture and the parent, similar to the two items used by Inkpen (1992). The last item assesses whether staff assigned to the venture are encouraged to share their experience with colleagues in the parent. The construct was modelled with reflective indicators.

The parent's involvement in managing details of eight functional areas of the joint venture, each rated by the respondent on a 7-point Likert scale. The first seven areas are generally applicable to a manufacturing operation; the last, dealing with Chinese government bodies, is specific to the Chinese context. The construct was treated as a composite of the scores assigned to the eight functional areas, i.e. as having formative indicators.

The parent's involvement in managing details of eight functional areas of the joint venture, each rated by the respondent on a 7-point Likert scale. The first seven areas are generally applicable to a manufacturing operation; the last, dealing with Chinese government bodies, is specific to the Chinese context. The construct was treated as a composite of the scores assigned to the eight functional areas, i.e. as having formative indicators.

The extent to which the parent has learned from the joint venture experience in nine areas, each rated on a 7-point Likert scale. These nine areas reflect the three types of knowledge examined: the first indicator refers to the outcome of vicarious learning (skills and competencies held by the Chinese partner), the second, third and fourth indicators concern managing the joint venture itself, and the remaining indicators refer to the knowledge and skills of doing business in China. The construct was modelled with formative indicators.

The extent to which the parent has learned from the joint venture experience in nine areas, each rated on a 7-point Likert scale. These nine areas reflect the three types of knowledge examined: the first indicator refers to the outcome of vicarious learning (skills and competencies held by the Chinese partner), the second, third and fourth indicators concern managing the joint venture itself, and the remaining indicators refer to the knowledge and skills of doing business in China. The construct was modelled with formative indicators.
Estimated by subtracting the year of formation of the joint venture from the year of survey (1996 for the Singapore survey).
Estimated by subtracting the year of formation of the joint venture from the year of survey (1997 for the Hong Kong survey).
One item in the questionnaire asks respondents to indicate the years of experience that their firms have in managing manufacturing operations in China.
One item in the questionnaire asks respondents to indicate the years of experience that their firms have in managing manufacturing operations in China.

Dichotomous variable coded '1' for years in which a company responded to CDP's questionnaire and permitted its response to be posted on CDP's Web site, and '0' otherwise. It was coded based on data from CDP's Web site and a report compiling these data (RiskMetrics Group, 2007). The database lists both the companies that publicly disclosed and those that declined to do so.

Dichotomous variable coded '1' when a firm had been targeted by at least one environmental shareholder resolution in a given year, and '0' if it had not been targeted by any environmental shareholder resolutions that year. Data came from the KLD Research & Analytics SOCRATES database on resolutions on climate change, environmental disclosure, and other environmental issues filed by members of the Interfaith Center on Corporate Responsibility. Because targeting a particular firm was rare, the variable was coded '1' if a firm was targeted by at least one shareholder resolution in the past two years.
time_window: past two years (one- and two-year lags)

variable_name: number of shareholder resolutions targeting others in the industry
description: The total number of environmental shareholder actions filed against all other firms that shared the focal firm's primary two-digit Standard Industrial Classification code in a given year, based on KLD SOCRATES data. The variable is based on one- and two-year lags.
time_window: prior two years (one- and two-year lags)

variable_name: state posing regulatory threat and sector likely targeted
description: Dichotomous variable coded '1' for companies headquartered in states posing a regulatory threat (charter members of the Regional Greenhouse Gas Initiative, states joining the Western Climate Initiative, and California in 2006) and in industrial sectors likely to be targeted by these regulations, starting the year the state joined either RGGI or WCI, and in 2006 for California; otherwise coded '0'. For RGGI states the only targeted sector was electric utilities; for WCI states the targeted sectors were expected to include electric utilities and most alternative plans also targeted the transportation sector and large sources of stationary combustion including oil refining, cement manufacturing, pulp and paper manufacturing, and hydrogen production.

variable_name: state posing regulatory threat but sector unlikely targeted
description: Dichotomous variable coded '1' for companies headquartered in states posing a regulatory threat but in other industrial sectors, starting the year the state joined either RGGI or WCI, and in 2006 for California; otherwise coded '0'. This variable measures general deterrence effects.

Stock market reaction was measured with standard event study methodology as the cumulative abnormal return, the cumulative difference between a firm's actual return and its expected return over the event window. Market model parameters were estimated over a 255-day period starting 46 days prior to the adoption announcement, using the CRSP value-weighted market index as the market proxy. Results are reported for a three-day event window (t-1 to t+1). The event date is the first public announcement date of poison pill adoption as it appears in PR Newswire and/or Business Wire.
time_window: three-day event window (t-1 to t+1); 255-day estimation period starting 46 days prior to the announcement

description: A dummy variable coded 1 if an announcement statement either pointed to the gains to be realized by shareholders following adoption or assured that the adoption does not close off possible advancements. Three business school graduate students (one being the first author) performed the content analysis of the adoption press releases, with good interrater reliability (Cohen's kappa = .84).

A dummy variable coded 1 if any statement in the announcement explicitly emphasized that the poison pill was designed to prevent negative outcomes or to ensure fair treatment in the event of a takeover. Coded from the same content analysis of the adoption press releases by three coders.

A dummy variable coded 1 when a dual CEO/chair is quoted in the firm's press release announcing the poison pill adoption. Data on framing by the dual CEO/chair were collected directly from the press releases by identifying who was quoted in the announcement.

The total number of times that a frame articulator was mentioned in the media during the one-year period prior to poison pill adoption. Data were collected by entering the name of the frame articulator into the LexisNexis database. Media sources were limited to five business publications that cover the entire sample period.
time_window: one-year period prior to poison pill adoption

description: Prior firm performance was operationalized using return on equity (ROE), which captures the efficiency with which shareholders' investments are managed, aligning it with the standard concerns of agency theory.

The number of recent adoptions was operationalized as the natural log of the total number of poison pill adoptions in the previous year. Data on the number of poison pill adoptions were collected from SDC Platinum.

Number of new branches opened in each year in each market (county) by each bank. For any given bank-year pair, the raw data files of the PME database provide one line for each specific branch, with an attached time-constant number, including address information; comparing the files for each pair of successive years enables the identification of new branches. The information is based on compulsory data provided by the firms to a governmental body and was confirmed with the APB yearly reports on bank branching.

variable_name: market attractiveness relative to the market reference point
description: Difference between a market's attractiveness and a focal firm's market reference point, both at time t-1. To distinguish situations where market attractiveness is above versus below firms' market reference point, the authors use two spline variables with a knot at 0: one for cases where attractiveness is equal to or above the reference point and one for cases where attractiveness is below the reference point. For table presentation the two spline variables were rescaled.

Composite index of three accounting-based proxies, standardized and summed: potential slack measured by the equity-to-assets ratio, recoverable slack measured by the ratio of general and administrative expenses to revenues, and available slack measured by the deposits-to-credit ratio. The choice of the three components follows Bourgeois and Singh's distinction between potential, recoverable and available slack.

Difference between the focal firm's performance and its aspiration level at time t-1. Performance is measured by return on assets at time t-1; the historical aspiration proxy is the firm's performance at time t-2 and the social aspiration proxy is industry median performance at time t-2. The aspiration level equals the social aspiration level when the firm's historical performance is below the social aspiration level, and equals 1.05 times the historical aspiration level when historical performance is at or above the social aspiration level. Two spline variables with a knot at 0 were constructed: performance relative to aspirations >= 0 and performance relative to aspirations < 0.

Market (county) population multiplied by market per-capita income and divided by the supply component. Market population is the number of workers engaged in professional activity within the focal county; market per-capita income is proxied by the 1989 average wage earned by workers within each county; the supply component is the total number of branches of competing banks in each county plus 1. The ratio captures the potential demand available for each branch.

Weighted average of market attractiveness at time t-1 for all markets where the focal firm already had branches, the weights being the proportions of the number of branches held by the focal firm in each market in relation to the firm's total number of branches. It represents the firm's status quo and is computed using the same subset of attributes as market attractiveness.

variable_name: EHC (share of employees with prior entrepreneurial experience)
description: Share of the firm's employees who have previously been entrepreneurs. Each employee's entrepreneurial experience is calculated from labor market records dating back to 1993; an individual is defined as an entrepreneur in the labor market records if they have owned an incorporated business, and sole proprietors are excluded. For each firm, the number of current employees who have previously been entrepreneurs is aggregated to obtain the firm-level EHC share.
time_window: experience traced back to 1993; firm-year observations 1997-2016

description: Dichotomous variable that takes the value 1 if the firm discontinues in t+1 and 0 otherwise. The exit variable encompasses both true failures and those who choose to discontinue, even if not strictly pushed out of the market through liquidation. Exits through mergers and acquisitions are excluded.

Dummy variables that equal 1 in the crisis years, focused on two large-scale macroeconomic shocks: the IT crisis of 2001 to 2003 and the Great Recession of 2008 to 2009. A uniform dummy for both crisis periods is used in some specifications, and separate dummies for each crisis in others; the crisis dummies are interacted with EHC.

variable_name: EHC long experience / EHC short-experience; total entrepreneurial years
description: Entrepreneurial experience is traced back to 1993 in the individual records and employees' total years of entrepreneurship are aggregated for each firm. One version separates the share of former entrepreneurs with more than five years of experience from those with fewer than five years. Alternatively, the accumulated number of years of experience of former entrepreneurs is used as a direct measure of EHC, and this total is also divided by the number of former entrepreneurs.

Firm size is measured by the number of employees; the natural logarithm of total employees is included among the control variables in the estimations. The marginal effect of EHC is plotted across the size distribution of the new ventures to test whether the relationship varies with organizational size.

Shares of former entrepreneurs whose entrepreneurial experience was obtained within the same related two-digit industry as opposed to unrelated sectors. These measures capture the industry-specificity of former entrepreneurs' knowledge base.

Shares of former entrepreneurs whose entrepreneurial endeavors occurred in high- or low-technology industries, capturing differences in technological background. New ventures are categorized into high-tech firms, that is, high-technology manufacturing or knowledge-intensive service industries according to the Eurostat definition, and all remaining firms.

variable_name: EHC Higher Educated / EHC Less Educated
description: Former entrepreneurs are categorized, using individual-level register data, into those having three or more years of tertiary education (highly educated) and the rest (less educated).

The focal independent variable is the firm-level proxy for intrinsic speed capabilities. The authors first estimate Regression Equation 1 by OLS, take the residual for each project as project speed, then compute the mean and standard deviation of speed for all projects in each industry i at time t and standardize each project speed observation. The firm measure is the average of the standardized speed of all projects completed at time t by firm j across all industries, which the authors say mitigates the influence of randomness and nonsystemic factors in the residual. The measure is reverse coded so that positive values indicate greater intrinsic speed.

Firm j's performance at time t is measured by Tobin's q, the ratio of a firm's market value to replacement costs of tangible assets. Market value is proxied by the sum of market value of equity, book value of preferred stock, book value of long-term debt, and current liabilities less current assets. Replacement costs of tangible assets are measured as total assets less current assets and intangibles, plus the book value of inventory.

Blockholding is the percentage of common stock held by institutional investors owning at least 5 percent of a company's outstanding common stock. The authors obtain it by averaging quarterly institutional ownership data from Thomson Financial 13F Filings for each firm-year in the oil dataset. They argue that larger stockholders can better monitor and control a company using the voting rights associated with their holding.

Leverage is measured as long-term debt over total assets. The authors state that leverage directly affects unobserved heterogeneity in firm discount rates: debt erodes firm value more for firms facing greater liquidity constraints and a higher external cost of capital, and these firms also typically have a higher discount rate.

R&D intensity is measured as firms' R&D expenditures over total assets. The authors state that the variable captures innovation effort and that q will be higher the greater a firm's R&D efficacy, so the covariance of its random coefficient with the speed coefficient is interpreted as the value a firm draws from its R&D investment.

Project development time is the lag between the start and end dates of plant development reported in the Oil and Gas Journal, reported in months. The official start (end) date is assumed to be the date on which the project is first (last) reported in the OGJ minus (plus) 90 days, because the OGJ reports each project's status only twice per year; where an expected completion date was reported, that date is taken as the official end date. In Regression Equation 1 the authors use a discounted transformation of time-to-build, where T is the measure of time-to-build in months and r is the industry discount rate.

The residual of Regression Equation 1 at the project level, used as the building block of the firm-level speed proxy; a negative (positive) residual means the firm completed the facility faster (slower) than the industry average after controlling for project type, location, and time fixed effects.

Treatment dummy coded one for SMOs that had primarily collaborative interactions with oil and gas firms in the three years preceding the Horizon spill and zero otherwise. Treatment groups were assigned from the coded archival media data on SMO-firm interactions. There are 15 collaborative treated SMOs.

Treatment dummy coded one if the SMO had primarily contentious interactions with oil and gas firms in the three years preceding the Horizon spill and zero otherwise. Contentious treated SMOs had an average of 2.8 contentious interactions with oil and gas firms before the spill. There are 33 contentious treated SMOs.

Log of an SMO's annual total contributions, collected from the annual form 990 tax filings in the NCCS archival database. Measured for each of the five tax years before and after the spill (2005 to 2009 and 2011 to 2015), omitting the tax year in which the spill occurred. Contributions are logged to correct for a pronounced skew resulting from the varying size of SMOs in the sample.

Number of collaborative interactions an SMO has with any firm in the 500-firm sample, calculated as quarterly sums from the archival media data collection. The quarter that includes the Horizon spill (April to June 2010) is excluded to ensure temporal precedence, and interactions with BP are excluded so that the analysis is not driven by reductions in collaborations with BP itself.
time_window: quarterly, 10 quarters before and after the spill

description: Indicator that equals one if period t occurs after the Horizon spill and zero otherwise; the period is a year in the analysis of contributions and a quarter (three months) in the analysis of collaborations.

Respondents rated the current CEO (sometimes themselves) and the ideal CEO for the Year 2000 on 11 areas of expertise using a 5-point forced-choice scaling system, and on 15 CEO behaviors using a 5-point Likert-type scale. Absolute differences between current and ideal ratings were summed and divided by the number of items in each set; the two scores were averaged together (r = 0.40, p < 0.001) and subtracted from 4.00, the largest possible average difference, to obtain the Leadership CSQ score.
scale: 5-point item scales; composite score = 4.00 minus average absolute difference

description: The basis was two sets of questionnaire items: competitive weapons/edge (11 items) and growth strategies (7 items), both scaled with a forced-choice system in which the three more important and three less important items were selected and scored. Average absolute differences between ratings of current and ideal future strategies were calculated for each of the two sets, the two were averaged together (r = 0.37, p < 0.001), and that average was subtracted from 4.00.
scale: 5-point forced-choice item scores; composite score = 4.00 minus average absolute difference

description: Based on the question 'How long have you been employed by this company?' asked of the respondent at the end of the questionnaire.
Based on the question 'How long have you worked in your current industry?'. The authors also create an 'Additional Tenure in the Industry' variable, industry tenure minus organizational tenure.

Derived from responses to a 4-point item: 'How would you describe the profitability of your firm?' 1 = unprofitable, 2 = breaking even, 3 = moderately profitable, 4 = very profitable. The authors used this subjective approach instead of more precise quantitative indicators so that respondents would not have to engage in any file searches.
scale: 4-point item from 1 = unprofitable to 4 = very profitable
level: firm, as rated by the responding executive

description: Because the multiple determinants of discretion do not necessarily covary, the discretion proposition was examined through two subsamples selected to represent the extremes of industry discretion. High-discretion environments were represented by foods/beverages, computing equipment, and scientific/measuring equipment (n = 44); low-discretion environments by public utilities, natural resources, and telecommunications services (n = 70).

A dummy variable for acquisition strategy. If an acquisition is categorized as a 'product extension merger' (i.e., related acquisition) by the FTC Large Merger Series, the variable 'related acquisition' was coded '1.' If classified as an 'other conglomerate merger' (i.e., unrelated acquisition), it was coded '0.'

Three-year average returns on assets (ROA) of the primary 3-digit SIC industry of an acquiring firm from the Compustat tape, covering the last full pre-acquisition fiscal year and the two preceding years. The profitability measure was converted to a profitability premium by subtracting from each profitability in year t the average ROA of all industrial firms in the Compustat tape in the same year.
time_window: 3-year average covering the last full pre-acquisition fiscal year and the two preceding years

description: Industry-adjusted firm profitability, obtained by subtracting industry average profitability from (absolute) firm profitability, measured as the 3-year average ROA covering the last full pre-acquisition fiscal year and the 2 preceding years. The measure was converted to a profitability premium by subtracting from each profitability in year t the average ROA of all industrial firms in the Compustat tape in the same year.
time_window: 3-year average covering the last full pre-acquisition fiscal year and the two preceding years

description: The firm's export sales to its foreign subsidiaries and to existing long-term customers were first subtracted from its total export sales, and the resulting value was divided by the firm's total export sales. The resulting value is the proportion of the firm's export sales that was newly developed to cope with the sudden downturn of the Korean economy. Total firm exports and export sales to existing long-term customers come from the auditor reports.
time_window: 1998 in the crisis period; 1997 in the stability period

description: Intrafirm trade is measured as the total of all the transactions (both sales and purchase) among foreign subsidiaries and between subsidiaries and headquarters in Korea in a given year; transactions among domestic subsidiaries were dropped. The measure is the change in intrafirm sales from the previous period to the focal period: (intrafirm sales in 1997 - intrafirm sales in 1996)/intrafirm sales in 1996, and (1998 - 1997)/1997. The location of subsidiaries was determined from company homepages, company news and affiliate/country information.
time_window: one-year change (1996-1997 for the 1997 measure; 1997-1998 for the 1998 measure)

description: Calculated for 1997-1998 in the manner suggested by Chung and Pruitt (1994) as the market value of common stock plus the book value of preferred stock plus the book value of debt, divided by the book value of total assets. The market value of common stock is calculated as the year-end share price multiplied by the number of shares outstanding.

Indicator distinguishing executives who received a first-time appointment to a board of directors from counterfactual executives without board appointments; in the promotion models Model 2 adds 'any certification' and Model 3 adds the specific inside and outside board appointment variables, with executives without board appointments as the omitted group.

Dummy variable taking a value of '1' for executives promoted to the board at their employer. The reference category consisted of the counterfactual executives, who received values of '0' on this binary measure.

Dummy variable taking a value of '1' for executives promoted to boards at companies other than their employers. The reference category consisted of the counterfactual executives, who received values of '0' on this binary measure.

Binary variable that took a value of '1' if promotion to CEO occurred that year and '0' otherwise. Executives' careers were tracked in Execucomp for five years following their initial inclusion in the sample, and only promotions to CEO at S&P 1500 firms were counted; testing began in the second year after matching.

Binary variable that took a value of '1' when the executive was promoted to CEO at his or her company and '0' otherwise, estimated in multinomial logit models relative to the omitted no-promotion category.

Binary variable that took a value of '1' when the executive was promoted to CEO at a firm other than his or her employing firm in t-1 and '0' otherwise, estimated in multinomial logit models relative to the omitted no-promotion category.

Captures whether the executive experienced a promotion in title above his or her current position, using two levels of promotion. An executive who was not a COO, CFO, or president and who moved into any of these positions in t+1 was coded as '1', and an executive who was a COO or CFO in t and was promoted to president in t+1 was assigned '1'; executives were removed from the risk group when promoted to CEO, creating a single measure of title promotions prior to CEO promotion.

Measured using the TDC1 variable in Execucomp, which includes the total value of an executive's salary, bonus, long-term incentive payouts, stock grants, option grants, and other income in a given year. Pay was measured following the first year an executive potentially joined a board (i.e., t+1) and was log transformed to lessen the influence of extreme observations.
Dichotomous variable coded one if a given commercial bank is lead manager on a particular bond issue (a firm/bank dyad is realized) and zero otherwise.

Binary variable indicating the presence (coded one) or absence (coded zero) of market ties in commercial banking, based on whether or not a given bank helped arrange syndicated loans for a firm in the previous five years.
