scale: 1 = only common symptoms to 5 = included highly uncommon, distant symptoms

description: Two experienced coders from the training program rated the formulations strategists generated in terms of novelty from 1 = not at all novel to 7 = highly novel; these coders were different from the coders who evaluated symptom distance. The final measure is the average novelty rating across the two evaluators; ICC(1) for agreement = .81 and ICC(2) for reliability = .90.
scale: 1 = not at all novel to 7 = highly novel

description: Categorical variable coded 1 if the participant was in the rational-analytic thinking condition during the attention allocation phase and 0 otherwise. Participants in this condition were instructed to analyze and reflect on the case, not to rely on intuition or first impression, to carefully appraise and rationally evaluate the situation, and to remain objective and avoid being influenced by personal feelings or emotions. Manipulation checks used three items averaged on a 1 = Strongly Disagree to 5 = Strongly Agree scale, and the manipulations were successful.

Categorical variable coded 1 if the participant was in the intuition condition during the judgment phase and 0 otherwise. Participants in this condition were instructed to trust their intuition about the situation and evaluate it based on their gut feelings, and to be open to their 'gut instinct' reactions. Manipulation checks used three items averaged on a 1 = Strongly Disagree to 5 = Strongly Agree scale.

Two coders familiar with the case study and blind to the hypotheses evaluated the degree to which distant symptoms were identified during the attention allocation phase on a Likert scale from 1 = only common symptoms to 5 = included highly uncommon, distant symptoms. The final measure is the average of the coders' ratings; ICC(1) for agreement = .74 and ICC(2) for reliability = .85.
scale: 1 = only common symptoms to 5 = included highly uncommon, distant symptoms

description: Two new coders who were not involved in other ratings and were unaware of the hypotheses rated the formulations strategists generated from 1 = not at all novel to 5 = highly novel, using the coding scheme described in the Online Appendix. The final measure of Novelty is the average of the ratings of the two coders; ICC(1) for agreement = .74 and ICC(2) for reliability = .85.
scale: 1 = not at all novel to 5 = highly novel

description: The only independent variable in the models, a time period variable representing the change over time of the rate at which firms lose superior profitability positions. Hypothesis 1 was represented in the model by this variable. The corporate event history models were also estimated with non-linear time axes, but the effect in these samples proved to be linear, so only the linear models are reported.
Time period variable in the business-unit event history models; the models at the industry, corporate and SBU levels were estimated with non-linear time axes.

Net income divided by total assets for firms, selected primarily for comparability with earlier economic and strategic management research in this area. A rolling 5-year window was used for all measures. ROA was one of the two measures used to operationalize economic performance.

The ratio of firm market value to the replacement cost of its assets, operationalized as the ratio of market value to the book value of assets; the authors state this ratio has been shown to be not only empirically but also theoretically equivalent to Tobin's q. It was selected as a market measure because results have been shown to vary between accounting and market measures, and because it enhances comparability with earlier work.
Segment net income divided by identifiable assets for business units. A rolling 5-year window was used for all measures.

Superior economic performance was determined with the Iterative Kolmogorov-Smirnov technique, which stratifies time-series data into statistically significantly different levels of performance; the number of strata was compressed in each period to three by creating supersets above and below the modal stratum. Firms remaining in the superior stratum for six or more windows (a 10-year period) were treated as having achieved persistent superior economic performance. The dependent variable in the event history models is the hazard that a firm exits the superior performance stratum, estimated with discrete time maximum likelihood models.

Business units were stratified relative to all business units, or all industries, or all firms, and for the business unit-level data 5 years (one window) was used to define persistent superior performance to enhance comparability with McNamara et al. (2003). Event history models estimated the hazard of exiting the superior performance stratum at the industry, corporate and SBU levels of the segment data.

variable_name: Incidence of the superior-not superior-superior performance pattern
description: For both performance measures the incidence of the pattern superior performance, then modal or below performance, then superior performance was noted in each three-period window as the window was rolled through the 24 periods in the study. These numbers were subjected to a 2 x 2 contingency analysis comparing the incidence and non-incidence of the pattern in the first and last 10 three-period windows of the study, using the likelihood ratio chi-square test of association.

The overall samples were divided into 'high-tech' industries (SIC codes 357x, 365x, 3661, 3674, 481x, and 7372) and 'low-tech' industries (all other SIC codes). In a second approach the 40 industry samples were aggregated to the 1-digit SIC level, yielding seven 1-digit industries.

variable_name: Shortening of persistent superior performance over time (period effect on exit hazard)
description: Hypercompetition is inferred from a decrease over time in the duration of persistent superior economic performance, measured with ROA and Tobin's q. It is tested through the time period variable in the discrete-time event history models of the hazard that a firm or business unit exits the superior performance stratum. For H2 the models are estimated separately for high-tech and low-tech industries and for seven 1-digit SIC groups, and hypercompetition is taken to be present wherever the period effect shows a shortening.
scale: Period coefficient in event history models of exit from the superior stratum

description: Counts the number of different renewable electricity technology trade groups each firm was a member of in each year from 2000 to 2010. The data were hand collected by contacting the five main renewable electricity technology trade groups for their membership rosters, covering technologies mandated by the federal and state RPSs or already in use by firms. A greater number signifies search for a greater variety of renewable electricity technologies, consistent with the concept of technological search breadth.

Coded 1 for 2002 and after because the federal government attempted to pass a national renewable portfolio standard in 2002, which is treated as the activation of the remote problem; the variable is 0 in 2000 and 2001.

Coded 0 in the years before the state in which a firm was operating passed a Renewable Portfolio Standard and 1 beginning with the year of passage and thereafter. States that never adopted RPSs were effects-coded as -1 to distinguish underlying differences between states.

Total megawatts of renewable electricity that each firm generated in the prior year, summed across all renewable sources, with a greater generation output signifying a higher level of technological capabilities. The variable captures the cumulative expertise that each electric utility has with generating renewable electricity and is built from archival information about the company found in Platts.

One of three survey questions concerning profitability, sales growth, and overall financial performance over the most recent three fiscal years, answered by the CEO. The profitability measure was employed as the dependent variable in this study.

Deviation score measure: all firms were ranked on structural integration and differentiation, and the correlation between profitability and the absolute value of the firms' rank differences was observed, so that a larger rank difference represents a poorer fit. Structural differentiation is a function of organizational dispersion and complexity measured with 11 survey items, and structural integration measured the extent to which firms use various rules, operating procedures and other integration devices.

A multiplicative interaction term of organizational size and structural formalization. The joint effect on profitability was measured by the partial correlation between profitability and the interaction term, from which the economic set and the main effects of the interaction variables had been partialled. Firm size was measured by the natural logarithm of the number of full-time employees; structural formalization is an abridged Aston scale.

A multiplicative interaction term of organizational size and formal planning comprehensiveness. The joint effect on profitability was measured by the partial correlation between profitability and the interaction term, with the economic set and the main effects of the interaction variables partialled. Planning comprehensiveness was measured by CEO ratings of 11 statements about the firm's strategy-making processes on a scale of 0 to 5, grouped into goal-setting, scanning and analysis.

A multiplicative interaction term of industry stability and structural formalization. Industry stability was captured by a dichotomous industry variable (apparel industry = 0, furniture industry = 1), with the furniture industry selected as stable and the apparel industry as unstable. The joint effect on profitability was measured by the partial correlation between profitability and the interaction term, with the economic set and the main effects of the interaction variables partialled.

A multiplicative interaction term of industry stability and formal planning comprehensiveness, industry stability being captured by the dichotomous industry variable (apparel industry = 0, furniture industry = 1). The joint effect on profitability was measured by the partial correlation between profitability and the interaction term, with the economic set and the main effects of the interaction variables partialled.

An abridged version of the original locus of control scale designed by Rotter (1966), which its developer designed as an additive rather than a correlative measure. CEOs indicated on a scale of 0 to 5 the accuracy of five statements concerning their own values and attitudes, anchored at either extreme with 'Very Accurate' and 'Not at all Accurate'.

A dummy variable that is equal to 1 when at least one release of firm i is released as a single in year t and is otherwise 0. The authors use a dummy rather than a continuous variable because the expected quality of the most promising outside option critically depends on whether firm i produces at least one single.
The number of new artists (i.e., new-to-the-world artists) in music firm i at year t. It serves as the dependent variable for the variation generation stage.

The number of new artists, who were given the chance of producing an initial release by firm i in year t, who rank in the top 20% in terms of lifetime popularity but experienced failure with their first release (which was not included in the top 10% of popular songs) and then moved to another firm to produce their subsequent release(s). The cutoffs (top 20% lifetime popularity and top 10% song popularity) are based on the author's interview with a former EMI producer. Lifetime popularity scores come from the Spotify Echo Nest API and song popularity scores from the Spotify Web API, matched to MusicBrainz using recording code ids, song names and artists' names.

variable_name: Performance target for selection and retention
description: The popularity of the most popular song in the first release (i.e., single or album) of the new artists who were not given second chances from the same firm. It is used as the dependent variable in the test of the mechanism behind the omission errors.

A multiple cut-off classification system was used to determine planning sophistication, sorting firms into three categories: structured strategic planners, structured operational planners and unstructured planners. The classification rests on the eight planning components identified by Bracker and Pearson (1986). Discussions with industry experts led the authors to omit the intuitive planning category, which they felt was not characteristic of the technically oriented individuals who own and manage electronic firms. The accuracy and stability of the planning classification procedure was verified by Bracker and Pearson (1986).

Entrepreneur orientation was determined by classifying owner/managers along Smith's (1967) continuum, whose end-points are the opportunistic and craftsman orientations. Bahaee (1987) computed the coefficient alpha on the Smith scale to be 0.72. Scoring guides for the entrepreneur scale may be obtained from the first author.
Size of firm was coded as large or small, with the cut-off based on a discussion with an industry expert (Norton, 1986). Firms with more than $3 million gross revenue were classified as large firms.

Planning histories were coded as long or short as a function of prior research by Bracker and Pearson (1986). Firms with a planning history of more than 5 years were classified as having a long planning history.

Growth in revenue was the average sales growth for the 5-year time frame; net income growth was the average net income before taxes; present value growth of the firm was the average book value of the firm, patents and goodwill; and CEO compensation growth was the average growth in CEO cash compensation. To obtain growth rates the initial year value (1979) was subtracted from the next year value (1980) and divided by the initial year value; this was done for each year, and the yearly figures were summed, divided by 5 and multiplied by 100 to obtain the percentage growth rate over the 1979-84 time frame. The dependent variables were based on interviews with experts in the electronics industry, entrepreneurs who own and manage electronic firms, and published industry data sources.

Firms were classified by Rumelt (1974, 1978) and Hawks (1984) into nine categories based on observed patterns of relatedness in marketing, distribution, R&D, and production; the authors compressed these into five nominal categories: single business, dominant vertical, constrained, linked, and conglomerate. Each firm's classification was assumed to remain unchanged, or stable, for a period around the classification year; for example, a firm classified as constrained in 1974 was treated as being constrained between mid-1972 and mid-1977.
time_window: classification years 1969, 1974 and 1980, treated as stable through the surrounding 5-year period

variable_name: Related versus unrelated strategy type (narrow and broad definitions)
description: Related and unrelated strategies were coded in two ways for the logistic regressions. The narrow strategy definition of a related strategy is Rumelt's constrained strategy type and of an unrelated strategy Rumelt's conglomerate strategy type, chosen to maximize any possible contrast between the two. The broad strategy definition of a related strategy is Rumelt's single business and constrained strategy types (high potential for sharing common technologies) and of an unrelated strategy Rumelt's linked and conglomerate strategy types (low potential for sharing resources).

variable_name: Shareholder value as a two-dimensional construct
description: Shareholder value was measured as a two-dimensional construct consisting of systematic risk and excess return, the two proxies being the slope and intercept coefficients of the market model. The two dimensions were analysed jointly as dependent variables in multivariate analyses of covariance, because corporate diversification can be undertaken for objectives that may affect one, the other, or both, and because a one-dimensional return statistic overlooks possible intercorrelations between risk and return.
time_window: final 150 trading days of each cycle

description: Estimated as the slope coefficient of the market model relating a firm's excess return to the market's excess return over the final 150 trading days of each cycle. In the model R_i is the individual firm's return to common stockholders (appreciation plus dividends) in day t, R_f is a proxy for the risk-free rate of return in day t, and R_m is a proxy for the return of all risky assets in day t, estimated by an equally weighted CRSP portfolio. Because individual firm betas tend to regress to the grand mean of all betas, the authors' tests rely on portfolio betas constructed by strategy and by market cycle.
level: portfolio of firms by strategy and market cycle (estimated from daily firm returns)
time_window: final 150 trading days of each cycle

description: Estimated as the intercept term of the market model over the final 150 trading days of each cycle, commonly referred to as Jensen's alpha. It is interpreted as the ability of a firm to out-perform (under-perform) an unmanaged portfolio of similar market risk; a positive alpha means that shareholders of that firm will earn a long-term return which is above the firm's required, or expected, rate of return. The authors argue alpha is better suited to evaluate returns associated with strategies than are event-related measures of abnormal returns because strategies have no clear starting date.
level: portfolio of firms by strategy and market cycle (estimated from daily firm returns)
time_window: final 150 trading days of each cycle

variable_name: Market cycle, three nominal categories (bear, bull, stable)
description: A cycle was defined by the direction of movement in the stock market time-series composite as presented in Value Line, a composite consisting of approximately 1700 securities that macroeconomists consider an important leading indicator of economic activity. A bear cycle was a general downward movement lasting at least 6 months, a bull cycle a general upward movement of the same duration, and a stable cycle at least a 6 month period that showed no discernible movement. The nine cyclical intervals were compressed into three nominal categories.

We created a dummy variable that indicates whether each focal dyad's never-before-included prospective partner firm was included by the lead venture capital firm in the focal investment syndicate (0 = no, 1 = yes). For each partner firm that the focal lead firm inaugurally included, a choice set was created that also included counterfactual observations of prospective partner firms that the lead firm did not include in prior syndicates it had assembled and did not include in the focal syndicate. Each observation is therefore a syndicate lead firm-prospective partner firm dyad nested within a choice set.
level: dyad (lead firm-prospective partner firm) within choice set
time_window: the year the focal investment syndicate was assembled

description: We created a dummy variable to indicate whether the lead venture capital firm and the prospective partner of each dyad were the same nationality (1) or not (0). To assign venture capital firm nationality, the authors first identified the headquarters of each firm from the PE Daily database, which distinguishes venture capital firms headquartered in China from those headquartered in Taiwan and Hong Kong. The sample was further constrained to Chinese-headquartered firms that sourced capital only from within China and to U.S.-headquartered firms that sourced capital only from within the United States.
time_window: the year the focal investment syndicate was assembled

variable_name: Collaborative first move by prospective partner
description: We determined whether each prospective syndicate partner firm had previously included the focal lead firm in an investment syndicate that it had assembled (0 = no, 1 = yes). A five-year window was used, which is consistent with previous studies.
time_window: five-year window prior to the focal syndicate

description: We used a dummy variable to indicate whether the focal lead venture capital firm of the focal investment syndicate was Chinese (0) or from the U.S. (1). Nationality was assigned from the headquarters of each firm as recorded in the PE Daily database, which distinguishes venture capital firms headquartered in China from those headquartered in Taiwan and Hong Kong, and was further constrained by the source of the firm's capital.
time_window: the year the focal investment syndicate was assembled

description: Board involvement was determined by averaging the involvement intensity score across the board members within each of the 42 organizations. Two anchored, seven-point involvement scales were constructed, one for the formation stage and one for the evaluation stage of the strategic decision-making process; respondents independently indicated perceived levels of their boards' involvement during the study period. Interrater reliability was .73 for the formation phase and .84 for the evaluation phase, and the ratings were averaged across directors for each organization.

Insider representation was defined as the percentage of insiders and affiliated outsiders on a board in 1985. Outsiders were classified as affiliated when they were former employees of the organization, possessed contractual relationships with the organization, or were major suppliers to the organization; such affiliated persons were counted as insiders.
Board size was defined as the total number of directors on a board in 1985. Information on board size and composition came from proxy statements and organization records.

Level of diversification was measured using the entropy measure, based on sales in each four-digit SIC category in which an organization sold. The data were restricted to percentage of organizational sales in 1985 because the SIC system changed substantially in 1986. For the three for-profit samples, sales data came from the Establishment database; for the hospitals, data came from organizational records.

Organizational age was computed by subtracting the year in which an organization was founded from 1985. The years of founding were obtained from Moody's Industrial Manuals for the public firms and from organizational records for the private hospitals.

Organizational performance was measured as an organization's average return on assets over a five-year period (1985-89) divided by the primary industry's average return on assets over that same period. Primary industries were determined by examining sales distributions by four-digit SIC categories and selecting the one with the largest proportion of sales, which essentially controlled for industry effects. The inclusion of the privately held hospitals precluded the use of a market-based measure of financial performance.

Six items based on prior research, taking the frequency and intimacy of contact as a reference and adding items in accordance with the territorial context of the sample. Responses were scored on a five-point Likert scale where 1 = fully disagree and 5 = fully agree. The variable was obtained as an average of all the items for each firm, and Cronbach's alpha was run to validate the reliability of scale items.
scale: five-point Likert scale (1 = fully disagree, 5 = fully agree)

description: Six items combining indicators used in prior research and additional items in accordance with the territorial context of the sample. Responses were scored on a five-point Likert scale where 1 = fully disagree and 5 = fully agree; the expression 'other firms' refers to all firms in contact with one individual firm, including customers, competitors or suppliers. The variable was obtained as an average of all the items for each firm, and Cronbach's alpha was run to validate the reliability of scale items.
scale: five-point Likert scale (1 = fully disagree, 5 = fully agree)

description: Eight items referring to the conversion of knowledge into new products, services or processes and to significant changes in existing ones, measured as the number of developments or introductions reported for each item over the last three years. To measure the variable, the number of innovations reported for each item was added up over the last three years, and Cronbach's alpha was run to validate the reliability of the scale of items. Only one dimension was used because of the incremental innovations common in the sample.

The percentage of managers in each agency annually who were female, measured as of the beginning of year t. Sex was coded from managers' first names by three individuals, with discrepancies resolved by agreement; ambiguous names were coded according to whether the name was more frequently given to girls or boys in U.S. Census data, and managers listed only by initials were uncodable.

variable_name: number of women's new job titles
description: Count of the managerial job titles created in an agency in year t that were initially filled by women. Job creation was defined as occurring in year t when a job title existed in that agency in year t + 1 but did not exist in year t, counting every unique combination of titles as a distinct job title. When more than one manager received the same new title in a year, only one occurrence was recorded; titles given to both a woman and a man in the year of creation were counted in both totals.
time_window: year t, identified by first appearance in year t + 1

variable_name: number of men's new job titles
description: Count of the managerial job titles created in an agency in year t that were initially filled by men. Job creation was defined as occurring in year t when a job title existed in that agency in year t + 1 but did not exist in year t, counting every unique combination of titles as a distinct job title. When more than one manager received the same new title in a year, only one occurrence was recorded; titles given to both a woman and a man in the year of creation were counted in both totals.
time_window: year t, identified by first appearance in year t + 1

description: Count of all managerial job titles created in an agency in a given year, obtained by summing the number of job titles that were unique to the agency in year t + 1 but not present in year t, and summed across partly new titles, new combination titles, and brand new titles. Agencies might create multiple unique job titles in a year.
time_window: year t, identified by first appearance in year t + 1

description: A dummy variable that equals 1 if the joint venture converted to a wholly owned subsidiary in year t and 0 otherwise. The treatment group consists of joint ventures converted into wholly owned subsidiaries and the control group refers to the continuing joint ventures. Each converted firm is matched with the most similar minority joint venture that did not convert throughout the sample period within the same three-digit SIC industry code and the same year.
scale: binary: 1 = converted to wholly owned subsidiary, 0 = continuing joint venture
time_window: conversion year t; matching covariates lagged to t-1

description: Return on assets, defined as net income divided by total assets. Performance is measured as the cumulative change in ROA from the year of conversion through one to three years after conversion and compared between converted wholly owned subsidiaries and matched continuing joint ventures (the average treatment effect on the treated). Observations with extreme ROA values, greater than 100 percent or less than -50 percent, are deleted.

U.S. industry-level average R&D intensity for each three-digit SIC industry code, taken from Compustat data from 1998 to 2006. U.S. values are used as exogenous information unaffected by the sample firms' own strategic R&D investment decisions. The median value of 1.19 percent within the sample is used to create two subsamples with roughly equal numbers of firms that are relatively higher or lower in technological assets; matching is conducted separately within each subsample.

U.S. industry-level average advertising intensity for each three-digit SIC industry code, taken from Compustat data from 1998 to 2006. U.S. values are used as exogenous information unaffected by the sample firms' own strategic advertising investment decisions. The median value of 2.15 percent within the sample is used to create two subsamples with roughly equal numbers of firms that are relatively higher or lower in marketing know-how; matching is conducted separately within each subsample.

The percentage share of the venture's equity held by foreign parents. It is included in the probit model of the conversion decision together with its squared term, in order to capture the level of foreign ownership. The variable is lagged by one year relative to the conversion decision.

Intangible assets divided by total assets, where technology, brands, and trademarks developed by multinational parents elsewhere and transferred to their foreign subsidiaries are usually treated as investments in intangible assets. The ratio is included among the covariates used to calculate the propensity score, lagged by one year, to capture asset specificity that may favor internalization.

The natural logarithm of intangible assets over time, which captures new transfers of technology or brand from foreign parents to local subsidiaries; differences in the natural logarithm of the variable are interpreted as percentage changes over time. Values are traced from the year before conversion through three years after conversion for converted wholly owned subsidiaries and continuing joint ventures.

For each observing firm, the number of its listed industry peers' fraud punishment cases in the population divided by the total number of such peer firms. All listed firms are classified into 22 industries according to the industry classification of the CSRC, and the variable is scaled by the size of the industry. It is coded from the whole population of listed firms in China and lagged one year relative to the dependent variable.

A binary variable capturing the observing firm's fraud commitment, assigned a value of 1 for corporate financial fraud commitment cases that were officially announced during 2002-2008 and a value of 0 for all nonfraud cases.

The number of fraud punishment cases committed by the national champions, excluding the fraud punishment cases of the observing firm itself, scaled by the total number of national champions in the stock market. Whether a firm is a prominent firm is dichotomously classified by whether it belongs to the national champions or 'central enterprises' in China.

The index of property rights protection of firms developed by the National Economic Research Institute (Fan et al. 2009), which reflects the development of the business legal framework in China; higher scores indicate better protection of property rights.

variable_name: Model-observer similarity (similar-status and dissimilar-status industry peers' fraud punishment)
description: Model-observer similarity is represented by two variables: similar-status industry peers' fraud punishment and dissimilar-status industry peers' fraud punishment. A firm's status in the industry is operationalized in terms of market share; each firm in the population is divided into higher-status and lower-status groups according to the three-year averaged market share in the industry, with firms at or above the industry median belonging to the higher-status group. Similar-status industry peers' fraud punishment is the number of fraud punishment cases on the industry peers that belong to the same status group as the observing firm, whereas dissimilar-status industry peers' fraud punishment counts the cases on peers that do not belong to the same status group.
time_window: three-year averaged market share; punishment variables lagged to t-1

description: Related diversification is one of two components used from the entropy measure developed by Palepu (1985). Total diversification (DT) was calculated from COMPUSTAT business segment data at the focal year, and unrelated diversification (DU) was calculated in a similar fashion but considered the sales of business segments in each two-digit SIC code. Since total diversification is the sum of unrelated and related components, the authors calculated DR by subtracting DU from DT. The equation for the entropy measure is not readable in the available text.

Unrelated diversification is the second component used from the entropy measure developed by Palepu (1985), calculated from COMPUSTAT business segment data at the focal year in a similar fashion to total diversification but considering the sales of business segments in each two-digit SIC code. It is measured at the focal year together with the other diversification and control variables.

Technological search scope is the degree to which a focal patent cites prior art from a variety of technological domains, and the measure is the same as the 'originality' measure of Trajtenberg, Henderson, and Jaffe (1997). The authors calculated the average search scope for firm i during the four years prior to the focal year (t-1 to t-4). Because the Herfindahl-type measure suffers from bias due to the count nature of the underlying data, they applied the procedure developed by Hall et al. (2001), multiplying the search scope measure by NCi/(NCi-1), where NCi is the total number of citations that firm i made and NCij is the total number of citations that firm i made in the three-digit technological category j. The greater the search scope, the broader the technological roots of the underlying research.

The authors measured innovation output of the focal firm by counting the total number of citations of its patents cited by subsequent patents from other firms within a four-year span from the focal year (t to t+3). Their choice of this measure is based on previous findings showing that the number of forward citations is highly associated with the technological importance of a patent.
time_window: four-year span from the focal year (t to t+3)

description: Count variable measured as the total number of interlocks to firms in which subsidiary establishment in China has been clearly successful. A subsidiary is counted as successful in the focal year if the firm has expanded to establish another subsidiary within China. The variable is lagged behind the dependent variable by one year.

Count variable measured as the total number of interlocks to firms in which subsidiary establishment in China has been clearly unsuccessful. A subsidiary is counted as unsuccessful if it was divested within its first three years of operation. The variable is lagged behind the dependent variable by one year.
Count variable of the total number of interlocks with firms that have not established a subsidiary in China. The variable is lagged behind the dependent variable by one year.

Count of ties in which a connected adopter had a higher coreness score than the focal firm. Coreness scores were calculated for each firm on the adjacency matrix for each year using a continuous measure of firm-level coreness that reduces to eigenvector centrality in network structures that conform to an overall core-periphery topology. The variable is lagged behind the dependent variable by one year.

variable_name: Event history variables for subsidiary establishment in China
description: Event history data representing the transition of interest consist of two variables: a dummy variable showing for each firm whether the event occurred during the observation period, and an integer variable measuring the number of years elapsed from the first observation to the event. The transition of interest is establishment of a subsidiary in China.

Statistics on employment in contingent work arrangements as a percentage of total employment in the industry at the four-digit SIC level, obtained from an unpublished study conducted by the Bureau of Labor Statistics. The two arrangements that were most explicitly contingent, and thus most closely demonstrated loose coupling, are contract agency workers and temporary help agency workers. Percentage-based variables for each industry were created by dividing employment in each contingent work arrangement by total employment in that industry, and these measures were aggregated to create an overall value for the use of contingent workers.

Data on strategic alliances were gathered from Securities Data Company's Joint Venture and Strategic Alliances Database, which provides the primary SIC code of each partner in each alliance, enabling counts of alliances by industry. Alliance counts were divided by number of firms in the industry to get a measure of degree of alliance formation for each industry.

IT intensity for each industry, based on the total value of IT equipment per full-time employee, taken from the digital economy data developed and used by the Bureau of Economic Analysis. IT equipment includes computers and peripheral equipment, software, and other information-processing equipment. The ratio for each industry is normalized by dividing through by the ratio of IT equipment per full-time employee for all industries, so an industry with a ratio exceeding 1 is more IT intensive than average.
scale: ratio normalized by the all-industry average (1 = average)

description: Based on the 1997 Benchmark Input Output data, which provide data on every commodity category input used by an industry. The authors used counts of every commodity category used by that industry, and divided this measure by 100 for easier interpretation of the regression coefficients.

To capture whether standards are available in the industry, the authors used the database of standards organizations provided by the American National Standards Institute. A dummy variable (0, 1) was employed to indicate whether the industry has a registered member of the ANSI that develops and administers standards for that industry.

Measured as growth in total factor productivity (TFP), a version of the Solow (1957) residual that measures industry-level rates of technological change. The Bartelsman-Gray manufacturing productivity database tracks TFP growth for every four-digit manufacturing SIC code; the measure is based on a five-factor production function (capital, production worker hours, nonproduction workers, non-energy materials, and energy) and the TFP growth index is the growth rate of output minus the revenue-share-weighted average of the growth rates of the five inputs. The measure used is the average TFP growth rate from 1990-1994 at the four-digit SIC level.

variable_name: Participate in CES / Participate in STVP
description: Dummy variable equal to one if the respondent indicated little, moderate, or heavy participation in either the Center for Entrepreneurial Studies or the Stanford Technology Ventures Program, rather than no participation. The survey asked each respondent to indicate the degree of participation on a four-point scale (no, little, moderate, heavy) and whether participation was as a student. In some specifications the authors include the two program dummies separately.
scale: dummy (0/1); underlying item ranges from no participation to heavy participation

description: Dummy variable for whether the respondent reported being an entrepreneur who founded any type of organization, for-profit or non-profit. The survey also distinguishes founders of incorporated companies, unincorporated companies, and non-profits.

Dummy variable indicating that the entrepreneur's first startup failed. The survey collected information on when each startup was created and whether it failed or exited through an IPO or was acquired by another firm. These first-startup outcomes are conditional on the respondent having founded a startup.
Dummy variable indicating that the firm remained private and alive without an exit at the time of the survey. The authors describe this outcome as survival as a private entity.

Dummy variable indicating that the entrepreneur's first startup exited through an initial public offering. The survey recorded whether each startup failed or exited through an IPO or was acquired by another firm.
Dummy variable indicating that the entrepreneur's first startup was acquired by another firm. The survey recorded whether each startup failed or exited through an IPO or was acquired by another firm.

Natural log of the revenue of the entrepreneur's first startup in the most recent year the firm was alive, reported in the 2011 survey. When available, these figures are verified by matching the firm names to the Dun and Bradstreet database.
time_window: most recent year the firm was alive, as of the 2011 survey

description: Natural log of the number of employees of the entrepreneur's first startup in the most recent year the firm was alive, reported in the 2011 survey and, when available, verified against the Dun and Bradstreet database.
scale: natural logarithm of number of employees
time_window: most recent year the firm was alive, as of the 2011 survey

variable_name: transfer of the target's resources to the acquirer
description: Extent to which the acquirer used resources from the target after the acquisition. Measured on a 5-point scale with 1 for a low extent of resource transfer and 5 for a very large extent of resource transfer. Assessed in three resource areas: innovation, marketing, and managerial. The independent variables are single-item survey measures.

variable_name: transfer of the acquirer's resources to the target
description: Extent to which the acquirer transferred its resources to the target after the acquisition. Measured on a 5-point scale with 1 for a low extent of resource transfer and 5 for a very large extent of resource transfer. Assessed in three resource areas: innovation, marketing, and managerial. The independent variables are single-item survey measures.

Joint transfer of the acquirer's resources to the target and of the target's resources to the acquirer. In Model 3 both directions are included together. Each direction is measured on a 5-point scale for innovation, marketing, and managerial resources.

Cumulative abnormal return for the acquirer over the event window from 20 days before to 1 day after the acquisition announcement in the Wall Street Journal. Abnormal returns are estimated using the market model; pre-event parameters are used for days -20 to -1 and post-event parameters for days 0 to +1. The measure is expressed in percent.

Measured by the highest weight in the function probability vector generated by the LDA model for the app's description. Because weights in the probability vector add up to one, the more weight allocated to the core function, the less is allocated to peripheral functions. Higher values therefore indicate greater relative focus on the core function.

Peripheral functions are meaningful noncore functions in an app, counted when their weight is less than the core function weight and more than 1/18. Successful apps are those above the 75th percentile in the monthly revenue proxy within the core function in the three months prior to the focal app entry; the revenue proxy aggregates reciprocals of an app's daily rank in the photo and video grossing list over a month. Peripheral function overlap is the average pairwise Jaccard similarity between the focal app's set of peripheral functions and the sets of all successful apps, computed as the intersection of the two sets divided by the union of the two sets. Higher values indicate greater overlap, that is, more imitation of successful apps' peripheral functions.
time_window: successful apps defined in the three months prior to the focal app entry

description: All individual ratings for all existing apps sharing a core function are pooled and the average rating is calculated; pooling individual ratings gives more weight to apps with a greater number of customer ratings. The average rating is reverse scored by subtracting it from six, so the variable ranges from one to five. A higher level of overall dissatisfaction means a lower average rating, indicating a higher level of customer dissatisfaction with existing apps.
time_window: three months prior to the focal app's entry month

description: An entropy measure of the heterogeneity of customer evaluations across apps that share the same core function. All individual ratings of existing apps are pooled and the proportion of user evaluations at one star, two stars, three stars, four stars, and five stars is calculated; these five percentages are used to compute the entropy measure E as the sum over the five star categories of P_i times the natural log of 1/P_i. A high value indicates that customer evaluations are not concentrated around any star rating in this core function.
time_window: three months prior to the focal app's entry month

description: Strength in the enforcement of non-competes, measured with an index elaborated by Garmaise (2011) and based on 12 questions proposed by Malsberger (2004). The index assigns one point for each dimension for which the jurisdiction's enforcement exceeds a given threshold, so total scores range from 0 to 12. Texas scored 5 before 1994 and 3 after the 1994 court decision; Florida scored 7 before 1996 and 9 after the 1996 legislative change.

Dichotomous variable that takes a value of 1 if the patent is in the top 5 percent in terms of forward citations received, with respect to all patents applied for in the same year (by application date) and in the same technological class (four-digit IPC classes), and 0 otherwise. Forward citations are counted since the year of the patent's application.
time_window: forward citations since the year of application

description: Dummy variable that takes the value of 1 if a patent received no forward citations and 0 otherwise, following Fleming and Singh (2010).
time_window: forward citations since the year of application

description: Dummy coded 1 if the patented invention referred to a primary patent class different from the primary classes of patents applied for by that organization in the previous five years, and 0 otherwise. The patent class refers to the first four digits of the IPC system, and a five-year window is used to account for the rate of organizational forgetting.

Classification of an innovation by the survey respondents: the authors classed innovations as encompassing when the respondents stated that an innovation changed the core concepts of the lithotripter. The classification based on the two usable firm responses was the same for 19 of the 25 innovations, and only consistently classified innovations were used in the analysis.

Classification of an innovation by the survey respondents: the authors classified an innovation as complementary when the respondents stated that an innovation changed the activities in the component technological system and did not change the core concepts in the lithotripter. The classification based on the two usable firm responses was the same for 19 of the 25 innovations, and only consistently classified innovations were used in the analysis.

Classification of an innovation by the survey respondents: the authors classified an innovation as incremental when the respondents stated that neither the core nor the component concepts changed. The classification based on the two usable firm responses was the same for 19 of the 25 innovations, and only consistently classified innovations were used in the analysis.

Whether the know-how required for a case of technological change was acquired through an equity-based interorganizational relationship. The authors classified the acquisition methods as equity-based relationships, nonequity relationships, and internal R&D based on the information in the published sources. It is the dependent variable in the binary logit model of equity-based relationships.

Whether the know-how required for a case of technological change was acquired through a nonequity interorganizational relationship, such as technology licensing, technology exchanges, testing agreements, technology sharing agreements, and research contracts. The authors classified the acquisition methods as equity-based relationships, nonequity relationships, and internal R&D based on the information in the published sources. It is the dependent variable in the binary logit model of nonequity relationships.

Whether the know-how required for a case of technological change was developed through internal R&D within the firm. The authors classified the acquisition methods as equity-based relationships, nonequity relationships, and internal R&D based on the information in the published sources. It is the dependent variable in the binary logit model of internal R&D.

Binary indicator of whether the U.K. subsidiary has achieved a competence-creating mandate. The authors distinguish on a 5-point scale subsidiaries that reported the functional scope of their output mandate as being limited to sales and service, assembly, or manufacturing (a lack of any local competence-creating mandate) from those whose scope included either product development or international market development (the presence of a competence-creating mandate). The mandate is treated as endogenous to the firm, including the subsidiary, and is decided first in a sequential decision process.
scale: binary (0 = no competence-creating mandate, 1 = competence-creating mandate)

description: The level of R&D expenditure of the U.K. subsidiary, and hence its R&D/sales ratio, which is the regressand of the R&D intensity equations. It is estimated conditionally on whether or not a competence-creating mandate has been achieved, with the binary subsidiary mandate variable providing an additive difference in the single-equation (selection) specification.

Dummy variable for a U.K. subsidiary located in a Development Area under the Regional Selective Assistance program. The authors treat government investment incentive programs as an inverse measure of overall locational quality, since the incentives are made available to firms locating in areas with a combination of low labor skills and high unemployment, poor infrastructure, and many other drawbacks, so locations designated as Assisted Areas have poorer qualities.

Dummy variable for a U.K. subsidiary located in an Intermediate Area under the Regional Selective Assistance program, the second category of Assisted Area used as an inverse indicator of locational quality. Locations in Intermediate Areas, like Development Areas, are treated by the authors as having poorer supply-related development characteristics.

The level of the subsidiary's local sales in its U.K. location, used as the measure of local output (demand). The authors expect higher local sales to raise the incentive to undertake process improvements and to differentiate output to bolster margins, and hence to increase R&D intensity in subsidiaries that are predominantly demand-driven.

The variability of local demand faced by the subsidiary, which the authors associate with higher variance in the subsidiary's rate of return and so with demand-side financial risk. Greater variability is expected to reduce commitment to R&D in demand-driven subsidiaries.

A composite measure of the extent of the subsidiary's strategic independence, described by the authors in terms of the subsidiary's strategic independence in human resource management and marketing, and built from the subsidiary-level decision variables in the survey as a factor score. A higher value indicates greater strategic independence.

Dummy variable indicating that the U.K. subsidiary was part of a group that was acquired by its current MNE group. The authors contrast such acquired subsidiaries with directly established subsidiaries whose ties and identification with the parent group go back longer.

Dummy variable indicating that the subsidiary operates outside of the parent MNE's main line of business, i.e. that it has to contend with a new line of business relative to its group. The parent firm's main line of business is defined in the paper as its largest non-U.K. sales segments whose cumulative contribution to the entropy index of diversification just exceeds 60%.

Dummy variable for a U.K. subsidiary whose MNE group is U.S.-owned, one of the home country dummy variables used to capture the nationality of ownership of the group. The authors argue that U.S.- and Japanese-owned MNEs are more likely to develop cross-border networks for innovation within Europe because they do not have a European home base on which to focus attention.

Dummy variable for a U.K. subsidiary whose MNE group is Japanese-owned, used to capture the nationality of ownership of the group. The authors attribute the greater observed likelihood of Japanese-owned subsidiaries acquiring a competence-creating mandate to the strategy of Japanese firms in the European Union and to their status as newer MNEs that have accorded a higher priority to technology sourcing.

Counts of forward citations of the subsidiaries' patents by other patents assigned within the parent MNE group and by other patents assigned within the host location, used to compare the knowledge generation strategies of the two types of subsidiary. The authors report much higher levels of citations of mandated subsidiaries' patents by other units within their corporate groups, while the two types of subsidiary are much more similar in terms of citations by other firms in the host location.

Composite variable consisting of the distinct measures referring to all partial controls, each measured on a Likert-type scale ranging from full autonomy to very tight control. The paper also reports results for control on strategic issues, control on output decisions (pricing), and control on resource acquisition and mobilisation, and further disaggregates resource controls into human resources, financial resources and purchasing.
scale: five-point Likert-type scale, 1 = full autonomy to 5 = very tight control

description: Ratio of debt to own capital, in logarithmic form. The authors use it as an indication of the enterprise's dependence on the state for loans.
Percentage of subsidies received as a proportion of revenue, in logarithmic form with a constant added throughout. It indicates the enterprise's dependence on state financial contributions.

Percentage of private capital to the total capital owned, in logarithmic form. The authors use it as an indication of the enterprise's access to funding sources other than the state, i.e., as the opposite of financial dependence on the state.
Percentage of sales to the public sector at large, used as an indication of the enterprise's output dependence on the state.
Continuous variable measuring the percentage of members of the board of directors directly appointed by government or supervising state authorities.
Number of end users or clients of the enterprise's products or services, measured on a Likert-type scale. The authors use it as one of the two indicators of political visibility.
scale: seven-point Likert-type scale, 1 = basically one dominant client to 7 = many clients, equally important

description: Scale measuring the orientation towards social versus business criteria in the selection of products and market segments. A high value means the SOE is heavily restricted in selecting markets and products according to profitability criteria; a low value means application of business criteria without restrictions.
Number of full time employees, in logarithmic form, averaged over the period.
Return on assets, in logarithmic form, averaged over the period; in SOEs with surpluses profit before taxes was used.

Ratio of value added to capital employed plus salaries and remuneration expenditure. Value added was measured as the sum of profit before taxation, depreciation, payroll and remuneration expenses, promotion expenditure, interest and other administrative overhead expenses.

Composite variable consisting of two measures, one for the perceived degree of receptability to new ideas and the other for the perceived degree of organised, systematic support to new ideas. Both were measured on a Likert-type scale.
Perceived intensity of competition in the markets of the main SOE products, measured subjectively by SOE managers themselves.
Perceived difficulty in estimating demand for the products or services of the enterprise, as perceived by SOE managers.
Dummy variable distinguishing enterprises with sales in international competitive markets from enterprises not selling in foreign markets, or involved only through noncompetitive trade agreements.

Dummy equal to 1 if the firm response was recorded after the tribunal ruling and 0 if before, in the subsample of rulings in favor of the state. Over the full sample, approximately 36% of firm responses were recorded after a tribunal ruling.
time_window: before versus after the tribunal ruling

description: Dummy equal to 1 if the firm response was recorded after the tribunal ruling and 0 if before, in the subsample of rulings against the state. It is the counterpart of Post ruling for the state-loss subsample.
time_window: before versus after the tribunal ruling

description: Dummy equal to 1 if the firm response was recorded after the tribunal ruling and 0 if before, in the subsample of rulings in favor of neither party. It is the counterpart of Post ruling for the neutral subsample.
time_window: before versus after the tribunal ruling

description: Dummy coded 1 if the firm identifies courts as a 'Major obstacle' or 'Very severe obstacle' to the current operations of the establishment and 0 if courts are not an obstacle or a minor/moderate obstacle. It is built from the WBES question asking: 'To what degree are <courts> an obstacle to the current operations of this establishment?'

Dummy coded 1 if the firm identifies licenses as a 'Major obstacle' or 'Very severe obstacle' to the current operations of the establishment and 0 if licenses are not an obstacle or a minor/moderate obstacle. It is built from the WBES question asking: 'To what degree are <licenses> an obstacle to the current operations of this establishment?'

Dummy coded 1 if the firm identifies tax administration as a 'Major obstacle' or 'Very severe obstacle' to the current operations of the establishment and 0 if it is not an obstacle or a minor/moderate obstacle. It is built from the WBES question asking: 'To what degree are <tax administration> an obstacle to the current operations of this establishment?'

A dichotomous variable indicating whether the firm or its owner participates in the ACFIC, the quasi-governmental collective organization representing industrial and commercial businesses in China. The authors state that they refer to 'Collective Action = 1' to indicate a firm participating in the ACFIC.
scale: dichotomous (1 = firm participates in the ACFIC)

description: A dichotomous variable indicating whether the firm's owner regards participation in the Congress or the Conference to be of great importance to the firm and thus expresses a strong interest in pursuing membership in either of these organizations. It is the dependent variable in the main analysis, which is restricted to firms whose owners are not members of the Congress or the Conference.

Obtained from the China Statistical Yearbook; it captures the level of economic development in the province. The authors use it as a proxy for the quality of the physical and institutional infrastructure in a province, because more-developed economies are more likely to have better infrastructure.

An index constructed in the NERI database based upon the average percentage of senior management time that is spent dealing with government officials and regulatory agencies in the province, as determined by a nationwide survey of Chinese firms; the firm-level responses were aggregated to the provincial level. The time and resources firms expend in governmental interactions are typically devoted to overcoming bureaucratic red tape and responding to bribe-seeking. A higher value indicates a lower level of bureaucratic red tape and thus stronger institutional infrastructure in that province.
scale: index (standardized to a 0-10 scale in the NERI reports)

description: An index based on the percentage of products whose prices are determined by the market instead of by the state. The lower the proportion of prices determined by the state, the better developed the province's market allocation mechanisms in product markets and the higher its value on the index. A higher value therefore indicates that the state has less redistributionary power in the province's product market.
scale: index (standardized to a 0-10 scale in the NERI reports)

description: A composite index composed of two subindices: the province's percentage of deposits in nonstate-owned financial institutions, and its percentage of bank credits offered to nonstate-owned firms. Because banks in China are dominated by administrative quotas and government policies that favor state-owned firms, greater access of privately owned firms to bank loans proxies for less state influence over bank credit. A higher value indicates that the state has less redistributionary power in that province's capital market.
scale: index (standardized to a 0-10 scale in the NERI reports)

description: Indicates whether governments or state-owned enterprises own any equity in the firm. It is used as an indicator of a firm's alternative channel of access to state actors.

Indicates whether the owner used to work for either the government or the Party before founding the firm. It is used as an indicator of the owner's alternative access to state actors through prior political connections.
The logarithm of the number of employees of the firm. Together with sales, it is used to designate firms as larger or smaller in the subsample analyses.
The logarithm of the firm's annual sales. Together with the number of employees, it is used to designate firms as larger or smaller in the subsample analyses.

A firm is designated as a 'larger firm' if its number of employees or level of sales exceeds the median value; otherwise, the firm is designated as a 'smaller firm.' This designation is used to split the sample for the tests of H1a and H1b.

The CSP of a firm is calculated as the sum of all strength items minus the sum of all concern items reported in the KLD database. The aggregation approach is used because the main theoretical argument concerns the range of stakeholder demands and social issues relevant to the firm, and considering all dimensions of CSP improves construct validity. The CSP variable serves as the dependent variable in the fixed-effects regressions.

Because different relationships are hypothesized for related and unrelated diversification, separate measures were needed; the entropy measure of diversification distinguishes between related and unrelated diversification, and therefore the entropy measure of unrelated diversification was used.

Because different relationships are hypothesized for related and unrelated diversification, separate measures were needed; the entropy measure of diversification distinguishes between related and unrelated diversification, and therefore the entropy measure of related diversification was used.
The most commonly used measure of international diversification in the literature, the foreign sales ratio, is defined as a firm's foreign sales divided by its total sales.

Since it is impossible to directly measure the level of a firm's focus on short-term profit maximization, an actual short-term profit measure, return-on-equity, is relied on as a proxy of this corporate-level, short-term profit orientation. Following Hill et al. (1988), a firm's short-term profit figure can be a useful measure for understanding the level of firm focus on short-term profit. Multiplicative terms between this variable and each diversification variable are used to test the moderation hypothesis.

In the post-spinoff years, the incentive compensation earned by the CEO of a spinoff firm; in the pre-spinoff years, the incentive compensation of the divisional president of the spun-off subsidiary. Incentive compensation is calculated as the difference between an executive's total compensation and the sum of his salary and bonus.
time_window: three years before through three years after each spinoff

description: In the post-spinoff years, the average incentive compensation earned by the top management team of a spinoff firm; in the pre-spinoff years, the average incentive compensation earned by the divisional management team that ran the spun-off subsidiary. Incentive compensation is total compensation minus salary and bonus.
time_window: three years before through three years after each spinoff

description: The spinoff firm's end-of-year market capitalization in the spinoff's effective year and the three years thereafter, and the parent firm's end-of-year market capitalization in the three years before the spinoff, since divisional managers' incentive compensation was aligned with the parent firm's stock market performance pre-spinoff.
time_window: three years before through three years after each spinoff

description: Indicator variable taking the value 1 in the effective year of a spinoff and the three years after it, and 0 in the three years before it.
scale: 1 = effective year and three years after a spinoff; 0 = three years before
time_window: three years before through three years after each spinoff

description: Indicator variable that takes the value 1 if one or more divisional managers of the spun-off subsidiary become top managers of the spinoff firm, and 0 otherwise.
scale: 1 = one or more divisional managers of the spun-off subsidiary become spinoff firm top managers; 0 = otherwise

description: Indicator variable that takes the value 1 if (a) a spun-off division has positive operating income, a good proxy for cash flows, and (b) at least one of the parent firm's remaining businesses has negative operating income.
scale: 1 = spun-off division has positive operating income and at least one remaining business has negative operating income; 0 = otherwise

description: Indicator variable taking the value 1 if a division does not share a three-digit SIC code with its parent firm, and 0 otherwise.
The incentive compensation earned by the CEOs of the parent firms, gathered pre- and post-spinoff.
time_window: three years before through three years after each spinoff

description: The average incentive compensation earned by the top management teams of the parent firms.
time_window: three years before through three years after each spinoff

description: The parent firm's market capitalization, measured on the last trading day of each fiscal year.
time_window: three years before through three years after each spinoff

description: Gompers et al.'s (2003) index of governance quality, which awards firms a point for each of the 16 provisions they have in place that restrict shareholder rights (e.g., poison pills, staggered boards, etc.). Higher values of G-Index reflect worse corporate governance.
scale: count of the 16 provisions restricting shareholder rights

description: Cumulative abnormal returns to spinoff announcements, generated using an event study that measures the shareholder value created by these deals. Following Anand and Singh (1997), normal returns are predicted from firms' daily stock returns and the stock market's returns during a 250-day estimation window [-800, -551] before each spinoff's announcement date; abnormal returns are then predicted within a three-day event window [-1, +1] around the announcement date, and cumulative abnormal returns are the cumulative sum of abnormal returns within that event window.
time_window: 250-day estimation window [-800, -551] and three-day event window [-1, +1] around each spinoff announcement

variable_name: Change in the ratio of parent firm CEO compensation to market capitalization
description: The change in the ratio of parent firm CEO compensation to market capitalization between the effective year of the spinoff and the year thereafter.
time_window: effective year of the spinoff to the year thereafter

variable_name: Change in the ratio of mean parent firm executive compensation to market capitalization
description: The change in the ratio of mean parent firm executive compensation to market capitalization between the effective year of the spinoff and the year thereafter.
time_window: effective year of the spinoff to the year thereafter

description: Entropy index of unrelated diversification computed from product-wise sales data obtained from CMIE. The authors also computed Herfindahl indices, but because the entropy and Herfindahl measures were quite highly correlated they used only the entropy measures in further analysis.
time_window: 1994 (base year for computing the diversification measures)

description: Entropy index of related diversification computed from product-wise sales data obtained from CMIE. The authors also computed a Herfindahl equivalent, but used only the entropy measures in further analysis because the two sets of measures were quite highly correlated.
time_window: 1994 (base year for computing the diversification measures)

description: Entropy index of total diversification computed from product-wise sales data obtained from CMIE. The authors also computed a Herfindahl equivalent, but used only the entropy measures in further analysis because the two sets of measures were quite highly correlated.
time_window: 1994 (base year for computing the diversification measures)

description: Proportion (%) of equity held by governmental agencies, measured as of 1993, preceding the measurement of diversification by a year.
Proportion (%) of equity held by for-profit financial institutions, measured as of 1993, preceding the measurement of diversification by a year.
Proportion (%) of equity held by mutual fund companies, measured as of 1993, preceding the measurement of diversification by a year.

Proportion (%) of equity held by foreign corporate investors, measured as of 1993, preceding the measurement of diversification by a year. Individual foreign nationals are not included in this category.
Proportion (%) of equity held by banks and banking companies, measured as of 1993, preceding the measurement of diversification by a year.

Diversification strategy is measured by entropy indices of related, unrelated and total diversification computed from product-wise sales data from CMIE. Herfindahl versions were also computed but only the entropy measures were used in analysis.

A firm-in-market level sales-at-risk measure of multimarket contact. We weighted the importance of each nonfocal market by the number of overlapping groups as a percentage of the total number of groups operating in that market, and by the focal group's sales in the nonfocal market as a ratio of its total sales. The measure ranges between 0 and 1 and takes the value of 0 for subsidiaries facing no multimarket rivals; it is greater if a group has large sales in markets in which many of the incumbent groups are also in the focal market. The specification itself was not readable in the available text.

Subsidiary discretion in investment decisions was coded 1 if the subsidiary had significant decision-making autonomy in investment decisions (''large autonomy'' in SESAME; ''total'' or ''important'' in the ER), and 0 otherwise. The item directly asked subsidiary managers the level of their subsidiary's autonomy from headquarters.

variable_name: Subsidiary discretion in setting its objectives
description: Subsidiary discretion in setting its objectives was coded 1 if the subsidiary had significant decision-making autonomy in determining its objectives (''decided by the subsidiary'' in the ER), and 0 otherwise. The item directly asked subsidiary managers the level of their subsidiary's autonomy from headquarters.

Inflow of financial resources into a subsidiary was coded 1 if the capital expenditure of the subsidiary was positive and greater than its auto-financing capacity, and 0 otherwise. Capital expenditure was measured by the subsidiary's total investment in tangible and intangible fixed assets. Auto-financing capacity (CAF), a standard accounting measure in France, corresponds to gross funds available at the end of the financial year before dividends are paid, measured as total cash flows from normal operations, accounting for taxes and interests paid but excluding non-cash expenses such as depreciation.

Measured by the log of the ratio of total sales of the group in the focal subsidiary's industry to the sales of the leading rival in that industry. It is included as a segment-level determinant of intrafirm resource allocation decisions and is one of the base terms whose effect multimarket contact is hypothesized to counteract.

Calculated from a log-linear growth model using corresponding industry production data from industry input-output tables for seven previous years (e.g., 1997 with data for 1990-1996, inclusive). The slope of the linear growth model corresponds to the average annual percentage change in industry size and is the measure of industry growth.

Coded as a categorical variable, growth as objective equals 0 if a growth or market share objective is not set, 1 if such an objective is set but is not the primary objective, and 2 if such an objective is set and is the primary objective of the subsidiary. The variable was coded as 3-point scales in SESAME (most important, second-most important, third-most important) and as a binary variable (1 if most important, 0 otherwise) in the ER.

Measured by the annual positive deviation in the subsidiary's relative market share. The authors state that this is a relatively more direct measure of competitive aggressiveness, as market share gains are associated with the market share losses of rivals.

The number of months elapsed between the submission of an NDA and its FDA approval, in line with prior empirical studies of FDA review times. The regulatory review occurs after the firm completes clinical development of the drug, compiles the results of clinical trials, and submits the application.

variable_name: Top medical publications about other mechanisms
description: Count of publications in the 5 years preceding the observation year that portrayed other drugs approved for the same therapeutic use as the focal drug but that build on a different mechanism; it considers publications on all other mechanisms available in the therapeutic class, even those introduced more than 5 years before the observation year. Top medical journals were identified from ISI lists, comprising journals in general and experimental medicine as well as in pharmacology, and were those that account for two thirds of the total impact factor in their domain, following prior work. The variable contains the natural logarithm of the resulting count, with one unit added to the original count to account for skewness.

Count of new mechanisms introduced in the same therapeutic class of the focal drug in the 3 years preceding the observation year. The identification of a new mechanism is based on the FDA approval of a new drug building on a mechanism that had never before been used in the respective therapeutic class. To test the contingency effect, models enter the interaction between this variable and top medical publications about other mechanisms using orthogonalized values.

The average annual value of stock option grants made to the CEO during 1996-99, measured in millions of dollars, with values computed using the Black-Scholes methodology applied to individual stock option grants. Values were obtained from Standard & Poor's Execucomp database for 88 of the 130 firms and from proxy statement data for the remainder; proxy-statement Black-Scholes data were converted to Execucomp Black-Scholes equivalents using linear regression equations estimated within industry categories and years.

A binary dependent variable for whether or not a firm restated its financial results downward under pressure from federal or state regulatory agencies between January 1, 2000, and June 30, 2004. Firms were identified by reviewing 12,222 newspaper articles for variations of the word 'restate' and were included only if they restated downward, for reasons unrelated to changes in accounting principles or nonfinancial matters, and only after pressure by regulatory agencies.
scale: binary (1 = restated downward under pressure, 0 = did not)

description: A binary variable coded 1 if a firm's CEO also served as the chair of its board of directors at any time during the 1996-99 period; otherwise it equaled 0.
scale: binary (1 = CEO is also board chair, 0 = otherwise)

description: A binary variable for the presence of board stock options, coded 1 for presence and 0 for absence.
Measured as the number of election cycles the firm gave to the misconduct candidate over the four prior-to-misconduct periods.

Measured as the sum of two types of uncertainty: close election and investigation. Close election was coded 1 if the politician either won reelection by less than five percentage points or lost, and 0 otherwise. Investigation was coded 1 if a criminal or ethics committee investigation of the misconduct politician had been initiated, and 0 otherwise. These two indicators were summed to form a measure of 0, 1, or 2, representing greater relational uncertainty.
Measured as the amount in dollars contributed by the firm to the focal politician's electoral campaign in each election cycle.

Coded 1 if a firm contributed to the campaign of a misconduct candidate's opponent for electoral office following a misconduct event but had not contributed to any of the misconduct candidate's opponents in the four prior election cycles, and 0 otherwise.

Measured as 1 if a firm resumed contributing to the misconduct politician's campaign in the election cycle immediately following the misconduct after first ending commitments in the election cycle during which misconduct occurred, and 0 otherwise.
time_window: election cycle immediately following the misconduct election cycle

description: Coded 1 if the firm did not contribute to the misconduct politician in the misconduct election cycle, after having given to that candidate in the prior election, and 0 otherwise. Firms that contributed to a candidate but received a full refund in the data were also coded 1.

Calculated as the percentage change in total firm-specific CEO wealth during a given fiscal year. The numerator consists of the one-year change in dollar values of the CEO's in-the-money options portfolio, restricted stock portfolio, and other equity portfolio, plus net proceeds from sales in each of these portfolios and nonequity components including annual salary, other annual compensation, long-term incentive payout, and other miscellaneous payouts; dividends were assumed to have been reinvested. The denominator includes the beginning-of-the-period dollar values of the equity wealth portfolios. The variable was transformed using the inverse hyperbolic sine function because the distribution was skewed and included negative values.
