description: Count of the firm's outside options that are allied with a rival of the focal firm, where rivals are identified as firms that operate in any of the 16 geographical regions where the focal firm also operates, using the route data for all firms. The complementary count, outside options that are not in a rival alliance, is entered as a separate variable in the same model.

Using the percentage of cargo delivered by each truck in each of the five product categories, the authors compute a Herfindahl-Hirschman Index by summing the squares of the percentages, and then compute 1-HHI to capture product variety. The fleet dedicated to specific product categories is eliminated from the sample.

The average number of equivalent boxes that the truck delivers to clients in a given month. Equivalent boxes are used because different product categories might have boxes with different volumes. It is used as a measure of the economies of scope attained by the product variety strategy.
A measurement of productivity: the total number of equivalent boxes that a truck successfully delivers to clients per month, where 'successfully delivered' means boxes actually received by clients.

Execution costs are not directly observed in the setting; they are estimated by subtracting from the expected volume given the observed product variety the expected volume given the drop size that is expected from the observed product variety. Because the resulting value is negative when the volume from drop size is larger than the expected total volume, the expression is multiplied by -1 to obtain positive values for execution costs.

variable_name: Percentage of each truck's volume represented by each category
description: The authors include the percentage of each truck's volume represented by each product category; because the categories sum to one, soft drinks-the largest category-are dropped, so the coefficients measure the effect of decreasing soft drinks and correspondingly increasing category j. The similarity ordering of the categories is spirits-wine-beer-soft drinks-confectionery, so spirits and confectionery are the most dissimilar and beer the most similar to the remainder.

The accumulated volume of truck i up to month t - 1, measured since January 2011, with the econometric estimations beginning in 2012 to avoid misrepresenting actual experience for the earlier months. Truck codes are almost perfectly matched to drivers, so experience is measured directly.
time_window: accumulated through month t-1, measured from January 2011

description: An analogous accumulated-volume variable computed from the volume of the other trucks that operate in the same distribution center and for the same carrier as the focal truck, measured since January 2011 with estimations beginning in 2012.
time_window: accumulated through month t-1, measured from January 2011

description: Indicator based on whether the app uses Apple's Game Center. Game Center is a service that allows users to play online multiplayer social networking games and includes tools for developers, letting consumers play with multiple players, share in-game achievements, challenge friends, and discover what games their friends are playing. Being Game Center enabled is a strong proxy for the potential for direct network effects.
time_window: read at the app's first release

description: Takes the value of 1 if the app gets an Editors' Choice award and 0 otherwise. Editors' Choice is the only official endorsement given by Apple; the award appears as a badge under the app's name for the app's lifespan and apps also appear in a special Editors' Choice section of the App Store. Apple gives the award early in the app's life, close to release and before the app has sufficient observable market performance.

App-level revenue cannot be observed, so revenue is proxied by the daily, platform-wide rank of the top 500 apps by revenue, coding the top-ranked app as 500 and the second-ranked as 499. For each developer, the daily revenue proxy is summed over a 3-month period and divided by the total revenue proxy for apps in the category, and the value is lagged by 1 month. The measure captures differences in revenue within each category.

Herfindahl index computed on the revenue proxy (built from the daily platform-wide rank of the top 500 apps by revenue) across developers within a category for a 3-month period, then lagged by 1 month.

Binary variable equal to 1 if the developer holds the second market share position in the category over the past 3 months. Analogous binary variables are created for #1 Developer (top market share), #3 Developer and #4 Developer, with all non-top four developers as the omitted category.

A count of the number of boycotts in which the sampled company was named as a target in a given year; the variable ranges from 0 to 6 in the study sample and is 0 for the vast majority of observations. Boycotts were identified by six independent coders who searched Factiva for each company's name together with the string 'boycott or boycotts or boycotting or boycotted' and read each result, selecting articles where the company was named as a target of a boycott. The coders identified 439 articles announcing activist challenges, referencing 210 unique boycotts.
time_window: firm-year (concurrent year); a one-year lagged version is used as the independent variable in the H1 models

description: A binary variable coded as 1 if a company sponsored at least one social movement boycott in a given year and as 0 if it did not. Six independent coders searched Factiva for each company's name along with the string 'boycott or boycotts or boycotting or boycotted' and pulled results in which a company was cited as voluntarily joining or initiating a social movement boycott without having been first targeted by the movement. This identified 74 corporate-sponsored boycotts over the 15-year period.
scale: binary (1 = sponsored at least one boycott in the year; 0 = did not)
time_window: firm-year; a one-year lagged version is used as the independent variable in the H1 models

description: A count variable indicating the total number of boycotts in the prior year in which activists were able to successfully coerce a concession from the targeted company. It is derived from the coding of boycott articles that recorded whether the boycott ended in a concession.

A count of the number of boycotts in the prior year in which activists were unable to successfully elicit a concession from the targeted company, derived from the coding of boycott articles that recorded whether the boycott ended in a concession.

Built from a content analysis of all articles published about the firm each year in USA Today, obtained via LexisNexis. Each article's affective valence was analyzed with the Linguistic Inquiry Word Count (LIWC) program; an article was coded as positive if at least 60% of its affective content was positively valenced and negative if at least 60% was negatively valenced. Articles about each company in a given year were collapsed with the Janis and Fadner coefficient of imbalance, where P is the number of positive articles, N the number of negative articles, and V the total number of articles; the coefficient's formula itself is not readable in the text provided. The resulting variable ranges from -1 to 1, with -1 indicating only negative coverage and 1 only positive coverage.

Company survey respondents were asked to provide the number of full-time voluntary leavers during the most recent 12 months and their number of full-time employees from 12 months prior to the survey. The former was divided by the latter to create the voluntary turnover rate, and the natural logarithm of the result was taken to transform the highly skewed dependent variable to a more normal distribution.

The company survey asked for the calendar year of the most recent reduction in force; an organization was considered to have downsized if its respondent reported a reduction in force in the survey's calendar year or in the preceding two calendar years. The survey also asked what percentage of employees was downsized; this response was converted to a proportion and then logged, after adding a constant of .0001 because the natural logarithm of zero is undefined. All company respondents reporting a downsizing also reported terminations, indicating that all reported downsizings involved terminations.
time_window: survey calendar year t or the two preceding calendar years

description: Two slightly modified items from Mowday, Steers, and Porter's (1979) Organizational Commitment Questionnaire: 'It would take a lot to get me to leave this organization' and 'I am glad I chose this organization over others I was considering when I joined.' Items were scored on a scale anchored by 'almost always untrue' (1) and 'almost always true' (5), with a coefficient alpha of .84 across all employee responses. The individual-level commitment score was the sum of the two item scores divided by two, and these scores were averaged within companies to create organization-level commitment (ICC(1, k) of .89 in 1998 and .91 in 1999).

Company survey respondents were asked about the presence of 'an ombudsman who is designated to address any employee complaints,' 'a confidential hotline or other confidential problem/resolution/complaint center,' and 'a grievance or appeal process available to nonunion employees.' Items were coded 1 for 'yes' and the values were then summed into a three-item additive index. The items evolve directly from the formal procedures section of Moorman's (1991) procedural justice scale.

An additive index of five HR practices identified as yielding job embeddedness perceptions along the fit and sacrifice dimensions: a defined benefits plan, paid sabbaticals, on-site childcare, hiring for organizational fit, and flextime. The company survey inquired about the presence of a defined benefits plan, paid sabbaticals, on-site childcare, and 'flexible or nonstandard arrival and departure times,' and the importance of organizational fit in hiring decisions; fit importance was ranked on a 1-14 scale on which 1 equaled 'the most important hiring criterion' and was reversed by subtracting from 15. The paid sabbatical and hiring-for-fit items separately addressed exempt and nonexempt populations and were weighted by exempt and nonexempt proportions; the five practice scores were then standardized and added.

An additive index of four practices likely to improve ability to compete in the external job market via enhanced signaling or search capabilities: a career resource center, assessment of skills, knowledge, and abilities to identify employees' development opportunities, formal succession planning, and a formal policy enabling either voluntary or required transfers 'to support learning (e.g., international assignments)' (an affirmative response to either transfer item served as a single indicator). All four practices were asked about for both exempt and nonexempt populations and were weighted by their respective proportions; the four scores were then standardized and added.

Using the description of each of the about 44 license types in the data, licenses are classified into three categories: Highly Open (the General Purpose License), Open (e.g., Lesser GPL, Common Public License, Sun Public License) and Closed (e.g., BSD, Python, MIT). Highly open licenses keep the source code open and limit commercial gains to the maximum extent, while closed licenses allow modifications and extensions of the source code to be integrated into commercial software that need not remain open. License type of the receiving project is a dimension defining the cells, with the interaction of developer type and license type giving the sorting parameters.

Size is the number of developers registered as formal members of the receiving project, including the project manager. In the regressions the average size of the receiving projects in each cell enters in logs and is interacted with the developer type to allow for sorting by developers on project size.

SourceForge identifies the intended audience of each project in one of 19 groups, which the authors aggregate into five categories (Developers (programming tools), End Users, System Administrators, Mixed, Other). Intended audience is a dimension defining the cells and is included as a complete set of dummies, with developer tools and end users additionally interacted with developer type.
scale: categorical: developers (programming tools), end users, system administrators, mixed, other

description: Dummy variable equal to 1 for projects that reveal the outcome of a contribution for at least 50 percent of the contributions they receive over the sample period. It is added as an additional dimension for defining the cells, and the baseline specification is re-estimated.

variable_name: dummy for contribution to corporate sponsored project
description: A project is classified as having a corporate sponsor if it was initiated by a for-profit company or if corporate involvement is present, either directly or through offering a proprietary product that incorporates the project's source code; projects had to indicate a clearly noncommercial intent and have no company support to be classified as not-for-profit. The dependent variable equals 1 if the contribution is to a corporate project and 0 if it is to a not-for-profit project, and only contributions to projects clearly identified as one or the other are included.

A contribution to project j in year t from a developer who is a member of project i is defined as reciprocal if project i received a contribution from j prior to year t. The dummy equals 1 if the contribution is reciprocal and 0 otherwise; the regression also includes dummies for whether the contributing and receiving projects match on license type, programming language, operating system and intended audience.

Count of source code contributions aggregated into cells defined by the contributing developer type and characteristics of the receiving project (license type, intended audience, programming language, operating system and project age). A contribution is any contributed source code that aims to advance the software regardless of whether the project manager accepts the submission, and the number of contributions made over the entire life of a project is counted. This count is the dependent variable in the negative binomial regressions.
level: cell (developer type x receiving project characteristics)

description: Project performance is the number of times a project is downloaded, entered as the log of one plus the number of downloads. It is related to the aggregate stock of contributions received, where stocks of different contribution types are treated as perfect substitutes with different marginal productivities, each computed as the cumulative number of contributions of the specified type from the project's inception.
time_window: project-year; stocks cumulative from project inception

description: A developer is classified as open if all of the projects to which he/she belongs as a registered member operate under highly open licenses. The contributing developer type is a dimension defining the cells and is interacted with the receiving project's license type, intended audience and size; the authors assume this group reveals intrinsic motivation.

Anonymous developers are those who contribute without revealing their identity to the receiving project manager or members. Because reputation cannot play a role for them the authors view them as intrinsically motivated and use them as a benchmark for reputation effects; the number of potentially contributing developers cannot be controlled for this group.

A developer is classified as closed if all of the projects to which he/she belongs as a registered member operate under closed licenses. Developers who are members of both highly open and closed projects are classified as mixed, and nonmembers are contributors who are not registered as members of any project.

The first measure of alliance activity focuses on the event of alliance formation, that is, whether a firm entered an alliance or not in a given year, with 1 indicating at least one alliance entrance and 0 indicating otherwise. This measure assesses the likelihood that a firm will engage in alliances in a given year, not the number of alliances. It is used as the dependent variable in the logistic regression models.

The total number of alliances formed by a firm in a year, which reflects the intensity of alliance activity. The number of alliances for any firm in a year is a nonnegative integer with a limited range, so it is modelled with a negative binomial specification rather than ordinary least squares.

Alliances were classified by type following Dataquest: joint R&D, manufacturing, marketing, technology-licensing, second-sourcing, and funding agreements. Alliances with an R&D component were classified as exploration alliances because the essence of joint R&D is searching and experimenting to find new, uncertain, and risky alternatives that will produce future profits. This variable is the dependent variable in model 8.

Alliance types other than joint R&D, such as manufacturing, marketing, technology-licensing, second-sourcing, and funding agreements, are oriented toward exploiting existing resources to improve returns from present strategies and competencies, so they were classified as exploitation alliances. This variable is the dependent variable in model 9.

The yearly percentage of change in total semiconductor industry sales, used to measure changes in market demand. Start-up firms are argued to be sensitive to yearly market fluctuations reflected by this measure.
Industry sales change squared, used as a second-order measure in the analysis because of the prediction of a U-shaped relationship between market demand changes and alliance formation.

A continuous measure counting the total number of technologies a firm had, following Dataquest's guidelines for measuring the scope of a firm's technological resources. Dataquest specifies nine distinctive technological areas according to product categories, and the more technologies a firm has, the more diverse its technological resources are.

A dummy variable coded 1 for firms with more than one technological capability (generalists) and 0 otherwise (specialists), used as a second measure of technological resources to test the stability of the results given the skewed distribution of the continuous measure.

Manufacturing resources were measured as a dummy variable, with 1 indicating a firm had a manufacturing facility and 0 indicating otherwise. Most firms in the sample that had manufacturing resources were limited to one fabrication facility.
The total capital funding a start-up firm had received since its inception, expressed in millions of dollars. For most start-up firms, venture capital is the primary source of financial resources.

Firm resources are represented by three resource types that the authors consider most critical in the semiconductor industry: technological resources (number of technology areas, or a generalist dummy), manufacturing resources (dummy for having a manufacturing facility) and financial resources (total capital funding received since inception, in millions of dollars). Resource-rich and resource-poor firms are interpreted through interactions of these variables with market demand change.

Factor score estimated from eight survey items adapted from previous research on measures of group identification and social identification. All items were answered on a 7-point scale (1 = do not agree at all, 7 = strongly agree) and concern feeling personally insulted by criticism of the firm, interest in what people think about the firm, saying 'we' rather than 'they', feeling personally complimented by positive remarks, the firm's successes being one's own, being a board member as a major part of who one is, and the perceived overlap between one's self-definition/self-image and the firm. A confirmatory factor analysis showed that all items loaded on the same factor, and factor scores were estimated with the regression method.

Factor score estimated from eight survey items that are similar to those measuring identification with the focal firm, adapted to the government and its agencies. Items were answered on a 7-point scale (1 = do not agree at all, 7 = strongly agree) and cover feeling personally insulted by criticism of the government, interest in what people think about the government, saying 'we' rather than 'they', feeling personally complimented by positive remarks about the government, the government's successes being one's own, being a member of the government as a major part of who one is, and the perceived overlap between one's self-definition/self-image and the government. All items loaded on the same factor in the confirmatory factor analysis.

Factor score estimated from the survey items said to be Questions 1-4 of the questionnaire. The behavior section of the questionnaire first asks how often the director attends board meetings (never, rarely, often, always) and then asks, on a 7-point agreement scale (1 = do not agree at all, 7 = strongly agree), whether the director monitors the strategic decision making by the CEO, criticizes and seeks to influence strategic initiatives that would be harmful to the firm, and provides comments on the design of CEO incentive schemes. A confirmatory factor analysis showed that the items for managerial monitoring loaded on the same factor and did not load on other factors, and factor scores were estimated with the regression method.
scale: 7-point agreement scale for the Likert items; factor scores

description: Factor score estimated from the survey items said to be Questions 5 and 6 of the questionnaire, both answered on a 7-point agreement scale (1 = do not agree at all, 7 = strongly agree). One asks whether the director provides advice and counsel on strategic issues, problems and challenges faced by the focal firm; the other asks whether the director provides personal referrals to third-party sources of strategic advice to the CEO whenever necessary. A confirmatory factor analysis showed that the items for resource provision loaded on the same factor and did not load on other factors, and factor scores were estimated with the regression method.

Dummy variable indicating whether the controlling shareholder of the firm is the state. It was coded 1 if the state owns more than 51 percent of shareholding of the firm, and 0 otherwise. The variable is used to split the sample into SOEs and non-SOEs and to form the interaction term with identification with the government.
scale: dummy (1 = state owns more than 51 percent, 0 otherwise)

description: Indicator variable that takes the value of 1 when a dispute resulted in litigation and a court-rendered judgment, and 0 if the dispute was settled by private negotiation, mediation, or arbitration. The three private modes are collapsed into a single category and a binomial probit model estimates the probability of a litigated outcome relative to private dispute resolution. The dispute resolution mode recorded reflects the final outcome of dispute resolution; in a few cases settlement occurred after litigation had been initiated.

Measured as the number of pages of technical specifications attached to the contract governing the exchange, because the technical details of the products or services exchanged are not directly observable. Both the main effect and a square term are included to capture the hypothesized nonlinear relationship between technical complexity and the likelihood of litigation.

Elapsed time in days between the beginning of the exchange relationship and the date at which the dispute arose. The beginning of the relationship is the start date of the first contract linking the exchange partners involved in the dispute (for first-time transactors, the current contract); the dispute date is the date of the first communication between the firms related to the dispute as recorded in the case file, usually an email or letter between managers.
time_window: from first contract linking the partners to the date the dispute arose

description: Dichotomous measure developed through content analysis of all descriptions of the exchange relationship in lawyers' notes from their initial meetings with managers of the client firm. It takes a value of 1 if the file contains explicit references to flexibility, participation, and/or solidarity in prior interactions between the partners; otherwise 0.

Number of days remaining in the existing contract at the time that the dispute arose, based on the projected termination date of the current contract. Because the variable is defined only for contracts with a specified duration, open-ended contracts take a value of 0 on it.
time_window: from the dispute date to the projected contract termination date

description: Dummy variable equal to 1 for those contracts that are open-ended and have no recorded end date, and 0 for time-bound contracts. A negative coefficient on Open indicates a reduced likelihood of litigation for open-ended contracts relative to time-bound contracts with zero time remaining.

Computed as the product of the binary alliance matrix at t and the vector of innovativeness scores for the firms in the industry, giving the summed innovativeness scores of a firm's alliance partners. A firm's innovativeness score is the proportion of prior art citations in the universe of U.S. semiconductor patents applied for in year t that refer to patents assigned to that firm. The alliance matrix incorporates all alliance activity during the previous five-year period (t-1 to t-5), with older alliances linearly depreciated so that alliances five years prior receive a weight of 0.2 and the lagged year a weight of 1.0. All variables enter as one-year lags.
time_window: alliances formed in t-1 to t-5

description: Computed as the product of the binary alliance matrix at t and the vector of partner size scores, giving the summed semiconductor sales of a firm's strategic alliance partners. Partner size is operationalized as annual semiconductor sales volume. The alliance matrix incorporates all alliances formed in the previous five years with linear depreciation of older alliances, and all variables enter as one-year lags.
time_window: alliances formed in t-1 to t-5

description: A count of the number of new semiconductor patents applied for by each organization in the sample in each year. Patents were retrieved from approximately 2,400 distinct U.S. patent classes containing semiconductor product, device, and design inventions, and the prior art citations on each patent were recorded. Family ownership trees were used to assign subsidiaries' patents to their corporate parents.

The outcome of the growth models is the log of firm i's semiconductor sales at time t, modeled as a power function of a covariate matrix and estimated with a least squares constants estimator that includes firm dummy variables. Because the coefficient on lagged sales is substantially less than unity, the specification estimates growth rates and the coefficients represent within-firm effects. Sales figures were taken from Dataquest for the firms it tracked and supplemented with Integrated Circuit Engineering Corp. STATUS volumes for captive producers.

The number of years since founding for dedicated semiconductor producers and the number of years since entry into the industry for diversified producers, included in the growth models and in interactions with the characteristics of the firm's alliance partners.

The log of the firm's sales in semiconductors during the previous year, included as the lagged sales term in the growth models and interacted with the size and innovativeness of a firm's alliance partners. The coefficient on lagged sales is substantially less than unity, implying that small firms have historically grown faster than large firms.

Four Twenty Seven's physical climate risk scores, which evaluate the magnitude of various types of climate exposure of each facility according to its specific location and the nature of its activity using geospatial, historical, and projection models. Four Twenty Seven translates raw indicators of physical climate exposures into a globally comparable standardized score ranging from 0 to 100 across hazards and locations, with higher scores indicating greater climate exposures, and assigns sensitivity factors to facilities based on the nature of their activities. Company-level scores aggregate the climate exposure of all of a firm's facilities that are at least 50% owned, with no weighting applied based on ownership, and cover the firm's direct operations rather than market- or supply-chain-related risks. The predicted scores were generated in 2019 and are assumed to be the same for each firm and each type of climate exposure during the sample period.
time_window: scores generated in 2019; projections for 2030-2040 against a 1975-2005 historical benchmark

description: A dummy variable equal to 1 if a company has one or more adaptation strategies directed to a specific climate exposure and 0 otherwise. It is hand-coded from the climate disclosure text that publicly traded companies reported with CDP: a category is coded 1 for a firm that discloses adaptation to one type of climate exposure in a specific category and 0 if not, and for firms that do not disclose any adaptation to a specific type of climate exposure all categories are filled in as zero. Some firms do not disclose climate-related information in certain years and these cases are treated as missing data.

Measures the diversity and extent of firms' adaptation by pursuing different strategies simultaneously; following Hoffmann et al. (2009) and Slawinski and Bansal (2015), it counts the number of adaptation categories a firm has in response to each type of climate exposure. The categories come from two rounds of intensive manual text coding of CDP disclosures, the first round inductively coding the disclosed adaptation activities of 1000 firms in 2017 and generating a list of 23 categories of adaptation strategies, which is then used to code the remaining firms and years.

A dummy variable that equals 1 if a firm has routine adaptation in place in response to a specific climate exposure. Routine adaptation focuses on the familiar characteristic of problems and potential solutions, modifies a firm's resource base and incorporates adaptation into previously established routine tasks; it requires less information processing and fewer resources and is usually operated by one unit within the organization.

A dummy variable that equals 1 if a firm has nonroutine adaptation in place in response to a specific climate exposure. Nonroutine adaptation creates a resource base with new actions taken specifically in response to climate change, involving building or reconfiguring internal and external competencies, changing a firm's boundaries, or shifting to a new mode of management; it often involves multiple departments and is therefore more disruptive to the organization.

One of the three measurements of Adaptation Breadth: the count of routine adaptation categories a firm has taken in response to one particular climate exposure. It is built from the same hand-coded categories of CDP disclosure as the other breadth measures.

One of the three measurements of Adaptation Breadth: the count of nonroutine adaptation categories a firm has taken in response to one particular climate exposure. It is built from the same hand-coded categories of CDP disclosure as the other breadth measures.

Measured by firms' disclosed magnitude of climate impact in their CDP reports. Each year the CDP asked companies to describe their inherent risks driven by changes in physical climate parameters for each type of climate exposure, including the magnitude of impact, ranging from 'Low' to 'High' with five choices. The author codes these levels with scores from 1 to 5 (1 = 'Low'; 2 = 'Low-Medium'; 3 = 'Medium'; 4 = 'Medium-High'; 5 = 'High'), where a higher score indicates a higher perceived impact of climate change.

The ESG score provided by Refinitiv (previously ASSET4), one of the most comprehensive ESG scores used in the literature, where a higher ESG score indicates better ESG capabilities. The author considers the three main categories classified by Refinitiv: environment, social, and corporate governance.

Measured by firms' disclosed risk time horizon in their CDP reports. Since 2014 the CDP has asked companies to describe 'how far into the future are risks considered?' at the corporate level and provides four choices; the author codes firms' time horizon with scores from 1 to 10 (1 = up to 1 year; 3 = 1-3 years; 6 = 3-6 years; 10 = > 6 years), where a higher score indicates a longer time horizon. For years before 2014, the author assumes firms' time horizons are the same as those in 2014.

For each team-season observation, the number of star players who voluntarily departed from that team before that season. A star is a player listed in the top 5% of the league in terms of player efficiency rating (PER). Voluntary departures are free-agent deals coded as voluntary (1) when the transaction was more favorable or equivalent to the player than their previous deal (salary x contract term); all other exits are coded as involuntary (0) and excluded from this count.

For each team-season observation, the number of non-star players who voluntarily departed from that team before that season. Non-stars are qualifying players who are not listed in the top 5% of the league in terms of player efficiency rating (PER). As with star exits, only free-agent deals that were more favorable or equivalent to the player than their previous deal (salary x contract term) are counted as voluntary.

To measure a team's performance, the authors used its winning percentage within each season. Only regular-season games were considered, as most teams use different game strategies and rosters in the post-season. The metric is visible and intuitive and allows comparisons with prior studies on sports teams.

A dummy variable marking the period after the 2001 elimination of the 'illegal defensive alignment' rule, which the authors treat as a proxy for a shift from a more pooled type of workflow interdependence to a relatively more reciprocal type. Before the start of the 2001-2002 season, the NBA eliminated the rule, making zone defenses legal and requiring relatively greater collaborative teamwork.

A factor score for the team's external human capital acquisition capability, taken from the first factor of a varimax-rotated principal components factor analysis of eight components; the two retained factors explained 72.8% of variance in the data. It is built from four components reflecting improvement in newly hired players: the average change in newly hired starting and rotating players' PER over the previous season, the number of newly hired players with improved PER over the previous season, and aggregated residuals from a regression of PER on prior PER, age, age squared and salary with position dummies, which removes idiosyncratic individual effects. The authors assumed that the improvement of newly hired players is related to external acquisition capabilities.

A factor score for the team's internal human capital development capability, taken from the second factor of a varimax-rotated principal components factor analysis of eight components. It is built from four components reflecting improvement in incumbent players: the average change in incumbent starting and rotating players' PER over the previous season, the number of incumbent players with improved PER over the previous season, and aggregated residuals from a regression of PER on prior PER, age, age squared and salary with position dummies, which removes idiosyncratic individual effects. The authors assumed that the improvement of incumbent players is related to internal development capabilities.

Variable distinguishing startups led by a female entrepreneur from those led by a male entrepreneur, used as the independent variable in the field analyses of investor question regulatory focus and of funding. Gender identification of speakers allowed all transcribed words to be attributed to entrepreneur presenters and to VC judges.

Total U.S. dollar value of funding received by each startup across various funding rounds, including seed, angel, and venture-led rounds. The measure was verified against Crunchbase, AngelList, press releases and representatives of the startups, and log transformed to account for skewed distributions, with a Log(funds + 1) transformation applied to values of zero funds raised.
time_window: over the course of the startups' lifetimes

description: Regulatory focus of the 1,857 investor questions, assessed by two complementary procedures combined into one validated measure (r = .71): LIWC frequency counts using a 27-word promotion and 25-word prevention dictionary, scored as the difference between the promotion and prevention terms, and blind manual coding of each question into promotion versus prevention intentions by two raters with .97 intercoder agreement. Firm-level measures were built by taking the difference in the number of promotion and prevention intentions, and a binary promotion/prevention code was derived from the sign of that continuous variable.

Continuous firm-level measure of the number of prevention-focused questions investors asked an entrepreneur, used as the continuous measure of prevention focus and as the mediator through which entrepreneur gender affects funding outcomes.

Regulatory focus of the 1,718 entrepreneur responses, assessed with the same LIWC dictionaries and blind manual coding used for investor questions, and used to determine whether an entrepreneur matched or switched relative to the focus of the question asked.
The amount each participating angel investor allocated to each of the four ventures, out of a hypothetical total of $400,000 in available funds, used as the continuous measure of the outcome.
scale: U.S. dollars out of a $400,000 total

description: Manipulated through six-minute audio vignettes in which a male-voiced VC asked 10 questions of an entrepreneur; question sets were written as promotion-focused or prevention-focused conditions, based on actual questions from the TechCrunch Disrupt transcripts, redacted of startup specifics and standardized for startup progress.

Manipulated in the same audio vignettes: each question set was paired with either promotion-focused or prevention-focused entrepreneur answers, producing promotion question-promotion answer, prevention question-prevention answer, prevention question-promotion answer, and promotion question-prevention answer conditions.
The amount each potential seed investor allocated to each of the four ventures, out of a hypothetical total of $400,000 in available funds, used as the continuous measure of the outcome.
scale: U.S. dollars out of a $400,000 total

description: Manipulated with the same audio vignettes used for the angel investor sample: a male-voiced VC asked 10 questions written as promotion-focused or prevention-focused conditions, based on redacted TechCrunch Disrupt transcripts.

Manipulated with the same audio vignettes: answers were written as promotion-focused or prevention-focused, yielding both matching (promotion-promotion, prevention-prevention) and switching (prevention-promotion, promotion-prevention) combinations.

Dummy variable indicating whether the firm's announced new product introductions were coded as valuable and difficult-to-imitate strategic actions. Announcements of intended change during the turnaround year were identified from The Wall Street Journal index and Lexis/Nexis database and summarized for an expert panel of two market analysts, who decided whether each action was valuable and, if so, whether it would be difficult for competitors to imitate within 1 year. An independent panel of six academics rated the same announcements as a reliability check, and dummy variables indicated whether the actions were valuable and difficult to imitate or not.
time_window: turnaround year (the 1-year period following the decline)

description: Dummy variable indicating whether the firm's announced mergers and acquisitions were coded as valuable and difficult-to-imitate strategic actions. Announcements of intended change during the turnaround year were identified from The Wall Street Journal index and Lexis/Nexis database and summarized for an expert panel of two market analysts, who decided whether each action was valuable and, if so, whether it would be difficult for competitors to imitate within 1 year, with an independent panel of six academics rating the same announcements.
time_window: turnaround year (the 1-year period following the decline)

description: Dummy variable indicating whether the firm's announced strategic alliances were coded as valuable and difficult-to-imitate strategic actions. Announcements of intended change during the turnaround year were identified from The Wall Street Journal index and Lexis/Nexis database and summarized for an expert panel of two market analysts, who decided whether each action was valuable and, if so, whether it would be difficult for competitors to imitate within 1 year, with an independent panel of six academics rating the same announcements.
time_window: turnaround year (the 1-year period following the decline)

description: Jensen's alpha, the intercept from the regression Ri - RFR = ai + bi(Rm - RFR), where Ri equals firm returns, Rm is market returns (CRSP value-weighted index with distributions), RFR is the average risk-free rate, and bi is the estimated beta. Weekly firm returns and weekly market index returns came from the CRSP tapes and weekly Treasury Bill rates used as the risk-free rate came from the corresponding week's Thursday edition of the Wall Street Journal. Because most alpha scores hover near zero, cluster analysis separated the sample into three groups, with an alpha of approximately zero representing a firm that met investor expectations, a large positive alpha a firm that exceeded expectations, and a large negative alpha a firm that failed to meet expectations.
time_window: the year following the turnaround year

description: Conventionality of the traditional (non-20th-century) operas in the focal opera company's repertoire, based on the conventionality index. The authors first count the number of times each traditional opera was produced by all the opera companies in the population in the last three years prior to the current year; this number varies between 0 and more than 50 (for La Bohème and Madama Butterfly). They then calculate the average of all traditional operas in the forward-aggregated repertoires to obtain the conventionality index of non-20th-century operas. Because conventionality is based on the three prior years and the repertoire on the current and two subsequent years, the first analysis year is 1998 and the last is 2003.
scale: average count, from 0 to more than 50
time_window: repertoire aggregated over years t to t+2; conventionality counted over the three prior years (t-3 to t-1)

description: Proportion of 20th-century operas in an opera repertoire, defined as the operas whose composers were born after 1880 and therefore had developed their adult musical style in the 20th century. Yearly repertoires are aggregated into rolling three-year repertoires by forward aggregation, i.e. the current year and the two subsequent years. This is the measure of the extent to which opera companies schedule unconventional operas.
time_window: three-year rolling repertoire (current year and two subsequent years)

description: Educational homogeneity, defined as the extent to which the educational achievement of the potential local (same-county) attending audiences is concentrated in people whose highest degree is from high school, college, or graduate school. It is measured with a normalized Herfindahl index in which s is the share of people over 25 years old in a county with highest degree i and N is the number of degree types; the formula block in the provided text is unreadable. Perfectly homogeneous audiences have an index of 1 and perfectly heterogeneous audiences an index of 0, so higher values indicate less divergent audiences.
level: county (matched to the opera company's location)

description: Funding homogeneity, defined as the extent to which the actual funding of an opera company from audiences is concentrated in attending audiences, private donors, or government donors. It is measured with a normalized Herfindahl index in which s is the share of the total funds provided by source i and N is the number of funding sources; the formula block in the provided text is unreadable. Perfectly homogeneous audiences have an index of 1 and perfectly heterogeneous audiences an index of 0. The authors later interpret this index as an indicator of convergent rather than divergent audiences, because attending audiences and private donors contribute more than 90% of the funding and are relatively similar in their preference for conventional operas.

Ratio of government donations to total budget, treated by the authors as a more appropriate indicator of divergent audience heterogeneity than the Herfindahl index, on the argument that attending audiences and private donors are more similar to each other in their preferences for conventional repertoire choices than to government donors, the audience most open to unconventional repertoire choices.

Competitive pressure is measured by the repertoire-size-weighted proximity of the focal opera company i to all the other opera companies in the population: R_j divided by d_ij squared, summed over the other companies, where R_j is the size (number of operas) of the repertoire of opera company j and d_ij is the distance in 100 miles from opera company i to opera company j. Distance is measured in 100 miles because operas within a 100-mile radius are treated as direct competitors, and the squared distance reflects the assumption that competitive pressures decay rapidly as the distance between opera companies increases. The formula block in the provided text is unreadable.

Conductor conformity is the weighted average of the conventionality of the composers in the conductor's repertoire in a given year, where the weight is the number of compositions by a composer included in the repertoire divided by the total number of compositions played by the conductor. A composer's conventionality at time t is the proportion of his compositions performed by other conductors in the field in the previous five years, scaled by the most played composer so that the most played composer receives a value of 1. The variable ranges between 0 and 1, where a value of 0 indicates a repertoire that included solely composers who were not played by any other conductors in the field, and a value of 1 indicates a repertoire based only on the most representative composer(s) in the canon. The authors illustrate the calculation with a conductor who plays three compositions by Beethoven and one by Moszkowski.
time_window: composer conventionality computed over the previous five years (t-1 to t-5); conductor conformity in year t

description: Ascribed status is measured with an indicator variable coded 1 for conductors who had high ascribed status, that is, conductors from Germany or Austria, and 0 otherwise. The category used is the conductor's country of origin, which the authors treat as a salient status-conferring category in classical music because Germany and Austria are regarded as unequivocally high status. The status of a given country is bequeathed to conductors originating from that country, thus constituting their ascribed status.

Achieved status is the cumulative number of recordings a conductor had made from the beginning of his or her career up to the current year, with recordings made under more prominent labels weighted more heavily and recordings under less prominent labels weighted less. The prominence of a label is computed as the proportion of recordings made under that label in a given year over the total number of all recordings made under all labels in that year. This cumulative score is converted into a relative standing by calculating the percentile ranking position the conductor occupied among active conductors in a given year, scaling the ranking by the total number of active conductors that year. Conductors with the same recording score are assigned the midpoint value of the ranks they take up.
time_window: cumulative from the beginning of the conductor's career up to the current year t

description: Dichotomous variable. A family firm was considered hierarchically inconsistent if the chair was not ranked the highest in the family hierarchy among all the family directors and executives, that is, the chair worked with at least one family member whose family rank was higher than him/her. According to the Chinese social norms, one is considered higher-ranked than the other in the family hierarchy if one is the other's grandparent(-in-law), parent(-in-law), sibling(-in-law) or cousin(-in-law) of the grandparents(-in-laws) or parents(-in-laws), elder sibling or cousin, or their spouse, spouse's elder sibling or cousin, or husband. A family firm was assigned a value of one if it featured hierarchical inconsistency and zero otherwise.

Dichotomous variable, coded as one if the firm committed any securities fraud in a given year, as officially reported by the China Securities Regulatory Commission (CSRC), Shanghai Stock Exchange, Shenzhen Stock Exchange, or other related government institutions (e.g., Ministry of Finance), and zero otherwise. The detailed enforcement announcement for each detected case provided information about the specific year(s) when the fraudulent acts were committed, and the variable was coded as one for all those years. Securities fraud committed included fictitious profit, fictitious assets, fictitious records, delay in disclosure, major omission in disclosure, false information in disclosure, unauthorized change in fund use, misappropriation of assets, insider trading, illegal share transaction, illegal guarantee, and ordinary misrepresentation of financial statements.

variable_name: Formal head with concentrated power in the formal hierarchy
description: Chair-CEO duality, used to indicate the formal head's power concentration in the formal hierarchy. In the Chinese business context, the chair is generally equivalent to the combined chair and CEO role in the U.S. governance context, and holding both positions of chair and CEO consolidates the formal head's power in internal and external activities. This variable was coded one if the chair was also the firm's CEO and zero otherwise. The information was collected from the China Listed Firms Corporate Governance Research Database in CSMAR and triangulated with manually collected information on family corporate elites.

variable_name: Informal head with unequivocal superiority in the informal hierarchy
description: Each family firm's head of the informal family hierarchy was identified by making pairwise comparisons between family members in the corporate elite group based on the family hierarchical orders. A family head is considered of unequivocally superior ranking in the informal family hierarchy if there are only family members from his/her next generation and/or his wife in the corporate elite. This variable was coded one if the family head led only his/her next-generation relatives and/or his wife in the top management team and board and zero otherwise.
Dummy variable coded 1 for an insider CEO and 0 for an outsider CEO. It comes from the survey question: 'When you were promoted to CEO, were you promoted from within or brought in from outside?'
Dummy variable coded 1 for yes and 0 for no. It comes from the survey question: 'Do you already have someone specific in mind that you would nominate as your successor when the time comes yes/no?'
Measured on a seven-point scale, with higher values signifying greater satisfaction. The survey question was: 'Indicate your level of satisfaction with your total compensation as CEO.'

variable_name: Perceived connection between personal financial wealth and firm wealth
description: Measured on a seven-point scale, with higher values signifying greater perceived connection. The survey question was: 'Indicate the degree of connection between the financial wealth of the company and your personal financial wealth.'

variable_name: Perceived connection between personal reputation as CEO and firm wealth
description: Measured on a seven-point scale, with higher values signifying greater perceived connection. The survey question was: 'In your opinion, what is the degree of connection between the financial wealth of the company and your personal reputation as a CEO?'

Firm performance, taken from COMPUSTAT, measured by average return on assets during the CEO's tenure. The period from 1979 to 1986 was the maximum period used for averaging and was used only for CEOs in the position at the firm for at least that length of time; for CEOs in office less than eight years, average return on assets was calculated to coincide with their time in office.

A count of the biotech patents assigned to the firm in each year. Biotech patents are defined using the list of technology classes and subclasses provided by the Patent Technology Monitoring Division (PTMD) of the USPTO that capture new knowledge stocks with a strong biotech component. The measure is constructed from the application date of the patent rather than the grant date, so that it is as close as possible to the actual date of knowledge generation.

The average distance (steps through ties) between any two inventors in the firm's knowledge network. The higher the average length, the broader is the firm's knowledge network base, and therefore the higher the potential for further knowledge recombination. Networks are built using a five-year rolling window and the resulting values are assigned to the last year of every time window.
time_window: five-year rolling window, value assigned to the last year

description: The degree to which the firm's network is organized around multiple local neighborhoods of dense interpersonal collaboration, where arguably knowledge recombination is more likely to occur because those clusters are more likely to be characterized by increased motivation to share knowledge, transfer knowledge, and knowledge of who knows what. Computed from the firm's co-inventing network over a five-year rolling window.
time_window: five-year rolling window, value assigned to the last year

description: The average intensity of collaboration used to generate a biotech patent. Using the five-year rolling window procedure, in order to derive a variable for year t, the total number of collaborative ties used to develop biotech patents from year t-4 to year t is divided by the number of biotech patents produced in year t.
time_window: years t-4 to t, value for year t

description: The average intensity of collaboration per inventor. The same total number of collaborative ties is divided by the total number of inventors participating in the knowledge production process during the same five-year window (i.e., the size of the network).

An annual count of the total number of exploration alliances entered by an incumbent firm. Grant, research, and R&D alliances were coded as exploration alliances because these alliances focus on the enhancement of upstream research and basic science knowledge, and alliances were tracked with universities, other research institutions and biotech firms. Multiple research assistants coded the alliances independently, with an inter-rater reliability of 98 percent.

The annual number of biotech-related acquisitions made by incumbent firms. Acquired firms directly involve (small) biotech firms, so that a stronger case that knowledge acquisition is the driver can be made.

Takes a value of one if a product is made by a firm that entered the industry as a start-up, and a value of zero if it is made by a firm that diversified into the industry from another market. The variable is time-invariant and is used to test Hypothesis 1.

Weights de novo status by tenure of the firm in the industry, calculated as Dj,t = exp[-Fj,t/10] * Dj,t, where Fj,t denotes tenure in the ODD industry for firm j at year t and Dj,t denotes de novo entry mode for firm j. It takes a value of zero for products made by diversifiers and inverted time-varying values for products made by start-ups, telling how much time has elapsed since the firm was founded: the more time elapsed since founding, the lower the value (closer to zero). Used to test Hypothesis 2.

variable_name: product-specific instantaneous rate of exit from the market
description: A product is considered to exit the market in year t if it is not shipped in year t + 1. This definition of product exit was used in prior studies of product longevity. The rate is modelled as the instantaneous rate of a product's exit from the worldwide ODD industry in continuous time.

The part of the market valuation of the firm attributable to future growth opportunities. The market value of the firm is decomposed into the value of growth options and the value of assets in place, the latter being the sum of the replacement value of assets and the present value of economic value added (EVA). The present value of EVA is calculated by dividing the firm's EVA by its weighted average cost of capital. The variable is expressed in units of billion Yen.
Measured as the number of host countries in which the Japanese firm operates manufacturing affiliates.

The market uncertainty that the firm faces in the host countries in which it operates affiliates. The volatility of a host country's economic growth is captured by regressing the country's gross domestic product (GDP) over 5 years against time and using the root mean square error (RMSE) of the regression scaled by the value of GDP, to arrive at a standardized proxy of market uncertainty for each host country and year. Market Uncertainty is then the average of the uncertainty measures across the host countries in which the firm is active.
time_window: 5-year GDP window; averaged for year t

description: Calculated as the Japanese firm's average equity stake in its foreign affiliates.

A time-varying measure of the financial resources invested in the foreign affiliates, constructed by combining information on employment and paid-in capital. A country- and industry-specific paid-in capital to employment ratio is calculated and then multiplied by each affiliate's annual number of employees (matched by country and industry). Investment Size is the average calculated financial investment of the firm's affiliates in a year, expressed in units of hundred-million Yen.

An indicator variable based on the parent firm's total investment in an affiliate, measured as the investment size of the affiliate times the firm's equity share in the affiliate. It takes the value 1 if a firm's investment in an affiliate is low when country uncertainty is high, or if its investment is high when country uncertainty is low; it takes the value -1 if the opposite holds. The threshold for investment size is the average investment size of the affiliates of all Japanese sample firms in the industry, and for market uncertainty the average uncertainty in the set of countries in which the sample firms operate manufacturing affiliates. If a firm has multiple affiliates in a country, the values of the indicators are averaged across the affiliates, and the indicators are summed up across all host countries to arrive at a firm-year measure.

Dummy variable that takes a value of one if the head coach had been selected in an NBA All-Star Game when he was an NBA player, and zero otherwise. The authors define an SPTM as a manager who had previously played in an NBA All-Star Game. Of the 195 managers in the sample, 37 (19%) had prior stardom.

Dependent variable that takes a value of one if the focal team wins, and zero otherwise. The authors use individual games rather than entire seasons as the unit of observation partly because head coaches are often fired mid-season and because rosters change within a season. In each game's observation the home team is taken as the focal team, so that a team's away games appear only as the opponent's home games.

Count of the number of players in a game's roster who were born in the same state as their coach or attended the same college as their coach. The logic is that role modeling requires visibility and that visibility is stronger when it is local. The variable is log-transformed, with one added before logging to avoid taking the log of zero.

Dummy variable that takes a value of one if the authors found any positive comments about the coach's speeches to his team, and zero otherwise; a total of 19 coaches were coded as one. Textual data in the form of published news articles, player interviews, commentary, and sports magazines were collected from Factiva and searched with preset morale-building keywords combined with each head coach's name, and two coders independently scraped the quotations and cross-checked relevance.

Dummy variable that takes the value of one if the head coach either is simultaneously serving as the team's GM himself or had previously served as a colleague of the GM (i.e., player-coach; head coach-assistant coach; former colleague as a team staff), and zero otherwise. In the NBA, authority over the biggest rewards and punishments for players - negotiating salaries and contractual terms, firing players, and supervising off-court behavior - is reserved for the GM, so this variable proxies the coach's influence over those decisions.

Count of the number of novice players in a game's roster, where novices are defined as players who debuted their first season in the NBA, on the assumption that their skillset and experience are more likely to be inferior compared to incumbent players. Players drafted from international professional leagues (such as Yao Ming) are excluded because they are not novice players in terms of skills or experience on the court. The count is log-transformed to adjust for skewness, so higher values mean less subordinate experience.

Average tenure of the team's assistant coaches in NBA assistant coaching jobs. The authors focus on the interaction between a head coach and assistant coaches - that is, middle managers - because every NBA team has several assistant coaches who help to train the players and prepare them for games (e.g., conditioning, practice, or opponent analysis), and they take experience as a proxy for the assistant coaches' effectiveness or skill.

Dummy variable that takes a value of one if the authors found evidence that the head coach is known for a specific strategy or floor plan, a practice known as 'system coaching', and zero otherwise; 44 system coaches were identified. Evidence came from Factiva searches of news articles and interviews using system-coaching keywords, as well as coaching books published by the NBA, books written by NBA coaches about their methods, and books written by commentators who study the NBA and its players.

The length of time the bank has offered online banking services, which indicates the length of time customers could possibly have been using online banking as their medium to conduct banking transactions. The authors reason that customers' online banking capabilities correlate with the length of time their banks have offered online banking services. The variable is transformed by taking the square root in order to give a diminishing capability effect over time.

The bank's ratio of total deposits to balance sheet assets, transformed by subtracting it from one so that increasing values correspond to increased 'aggressiveness.' A high value of the untransformed ratio is indicative of a strategy in which the bank relies largely on traditional sources of funding such as deposits, whereas reliance on other sources of funds may require the bank to follow a more aggressive strategy with respect to generating loan and fee income. The authors use this as the proxy for banks' existing cross-selling capabilities and lag it one year to avoid potential endogeneity with the dependent variables.

Computed as a ratio of total noninterest income and the total number of deposit accounts. The total number of deposit accounts includes all demand, savings, and time accounts. Examination of the distribution revealed the dependent variables were highly skewed, so they were Winsorized at the top and bottom 0.1 percentile of their respective distributions.

Computed as a ratio of total noninterest expense for the period and the total number of deposit accounts. The figure reflects total expenditures for all the physical assets of the bank as well as total wages. The dependent variable was Winsorized at the top and bottom 0.1 percentile of its distribution.
Noninterest income minus noninterest expense for the period, divided by the total number of accounts. The dependent variable was Winsorized at the top and bottom 0.1 percentile of its distribution.

Net income for the period divided by the total number of accounts. The authors describe this as a measure of profitability that goes beyond the narrower measure of net noninterest income/account since it encompasses all profits generated by the bank. The dependent variable was Winsorized at the top and bottom 0.1 percentile of its distribution.

Public strategy presentations were identified by electronically searching StreetEvents under the search terms 'strategy presentation,' 'strategy meeting,' 'strategy announcement,' 'strategy review,' and 'strategy update.' Only presentations that were public and relevant to the whole business were included, and confounding events such as dividends, mergers and acquisitions, earnings announcements, major contract awards, new product announcements, and significant liability suits during a 21-day window (day -10 to day +10) were screened out.

CAR is calculated using a market model for each firm, as the deviation between expected returns and actual returns, with the 260 trading days prior to the event window as the estimation window and a NYSE and NASDAQ equally weighted index as the market index. The main analysis uses a short three-day event window (t = -1 to +1), which allows for leakage of information prior to the presentation. The model estimated is a static linear panel data model where CARit is the cumulative abnormal return for firm i for event t.
time_window: three-day event window (t = -1 to +1); 260-trading-day estimation window

description: New chief executive is coded as a binary variable: '1' for those appointed in the 100 (or 200) days prior to strategy presentations and '0' otherwise. Data on new chief executives were gathered by searching OneSource for the CEO's appointment date, Factiva and Lexis/Nexis for succession announcements, and company websites where necessary.
time_window: 100 or 200 days prior to the presentation

variable_name: Internal, non-heir apparent new CEOs' strategy presentations
description: Coded '1' if the new CEO presenting his or her strategy was appointed from inside the organization but was not an heir apparent, and '0' if otherwise. Heir apparents were those who had previously held the title of president, chief operating officer (COO), or both in the firm and who were at least five years younger than the incumbent CEO.

variable_name: External, within-industry new CEOs' strategy presentations
description: Coded '1' if the new CEO presenting his or her strategy was appointed from outside the organization (but from inside their main industry), and '0' otherwise.

variable_name: External, outside-of-industry new CEOs' strategy presentations
description: Coded '1' if the new CEO presenting his or her strategy was appointed from outside the firm's main industry (and organization), and '0' otherwise, using the two-digit Standard Industrial Classification (SIC) code.

The percentage of all directors on the board who had political experience. A director was coded '1' if s/he had current or former political experience - that is, was a current member in Chinese legislative bodies (the National People's Congress and the Chinese People's Political Consultative Conference) or was a government official before joining the company - and '0' otherwise. Political experience was manually coded from directors' biographical sketches disclosed in annual reports.

The value of a firm's other receivables over total assets. Other receivables (OREC) is an accounting item in Chinese corporate balance sheets referring to any receivable amounts and temporary prepayments other than those recorded as notes and accounts receivables. Given that disclosure requirements for OREC are not well specified, the account reflects related-party transactions for non-operational purposes, especially loans to parent companies and their unlisted subsidiaries.

A binary variable coded '1' if a company's controlling blockholder was private, or '0' if a government agency. It was constructed from ownership and control information that listed companies have had to disclose since 2001, when the CSRC required all listed companies to disclose details of their controlling shareholders.

A binary variable denoting the significance of government regulation in the sample firms. Based on two-digit sectors, a firm was coded '1' if it belonged to Petrochemical, Pharmaceutical, Metallurgical, or Machinery industries and '0' otherwise, because these capital-intensive, heavy industries are still subject to enormous influences from the Chinese state's industrial policies.

The NERI index of marketization in Chinese provinces, a yearly index assessing the quality of market-supporting institutions along five dimensions: the relationship between the government and the market, the development of the private sector, the product market, the factor market, and market intermediaries and legal environments. A weighted average of the scores in the five dimensions results in the overall index for each province in each year. The index was matched with sample firms in the provinces in which they were located, and a two-year lag was allowed because the yearly indices are available only from 1997 to 2009.
time_window: two-year lag (e.g., firms' 2011 ORECTA data were regressed on their corresponding marketization index in 2009)

description: Dependent variable indicating disclosure activity in the academic year 1996-1997 through the academic year 1998-1999. Coded zero if the individual did not file an invention disclosure in the three-year window and one if the individual filed one or more invention disclosures. The probability of disclosing is estimated using a probit model.

Total number of patents applied for by the individual's graduate institution in the five years preceding the date of the faculty member's graduate degree, intended to capture activity at the time the individual was in training. It proxies the intensity of a university's technology transfer culture. The range in the data was from 0 to 114, a highly skewed distribution with a mean of 5.33 and a standard deviation of 9.96.
time_window: five years preceding the graduate degree

description: Dummy variable equal to one if an individual has an advanced degree from Stanford, described by the authors as a simple alternative measure of protechnology transfer imprinting. Stanford was mentioned several times in faculty interviews as a well-known example of a protechnology transfer university with a strong history of patenting activity.
Number of years since the faculty member received their last advanced degree, used to capture the timing effect associated with the individual's training, or experience years.

Dummy variable indicating whether or not the chair of the department disclosed an invention to the TTO in the 1991-1995 time period. The variable is coded 1 for yes and 0 for no. Department chairs typically hold this leadership position for extended periods of time and there was no turnover in the chair in any of the departments during the period studied.

Percentage of faculty at the same rank within the individual's department who disclosed in the 1991-1995 time period. An individual's cohort is defined as those individuals of the same rank in the same department, and rank in 1993, the midpoint of the first period, was used to construct the cohort variables. The mean cohort participation was 0.176 with a standard deviation of 0.154.

A dollar measure of NIH funding received by each faculty member in the previous time period, included to control for individual ability and used in the symbolic/substantive analysis as an indicator of formal agency mandates. In the symbolic compliance models the dollar amount of individual NIH awards is positive and strongly statistically significant.

Dummy variable equal to one for those individuals who disclosed once in the current time period and had no more than one disclosure in the previous time period. It is the dependent variable in the first set of symbolic-versus-substantive models. There were 168 symbolic individuals.

Dummy variable equal to one if the individual had more than one disclosure in the current time period. It is the dependent variable in the second set of symbolic-versus-substantive models. There were 136 individuals who were considered substantive.

Four items spanning the concept domain of collective teaching, selected on the basis of practitioner interviews and prior research. Two items describe how routinely the source organization involves members of the receiving organization in its field of interaction, such as through joint projects and cross-functional meetings; the other two items ask the extent to which members of the receiving organization were exposed to the interrelational coordination among members of the source organization when solving complex problems or carrying out a technical project. Respondents from the receiving organization evaluated the degree of regularity with which the strategy was applied from the onset of the source-recipient relationship, on a seven-point Likert scale.
time_window: from the onset of the source-recipient relationship

description: A two-item scale based on the research of Almeida and Grant (1998). The items concern how routinely the source organization arranges for experts to teach technical skills to members of the receiving organization, whether in a classroom setting or through on-site technical assistance. Respondents evaluated the regularity of this activity on a seven-point Likert scale.
time_window: from the onset of the source-recipient relationship

description: Five items designed to span the structural and cultural features of the receiving organization conducive to knowledge absorption, based on fieldwork and relevant studies. Two items inquire about the extent to which the receiving organization's structure is open and flexible, two items ask about the effectiveness of its knowledge infrastructure, and one item focuses on the level of team orientation of the receiving organization. Responses were given on a seven-point Likert scale.

Two items asking the respondent to take stock of the percentage of engineers in his or her organization who have received training in two key areas of engineering tasks: product design and project management. The response scale runs from one (0 percent) through four (50 percent) to seven (100 percent).

A four-item scale developed for this study to measure the improvement in the receiving organization's stock of collective knowledge during the past three years. The first two items relate to interfunctional and interpersonal communication and coordination ability among employees; the last two concern the norms commonly shared among employees. Responses were given on a seven-point scale.

A three-item scale based on Lyles and Salk (1996) measuring the improvement in the receiving organization's stock of individual knowledge during the past three years. The items involve the overall improvement in technical knowledge, project management skills, and necessary job-related competencies of the receiving organization's employees. Responses were given on a seven-point scale.

The portion of the firm's value attributable to growth options, obtained by decomposing the market value of the firm into the value of growth options and the value of assets in place and then substituting Stern Stewart measures (capital employed and the present value of current economic value added). The equation used to rewrite and substitute these measures is unreadable in the extracted text.

The total dollar value of stock options held by top management, using Black-Scholes valuations; the values for each of the five top managers identified in ExecuComp are summed for each year and then normalized by the annual total compensation of the top management team. The authors use the dollar value of options held rather than the number of options held, and this is a 'stock' measure representing the total amount held rather than an annual 'flow' measure.

The total number of shares held by top management multiplied by the firm's closing stock price; the values for each of the five top managers identified in ExecuComp are summed for each year and then normalized by the annual total compensation of the top management team. This is a 'stock' measure of the total amount held rather than an annual 'flow' measure.

Annual salary and annual bonus, summed together to form the measure; the values for each of the five top managers identified in ExecuComp are summed for each year and then normalized by the annual total compensation of the top management team.

The average Tobin's q for all publicly held firms in an industry, where Tobin's q is measured following Kaplan and Zingales's approach: total assets plus the market value of common equity minus the book value of common equity minus deferred taxes, all divided by total assets, using data available from Compustat. The authors center the managerial incentives and industry growth opportunities variables to examine the interaction effects.

The premium is computed as the percentage difference between the actual price paid per target share by the acquirer and the target's share price one week prior to the announcement of the acquisition. This measure balances minimizing the possibility of confounding events against capturing potential preannouncement anticipation by investors, sitting between the four-week and announcement-day premiums used in existing research.
time_window: one week prior to the announcement

description: Short-term cumulative abnormal returns are computed over multiple windows of three (-1, 1), five (-2, 2) and seven (-3, 3) trading days surrounding the announcement date. The CAR is the part of the return that is unanticipated by a model of anticipated, normal returns. Short windows are used to avoid confounding events while allowing for some leakage of information prior to the announcement.
time_window: 3, 5 and 7 trading days surrounding the announcement date
