Measured as the median analyst recommendations for each firm from IBES. The analyst recommendations take on five ordinal values, from 1 ('strong buy') to 5 ('strong sell'), and the variable was reverse-coded to aid in interpretation.
scale: five ordinal values (1 'strong buy' to 5 'strong sell'), reverse-coded

description: Calculated as net income divided by total invested capital, used as an accounting-based measure of firm performance.

The measure is based on structural equivalence: startups that have relationships with the same partner firms form a group. It is the dispersion of a group's intergroup densities around the network average, normalized by a measure of how structured the network is in a time period; it is bounded by zero and one and expresses each group's percentage contribution to network structure. A higher value indicates that a group's relationships are more tightly packed with its partner groups, that is, more partner sharing and greater social capital available to the group. The authors note that the measure penalizes small groups of firms with small partner groups.
level: startup group (assigned to the firms in the group)

description: The change over the period in a startup group's social capital. It is the dependent variable in the regressions of change in social capital on the number of new relationships (with entering and with incumbent partners) and on the level of social capital at the beginning of the period. The authors state that if a group's contribution to network structure increases with new relationships, startups have chosen partners so that social capital is increased; the text does not give the formula in prose.
level: startup group (assigned to the firms in the group)

variable_name: Number of new relationships with entering partners
description: Count of the new cooperative agreements a startup forms in each period with partners that are entering the network, that is, partners that were not already in the network (as opposed to incumbent partners already in the network). It is one of the two dependent variables in the regressions explaining new startup relationships, and the tests are designed at the firm level for each pair of years.

variable_name: Number of new relationships with incumbent partners
description: Count of the new cooperative agreements a startup forms in each period with partners already in the network, that is, incumbent partners. It is the second of the two dependent variables in the regressions explaining new startup relationships, estimated separately from relationships with entering partners.

The performance context of a firm at the time of the succession event was approximated by cumulating its excess returns over 200 trading days, beginning 300 trading days before the first public announcement of the executive change. The 100 trading days immediately preceding the announcement were excluded to minimize the chance that the succession event itself would bias the context measure. About 65 percent of the firms studied performed less well than firms with similar risk during the designated context period.
time_window: 200 trading days beginning 300 trading days before the announcement

description: The origin of the successor CEO was determined in a categorical way: an insider was a successor with at least five years of tenure with the firm in question and an outsider a successor who had not been with the organization for more than one year before moving to the top. Origin is a dichotomous dummy variable defined as 0 if a successor was an insider and as 1 if a successor was an outsider; cases falling into neither category were excluded.

The dependent variable is the CRSP daily excess return, computed through a three-step procedure: a Scholes-Williams beta is estimated for each security using a three-day moving-average market window, securities are ranked into ten risk classes on the basis of average annual betas, and each firm's one-day common stock return (price change adjusted for stock splits or dividends) is reduced by the one-day return of the portfolio of firms in its risk class. Excess daily returns were cumulated over five horizons surrounding the first public announcement of a succession: the 2-day announcement period (t - 1, t = 0), the 51-day presuccession period (t - 50, t = 0), the 50-day post-succession period (t + 1, t + 50), the 101-day cumulative interval (t - 50, t + 50), and the 200-day long-term leadership period (t + 100, t + 300).
level: firm (daily returns cumulated over each horizon)
time_window: five cumulation horizons from 50 trading days before to 300 trading days after the announcement

description: Measured as the level of cash reserves in a given year; cash is described as the most easily deployed resource, giving managers the greatest degree of freedom in allocating it to alternate uses. The financial slack measures were calculated for each of the four years. Because slack is operationally defined as excess absolute levels of resources, slack was calculated as the deviation from the mean of each of the 43 industry subsectors.

Measured as the debt-to-equity ratio. In private firms, debt capacity is typically lower than in publicly traded firms because these firms tend to be undercapitalized, so higher debt levels restrict the freedom to reallocate resources or raise additional debt to meet expedient needs; debt also serves to temper managerial overconfidence. Slack was calculated as the deviation from the mean of each of the 43 industry subsectors.

The permanent capital of a firm (owner's equity plus debt) less fixed assets and other noncurrent assets. It was developed as one of two measures capturing the ephemeral nature of transient slack, and was calculated as the deviation from the mean of each of the 43 industry subsectors.

An estimate of cash required (five days worth of sales) plus accounts receivable and inventory less accounts payable. It was developed as one of two measures capturing the ephemeral nature of transient slack, and was calculated as the deviation from the mean of each of the 43 industry subsectors.

Gross profit, calculated as revenues less the cost of goods sold. The authors describe gross profit as a good indicator of profitability and report that it was correlated with net income at .94 and with net worth at .96. They refrained from using net income or net worth because possible variability in the tax treatment of income in private firms might undermine the reliability of performance estimates.
Firm age was measured as years since incorporation.

Herfindahl's index of homogeneity in industry competition and concentration of resources, measured as the sum of the squared market shares of publicly traded firms in a sector (four-digit SIC). The index assumes a value of 0 to 1, where 0 reflects perfect competition among numerous incumbents with infinitesimal market shares; a high value represents large players and a disproportionate concentration of sales that restricts smaller firms' ability to enhance performance by limiting their strategic choices.

Slack is measured with financial ratios from private-firm data: high-discretion slack as cash reserves, low-discretion slack as the debt-to-equity ratio, and transient slack through resource availability and resource demand. Each is calculated as the deviation from the mean of the firm's industry subsector and interacted with firm age and industry complexity.

Constructed by using the preshock decreasing-demand word count for each firm, normalized by the total number of words within abstracts for the same firm. Preshock characteristics are measured by pooling award abstracts over the 5-year preshock period (1996-2000) and counting the number of associated words in these abstracts, ensuring that the measure represents a stock immediately before 2001.

Constructed analogously to preference-decreased technological capabilities, using the preshock increasing-demand word count for each firm, normalized by the total number of words within abstracts for the same firm. Preshock award abstracts are pooled over the 5-year period 1996-2000.

Measured at the portfolio level across all DoD agencies (customers) granting SBIR awards; the number of agencies that have granted more than one award to the focal firm divided by the total number of agencies that have granted awards to the focal firm. The numerator reflects the depth of repeated relationships with existing customers, while the denominator captures the breadth of relationships with all existing customers who have at least one tie with the firm. For example, a firm with awards from five agencies, two of which awarded it more than once, has a value of 2/5 = 0.4.

The SBIR award count in each firm-year is partitioned into extension-based awards, in which the award abstract contains at least one decreasing-demand and one increasing-demand word. The natural log of one plus the raw number of such awards is used, so that the model estimates the within-firm percent change in the extension-based award count from preshock to postshock. The mean of the nonlogged variable is 0.32, with a SD of 1.10 and a range of 0-25.

The SBIR award count in each firm-year is partitioned into novelty-based awards, in which the award abstract contains at least one increasing-demand word but no decreasing-demand words. The natural log of one plus the raw count is used to estimate the within-firm percent change in novelty-based awards from preshock to postshock. The mean of the nonlogged variable is 0.15, with a SD of 0.75 and a range of 0-16.

A dummy variable that is 1 if a new venture is a spinout and 0 if it is an incumbent new establishment. Spinouts are identified in the LEHD employee-movement data as new firms in which at least three-quarters of employees came from an existing parent establishment with the same four-digit NAICS code, where that founding cluster did not constitute a majority of the parent establishment and had fewer than 20 employees.

A dependent variable in the parent-year incidence analysis that classifies parent firms into those that spawn only spinouts, those that spawn only incumbent new establishments, those that spawn both types of new ventures, and those that spawn neither. Because the number of parents that do not spawn any new venture is very large, a 25% random sample of such non-spawners is used while all other parents are retained, with regressions weighted accordingly.
scale: four categories (only spinouts, only INEs, both, neither)

description: The logarithm of the number of employees in a year, used to measure parent financial resource availability. The authors note that this variable has been used in prior studies as a measure of resource advantages of firms.
time_window: year in which the new venture is formed

description: The logarithm of the number of NAICS-4 industries a parent is present in. It is used as a proxy for parent redeployment opportunities because firms present in many industries are likely to have more opportunities to redeploy their resources than those present in only one industry.
time_window: year in which the new venture is formed

description: The ratio of total industry assets to total industry employment obtained from Compustat. Capital-intensive industries require large investments in physical capital.
time_window: year in which the new venture is formed

description: The logarithm of the number of employees at the new venture, examined at ages 0, 3, 5, and 7. A panel specification containing observations across all years for a new venture is also estimated, and specifications that control for initial size analyze growth implicitly.

A dummy indicating whether the new venture survived to a given age, examined at ages 3, 5, and 7. Cox and Weibull survival models are also estimated to understand how the key independent variables are associated with the hazard rate of exit.
scale: 1 = survived to the given age, 0 = otherwise

description: Operationalized as the total number of complementary technologies provided by Apple and other firms in the iOS ecosystem connected to the focal app. Information on connections with complementary technologies provided by Apple (such as Camera, Siri, Bluetooth, and iCloud) was extracted from the iTunes website; connections with complementary technologies provided by other firms were extracted from the textual description of each focal app by capturing the names of any other apps included in the description. The variable was updated based on apps' version history updates to identify if the connections were introduced as part of a version update.
time_window: monthly observations; updated with version history through December 2015

description: Operationalized as the total number of ecosystem-specific complementary technologies leveraged by the focal app. Complementary technologies were categorized as ecosystem-specific if they are available only to the apps participating in the iOS ecosystem, including the set of complementary technologies provided by Apple (such as Camera) and software applications such as Apple Map, Siri, and iCloud, as well as software applications by other developers that are available only in the iOS ecosystem.

Operationalized as the total number of ecosystem-generic complementary technologies leveraged by the focal app. A complementary technology was considered ecosystem-generic if it is also available in the Android ecosystem, for example the Facebook app, the YouTube app, and the Dropbox app, which are available in both Android and iPhone ecosystems.

The number of months between the observation month and the month in which the latest generation of the iOS was launched. This measure was multiplied by -1 for ease of interpretation with respect to the hypotheses, so higher values correspond to an early period of the new technological architecture within the ecosystem. Between 2008 and 2015 the iPhone ecosystem underwent six episodes of architectural changes enabled by new generations of the iOS.

A dichotomous measure of whether the focal app made it to Apple's daily Top 500 apps list by revenue, used as the measure of an app's successful commercialization in the main analysis. We would ideally like to use actual revenues or profits, but data on revenues earned by apps in an iOS ecosystem are not available publicly; the Top 500 list stratifies apps by daily revenue and is followed by industry observers and analysts as a reference for successful apps.
time_window: daily Top 500 list from February 2010 onward, matched to monthly observations

description: The number of a spinout's alliance partners during the five years after founding that overlap with any of its parent's partners in alliances formed before the corresponding spinout alliance. Alliances involving parents were compiled by triangulating the same three alliance databases. Overlapping alliance partners were identified with fuzzy-string comparison algorithms and then manually confirmed based on similarity scores.

The (logged) number of patents filed by the spinout during the five years after founding that cite its parent's patents. Patent citations gauge successive additions by a spinout to its parent's knowledge. The measure covers medical or veterinary science patents under IPC class A61 and is constructed after excluding spinout patents with more than 100 backward citations.

The ratio of shared medical specialties for which both a spinout and its parent received FDA approvals during the five years after founding to the number of medical specialties for which the parent received FDA approval. The list of approved devices is built by appending the PMA and 510k FDA databases. Two devices in the same medical specialty are assumed to have the highest level of overlap in serving the same customers, sales substitution, and market rivalry.

Binary treatment variable taking the value '1' if the corporate gift was made through an international NPO specialized in humanitarian relief and '0' otherwise. Coding was based on the recipient channel recorded in the donation data. The main analyses are limited to cases where the firm used only one governance mode, and observations involving corporate foundations (2.7% of the data) were dropped.

Continuous variable for the total dollar amount of each company gift disbursed within the year immediately following the disaster (from t0 to t1, where t0 is the disaster date). Cash and in-kind donations are pooled; in-kind services and products were valued monetarily using the financial value reported by the donor or other entity, current prices in the affected country, or an equivalent pecuniary value based on similar donations to the same disaster, and converted to U.S. dollars at the exchange rate on the donation date. The data cover 74,131 donations from 34,258 firms, and the average total donation for a firm to a single disaster was $1.6 million.
time_window: within the year immediately following the disaster (t0 to t1)

description: Variable that takes a value of '1' when the firm has an affiliate in the focal country and '0' otherwise, measured at the time of disaster. It was calculated from the Lexis Nexis Corporate Affiliations database. Subsidiary characteristics such as size or time-in-country are not accounted for.
time_window: at the time of the disaster

description: Composite measure that averages the percentile ranks among all countries of two World Bank Worldwide Governance Indicators dimensions, ranging from 0 (low institutional development) to 100 (high institutional development). The data set is divided into three equally sized groups using the annual 33.3 and 66.6 percentiles as cutoff points, yielding countries with low, medium, and high institutional development.
Dummy variable coded 1 for PCTs (low-status organizations) and 0 for hospitals and administrative organizations (high-status organizations).
Dummy variable coded 1 for nondoctors (low-status professionals) and 0 for doctors (high-status professionals).

Rank-ordered categorical variable for actors' hierarchical position, ranked low to high: 1 deputy head/assistant director, 2 head of service, 3 nonexecutive director, and 4 executive director with a seat on the organization's board. Because no individual occupied lower positions in the organizational hierarchy, the variable was centered around its mean.

variable_name: degree of divergence from the institutionalized model of organizations' role division
description: Rank-ordered categorical measure built from six questionnaire items assessing the degree to which change projects diverged from the institutionalized model of role division among organizations. Each item was assessed on a three-point rank ordered scale ranging from 1 (no extent) to 2 (some extent) to 3 (great extent). Change project descriptions written after three months of implementation were coded by three raters; the scale score is the average of the six items.

variable_name: degree of divergence from the institutionalized model of professionals' role division
description: Rank-ordered categorical measure built from four questionnaire items assessing the degree to which change projects diverged from the institutionalized model of role division among professionals. Each item was assessed on a three-point rank ordered scale ranging from 1 (no extent) to 2 (some extent) to 3 (great extent). Change project descriptions written after three months of implementation were coded by three raters; the scale score is the average of the four items.

variable_name: Mean of standardized citations received per patent
description: The average standardized citations received by the patents the inventor has filed up to a given point of time. Each patent's citations are standardized by the mean citations received by the population of patents applied in its same year and technological category. The variable is computed in a cumulative way up to each of the inventor's risk periods; the continuous variables are log transformed in the models.
time_window: cumulative up to each risk period

variable_name: Mean number of coinventors per patent
description: The mean number of coinventors per patent in the inventor's set of patents up to a given point in time. The number of inventors listed in the patent document captures the team that actually worked on the innovation, given that all relevant contributors must be stated in the patent document if the property right is to be enforced. The variable is computed cumulatively up to each risk period.
time_window: cumulative up to each risk period

variable_name: Percentage of patents in the core per inventor
description: The percentage of the inventor's patents that falls within the firm's core up to that time. An innovation falls within IBM's core if its patent class coincides with some of the time-variant highest frequent classes in the firm's portfolio; core classes are those representing more than 2.5% of the firm's portfolio in a given five-year time window.
time_window: cumulative up to each risk period; five-year windows for defining core classes

description: The mean dominance of IBM in the technological subcategories in which the inventor has patented up to that point. Dominance in a subcategory is the share of IBM patents filed in a given technological subcategory and time window with respect to the total number of USPTO patents in that subcategory and interval, capturing the relative importance of IBM innovations in the area.
time_window: cumulative up to each risk period; time windows for computing shares

description: Dummy variable taking value 0 if the inventor does not move in the subsequent period he is at risk, i.e., if the next patent is assigned to IBM, and 1 otherwise. Each observation captures the characteristics of the inventor's stock of knowledge at a point in time and whether he files his next patent with IBM or with a different firm.

Categorical variable that takes a value of 1 for the first entrant to a market, 2 for an early follower (second or third entrant), and 3 for a later entrant (fourth entrant and up). It is the dependent variable of the multinomial logit model of entrant profiles.
Dummy variable equal to 1 if an organization entered the market first with the semi-submersible rig, 0 otherwise. It is used as an independent variable in the market share and survival models.
Dummy variable equal to 1 if an organization was the second or third entrant, 0 otherwise. It is used as an independent variable in the market share and survival models.

The log of the time in years from product development, 1962, to the year of first-entry to each country. It is the dependent variable of the survival model of the location and timing of entry; negative coefficients denote earlier entry.
Population, used as one of two indicators of market size and reflecting oil need. Exhibit a low level of collinearity with MARKET RESERVES and MARKET DEVELOPMENT.
Expected offshore oil reserves from geophysical surveys, reflecting potential oil exploration prospects; the second indicator of market size.
A country's literacy rate, used as an indicator of educational and infrastructural development.
Market centralization is measured by a dummy variable equal to 1 if the market is the USSR, PRC, North Korea, Yugoslavia, or Romania, 0 otherwise.
The number of market incumbents with rigs in more than one country in 1962, the year of product development.
The number of markets entered by the absolute first entrant in the same year.
The number of rigs in an entrant's fleet at the time of entry.
Dummy variable equal to 1 if an entrant had rigs in more than one country at the time of entry, 0 otherwise.
Dummy variable equal to 1 if an entrant was an incumbent in the local market with other than semi-submersible rigs at the time of entry, 0 otherwise.
The proportion of all semi-submersible rigs in a market operated by an entrant. An average market share of years 9 to 11 was used to control for market duration and annual market share instability.
time_window: average of years 9 to 11 since entry

description: The number of years between a firm's entry and withdrawal from a market. Entrants surviving after 1984 were censored due to the end of the study period.
Dummy variable set to 1 if an entrant was Odeco, Santa Fe, or Sedco, 0 otherwise. The correlation between FIRST ENTRANT and EARLY PIONEER is relatively high.

The authors adopt a measure of strategic risk taking using long-term debt, R&D spending and capital expenditures from Compustat. Long-term debt was measured taking the debt with maturity beyond 1 year held on each firm's balance sheet, R&D spending was measured by the annual expenditure in a given year, and capital expenditure is the firm's spending on plant, equipment and property. All three measures loaded above 0.80 on a single factor with an eigenvalue of 2.3 accounting for 76% of the variance, so for each CEO the sum of the three expenditures was computed into a single variable.

CEO equity risk bearing was calculated using the combined value of exercisable and unexercisable stock options. The authors take the number of options from each option grant and multiply it by their corresponding spread (for in-the-money options) on the last day of each firm's fiscal year in t-1. Data on stock options was collected from Execucomp. Stock options are used to capture the CEO equity wealth that creates risk bearing.

CEO personality was measured using the California Adult Q-Set (CAQ), a 100-item validated instrument, closely following the historiometric technique used by Peterson et al. (2003). Two of three trained coders independently used the CAQ to describe each CEO based on the dossiers; ratings were aggregated to the mean rating of each CEO after reliability, consistency and agreement checks, and factor scores for each personality dimension were computed using the factor loadings for the CAQ reported by McCrae et al. (1986). All scores were subsequently rescaled to a 9-point scale. An example CAQ item for conscientiousness is 'Behaves ethically'.

Two of three trained coders independently used the CAQ to describe each CEO based on the dossiers; ratings were aggregated to the mean rating of each CEO after reliability, consistency and agreement checks, and factor scores for each personality dimension were computed using the factor loadings for the CAQ reported by McCrae et al. (1986). All scores were subsequently rescaled to a 9-point scale. An example CAQ item for neuroticism is 'Is critical, sceptical, not easy to impress'.

(1986). All scores were subsequently rescaled to a 9-point scale. An example CAQ item for extraversion is 'Behaves assertively'.

Two of three trained coders independently used the CAQ to describe each CEO based on the dossiers; ratings were aggregated to the mean rating of each CEO after reliability, consistency and agreement checks, and factor scores for each personality dimension were computed using the factor loadings for the CAQ reported by McCrae et al. (1986). All scores were subsequently rescaled to a 9-point scale. An example CAQ item for openness is 'Has a wide range of interests'.

Respondents assessed on a five-point scale the extent to which their firms implemented four practices associated with product upgrading: regular introduction of new and higher-value wines, emphasis on quality over cost, experimentation with new blends, varietals, and clones, and monitoring domestic and overseas markets. An exploratory factor analysis with oblimin rotation on 22 questions extracted five factors; two of the factors were associated with distinct aspects of product upgrading (overcoming technological and market uncertainties), each containing four items. The dependent variable was the additive score of responses to the eight questions loading on the two product upgrading factors, with a Cronbach's alpha coefficient of .78.
scale: five-point scale; additive index of eight items

description: Count of a focal firm's ties to all of the types of organizations and institutions in the survey (firms, GSIs, associations, banks, cooperatives, and schools). A tie was defined as any relationship between a focal firm and an alter, generated from the total count of mentions of an alter, including repeated counts of the same alter if a focal firm identified it as providing useful information or services in multiple operational areas. The variable was Box-Cox transformed before estimation.

Count of the number of ties between the focal firm and firm alters (wineries, independent grape growers, technology suppliers, etc.). Ties were generated from the total count of mentions of an alter, including repeated counts of the same alter when it was identified as providing useful information or services in multiple operational areas. The variable was Box-Cox transformed before estimation.

Count of the number of ties between the focal firm and government support institutions. Ties were generated from the total count of mentions of an alter, including repeated counts of the same alter when it was identified as providing useful information or services in multiple operational areas. The variable was Box-Cox transformed before estimation.

variable_name: ties to all alters except firms and GSIs
description: Count of the number of ties between the focal firm and associations (trade, peak level, etc.), banks, cooperatives, and schools (universities, technical schools, etc.). In the first set of models these alter types were entered separately as ties to associations, ties to banks, ties to cooperatives, and ties to schools; in the second set of models they were collapsed into ties to all alters except firms and GSIs. Each variable was Box-Cox transformed before estimation.

Count of the number of ties between the focal firm and public-private institutions, obtained by decomposing ties to GSIs. The public-private institutions included Fondo de Vitivinicola, Fondo para la Transformacion y Crecimiento, IDR, ProMendoza, INTA Mendoza, INTA San Juan, and ITU. The variable was Box-Cox transformed before estimation.

Count of the number of ties between the focal firm and old GSIs, obtained by decomposing ties to GSIs. Old GSIs were all GSIs other than the public-private institutions, which predated the public-private institutions and differed in their governance. The variable was Box-Cox transformed before estimation.

For each focal firm, the total number of ties to firm alters ranked in the top decile of in-degree centrality (number of ties with focal firms). Firm and GSI alters were identified separately and ranked separately by number of ties with focal firms; those in the top decile were considered highly central alters.

For each focal firm, the total number of ties to GSI alters ranked in the top decile of in-degree centrality (number of ties with focal firms). Firm and GSI alters were identified separately and ranked separately by number of ties with focal firms; those in the top decile were considered highly central alters.

variable_name: ties to top geographically diverse firms
description: The total number of ties a focal firm had to firm alters ranked in the top decile on geographic diversity. Geographic diversity of an alter was computed by calculating the alter's total number of ties, assigning those ties to zones according to the geographic location of the surveyed firms that identified the relationship, and deriving a Herfindahl index score for each alter based on the number of ties in each zone; the index was subtracted from 1 so that a higher score represented greater geographic diversity.

variable_name: ties to top geographically diverse GSIs
description: The total number of ties a focal firm had to GSI alters ranked in the top decile on geographic diversity. Geographic diversity of an alter was computed by calculating the alter's total number of ties, assigning those ties to zones according to the geographic location of the surveyed firms that identified the relationship, and deriving a Herfindahl index score for each alter based on the number of ties in each zone; the index was subtracted from 1 so that a higher score represented greater geographic diversity.

An established four-item scale capturing the extent to which the firm was involved within the IJV in drawing up strategic plans, approving budgets and plans, monitoring the joint venture, and coordinating joint venture and parent actions. Respondents were asked 'To what extent are joint venture board members involved in the following?' on a five-point scale anchored with the labels 'no extent' and 'very large extent.' Factor analysis revealed that all four indicators loaded on a single factor that explained 54.3 percent of the variance, with a Cronbach alpha of 0.74 and all loadings higher than 0.70.
scale: five-point scale from 'no extent' to 'very large extent'

description: Three Likert-type items measuring the degree to which the firms operate in similar product markets, geographic markets, and customer segments. Respondents were asked 'How similar were your firm and your partner(s) before the joint venture in terms of . . . ?' on a five-point scale ranging from 'strongly disagree' to 'strongly agree.' The three items were multiplied to form the measure, the multiplicative form reflecting the idea that competition might be less relevant if firms in the same country do not also compete in the same product markets, or if they target different customer segments.
scale: five-point agreement scale per item; items combined multiplicatively

description: A 0-1 indicator variable for whether the IJV had an R&D component. Respondents were asked to indicate which functional activities were within the scope of their collaborations in order to determine whether or not the IJV involved R&D.

The average distance between the parent firms' home countries, measured with the GLOBE practice scores and Sarala and Vaara's (2010) composite index, which represents the aggregate national cultural distance based on nine dimensions. The practice scores were used rather than the values scores because the former are more directly relevant to the activities that IJV boards of directors undertake. For joint ventures involving three or more partners the measure averages the distances between the partners' home countries; the formula combining the dimensions and partners is not readable in the provided text.

variable_name: Environmental uncertainty in the host country
description: Respondents indicated the degree to which five external factors were predictable—government policies and regulations, customer demand, supply of raw materials and equipment, competitive climate, and technological trends—on a five-point scale anchored at 'not at all predictable' and 'accurately predictable.' These Likert-type scores were reverse coded to create individual uncertainty items, and respondents separately allocated 100 points among the five factors according to their importance in determining the ultimate success of the joint venture. The measure combines the weights and the individual uncertainty scores; the combining formula is not readable in the provided text.
scale: five-point predictability scale per item, weighted by 100 points allocated across items

description: The standardized monthly volatility of the focal firm's stock in the year prior to the network change. The monthly volatility is calculated as the coefficient of variation for firm j's annual monthly stock closing price: the standard deviation of the firm's monthly closing price divided by its average monthly closing price for the year. Dividing the standard deviation by the mean allows the measurement of uncertainty to be interpretable across firms with different price ranges; the higher the volatility, the more uncertainty. Monthly stock price data were obtained from Compustat and from CRSP when Compustat data were unavailable.
time_window: the year prior to the network change (i = 1987 to 1992)

description: The mean monthly stock price volatility of all sampled firms in the focal firm's industry grouping in the year prior to the network change, not including the focal firm. The same monthly price coefficient of variation used for firm-specific uncertainty is averaged across the Fortune firms in the focal firm's industry grouping. Uncertainty is measured in year i and network partner changes are examined in year i + 1.
level: firm-year (industry measure assigned to the focal firm)
time_window: year i, with network changes examined in year i + 1

description: A count of the annual alliance broadening events for each sampled firm: an alliance broadening event occurs when a focal firm establishes an alliance with another firm where no alliance existed from 1988 to the year prior to the observed year. Using 1988 as the base year, alliance changes were examined during 1989, 1990, 1991, 1992, and 1993.

An interlock broadening event occurs when a focal firm establishes a sent or received interlock with another firm where no interlock existed during the year prior to the observed year. Using 1990 as the base year, interlock changes were examined from 1990 to 1991, 1991 to 1992, and 1992 to 1993.

A count of the annual alliance reinforcing events for each sampled firm: an alliance reinforcing event occurs when the focal firm establishes another alliance with a firm with whom they had an alliance during any year from 1988 to the year prior to the observed year. If, for example, two additional interlocks are created with an existing interlock partner, two reinforcing events are counted.

An interlock reinforcing event occurs when the focal firm establishes a sent or received interlock with a firm with whom they had an existing interlock during the prior year. If two additional interlocks are created with an existing interlock partner, two reinforcing events are counted.

The authors counted firms adding an interlock to a firm with whom they had an alliance in the past, or adding an alliance to a firm with whom they had an interlock, for the years from 1988 to 1992, giving five years of firm observations. To count alliances added to a firm with whom they had an interlock, interlock ties in 1985 were compared with alliances for the years from 1988 to 1990, and the interlock data in the prior year were used for alliances during 1991 to 1993. Because interlock data were not available in 1989, interlocks added to an existing alliance could not be calculated for 1989.
time_window: 1988-1992, with 1985 interlock data as a base

description: Captures whether the focal product innovation is carried through autonomous governance (coded 0) or horizontal collaboration (coded 1). All independent variables of the first-stage model were estimated at the time of project launch, which the authors assume is one year prior to prototype first flight.
time_window: at project launch, assumed one year prior to prototype first flight

description: Captures the extent to which firms made the choice predicted by the first-stage model. For firms that chose to collaborate, Governance Fit is the first-stage predicted probability of alliance; for firms that opted for autonomous governance, it is computed as 1 minus the predicted probability of alliance.

The cumulative number of units produced over the life cycle of the aircraft. For the 64 aircraft still in production by the end of the study period (2000), unit sales were extrapolated based on the average sales schedule of all terminated aircraft projects.
The number of years between the prototype first flight and the first delivery of a production aircraft.
time_window: from prototype first flight to first delivery of a production aircraft

variable_name: Price (price of the rock / price of ore)
description: A price per ton of ore mined, specific to each mine-year, computed by multiplying the average quantity of each mineral found per ton of rock mined by its international price, as reported by the Chilean Ministry of Mining and the World Bank. It reflects the exogenous shock to the price of the output that each mine experienced during the period under study. The variable is log-transformed and mean-centered.

Average annual earnings per employee at mine i in year t, which is the actual average compensation received by employees after all social security costs and taxes have been deducted. The variable includes bonus payments made in year t, if any. Because the database reports average earnings per employee per hour, average hours worked per employee and bonus payments, the authors obtain average earnings per worker in year t by multiplying average earnings per hour by average hours worked and adding bonus payments. The variable is log-transformed and mean-centered.

Country score from the Executive Opinion Survey question 'In your country, wages are (1 = set by a centralized bargaining process, 7 = up to each company)'. A high value implies a more decentralized negotiation process, so the item is reverse coded relative to the centralization construct. The raw scores on the one-to-seven scale are used and the variable is mean-centered and not log-transformed.

Country score from the Executive Opinion Survey question 'The hiring and firing of workers is (1 = impeded by regulations, 7 = flexibly determined by employers)'. A higher value implies more flexibility to hire and fire workers. The raw scores on the one-to-seven scale are used and the variable is mean-centered and not log-transformed.

Country score from the Executive Opinion Survey question 'In your country, pay is (1 = not related to worker productivity, 7 = strongly related to worker productivity)'. A higher value implies that wages are more closely correlated with worker productivity. The raw scores on the one-to-seven scale are used and the variable is mean-centered and not log-transformed.

A continuous variable ranging from zero to one, where a higher value indicates more state ownership: zero implies no state ownership (the mine is completely privately owned) and one indicates that the state is the sole owner of the mine. Total state participation in a mine is the sum of the state's direct and indirect participation, where indirect participation is the percentage of state ownership through another (nonstate) firm. The authors review the name and percent ownership of each mine's shareholders for each year and check the shareholders of each owner to determine whether they are governmental agencies. Because of its almost nonexistent within-mine variance, the variable is not included as a standalone regressor but enters the models through its interaction with price; it is mean-centered and not log-transformed.

The complete ownership structure of each mine in each year is analyzed and a Herfindahl-Hirschman index of ownership concentration is computed, equal to the sum of the squares of the individual ownership percentages. A higher HHI value implies higher ownership concentration.

The level of knowledge created is measured by summing the ISI impact factors for all journal articles published by each scientist each year. Weighting each publication by the ISI impact factor for the journal in which it was published allows the relative importance of the knowledge provided to the scientific community to be evaluated. The measure also eliminates any advantage of larger over smaller journals, of frequently issued over less frequently issued journals, and of older over newer journals.

Average tie strength is captured through the frequency of interaction, indicated by the number of publications with a given coauthor during the previous three years, averaged across all of the researcher's coauthors. Specifically, the number of coauthors a scientist published with during the previous three years is totaled (double counting those coauthors with whom the author published two papers, triple counting those with whom the author had published three papers, etc.) and divided by the number of unique coauthors. The measure reflects that working with the same coauthor on a given number of projects results in a higher frequency of interaction than working with different coauthors on the same number of projects.

Following Borgatti et al. (1999), a density score was calculated for each scientist's professional (ego) network as ego network density = actual ties / maximum number of pairs. Actual ties are defined as the number of a scientist's coauthors who have published at least one other paper with another of the scientist's coauthors during the previous three years, while pairs are defined as potential ties. An average density measure was calculated for eight three-year windows from 1989 through 1998.

Total number of tactical competitive actions initiated by a focal firm in the 90 days after a rival's earnings release. Tactical competitive actions are counted as the total number of pricing actions, marketing actions, product or service improvements, minor production adjustments, and legal actions, identified and classified from news articles in the RavenPack News Analytics database. The variable is calculated relative to the time of a rival's earnings release, so actions falling in the window are counted regardless of whether they took place in the same quarter or in different quarters. Strategic actions are not counted because they are implausible within 90 days of a rival's earnings surprise.
time_window: 90 days after a rival's earnings release

description: Absolute value of the difference between the rival firm's actual reported quarterly earnings and analysts' consensus estimates - the median forecasted earnings for that fiscal quarter among all analysts who covered the firm - scaled by the rival's stock price at the end of the previous quarter. The variable takes this value for all observations in which earnings were lower than consensus estimates and is 0 otherwise. The absolute value is used because a focal firm's competitive actions are likely to increase with the magnitude of the deviation.
time_window: quarter of the rival's earnings announcement; stock price at the end of the previous quarter

description: Absolute value of the difference between the rival firm's actual earnings and analysts' consensus estimates, scaled by the rival's stock price at the end of the previous quarter, for all observations in which earnings were higher than consensus estimates, and 0 otherwise. Defined symmetrically to the rival negative earnings surprise.
time_window: quarter of the rival's earnings announcement; stock price at the end of the previous quarter

description: Language complexity of the rival's conference call measured using the Fog Index, which is based on two aspects of language complexity: average sentence length and the number of complex words used (words containing three or more syllables). The score indicates how many years of formal education a person needs in order to understand a message on the first reading. The formula block in the paper was not readable in this source, so the exact specification of the index is not reproduced here.

A word-count measure of the vagueness of the rival's conference call: a count of vague words and expressions normalized by the total number of words in each conference call to control for call length. Vague words and phrases are identified using Hiller's Communication Vagueness Dictionary, which contains 362 vague words and expressions on 10 dimensions of vagueness, including qualifiers before a number, nonnumerical terms referring to indefinite amounts, approximation terms, and bluffing terms.

Dichotomous variable taken from the first general TQM question (Appendix 1b, item 1), coded 1 = TQM and 0 = no TQM, based on whether the organization had ever made a significant commitment to Total Quality Management or a similar Total Quality program.

A 6-point scale (Appendix 1b, item 2) on which respondents compared how advanced the implementation of their quality program was with programs of other organizations they were familiar with, ranging from far more advanced to no significant involvement.

Mean response to all TQM items in Appendix 1c except those for flexible manufacturing, which do not apply to service firms. The items are rated on a 0 to 5 scale (5 = highly advanced in implementation; 1 = have not begun implementation but intend to; 0 = do not intend to implement).
The number of years since the firm adopted TQM, used to compare long-term adopters, defined as firms with more than 4 years of TQM experience, with short-term adopters.
Dichotomous contextual variable taking the value 0 for service firms and 1 for manufacturing firms.

Respondents rated their firms' overall performance over the past 3 years on the five items in Appendix 1d, using the 1-5 agree-disagree scale (5 = agree strongly, 1 = disagree strongly). The items address profitability, sales growth, and overall financial performance.
Respondents indicated how their TQM programs had impacted performance by answering each item in Appendix 1e on the agree-disagree scale; the measure captures satisfaction with the TQM program.
Scale measuring top management commitment to the quality program, with items rated on the 0 to 5 implementation scale of Appendix 1c.
Scale measuring the adoption and communication of the TQM philosophy, with items rated on the 0 to 5 implementation scale of Appendix 1c.
Scale measuring closeness to customers, with items rated on the 0 to 5 implementation scale of Appendix 1c.
Scale measuring closeness to suppliers, with items rated on the 0 to 5 implementation scale of Appendix 1c.
Scale measuring competitive benchmarking activity, with items rated on the 0 to 5 implementation scale of Appendix 1c.
Scale measuring training in quality principles, problem-solving, and teamwork, with items rated on the 0 to 5 implementation scale of Appendix 1c.
Scale measuring an open, less bureaucratic organization with empowered teams, with items rated on the 0 to 5 implementation scale of Appendix 1c.
Scale measuring employee involvement, suggestion systems, autonomy, and interaction with customers and suppliers, with items rated on the 0 to 5 implementation scale of Appendix 1c.
Scale measuring a zero-defects mentality, with items rated on the 0 to 5 implementation scale of Appendix 1c.
Scale measuring flexible manufacturing practices, applicable only to manufacturers, with items rated on the 0 to 5 implementation scale of Appendix 1c.
Scale measuring process-improvement programs reducing cycle times, paperwork, and waste, with items rated on the 0 to 5 implementation scale of Appendix 1c.
Scale measuring the measurement of quality performance, with items rated on the 0 to 5 implementation scale of Appendix 1c.

Cumulative abnormal stock market return over a two-day event window (t = -1/0) around the announcement of the new alliance. Abnormal returns are estimated with the world market model over an estimation period of 250 trading days (t = -260 to t = -11), using local market indexes that include airlines in their home country, the MSCI-EAFE for world market returns adjusted orthogonally to the local indexes, and exchange rates between the U.S. dollar and the respective local currencies. For firms from Australia, Hong Kong, Japan, Korea, Malaysia, New Zealand, Singapore, and Thailand the data were lagged by one day to account for time zone differences.
time_window: two-day window (t = -1/0); estimation period of 250 trading days

description: Number of itineraries that could be created by combining the city-pair markets contributed by the new alliance with the existing city-pair markets to which the focal firm had access through other ongoing alliances at the time of the new alliance formation. The authors identified and counted all combinations where the to-destination of the existing city-pair markets matched the from-destination of the newly contributed city-pair market/s and where the from-destination of the existing city-pair markets matched the to-destination of the newly contributed city-pair market/s. Only combinations for which the ratio of the total stopover flight stage length to the total direct flight stage length did not exceed 125 percent were considered.
time_window: at the time of the new alliance formation

description: Sum of the individual increases in market domain overlap between the focal firm and the alliance partners in its alliance portfolio due to the newly formed alliance. For each partner j, the city-pair markets served by the partner through direct or indirect service that overlapped with the city-pair market/s contributed by the new code sharing agreement and/or with the city-pair market/s the focal firm could serve by combining its own city-pair markets with the newly contributed ones were identified and counted. This sum was divided by the total number of city-pair markets served by partner j to assess the proportion of j's business affected, and the individual overlap increases were then summed across the portfolio partners. Indirect services were only considered when the ratio of total stopover to total direct flight stage length did not exceed 125 percent.
time_window: at the time of the new alliance formation

description: Reported investments in R&D per sales dollar, taken from a single question on the mailed questionnaire. R&D intensity, which is the proportion of sales revenues spent on R&D, is used as a covariate in the model. The authors note that this measure is probably not a perfect indicator of R&D activity.

Changes (improvements) in market share for the principal product of the firm, measured with a single item and controlled by initial market share. It was validated by correlation with market share in the major product group of the firm or unit and with new product revenue.

A constructed summed scale consisting of answers to two items on the mailed questionnaire: the general level of automation in the plant ('your factory') and the highest level achieved. Both items were scored on an anchored 10-point scale. The Cronbach alpha for this two-item scale was 0.80. The measure could not be independently verified because plant visits were not arranged.

The average of percentage improvements in five areas: speed of product development, on-time deliveries, customer service, manufacturing lead time, and delivery time. The standardized item alpha of this scale was 0.75; the mean of the average percentage improvement was 24%. Product variety was excluded because including it lowered the standardized item alpha and had a low corrected item-total correlation.

For every firm, the sum of the absolute deviations of its topic weights from the industry-average topic weight is calculated over every topic of the 100-topic LDA model. Primary four-digit industry codes are used for these calculations, taking the industry as representative of the category the firm predominantly operates in. The measure mirrors measures of strategic deviation or strategic distinctiveness, and its square is included to test for curvilinearity.
scale: ranges from 0.254 to 1.987, with an average of 0.879

description: The sum of the standard deviations of the topic weights over every topic, where N is the number of firms with a website in the industry. Industry-specific spreads in each topic's usage are thus calculated and summed up. The variable is interacted with distinctiveness and its square.

Respondents were asked to indicate in which bracket their total revenues in Euro earned during the past year fit, from no revenues (value zero) through ten higher brackets up to more than 5,000,000 (ten). Respondents were asked to categorize their revenues, as pretests showed that they tended to be unaware of their exact revenues. For the analysis the brackets were combined into 0-12,499, 12,500-24,999, 25,000-49,999, 50,000-99,999, and 100,000+ Euro, implying that the model estimates a set of four equations.
scale: eleven ordered revenue brackets coded zero to ten; combined into five brackets for the analysis

description: We calculated ownership concentration as the percentage of shares held in blocks of 5 percent, or more. Ownership concentration was considerably greater in these firms than that found in the United States, averaging just over 45 percent, although there was significant variation in concentration.

An indicator variable designating whether a firm had adopted a stock-based incentive plan. Both stock option plans and phantom-stock incentive plans were coded as stock-based incentive plans; if a firm had a stock-based incentive plan during the year, the variable was coded 1, and 0 otherwise. Due to data limitations the authors were unable to measure the size of stock-based incentive compensation grants. The data were collected and coded on a firm-by-firm and year-by-year basis.

Indicator variables coding each firm's accounting convention: if the firm adopted GAAP or IAS accounting conventions during a year it was coded 1, and it was coded 0 if the convention was HGB. Firms make explicit disclosures in their annual reports about the accounting method used. Under the strict coding procedure, if firms reported key figures like net income, assets, etc. according to German accounting principles they were counted as using HGB accounting rules; if these key figures were computed according to the rules of IAS or GAAP they were counted as using the more transparent method.

Our measure of divestitures is the number of divestitures completed during the year. The authors note that this type of count measure has been widely used in studies of acquisitions, divestitures, and alliances.

Return on sales, smoothed over 2 years to avoid abnormal events or years from biasing the results. The measure is adjusted by industry, so that performance is gauged relative to firms facing similar economic and competitive factors, and prior levels of firm performance are controlled for.

Market capitalization values were log-transformed. The measure is adjusted by industry, so that performance is gauged relative to firms facing similar economic and competitive factors, and prior levels of firm performance are controlled for.

The market-to-book ratio measures how much value the market expects the firm to be able to extract from its pool of assets and is theoretically and empirically equivalent to Tobin's q. The measure is adjusted by industry, and prior levels of firm performance are controlled for.

variable_name: Stock-based incentive plan adoption and transparent accounting adoption indicators
description: Governance reform is measured by two firm-year indicator variables. Stock plan adoption is 1 if the firm had a stock option or phantom-stock incentive plan during the year and 0 otherwise. Accounting change is 1 if the firm adopted GAAP or IAS accounting conventions during the year and 0 if it used HGB. Both are coded firm by firm and year by year and enter the Poisson divestiture models lagged one year. The two indicators are recorded separately as m_stock_plan and m_acct_plan.

variable_name: Change in business strategy similarity (focal firm)
description: Business strategy is measured by resource allocations across five strategic dimensions: advertising intensity (advertising expense/sales), plant and equipment newness (net plant and equipment/gross plant and equipment), research and development intensity (R&D expense/sales), overhead efficiency (selling, general, and administrative expense/sales), and financial leverage (total debt/equity). Similarity of the focal firm to the other N-1 firms in its primary industry (two-digit SIC code) is an overall Euclidean distance score that adjusts for the number of competitors and differences in metrics across dimensions; the equation is not readable in the text as extracted. Change in strategic similarity was measured for the focal firm as strategic similarity at t+2 minus strategic similarity in the current year, and this value was subtracted from the highest value in the sample so that higher values indicate greater increases in similarity.
time_window: two-year change (t+2 minus t), analyzed over 1990-1994

variable_name: Change in business strategy similarity of tied-to firms
description: An analogous change-in-similarity measure of business strategy was developed for each tied-to firm, lagged by one year, and the average value was computed. The set of tied-to firms includes all companies at which a director from the focal firm had a board appointment, including the board ties of both inside and outside directors; indirect ties were not included.
level: firm-year (averaged across the focal firm's interlock partners)
time_window: tied-to firm measure lagged by one year

variable_name: Change in acquisition activity similarity (focal firm)
description: Acquisition activity similarity was measured with measures that directly parallel the business strategy similarity measures. The level of acquisition activity is the number of acquisitions over a two-year period; an acquisition is classified as related when the two-digit SIC code of the acquiring firm matched that of the acquired firm and as diversified when the codes did not match. Separate analyses were conducted for each type of acquisition.

variable_name: Change in acquisition activity similarity of tied-to firms
description: An analogous change-in-similarity measure of acquisition activity was developed for each tied-to firm, lagged by one year, and the average value was computed across the companies at which a director from the focal firm had a board appointment. Separate measures were used for related and diversified acquisitions.
level: firm-year (averaged across the focal firm's interlock partners)
time_window: tied-to firm measure lagged by one year

description: The use of performance-contingent compensation was measured for each year as the total value of long-term incentive grants to the CEO divided by the CEO's total direct compensation. Long-term incentive grants include stock options, restricted stock, and so-called performance incentives (granted in shares, units or cash); the Black-Scholes method was used to estimate the value of stock options and other stock-based grants were valued using the market price on the date of grant. Measures of compensation similarity directly parallel the measures of strategy similarity described above.

variable_name: Change in compensation similarity of tied-to firms
description: An analogous change-in-similarity measure of performance-contingent compensation was developed for each tied-to firm, lagged by one year, and the average value was computed across the companies at which a director from the focal firm had a board appointment.
level: firm-year (averaged across the focal firm's interlock partners)
time_window: tied-to firm measure lagged by one year

description: Survey items asked respondents to assess the extent to which the firm's strategic decision-making process involved specific actions to determine the level of spending on R&D: acquiring data on how much competitors spend on R&D; comparing the spending of competitors with spending at the focal firm; and using this analysis to plan changes in spending levels to ensure that practices are in line with other firms in the industry. Five additional items asked about the use of mimetic processes in determining other dimensions of business strategy, and an analogous set of questions gauged the use of imitation in making decisions about CEO compensation and acquisitions; the items loaded on three factors with reliabilities (alpha) of .86 for the business strategy scale, .87 for the acquisition activity scale, and .91 for the compensation scale. Items used 5-point Likert-type response formats and were answered by CEOs and, in a second questionnaire, by outside directors (kappa coefficients exceeded .75 for all scale items but one).
time_window: exogenous construct measured in the prior year (t-1)

variable_name: Change in similarity to industry peers on a policy dimension (tied-to firms)
description: Cross-policy similarity of tied-to firms is the lagged change in similarity to industry competitors on one policy dimension (business strategy, acquisition activity or CEO compensation), averaged across all firms where a director of the focal firm held a board appointment.
scale: Change in similarity score, averaged across tied-to firms

variable_name: Change in similarity to industry peers on a different policy dimension (focal firm)
description: Cross-policy similarity of the focal firm is the change in the focal firm's similarity to other firms in its industry on one policy dimension (business strategy, acquisition activity or CEO compensation), predicted from tied-to firms' similarity on a different dimension. Similarity is a Euclidean distance based score computed from archival data.

Coefficient of variation (standard deviation divided by the mean) of the average winter snowpack depth in feet at each resort, computed over the previous 10 years. Average winter snowpack depths for each year were calculated using monthly mean winter snowpack depth data from November to April, simulated with the PRMS program. The measure is lagged by one year, so that in 2003 ecological uncertainty is the coefficient of variation of average winter snowpack depth from 1993 to 2002.

SACC rating of new terrain developed over the previous year, used to capture buffering adaptation: terrain expansion can buffer ski resorts from snowfall uncertainty by providing access to potentially snowier terrain. The raw rating measures how well resorts avoided this practice, so it was reverse-coded to capture the extent to which resorts adopted it. Each rating was converted to a ratio score (points awarded divided by total possible points) because maximum scores changed from year to year.

SACC rating of new snowmaking adopted over the previous year, used to capture substitution adaptation: snowmaking, where feasible, is a ground-water-intensive substitute for snowfall. The raw rating measures how well resorts avoided this practice, so it was reverse-coded to capture the extent to which resorts adopted it. Each rating was converted to a ratio score (points awarded divided by total possible points).

SACC rating of new real estate development on undisturbed land from the previous year, used to capture diversification adaptation: on-mountain real estate development generates alternative revenue streams that are less vulnerable to ecological uncertainty. The raw rating measures how well resorts avoided this practice, so it was reverse-coded to capture the extent to which resorts adopted it. Each rating was converted to a ratio score (points awarded divided by total possible points).

A summative index of four SACC ratings of resorts' practices to reduce and promote reductions in GHG emissions. Before summing the ratings into the index, each rating was converted to a ratio score (points awarded divided by total possible points) because the maximum SACC scores differed across ratings and the authors wanted the practices to receive equal emphasis. The authors treat the measure as a formative construct.

League of Conservation Voters (LCV) scores, which measure the percentage frequency of each state's congressional delegation legislative votes in favor of issues on the 'environmental agenda' in each year. The authors average the LCV scores for each state's House of Representatives and Senate congressional delegation in each year. The measure is at the state level and is lagged by one year.

Brand equity scores provided by the Harris Poll EquiTrend study. The company conducts annual online surveys of more than 20,000 U.S. customers aged 15 and older that are representative of the entire population, and it calculates brand equity scores for more than 1,000 brands. Brand equity (0-100) is measured by data on perceived quality, which is the primary component of a brand's image, and familiarity, which corresponds to brand awareness. The authors focused on publicly traded companies with a prominent central brand that accounts for the majority of firm profits, identified by two independent coders.

MSCI's human capital metric, capturing skill-, motivation-, or opportunity-enhancing HR practices. Each year, MSCI evaluates about 1,800 global companies, drawing on several sources such as company interviews and corporate documents, to calculate human capital scores (0-10). The score is determined by the dimensions of employee motivation and development (EMD), health and safety (HS), and labor relations (LR), where EMD captures training and development programs and employee engagement, HS evaluates a company's health and safety management system, and LR assesses the extent to which companies provide performance incentives and offer professional development programs.

A forward-looking financial metric that the authors use to gauge firm value; it is less affected by accounting conventions and is independent of industry. The authors follow Chung and Pruitt's (1994) method to calculate Tobin's q.
time_window: one-year lag after the independent variables

description: The authors used cash flow from operations scaled by total assets. The authors state that linking brand equity and human capital to cash flow metrics allows marketers and HR managers to communicate their contribution to value added in financial language.
time_window: one-year lag after the independent variables

description: Computed as the ratio of a firm's quarterly cash flow coefficient of variation to the market's cash flow coefficient of variation. Annual coefficients of variation are calculated on the basis of the respective year's quarterly cash flow observations. Because the cash flow volatility model exhibits a non-normal distribution, the authors applied a log-transformation.
time_window: annual, based on the respective year's quarterly cash flow observations

description: Industries were first classified using the North American Industry Classification System (NAICS), with codes starting with 3 treated as manufacturing and services otherwise. Services were then subdivided into retail (e.g., Best Buy) and services (e.g., US Airways), and manufacturing industries were subdivided into fast-moving consumer goods (FMCG; e.g., Coca-Cola) and consumer durables (e.g., Toyota). 'Services' constitutes the reference group in the estimated models.
Robustness measure only; no description reported in the main analysis.

The total number of divestiture events—sell-offs, liquidations, or spinoffs—each business segment conducted in a given year. The count is used as a measure of divestiture activity because each event represents a meaningful change requiring managerial attention. The sample includes firms with no divestiture activity.

The count of divestiture events that involved selling, liquidating, or spinning off a complete resource such as a unit or subsidiary of a given business segment. Events were coded as full by reading the description of the resource being sold, starting from SDC Platinum and using LexisNexis where information was unavailable.

The count of divestiture events where only a portion of the unit, a product line, or plant from an ongoing business unit were sold, liquidated, or spun off. Coding used SDC Platinum descriptions supplemented by LexisNexis when needed.

Takes the absolute value of the Historical aspiration gap when this gap is negative, and 0 otherwise, to reflect decreasing performance. Historical aspiration gap is the absolute value of the difference between a firm's prior ROA and the historical aspiration level, which is the average ROA of the last three years. The variable is lagged by one year.
time_window: three-year historical ROA average; lagged one year

description: Takes the value of the Historical aspiration gap when this gap is positive, and 0 otherwise, to reflect increasing performance. Historical aspiration gap is the absolute value of the difference between a firm's prior ROA and the historical aspiration level, which is the average ROA of the last three years. The variable is lagged by one year.
time_window: three-year historical ROA average; lagged one year

description: Corporate return on assets, measured as the prior level of corporate performance. Used as a main effect and to test the joint effects of performance level and historical aspiration gap. The variable is lagged by one year.

Coded from the question 'Compared with people you consider peers in your chosen field, how successful has your career been? Would you say that you are ahead/level/behind your peers?'. Coded as 1 (ahead of positive gap), 2 (level with no gap), or 3 (behind negative gap). The authors note the coding imposes equidistance between the aspiration levels and that results hold when using dummies. Both linear and squared aspiration terms are entered in the models.

Respondents were asked to rate eight different collaboration scenarios. Every scenario combined one funding source, one type of organization, and four specifications about the individual partner (shared contacts, prior familiarity, shared knowledge, and seniority). Respondents expressed low or high interest in the scenarios by rating them between 0 and 10.

The mean of six items measuring self-assessments of networking skills. The item responses range from -3 (strongly disagree) to +3 (strongly agree) on a Likert-type scale. Sample questions are 'I very often see opportunities for collaboration between people' and 'I always try to forge connections between people dealing with similar issues'. The factor analysis with promax rotation of these six items revealed a single factor, and the Cronbach's alpha of the scale was 0.82.

A subset of respondents seeking specific knowledge was presented with six names of network members with expertise in their chosen domain and asked how well they knew the person (between 0 and 10) and whether they would want to collaborate with that person. The authors coded every response on knowledge/preference that was above (below) the respective mean as 1 (0) and summed the number of times the actor preference was above the mean while the actor knowledge was below the mean. Theoretically the variable runs from 0 to 6, but 0-5 in the data; its correlation with network awareness is -0.32.

Defined as the sum of the responses to how well the respondents knew each of the six network members with expertise in their chosen domain (rated between 0 and 10 for each named person). Its correlation with networking openness is -0.32.

Captures the introduction of the mobile number portability (MNP) policy in a given country. It is equal to 1 for observations in the quarters after the policy introduction in the focal country and 0 for observations before the policy introduction. MNP introduced an exogenous reduction in customer switching costs.

Average revenue per user (ARPU) for the prepaid (basic) plan in a given quarter, used to capture the firm's average price per user in the prepaid plan. ARPU refers to the total recurring revenue per user per month and is averaged for a given quarter because GSMA Intelligence reports all variables at the quarterly level. The natural logarithm of the variable is used to avoid skewness.

Average revenue per user (ARPU) for the postpaid (advanced) plan in a given quarter, capturing the firm's average price per user in the postpaid plan. It refers to the total recurring revenue per user per month, averaged for a given quarter, and is used in natural logarithm form to avoid skewness.

Average revenue per user for the firm overall, used to proxy for the average market price. ARPU refers to the total recurring revenue per user per month, averaged for a given quarter, and is used in natural logarithm form to avoid skewness.

Earnings before interest and taxes, calculated as the firm's total operating profit in a given quarter, before interest and tax, excluding any profit or loss on the disposal of fixed assets and exceptional items, and reported in billions. The authors also construct EBIT (log), the natural logarithm of EBIT after a transformation to avoid nonpositive numbers.
The proportion of a firm's postpaid subscribers relative to its total subscribers in a given quarter. The value ranges between 0 and 1.

An index of concentration in the postpaid market that varies between 0 and 10,000, calculated based on firms' postpaid market shares prior to MNP, which are unaffected by potential changes due to the introduction of the policy. A high Postpaid HHI indicates that the advanced version market is a concentrated market where firms have high market power (arguably due to differentiation). To facilitate reporting the authors divide Postpaid HHI by 1,000 so that the coefficient of interest captures the effect of a 1,000-point increase.

Branch performance is based on branch-level sales measured monthly for the period February 2010 to January 2011. The measure is an index of how well the branch met its sales goal each month, with a range of 0-150% representing the percentage of the branch sales goal achieved in that month. Branch performance is lagged by one month because sales before and after a turnover event within a given month cannot be differentiated. Sales goals are set at the corporate level based on size of market, number of employees, and previous branch performance, and are revised annually.

To isolate a single branch-level turnover event for employees, the first turnover event during the sample period within each branch was used. Each branch was assigned a value of 0 for any month prior to the initial turnover event and a value of 1 for the month of turnover and any subsequent months in the sample. A statistically significant and negative coefficient means that branch sales performance decreases at the time of a turnover event.

The manager turnover event was coded using the same methodology as the employee turnover event: a value of 0 for any month prior to the manager turnover event and a value of 1 for the month of turnover and any subsequent months in the sample. A statistically significant and negative coefficient means that branch sales performance decreases at the time of the manager turnover event.

The recovery rate for employees was coded by assigning a value of 0 to any month prior to and including the month of the initial employee turnover event, with the value increasing by one for all subsequent months (i.e., 1, 2, 3, etc.). The variable captures the change in linear performance after a turnover event, so a significant positive coefficient means the linear growth rate is faster for branches after the turnover event.
scale: 0 to number of months since the turnover event
time_window: months following the initial employee turnover event within the sample window

description: The recovery rate for managers was coded by assigning a value of 0 to any month prior to and including the month of the initial manager turnover event, with the value increasing by one for all subsequent months. The variable captures the change in linear performance after the manager turnover event, so a significant positive coefficient means the linear growth rate is faster for branches after the event.
scale: 0 to number of months since the turnover event
time_window: months following the initial manager turnover event within the sample window

description: Interdependence was measured in December 2009 using two survey items: 'The people I work with cooperate to get the job done' and 'People in my work branch help me out when my workload is high.'
