The alpha value for the measure is .71, the mean rwg is .85, ICC1 is .16 and ICC2 is .52; the agreement and ICC results were used to justify aggregating individual scores to create a branch-level metric of interdependence. The items were developed for the sponsoring organization by a consulting firm.

The total number of formerly nontradable shares (owned by controlling shareholders) transferred to the ownership of tradable shareholders (owned by minority shareholders) as compensation, divided by the number of previously tradable shares. When cash grants were used alone or in combination with stock grants, the firm converted the cash value into an equivalent amount of stock using the prereform stock price to calculate an overall compensation ratio. A higher compensation ratio indicates greater compensation paid by controlling shareholders to minority shareholders. The variable was winsorized at both the 1st and 99th percentiles and ranges from 0.05 to 1.27 across the sample firms.

Calculated by dividing the firm's market valuation by the firm's book value (divided by 100). It is based on the q-theory arbitrage argument that the firm will invest when the ratio of the market valuation of a firm's capital stock to its replacement value exceeds one. A higher Tobin's Q indicates that the firm expects to create higher value from future investments.

Initially developed by Kaplan and Zingales (1997) and subsequently formulated by Lamont, Polk, and Saa-Requejo (2001), and commonly used in research and practice in finance to capture firms' overall financing constraints. It is constructed from a model that predicts the probability that a firm becomes financially constrained based on debts (including bank loans), cash flow, market value, dividends, and cash holding, all scaled by total assets. A higher value of the K-Z Index indicates more severe overall financing constraints faced by the firm.

The proportion of nontradable shares among all outstanding shares, described as a direct measure of controlling shareholders' ownership benefits. Subsamples for testing the moderating effect were formed by splitting firms at the median value of Nontradables.

A common measure of the extent to which large shareholders in the firm can reap private gains, following Claessens et al. (2002). The authors identify each firm's controller as disclosed in its annual report, calculate the controller's cash flow rights and control rights along the ownership chain (control rights equal the weakest link in the chain, cash flow rights the product of the ownership stakes), and take the difference between control rights and cash flow rights. Subsamples were formed by splitting firms at the median value of the Control-cash gap.

Count of all voluntary public disclosures about the firm's independent R&D efforts occurring between the inception of an R&D project and the initial discovery phase, before the firm began to develop and test new products or services. Each disclosure was coded as 1 if it included information of the particular type and 0 otherwise, and the variable equals the sum of Early-Stage R&D Disclosures Excluding Alliances and Alliance Early-Stage R&D Disclosures. Measured in year t-1.

Count of early-stage R&D disclosures that make no mention of R&D activities involving one or more partners. Each disclosure was coded as 1 if it included information of the particular type and 0 otherwise. Measured in year t-1.

Count of early-stage R&D disclosures involving the focal firm and one or more partners. Each disclosure was coded as 1 if it included information of the particular type and 0 otherwise. Disclosures were coded as R&D or non-R&D and each R&D disclosure was further coded as early-stage, early-stage alliance, or nonalliance early-stage, with an inter-rater reliability above 90 percent. Measured in year t-1.

Binary variable equaling 1 when voluntary departures occur in a firm-year and 0 when they do not. Data were collected from the LexisNexis database of articles and press releases, focusing on firm press releases issued through PR Newswire and Business Wire, which report turnover at the level of director, vice president, or above as identified by the disclosing firm. Turnovers were classified as voluntary when press releases provide information about an executive's future employment and do not suggest he/she was fired, forced from his/her position, or departed because of unspecified policy differences, a classification verified against secondary public sources.

Ratio of a firm's stock market value to its book value of total equity, included to control for expectations about the firms' future prospects, where a high market-to-book ratio indicates that investors believe the firm represents a strong future investment opportunity. To test the interaction hypotheses the panel was split into two subsamples based on firms' market-to-book ratio above and below the median. Measured in year t-1.

Annual self-reported data on the product portfolio of each winery in The Wines and Vines Annual Directory were used to indicate whether a winery was present in the table wine market. The mere fact of a winery's mentioning table wine as being among its offerings was validated with ancillary models as an adequate substitute for a direct measure of table wine production by individual wineries. The variable is coded 1 for yes and 0 for no.

Indicator distinguishing wineries that were table wine producers from their founding from those that were not. It is entered alongside later entry into the niche in the mortality models to separate founding in the new niche from diversification into it.

variable_name: Table wine producer through later entry
description: Indicator for wineries that initiated table wine production later in their histories, that is, existing wineries that diversified into the table wine niche after founding. It is entered in the mortality models together with table wine production from founding.

Each organization's life history was divided into a series of annual spells, or organization-years; a censoring indicator takes a value of 0 if the organization was alive at the end of a spell and 1 if it failed during a spell. Covariates were assumed to change as annual step functions and were calculated at the beginning of the year in which the organization reached a given age. Parameters were estimated by maximum likelihood allowing for right-censored data, with the mortality rate specified as a Gompertz model in which age dependence is captured by an exponential term in age.

A measure of the broad construct established by summing and standardizing the standardized measures for autonomy in hiring, distance from the plan, importance of profit, incentive intensity, and dependence on officials (reverse coded). It is an 'emergent' construct, construed as an 'effect' of its indicators rather than a 'latent' construct. As a check for known group validity, central and provincial-level state-owned enterprises had lower mean values than collective, private or foreign enterprises.

Measured by summing the standardized measures for market attractiveness, market growth, and competitive intensity (reverse coded) to give a 'mechanical composite scale', which was itself then standardized. It is an emergent construct formed from its indicators.

Measured with a standardized summation of the standardized scales for the value of technology, research-based technological opportunity, industry-based technological opportunity, and the ease of copying (reverse coded). It is an emergent construct formed from its indicators.

Fourteen statements representing marketing intensity, emphasis on efficiency, product line breadth, and commodity-to-specialty products were presented to respondents; these were drawn from the original English versions used by Zahra and Covin (1993) and tested in Chinese by Davies and Ma (2000). Exploratory factor analysis identified four factors and the Cronbach alpha coefficients all exceeded the conservative threshold level of 0.7. After standardizing the scores, the same clustering procedures used for the environment were used to identify three strategy 'gestalts': 'aggressive' (all four dimensions above the mean), 'intermediate' (values between the other clusters), and 'passive' (all four dimensions below the mean).

Performance was measured through a set of eight questionnaire items concerning objective measures of sales and profit growth, sales, market share, profits, and operational success. Exploratory factor analysis found only one underlying factor and the scale had a Cronbach alpha in excess of 0.9. That scale was calculated and standardized. The dependent variables were placed after the independents in the questionnaire to reduce the impact of respondents' implicit effectiveness theories, and exploratory factor analyses across sets of items gave no evidence that common method variance was serious.

Strategic trade-off is assessed from the cluster analysis of four survey-based strategy dimensions (marketing intensity, efficiency emphasis, product line breadth, commodity to specialty products). A trade-off would appear as a cluster scoring high on some dimensions and low on others; the clusters found were passive, intermediate and aggressive, with no such pattern.
scale: Cluster membership on four standardized strategy scales

description: A summative scale of seven items divided by the number of members of the target's top management team, where the top management team is defined as top officers who also serve as inside members of the company's board of directors. The seven items are based on the number of TMT members with affiliations to elite social circles (Social Register and Forbes 400 networks), elite economic circles (financial, non-profit, and for-profit board networks) and elite political circles (officers in trade/professional associations and high government officials). The measure was designed to tap both the depth of the team's involvement in elite circles and the breadth of their connections, while adjusting for the effect of team size.
time_window: proxy statement filed before the tender offer

description: Computed the same way as managerial prestige except that it is based on the target's outside board members only.
time_window: proxy statement filed before the tender offer

description: Similar measures of prestige were computed for the bidders' managers (inside board members) as for the target's top management team: a summative scale of the seven elite-affiliation items divided by the number of team members.
time_window: proxy statement filed before the tender offer

description: Similar measures of prestige were computed for the bidders' outside board members, using the same seven elite-affiliation items divided by the number of team members.
time_window: proxy statement filed before the tender offer

description: The five dimensions of the target's managerial power, defined as dominance over the target's board of directors, were operationalized using five independent measures: numerical superiority on the board, greater corporate experience, more elite connections (prestigious dominance), family representation on the board, and a lack of supervision by higher level board members. A high score equals high managerial power on all but one of these measures; the exception is the board oversight measure, where a high score equals low managerial power. Prestigious dominance was dropped from all multivariate analyses because it was highly correlated with managerial prestige.
time_window: proxy statement filed before the tender offer

description: A binary variable where resistance equals 1 and cooperation equals 0. An initial bid was categorized as resisted if the target's first reaction was to raise any defense or objection against the takeover, including the use of knights, poison pills, fair price provisions, scorched earth policies, pac-man defenses, greenmail payments, reincorporations, law suits, changes in the corporate charter, by-laws or board of directors, and any other noncooperative actions, including the triggering of a previously adopted pre-emptive defense. Cooperation refers to active cooperative behavior or, at a minimum, acceptance of the bid without active resistance. Resistance was determined by four independent coders after examination of reports in the Wall Street Journal, other articles listed in Predicast's F & S Index, and summaries of the targets' reactions in the 14(D)1 filings; at least three of the four coders agreed on the categorization of 98.1 percent of the offers.
time_window: target's first reaction to the first bid to put the target into play

description: The initial premium offered by the bidder, used as the dependent variable in OLS regressions together with the final premium paid on completed deals and the percentage increase in the initial offer. The type of offer (all cash versus a mixture of cash and securities) could not be studied statistically because only 3 of the 106 offers in the sample involved a mixture of cash and securities.

variable_name: Value of direct contacts' combinatory knowledge
description: Each patent is assigned to many technical classes, and the number of technical classes indicates the number of different technical domains combined in its creation; the value of the knowledge embedded in the patent is measured through normalized forward citations. A patent is categorized as hi-co if both the forward citations received and the number of combinations are more than the fiftieth percentile. The value of a contact's combinatory knowledge is the proportion of hi-co patents in that contact's portfolio of patents filed during the three-year moving window prior to the focal innovation being created. The average combinatory knowledge of all the direct contacts gives the value of direct contacts' combinatory knowledge available to all co-inventors on the focal patent.
time_window: three-year moving window prior to the focal innovation

variable_name: Value of indirect contacts' combinatory knowledge
description: Built identically to the measure of direct contacts' combinatory knowledge, but using the portfolio of patents of the focal inventor's indirect contacts (contacts at path distance 2). A patent counts as hi-co if both its forward citations and its number of combinations are above the fiftieth percentile. The value of a contact's combinatory knowledge is the proportion of hi-co patents in that contact's portfolio of patents filed during the three-year moving window prior to the focal innovation. The average across indirect contacts gives the value of indirect contacts' combinatory knowledge available to the co-inventors on the focal patent.
time_window: three-year moving window prior to the focal innovation

description: Measured as the diversity of unfamiliar technical classes in the prior patents of network contacts, where unfamiliar technical classes are technical classes on which direct and indirect contacts have worked but co-inventors of the focal patent have not worked in the past. It uses the distribution of technical classes of patents on which the direct contacts have worked in the three-year moving window prior to the focal innovation. It is calculated as 1 - sum over t of (n_t / n)^2, where n_t is the number of unique patents applied for by direct contacts in the last three years prior to the focal innovation which belong to the unfamiliar technical subclass t, and n is the total number of patents applied for by the team's direct contacts in all the unfamiliar technical classes in the last three years.
time_window: three-year moving window prior to the focal innovation

description: The measure is identical to direct contacts' knowledge heterogeneity but is based on the patents applied for by indirect contacts rather than direct contacts. It uses the distribution of unfamiliar technical classes of the patents on which the indirect contacts have worked in the three-year moving window prior to the focal innovation. It is calculated as one minus the Herfindahl of concentration of technical classes of contacts' patents.
time_window: three-year moving window prior to the focal innovation

description: The innovative performance of a patent is measured as the forward citations of the focal patent excluding self-citations. Forward citations are the later patents that cite the focal patent, collected until November 2007. To address truncation bias, the measure was constructed with normalized forward citation figures, that is, forward citation counts divided by the average forward citation count for all patents issued during the same application year and in the same primary three-digit technical class. It is modeled as a count variable in a negative binomial regression.

variable_name: voting threshold condition (one vs. two yes votes)
description: Teams and their members were randomly assigned to a threshold of one yes vote or a threshold of two yes votes. In the one-vote condition participants were told 'If just one team member votes yes, your team will invest in the specific venture'; in the two-vote condition they were told 'If two or more of the team members vote yes, your team will invest in the specific venture.' Study materials were identical across conditions except for the information on how individual votes were aggregated at the team level.

Participants indicated their yes/no investment vote for each of nine company profiles. The total number of yes votes for each participant was computed to capture the count-dependent variable of 'support of uncertain projects.'

variable_name: voting threshold condition (one vs. two vs. three yes votes)
description: Teams and their participants were randomly assigned to one of three experimental conditions: a threshold of one yes vote, a threshold of two yes votes, or a threshold of three yes votes. Procedures otherwise resembled those of Study 1A, with the task administered online.
The number of yes votes cast by each participant across the nine ventures, ranging from 0 to 9, predicted from the study condition.

variable_name: voting threshold condition (one vs. two yes votes)
description: Participants were randomly assigned to a threshold of one yes vote or a threshold of two yes votes. The procedures were based on those of Study 1B, except that participants were also given the third option to abstain on each project.
The number of yes votes cast by each participant across the nine ventures; abstentions and no votes were analyzed separately in supplementary models.

variable_name: threshold condition coded 0 for three no votes and 1 for one no vote
description: Participants were randomly assigned to either a threshold of three no votes or a threshold of one no vote. In the former condition participants were informed that '(i)f three or more of the team members vote no, your team will not invest in the specific venture'; in the latter condition that '(i)f just one team member votes no, your team will not invest in the specific venture.' The threshold condition was coded 0 for the threshold of three no votes and 1 for the threshold of one no vote.
The number of yes votes cast by each participant across the nine ventures, predicted from the threshold condition.

variable_name: voting threshold condition (one vs. three yes votes)
description: Participants were randomly assigned to one of four conditions in a two (threshold: one vs. three yes votes) by two (group size: three vs. six) between-subjects design; the group size was additionally coded as a dummy for the analysis.
The number of yes votes cast by each participant across the nine ventures, predicted from the threshold condition, the group size dummy, and their interaction.

variable_name: voting threshold condition (one vs. three yes votes)
description: Participants were assigned to one of four conditions in a two (threshold: one vs. three yes votes) by two (deliberation: absent vs. present) between-subjects design. The voting threshold was manipulated at the group level using Qualtrics question randomization, whereas deliberation was manipulated at the seminar session level.
The number of yes votes cast by each participant across the nine ventures, predicted from the threshold condition, the deliberation dummy, and their interaction.

variable_name: voting threshold condition (one vs. three yes votes)
description: Participants were randomly assigned to either a one-yes-vote condition or a three-yes-votes condition in a one-factorial between-subjects design.
The number of yes votes cast by each participant across the nine ventures, predicted from the study condition in a Poisson regression and used as the outcome in the mediation model.

Two items anchored on a five-point answer scale ranging from 1 = strongly disagree to 5 = strongly agree: 'My "yes" vote only matters if my teammates had a negative opinion of the venture' and 'If all of my teammates vote "no," my "yes" vote can hurt my team's performance.' Both items were reverse-coded before computing their average.
scale: five-point agreement scale (1 = strongly disagree to 5 = strongly agree)

description: Participants were randomly assigned to a control condition or an information-inference priming condition while the voting threshold was held constant at one yes vote. In the priming condition, participants were asked to write an essay envisioning the situation in which the team invests in a venture only because of their yes vote, elaborating on three issues: how many team members must have voted yes for this to occur, what can be inferred from these votes about the venture's quality, and whether it was retrospectively a good choice to vote yes. Control participants wrote on a topic unrelated to the task.
The number of yes votes cast by each participant across the nine ventures, predicted from the priming condition (information inference vs. control) in a Poisson regression.

variable_name: voting threshold condition (one vs. two yes votes)
description: Participants were randomly assigned to either a one-yes-vote or a two-yes-votes threshold condition in a one-factorial between-subjects design.
The number of yes votes cast by each participant across the nine ventures, predicted from the threshold condition and used as the outcome in the perceived-pivotality mediation model.

A single item built on the belief elicitation approach of Duffy and Tavits (2008), anchored on a nine-point semantic differential scale with 'Very unlikely' and 'Very likely' as anchors: 'Given this voting rule, how likely is it you will find yourself in a constellation in which your individual vote is going to make a difference for the joint team decision?'
scale: nine-point semantic differential scale ('Very unlikely' to 'Very likely')

variable_name: voting threshold condition (one vs. two yes votes)
description: Participants were assigned to a threshold of either one yes vote or two yes votes; except for the details of how individual votes were aggregated at the team level, study materials were identical across the two threshold-level conditions.

Level of information was manipulated as a within-subjects factor: four randomly selected company profiles in each participant's handout contained five to six lines of blurred-out, unreadable text (low level of information) with instructions that some teammates had done additional research and had this information, whereas five profiles contained five to six lines of bold and underlined text (high level of information) with instructions that this information was exclusively the participant's and lacked by teammates.

Because individual company profiles differed in terms of information levels, the analysis moved to the trial level and the dependent variable of investment was coded as a dummy variable for each company. Individual trials were nested within participants and analyzed with random-intercept logistic regression using participant as the clustering variable.

CEO total pay is the sum of salary, bonus, and all long-term components of CEO pay (stock options, restricted stock, and other long-term compensation). In all cases the authors used the natural logarithm of compensation to reduce heteroscedasticity. Stock options were valued at the time they were awarded, using the method that values them at 25 percent of their exercise value rather than the Black-Scholes method. It is the dependent variable for Hypotheses 1-3.

Total long-term pay comprises the long-term components of CEO pay and was used as an independent variable in testing Hypotheses 4a and 4b, in natural logarithm form. In those tests the authors used the average value of long-term pay for two previous years. It is also the largest component of CEO total pay.

To create the pollution prevention measure the authors estimated total waste generation levels and contrasted this estimate with the real values. Each chemical's quantity was weighted by its human toxicity potential (HTP) factor, results were aggregated across chemicals at the facility level, multiplied by the facilities' corresponding production ratios, aggregated by parent company, and then compared against real values. Separate index values for carcinogens and noncarcinogens were computed, log-transformed to achieve normality, and, given a Cronbach alpha of .96, standardized and averaged to create the final pollution prevention variable.

End-of-pipe pollution control is a ratio in which the numerator is the sum of chemicals recycled, treated on-site, and transferred to other locations for further treatment, and the denominator is the total waste generated by a firm. Chemical figures were weighted by the average HTP values before the ratio was calculated. Cancer and noncancer figures were combined into a single composite by standardizing and averaging them, given a Cronbach alpha of .79.

Environmental governance is a composite created by adding two dummy variables. The first is coded 1 if a firm's proxy statement contained at least one text block coded as showing an explicit relationship between executive pay and environmental performance, and 0 otherwise. The second is coded 1 if the firm had an environmental committee within its board, and 0 otherwise. The composite therefore has a 0-2 range for each firm, with a 2 indicating the presence of both.

The industry pollution position index reflects the mix of sectors in which a firm operates and accounts for their pollution intensity. The paper states that the procedure to calculate this index appears in Appendix B, part 3. It is used as a control variable in the compensation models and as the moderator in Hypothesis 4b.

variable_name: Pollution prevention and end-of-pipe pollution control
description: Environmental performance is captured by two measures based on EPA Toxics Release Inventory data: pollution prevention, the gap between predicted and actual toxicity-weighted waste generation, and end-of-pipe pollution control, the toxicity-weighted ratio of waste recycled, treated or transferred to total waste. Both are aggregated to the parent company level.

Groups were randomly assigned to a control condition that received only the common set of instructions, or to one of three formal intervention conditions: sharing information, questioning others, and managing time. Each experimental condition received one additional instruction printed in bold on the instruction sheet (e.g., asking the group to question the different members of the group for possible causes of the salmonellosis outbreak during the discussion, or to manage their time carefully during the discussion).
scale: four categories (control, sharing information, questioning others, managing time)

description: The number of attention switches, coded from transcripts by coders blind to condition, that fall in the category prescribed by the group's formal intervention: managing time switches for the managing time condition, questioning others switches for the questioning others condition, and sharing information switches for the sharing information condition.

The number of attention switches to knowledge integration behavior categories that were not the target of the group's formal intervention. For example, managing time and sharing information switches for groups in the questioning others condition, and questioning others and sharing information switches for groups in the managing time condition.

Attention switches were graphed according to their time of occurrence on a 60-minute timeline in 30-second intervals for each group, and an adjacent set of attention switches was labeled a cluster. Adjacency was defined as two attention switches occurring within 90 seconds of each other, with a third switch within 90 seconds of the second also considered adjacent, and so on. Clustering was measured as the percentage of total attention switches appearing in clusters and as the number of clusters containing two and three or more attention switches.

variable_name: number of attention switches in the interruption
description: Each interruption in all 40 groups, whether a single attention switch or a cluster of attention switches, was coded according to the number of attention switches it included. The analysis compared interruptions with one, two, three, and four attention switches.
scale: count of attention switches (analysed in categories of one, two, three and four)
level: interruption (single attention switch or cluster) within a group

variable_name: number of different types of attention switches
description: Each interruption was coded for the number of different types of attention switches it included, that is, the number of different aspects of the knowledge integration process it addressed.
level: interruption (single attention switch or cluster) within a group

description: Each interruption was coded for the number of different group members speaking during it.
level: interruption (single attention switch or cluster) within a group

variable_name: number of specific suggestions for improving the knowledge integration process
description: Each interruption was coded for the number of specific suggestions for improving the knowledge integration process proposed by members, also reported as the number of activities or paths to follow suggested.
level: interruption (single attention switch or cluster) within a group

description: A score for the change from the period prior to the interruption to the period following it, built from four measures: person leading the discussion, topic under discussion, changes from seeking confirming to seeking disconfirming evidence (or vice versa), and changes from presenting to combining information (or vice versa). The score ranges from 0 for no changes to 4 for changes in all measures.
level: interruption (single attention switch or cluster) within a group
time_window: from before to after the interruption

variable_name: total number of critical facts identified
description: A knowledge integration score computed by summing the number of facts that the group identified related to the food poisoning outbreak. Twenty-six critical case facts were present, of which 16 were simple facts findable in a single information packet and 10 were combined facts requiring synthesis of information from two or more packets. Each time one of the critical facts was identified in the group discussion, it was scored by the coder.
scale: count of critical facts (26 critical facts present)

variable_name: knowledge integration gain after an interruption
description: The number of critical facts identified by members after an interruption (a single attention switch or a cluster of attention switches), but before the next interruption.
level: interruption (single attention switch or cluster) within a group
time_window: between one interruption and the next

description: Dummy variable distinguishing incumbents from entrants. A firm was classified as an incumbent if it had been present in the anticancer drug market prior to 1983, the start of the biotechnology revolution in that market; otherwise it was classified as an entrant.

Firm category identifying the subset of entrants with full access to the new capabilities. Based on interview material and historical accounts of the evolution of large-molecule drugs, 1990 was taken as the cutoff date to identify pioneers; Walsh's (2003) report was used to identify all large-molecule drugs approved up to 1990 irrespective of market application, and this was combined with Pharmaprojects to pinpoint the developing firms. A firm was classified as a pioneer if it had a large-molecule drug that had been developed in house, had been approved in 1990 or earlier, and was the first drug with that active ingredient. For the statistical analyses the two firm categories are expanded into three mutually exclusive categories: biopharmaceutical technology pioneers, incumbents, and entrants that are not pioneers.

variable_name: Count of patented anticancer drug molecules
description: The set of drug molecules each firm patented was identified using the code that identifies anticancer drugs in the Derwent World Patent Index in 1994-2004, regardless of whether the originating firms entered them into clinical trials; each record is a stand-alone innovation catalogued under the same molecule. The data set had 19,106 patented anticancer drug molecules, of which 3,672 were small-molecule and 5,365 were large-molecule targeted drugs. Because the rate of patenting can vary over the period, the count was analyzed with a Cox regression with repeated events clustered by firm; the start of risk for each firm was set at the time of first entry into each technological variant, and the time at risk for subsequent cases within a firm started the day immediately after the previous event.

As in prior research (Sosa 2009a), the variable oncology research prior to 1983 is equal to the cumulative number of publications in the field of oncology as available in Thomson Reuters' Web of Science database per year up to 1982, a year before the start of the disruption that biotechnology imposed on the anticancer drug market.

Expertise in the capability of biopharmaceutical technology was measured with the Derwent World Patent Index: an expert interviewee selected the relevant DWPI codes, and the resulting set of three specific manual codes paired with the 165 firms in the sample in 1994-2004 generated a data set of 2,092 patented innovations in biopharmaceutical technology. The variable is the cumulative count of these innovations per firm per month-year.

variable_name: Expertise in oncology research and in biopharmaceutical technology
description: Strategic value of a capability is operationalized through two capability variables: oncology research (cumulative oncology publications up to 1982) and biopharmaceutical technology (cumulative count of patented biopharmaceutical innovations). Their strategic value is compared through the size of their coefficients in the R&D performance model.

We measure VC status with Bonacich's (1987) eigenvector centrality, which takes into account the centrality of the actors to which a focal actor is connected. We defined the home-country network as the co-investment network of all VC firms investing in any industry in the focal VC firm's country. We constructed co-investment matrices for each country in 10-year windows, roughly the length of an investment cycle, and normalized the measure such that it varies between zero and one for each network. When there are several cross-border VC firms investing in a venture, we focus on the cross-border VC with the highest status.
level: VC firm within its home-country network

description: Performance is measured by the occurrence of an IPO or an acquisition anywhere in the world. The information was hand collected from VentureXpert, SDC Platinum, Zephyr, and venture websites (and web archives) when available. We included only true acquisitions, gathering qualitative data on each acquisition to exclude fire sales after bankruptcy.

We construct a country-level VC-flow matrix by counting the annual number of cross-border VC investments in the biotechnology industry between each country dyad. The Interconnectedness of the cross-border VC firm's country with the venture's country is operationalized as the strength of the tie between the VC's and venture's countries in the VC-flow network.

We calculate the position of each country in the country-level VC-flow network using closeness centrality. We then calculate the ratio of the centrality of the VC firm's country to that of the venture's country. This measure is greater than one if the VC firm is in a more central country than the venture, and smaller than one if the venture is in a more central country than the VC firm.

Because the author was interested in the intensity of the wealth effects provided by stock ownership, stock ownership was measured as the dollar value of shares owned by the CEO rather than as the percentage of shares she or he owned. The variable was measured in the year preceding the acquisition and divestiture activity being estimated.
time_window: year preceding the acquisition and divestiture activity being estimated

description: Measured as the value of stock options granted to the CEO during a given year. Options were valued using the SEC present-value method, in which one computes the present value of stock options by assuming that stock price appreciates 5 percent per year over ten years, subtracting the option price, and then discounting the potential gain at 5 percent per year. The great majority (71%) of the S&P 500 firms reported stock option values using this method. The variable was measured in the year preceding the activity being estimated.
time_window: year preceding the acquisition and divestiture activity being estimated

description: Measured as the number of acquisitions completed during a year, determined by examining Mergers & Acquisitions for the number of transactions in which a firm acquired a controlling interest in another firm. The author used the number of transactions completed rather than transaction value because most transactions are reported without a value, because a count measure matches the theory tested, and because it aids comparison with other studies.
Measured as the number of divestitures in each year. Divestitures were identified in the same manner as acquisitions, that is, by examining Mergers & Acquisitions.
Measured as the number of years an executive had held the CEO title at the sampled firm.
time_window: year preceding the acquisition and divestiture activity being estimated

description: Firm performance was measured as return on assets (ROA), because its frequent use in other studies of acquisitions and divestitures facilitated comparing results across studies. It was included as a control in all models in addition to being hypothesized as a moderating variable.
time_window: year preceding the acquisition and divestiture activity being estimated

description: The focal firm's betweenness centrality among the members of a multipartner alliance in the prior network. All alliances among the focal firm and the other partners of the multipartner alliance during the five-year period before its formation (1995-1999) are identified, and two separate matrices are created in which '1' indicates an alliance relationship and '0' implies no relationship. Freeman's betweenness centrality measure is then calculated in UCINET; the variable is continuous.

The focal firm's betweenness centrality among the members of a multipartner alliance in the subsequent network. All alliances among the focal firm and the other partners during the five-year period after the formation of the multipartner alliance (2000-2004) are identified, and matrices using '1' for an alliance relationship and '0' for no relationship are built. Freeman's betweenness centrality is calculated via UCINET; the variable is continuous.
The total number of partners in a multipartner alliance, including the focal firm. In the sample, the ISMs vary in the total number of founding members from 4 to 21, with a mean of 14.
The variation coefficient of firm size among the partners of a multipartner alliance, used as a proxy for size heterogeneity. Firm size is measured as the number of employees of a firm, in thousands.

The actual number of alliances among the partners of a multipartner alliance relative to the total number of possible alliances among the same partners between 1995 and 1999, prior to the formation of the alliance.

A Theil entropy score for the degree of task diversity within a job, calculated for each worker(i)-year(t) using the share of each activity a. Jobs with a higher score are closer to an even mix of task types, while jobs with a lower score have a more homogenous set of tasks. The entropy formula itself is not recoverable from the text provided.

Each nodal worker's share of a task out of his or her union's total work in that task category; the measure uses the largest of those task shares as the job turf accessible to the worker. As a worker increases his or her share of a given task relative to coworkers the measure approaches 1, and it equals 1 when the worker is the sole employee of a union doing a given task. The formula itself is not recoverable from the text provided.

Coworkers' average task variety in the union, entered separately from the nodal worker's own task variety so that the two can be distinguished. The authors do not give a separate formula for this variable in the text provided.

Gross salary payments to each individual employee, logged and adjusted for inflation. The authors report that the variance of logged earnings in the sample is .39, around the mean within-industry variance of annual earnings in the Current Population Survey Annual Social and Economic Supplement during the same time period.

Number of the focal firm's partners that had at least one therapeutic area in common with the partner P in a year. Therapeutic areas were identified from the technologies and resources each firm sold or licensed to other firms, using the 22 therapeutic areas listed in Recap, and a firm was assumed active in an area from two years prior to its outlicensing year in that area until termination of the licensing agreement or censoring; information on P's alliances with firms outside F's portfolio was also collected. The count in the previous year served as the measure of competition, which assumes P is a source of concern even before operating in a therapeutic area.
Dollar value of equity investment in each alliance, as reported by Recap. Alliances for which no equity was reported were treated as non-equity alliances.

Proportion of the number of ties between all partners in the focal firm's portfolio to the total number of possible ties in that portfolio. Computed for each year of the study and used with a one-year lag.

Number of ties through which P's resources could be transferred to the competitors PC s other than through F, measured as the number of PC s that have a direct path to P through an alliance. Ties were tracked from formation to termination or censoring, and for alliances whose termination could not be established the average duration of ties in the sample, five years, was used. The variable was lagged by a year.

Indicator variable that took the value of 1 if the partners operated in the same four-digit SIC. Operating within the same SIC, in an industry as subject to regulatory oversight as biopharma, is argued to result in similarity of strategic characteristics.

Dummy variable (0-1) noting whether an alliance was terminated during the study period. Because Recap reported termination for only 10.5% of alliances, an intensive search of Factiva press releases identified termination for an additional 12.5% of alliances, and for alliances without termination dates the stream of press releases was followed until the final press release, whose year was adopted as the termination year, adding estimated termination dates for another 34% of alliances. In total, 926 (57.1%) of the 1,621 alliances were established as terminated during the study period, and the remaining 695 (42.9%) alliances were treated as right-censored at the end of the study period.

Respondents were asked on the strategic planning survey, using a scale ranging from 1 (a weak emphasis) to 10 (a strong emphasis), how much emphasis their banks place on each of the strategic planning components. The measures are based on Armstrong's (1982) review of 12 strategic planning studies, whose components included mission, objectives, internal and external environmental analyses, strategic alternatives, strategy implementation, and strategic control. The seven items served as the measures of the strategic planning intensity latent variable in the LISREL model.

Strategic planning expertise was measured by asking the CEOs to indicate the level of expertise that exists in their bank to perform strategic planning. On a 10-point scale, their choices ranged from very low (1 point) to very high (10 points). A test-retest reliability coefficient of 0.86 was derived after an item-by-item analysis of two administrations of the survey.
scale: 10-point scale from very low (1) to very high (10)

description: Beliefs about planning-performance relationships were measured by asking the CEOs the question: 'How critical do you feel strategic planning is (or can be) to a bank's financial success?'. The CEOs indicated their beliefs on a 10-point scale ranging from not critical (1 point) to very critical (10 points). A test-retest reliability coefficient of 0.88 was derived after an item-by-item analysis of two administrations of the survey.
scale: 10-point scale from not critical (1) to very critical (10)

description: A complex environment was described to the CEOs as being characterized by rapid change and containing a large number of factors to be considered during the strategic planning process. On a 10-point scale ranging from very simple (1 point) to very complex (10 points), the CEOs were asked to indicate how complex they perceived their banks' environment to be. The measure was derived from Yasai-Ardekani's (1989) composite measure of perceived environmental pressures, and a test-retest reliability coefficient of 0.79 was derived for this measure.
scale: 10-point scale from very simple (1) to very complex (10)

description: Environmental change was measured as the number of years since a bank was incorporated. The authors cite Carroll's suggestion that organizational age will coincide roughly with the amount of environmental change experienced by an organization, so that aging may be a surrogate measure of a bank's exposure to environmental change. They later note that aging may not be a very good surrogate measure, given the low squared multiple correlation for this variable.

Bank size was measured as the natural logarithm of bank assets. This measure is described as an established way of accounting for differences in firm size when examining organizational outcomes, and it has been used in other bank-related studies.

Bank structural complexity was determined by the extent to which banks in the sample involved themselves in lines of business other than strictly banking (e.g., leasing, insurance, credit cards). Borrowing from the methodology employed by Gup and Whitehead (1989), banks were categorized into three classes of structural complexity: a small unit bank or a bank involved in no more than three other lines of business was assigned a 1 (low structural complexity), banks involved in four to seven other lines of business were assigned a 2 (moderate structural complexity), and banks involved in eight or more other lines of business were assigned a 3 (high structural complexity).
scale: 1 = low structural complexity, 2 = moderate structural complexity, 3 = high structural complexity

description: Profits (or net income) was used as a general measure of banks' financial performance, chosen because of its extensive use in past studies that examined the strategic planning-financial performance relationship.

Return on equity was calculated as net income divided by shareholders' equity. The selection of this measure was based partly on Earle and Mendelson's statement that the true measure of the strength of any financial institution is its return on shareholder equity, and other banking-related articles concur that ROE is the preferred measure of banks' financial performance.

Deposit growth was measured as the percent change in consumer demand deposits for each bank between 1993 and 1994. The measure was selected because it is unique to banking and related financial services industries, and because deposits represent the largest and most important fund-providing function for banks, accounting for approximately 70 to just under 90 percent of a bank's sources of funds.

Calculated as the average percentage of markets (out of the total number of markets in which the firm competes) that a focal hospital shares with the firms already competing in a market that it could potentially enter. It is a firm-in-market construct, so it can vary for each service market a firm could potentially enter; scaling to the firm's total number of markets distinguishes a hospital sharing 5 of 5 markets from one sharing 5 of 50. The measure ranges from a low of zero to a maximum of one (100%). Because Hypotheses 1 and 2 argue for a nonlinear effect, the squared value of the measure was also calculated.

The dependent variable, market entry, was measured as a dichotomous variable. For each market a hospital could potentially enter in each year, a value of one represented the event of entry into the service market by that hospital in that year, and a value of zero indicated that no entry was made by the hospital into the particular service during the year. The dependent variable was measured as indicating an entry (or not) occurring from the current period to the next period (t to t + 1). Once a hospital entered a specific market it was removed from the risk set for that service.

A binary variable set to one if the CEO had been in the position for less than three calendar years and zero otherwise. To test Hypotheses 3 and 4 the sample was divided into two subsamples based on CEO tenure: observations where the CEO had been in place for three or more years and observations where the CEO had been in place for fewer than three years, and the model was rerun on each subsample with the new CEO measure omitted.

Indicator variable set to 1.00 for company-owned outlets and to 0 for franchised outlets in the first dependent-variable set. Whether an outlet was owned by the franchisor or a franchisee was determined by the address of its headquarters; company-owned outlets share a common headquarters' address and are typically numbered (e.g., Store #123).

Indicator variable set to 1.00 for outlets that are part of a multi-outlet franchise in the second dependent-variable set, which considers only franchises. Multi-outlet franchisees were paired with their outlets based on common mailing addresses for the owner's headquarters and common company names. Whether an outlet was owned by the franchisor or a franchisee was determined by the address of its headquarters.

The category of outlets that could not be paired with a multi-outlet owner through a common mailing address for the owner's headquarters or a common company name; the remaining outlets were coded as single-outlet franchisees. In the second dependent-variable set multi-outlet franchises are set to 1.00, so single-outlet franchises are the 0 category.

The location address for every outlet was converted to latitude and longitude coordinates, and geographic mapping software (ArcView) was used to calculate the distance in miles to the franchisor's headquarters. All continuous variables were standardized in the regressions.

Geographic mapping software was used to calculate the distance in miles from each outlet to the headquarters of its owner, based on the latitude and longitude coordinates of the outlet and headquarters addresses. For company-owned outlets this distance is identical to the distance to the franchisor's headquarters. All continuous variables were standardized in the regressions.
Distance in miles between each outlet and its nearest neighbor in the same chain, computed within a maximum 60-mile radius. All continuous variables were standardized in the regressions.
A coding of whether the focal outlet's nearest neighbor in the same chain is a company-owned outlet. It is one category of the nearest neighbor's ownership.
A coding of whether the focal outlet's nearest neighbor in the same chain is an outlet of a multi-outlet franchise. It is the other category of the nearest neighbor's ownership.

Measured as the population of the county in which the outlet was located, based on the 2005 Census update for one of Florida's 67 counties. All continuous variables were standardized in the regressions.
Measured by the number of seats in each outlet as reported by the Division of Hotels and Restaurants. All continuous variables were standardized in the regressions.

The number of figures correctly solved out of 36 in the 20-minute timed version of Raven's Advanced Progressive Matrices test, used as a proxy for cognitive ability. The test requires subjects to select the missing figure out of eight possibilities that completes a logical pattern. Students took the test one week before the start of the entrepreneurship program.
time_window: one week before the start of the entrepreneurship program

description: The team-level average score of members on the 20-minute timed version of the Raven's APM test, with a maximum of 36 figures. It summarizes the central location of the team's ability distribution and is used together with the coefficient of variation as the team-level ability composition measure.
scale: average test score, sample range 14.00 to 23.22
time_window: measured before the program; team composition as at the start of the program

description: The coefficient of variation in team members' scores on the Raven's APM test, used as a scale-invariant measure of ability dispersion in teams. Squared terms and spline segments of this variable are used to probe nonlinearity. The sample average of teams' coefficient of variation in test scores is approximately 0.22.
scale: coefficient of variation, sample range 0.07 to 0.47
time_window: measured before the program; team composition as at the start of the program

description: Sales in euros of the student company, taken from the approved annual report of the team's company.

Profits calculated as the difference between sales and costs, including tax and social security payments but excluding wage costs, since students could determine their own wages. Taken from the approved annual report.
A binary indicator for whether the team's profits are positive, included because many students view as the bottom line result whether or not they are able to satisfy shareholders.
Team profits divided by the number of shares issued by the company, taken from the approved annual report.

Count of problems coded from the NTSB accident and incident reports that belong to the human factor categories. For the rule-proposing models this count was the accumulated number of human factor problems in the prior two years up to the last month, lagged by one month.
time_window: two-year accumulated window up to the last month, lagged one month

description: Count of problems coded from the NTSB accident and incident reports that belong to the nonhuman factor categories. For the rule-proposing models this count was the accumulated number of nonhuman factor problems in the prior two years up to the last month, lagged by one month.
time_window: two-year accumulated window up to the last month, lagged one month

description: Count of all problems (human and nonhuman factor problems) used to test the urgency effect hypotheses. It was updated monthly with a one-month time window because a short time window can capture the presence of urgency faced by the agency.

A monthly event count of the number of proposed rules for a specific rule domain in a given month, based on the date the rule was proposed as stated when the FAA issues a rule. The model for all rules uses the count across all domains; separate models use the count of human factor rules and of nonhuman factor rules. Rules are sorted into eight FAA categories or domains.

The transition rate of a proposed rule being finalized; a rule enters the risk set when it is proposed and exits when it is finalized or withdrawn. Rules that were finalized were coded as 1 and rules the agency regards as ones that should not be finalized (withdrawn) were coded as 0; rules still in process of finalization in the year 2000 were treated as right censored. Split spells were used to update the covariates monthly, and the time variable is the number of days after a rule has been proposed.

variable_name: Average ROE of the airline industry
description: The average return on equity for all airlines, collected from the Financial Statistics published by the Air Transport Association and updated quarterly.

Measured by a linear composite combination of three variables: the number of parties involved in the rule finalization process, the total number of comments from all participants, and the total number of different areas of a particular rule that the comments are addressed to; the number of comments was logged for this calculation because this variable is highly skewed. The factor loading coefficients for the number of comments, the number of parties, and the number of concerned rule areas by the commentators are 0.79, 0.8, and 0.58, respectively. For tests of Hypothesis 4, rules of high complexity have complexity scores above the mean and rules of low complexity have scores below the mean.

Each TMT member was asked to identify the total number of his or her contacts in each of nine external categories. To create a company score for network size, the number of social ties across the external categories was summed for each TMT and divided by the number of respondents.
time_window: at the time of the survey

description: Range was the proportion of the nine external categories to which a TMT was linked by at least one member. It captures the diversity of contacts, measured as the number of different groups or actor categories a network accesses.
time_window: at the time of the survey

description: Strength of ties was measured as the linear combination of the standardized scores of three components: interaction frequency, relationship duration, and emotional intensity. Interaction frequency was the average number of times per month a TMT member interacted with identified contacts; relationship duration was based on the TMT member's response to how long he or she had known these critical contacts; emotional intensity was measured through the response to how close the relationship with these contacts was (1 = 'not at all close,' and 5 = 'extremely close'). The TMT tie strength score was the average of the respondents' scores.
time_window: at the time of the survey

description: Each TMT member was asked to identify the total number of his or her contacts in each of four internal categories. To create a company score for network size, the number of social ties across the internal categories was summed for each TMT and divided by the number of respondents.
time_window: at the time of the survey

description: Range was the proportion of the four internal categories to which a TMT was linked by at least one member. It captures the diversity of contacts, measured as the number of different groups or actor categories a network accesses.
time_window: at the time of the survey

description: Strength of ties was measured as the linear combination of the standardized scores of three components: interaction frequency, relationship duration, and emotional intensity, assessed for internal contacts. The TMT tie strength score was the average of the respondents' scores.
time_window: at the time of the survey

description: An additive index of eight items covering training, performance assessment, and rewards designed to help and encourage top managers to build relationships with external and internal actors, collected from each firm's CEO. The scale showed good reliability (alpha = .76), and a principal components analysis with varimax rotation showed the items loading cleanly on a factor separate from incentive pay practices.
time_window: at the time of the survey

description: Sales growth for the fiscal year that followed the collection of the HR practice and social network data, collected primarily from COMPUSTAT. For private firms, a one-year lagged self-reported measure of sales growth from the Mid-AtlanTech Almanac was used; the self-reported measure was collected for public firms as well and was highly correlated with the COMPUSTAT data (r = .94), suggesting that it was a reliable measure of sales growth.

One-year stock returns collected from COMPUSTAT for the fiscal year that followed the collection of the HR practice and social network data. Twenty-one firms either did not trade their stock publicly or had been trading it for less than one year, so correlations and regressions with stock returns were calculated for a sample of 52 firms.

The population of acquisitions reported in Mergers & Acquisitions during the period was divided into U.S. acquisitions of other U.S. firms and foreign acquisitions of U.S. firms before the sample was drawn, and a random sample was drawn from each category. Of the 270 U.S. targets with complete top management team data, 168 (62 percent) were acquired by foreign buyers and 102 (38 percent) by U.S. buyers.

The sample of U.S. targets acquired by foreign firms was divided into two groups: those acquired by firms headquartered in the 'Anglo' countries (United Kingdom, Canada, and Australia) and those acquired by firms headquartered in the 'non-Anglo' countries. T-tests were performed to test for cumulative turnover differences between the two groups in each of the 5 years following the acquisition.

To test Hypothesis 3, t-tests were performed to compare differences in cumulative turnover between U.S. firms acquired by Japanese firms and U.S. firms acquired by 'non-Anglo' foreign firms in each of the 5 years following the acquisition. The Japanese category is a subset of the non-Anglo foreign acquisitions examined in the test of Hypothesis 2.

Members of each target company's top management team were identified immediately prior to the acquisition in Standard & Poor's Register of Corporations, Executives and Directors, or, failing that, in Dun & Bradstreet's Million Dollar Directory; the team was defined by the list of managers and job titles reported by the company, a list that includes chairman, chief executive officer, president, chief operating officer, vice president, controller, and treasurer. Turnover in each of the 5 years following the acquisition was the number of managers employed by the target in the year prior to the acquisition who departed during the year in question divided by the total number of managers employed in the year prior to the acquisition; departures of managers hired after the acquisition were excluded. Cumulative turnover rates are reported by year following the acquisition; the data did not allow voluntary turnover to be separated from involuntary turnover.
time_window: each of the 5 years following the acquisition

description: The number of years since the firm was founded. Age also enters nonparametrically as a vector of categorical variables, as an interaction term with Diversify, and as a dummy variable (age_old) that is equal to one when a firm launches a new product and is above the median age and is zero otherwise. The sample includes 522 major new product introductions for firms that were older than the median age at the time of diversification and 630 for firms that were younger than the median age.

A dummy variable that is equal to one in the month in which a firm launches a new fund and zero otherwise, used for the instantaneous measure of diversification. To ensure that a new fund is a major diversification event, distinctiveness is measured based on the pairwise correlation of the time series of raw returns between each fund and every other fund in the firm's portfolio; a fund whose within-firm return correlation is below the pairwise correlation between the new fund and an index of passive predicted returns (on average 0.35) is called explorative diversification, and launches with a raw return correlation of 0.75 or above are treated as highly related and are not treated as major diversification events.
A categorical variable that is equal to one in all months subsequent to the firm's first diversification event, and zero otherwise.

A standard measure of average historical excess returns used to capture ex ante performance. At the fund level, CAR is the sum of n lagged excess returns divided by the number of months the fund was in operation at time t, up to a maximum of 24 months. An equal weighted average of fund returns gives a firm-level CAR. CAR is used as the explanatory variable in regressions of the instantaneous diversification rate for older versus younger firms.
time_window: up to 24 months of lagged excess returns

description: Risk-adjusted excess returns from a fund-level longitudinal regression of a fund's raw return from TASS and HFR on the seven risk factors of Fung and Hsieh's (2001) hedge fund asset pricing model plus a traded liquidity factor. Excess returns are the sum of the time-invariant component of a fund's excess performance and the mean-zero residual, capturing the combination of a fund's skill and luck relative to a market benchmark. Firm performance is the arithmetic average of fund performance in multifund firms.
level: firm-month (fund-level returns aggregated to the firm)

description: A dynamic version of the information ratio, which divides the fund's excess return in any time period by the standard deviation of the fund's excess returns. It is used as an alternative performance measure that accounts for the nonsystematic riskiness of a fund's underlying investments.
level: firm-month (fund-level returns aggregated to the firm)

description: Average consensus recommendation for firm i in year t, computed as the mean of the I/B/E/S recommendation variable. The I/B/E/S recommendation variable is coded 1 = 'strong buy,' 2 = 'buy,' 3 = 'hold,' 4 = 'underperform,' and 5 = 'sell,' so an increase in this variable indicates more negative analysts' recommendations. The variable is lagged one year in the models. Because the models use within-firm variation over time, they capture changes in this variable rather than differences between firms.

Strategic investments were measured using data on capital expenditures and R&D expenses collected from Compustat; the two measures were summed. Missing R&D data were coded as zeroes, following prior research that assumes missing R&D represents zero values, and a dummy variable equal to 1 for these firm-years was included. The models reported treat the dependent variable in logarithmic form.

The log of the value of share repurchase announcements at the time of announcement. Since there are zeroes in many years for the repurchase announcement data, 1 was added to each observation before calculating the log. Data on repurchases were accessed from Securities Data Corporation and Thomson Research.

A technology change dummy variable, coded 1 in the years for the firms in the industries undergoing a technological change and 0 otherwise. The first cameras incorporating digital technology were introduced in 1991, so the technology change period in photography began as early as possible (starting in 1993, the first year analyst recommendation data are available); newspapers began to develop websites in the late 1990s, so the dummy was coded 1 starting after 1999; in telecommunications the change to VoIP began in the early 2000s, so the dummy was coded 1 beginning after 2000.

Calculative practices scale constructed as a simple sum of ten dichotomous (0-1) items: individual performance appraisals at the managerial, professional/technical (nonmanagerial), clerical and manual levels of employment; individual reward systems (merit pay/performance-related pay) at the same four levels; and formal evaluation of the effectiveness of personnel training immediately after the training and some months after it. The scale ranges from a minimum of 0 to a maximum of 10, with a mean of 4.70, and is one of the two dependent variables in the regression analysis. Items were selected with Mokken scaling and the scale has satisfactory reliability.

Collaborative practices scale constructed as the sum of six dichotomous (0-1) items: a written mission statement; formal briefings about the company's strategy at the managerial, professional/technical (nonmanagerial), clerical and manual levels; and a written policy for communication with employees. The scale varies from 0 to a maximum of 6, with a mean of 3.75, and is the second dependent variable in the regression analysis. Items were selected with Mokken scaling and the scale performs reasonably well, although the authors note that some items share smaller common variance with the set.

Categorical regressor for the country in which the firm is located, entered in the regression analysis as a set of five design variables with the United Kingdom as the reference category. The regression constant may be interpreted as the predicted value on the CALC scale for British firms when the remaining regressors are set to zero. Country is the main regressor and the authors describe it as national embeddedness.

Categorical regressor for the industry in which the firm operates, represented in the regression analysis by five design variables with manufacturing as the reference category. Industry dummies are entered alongside country and firm size in the regressions for the CALC and COLL scales.

The natural logarithm of firm size, the only continuous regressor in the regression analysis. Firm size is understood in terms of the number of employees, and the surveys targeted firms with more than 100 employees. Larger values indicate larger firms.

variable_name: subsidiary's need to engage in bribery
description: Six items asking 'How often do firms like yours nowadays need to make extra, unofficial payments to public officials . . .' across a range of activities. In its original form, responses ranged from 1, 'always,' to 6, 'never'; for ease of interpretation the variable was reverse coded so that higher numbers indicated a greater need to offer bribes. A factor analysis using varimax rotation of survey items with common anchors confirmed the presence of a corruption factor; Cronbach's alpha was 0.89.

variable_name: degree to which corruption pressure poses an obstacle to business performance
description: Managers reported the extent to which corruption pressures posed an obstacle to their firm's business performance, measured using a five-point Likert scale with anchors 'no obstacle' and 'major obstacle.' The corruption scale was standardized to account for respondents' perceptions regarding obstacles created by 17 different issues, so the construct reflects the degree to which corruption creates more or less of an obstacle to business performance than other factors in the Ghanaian environment. Cronbach's alpha was 0.86.
scale: five-point Likert scale ('no obstacle' to 'major obstacle')

description: The host country corruption environment was measured using Transparency International's CPI, which draws on 18 separate surveys administered by twelve independent organizations pertaining to 146 countries. As published, high scores indicate a less corrupt national environment; for ease of interpreting the results, the variable was reverse coded and standardized using z-scores, so that higher numbers reflect more corrupt institutional environments. Countries' scores from 2003 were used.

An MNE's home country corruption level was operationalized by the CPI score of its home country. CPI scores were reversed and standardized so that higher numbers reflect more corrupt environments, and the variable was operationalized using the CPI scores for 2000 because the BEEPS survey was administered in 1999-2000.

An MNE's home country corruption level was operationalized by the CPI score of its home country, reversed and standardized so that higher numbers reflect more corrupt environments. Because data for the Ghana sample were collected in 2004-2007, Transparency International's 2004 CPI scores were used.

variable_name: Home country entry into force of the OECD convention
description: For the Eastern Europe sample, MNEs' home countries were coded as '1' if they had entered into the force of the OECD Convention on Combating Bribery of Foreign Public Officials in International Business Transactions on or before 1 January, 1999, and as 0 otherwise. By 1999, eight of the 12 home countries represented in the sample had entered into the force of the convention.

variable_name: Home country entry into force of the OECD convention
description: For the Ghana sample, home countries were coded as '1' if they had entered into the force of the OECD Convention in or before June, 2007, and as '0' otherwise. Sixteen of the 34 home countries represented in the sample had entered into the force of the convention by this time, and no country entered between 2004 and August, 2007.

For the Eastern European firms, partial local ownership was measured as a dichotomous variable; firms with any local ownership were coded as '1' and those that were fully foreign owned were coded as '0.' Due to data constraints the authors were unable to identify the composition of this local ownership and assume that firms reporting partial local ownership fall into the category of a single local equity partner that plays a role in the firm's strategy and operations.

In the Ghana dataset, managers were asked to report the number of strategic alliances and joint ventures in which their firm had participated with Ghanaian-owned companies. Since few firms reported more than one local alliance, this variable was dummy coded as '1' when an alliance was present and as '0' when no alliances were reported.

In the Ghana dataset, decentralized decision making was operationalized based on a three-item scale in which subsidiary managers were asked if strategic decisions were decentralized to the host country subsidiary. It was measured using a five-point Likert scale with anchors from 'strongly disagree' to 'strongly agree.' A factor analysis using varimax rotation of survey items with common anchors confirmed the presence of a decision making factor; Cronbach's alpha for this scale was 0.70.
scale: five-point Likert scale ('strongly disagree' to 'strongly agree')

description: In the Ghana dataset, this variable was coded as '1' when the managing director was Ghanaian and as '0' otherwise.

A weighted composite index, developed by Hecht (2004), of private property rights acts (PPRAs) that vary by state and year; the index distills 13 attributes of 20 different property rights acts, weighting rules according to their severity. These acts function as ex ante administrative procedures that constrain agency decision making. The index ranges from 0 to 100, with a high score indicating that state regulators have little discretion; the authors reverse-coded the variable so that 100 represents the highest possible amount of discretion and 0 the lowest. The variable was standardized to minimize collinearity on interaction terms and lagged by one year.

Dummy variable coded as 1 for new entrants (de novo entrants: entrepreneurial startups originating in the hydroelectric power industry that have not previously received a license approval) and 0 otherwise. It is interacted with the predictor variable regulatory discretion in the analysis. In the sample, 39 percent of new licenses are coded as new entrants.

Dependent variable is license approval of hydroelectric facility projects (0 if not approved, 1 if approved), with the permitting case dropped from the data set after an approval, withdrawal, or denial event. Because 91 percent of licenses are eventually approved and approval time can vary from one to over 20 years, license approval is modeled with an accelerated failure time (AFT) model, estimated by maximum likelihood, where the dependent variable is the firm's observed time to license approval.
scale: 0/1 indicator; time to approval in days in the AFT model

description: For the lower- and upper-chamber legislative levels the authors used the percentage of seats by which the dominant party held a majority; for gubernatorial elections they used the margin of victory. Political competitiveness is coded as high if the margin of victory was less than 5 percent for gubernatorial elections, and high if the margin by which the dominant party in that chamber held a majority was less than 5 percent for legislative seats. Political competitiveness for gubernatorial and upper- and lower-chamber elections are dummy variables coded as 1 if political competitiveness is high and 0 otherwise.

For each level of government-the legislative chambers and executive-the authors coded dominant party control. This variable is coded as 1 if state government has divided control and 0 otherwise; control is united when the same political party controls the legislative and executive levels of government and divided when the same party does not control them.
The number of years since the studio has first released a game. It is used to test H1A-H1C and is lagged by one year in the estimations.

The average studio-specific tenure of all employees who were part of the lead team for any games released by the studio in that year. The studio-specific tenure for an employee who is part of any lead team is the number of years since that employee first appeared as being credited in any role in a game that was released by the focal studio. Its interaction term with studio age is used to test H2A-H2C, and the variable is centered around its sample mean before the interaction term is constructed.

The average industry tenure of all employees who were part of the lead team for any games released by the studio in that year. The industry tenure for an employee who is part of a lead team is the number of years since that employee first appeared as being credited in any role in a game, regardless of the studio that developed that particular game. Its interaction term with studio age is used to test H3A-H3C, and the variable is centered around its sample mean before the interaction term is constructed.

The average scores of the media reviews for the games a studio released that are either part of sequels or use franchised content (i.e., non-original-content games). The authors do not suggest that these games involve no exploration at all, but state that relative to games that are neither sequels nor use franchised content they are more exploitative and less exploratory.

The average scores of the media reviews for the games a studio released that are neither parts of sequels nor use franchised content (i.e., original-content games), which are characterized as involving greater exploration.
