The average score of the media reviews of original-content (i.e., exploratory) games released by the studio in a given year minus the average score of the media reviews of non-original-content (i.e., exploitative) games released by the studio in that year. The measure captures the difference in the quality of original-content games compared to non-original-content games in a given year.

Team-level index of batting skill that includes 13 indicators, all of which relate to scoring runs, with a minimum-use criterion of at least ten at-bats during the season; the coefficient alpha for the index is .84. For each indicator a three-year lagged player average was calculated and then a team-level simple average per indicator was computed. Comparative scores per dyad were created by comparing team A's batting resource with team B's batting resource, so positive values represent a resource advantage for team A and negative values a disadvantage.
time_window: three-year lagged player averages; season in which the dyad occurs

description: Team-level index of pitching skill with seven indicators that relate to the ability and endurance of the pitching squad and the lack of pitching errors; the minimum-use criterion was at least ten innings over the 162-game season and the coefficient alpha is .84. Comparative dyad scores compare team A's pitching resource with team B's pitching resource. Subindices for starting and relief pitchers were also created to assess Hypothesis 4.
time_window: three-year lagged player averages; season in which the dyad occurs

description: Team-level index of fielding skill with two indicators and a minimum-use criterion of ten innings played; the coefficient alpha is .67. Comparative dyad scores compare team A's fielding resource with team B's fielding resource, with positive values indicating a resource advantage for team A.
time_window: three-year lagged player averages; season in which the dyad occurs

description: Subindex of the pitching skill index for starting pitchers, defined as the four pitchers on a team who had the most starts during the season; this operationalization captures over 71 percent of the games started over the three seasons. The coefficient alpha for the starting pitchers index is .81.
time_window: three-year lagged player averages; season in which the dyad occurs

description: Subindex of the pitching skill index for relief pitchers, defined as all pitchers on the team's roster other than the starting pitchers. The coefficient alpha for the relief pitchers index is .86.
time_window: three-year lagged player averages; season in which the dyad occurs

description: Comparative managerial advantage was measured as the differential between the simple and the weighted team average for each indicator: the simple team average represents baseline skill sets and the weighted team average (based on actual deployment) the realized skill sets, so positive differentials indicate the degree to which resources were successfully bundled and deployed. The per-indicator managerial scores were combined into team-level indices following the same procedure used for the skill set indices and then differenced within the dyad. The coefficient alpha for the batting resource management measure is .94.
time_window: season in which the dyad occurs

description: Calculated as the differential between the simple and the weighted team average per indicator, aggregated into a team-level index and compared within the dyad so that positive values indicate successful bundling and deployment. The coefficient alpha for the overall pitching resource management measure is .89. Separate measures were created for the management of starters and the management of relievers.
time_window: season in which the dyad occurs

description: Calculated as the differential between the simple and the weighted team average per indicator, aggregated into a team-level index and compared within the dyad so that positive values indicate successful bundling and deployment. The coefficient alpha for the fielding resource management measure is .88.
time_window: season in which the dyad occurs

description: Separate measure of resource management for starting pitchers, built as the differential between simple and weighted team averages per indicator and aggregated as an index. The coefficient alpha for this measure is .91.
time_window: season in which the dyad occurs

description: Separate measure of resource management for relief pitchers, built as the differential between simple and weighted team averages per indicator and aggregated as an index. The coefficient alpha for this measure is .76.
time_window: season in which the dyad occurs

description: Parity was operationalized by grouping sample observations on the comparative resource advantage of the focal skill set. The 'similar' group consisted of 10 percent of the sample's observations in which the focal skill set of team A is most similar to team B, and the 'dissimilar' group had a high part (10 percent where team A held a very high comparative advantage) and a low part (10 percent where team A held a very high comparative disadvantage).
time_window: season in which the dyad occurs

description: Parity was operationalized by grouping sample observations on the comparative resource advantage of the focal skill set. The 'similar' group consisted of 10 percent of the sample's observations in which the focal skill set of team A is most similar to team B, and the 'dissimilar' group had a high part (10 percent where team A held a very high comparative advantage) and a low part (10 percent where team A held a very high comparative disadvantage).
time_window: season in which the dyad occurs

description: Parity was operationalized by grouping sample observations on the comparative resource advantage of the focal skill set. The 'similar' group consisted of 10 percent of the sample's observations in which the focal skill set of team A is most similar to team B, and the 'dissimilar' group had a high part (10 percent where team A held a very high comparative advantage) and a low part (10 percent where team A held a very high comparative disadvantage).
time_window: season in which the dyad occurs

description: The dependent variable is the relative performance of the teams in the dyadic competitive contests within each season, measured as team A's win percentage for within-dyad games. Teams were randomly assigned as team A and team B, and team A was used as the referent for all comparisons.

The contemporaneous ethnicity of the inventive workforce in the firm's RDHQ, measured in the same way as the satellite outcome but using inventors located at RDHQ. It is the average share of the RDHQ's inventor-patents accounted for by inventors of neither Anglo-Saxon nor European ethnicity and ranges continuously from 0% to 100%.

The observed ethnicity of the inventive workforce at the satellite aggregating over inventor-patents; the average share of the satellite's inventive workforce of neither Anglo-Saxon nor European ethnicity. The variable ranges continuously from 0% (all inventors of Anglo-Saxon/European descent) to 100% (all inventors of other ethnic descent).

variable_name: R&D centralization of firm in initial period (RDCentr)
description: The share of a firm's U.S.-based domestic patents that occurred in its RDHQ in the first period observed; a time-invariant measure. RDHQs are identified as the top MSAs accounting for 30% or more of the firm's U.S.-based inventor-patents, allowing up to three RDHQ facilities. The authors report an average initial centralization of 64.7% with a range of 31.6%–98.3%.
time_window: first period observed for the firm

variable_name: Rate of inventor collaboration over locations
description: The rate of team collaboration on patents between the satellite location and its parent RDHQ; the sample average is 30.1% collaboration. The authors split the sample by period into halves based upon median rates of observed inventor collaboration between satellites and their parent RDHQs.

variable_name: Rate of intrafirm career mobility to RDHQ
description: Mobility is defined for inventors based upon whether they patent when working at RDHQ at least once during their career, a career-level definition used because of out-and-back movements from RDHQ. The sample average rate of inventor mobility between the satellite and RDHQ is 10.1%.

Indicates whether the satellite location has the same technology focus as its RDHQ, defined using the modal NBER subcategories of inventor-patents for the two locations. The authors also report a tighter match using the primary USPC technology of the locations.

Not an inventor-level variable: the authors quantify organizational reproduction as the estimated link between the ethnic inventor share of a satellite location and the contemporaneous ethnic inventor share of the firm's RDHQ, benchmarked against the explanatory power of the satellite's host city for the same outcome. The relative size of the two links is used to gauge the magnitude of reproduction.
time_window: contemporaneous period of the satellite observation

description: The ethnic share of the RDHQ's inventive workforce during the initial legacy period 1975–1984, used as the explanatory variable for the ethnic composition of satellites after 1995. It is constructed in the same way as the contemporaneous RDHQ ethnic share.

variable_name: Ethnic share of inventors in satellite locations after 1995
description: The ethnic share of inventors in satellite locations of legacy firms, observed in the periods after 1995 (1995–2004 and 2005–2014) and regressed on the ethnic workforce present in RDHQ during 1975–1984.

Indicator variable coded '1' for those selected contacts in the investor-centric set (370 contacts) and coded '0' for those selected contacts in the entrepreneur-centric set (314 contacts). The investor-centric set consists of names of new contacts, not already named in 'entrepreneur-centric contacts', that entrepreneurs listed after the identity and background of the targeted investors were disclosed, to help them connect to these investors.

Indicator variable representing the reciprocity persuasion template assigned to a contact. The template provides the same information as the baseline condition and adds a promise of future reciprocity. Contacts were first stratified based on closeness and then randomly assigned to receive one of the three templated messages, with the baseline as the omitted comparison condition.

Indicator variable representing the monetary incentives persuasion template assigned to a contact. In addition to the information in the baseline condition, a 'finder's fee' of 1% of the funds raised capped at SGD 1,000 was proposed. The template was randomly assigned to contacts after stratification by closeness, with the baseline as the omitted comparison condition.

The count of successful referrals to panel investors that originated from a selected contact of the entrepreneur, ranging from 0 (no successful referral to any investor) to 4 (successful referrals to all four investors). A digital message is coded as a successful referral only if the investor informs the research team that the message that reached them came from a person whom the investor would respond to.
time_window: three-day window following the day of the workshop

description: Firm gender diversity is measured with the conventional Blau's index: 1 minus the squared percentage of women workers minus the squared percentage of men workers. The resulting variable ranges from 0 to 0.5, with a higher value indicating greater gender diversity. The measure is lagged by one year. Data come from Bloomberg, which collects workforce diversity information from firms' annual reports.

variable_name: Country avg female pct on boards
description: The average percentage of women board members in a firm's country. Because the main sample is biased toward larger firms, the measure is constructed using a more representative sample in each country and industry, the S&P Global Broad Market Index, for which Bloomberg offers annual board composition data for over 80% of firms. Having women in important and visible positions is taken to signal that organizations value gender diversity.

variable_name: Industry avg female pct on boards
description: The average percentage of women board members in a firm's industry, constructed from the more representative S&P Global Broad Market Index sample for which Bloomberg provides annual board composition data. The prevalence of women on boards is used as a signal of the normative legitimacy of gender diversity in the environment.

variable_name: Country pct firms with diversity policy
description: The percentage of firms in a country that have publicly announced pro-diversity policies or programs. Bloomberg tracks over 8,000 firms in the Broad Market Index each year on whether they have announced, through press releases or investors' reports, a commitment to increase diversity, ensure equal employment, promote affirmative action, or otherwise support diversity.

variable_name: Industry pct firms with diversity policy
description: The percentage of firms in an industry that have publicly announced pro-diversity policies or programs, based on Bloomberg's annual tracking of whether firms announce a commitment to increase diversity, ensure equal employment, promote affirmative action, or otherwise support diversity. Organizations' public commitment to diversity is taken to reflect the normative legitimacy of diversity in the environment.

variable_name: Country laws supporting women at work
description: Regulatory legitimacy is measured with the Women, Business, and the Law database of the World Bank Group, which examines each country's legal environment for women in the workplace. A section of the report covers laws on maternity and parental leave, nondiscrimination and equal remuneration, retirement age, and legal restrictions to certain occupations and tasks. Using this information, the author assigned each country a score used as the measure of the regulatory legitimacy of gender diversity in each country-year.

Tobin's Q is calculated as a firm's market value over the replacement value of its assets. Because investors determine the market value, Tobin's Q directly measures the market's perception of a firm's long-term value. Models predicting Tobin's Q control for ROA.

ROA measures actual return without taking into account stock market speculations. It is used as the measure of the firm's revenue-related performance and is correlated with Tobin's Q at 0.5. Because ROA can influence market valuation, it is included as a control in models predicting Tobin's Q.

Gender of the entrepreneur delivering the pitch, used as the grouping variable for comparing men's and women's language use. The sample analyzed consisted of 93 male and 36 female early-stage entrepreneurs.

Abstraction was measured with the Brysbaert Concreteness Index (BCI), which relies on concreteness norms created for 40,000 commonly used English word lemmas rated from 1 (abstract or language based) to 5 (concrete or experience based). A BCI score was computed for each pitch based on the words in the Brysbaert dictionary, including a mean estimate of the overall concreteness of the language used and an estimate of variability in linguistic concreteness. Higher values indicate more concrete, hence less abstract, speech.

A manual coder blind to the study variables identified words in four linguistic categories falling along an abstractness continuum, from least abstract to most abstract: descriptive action verbs, interpretive action verbs, state verbs, and adjectives. An overall abstraction score ranging from 1 to 4 was constructed for each participant using a weighted index of these categories; the exact weighting formula in the text is not legible.

The application included a measure of founder gender, used as a dummy variable indicating whether the entrepreneur was female (Female = 1, Male = 0). The VC firm specified that the application should be completed by the founder or CEO, who would also be the primary contact.

An overall concreteness score was computed for each entrepreneur's written proposal using the BCI, following the same procedure as in Study 1, producing both a mean estimate of the concreteness of the language used and an estimate of the variability in linguistic concreteness. The BCI concreteness measure was then reverse-scored to provide a measure of abstraction and facilitate interpretation of any effect.

Perceptions of long-term growth and scalability were measured with a three-item scale adapted from validated scales of entrepreneurial growth and scalability. On a Likert-type scale ranging from 1 (not at all) to 5 (a lot), investors rated each startup on three items; Cronbach's alpha was .89.

Investors performed an initial screening, upon which approximately 90% of startups were eliminated from consideration. Investment likelihood was assessed as a binary measure of whether the startup was one of the approximately 10% of startups (122 out of the total 1,284 startups) that made it through the initial stage of funding consideration.

The style of the pitch was experimentally manipulated so that investors received either a concrete or an abstract description of the same baseline venture (a Nanospray glass coating). In the concrete condition the coating was described as producing a water-resistant layer only around 100 nanometers thick that can bond to any surface; in the abstract condition it was described as highly flexible and breathable and able to bond to a wide range of surfaces.

Perceptions of long-term growth and scalability were measured in similar fashion to Study 2, using a two-item scale that sought to distinctly capture investors' perceptions of long-term growth orientation. Investors rated each item on a five-point Likert scale; alpha was .86.

Investors indicated their likelihood of making an investment in the entrepreneur on a five-point Likert-type scale in response to a single item: 'This is a company that you would invest in,' with 1 = strongly disagree to 5 = strongly agree.

Number of the supplier's display-related U.S. patents over the last 5 years. Display-related patents were defined as those containing the terms 'liquid crystal display' or 'LCD' or classified in International Patent Classification sections G02F 1/-, G09G 3/-, G09F 9/3-, or G09F 13/-.

Number of previous years in which the manufacturer had purchased at least one notebook computer display from the supplier. Decisions made in the first three years of a buyer being present in the data were not modeled because the measure of the relationship would otherwise be truncated.

Total number of different notebook computer models for which the given supplier had supplied displays to the manufacturer, used to capture the intensity of the past relationship. Like the duration measure, it is truncated for transactions that took place before the buyer entered the data, so early decisions were not modeled.

Indicator variable set to 1 if the supplier is part of the same company as the notebook manufacturer. The value of previous transactions may differ for internal and external suppliers, so the measure is also interacted with the two measures of past relationship.

Indicator variable set to 0 for all potential suppliers except the one the manufacturer chose, for which it was set to 1. In the set of observations related to a manufacturer's introduction of a given innovation, exactly one supplier is coded 1.
level: buyer-supplier dyad within a model introduction

variable_name: innovation type (modular vs. systemic display innovation)
description: Innovations in which the display's resolution was increased are classified as modular, and innovations in which the display's size was increased are classified as systemic, based on the technological argument that size increases interact extensively with the design of the rest of the computer while resolution increases are mostly contained within the display. The two types of innovation are estimated in separate regressions rather than as a single interacted variable.

A count measure of multimarket contact, following Gimeno and Woo (1996), that sums the number of markets other than focal market m in which firms i and j also compete, computed for R&D activity. An instance of multimarket contact in exploration is coded 1 when firm i, an incumbent researching new drugs in market m, and rival firm j, which also researches in market m, also meet in market n. The average intensity of multimarket contact in exploration averages these contacts with all of firm i's relevant competitors from market m. The paper's generic mathematical expression for the measure could not be transcribed from the text; the description follows the prose definition.

A count measure of multimarket contact, following Gimeno and Woo (1996), that sums the number of markets other than focal market m in which firms i and j also compete, computed for sales activity. An instance of multimarket contact in exploitation is coded 1 when firm i, an incumbent selling drugs in market m, and rival firm j, which also sells drugs in market m, also meet in market n. The average intensity of multimarket contact in exploitation averages these contacts with all of firm i's relevant competitors from market m. The paper's generic mathematical expression for the measure could not be transcribed from the text; the description follows the prose definition.

Coded 1 if a firm began making R&D investments in a particular market between the beginning and the end of a given year, and 0 otherwise. Coded from BioScan, the biotechnology industry reporting service, which captures R&D investment (and divestment) information by market six times a year. Markets are FDA therapeutic classes in which the firm conducts biotechnology R&D.

Coded 1 if the firm divested a research line between the beginning and the end of a given year, and 0 otherwise. Coded from BioScan, which captures R&D investment (and divestment) information by market six times a year.

Drawing on the PDR data, coded 1 if the firm began selling products in a given market within a given year, and 0 otherwise. The PDR identifies markets in which firms sell existing products under the FDA therapeutic-class taxonomy.

Drawing on the PDR data, equals 1 when firms ceased to sell drugs in a given market, and 0 otherwise. The PDR identifies markets in which firms sell existing products under the FDA therapeutic-class taxonomy.

The total number of Airbnb listings in each county, calculated from the listings posted on Airbnb.com from February 2013 to September 2017 and merged into the tourist hotel dataset by month and county in which each hotel was located. In the estimation equations the variable is the county-month specific number of Airbnb listings.

The monthly average occupancy rate, defined as the ratio of the number of occupied rooms per month, from the population-based administrative profile of hotel performances in Taiwan. The logarithm of the occupancy rate is the dependent variable in the estimation equations.
The average daily room rate per night, taken as the hotel price and used as the dependent variable in the price equations. The logarithm of the price is the dependent variable.

variable_name: Employee_room (investment in service quality in room department)
description: The number of employees in the room department (housekeeping per room), used as the measure of service quality in lodging. More human resources per guestroom imply a longer duration of service time and shorter customer waiting time, so a larger value indicates better service quality. The logarithm of this variable is the dependent variable in the service quality equation.

variable_name: Employee_food (investment in service quality in F&B department)
description: The number of employees in the food and beverage department per guestroom, used as the measure of service quality in F&B. A larger value indicates better service quality, and the logarithm of this variable is the dependent variable in the service quality equation.
An indicator for hotels ranked with five stars in the Taiwan Tourism Bureau ranking system, interacted with the number of Airbnb listings in the occupancy rate, price, and service quality equations.

variable_name: low quality hotels (three stars or fewer)
description: An indicator for hotels ranked with three stars or fewer in the Taiwan Tourism Bureau ranking system, interacted with the number of Airbnb listings in the occupancy rate, price, and service quality equations.
scale: binary (1 = hotel with three stars or fewer)

description: A composite of the individual resources: the authors state that they standardized each of their eleven resources and combined the standardized scores, describing it in one place as the average of the standardized values (P101) and in another as summing these standardized scores (P124). It is entered as a main effect and interacted with strategic change to predict subsequent enrollment.
time_window: year t (1971 in the cross-sectional model, time t in the time-series models)

description: The percentage of out-of-state enrollment, which captures the breadth of a college's renown and the extent to which it has national drawing power. Any organization with national recognition and the ability to reject a large percentage of would-be customers can be seen as enjoying a resource advantage.
time_window: year t (measured in 1971 in the cross-sectional model)

description: The percentage of applicants rejected in any given year. This captures the depth, or strength of reputation, in addition to its breadth.
time_window: year t (measured in 1971 in the cross-sectional model)

description: A college's philanthropic support in a given year, measured as total giving divided by total revenue. Annual financial support from alumni, parents, and other donors is an important resource that is highly variable across colleges.
time_window: year t (measured in 1971 in the cross-sectional model)

description: The average (within rank) salary of a college's faculty, a commonly used indicator of organizational quality in higher education that is related, however imperfectly, to the underlying construct of faculty excellence.
time_window: year t (measured in 1971 in the cross-sectional model)

description: The percentage of faculty who were full professors, included on the logic that rank provides an alternative indicator of faculty excellence.
time_window: year t (measured in 1971 in the cross-sectional model)

description: Following Levinthal (1995), financial resource endowments are defined literally as the annual market value of a college's endowment.
time_window: year t (measured in 1971 in the cross-sectional model)

description: A variable capturing organizational age as an indicator of the organization's cumulative experience and learning. Age is described as a less specific resource indicator than the others considered, but relevant because each additional year of survival reveals evidence of increasing capability.
time_window: year t (measured in 1971 in the cross-sectional model)

description: The median SAT score of entering freshmen, one of two time-varying indicators of student quality.
time_window: year t (measured in 1971 in the cross-sectional model)

description: The percentage of students who continue to graduate school, the second time-varying indicator of student quality.
time_window: year t (measured in 1971 in the cross-sectional model)

description: Scale is measured simply as the size or enrollment of a college in a given year, used as a predictor of strategic change and of enrollment change.
time_window: year t (measured in 1971 in the cross-sectional model)

description: Scope of operations is measured as a count variable, capturing the total number of fields in which a college granted undergraduate majors.
time_window: year t (measured in 1971 in the cross-sectional model)

description: The percentage of degrees that a college grants in non-liberal-arts fields in a given year, computed as non-liberal-arts degrees divided by total undergraduate degrees. Liberal arts fields were defined to include biology, fine arts, foreign languages, humanities and letters, mathematics, physical sciences, psychology, social sciences, theology, and interdisciplinary studies; non-liberal-arts fields are all others. Changes in this variable over rolling four-year intervals from t to t + 4 (and cumulative change from 1971 to 1986) measure strategic change.
time_window: year t (change measured from t to t + 4 and, in the cross-sectional models, from 1971 to 1986)

description: Performance is measured in terms of changes in a college's full-time-equivalent undergraduate enrollment. The cross-sectional model predicts enrollment in 1986 while controlling for enrollment in 1971; the time-series models predict enrollment at t + 5 as a function of strategic change over t to t + 4; a dichotomous measure of enrollment change (enrollment decline) is used in the event history models.

Measured following Trajtenberg et al. (1997) with the USPTO classification system, using all of the three-digit classes of the prior art patents cited by the focal patent. The distance between two prior art patents is 0 if they belong to the same three-digit technological class, 0.33 if they are in the same two-digit class, 0.66 if they are in the same one-digit class, and 1 if they are in different one-digit classes or have no prior art. The higher the value of this measure, the more distant the knowledge combined; cases where patents have no prior art are controlled for. The aggregation formula is unreadable in the supplied text.

A Herfindahl index of the concentration of USPTO patent classes in the prior art cited by the focal patent, following Hall et al. (2001), who termed it 'patent originality'. The higher the value of diversity, the more diverse the sources of knowledge a patent combines. As suggested by Hall (2002) the measure was adjusted to correct for downward bias in patents with few citations to prior art. For patents that cite no prior art the measure cannot be calculated, so the value is set to 0 and a 'No prior art' dummy is included as a control.

An indicator variable where 1 identifies those patents that originate a new topic in the body of knowledge. Topics are produced by applying latent Dirichlet allocation topic modeling to the abstracts of the patents, with the model limited to 100 topics. Topic-originating patents are those over a threshold weighting of 0.2 for a topic and appearing in the first 12 months of the topic formation, based on application date. The average number of topic-originating patents identified this way is 1.89 per topic, for a total of 189.
time_window: first 12 months of topic formation (application date)

description: The count of forward citations, that is, prior art citations made to the focal patent by subsequent patents, over a five-year window measured from the grant date. Estimated with a negative binomial response function in the generalized structural equation model.
time_window: five years from the grant date

description: A dummy variable indicating whether a patent is in the top 5 percent of cited patents in the dataset. It is estimated with a probit response function in the generalized structural equation model.
time_window: five years from the grant date

description: Dummy variable coded one when the change in the number of permanent employees between year t and year t+1 exceeded 0.05, and zero otherwise. Change is computed as the number of permanent employees in year t+1 minus the number in year t, divided by the number in year t; permanent employees are all employees except temporary workers. Firms that went out of business in year t+1 were excluded from the calculation.

Dummy variable coded one when the percentage growth of the focal firm in earnings before interest and taxes between years t-1 and t was above the average of the sub-manufacturing sector to which the focal firm belonged, and zero otherwise.

Dummy variable coded one when the percentage growth of the focal firm in sales between years t-1 and t was above the average of the sub-manufacturing sector to which the focal firm belonged, and zero otherwise.

Measured from the entropy index of branch dispersion, the sum over the 17 Spanish regions of pk ln(1/pk), where pk is the percentage of the focal firm's branches in the kth region. Regional concentration is reverse coded from this dispersion measure: a firm's score is the difference between the maximum dispersion score of all firms and the firm's own dispersion score, so a higher score means the firm's branches are situated in fewer regions. The component terms were centered before interactions were constructed.

Firm-level variable combining the percentage of the firm's branches in each of the 17 Spanish regions with a dummy coded one when the region was governed by a regional-national party and zero otherwise. The equation defining the variable was not extractable from the paper's rendering, so the exact weighting cannot be reported. The component was centered before interactions were constructed.

variable_name: Regional Government Spending on Industrial Development (centered)
description: Spending in region k is the percentage of that region's regional government budget spent on industrial development; the firm-level variable combines this with the percentage of the firm's branches in each of the 17 regions. The equation defining the variable was not extractable from the paper's rendering, so the exact weighting cannot be reported. The component was centered before interactions were constructed.

Built from the employment rate of the manufacturing sector in region k and the percentage of the focal firm's branches in each of the 17 Spanish regions. The equation defining the variable was not extractable from the paper's rendering, so the exact weighting cannot be reported.
The logarithm of the focal firm's total assets. The component was centered before interactions were constructed.
Dummy variable coded one when the owner (and his family) worked in the top management team of the focal firm, and zero otherwise. The component was centered before interactions were constructed.

Ethnic diversity was measured by the Blau index (1 − Σp², where p is the category proportion) of the racial distribution among five groups: Caucasian, African American, Chinese, Japanese, and American Indian. Blau indexes take a maximum value of unity and are interpreted such that higher values mean greater diversity.

Calculated from the census data on the national origin of the foreign-born individuals, this variable is the Blau index over the 40 categories (plus a residual) in the census. The categories are fine-grained for European origins and provide information at the country level, but those for non-European origins were more broadly defined. Some categories are not independent countries, but the original categories were not modified because they reflected salient divisions at the time. Higher values mean greater diversity.

A Blau index over the membership of different categories of churches in the county. There are 58 categories of churches in the census data, reflecting the highly diverse religious life at the time and the high priority given to mapping churches accurately in the census; the original categories are used without modification. Higher values mean greater diversity.

Operationalized by the inequality of farm size based on the census categorization of farms (fewer than 10 acres, 10–19 acres, 20–49 acres, 50–99 acres, 100–499 acres, 500–999 acres, and 1,000 acres and over). It is calculated as a Gini index with an adjustment for categorical source data (Gastwirth 1972); i is the category center point and p_i is the proportion of farms in each category. The exact formula is not readable in this text. The Gini index takes a maximum value of unity, and higher values mean greater inequality.

Bank runs are measured using bank suspensions. Banks faced with a bank run temporarily suspend deposit withdrawals, which allows them time to procure funds to pay back deposits; suspension is different from failure, as banks that become insolvent move directly to failure without a preceding suspension. Data on bank suspensions were obtained from the January 1894 issue of Bradstreet's, which contains a complete list of suspensions that occurred during the 1893 bank panic, including whether the bank had failed following the suspension or had reopened.

Distance-weighted influence from all prior bank runs, including runs outside the 22 sample states, so that the probability of a bank run is determined by the product of the contagion effect from earlier runs and the susceptibility of each bank. Rather than assuming one specific functional form, multiple forms were tried and the best-fitting inverse-log specification (1/ln(D), where D is distance) was chosen by Bayesian information criteria. The contagion term was kept updated at all times by event-based spell splitting, which created new spells for all banks whenever there was a bank run.
time_window: updated continuously from April 1 to August 31, 1893

description: A state-specific influence term of the same functional form as distance-weighted runs but with only same-state bank runs, added to account for the stronger influence of runs that occurred within the same state compared with other states. Because all within-state bank runs are also in the all-bank-runs influence vector, its coefficient shows how much more influential same-state runs are.
time_window: updated continuously from April 1 to August 31, 1893

description: A Blau measure across three board attributes: (1) whether the board members are in different regions (U.S. states); (2) whether the board members' organizations are in different 2-digit Standard Industrial Classification codes; and (3) whether the board members represent different organization types (e.g., a venture capital firm; a manufacturing firm; a research institute; a bank, including investment banks; a university; a corporate investor; or other organizations). A separate Blau index is calculated for each attribute, and their geometric mean is used to create a combined Blau index. The separate Blau indices are correlated between r = .75 and .86.

A multiplex board tie is when an outside board member has another relationship with the focal firm, such as being a customer, an investor, or a 'parent.' The measure counts the total number of types of board multiplexity (customer, investor, or parent) across all outside board members. It was calculated yearly through to 1990 and ranges from no ties to all three types of multiplex ties.

Centrality asymmetry in the board network is measured by calculating the skewness of board centrality scores, using yearly board member-level matrices. A firm-affiliation matrix is used to create an affiliation-affiliation matrix and each board member's standardized degree centrality score, which captures the number of ties for each board member. When there is no skewness, centrality scores are evenly distributed around the mean; positive skewness indicates a longer tail on the right-hand side and negative skewness a long left-hand tail. In the models the differences are separated by a spline method into positive skewness and negative skewness, with both spline variables taking on positive values (e.g., using the absolute value of negative skewness).

Measured as the difference in centrality between the most central noninvestor, outside board member and the most central investor board member in each year when the outsider has higher centrality and zero otherwise. Two separate matrices (an investor board matrix and a non-investor board matrix) are created and degree centrality is calculated for each board member, so investor centrality is not a subset of board centrality. The differences are separated into investor dominance and board dominance with a spline method.

Measured as the difference in centrality between the most central investor board member and the most central noninvestor outside board member in each year when the investor board member has higher centrality and zero otherwise. Two separate matrices (an investor board matrix and a non-investor board matrix) are created and degree centrality is calculated for each board member, so investor centrality is not a subset of board centrality. The differences are separated into investor dominance and board dominance with a spline method.

The dependent variable in the first set of analyses is the speed with which a firm is able to establish three different types of alliances, so the measure takes into account the timing and type of alliances. Monthly data were collected on all formal alliances formed early in the new ventures' lives (excluding ties to investors), with the month and year for the start and end of each alliance. The time to portfolio emergence is measured as the attainment of three types of alliances.

When diverse alliance portfolio is used as an independent variable for the revenue milestone analyses, the measure is the cumulative number of types of alliances, updated monthly. It counts the number of different types of alliances the firm has obtained, based on monthly data on all formal alliances formed early in the venture's life.

The dependent variable is whether and when important revenue milestone events are reached; the authors code the year in which the firm obtains US$10 million, US$20 million, and US$50 million in annual revenues. The US$10 million and US$20 million milestones are used in the analysis, and the authors also predict to US$50 million in revenues to examine a longer-term effect.

Director gender, coded female = 1 (male = 0). To identify director gender, ISS data were matched with director biography profiles in the BoardEx database using string matching and extensive hand checking.

variable_name: Female (W female t) and male (W male t) interlock network matrices
description: Separate annual firm-by-firm network matrices constructed from the ISS board rosters. Cell i,j in the female matrix contains a 1 if firms i and j share a female director in year t and zero otherwise; the male matrix is constructed analogously for shared male directors. These matrices form the basis for modeling interorganizational network influence and comparing how male and female directors differently drive this influence.

The focal dependent variable for Analysis 1 is the number of board seats that the director held in time t, taken from ISS director rosters. In Analysis 2 the number of board seats held in the prior year is used as a predictor of holding a key committee chair position, entered both as dummy categories (2, 3, 4, 5+ board seats, with one board seat as the reference) and as a continuous measure.

Whether the director held a key committee chair position (= 1). Key committee positions are a long-standing indicator of an individual director's influence and include the audit committee, which oversees the firm's financial reporting, and the compensation committee, which oversees compensation of top executives.

A six-item index that captures the focal firm's corporate governance profile. High scores indicate that managers are more entrenched, whereas low scores indicate more shareholder friendly governance. The e-index is widely used in research on corporate governance as an indicator of firms' shareholder friendly versus managerialist governance.

variable_name: Network autocorrelation social influence estimate (ρ1, ρ2)
description: Models estimate the effect of network neighbors' e-index scores in the previous year on the focal firm's e-index score, as mediated through male and female director interlocks. The male weight matrix captures the firm-to-firm interlock network formed through male directors in the previous year and its estimate is ρ1; the female weight matrix captures the interlock network formed through female directors in the previous year and its estimate is ρ2. Firm fixed-effects constrain the social influence effect to within-firm variance, so that ρ1 and ρ2 estimate changes in the focal firm's e-index score as a function of changes in neighbors' scores.
time_window: predictors at t-1; outcome at t

variable_name: Segment's share of value in the sector
description: Segment's market capitalization is calculated by summing the adjusted market capitalization of all participating firms within each segment-year; the market capitalization of the entire sector is derived by adding the market capitalization of all segments by year. Dividing each segment's market capitalization by the sector's total market capitalization for each year yields the dependent variable. Because a fixed-effects model is estimated, the variable is really the change in the market capitalization of a segment compared with the sector as a function of changes in other attributes. An alternative 'discrepancy' dependent variable deducts the share expected by virtue of the mathematical ratio between the kingpin's market capitalization and the rest of the segment.

Calculated as the kingpin's share of R&D expenditure relative to its segment's total R&D expenditure in each segment-year. The focus is on the distribution of the variable rather than its level: high values mean a major inequality in technological investment among participating firms in a segment-year. Each segment has one kingpin in each dimension, which may or may not be the same firm.

Calculated as the kingpin's share of market capitalization relative to its segment's total market capitalization in each segment-year. Kingpins were identified as the firms with the highest market capitalization in their segment. High values for the kingpin's share mean there is a major inequality in value among participating firms in a segment-year.

variable_name: Segment's share of value excluding that of the kingpin
description: For the strong test of the externality argument, the kingpin was excluded from the analysis of the share of value: the kingpin's market capitalization amount was excluded when calculating each segment's market capitalization, so that the variable shows how the fringe firms in the segment, over and above the kingpin, are affected. This segment-level share of value is again estimated with segment fixed effects.

A dummy variable constructed from the filing date of adverse financial restatements. It takes a value of 1 during the 5 years following the year of the restatement and takes a value of 0 during the 5 years prior to the filing, and the year of the restatement filing is excluded from the analysis. In the baseline analysis, firms affected by a peer restatement event are compared with firms not affected by one.
time_window: 5 years before to 5 years after the restatement filing; filing year excluded

description: A dummy variable constructed from the filing date of adverse financial restatements. It takes a value of 1 during the 5 years following the year of the restatement and takes a value of 0 during the 5 years prior to the filing, and the year of the restatement filing is excluded from the analysis. The main analysis is limited to the subset of firms that were treated by a peer restatement.
time_window: 5 years before to 5 years after the restatement filing; filing year excluded

description: By year, each director who is a concurrent member of the board's audit committee and nomination committee is identified. This director-year level measure is aggregated up to the firm-year level to create a total count of audit-nomination MCDs on a yearly basis for each firm.
Counts the number of new directors who were appointed to the board in a given year.

Counts the number of new directors who were appointed to the board in a given year who possess prior board experience at a publicly traded firm. The measure takes a value of 0 if the board did not appoint any new directors or if the board appointed new directors who did not possess prior board experience.

Counts the number of new directors who were appointed to the board in a given year who possess prior board experience at a publicly traded firm. The measure takes a value of 0 if the board did not appoint any new directors or if the board appointed new directors who did not possess prior board experience. It is the dependent variable in the test of Hypothesis 1.

Counts the number of new directors who were appointed to the board in a given year who possess prior experience on an audit committee on the board of a public firm. The measure takes a value of 0 if the board did not appoint any new directors or if the board appointed new directors who did not possess prior audit committee experience.

Counts the number of new directors who were appointed to the board in a given year who possess prior experience on an audit committee on the board of a public firm. The measure takes a value of 0 if the board did not appoint any new directors or if the board appointed new directors who did not possess prior audit committee experience. It is the dependent variable in the test of Hypothesis 2.

Counts the total number of adverse financial restatements filed within each firm in the panel dataset on an annual basis, using the same Audit Analytics data used to identify restatements at peer firms. To account for the time that elapses between the issuance of inaccurate financials and the subsequent filing of a restatement, each firm-year observation is matched to financial restatements, if any, filed in the subsequent year. Due to the relative infrequency of financial restatements, this variable often takes a value of 0.
time_window: leading count, matched to the subsequent year

description: A counter representing the year in the sample, ranging from 1 to 60 for the years 1950 to 2009. It serves as the independent variable in the Tobit regressions predicting |CAR|; Hypothesis 1 receives further support if the year counter is positively significant.

Eventus generates a predictive model estimating the expected market returns for each firm had the event not occurred, using all trading data from the year prior to and ending 30 days before the event (between 255 and 30 trading days prior to the event); expected returns are subtracted from actual market returns to generate abnormal returns. Cumulative abnormal returns (CARs) are calculated for the 0-0 day, 0-1 day, 0-3 day, and 0-5 day event windows, where 0 is the day of the event, and each signed CAR is converted to its absolute value (|CAR|). The multivariate analysis predicts |CAR| for the (0, 1) and (0, 3) windows, and all continuous variables including |CAR| were Winsorized at the 1 and 99 percent levels.
time_window: event windows of 0-0, 0-1, 0-3 and 0-5 days around the death

description: Cumulative abnormal returns for the 0-0, 0-1, 0-3 and 0-5 day event windows, computed as actual market returns minus expected returns from the Eventus predictive model. The paper reports that there was a small but significant negative reaction on the event day (mean abnormal return = -0.92%, p < 0.01), while abnormal returns were nonsignificant for the five days leading up to the event. Two-tailed t-tests showed no significant change in mean CAR across the three time periods.
time_window: event windows of 0-0, 0-1, 0-3 and 0-5 days around the death

description: The individual's base salary, one of the three components of pay examined. All monetary variables were scaled in 1980 dollars using the Consumer Price Index, and base pay was measured as a natural logarithm. For the organization-level analyses of performance, the authors used average residuals of base pay from Equation 1.

variable_name: Ratio of bonus to base pay
description: The ratio of bonus pay to base pay, one of the two measures the authors designed to capture important aspects of pay mix. Monetary values were scaled in 1980 dollars using the Consumer Price Index. Organization-level analyses used average residuals of this variable from Equation 1.
level: individual manager (aggregated to organization for the performance models)

description: A dichotomous measure coded 1 = yes, 0 = no for eligibility for long-term incentives, the second of the two measures designed to capture pay mix. Organization-level analyses used average residuals of this variable from Equation 1.
level: individual manager (aggregated to organization for the performance models)

description: Years of education and years of potential labor market experience (age minus years of education minus 6), together with length of firm tenure and length of job tenure. Squared terms for the last three variables were used to test the human capital theory prediction that returns diminish as experience increases.

The number of reporting levels between a company's board of directors and a job, and the number of management levels the job's incumbent supervised. In the descriptive statistics the levels relative to the board of directors appear as separate indicators.

Organizational effects were measured using a dummy variable for each firm, added to equations that already contained human capital and job attributes. The increment in explained variance from adding these dummies indicates the general organizational effect.

A company's two-digit Standard Industrial Classification (SIC) code; only industries represented by three or more firms were used, with a further breakdown of some two-digit industries into three-digit industries. Dummy variables for industry were included in the equations.
Size was measured as firm sales, business unit sales, and total employees.

Net income divided by assets. ROA served both as one of the specific organizational characteristics in the pay equations and as the dependent variable in the performance models, where yearly ROA and mean ROA over three years were examined.

Organization responses to the survey question "How do you define your target pay level?", with response options below the median, at the median, between the median and the 75th percentile, at the 75th percentile, and above the 75th percentile. Because the survey did not elicit these self-reports before 1983 and not all organizations provided them, data from only 124 organizations were available for this analysis.
scale: ordinal, five categories from below the median to above the 75th percentile

variable_name: Orientation toward Earlier Stages of Opportunity Advancement
description: A firm's degree of attention toward earlier-stage exploration is proxied through its venture portfolio, reflecting actual resource allocation decisions. The measure uses a weighted means approach with weights reflecting average investment required at each stage: $0.6875 per ton for prospecting, $5.13 per ton for developing, and $76.00 per ton for exploiting. The text's formula block is unreadable in the provided payload, but the authors state that ni refers to the number of ventures in the firm's portfolio at stage i and fi refers to the factor weight for each venture type i; they reversed the measure so higher scores reflect a stronger orientation toward earlier stages of opportunity advancement.

The dependent variable captures the duration of time (Duration) to reach any of the four events. For termination, a venture in the prospecting stage at time t is coded '2' (Terminate during Prospecting) when it is no longer present at time t+1, and a venture in the developing stage at time t is coded '4' (Terminate during Developing) when it is no longer present at time t+1; otherwise it is coded '0'. The competing risks event history model estimates the hazard of termination.

The dependent variable captures the duration of time (Duration) to reach any of the four events. For advancement, a venture in the prospecting stage at time t is coded '1' (Advance to Developing) when it is listed at the developing stage at time t+1, and a venture in the developing stage at time t is coded '3' (Advance to Exploiting) when it is listed at the exploiting stage at time t+1; otherwise it is coded '0'. The competing risks event history model estimates the hazard of advancement.

A time-varying covariate capturing the price variability of a mineral (i.e., its amplitude around the trend) over the preceding 12 months. The authors take a moving window of the standard error of the coefficient b from a regression of time against the monthly price of a mineral, following Dess and Beard (1984) and Boyd (1990). For a venture involved with multiple minerals, they use the mean of the dynamism score of each mineral.
I calculated cultural distance using Hofstede's (1980, 2001) country scores and Kogut and Singh's (1988) cultural distance index. The index measures the distance between Japan and each host country.
I calculated cultural distance using Hofstede's (1980, 2001) country scores and Kogut and Singh's (1988) cultural distance index. The index measures the distance between Japan and each host country.

variable_name: Percentage of expatriate parent country nationals in work force
description: I calculated the proportion of expatriate parent country nationals in a subsidiary's workforce by dividing the number of Japanese expatriates by the number of subsidiary employees. Because using the proportion as a dependent variable in an ordinary least squares regression may violate regression assumptions, a logit transformation of the proportion was used in the regression analysis.

I dummy-coded CEO nationality with 1 for Japanese nationals and 0 for non-Japanese nationals. Two Japanese scholars independently judged CEOs' and top managers' nationalities by examining their names; for individual (including CEO) names the two coders reached a 99 percent agreement rate, and disagreements were resolved through discussion to final consensus.

variable_name: Percentage of parent country nationals on TMT
description: I calculated the proportion of parent country nationals in a TMT by dividing the number of Japanese top managers by the number of subsidiary top managers. Top managers included subsidiary CEOs and presidents and major functional heads. A logit transformation of the proportion was used in the regression analysis.

I measured subsidiary labor productivity as sales over the number of subsidiary employees. The logarithm of labor productivity was used in data analyses. I controlled for the industry effect on labor productivity in the analysis.

I measured subsidiary labor productivity as sales over the number of subsidiary employees. The logarithm of labor productivity was used in data analyses. I controlled for the industry effect on labor productivity in the analysis.
The number of years of operation of the subsidiary was included among the control variables and was also entered as an interaction term with cultural distance in the analyses.

The number of years of operation of the subsidiary was included among the control variables and was also entered as an interaction term with cultural distance and with the proportion of parent country nationals on the TMT.

Predecessor CEOs remaining as board chairs were distinguished, in the press releases announcing new CEO appointments, between those with and those without a departure plan; 'predecessor CEOs staying on as board chairs' referred to those staying on without an explicit departure plan. For these predecessor-board chairs, the authors collected data on whether they continued to be the board chair in each year of the new CEO's first three years of tenure. The variable was coded as 1 if a predecessor stayed on as the board chair in the focal year, and 0 otherwise.
time_window: each year of the new CEO's first three years of tenure

description: The stock market reaction to a new CEO appointment was estimated by calculating the cumulative abnormal return (CAR) following a standard event study approach over the event window [day -2, day +2]. Because a positive stock market reaction may reflect a manipulated result, the authors focused on strong negative stock market reactions: the sample was divided into five subgroups based upon CAR (from top to bottom) and the variable was coded as 1 if the announcement of a new CEO's appointment resulted in a CAR that fell in the top two subgroups, in which all CARs were negative.

Following the prior literature, the authors used a three-step procedure to identify CEO early dismissals. First, CEOs who left office within three years of their tenure were identified from the Factiva database. Second, if any press release during the window [turnover date -1 year, turnover date +1 year] mentioned that the CEO was fired, forced to resign, or departed due to unspecified policy differences, the turnover was classified as a dismissal. Third, other early turnovers in which the departing CEO was under the age of 64 and claimed that the reason for their departure was a resignation along with a termination of directorship or was not related to death, poor health, retirement, or the acceptance of another position were also classified as dismissals.

A research assistant wrote a Python program to automatically search for the first name, last name, and nickname of each predecessor CEO in the opening remarks of the corresponding new CEOs in the earnings conference calls; two coders read the paragraphs with a matched name and assessed whether the contents constituted praising of the predecessor CEO. The variable was coded as 1 if a new CEO complimented the predecessor CEO in the opening remarks of at least one conference call.
time_window: the year the CEO took office and three consecutive years, or until the CEO left office

description: Measured by performing computer-aided content analysis with DICTION 7 software on new CEOs' opening remarks, utilizing DICTION's 'activity' master variable, which refers to language featuring change, the implementation of ideas, and the avoidance of inertia. The master variable is constructed by aggregating seven categories of dictionaries; the score on each category is converted to a z score and combined by the DICTION formula, and the authors did not add 50 to the final score. The score was reverse-coded by multiplying it by -1 to bring it in line with new CEOs' commitment to strategic continuity, and was measured as the average across all earnings conference calls in a focal year.
time_window: focal year, over the first years of tenure

description: Measured by computer-aided content analysis (DICTION 7) of new CEOs' opening remarks, utilizing the 'self-reference' category of the predefined dictionaries, which includes all first-person singular references (e.g., 'I,' 'I'd,' 'I'll,' and 'my') and refers to acts of indexing whereby the locus of action resides in the speaker. The score was not reverse-coded and was measured as the average across all earnings conference calls in a focal year.
time_window: focal year, over the first years of tenure

description: Measured by computer-aided content analysis (DICTION 7) of new CEOs' opening remarks, utilizing an imported category 'strong modal' built by Loughran and McDonald by including terms expressing levels of confidence. The score was not reverse-coded and was measured as the average across all earnings conference calls in a focal year.
time_window: focal year, over the first years of tenure

description: Measured as the ratio of R&D spending to sales. Because firms are not required to report R&D spending that is less than 10% of sales and general administrative expenses, nonreported (e.g., missing) values for R&D spending were replaced with 0. A dummy variable for missing R&D was included in the analysis to control for such replacement.

The effect of inconsistent feedback in the case of negative prospects and positive feedback was studied by including an interaction term between the two variables. Negative prospects was the absolute difference between the firm's future performance expectation and current target when the performance expectations were below the target, and 0 otherwise. Positive feedback was the absolute difference between the firm's past performance and aspiration when the performance was above the aspiration, and 0 otherwise. All four feedback and prospect variables were winsorized at the 0.5% level.

An index of the sum of four standardized components: (1) CEO duality, measured as 1 if the CEO also served as the chair of the BOD, and 0 otherwise; (2) the number of non-CEO TMT members who sat on the BOD (reversed); (3) title inequality; and (4) pay inequality. Title was a count measure based on information available in Execucomp about the different titles that each TMT member held. Pay was the natural logarithm of total compensation received by each TMT member, using the TDC1 variable from Execucomp. TMT members, including the CEO, were considered to be the five highest-paid executives within the firm.

An index of the sum of two standardized components: (1) whether the CEO was a founder of the firm, coded as 1 if the CEO was, and 0 otherwise; and (2) the CEO ownership percentage as a proportion of the summed ownership percentage of outside directors and institutional blockholder investors, namely institutional investors who owned at least 5% of the total firm stock.

An index of the sum of three standardized components: (1) CEO tenure in the firm, (2) the number of roles that the CEO had in the firm, and (3) the number of functional areas in which the CEO had served the firm. The functional areas used were production and operations, R&D and engineering, accounting and finance, management and administration, marketing and sales, law, and personnel and labor relations.

An index of the sum of three standardized components: (1) the number of public boards the CEO sat on, (2) the number of nonprofit boards the CEO sat on, and (3) whether the CEO had an elite education, coded as 1 if the CEO had a degree from an elite institution, and 0 otherwise. The list of elite institutions was adopted from Gomulya and Boeker (2014).

Respondents were asked on a 1 (not at all) to 5 (to a great extent) scale: 'To what extent did you observe the following activities of the group pursuing the initiative?' The items were based on descriptions in Bower (1970) and Burgelman (1991) as well as executive interviews, and the scale has a reported alpha of 0.89. For multiple-respondent cases, item means were calculated across the initiative supervisor, initiative leader, and one member, and items were summed to form the scale.

Respondents were asked on a 1 (not at all) to 5 (to a great extent) scale the extent to which they observed the listed activities of the group pursuing the initiative. Item content is based on discussions in Mintzberg (1983) and Pfeffer (1992) and wording suggested by the executive interviews, and the scale has a reported alpha of 0.81. Responses of multiple respondents were aggregated as item means and summed into a scale.

The scale was developed to assess the extent to which groups tried to gain informal support from other organizational actors; item content is based on Stevenson et al. (1985) and the executive interviews, and the reported alpha is 0.88. Respondents answered on a 1 (not at all) to 5 (to a great extent) scale how far they observed the listed activities of the group pursuing the initiative. Multiple-respondent data were aggregated as item means and summed.

Respondents were asked: 'When the initiative was launched, how compatible was the initiative in comparison to the following characteristics of the organization?' (1 = not at all compatible, 5 = very compatible). The 12 items were derived from Leonard-Barton's (1992) definition of capabilities, and principal component analysis resulted in a single factor that was reverse scored to measure degree of exploration (alpha = 0.91).

Respondents assessed the performance of the initiative using 11 items on a five-point scale (1 = not at all; 5 = to a large extent); the authors report an alpha of 0.87. Five of the items referred to meeting objectives with respect to time, cost, efficiency, and so forth, and respondents were also asked to assess performance in terms of achieving the initiative's overall purpose and intended outcome and from different managerial perspectives. Principal component analysis resulted in a single factor with 11 items.
time_window: last three months for the objectives items

description: Measured as the time to retirement for a CEO, as it captures the remaining career horizon of a CEO. It was calculated as 70 (retirement age and a few years of service on boards) minus the age of the CEO, so the younger the CEO the longer the career horizon. All continuous variables were standardized.
A binary dependent variable coded at 1 when an international acquisition took place during the year, 0 if otherwise. Data on international acquisitions were collected from SDC Platinum.

To emphasize the 'value at loss,' value of equity holdings is measured as the natural logarithm of the market value of shares owned by the CEO at year end, in line with Sanders (2001). Equity data were collected from the SEC filings and stock prices were collected from S&P's COMPUSTAT. Continuous variables were standardized.

To emphasize the 'value at loss,' value of stock options holdings is measured as the natural logarithm of the Black-Scholes value of vested and unvested in-the-money options held by the CEO. Data were collected from the SEC filings. Continuous variables were standardized.

The dependent variables are the log prices of the Big Mac, Quarter Pounder, Double Quarter Pounder, Chicken McNuggets 6 pc., and Filet-O-Fish meals. These meals were not part of the Dollar Menu and were all offered both in 1999 and in 2006, enabling comparison of their prices before the 2002 campaign with their prices after the campaign.

Dummy variable for the outlet's organizational form: whether the store is franchised or owned and operated by the franchisor. The regression coefficient on this variable corresponds to the difference between a meal's average price in franchised outlets and its average price in corporate outlets, conditional on the controls.

Dummy variable that indicates whether an observation was collected in 2006, after the Dollar Menu was introduced. The Dollar Menu advertising campaign was initiated nationwide in September 2002, and McDonald's added $20 million to its advertising budget in the last quarter of 2002.

The main proxy for repeat customers is the distance of an outlet from a highway; the dummy far from highway is coded 1 if an outlet is located more than 0.25 miles from a highway exit and 0 otherwise. The presence of a playground and whether wireless service is offered are used as additional proxies for an outlet's level of repeat customers, and a combined proxy is defined as the interaction of these three proxies.
scale: dummy (0/1) for far from highway; presence/absence for playground and wireless service

variable_name: close substitutes among Dollar Menu items
description: Meals were classified according to whether they exhibit high substitutability with the items advertised in the Dollar Menu campaign. Using monthly sales data from one McDonald's franchised outlet and an additional survey, the authors consider the Big Mac, Quarter Pounder, and Double Quarter Pounder meals as meals that have close substitutes among the items of the Dollar Menu, whereas the shares of the Chicken McNuggets 6 pc. and Filet-O-Fish meals remained fairly stable.

Ratio of firm-level advertising expenditures to total sales, averaged for 1991-96. The authors state that this expenditure flow measures the stock of accumulated advertising assets. It is one of two expenditure intensity terms used to measure the firm's intangible assets.

Ratio of firm-level research and development (R&D) expenditures to total sales, averaged for 1991-96. The authors state that this expenditure flow measures the stock of accumulated technological assets. It is the second of two expenditure intensity terms used to measure the firm's intangible assets.

Logarithmic transformation of the number of years of investment history the firm had in the host country, measured at the end of 1996 for surviving subsidiaries or at the time the subsidiary exited. Investment history was computed from the sample of 12,204 subsidiaries by summing, for each subsidiary the firm had formed, the difference between its founding date and the last date of observation; the sum was then logarithmically transformed.
time_window: through the end of 1996 (or the time of exit)

description: The firm's investment history with joint ventures when the focal entry was a joint venture, and its investment history with wholly owned subsidiaries when it made an independent entry; it has the same operational definition as the host country experience measure (summed years of investment history, logarithmically transformed). A joint venture was an entry in which a Japanese firm and a local firm each held at least 5 percent of the subsidiary's equity, and wholly owned subsidiaries had 95 percent or greater equity ownership by one firm.
time_window: through the end of 1996 (or the time of exit)

description: Whether the subsidiary continued to exist or exited. Subsidiaries listed in earlier editions (1986, 1989, 1992 and 1994) of the directory but not in the 1997 edition were treated as exits, and the definition of exit includes exits by divestiture and dissolution. The survival analysis covers 3,080 subsidiaries with 650 exits, separately for the wholly owned and joint venture samples.

Ratio of firm-level advertising expenditures to total sales, averaged for 1991-96. The authors state that this expenditure flow measures the stock of accumulated advertising assets. It is one of two expenditure intensity terms used to measure the firm's intangible assets.

Ratio of firm-level research and development (R&D) expenditures to total sales, averaged for 1991-96. The authors state that this expenditure flow measures the stock of accumulated technological assets. It is the second of two expenditure intensity terms used to measure the firm's intangible assets.

Logarithmic transformation of the number of years of investment history the firm had in the host country at the end of 1996. Investment history was computed from the sample of 12,204 subsidiaries by summing the difference between each subsidiary's founding date and the last date of observation, and the sum was then logarithmically transformed.

The firm's investment history with joint ventures when the focal entry was a joint venture, and with wholly owned subsidiaries when it made an independent entry; it shares the operational definition of the host country experience measure. A joint venture was an entry in which a Japanese firm and a local firm each held at least 5 percent of the equity; wholly owned subsidiaries had 95 percent or greater equity ownership by one firm.

The subsidiary's general manager or the equivalent classified the subsidiary's financial performance in 1996 into one of three categories: loss, breakeven, or gain, in response to a question in Toyo Keizai's survey. The authors describe this measure as based on a managerial assessment of profitability that has been demonstrated to have construct validity. The classification was an absolute assessment made without reference to other subsidiaries of the multinational, and the measure consisted of a single item.

Indicator of whether the subsidiary was a joint venture or a wholly owned subsidiary, used to split the sample into wholly owned and joint venture subsamples. A joint venture was an entry in which a Japanese firm and a local firm each held at least 5 percent of the subsidiary's equity, and wholly owned subsidiaries had 95 percent or greater equity ownership by one firm.

Network density is the average level of communication between any two members of team k. Tie strength is measured with communication or interaction frequency from the sociometric data, where the frequency at which team member i reports communicating with team member j takes values from 0 to 4. The reported ties are scaled by the largest of i's reported ties to anyone on the team, and density is the average over the members of the team. Density varies from zero (no communication between team members) to one (maximum strength communication between all team members). The formula for the measure is given in a formula block that could not be extracted.

Network heterogeneity measures the extent that scientists allocate a large proportion of their network time to colleagues far removed in the team's tenure distribution. It is calculated from two dyadic components: the proportion of scientist i's interaction that she allocates to colleague j on team k, and the degree of tenure similarity between scientist i and colleague j; the tenure-similarity component transforms tenure differences into similarity and normalizes each scientist's similarity to a colleague by the scientist's similarity to all team members. For the team, network heterogeneity is the mean of these individual-level scores. The formulas for the measure are given in formula blocks that could not be extracted.

Managers were asked to indicate how many of 11 written products and/or prototypes the team had produced over the last three years, choosing for each item among 0, 1, 2-5, or more than 5. The correlation matrix between the 11 items was factor analyzed using unweighted least squares; three factors were extracted and the first factor is treated as the summary-productivity measure. The resulting productivity variable is a factor score, computed as a weighted average of the 11 items with weights estimated from the observed correlations between the items.

A proxy for the SEW endowment that combines family control of firm equity and the board chairperson position. The variable is set to 0 if the chairperson of the board is not a family member; when the family occupies the board chairperson position, it takes values corresponding to the continuous share of equity held by the family, ranging from 50% (or 25% for listed firms) up to 100%.
scale: 0 or a continuous share of family equity between 50% (25% for listed firms) and 100%
time_window: at the time of the leadership succession

description: Measures firm performance before the succession event compared with other firms in the same industry, using averages computed over the pre-succession years. Competitors' performance is measured as the average performance of firms in a given industry and year. If the difference is negative, the absolute value of the difference in ROA is taken; otherwise the variable is set to 0.

A dummy equal to 1 if the incoming leader is the firstborn of the leaving leader and to 0 otherwise. The classification of successions is based on a manual reconstruction of the family nucleus related to each leaving leader at the time of the leadership transition, using the leaving leader's number of offspring, gender and age to reconstruct birth order. The authors report that 238 firms experience this type of succession.
time_window: at the time of the leadership succession

description: A dummy equal to 1 if the incoming leader is the second- or subsequent-born offspring of the leaving leader and to 0 otherwise; the authors report that 106 firms experience this type of succession. The remaining successions are appointments of a non-family leader (176 cases) and appointments of non-offspring family members (251 cases).
