time_window: at the time of the leadership succession

description: Return on assets, computed as the ratio between operating income and total assets, used as the dependent variable of the performance analysis. The performance analysis exploits the full longitudinal variation of the data, including pre- and post-succession years around each succession event.
time_window: 2000-2014, including pre- and post-succession years around each event

description: The performance model is estimated separately for firms with leaving founders and firms in which the leaving leader is not the founder. The distinction is based on the manually reconstructed family nucleus, which records whether the leaving leader was the company founder.
time_window: at the time of the leadership succession

description: We measured return on sales by dividing net profit by firm turnover. For most firms in the GC100, turnover was equivalent to firm sales; for banks the GIPC measured turnover by gross interest income plus commission and fees, and for insurance firms it was net premium earned plus investment income. The measure was calculated by averaging 2003 and 2004 to average out single year effects.
We measured return on equity by dividing net profit by firm equity. The measure was calculated by averaging 2003 and 2004 to average out single year effects.

Net profit was provided directly from the GC100 dataset. Because the distribution displayed considerable departure from normality, the natural log transformation was employed and the transformed variable, net profits nl, was used in the analysis. The measure was calculated by averaging 2003 and 2004.

The GIPC provided 2005 data on the amount of firm expenditure on CSR, and this measure was generated by dividing firm expenditure on CSR by the number of employees. Because the ratio displayed considerable departure from normality, the natural log transformation (CSR/employees nl) was used in the analysis.

The GIPC provided 2005 data on the amount of firm expenditure on CSR, and this measure was generated by dividing firm expenditure on CSR by firm equity. Because the ratio displayed considerable departure from normality, the natural log transformation (CSR/equity nl) was used in the analysis.

For the third measure we took the natural log of a firm's expenditures allocated toward CSR, permitting an assessment in relation to absolute CSR spending as well. The GIPC provided 2005 data on the amount of firm expenditure on CSR.

Indicator variable equal to one if the implied contract exception has been adopted in the state of the firm's headquarters by year t. The effects of the law are expected to arise with lags of one to three years, and the baseline specification uses the three-year lag ICt-3. The state of headquarters is used as governing the firm's overall labor contracts.
time_window: lagged one to three years; three-year lag in the baseline

description: Binary variable equal to one if a firm's performance (ROA) is lower than the industry benchmark, where the benchmark is defined as the median ROA at the four-digit SIC level for each fiscal year. In an additional analysis the binary measure is revised into linear splines of firm performance relative to the industry benchmark with knots at the 25th and 75th percentiles, forming four quartile variables.

Log of the number of patent applications filed by the firm in a firm-application year, used to proxy for the quantity of innovation. Patent records come from the latest NBER patent database matched to Compustat firms.

Number of citations received by the firm's patents, used to proxy for the quality of innovation; the author weights the citations received with a truncation index by Hall et al. (2001). In the analysis of the quality distribution, patents are divided into top and bottom halves based on the number of citations received for each patent class and year.
level: firm-year (log) and patent within class-year for the split

description: Market value of a firm's patents, taken from Kogan et al. (2017), who measure a patent's market value based on three-day abnormal returns in response to news of its grant by the USPTO. It is used as an alternative dependent variable, and the improved match between Compustat and USPTO application files yields a larger sample.

Measure of patent novelty obtained from Eggers and Kaul (2018): a patent is assessed to contain novel technology if it combines technology classes that have not been frequently combined before by other patents in the same USPTO three-digit technology class in the past five years. Models 1 and 2 examine the number of firm-year patents (log) falling in the top 50% and bottom 50% of the novelty score.
scale: novelty score split at the 50th percentile
time_window: five-year look-back in the novelty score

description: Count of distinct three-digit patent classes (nclass) in which a firm files for patents each year, used as a proxy for the level of resource adjustment and experimentation based on the breadth of technological search rather than its direction.

An inventor who produces his or her first patent at a given firm after producing at least one patent at a different firm prior to that. The count is aggregated at the firm-year level over a three-year window (t+0, t+1, t+2) and entered in log form; the three-year window is used because the precise years of inventor movements are revealed only when inventors file for patents.

An inventor who files for a patent at a different firm, counted at the firm-year level over a three-year window (t+0, t+1, t+2) and logged. The measure contains both involuntary and voluntary turnover, so it captures the share of turnover related to low performance.

Firm R&D intensity used as a direct proxy for the amount of effort at innovation. The specification directly follows Chen and Miller (2007), including a shorter lag of one year because R&D spending, as an input to the innovation process, can be adjusted more immediately than patents; the formula is not given in the prose.

Indicator of whether a firm changes its position between leader and laggard from one year to the next, estimated with a conditional fixed effects logit model. The authors separate all transitions, upward reversion (laggard to leader) and downward reversion (leader to laggard).
time_window: year-to-year transitions, treatment lagged three years

description: Each four-digit SIC code is assigned as a high- or low-velocity sector based on the mean speed at which patents accumulate citations, calculated as the share of citations accumulated by a patent within the first three years of its grant. The measure closely resembles the notion of a half-life and intends to capture the speed at which new technology is adopted; for example, patents in the pharmaceutical industry accumulate the majority of their citations within the first three years of grant, whereas patents in petroleum and natural gas continue to accumulate citations after six years.

A continuous variable that equals the average fraction of negative words used across all tweets posted by a given CEO in a day. Negative words are taken from the list compiled by Loughran and McDonald (2011). The observations are on the firm-day level. A lack of negative words indicates that the CEO is confident, so the lower the value, the more confident the CEO is deemed to be.

A continuous variable that equals the fraction of negative words used by a given CEO during the conference call discussing quarterly earnings. Transcripts are drawn from a stratified random subsample of all S&P 1500 firms based on industry with a sampling fraction of 10 percent. The observations are on the firm-month level. The lower the value, the more confident the CEO is deemed to be.

A continuous variable that equals the difference between forecasted quarterly earnings-per-share (EPS) and actual quarterly EPS, scaled by lagged price-per-share. Management earnings forecast data come from the FirstCall database for the S&P 1500 firms that provide earnings guidance. The observations are on the firm-month level. Higher values indicate forecasts that are further above actual earnings.

Following Dezso and Ross (2012), the variable is the natural log transformation of the ratio of a given CEO's vested in-the-money option value to the CEO's total compensation value, computed by fiscal year. The value of total compensation uses Execucomp's TDC1 field. The observations are on the firm-year level. A CEO who delays the exercise of his or her exercisable in-the-money options is deemed overly optimistic about the firm's prospects.

Equals one for founder CEOs and zero for professional CEOs. Founder status is determined from public information: the company's official website and SEC filings, a Google search using the company name plus the word founder, and the CEO's profile page on Bloomberg Businessweek, Forbes, and Wikipedia, with company profile pages used to double-check the information.

Degree to which the CEO agrees that the EU enlargement is positive for the company, measured with two items adopted from the work of Thomas and McDaniel (1990) on seven-point Likert response scales. The interitem reliability (Cronbach's alpha) was 0.91. Collected in the first survey wave.

Degree to which the CEO agrees that the EU enlargement is negative for the company, measured with two items adopted from the work of Thomas and McDaniel (1990) on seven-point Likert response scales. The interitem reliability (Cronbach's alpha) was 0.80. Collected in the first survey wave.

The similarity component of the similarity-intensity model, computed as minus the absolute difference between the dominant evaluation (D) and the competing evaluation (C), that is -|D - C|, using the unstandardized positive and negative evaluation scales. It captures the degree to which opposing evaluations of the issue are similar in magnitude; it is one of the two component measures the authors use instead of the combined similarity-intensity measure.

The intensity component of the similarity-intensity model, computed as the mean of the dominant evaluation (D) and the competing evaluation (C), that is (D + C)/2, using the unstandardized positive and negative evaluation scales. It takes into account how strong the combined evaluations are on both dimensions and taps the emotional sense of 'torn-ness' and unusualness.

In the second survey instrument the executives were asked whether their firms took any actions specifically in response to the EU enlargement, and a categorical variable was created where any action was coded as 1 and no action was coded as 0.

Single item asking respondents to describe the action that the company specifically initiated in response to the EU enlargement; the scope of the action was assessed with one item ranging from 1, very small, to 7, very large. In the tobit models the variable was treated as left-censored at zero for firms that took no action.

Single item asking respondents to describe the action that the company specifically initiated in response to the EU enlargement; the perceived riskiness of the action was assessed with one item ranging from 1, very small, to 7, very high. The variable was treated as left-censored at zero for firms that took no action.

Single item asking respondents to describe the action that the company specifically initiated in response to the EU enlargement; the novelty of the action for the firm was assessed with one item ranging from 1, continued existing activities, to 7, completely new. The variable was treated as left-censored at zero for firms that took no action.

Binary variable generated by searching three publication outlets for any mention of DJSI membership using the terms Dow Jones, DJSI, index, and sustainability. The outlets are annual reports filed with the SEC, corporate social responsibility or sustainability reports, and corporate press releases specifically designed to communicate the firm's inclusion in the DJSI; sustainability reports were also visually scanned for the DJSI logo. Coded as 1 for every year that a firm publicized its membership in the DJSI and 0 otherwise, yielding 883 instances of publicizing over the panel.

Dichotomous variable coded as 1 for any firm that had been targeted by at least one environmental shareholder resolution in the prior two years, and 0 otherwise. A dummy rather than a count was used because shareholder action targeting a specific firm is a relatively rare event.

The total count of newspaper articles mentioning an environmental protest, boycott, or lawsuit in the previous two years. Articles were obtained from LexisNexis with a search string requiring an environmental group, organization, activist, or environmentalist within the same paragraph as protest, boycott, demonstration, or lawsuit and the company name, and were manually screened to eliminate false positives. The value was top-coded at the 99th percentile of the distribution (a count of 14 articles).
Dichotomous variable that equals 1 if the firm had been the target of a shareholder resolution in the past two years outside an environmental domain, and 0 otherwise.
The number of newspaper articles that mentioned a nonenvironmental protest, demonstration, boycott, or lawsuit involving the firm, top-coded at the 99th percentile (34 articles).

Created by summing the number of environmental strengths in every firm-year from the MSCI ESG STATS (KLD) social ratings data. The environmental strengths are dichotomous variables that evaluate the processes and efforts that firms employ to improve their environmental performance; assessments are performed annually and are primarily based on publicly available information reported by the media.

A proxy for DJSI legitimacy computed as the cumulative number of media articles (per 1,000) that mentioned the DJSI, obtained from Factiva using the search terms Dow Jones Sustainability, DJSGI, and DJSI. The count rests on the assumption that media coverage reflects the accumulated discourse and cognitive legitimacy of a practice.

A cumulative count of a bank's information technology events, drawn from the Predicast Index. In the coding, a bank was assigned one point for each of the categories whenever it generated an event reported in the Predicast Index, and the score is the cumulative number of events for each category recorded since 1977, the starting year of observation. The final score for each bank is the cumulative number of events up to the point of adoption. The category covers all types of hardware, software or telecommunications events.
time_window: 1977 up to the point of adoption; right censored in 1988

description: A cumulative count of a bank's interfirm arrangements, drawn from the Predicast Index. Arrangements include joint ventures, licensing or contracting the rights to use, produce or market products, systems or services without transferring ownership rights, marketing agreements, R&D agreements and supply agreements. All interorganizational linkages up to the year of adoption or the year of right censoring (1988) yielded a networking score, which can be decomposed into specific types of linkages. An occurrence of technical projects employing interfirm arrangements was coded as both a technological experience and an interorganizational linkage.
time_window: 1977 up to the year of adoption or right censoring (1988)

description: The firm's investment expenditure in systems and equipment, measured as the percentage of capital spending in equipment to assets. This financially derived measure of capital investment approximates what the authors call 'learning by using,' and is assumed to foster strategic readiness to innovate in certain technological directions.

variable_name: Productivity index of systems and equipment
description: A productivity efficiency index measured as the ratio of interest revenue to non-interest expenses, consisting of equipment and personnel expenses. The authors note that the index is also sensitive to other factors, particularly those residing in the environment, but is often used in the banking community to gauge the productivity of equipment outlays. Like the investment measure, it approximates 'learning by using.'

variable_name: Adoption of video banking (entering video banking)
description: The dependent variable is the adoption event, a dichotomous variable. The firms received a score of 1 if they adopted video banking during the period 1981-87, and 0 otherwise. The very first adoption took place in 1981, rendering the data set left censored at this year, and the data are right censored up to the point of the study, 1988. The list of adoptions was compiled by checking several publications against one another.

Developed from after-tax earnings (including extraordinary items) on end-year book value of total assets of the firm for the years 1968-1977, with an arbitrary one year acquisition performance effects lag. The net income summed for all years was taken as a percentage of the total assets summed for all years, using Moody's Industrial Manual as the data source, to provide a weighted average measure.

Individual year market returns were computed for each acquiring firm, again allowing for a one year performance effects lag, using the arithmetic mean of high and low market price per share of stock in a calendar year obtained from Value Line, the same for the prior year, and the dividend per share in the year. The market return performance of a firm over the entire 1968-1977 period was obtained by taking the geometric mean of the individual year returns. The printed formula for the annual return is not readable in the extracted text.

The acquiree asset weighted mean as a percentage of the acquirer's assets at the end of the year prior to acquisition. Percentage measures are with respect to the total of those acquisitions for which the particular element of data is available. The measure is biased towards higher values because of the tendency of firms to report larger acquisitions more consistently and thoroughly.
time_window: year end prior to each acquisition

description: The mean number of acquisitions per year over the study period; the firms in the analysis group were highly active acquirers.
The mean number of acquisitions per year divided by 1976 assets. This acquirer size adjusted measure tends to place all firms on the same size basis for analysis purposes.

The percentage ratio of assets acquired in the study time period (1967-1976) to end-period (1976) assets. This proportion understates the true proportion of 1976 assets acquired in the study period because of under-reporting of the assets involved in smaller acquisitions.

The percentage of acquired assets which were of the same SIC code as the acquirer, analysed at the two-digit level. SICs of acquiring companies were those developed from a consensus of sources as applicable to the firm at the beginning of the period and were held constant throughout the period. It was infeasible to use a weighted average SIC measure for the acquirees.

The ratio of the Standard and Poor 500 average value for the third month prior to the effective date of acquisitions to the Standard and Poor trend value for that month; the trend line was regressed from monthly averages of this index from January 1950 through December 1977. For cash acquisitions, a mirror image value was obtained by subtracting the timing measure as computed above from a value of 2.0.
time_window: third month prior to each acquisition's effective date; S&P trend line January 1950-December 1977

description: The percentage of asset acquisitions in dollars accomplished for cash. The bulk of acquisitions by the analysis group during this period used securities in payment.

The acquiree net income after taxes as a percentage of the assets of the acquiree in the year prior to acquisition. The range of acquiree profitability is large and includes some acquirees which were operating at a loss, representing two different acquirer strategies, i.e. acquire current earnings vs acquire future earnings (turnaround strategy).

The acquiree net income after taxes in the year prior to acquisition as a percentage of the price paid; this reciprocal of the price paid to income stream was the primary measure for this factor. Since the valuation and value of acquiree assets have been shown to be primarily determined by common stock market price, an alternative measure, price paid as a percentage of the book value of acquiree assets, was also used to test this basis for valuation.

An alternative measure described for the price paid factor: price paid as a percentage of the book value of acquiree assets, used also to test the basis for valuation. It does not distinguish differential price effects on acquirer performance but reflects that acquirees with higher earnings command a better price.

Return on asset is equal to net income before extraordinary items divided by total assets for a given fiscal year. The authors made an industry adjustment by subtracting from a focal firm's ROA the industry median ROA of the firms in Compustat in a given three-digit SIC code and year.
The level of downsizing was measured as the percentage change in the number of employees from year t-2 to t-1. Lower values on the percentage measure indicate that CEOs are more active in downsizing.
time_window: change from year t-2 to t-1

description: The level of refocusing was measured as the numerical change in the entropy index of diversification from year t-2 to t-1 (Palepu, 1985). Lower values on the change in diversification entropy indicate that CEOs are more active in refocusing. The entropy index was computed for each firm using sales data at the 4-digit SIC code levels in the Compustat Business Segment file.
time_window: change from year t-2 to t-1

description: Following Flammer (2015), the authors used the total number of CSR strengths in the following dimensions: community relations, diversity issues, environmental issues, employee relations, and human rights. CSR strengths were distinguished from concerns because CSR and CSiR (corporate social irresponsibility) are theoretically distinct constructs.

Takes 1 if CEOs were forcibly discharged from the firm. Following Shen and Cannella's (2002) procedures, 636 CEO successions were evaluated using newspaper articles, and CEO age and continuity in board membership at the time of succession were examined; dismissals were identified when CEOs were reported to depart as both CEO and board member before the age of 64 for reasons other than death, illness, acceptance of comparable positions at other organizations, or merger and acquisition. The authors identified 212 dismissals occurring at 126 unique firms.

The distance in meters between two senators' desks in the U.S. Senate Chamber in a given Congress. Chamber seat locations were estimated using scale drawings of the Senate Chamber and each senator's desk location was transposed into Cartesian space; these coordinates were then used to construct the distance between two senators' desks. This measure is the key independent variable.

The total number of bills that two senators co-sponsor in a given Congress t, counted for each of the senator dyads in the sample to create a senator-by-senator one-mode adjacency matrix. The measure uses nondirected ties and does not discriminate between initial and subsequent sponsors. Directed author-to-co-sponsor ties were also considered but did not substantively change the results.

Indicator variables for dyads containing zero, one or two senators in the top 50th percentile of the tenure distribution, where tenure is the total number of Congresses a senator has served to date; dyads with no high-tenure senator serve as the reference group. Each indicator is interacted with Chamber distance.

Indicator variables for dyads containing zero, one or two senators holding a committee leadership position, that is, the chairman or the ranking minority member of a Senate standing committee, in a given Congress; dyads with no committee leader serve as the reference group. Each indicator is interacted with Chamber distance.

variable_name: i and/or j in election cycle (indicator)
description: Indicator variable equal to 1 if either senator i, senator j, or both, are in an election cycle, and equal to 0 otherwise. The model includes this indicator together with an interaction between the election cycle indicator and Chamber distance.

The weight given to the previous aspiration level relative to realized performance when the historical aspiration level is updated; a higher value means that the previous aspiration level receives more weight and that updating is slower. The parameter is estimated directly by maximum likelihood from the probability of a format change, which is specified as a sum of an intercept and the effects of a multiunit indicator and a high-density indicator. In the model that assumes equal updating in all stations it is estimated to 0.659, with a standard error of 0.083.
scale: theoretically between zero and unity, but not constrained in estimation

description: A dummy variable, indicating a high-density market, entered in the expression for the aspiration-level updating parameter. Density is the number of stations in the market; two different thresholds define low and high density in Models 4 and 5.

A dummy variable, indicating whether the station belongs to a corporation viewed as a branch system, entered in the expression for the aspiration-level updating parameter. Model 2 views all corporations with three or more stations as branch systems, while Model 3 uses a higher limit of five or more stations.

The unobserved aspiration level for the station's audience market share, computed from the performance history as a weighted average of the previous aspiration level and realized performance, with the updating parameter giving the weight on the previous aspiration level. Market share data were coded since 1975, or the first year a market entered the source data, so that enough years of performance precede the behavioral measurement to initialize the historical aspiration level.
time_window: market share history from 1975 or market entry

description: Dummy variable equal to one for the 105 start-ups randomly assigned to the design-based experimentation training arm of the RCT and zero otherwise. It is the treatment indicator entered in the cross-sectional regressions.

Dummy variable equal to one for the 102 start-ups randomly assigned to the theory-based experimentation training arm of the RCT and zero otherwise. It is the treatment indicator entered in the cross-sectional regressions.

Entrepreneurs were directly asked to estimate, on a scale from zero to one, how much information they had gathered about their customers, sector, resources and competitors. The total amount of information collected is the average of these four components, so the variable assumes that entrepreneurs search within a bounded space in which acquiring all available information corresponds to the upper bound of one; the cumulative version averages the values over the rounds of data collection for each start-up.
time_window: across the data collection window (November 2020 to February 2022)

description: Calculated as the product of the amount of information gathered and its direction, both reported by the entrepreneur on a scale from zero to one. Zero represents negative information and one represents positive information; for example, information of 0.7 with a direction of 0.8 gives favorable information of 0.56. The cumulative version averages the values over the rounds of data collection for each start-up.
time_window: across the data collection window (November 2020 to February 2022)

description: The entrepreneur's estimated probability of success of the business idea, reported on a scale from zero to one in each round of data collection. The same variable provides the lower threshold (the belief p at the moment of termination, if any) and the upper threshold (the belief at the moment of commitment).
time_window: each round of data collection (November 2020 to February 2022)

description: Dummy variable equal to one if entrepreneurs declared to abandon their project and zero otherwise. In the cross-sectional analysis the dependent variable is averaged over the data points collected for each start-up.
time_window: within the data collection window (November 2020 to February 2022)

description: Dummy variable equal to one if four conditions are jointly satisfied for the two last rounds of data collection in a row; otherwise it is equal to zero. The four conditions are: the start-up does not terminate during the observation window; the hours spent weekly working at the start-up are above the average of hours spent by start-ups that terminated; the self-assessed probability to terminate is below the average in case of termination; and the self-assessed probability to change the idea (pivot) is below the average in case of termination. The measure is threshold-based because asking entrepreneurs whether they committed is not reliable, as they are tempted to signal willingness to commit.
time_window: two last rounds of data collection in a row

description: Cumulative revenue in euros accumulated by the start-up within the observation window, measured at the latest data point collected for each start-up. The distribution is right-skewed, with most start-ups reporting no revenue.

Dummy variable equal to one if the entrepreneur reported that the business idea is based on a patent and zero otherwise. It is interacted with the DbE intervention to compare the two treated groups for innovative ideas.

Takes a value of 1 if the announcement pertains to an investment within the decentralized model and 0 if it pertains to an investment within the centralized model. Announcements were narrowed by keywords and then manually coded by two trained raters to identify investments in each model. The authors note that ideally they would have also liked to know about the scale of the investment, but such information was generally not mentioned in the announcements.

The cumulative abnormal return of the firm's stock for a five-day [-2,2] window centered on the focal announcement, used to assess the impact of the investment announcement on the firm's valuation. Abnormal returns are measured using EVENTUS software with CRSP data and the CRSP-weighted market index as the proxy for market return. Market model parameters are estimated by OLS over a 255-day period starting 46 days prior to the announcement.
time_window: five-day [-2,2] window centered on the announcement

description: Calculated using the incumbent utility's total generation capacity in megawatts (MW) in a given year, developed from Form EIA-860 data. The variable is log transformed to account for skewness in the data. As a robustness check the authors use an alternative measure based on the number of electricity generators reported in Form EIA-860.

The proportion of the utility's sales in non-Retail Choice states. Some states are categorized as 'Retail Choice' because state-level regulation mandates that consumers should have a choice of electricity providers, while in non-Retail Choice states utilities operate as monopolies. The more sales in non-Retail Choice states, the higher the value of the variable, implying that the electric utility is subject to lower competitive pressures. For example, if Utility X sells 40% of its electricity in non-Retail Choice states, Nocompetition = 0.4.

Takes the value of 0 if the investment is conducted by the incumbent utility alone or 1 if it is conducted jointly with an external partner. This categorization is based on the coding of the announcement text. In the sample, 89% of alliances in the new decentralized model are with firms from outside the electric utility industry, in contrast to 51% of alliances in the centralized model.

Coded as '1' if the patent in year t is jointly cited, in the 5 years from (including) t, with at least one other of the firm's patents from another class in year t, and '0' otherwise. Only patents from different classes count, and the measure drops instances where the patent in another class that is jointly cited with the focal patent is itself disclosed.

Equals '1' if the patent was ever disclosed to an SSO and '0' otherwise. The dependent variable is restricted to disclosures with traceable patents, and to patents applied no later than 2004 to minimize right truncation.

For each technology class in which the firm files for patents in the year, the number of other firms that also file for patents in the class is counted; the measure is the average of these counts across all classes in which the firm files for patents in the year. At the patent level, the technology class of the focal patent is excluded from the calculation.

For each SSO-year, the (nonfocal) firm with the maximum number of disclosures over the prior 5 years is identified, using the 2013 SSO membership list supplemented with firms that disclosed to the SSO during the year; this experience-based measure proxies the firm's ability to expropriate. An SSO is deemed relevant to the focal patent if the focal patent is in one of the technology categories assigned to patents disclosed to that SSO in the year, and the patent-level measure averages the experience measure across all SSOs to which the focal patent is matched.
time_window: prior 5 years for the experience measure

description: For each year t, the firm counts the instances where a pair of its patents filed in the year across different classes were cited jointly (by any patent) in the subsequent 5 years (including t). Multiple citations received by a pair are treated as one instance, and the count is divided by the total number of potential pairs of the firm's complementary technologies as defined by these criteria. The measure is reported in percentages.
time_window: 5 years from (including) t; variables lagged 5 years relative to disclosure

description: Equals '1' if the firm makes at least one disclosure in the year and '0' otherwise. At the firm level, the restrictions of keeping only disclosures with traceable patents or patents before 2004 are not imposed, so as to include 'blanket' disclosures.

For each technology class in which the firm files for patents in the year, the number of other firms that also file for patents in the class is counted, and the average is taken across all classes in which the firm files for patents in the year. In the firm-level analyses all classes that the firm patents in the year are included, since the dependent variable also captures blanket disclosures for which the focal technology class cannot be determined.
time_window: variables lagged 5 years relative to disclosure

description: For each SSO-year, the (nonfocal) firm with the maximum number of disclosures over the prior 5 years is identified as the expropriation-risk proxy. An SSO is deemed relevant to the focal firm if the firm files for at least one patent in the technology classes associated with disclosures to that SSO in the year, and the firm-year measure averages the experience measure across all SSOs to which the focal firm is matched.
time_window: prior 5 years for the experience measure; variables lagged 5 years relative to disclosure

description: A dummy variable that takes the value of 1 for all years after Craigslist has entered the county in which the concert venue is located. Craigslist is a platform for ticket resale, and therefore its entry into a county can indicate that the secondary market for tickets in the county has thickened. These data were hand-collected from www.craigslist.org and have been used in studies of Craigslist's impact in other settings.

Mean price is total revenues divided by the total number of tickets sold for the show. The authors use ticket prices in the primary market to measure whether firms benefit from or are hurt by the entry of Craigslist, because under certain conditions prices can be thought of as representing the value split between the seller and the customer on a given transaction.

The number of revisions to an artist's Wikipedia page in a given year, used as a measure of her relative popularity in that year. Artists without a Wikipedia page are registered as zero revisions. Because the empirical analysis controls for artist-level fixed effects, the measure captures variation in popularity for a given artist over time, not across artists.

The average capacity arranged by a promoter in a geographic area in a given year, where the average is taken across all concerts arranged by that promoter in that geographic area for that year. It is regressed on the indicator for whether the show occurred after Craigslist's entry into the focal market with promoter, two-digit ZIP code, and year fixed effects.

An indicator variable equal to 1 if the show capacity is equal to tickets sold. The authors estimate a logistic regression of sellout on a quadratic for show capacity, a quadratic for Wikipedia revisions, an indicator for whether the show took place during the summer months, and year, two-digit ZIP, and artist fixed effects. The predicted probability of selling out is then collapsed into buckets of 10 percentage points to proxy for the price setters' ex ante expectation that the show is likely to sell out.

The difference between the reputation of the Focal seller and the reputation of the Competitor, standardized by the combined reputation stock of the two competing sellers. Reputation of each seller is measured as the difference between the number of positive and negative ratings. Because the functional form of the relationship is not specified, the authors estimate the second-order approximation of the Taylor series expansion of the standardized gap function, so a squared term of the reputation gap is included as well.

The final auction price obtained by the Focal seller minus the final auction price obtained by its matched Competitor. The authors note that in a second-price English auction the purchase price equals the customer's willingness to pay, so this difference corresponds to the value added by the Focal seller. It is computed per matched pair of transactions.

The difference between the number of positive and negative ratings of the Focal seller, which the authors choose as the most easily accessible indicator of a buyer's reputation. It measures the absolute reputation stock of the focal selling party in the matched pair.

The difference between the number of positive and negative ratings of the Competitor, using the same rating-difference measure applied to the matched competitor in the pair. It measures the absolute reputation stock of the competing selling party.

Kogut and Singh's (1988) established cultural distance index, based on Hofstede's four original cultural values dimensions, following the approach used in the literature. The authors note that I_ij stands for the index for the i-th cultural dimension and j-th country, V_i is the variance of the index of the i-th dimension, u indicates Japan, and CD_j is the cultural difference of the j-th country from Japan. The formula block was unreadable in the source text, so the exact specification is a gap.

The tightness - looseness measure from Gelfand et al. (2011), which provides country scores for 33 countries based on survey data from 6,823 respondents from various occupations. The survey was built on a six-item Likert scale. Out of the 33 countries in the original list, the authors used tightness - looseness scores for 28 countries.
Calculated by dividing the total number of expatriates by the total number of employees in a subsidiary, following prior studies.

variable_name: Prac. leaders, same J.D., same time (dummy) mi-nj-t
description: A dummy that takes the value of one if at least one practice leader in practice area mit attended the same law school at the same time as at least one practice leader in practice area njt. Attending at the same time is coded as graduating from the same law school within two years of each other, because law school requires three years. It is the authors' proxy for the presence of an educational affiliation tie, and the same approach was used by Rider (2014).
level: practice area m × practice area n × year

variable_name: Prac. leaders, same J.D. diff time (dummy) mi-nj-t
description: A second dummy equivalent to Prac. leaders, same J.D., same time (dummy) except that it tracks whether practice area leaders attended the same law school but their time of attendance did not overlap. The authors argue that individuals who attended the same law school at different times should have weaker affiliation ties than those who attended at the same time.
level: practice area m × practice area n × year

description: The number of attorneys hired by practice area m of firm i from rival practice area n of firm j in year t; this is the dependent variable of the main regression. In later tests the authors split it into the number of senior attorneys (partner and of counsel positions) hired and the number of junior attorneys (associates) hired. In the logit models the variable was converted to a zero/one dummy indicating whether hiring occurred.
level: practice area m × practice area n × year

description: Gross flow of funds invested in fixed assets by a given firm in a given period divided by the beginning-of-period stock of fixed assets (property, plant, and equipment). Investment excludes company acquisitions, and the capital stock is the stock of fixed assets with an expected useful life over one year as of the beginning of the fiscal year. All data are in local currency, and normalizing investment by the capital stock reduces heteroscedasticity.
time_window: investment flow during the fiscal year, divided by beginning-of-period capital stock

description: An adjusted beginning-of-period value calculated as the sum of the market value of common equity, the book value of preferred stock, the book value of debt, and deferred taxes, divided by the book value of total assets minus intangible assets. Theoretically it is the market value of the firm divided by its replacement cost. For U.S. firms the market value of equity is taken from Compustat; all other data items are from Worldscope, and for German firms pension liabilities are subtracted from reported total assets.

The internal cash flow of the firm, defined as funds from operations during the fiscal year, normalized by the beginning-of-period capital stock. Where a funds flow statement was not given, cash flow was estimated by Worldscope from net profit before preferred dividends plus or minus all noncash charges and credits.
time_window: fiscal year, normalized by beginning-of-period capital stock

description: Firms in the sample are grouped by their home nation. German and Japanese firms are characterized as coalitional firms, where investment is the outcome of a cooperative bargaining process among a broad array of constituencies, and U.S. firms as shareholder firms, where investment is made primarily to maximize shareholder wealth. Separate regressions are estimated for each national group and the groups' coefficients are compared.

variable_name: Level of internal global environmental performance standards
description: Scale of two survey items rated on a seven-point Likert scale, developed through factor analysis of seven survey items covering the three standardization dimensions. One item asks whether the business unit's internal standards are tougher than those of competitors with similar standards, the other whether internal standards are set at the level of environmental regulations in the country with the toughest regulations in which the company operates. The authors report the scale's reliability in the appendix and assessed convergent validity against toxic releases per dollar of sales in the United States from the TRI database.

Scale of three survey items rated on a seven-point Likert scale, developed through factor analysis. Respondents are asked to what extent listed elements of their business unit's environmental strategies are standardized at a global (worldwide) level. The authors report the scale's reliability in the appendix and assessed convergent validity against publicly stated company policies.

Scale of two survey items rated on a seven-point Likert scale, developed through factor analysis. Respondents are asked to what extent listed elements of their business unit's environmental strategies are standardized at a global (worldwide) level. The authors report the scale's reliability in the appendix and state that convergent validity could not be assessed because indicators for the extent of standardization of environmental communication were not available from other sources.

Scale developed through factor analysis of ten survey items covering government, customer, and industry pressures and pressures for local adaptation. Three items, rated on a seven-point Likert scale, ask about the respondent's expectations that environmental regulations will be more similar across countries in ten years and that global and regional environmental standards will gain in importance for the industry.

Scale developed through factor analysis of ten survey items covering government, customer, and industry pressures and pressures for local adaptation. A single survey item, rated on a seven-point Likert scale, asks whether the environmental strategies the business unit implements in one country considerably affect its environmental reputation with customers in other countries.

Scale developed through factor analysis of ten survey items covering government, customer, and industry pressures and pressures for local adaptation. Three items, rated on a seven-point Likert scale, ask whether industry initiatives and associations advocate worldwide environmental standards, whether major competitors set worldwide environmental standards for their operations and products, and whether major competitors implement environmental strategies on a worldwide basis.

variable_name: Global standardization of other functional strategies
description: Scale of three survey items rated on a seven-point Likert scale, developed through factor analysis of seven survey items covering functional strategy standardization and subsidiary dependence. Respondents are asked to what extent listed elements of their business unit's competitive strategy are standardized at a global level.

Scale of survey items rated on a seven-point Likert scale, developed through factor analysis of seven survey items covering functional strategy standardization and subsidiary dependence. Items relating to the centralization of value chain activities were used as indicators because in MNCs with high levels of centralization, subsidiaries are likely to depend on other parts of the MNC for resources; respondents indicate where each activity is performed in relation to the geographic markets in which the products are sold, from the local level to the global level.

Dependent variable coded as 1 if a firm i acquired target j, and 0 otherwise. Each panel consists of an actual deal matched to counterfactual targets that were similar on total patents, patenting classes, disease areas, and medical technologies.

Proportional change in the acquirer's Burt (1992) constraint measure if the acquirer's node and the potential target's node were collapsed into one and the acquirer inherited the target's ties: [(post-acquisition measure - pre-acquisition measure)/pre-acquisition measure]. The network was reset and the measure recalculated for each potential target in the choice set. Declining constraint indicates an increase in access to structural holes.
time_window: year prior to the acquisition versus the reconstructed post-acquisition network

description: Proportional change in the acquirer's Bonacich (1987) eigenvector centrality if the acquirer's node and the potential target's node were collapsed into one and the acquirer inherited the target's ties: [(post-acquisition measure - pre-acquisition measure)/pre-acquisition measure]. The network was reset and the measure recalculated for each potential target in the choice set. Increasing eigenvector centrality indicates an improvement in network status.
time_window: year prior to the acquisition versus the reconstructed post-acquisition network

description: The number of common partners between the acquirer and target pre-acquisition, measured from their alliance ties. It serves as a contingency variable and control because overlapping networks can affect tie formation and stability.

variable_name: target has a tie to a university but the acquirer does not
description: An indicator of whether the target has a tie to a university but the acquirer does not. In that case, the target's ties complement the acquirer's by providing novel university access. Alliances with universities are used because they focus on basic science, are harder to establish, and are more enduring than ties to for-profit partners.

Three indicators of the acquirer's technological diversification, categorizing firms by whether the number of disease areas or patenting classes in which they are actively involved, or both, are above (= 1) or below (= 0) the sample median.

For each of the 11 processes considered in the study an efficiency score is determined with an extension of Data Envelopment Analysis, each bank's distance from the frontier serving as its efficiency score, and banks are ranked according to their efficiency score for each process, yielding individual process performance ranks. These individual process analyses are then aggregated, using tournament ranking techniques that accommodate missing data, into an institutional aggregate process efficiency rank for each bank. Lower values of the rank indicate better aggregate process performance.

The standard deviation of each bank's set of up to 11 individual process performance ranks. The measure thus captures variation across the processes a bank performs, not variation across banks. Higher values indicate less consistent performance across the bundle of processes.

Return On Assets is used as the measure of financial performance because it captures the efficiency of management's use of a firm's assets, independent of the firm's capital structure and size. The authors contrast it with Return On Equity, which they say evaluates both operational performance and capital structure. The text does not give the computational formula for ROA.

A dummy variable set to a value of 0 in the pre-IPO years, when firm i was still private, and taking on a value of 1 in the year of and years subsequent to IPO. It remained equal to 0 throughout the observation period for firms that did not experience an IPO. Firms went public at different times, so exposure to treatment was staggered across time and firms served as their own comparison group.

The number of patents filed by each firm in the sample during each year in the observation period. Patent data from the USPTO and Delphion were combined into a data set of utility patents granted in the United States from January 1, 1975 through December 31, 2008 and aggregated to the firm level so that each firm had a corresponding patent portfolio. Because the dependent variable is a count, Poisson quasi-maximum likelihood regression was used.

variable_name: number of FDA medical device approvals filed (product count)
description: The number of FDA medical device approvals filed by each firm in a given year. Firms can bring a device to market through two approval routes, premarket notification (510(k)) and premarket approval (PMA) applications, and the measure aggregates both types of device approval applications. PMAs represent the more stringent type of device marketing application, whereas 510(k)s reflect incremental innovations.

Conditional on firm i having filed at least one patent in time t, the quality or impact of a firm's patent output at time t is the average number of citations received by those patents within five years of the grant date. It is computed as the number of citations received within five years of grant date on patents applied for by firm i in time t divided by the total number of patents filed by firm i in time t. Poisson QML estimation was used because the variable is positive and continuous.
time_window: citations within five years of the grant date; annual, 1980-2008

description: Conditional on firm i having filed at least one patent in time t, the proportion of the firm's innovation search that explored new or unfamiliar knowledge at time t is the number of new citations made by firm i in time t divided by Total cites it, the total number of citations made by firm i's patents in time t. New or unfamiliar citations are citations to patents that have not been previously cited by the firm, i.e., neither self- nor repeat citations; these indicate building on unfamiliar knowledge rather than on the firm's own existing or familiar knowledge. This measure defines exploratory search from the firm's perspective.

Conditional on firm i having filed at least one patent in time t, the proportion of the firm's innovation search that explored recently developed knowledge at time t is the number of citations made by firm i in time t to patents granted/filed within the past 3 years divided by Total cites it. Recent patents represent more current technologies compared with older patents, and three years was used as the cutoff given that the midpoint of the medical device product life cycle is about three years; self-citations were excluded. This measure defines exploratory search from the field's perspective.
time_window: three-year look-back for cited patents; annual, 1980-2008

description: Conditional on firm i having filed at least one patent in time t, the proportion of search exploring scientific knowledge at time t is the number of nonpatent publications cited by firm i in time t divided by Total cites it. Following Gittelman and Kogut (2003), a firm's citations to nonpatent literature were counted because scientific knowledge is typically more basic and distant from product commercialization stages and is hence regarded as more exploratory. This measure defines exploratory search from the field's perspective.

Dependent variable capturing the hazard of a Japanese parent firm establishing a manufacturing affiliate in a host country. It is a binary variable that takes the value one when the firm enters a country and zero otherwise, and it is measured for all potential host countries and all years, so the unit of analysis is the firm-country-year level. The set of countries includes countries entered at some point (non-censored) and countries never entered by the end of the period (censored).

The reduction in labor cost correlation in the foreign affiliate portfolio due to the addition of a potential host country to the portfolio. Following Belderbos et al. (2014), labor cost correlation uses dollar-denominated labor costs in host countries j and k for year t, average labor costs over the 5 years including the focal year in each country, and the standard deviations of labor costs within these past 5 years, with N the total number of countries in which the firm operates manufacturing affiliates. The variable is calculated for the existing portfolio and for the new portfolio that would result from the focal entry, and Flexibility increase is the labor cost correlation in the existing portfolio minus that in the new portfolio. The equation block in the text is unreadable in this record, so only the surrounding prose specification is reported.

Measured as the increase in the dispersion of labor cost levels in the firm's portfolio of affiliates due to the addition of a new host country. Labor cost level dispersion is the standard deviation of labor cost levels of the host countries, where the average labor cost in the portfolio is subtracted from the labor cost level of host country j and N is the total number of countries in which the firm operates manufacturing affiliates. The variable is the dispersion of the new portfolio minus the dispersion of the existing portfolio, and it is interacted with Flexibility increase and with its own quadratic term. The equation block in the text is unreadable in this record, so only the prose specification is reported.

Relatedness-weighted product diversification of the affiliate portfolio, defined as (1 - relatedness) times the number of industries in the portfolio. The relatedness matrix is constructed from three salient resource characteristics: capital intensity (total capital/employees), material intensity (material costs/sales), and R&D intensity, using data for all publicly listed firms in Japan from the Development Bank of Japan database. Higher values indicate more unrelated diversification and hence greater difficulty and cost of shifting production flexibly across countries.

Calculated as the standard deviation of labor cost over a five-year period (from t - 4 to t) for the focal country. The variable and its quadratic term are included to test the prediction that its positive effect on entry declines at higher levels of volatility.

variable_name: Labor cost level dispersion increase x Flexibility increase
description: Interaction term used to test the moderating hypothesis: Labor cost level dispersion increase and its quadratic term are interacted with Flexibility increase. The linear interaction coefficient is significantly positive and the quadratic interaction coefficient is significantly negative.

Interaction term used to test the moderating hypothesis that product diversification in the affiliate portfolio reduces the positive impact of Flexibility increase on the propensity to enter a host country.

The age of the respondent's work organization at a given point in time, taken from the career history accounts respondents gave of the organizations where they were employed. In the rate model this is T, the age of person j's work organization, updated for each person-year segment of a job spell.

The size of the respondent's work organization, reported in the career history survey and used in the models as the logarithm of (number of employees + 0.1). In the rate model this is S, the size of person j's work organization, updated for each person-year segment of a job spell.

A 0/1 indicator of whether the respondent's primary position in her current work organization was the founder role, coded from survey answers about primary positions and distinguished from the member (nonfounder) role. In the model F_j and M_j are 0/1 indicator variables measuring whether person j is the founder or a member of her current work organization.

The event in which a reported job change led to assuming the role of company founder, coded as a transition to entrepreneurship in the year it occurred. This coding distinguishes entrepreneurship from self-employment not involving the creation of a new organization and from a mere investment in a new venture without personal involvement. The dependent variable in the models is the instantaneous rate at which such transitions occur, with spells divided into person-year segments.

Dichotomous measure that assumes the value 1 if the materials procurement process is centralized at headquarters and 0 if delegated to the project level. ONDAC determines whether procurement of building materials for each project is fully executed at the contractor's headquarters or whether a substantial portion of the procurement activities is executed at the project level. Delegation requires that the project officers execute at least management of specifications, coordination of customized fabrication, coordinating delivery, execution of quality control, and management of materials storage.

Each of the nine specialty trades observed for a project was assigned the value 1 if integrated and 0 otherwise. The measure was standardized for each specialty trade across all projects and then averaged across specialty trades for each project, so it represents the standardized percentage of integrated specialty trade activities at the project level.
Large projects tend to be more complex and face more interdependencies, which affect governance choices. The variable is the natural logarithm of the project area in square meters.

Nonhousing projects face more alterations via change orders and are more complex than housing projects because they are less standardized and face more interactions. A dummy variable that assumes a value 0 if the project is a housing complex, residential building, or single family home, and 1 otherwise.

Fast-track (design-and-build) projects begin when a basic design is ready, which increases uncertainty, unplanned disturbances, and the need for adaptive capacity. The authors first compute for each year and contractor the percentage of contractor volume executed in the housing market, and then a dummy variable that takes the value 1 if the project is a housing project and the contractor executes at least 60 percent of its volume in housing, and 0 otherwise.

variable_name: Prior interactions with the project director and warehouse manager
description: Two dummy variables capture prior interactions between the contractor executing the project and each project officer. The first assumes the value 1 if the project director has been the project director of any previous project for the contractor executing the focal project; the second is analogous, but considers the project warehouse manager. The two dummies are multiplied to capture the greatest trust in delegated procurement, corresponding to prior interactions of the contractor with both officers.

The March 2008 change in labor law made trials faster and increased the percentage of cases decided in favor of workers, so firms experience more difficulties firing workers who underperform, increasing employment agency costs. The changes were implemented in phases across Chile's 15 regions from the beginning of 2008 to the end of 2010. The variable is a dummy that assumes the value 1 if the project began after the legal change in each region.

A distant project is more difficult to monitor, impeding clear control of procurement activities and increasing agency costs. Project distance was measured by computing the distance between a project's region and the region that contains the highest percentage of total square meters built by the contractor in that year.

variable_name: local partners' affiliation with a business group
description: An indicator variable identifying whether a Chinese partner was affiliated with a business group in a given year; it took a value of 1 if a Chinese partner was a business group affiliate and 0 otherwise. Group affiliation status was checked against the formation time of a business group, and the year each Chinese partner joined a business group was checked so that the partner belonged to the group during the observation period. Affiliations were coded from Large Corporations of China, the SASAC list, and press releases, annual reports, and/or Web sites of local partners and business groups.

variable_name: local partners' affiliation with a national business group
description: An indicator variable for the political rank of the business group, taking a value of 1 if a Chinese partner was affiliated with a national-level business group and 0 otherwise. Business groups' ranks were differentiated using the list of 189 business groups developed by the SASAC, which are directly under the State Council and are called China's 'national teams'.

variable_name: local partners' affiliation with a regional business group
description: An indicator variable for the political rank of the business group, taking a value of 1 if a Chinese partner was affiliated with a regional-level business group and 0 otherwise. It was defined alongside the national group indicator from the coding of local partners' group affiliations.

An indicator variable for locational restriction, coded 1 if an IJV was not located in one of China's FDI-open economic regions, which comprise the five special economic zones and the 14 'open coastal cities', and 0 otherwise. The variable was time varying depending on when a region was designated a special economic zone or open coastal city.

An indicator variable coded 1 when an IJV was in an FDI-restricted industry, defined as an industry in which local partners were required for entry, using the IJV's three-digit SIC code. Coding was based on the first two editions (1995 and 1997) of the Industry Catalogue for Foreign Investment, promulgated by the State Council, which regulated and administered foreign investments from the early 1980s until 2001.

Exiting IJVs were identified by comparing preceding editions of Kaigai Shinshutsu Kigyou Souran with later editions; IJV exit was coded 1 and IJV survival was coded 0. In the event history analysis each joint venture was at risk of exit in each time period until an exit occurred or the data were right-censored, with duration measured as IJV age.

The annual rate of IJV sales growth. Annual subsidiary sales information was obtained from successive editions of Kaigai Shinshutsu Kigyou Souran, and an annual sales growth rate was computed for each IJV.

Herfindahl concentration ratio calculated across the 12 categories of machine tool products, with the shares denoting the proportion of the firm's total products classified in each segment. The measure ranges from 0 to 1, with 1 indicating the highest level of specialization. The equation itself is unreadable in the supplied text.

Variance of the list prices of the firm's products, normalized by dividing through by the largest variance in prices for any firm in that year. The resulting measure has a minimum of 0 (generalist) and a maximum of 1 (specialist). The equation itself is unreadable in the supplied text.

The number of distinct new models a firm introduces, divided by the total number of products offered by the firm. Product listings with the same name and the same characteristics as products available in early years do not count as new models. Because the measure is a proportion ranging only from 0 to 1, tobit regression is used to estimate the parameters.

The number of distinct new models a firm introduces, divided by the total number of products offered by the firm. Product listings with the same name and characteristics as products available in earlier years are not counted as new models. Estimated with tobit regression.

The number of products a firm introduces outside its existing niche divided by the total number of new products offered by the firm. For machine tools the niche is the range of engine sizes (in HP) produced by the firm; any new product with an engine size below the previous minimum or above the previous maximum counts as an out-of-niche expansion, and all new products introduced outside those boundaries in a year count, not just the extreme values. Estimated with tobit regression.

The number of products a firm introduces outside its existing niche divided by the total number of new products offered by the firm. For workstations the niche boundaries are the cheapest and most expensive products offered by the firm in the prior year. Estimated with tobit regression.

A 0/1 indicator for adoption of numerical or computer numerical control (CNC/NC) machine technology. In nearly every case, once a machine tool manufacturer adopts CNC it incorporates it in all of its new models going forward (19 exceptions out of 564 cases), so these adoptions are treated as one-time events. Modeled as a discrete time failure rate model with logit regression.

The number of new products offered that incorporate either an operating system or a microprocessor not previously used by the firm, divided by the total number of products offered. Estimated with tobit regression.

An incumbent is coded as failing when it no longer offers products in that industry. Three additional events that might explain why a firm no longer offers products are coded—bankruptcy, divesture from the business by a diversified corporation, and merger with another company or acquisition by a company wishing to enter the industry—and news reports and trade journals are used to determine whether a merger or acquisition resulted in substantial organizational change and therefore counts as an exit. The exit rate is estimated with piecewise exponential survival models using the proportion of new products introduced this year and in the previous year.

The relative frequency with which a firm's new four-digit SIC-code business areas were attributable to acquisitions of other firms rather than to internal development. New SIC-code business areas were those in which the firm conducted business at the end of 1981 but not at the beginning of 1977, and an acquisition had the status of a new SIC-code business only if the acquiring firm was not involved in that SIC code at the time of acquisition and the acquired company was doing business in it at that time. The range of possible scores is continuous between 0 and 1, with the midpoint of .5 representing a balance between the two modes of diversification and 0 indicating purely internal diversification.

Average annual growth in total corporate sales between 1977 and 1981. The authors included this measure because internal development projects often require long time periods before yielding positive returns, whereas acquisitions will in most cases instantaneously increase the acquiring firm's revenues, so there should be differences in sales growth between internal and acquisitive diversifiers.

Average annual return on assets between 1977 and 1981, calculated on the basis of operating incomes before taxes and interest. The authors describe ROA as a more robust measure of relative efficiency than ROI or ROE because it is not sensitive to differences in debt structure (Brealey & Myers, 1984).

Average annual return on investments between 1977 and 1981. Together with ROA and ROE it incorporates the firms' levels of profitability and represents a measure of relative efficiency across the sample; ROI is sensitive, to a lesser extent than ROE, to differences in debt structure.

Average annual return on equity between 1977 and 1981. It incorporates the firms' levels of profitability and is, like ROI, sensitive to differences in debt structure across the sample, ROE more so than ROI.

The level of institutional development of a host country is measured with 12 national institutional characteristics used as proxies for economic, political, and social institutions, obtained from the World Competitiveness Yearbook, International Monetary Fund, Freedom House, and International Country Risk Guide (PRS Group) for the period 1996-2001. A principal components analysis with a varimax rotation was conducted for all 12 items for each year; the items loaded significantly on one factor (institutional development) with an eigenvalue of 7.51-8.60, and explained 68.0-71.4 percent of the variance. Confirmatory factor analyses showed that a three-factor model did not provide a significantly better fit than the one-factor model. Institutional development scores were calculated for each country to form the IDI, and both linear and quadric terms were included in the models.

The level of foreign affiliate performance (return on investment) is measured by the return on sales (ROS) of the foreign affiliates of MNCs. The authors use ROS rather than return on assets because ROS is regarded as a superior measure in the global environment, since foreign affiliates focus on ongoing businesses and sales better reflect their performance across changes in the business climate than fixed assets. A second reason given is that asset turnover may vary significantly among host countries due to differences in their market value, so ROA may not correctly reflect the economic performance of foreign affiliates.

The variation in foreign affiliate performance (risk of investment) is measured by the extent to which the ROS of foreign affiliates deviates from the host country mean. In the operational definition, risk is the absolute value of the deviation between the ROS of the ith foreign affiliate in the tth year and the mean country ROS in that year. The measure captures the variation in performance among foreign affiliates within a host country in each year, rather than variation within a business unit across years, and it incorporates both downside and upside return streams. The equations giving the operational definitions of risk and return are not legible in the supplied text.
Number of product models for the firm, observed monthly for each of the four firms in the computer printer market. The authors use product line length and breadth interchangeably.

The total action of the firm's major competitor(s) in product line in the period previous to t, taken from the monthly data on competitors' product line length. It enters the estimated product line equation as the lagged competitor product line action.

The anticipated total action of the firm's major competitor(s) in product line in the period following t. Because anticipated actions are unobservable, they are modeled under rational expectations: anticipated competitor action is expressed as a function of past competitor action (extrapolative expectations) and the predicted values of that equation are used for anticipated competitor actions in the action equation.

Elasticity of the firm's sales with respect to its own product line length, computed from the parameter estimates of the sales response equation based on average values of the relevant variables and reported separately for the market leader and the follower firms. The authors term it the firm's clout.
time_window: average values over the data period

description: Elasticity of the firm's sales with respect to competitors' product line length, computed from the parameter estimates of the sales response equation and reported for HP and for the follower firms. The authors term it the firm's vulnerability.
time_window: average values over the data period

description: Weighted average price of the firm, based on the prices of its different product models weighted by their sales, observed monthly and modeled as the firm's price action at time t.
Weighted share of the firm's presence in the channels through which the products are sold, observed monthly and modeled as the firm's distribution action at time t.

variable_name: Market leader (HP) versus market followers (Canon, Epson, Lexmark)
description: HP is identified as the market leader, with $520 million in monthly sales and the longest product line, whereas Canon, Epson, and Lexmark are the follower firms. A Chow pooling test rejected homogeneity of parameters between HP and each of the other firms (p < 0.01) and did not reject homogeneity across Canon, Epson, and Lexmark (p < 0.10), so the system is estimated separately for HP and for the pooled followers.

A binary variable that discriminates the marginal effect of being foreign. Firms are classified as foreign or domestic using the data on equity held by nonresidents, those with a foreign participation greater than 10 percent being classified as foreign owned; domestic entrants form the reference group.

The propensity to develop firm-specific assets is measured by the share of college graduates among the firm's labor force. The conventional measurement of human capital relies on different measures of the educational levels of individuals, college being a threshold sometimes employed.

Size was measured by the number of persons in the firm. Current size, rather than start-up size, is used because current size includes information on the reaction of firms to their market success over time, and models using current size are better predictors of survival. Values of explanatory variables are updated yearly through their one-year lagged values.

Growth is used as an indirect measure of economic performance, in place of profits, which are problematic for multinational firms because of the transfer pricing problem. The use of growth rests on the argument that firms with good outcomes grow while those with bad times contract or exit, and that growth signals optimistic expectations of success.

Firms in the data set may operate under either limited or unlimited liability, and domestic and foreign firms differ widely in the legal form adopted. The variable distinguishes firms operating under limited liability from those of unlimited liability.

Duration is measured in yearly intervals from the firm's first report to the survey, so measured durations are grouped into yearly intervals. The models include dummies identifying the firm's age; the coefficients of the age dummies are not reported in the tables but are presented as baseline hazard rates in Figure 2.

The left-hand side variable is the logarithm of the hazard rate, that is, the log of the probability that the firm exits at time t, given that it survived until t-1. A firm is classified as exiting in the first year it ceases to report to the survey, requiring that it be absent from the file for at least two years; firms still active in 1991 are right-censored.
time_window: yearly intervals from the 1983-89 cohorts to 1990

description: Built from a single-mode inventor-inventor collaboration network in which inventors are nodes and copatenting within the same firm is a tie, derived from patents-issued information. The network is updated annually, using a moving three-year window of collaboration ties ending in year t, with ties older than three years treated as dissolved. Centrality is the Bonacich (1987) power measure, which takes into account the centrality of the other inventors connected to the focal inventor, calculated in UCINET VI. The weight beta is set equal to three-quarters of the reciprocal of the largest eigenvalue of the adjacency matrix, so that an inventor linked to highly central others is also highly central.
time_window: moving three-year window ending in year t

description: Patents represent an inventor's knowledge, and impact is measured as the number of citations received by all of an inventor's patents from others in her firm, counted from the patent's grant date to the end of 1999. The observation period is split into annual spells, so the measure is the total citations an inventor receives in a given year, predicted by variables measured in year t. The application date of the citing patent is used rather than the grant date.
time_window: annual spells; citations from grant date to end of 1999

description: Structural centrality of a firm in the interfirm research alliance network. An interfirm network is created each year from research ties formed by all firms during the three-year period ending in year t, with ties assumed dissolved after three years. The firm's centrality is calculated in UCINET VI using the same Bonacich formula described for inventor centrality.
time_window: moving three-year window ending in year t

description: Burt's (1992) span of structural holes measure computed in UCINET VI from the yearly interfirm research alliance network. The formula uses the proportion of firm i's ties invested in connection with contact q, the marginal strength of the relationship between contact j and contact q, and the total number of contacts for firm i. Higher values represent spanning larger structural holes, and the values ranged from 0 to 1.
