The previous number of projects carried out by each early-stage biotechnology firm in a period minus the previous number carried out by the early-stage biotechnology firm with the lowest number in that period. Previous biotechnology R&D alliances for each firm were identified by searching Recap.

How much greater a pharmaceutical firm's previous experience with late-stage projects is relative to the paired pharmaceutical firm with the least experience, obtained by subtracting the number of previous late-stage projects of the least experienced firm in each period from each pharmaceutical firm's number.

The absorptive capacity of each pharmaceutical firm involved in a late-stage alliance in each period, captured by its R&D intensity using Compustat data, divided by the value for the pharmaceutical firm with the lowest absorptive capacity in that period.

The size of the biotechnology firm's shareholders' equity, in millions of dollars, obtained from Compustat and from IPO prospectuses. A larger shareholders' equity indicates a lower need for external funding.

For every pharmaceutical firm in each year, the authors identified the number of projects it had at each stage of the regulatory approval process, using data from Pharmaprojects and NDA Pipeline. Following Higgins and Rodriguez (2006), these values were then weighted and summed to generate a measure of pharmaceutical pipeline health.
The number of concurrent biotechnology alliances in which each pharmaceutical firm was involved at signing.

The logarithm of the cumulative past number of RMs, with the count starting in 2001. The variable was lagged to allow for temporal ordering and to avoid simultaneity bias, and it was orthogonalized with the proportion of lower-status adopters using Stata's orthog command to address the high correlation between the two variables.

The weekly count of new RMs, measured using the day of the announcement of the RM, starting on August 1, 2002, and ending on December 31, 2012 (521 weeks in total). RMs were aggregated on a weekly level because it takes approximately two weeks for a firm to consummate an RM. The count is modeled as a random variable drawn from a Poisson distribution (estimated with a negative binomial specification).

The past number of RMs by lower-status firms divided by the total number of RMs, expressed as a percentage. Firms were categorized as lower status if they hired trivially small auditing firms with fewer than five partners and 10 professional staff members. The variable was orthogonalized with the past number of RMs and lagged.

The weekly count of media articles depicting RMs negatively, collected from Factiva's Major News and Business Publications between 2001 and 2012, and lagged to avoid simultaneity bias. Of the 267 articles identified, 148 had a neutral tone, 113 had a negative tone, and only 6 had a positive tone, so negative articles were contrasted with the combination of neutral and positive articles; inter-rater reliability (kappa) was 0.88.

Weekly abnormal stock market returns estimated for each RM using the market-adjusted model ARit = Rit - Rmt, where Rit is the return for firm i in week t and Rmt is the Nasdaq Composite Index return, implicitly assuming a market beta of 1 for all firms. An equally weighted portfolio of the weekly abnormal returns of all RMs that were traded at any point in time was then constructed.

Measured using two sets of variables, one based on the number of brands carried by the DC and the other based on the number of SKUs. To avoid collinearity between number of brands and number of SKUs, the SKU measure was orthogonalized. An SKU is defined as a unique combination of brand, content, flavor, weight, container material-size, and package material-size. The time-varying counts were also decomposed into a cross-sectional average component and an intertemporal deviation component.

The number of units from which DC i received shipments for all SKUs in period t. It was also decomposed into a cross-sectional component, the average number of units DC i sourced from over the sample period, and an intertemporal component, the number of units DC i sourced from in period t. Because the number of units in the network is constant over the sample period, the total number of inter-unit sourcing relationships in the network is perfectly correlated with the number of sourcing relationships for each DC.

A dummy variable that takes the value of 1 if SKU s experienced at least one stockout at DC i in period t, and is 0 otherwise. Stockouts were measured using a dummy rather than a continuous variable because the distribution of stockout quantity is highly skewed. Stockouts occur when a DC cannot deliver an entire order for an SKU to a given retail outlet, and unfilled demand is not backordered.

A dummy variable that captures if DC i shipped SKU s to at least two other DCs during period t. Based on the sourcing network constructed for each SKU in each period, all the hubs for each SKU were identified. The number of DCs the hub supplied to (its outward linkages) was also used.

A dummy variable that captures if DC i received SKU s through a hub. It was measured based on whether the focal DC sourced through a hub for any SKUs that it carried, not just the focal SKU, and was later separated into sourcing through a hub for the focal SKU and sourcing through hubs for any non-focal SKUs.

variable_name: entrepreneurial proclivity of the ancestral founders
description: We used a count of the number of start-ups founded by founders as a proxy for their entrepreneurial proclivity. As a dependent variable this is the number of start-ups the ancestral founders established in a given year t. To address Hypothesis 2a it serves as an independent variable, a count of the number of start-ups established by ancestral founders over the period of the study, normalized by dividing it by the maximum value it received over the entire period of analysis, so that it received a value between 0 and 1, where 1 indicates the highest entrepreneurial proclivity possible.
scale: count per year (dependent variable); normalized count between 0 and 1 (independent variable)
time_window: yearly observations, from the year the ancestral founders of the focal genealogy established their first venture to 2005

variable_name: entrepreneurial proclivity of the second generation
description: As a dependent variable, the number of start-ups created by the second generation in a given year t by the organization members who left the founding parents' firms. To test Hypothesis 2b it serves as an independent variable, coded as the cumulative number of start-ups established by second-generation founders and normalized, and was also used in the first-stage logit estimation of the likelihood that a second generation was formed.
scale: count per year (dependent variable); normalized cumulative count (independent variable)
time_window: yearly observations from the year the ancestral founders established their first venture to 2005 (second-generation analysis); from the year the second generation was established to 2005 (third-generation analysis)

variable_name: entrepreneurial proclivity of the third generation
description: The number of third-generation start-ups in a given year t, that is, start-ups created by organization members who left second-generation start-ups; this number reflects the entrepreneurial proclivity of the third generation per year.
time_window: yearly observations starting at the year the second generation of the focal genealogy was established and ending in 2005

description: For each firm, the variable cooperative era was assigned a value of 1 if its ancestral firm was founded up to the year 1977, and 0 otherwise. Similarly, for each firm, the variable competitive era was assigned a value of 1 if its ancestral firm was founded between the years 1977 and 1985, and 0 otherwise. Because the two variables could not be included together in the regressions, the authors omitted formation during the cooperative era in the analyses.
time_window: founding year of the ancestral firm (up to 1977 for the cooperative era; 1977-1985 for the competitive era)

description: A founder's entrepreneurial tenure is measured as the natural log of the duration of time (in years) since the year in which that individual established his or her first venture up to the year of the analysis. Since, at this point in time, the prospective founders of the second generation have no entrepreneurial experience at all, the entrepreneurial tenure of the ancestral founders reflects the temporal entrepreneurial gap between them and the second generation. The natural log is used based on the assumption that tenure has a diminishing marginal impact. Hypothesis 4 is tested with the entrepreneurial tenure by entrepreneurial proclivity of the first generation interaction.
time_window: yearly, from the year the founder established his or her first venture up to the year of analysis

description: A count of the number of female partners listed as employed by a focal law firm i in year t. In all models the authors control for the total number of firm partners, so a change in the firm's number of female partners can be directly interpreted as a change in the firm's gender diversity. The gender of partners is taken from annual surveys of the law firms.

The weighted and averaged percentage of female executives in the buyers that bought legal services from a focal firm's competitors but not the focal firm in year t. The extent of rivalry between the focal firm and each competitor serving those buyers is used to weight the impact of each rival buyer's gender diversity, using similarity in profits-per-partner to determine the extent of rivalry. The authors state that construction details are provided in Online Appendix 1.
time_window: year t, lagged two years relative to the dependent variable

description: The rivalry-weighted average percentage of female partners in the competitors of the focal firm. The authors first computed the percentage of female partners (to all partners) in each competitor of the focal firm and multiplied these percentages by the corresponding rival weight, then summed the weighted percentages and divided by the number of competitors, before finally multiplying by 100. The authors note the equation as rendered in the text is unreadable; the specification is described in prose.
time_window: year t, lagged two years relative to the dependent variable

description: The percentage of partners in focal firm i in year t that are not identified as 'white.' Racial minority (non-White) partners are identified through the annual surveys administered by Vault. Data limitations prevented the decomposition of racial minority into subcategories.
time_window: year t, lagged two years relative to the dependent variable

variable_name: Relative standing (with respect to VC investment size)
description: Relative standing of a venture in a VC's portfolio is measured with respect to the size of the investment the VC has already made in the venture. It is calculated as the VC's investment in the venture minus the mean VC investment in the other ventures in that VC's portfolio, divided by the standard deviation of the VC investment in the other ventures in the VC's portfolio. The authors argue that if a VC has a positive evaluation of a venture's prospects, it is likely to have invested a larger amount.

The dependent variable in the second-stage model takes on 1 if the venture exits through IPO or M&A by the end of 2004, and 0 otherwise. Because conventional measures of performance are not available for private biotechnology ventures, exit is used as the indicator of the benefits a venture receives from the VC affiliation. An IPO is one of the primary ways for VC firms to realize their return on investment in a venture, and M&As have become prevalent routes of exit.

VC portfolio size is the number of ventures funded by the VC within the past five years. It enters the models as a control and is interacted with relative standing to test how it conditions the effect of relative standing on exit. The authors argue that greater demands on the partner's resources create more intense competition among the ventures in the portfolio and that a partner with more ventures has more leverage over each venture.

The authors measure VC status by calculating Bonacich's power centrality in the syndication network. The centrality of VC firm i at year t is defined through the centrality of VC firm j, the relationship matrix R showing the number of co-investments between VC firms i and j for the period between t-5 and t, and the total number of VC firms active at any time between t and t-5. The weighting coefficient is set equal to 0.75 of the reciprocal of the largest eigenvalue of R, and the scaling is set so that the maximum centrality for each year is equal to 1. The exact equation block itself was not recoverable from the text, so only the components described in prose are recorded.

To measure the discrepancy in total reported profit between the MOST and SAIC books, the authors subtract the latter from the former and label the difference Profit Gap, where profit is measured as earnings before taxes. In the OLS models the profit gap is Winsorized at one percent to reduce the influence of extreme values. A second specification uses the natural logarithm of the profit gap, ln[1 + (Profit MOST - Profit SAIC)], which drops six observations with negative values.
time_window: same accounting period (fiscal year) for both filings

description: A dummy variable that equals one if a nontrivial profit discrepancy exists between the MOST and SAIC books, that is when the two profit numbers are discrepant by more than 20 percent, (Profit MOST - Profit SAIC)/(1 + Profit MOST) > 0.20. Firms reporting consistent profit numbers to the two agencies form the omitted category.
time_window: same accounting period (fiscal year) for both filings

description: Hand-coded from the resumes that all company founders submit as a mandatory part of the Innofund application process, which provide detailed information on founders' educational background, former employers, major career achievements, and recognitions from the government. The indicator denotes that one or more company founders previously worked in the Chinese government or once held membership in the People's Congress (PC) or the Chinese People's Political Consultative Conference (CPPCC). By this definition, 102 firms, or 21.84 percent of the sample, qualify as politically connected.
time_window: at the time of the Innofund application

description: A dummy variable that is 1 when any equity owner in the company is an organization, such as another corporation or a university. Firms with only individual owners form the omitted category in the regressions.

A dummy variable that is 1 if one or more of the organizational equity holders is listed as a VC firm by the State Development Planning Council and has a profile on the website of China's premier VC/PE information provider, Zero2IPO. In the regressions separating owners by type, companies with VC investors are labelled VC OEH and are compared with companies whose organizational equity holders are not VCs and with companies owned entirely by individual shareholders.

A dummy variable that equals 1 if a firm receives an Innofund grant from the MOST. Information on all grant recipients was collected from the Innofund website. Of the firms in the sample, 54 percent received Innofund funding.

The size of the Innofund award received by the firm, in thousands of yuan RMB. The authors interpret the coefficient on profit manipulation as the increase in the Innofund award size when an otherwise similar firm switches from being honest to cheating.

A binary variable equal to 1 once a CVC invests in the venture, and 0 otherwise, i.e., when the venture is funded solely by VCs. It is lagged one year relative to the annual patent and publication counts.

A count of patents for venture i at year t, measuring a venture's patenting output in line with extant work. Patent data were collected from the USPTO and patent assignee information was hand-matched to the biotechnology ventures in the sample. Patent and publication activity was collected through 2005 filings, which become observable later.
A count of scientific publications for venture i at year t, measuring a venture's publications output. Publications were collected from the Web of Knowledge (ISI) database, widely used in prior work.

variable_name: CVC Accessibility High or Low i,t-1
description: Decomposes CVC backing into two nested binary variables based on the distance to the venture. If a venture is funded by a CVC that is based in the same region, the high-accessibility variable is equal to 1; if the CVC is based in a different region, the low-accessibility variable is equal to 1. Regions follow the U.S. Small Business Administration regional classification.

An indicator variable that takes the value of 1 when the venture operates in a sub-industry that is subject to the FDA regulatory process, and 0 otherwise. The VentureXpert Industry Classification (VEIC) description of the sub-industry, from Venture Economics, was matched to the categories subject to FDA approval according to FDA regulation.

variable_name: Time to EJV formation (rise period hazard)
description: The dependent variable is measured by the time difference in number of days between the date of a focal EJV formation and the date of the first acquisition in the industry. It is estimated as the hazard of an EJV being formed by a foreign firm and a local firm based in a given home country, with the foreign entry event as the level of analysis. The rise period is tested separately using the censoring technique, with an EJV established after 1993 treated as a right-censored case. The rise-period analysis uses 174 observations in the nine industries in which the first foreign M&A occurred before 1994.

variable_name: Time to EJV formation (decline period hazard)
description: The dependent variable is measured by the time difference in number of days between the date of a focal EJV formation and the date of the first acquisition in the industry, estimated as the hazard of EJV formation for the decline period. EJVs established after 2003 are treated as right-censored. The left truncation time is decided either by the year 2003 for the nine industries or by the date of the first foreign acquisition in the other five, and 1,083 observations in all selected industries are included.

The number of equity joint venture adoptions by foreign firms based in the same home-country industry. The variable is time-varying, collected from the SDC database, and lagged by one year because the frequency of adoptions or rejections one year prior is expected to affect subsequent EJV entries. The primary industry for each firm was identified according to its two-digit SIC code.

The number of equity joint venture adoptions by foreign firms based in the same home-country industry, lagged by one year and time-varying over the decline period. In the decline period the authors read a positive effect of this frequency as an increased number of EJV rejections relative to the peak year. The variable was collected from the SDC database with industries identified by two-digit SIC code.

The number of equity joint venture adoptions by foreign firms based in the same host-country industry. The measure is time-varying, drawn from the SDC database and lagged by one year. The primary industry for each firm was identified according to its two-digit SIC code.

The number of equity joint venture adoptions by foreign firms based in the same host-country industry, lagged by one year and time-varying over the decline period. It captures mimetic imitation based on the host-country industry reference group during the EJV decline period.

The number of merger and acquisition adoptions by foreign firms based in the same home-country industry, capturing the emergence of the competing M&A entry strategy within that reference group. The variable is time-varying, collected from the SDC database and lagged by one year.

The number of merger and acquisition adoptions by foreign firms based in the same home-country industry, lagged by one year and time-varying over the decline period. Both partial and full acquisitions are included in the M&A sample drawn from the SDC database.

The number of merger and acquisition adoptions by foreign firms based in the same host-country industry, capturing the spread of the competing M&A strategy in the host-country field. The variable is time-varying, drawn from the SDC database and lagged by one year.

The number of merger and acquisition adoptions by foreign firms based in the same host-country industry, lagged by one year and time-varying over the decline period. It also serves as the moderator of the imitation effect in the host-country industry, and both partial and full acquisitions are included.

Labor productivity is calculated as the ratio of total sales to the total number of employees. It is the dependent variable of the two productivity regimes (with and without organizational change), which are estimated jointly with the reorganization decision.

ICT investment is used as a proxy for the ICT capital stock, entered in logs in the estimated productivity equations. The data on ICT investment are taken from the 24th wave (first quarter of 2000) of the SSBS.

Non-ICT capital is measured as investment in physical capital, entered in logs in the estimated productivity equations. The authors note that a capital stock could potentially be calculated with the perpetual inventory method, but that the SSBS panel is too volatile for this. The data are taken from the 24th wave (first quarter of 2000) of the SSBS.

Labor input is measured by the total number of employees of the firm, entered in the productivity equations; the data on total employment are taken from the 24th wave (first quarter of 2000) of the SSBS.

A dummy variable indicating whether the firm reported that the enhancement of group work took place within the firm during the past three years. Firms had three answering possibilities: yes, no, and do not know. Information comes from the 26th wave of the SSBS (third quarter of 2000); group-work reinforcement is the more important type of workplace reorganization, with a share of 39% of the firms in the sample.
time_window: past three years, as reported in the third quarter of 2000 (26th wave)

description: A dummy variable indicating whether the firm reported that the flattening of hierarchies took place within the firm during the past three years. Firms had three answering possibilities: yes, no, and do not know. Information comes from the 26th wave of the SSBS (third quarter of 2000); flattening of hierarchies was introduced by 28% of the analyzed firms.
time_window: past three years, as reported in the third quarter of 2000 (26th wave)

description: An entrant's rank order of entry into a technical subfield, measured relative to all entrants to that subfield. The rank order variable was transformed by its natural log, progressively reducing the influence of late entry.

An industry incumbent's rank order of entry into a technical subfield, measured relative to other incumbents in that subfield. It was transformed by its natural log, progressively reducing the influence of late entry.

Entrants were split into the two classes of newcomers and incumbents, and the two categories were analysed separately so that differences in performance means and variances could be estimated for each category. The entrant-type prediction was tested by comparing the intercepts of the newcomer and incumbent models. Because some newcomers entered more than one subfield, some firms were classed as newcomers on their entry to one subfield and then as industry incumbents on their entry to another.

The average market share within a technical subfield of the imaging industry attained during a firm's first 4 years of participation in the subfield. The measurement started with the January of the calendar year following a firm's entry and did not include a firm's final year of participation; if a firm survived less than 4 years the variable recorded its average share for the 1-3 years it did participate. The study also measured a firm's 1-year market share in its 7th and 9th years of participation, for firms that had survived at least 8 and 10 years respectively.
time_window: first 4 years of participation; 1-year market share in the 7th and 9th years

description: Survival was defined as a spell equal to the number of years that an entrant to a technical subfield manufactured imaging systems, with a minimum of 1 year for firms that entered and exited during the same calendar year. If an exit date was not observed during the period of the study the record was coded as being right-censored.

Performance in the subfield is measured two ways: the average market share attained in the first 4 years of participation in the subfield, and survival, the number of years the entrant manufactured imaging systems in the subfield (right-censored if no exit was observed). Each hypothesis is tested on both.

The difference between the firm's ROA and the median ROA of its main industry (two-digit Standard Industrialization Code). The authors use it as the dependent variable because ROA takes into account the efficiency of using the firm's resources and reflects a firm's profitability, and because their argument concerns the efficiency of a firm's internal operations.

Dummy indicating whether the family is the largest shareholder of the firm. Total family ownership is calculated as the percentage of shares owned by individual family members and other firms controlled by family members; among firms where the family is the largest shareholder, the average ownership share held by the family is 30.12%.

Dummy indicating whether a family member (a member of the controlling owner's family) serves as chairman of the board (tung shih chang), the most powerful executive position in the firm, equivalent to the chairman/CEO position in the United States and charged with overall goal setting and strategic decision making.

Dummy indicating whether a family member serves as the general manager (tsung ching li), the second most powerful position, equivalent to the U.S. chief operating officer and responsible for managing day-to-day business operations and administration.

variable_name: Firm type dummies (Type 1, Type 2a, Type 2b, Type 3, Type 4)
description: Firms are grouped into five types based on family ownership, strategic (chairman) and operational (general manager) control: family firms with ownership control alone (Type 1), family firms with strategic control but not operational control (Type 2a), family firms with operational control but not strategic control (Type 2b), family firms with complete management control (Type 3), and nonfamily firms (Type 4). Four dummy variables indicating the types are used in the models, and firms with only family ownership control are treated as the omitted category.

variable_name: Industries with weaker versus stronger market institutions
description: Industries are classified based on three indicators: foreign investment (average percentage of shares of firms in the industry owned by foreign investors), analyst following (percentage of firms in the industry covered by at least one analyst), and appointment of independent directors (percentage of firms in the industry with at least one independent director on the board). Industries that scored above the median on all three indicators are coded as having relatively strong market institutional development.

variable_name: Percentage of independent directors on the board
description: The percentage of independent directors on the board. Following Aiken and West (1991), the percentage of independent directors is centered and standardized in the interaction terms with the firm types.

Patent counts is the natural logarithm of one plus the total number of patents filed by a firm and eventually granted in the year. The patent application year is used instead of the grant year to better capture the actual invention date, and focusing on granted patents avoids counting rejected applications. Patent counts is measured one year forward (t + 1) when testing the impact of the reforms on firm innovation and three years forward when testing the mechanisms.
scale: natural logarithm of one plus a count
time_window: t + 1 (three-year forward in the mechanism test)

description: Patent citations is the natural logarithm of one plus the number of citations generated by all patent applications filed by a firm and eventually granted in the year. It is used together with patent counts to capture the quantity and quality of innovation output. It is measured one year forward (t + 1) in the reform effect tests and three years forward in the mechanism test.
scale: natural logarithm of one plus a count
time_window: t + 1 (three-year forward in the mechanism test)

description: Female representation is the ratio of female directors without major committee roles to the total number of directors in a given year. The major board committees are the audit, compensation, nomination, and governance committees. In the mechanism test the authors use the reform-induced change, computed as the difference between the average over the two years after the reform and the average over the two years before the reform, divided by the two-year prereform average.
time_window: contemporaneous year; two-year windows around the reform for the change variable

description: Female empowerment is the ratio of female directors with major committee roles to the total number of directors in a given year, where major committee roles are chairs or members of the audit, compensation, nomination, and governance committees. In the mechanism test the authors use the reform-induced change, computed as the difference between the average over the two years after the reform and the average over the two years before the reform, divided by the two-year prereform average.
time_window: contemporaneous year; two-year windows around the reform for the change variable

description: After reform is an indicator variable that equals one from the year a major board gender diversity reform becomes effective in the country, and zero otherwise. Reform country is an indicator variable that equals one if a firm's country of incorporation implemented board gender diversity reforms during the sample period, and zero otherwise. The interaction term between the two variables is the main DID estimator, capturing the change between the pre- and postreform periods in the outcome variable for firms in reform countries relative to the corresponding change for firms in the control group.
time_window: from the reform's effective year onwards

description: Comply is an indicator variable that equals one if the country implemented comply-or-explain reforms during the sample period, and zero otherwise. It is used to evaluate possible differences in the measured effects between comply-or-explain-based and rule-based board gender diversity reforms.

High_GII equals one if the firm is in a country where the average United Nations' Gender Inequality Index (GII) during its prereform period was above the sample country median, and zero otherwise. The GII includes indicators such as reproductive health, empowerment, and political participation. GII values range from zero to one, with a higher value representing a situation where women fare more poorly in comparison with men, signifying greater gender inequality.

High_supply equals one if a firm is in a country where the average proportion of female employment in senior and middle management positions during its prereform period was above the sample country median, and zero otherwise. The data come from the World Bank and are used to measure the supply of qualified female directors in a country.
A dummy variable taking the value one in the case of stock-based acquisitions or when the payment of the transaction price was made through a combination of stock and cash, and zero otherwise.
time_window: year of the M&A deal (one-year constant variable)

description: The control premium paid by the acquiring firm represents the percentage difference between the purchase price paid per target share and the target stock price 10 days prior to the day when the target received its first official bid.
time_window: year of the M&A deal (one-year constant variable)

description: Binary indicator of whether or not an acquirer announced in its proxy statements the adoption of a new long-term incentive plan over the seven-year window under investigation. LTIPs include stock purchase plans, phantom stock plans, restricted stock awards, and performance units/shares, and exclude stock option plans and stock appreciation rights. The variable was attributed the value one only in the year when it was implemented for the first time, and took the value zero in the following year if it still existed or ceased to exist; enlarging an existing plan with additional incentive mechanisms also counted as a new adoption.
time_window: seven-year window (3 years pre- and 4 years post-acquisition)

description: Binary indicator of whether or not an acquirer announced in its proxy statements the new implementation of an employment agreement over the seven-year window under investigation. The variable equals one only in the year of first implementation, and zero in the following year if the attribute still existed or ceased to exist.
time_window: seven-year window (3 years pre- and 4 years post-acquisition)

description: Binary indicator of whether or not an acquirer announced in its proxy statements the new implementation of a severance provision over the seven-year window under investigation. The variable equals one only in the year of first implementation, and zero in the following year if the attribute still existed or ceased to exist.
time_window: seven-year window (3 years pre- and 4 years post-acquisition)

description: Binary indicator of whether or not an acquirer announced in its proxy statements the new implementation of a golden parachute clause over the seven-year window under investigation. The variable equals one only in the year of first implementation, and zero in the following year if the attribute still existed or ceased to exist.
time_window: seven-year window (3 years pre- and 4 years post-acquisition)

description: Stock market returns were calculated as annual per share increase or decrease in the price of the stock plus dividends accumulated during the current year, divided by the stock price of the acquiring firm at the end of the previous year.
time_window: current year relative to the previous year-end

description: The accounting return on assets was measured by dividing the annual net earnings per total assets in the current year.
The natural logarithm of total sales was retained as a measure of corporate size, given that the logarithmic transformation enhances the statistical fit of the regression model.

The seven-year window surrounding M&A activities was broken down into a post-M&A period, which accounts for the four years following the transaction completion including the base year of acquisition completion, and a pre-M&A period of three years preceding the deal. Interaction terms of the acquirer features with the post-M&A indicator allow the regression slope to be compared between the pre- and post-acquisition periods.
time_window: four years following the transaction completion (including the base year)

description: A modified Terhune (1963) nationalism scale, an accepted and validated scale used by other analysts. The scale's questions formed part of the second part of the questionnaire, which consisted of 25 questions grouped into the five independent variables; the answers for the questions concerning each scale were averaged to arrive at a separate nationalism score for each elite.

Scale of internationalist orientation forming part of the second part of the questionnaire, which consisted of 25 questions grouped into the five independent variables. The answers for the questions concerning the scale were averaged to arrive at a separate internationalism score for each elite.

Scale measuring an individual's economic ideology through his attitude toward private big business and economic concentration and his preference for a specific property modality (private vs. collective). The answers for the questions concerning each scale were averaged to arrive at a separate economic ideology score for each elite.

Scale assessing Arab elite perception of their ability to influence the global economic system; specifically perception of power and leverage vis-a-vis the multinationals as well as the oil consuming industrial countries. The answers for the questions concerning each scale were averaged to arrive at a separate confidence score for each elite.

Scale of satisfaction in direct personal contact or association with multinational firms, i.e. satisfaction of personal objectives through contact with multinational firms. The answers for the questions concerning each scale were averaged to arrive at a separate satisfaction score for each elite.

Questions in the questionnaire intended to measure the frequency of direct personal contact between the elites and multinational firms. The authors report the level of contact of the different elite groups and its correlation with the satisfaction scale.

The first part of the questionnaire dealt with the overall attitude of Arab elites toward multinational firms, the dependent variable. The authors correlate the personal determinant scores with the respondent's overall attitude toward multinational firms questions (Y).

Structured content analysis of the firm's press release issued on the day the violation was announced. Each press release was evaluated as the unit of analysis and coded based on its primary message along a seven-point scale, with 1 representing low accommodativeness and 7 representing high accommodativeness. A trained graduate student blind to the study's hypotheses coded a random sample of 200 press releases from the complete GAO dataset, yielding a Krippendorff's alpha of .92.

Structured content analysis of the firm's press release on the day the violation was announced, coded on its primary message along a seven-point scale from 1 (low accommodativeness) to 7 (high accommodativeness). Because firms are not required to respond to an EPA violation, when a firm press release was not available the EPA's press release, which often included a statement from the firm, was used.

Computer-aided text analysis measure built from a unique dictionary representing capability reputation, applied to firm media coverage. The measure is the proportion of dictionary words over the total words in the corpus, multiplied by 100, captured using the Linguistic Inquiry and Word Count (LIWC) software. Media coverage was collected from the day of the violation to 7 days after the violation for the dependent variable, and from one year prior to the day before the violation for the endowed reputation control.
scale: continuous proportion of dictionary words, multiplied by 100
time_window: t + 7 days (day of violation to 7 days after); endowed reputation measured over the year before the violation

description: Computer-aided text analysis measure built from a unique dictionary representing capability reputation, applied to firm media coverage. The measure is the proportion of dictionary words over the total words in the corpus, multiplied by 100, captured using the Linguistic Inquiry and Word Count (LIWC) software. Media coverage was collected from the day of the violation to 7 days after the violation for the dependent variable, and from one year prior to the day before the violation for the endowed reputation control.
scale: continuous proportion of dictionary words, multiplied by 100
time_window: t + 7 days (day of violation to 7 days after); endowed reputation measured over the year before the violation

description: Computer-aided text analysis measure built from a unique dictionary representing character reputation, applied to firm media coverage. The measure is the proportion of dictionary words over the total words in the corpus, multiplied by 100, captured using the Linguistic Inquiry and Word Count (LIWC) software. Media coverage was collected from the day of the violation to 7 days after the violation for the dependent variable, and from one year prior to the day before the violation for the endowed reputation control.
scale: continuous proportion of dictionary words, multiplied by 100
time_window: t + 7 days (day of violation to 7 days after); endowed reputation measured over the year before the violation

description: Computer-aided text analysis measure built from a unique dictionary representing character reputation, applied to firm media coverage. The measure is the proportion of dictionary words over the total words in the corpus, multiplied by 100, captured using the Linguistic Inquiry and Word Count (LIWC) software. Media coverage was collected from the day of the violation to 7 days after the violation for the dependent variable, and from one year prior to the day before the violation for the endowed reputation control.
scale: continuous proportion of dictionary words, multiplied by 100
time_window: t + 7 days (day of violation to 7 days after); endowed reputation measured over the year before the violation

description: Firms that engaged in unintentional financial accounting restatements as recorded by the GAO. Restatements were classified as intentional or unintentional using Hennes et al.'s (2008) classification; unintentional restatements represent errors or mistakes in the interpretation of accounting rules, which signal a lack of capability.

Civil cases and settlements brought against a firm by the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency for violations of law and federal policy, including the Clean Air Act, Clean Water Act, and Superfund Act, gathered for violations over $50,000 committed by publicly traded firms. Prior work has suggested that environmental violations represent an important context for studying character violations.
A yearly count variable of the firm-level number of alliances between two nations in a dyad, used to test Hypothesis 1.

The proportion of equity alliances in year t, calculated by dividing the number of cross-border firm-level equity alliances by the total number of alliances in a nation-dyad. Extreme outliers of the ratio of equity to nonequity alliances (values greater than 4) were excluded.

The proportion of nonequity alliances, calculated similarly to the proportion of equity alliances by dividing the number of cross-border firm-level nonequity alliances by the total number of alliances in a nation-dyad.

The cumulative number of conflicts in the previous year for the nation-dyad identified in the ICB database, 1918 to the current year. Militarized conflicts such as large-scale military attacks, border conflicts, and war are also included.
time_window: cumulative from 1918 through the previous year

description: The yearly imbalance in the imports between two nations with respect to each one's total trade in that year. As an import imbalance increases, the importing nation is more likely to be perceived as antagonistic.

variable_name: Estimated dyadic error term as a proxy for unobservable dyad characteristics that drive conflict
description: The dyadic error term predicted from estimating the probability of dyadic conflict in the prior year, used as a proxy for unobservable dyad characteristics that drive conflict between two nations. The authors hold that conflict reflects anticipation of reaction from the other nation in a dyad, while taking trade as given, so that conflict is in the error term.

variable_name: Conflict network measure of dissimilarity in degree of conflict relationships of i versus j
description: Constructed from the conflict network of all nation-dyads using UCINET, the dissimilarity in the degree of prior conflicting relationships of nation i versus j with other nations in the network over 1918-87, computed as the Euclidian distance between them. It is the squared difference of the strength of the first nation's ties to a third nation from the strength of the second nation's ties to the third nation, summed for all nations other than the dyad nations.

variable_name: Total number of one-sided conflicts initiated by i and j with other nations in network in previous year
description: Using the classification of conflicts in the ICB database, the cumulative antagonism in a nation-dyad is measured by adding up the total number of conflicts for nations i and j in which at least one of the two nations was classified as the initiator in a conflict with a third nation outside of the dyad, excluding the conflicts in this dyad.

variable_name: Number of equity alliances between i and j in previous year
description: A count variable of the total number of equity alliances between nations i and j in the previous year, used to test the learning-to-contract hypothesis.

variable_name: Number of nonequity alliances between i and j in previous year
description: A count of the number of nonequity alliances between nations i and j in the previous year, used as the comparison case for the learning effect of prior equity alliance experience; the authors report that the number of prior-year nonequity alliances between i and j is statistically insignificant and contributes no additional explanatory power to the base model.

All tags assigned to questions related to deep learning and machine learning are used to measure developers' problem complexity. In the first step a tag-level interdependence measure is calculated for each tag in Stack Overflow's tag pool as the average frequency of co-occurrence (co-assignment to a question) of a focal tag with other tags, using a cross-sectional snapshot of the tag assignment records of all questions posted on Stack Overflow by the end of the sampling period. In the second step a question-level complexity measure is calculated from the tags of a question; in the third step question-level measures are averaged to the individual-month level. The equations in the payload are unreadable, so the exact formulas are not recorded.

DL is a binary variable that equals 1 for developers interested in deep learning and subject to the influence of AlphaGo's win (the treatment sample) and 0 for those interested in machine learning excluding deep learning (the control sample). AlphaGo denotes the months before and after the shock, with a value of 0 for all months before March 2016 (the month of the shock) and a value of 1 for all months after. The interaction term DL × AlphaGo identifies the treatment effect of AlphaGo's win.

Operationalized by the diversity of a developer's tag assignment in deep learning or machine learning-related questions before the observation window, which represents the developer's existing knowledge relevant to the focal methods. The search concentration of deep learning and machine learning-related questions across different tags is calculated using the Herfindahl-Hirschman concentration index; the complement of this index (i.e., 1 minus the index) represents developers' prior search breadth.

Represents developers' active trials with previously unknown or unused tags. The developer-specific tag assignment history between account creation and the start of the observation window is reconstructed for each developer; each assignment of novel tags by a given developer in each month of the observation period is then identified. The number of previously unassigned tags tried by a developer each month, weighted by all of the questions posted by that developer in the corresponding month, captures the developer's overall experimentation intensity with unfamiliar knowledge.
time_window: monthly during the observation period, based on tag history before the observation window

description: Dichotomous variable that takes on the value of unity if any of the citations referenced by a particular subsidiary patent are to prior patents generated by the headquarters organization, and zero otherwise. A headquarters patent is defined as a patent that is assigned to the parent firm and whose first inventor is located in the home base of the firm. The authors note that the measure captures a process of adaptation rather than mere adoption, as indicated by the issuance of a patent to the subsidiary for its own work.
scale: dummy (1 = cites a prior headquarters patent; 0 otherwise)

description: The subsidiary's share of total company patents in the particular technical field of the citing patent, by application year of the citing patent. It is calculated based on the company's patenting profile in the same year as the subsidiary's patent application, with a subsidiary's larger share taken to indicate greater capability in that field relative to other units in the company. Technical fields are defined by a concordance between the approximately 400 patent classes in the U.S. patent classification system and 33 broad fields of technology.
time_window: application year of the citing subsidiary patent

description: Dummy variable equal to 1 if the citing subsidiary patent is in a technical field in which the subsidiary's home country has an RTA greater than 1 in the application year, and 0 otherwise. Raw RTA scores were calculated in the same year as the subsidiary patent and based on the full set of 400 patent classes, then converted to dummy variables. The RTA index is a location's share of patents in a technical field relative to that location's share across all fields; the text presents the formula in notation that is only partly readable.
scale: dummy (1 = home country RTA greater than 1; 0 otherwise)
time_window: application year of the citing subsidiary patent

description: Dummy variable equal to 1 if the citing subsidiary patent is in a technical field in which the United States has an RTA greater than 1 in the application year, and 0 otherwise. Based on the revealed technological advantage index calculated for the host country in the same year as the subsidiary patent.
scale: dummy (1 = host country RTA greater than 1; 0 otherwise)
time_window: application year of the citing subsidiary patent

description: Dummy variable equal to 1 if the citing subsidiary patent is in a technical field in which the subsidiary's host state has an RTA greater than 1 in the application year, and 0 otherwise. It is a proxy for patterns of local technological specialization within the subsidiary's immediate geographic locale.
scale: dummy (1 = host state RTA greater than 1; 0 otherwise)
time_window: application year of the citing subsidiary patent

description: A count-based measure: the log of the total number of patents issued to the focal subsidiary across all technical fields, measured in the application year of the citing subsidiary patent. The authors use it as a proxy for the scale of the unit's technical effort, while noting the implicit assumption of equality in the propensity to patent across technical fields.
time_window: application year of the citing subsidiary patent

description: The log of the number of days between the application date of the citing subsidiary patent and the application date of the subsidiary's first patent. The authors acknowledge that the measure suffers from left censoring of the first patent application date, since the earliest patent application in the data base was filed in the early 1970s.
time_window: from the subsidiary's first patent application to the citing patent application

description: The log of the total number of patents issued to all U.S.-based units (including acquisitions and joint ventures) belonging to the company, measured in the application year of the citing subsidiary patent. The number of patents issued to the focal subsidiary is subtracted out of the company's U.S. total before taking the log, so that the measure captures the parent's network independent of the subsidiary's own technical scale.
time_window: application year of the citing subsidiary patent

description: Dichotomous measure of whether the cited invention was developed by inventors in the home base of the firm, i.e., the home country of the parent. The fundamental unit of analysis is a patent citation, and all intrafirm citations (to headquarters, other subsidiaries, or the citing subsidiary itself) were excluded from the statistical analysis.
scale: dummy (1 = citation originates in the home country; 0 otherwise)

description: Dichotomous measure of whether the cited invention was developed by inventors in the host country, i.e., anywhere in the United States. It is one of three geographic dependent variables derived from the geographic information contained on each citation listed by a U.S. subsidiary's patent.
scale: dummy (1 = citation originates anywhere in the U.S.; 0 otherwise)

description: Dichotomous measure of whether the cited invention was developed by inventors in the U.S. state in which the subsidiary is based, the 'host state'. The authors note that political boundaries do not necessarily correspond to boundaries of economic regions, and they also experimented with measures at the level of the 'economic area'.
scale: dummy (1 = citation originates in the subsidiary's host state; 0 otherwise)

description: Each of the nine commodity exchange markets was classified as a spin-off or a startup. Spin-offs are defined as organizations where the controlling packet of stock (51% or more) was owned by one individual extant organization, and their founders came from former state suppliers and state agencies; startups were created by economic outsiders from research institutes, universities or Party youth organizations.

The density, or extent of overlap of social ties in the founding groups, is measured as a proportion of the number of asymmetrical ties between market organizers. T equals the total number of actual ties in the network, measured as the sum of the numbers given in answers to the question: how many of the organizers in the group did you know before you joined it. The paper gives the exact specification only in a formula whose rendering is unreadable here.
level: founding group of a commodity exchange

description: Diversity was calculated as a Herfindahl index of concentration (Blau 1977) which ranges from 0 (complete diversity) to 1 (uniformity) and was applied here to founder education. Educational categories included engineering, management, theoretical physics, computer science, social science and humanities.
level: founding group of a commodity exchange

description: The number of founders in each exchange's organizing committee (org komitet). The list of founding network members was corroborated by asking each member surveyed to confirm the network membership list, and only in one instance was an additional name proposed that others did not accept.
level: founding group of a commodity exchange

description: The diversity of the client-base is a Herfindahl index based on the client firms' placement in one of seven categories: large state producer, small state producer, small private producer, state trader, private trader, state administrative organ, and service provider. The diversity of industry is the analogous index based on ten categories, including energy, electronics, heavy equipment, autos, light hardware and foodstuffs. Both indices range from 0 (complete diversity) to 1 (uniformity), so higher values indicate a more concentrated client-base.

Clients were asked, among other things, about their motives for trading, and the study compares member-firms' concern with price, with profit-making and with the reliability with which trades are actualized across the two exchange types. The authors also describe clients of startup exchanges as committed less to past traditions than to profitable arbitrage and as more willing to bear the risks of arms-length trading.

variable_name: reliability with which trades are actualized
description: A motive item collected in the client survey measuring member-firms' concern with the reliability with which trades are actualized at their exchange; the study compares this concern across startup and spin-off exchange clients.

Average monthly trading volume computed from the daily transaction statistics of each commodity exchange, used together with the number of sales as a performance measure because of rampant reporting problems associated with tax evasion.
Variability in prices paid for one unit of the same product within an exchange, measured as a coefficient of variation and computed from the daily transaction statistics.

Sample firms were placed in one of three subsample groups according to their acquisition strategy. A firm was classified as marketing-related when at least two-thirds of its individual acquisitions had a primary marketing link, indicated when the merging firms' main businesses shared common or similar channels of distribution and/or marketing approaches. As a confirming second step, integration with the parent at the group level, becoming part of a group organized around the same channels or markets, was considered to indicate a marketing link. Two raters agreed on over 90 percent of the 64 firms, and where agreement was not present a third rating determined the final classification.

A conglomerate link was considered to exist through a process of elimination: if neither marketing nor technological links were present between the firm's main business and the acquired firm, the acquisition was considered to be conglomerate in nature. As a confirming second step, the establishment of a new, autonomous unit was considered to indicate a conglomerate acquisition. Firms were classified as belonging to the conglomerate category as long as two-thirds of their individual acquisitions were linked in this way.

A technological link was assumed to exist when the main business of both merging firms had common or similar manufacturing procedures or product technology. As a confirming second step, integration into a division, or a group with a common technology, was considered to indicate a technological link. Firms were classified as belonging to the technology-related category as long as two-thirds of their individual acquisitions were linked in this way.

Calculated for 1965 and 1979 by dividing the employment figure of a firm in a particular industry by the total employment for that industry; the 1965 firm figures come from the Fortune Plant and Product Directory and industry employment from the 1966 Annual Survey of Manufacturers, while 1979 values are based on market share figures available from the EIS data file. These market share figures, for each firm in each of its industries, are then multiplied by the industry weights for each company and then summed, giving each firm's weighted average market share.

Assessed for the year 1966 and 1977. Concentration ratios are calculated by comparing the value of shipments for an entire industry to those of the four leading firms. The concentration ratios of each industry a firm is involved in are multiplied by the weights representing the proportion of the firm's total sales accounted for by each industry, and the resulting values are summed to give a single weighted average industry concentration ratio for each firm. The data are derived from the Census of Manufacturers for 1977.

An index indicating the average annual dollar growth in shipments for the industries a particular firm operated in compared to the growth for all manufacturing industries during the same period. The percentage growth rates of each industry were weighted and summed; this figure is then divided by the average growth rate for all manufacturing industries. The index is calculated for 1964-68 and 1974-78, and the data are derived from the Annual Survey of Manufacturers.

Calculated by placing industry value-added over industry fixed assets and inventory, giving an approximation of return on assets (ROA) for each industry at the three-digit SIC code level. The industry ROA figures are multiplied by the industry weights for each company and then summed, and the figure is then divided by the average ROA for all manufacturing industries, making industry profitability relative to the average profitability of all manufacturing industries. The data were taken from 1964, 1967, 1969 and 1974, 1976, 1978, from the same source as for industry growth.

The change in the firm's weighted average market share between 1965 and 1979, i.e. the difference between the 1979 and 1965 values of the market share variable. It is one of the four change variables used to assess whether strategies differ in changes in market position during the research period.

The change in the firm's weighted average industry concentration ratio between 1965 and 1979, i.e. the difference between the 1979 and 1965 values of the industry concentration variable. It is one of the four change variables used to compare changes in market position across strategies.

The change in the firm's weighted average industry growth index between 1965 and 1979, i.e. the difference between the 1979 and 1965 values of the industry growth variable. It is one of the four change variables used to compare changes in market position across strategies.

The change in the firm's weighted average industry profitability index between 1965 and 1979, i.e. the difference between the 1979 and 1965 values of the industry profitability variable. It is one of the four change variables used to compare changes in market position across strategies.

Years since leaving the franchisor, the classification variable that captures the impact of having left the franchise system. It was formed by comparing the franchisee mailing lists from 1990 and 1995 to identify owner-managers who left the system. In the six-year panel establishments may contribute multiple posttreatment observations with the variable increasing over time; in the 1994 cross-section establishments are observed once and the variable varies across establishments.

Establishment-specific propensity to execute the prescribed administrative practices, taken as the coefficient on the establishment dummy in a pooled probit regression of all practices that controls for differences in adoption across practices using practice dummies. Separate models were formed for administrative practices and entrepreneurial practices, and establishments in the right tail are fully compliant.

Establishment-specific propensity to adopt the franchisor's innovative practices, taken as the coefficient on the establishment dummy in a pooled probit regression of all practices that controls for differences in adoption across practices using practice dummies. Separate models were formed for administrative practices and entrepreneurial practices, and establishments in the right tail are fully compliant.

The sum of net owner income (profits plus owner salary) and royalties (the recurring franchise fee), gathered by the mail survey for each of six years. The authors use this measure rather than net owner income alone because the combined figure is the total monies available to the owner upon leaving the franchise system; it enters the models in natural log form, ln(total returns).

Establishment sales, gathered by the mail survey for each of six years and used in natural log form, ln(sales). The authors examine sales output as an additional metric because enterprise size may enter owners' utility and because royalties are based on a percentage of sales.

The number of active cardiologists in a given urban area, supplied by the Physicians Information System, divided by the total county population from the 2000 U.S. Census. The result is a measure of the number of cardiologists per capita, a standard measure of physician supply; specialists in urban areas with more cardiologists per capita face higher competition for referrals from local generalists.

The number of VCCs involving a given rural hospital and rival cardiology practices in the immediate prior year. To test the shape of the relationship, the authors include a squared term in the alliance involvement model.
level: dyad of cardiology practice and rural hospital, by year

description: The distance between the rural hospital and the closest rival cardiology practice. This distance may be more or less than the distance between a given cardiology practice and a specific rural hospital.
level: dyad of cardiology practice and rural hospital, by year

description: The involvement of a cardiology specialty practice in a VCC with a rural hospital in a given year. Because these referral alliances are reviewed and renewed regularly, their status can change from year to year.
level: dyad of cardiology practice and rural hospital

description: The sum of all of the trips that the specialist PSF makes to all rural hospitals in a given month. The unit of analysis is the urban cardiology practice.
scale: count of monthly visits to all rural hospitals

description: The average number of visits per month to a particular rural hospital. These visits reflect significant, nontransferable, nonrecoverable investments by the cardiologists in the specific referral alliance. The unit of analysis is the individual referral alliance involving a particular dyad of a cardiology practice and a rural hospital.
level: dyad of cardiology practice and rural hospital

description: For a given year, the total number of days in the past year that a VCC was held in an average month at a given location by rival specialists; it is determined for each pairing of cardiology practice and rural hospital separately.
level: dyad of cardiology practice and rural hospital

description: Annual competition in state legislatures measured using the Fremeth and Holburn (2010) measure, which is scaled between zero and one. The measure equals one for a perfectly competitive legislature, with an equal number of legislators in the majority and minority party, and zero for a perfectly noncompetitive legislature, where one party controls every seat. The formula used to construct the measure is not readable in the available text.

Count of young firm exit divided by the count of young firms in the prior year, constructed from the state-year level aggregate BDS data. Young firms are classified as firms that are five years old or younger. This measure allows investigation of changes in the likelihood of exit of young firms and focuses exclusively on firm death, not voluntary firm movement.

The proportion of young firm exits over total firm exits in a given state-year, constructed from the state-year level aggregate BDS data. This measure allows investigation of whether young firms are exiting disproportionately relative to older firms. It focuses exclusively on firm death and does not include voluntary firm movement.

variable_name: Count of incentives and subsidies offered to incumbents
description: At the state-year level, the count of subsidies and incentives offered by the state in the given year to incumbent firms, taken from the Good Jobs First Subsidy Tracker. Programs targeted toward universities or colleges and start-ups or young firms are excluded from the count. Subsidies and incentives of over 10 million dollars are also excluded, as such large subsidies are typically provided to large conglomerates rather than the local firms that are the focus of the research.

variable_name: Value of subsidies and incentives offered to incumbents
description: The logged dollar value of subsidies and incentives offered to incumbent firms, measured in millions of dollars, calculated from the Good Jobs First Subsidy Tracker. Programs targeted toward universities or colleges and start-ups or young firms are excluded, as are subsidies and incentives of over 10 million dollars. Specifications including the value of state and local incentives exclude 95 of 1,323 state-year observations for which the GJF data lists subsidies or incentives that were granted but is unable to verify the value of the subsidy.

The number of patents of a focal firm appearing in the list of 1,497 breakthrough patents in a given year. Breakthrough patents were identified by first scaling the forward citation counts of patents by dividing the counts by the mean value of citations of all patents in their technological subcategory granted in the same year in the NBER database, and then selecting the top 3 percent (1,497 patents) out of the 49,900 patents of all the sample firms during the observation period.

Measured with the Herfindahl-Hirschman index as applied by Lin, Chen, and Wu (2006): H = 1 - sum over i = 1 to 37 of (Xi / sum Xi) squared, where Xi is the number of patents of the alliance portfolio in technological subcategory i and there were 37 technological subcategories across which alliance portfolio patents of the sample firms were distributed. The value of H was missing when the sum of alliance portfolio patents was zero, and a low value of .05 was imputed for such observations following Cameron and Trivedi (1998).

Measured as the sum of the citation-weighted count of all alliance partners' patents successfully applied for in a given year. A weighting scheme assigned higher weights to alliances that contained a high intensity of relationships and to areas more important in the semiconductor industry such as R&D and manufacturing, and real dyadic alliances were weighted higher than multilateral alliances converted to dyadic alliances, using alliance weight (ALw) = (4 x R&D + 3 x manufacturing + 2 x cross-licensing + licensing + marketing + technology transfer) x partner weight, where partner weight (>= .25, <= 1.0) factored in the number of partners. The algebraic specification of the formula is not readable in the text provided.

Measured as the proportion of portfolio quality resources that a firm leveraged, so that the variable varied from 0 to 1; if a focal firm did not cite any of its alliance partners' patents its portfolio leverage intensity was 0, and if it cited patents of all of its portfolio partners it was 1. A lever weight (Lwij) was introduced as a multiplier, equal to 1 when focal firm i cited partner j's patents during the t - 3 to t + 3 window around alliance year t and 0 when it did not. The algebraic specification of the formula is not readable in the text provided.
time_window: t - 3 to t + 3 window around alliance year t

description: Measured using the range of the focal firm's patents across technological subcategories (Miller, Fern, & Cardinal, 2007) and computed using the Herfindahl-Hirschman index as described for portfolio resource diversity.
Measured as the focal firm's share of patents among all the patents of the sample firms in the industry in a given year.

Bankruptcy is binary: all members of the experimental group filed bankruptcy over the period and none of the members of the matched control group did so. The bankruptcy variable is for the year in which the filing occurred. Experimental firms filing Chapter 11 bankruptcy during 1990 were identified from Predicast's F & S Index of Companies.

Addresses whether the CEO concurrently serves as board chairperson (duality) or otherwise. Governance data were collected from Standard and Poor's Register of Corporations, Directors, and Executives and were measured in three periods: 5 years and 3 years prior to the bankruptcy filing and the year of the filing. The authors do not state in prose which value is coded 1.
time_window: 5 years and 3 years prior to filing and year of filing

description: The absolute number of board members coded as independent, that is, members of the board traditionally classified as outside directors who were appointed to the board prior to the current CEO's appointment. The interdependent category comprises board members traditionally classified as insiders as well as outside directors appointed by the current CEO. Collected from Standard and Poor's Register of Corporations, Directors, and Executives.
time_window: 5 years and 3 years prior to filing and year of filing

description: The proportion of the board made up of independent directors, where directors are coded as independent if they are members of the board traditionally classified as outside directors and were appointed to the board prior to the current CEO's appointment. The interdependent category comprises insiders and outside directors appointed by the current CEO. Collected from Standard and Poor's Register of Corporations, Directors, and Executives.
time_window: 5 years and 3 years prior to filing and year of filing

description: The dependent variable is the number of new chemical entities introduced by firm i in year t. Data describing these product introductions are taken from annual De Haen surveys for 1969 through 1987; the data base was screened and all NCEs introduced by firms contained in the COMPUSTAT data base were extracted. All but the first introduction of each NCE were purged, NCEs developed by a subsidiary were attributed to the parent firm, and where the developing and introducing firms differed responsibility was assigned to the developing firm. Unweighted NCE counts were used, and no company has more than three NCEs in any given year.

variable_name: Average R&D expenditure for six prior years in constant dollars (R6it)
description: R&D expenditures were taken from COMPUSTAT for the period 1969-87. For firms for which COMPUSTAT line-of-business data were available, only the part of R&D expenditures classified as SIC 2834 (pharmaceuticals) was included; when only sales line-of-business data were available, R&D was prorated according to 2834 sales as a proportion of total sales, with the 1983-1987 average ratio used for earlier years. R&D data were deflated using Mansfield's R&D deflators, with implicit GNP deflators spliced on for periods in which Mansfield's deflators were unavailable. The measure is the average of R&D expenditures for the 6 years prior to the introduction of the NCE.

Number of employees as reported by COMPUSTAT, expressed in thousands. The total firm employee count was used rather than the count of employees in the 2834 line of business, so as to capture the full effect of firm size regardless of the lines of business in which the firm participated.

Indicator that a hospital belongs to one of the actual local multihospital systems studied rather than being an independent hospital. Local systems are identified as three or more community hospitals in the same geographic market sharing common ownership, with ownership determined from the OSHPD data and the American Hospital Association Annual Guide for 1989. The analysis compares actual systems with randomly constructed pseudo systems that have the same number of hospitals and a comparable number of beds.

Sum total of six high tech service offerings, recorded as the presence or absence of each service in a hospital. The six services are magnetic resonance imaging, open heart surgery, radioisotope therapy, cardiac catheterization, therapeutic radiology, and neonatology. At the system level the service offerings of the member hospitals are aggregated.

Sum total of five service offerings that are not generally associated with a high degree of technological sophistication. The five services are deliveries, alternate birthing, pediatrics, substance abuse, and home care. They are included because a differentiation strategy might lead a system to provide substantially more or fewer of them.

Costs per admission, calculated so as to control for hospital level differences in case mix and market level differences in total costs; a case weight adjustment is used, with weights reflecting the average cost per discharge for patients with given illnesses as calculated by the U.S. Health Care Financing Administration. At the system level, COST is calculated by aggregating adjusted costs and dividing by total admissions rather than taking the simple average across hospitals. ADJUSTED COST is the residual from a multivariate regression of cost on HIGH TECH, HIGH TOUCH, MEDICAID and CHARITY.

Administrative costs as a percentage of total costs, measured as the sum of general services, fiscal services, and administrative services as reported by OSHPD. At the system level the authors aggregate costs and administrative expenses rather than taking simple averages. ADJUSTED ADMIN COST is the administrative cost measure after multivariate control for payor-mix and service offerings.

Average price-cost margin obtained from privately insured patients, computed as the Lerner index, which equals (price-cost)/price. Unit prices net of insurer discounts and unit costs are estimated for major hospital cost centers and aggregated to determine the transaction price and cost for a fixed market basket. Revenues and costs are aggregated at each cost center up to the system level to calculate system Lerner indices, and hospitals lacking adequate market basket data were excluded.

Measured by the coefficients of variation across the hospitals of a system on six variables: the ratio of nursing expenditures to total expenditures, the ratio of registered nursing expenditures to total nursing expenditures, the ratio of inpatient expenditures to total expenditures, the ratio of clinical laboratory expenditures to total expenditures, the price-cost margin, and the ratio of bad debt and charity care to total revenues. Each characteristic is first regressed on bed size and the residuals are used as the basis for calculating the coefficients of variation, with a constant added so that all residuals had positive values. The system's SYSTEMNESS score is the mean percentile score of its individual coefficients of variation, so that lower coefficients of variation correspond to higher systemness.

Net operating revenue divided by net operating expense, with revenue and expense aggregated to the system level to calculate system operating margins. Operating margin is used rather than asset based profitability measures, which the authors consider difficult to measure and interpret for nonprofit institutions. OPMARGIN2 is the operating margin controlling for the system's levels of bad debt, charity care, and provision of care to Medicaid patients.

Net income divided by the average of beginning and end of year equity of the subsidiary held by the parent, computed after applying the parent's tax rate. Business unit data were used beginning with 1973, the first year in which equity accounting was mandated, and a subsidiary had to have at least two consecutive years of complete data because a lagged return was used in the analysis. Subsidiaries with equities of at least $1,000,000 were included.

The ratio of regulatory commission expenses, largely labor-based costs incurred in producing and defending rate case requests and responding to commission inquiries, to the stockholder equity of the parent. Only costs directly attributable to the home state commission of the company were used, removing those for other states and federal agencies, and a three-year moving average was taken.
