Consistent with the conceptualization of quasi-integration as the degree of the independent agent's dedication to its focal carrier, the construct is measured in terms of the percentage of business (commercial premiums) directed to the focal carrier, an indicator consistent with John and Weitz's (1988) view of forward integration as 'percentage of direct sales to end-users'. In the analysis a transformed version of this variable is used, consistent with Caves and Bradburd (1988). The transformation is QI* = LN[QI/(100 - QI)].

Following Thompson (1967) and Heide and John (1990), this construct was measured using three indicators designed to capture the extent of planning and forecasting of the agency's business activities jointly carried out by the agency and the carrier. Respondents indicate the extent to which they jointly plan marketing strategy, new product launches and premium volumes with the focal carrier, on seven-point scales from 'significant joint action' to 'insignificant joint action'.

Board demographic diversity is the sum of three standardized Blau indexes for gender, racial, and nationality diversity. Gender diversity is calculated from the percentage of female and percentage of male directors using BoardEx data. Racial diversity uses directors' race from the ISS Directors database, classifying directors into White, African American, Asian, Hispanic, and 'other', with missing race classified from names; nationality diversity uses directors' citizenship from BoardEx, or country of first board appointment where citizenship is missing. A Blau index value of zero represents complete homogeneity, whereas higher values indicate greater diversity; the three indexes are standardized and added together.

Governance problems is a standardized index built from four prominent indicators of governance problems. CEO duality equals one if a CEO is also the chair of the board and zero otherwise; directors appointed during CEO tenure is the ratio of directors appointed during a CEO's tenure to the total number of directors on the board; average director tenure is the average duration of tenure on a board of directors; and board busyness is the ratio of the number of directors who hold three or more directorships to the total number of directors on a board. Each of the four indicators is standardized and the four are added together to obtain an overall index.

Performance problems is measured as the average shareholder returns of a firm's industry peers, based on the Fama-French 48 industry classification, minus the firm's shareholder returns. Shareholder returns equal the ratio of the share price at the end of a given year plus the value of dividends issued during that year to the share price at the beginning of the year, minus one. Higher values indicate more severe performance problems.

Hedge fund activism equals one for firm-years associated with hedge fund activism and zero otherwise. Targeting is identified through Insightia, which uses regulatory filings, activist websites, media accounts, and professional relationships to provide comprehensive information on activist hedge funds and their campaigns. Of the firm-years in the sample, 354 correspond to instances of hedge fund activism involving 253 firms targeted by 113 activist hedge funds.

To test Hypotheses 2(a) and 2(b), the authors follow Insightia to identify dedicated activist hedge funds. Following Insightia's classification, they construct a nominal variable in which a firm-year receives a value of zero if it is associated with no hedge fund activism, a value of one if it is associated with targeting by a nondedicated activist hedge fund, and a value of two if it is associated with targeting by a dedicated activist hedge fund.

Response time is measured as the number of days that have lapsed between the announcement date of a hedge fund campaign and the date the firm responds to the activist with a formal decision of how to proceed (e.g., settle with the activist or proceed to a proxy vote), as reported in Insightia. The longer a board takes to deliberate and respond to an activist, the longer the firms' response time and the higher the value.

Based on prior research and information from FactSet, target acquiescence is coded as one when a target firm undertakes clear actions that aim to enhance shareholder value (e.g., repurchasing shares, issuing dividends, or divesting business units) in response to hedge fund activism and zero otherwise.

variable_name: Positive change in the exchange rate of the host country of a subsidiary (Delta1 ERit)
description: The magnitude of the annual percentage change in the host country's exchange rates is calculated for each subsidiary as the annual mean of exchange rates at time t minus the annual mean of exchange rates at time t-1, divided by the annual mean of exchange rates of the host country at time t-1. A dummy variable is then created (depreciation: 1, appreciation: 0) to indicate that a depreciating currency is favorable for the focal subsidiary. The data of monthly exchange rates for each host country is obtained from the International Monetary Fund website.
time_window: annual change from t-1 to t

variable_name: Change in production of a subsidiary (Delta1 Pit)
description: The production change of a subsidiary is measured using the sales volume of the subsidiary, computed as the percentage change in each subsidiary's sales volume from t-1 to t. This variable is used as the dependent variable in Hypothesis 1 and as the independent variable in Hypothesis 3. Sales information for each foreign subsidiary is located from the database of the Korea Listed Companies Association.
time_window: percentage change from t-1 to t

variable_name: Change in production of other subsidiaries in the same MNC (Delta1 P-it)
description: Measured by subtracting the sales volume of a subsidiary from the total sales volume of its parent MNC, then computing the annual percentage change in sales volume for the remaining subsidiaries. In the two-stage least squares model this variable is instrumented with changes in interest rates, computed as the weighted interest rates of all other subsidiaries' host countries by total investment amount in each country, and a lagged value of the variable is also included.
time_window: annual percentage change, with a one-period lagged value used as an instrument condition

description: Return on assets (ROA) is used to measure subsidiary performance in the test of the positive impact of a subsidiary's production increase on its performance.

variable_name: Number of disasters experienced by a mine in a given year
description: Count of the disasters experienced by a mine in a given year, where a disaster is defined as a coal-mining accident resulting in one or more fatalities, coinciding with MSHA's most severe accident category. The authors report that fatal coal-mining accidents were very rare during the period, with fatal accident rates averaging close to two fatal accidents per 10 million employee-hours worked, and that a total of 938 fatal coal-mining accidents occurred during the sampling period.

variable_name: Minor accidents at one- to five-year lags
description: Counts of reportable mining accidents that did not result in permanent disability or death experienced by the focal mine, included in the analysis at one- to five-year lags. Such minor accidents were much more common than fatal accidents; 65,126 minor accidents occurred during the sampling period, making them about 70 times more common than fatal accidents. Five years was selected as the maximum lag length because preliminary analyses found that none of the counts had a significant impact at lags greater than five years.

variable_name: Fatal accidents at one- to five-year lags
description: Counts of the disasters (fatal accidents) previously experienced by the focal mine, included in the analysis at one- to five-year lags. Five years was selected as the maximum lag length because preliminary analyses found that none of the counts had a significant impact on the dependent variable at lags greater than five years.

variable_name: Others' fatal accidents at one- to five-year lags
description: Lagged counts of the total number of fatal coal-mining accidents in the United States, excluding those experienced by the focal mine, included at one- to five-year lags. These variables index prior vicarious experience with fatal accidents at other mines. Year dummies are not included in the models testing hypotheses concerning vicarious learning because they are collinear with industry-level disaster counts.

variable_name: GMO approval events by the USDA
description: The dependent variable is the event of GMO approval by the USDA, analyzed as the rate of petition approval in an event-history analysis. Data on petitions came from the USDA's Animal and Plant Health Inspection Service and contain information on the petitioning firm, the species or crop in question, the date the request was received, the start and end dates of the Federal Register comment period, the status of the request, whether the application contains confidential business information, and the phenotype category and genotype of the material.

A count variable equal to the number of letters the USDA received from farm associations requesting product approval; each letter represented a particular farm association. About 34 percent of the petitions received farm association endorsements. Information on farm association requests was obtained from the USDA.

A binary variable indicating whether the product received an FDA memorandum letter prior to the USDA decision. The authors read all FDA consultation memoranda and found them to consist of a standard form letter declaring the GMO nutritional labeling acceptable. About 35 percent of the petitions received a completed FDA consultation memorandum prior to the USDA decision; information on FDA consultations was obtained from the FDA.

Measured using Congressional Quarterly's forecasts for Senate and House contests. The competitiveness measure is a four-point variable: 0 indicates a safe seat, 1 that a particular candidate is favored, 2 that the race is leaning toward a particular candidate, and 3 that there is no clear favorite. All Senate and House races were averaged to create a composite yearly score.

Measured by summing the annual number of protests against GMOs reported in local and national US newspapers using the Lexis-Nexis newspaper database. The authors argue this is a reliable measure of the potential of protesters to gain support among various audiences, because protests that receive no media attention are apt to be invisible to the broader public.
A dummy variable indicating whether a petitioning firm was of non-US origin.

A binary variable representing whether the genetic transformation used to create a GMO was fundamentally different from that of a previously approved organism. The USDA records this information in its registry of GMO petitions.

Cumulative abnormal returns (CAR) on the target's stocks over the trading days around the deal announcement, using the event study method described in Brown and Warner (1985). Market model parameters are estimated on the period from 260 to 20 trading days before the announcement, and the CRSP value-weighted index is used to measure market returns. At least 100 days with nonmissing returns during the estimation period and nonmissing returns in each day of the event window are required. The baseline window is [-1, 1] and the variable is winsorized at the 1st and 99th percentiles.
time_window: [-1, 1] trading days around the deal announcement; market model estimated from 260 to 20 trading days before the announcement

description: Average travel time in hours between the focal target and its DLAs at the deal announcement. Travel times are computed from the centroids of firms' CBSAs following the methodology of Giroud (2013), finding the route and means of transportation - car or plane - that optimize travel time, where variations across years are due to the introduction or removal of airline flights. Firms are assigned to the CBSA with the closest centroid to their headquarters' zip code. DLAs are the latent acquirers more than 300 miles from the focal target, identified as the five firms with the highest predicted probability of bidding for the target.

Average travel time in hours between the focal acquirer and its DLTs at the deal announcement. Travel times are computed from the centroids of firms' CBSAs in the same way as for the target. DLTs are the latent targets more than 300 miles from the focal acquirer, identified as the five firms with the highest predicted probability of receiving a bid from the acquirer.

The number of competing bids for the target following the first bid. In the sample of this study only 4.6% of the deals have observed competing bids; among deals with competing bidders, the average number of competing bidders is 1.2. The variable is analyzed with Poisson pseudo-likelihood regressions that include time-constant CBSA and industry fixed effects and year fixed effects.
time_window: following the first bid for the target

description: Months of work experience in the currently held occupation, reconstructed from each applicant's employment application and résumé. Restrictive criteria were used for assessing sameness of occupation, and in ambiguous cases occupation was treated as missing. The variable was logged to better fit the diminishing marginal value of experience.

Months of work experience in the property and casualty sector of the insurance industry prior to employment at InsurCo, reconstructed from each applicant's employment application and résumé. Employers were assigned an industry using NAICS codes listed in Compustat for publicly held employers and web searches for employers not listed in Compustat. The variable was logged to better fit the diminishing marginal value of experience.

Elapsed months between hire into the firm and the end of data collection (May 2003). The authors note that experience-based learning theory rests on the number of times a task is performed rather than a time-based measure such as tenure, but argue that a time-based measure better accounts for experience at the job rather than the task level. The variable was logged to account for diminishing returns to experience.

Average of the ratings for 11 dimensions of competence from the employee's most recent job competency evaluation, in which supervisors and HR managers evaluate work product such as case files and recorded phone interactions. Each area is rated on a scale of 1 to 5, with 5 being the highest level of competence. A principal factors factor analysis showed all 11 items loaded on a single factor accounting for 91% of the total variance, with a Cronbach's alpha of 0.95.

The employee's most recent annual performance review rating, quantified with an ordinal number from 6 ('clearly exceeds') to 1 ('development needs'). Reviews are done annually at the worker's anniversary date using a standardized form that calls for assessing achievement versus individual goals; the supervisor's initial draft is revised by upper levels of management and the HR director to ensure comparability across supervisors.
time_window: most recent review prior to the end of data collection

description: Cumulative count of the number of shareholder proposals initiated, coded at the firm level of analysis. Comparable cumulative counts were coded for proposals opposed, proposals challenged, and proposals settled.

Composite measure built from KLD data, which analysts rate each company on using an objective set of screening criteria applied consistently to all companies. Following prior research, the authors used KLD's community, diversity, employee relations, environment, and product quality ratings, adding the strengths and subtracting the weaknesses for a composite measure.

Ordered categorical variable coded from IRRC News for Investors. The authors classified instances of omissions as challenges, voting as opposition, and withdrawal as settling, except that proposals withdrawn because proponents believed they would be successfully challenged at the SEC were classified as challenges. For Hypothesis 2, responsiveness was coded as an ordered categorical variable taking the values 1 (challenge), 2 (oppose), and 3 (settle).

Cumulative count of the number of shareholder proposals settled, coded at the firm level of analysis. Proposals were classified as settling when they were withdrawn and were not withdrawn because proponents believed the proposal would be successfully challenged at the SEC.

variable_name: Proponent ownership, shareholder group affiliation, stakeholder issue
description: Proponent ownership is a dummy coded 1 for larger-block shareholders (more than 1,000 shares) and 0 otherwise; owners were classified as larger block in all firms if they owned larger blocks in at least one firm, and as smaller block if their ownership stake could not be determined in any firm, because proxy rules do not require disclosure of advocates' ownership percentage. Shareholder group affiliation is a dummy coded 1 for proposals coordinated with the ICCR or affiliated with the CII, and 0 otherwise, determined from the IRRC's News for Investors and organizational websites. Stakeholder issue is coded 0 if the proposal concerned a social issue and 1 if it concerned primary stakeholders.

Percentage difference between the offer price and the target firm's stock price four weeks before deal announcement. To correct for outliers, premium data were Winsorized between 0 and 200 percent. It is the dependent variable of the second-stage regression and the outcome predicted in the first-stage hedonic regression.

The premium paid by another firm that made the acquisition directly preceding the focal deal in a given country and target industry (established by four-digit SIC code), calculated like the focal premium. Entering the second stage as the deviation between the preceding premium and the predicted focal premium, it identifies the anchoring effect.
time_window: the acquisition directly preceding the focal deal

description: Calculated by the number of days between the preceding and focal deal, then reversed so that higher values corresponded to more recent preceding deals. It is entered as a main term and in interaction with the anchoring effect.
time_window: days between the preceding and focal deal

description: The percentage difference between the deal values of the preceding and focal deals. The absolute value was taken to make it consistent for both large and small focal deals, and the measure was reversed so that larger values indicated more similar deal sizes. It is entered as a main term and in interaction with the anchoring effect.
A dummy variable used to distinguish international acquirers from domestic acquirers, entered as a main term and in interaction with the anchoring effect.

Count of completed acquisitions that the firm made in the focal target industry prior to the acquisition, capturing related instead of unrelated experience. It is entered as a main term and in interaction with the anchoring effect.
Measured by counting the average number of acquisitions in the two years prior to the focal deal. It is entered as a main term and in interaction with the anchoring effect.
time_window: two years prior to the focal deal

variable_name: number of collaborative publications with host country
description: The number of publications a nonmigrant scientist has with coauthors from the fellow's (or unsuccessful applicant's) host country in each year, generated from the scientist's publication record. The outcome is a per-scientist per-year count that is inverse hyperbolic sine transformed in the regressions, so coefficients can be interpreted as elasticities.
time_window: each year over the three years before and six years after the fellowship (or unsuccessful application)

variable_name: number of new collaborative relationships with host country
description: The number of new coauthoring relationships a nonmigrant scientist forms with scientists from the fellow's (or unsuccessful applicant's) host country in each year; if the focal nonmigrant scientist collaborated with a scientist from the host country for the first time in a given year, that counted as one new coauthoring relationship that year. The count is inverse hyperbolic sine transformed in the regressions.
time_window: each year over the three years before and six years after the fellowship (or unsuccessful application)

description: Indicator for whether the fellow's (or unsuccessful applicant's) home country had high gender parity in the year of fellowship or application. Gender parity is measured with the Gender Development Index from the United Nations Development Programme, covering 162 countries from 1995 to 2019, which measures gender inequality in health (female and male life expectancy at birth), education (expected years of schooling for children and mean years of schooling for adults 25 and older), and command over economic resources (female and male estimated earned income). Following the UNDP definition, countries were classified as having low equality between men and women if they had an absolute deviation from gender parity of more than 10%, and missing country-years were interpolated.
time_window: year of the fellowship (or unsuccessful application)

description: Indicator for whether the fellow's (or unsuccessful applicant's) host country had high gender parity in the year of fellowship or application. Gender parity is measured with the Gender Development Index from the United Nations Development Programme, which measures gender inequality in health, education, and command over economic resources. Following the UNDP definition, countries were classified as having low equality between men and women if they had an absolute deviation from gender parity of more than 10%, and missing country-years were interpolated.
time_window: year of the fellowship (or unsuccessful application)

description: Announcements of CEO changes were identified from the Wall Street Journal 'Who's News' section. For each event the firm name, announcement date, and successor origin were noted, and the announcement date was designated day 0 for the event study.

The firm's return-generating process is modeled as the market model, in which the security's return is a linear function of the return on a portfolio of all risky assets. Residuals which deviate significantly from zero indicate a firm's abnormal return after controlling for the overall market return, and t-tests of the difference between the residuals and zero are run before, at, and after the announcement. To reduce the noise inherent in individual firm reactions, the sample firms were combined in a portfolio approach for insider and outsider successors, and the average estimated residuals are cumulated over event time.
time_window: 30 days before and after the announcement (event day 0)

description: The Chow ANCOVA test asks whether two sets of observations (the pre-succession and post-succession regressions) belong to the same regression model. The sum of squares of the residuals assuming equality of coefficients is compared with the sum of squares without assuming equality, and the ratio of the difference to the latter sum, adjusted for degrees of freedom, is distributed as an F ratio under the null hypothesis. The test is performed on the 300 days before and after the announcement and controls for both a firm's prior performance and the overall market performance.
time_window: 300 days before and after the announcement

description: Each CEO change announcement was classified by whether the successor was an insider, an outsider, or unannounced, with unannounced successors excluded from the final sample. The final sample is composed of 184 insider and 25 outsider successions, and the event study portfolios were formed separately for insider and outsider successor firms.

Multimarket contact is assessed based on the number of FDA product categories in which the firm and its rival both had products approved during a 5-year window from the year of application. The authors use market overlap rather than a scaled measure to facilitate interpretation of the results. Product code overlap is considered to help ensure that both firms are actively developing products in the markets where they overlap.
time_window: 5-year window from the year of application; t-1

description: Dichotomous dependent variable set to '1' if the focal firm filed a patent lawsuit against a specific rival firm in observation year t and to '0' otherwise. Patent lawsuits are identified from records where each firm was listed as a plaintiff or defendant.

variable_name: Focal firm's technological quality of knowledge (citations per patent)
description: Measured using the focal firm's 5-year average number of citations per patent, where the focal firm's number of citations received during the previous 5 years was divided by the number of patents that received citations during the previous 5 years.

variable_name: Rival's ability to protect its knowledge (lawsuits as plaintiff % patents)
description: Measured using the rival firm's yearly number of patent lawsuits as plaintiff scaled by the rival firm's total number of patent applications, since rival firms that have initiated patent litigation have demonstrated the ability to protect their knowledge-based resources.

Binary variable that equals one if the focal firm was founded during or after the year 2000 and zero otherwise. The authors use 2000 as the focal date for the creation of the new growth exchanges because that was the year in which firms were first able to list on those exchanges, when the Tokyo Stock Exchange and the Osaka Stock Exchange opened MOTHERS and JASDAQ (later HERCULES) with easier listing requirements compared to their parent exchanges.

Binary variable equal to one if the focal firm is engaged in a technical business and zero otherwise. The authors note that this coding reflects only the classification of a firm into an industry category and is not reflective of the firm's innovativeness or other technical qualities.

The log value of the opening capital account when the firm was founded, in thousands of constant 2009 yen, obtained from the COSMOS 3 database. The authors select initial capital to represent the commitment of financial resources that providers and stakeholders make to the firm at its outset.

The compound annual growth rate of sales revenue since founding. The authors use a standard compound annual growth rate calculation that takes the nth root of the total percentage growth rate, in which n is the number of years in the period considered, using a beginning value of 1 yen.

Scientific reputation was measured with two proxies: publication counts and citation rates. Publication counts is the number of publications each founding chief scientist published prior to the date in which a focal alliance was formed in the 12 leading biotechnology journals identified by a survey of 40 biotechnology scientists at five universities; for companies with more than one founding chief scientist it is the average number of publications. Citation counts is the natural log of the total number of times a founding chief scientist was cited in other articles prior to the formation of the focal alliance, averaged across founding chief scientists. Because the two measures were highly correlated (r = 0.65), the reported results use a factor score obtained from a principal factor analysis of the two measures (one factor, eigenvalue 1.84).
scale: publication count; natural log of citation count; factor score
level: founding chief scientist, averaged to the biotechnology company
time_window: prior to the formation of the focal alliance

description: Status was measured using the academic status of the school from which the founding chief scientist graduated with an advanced degree. The latest available US News and World Report rankings of doctoral programs in the biological sciences were used for each year; the rankings, which run from 1 to 30, were reverse coded so that the higher a school's ranking the higher its status, and averaged for companies with more than one founding chief scientist. To remove the halo effect of prior performance, the authors ran a preliminary multiple regression of the reputation variables on the status scores, used the coefficients to build a predictive model for status, and subtracted that model from the observed ranking scores, producing halo-removed status ratings used in the models.
level: founding chief scientist, averaged to the biotechnology company
time_window: latest rankings available for each year; degree obtained before the focal alliance

description: Each dyad had a dummy variable indicating whether the incumbent and the biotechnology firm formed an alliance with each other in the given year. To predict alliance formation, biotechnology companies that did form alliances were compared with those that could have formed alliances but did not, supplementing the sample of alliances actually formed with a random sample of 300 potential alliances that might have formed but never did; the risk set was created from yearly CorpTech lists of all U.S. biotechnology companies from 1990 to 2003. The combined sample of 575 alliances was used to estimate each alliance's likelihood of formation.

The timing model predicted the stage in the commercialization in which each alliance was formed. Biotechnology commercialization is divided into nine stages (Office of Technology Assessment, 1993) indicating the degree to which a technology has been developed, running from first discovery and early development to the introduction of a product. Information about the stage of each product in each alliance was obtained from Recap, which determines it from press releases or the alliance's agreement and, when lacking, from its analysts' own research using sources such as company websites and SEC filings. The different stages were treated as a set of ordered categories, predicting in which of these stages the alliance was formed.
scale: nine ordered stages; lower values indicate earlier stages
time_window: stage at the time the alliance was signed (1990-2003)

description: To correct the timing analysis for sample selection bias, parameters from the formation model were used to calculate each alliance's likelihood of formation, which was included as a control (lambda) in the timing analysis.

The measure captures the breadth of knowledge domains that are combined in an invention. Two graduate students with engineering or science undergraduate degrees classified all inventors into the 172 scientific specializations used by ISI on the basis of the schools and departments in which they were employed, with disagreements resolved by consulting experts. Science distance was calculated as one minus the proximity value calculated using the science proximity matrix of cross-citation patterns between the 172 subject categories, so that high values represent limited cross-citation between two fields. The dyadic distance of every pair of inventors was aggregated and averaged across all dyads to get a team-level measure. Science distance is bounded by 0 and 1, with 0 indicating that all inventors are in domains with high knowledge overlap and 1 indicating little overlap between inventors' knowledge domains.
time_window: static measure based on data from the end of the sample period in 2006

description: Prior licensing experience for a team was measured as the total number of prior licenses held by its members from 1960 until the time of licensing or censoring, as appropriate, divided by team size.

Measured as the proportion of dyads in an inventor team with prior collaboration experience. The authors counted the dyads who had worked together prior to the licensing date or censoring date, as appropriate, and divided this count by the total possible number of dyads in an inventor team. The variable ranges from 0 to 1, where 0 implies no inventors have worked together before and 1 implies that all the inventors have worked together before.
time_window: until the licensing date or censoring date

description: The dependent variable is the licensing odds for a given invention, estimated as the survival odds of an invention, that is, the odds that an invention survives in the observation period without a licensing event. Survival odds are the inverse of licensing odds; coefficients that are negative and significant imply that an increase in the independent variable leads to an increased hazard of licensing. Disclosures are right censored, and multiple failure events (multiple licenses of the same disclosure) are controlled for.
time_window: from disclosure to licensing or censoring

description: A dummy variable with a value of '1' indicating that a private firm was privatized from an SOE and '0' indicating that a private firm was founded as private. It was constructed from the survey question 'Was your company privatized from an existing state-owned or collectively owned firm?', where collective enterprises were one type of relatively small SOEs controlled by local governments.

The logarithm of the amount of charitable contributions a firm reported having made since its registration as a private firm, as asked in the 2006 and 2008 surveys. The authors calculated the logarithm of charitable contributions as their measure. The face-to-face interview method and the strong official backing for the survey were used to encourage honest and precise answers.
time_window: since registration as a private firm

description: A dummy variable with a value of '1' indicating that the current owner of a privatized SOE had laid off workers and '0' otherwise. It was created from the survey question 'How did you obtain your firm?', one answer being ''zero' acquisition - paid nothing to take over an SOE by using its assets to pay off debts and reemploying laid-off employees.' The measure is only for the subsample of privatized SOEs.

The unemployment rate in the province where a privatized SOE was located in the year before its registration as private, measured using firms' postal codes reported in the surveys. Capturing a firm's location at the province level is defended by the authors on the grounds that provinces in China are independent of each other and have relatively homogenous within-province economic conditions.
time_window: the year before the firm's registration as private

description: A dummy variable with a value of '1' for firms choosing the two answers to 'How did you obtain your firm?' that suggest possible involvement in privatization - 'Obtained by the original leaders of the SOE' and 'Obtained by the SOE's employees or managers with major ownership' - and '0' otherwise. The measure is only for the subsample of privatized SOEs.

The provincial number of jinshi - candidates who succeeded in the national civil service exam (keju) - assigned to provinces according to residential addresses, weighted by the provincial population in 1880. Systematic data are available for all 112 jinshi exams in the Qing Dynasty (1644-1911). The authors note that this specification might reflect the Qing government's fixed jinshi quota for each province rather than the actual influence of Confucianism.

The provincial number of weike (the first few spots of each national exam) assigned to provinces according to residential addresses, weighted by the provincial population in 1880. Weike was not influenced by the quota system but determined by the performance of candidates on exams and is thus likely to better reflect the actual effort of studying for the civil service entrance exam.

Tenure of a privatized SOE's current leader in the SOE that he or she privatized, estimated as registration year - (birth year + start age), where birth year is the survey year minus the leader's age and start age is 18 in the reported test. The estimation assumes that the current leader of a privatized SOE stayed in the same SOE, which the authors note overestimates tenure for those violating this assumption. The measure is only for the subsample of privatized SOEs.
time_window: from entry into the SOE to registration as private

description: Coding of whether an informant confirmed that his or her laid-off SOE workers experienced great distress, derived from the transcripts and tabulated across informants. All of the informants but two confirmed that their laid-off SOE workers experienced great distress. Informants recalled difficulties such as being unable to find a new job due to highly specialized skills, a complete lack of skills, or a drastic drop in social status.

Coding of whether an informant described feeling guilt or nei jiu toward laid-off SOE workers, derived from the transcripts and tabulated across informants. Twenty-one of the 25 informants said that they experienced a feeling of guilt. Informants alluded to reasons such as 'not leading them well', 'not fighting for more compensation for them', or 'their sacrificing for the reform'.

Coding of whether an informant described guilt-driven engagement in philanthropy, derived from the transcripts and tabulated across informants. Eighteen of 25 informants confirmed that guilt felt toward laid-off SOE workers influenced firm leaders' and their firms' subsequent engagement in philanthropy. Restitution was made predominantly as a part of corporate philanthropy rather than as a personal endeavor.

Subjects' answers to questions about the guilt they felt toward laid-off SOE employees, collected after the vignette and adopted from Kugler and Jones (1992). The measure exhibited high reliability (Cronbach's alpha = 0.83). Guilt items were presented on a screen separate from the philanthropic intention items to reduce common method biases.

Subjects' intention to engage in philanthropy after their firm's financial conditions improved, adopted from Smith and McSweeney (2007). To reduce common method biases, the guilt and philanthropic intention items were separated into two screens and subjects were asked to imagine a new condition when answering the philanthropic intention questions. The measure exhibited high reliability (Cronbach's alpha = 0.90).

variable_name: Diff in i's and j's rating
description: For each Zagat-rated restaurant-year the authors created an overall restaurant rating as the mean of the restaurant's food, décor, and service scores on a 30-point scale (Cronbach α = 0.84). They then calculated the difference between restaurant i's and j's rating in year t − 1. Zagat volumes were released in the final quarter of the previous calendar year, so the reviews are lagged slightly more than one calendar year and are updated (time-varying) yearly.
time_window: t − 1 (lagged slightly more than one calendar year)

variable_name: Difference in sales between restaurants i and j
description: The outcome is the urban CPI-deflated difference in sales between restaurants i and j in year t, taken from restricted-access government data from the BR consisting of detailed private business information. This represents yearly sales performance differences for private firms. Reported estimates are in $1000s of urban CPI-deflated dollars.

variable_name: Post-online restaurant rating platform entry/expansion period
description: A dummy variable distinguishes the pre- and post-online restaurant rating platform entry period around the founding of Yelp in 2004 and the contemporaneous expansion of Tripadvisor and OpenTable. A second binary variable indicates the post-2010 online platform expansion period, when Yelp expanded to new international markets, as it is plausible that the ratings effect became more pronounced over time. A third, continuous variable codes all years before 2005 as 0, 2005 = 1, 2006 = 2, …, 2013 = 9, treating information as a continuous treatment rather than a discrete shock.

variable_name: Both i and j located in a tourist area
description: The authors extrapolate areas frequented by tourists by identifying areas with a high concentration of hotels relative to city residents. They tabulated the 20 largest hotels by available beds in New York City by zip code, all of which fall in zip codes denoted as tourist neighborhoods, and used US Census population data to calculate the ratio of residents in tourist versus residential zip codes. A binary measure denotes that both restaurants in a dyad are located in an area designated as tourist-concentrated, a designation covering sites such as the Broadway Theater District, Times Square, the southern part of Central Park, and the World Trade Center/Freedom Tower.

variable_name: Both i and j in the $$$$ price tier
description: An indicator variable denotes that both restaurants in a dyad are in the highest price-tier ($$$$), corresponding to the 'very expensive' price point designated by Zagat and later Yelp. Price reflects the average sale price per customer for dinner including one drink and tip, derived from survey responses from all consumers rating a particular restaurant in a given year, and all price figures are deflated using the urban CPI for cross-year comparability.

Keyword searches of newspapers and wire databases using terms such as 'fire,' 'gas leak,' 'explosion,' 'chemical spill,' 'chemical release,' and 'chemical discharge' uncovered 359 possible accidents. Accidents were qualified only when the date, magnitude, location and responsible firm could be determined; accidents related to petroleum transport and refining, accidents that caused neither injury nor death, the Bhopal event, and events confounded with other corporate news were removed, leaving 92 accidents.

The abnormal return of a stock is the difference between the actual return of that stock and its expected return, estimated from a market model relating each company's stock value to the CRSP value-weighted index with dividends, with beta computed over t = -254 to t = -1. The cumulative abnormal return is the sum of abnormal returns over the event window, with ln(1 + R) used in place of R to allow for continuous compounding. The event window begins on the day of the accident if it occurred during trading hours on a trading day and otherwise on the next trading day, and closes on the fifth day after the event.
time_window: event window of five days after the accident; beta estimated over t = -254 to t = -1

description: A dummy variable that captures the time period from the beginning of the sample through the end of 1984, when the Bhopal leak occurred; events occurring in this period were coded 1 and those occurring later were coded 0. A value of 1 therefore indicates the period before the major crisis and a value of 0 the period after it.

To capture the post-Responsible Care period, the authors created a dummy variable coded 1 if after 1989 and 0 otherwise. Aspects of the Responsible Care program began shortly after the Bhopal crisis, but no elements of the program were promulgated until late in 1989.

The variable ACC member was assigned a value of 1 if the ACC listed the company as a member in a given year, and 0 otherwise; from 1990 onward, participation in Responsible Care was a condition of membership in the ACC. A separate dummy variable, Responsible Care member, indicated ACC membership during a year when the Responsible Care program was in existence.

Two variables captured whether or not a firm that had an accident was a member of the American Chemistry Council (perpetrator in ACC) or of the Responsible Care program (perpetrator in Responsible Care). These variables identify the membership of the firm responsible for an accident in order to examine whether spillovers differ depending on the identity of the perpetrator.

Cumulative abnormal returns around the acquisition announcement, computed with the conventional event study methodology. A market model estimates the relationship between firm returns and equally weighted market returns over the 250 trading days starting 30 days prior to the announcement, an interval chosen to remove take-over news already incorporated in the acquiror's price. Immediate acquisition returns are the abnormal returns of the acquiring firm over a 5-day interval: the day of the announcement and the two days immediately prior to and after it. CRSP is the source of the firm and market returns data.
time_window: 250 trading days for the market model; 5-day window around the announcement

description: Security analysts working in each of the six industries were surveyed about the acquisition performance of the firms in the industry they follow. Analysts were presented with a list of a focal firm's acquisitions in chronological order, the earliest being no more than 5 years old, and asked whether they agree that a focal acquisition generated shareholder wealth, where 7 is strong agreement and 1 is strong disagreement. The measure was used only for acquisitions worth at least 5.0% of the acquiring firm's market capitalisation, and at least 2 analysts' ratings were sought for each acquisition, with analysts telephoned when the letters did not yield two ratings.
scale: Likert scale from 1 (strong disagreement) to 7 (strong agreement)
time_window: acquisitions no more than 5 years old at the time of the rating

description: A simple percentage score that calculates the percentage of prior acquisitions that conform to the most common 4 digit SIC code. If all prior acquisitions are within the same SIC code the score is 1; if no two acquisitions share the same SIC code the score is 0; if two out of the firm's four acquisitions share the same code the score is 0.5. The scores are multiplied by a factor of 10 so that their squared terms represent higher scores when the inverted U-shaped relationship is modelled.
time_window: prior acquisitions from 1985 to the focal deal

description: The number of times a firm recorded an announcement loss of less than 3%, measured by the cumulative abnormal return methodology used for the dependent variable. Announcement returns, rather than analysts' ratings, were the basis for calculating small losses because analysts' ratings data for smaller acquisitions were lacking. A firm with two prior acquisitions that yielded an abnormal loss between 0 and 3% receives a score of 2; a firm with only one such acquisition receives a score of 1.
time_window: prior acquisitions from 1985 to the focal deal

description: The mean number of days between prior acquisitions, excluding the focal acquisition. If the firm has only one prior acquisition, a maximum interval is imputed as the date of the acquisition less the date when acquisition records were first collected (January 1, 1985). The squared term of this variable is included to model the curvilinear relationship tested, and the variable is also modelled as a natural log.
time_window: prior acquisitions from 1985 to the focal deal

description: The number of days between the focal acquisition and the one before it. When the focal acquisition is the firm's only one, the same imputation procedure as for the timing of prior acquisitions is used. The inverted U-shaped relationship is modelled with the addition of a squared term.

The sum of recent acquisitions undertaken by the firm, from 1985 to the focal deal. Firms that made their first acquisition during the focal period (1990-1995) received an experience score of 0. The variable is included to control for the amount of experience since the results of the similarity measures may be according to the number of preceding acquisitions.

variable_name: product category (index, SRI, regional and industry funds)
description: The four product categories analysed are classified by their fit with institutionalized professional norms: index and SRI funds are considered counter to core analyst norms, and regional and industry funds are the closest comparable hold-out funds, fully in line with extant norms of appropriate products and introduced into the market about the same time. Both regional and industry funds are equity funds that build on the idea of active asset management and differ only in their investment objectives. The classification is grounded in the qualitative interview material on what finance professionals consider appropriate products.

variable_name: hazard of adoption (time to product adoption)
description: The dependent variable is the hazard of adoption, the marginal likelihood of a firm adopting a product category for the first time. Firms become at risk of adopting a specific product category only after there has been a first industry-pioneering adoption, and enter the risk set only after their entry into the industry; once a firm has adopted a product category it is dropped from the risk set for that category. Day, month, year and category of product adoption per firm were collected from the SSAFM, which registers all new products, so the dataset is a complete inventory of the exact timing of all products ever introduced in Sweden.

A categorical variable for the majority ownership of the firm, distinguishing three ownership groups identified from the qualitative interview data: privately held firms, union-held firms, and state-owned firms. Private ownership is the reference category. Data on ownership was coded from the archives of the SSAFM.

The analyst intensity of a firm is calculated as the ratio of equity analysts and fund managers to the number of equity funds marketed by a firm at a given point in time. Data was coded primarily from the annual member directory of the SSFA and, where necessary, supplemented by information from annual reports, interviews, and visits to the archives of the Royal Swedish Banking Inspection. All time-varying covariates are updated annually and lagged one period.

Deregulation was measured with a dummy variable that takes a value of 1 for the period October 24, 1978, through June 30, 1985, and a value of 0 otherwise. It was an independent variable in the change analysis and a control variable in the failure analysis.

Four dependent variables were used: a change from specialism to generalism and a change from generalism to specialism at the business level and at the corporate level. Business-level changes were recorded from product mix: a change from specialism to generalism when a single-product airline became a multiproduct one, and a change from generalism to specialism when a multiproduct airline became a single-product one. Corporate-level changes were recorded from airline acquisition data, with a change from specialism to generalism when an airline moved from no diversification to related or unrelated diversification or from either of those to a pattern of both, and a change from generalism to specialism when divestiture left it with no related subsidiaries, no unrelated subsidiaries, or no subsidiaries. The probabilities of these changes were modeled as marginal intensity functions r(t) = exp(BX), where X is a vector of independent variables at time t.

To calculate the age of an airline, the authors subtracted the time of founding from the time of any change in strategic orientation or failure. Airline foundings were recorded as the date of certification by the CAB for airlines founded during the regulated period and as the first date of flying operations for airlines founded before regulation or after deregulation. Age was an independent variable in the change analysis and a control variable in the failure analysis.

Organizational size was measured as the natural logarithm of airline assets at the time of any change in strategic orientation or of failure. Total assets are reported in quarterly financial reports, and the figure for the preceding quarter nearest to the time of an event was used. Airlines with subsidiaries reported only total airline assets rather than total organizational assets, so the measure is airline assets; size was an independent variable in the change analysis and a control variable in the failure analysis.

Two cumulative change variables capture the cumulative number of changes in strategic orientation at the business level that each airline had experienced up to the time of a change or failure. Because airlines report product mix data monthly to the CAB, business-level core feature changes can occur only at the end of a month, so every airline had two cumulative business-level variables that were updated monthly. They were used as independent variables in both the change and failure analyses.
time_window: updated monthly, up to the time of a change or failure

description: Two corporate cumulative change variables capture the cumulative number of changes in strategic orientation at the corporate level that each airline had experienced up to the time of a change or failure. Because data on the exact timing of acquisitions and divestitures were available, corporate-level changes could occur on any day of the observation period, so each airline had two cumulative corporate-level variables that were updated daily. They were used as independent variables in both the change and failure analyses.
time_window: updated daily, up to the time of a change or failure

description: The hazard function h(t) was the dependent variable in the analysis of the probability of failure; it represents the instantaneous probability of an event's occurring at time t, given that the event has not occurred before t. Each airline's history continued until the date it failed, and cases alive at the end of the observation period were right-censored and recorded as June 30, 1985, with censored cases assumed to occur randomly from a uniform distribution.
Respondents provided information on the number of employees who quit in 1995 and the average number of production workers employed in 1995. The ratio of the two components formed the measure.

The five HRM investments and inducements (pay level, benefits level, job stability, training, and procedural justice) were used to form the index. Pay level was the average annual pay for production workers; benefits level was the percentage of health insurance premiums paid by the company; job stability averaged two layoff items; training was the mean of six items; procedural justice was assessed with three items. The index standardized and averaged scores from the five measures, and the reliability of the linear composite was .69.

The number of labor hours worked by production employees in a focal year divided by the tons of concrete products produced in the same year. It was derived from respondent reports by multiplying the number of production employees during average, peak, and slow months by the number of regular working hours in these months, adding average overtime hours worked per employee, and dividing by tons of concrete products produced. Fewer labor hours per ton indicates better performance.
The number of 'lost-time accidents' in the plant in the last five years divided by the number of production employees. A lower accident rate indicates better performance.

Respondents provided information on the number of company drivers who had quit in the past year and the average number of company drivers during the year. The ratio of quits to total drivers represents voluntary turnover.

The aggregated composite was assessed with the same five HRM practices used in Study 1. Pay level was the average annual pay for the typical driver; benefits level was the percentage of health insurance premiums for drivers paid by a company; job stability averaged two items; training was the mean number of hours per year of formal, organization-specific training; procedural justice was assessed with five items. The index was the average of the standardized scores from the five measures, with a composite reliability of .77.

The amount of revenue generated per employee. The numerator, the average gross freight revenue for 2000 and 2001, was obtained from the Blue Book; the denominator was the total number of drivers employed by an organization, as reported in the questionnaire.

Obtained from SAFER for the two-year (2000-01) period; the number of trucks or drivers taken out of service owing to driver fault, divided by the total number of inspections times 100. It shows the frequency of violations attributable to driver mistakes and does not include factors beyond the drivers' control.
Defined as accidents per million miles driven. Total accidents for 2000-01 (SAFER) were divided by total miles driven for the same period (Blue Book) and multiplied by 1,000,000.
Total operating expenses divided by total gross revenue times 100. It was calculated as the 2000 and 2001 calendar year average. Higher values indicate worse performance.
Indicates profit on invested capital; defined as net income divided by total equity. It was calculated as the 2000 and 2001 calendar year average.

variable_name: Number of peers in primary SIC code
description: Industry self-categorization is the number of companies in a board's chosen peer group that had the same 2-digit SIC code as the board's own company. Peers chosen as published industry indices were expanded into all companies within the chosen index, and a peer's industry membership was its 2-digit SIC category with the highest percentage of company sales. When boards selected multiple peer groups, industry membership was computed using all companies present in all of the groups. A complementary variable, the number of selected peers whose 2-digit industry membership differed from the board's company, was constructed to test H5.

variable_name: Number of peer sentences in proxy
description: Peer discussion is measured as the number of sentences in the 'Report of the Compensation Committee' section of a company's 1993 proxy statement that contained at least one instance of the peer category. Coding was done with the VBPro automated content-analysis package using a category of peer-reference words and phrases built and refined iteratively (e.g., 'competitors', 'peers', 'comparison group', 'S&P'), validated by manual comparison of hits, misses and false hits on random 10-percent samples of companies. The complete text corpus consisted of a total of 12,500 sentences (mean = 42.8 per company).

Company performance was operationalized using two indices. The first is the log of the five-year total shareholder return on the company's stock for the period 1988-1992, obtained from the company performance graphs in the proxy statements using the same method as for peer-group performance. The second is the average annual return on assets from 1988 through 1992, obtained from COMPUSTAT data.

Total annual return and market capitalization data were collected from COMPUSTAT on all firms for each 2-digit SIC code represented in the sample. To estimate industry performance for a given year, each company's total annual performance (percentage change in value, including reinvested dividends) was weighted by its market capitalization for that year; the weighted values were summed and divided by the total market capitalization for the entire industry. The five annual performance measures were then used to calculate the value of a $100 investment in the industry over the previous five years, and the measure was logged.

CEO annual pay was operationalized as the sum of a CEO's 1992 base salary and bonus as reported in the company's 1993 proxy statement; annual pay was logged so that extreme values would not bias the results. Long-term compensation was operationalized as the logged gain realized by the exercise of any stock options or restricted stock by the CEO in 1992, also obtained from the 1993 proxy statements.

Owner power is a dummy variable coded 1 if there were any outsiders listed as significant shareholders in the 1993 proxy statement, and 0 otherwise. A significant shareholder was deemed to be anyone who controls 5 percent or more of the company's outstanding common stock. Consistent with SEC regulations, an outsider was defined as any individual or group who is not and never has been a member of management, is not engaged in legal or consulting activities with the company, and is neither a member nor a descendent of the company founder's family nor the representative or beneficiary of a family legal entity.

Shareholder activism is defined as the number of resolutions presented by shareholders that were to be voted on at the 1993 shareholder meeting, as listed in the company's 1993 proxy statement. Larger numbers of shareholder resolutions are indicative of greater levels of shareholder activism.

Peer-group performance is the average five-year total shareholder return of all peer groups reported in the performance graph of a company's 1993 proxy statement, representing the value on 12/31/92 of $100 invested on 1/1/88 in the stock of the companies comprising a focal company's peer groups. Annual returns for each peer group were calculated as the total return (stock price change plus reinvested dividends) weighted by the company's market value for a given year. When firms presented graphs for only one peer group, this measure represented the five-year return of that peer group.

Companies were coded as led by a charismatic CEO if the CEO was labeled charismatic by at least one of three archival sources: articles accessible through Dow Jones Interactive, organizational behavior textbooks, and scholarly journals on management and leadership. The initial sample totaled 97 CEOs; the final sample consisted of 44 CEOs of companies listed by Fortune among the 500 largest industrial or 500 largest service firms between 1985 and 1994. Companies headed by charismatic leaders were contrasted with the median companies in their respective industries.

Manipulated by having half of the subjects view a 20-minute video of Steve Jobs, CEO of Apple Computer, presenting the iMac at a large trade show before making their investment decision, while the other half made their investment decision before viewing the video. The video described the company's history and current financial position and argued that Apple was poised to make a dramatic turnaround. The authors state that the manipulation provided different levels in the salience of charisma rather than alternatives in specific leadership styles.
scale: binary (video before vs. after the investment decision)

description: At the end of the experiment subjects rated the extent to which Steve Jobs exhibited each of nine behaviors that help define charismatic leadership, using a 9-point scale ranging from 'Not at all' to 'To a great extent'. Ratings were averaged to create an overall measure of attributed charisma.
scale: 9-point scale (1 = 'Not at all' to 9 = 'To a great extent')

description: The measure started with Fortune's report of 'total return to investors', which included both price appreciation and dividend yield, and the annual dividend was subtracted from the measure of total return for each focal firm during the years 1985-94. For comparison, Fortune's data on total return to investors for the median firm in the relevant industry were collected for the same years; these industry returns were not adjusted for dividend yield. Because firms headed by charismatic leaders were also part of the industries from which medians were calculated, the authors describe the comparison as a conservative test.

The amount of the inherited $10,000 that subjects allocated to the common stock of Apple Computer Inc., one of three investment options they could choose among (a money market account, Fidelity Index Fund, and Apple Computer stock). The only constraint was that subjects had to allocate the entire $10,000 among the three investment options, with the specific amount allocated to any one option ranging from $0 to $10,000.

Annual data on gross domestic product were collected for the years 1984-94 and the percentage increase or decrease in GDP from the previous year was calculated. A dummy variable was created to account for whether economic conditions were relatively strong or relatively weak, using a median split to divide the measure of GDP growth.
scale: dummy (0 = strong economic conditions; 1 = weak economic conditions)

description: An industry-specific measure of the conditions facing firms in the sample was created using a dummy variable for the industry's growth rate, measured as the median change in sales in the industry.
scale: dummy (0 = strong industry growth; 1 = weak industry growth)

description: After baseline financial data on Apple Computer was presented, subjects read varying descriptions of the company's future: one condition furnished positive information about Apple's financial and market outlook and a second condition gave negative information about Apple's future. These forecasts were designed to vary the direction of Apple's prospects, so that positive forecasts combined with the objective data made a turnaround clearly evident while negative forecasts made the prospects more dubious.

In the endowment condition the inherited $10,000 was described as already divided among three separate financial assets: $2000 in a money market account, $4000 in a popular stock index fund ('Fidelity Index Fund'), and $4000 in the common stock of Apple Computer, Inc. In the no-endowment condition subjects were not presented with a previously invested portfolio; regardless of any previous allocation, all subjects then distributed or redistributed the $10,000 among the same three investment options.
scale: binary (endowment of stock vs. no endowment of stock)

description: A simple ratio of risky versus conservative investments; the numerator is the amount of money invested in Fidelity Index Fund and the denominator is the amount of money available after investing in Apple stock ($10,000 minus the Apple amount). Investment in Apple Computer was excluded from the measure because it was the target of the charismatic appeal, so as subjects increased the amount invested in Fidelity Index Fund relative to the amount invested in the money market account the ratio increased. Three cases were dropped from the analyses because these subjects invested all $10,000 in Apple stock, which would have made the denominator equal zero.

A dichotomous variable representing whether each firm committed illegal behavior in each of the 19 years (0 = no illegal behavior, 1 = illegal behavior). Data on convictions were compiled from Westlaw and loose-leaf legal services, with a history of all decisions in every case compiled to insure exclusion of cases with overturned decisions; because the exact date on which behavior began was usually not available, the last year in which the behavior occurred was used. Cases were selected by identifying convictions made during 1974-83, but the illegal behavior itself occurred over 1963-81 and was judged against what was illegal at the time the act was committed.

Industry growth rate—the change in value added (the difference between purchases of raw materials, fuel, and so forth and sales) in an industry from one year to the next adjusted for inflation. Simpson (1986) used growth in value added as an indicator of scarcity or munificence, and data were available in the Annual Survey of Manufactures. The variable was transformed from continuous to categorical form and divided into three categories coded 1, 2, and 3 for values in the lower, middle, and upper thirds of the distribution.
scale: three categories coded 1, 2, 3 (lower, middle, upper thirds)

description: The variance in the value of shipments in an industry over the 19-year period, adjusted for inflation, obtained from the Annual Survey of Manufactures. The value of shipments was treated as a measure of both turnover and firms' interconnectedness because it reflects demand for the industry's products. Dynamism was the only antecedent variable that was not a time-varying explanatory variable; it was divided into three categories coded 1, 2, and 3 for values in the lower, middle, and upper thirds of the distribution.
scale: three categories coded 1, 2, 3 (lower, middle, upper thirds)

description: The number of different four-digit SIC code industries in which the firm and its divisions competed, on the argument that firms in four-digit industries confront homogeneous environments. Data were obtained from Standard and Poor's Register of Corporations, Directors and Executives. The variable was divided into three categories coded 1, 2, and 3 for values in the lower, middle, and upper thirds of the distribution.
scale: three categories coded 1, 2, 3 (lower, middle, upper thirds)

description: Return on investment (ROI), or net profit after taxes divided by total assets; the Standard and Poor's COMPUSTAT data base provided data for computing ROI. The variable was divided into three categories coded 1, 2, and 3 for values in the lower, middle, and upper thirds of the distribution.
scale: three categories coded 1, 2, 3 (lower, middle, upper thirds)

description: Number of employees, information available on the COMPUSTAT data base; the authors chose employees because it is the most common measure of size. The variable was divided into three categories coded 1, 2, and 3 for values in the lower, middle, and upper thirds of the distribution.
scale: three categories coded 1, 2, 3 (lower, middle, upper thirds)

description: A financially derived measure of unabsorbed slack: the firm's quick ratio minus an industry's quick ratio, where the quick ratio is the sum of cash, short-term marketable securities, and receivables divided by total current liabilities. The difference indicates the excess resources available to the firm relative to other firms in the industry, and a three-year moving average was used to smooth short-term variations in firm liquidity. Data for computing firms' quick ratios were available from COMPUSTAT, and industry quick ratios appear in Robert Morris Associates: Statement Studies. The variable was divided into three categories coded 1, 2, and 3 for values in the lower, middle, and upper thirds of the distribution.
scale: three categories coded 1, 2, 3 (lower, middle, upper thirds)

description: Three dichotomous variables representing one, two, and three or more prior violations. For each firm in each year, each variable was coded 0 if prior violations had not occurred or if the number of violations was less than the number represented by the variable, and 1 if the number of prior violations was equal to or more than the number represented by the variable; once a firm committed a violation, the variable representing one prior violation was coded 1 in the remainder of the years of the study.

Six dichotomous variables representing the two-digit industries with the highest incidences of illegal behavior: the chemicals industry (SIC code 28), the food industry (20), metal manufacturing (33), lumber and wood products (24), petroleum refining (29), and transportation equipment (37). These were the six industries in which firms had committed ten or more violations. For each firm in each of the 19 years, each variable was coded 0 if the firm was not operating in that industry and 1 if it was doing so.
scale: 0/1 for each of six industry variables

description: Four separate models were generated, each with a different type of violation as the dependent variable and all the hypothesized antecedents as independent variables; each analysis had a set of 4,845 corporation-industry-years. The four categories of illegal behavior included in the data were discrimination violations, per se antitrust cases, product liability cases involving punitive damages, and other violations.

Log of the number of participants in the firm's defined benefit pension plans. Firms can have multiple plans operating simultaneously in a given year (between 0 and 167 in the sample), and participants were aggregated across all plans to create an overall participant count for each firm, for each type of plan, and for all years the firm was active. The measure was constructed from Form 5500 files, with firm employer identification numbers manually identified for each year and retirement data verified at the plan level.

Dummy variable identifying the largest shareholder in each firm annually. Coded 1 when the firm's largest equity ownership block greater than 5% is held by a passive financial investor, which includes mutual funds, insurance companies, and investment banks. Firms in which no entity owns more than 5% of the stock are dispersed stock ownership firms, the comparison category. The data are lagged one year.

Dummy variable identifying the largest shareholder in each firm annually. Coded 1 when the firm's largest equity ownership block greater than 5% is held by an active financial investor, which includes private equity, hedge funds, and other private investors or groups. Firms in which no entity owns more than 5% of the stock are dispersed stock ownership firms, the comparison category. The data are lagged one year.

Percentage of the total number of shares outstanding for the focal firm that is controlled by institutional investors classified as dedicated in Bushee's (1998) classification of institutional investor strategies. All institutional investors are classified annually so that any change in investment strategy is reflected in the data, and the classification applies only to firms that are publicly traded. The data are lagged one year.

Percentage of the total number of shares outstanding for the focal firm that is controlled by institutional investors classified as transient in Bushee's (1998) classification of institutional investor strategies. All institutional investors are classified annually so that any change in investment strategy is reflected in the data, and the classification applies only to firms that are publicly traded. The data are lagged one year.

Log of the number of DB participants that are covered by collectively bargained pension plans. Collective bargaining status comes from a field on the Form 5500 reports indicating whether or not a pension plan is part of a collective bargaining agreement. Collectively bargained plans limit the ability of firms to unilaterally modify the plan's terms, which is expected to safeguard the number of participants in firms' DB plans. The data are lagged one year.

The number of violations recorded in each audit, obtained from the social auditing firm's database. The authors include only the types of violations that the auditing firm says apply in all industries and are interpreted by auditors in the same way in all countries. During an audit the auditors code a common set of dichotomous indicators (violation or no violation) in each category, and the categories are summed into a count.
Coded 1 when at least one member of the focal audit team had participated in one of the supplier's previous audits during the sample period, and 0 otherwise.

Measured as the highest number of years that any member of the audit team had worked at the auditing firm, based on data from the auditing firm's database. A squared term is included to capture the curvilinear effect. The authors report that using average tenure rather than maximum tenure yielded nearly identical results.
Coded 1 when at least one member of the audit team had a graduate degree and 0 otherwise. The authors focus on graduate education because nearly all auditors in the dataset had a bachelor's degree.

The largest number of the auditing firm's training courses that any audit team member had completed. These courses teach skills such as how to interpret national labor laws and how to detect payroll manipulation that might indicate wage violations.

variable_name: all-female audit team, all-male audit team, mixed-gender audit team
description: Team gender composition is measured with three dummy variables: all-female audit team, all-male audit team, and mixed-gender audit team. The authors use these dummies rather than a continuous measure such as the proportion of the audit team that is female because the database indicated that 97 percent of the audit teams in the sample were all female, all male, or evenly divided.

A dummy variable indicating that the audit team was mixed-gender, part of the set of three dummies (all-female, all-male, and mixed-gender) used to capture team gender composition. In the tests it is compared with the all-male baseline category and with all-female teams.

Indicates whether a patent was ever pledged as loan collateral since its application to the time when the study was conducted, coded 1 if yes and 0 otherwise. Pledge information comes from records in the USPTO Patent Assignments Database whose self-asserted 'nature of conveyance' is a security agreement. Only the first-time pledge of a patent was counted.
time_window: from patent application to the time the study was conducted

variable_name: Newness of focal patent's external technology linkage
description: Calculated as the average age of other firms' patents cited by the focal patent, where the age of a cited patent is the time elapsed since the patent's application. The average age was multiplied by -1 so that a higher value indicates that the focal patent cited newer patents of other firms. The variable was measured at the time of the patent's application.
time_window: at the time of the patent's application

description: The forward-citation measure: the share of citations that a firm's patents receive from follow-on patents granted to the focal firm. A larger value indicates a higher level of firm specificity in the firm's patent assets. For a given patent it was measured in the year when the patent was applied. The authors report that the forward- and backward-looking measures are highly correlated (r = 0.788) and produced highly consistent results, and they report the results using the forward-citation measure.
time_window: the year when the focal patent was applied

variable_name: Firm's specialization in focal patent's technological domain
description: Measured by the firm's revealed technology advantage (RTA) in the technological class where the focal patent belongs. The RTA index is defined as the firm's share of patents belonging to the technological domain in the firm's total semiconductor patents, divided by all the sample firms' share of patents belonging to the technological domain in their total semiconductor patents. A higher index indicates a higher level of specialization in that domain relative to other firms in the industry; the index was measured in the year when the patent was applied. The equation itself is not readable in the text; the definition is taken from the prose.
time_window: the year when the focal patent was applied

description: Women's proportional representation among proprietorship owners in each zip code on January 1 of each yearly observation, computed as the area's female-owned proprietorship count divided by its total proprietorship count. It is constructed from all establishments in business from 1990 through 2003, while the first-step estimation uses only the 1990-2003 foundings. Owner gender is identified from first names using the Social Security baby name database and the Texas marriage and divorce records, assigning a gender to 1,365,084 (94.3%) of the proprietorships by the 20:1 rule.

variable_name: βWZIPYR (log of the female/male hazard ratio)
description: Coefficient vector from first-step Weibull proportional hazard regressions of proprietorship exit, estimated from zip code-year and SIC code-year interactions with an owner's gender.
