Positive values suggest a gender gap, negative values a female advantage; its exponentiated form is the hazard ratio between the estimated instantaneous hazard rate of female-owned and male-owned businesses. This coefficient is the dependent variable of the second-step zip code-year regressions.
time_window: foundings 1990-2003 followed to the end of October 2006

description: The number of bank branches in a zip code in each year, counted using the FDIC's annual 'Bank Branches and Locations' files. One was added before logging because many zip codes had zero banks. The logged value was then interacted with proportional representation to test Hypothesis (H2).

variable_name: Customer presence in zip (count of McDonald's, logged)
description: The count of McDonald's in a zip code, used as a proxy for customer presence on the basis of academic references to the accuracy of McDonald's in finding customer-rich locations. One was added before logging because many zip codes had no McDonald's, and the logged value was interacted with proportional representation to test Hypothesis (H3).

Proprietor density in the zip code, computed as proprietors divided by the population of the zip code, used as a proxy for network opportunities. The density was logged after adding one, and the logged value was interacted with proportional representation to test Hypothesis (H4).

ACAP was based on the scale developed by Jansen, Van den Bosch, and Volberda (2005), which measures the acquisition (six items), assimilation (three items), transformation (six items), and exploitation (six items) of new knowledge. The questions were originally based on a business-unit level and were modified to fit the context of SMEs. The scale showed acceptable reliability (alpha = 0.83).

EO was measured based on the Covin and Slevin (1989) scale, which examines innovativeness (three items), risk taking (three items), and proactiveness (three items). The scale showed acceptable reliability (alpha = 0.88).

Prospective compounded three-year growth rate in sales for the years 2008, 2009, and 2010 taken from Affärsdata. Sales are measured annually in Swedish Krona. The firm growth rate was industry-adjusted by subtracting its median scale value.

Prospective compounded three-year growth rate in operating profit for the years 2008, 2009, and 2010 taken from Affärsdata. Operating profit is sales minus the cost of goods sold. The firm growth rate was industry-adjusted by subtracting its median scale value.

Prospective compounded three-year growth rate in return on assets for the years 2008, 2009, and 2010 taken from Affärsdata. ROA is the ratio of net profit, or EBIT, to year-end asset value in Swedish Krona. The firm growth rate was industry-adjusted by subtracting its median scale value.

The survey asked firms who founded the company, whether the founder(s) were still with the company, and in what capacity the founder(s) were then active. The chief executive officer is defined as the highest-level manager of the firm and includes the role names CEO, chief executive officer, and President for this sample. Founder identification and current role information was validated using the Management Section of the SEC S-1 IPO document, with agreement between the two sources in 89 percent of cases; in cases of disagreement the archival record was used. The variable indicates whether the firm's chief executive officer at IPO is a founder.

A ratio of the number of inside board members to total board members at IPO. An inside board member is defined as any member of the board of directors who was, or ever had been, a member of management, or was a member or descendent of the company founder's family or a representative or beneficiary of any legal entity set up in the founder's family's name.
Coded as 1 if one individual holds the positions of chief executive officer and chair of the board of directors simultaneously at IPO.
scale: dichotomous (1 = one individual holds both roles)

description: A corporate investor firm is defined as any corporation owning a portion of the firm before public shares are sold. A corporate investor board member is a member of the firm board of directors who is identified as holding a seat on behalf of the corporate investor before public shares are sold. The variable is dichotomous, designed to indicate the imposition of a corporate investor model on the firm, and is used as both a dependent and a control variable in this study.
The percentage of firm ownership held by corporate investors before public shares are sold.

The percentage of firm ownership held by the CEO after public shares are sold. To improve the shape of its distribution for regression analysis, the variable is transformed by taking the square root. It is used as both a dependent and a control variable in this study.

The sum total of all founder equity as a percentage of firm ownership after completion of the IPO. The measure includes the influence of non-CEO founders in directing management structure. It is used as a dependent and an independent variable in this study.

The percentage of firm ownership released for purchase at IPO. It is operationalized as 100 percent less the percent share ownership of the top management team, including all members of the board of directors, after public shares are sold. Top management team members are specifically and necessarily identified as a group in the Management section of the S-1 IPO document.

At IPO, calculated as [(price per share) - book value per share] / (price per share). The measure uses both accounting-based and stock price information in an effort to measure 'difficult to account for' assets of the firm; the authors note that it has been suggested to reflect the value of a firm's intangible assets, though this has not been empirically demonstrated. It is used as an indicator of the relative value of the firm as assessed by investors, controlling for the book value of the firm.

Scope conformity is operationalized as the sum of the products of dummies for each of the nine CSR issue fields and the prior period's eigenvector centrality scores for each issue field; a higher score indicates greater scope conformity. Weights for each of the nine CSR fields were derived with the concept network method: a two-mode affiliation matrix of firms and CSR fields was created for each year and transformed into a one-mode concept network of fields, and eigenvector centrality values evaluated the importance of each field. The value therefore depends both on the number of issue fields addressed and on the importance of those fields. Both conformity and differentiation measures are continuous variables and standardized scores are used in subsequent analyses. The formula printed for this variable is unreadable in this text and is not reconstructed here.
time_window: contemporaneous firm CSR reports, with prior-period eigenvector centrality weights

description: Emphasis differentiation is a continuous measure calculated from the percentage of a firm's efforts devoted to each CSR issue field. The difference between a firm's emphasis and the industry average emphasis in each field was computed, the absolute value of these differences was weighted by the eigenvector centrality of each field, and the sum of the weighted differences across all nine CSR fields was used as the indicator. Lower scores indicate greater similarity to commonly adopted practices, whereas higher scores indicate greater differentiation. Standardized scores are used in subsequent analyses. The formula printed for this variable is unreadable in this text and is not reconstructed here.

Adjusted analyst coverage is the share of analysts covering an industry segment j that find it attractive to cover firm i. If there are Aj analysts covering industry segment j and a count ai of these analysts chooses to cover firm i in that industry segment, adjusted coverage equals ai divided by Aj. An analyst is counted as covering a firm in year t if the analyst issued an annual earnings forecast for that firm's fiscal period ending in year t.

The mean investment recommendation for each firm in a given year, where each recommendation has equal weight. Recommendations were originally recorded on a 5-point scale with 1 indicating a 'strong buy' and 5 indicating a 'sell'; the score was reversed when the variable was constructed so that higher values indicate more favorable recommendations.

Tobin's q is calculated as the sum of the market value of equity and the book value of debt divided by the book value of total assets. Market value is based on expected cash flows and risks, which indicate future corporate performance.

A dummy variable indicating a firm's ownership type, based on the status of the firm's ultimate controllers; firms controlled by state asset-management agencies or other government agencies are coded as state owned, and all other firms as nonstate owned.
Firm visibility is operationalized as advertising intensity, calculated as the ratio of selling and administrative expenses to sales.

Measured as the ratio of star houses to the total number of brokerage houses that cover a firm. Chinese analysts, often working in teams for brokerage houses, are ranked annually by New Fortune magazine, and a brokerage house is coded as a star house if it has analyst teams on the New Fortune Best Analyst list.
Measured as the difference between analysts' consensus forecasts of a firm's earnings in year t and the firm's actual earnings for year t.

Relational capital is measured with five items on a balanced 7-point Likert-type scale on which 1 = Strongly Disagree and 7 = Strongly Agree. The items cover close personal interaction, mutual respect, mutual trust, personal friendship and high reciprocity between the partners at multiple levels. Items were selected from extant literature and the authors' fieldwork and were pretested; a composite score based on the items was used in the analyses.

Conflict management is measured with six items on the same balanced 7-point Likert-type scale (1 = Strongly Disagree, 7 = Strongly Agree). The items cover explicit mechanisms to address or resolve conflicts, close monitoring of managerial interaction to identify potential conflicts, strong two-way communication, emphasis on dealing with cultural obstacles, joint problem solving, and involvement of top management from both sides. A composite score based on the items was used in the analyses.

Learning is measured with three items on the balanced 7-point Likert-type scale (1 = Strongly Disagree and 7 = Strongly Agree). The items ask whether the company learnt or acquired new or important information from the partner, whether it learnt or acquired a critical capability or skill from the partner, and whether the alliance helped the company enhance its existing capabilities or skills. A composite score based on the items was used in the analyses.

Protection of proprietary assets is measured with two items on the balanced 7-point Likert-type scale (1 = Strongly Disagree and 7 = Strongly Agree). The items ask whether the company has been able to protect its core capabilities or skills from the partner and whether it has been successful in protecting its crown jewels from being appropriated by the partner. A composite score based on the two items was used in the analyses.

The composite VC reputation index developed and validated by Lee et al. (2011), aggregating five z-scored measures of past VC investment action and performance: number of portfolio companies invested in the past 5 years, amount invested in the past 5 years, total funds raised in the past 5 years, number of funds raised in the past 5 years, and number of portfolio companies taken to IPO during the past 5 years. Scores are updated annually, placing each VC firm relative to all others in a given year. Because the z-scores take negative values, the aggregate was transformed to a 100-point scale by adding a constant equal to 0.01 and the minimum reputation score for that year and then dividing each value by the highest reputation score observed in that year, resulting in a positive score that maintains ranking among the VC firms. Although Lee et al. (2011) include VC firm age in the index, the authors include age as a control variable instead.

The composite VC reputation index developed and validated by Lee et al. (2011), aggregating five z-scored measures of past VC investment action and performance: number of portfolio companies invested in the past 5 years, amount invested in the past 5 years, total funds raised in the past 5 years, number of funds raised in the past 5 years, and number of portfolio companies taken to IPO during the past 5 years. Scores are updated annually, placing each VC firm relative to all others in a given year. Because the z-scores take negative values, the aggregate was transformed to a 100-point scale by adding a constant equal to 0.01 and the minimum reputation score for that year and then dividing each value by the highest reputation score observed in that year, resulting in a positive score that maintains ranking among the VC firms. Although Lee et al. (2011) include VC firm age in the index, the authors include age as a control variable instead.

Composite index of the three sector legitimation factors identified by prior research-media attention, regulatory approval, and actions by peers. Media attention is measured as the number of media articles containing 'clean energy,' 'green energy,' 'alternative energy,' or a specific clean energy generation technology in the headline and lead paragraph, in the year prior to the focal investment year. Regulatory approval is measured as the number of federal financial incentives for renewable energy and energy efficiency in a given year listed on DSIRE. Actions by peers is measured as the cumulative number of all VC firm investments in the clean energy sector up until the focal investment year. The three variables were standardized and aggregated into a single index.
time_window: media attention in the year prior to the focal investment year; peer investments cumulative up to the focal investment year; lagged 1 year

description: Composite index of the three sector legitimation factors identified by prior research-media attention, regulatory approval, and actions by peers. Media attention is measured as the number of media articles containing 'clean energy,' 'green energy,' 'alternative energy,' or a specific clean energy generation technology in the headline and lead paragraph, in the year prior to the focal investment year. Regulatory approval is measured as the number of federal financial incentives for renewable energy and energy efficiency in a given year listed on DSIRE. Actions by peers is measured as the cumulative number of all VC firm investments in the clean energy sector up until the focal investment year. The three variables were standardized and aggregated into a single index.
time_window: media attention in the year prior to the focal investment year; peer investments cumulative up to the focal investment year; lagged 1 year

variable_name: Likelihood to invest in the emerging sector
description: This variable takes a value of 1 if the focal VC firm invested in at least one clean energy startup and 0 otherwise. Out of the total population of 3,574 VC firms, 172 (4.8%) invested in clean energy for the first time during the observation period.

The average number of syndicate partners (i.e., the VC firms with which the focal VC firm co-invested) in all of the rounds of its clean energy investments in the focal year. Only the first-time investments by the focal VC firm in each startup were included in the calculation.
time_window: focal year; independent variables lagged 1 year

description: The average stage of the clean energy startups in which a VC firm invested in the focal year. Only the first-time investments by the focal VC firm in each startup were included in the calculation.
time_window: focal year; independent variables lagged 1 year

description: The number of clean energy startups funded by a focal VC firm in a given year divided by the total number of startups the VC firm funded in that year. Only the first-time investments by the focal VC firm in each startup were included in the calculation. This variable ranges from 0 to 1.
time_window: focal year; independent variables lagged 1 year

description: In the SEO prospectus, the 'Use of Funds' section lists how firms intend to use the capital from the SEO. If the 'Use of Funds' section indicates 'acquisitions,' this variable takes the value of 1, and 0 otherwise. The 'Use of Funds' section of the SEO prospectus is not binding, so investors and competitors can interpret the contents of this section in many ways.
time_window: SEO issued in the year prior to the acquisition announcement

description: In the SEO prospectus, the 'Use of Funds' section lists how firms intend to use the capital from the SEO. If the 'Use of Funds' section indicates 'acquisitions,' this variable takes the value of 1, and 0 otherwise. The 'Use of Funds' section of the SEO prospectus is not binding, so investors and competitors can interpret the contents of this section in many ways.

Count of the number of analysts downgrading their recommendation of the firm within the 1-month period following an acquisition announcement, taken from the I/B/E/S Detail database. The measure includes any degree of a downgraded recommendation (e.g., strong buy to buy).

The dispersion of security analyst buy-sell recommendations for a firm is calculated as the standard deviation of the recommendations. Recommendations take a value from 1 (strong buy) to 5 (strong sell), so a numerical dispersion can be calculated and is provided by I/B/E/S.

Analyst downgrades as described for the acquisition tests, used here as an independent variable to gauge the reaction of analysts to foreshadowing, defined as the number of downgrades following the seasoned equity offering.

Dichotomous variable indicating whether a firm issuing an SEO subsequently announced an acquisition within the following year. A value of 1 was assigned to firms that undertook an acquisition, and 0 to firms that did not.

As is common in the literature, the average return-on-assets (ROA) in the 3 years prior to the succession event was used as a measure of firm profitability. The data were obtained from Standard & Poor's COMPUSTAT data base.
time_window: 3 years prior to the succession event

description: Firm growth was measured as the percentage change in total company sales over the three years preceding the CEO succession event. To control for the effect of macroeconomic growth, sales data used to compute firm growth were standardized using gross domestic product (GDP) implicit price deflators.

R&D intensity was measured as the firm's expenditure on R&D as a percentage of its sales, averaged over the 3-year period preceding the CEO succession event. The authors describe the measure as common in the literature. Data on organizational characteristics including R&D intensity were obtained from the COMPUSTAT data base.

Consistent with the criteria used by Sambharya (1987) and Vancil (1987), CEOs having fewer than 5 years of organizational tenure at the time of succession were categorized as outsiders. Organizational tenure and length of time in the CEO position were available in the Business Week data base, allowing for a calculation of an individual's tenure with the organization at the time of their selection as CEO. There were 41 CEOs classified as outsiders in the sample.
time_window: organizational tenure at the time of succession

description: Executives with primary functional background experience in engineering or research and development or manufacturing/production were categorized as having technical backgrounds. In the sample, 72 CEOs had technical backgrounds and 120 nontechnical backgrounds.

Education level was calculated based on the highest degree earned by the selected CEOs. Following Guthrie et al. (1991), a CEO's education level was estimated using the following criteria (estimated years of education in parentheses): doctoral degree (21); masters degree (18); other graduate degree (18); bachelors degree (16); some college (14); high school diploma (12). Selected CEOs in the sample had an average of 17.3 years of education.
scale: estimated years of education from 12 to 21

description: Dummy variable that equals 1 if the bank adopts derivatives and 0 if the bank does not, used to test predictions about a full-fledged Islamic bank's likelihood of using derivatives. The authors report that only 12.8% of derivative usage among full-fledged Islamic banks was observed out of the total observations.

The authors first coded whether a full-fledged Islamic bank i used derivatives at time t, then calculated peer derivative use as the count of full-fledged Islamic banks using derivatives in country c at time t. The count measure follows prior work arguing that the prevalence of an entity increases exposure to it, which in turn affects a focal firm's strategic response. The variable is lagged by one year.

The authors coded whether a CB-owned Islamic bank i used derivatives at time t and then counted the number of CB-owned Islamic banks using derivatives in country c at time t. The variable is lagged by one year.

The authors first coded whether a CB-owned Islamic bank i paid zakat at time t from their data sources, and then calculated the moderator as the count of CB-owned Islamic banks paying zakat in country c at time t. The variable is lagged by one year.

Measured with a survey item asking whether the firm sourced each item internally, externally, or concurrently over the prior year. For concurrent sourcing, respondents reported the percentage of internal production using six choices; a 10 percent cutoff classified components produced at least 90 percent internally as 'made,' those outsourced 90 percent or more as 'bought,' and the rest as concurrently sourced. For the pair of components, the joint choice has nine combinations, which the authors pool into four categories: make/make, buy/buy, concurrent/concurrent, and mixed mode. Hypotheses 1 and 2 compare concurrent/concurrent with make/make.
scale: four categories (make/make, buy/buy, concurrent/concurrent, mixed mode)

description: Constructed by multiplying the mean-differenced firm and supplier expertise variables for each component, for example firm expertise—die design × supplier expertise—die design. This captures aggregate expertise of a firm and its potential suppliers related to a component, based on both dissimilar factors (such as a firm's skilled labor versus a supplier's unique equipment) and related factors (such as a firm's experienced engineers and the supplier's use of advanced design software). The analysis uses separate interfirm expertise variables for die design and die construction in the complementary pair.
level: component within a pair of components

variable_name: Within-firm shared expertise—die design and die construction
description: Constructed by multiplying the mean-differenced firm component expertise scores for the two components. The interaction assumes the expertise of one component can enhance the expertise of another due to shared skills and other resources, making the aggregate expertise greater than the sum of its parts.

Measured as the number of bids won by each firm in a given year. Winning bids are treated as substantive ceremony participation because contract bid lettings are the primary venue where winning bids are announced.

Measured based on a firm's rank on auction bids, in which a rank of one is the lowest (i.e., winning) bid, a rank of two is the second lowest bid, and so on, so that as rank increases a bid becomes more symbolic. The measure is each firm's average rank on all bids submitted within a calendar year. Because all firms submitting contracts were required to be present at the ceremonies at which contracts are awarded, increased contract submissions result in increased participation and visibility at the ceremonies.

Status is measured with eigenvector centrality, which is a function of the centralities of those to whom an actor is connected and therefore incorporates both direct and indirect ties. The relational matrix element Rij represents the number of contracts shared by firms i and j during one year, and a scaling parameter beta is set equal to three quarters of the largest eigenvalue so that a unit's status is a positive function of the statuses of those with which it is in contact. The centrality of all 1,267 state construction firms active from 1995 to 2005 was calculated using directed ties between contractors and subcontractors in UCINet Version 6. The equation itself appears as a formula block that the text does not render here.

Each firm's annual profit margin based on the bidding return (i.e., percentage of revenue in excess of cost) at the time the project was awarded. It was computed based on all awarded projects within a given year to capture persistent versus episodic bidding returns.
scale: percentage of revenue in excess of cost

description: The measure of reliable vicarious learning between firms in period t-1 is the average interfirm correlation between a firm's failure trajectory and another firm's failure trajectory in the past. It is constructed in two stages: the first stage calculates the slope of the failure trajectory for a firm (the change in failures per month due to past failure experience over time), and the second stage estimates the correlation between the firm's trajectory and all others. A significant coefficient suggests that failure patterns exist between firms and reflect either a reduction in adverse events (a negative coefficient) or an increase in adverse event reporting (a positive coefficient).

variable_name: Vicarious learning given volume of experience
description: The average interfirm correlation between a firm's failure trajectory and another's failure trajectory for past observations when the other's volume exceeds a threshold of adverse events. The threshold is iteratively increased in 10-report increments, from 0 to 600 reports per month, until t-1; for example, the effects for others with over 100 adverse events per month are obtained by calculating the average correlation when adverse events for the other firm exceeded 100 per month.

First, the authors measure the average delay for each other firm in each period, D_j,t. Second, they estimate the correlation of failure trajectories between the focal firm and another firm's trajectory for those past observations when the other firm's delays exceed a threshold; the threshold increases in 10-day increments from 0 to 500 days. Delays are the time between the occurrence and the reporting of an adverse event, which the FDA requires within 30 days of learning of an incident.
The number of adverse events reported by a firm i from the current month (t). The dependent measure is event based and is not scaled, unlike prior operationalizations of accident and incident rates.

Measured as the absolute difference between the rank order of divisions within a firm by performance and the rank order of divisions by the amount of capital received. Firms that allocate capital strictly proportional to divisional performance receive a score of 0, which represents pure winner-picking, and the value increases as managers allocate more capital to weaker-performing divisions. Divisional performance is the ROA of the division standardized by segments in other firms in the same three-digit industry-year, where ROA is operating profits divided by assets, and capital allocated to a division is the capital expenditures allocated to a business segment in each fiscal year, standardized by division assets. In the primary models the raw value is used and the total number of divisions is controlled for.

Analysts' projections of the firm's EPS growth over the course of the coming 5 years, derived from I/B/E/S and intended to reflect future performance using both historical performance data and pro forma projections given firm and market conditions. The variable represents a geometrically weighted EPS growth trajectory that places more emphasis on periods in the near future rather than toward the end of the 5-year period. It is standardized according to the industry in which the firm competes (three-digit SIC codes) in the fiscal year of the observation, and in the EAH models it is split into a group mean-centered within-firm term and a group mean between-firm term.
time_window: 5-year forward EPS growth projection, standardized in the fiscal year of the observation

description: A Shannon index of the divisional asset structures according to the industries in which the divisions compete. The authors added together all of the divisional asset structures across the segments within the firm following the BEA categorizations, and then calculated the Shannon index value (the sum of the natural logs of proportions) of each potential asset input across 13 different categories identified by the BEA. If all of the divisions within the firm compete in the same industry or have identical asset structures, the variable takes the value of 1, whereas it takes the value of zero if there is absolutely no overlap between the asset structures of the divisions.

The authors adopt the measure Souder and Bromiley (2012) refer to as historic temporal orientation, which captures the firm's asset durability in the years leading up to a given year rather than annual asset durability. It is calculated as the expected life of a firm's capitalized assets minus the industry average expected life of capitalized assets, where expected life reflects gross PP&E divided by the depreciation expense.
time_window: Years leading up to the focal observation year

description: Firms were assigned to strategic groups based on similarities in strategic actions. Different strategic group structures in distinct time periods were tested for their existence using a procedure based on a combination of variance-covariance matrix testing, multivariate analysis of variance, and cluster analysis.

Total risk for each firm was measured by the standard deviation of AROS about the temporal mean for each of the four periods with a stable strategic group structure: 1963-69, 1970-74, 1975-79, and 1980-82. The authors chose total risk rather than systematic risk because beta was difficult to estimate at the business level and because management is responsible to stakeholders beyond shareholders.

A return on sales (ROS) measure was defined for the pharmaceutical operations of each firm as the ratio of net income before interest and taxes from pharmaceutical operations to total pharmaceutical sales. Following Winn (1975), ROS was adjusted for inflation effects: income statement elements were expressed in constant 1982 values, and depreciation charges were restated. The resulting measure, adjusted return on sales (AROS), served as the indicator of return.

variable_name: share of aid from locally active firms
description: Our variable is the amount of aid from these firms divided by the total amount of aid received by a nation in the year following a disaster. Firms were coded as locally active if they were located, or had a subsidiary, in the affected country. Because the distribution of corporate giving is highly skewed, we analyzed three levels of treatment: the 75th (7.7% of aid is from locally active firms), 95th (24.5%), and 99th (44.4%) percentiles.

variable_name: share of aid from locally active firms
description: Our variable is the amount of aid from firms located, or with a subsidiary, in the affected country divided by the total amount of aid received by a nation in the year following a disaster. For the recovery analysis, disasters within the same country-year were combined into a collective annual disaster. Three treatment levels were used: the 75th (7.7%), 95th (24.5%), and 99th (44.4%) percentiles.

variable_name: % of disaster aid, first four weeks
description: As with previous studies of disaster management, we used the portion of total disaster aid provided in the four weeks following a disaster as a proxy for the speed of aid provision. The outcome is the accumulated amount of disaster aid for the first four post-disaster weeks, expressed as a percentage of total disaster aid.
time_window: first four weeks after the disaster

variable_name: annual growth rate of HDI score
description: We analyze a nation's recovery from disaster based on the annual growth rate of its Human Development Index (HDI) score, which is a measure of aggregate social welfare. A country's HDI score is calculated annually by the United Nations Development Programme and tracks a nation's level of health and longevity, knowledge and education, and standard of living. The outcome variable is the percentage of HDI annual growth at the end of the 10th post-disaster year.

variable_name: related giving (value of related aid divided by the total value of disaster aid from locally active firms)
description: To calculate relatedness we began by using a firm's four-digit Standard Industrial Classification code to identify its key business activities, and coded the dollar amount of in-kind donations that aligned with these activities as related. Our specific variable is the value of related aid divided by the total value of disaster aid from locally active firms. As the distribution for relatedness is relatively normal, we used the mean (26.9% of corporate aid is in the form of related giving) and plus or minus one standard deviation (11.5% and 42.4%) for treatment indicators.

variable_name: related giving (value of related aid divided by the total value of disaster aid from locally active firms)
description: Relatedness reflects the degree to which disaster aid leverages firm-specific routines or resources: in-kind donations aligned with a firm's key business activities, as identified from its four-digit Standard Industrial Classification code, are coded as related, and the value of related aid is divided by the total value of disaster aid from locally active firms. Treatment levels are the mean (26.9%) and plus or minus one standard deviation (11.5% and 42.4%), analyzed at each level of the share of aid from locally active firms (7.7%, 24.5%, and 44.4%).

Pre-tax return on investment splits the market share leaders into high return and low return groups; the 41 low return leaders all earned a pre-tax ROI of less than 10 per cent. Market share change was included to eliminate those share leaders with low return due to share building and those share leaders with high returns due to share liquidations. The average value for each variable over the four years was used.

A set of 17 variables listed in Figure 1 measures market stability: life cycle stage, real market growth, age of product, product change, technological change, number of competitors, industry concentration, geographic location, proprietary products, proprietary process, competitors enter market, competitors exit market, value added/revenue, buyer fragmentation, supplier concentration, supplier integrated into served market, and cost-price squeeze. The authors note that these variables would reflect the degree of stability or turbulence in the market, and that market stability was further represented by competitive entry, exit, forward integration by suppliers, concentration of suppliers and customers, margin deterioration of the industry and the age of the product. The average value for each variable over the four years was used.

Three variables listed in Figure 1 represent demand characteristics: auxiliary services, professional advisers and type of business. Auxiliary services capture whether services and support are important in the purchase decision, professional advisers capture whether such advice is provided, and type of business distinguishes the products sold, such as components, raw or semi-finished materials and capital goods. The average value for each variable over the four years was used.

Five variables listed in Figure 1 measure internal commitments: dollar internal purchases, dollar internal sales, shared facilities, shared marketing and distribution channels, and shared marketing programs. Within the data base, the variables available for measuring these internal commitments were percentages of purchases from and sales to internal divisions and the degree of shared facilities, distribution channels and marketing programs.

Twelve competitive strategy variables listed in Figure 1 describe how the business competes: relative price, relative quality, relative new product emphasis, relative product breadth, process R&D/revenue, product R&D/revenue, relative vertical integration (backwards), relative vertical integration (forward), relative advertising, relative sales force, product standardization and relative direct costs. Relative quality is defined by PIMS as the difference between the percentage of superior products and the percentage of inferior products for each business. Within each cluster, discriminant analysis formed linear combinations of the 12 variables (log-odds functions) to maximize the competitive differences between low return and high return market leaders.

A summative index of three widely used measures of CEO power. The components are CEO duality, coded 1 when the CEO also serves as board chair and 0 when the CEO and board chair are separate; board independence, the percentage of board members classified as independent; and CEO stock ownership, the percentage of outstanding firm stock owned by the CEO. All components were standardized, board independence was reverse-coded because it measures the board's power over the CEO, and the components were then summed. The authors chose these components because they are mostly discretionary sources of CEO power that boards can manipulate.
time_window: focal year; independent variables lagged one year

description: The percentage of a firm's net sales emanating from each specific country was matched with that country's cultural power distance value and multiplied by the sales percentage, and the weighted values were summed across all countries for each firm-year to create a weighted average of the firm's demand-side exposure to cultural power distance. Country cultural power distance values came primarily from GLOBE, with Hofstede's VSM 2013 values used only when GLOBE data were unavailable and rescaled by regressing GLOBE on Hofstede to a common 100-point scale. When firms reported sales for groups of countries whose power distance standard deviation was below 15, the values were averaged across the countries; 'North America' was recognized as an average of the United States, Canada, and Mexico. The measure was standardized prior to analysis.
scale: 100-point scale for country values; weighted average standardized
time_window: lagged one year behind the dependent variable

description: A Herfindahl-Hirschman Index of each firm's sales to different countries, constructed by squaring the percentage of a firm's sales in each country for each year and then summing these squared percentages. The index has a potential minimum value of 0, indicating sales evenly distributed across an infinite number of locations, and a potential maximum of 1, indicating that all revenues emanated from the same geographic location. It was standardized prior to analysis to reduce collinearity with the demand-side cultural power distance measure.
time_window: lagged one year behind the dependent variable

description: The variance in a firm's demand-side cultural power distance, measured as the standard deviation of cultural power distance values across all countries in which a firm competed in each year.

A dichotomous variable labeled 'Pharmaceuticals,' which took a value of 1 for firms in the pharmaceuticals industry and a value of 0 for firms in the semiconductors industry. Pharmaceutical firms are treated as having high bargaining power over customers and semiconductor firms as having low bargaining power over customers.

Dyad-year count of the number of inventors moving from competitor j to the focal firm i during the period t-5 to t-1. Inventor mobility was identified by observing the inventor names on both firms' patents, combining the methodology of Hoisl (2007) and Corredoira and Rosenkopf (2010). Each mobility event was manually verified through externally available information to exclude false positives such as inventors appearing on several firms' patents without being mobile. The natural logarithm of the number of inventors moving from a competitor to the focal firm over the five-year window is used in the multivariate analyses.

Firm-specific knowledge of a mobile inventor about her prior firm is measured as the number of unique co-inventors on the patents that she filed before the move. To aggregate at the dyad level, all mobile inventors moving from a specific competitor to the focal firm in the past five years are considered, their average number of co-inventors is computed, and the natural logarithm is taken.
time_window: patents filed before the move; mobile inventors moving in t-5 to t-1

description: Familiarity is computed as the number of unique citations that patents filed by firm i and competitor j in the period t-5 to t-1 have in common, normalized by the total number of unique citations contained in i's patent filings in t-5 to t-1. It does not rely on citations made by the firm to the competitor's patents but captures the extent to which the two firms draw upon the same knowledge resources in their own R&D activities.

Dummy coded 1 if the two firms in a dyad formed a joint R&D alliance in a given year, 0 otherwise. Joint R&D alliances are agreements where firms specifically agree to jointly perform R&D activities for developing a new technology. The variable varies over dyads and years.

Dummy coded 1 if the two firms in a dyad formed a technology-development alliance in a given year, 0 otherwise. Development alliances are partnerships where firms interact to share knowledge and together develop a new technology, pooling joint R&D alliances with agreements where firms share and recombine existing technologies.

Dummy coded 1 if the two firms in a dyad formed a technology-transfer alliance in a given year, 0 otherwise. Transfer alliances are agreements where one firm passes its knowledge on a specific technology over to another company, akin to licensing arrangements.

Each alliance was coded into five categories according to the SIC code overlap with the partner: '4' for a partner in the same four-digit SIC code, '3' same three-digit SIC code, '2' same two-digit SIC code, '1' same one-digit SIC code, and '0' sharing no SIC code. The portfolio-level diversity measure was computed with the Blau Index of Variability and, because portfolios differed in size, the absolute diversity score was divided by the highest possible Blau score based on the size of the firm's alliance portfolio.
time_window: Alliances formed January 1985 to December 2005, portfolios measured at 2000 and 2005

description: A continuous variable counting foreign countries represented in the firm's alliance portfolio: '0' for a portfolio with alliances with no foreign partners, '1' with partners from one foreign country, '2' with partners from two foreign countries, and so on.
time_window: Alliances formed January 1985 to December 2005, portfolios measured at 2000 and 2005

description: Alliances were coded for ownership: '1' for same ownership (public-public, private-private) and '0' for different ownership (public-private, public-government, private-government). The portfolio-level diversity measure was obtained using the Blau Index of Variability, with the absolute diversity score divided by the highest possible Blau score based on portfolio size.
time_window: Alliances formed January 1985 to December 2005, portfolios measured at 2000 and 2005

description: Alliances were coded for organizational level: '1' for same organization level (parent-parent, subsidiary-subsidiary) and '0' for different organization level (parent-subsidiary). The portfolio-level diversity measure was obtained using the Blau Index of Variability, with the absolute diversity score divided by the highest possible Blau score based on portfolio size.
time_window: Alliances formed January 1985 to December 2005, portfolios measured at 2000 and 2005

description: Alliances were coded into four functional categories where marketing is '1,' manufacturing '2,' R&D '3,' and other '4' (other activities had insufficient numbers to justify individual coding). The portfolio-level diversity measure was obtained using the Blau Index of Variability, with the absolute diversity score divided by the highest possible Blau score based on portfolio size.
time_window: Alliances formed January 1985 to December 2005, portfolios measured at 2000 and 2005

description: Each alliance was coded into six governance categories: '1' = nonequity, '2' = minor equity share up to 20 percent, '3' = substantial equity share 21-49 percent, '4' = equal equity share 50 percent, '5' = major equity share 51-79 percent and '6' = dominant equity share 80 + percent. The portfolio-level diversity measure was obtained using the Blau Index of Variability, with the absolute diversity score divided by the highest possible Blau score based on portfolio size.
time_window: Alliances formed January 1985 to December 2005, portfolios measured at 2000 and 2005

description: Corporate-level three-year average of net profit margin computed for 2000-2002 at time point one and 2005-2007 at time point two. A lagged three-year average performance in each time period was used to reduce the likelihood of spurious results due to one unusual performance year.

Imitation time lag was measured as the time difference in years between the FDA approval date of the innovator drug and the approval date of the imitator drug, where the innovator is the first drug in a mechanism of action and all subsequent entrants are imitators. FDA approval dates were taken from the Orange Book. The authors state that they expect the sign on this coefficient to be positive.

For each imitator drug, NewInd is the indications offered by the imitator drug but not the innovator drug, RedInd is the indications offered by the innovator drug but not the imitator drug, and InnTotInd is the total number of indications offered by the innovator drug. Difference in indications was measured as (NewInd − RedInd)/InnTotInd. The authors state that they expect the sign on this coefficient to be positive.

For each imitator drug, NewSE is the side effects engendered by the imitator drug but not the innovator drug, RedSE is the side effects in the innovator drug but not the imitator drug, and InnTotSE is the total number of side effects in the innovator drug. Difference in side effects was measured as (NewSE − RedSE)/InnTotSE. The authors state that they expect the sign on this coefficient to be negative, since more side effects than the innovator indicate lower quality.

For each year all drugs within a product class (mechanism of action) were ranked by sales revenues. Each imitator drug for each year was coded zero if its sales rank was lower than that of the innovator and coded one if its sales rank was higher. When the imitator beat the innovator, it also became the market share leader in the product class.

Firms were classified as Manager-Controlled (MC), Owner-Controlled (OC) or Owner-Managed (OM). MC firms are those in which no individual or institution other than an employee benefit plan owns 5 percent or more of the firm's outstanding voting stock. OC firms are those in which at least 5 percent of the firm's outstanding voting stock is in the hands of one individual or organization that was not involved in the actual management of the company or was not an employee benefit plan, and OM firms are those in which at least 5 percent of the stock is in the hands of one individual who was involved in the actual management of the company. Stock ownership information was obtained from proxy statements obtained from the SEC website.

Estimated by regressing change in pay level on change in size and change in ROA separately for MC, OC, and OM firms; the coefficient on change in ROA captures the pay-performance sensitivity within each ownership category. The standardized betas and significance of each variable in the model are reported along with the R2, F, and adjusted R2 of each model. Change in executive pay level was included as a control variable in each of the three models.

Estimated by regressing change in pay level on change in size and change in ROA separately for MC, OC, and OM firms; the coefficient on change in size captures the pay-size sensitivity within each ownership category. The standardized betas and significance of each variable in the model are reported along with the R2, F, and adjusted R2 of each model. Change in executive pay level was included as a control variable in each of the three models.

Calculated as the change in average compensation expense per employee from 1997 to 1998. This includes salaries, wages, pension costs, profit sharing, incentive compensation, payroll taxes, and other employee benefits, but excludes commissions. Total compensation and number of employees were obtained from COMPUSTAT.
Measured as the change in a composite of assets, sales, and number of employees. Assets, sales, and number of employees were standardized and averaged to create the size variable (alpha = 0.83).
Measured as the change in return on assets (ROA), which the authors note has been frequently used as a measure of performance in compensation and governance research.

Measures whether a seller is located in a rural or an urban area. A seller's local environment is divided into five levels ranging from the village to the city center: the village (cun), the township and county (xiang/xian), the outskirts of a city (shijiao), the city proper (shinei), and the city center (shizhongxin). The variable is 0 for sellers located in the city center, city proper, or city outskirt, and 1 for sellers located in villages or townships/counties. Roughly 40 and 60% of the sellers are categorized as rural and urban sellers, respectively, and sellers who moved between rural and urban areas during the window of observation were removed from the sample.

Indicates the level of category focus in a seller's product portfolio - the extent to which sellers focus their resources toward building up a rich product line in one or a few categories. It multiplies a Herfindahl index that measures the concentration of product items across different categories by the total number of distinct products. A distinct product is defined as a product with its unique product name and unique webpage, and a product category is the 'secondary product category' per platform definition; the dataset only contains product data on the three top-grossing categories. In all regressions the logarithm of the measure, log(Category Focus), is used so that results can be interpreted in percentage terms.

Logged monthly sales, where sales are the sum of all sales from a seller's top three grossing categories in a given month. All sales data are multiplied by an unknown number to ensure anonymity. The normalized average monthly sales in the sample is 24, which publicly available data suggest roughly corresponds to $50-$80 per unit.

The number of months from when the design change happened (May 2013); observations from February 2013 have temporal distance = -3 and observations from January 2014 have temporal distance = 8. The interaction term Rural × Temporal Distance equals the temporal distance only for rural sellers and equals 0 for urban sellers.

The percentage of independent directors on a firm's board, obtained by dividing the number of independent directors on a board by the total number of board members. Board members were classified as insiders if they were corporate officers, corporate retirees, relatives of officers, or division heads; as interdependent if they were financiers, consultants, CPAs, lawyers, or other interdependent decision makers such as major suppliers or customers; and as independent if they appeared to have no ties to the corporation or whose board they sat, including directors of public organizations, directors serving on several boards with no primary employer, CEOs of companies with no discernible ties to the firm, academicians, investors, or independent decision makers.
time_window: the year the pill was adopted (1985-88) for adopters; 1988 for non-adopters

description: A dichotomous variable representing board leadership, coded 1 for single leadership (one individual serving in both roles of CEO and board chairperson) and 2 for dual leadership. The necessary information was obtained from proxy statements and Standard & Poor's Register of Corporations. In the study group, 477 companies had single individuals serving in the dual roles and 196 companies had two people in these roles.
time_window: the year the pill was adopted (1985-88) for adopters; 1988 for non-adopters

description: Tenure data, measured as number of years served on a board, were collected from proxy statements on all independent directors and aggregated and averaged for each firm. To test for a curvilinear effect, the quadratic function of this variable was included in the model.
time_window: the year the pill was adopted (1985-88) for adopters; 1988 for non-adopters

description: Tenure data, measured as number of years served on a board, were collected from proxy statements on all independent directors and CEOs.
time_window: the year the pill was adopted (1985-88) for adopters; 1988 for non-adopters

description: The percentage of total shares inside directors held for each company, based on each board member's beneficial shares, which are common shares an individual owns or has voting control over and stock options exercisable in the very near future.
time_window: the year the pill was adopted (1985-88) for adopters; 1988 for non-adopters

description: The percentage of total shares independent directors held for each company, recorded from each board member's beneficial shares (common shares an individual owns or has voting control over and stock options exercisable in the very near future).
time_window: the year the pill was adopted (1985-88) for adopters; 1988 for non-adopters

description: Data on institutional holdings were recorded as the percentage of total shares held by institutions.
time_window: the year the pill was adopted (1985-88) for adopters; 1988 for non-adopters

description: A dichotomous dependent variable representing the existence or absence of a poison pill. The names of companies that had adopted poison pills and the dates of their adoption were obtained from two organizations that track corporate takeover defenses. Of the 760 poison pill provisions in place through the end of 1988, only four had been enacted prior to 1985, and those four firms were excluded from the analysis.

The number of patents the inventor applied for in the past. The explanatory variable is used at time t before the focal event, and inventor fixed effects are included because the output-based measure of experience may also proxy for inventor ability.
time_window: from the start of the inventor's career (1978 at the earliest) to time t

description: The rate at which an inventor produces a generic patented invention. It is estimated with a continuous Cox regression at the inventor level, in which the failure event is the application for a new EPO patent and the baseline hazard is left unspecified, with inventor fixed effects.
time_window: spells start after a new invention or at the beginning of the career and end with another invention or censoring

description: A dichotomous variable that takes a value of 1 if the invention is a breakthrough and 0 otherwise. Breakthroughs are patented inventions in the top 5% of the distribution in terms of citations received from subsequent patents, measured within the same year (application date) and the same ISI-INPI-OST technological category. Of the 35,005 patents in the sample, 2,055 are breakthroughs according to this measure.

The rate at which an inventor produces breakthroughs, estimated with Cox regression models at the inventor level in which the failure event is a breakthrough rather than a generic invention, again with inventor fixed effects.
time_window: spells start after a new invention or at the beginning of the career and end with another invention or censoring

description: Takes a value of 1 if the invention was the main achievement or a by-product of a firm-sanctioned research project whose target was defined ex ante by the firm, and 0 if the idea originated outside the firm's control, such as from an individual inventor's inspiration. Because the information is available only for surveyed patents, the inventor average of this variable is used to define the targeted nature of all the other projects of the same inventor in the same organization, and mobile inventors are excluded when the interaction term is introduced.

The traditional insider/outsider approach, designated by the authors as ratio 1. Officers of the firms were defined as insiders and all other members of the dominant coalitions as outsiders. The number of insiders was then divided by the number of outsiders to create a ratio value which ranged from a high of 1.500 to a low of 0.333.

Members of the dominant coalitions were classified as either internally or externally oriented on the basis of whether they assigned greater weights to the individual internal or external items; respondents weighted the ten factors on a five-point scale in terms of the priority given to each over the past three years. An internal score was calculated for each respondent by summing the numerical values assigned to each internal factor, and an external score was similarly computed; the scores were normalized to adjust for the possibility that the five internal and five external factors were not equally important. Ratio 2 was created by dividing the number of internally oriented individuals in a firm by the number of its externally oriented individuals, and yielded ratios which ranged from a high of 1.667 to a low of 0.400.
time_window: priorities over the past three years

description: A measure of the internal/external orientation of the dominant coalition within each organization as a whole. The summed values for all internal factors by a firm's dominant coalition members divided by summed values for the set of external factors were used to create ratio 3. Values obtained for ratio 3 ranged from a high of 1.047 to a low of 0.904.
time_window: priorities over the past three years

description: One of four profitability policy measures, which the authors say has long been considered by financial analysts to be the indicator of the relative operating efficiency of the firm. A percentile ranking was computed for each bank on this measure relative to a control group of the 70 other banks located in the state. The ranking was based on an average of the immediately preceding three-year period, and the mean figure for the period was used in the correlational analysis.
time_window: average of the immediately preceding three-year period

description: One of four profitability policy measures, described by the authors as generally regarded as the best single measure of the financial performance of a banking organization. A percentile ranking was computed for each bank relative to the control group of 70 other banks in the state, based on an average of the immediately preceding three-year period.
time_window: average of the immediately preceding three-year period

description: One of four profitability policy measures, defined as the difference between interest income and interest expense, which the authors describe as a major factor affecting bank earnings. A percentile ranking was computed for each bank relative to the control group of 70 other banks in the state, based on an average of the immediately preceding three-year period.
time_window: average of the immediately preceding three-year period

description: The fourth profitability policy measure, an alternative measure of profitability used to gauge the owners' direct benefit and described by the authors as clearly inferior to return on assets as a measure of the firm's overall profitability. A percentile ranking was computed for each bank relative to the control group of 70 other banks in the state, based on an average of the immediately preceding three-year period.
time_window: average of the immediately preceding three-year period

description: One of the two measures of the firms' credit policies, which the authors say reflect their attitudes toward risk. A percentile ranking was computed for each bank relative to the control group of 70 other banks in the state, based on an average of the immediately preceding three-year period.
time_window: average of the immediately preceding three-year period

description: The second of the two measures of the firms' credit policies, which the authors describe as essentially a measure of bad debt expense. A percentile ranking was computed for each bank relative to the control group of 70 other banks in the state, based on an average of the immediately preceding three-year period.
time_window: average of the immediately preceding three-year period

description: One of the two capitalization policy measures, also described by the authors as a measure of risk; they note that regulatory constraints limit the range within which management is able to adjust the proportions of capital to assets. A percentile ranking was computed for each bank relative to the control group of 70 other banks in the state, based on an average of the immediately preceding three-year period.
time_window: average of the immediately preceding three-year period

variable_name: Loans to deposits less public funds
description: One of the two capitalization policy measures, also described by the authors as a measure of risk. A percentile ranking was computed for each bank relative to the control group of 70 other banks in the state, based on an average of the immediately preceding three-year period.
time_window: average of the immediately preceding three-year period

description: Measured as the volatility of the net sales of each firm's portfolio of four-digit SIC industries. It was calculated by regression analyses in which a variable for each year was regressed on a variable for net industry sales, using five years of data for each regression (e.g., net industry sales values from 1980 through 1984 were used to predict volatility in 1985). Volatility was the standard error of the regression slope coefficient divided by the mean of sales, and larger values indicated greater environmental uncertainty. The four-digit industries were identified from annual reports and Compact Disclosure, and the data for the regressions came from COMPUSTAT.

Operationalized by cluster analysis of an entropy measure and a specialization measure. Entropy yields related diversification (DR, sales from four-digit SIC segments within the same two-digit groups), unrelated diversification (DU, sales from different two-digit SIC industry groups) and total diversification (DT, the sum of DR and DU); specialization is sales of the largest four-digit SIC segment divided by total firm sales. Cluster analyses of those measures resulted in five diversification strategy types, and each firm was coded on the basis of its type (single businesses coded 1 and unrelated businesses coded 5). Data came from the COMPUSTAT business segment tapes, and diversification strategy was computed for 1985 through 1992.

A continuous index accounting for weighted changes in a parent company's lines of business through acquisition and divestiture actions, built from two components: changes in the parent company's lines of business (CHLOB), the number of lines of business in year t minus the number in the preceding year, and changes in company size (CHSIZE), the log of employees in year t minus the log of employees in the preceding year. The index is the product of the absolute value of CHLOB and CHSIZE (the absolute value rule avoids double negatives). It ranges from -1 to 1, with zero representing no portfolio restructuring; negative values represent divestitures and positive values acquisitions, and values closer to -1 or 1 reflect greater amounts of restructuring. Each measure was computed yearly for 1986 through 1993, reflecting a one-year lag on the independent variables.

variable_name: Percentage change in the number of lines of business owned
description: Portfolio restructuring measured as the percentage change in the number of lines of business owned, computed from the number of business lines owned in year t and the number owned in the next year. The printed formula is garbled in the available text, so the exact arithmetic cannot be read from the prose. Each measure was computed yearly for 1986 through 1993, reflecting a one-year lag on the independent variables.

Portfolio restructuring measured as the total number of business lines acquired divided by the total number of business lines divested. Values above 1 indicate that a greater number of business lines were acquired than were divested, whereas values below 1 indicate that a greater number of business lines were divested than acquired. Each measure was computed yearly for 1986 through 1993, reflecting a one-year lag on the independent variables.

Denotes whether the IPO firm became the object of an equity alliance. The authors collected the date the firm went public and the date the first minority equity investment was made in the firm, if such a partnership was formed. Firms still operating independently without an equity partnership at the end of the sample period were treated as right censored, and other events such as outright acquisitions or delistings were treated as distinct competing risks.
time_window: from the IPO until the end of the sample period

description: Follows Kester (1984): the firm's value (V) is measured as the market value of its common stock plus the book value of its preferred stock as well as its debt, and a 20% rate is applied to capitalize the firm's current earnings to obtain its value of assets in place (VAIP). The firm's growth option value is then calculated as the value of growth options stated as a percentage of the firm's market value. The measure is a residual using both financial and accounting information and can take on values that are either negative or greater than one.

The number of alliances the firm had previously formed, counted using SDC. The variable is defined as the log of one plus the number of alliances, to remedy positive skewness in the pretransformed count measure; one plus the number of alliances is used because some firms had no prior alliances and the log of zero is undefined.

Measured using the ranking index first developed by Carter and Manaster (1990), which is constructed according to the positions that investment banks occupy in tombstone announcements listing members of the underwriting syndicate. Banks that always appear in the highest bracket receive a ranking of nine, whereas investment banks receive lower rankings should their position in successive tombstone announcements drop. The authors focus on the reputation index of the IPO's lead underwriter and use the data on investment bank reputation from Loughran and Ritter (2004).

Measured as the number of media mentions found by searching through newspapers and articles available about the IPO firm in the major newspaper and other databases of Lexis-Nexis. Following Demers and Lewellen (2003), media mentions are examined from two months before the IPO to two months after. To account for substantial skewness in the data, a log transformation is used and one is added to all observations before taking the logarithm.
time_window: from two months before to two months after the IPO

description: A franchisee's multimarket contact with same-firm franchisees, constructed with the common 'firm-in-market' multimarket contact variable considered ideal for studies of entry, based on the number of contact points among franchisees existing at the time a new unit was opened. For each franchisee j, up to five units that were the closest to each of j's units within a five-mile radius were found, and those belonging to other franchisees that also owned units among the up-to-five closest units within five miles of the new unit i were counted. Relative distances between all pairs of units were calculated from longitude and latitude coordinates obtained by geocoding the unit addresses in the sales tax data; the five-mile cutoff follows a restaurant location guide stating that customers rarely travel over five miles for fast food.
level: franchisee division (choice alternative) within each new-unit observation
time_window: at the time a new unit was opened

description: A franchisee's multimarket contact with other-firm franchisees, built with the same 'firm-in-market' multimarket contact variable as the intraorganizational measure and based on the number of contact points among franchisees existing at the time a new unit was opened. For each franchisee j, up to five units closest to each of j's units within a five-mile radius were found, and contact points with franchisees of other firms that also owned units among the up-to-five closest units within five miles of new unit i were counted. Distances were computed from geocoded longitude and latitude coordinates of the unit addresses.
level: franchisee division (choice alternative) within each new-unit observation
time_window: at the time a new unit was opened

description: Binary variable set equal to one if the number of units affiliated with the same franchisor that was adding the unit of interest within five miles of the new unit was greater than or equal to the number of other franchisors' units within five miles. Otherwise the variable was set equal to zero. It is a market-level characteristic that does not vary among the rows within each observation.
time_window: at the opening of the new unit

description: Binary variable for county-level income decline, set to one if per capita income had declined in the year the new unit was opened relative to its level two years previously. Markets with declining per capita incomes are often those in which uncertainty regarding a unit's viability is high. It is a market-level characteristic that does not vary among the rows within each observation.
time_window: year of opening relative to two years previously

description: Observed binary dependent variable for the choice among franchisees for the mandate to operate a new unit. Within an observation, the row corresponding to the franchisee division assigned the mandate for the new unit was set to one, and the other rows, each associated with a specific franchisee that was not assigned the mandate, received a value of zero. It equals one if the latent value Vij exceeded that of all other alternatives k.
level: franchisee division (choice alternative) within each new-unit observation

description: Count of all buyouts made in a given calendar year of companies located in the focal state, which is the dependent variable of the state-level activity analysis. The analysis covers 750 state-year observations for the 50 states and Washington, D.C., over the years 1983 to 2003. Because many state-year dyads are censored, the model is estimated by zero-inflated Poisson.

Dummy variable that has a value of '1' if the Republicans won the presidential elections that directly preceded the buyout in the focal state and a value of '0' otherwise. It operationalizes the local political environment prior to, at the time of, and after the buyout decision and is measured at the state level because county-level data are not available for the majority of the covariates.
time_window: presidential election directly preceding the buyout

description: Dummy variable that has a value of '1' if both the Republicans won the presidential elections that directly preceded the buyout in the focal state and the Democrats won the presidential elections before that, and a value of '0' otherwise. It captures a recent shift of the state's dominant political context toward the Republican platform.
time_window: the two presidential elections preceding the buyout

description: Dummy variable that has a value of '1' if both the Democrats won the presidential elections that directly preceded the buyout in the focal state and the Republicans won the presidential elections before that, and a value of '0' otherwise. It captures a recent shift of the state's dominant political context away from the Republican platform, so it is coded in the opposite direction to the construct.
time_window: the two presidential elections preceding the buyout

description: Categorical measure of the exit success of an individual buyout transaction, with the outcomes successful exit, unrealized (censored, living-dead), and write-off. A successful exit is an initial public offering, secondary LBO, or trade sale observed within five calendar years following the investment date. This is the dependent variable of the ordered probit model of exit success.
time_window: five calendar years following the investment date

description: Dummy variable that has a value of '1' if the Republicans won the presidential elections that directly preceded the buyout in the focal state and a value of '0' otherwise. It is used as a focal covariate in the deal-level analysis of exit success alongside the transaction and fund controls.
time_window: presidential election directly preceding the buyout

description: Dummy variable that has a value of '1' if both the Republicans won the presidential elections that directly preceded the buyout in the focal state and the Democrats won the presidential elections before that, and a value of '0' otherwise. It captures a recent shift of the state's dominant political context toward the Republican platform.
time_window: the two presidential elections preceding the buyout

description: Dummy variable that has a value of '1' if both the Democrats won the presidential elections that directly preceded the buyout in the focal state and the Republicans won the presidential elections before that, and a value of '0' otherwise. It captures a recent shift of the state's dominant political context away from the Republican platform, so it is coded in the opposite direction to the construct.
time_window: the two presidential elections preceding the buyout

description: Shareholder discontent with director monitoring is captured as the percentage of votes withheld (i.e., ballots cast against the individual director) in each director election. Because the distribution of votes withheld is positively skewed, the authors first add 1 to the percentage of votes withheld and then log-transform the data, so that the dependent continuous variable exhibits a normal distribution. The 2,099 directors in the sample received between 0% and 50% of votes withheld.
scale: percentage of votes withheld, 0% to 50%, log-transformed after adding 1

description: Operating performance is measured using return on assets, that is, net income divided by total assets. Firm performance was tested using prior-year, three-year, and five-year windows, and the final model includes prior-year accounting-based performance.
time_window: prior year (2005) in the final model

description: A stock-market-based performance measure. Firm and market returns for one year, three years, and five years were all tested with similar results; the final model includes prior-year returns to shareholders in line with the accounting-based performance and other measures.
time_window: prior year (2005) in the final model

description: CEO compensation is measured as the log of total CEO pay, including short-term (i.e., cash salary and bonus) and long-term (i.e., stock options) compensation reported for 2005. Industry-average CEO pay, calculated by two-digit SIC code, is included as a control to focus the measure on CEO compensation in excess of the industry average.
Board size is measured as the total number of members on the board.

Director dependence is measured in part with a dummy variable indicating affiliated status, determined by official SEC reporting guidelines of material relationships with the firm. Within the sample, 1,558 directors are outsiders, 251 are affiliated, and 290 are inside directors.

Director dependence is also measured with a continuous measure reflecting tenure on the board. Tenure was collected for each director as of 2005; the longest-tenured director facing (re)election had 52 years of service, and approximately one-fourth of the sample had tenure greater than 10 years.

Each director's equity stake in the firm is measured in two ways; the final model includes a dummy variable indicating director equity stake as a blockholder (i.e., 5% ownership position), calculated as shares held by the director divided by the firm's total shares outstanding. The alternative measure, the dollar value of equity holdings, equals the number of shares multiplied by the share price at fiscal year-end, log-transformed after adding 1 to allow transformation of zero values.

Number of board seats represents the number of public firm board seats held by each director in 2005, not counting the firm of current election. Nearly one-third of the sample holds no other board seats in 2005, whereas a small number have as many as six or nine directorships in addition to the board where she or he faces (re)election.

An occupational minority appointed CEO was coded as a one, and a white man appointed CEO was coded as a zero. In the savior effect analysis, transitions were compared across whether a white man followed an occupational minority CEO, a white man followed a white man CEO, and an occupational minority followed an occupational minority CEO. CEO gender and race were collected using reference websites and company websites.

variable_name: Firm performance measures (ROA, ROE, shareholder returns)
description: Return on assets and return on equity represent accounting-based measures and share price return represents a market-based measure. Firm performance measures were calculated for the year leading up to the transition, the two-year average leading up to the transition, and the three-year average leading up to the transition. All firm performance measures are reported in percentages.
time_window: one year, two-year average and three-year average leading up to the transition

description: CEO tenure was collected from reference websites and company websites along with CEO names, gender, race, year of appointment and prior experience. Tenure was reported in months. Tenure length of traditional and occupational minority CEOs was compared with an independent t-test.

variable_name: Transition of a traditional white male leader replacing an occupational minority CEO
description: The dependent variable to test the savior effect: the transition in which a traditional white male leader replaced an occupational minority CEO.
