The county's annual degree of content similarity between all TV shows aired in a year and all news mentioning the county is calculated, the equivalent degree of content similarity between all movies released in a year and the same news is calculated, and the latter is subtracted from the former. Content similarity was computed with SenseClusters using bigrams, treating a TV show description and a news abstract as similar if they shared at least one bigram; news programs were excluded from the TV show corpus.

County median family income, inflation adjusted, taken from decennial census data and linearly interpolated for non-decennial years. The variable is lagged by one year and expressed in units of 10,000 dollars in the models.
The proportion of a county's population with college degrees, taken from decennial census data and linearly interpolated for non-decennial years. The variable is lagged by one year.
The proportion of a county's population that is foreign-born, taken from decennial census data and linearly interpolated for non-decennial years. The variable is lagged by one year.

Information about acquisition activities was drawn from the Thomson Reuters Refinitiv database. The number of all acquisitions was aggregated yearly to resemble the number of acquisitions performed by the focal firm each year. Because the distribution was highly skewed, the yearly counts were recoded into four categories: 0 (zero actions performed, 'no activities'), 1 (one to two actions performed, 'low level of activity'), 2 (three to five actions performed, 'moderate level of activity'), and 3 (six or more actions performed, 'high level of activity').
time_window: yearly, recorded on each year's final day

description: Information about divestiture activities was drawn from the Thomson Reuters Refinitiv database. The number of all divestitures was aggregated yearly to resemble the number of divestitures performed by the focal firm each year. Because the distribution was highly skewed, the yearly counts were recoded into four categories: 0 (zero actions performed, 'no activities'), 1 (one to two actions performed, 'low level of activity'), 2 (three to five actions performed, 'moderate level of activity'), and 3 (six or more actions performed, 'high level of activity').
time_window: yearly, recorded on each year's final day

description: Presence or absence of an interlock in which the focal firm sends one of its executives to another firm's supervisory board; agency for this network lies with the firm sending the executive. The network was observed yearly at the end of December, and a tie lasting from November 2014 to June 2015 appears in 2014, not 2015. Cases in which a firm sent two executives to the same other firm's board were extremely rare, so only the presence or absence of board interlocks between two firms was captured. There was no missing data regarding board interlocks.
time_window: observed yearly at the end of December, 2013-2018

description: Presence or absence of an interlock in which an executive director of another firm is invited to serve on the focal firm's supervisory board; agency for this network lies with the firm inviting the executive. The network was observed yearly at the end of December, with a tie counted in the year in which it appears. Only the presence or absence of board interlocks between two firms was captured because sending two executives to the same board was extremely rare.
time_window: observed yearly at the end of December, 2013-2018

description: Presence or absence of an undirected interlock formed by individuals who serve on the boards of both a focal and another firm but hold no executive role - and thus no primary affiliation - in either firm. The network was observed yearly at the end of December. Because the network is undirected, agency is assumed to lie with both firms, and a receiver effect cannot be distinguished from a sender effect.
time_window: observed yearly at the end of December, 2013-2018

description: HR managers reported the number of female and male top managers (im-won) for the year before the survey, effectively lagging this variable by 1 year relative to employee participation and firm performance. Female representation in top management was measured by the number of female top managers; its average was .39 and the average top management team size was 15.46.

Employees responded to three survey items about employee participation using a 5-point Likert scale (1 = strongly disagree to 5 = strongly agree); Cronbach's alpha was .73. Employee ratings were aggregated to the firm level based on rwg of .90, ICC(1) of .11, and ICC(2) of .76.
scale: 5-point Likert scale (1 = strongly disagree to 5 = strongly agree)

description: Firm performance was measured as return on assets, operating income divided by total assets, an accounting-based measure chosen to better capture the influence of internal operations. To mitigate the influence of outliers, the variable was winsorized at the 5% level (5th and 95th percentile).
Measured as the number of female middle managers divided by the total number of middle managers.
Measured as research and development (R&D) spending over total sales. If a company did not report its R&D expenses, a value of zero was assigned.
Measured as total labor costs (wages, pensions, and other employee benefits) over total sales.
Takes the value of '1' if, in the focal fiscal quarter, a CEO departed within 3 years of taking the position, and '0' otherwise.

Calculated as the share price at the end of quarter t - 1 minus the share price at the end of quarter t - 3, plus dividends over the two quarters, all divided by the share price from quarter t - 3, adjusted by the industry median TSR at the four-digit SIC level.
A binary variable taking the value of '1' if a focal CEO directly succeeded an interim CEO, and '0' otherwise, identified by manually inspecting titles in BoardEx.
Proportion of directors in the focal year who were on the board when the CEO was hired.
Proportion of outstanding firm shares owned by all outside directors on the board, winsorized at the 99th percentile.
The number of car models based on the same vehicle platform as the focal product.
Logarithm of the number of customer complaints reported to the NHTSA surfacing up until 6 years after a specific yearly product version has been brought to market.
time_window: Complaints surfacing up to 6 years after model-year product introduction; reliability attributed to introduction year t.

description: Number of recalls of an automaker's car models net of the focal car model occurring in the 3 years prior to the focal product's production.

variable_name: Prior defects of other, task co-using products
description: Number of recent recalls of other task co-using products occurring in the 3 years prior to the focal product's production, excluding defects that directly involved the co-used task.
Binary variable set to one if a CEO has been involved with at least one charitable organization during their career.
The change in imports from China from the previous year divided by the sum of US industry shipments and Chinese imports minus US exports for each 4-digit SIC industry.
Binary variable recorded by comparing the CEO's name reported in the 10-K filing for year t + 1 to the name reported in the previous year.
CEO first year equals year joining firm; analysis restricted to first5 tenure years; higher implies lower prosociality.
Embedding cosine similarity of employee and fair words in annual reports.
We count normalized by all words in earnings-call presentation/Q&A, averaged over calls.
Share of campaign donations to Republican candidates; higher proxy indicates lower prosociality.
CEO turnover split by press-report-based forced classification; forced/unforced distinction is imperfect and may undercount forced departures.
CEO turnover split by press-report-based forced classification; forced/unforced distinction is imperfect and may undercount forced departures.
State-level layoff-cost condition; source refers to Appendices F/G for data construction. Do not invent numeric cutoff or source provider.
State-level layoff-cost condition; source refers to Appendices F/G for data construction. Do not invent numeric cutoff or source provider.
A binary variable that identifies games developed by Indie developers, representing complementors with weak resource endowment.
A binary variable indicating multiplayer games, capturing reliance on network effects.
A binary indicator coded as one if the game is available on both platforms and zero otherwise (remains exclusive to Steam).
A binary indicator equal to one if game i participated in a Steam sale s, and zero otherwise.
time_window: One year before and one year after EGS launch

description: Binary indicator equal to one for Steam sales that took place after the launch of the Epic Games Store (December 2018) and zero for sales in the year before. The main specification uses a two-year window, one year before and one year after the launch, in a difference-in-differences design.
time_window: 1 year before and 1 year after EGS launch

description: Indicator variable coded as 1 for women and 0 for men sourced from LISA data.
Binary indicator equal to 1 if the individual exited wage employment to launch an incorporated organization and 0 if they stayed in wage employment.
Log labor income of individual i in year t based on comprehensive information on individual annual earnings reported to the Swedish tax authorities.
Individual's cumulative high school grade point average measured in the 12th grade.
Defined as industries with more than 50% men.
A dummy variable taking value 1 for groups that signed up to compete as groups (joint search), and 0 for groups constructed synthetically through a matching process (independent search).
Total number of solutions submitted by groups for each competition, aggregating individual submissions for independent search groups.
Standard deviation of public scores on all solutions submitted by the groups, measuring the variance of their search attempts.
Measured as the number of days between when a firm submitted a 510(k) application to the FDA and when it received a substantial equivalence ruling from the FDA.
A count of the number of predicate devices listed in the 510(k) application for each device.

variable_name: Citation of External Predicate in Same Product Code as Device
description: A binary measure, equaling one if the focal applicant device includes a predicate reference to one or more devices that share the same product code.
A binary variable that captures whether the applicant device cites one or more predicate references that are exemplars (highly cited devices in the same product code).
A binary variable reflecting whether the applicant firm's own first device is cited as a predicate in the 510(k) application for their second device.

A dummy variable that equals 1 if a firm is majority owned or controlled by the Chinese government (at the central or local level) or its agencies, and 0 otherwise. More precisely, it takes the value of 1 when CSMAR reports the controlling shareholder as a government entity or another firm controlled by a government entity. It is time-invariant during the sample window.
The sum of all three types of patents filed by a firm in a given year. It is a count variable estimated with a zero-inflated negative binomial model.
The number of invention patents filed by the firm in a given year. It is one of the four count dependent variables used to test H1.
The number of utility model patents filed by the firm in a given year. Utility model patents are petty patents for incremental innovation.
The number of design patents filed by the firm in a given year. It is one of the four count dependent variables used to test H1.

variable_name: Number of new IPC sub-classes (firm level)
description: At the firm level the authors aggregate the number of new four-digit IPC sub-classes in each invention patent filing of firm i in year t up to the firm-year level. At the patent level the four-digit IPC sub-classes of an invention patent filing are compared with those in prior invention patents of the same firm in the preceding three years and the number of new sub-classes is counted. A higher value indicates a larger number of technological areas new to the firm.

variable_name: Number of new IPC sub-classes (patent level)
description: For each invention patent filing of firm i in year t, the four-digit IPC sub-classes are compared with those in prior invention patents of firm i in the preceding three years (t-1, t-2, t-3), and the number of new four-digit IPC sub-classes in the focal filing is counted. Estimated with a zero-inflated negative binomial model.

A Blau index of the firm's invention patent filings across four-digit IPC sub-classes: Technological diversity_it = 1 - sum_k (n_k/n)^2, where n is the total number of invention patent filings of firm i in year t and n_k is the number of invention patent filings in the kth four-digit IPC sub-class of firm i in year t. A higher value indicates a more diverse scope of technology.

variable_name: Similarity between new and prior invention patents (firm level)
description: Cosine similarity between the firm's IPC sub-class portfolio of invention patent filings in year t and its IPC sub-class portfolio of invention patent filings from the preceding three years (t-1, t-2, t-3). The higher the value, the closer the technological areas between the focal year's patents and prior invention patents.

variable_name: Similarity between new and prior invention patents (patent level)
description: Cosine similarity between the vector of IPC sub-classes in the focal invention patent filing (A) and the vector of IPC sub-classes in invention patent filings applied by the same firm in the preceding three years (B), where A_k and B_k are the numbers of the kth IPC sub-class in each vector. The higher the value, the closer the technological areas between the focal patent and prior invention patents.

For a given invention patent filing, each unique section is worth 3 points, each unique class 2 points, and each unique sub-class 1 point; the points are added up to obtain the Recombinant scope score. The larger the value, the broader the technological scope of the focal invention patent.

The mean value of the ratio of R&D expenditure to total sales in the previous three years (t-1, t-2, t-3) for firm i in year t. R&D expenditure of the sample firms is obtained by matching them with China's Census dataset. Included both as a control and in the three-way interaction SOE * After * R&D intensity.

The mean value of the ratio of export sales to total sales in the previous three years (t-1, t-2, t-3) for firm i in year t. The information is sourced from China's Census dataset. Included both as a control and in the three-way interaction SOE * After * Export intensity.

A dummy variable that equals 1 for those industries that are monopolized by the state, and 0 otherwise. State monopoly is defined by referring to several legal and policy documents, including the Protocol on the Accession of the People's Republic of China to the WTO, the Catalogue for the Guidance of Foreign-Invested Industries, and the Thirty-Six Guidelines on Encouraging and Supporting the Development of Non-Public Sector. The classification is unchanged during the study period.
A dummy variable that equals 1 for high-technology industries defined by China's National Bureau of Statistics, and 0 otherwise. The classification is unchanged during the study period.

Sum of annual values of investments in innovation (R&D expenditures), corporate venturing (Crunchbase aggregated capital), and strategic renewal (technological acquisitions from SDC Platinum), divided by total assets.
The number of directors serving on a given board in each year who were classified as possessing entrepreneurial skills using keywords in proxy statement biographies and nomination rationales.
The number of directors on the board who were classified as possessing skills in finance using keywords in proxy statement biographies and nomination rationales.
Count restricted to directors serving on the corporate development committee, identified from proxy statements.
Count restricted to directors serving on the corporate development committee, identified from proxy statements.

Following Eggers and Kaul (2018), the non-AI citations made by the focal patent are compared with the non-AI citations of other patents in the same technology space, defined by the patent's subclass in the USPTO CPC system. For a non-AI citation from technological domain i to domain j, all other patents in domain i in the prior 5 years (t-5 to t-1) are taken and the percentage of their backward non-AI citations that were to domain j is calculated, giving the LINK score; a lower LINK score indicates a less explored citation combination. Patent-level novelty is 1 minus the lowest LINK score for all non-AI citations made by the focal patent, and the score is normalized by subtracting the average score for all patents in the same technological domain in the prior year. Citations to AI patents are excluded from the calculation of the LINK scores and the novelty measure.
time_window: prior 5 years (t-5 to t-1); normalized against the prior year (t-1)

description: Takes on a value of 1 when a focal patent cites a patent identified as AI prior art by the Giczy et al. (2022) methodology, and 0 otherwise.
Takes on a value of 1 when the most novel citation (i.e., the citation with the lowest LINK score) also cites an AI patent, and 0 otherwise.
The key independent variable in the H2b analysis, indicating whether the candidate cited patent also builds on AI.
level: patent-pair observation (focal patent and candidate cited patent)

description: Equals 1 if a recombination between the focal patent and a candidate cited patent is realized and 0 otherwise.
Logged count of AI citations in focal patent; alternative intensity specification for H1. Zero-offset convention not specified in these source passages.
Logged number of distinct AI categories cited, measuring breadth of AI input; alternative H1 specification.
Logged AI citations in candidate cited patent, alternative H2b predictor.
AI-citation share in candidate cited patent, alternative H2b predictor. Denominator is not independently specified by P135/table label.

Community network closure is built from the county-level Facebook Social Connectedness Index, a measure of social connectedness between all dyads among U.S. counties created by mapping U.S. Facebook users to their counties of residence and counting friendship links among users who interacted on Facebook in the 30 days prior to the snapshot. For each pair of counties the index is the normalized total number of friendship links for that geographic pair. Community network closure measures, for individuals in the county where the focal gym operates, the proportion of within-county ties to overall ties, so smaller values indicate networks that span to other U.S. counties and larger values indicate more insular networks. The authors take the natural log of the variable to account for skewness of the raw measure; the exact formula is not readable in the text.
time_window: Social Connectedness Index data as of August 2020, constructed from friendship links as of July 30, 2020

description: Community ethnic segregation is captured with the Relative Diversity Index, which relies on county- and census-tract-level data and captures the ratio of within-tract diversity to total diversity in the county. Using 2020 decennial census data, the authors counted non-Hispanic Asian, non-Hispanic Black, Hispanic, non-Hispanic White, and non-Hispanic Other individuals within each tract and used these counts to calculate the Simpson Interaction Index at the county and census tract levels. The index can take values from zero to one, with zero indicating that all tracts have the exact same diversity as the county as a whole and one representing a county where tracts have no diversity. A score close to 1 indicates high segregation, with separate ethnic groups concentrated in different neighborhoods, while a score near 0 suggests ethnic groups being more evenly distributed.

Community issue connectedness is computed from the Meta Social Connectedness Index at the county-dyad level, focusing on connections between each county and Hennepin County, Minnesota, where George Floyd was killed. As in the network closure measure, the index reflects total normalized Facebook friendship links among county residents based on 30-day interaction cutoffs. Higher scores indicate stronger friendship links and a closer social connection to the community that was directly impacted, while lower scores suggest a more distant, indirect exposure likely through media rather than direct community ties. The authors take the natural logarithm to address the skewness of the data.

Community dependence is measured from Google Community Mobility Reports data capturing county-level changes in daily movements. For each county the authors calculated the mean percentage change in workplace mobility between March 14 and June 7, 2020, relative to January-February 2020 baseline levels, and took the absolute value of these changes for ease of interpretation, with larger values indicating greater mobility declines. The authors argue that in all counties the mobility drops resulted from exogenous changes in consumer behavior attributable to the pandemic, not to the statements about George Floyd's death.
time_window: March 14 to June 7, 2020, relative to a January-February 2020 baseline

description: Community-level issue salience is measured from ACLED protest data on the Black Lives Matter movement. The authors isolated protest events that took place between May 26, 2020 (the day after George Floyd died) and June 6, 2020 (the day before Glassman's comments were posted online) and were listed by ACLED as involving the Black Lives Matter movement. They then created a count of protest events meeting these criteria at the county level, added 1, and took the natural logarithm to account for potential skewness, which separates the salience measure from activity that could have more directly influenced firms to respond.

Firm responsiveness is measured with an indicator variable that takes the value 1 if a gym publicly stated its intention to disaffiliate from CrossFit and 0 otherwise. Announcements were collected from a public crowdsourced list maintained by Morning Chalk Up, then validated by a research assistant who filtered out non-U.S. gyms, verified U.S. announcements, checked naming inconsistencies, and removed firms whose statements did not actually declare an intention to disaffiliate. Public disaffiliation statements were typically made by gym owners and posted on gyms' social media accounts and/or official websites between June 6 and June 26, 2020. Out of 4,979 U.S.-based CrossFit gyms, 754 firms declared their intention to disaffiliate.
A binary variable equal to 1 if the entrepreneur who launched the focal firm owns or is the CEO of other companies at the same time.
Reflects the number of years the focal firm survived, ranging from 1 to 5.
Log(Revenue + 1) of the focal firm for a given year t.
Calculated as 1 minus a Redeployability Index based on BEA capital flow tables; measures the extent to which assets in a particular industry lack alternative uses in other industries.

The document-topic score that latent Dirichlet allocation (70-topic model) assigns to topic 6 for each job posting; each document-topic score represents the proportion of a job posting's content dedicated to that particular topic. Topic 6 was selected by the authors as the topic that most closely captures purpose claim language, using words such as people, impact, and help, being future oriented, and emphasizing ambitious, aspirational goals and a collective objective.

The subject-level average of the set of Likert-scale statements the authors developed to capture the dimensions of a purpose claim (ambitious or challenging goal, collective and/or unifying endeavor, future orientation, societal orientation) for the job post a participant evaluated. Responses used a five-point agree/disagree scale, and the block is highly reliable (Cronbach's alpha = 0.91).

The percentage of a job post devoted to purpose language, that is, the strength with which topic 6 is present in the job description as given by topic modeling. The distribution across job posts is skewed, with a median of 0.61%, an average of 1.62%, and a 99th percentile of 14.11%.

The total number of applications that each job received on the university job board, taken from the application records. Only applications made by last-year undergraduate (senior) and master's students with U.S. citizenship are considered. The number of applications is an overdispersed count variable (average of 0.64 and variance of 8.98 applications per job).

variable_name: Firm size (Small Firm and Medium Firm dummies)
description: The number of employees of the hiring firm, as reported on the job posting and used as a proxy for capacity. It is modeled as a categorical variable: Small Firm equals one if the firm has less than or equal to 50 employees; Medium Firm equals one if the firm has between 50 and 1,000 employees; large firms (more than 1,000 employees) are the baseline. Information on employees was available in nine ordinal categories.

The average of three seven-point agree/disagree Likert items about the company's capacity, ability, and resources to address the world's greatest hunger challenges; the items exhibit high reliability (Cronbach's alpha = 0.94).

The average of three seven-point agree/disagree Likert items measuring perceptions of the authenticity of the company's claim, an adjusted scale based on the authenticity literature (Cronbach's alpha = 0.95).

Participants' score on a single seven-point likely/unlikely Likert item asking how likely they would be to apply for the job, assuming the job was in their field and they had the proper credentials. The variable ranges from one to seven.
Indicator variable for Intervention A in the regressions, set to one for farmers in villages randomized to Intervention A and set to zero for the base program, which is the control group.
Indicator variable for Intervention B in the regressions, set to one for farmers in villages randomized to Intervention B and set to zero for the base program, which is the control group.

A binary indicator of the farmer's intention to continue in the following year, coded one if the farmer intended to stay in the program and zero otherwise. It was measured only post-experiment, so it cannot be analyzed as a change score.

Gauges the farmer's intended land allocation for Crop X for the following year's program, measured in hectares and set to zero if the farmer did not intend to continue in the program. It was measured pre-experiment (for the current year) as well as post-experiment.

A count measuring the extent of soil turning employed by a farmer, used as a measure of adoption of the climate-friendly practice of reduced land tillage. It was measured pre-experiment as well as post-experiment via in-person surveys and analyzed as a change score.

Defined as the average of two kinds of inorganic fertilizers - diammonium phosphate (DAP) and urea - used by the farmer, in kilograms per hectare, used as a measure of adoption of the climate-friendly practice of reduced inorganic fertilizer use. It was measured pre-experiment as well as post-experiment via in-person surveys and analyzed as a change score.
The difference between published one-year demand growth forecasts and actual historical results, defined as ( | Forecast demand growth - Actual demand growth | X 100 ) / (Actual demand growth).
time_window: Five-year periods before and after discontinuities

description: Mean annual sales growth in units (tons of cement, passenger-seat-miles, or minicomputer units), adjusted for real GNP growth.
time_window: Five-year periods before and after discontinuities

variable_name: unweighted variance in five-year sales growth percentage
description: Unweighted variance in five-year sales growth percentage among firms; available for airlines and minicomputers, not cement (Table 2).
Annual improvement of largest kiln barrel-per-day capacity relative to prior-year frontier. Identify standout discontinuities from equipment histories.
time_window: Industry-specific historical coverage; five-year eras where applicable

description: Passenger seats multiplied by miles flown at normal speed and average annual hours; compare frontier capacity against prior year.
time_window: Industry-specific historical coverage; five-year eras where applicable

description: Central processor cycle time identifies performance changes and major discontinuities.
time_window: Industry-specific historical coverage; five-year eras where applicable

description: New entrant sold no products before industry entry; existing firm sold at least one product beforehand. Locus measure is proportion of new firms among earliest adopters, distinct from hypothesis 7 first-four rule.
time_window: Industry-specific historical coverage; five-year eras where applicable

description: Entry at first production; exit when production ceases or firm acquired. Acquirer counts as entrant only if previously outside product class. Bankruptcy only if production stops. Compare five-year eras; airline regulated 1938–1979 omitted; zero-exit era ratio undefined.
time_window: Industry-specific historical coverage; five-year eras where applicable

description: First four adopters of each innovation versus all other firms; four selected arbitrarily to balance group size and early status.
time_window: Industry-specific historical coverage; five-year eras where applicable

description: Table 2 describes end/start five-year sales ratio; Table 9 note reports mean annual percentage growth. Preserve this operational wording distinction. Two periods lack interpretable statistics because new firms have zero base-year sales.
time_window: Industry-specific historical coverage; five-year eras where applicable

description: Technological discontinuities were identified from year-by-year key performance parameters (kiln capacity in cement, passenger-seat-miles per year in airlines, processor cycle time in minicomputers) as the few innovations that markedly advanced the state of the art. Each discontinuity was then classified by the authors from industry histories as competence-destroying if it required new skills and knowledge and rendered existing know-how obsolete. Two of the eight discontinuities after the niche openings were classified this way: powdered coal and rotary kilns in cement, and integrated circuits in minicomputers.

Technological discontinuities were identified from year-by-year key performance parameters (kiln capacity in cement, passenger-seat-miles per year in airlines, processor cycle time in minicomputers) as the few innovations that markedly advanced the state of the art. Each discontinuity was then classified by the authors from industry histories as competence-enhancing if it built on existing know-how without making old skills obsolete. Six of the eight discontinuities after the niche openings were classified this way, such as the Edison and Dundee kilns in cement, jet and widebody aircraft in airlines, and semiconductor memory in minicomputers.
The authors use return on sales as the dependent variable in all models. They present findings based on a ROS measure as the dependent variable in all models.

The authors used a Herfindahl-type quantitative index based on the share of a firm's sales in each four-digit SIC industry. It is defined as product diversity = 1 - 2S,, where S; is the proportion of a firm's sales reported in product group j. The measure takes into account the number of segments in which a firm operates and the relative importance of each segment in sales.

Multinationality is measured as the proportion of a firm's sales derived from operations outside the home country to total sales. The authors note that it includes resale of intermediate goods and thus is not an absolute measure of the size of foreign operations, but it provides a relative indicator of international diversity.
Country scope was measured as the number of foreign countries in which an MNE had operating subsidiaries in 1987. The authors use it as a proxy for the geographical scope of international operations.
Firm size, a commonly used control variable often related to diversity levels, was measured by total revenues for 1987.
Firm leverage is measured as the percentage of long-term debt to total capital (debt plus equity).
The industry variable was measured as the average annual growth of industry shipment over the 1982-87 period using data from the Survey of Current Business.

variable_name: number of long-term contracts with stars
description: We obtained data on the number of long-term contracts with stars that were held by each studio or its producers for each of the years studied. These biographies were all coded individually to link the relevant stars to all the major studios for every year of the study. All contracts for stars that ran for four or more years during the period between 1936 and 1965 were included in the data.
time_window: each year of the study; contracts running for four or more years during 1936 to 1965

variable_name: number of domestic theaters owned or under long-term lease
description: We obtained information on the number of domestic theaters owned or under long-term lease for each studio for each year from figures provided in Moody's Industrial Manuals.

variable_name: percentage of Academy Awards won annually
description: The level of these skills is in part reflected by the number of Academy Awards that a studio won each year. We gathered data on the percentage of Academy Awards that were won annually by each studio. The primary source for this data was a complete listing of Academy Awards published by Michael (1968).

variable_name: last two years' average production costs per film
description: The scale and complexity of past projects is reflected in the last two years' average production costs per film. We obtained this data on film costs and producers' fees from the annual financial statements of each studio. We averaged production costs for the films that had been released by the studio over the previous two years to reflect the recent history of expenditures.

We did, however, compute annual return on sales, both with and without theater revenues and profits. In every instance, we were concerned only with the revenues and profits from a studio's film business.

We did, however, compute annual return on sales, both with and without theater revenues and profits. In every instance, we were concerned only with the revenues and profits from a studio's film business.

We also examined operating profits, but without the theater operations. We did not measure operating profits with theaters as this would have artificially penalized and rendered noncomparable the studios that did not own any theaters.

Finally, we included the domestic market share figures for each of the studios. Annual market share data for each studio were derived from its revenues as a percentage of total box office receipts for the year.

Environmental uncertainty was operationalized as a period split. The years 1936 through 1950 are treated as the predictable era and 1951 through 1965 as the uncertain era, and the models are estimated separately for each 14-year period. The authors checked the split with year-to-year correlations of studio revenues, market shares and profits in each era, and with turnover of studio production heads.
Our dependent variable, sales, represented monthly retail sales for each store. Sales is measured in dollars for each store-month observation in the established store sample.

For the comparative analyses relevant to Hypothesis 6, the dependent variable was Month 6 sales, which was retail sales in the sixth month following the opening of the new store. It is measured for each new store.

In established stores, transfers in were measured as the rolling sum of transfers in each month over the prior six-month period. The authors chose a six-month period because the effects of transfers are unlikely to show up immediately and may be less detectable after an extended period.

Comobile transfers in were measured as the rolling six-month sum of transfers in in each month who entered the store with at least one other individual from their prior store. The measure focuses on the number of people who move together rather than the number of relationships.

Multisource transfers in refers to the rolling six-month sum of transfers in in each month who did not enter a store with any other individual from their prior store. Comobile transfers in and multisource transfers in add up to the total number of transfers in.
Transfers out were measured as the rolling sum of transfers out in each month over the prior six-month period.
Comobile transfers out were measured as the rolling six-month sum of transfers out in each month who left the store with at least one other individual from their current store.

Multi-destination transfers out refers to the rolling six-month sum of transfers out in each month who did not leave their store for their subsequent store with any other people from their store. Comobile transfers out and multi-destination transfers out add up to the total number of transfers out.

In new stores, initial transfers in was measured as the number of individuals in a store's first full three months of operation who came from a different store in the organization. The first three months were used because stores often needed that long to become fully and stably staffed.
time_window: first full three months of operation

description: Initial comobile transfers in refers to the subset of the initial transfers in that moved to the new store with at least one other person.
time_window: first full three months of operation

description: Initial multisource transfers in refers to the number of initial transfers in that moved to the new store without any individuals from their prior store.
time_window: first full three months of operation

description: Stores were classified as established stores if they were in operation prior to the beginning of data collection, and as new stores if they opened during the data collection period. Of the 1,143 stores with data on retail sales, 884 were established stores and the remaining 259 were new stores; analyses for Hypotheses 1-5b used only established stores, while Hypothesis 6 compared new and established stores.

The weekly average number of teams that an employee belonged to during the six-month focal period (July to December 2012), computed from weekly work-hour registrations. For example, three teams per week on average across the six-month period.
time_window: six-month focal period, July to December 2012

description: The number of unique ongoing teams in which the employee's membership started or ended during the focal six-month period. A team entry event was coded when the employee worked on the team during the focal period but not during the pre-period (January 2011 to June 2012); a team exit event was coded when the employee worked on the team during the focal period but not during the post-period (January to December 2013). If an employee both joined and left the same team during the focal period, the team was counted only once, and cases involving entire teams simultaneously forming or disbanding were excluded.
time_window: focal period July to December 2012 with pre-period January 2011 to June 2012 and post-period January to December 2013

description: Five items from the organization's employee satisfaction survey, rated on a scale from 1 (low) to 10 (high) and averaged into a mean score (alpha = .83). Three items reflected the mobilization of resources: the extent to which I receive feedback from my colleagues, the extent to which knowledge is shared by my colleagues, and the amount of inspiration I get from my colleagues. Two items reflected mutual respect and goodwill among coworkers: the mutual respect among colleagues and the honesty between colleagues.
time_window: employee satisfaction survey in the final month of 2012

description: The organization's systematic and multisource end-of-year appraisal procedure, resembling a 360-degree feedback process including employee self-ratings as well as assessments by formal supervisors, project team leaders, peers, and customers. Employees were evaluated on technical proficiency, planning and organizational skills, and research output; all ratings were gathered in a standardized form and condensed into a single overall performance score ranging from 1 ('substantial need for improvement') to 5 ('highly effective and well-functioning'). The subsequent (2013) score was used as the dependent variable while controlling for the prior (2012) score.
scale: 1 ('substantial need for improvement') to 5 ('highly effective and well-functioning')

description: An established one-item measure asking employees to indicate, on average, in how many teams they had simultaneously worked during the past six months.

Two items aligned with the definition of FTM as the frequency with which an employee joins and leaves ongoing teams over time: 'How often did you join a team during the past six months?' and 'How often did you leave a team during the past six months?' Employees responded on a 5-point Likert scale (1 = 'never,' 5 = 'extremely often').

A five-item scale from Subramaniam and Youndt (2005), with employees responding to five statements on a 5-point Likert response scale (1 = 'strongly disagree,' 5 = 'strongly agree'); internal consistency was alpha = .94. The measure applied a collective referent based on a referent-shift consensus model ('the employees') and contained items reflecting the structural and purposive nature of organizational social capital; an example item is 'The employees interact and exchange ideas with people from different areas of the company.' The latent between-firm component of employees' ratings was used in the multilevel analyses.
level: firm (latent between-firm component of employee ratings)

description: Operating profits (in million EUR) taken from the firms' annual balance sheets at the end of the year in which the survey data were collected, with the firms' prior performance levels (from the preceding business year) controlled for.
time_window: end of the survey year, controlling for the preceding business year

description: An established 4-item measure from Carmeli et al. (2009) with an individual referent, using items that reflect the relational dimension of social capital; items tapped access to and mobilization of personal resources (example item: 'To what extent do you get help from your colleagues at work?') and the experience of respect and goodwill from one's coworkers (example item: 'To what extent do you feel close to your colleagues at work?'). Employees responded on a 5-point Likert scale (1 = 'not at all,' 5 = 'to a very large extent'); alpha = .88.
scale: 5-point Likert scale (1 = 'not at all,' 5 = 'to a very large extent')

description: A general goal achievement measure from Kunze, Raes, and Bruch (2015), asking all employees to indicate the percentage of goals they had achieved in the past six months, as agreed upon with their direct supervisor, from 0% to 100%.

The latent between-firm component of employees' individual MTM scores in the multilevel analyses. Employees' nesting in firms explained 6% of the variance in MTM (ICC1 = .06, F = 6.44, p < .001; ICC2 = .84), indicating that firms varied significantly in their use of MTM structures.
level: firm (latent between-firm component of employee scores)

description: The latent between-firm component of employees' individual FTM scores in the multilevel analyses. Employees' nesting in firms explained 8% of the variance in FTM (ICC1 = .08, F = 9.98, p < .001; ICC2 = .90), indicating that firms varied significantly in their use of FTM structures.
level: firm (latent between-firm component of employee scores)

description: A latent firm-level factor consisting of the latent firm-level components of MTM and FTM, described by the authors as a second-order construct. The multilevel CFA included the latent firm-level components of MTM and FTM forming a latent flexible team arrangements factor.

The transcripts of CEO speech during earnings conference calls were content-analyzed, focusing on the managerial discussion section as opposed to the question and answer section. Positive words minus negative words, scaled by the total number of words the CEO used in the call. Tone words were identified with the Loughran and McDonald dictionaries, which comprise 354 positive words and 2,355 negative words tailored to business contexts.

A binary indicator that is 0 for the four quarters before the first short seller attack on a competitor and 1 for the four quarters after the attack. The moderators all interact with this binary effect. Firms were identified as competing with attacked firms in the year the attack occurred, and each firm-level observation was included only once.
time_window: four quarters before and four quarters after the first attack on a competitor

description: Combines two components: the TNIC-3 product similarity score, which quantifies product-market overlap, and the ratio of the attacked firm's market share to that of its competitor in markets where both compete. Both metrics were min-max normalized to place all values on a positive spectrum, and the product of the two components was then normalized based on the minimum and maximum values of each quarter across the entire TNIC sample. The measure was rescaled by multiplying by 100, resulting in a range between 0 and 100; higher values indicate a higher level of market overlap where the attacked firm holds a dominant position.

Cumulative abnormal returns (CAR) after a short attack, based on a market model estimated over a 240-day period that concludes with a 30-day gap before the short attack, with a three-day window [-1, +1] used to calculate CAR. Declines were captured using the absolute value of negative CAR values; positive CAR values were set to zero and separately included in the model as a spline term, so larger values indicate greater declines.
time_window: three-day window [-1, +1] around the attack; 240-day estimation period ending 30 days before the attack

description: The focal firm's stock returns in the quarter prior to the conference call, standardized for each quarter based on the firm's competitors. Higher values indicate stronger prior stock price performance.
time_window: quarter prior to the conference call

description: Status is measured as the amount of sell-side security analyst coverage, scaled by a focal analyst's industry expertise. To obtain analyst industry expertise, the authors first count the number of firms each analyst covers in each industry using China's three-digit Standard Industrial Classification system; the analyst(s) covering the largest number of firms in a given industry is assigned a score of 1, and other analysts' scores are the ratio of the number of firms they cover to the number covered by the analyst covering the largest number of firms in that industry; the firm's status is the aggregate of the industry expertise scores of the analysts who cover that firm. Status is winsorized at 1% thresholds, and all independent variables are lagged by one year.

Following Sanders and Hambrick (2007), the authors measure financially uncertain investments as the logged sum of capital (CAPEX), R&D, and acquisition expenditures in Chinese yuan. CAPEX, R&D, and acquisitions are treated as uncertain investments because they represent long-term commitments of capital whose outcomes are difficult to assess a priori.

Historical benchmarks are calculated as an exponentially weighted average of past ROA; the specification of the weighting formula is not readable in the text, though the prose states that the aspiration level At is a function of ROA at t-1 and a weight a given to the most recent aspiration level, with a set at 0.3. The historical benchmark is then subtracted from the focal firm's ROA in a given year. A score of 0 means the firm met its historical benchmarks, and a score above (below) 0 means it exceeded (fell short of) that benchmark.
time_window: past ROA, exponentially weighted; weight a = 0.3

description: Industry benchmarks are calculated as the average ROA of other firms in the same industry in a given year. The industry average ROA is deducted from the focal firm's ROA in that year; a score of 0 means the firm met its social benchmarks, and a score above (below) 0 means it exceeded (fell short of) its social benchmarks.

Status benchmarks are calculated by comparing a focal firm's ROA to the ROA of other firms of similar status. Firms above the 66th percentile are classified as high-status firms in a given industry for a particular year, firms below the 33rd percentile as low-status firms, and all other firms as middle-status firms; the average ROA of each status group for a given industry in a given year is used as the status benchmark and is deducted from the focal firm's ROA in that year. A score of 0 means the firm met its social benchmarks, and a score above (below) 0 means it exceeded (fell short of) its social benchmarks.
Disaggregated component of financially uncertain investments. Log transformed; add one when measure contains zero. Secondary decomposition outcome, not new ex ante hypothesis.
Disaggregated component of financially uncertain investments. Log transformed; add one when measure contains zero. Secondary decomposition outcome, not new ex ante hypothesis.
Disaggregated component of financially uncertain investments. Log transformed; add one when measure contains zero. Secondary decomposition outcome, not new ex ante hypothesis.
Spline component: firm ROA minus historical benchmark ROA when performance is below the benchmark, and zero otherwise. Secondary decomposition of existing moderator.
Spline component: firm ROA minus historical benchmark ROA when performance is above the benchmark, and zero otherwise. Secondary decomposition of existing moderator.
Spline component: firm ROA minus industry benchmark ROA when performance is below the benchmark, and zero otherwise. Secondary decomposition of existing moderator.
Spline component: firm ROA minus industry benchmark ROA when performance is above the benchmark, and zero otherwise. Secondary decomposition of existing moderator.
Spline component: firm ROA minus status benchmark ROA when performance is below the benchmark, and zero otherwise. Secondary decomposition of existing moderator.
Spline component: firm ROA minus status benchmark ROA when performance is above the benchmark, and zero otherwise. Secondary decomposition of existing moderator.

Directors were classified by the SIC industry of the company they worked for. The economic performance of the 18 SIC industry sectors over 1971-81 was measured from the index of industry sector output at constant factor cost, smoothed by the percentile variation from the underlying national GDP and by regression on the adjusted indices; the sign of the ranked betas indicates growth or decline relative to the underlying momentum of GDP. Five sectors showed 'real' growth (winners) and 13 'real' decline (losers), and a third category of greater variability relative to the aggregate national trend was labelled turbulence; the sector categories were therefore growth (GOGOs), turbulence (YOYOs) and decline (DODOs).

Directors' international work experience and their valuation of it, reported in the questionnaire. The authors report that GOGOs showed an international grooming in terms of work experience and were very positive about its value upon their managerial capabilities, while DODOs showed the reverse.

The function in which directors started their careers and their major functional experience, self-reported. Growing-sector directors were more likely to start in the financial function and declining-sector directors in the production area, but promotion to general management masked functional differences; directors were also asked which functional route was the fastest route to the top.

Length of service of the director with the company, self-reported; the authors note the average tenure of the directors with their companies was 19 years. Declining-sector directors stayed with their companies far longer while GOGOs were occupationally mobile.

Directors' perception of whether contacts or the 'old boy network' advance managerial careers, reported in the questionnaire. Declining sectors considered the 'old boy network' certainly exists, but not for them.
Directors' pay, self-reported; the authors report that 38 per cent of GOGO directors were paid in excess of £50,000 (1981 = $90,000) compared to 21 per cent of directors in declining industries.

The directors' working hours and the increase in hours worked over the last 10 years, as they reported. Directors of declining sectors recorded a decrease in the hourly working week whereas the more active categories showed the reverse; business travel and holidays taken were also measured but gave no significant results.

Directors reported their sibling position, parents' marital status, single-parent upbringing, parental influence, parents' occupation and their own marital status. The only positive result in this sub-section related economic performance to a single-parent upbringing: directors whose industries were growing came from divorced parents, whereas those in decline had a single-parent upbringing caused by death.

The geographic location of the director's childhood, reported on the questionnaire and coded as 'Inner Britain' (south-east), 'outer Britain' (the north), Scotland and outside the UK. A second measure segmented directors into urban, suburban and rural childhood locations, which gave no significant result.

Secondary education (public fee-paying, grammar, other), university attended (Oxbridge, red brick, grey brick), tertiary education (arts vs. science degree) and MBA achievement, all self-reported. None of these related to industry economic performance.

Whether the director played team or individual sports at university, and the importance they attached to winning at sports, both self-reported. Directors in declining sectors preferred individual sports while those representing growth industries preferred team sports; the importance of winning was not significant.

Directors' ratings of the personal characteristics important for executive success, self-reported. Intelligence was of prime importance for GOGOs with creativity a close second, concern for people was held to be the most important characteristic for YOYOs, and personal integrity was the most valued trait for DODOs.
The perceived influence of the director's first boss on his career, self-reported. The greater the industry decline, the more this variable was perceived as a factor.

Directors' self-perception of their management style, reported on the questionnaire. The authors report the result was inconclusive, perhaps because style was perceived through the directors' own eyes rather than those of their subordinates.

Directors' attitude towards early retirement, self-reported. YOYOs wanted to retire early; GOGOs were satisfied with their choice of careers and would stay the course, while DODOs would choose a different career if free but would 'soldier on' as long as possible.

Whether the director would choose the same career again and whether he would continue if financially independent, as self-reported. GOGOs were satisfied with their choice of careers, and would stay the course, whereas DODOs would choose a different career if free.

Directors' drinking, smoking, exercise and sleeping habits, outside interests and second career, time with family and stress, all self-reported. The authors report that no evidence whatsoever existed for the populist view of directors as jetsetting, heavy drinking and highly stressed; relative to economic performance, DODOs smoked more heavily.

The importance of religion in the director's life and his religious denomination, self-reported. DODOs considered religion to be a significant factor in their lives, whereas GOGOs appeared to place little value on non-secular philosophies.
The director's age, self-reported. Directors of growing industries were significantly younger than those who operated within declining sectors.

Director characteristics were measured with a mailed questionnaire to executive directors of the largest 450 British companies, and each variable was compared across the three industry performance groups (GOGOs, YOYOs, DODOs). The variables are grouped as job-centered factors, hygiene factors (remuneration, hours worked and their change, business travel, holidays, perceived company status), international exposure, family influences, childhood location, education, success traits, management style, attitudes and personal habits. The hypothesis on file (H.6 to H.10) concerns the hygiene factor items.
scale: mixed questionnaire items (nominal, ordinal and interval), each tested separately

description: The lagged (1997 through 2001) standard deviation of the sample firms' quarterly returns on assets. It is an accounting-based risk measure used together with a market-based measure to enhance the robustness of the findings.

variable_name: Standard deviation of total returns to shareholders
description: The lagged standard deviation of monthly total returns to shareholders. It is the market-based risk measure used alongside the accounting-based measure of the standard deviation of ROA.

variable_name: Ratio of managerial salary stream to ownership incentives
description: Average salary stream values divided by the combined values of stock and option holdings as of 1996. Salary stream values were obtained by identifying each executive's 1996 salary, estimating years left in the career by subtracting age from 65, and calculating the present value of the salary annuity discounted at 3 percent; the values of the top five executives' annuities were averaged.

variable_name: Average top management team option holdings
description: The average of the values of the top management team members' at-the-money option holdings in 1996, valued using Kerr and Kren's modified version of the Black-Scholes model, which reflects the underlying volatility in the sample firms' share prices.

variable_name: Average top management team stock ownership
description: The number of shares the CEO and the four senior managers owned in 1996 multiplied by the average monthly closing stock prices of their enterprises for the same year, divided by five to derive the value of the average top management team member's shareholdings.

variable_name: Number of products added (current product groups)
description: We measure each organization's simultaneous product additions by counting the number of new product categories entered by an organization (above one) in a given year. If an organization added products in a group where it already produced, then this was counted in the variable number of products added (current product groups). The multiple-product addition variable begins set at zero when the organization is born and then is set at the number of products added in the most recent multiple-product addition, if any.

Our dependent variable is organizational failure, operationalized as occurring when a semiconductor manufacturing organization ceased operating. If a semiconductor manufacturer continued to operate through 1984, the end of the study period, then its life is coded as right censored as of 1984 and no failure event is recorded. Mergers and acquisitions were investigated to see whether name changes, changes in location, and significant changes in product offerings implied that an ownership change involved the ending of operations by the existing semiconductor organization; only in those cases were ownership changes regarded as organizational failure events.

Each time-since-change clock is set at zero until a given type of change occurs, and then increments upward annually until another change of that type occurs. In the year following the next change, the clock is then reset to zero and again increments upwards each year until the next change.

Count of the products offered in a given year by the organization that were the first ever of a given product category to appear in the industry. The sum of the organization's product offerings and its effect are decomposed into this term and the number of follower products offered in the year.

Count of the products offered in a given year by the organization within product categories that had already appeared in the industry. All product offerings that come later within a category than the first ever product of that category are considered followers.

The number of product categories in which the organization offered a product in a given year. Products were coded according to a standard set of 80 product categories, and for each firm the data record the categories in which it offered products in its initial year and each subsequent year.

The number of products offered by other organizations in a given year in the same product categories in which the focal organization offers products; measures of product densities exclude products of the focal organization. The product density term is decomposed into two parts corresponding to whether rival products arrived to market earlier or later in a given product category than the focal organization's product offering did. A separate nonrival product density term counts the number of products in categories where the organization has no products.

Each organization's tenure in the industry was defined as the time (in years) passed since it entered the industry. Tenure dependence was modeled using the piecewise exponential specification, which allows the effects of duration to be estimated without specifying a parametric distribution for duration dependence.

variable_name: number of new product groups added
description: If a firm added products in a group where it did not previously offer a product, then this addition was counted in the variable number of product groups added. This variable counts the number of product groups being entered by the organization that are technologically distant from the organization's current products.

The change indicator variable AP is equal to zero until the organization changes its product offerings and equal to one thereafter, starting with the year after the first change. The product addition indicator distinguishes product additions from product deletions and is paired with a product addition clock.

Product exits are distinguished from product additions by decomposing the change indicator variable and its clock; the product exit indicator is set equal to one once an organization drops a product, and is paired with a product exit clock.

A binary variable denoting whether the time point t of each observation falls in the pre-implementation (assigned a value of 0) or post-implementation (assigned a value of 1) period of the PopRec algorithm.

A binary variable denoting whether the time point t of each observation falls in the pre-implementation (assigned a value of 0) or post-implementation (assigned a value of 1) period of the PersRec algorithm.

The Herfindahl–Hirschman Index (HHI) of dish genres, calculated at the complementor-day level by squaring the share of each dish genre within a complementor's daily offerings and summing the squared shares. To capture the changes in the concentration of dish offerings over time, the authors perform a first-order difference on the HHI (denoted by ΔHHI), which serves as the main dependent variable.
The daily number of newly introduced dishes, which is the primary metric for complementors' new product introductions.

variable_name: Lorenz curves and Gini coefficients of revenue and order amounts
description: The authors aggregate the total revenue and order amounts of each complementor before and after the PopRec and PersRec upgrades, estimate Lorenz curves for both revenue and order amounts, and calculate the corresponding Gini coefficients. Changes in the Lorenz curves and Gini coefficients are observed over 30-day periods before and after the algorithm upgrades; a Lorenz curve closer to the 45-degree line of equality and a lower Gini index indicate a more equal distribution.
time_window: 30-day periods before and after the algorithm upgrades

description: This binary variable takes a value of 1 if family members make up at least 25% of the fund managers or a relative of the founder serves as a fund manager.

This binary variable takes a value of 1 if the fund is not family-managed and the VC fund is based in the same country as the entity that raised it. It serves as the reference category in the regressions.
This binary variable takes a value of 1 if the fund is not family-managed and the VC fund is not based in the same country as the entity that raised it.
This binary dependent variable takes a value of 1 if the VC fund's headquarters is located within 25 kilometers (15.5 miles) of the startup.
This variable represents the count of syndicate partners located within 25 kilometers of the VC fund.

Following DeSantola et al. (2023), the authors use the natural logarithm of the ratio between the total number of VC funds raised in the year in the country where the VC fund is based (multiplied by 3) and the total number of VC funds raised in the previous 3 years in the same country. Unlike DeSantola et al. (2023), who focused on a single country, the ratios are computed within each country to account for cross-country heterogeneity.
time_window: deal year and prior three years

description: This variable takes a value of 1 if the entity that raised the VC fund completing the deal had raised a follow-on VC fund (i.e., a fund raised after the focal one in the same country) by the year in which the VC fund completed the focal deal. Higher values therefore indicate a lower necessity to fund-raise.

A Family VC is classified as having high family involvement when family members collectively led a higher number of investments as lead partners than any non-family member. Pitchbook provides information on the identity of the lead partners responsible for completing deals.
Family VCs not classified as having high family involvement, that is, funds where family members did not collectively lead a higher number of investments as lead partners than any non-family member.
The authors distinguish between eponymous and non-eponymous Family VCs, that is, funds named after the family versus those that are not. The prose does not detail the coding further.
Family VCs that are not eponymously named; the authors distinguish them from eponymous Family VCs when testing whether eponymy accentuates the propensity to engage in local deals.

An estimate of the monthly volume of illegal online pharmacies' sales of prescription drugs to US consumers, measured in "legal prescription equivalent" units, namely the number of pills, tablets or any other units that are provided in a legal prescription, so that it can be compared against the volume of legal pharmacies' sales. The dataset identifies IOPs active in a given month, uses traffic volume data to assess sales to US consumers, and keywords and SEO variables to estimate drug-specific sales. The variable enters the model as its natural logarithm.
scale: count of legal prescription equivalent units, logged

description: Shortages are identified from the UUDIS database, which provides start and end dates for drug shortages at the active ingredient level and considers a shortage resolved when all suppliers have all product versions available or have discontinued their products. Sit is a dummy equal to 1 in those months where the shortage is active and 0 otherwise, and ASit is a dummy equal to 1 in those months after the shortage is resolved and 0 otherwise.
time_window: 6 months before the shortage until 6 months after the shortage is resolved

variable_name: category spanning (independent variable in the primary studies)
description: The 90 studies included in the meta-analysis theorized category spanning as an independent variable and reported an effect size for its relationship with audience appeal, with proper controls in place. These 154 effect sizes are the observations coded for the meta-analysis.

For each effect size the authors computed a partial correlation coefficient measuring the association between spanning (x) and audience appeal (y), conditional on control variables (z). Effect sizes were coded so that a positive value indicates that spanning helps producers and a negative value indicates that it hurts producers. This variable is the dependent variable in the meta-regressions.

Dummy variable coded as 1 when the underlying category system was bounded, that is, when it comprised a countable number of categories known ex ante to industry players (e.g., 28 IMDb movie genres, 428 US patent classes). Coded as 0 in the unbounded scenario.

Dummy variable coded as 1 when industry third parties were the categorizers in a given study, that is, when they assigned producers and products to categories (e.g., government agencies, industry associations, specialized analysts and critics, industry data aggregators). Coded as 0 when organizational insiders, such as cofounders, senior executives, or their representatives, matched the producer or products to categories.

Dummy variable coded as 1 for effect sizes estimated at the product level (e.g., products associated with several styles, market subsegments, or technologies). Coded as 0 for effect sizes estimated at the producer level (e.g., producers associated with several industries; with several strategies, such as for-profit and social enterprise models; or with several production methods, such as spanning traditional and modernist approaches to winemaking).

Dummy variable coded as 1 for effect sizes involving the simultaneous spanning of categories (e.g., a multi-genre movie, a firm associated with multiple SIC codes in a given year). Coded as 0 when spanning unfolded over time (e.g., a producer or product associated with category A at time t and category B at time t + 1).

variable_name: Direct inflow concentration x Indirect inflow concentration
description: Occupation of the tip-of-the-funnel position is captured by the interaction between a firm's direct inflow concentration score and its indirect inflow concentration score, computed annually. The authors interpret a negative interaction as indicating that high direct inflow concentration combined with low indirect inflow concentration—the tip-of-the-funnel position—corresponds to a higher outcome level than other positions. In the panel matching method, the treatment is defined as low indirect inflow concentration among firms with a high level of direct inflow concentration.

Individual-level mobility data are first aggregated at the dyadic firm-to-firm level to produce inflow and outflow mobility flows. Building on the network-based measure suggested by Bothner et al. (2010), the authors compute a Herfindahl index of the employee mobility flows directed from each source firm j to firm i, calculated for each firm for each year. If the index equals one the firm receives all new hires from just one firm (maximally concentrated); where it equals 1/(n-1) the firm hires from nearly an infinite number of other firms (minimally concentrated).

The authors generated the indirect concentration scores by calculating the average of alters' direct inflow concentration scores for each year. It therefore captures whether the firms that the focal firm hires from themselves hire from a broad or a focused set of firms.

The ratio of firm-level patent counts granted in a given year to the firm's assets, which normalizes the number of patents with total assets so that firms of different scales can be compared. The authors count patents awarded by grant year rather than application year because they seek to capture the success of innovation activities. Because the average time for getting a patent in the United States is around two years, the variable is lagged by two years.

Firm-level total factor productivity estimated with the semiparametric method of Imrohoroğlu and Tüzel (2014), measuring the overall effectiveness with which capital and labor are used in a production process. The production function is yit = β0 + βk kit + βl lit + ωit + ηit, where yit is the log of value added for firm i in period t, lit and kit are log values of labor and capital, ωit is productivity, and ηit an error term. The parameters are estimated with industry-specific time dummies and firm-level log TFP is obtained as ωit = yit - bβ0 - bβl lit - bβk kit.

variable_name: organizational cultural dimension index (Concept Mover's Distance)
description: Word embeddings and Concept Mover's Distance are applied to the corpus of Glassdoor employee review texts. For each review, the authors calculate the optimal distance between the words in the review and an "ideal" pseudo-document consisting of only words denoting one specific concept, for four dimensions: collectiveness, efficiency, diversity, and innovation. This creates a one-dimensional continuum where reviews closer to a dimension indicate a greater emphasis on it, and the index is then aggregated across all reviews belonging to each firm for each year, reflecting employees' perceptions of each cultural value.

Built from the firm-year index of each of the four cultural dimensions. Intensity is calculated as the mean of the index across the sample period, and consistency is calculated using the coefficient of variation (the ratio of the standard deviation to the mean) of the dimension across years. The authors then created a dummy variable, Strong organizational culture, where both intensity and consistency were above the median values.

The count of promises articulated by the CEO during the specific quarterly earnings call. Promises were identified by OpenAI's o3-mini reasoning model from the presentation segment of the earnings call transcript; the authors retained only statements unambiguously classified as promises with a strong level of commitment and excluded statements identified as earnings guidance.
Measures how long, in years, the CEO has served in the current role.
A dummy variable coded 1 in the first 3 years after a new CEO appointment, and 0 otherwise, constructed as an alternative to the continuous CEO tenure measure.
Coded 1 for male CEOs and 0 otherwise, drawn from ExecuComp and the COVID-19 pandemic period database.
A dummy coded as 1 if the firm's quarterly earnings per share is lower than the consensus analyst forecast, and 0 otherwise.
An alternative continuous measure replacing the missed forecast dummy, measured as the difference between actual earnings and consensus forecasts scaled by stock price.
Measured following common practice as the cash-to-assets ratio.

The firm-level political risk (PRisk) measure developed by Hassan et al. (2019), used because it captures firm-specific variation in a key dimension of environmental uncertainty rather than applying uniformly across firms.

The Economic Policy Uncertainty Index by Baker et al. (2016), a widely recognized measure that provides a macroeconomic view of uncertainty; it is divided by 1000 to improve readability, and because it varies only annually the models using it omit year-quarter fixed effects.
The proportion of uncertainty-related words in CEO speech, computed with the Loughran-McDonald Master Dictionary, which the authors describe as a close measure of perceived uncertainty by the CEO.

A dummy coded 1 for quarters between 2020-Q2 and 2021-Q3, and 0 otherwise, used as a measure of environmental uncertainty because the pandemic represented a major exogenous shock that significantly heightened uncertainty for firms across industries.

The average number of months specified for promises with defined timelines, restricted to firm-quarter observations containing at least one promise with a specified horizon. An LLM translated the conference date and the stated delivery time into the maximum number of whole months between the call and the promised fulfilment, returning 'unclear' when no interpretable date could be inferred; large horizon values were capped at the sample mean plus five standard deviations.

variable_name: Proportion of Promises with Vague Horizon
description: The proportion of promises made with vague or unspecified timelines, calculated as the ratio of vague-horizon promises to total promises per earnings call.
Promise specificity was measured through LLM-based ratings that evaluated each promise's specificity on a scale from 1 (least specific) to 5 (most specific).

Indicator for stores randomly assigned to the performance trajectory group. Twice every week during the treatment period, each worker in these stores was sent the performance trajectory of an anonymous high-performing senior worker from her region through the firm's workforce management app. The message included the year and month the senior worker joined the firm, the region of her store, and her performance statistics—customer picks and sales—in month 1, month 3, month 6, month 12 of tenure, and the month prior to message delivery.
level: store (treatment assigned at store level; messages received by workers)
time_window: Twice weekly from June 22 to December 31, 2019

description: Indicator for stores randomly assigned to the peer performance group. Workers within each region were divided into four tenure-based cohorts, and twice each week one worker from each region-tenure group was randomly selected and her customer pick and sales statistics from the previous month were anonymously shared with all workers in the same region-cohort group.
level: store (treatment assigned at store level; messages received by workers)
time_window: Twice weekly from June 22 to December 31, 2019

description: Worker-month indicator coded as 1 if an employee leaves during a given month and 0 otherwise, constructed from monthly data on the attrition of individual spa workers from June through December 2019. Regressions are estimated separately for new workers and senior workers and pooled with a new-worker interaction.

variable_name: belief revision about senior workers' early-stage performance
description: Post-RCT survey items assessing belief revision and perceptions of senior worker performance, collected through the firm's workforce management app. The authors report that new workers in the trajectory group report a larger downward belief revision about senior workers' early-stage performance, while the effect is absent for senior workers.

Warwick-Edinburgh Mental Wellbeing Scales, covering 10 distinct dimensions such as optimism, exhaustion, and curiosity. All survey questions are measured on a 1–5 Likert scale with higher values indicating greater satisfaction or more favorable evaluations; average scores are computed within each dimension and responses aggregated to the worker-month level.
