description: Set equal to hotel chain i's cumulative (discounted) experience in Manhattan between the year component j joined chain i and the time hotel chain i was founded, based on the number of component hotels the chain operated in Manhattan. For hotels not affiliated with chains the variable is set equal to zero.
time_window: from the chain's founding to the year the component joined the chain

description: Set equal to hotel chain i's cumulative (discounted) experience in Manhattan between the current year and the time component j joined the hotel chain, based on the number of component hotels the chain operated in Manhattan. For hotels not affiliated with chains the variable is set equal to zero.
time_window: from the year the component joined the chain to the year before the current year

description: Set equal to the cumulative operating experience of hotel chain i at the time component j joined chain i, computed by substituting the number of components operated outside Manhattan by the chain for the number operated in Manhattan.
time_window: from the chain's founding to the year the component joined the chain

description: Set equal to the cumulative experience of hotel chain i since the time component j joined chain i, computed by substituting the number of components operated outside Manhattan by the chain for the number operated in Manhattan.
time_window: from the year the component joined the chain to the year before the current year

description: Classification of the innovation project by whether it was triggered by users' orders or serious inquiries (user initiated) or by the innovator's own search for markets and techniques (innovator initiated). Used to sort firms into the four cells of the research scheme.

variable_name: Local availability of related foreign products
description: Classification of whether related foreign products were locally available from which the firm could learn and creatively imitate. Used with the source of initiation to sort firms into the four cells of the research scheme.

Interval variable for the customer's role in generating ideas for the innovation. Compared across the four firm types with Kruskal-Wallis ANOVA on mean ranks; the authors report that Type I and II groups (firms with RFPs locally available) showed higher scores than the other two groups.
Interval variable for the customer's role in technical problem solving. Type I and II groups (firms with related foreign products locally available) reported higher scores than the other two groups.

variable_name: Entrepreneurs as key person in idea generation
description: Nominal variable for whether the entrepreneur was the key person in idea generation, reported as the proportion of firms in each type. There was no difference among the four groups: in any group 60 to 70 percent of firms reported that it was the entrepreneurs that contributed significantly to the initiation.

variable_name: Entrepreneurs as key person in problem solving
description: Nominal variable for whether the entrepreneur played the key technical role in problem solving. The proportion was significantly higher in Types III and IV (firms with no RFPs locally available).

Nominal variable for whether the firm used overseas observation of foreign firms producing related products. Type II and IV groups (firms with innovator initiated innovations) reported higher scores than the other two groups.
Interval variable for the contribution of domestic observation of local firms using related foreign products. Type I and II groups reported higher scores than the other two groups.
Interval variable for assistance obtained from local R&D institutes. Types II and IV (firms with innovator initiated innovations) reported higher scores than the other two groups.
Interval variable for the usefulness of catalogs of related foreign products. Type I and II groups (firms with RFPs locally available) reported higher scores than the other two groups.
Interval variable for the degree to which the innovation imitated a related foreign product. Innovations in Type I were most imitative and those in Type IV least imitative.

Nominal variable for whether the firm obtained a patent for its newly developed innovative machine, reported as the proportion of firms in each type. 66.7% of innovations in Type IV group were patented compared with only 5% in Type I group.

variable_name: Opportunity opened by import substitution policy
description: Interval variable for the opportunity opened by the government's import substitution policy. The Kruskal-Wallis result is not statistically significant, but mean ranks are higher in Type I and II groups (firms with RFPs locally available) than in the other two groups.

variable_name: Educational level of key technical person
description: Variable for the educational level of the key technical person, entered in the stepwise discriminant analysis of the four groups. The authors note that Types III and IV required higher quality key technical persons within the firm.

variable_name: Position of key technical person within the firm
description: Variable for the position of the key technical person within the firm, entered in the stepwise discriminant analysis of the four groups.

The innovation pattern was measured as a set of questionnaire variables on the idea generation, problem solving and implementation stages of the innovation process, such as the roles of customers and entrepreneurs, use of overseas and domestic observation, local R&D institutes, catalogs, degree of imitation and patenting. These variables are compared across the four firm types with cross tabulation, Kruskal-Wallis ANOVA and stepwise discriminant analysis.

variable_name: Historical competition faced by organization in the market
description: Organization-years of rivalry that the organization faced historically in a given market. In the failure-rate model for the microcomputer market it is entered for the midrange and mainframe markets, and in the entry model for midrange firms entering microcomputers it is entered for the midrange market. The models also distinguish recent historical competition from distant-past historical competition.
time_window: cumulative historical exposure up to each observed organization-year

variable_name: Organizational exit rate from the market
description: The rate at which an organization exits a market, estimated as a function of its market tenure, its historical exposure to competition in that and other markets, being in multiple markets, market density, size, tenure, macroeconomic conditions and other controls. In the model the failure rate of organization j varies as a function of its market tenure, and the baseline failure rate is estimated in terms of the control variables.

variable_name: Entry rate of midrange manufacturers into the microcomputer market
description: The rate at which midrange manufacturers enter the microcomputer market, estimated with piecewise market tenure effects and with controls for real GDP, the prime interest rate, de alio status, shipments, lagged entries, failures and density in both the microcomputer and midrange markets, and with specifications of the historical competition the organization faced in the midrange market.

Team members indicated up to three of seven functional categories in which they gained the most experience during their career. From the two-dimensional team member-function frequency table, the entropy-based transmission measure Txy = (Hx + Hy - Hxy) was computed, which captures between-member FB diversity net of intrapersonal functional diversity. A large value of Txy implies high FB diversity with expertise uniquely distributed over team members.

LOC was measured with a Dutch translation of the Rotter scale, consisting of 23 forced-choice items in which the respondent chooses between an internal and an external control alternative. Internality was measured by counting the number of internal control alternatives chosen (minimum 0, maximum 23); the reliability of the scale equaled 0.61. LOC diversity was measured using the standard deviation of the team-member scores.

All executives rated three items on a five-point Likert scale measuring a TMT's teamness. The reliability of the scale equaled 0.733; the median within-team interrater agreement coefficient was high (0.83) and the team-member ratings differed significantly between teams, warranting use of the team's mean as a team-level collaborative behavior variable.

CEOs and all other top managers evaluated four statements on a five-point Likert scale taken from O'Reilly and Roberts (1976); the reliability of the scale equaled 0.752. The median rwg equaled 0.76 and a one-way analysis of variance revealed significant between-teams effects. Scores were reversed and the mean was calculated to create a team-level variable of accurate information exchange.

Respondents indicated for each of 15 major decision categories (defined with the help of IT experts) the team member, including him/herself, who was the most influential, with real content-related influence; only one person could be indicated per decision area. Interrater agreement of the proportion of decision areas attributed to the CEO was high (median rwg 0.95) and team differences were significant, supporting aggregation. Decentralization was measured as one minus the mean proportion of decision areas that the team members (including the CEO) attributed to the CEO.

ROS in the year of the visit to the firm, defined as operating income (operating revenue minus operating expenses) divided by sales. A Kolmogorov-Smirnov test revealed that the ROS scores did not significantly depart from a normal distribution.

Profitability at the firm level is measured by the average 1975-77 return on invested capital, defined as net income after tax plus interest divided by equity and long term debt. The measure has a long history in the literature and represents the return to all employed resources.

A weighted average of return on assets in 3-digit markets, where the weight is the percentage of the firm's total sales in each 3-digit market, using 1975 return on assets. Data limitations forced the use of return on assets instead of return on invested capital at the industry level; the authors note the two profitability measures typically correlate very strongly.
A weighted average of an annuity measure of shipment growth (in dollars) in 4-digit markets, 1972-76, where the weight is the percentage of the firm's total sales in each 4-digit market.

The Herfindahl index of diversification, computed as one minus the sum over 4-digit SIC markets of the squared fraction of firm i's sales in each market; a denominator is added to accommodate firm sales data whose percentage totals do not sum to one, as happens in the EIS database when some sales are in foreign markets. Low scores are treated as efficient diversifiers and high scores as inefficient diversifiers, with the median score (DIVERS4 = 0.7862) dividing the sample. Montgomery (1982) found a strong correlation between the Herfindahl index and Rumelt's taxonomy of diversification.

variable_name: Index of technological sophistication of the firm
description: Entrepreneurs evaluated the importance of their firms' product attributes for their competitive advantage on three quasi-Likert ordinal scales from 1 to 5. The three scales were aggregated for each product separately to derive a product-specific index of technological newness, and the product-specific indices were summed to derive the index of overall technological sophistication of the firm. The reliability of the additive indices for each product was sufficiently high to justify their use as a measure of a single construct, with Cronbach's alphas between 0.53 and 0.57, and the firm-level index had an alpha of 0.70.

variable_name: Risk associated with use of the firm's products
description: Three MDs independently estimated the risk associated with use of each product on two quasi-Likert ordinal scales from 1 to 7. The panel's raw scores were aggregated consecutively and tested for reliability, and an overall index of risk associated with use was created for each product by aggregating the two dimensional scores. The overall index of risk associated with product use for each firm was derived by averaging the product-specific indices for the first three products introduced by each firm.

variable_name: Impact of the FDA regulations on the firm
description: The reported impact of the FDA regulations on the firm's operations and management decision-making, estimated by the entrepreneurs. The entrepreneurs reported that the FDA regulations influenced their product strategies on the average 3.2 points on a 5-point scale, and their impact on the firm in general, as measured by the number of operational issues impacted by the regulations, 2.8 points on a similar 5-point scale.

The estimate of the out-of-pocket expenses precipitated by the requirements of the FDA interactions, including external consultants, costs of clinical tests, special facilities or labeling procedures and other similar costs. The sampled firms' reported expenses ranged from none to $120,000 per annum, with a $30,000 median; some entrepreneurs could not evaluate their FDA interface expenses.

To smooth temporary fluctuations of sales, the authors used the average of the firm's annual sales between 1980 and 1983 as the indicator of the firm's commercial success. This index was highly correlated with the 1983 market value of the firm as estimated by the entrepreneur, with the average number of the firm's employees for the same four years, and with the growth in annual sales, validating its possible use as a single measure of the firm's success.

The initial capital mobilized by the firm, comprising initial equity and initial loans raised during its first two years of existence. The co-founders and their families provided approximately 62% of the initial capital base, with venture capitalists and banks playing quite a minor role at this initial stage. The analysis distinguishes firms that reached a threshold of initial financing from those that did not.

Documented from open-ended responses to the question: "HAS ANYONE JOINED, MOVED INTERNALLY, OR LEFT THE FIRM THAT HAS HAD AN IMPORTANT INFLUENCE ON INNOVATIVE DECISION-MAKING?" Responses were coded into personnel that had recently (3 years) left and recently arrived, recorded in one of six occupational categories, and the net count (gains + losses -) was computed. In three cases unclear or irrelevant information was assumed to be no significant manpower flow gain.

The positive-gain count of innovative-impact manpower arrivals recorded in one of six occupational categories. Only 23 (41%) of the 56 firms reported any significant, innovation-impact personnel additions, and 15 of these involved one management position.

variable_name: Sum of Staged Adoption Behaviors, Retort Pouch
description: A twenty-one item scale, with yes and no responses to events, behaviors, and decisions, that was factor analyzed into five stages and summed; Cronbach alpha = 0.91. Obtained in interviews.

The number of radical (new to the industry) process innovations adopted in the last three years, taken from the mail survey. Examples were given and evaluated by researchers for appropriateness, and the number of innovations was the measure.

The number of new products introduced during the last two years, taken from the mail survey. Examples were given and evaluated by researchers for appropriateness, and the number of innovations was the measure.

The number of incremental process innovations adopted in the last three years, taken from the mail survey. Examples were given and evaluated by researchers for appropriateness, and the number of innovations was the measure.

Aston group measure of organization structure obtained in interviews, with a reported Cronbach alpha of 0.94. Used to split firms at the median into high and low categories for the moderated correlations.

Aston group measure of organization structure obtained in interviews, with a reported Cronbach alpha of 0.91. Used to split firms at the median into high and low categories for the moderated correlations.

Aston group measure of organization structure obtained in interviews, with a reported Cronbach alpha of 0.84. Used to split firms at the median into high and low categories for the moderated correlations.
Whether the firm has products in nonfood markets, taken from the mail survey, used as a yes/no condition in the moderated correlations.
The presence of engineering or technical groups in the firm, taken from the mail survey, used as a yes/no condition in the moderated correlations.

A single question attitude scale from the interview: "Do you feel that this company has sufficient slack (actual or potential resources, e.g., retained earnings or credit rating) to adopt a significant, new processing technology or offer a product that's the first of its kind?" Responses range from "yes," scored 5, to "definitely not," scored 1.

The log of the number of full-time, year-round employees, taken from the mail survey; used as an indicator of slack resources for innovating and as the control for organization size. In the moderated correlations firms were split at 140 employees.

A two-item scale (Cronbach Alpha = 0.63) from the mail survey: (a) whether the firm's performance was much better than expected a year ago to much worse than expected; (b) whether the after-tax rate of return for the last fiscal year was much higher to much lower than five years ago. Firms were split at a score of six on a 10-point scale in the moderated correlations.

variable_name: Innovation outcome measures (new products, radical and incremental process adoptions, staged adoption of the retort pouch)
description: Innovative outcomes were measured with four variables: the number of new products introduced in the last two years, the number of radical (new to the industry) process innovations adopted in the last three years, the number of incremental process innovations adopted in the last three years (all from the mail survey), and the sum of 21 staged adoption behaviors for the retort pouch (from interviews, Cronbach alpha 0.91). Each outcome was correlated separately with the manpower flow measures.
Dependent variable in the work item analyses: the number of work item contributions, i.e., the number of times a firm supports a work item by joining a committee.

The number of approved sole authored change requests made by each firm in each year. Change requests are written requests to alter an ongoing specification and can be accepted or rejected by the technical specification group through a consensus process, or withdrawn or revised by the sponsor.

Binary indicator for a successful change request, estimated separately for each change request submitted. Change requests can be accepted or rejected by the technical specification group through a consensus process or withdrawn or revised by the sponsor.

Unique connections to other 3GPP members through the unipartite consortium network; only unique connections are included, i.e., duplicate comemberships with the same peers are ignored. Entered in the estimations in natural logarithmic form.
Total consortium memberships: the number of consortia, out of the consortia affiliated with the wireless telecommunication industry, in which the firm is a member (bipartite degree).

Memberships in consortia institutionally related to 3GPP, i.e., consortia that are 3GPP market representatives or organizational partners. Contrasted with memberships in consortia that are formally not affiliated with 3GPP.
Number of 3GPP member alliance partners. Alliance data are obtained from the CATI database of technology intensive strategic alliances; only alliances with 3GPP peers are included.
Number of alliances with other 3GPP members, from the CATI database of technology intensive strategic alliances; only alliances among 3GPP members are included.

Number of unique connections made in work item committees, i.e., connections to peers formed by common participation in the committees developing new technical features. Used as a lagged explanatory variable in the change request analyses.
time_window: annual observation, 2000-2003; lagged by one period in the change request success model

description: Number of work item committees joined by the firm, i.e., its contributions to specification development. Used as a lagged explanatory variable in the change request analyses.
time_window: annual observation, 2000-2003; lagged by one period in the change request success model

variable_name: Consortium memberships, consortium connections and alliances
description: Participation in external cooperative organizations was measured with firm-year network variables: total consortium memberships (and related versus unrelated memberships), log of unique connections to other 3GPP members through the consortium network, and the number of 3GPP alliance partners and alliances from the CATI alliance database. These enter the models as explanatory variables for work item contributions and change requests.

Strategy content was operationalized by grouping the sample firms on the basis of a cluster analysis of three key dimensions related to business strategy over which the managers had control: product mix, pricing, and internal operating efficiency. Clustering used the BMD-P2M algorithm with a Euclidean distance measure to link cluster centroids in a stepwise fashion and produced three strategy types: Focused Retailer, High-priced Inefficient, and Focused Commercial. The strategy content variables were identified by the author as representative of basic components of a business strategy for firms in this industry and cross validated by interviews with industry experts.
Performance level (return) for each bank was operationalized as the average return on assets for the five-year period 1975-1979.

variable_name: Risk (standard deviation of return on assets)
description: Performance variation (risk) for each bank is the standard deviation of its return on assets over the same five-year period. Accounting measures of risk are used because accounting measures of risk have been shown to be good surrogates for securities market measures of risk.
Total assets divided by number of employees, one of the three strategic variables used in the cluster analysis; higher scores mean more efficient.
The place in the hierarchy where a variety of decisions are made; lower scores indicate more centralization. Measured with multiple raters per firm using the instrument of Lenz (1978).

The extent to which strategic planning is formalized; higher scores indicate more formalization. Measured with the planning activities instrument of Lenz (1978), with reliability based on multiple raters for each measure.

The extent to which strategic planning is operationalized, that is, the extent to which aspects of the plan are converted into measurable outcomes; higher scores indicate more operationalization. Measured with the planning activities instrument of Lenz (1978), with reliability based on multiple raters for each measure.

Percent of time dealing with outsiders; higher scores indicate more interaction. Part of the environmental interaction instrument attributed to Jemison (1981), with reliability based on multiple raters for each measure.

Boundary spanning activities capturing the segments of the environment with which managers choose to interact: customer contact, input acquisition, information control, representing the firm to outsiders, and information acquisition; higher scores indicate more interaction. Part of the environmental interaction instrument attributed to Jemison (1981), with reliability based on multiple raters for each measure.

Two aspects are measured: the respondent's department's dependence on other departments ('you on others') and other departments' dependence on the respondent's department ('others on you'); higher scores indicate more dependence. Measured with the instrument of Rousseau (1978), with reliability based on multiple raters for each measure.

variable_name: Distribution of influence on strategic decisions
description: Influence of a department on a series of strategic decisions; higher scores indicate more influence. Measured with the instrument of Hinings et al. (1974), with reliability based on multiple raters for each measure.

The date of the press announcement that the firm would withdraw from South Africa was used as the event date (day 0). When announcements appeared on weekends, the following business day was used as the event date. Firms whose withdrawal decision was not carried in one of the seven major newspapers searched were excluded.
time_window: day 0 (event date), with cumulative windows from day -30 to day 10

description: An abnormal return is the difference between the return expected on the event day, estimated from a regression line fitted to the firm's stock prices for several months preceding the event date with overall market performance controlled, and the actual return observed. The difference between predicted and actual return for a period is the cumulative abnormal return. Parametric tests were performed to see whether CARs differed from zero.
time_window: Cumulative windows from day -30 to day 0 through day -2 to day 10

description: Firms were split into two groups: those whose withdrawal announcements appeared in 1986 or before (early withdrawers, N = 19) and those whose announcements appeared in 1987 or thereafter (late withdrawers, N = 20). The 1986 cutoff was chosen because the Anti-Apartheid Act was passed in late 1986 and because it produced a balanced split.

Self-categorization item in which CEOs were requested to select from among four alternative, unlabeled organizational descriptions the one that best described their own firm, and were invited to further describe their firm in their own words. Stage numbers and labels were not in the questionnaire; the descriptions used are reproduced in Appendix A. The item was administered in both waves and was pre-tested with venture CEOs, a venture capitalist, an industry analyst and academics.

The del procedure for prediction analysis of cross-classification tables was applied to the cross-classification of wave 1 and wave 2 stages. Prediction rule one states that TBNVs in Stage 1, Stage 2 or Stage 3 in wave one advance only one stage between the two waves and that Stage 4 ventures stay in the same stage; predicted cells receive an error weight of 0 and error cells an error weight of 1. Prediction rule two reduces the error weight from 1 to 0.5 for advancing two stages and for staying in the same stage in Stages 1 to 3. Del is interpreted as the proportionate reduction in error from using the prediction rule, ranging from 0 to 1.

CEOs were asked to report the total number of employees of the firm. Used as one of the commonly accepted measures of growth in the one-way analyses of variance and in the discriminant analysis validating the stage of growth measure.

CEOs were asked to report the age of the firm in years. Used as one of the commonly accepted measures of growth in the one-way analyses of variance and in the discriminant analysis validating the stage of growth measure.

CEOs were asked to report sales for the current year and sales for the previous year; sales figures were used to calculate the percentage rate of growth in sales, the current year's sales divided by the previous year's sales. Used to validate the stage of growth measure and in the assessment of performance related nonresponse bias.

Excess returns were measured using the Single Index Market Model, with parameters estimated from the pre-event period -300 < t < -61. Excess returns for individual stocks were averaged into portfolio excess returns for the two subsamples, and cumulative average excess returns were computed over intervals around the Wall Street Journal announcement date.
time_window: event windows from -60 to 0 trading days relative to the announcement date

description: Accounting performance measures around duality status changes: return on common equity, return on total assets, operating cash flow divided by total assets, and operating cash flow divided by sales. Results show the percentage change in each ratio, measured as the ratio value 2 years after the change minus the value in the year of the change, divided by the value in the year of the change.
time_window: from year 0 (the year of a change in duality status) to year +2

description: The change in MVA between 1986 and 1991 was standardized by dividing by the beginning (1986) value of total capital, then adjusted for industry effects by subtracting the change in the industry average standardized MVA from the individual firm values. Regressions used both the percentage change in industry-adjusted standardized MVA and the percentage change in standardized MVA (unadjusted for industry effects).

A firm was classified as having a duality structure in a year if the CEO and Chairperson of the Board were the same individual; nonduality firms were those where the positions were held by separate individuals. Firms whose status could not be clearly established because of nonstandard managerial titles were dropped for the years of indeterminate status.
A dummy variable set equal to 1 if the Chairman of the Board was previously a member of the company's management team, 0 otherwise.
Firm size measured as the natural log of average annual sales between 1986 and 1991, included to control for firm size effects.
Average annual total debt to total assets ratio, computed over the period 1986-91, controlling for the disciplining impact of capital structure.
Average annual dividend payout ratio included in the regressions as a control for agency problems.
Firm risk controlled with the Value Line beta at the end of 1991.
The proportion of inside ownership as reported in Value Line at the end of 1991.

variable_name: Partial, Total and Inside dummy variables
description: Dummy 'partial' is set equal to 1 for firms with partial nonduality during the period, 0 otherwise; dummy 'total' is set equal to 1 for firms with total nonduality during the period, 0 otherwise; the omitted class is the total duality set of firms. An additional dummy variable 'inside' reflects whether the Chairman of the Board was previously a member of the company's management team.

One of the first three questionnaire items dealing with the presence of conflict in the decision process; managers indicated on a five-point scale the extent to which "Conflict between goals" describes the problem.

One of the first three questionnaire items dealing with the presence of conflict in the decision process; managers indicated on a five-point scale the extent to which "Conflict between people" describes the problem.

variable_name: Conflict because of the organizational structure
description: One of the first three questionnaire items dealing with the presence of conflict in the decision process; managers indicated on a five-point scale the extent to which "Conflict because of the organizational structure" describes the problem.
Factor score formed from the evaluative adjective pairs that loaded most highly on Factor 1, generated by summing the items used to define the factor.
Factor score formed from the evaluative adjective pairs that loaded most highly on Factor 2, generated by summing the items used to define the factor.
Factor score formed from the evaluative adjective pairs that loaded most highly on Factor 3, generated by summing the items used to define the factor.
Each executive's organization was classified as for-profit or not-for-profit, and the sample was divided on this basis for the correlation analyses.

The index is built from the logistic practice model estimated on the 159 districts. That model generates a predicted probability of going direct in a district (Pi) as a function of characteristics of the district (the industry rule); if the district is direct, the index of observance is Pi, and if the district is rep, the index is the probability of going rep, 1 - Pi. The index represents the strength of the industry's recommendation, based on the rule, that the district make its observed choice. It runs from 0 to 100% in theory and from 7% to virtually 100% in the data set.

Efficiency is the sales/selling cost ratio. Firms reported dollar sales for each sales district plus district-level totals of salesperson salaries and benefits, incentive compensation, variable selling expenses, and district sales office overhead, and also corporate sales overhead and the fraction of the corporate sales division's time spent on each district. The cost term adds the four district-level cost categories plus a share of corporate sales overhead determined by the percentage of corporate time spent on the district. Sales ranged from approximately 1 times cost to 45 times cost.
scale: ratio of dollar sales to selling cost

description: A multi-item scale covering two sources of uncertainty, developed by adding standardized scores and then applying the zeta squared transformation to make all scores nonnegative. One source is turbulence/instability (items 1-5), reflecting an environment that is complex, volatile, difficult to monitor, and difficult to forecast correctly. The other source is venturing into the unknown (new products and new markets, items 6-9), which means prediction is inherently difficult for the firm; the measure mixes perceptual and objective questions (past forecast error) to arrive at a composite reflection of uncertainty. Coefficient alpha is 0.65.

The observed choice in a sales district, where the dependent variable is the observed choice coded 0 for rep or 1 for direct. It is the dependent variable of the logistic practice model estimated on the 159 districts, whose predictions are estimates of the probability of going direct rather than rep in a sales district.

The number of years the CEO had been in his or her position. The sample was split into long- and short-tenure subgroups according to median CEO tenure, 10 years, a cutoff chosen because the forces of momentum were thought to be well under way after such an interval and because it generated subgroups of similar and substantial size. The tenure means for the long and short subgroups were 18.4 years (s.d. = 8.4, N = 55) and 4.9 years (s.d. = 1.7, N = 40) respectively.

Each component is the squared difference between the standardized scores of a pair of environmental and structural variables specified by one of the match relationships of Hypothesis 1. Whenever an inverse relationship was hypothesized the original seven-point scale of the structural variable was inverted before standardization, and all mismatch components were summed and made negative to yield the structural match index. Only one variable from any highly intercorrelated pair (r > 0.45) was incorporated, which dropped cost of innovation and heterogeneity. All variables were standardized to mean 0 and standard deviation 1.

Calculated in the same way as the structural match index, substituting the relationships and variables of Hypothesis 2 for those of Hypothesis 1: each component is the squared difference between the standardized scores of a pair of environmental and strategy variables, summed and made negative. Only one variable from highly intercorrelated pairs was incorporated (cost of innovation and heterogeneity were dropped).

Measured using quantitative indices: five-year (1978-1983) averages of return on investment, growth in sales and growth in net income, obtained from financial statements or, where access to such statements was denied, from the CEO. The CEO was also asked to compare his firm's profitability relative to that of his major competitors for the last five years. All performance measures were standardized. In the LISREL analysis performance is a latent variable measured with error by relative profitability, growth in sales, growth in profits and return on investment.

Assesses the degrees of change and unpredictability of customers, competitors and technologies on a seven-point scale; the median in the sample was 3.2. The short- and long-tenure subgroups had means of 3.5 (s.d. = 1.0) and 3.4 (s.d. = 1.2) and did not differ at even the 0.40 level of significance.

Reflects the range of differences in customer buying habits, competition, and required methods of production or service; the environmental variables were those of Miller (1988) and were measured on the questionnaire scales.
The centralization variable was taken from the Aston research (Inkson, Pugh and Hickson 1970; Pugh and Hickson 1976). The text gives no further detail on the items or scale.
The formalization variable was taken from the Aston research (Inkson, Pugh and Hickson 1970; Pugh and Hickson 1976). The text gives no further detail on the items or scale.
The specialization variable was taken from the Aston research (Inkson, Pugh and Hickson 1970; Pugh and Hickson 1976). The text gives no further detail on the items or scale.
One of the structural variables taken from Miller (1988); it measures the use and empowerment of highly skilled and well-trained technocrats. The text gives no further detail on the items or scale.
One of the structural variables taken from Miller (1988); it measures the use of liaison devices to integrate the efforts of specialists. The text gives no further detail on the items or scale.

Measured in two ways. The first employed scales assessing product innovation, new product development expenditures, and strategic aggressiveness toward competitors, with each of the three dimensions scored and weighted equally and then averaged. The second measure used only purely quantitative measures of R&D and new product commercialization expenses as a percentage of sales, to reflect only the most complex type of innovation.

Gauged by advertising intensity, market segmentation and prestige pricing (Miller 1988); the strategy measures were built from items taken from Hambrick's (1983) and Dess and Davis's (1984) panels of experts.

Gauged by dimensions of cost control, price cutting, minimization of marketing and product development costs, and conservatism in responding to markets. Capacity utilization and indices of production efficiency were not measured because they pertain mainly to manufacturing firms' performance.

Measures of Porter's strategies, including focus, were built from items taken from Hambrick's (1983) and Dess and Davis's (1984) panels of experts; the text does not describe the focus items in further detail.
Measured as the percentage of shares owned by one party; the sample was bifurcated along the median, which was 50% of shares owned by one party.
scale: percentage of shares owned by one party

description: The surrogate for product line breadth available in the PIMS data base, reported by the business relative to its competition. The authors describe the measure as subjective in nature and state that product line breadth ranges from 1 to 3, so that a one unit change is relatively large and the total direct effect of PLB on market share is twice the estimated coefficient. They caution that multiple measures of line breadth may be necessary to capture product line differences across firms.

Percentage sales of the served market, one of the six endogenous variables in the estimated system. The authors note that strategic measures reported in the PIMS data base exhibit limited variation in the short term, which is why they also estimate the model on four-year average data.

Average selling prices of the business relative to the average of its three leading competitors. It is one of the six endogenous variables of the model and also appears as a predictor of market share in the market share equation.

Average direct costs of the business relative to the average of its three leading competitors. The authors state that the relative direct costs index varies from 85 to 125. It is one of the six endogenous variables and enters the manufacturing cost and return-on-investment equations.

Average finished goods plus raw material plus work-in-process inventory expressed as a percentage of net sales. It is one of the six endogenous variables and also enters the manufacturing cost equation.

Total manufacturing expenses (direct plus overheads) as a percentage of net sales; the authors state that manufacturing costs range from 0 to 100. It is one of the six endogenous variables and also appears as a predictor of relative price and of return on investment.

Net income as a percentage of average investment less book value, used as the measure of profitability. The authors state that a unit increase in market share raises profitability by 0.54 points in consumer markets and 0.27 points in industrial markets.

A linear combination of standardized unused borrowing capacity (BORCAP) and top management team prestige (PREST) whose weighting was established empirically by multiple discriminant analysis in T-1. The function estimates a constant which calibrates the cutoff point (minimum acceptable level of D Score) to zero, so that firms with D Scores above zero are likely to be survivors and scores below zero indicate a high probability of bankruptcy. The parameters are positive, indicating that BORCAP and PREST contribute to survival.
time_window: Weights estimated in T-1; scores compared across T-5 to T-1

description: Operationalized as total equity/total debt, standardized to mean zero and standard deviation one; this variable reflects the remaining borrowing capacity of a firm because it is the inverse of the leverage ratio. Financial liquidity was operationalized using the current ratio (current assets/current liabilities) and working capital/total assets, but liquidity was dropped from the definition of dependability for parsimony because both liquidity measures were highly correlated with BORCAP.
time_window: Five years preceding bankruptcy (T-5 to T-1); interacted with net fixed assets as of T-1

description: A scale designed to capture both educational and board affiliations, comprised of the sum of five standardized items: three measures of top managers' outside board affiliations and two measures of top managers' educational attainment. The scale was standardized (mean = 0, s.d. = 1); each of the five items correlates highly with PREST, and PREST is not highly correlated with the top team's size.
time_window: Five years preceding bankruptcy (T-5 to T-1)

description: The dependent variable in the logistic regressions is the probability of survival versus bankruptcy in T-1. The sample is comprised of 57 large bankrupt firms and 57 matched firms; firms filing either a Chapter X or XI bankruptcy petition were eligible for inclusion, and a match was a firm that closely resembled the bankrupt firm in sales size and product/market mix five years prior to the bankruptcy and was not in the process of failing.
time_window: T-1 (bankruptcy year); matching criteria measured at T-5

description: Standardized net fixed assets used as a proxy variable for saleable assets, because a measure of saleable (nonessential) assets was not available; it serves as an imperfect measure because it is based on historical cost and the varying depreciation methods adopted by the firms. In the interaction model, NFA is entered as a dummy variable D2 that equals 1 where NFA is high (in the upper half of the sample) and 0 otherwise.
scale: standardized (mean = 0, s.d. = 1); dummy split at the upper half of the sample

description: Downsizing was examined with growth in net fixed assets, growth in the number of employees, the number of locations served by retail and transportation firms, and throughput (sales plus change in inventory) of retail and manufacturing firms. Prose reports that the temporary survivors cut back employees in four out of five years, reduced their fixed assets in real terms, cut their throughput activities, reduced the number of locations they served, and were forced to reduce their long-term debt in T-1.

variable_name: Growth in employees, sales, net fixed assets and long-term debt
description: Evidence on growth compares low dependability survivors to low dependability bankrupts at T-1. The authors report that the undependability of survivors may be associated with debt financed growth in employees, inventory, net fixed assets and sales from T-2 to T-1, while the undependable bankrupts exhibited downsizing (declining real sales and employees).
time_window: Change rates from T-2 to T-1

description: Evidence of a turnaround is based on improving costs and sales for low dependability survivors compared to low dependability bankrupts at T-1. The authors report that the evidence supports the idea that some undependable firms survive because they show evidence of improving costs and sales, whereas the undependable bankrupts exhibited worsening cost structures, especially selling, general and administrative costs, from T-2 to T-1.
time_window: Change rates from T-2 to T-1

description: The business unit's dollar market share divided by the sum of its three largest competitors' dollar market share, lagged one year. It enters the price and cost equations in linear and quadratic terms.

The change in the business unit's dollar market share in the current year relative to the previous year. It enters the price and cost equations in linear and squared (quadratic) terms, the quadratic term included to capture any nonlinearities.

A derived dependent variable that isolates the change in the firm's average unit price: y_t equals ln DTR_t minus ln DTR_(t-1) minus ln GS_t minus ln $MS_t plus ln $MS_(t-1) plus ln RP_t minus ln RP_(t-1), where DTR is disguised total revenues, GS the industry growth rate, $MS dollar market share and RP the firm's price relative to the industry average price. Taking logs of the total revenue identity and differencing removes the unknown disguise factor and unobserved industry sales.

A derived dependent variable that isolates the change in the firm's average unit cost: W_t equals ln DTC_t minus ln DTC_(t-1) minus ln GS_t minus ln $MS_t plus ln $MS_(t-1) plus ln RP_t minus ln RP_(t-1), where DTC is disguised total costs. The same logging and differencing procedure removes the disguise factor and the firm-specific fixed component.

An aggregate measure of power over buyers: the five PIMS measures associated with this force are standardized (mean zero, standard deviation one) and summed, and the force is then additively rescaled so that the firm with the lowest value equals zero, with all others greater than zero. Increasing values imply increasingly good competitive conditions.

An aggregate measure of power over suppliers formed by standardizing (mean zero, standard deviation one) the two PIMS measures associated with this force and summing them, then additively rescaling so that the lowest value equals zero. Increasing values imply increasingly good competitive conditions.

An aggregate measure of lack of competitive rivalry formed by standardizing (mean zero, standard deviation one) the nine PIMS measures associated with this force and summing them, then additively rescaling so that the lowest value equals zero. Increasing values imply increasingly good competitive conditions; capacity utilization is removed from this measure in the cost equation.

An aggregate measure of lack of threat of entry formed by standardizing (mean zero, standard deviation one) the three PIMS measures associated with this force and summing them, then additively rescaling so that the lowest value equals zero. Increasing values imply increasingly good competitive conditions.

variable_name: cumulative number of joint venture adoptions N(t)
description: Adoption data on parent firms developed by noting the year a firm announces the formation of a joint venture over the period 1972 to 1988; only joint ventures that constitute first-time adoptions by a firm are considered. The dataset was assembled from public sources such as Mergers & Acquisitions and Funk & Scott Index of Corporate Change.
Data on 127 M-form adoptions for the period 1950 to 1974 compiled by Rumelt (1974) and used by Mahajan et al. (1988); reanalyzed in this paper within the same analytical framework.
level: population of large corporations time series (annual)

description: The coefficient of internal influence in the diffusion model, obtained from the linear regression analogue of the internal-influence model (OLS) and from the nonlinear functional form (NLS). The model makes the diffusion rate a function of the number which has already adopted the innovation and the remaining number of potential adopters. The authors note that the linear approach has econometric limitations such as multicollinearity and nonavailability of standard errors for the crucial parameters.

The coefficient of external influence in the diffusion model, obtained from the linear regression analogue of the external-influence model (OLS) and from the nonlinear functional form (NLS). In this specification the diffusion rate at time t depends only on the potential number of adopters present in the social system at time t, giving rise to a modified exponential diffusion curve with a negative exponent.

The coefficient of internal influence estimated for the M-form adoption series using the same linear (OLS) and nonlinear (NLS) specifications applied to the joint venture data. Under the NLS estimation the internal-influence model remains insignificant for M-form structure.
level: population of large corporations time series

description: The coefficient of external influence estimated for the M-form adoption series using the same linear (OLS) and nonlinear (NLS) specifications applied to the joint venture data. Under the NLS estimation the external-influence model is significant for M-form structure.
level: population of large corporations time series

description: Short-term annual growth rate of product shipments in the venture's four-digit SIC industry. The constant-dollar shipment series for each industry was normalized by dividing by its first year (1965), then first differenced and divided by the lagged year. It is entered into the analysis as a time-varying covariate with a one-year lag.

Forecasting error from a long-term trend in industry shipments: the residual is the difference between the actual normalized shipment value and the value predicted by an estimated linear time trend for the industry. It is entered into the analysis as a time-varying covariate with a one-year lag.

Dependent variable indicating whether the venture terminated by acquisition by one of the partners or a third party. Of the 92 manufacturing ventures, 37 terminated by acquisition; ventures that terminated by dissolution are treated as censored, as are the ventures still in effect.
time_window: venture life, with two annual follow-ups

description: Dependent variable indicating whether the venture terminated by dissolution; 27 of the 92 manufacturing ventures terminated by dissolution. The same covariates used for the acquisition hazard are used to estimate the likelihood of termination by dissolution.
time_window: venture life, with two annual follow-ups

description: Four-firm concentration ratio at the four-digit SIC level. Because concentration ratios are published for every fifth year, the ratio nearest the midpoint of the venture's life is employed.
time_window: ratio nearest the midpoint of the venture's life

description: A latent construct measured by asking respondents to indicate on a scale of 1-5 the relative influence of the headquarters and the subsidiary on three decisions: major reorganizations in the subsidiary involving creation or dissolution of departments, career development plans for subsidiary managers, and changes in product design. The scale runs from 1 (headquarters decides alone) to 5 (subsidiary decides alone), so higher values represent greater autonomy and lower centralization. The construct is the obverse operationalization of centralization.

A latent construct measured by asking respondents to provide estimates of (1) time spent in interunit (e.g. subsidiary and headquarters) committees, teams, and task forces, (2) time spent in interunit meetings and conferences, and (3) time spent in the world headquarters, all measured in days on the most recent annual basis.

Respondents indicated on a scale of 1-5 the typical frequency of their communication with the head office. The scale was 1: daily; 2: weekly; 3: monthly; 4: annually; 5: less than annually. The responses were reverse scored in the analysis so that higher scores represent more frequent rather than less frequent communication.

Respondents indicated on a scale of 1-5 the typical frequency of their communication with each of the other national subsidiaries of the company that were included in the survey (1: daily; 2: weekly; 3: monthly; 4: annually; 5: less than annually). An aggregate intersubsidiary communication score for each respondent was calculated by adding up the individual's intersubsidiary communication frequency scores. Responses were reverse scored so that higher scores represent more frequent communication.

A latent construct measured by asking respondents to indicate on a scale of 1-5 the relative influence of the headquarters and the subsidiary on three decisions: major reorganizations in the subsidiary involving creation or dissolution of departments, career development plans for subsidiary managers, and changes in product design. The scale runs from 1 (headquarters decides alone) to 5 (subsidiary decides alone), so higher values represent greater autonomy and lower centralization. The construct is the obverse operationalization of centralization.

A latent construct measured by asking respondents to provide estimates of (1) time spent in interunit (e.g. subsidiary and headquarters) committees, teams, and task forces, (2) time spent in interunit meetings and conferences, and (3) time spent in the world headquarters, all measured in days on the most recent annual basis.

Respondents indicated on a scale of 1-5 the typical frequency of their communication with the head office. The scale was 1: daily; 2: weekly; 3: monthly; 4: annually; 5: less than annually. The responses were reverse scored in the analysis so that higher scores represent more frequent rather than less frequent communication.

Respondents indicated on a scale of 1-5 the typical frequency of their communication with each of the other national subsidiaries of the company that were included in the survey (1: daily; 2: weekly; 3: monthly; 4: annually; 5: less than annually). An aggregate intersubsidiary communication score for each respondent was calculated by adding up the individual's intersubsidiary communication frequency scores. Responses were reverse scored so that higher scores represent more frequent communication.

Dependent variable is the logarithm of the constant-dollar stock market value of common equity for each observation. Data for M, the constant dollar stock market value of common equity, are taken from the COMPUSTAT tapes and supplemented by the National Stock Summary, and stock prices are deflated by the U.S. GNP deflator.

Dependent variable is the number of new chemical entities introduced. Idrug consists of nonbiological, self-originated, single new chemical entities; drugs discovered by one firm but marketed by another are attributed to the discovering firm, and compound drugs are excluded. Data on Idrug are from DeHaen.

variable_name: Sij and Pj (estimated coefficients of synergy)
description: The concentric index uses coefficients of synergy Sij between industries i and j, computed as OLS coefficients on variables Fi*Fj such as (% drugs*% chemicals) or (% drugs*% health). When Sij is estimated to be positive there is synergy, when negative there is dissynergy, and when zero there are neither. In the innovation equation, the coefficients of synergy Pj indicate whether the combination of pharmaceuticals and industry j improves or worsens the innovative productivity of drug research.
time_window: four time periods within 1960-1980 and pooled with (year-60) interactions

variable_name: % of firm sales in each industry (% Drug, % Chemicals, % Health, % Agriculture, % Other)
description: Diversification is measured with the shares of sales of a firm in various industries rather than asset shares, because asset data are unavailable before the mid-1970s. The study starts with highly reliable estimates of pharmaceutical sales for each sample firm in each year drawn from the proprietary reports of IMS, which allow corporate sales to be disaggregated by product area with greater accuracy.

Production relatedness covers commonality in physical product characteristics, raw materials, or manufacturing processes. General chemicals and agricultural products (predominantly pesticides and veterinary drugs) are treated as production-related to pharmaceuticals because they have the same 2-digit SIC code (2800), while health-care products (3800, 2000) and all other industries have differing 2-digit SIC codes.

The drug-health products combination (SIC codes 3830, 3840, 3850, 2020) is primarily marketing and to a lesser extent innovation in origin. By the output-based 2-digit SIC rationale health products (3800) and drugs (2830) appear unrelated, but they are related on the basis of marketing to hospitals and physicians.

The sample is split into four time periods, with the date of the 1962 Amendments to the Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act as a natural dividing point and the remaining 18 years divided into three six-year periods. Because of the clear trend over time in most coefficients, a pooling of all four time periods is reported with interaction terms of each base variable multiplied by (year-60).

Dependent variable in the multinomial logit: the continuation type of the patent. The choice set is j = 0 no continuation (base category), j = 1 CAP, j = 2 CIP, j = 3 divisional, j = 4 combination; the CIP alternative is j = 2. Patents issuing from more than one continuation type are coded as combination and included in the estimation but not interpreted.
scale: categorical (no continuation, CAP, CIP, divisional, combination)

description: Alternative j = 1 of the multinomial logit dependent variable, indicating that the patent issued from a continuation application. Base category is patents with no continuation in their history.
scale: categorical (no continuation, CAP, CIP, divisional, combination)

description: Alternative j = 3 of the multinomial logit dependent variable, indicating that the patent issued from a divisional application. Base category is patents with no continuation in their history.
scale: categorical (no continuation, CAP, CIP, divisional, combination)

description: The patenting intensity of firms, calculated as the annual log number of patents divided by millions of dollars of annual R&D; the suffix ln indicates the natural log. It is entered both alone and interacted with lnCAPINT and with lnRDINT.
The R&D intensity of firms, measured as the log of annual R&D expenditure in millions of dollars per 1,000 employees. It is entered alone and in the multiplicative interaction with lnPATINT.

The capital intensity of firms, measured as the log of the book value of plant, property, and equipment in millions of dollars per 1,000 employees. It is entered alone and in the multiplicative interaction with lnPATINT.

The technological importance of the invention, measured by the number of forward citations the patent received within the first four years following its issue (including the issue year). The four-year window is used to reduce truncation bias, since older patents accumulate more citations.
time_window: four-year window from the patent's issue date

description: The variable equals the assessed subjective probability that the computer competitor's first bid would be $1.00. Subjects wrote down this probability before starting the simulation, so it represents what the subjects think the competitor thinks is the appropriate action in this situation.

Binary variable indicating the manager's bid on a round of the simulation. Cooperative choices ($1.00 bids) are assigned a value of 1 and noncooperative choices ($.95 bids) are assigned a value of 0. The data set consists of 350 observations (moves) made by 35 managers over ten rounds (Rounds 3 through 12).

The move that the competitor made in the previous round, coded as 1 if the computer's last move was a $1.00 bid or as a 0 if its last move was a bid of $.95. All subjects received information about the competitor's behavior, which is why competitor behavior from rounds other than Round t-1 is not used.

Equals 1 if a message suggesting that Moxy would bid $1.00 next time was sent last period, which occurs if the subject was in the message group and had just bid $1.00. If the subject was not in the message group, or if a subject in the message group had just bid $.95, the variable equals 0.

Equals 1 if Moxy sent a message indicating that it was about to bid $.95, which occurs if the subject had just bid $.95 and the subject was in the message condition. Otherwise the variable is assigned a value of 0.

A continuous variable representing the round in the simulation for which the manager's move is observed. It ranges over Rounds 3 through 12; Rounds 1 and 2 are excluded because the model cannot be estimated for them.

Defined as the sum total of the competitors actually affected by an action. Competitors affected by each action were further defined as those airlines which provided service in at least one of the sample airports affected by the action; the 37 U.S. large air traffic hubs defined by the Department of Transportation were selected as sample airports. The sample airports affected by each of the 191 actions were first identified based on the reports of Aviation Daily, and the number of airlines serving at least one of these airports was counted.

The attack intensity of an action for each competitor affected was determined as the proportion of passengers served by an airline in the year an action was taken that were affected by that action. Different units of analysis were used: in predicting the number of responses, an action's overall attack intensity was developed by averaging attack intensity measures across all competitors affected by the action; in predicting response lag, a given responding competitor's proportion of passengers affected by the action was used.
time_window: year in which the action was taken

description: The degree of effort an initiating firm requires to execute an action, as reflected by the amount of time spent preparing to execute that action. It was measured as the time difference between the date Aviation Daily reported an action and the date that action was executed as indicated in the journal. If no further report appeared indicating a change, the announced date of execution was assumed valid; otherwise the measure was recalculated, and an action was excluded if its execution was later reported to have been canceled.

A dichotomous classification of each action as strategic or tactical, coded strategic = 1 and tactical = 0. All sample moves were first deductively classified into 16 generic types (e.g., merger and acquisition, price changes, promotion, expansion into a new market, service improvement), and the classification of these types into strategic and tactical categories was achieved with total agreement among all three authors, who coded independently.
The total number of competitors who actually respond to an action, determined by counting the number of airlines that responded to an action as reported in Aviation Daily.

The length of time a competitor takes to respond to an initiator's competitive action, measured as the number of days between the date a specific action was first reported in Aviation Daily and the date that journal first made public the airline's response.

Natural log of the sum of one plus the number of standards published by company employees during the prior three years. Published standards are 'standards-track RFCs' in IETF terminology: documents that have undergone peer review within a working group and generated consensus in the working group and the community in general.

Natural log of the sum of one plus the total number of technical proposals authored by firm employees per period that are under active consideration within an IETF working group. These technical proposals, or Internet drafts, typically go through a number of successive revisions, and the variable increments its count for each active draft in each time period. Only technical proposals presented to working groups are eligible for publication as standards, and the success rate is below 40%.
Natural log of the sum of one plus the total number of firm employees who attended IETF conferences during the prior three years.
Natural log of the sum of one plus the number of periods a firm employee has held a working group chair position during the prior three years.

Equals one for the announcement of an IPO or acquisition in the next trimester. The one-period lag relative to the announcement was instituted to guard against the possibility that observed IETF involvement is a consequence rather than a cause of an actual or anticipated liquidity event.

Degree centrality of a subsystem in the product architecture network, computed as the sum of the weights of the links emanating from a node; the weight of the link between two subsystems is the number of new release ECOs that include parts from both subsystems. Centrality scores were calculated using UCINET 6. To look for the conjectured U-shaped relationship, the square of degree centrality was also included as an independent variable.
time_window: new release ECOs initiated during calendar years 2002–2005

description: For each node (subsystem) i, the coordination deficit is the sum over all j of max(Aij − Cij, 0), where Aij and Cij are the proportion of total link weight from subsystem i to subsystem j in the product architecture network and in the organizational coordination network, respectively. Only links where the architectural connection is stronger than the coordination connection are counted, so excess coverage along one link is not allowed to offset inadequate coverage along another.

The number of warranty incidents (IPTV, incidents per thousand vehicle) reported during the first 12 months after the vehicle launch, aggregated from roughly 17,000 unique problem codes up to the subsystem level.
time_window: first 12 months after vehicle launch (calendar years 2005 and 2006)

description: An index capturing the growth of organized innovative primary care services instituted by the ICJV unit over the period of study. Each organized service was weighted by the formula 1 - n/N, where n was the number of other ICJVs that instituted that service and N was the total number of ICJVs, so the weight ranged from 0 (least innovative) to 1 (most innovative); the weighted values were summed to form an overall index. The index quantifies both the number and the uniqueness of new services, with ICJVs adding the greatest number of relatively unique new services considered most innovative.
scale: index weight ranging from 0 to 1 per service, summed
time_window: over the period of study (through the fourth year)

description: A factor analytic variable formed from the number of primary care physicians per capita at the beginning of the study period, the change in the number of primary care physicians per capita during the study period, and the number of organized services provided by other community health agencies in the area at the beginning of the study period. Factor loadings were .93, .62, and -.34, with an eigenvalue of 1.76. The higher the score, the greater the degree of competition.
time_window: beginning of the study period and change during the study period

description: A factor analytic variable made up of the average family income in the ICJV service area, the percentage of Medicaid recipients in the service area, and the ICJV sponsor's percentage of allowances or discounts from revenue; components were measured at the beginning of the study period. Factor loadings were -0.80, 0.71, and 0.50, with an eigenvalue of 1.89. A high score indicates relatively greater resource scarcity.

An index that captures the growth, in terms of number and uniqueness, of organized innovative primary care services instituted by the sponsoring organization during the period of study. The measure resembles that used to determine ICJV innovation and was collected in the same manner, this time measuring the innovativeness of the sponsoring organization itself.

The number of related alternative service delivery programs previously operated by the hospital, such as ambulatory surgery centers, satellite clinics, home health services and outpatient diagnostic testing services. The measure was taken at the beginning of the study, was obtained from the ICJV director (and verified via phone conversations), and is based on archival data kept by the hospitals.

The standard deviation of physician ages in the ICJV unit; the physician age data were provided by the ICJV director. O'Reilly and Flatt (1988) used a similar measure of age diversity in their study of innovation.

A continuous variable indicating the number of linkages established by the ICJV medical director via participation in top-level hospital committees, typically management committees such as the executive management committee and the strategic planning committee. These linkages were seen as enabling the ICJV medical director to educate the hospital about the ICJV and highlight its strategic role.

Growth in the operating margin for the unit, with data obtained from audited financial statements. Operating margin equals (net operating revenue - operating expenses)/operating expenses; slack equals [Operating Margin (year 3) - Operating Margin (year 1)]/Operating Margin (year 1). A three year period was used because an earlier period would not have allowed for the accumulation of slack, and no later measures of slack were taken.
time_window: first three years of the program (innovation measured through the fourth year)

description: A composite variable indicating the extent to which the unit was free to determine its own policies with respect to marketing, budgeting, and physician personnel. It ranges from a value of one (least autonomous) to nine (most autonomous) and represents a summation of the ICJV director's assessment (on a three point scale) of the unit's autonomy in each of the three areas. Marketing, personnel, and budgeting were considered the most important areas with regard to the ICJV's ability to adopt and maintain new programs.
scale: composite ranging from 1 (least autonomous) to 9 (most autonomous)

description: Ratebeer.com product ratings pages display the corporate owner's identity after acquisition, while beeradvocate.com pages do not; this design feature makes all visitors of the treatment website aware of the craft brewer's corporate ownership. T is a dummy equal to one if the observation is from ratebeer.com, P is a dummy equal to one if the review occurred after the craft brewer was acquired, and their interaction identifies the effect of knowledge of inauthenticity. Because the date ratebeer.com updated the brewery name cannot be precisely identified, treatment is assumed to occur on the first day any LexisNexis news source reported the acquisition, or the date of the official press release, whichever is sooner.
time_window: one year before to one year after the acquisition

description: The weighted taste, aroma, appearance, and palate measures are aggregated into a composite score of audience perceptions of product quality. Each objective dimension is standardized and rescaled to match the weightings used by beeradvocate.com: taste 40%, aroma 24%, mouthfeel 10%, and appearance 6%. Ratings are rescaled to a 100-point scale so that coefficients can be interpreted as percentage points.

To operationalize symbolic value, the user's perception of quality rating is subtracted from their overall rating, on the assumption that the difference between the overall rating and the perception of quality rating can be attributed to symbolic value. The resulting measure is on a 100-point scale.

The fifth ratings dimension required by both websites, labeled "overall" and described by ratebeer.com as "Your overall impression of the beer"; it includes all objective criteria, like taste, as well as any other value the rater derives from consuming the product. Ratings are rescaled to a 100-point scale so that coefficients can be interpreted as percentage points.

A combined measure of patent and copyright use. High IP is set equal to 1 if an ISV has either a high number of patents (greater than 0, because 95% of ISVs have zero patents) or a high number of copyrights (greater than the median), and 0 otherwise. The patent stock is generated by date of grant from the USPTO patents database, restricted to software patents identified by taking the intersection of USPTO class-subclass combinations and a Boolean keyword query, and is citation-weighted using the method of Hall et al. (2002). The copyright stock is the firm's stock of registered copyrights described as 'computer files' in the U.S. Copyright Office classification scheme.

A discrete measure of the ISV's stock of trademarks used as a proxy for the stock of marketing-specific downstream capabilities and a firm's brand capital. High trademark is set to 1 if an ISV's stock of trademarks is greater than the sample median and 0 otherwise. Only software trademarks that are currently 'live' as of the date of observation are used, obtained from the USPTO trademarks database.

Growth prospects are characterized by demand in the vertical industry the ISV serves. The sales growth rate in each industry-year (master code-year) is calculated using the CorpTech universe of ISVs and equals (current year sales of all ISVs that serve the industry)/(previous year sales of all ISVs that serve the industry). The firm-year variable Sales growth is defined as the arithmetic average of growth rates across all the industries that an ISV serves; target industries are manually coded from the ISVs' target industry descriptions using the SAP 'master code' industry classification.
level: firm-year (industry growth averaged to the firm)

description: An alternative measure of growth opportunities based on the size of the horizontal product market. Each CorpTech SOF product code is treated as a distinct market and the market (product code) level entry rate is defined as (number of ISVs in the current year - number of ISVs in the previous year)/(number of ISVs in the current year). The variable entry rate is the arithmetic average of market level entry rates across the ISV's product portfolio.
level: firm-year (product-market rate averaged to the firm)

description: The dependent variable is whether an ISV enters into partnership with SAP in a particular year. Partnership formation events are identified through press releases searched in LexisNexis; for ISVs with multiple SAP partnership events, the first such event is used as the time the ISV joins SAP's platform. The unit of observation is a firm-year, with the partnership variable equal to 1 if a first-time alliance is formed in that year and 0 otherwise; post-partnership observations are deleted because partnership is treated as an absorbing state.

A binary variable that equals one if a given firm has a public API operating on a given date. The first date a firm's APIs are submitted to ProgrammableWeb is used to proxy when the firm initiated a public API strategy.
Log of the firm's market value, with market capitalization and other financial outcomes provided by Compustat at the quarterly level.

variable_name: betweenness centrality, degree, effective network size (mean, max, sum)
description: Each node corresponds to a firm's API and each link connects a firm's APIs via third-party applications. Betweenness centrality is the share of shortest paths between nodes passing through a node; degree sums the total number of connections between a node and other nodes; effective network size is the number of connections minus redundant connections between nodes. Averages, maximums, and sums of these statistics across all the APIs a firm operates are computed for each quarter in which it has at least one operational API, and the statistics are centered and scaled.
scale: centered and scaled (mean zero, standard deviation one)

variable_name: breach event by type; log count of records exposed
description: The outcome is a binary indicator of whether a specific type of breach event occurred (any breach, breach of credit card info, breach via malicious hack, breach via stolen document or fixed computer, breach via portable computer, breach via malicious insider), or the log of the total amount of records breached. Events come from PRC public breach announcements as matched to Compustat firms, with breach by malicious insider often being misuse of an authorized API key.

variable_name: follower count, developer count, change count
description: Follower count is a firm-level sum of the number of ProgrammableWeb users who follow that firm's APIs, a self-reported measure of interest in those APIs. The number of developers tracks the interest of self-reported developers who claim to work on applications using that API, and change count reports the total number of updates the firm has made to all of its APIs.

Tobin's Q, the ratio of market capitalization to assets, is used as the standard approach to measuring whether a firm's investment is limited by capital adjustment costs. The authors run regressions analogous to the baseline specification with the addition of the log of firm assets, so that the API coefficient measures the effect of API adoption on log(Q).

For the proprietary data set, the date of API adoption is measured as the first date the firm is observed with nonzero data flows through one of its APIs. To measure the effect of purely internal APIs, the authors use the subset of firms in this data set that do not have any APIs reported on ProgrammableWeb, leaving only internal API use as the treatment; approximately 0.7% of firm-quarters represent internal API use.
Log of the firm's market value from Compustat, matched to the proprietary private-API data, used as the outcome when estimating the effect over time of adopting purely internal APIs.

Binary indicator of whether a job listing requires at least one skill falling into the AI and data science technology categories, as grouped by the data provider's clustering methods. Base-level categories include machine learning, business analytics, julia, and natural language processing, each of which contains more detailed skills.

Job listings are identified as requiring domain knowledge (DOM) if they require at least one skill that aligns with the O*NET knowledge categories. Computers and Electronics, Engineering and Technology, Telecommunications, and Mathematics were removed from the full list because they overlap with algorithmic skill measures.
