The narrow focus state (California) is the comparison against the broad focus state (Arizona) that serves as the constant in the model.
time_window: time periods within the first three years of tenure

description: Indicator variable measuring type of employee, used in the within-jurisdiction comparison of auditors and nonauditors in the narrowly focused, two-year jurisdiction. A value of 1 is assigned to auditors; nonauditors are the constant, as all data for this analysis are from California.
time_window: time periods within the first three years of tenure

variable_name: Month interval of the transition rate increase
description: The timing of the hazard shift is located by comparing exit rates in adjacent month intervals: 7-12 months versus 13-18 months under the one-year requirement, and 19-24 months versus 25-27 months under the two-year requirement. The interval in which the rate rises marks when the shift occurs in each jurisdiction.

variable_name: Difference in transition rates before and after expected shift
description: The size of the hazard shift is the difference between the resignation transition rate in the period just before and the period just after employees complete the experience requirement. A lower rate before and a higher rate after means a shift, and a larger difference means a larger shift. Rates are estimated from personnel records with event-history models and compared across jurisdictions and employee types.
time_window: periods around the end of the one- or two-year requirement

description: The annual loan review reevaluated the creditworthiness of a borrower on a seven-point risk-rating scale on which 1 represented extremely low risk and 7 represented a high probability of the borrower's not repaying the full principal of the loan. The rating reflected the lender's perception of the chance the borrower would not repay, based on the borrower firm's management capabilities, market position, financial health, collateral and sources of loan repayment. Only observations with ratings of 3, 4 or 5 were included in the analysis.

variable_name: average interest rate above the prime interest rate
description: Because borrowers often had more than one credit line, the interest rate was calculated as an average of the rates on a borrower's lines weighted by the size of each line of credit, computed each year for each borrower. Only borrowers with variable-rate loans were retained, and for these the rate was specified as the number of percentage points above the prime interest rate, so the measure is the average interest rate charged above prime.

The after-tax return on assets the bank expected from the customer, calculated by the lending officer as part of the borrower analysis. It included an administrative charge and a loan loss provision charge that varied according to the assigned risk level, both derived from studies of historical costs associated with borrowers at each risk level. The bank first began using the ROA calculation in 1990, so only 104 observations were available for this measure.
Indicator variable coded 1 if the borrower's risk rating had been upgraded since the last annual review, and 0 otherwise.
time_window: within the past year, relative to the annual review

description: Indicator variable coded 1 if the borrower's risk rating had been downgraded since the last annual review, and 0 otherwise.
time_window: within the past year, relative to the annual review

description: The number of relations for a given scientist-year was the sum of that scientist's coauthors during the previous five years; for example, the number of relations for a given scientist in 1994 was the count of that scientist's coauthors from 1989 through 1994, inclusive. To test for the hypothesized curvilinear association, the number of relations squared was also included. The measure was centered to minimize potential multicollinearity in the squared term.

Measured by counting the total number of times that a scientist published with each coauthor during the previous five-year window. These numbers were summed for each researcher and divided by the total number of coauthors to create an average number of times published per coauthor during the five-year window. The curvilinear association was tested by including strength of relations squared, and the measure was centered.

The impact-factor-weighted articles published by each scientist each year were summed, following Stephan and Levin (1991), using the Institute of Scientific Information's 'impact factor' to assess knowledge creation represented by a given scientist's publications in a given year. For example, if a scientist has four publications in two journals, with three in journal A, which has an impact factor of 1, and one in journal B, which has an impact factor of 5, the value for the scientist on the variable for knowledge creation would be 8 ([3 x 1] + [1 x 5]).

variable_name: respect for nature subscale of the sustainable development values scale
description: Subscale with four items on which participants chose between two alternative statements on a seven-point Likert-type scale. The items contrast a statement that resources may be sacrificed or that only minor changes are needed with a statement that all precautions must be taken to protect natural resources and that major changes are needed. Internal reliability for the analyses was a Cronbach's alpha of .79.

Scale of 22 items describing tasks and roles typical in the entrepreneurial context; respondents rated their belief in their ability to accomplish a task on a five-point scale from 1 = 'completely unsure' to 5 = 'completely sure'. Internal reliability for the analyses was a Cronbach's alpha of .93.

Three-item scale reported by Covin and Slevin (1989) and based on Khandwalla (1976/1977), assessing the environmental munificence the respondents' firms face. Scores were reverse-coded because the original scale had lower scores representing greater perceived munificence. A confirmatory factor analysis revealed one factor with a Cronbach's alpha of .60.

variable_name: weight assigned to a specified harm to the natural environment
description: Founders assessed the attractiveness of conjoint opportunity profiles (1 = 'not at all attractive,' 11 = 'very attractive') in a neutral environmental impact condition and in a condition in which the opportunity was described as causing a significant decline in the natural environment locally and in other parts of the world. A founder's assessment policy was decomposed into a coefficient for each assessment attribute and an intercept, and the weight assigned to the specified harm is the coefficient capturing the effect of the harm information on assessments of opportunity attractiveness (in the reported models the harm intercept is negative, so a more negative value means more weight placed on harm).

variable_name: image-strength score for the vision statement
description: Two coders assessed image-based words based on the properties of language that induce imagery. Each codable word was rated from 0 to 10, whereby a word associated with a weak image yielded 0 points and a word associated with a strong image yielded 10 points, and the points for all of the words were added together to determine a final image-strength score for each statement. Interrater reliability among the coders was strong, ICC = .877.
scale: 0-10 per word, summed to a statement score

variable_name: number of values in values statements
description: Coders counted the number of values in values statements, focusing on the idea that a value is a concise, abstract description of a 'desired end-state'. A value had to be stated as if it were representing the organization rather than an individual.

The percentage of Medicare patients who were not readmitted to the hospital within 30 days following discharge, for patients admitted with a heart attack. Medicare adjusts the measure for patient risk by taking into account a patient's age, gender, past medical history, and any other diseases or conditions the patient had upon arrival at the hospital.

Participants were shown one of two visions matched on cadence and sentence structure and varying only in the number of image-based words, with the number of words set in line with Fortune 500 company vision statements. The weak-imagery vision was 'Our vision is that our toys-all of them made to perfection by our employees-will be enjoyed by all of our customers', and the strong-imagery vision was 'Our vision is that our toys-all of them crafted flawlessly by our workers-will make wide-eyed kids laugh and proud parents smile'.

One value for the 'small number of values' condition and nine values for the 'large number of values' condition, chosen because one and nine represent about one standard deviation below and above the hospital mean. In the nine-value conditions each value was displayed with a brief description; in the one-value condition a single value was randomly selected for each iteration and displayed with its description.

Participants described their goals, including what they perceived as the ultimate purpose of the task, in open-ended dialogue boxes. A computer algorithm calculated the amount of overlap among team members in their construal of the ultimate goal, giving a team one point when multiple members wrote down the same word or phrase related to the ultimate goal; concrete (vision-based) and conceptual (values-based) descriptions were added together into a single variable.
scale: count of shared words or phrases

description: Coordination was measured through error prevention because it proxies how effectively the first member took the perspective of the second member when describing the toy design and how well the second member used the instructions while taking operational constraints into consideration. Error was calculated as the amount that the budget exceeded the maximum allowed in choosing materials to assemble the prototype.
scale: amount by which the budget was exceeded

variable_name: performance quality (quality of the toy design)
description: One of the study authors first evaluated the toy designs to determine which ones could not be built given the available materials; seven children ranging in age from 7 to 12 then evaluated how much they would want to play with each toy on a scale from 0 (no value) to 100 (maximal value). Ideas for toys that could not be built and participants who did not provide a design idea were given a 0. Interrater reliability, as measured with an intraclass correlation coefficient, was .611.

Individual creativity is measured by computing the number of awards and nominations each creator received in a given year. Awards and nominations were collected from professional societies of critics and peers that bestow awards on individual creators rather than on the movie as a whole. The authors argue that a count measure accounts for the continuous nature of creativity and that these awards reflect the sociocultural expectations of the field regarding the creativity of a given outcome.

The domain of each movie is identified with the main genre of the movie. Knowledge depth for a creator at year t is operationalized as the number of movies the creator has worked on that include the main genre of the movie he or she realized in year t. For example, if the three movies prior to the focal movie all have 'comedy' as the main genre, the creator has a knowledge depth equal to three.
time_window: up to and prior to the focal year

description: Since movie genres represent different domains, knowledge breadth is measured as the number of different genres an individual has worked on up to the focal year. For example, a creator who worked on a movie classified as sci-fi/comedy and another classified as comedy/adventure has a knowledge breadth equal to three.

The authors first identified the year of the creator's first contribution to the field, the Hollywood animation industry, which could be of any nature and in any role. Career age is then operationalized as the time elapsed between the year of the first contribution to the field and the observation year.
time_window: year of first contribution to the observation year

description: Network constraint was computed with Burt's (1992) measure of the extent to which an artist's network was closed. Constraint increased from 0 to 1 according to the extent to which a person had few contacts (size), those contacts were strongly connected directly to one another (density), or strongly connected indirectly through their connections to the same other person in the network (hierarchy). The independent variable was operationalized as 1 − constraint, so that high scores reflect openness and low scores reflect closure. Constraint was computed within four-episode time windows for the panel data set.
time_window: four-episode time window (the focal episode plus the immediately preceding three episodes)

description: Each episode was described by a profile of 41 binary variables: three distinguished story type, three distinguished story setting, 12 distinguished incarnations of the Doctor, and 23 distinguished the kind of alien opposing the Doctor. The content on which an artist had worked was defined by M content profiles, where M is the number of episodes the artist had contributed to within the four-episode time window. Jaccard coefficients were used to measure dissimilarity between pairs of the M profiles, and the M2 elements of the resulting association matrix were averaged to measure the artist's content heterogeneity. Because one-episode artists would naturally receive a score of 0, their score was shifted from 0 to .33.
scale: Jaccard coefficients averaged; 0 to 1, with single-episode artists shifted from 0 to .33
time_window: four-episode time window (the focal episode plus the immediately preceding three episodes)

description: Network stability was measured as 1 − (n new ties / max new ties). New ties were computed as the number of new faces on the creative team the artist was working with on a given episode, where a collaborator was treated as 'new' if the artist had not worked with them before the current episode. Given the small team sizes, the number of new faces in a given episode was typically one or two, with many instances of no new faces (13.39%).

Two expert judges independently rated the creativity of the producer, the director, the writer, and overall episode creativity on a 5-point scale (1 = not creative, 5 = very creative). For the panel data set, the creativity of the creator's role was used as the measure of their creativity in the given episode; if the creator covered more than one role, the average of the two scores was taken. Interrater agreement was measured with Cohen's weighted kappa, with scores between .79 and .83.
time_window: ratings provided two years after the last episode was broadcast

description: Using films' writer and director credits, the individuals credited for each of the three stages (generation, elaboration, implementation) were delineated. Films were late handoff if another person drove both generation and elaboration before the director drove implementation (n = 1,604; 28.26%); no handoff if the director drove all three stages (n = 2,821; 49.70%); early handoff if another person drove generation before the director drove both elaboration and implementation (n = 483; 8.51%); and serial late handoff if one person drove generation, then a second person drove elaboration, before the director drove implementation (n = 768; 13.53%). Films with more than one individual credited for any stage were omitted.

Composite critic score from Rotten Tomatoes, a website that aggregates critics' independent reviews into composite scores. The authors primarily report the 0-10 mean ratings because they are more consistent with the Consensual Assessment Technique and more granular than the 0-100% score. Independent ratings of 2,000 critic reviews on 200 films were collected to support the validity of using these scores to measure creativity.

Independent raters (recruited via MTurk and separate from the participants) rated participants' three-slide final ads using the Consensual Assessment Technique. Creativity was defined to raters as 'Overall degree to which the ad is both novel and useful,' evaluated on a 7-point scale (1 = extremely low, 7 = extremely high). The 600 ads were randomly divided into 10 groups of 60, with 30 raters assigned to each group; each ad was rated by 30 raters, and ads from the same yoked group were assigned to different rater groups.

Six items adapted from prior measures of psychological ownership, rated directly after participants submitted their final ads on a 7-point Likert-type scale (1 = strongly disagree, 7 = strongly agree); two items were reverse-scored. The scale's alpha was .93. Psychological ownership correlated .27 with creativity and .13 with product coherence.

Independent raters separate from the creativity raters assessed participants' final ads; product coherence was defined to raters as the 'Degree to which the different parts or elements of the ad work well together as a whole,' rated on the same 7-point scale used for creativity. Each ad was rated by 30 raters; interrater agreement was ICC(1,30) = .79.

The entirety of the CEO's speech from the question-and-answer portion of each earnings call was analyzed according to text analysis dimensions identifying words that paint a picture of perceivable reality versus words that are abstract. The authors created a composite variable in R that averaged three measures drawn from three established linguistic dictionaries: two from the MRC linguistic database (one concreteness dictionary and one imagability dictionary) and one developed by Brysbaert, Warriner, and Kuperman (2014). The reliability among the three variables was strong (a = .92).
time_window: one-year lag between independent and dependent variables

description: To assess dispositional concreteness, the authors used the 18-item scale validated by Reyt and Wiesenfeld (2015). Participants were shown 18 activities (e.g., 'writing business correspondence') and, for each one, asked to choose the extent to which they construed the activity in terms that were concrete ('composing an email') or abstract ('maintaining a good business relationship'). The scale also captures the direction people tend to move in over time, either asking 'how' a problem can be solved or 'why' the problem should be pursued (a = .85).

The primary measure simultaneously accounted for the number of management layers and concentration of authority by summing every downward hierarchical connection - that is, every link from one person to an individual in the level(s) below them. This value increases simultaneously as a function of increasing layers of management and increasing concentration of authority in a way that accounts for the interdependence between the two dimensions.

Hierarchy was manipulated with a description of the overall hierarchy at Sprig Comforts and the authority structure within the top management team. In the strong hierarchy condition, participants were informed that Sprig Comforts had a strong overall organizational hierarchy, reflected in part by three layers of hierarchy within the TMT: the CEO (layer 1), a COO (layer 2), and three top executives (layer 3). In the weak hierarchy condition, the TMT had no COO, meaning the day-to-day tasks of TMT executives were directly supervised by the CEO, with the CEO (layer 1) and four top executives (layer 2).

Adopted three factors reflecting change through both growth and reduction, and change that is both internally generated and externally obtained: acquisitions (externally obtained, growth-directed change), R&D spending (internally generated, growth-directed change), and property sales (reduction-based change). The authors accounted for the absolute amount of change, such that a $10 million increase in R&D spending was equivalent to a $10 million decrease; to reduce recursive relationships and reverse causality, they subtracted the absolute value of change one year after the independent variable from the absolute value of change two years after the independent variable. The three items were z-scored and then averaged.
time_window: change two years after minus one year after the independent variable

description: Employed the same three dimensions as in Study 1. For property sales, CEOs were told the company currently owns five physical stores and that they can buy or sell between zero and five. For R&D, CEOs could spend nothing or develop items more relevant to the pandemic with between 10% and 50% of the company's budget. For acquisitions, CEOs could take no action or acquire a small, medium, or large firm. Each variable was z-scored and averaged to create an index of change.

Assessed with 12 items (a = .90), six of which related to time horizon and six of which related to breadth of scope. Example items are 'My time is better spent planning what the company might look like several years rather than several weeks into the future' (attention toward long-term goals) and 'I'd rather focus on the "big picture" of Sprig Comforts than smaller operational details' (attention toward broad goals).

An index with two components: the first captures the extent to which tie mobilization is spread across the different idea-elaboration stages (dispersion), and the second measures the consistency in timing in terms of mobilizing inner-circle ties before outer-circle ones. Inner- versus outer-circle ties are characterized by the number of shared third-party ties from an alter-alter matrix: the greater the fraction of ties held by individual i that are also held by j, the more likely j belongs to i's inner circle. The four stages of idea elaboration at which a contact is first told about the idea range from 'almost immediately after first getting the idea' to 'after validation in a lab/trial environment'. Ties for which respondents indicated they would never disclose the idea or chose 'not applicable' were excluded from the calculation.

The firm's annual performance review system allocates individuals to three bands based on an elaborate assessment of their contributions to innovations that generate revenue or reduce costs, or that offer significant promise of such outcomes. Each individual completes a review document with detailed and verifiable evidence of contributions to five main projects, and completed documents are compared across pools of scientists and engineers of the same rank by a committee of line managers, who allocate individuals to one of three performance rating bands following a forced distribution. Ratings were obtained six months after the survey.
time_window: ratings obtained six months after the survey; cover the six months of the survey plus six months after

description: A newly developed six-item scale intended to measure both the degree of autonomy granted to R&D scientists and engineers and the degree of managerial accountability; the six items loaded on two factors. The first factor, measuring accountability, has four items, with a Cronbach's alpha of .61 and interitem correlations between .20 and .43. The measure of the accountability that R&D scientists and engineers experience in their division and site is derived by averaging the responses of the R&D managers at that site and division.

Based on two survey questions: a question in the scientist/engineer and manager surveys asking individuals to nominate up to four people involved in important project-related decisions whose opinion was critical during project review and evaluation, yielding a list of influential managers per division; and a question in the scientist/engineer survey on the perceived level of support received from the managers with whom they most closely collaborated, measured with a 6-item scale adapted from a supervisory support scale (Cronbach's alpha = .92). The items were reverse-coded and the responses in relation to each of the nominated managers in a division were averaged.

A 4-item scale developed by Danneels (2008) (Cronbach's alpha = .81), incorporated into the survey of R&D directors, who were judged best placed to answer questions about slack resources because they manage the financial budgets of their units. The items were reverse-coded relative to the original scale to measure the lack of slack resources, and where responses from multiple directors for the same division were received, the average was computed.

A 5-item scale developed by Chandy and Tellis (1998) and adapted by Danneels (2008) (Cronbach's alpha = .70), incorporated into the survey of R&D directors, who were judged best suited to assessing the willingness of a division to cannibalize because they are responsible for strategic decision-making at the divisional level. The items were reverse-coded relative to the original scale to obtain a measure of reluctance, as opposed to willingness, to cannibalize existing assets, and scores were averaged whenever multiple responses from the same division were received.

Composite index created by transforming the four image-based cue variables into z-scores and taking their mean (two variables for each image-based cue measure): before and after images and self-portraits for competence, and group images and personal life images for warmth. Before and after images and self-portrait images were counted from the influencer's posts, with three raters independently evaluating 500 posts; group images included three or more individuals and personal life images showed kids, pets, vacations, and vistas.
time_window: monthly observation over the six-month study period

description: Composite index created by transforming the six word-based cue variables into z-scores and taking their mean (three variables for each word-based cue measure): analytic words in posts, analytic words in replies, and first-person singular pronouns for competence, and positive affect words in posts, positive affect words in replies, and other-inclusive first-person plural and second person pronouns for warmth. All variables were measured using the analytic, pronoun, and positive affect dictionaries in LIWC.
time_window: monthly observation over the six-month study period

description: Composite measure created by taking the mean of the z-scores for the three word-based and two image-based competence cue measures.
time_window: monthly observation over the six-month study period

description: Composite measure created by taking the mean of the z-scores for the three word-based and two image-based warmth cue measures.
time_window: monthly observation over the six-month study period

description: The number of followers the influencer had at the end of each month, collected from the influencer's profile. Because the within-month change in followers is typically small and the authors focus on between-influencer differences, the end-of-month value is used. The measure was log-transformed to address its right-skewness.

Calculated using the positive affect dictionary in Linguistic Inquiry Word Count (LIWC); the authors content-analyzed followers' responses to the influencer's posts and counted the number of positive affect words used by others in the comments portion of the influencer's posts.
time_window: monthly aggregation over the six-month study period

description: Binary variable capturing whether a job seeker indicated interest in a viewed job posting (pressed the tick symbol = 1) or not (pressed the cross = 0). Job seekers could rate each unique job only once and could only view the next advertisement after choosing one of the two options; pressing tick formally enters the job seeker into the candidate pool.

Coded algorithmically from job seekers' first names using the genderize.io API, which compares each name with a database of over 200,000 distinct names across 89 languages and provides a probability that each name-gender attribution was correct. A threshold of 85% was used to assign gender; '0' = man, '1' = woman.

variable_name: Proportion of women in the startup
description: The gender composition of the company (proportion of men and women) reported by startups on each of their job advertisements, captured as the proportion of women employed by the startup. It ranged from 0 (0% women) to 1 (100% women).

Operationalized using Highhouse et al.'s (2003) 5-item application intentions scale, rated on a 5-point Likert-type agreement scale from 1 'strongly disagree' to 5 'strongly agree', with items averaged into a composite (alpha = .89). Secondary measures used in robustness checks were application decision (yes = 1, no = 0) and behavioral interest (whether they wanted to be forwarded to the company's career page; yes = 1, no = 0).

Self-reported in response to the question 'What is your gender?' with answer options 'Man,' 'Woman,' 'Another identity not listed,' and 'Prefer not to answer.' Only men and women were retained for analysis ('0' = man, '1' = woman).

Randomly assigned manipulation embedded in an otherwise identical fictitious employer profile for a company called 'ScaleIT' (founding year 2019, 11-50 employees, software, average employee age 30). The diversity debt signal condition showed '95% men/5% women' and the no diversity debt signal condition showed '60% men/40% women'.
Measured using a scale by Kroeper et al. (2022) rated on a 5-point Likert scale ranging from 1 'not at all' to 5 'an extreme amount'; items were averaged into a composite (alpha = .95).
scale: 5-point scale (1 = not at all to 5 = an extreme amount)

description: Cumulative abnormal return (CAR) over the three-day (−1, +1) period surrounding the earnings announcement. Excess returns were calculated using the Fama–French plus momentum model provided by the EVENTUS program, which calculates abnormal returns relative to the Carhart four-factor framework, with an estimation window spanning from 255 days to 46 days prior to the event. The abnormal return is then aggregated over the event window to arrive at CAR.
time_window: three-day (−1, +1) event window; estimation window 255 to 46 days prior to the announcement

description: Spline variable that equals the magnitude of the earnings surprise when a firm experiences a material positive surprise, and zero otherwise, so that non-material surprises are treated as meeting predictive expectations. Earnings surprises were computed as the percentage difference between a firm's actual quarterly earnings and the mean analyst estimate for that quarter, and material surprises were defined as the top quartile of positive surprises within a given industry-year-quarter.
scale: top quartile of positive surprises within industry-year-quarter; zero otherwise

description: Spline variable that equals the magnitude of the earnings surprise when a firm experiences a material negative surprise, and zero otherwise, so that non-material surprises are treated as meeting predictive expectations. Earnings surprises were computed as the percentage difference between a firm's actual quarterly earnings and the mean analyst estimate for that quarter, and material surprises were defined as the top quartile of negative surprises within a given industry-year-quarter.
scale: top quartile of negative surprises within industry-year-quarter; zero otherwise

description: Indicator coded 1 if the current quarter's earnings surprise was lower than the previous quarter's earnings surprise, and 0 otherwise. The measure treats a comparison of the current earnings surprise with the firm's own past earnings surprise as the prescriptive expectation.

Indicator variable that equals 1 when a firm's earnings surprise falls below the current industry average earnings surprise, excluding the focal firm, and 0 otherwise. It captures the firm's performance relative to a prescriptive expectation of industry peer comparison.

Percentage change in Tobin's Q over the (−7, −1) window in the days leading up to the earnings announcement, calculated as the difference between Tobin's Q at the end and at the beginning of the window divided by the Q value at the beginning. Tobin's Q was estimated as the market value of the firm divided by its total assets, with market value calculated as the sum of the values of common stock, preferred stock, long-term debt, and short-term debt with a maturity of less than one year.

A binary variable for the between-individual analyses, coded 1 for individuals who left a film with professionally ambiguous attributions and 0 for formerly attached directors of matched films who left with external attributions (such as scheduling conflicts or a change in production plans). The comparison set comprised 41 creative difference directors and 41 attached directors, all of whom had left a film project.
time_window: five years before and after the reported creative differences

description: A binary variable for the within-individual analyses representing the time phase experienced by individual creative difference directors, with 1 denoting the time phase after the creative differences and 0 denoting the time phase prior. Each director's career was observed for five years before and five years after the event.
time_window: five years before and after the reported creative differences

description: A dichotomous variable comparing films associated with professionally ambiguous attributions to films without this potential stigma, coded 1 for creative difference films and 0 for twin films. Twin films were matched on budget, year and season of release, and genre.

Reported production budgets collected from IMDb of each feature film directed by a sampled director, adjusted into 2015 U.S. dollar inflation-adjusted value using Consumer Price Index data. This provides a measure of the relative size and scope of the project the director was employed on, capturing the financial scale of future projects. Log-transformed and standardized.
time_window: five years after the reported creative differences

description: The count of feature film projects directed by a sampled director in the given period, providing a measure of the frequency of the director's employment. Log-transformed and standardized.
time_window: five years after the reported creative differences

variable_name: U.S. domestic and global box office
description: U.S. domestic and global gross box-office figures collected from IMDb, adjusted into the 2015 U.S. dollar inflation-adjusted value using Consumer Price Index data. In additional analyses the authors assigned a box-office value of zero to films that were never finished.
time_window: theatrical release of the focal film

description: The distributor information on IMDb was used to capture whether a feature film directed by a sampled director was distributed by a core studio, coded 1 for distribution by a major studio, mini-major, or one of their subsidiaries, and 0 otherwise. It serves as the mediator, as a proxy for the continuation or discontinuation of professional relationships with the core of the industry.
time_window: five years after the reported creative differences

description: The IMDb Pro STARmeter ranking of the top two billed actors, where the top-ranked star is number one and lesser-ranked stars receive a higher figure. The authors manually collected each star's ranking, used the median ranking in eight- or 16-week intervals around the reported date of creative differences, and calculated the peak ranking of collaborated stars by taking the minimum of the reversed individual median STARmeter rankings. Reverse-coded so that higher values indicate higher status.
time_window: eight- or 16-week intervals around the reported date of creative differences

description: Hedge fund firms are comprised of multiple funds, and fund managers' performance is assessed based on the performance of the fund(s) they manage. The authors focused on a fund's Sortino ratio, a measure of investment returns adjusted for the risk-free rate of return and downside investment risk, for a manager's primary (i.e., sole or largest) fund. They first estimated a regression model predicting fund manager performance based on fund strategy dummies, fund size, firm size, firm age, and a dummy for whether the firm was located in a geographic hub, and then computed a manager's residual performance for each month. Residual performance reflects the extent to which a manager's fund performs above (positive residual value) or below (negative residual value) its expected performance based on those firm- and fund-level factors.
time_window: monthly; performance analyzed over the six months before and the seven months after the mobility event

description: Prior interorganizational moves were assessed as the number of times a fund manager changed hedge fund employers between their entry into the industry and their final mobility event. Interorganizational moves were identified based on changes in a manager's employer from one month to the next, excluding employer transitions resulting from an acquisition.
time_window: from the manager's entry into the industry to their final mobility event

description: Mobility is coded as 0 in all observation periods preceding the mobility event, and then takes the value of 1 in the period during which the mobility event occurs and each period thereafter. The coefficient for mobility reflects the immediate change in an individual's performance in the period mobility occurs (i.e., a shift in the intercept associated with the mobility event). A negative coefficient therefore reflects an immediate decrease in performance following mobility.
time_window: monthly, centered on the month of the mobility event

description: Recovery takes the value of 0 up to and including the observation period in which the mobility event occurs, and then takes the value of 1 in the period immediately following the mobility event, increasing by one in each subsequent observation period. The recovery hypotheses were tested by comparing the number of months it takes managers to recover to their pre-mobility performance levels rather than by the rate of performance recovery.
scale: count of months since the mobility event
time_window: monthly; up to seven months following the mobility event

description: Using the addresses of firms' offices, the authors identified geographic hubs in those regions with the heaviest concentration of hedge fund firms (i.e., California, Connecticut, Florida, Illinois, Massachusetts, and New York). Unfamiliar move is a dummy variable set equal to 1 when a manager moves to a firm located outside a hub in which they have previously worked, 0 otherwise.

The authors first calculated shared dyadic tenure for each dyad of incumbent managers in the firm—the number of years of overlapping tenure shared between each pair of managers. They then computed the mean shared dyadic tenure across all managers, reflecting the average shared tenure among all incumbent managers at the firm. The variable is modeled at Level 3 of the growth model.

This dummy variable is set equal to 1 for managers whose primary fund is a comanaged fund, 0 otherwise. Whereas in all other funds a single fund manager has sole discretion and responsibility for investment decisions, in comanaged funds investment decisions are made jointly with at least one other fund manager.

The dependent variable in all models is the hazard of entry into angel investment. Entrepreneurs enter the observation window in the year they founded their first venture-backed company and exit when they make their first angel investment or in 2020. Entrepreneurs who began angel investing before founding their first company are excluded. All investments in startups made by individuals, other than investments in their own company, are considered angel investments.
time_window: enter in founding year (2005 or later); exit at first angel investment or 2020

description: Dummy variable equal to 1 if the focal entrepreneur's ventures had received an angel investment as of year t. Investments by individuals are counted, deliberately excluding angel groups and syndicates that invest through collective decision-making. Built by matching Crunchbase investment data with People Data Labs biographical information. Dollar amounts for investments received are unavailable because Crunchbase does not disaggregate individual investor contributions within rounds.

variable_name: Count of investments from same-school Angels
description: Count of the focal entrepreneur's investments received from angels who attended the same higher education institution as the entrepreneur. Constructed by matching Crunchbase investment data with People Data Labs biographical information. Angels were coded as same-school at any point in time rather than requiring temporal overlap.

variable_name: Count of investments from same-company Angels
description: Count of the focal entrepreneur's investments received from angels who worked at the same company as the entrepreneur. Constructed by matching Crunchbase investment data with People Data Labs biographical information. Angels were coded as same-company at any point in time rather than requiring temporal overlap.

variable_name: Count of investments from same-location Angels
description: Count of the focal entrepreneur's investments received from angels whom Crunchbase listed in the same metropolitan area as the entrepreneur. Constructed by matching Crunchbase investment data with People Data Labs biographical information. Angels were coded as same-location at any point in time rather than requiring temporal overlap.

Participants were advised to move $30,000 out of the stock market and then chose between two investment opportunities of equivalent risk, presented in randomized order: a local 3D printing startup whose founder was looking to gauge their interest in making an early investment (the angel investing option) and a local commercial real estate project. The choice of the startup is the main outcome variable, intended to closely proxy entry into angel investment.

Participants were told their startup was funded either by personal funds and two VC funds (Condition 1) or by a VC fund and an individual investor (Conditions 2–5). Conditions 2–5 mirror entrepreneurs who received both VC and angel investment in the archival sample. The manipulation focused on the presence and nature of angel investment while holding constant the presence of VC funding.

Participants were told their startup was funded by a VC fund and an individual investor who had met them at an alumni association meeting for an educational institution the respondent attended. This condition explores Hypothesis 2a in the experiment.

Participants were told their startup was funded by a VC fund and an individual investor who had previously been employed at the same company, but in different cities. This condition explores Hypothesis 2b in the experiment.

Participants were told their startup was funded by a VC fund and an individual investor whom they had met through the local business community. This condition explores Hypothesis 2c in the experiment.

Participants rated their likelihood of investing in a 3D printing startup on a 7-point scale (1 = "definitely will not invest" to 7 = "definitely will invest"). This continuous measure replaced Study 2's dichotomous choice to improve statistical power for mediation analysis and reduce noise from extraneous factors.

In Condition 2 (treatment), participants were told their company had received funding from a VC fund and an individual investor who provided crucial early funding, advice, and mentorship; in Condition 1 (control), participants were told their company had been funded by personal funds and two VC funds.

Participants rated on a scale from 1 = "not at all" to 7 = "completely" the extent to which their decision was a function of (a) "feeling grateful for help I received as a founder" and (b) "a desire to give back to entrepreneurs". The items were designed to capture the emotional experience of gratitude and the broader prosocial motivation it engenders without implying direct reciprocity. The two items were averaged into a composite measure (alpha = 0.777).

Participants rated the extent to which their decision was influenced by (a) "being seen as someone who supports entrepreneurs" and (b) "enhancing my standing among peers". The items were designed to assess community-level perceptions and specific professional relationships that constitute reputation management. The two items were averaged into a composite measure (alpha = 0.674).

As in Study 3, participants rated their likelihood of investing in the 3D printing startup on a 7-point scale, using a continuous measure rather than a binary choice to enhance statistical power and reduce the influence of extraneous factors.

variable_name: Received funding from an embedded angel (same educational institution)
description: In Conditions 2A and 2B, participants were told their successful SaaS business had been funded by an embedded angel investor, specifically one who had attended the same educational institution; in Conditions 1A and 1B, it had been funded by an unrelated angel investor. Educational embeddedness was chosen as a clear and salient form of embeddedness for the experimental setting.

variable_name: Investment opportunity in a founder sharing a school tie
description: Crossing the funding manipulation, participants in Conditions 1B and 2B were presented with an opportunity to invest in a founder with whom they shared a school tie, while participants in Conditions 1A and 2A were presented with an opportunity to invest in an unrelated founder. The design tests whether embeddedness in the original funding relationship influences preferences for embedded investment targets.

Mediation analyses paralleling those in Study 3 were conducted on the gratitude measure to examine the psychological mechanisms underlying the interaction effect; gratitude significantly mediated the effect of receiving embedded funding on the likelihood of investing in an embedded founder (indirect effect = 0.263, p < .001).

Mediation analyses paralleling those in Study 3 were conducted on the reputation measure; reputation concerns did not mediate the effect of receiving embedded funding on the likelihood of investing in an embedded founder (indirect effect = -0.003, bootstrapped 95% CI: [-0.033, 0.025]).

A six-item, 7-point scale capturing a predisposition to bring people together in collaboration, including introducing disconnected others and forging stronger ties between others who may already have ties with one another. The scale had a reliability (Cronbach alpha) of .85 in a pretest and .88 in the final study; a confirmatory factor analysis showed minimal interscale correlation with individualism-collectivism, conflict-handling styles, proactive personality, and the Big Five dimensions.

An egocentric network measure based on a single list of alters generated from name-generator questions about different relations, with a tie recorded between alters if the respondent indicated any relationship other than 'prefer to avoid this person'. Density is the ratio of existing ties between those in a subject's network out of all possible ties, and it reflects the level of cohesion necessary for coordinated action; it was calculated in UCINET. Higher density means fewer structural holes.
scale: ratio of existing ties to all possible ties

description: Burt's (1992) measure of constraint, capturing the extent of an individual's dependence on the others in his or her network as well as his or her access to novel, non-redundant information; low constraint corresponds with larger numbers of structural holes. It is a function of the existence of direct ties between ego and alter and of the extent to which the alter has other ties in ego's network, and it was calculated in UCINET. Higher constraint means fewer structural holes.

A single self-report item emphasizing familiarity with the respondent's area of functional expertise: 'In general, how comfortable are you addressing the more advanced technical issues associated with the following areas?' asked for each of ten technical areas, with the measure referring only to the response for the area in which the respondent was based (1 = 'not comfortable at all' and 7 = 'very comfortable').
scale: 1 = not comfortable at all to 7 = very comfortable

description: The respondent's answer to 'In general, how easy would it be for you to get candid, behind-the-scenes input regarding G5 issues concerning the following areas?' asked for each of ten technical areas (1 = 'not comfortable at all' and 7 = 'very comfortable'). The ten responses formed a social knowledge scale with a reliability (Cronbach alpha) of .88.
scale: 1 = not comfortable at all to 7 = very comfortable

description: The number of years employed by NewCar, used as a measure of accumulated technical and social knowledge reflecting familiarity with the organization's culture and language, insight into other individuals' and groups' preferences, and instincts about how to advocate for innovation.

A binary education measure: those with a master's degree in an engineering or engineering-related area received a 1 and all others a 0. Advanced degrees also conferred an enhanced status beyond the associated formal knowledge at NewCar.

Respondents evaluated their level of involvement in each of the 73 innovations using Ibarra's scale of five categories, from initiator to knowing nothing about the innovation. A respondent's innovation involvement reflected the highest level of involvement reported across all 73 innovations, so that an individual reporting being an initiator for one or more innovations was designated an initiator. The coding was reversed so that factors contributing to innovation involvement would display a positive regression coefficient; self-reports of initiator and major role were reviewed and changed as appropriate using evaluations by 49 experts.
scale: five ordered categories (initiator, major role, minor role, know about the innovation, did not know anything about the innovation)

description: Density of ties among a focal inventor's collaborators, calculated as the unique number of pairwise collaborations between a focal inventor's collaborators that did not include the focal inventor, divided by the total possible pairwise collaborations. The data show that most individuals broker their collaborative relationships: 67 percent of the observations indicate no relationships between the other collaborators. Low density indicates brokerage.

Density measure of the ties between each of the others in the focal inventor's network. Calculated as the unique number of pairwise collaborations between a focal inventor's collaborators that did not include the focal inventor, divided by the total possible pairwise collaborations; includes all unique pairwise relationships from collaborators' patents that did not include the focal inventor in the three-year time period. The data show that most individuals broker their collaborative relationships: 67 percent of the observations indicate no relationships between the other collaborators.

Number of new subclass pairs within each of a focal inventor's patents. The measure steps through subclass assignments and identifies the first appearance of a previously uncombined pair of subclasses; this indicator is summed for all patents during each three-year window of the focal inventor's career.

Counts how many times other inventors used the focal inventor's new combinations. When a new combination is used twice within a single three-year window, only the first use is counted as a new combination and the second adds to the uses variable.
Natural log of the number of unique subclasses in which the focal inventor had worked prior to the current time period.
Natural log of the number of unique subclasses in which the focal inventor's collaborators had worked prior to the current time period.
Natural log of the number of assignees that appear in the inventor's patents over the three-year time period; indicates whether the inventor has worked in multiple firms over the time period.
Natural log of the number of external ties to a focal inventor's collaborators. External ties are ties to the focal inventor's collaborators who do not have a direct tie to the focal inventor.

Main experimental treatment contrasting the two organizational designs imposed on the subject as central coordinating agent. In the price-directed scheme prices for assignable square feet and a student-faculty surcharge were the variables under the control of the president; in the resource-directed scheme the president assigned to each college its square footage allocation and a student-faculty ratio designation.

Treatment with two levels of decision time pressure. Low time pressure meant the subjects had a maximum of five minute to make a decision in each iteration. The high time pressure treatment started each subject with four minutes maximum decision time and reduced it by 20 seconds in each iteration until a minimum of two minutes.

variable_name: overall contribution of the final proposal
description: Criterion variable for the analysis of variance, the overall contribution of the final proposal for each subject. For price-directive subjects it was the contribution of the final, special iteration, averaged over the subjects in a given cell of the design; for resource-directive subjects it was the contribution of the best feasible proposal, again averaged over the subjects in a given cell.

Application of the Dantzig-Wolfe decomposition procedure to the same problem, used as a benchmark for human subject performance. It yielded high negative payoff for the zero-th and first two iterations, and its performance for subsequent iterations is compared with the average of all the resource-directive subjects for each iteration.

Dummy variable equal to 1 if the team received the information in that period and 0 otherwise. Each team received the four market research studies in the first two periods so that they could familiarize themselves with their content; for the next seven periods teams were randomly chosen to receive the information, subject to the constraint that across all four industries each team received the information the same number of times. In any period either one, three or five teams received the information.

Net marketing contribution of team i in period j. In MARKSTRAT the marketing department is a profit center and net marketing contribution refers to cumulative gross contribution across all brands (revenues minus cost of goods sold minus brand specific inventory holding and advertising costs) minus R&D, sales force and marketing research expenses.

The number of competitors in team i's industry who received the information in period j (possible values = 0, 1, ..., 4). It is included in the performance equation to capture competitive effects and is also used as further evidence on the information-performance relationship.
The dollars spent on advertising (across all brands) by team i in period j.
The dollars spent on the sales force by team i in period j.
The dollars spent on R&D to develop new products by team i in period j.
The dollars spent on R&D to improve existing products by team i in period j.
The average price charged by team i for the brands it marketed in period j.

The average Euclidean distance between the starting position and final specified position for a firm's brands, indicating the relative amount of repositioning activity undertaken by team i in period j. Firms make these positioning decisions each period even if they do not have access to the perceptual map study.
The number of different brands marketed by team i in period j (max = 5, imposed by the simulation).

variable_name: DECISION (ADVERT, SALESF, NEWRD, IMPRD, PRICE, REPOS, NBRAND)
description: The set of seven marketing-mix decisions each team made in a period: advertising dollars, sales force dollars, new-product R&D dollars, product-improvement R&D dollars, average price, average repositioning distance, and number of brands. Each decision was analyzed in its own regression and each was entered separately as a predictor of net marketing contribution.

Subjects allocated all 400 units over the ten rounds; the decision number chosen in a round is the number of units allocated in that round and any units remaining after the ninth round are automatically allocated in round 10. The reported measure is the observed mean allocation in each round, pooled over the 19th and 20th iterations of the task. Predicted allocations are the earnings-maximizing allocations derived from the first-order conditions.
scale: units of the 400-unit endowment, per round

description: The myopia measure for a session is based on the cumulative distribution of mean units allocated by round. A subject or group is more myopic than another if its cumulative unit distribution is everywhere above the other's across rounds 1 to 10. Myopia orderings are read from plots of the cumulative distributions of mean investment allocations in the 19th and 20th iterations of the four sessions.

variable_name: Session 2 payoff structure (short- and long-term bonus scheme)
description: Earnings consisted of two components: current round earnings and earnings based on the moving average of output of the past 4 rounds; during the first three periods these means were taken over one, two, and three periods respectively. The sum of the two components was multiplied by the round's multiplier. This payoff structure is the laboratory version of Corporation X's existing combined short- and long-term bonus scheme.
time_window: 10-round task, first three rounds use shorter moving averages

description: In the magnifier sessions, output earned in any round was first multiplied by the magnifier and then by the multiplier; multipliers were identical to those used in the other sessions and induced a discount rate of 20%. The magnifier magnifies output earned in later rounds at rate a discounted back to the session's first round. In Session 3 the rate a was set so that output was valued equally across all rounds (a = 0.20), while in Session 4 a was set at 0.08 so that the magnifier does not completely offset the subject's discount rate.
time_window: applied in every round of the 10-round task

variable_name: observed mean allocation path versus predicted allocation path
description: The observed mean allocation path in the 19th and 20th iterations is compared with the allocation predicted by the theory, and the cumulative distribution functions of the hypothesized and empirical populations are compared with the Kolmogorov-Smirnov test. Mean deviations between predicted and observed allocations are reported for each session.

Indicator variable capturing whether a patent came from a single inventor or from a team: it is set to 0 for a patent from a single inventor and 1 for a team of two or more inventors. It is one of two indicators the authors use to capture dimensions of 'lone inventor'.

Indicator capturing whether the patent originated outside the boundaries of any organization (0) or from within an organization (1). Assignee names and parent-subsidiary matching were corrected based on procedures described in Singh (2007).

The number of future citations a patent receives, used as the measure of the impact and ultimately the success of the invention. For comparisons across different technologies the authors use a citation impact measure normalized relative to the average citation impact in the same year-technology class cohort.
Indicator variable set to 1 if and only if a patent is in the top 5% in terms of frequency of future citations received, compared with patents of the same application year and technology class.
Indicator variable set to 1 if and only if a patent receives no citations.

The number of distinct technology classes the inventor or inventors have patented in before the focal patent. The authors assume that knowledge of more technical areas offers a greater diversity of ideas available for recombination or criticism.

For the focal patent, the number of unique inventors that are at a social distance of not more than two from the focal inventor(s), i.e., are either recent collaborators or collaborators' collaborators for one or more of the inventor(s).
time_window: recent collaborations prior to the focal patent

description: Breadth is computed from the technology classifications of the backward citations (prior art) listed in the examiner's search report associated with the inventor's patents, aggregated over the inventor's patents at the inventor-priority year level. Each referenced patent j is distributed over K discrete technological domains, with s_jk being patent j's share of technology classifications in area k; the authors adapt the Herfindahl index so that it rewards recombination at the referenced patent level, using S, the cumulative number of unique classifications attributed to patents in the search report. The index can vary between 0 and 1, with a maximum of 0.90 observed in the data. The printed formulas are partly garbled by the PDF conversion.
time_window: aggregated across each inventor's patents by priority year

description: A set of dummy variables distinguishes three fields of study: science (e.g., physics, chemistry), engineering (e.g., mechanical engineering, process engineering), and other fields (e.g., mathematics, economics). For deeper analysis the science dummy is split into three dummies: physics, chemistry, and other scientific fields. Engineering is the reference group in the regressions.
A dummy variable flags inventors who attained a doctoral degree (1) and those with lower educational degrees (0).

The number of years that have passed since the inventor completed his education. The variable is calculated at the level of the inventor's patents: for each patent, the year in which the inventor obtained his highest degree was subtracted from the priority year of the patent (year of first application).
time_window: measured at each patent's priority year

description: Research ability is proxied by four pieces of survey information: time to complete first baccalaureate degree, Ph.D. program ranking by field of science, whether a scientist received a grant during her doctoral program, and parental educational levels. Time to complete the first bachelor degree is defined as the negative of years spent in completing it (a 4-year degree is coded as 4), so a marginal increase means less time of completion. Ph.D. program ranking comes from the National Research Council's evaluation of Ph.D. program quality, and a marginal increase means a higher ranking of a Ph.D. program.

Survey responses to questions asking scientists to rate the relative importance they placed on nine job characteristics, coded on a four-point scale, one being not important at all to four being very important. Three related measures are used: the nine original variables of job importance, averages of salary and benefits as pecuniary factors and of intellectual challenge, responsibility, and independence as nonpecuniary factors, and factor-analysis predicted values from the Bartlett scoring method.
scale: four-point scale: 1 = not important at all, 3 = very important? The answers were coded on a four-point scale, one being not important at all to four being very important

description: Dummy dependent variable that takes the value of 1 if a scientist conducts basic research and 0 if applied research, defined within each institutional setting from the SDR question about the type of job activity on which the majority of time is spent.

Dummy variable that takes the value of 1 if a scientist is an academic scientist and 0 if an industrial scientist. Respondents who reported that their employer was a four-year college or university, medical school, or university-affiliated research institute are identified as working in academia, whereas respondents who reported their employer as private for profit are identified as working in industry.

Self-reported annualized salary, excluding bonuses, overtime or other additional compensation, deflated by the consumer price index with base year 1995, used as the dependent variable in earnings regressions estimated separately for each career option. The regressions include labor market experience, measured as age minus years of schooling minus six years, with both linear and quadratic terms, and demographic controls.

variable_name: constant term of the earnings equation
description: The constant term from the OLS earnings equation estimated for each career option on labor market experience and its square, compared across career options with p-value tests of equality of coefficients. The authors read these estimated trajectories as showing where earnings start and how they evolve for each career option.

The linear and quadratic coefficients on labor market experience from the same OLS earnings equations, interpreted as the slope of the earnings profile for each career option. Tests of equality of the constant, linear, and quadratic terms of labor experience across pairs of career options are reported, and the estimated earnings trajectories are plotted at sample mean values of all other independent variables.

variable_name: past success in generating implemented ideas
description: Cumulative number of implemented ideas proposed by individual i before day t. The specific date when an idea was implemented is determined from dated update comments posted by Dell administrators, so the measure is based on implementation dates, not submission dates. Log transforms are used because the explanatory variables are highly skewed.

Binary variable where a value of one indicates that individual i proposed an idea in day t that was eventually implemented by Dell (otherwise zero). Observations are included only if individual i proposed an idea not already offered by Dell in day t.

Count of the number of ideas proposed by individual i in day t that are not in the same categories as their prior implemented ideas. Idea categories are used as an objective measure of the extent to which an idea differs from an individual's previous ideas.

Entropy measure over the idea categories, Pj pj ln(pj), where pj is the proportion of others' ideas in category j that individual i commented on before day t. Comment dates were compared with the dates of submitted ideas to construct the measure.

Dummy distinguishing the market origin of the problem solver who provided an idea. It is coded 0 when the idea originates from a target market problem solver and 1 when the idea originates from an analogous market problem solver. A recoded three-level version distinguishes target market solvers (0), solvers from near analogous markets (1), and solvers from far analogous markets (2).
level: idea (nested in problem solver and market)

description: An idea's novelty was measured with two items: the extent to which an idea reflects a truly creative thought and the extent to which the concept is different from products currently available on the target market. The five-point rating scales were merged into a single index, and the averaged scores were standardized by a z-transformation to allow comparison of ideas between markets.
scale: five-point rating scales (1 = very low, 5 = very high), merged and z-transformed

description: An idea's usefulness was measured with two items: the degree of usefulness to solve the problem and the number of users who would find it useful. These items were likewise merged into a single index, and the averaged scores were standardized by a z-transformation to allow comparison of ideas between markets.
scale: five-point rating scales (1 = very low, 5 = very high), merged and z-transformed

description: In study 1, the artificial treatment scores were presented as a range (e.g., 2-5), and the range of scores was always directionally two to three points either slightly above or below the initial evaluation score given by the focal evaluator, so evaluators were exposed to relative feedback. Treatment score valence is a categorical variable taking the value lower treatment scores if the treatment score range is below the evaluator's original score, higher treatment scores if it is above, and neutral treatment scores if it is within the same range as the evaluator's own score. Only the middle scores, between 3 and 6, were completely randomized to both lower and higher scores with respect to the original proposal score.

The difference between the updated score after exposure to the treatment scores and the original score. In study 1, evaluators scored proposals on feasibility, impact, innovation and expertise (1 = worst to 6 = best) and provided an overall scientific merit score (1 = worst, 8 = best); the change is taken on the overall scientific merit score. Score updates were in the direction of the other reviewers' scores more than 99% of the time.

In study 2, the other reviewers' scores were exogenously varied over the entire range of possible scores and constructed as three score ranges, "1-3," "4-6," and "7-9," corresponding to "low," "moderate," and "high" treatment scores, so evaluators were exposed to absolute feedback independent of their own initial score. The categorical variable took the value lower treatment scores if the treatment score range was below the evaluator's original score, higher treatment scores if above, and neutral treatment scores if within the same range.

The difference between the updated score after exposure to the treatment scores and the original score. In study 2, evaluators scored proposals on feasibility, impact, innovation and expertise (1 = worst to 5 = best) and provided an overall scientific merit score (1 = worst, 9 = best); the change is taken on the overall scientific merit score.

variable_name: Newly Hired by Employer w/ Scandal
description: A binary indicator set to one if a staffer changes employers and joins an MC previously implicated in scandal and zero otherwise. The authors use it as the dependent variable in the difference-in-differences estimation and as one outcome of the competing risks hazard model.

variable_name: Newly Hired by Employer w/o Scandal
description: One of the three career outcomes jointly explored in the competing risks hazard model, capturing joining a nonstigmatized employer. It is modeled as a competing event alongside joining a stigmatized employer and leaving the industry.

A binary variable set to one if a staffer is no longer employed as a congressional staffer in the year following the focal year and is not rehired within three years, and zero otherwise. It is used both in the difference-in-differences estimation and as a competing event in the hazard model.
time_window: focal year, with a three-year rehire window

description: For staffers who work for an MC who is implicated in a scandal, Postscandal takes a value of one for all years after the scandal breaks and zero otherwise. It is the independent variable in the difference-in-differences estimation and represents exposure to associative stigma arising from an MC's scandal.
time_window: years after the scandal break date

description: Takes a value of one for staffers associated with MCs involved in personal scandals and zero for staffers associated with MCs involved in professional scandals. The Post x Personal Stigma variable is the interaction term between Personal Stigma and the Postscandal indicator. Scandals are classified into professional and personal categories using GovTrack's scheme, and Personal Stigma and Professional Stigma are mutually exclusive categories.

Measured by asking participants: 'If you have to make a decision at this point, how likely are you to hire this applicant?' Answers were on a 10-point Likert scale (1 = highly unlikely, 10 = highly likely).
scale: 10-point Likert scale (1 = highly unlikely, 10 = highly likely)

description: Measured by asking participants 'If you have to make a decision at this point, how likely are you to accept this job offer?' on a 10-point Likert scale (1 = highly unlikely, 10 = highly likely).
scale: 10-point Likert scale (1 = highly unlikely, 10 = highly likely)

description: Participants responded to the nine-item stigma apprehension scale adapted from Quinn et al. (2006, 2014) and Quinn and Chaudoir (2009) on a seven-point Likert scale (1 = not at all likely, 7 = very likely). Items were presented in a randomized order for each participant (Cronbach alpha = 0.94). The scale contains two subscales: perception of limited opportunity structure (items 3-5, 8, and 9) and worry of devaluation (items 1, 2, 6, and 7).
scale: seven-point Likert scale (1 = not at all likely, 7 = very likely)

description: The same nine items used in Experiment 1, modified to reflect the perspective of the worker, measured on a seven-point Likert scale (Cronbach alpha = 0.97). The nine items were shown in a random order for each participant.

In the personal and professional worker scandal conditions, the perceived accountability/culpability of the worker was measured with two items ('Employees of this firm bear some responsibility for the scandal' and 'It is possible that employees of this firm share in the blame for the scandal') on a 10-point Likert scale (1 = not at all likely, 10 = very likely; Cronbach alpha = 0.87).
scale: 10-point Likert scale (1 = not at all likely, 10 = very likely)

description: In the personal and professional employer scandal conditions, participants rated the perceived accountability of the employees of the hiring firm with the same two items as in Experiment 1 (Cronbach alpha = 0.86).

In the personal and professional worker scandal conditions, the perceived risk of future contamination was measured with two items ('Hiring a job candidate who has worked at this firm could contaminate my firm's reputation' and 'If I hire this applicant, my firm's reputation may suffer by association') on a 10-point Likert scale (1 = not at all likely, 10 = very likely; Cronbach alpha = 0.95).
scale: 10-point Likert scale (1 = not at all likely, 10 = very likely)

description: In the personal and professional employer scandal conditions, participants' perceived risk of future contamination by joining the stigmatized firm was measured by the same two items as in Experiment 1, with the only change in the perspective (Cronbach alpha = 0.96).

Each of the 70 product cases was defined as a success or a failure. Failures were products totally rejected by the market and ceased to exist, or products that failed in market tests and were aborted; successes were products that generated substantial positive financial results. The classification of each patent as a success or failure was obtained by contacting and interviewing the inventors of each patent.

The 127 cases were taken from three books containing data on successes and failures of new products and were classified with the same criteria as in Study 1, which is in line with the books' own criteria; only products that generated substantial positive financial results were included in the books as successes. Four product cases were excluded because of classification ambiguity.

Each product was classified by a group of three judges trained in template identification. The categories used for template classification were components templates, attribute dependency template, and not a template. The average agreement between the judges was high (alpha = 0.89), and the correlation between the two template variables was 0.22.

Cases were classified according to template affiliation by a group of three judges trained in template identification, following the same procedure as in Study 1. The average interjudge agreement in this group was high (alpha = 0.89).

The source variables were classified from the details of each case by judges, using the three-part classification of source variables. Need spotting refers to need identification preceding product-form development; solution spotting refers to a form being identified and a suitable need searched for, or need and solution being identified concurrently.
Coded by judges from the case details as a source of the idea: the idea is based on a decision to innovate and on internal cognitive process rather than on external market stimulus.
Coded by judges from the case details as a source of the idea: the product was developed to follow a market trend in a different class of products.

A project-level determinant judged for each case by a group of three experienced marketers, using the classification summarized in the appendix. Newness to the market is illustrated by shampoo, which was classified as a new but not radically new product.

A project-level determinant judged for each case by a group of three judges, using the classification summarized in the appendix; the first shampoo, introduced by a soap manufacturer, was not very new to the firm.
The level of required technology change was classified into three groups: minor, moderate, and major. This determinant was judged for each case by a group of three engineers.

variable_name: template affiliation and source of idea
description: The early determinants were the idea-based variables, namely template affiliation (attribute dependency and component templates) and the source-of-idea variables (need or solution spotting, mental invention, following a trend). Judges coded each product case on these variables, and they were entered together in the logistic regression predicting product success.

Respondents selected which of four categories—job shop, batch shop, production line, or continuous shop—comes closest to characterizing their dominant processes. Definitions of each category were provided in the questionnaire.

Respondents chose which of several descriptions most typified the production in their plant, ranging from customized products to standard products. This question measured the plant's product plans on the customization axis of the product-process matrix.

Respondents characterized the demand for their primary product line. The authors used this question as a measure of volume and reported the Spearman correlation between process choice (Q1) and volume (Q3).
Respondents rated the overall performance of manufacturing in their plant relative to corporate performance criteria.
Respondents rated the performance of the operations function relative to plants owned by other companies in the same industry.

Plants were classified as on-diagonal if their cross-tabulated process choice (Q1) and product plan (Q2) fell in cells on or immediately adjacent to the main diagonal of the product-process matrix; other cells were off-diagonal. Numbers in boldface in Table 5 represent on-diagonal positions.

Factor score for QUALITY from a maximum likelihood factor analysis with oblique Promax rotation of 13 competitive-priority variables. Four variables dealing with quality level, physical product aspects, conformance to specifications, and customer perceptions of quality loaded on this factor.

Factor score for COST from a maximum likelihood factor analysis with oblique Promax rotation of 13 competitive-priority variables; it is composed of product cost and product price. For this factor a higher score means worse achievement.
Factor score for TIME from a maximum likelihood factor analysis with oblique Promax rotation of 13 competitive-priority variables; it is made up of delivery time and dependability on delivery.
