Factor score for product flexibility (PFLEX) from a maximum likelihood factor analysis with oblique Promax rotation of 13 competitive-priority variables; it corresponds to the ability to customize and respond to the unique needs of customers and primarily captures the customization dimension of product flexibility.

Factor score for development speed (DVSPEED) from a maximum likelihood factor analysis with oblique Promax rotation of 13 competitive-priority variables; it deals with the speed of introducing new products.

Factor score for volume flexibility (VFLEX) from a maximum likelihood factor analysis with oblique Promax rotation of 13 competitive-priority variables; it deals with the ability to adjust capacity rapidly.

variable_name: QUALITY, COST, TIME, PFLEX, DVSPEED, VFLEX
description: Competitive priorities were measured with 13 survey items on the importance and achievement of manufacturing priorities in the plant. A factor analysis reduced them to six priority factor scores: quality, cost, time, product flexibility, development speed and volume flexibility.

variable_name: Centrality scores (referral, joint program, formal communication, informal communication networks)
description: Centrality scores were computed with the Diagraph Analysis Program developed by Laumann. The program first calculates a reachability matrix based on binary data, where reachability is the minimum number of links required for one organization to reach another, representing both direct and indirect ties. Centrality was measured as an organization's distance from the centroid of the reachability matrix and standardized for each county.

Respondents were asked to list organizations to which their organization commonly sent adult disadvantaged clients and to indicate the approximate number of clients sent to each organization; referrals received were not measured. Centrality in this referral network was computed as the organization's distance from the centroid of the reachability matrix and standardized for each county.

Respondents were asked to list organizations that were very influential in shaping community policies related to the provision of employment and training services to disadvantaged adults. The number of nominations received by each organization was counted.

Respondents were asked to list organizations with which they had jointly planned and implemented any specific programs or activities during the past three years. Centrality in this joint program network was computed as the organization's distance from the centroid of the reachability matrix and standardized for each county.

Respondents were asked to list organizations from whom they regularly received newsletters, annual reports, or other information. The most central organization was the one whose formal communications were more widely received by other organizations; centrality was computed as distance from the centroid of the reachability matrix and standardized for each county.

Respondents were asked to indicate those organizations for which they had personally met with the administrative director during the last year to discuss the activities of their respective organizations. Centrality in this informal communication network was computed as distance from the centroid of the reachability matrix and standardized for each county.

Respondents were asked if their organization had a board of directors or advisory council. The variable was used as a strategy indicator in the regressions of referral centrality and attributed influence.

Measured through calls to regional, state, and federal administrators as well as calls to all local agencies. The measure was the number of problems of the typical client served by an agency: a client with a single problem was assumed to be the least difficult to serve, clients having two or three problems were viewed as moderately difficult, and clients with more than three problems were viewed as most difficult.

Ascertained through telephone calls to federal, state, and regional administrators and calls to all local agencies. The measure was binary: state or federally administered versus locally administered agencies.
Staff size was determined through the interviews with agency administrators. The authors report that the organizations in the sample had small staffs, with a mean staff size of about 23.

Extent of services was determined through review of agency documents and phone calls to local administrators. Fifteen distinct services were identified, and the number offered by each organization was used as a measure of size.

These data were compiled by the interviewers using the following scale: 6 = same office or building; 5 = within two blocks; 4 = same side of city (8-15 blocks); 3 = across town; 2 = different city, but same county; 1 = in next county. A score for each organization was computed by calculating the organization's mean distance to all other organizations in the sample site.

Factor analysis of 12 interview items yielded three types of ideologies: blaming the client, blaming the environment, and blaming the system. Items with loadings above .40 were weighted with factor weights, standardized, and summed to create the three scores. The final measure was computed by taking the mean difference between each organization and each other organization in the network for each ideological score, and these mean differences were then added together; the scale was inverted so that a larger value represented greater ideological conformity.

Determined from a review of federal and state legislation and calls to federal, state, and regional administrators; the measure included mandates resulting from court orders, as in the case of probation officers. The number of organizations mandated to work with each focal organization was computed.

Respondents were asked to list organizations with which they had ties with one or more members and to select among the following reasons: grew up with the person, attended the same college or similar institution, or had common membership in a fraternal organization. These three items indicated informal ties.

Respondents were asked to list organizations with which they had ties with one or more members and to indicate whether they had previously worked in an organization with the other person. This fourth item indicated work ties.

Event study estimate of the extent to which the health care portfolio's observed stock returns differed from the expected, or normal, returns based on the portfolio's historical relationship with the general market. Returns were examined for the day after each legislative event, the day on which the event was announced in the press. A single portfolio of health care firms was used for each law.

Each firm's abnormal return was cumulated over a 12-day window, from 10 days before through 1 day after an event, which allows for the possibility that information leaked out prior to the public announcement. It was standardized to control for heteroskedasticity and used as the dependent variable in the cross-sectional regression of firm characteristics.
time_window: 12-day window (10 days before through 1 day after the event)

description: The percentage change in a firm's net income over the two years preceding the relevant legislation. It entered the cross-sectional regression as an independent variable, with a negative coefficient expected.
time_window: two years preceding the relevant legislation

description: The ratio of total liabilities to total assets. It entered the cross-sectional regression as an independent variable, with a negative coefficient expected.
A firm's net sales, used as the measure of firm size. It entered the cross-sectional regression as an independent variable, with a positive coefficient expected.

Bank managers indicated the extent to which they agreed that the bank (1) encouraged bank managers to play helpful and advisory roles with their small business clients, (2) encouraged bank managers to act with significant flexibility in meeting small business client borrowing and other financial needs, (3) focused on improving bank-small firm relationships by selling products that fit a specific client's needs, and (4) attempted to understand the businesses and marketplaces of its small business clients. Responses were on a scale from 1, 'very infrequently,' to 7, 'very frequently.' The variable was constructed from the simple average of its items, and managers' responses were aggregated to one bank-level score for each bank.

Managers rated how much they agreed with three statements about personnel stability in dealing with small business clients. Responses were on a scale from 1, 'strongly disagree,' to 7, 'strongly agree'; the third item ('Employees with direct client interaction are rotated between branches and/or departments on a regular basis') was reverse-coded. The variable was constructed from the simple average of its items.

Customers indicated the extent to which they agreed that they (1) could freely share concerns and problems and know that the bank would be interested in listening, (2) could freely share concerns and problems and know that the bank would respond constructively, (3) shared common business values with the bank, and (4) felt that the bank would act in a fashion consistent with the customers' wishes without prior discussion with the bank. Responses were on a scale from 1, 'very rarely true,' to 7, 'very often true.' The variable was constructed from the simple average of its items; the word 'trust' was avoided in the items.

Subjects indicated the extent to which they were likely within the next year to (1) switch to an alternative bank to service their borrowing needs, (2) switch to an alternative bank for checking and other deposit accounts, (3) move accounts to banks with slightly more attractive interest rates, (4) move accounts to banks with slightly more attractive fees, and (5) shop for banks with more attractive fees and interest rates. Responses were on a scale from 1, 'very unlikely,' to 7, 'very likely.' The variable was constructed from the simple average of its items.

Burt's (1992) efficiency measure, the ratio of non-redundant ties to total ties for a focal team, computed on the network of current ties among production teams. A high value indicates that the focal team's ego network is non-redundant and thus rich in structural holes.

The same efficiency measure applied to the past time window: the ratio of past non-redundant ties to total past ties for each focal team, computed on the co-membership team-by-team matrix built from the seven-year moving window of past ties.
time_window: seven-year window preceding the focal team's production year

description: The accumulation of the past performance (audience) of the focal team's past alters, standardized to correct for its skewed distribution. Only alters linked to the focal team by critical roles in TV production (director, screenplay writers, original author, producer, actors in major starring roles; average of six per team) were selected, and recent successes were weighted more heavily by a decay function based on the age of the past alters' broadcast (1/7, 1/6, and so on).
time_window: seven-year window preceding the focal team's production year

description: The Freeman degree centrality of the focal team in the network of past ties, computed over a seven-year window.
time_window: seven-year window preceding the focal team's production year

description: The valued density of past ties among the members of the focal team, capturing their previous collaborations over the prior seven years. Each prior tie is weighted by the number of previous collaborations. It was computed with the DENSITY procedure in UCINET VI, using a blocking vector to select the members of the focal team, producing a square submatrix of the number of times specialists in the team worked together in the past.
time_window: seven-year window preceding the focal team's production year

description: The content similarity among the past alters of each focal production team, measured from the content analysis of synopses over 11 content variables. The two-mode production-by-content matrix was transformed into a one-mode production-by-production matrix using the similarity procedure of UCINET VI, with similarity measured as the proportion of exact matches.
time_window: seven-year window preceding the focal team's production year

description: The content homogeneity among the focal team's current alters, computed following the same procedure and measures adopted for the past alters but using the network of current (rather than past) ties to identify the alters of a focal TV production team.

The natural log of the audience share that watched the TV show, based on Auditel audience data. Rebroadcast audience numbers were excluded so that all productions had an equal chance of reaching an audience.

Binary variable equal to zero if the contract is a time-and-materials contract and one if it is a fixed-price contract. Of the 93 projects, 55 are time-and-materials and 38 are fixed-price contracts. Contract-specific information was provided by the marketing or business unit manager.

Perceptual variable built from several questionnaire items adapted from earlier work on software development risk (Barki et al. 1993). Confirmatory factor analysis (principal components) was performed on the questionnaire items before use, and the principal component was used in subsequent analysis rather than the individual items, to conserve degrees of freedom.
Project effort, an interval variable that is large compared to the other variables, so the authors standardize it before estimation. It is used to capture project size in terms of effort.

Perceptual measure of the risk that trained personnel will not be available for the project; the human resources variables were adapted from previous research (Gopal et al. 2002). The measure is based on questionnaire items answered by project personnel.

Multiple-item perceptual variable newly created for this study, based on Lacity and Hirschheim (1993) and discussions with project managers; the items showed good validity and reliability. The principal component of the items was used in the analysis.

Multiple-item perceptual variable newly created for this study, based on Lacity and Hirschheim (1993) and discussions with project managers; it showed good validity and reliability. It captures the client's prior experience with offshore outsourcing.
Single-item perceptual measure of the client's reputation, answered on the questionnaire. The authors note that single-item measures are potentially susceptible to measurement problems.

Single-item perceptual measure of the possibility of future business with the client, answered on the questionnaire. The authors note that single-item measures are potentially susceptible to measurement problems.
Client size, an interval variable that is large compared to the other variables, so the authors standardize it before estimation.

Perceptual measure of the importance of the project to the client, gathered through the questionnaire. The authors note that some of their measures are single item and are therefore potentially susceptible to measurement problems.

Single-item measure of the presence of alternative developers in the client country, answered on the questionnaire. The authors note that two single-item measures were used to characterize competition, which could lead to ambiguous results.

Single-item measure of the presence of other vendors in India (the vendor country), answered on the questionnaire. The authors note that two single-item measures were used to characterize competition, which could lead to ambiguous results.

Count of the projects the vendor had already completed for the same client, extracted from company records. The projects in the sample were completed for 32 clients, with the highest number of projects per client being four.

Net profits attributed to each project, calculated by subtracting all travel- and project-related costs from the total revenues attributable to the project. Profits are measured in Indian rupees and were not converted into dollars to avoid confounding the analysis with currency exchange risks and currency fluctuations during the project.

The actual duration of the project (cycle time), included as an ex post development factor. The authors note that although the parties may have expectations of the schedule, actual duration is susceptible to unforeseen circumstances such as rework.

The core number of programmers assigned to the development team during the project. The authors note that the actual number of people working on a project changes over time but the core team personnel remain on the project.

Rather than the number of employees quitting during the project, the authors use two questionnaire items filled out by the project manager to capture the loss of personnel of differing importance in the project team.

A dummy that takes value one if a major's route outsourced to a regional airline in the fall quarter of 2006 (two years before the shock) was still outsourced to the same regional in the fall of 2010 (two years after the shock) and value zero otherwise. The authors say a major outsources a given route to a regional if it outsources at least one of the flights it tickets on the route. Routes that a regional operated in 2010 but not in 2006 are excluded.

The average across all routes flown by a regional for a major in 2006 of the historical average inches of snow on each route, computed at the route's airport for which the value is highest. Following Forbes and Lederman (2009), the historical average of snowfall is taken between 1971 and 2000.

The average across all routes flown by a regional for a major in 2006 of the historical average inches of precipitation on each route, computed at the route's airport for which the value is highest. Following Forbes and Lederman (2009), the historical average of precipitation is taken between 1971 and 1995.

The average across all routes flown by a regional for a major in 2006 of the historical average number of freezing months on each route, computed at the route's airport for which the value is highest. Following Forbes and Lederman (2009), the historical average of the number of freezing months is taken between 1971 and 1995. The authors interpret a higher number of freezing months as indicating clearer skies, so the measure is inversely related to relationship PDV.

Measured, in line with earlier research, as the number of an MNC's subsidiaries in a host country in a year, which captures the MNC's investment level because establishing a subsidiary represents a substantial commitment to the host country. A logarithmic transformation is applied to mitigate the skewness of non-negative integers, so that MNC investment is the logarithmic score of one plus the number of subsidiaries of MNC i in host country j in year t.

Drawn from the Environmental Performance Index (EPI) dataset, which includes each country's Climate Change (PCC) and Environmental Health (HLT) scores based on 22 indicators across five pollution issues. The indicators range from 0 to 100, with higher values indicating lower levels of environmental pollution and better environmental conditions; the variable is therefore measured as 100 minus the average of the PCC and HLT scores for a host country in a year, so that higher values correspond to worse environmental pollution.
Measured as the ratio of total enrollment in tertiary education to the population of the corresponding age group in each country-year, using World Bank data.
Measured as the annual volume of goods transported by railway, calculated in metric tons times kilometers traveled per year, using data collected from the World Bank.

Following selection criteria used in prior research, which often classifies labor-intensive industries as those with low value added per employee, the authors code labor-intensive industries as 1 if the MNC operates in the food, textile, apparel, lumber, furniture, leather, retail, or service industries, and 0 otherwise. The main effect is not time-varying and is omitted in the models.
Following prior research, the authors classify consumer goods industries based on four-digit SIC codes. The main effect is not time-varying and is omitted in the models.

Percentage of total annual sales that firms report paying in informal payments to public officials 'to get things done'. The question is asked with indirect framing ('firms like yours') and placed late in the survey to reduce self-censoring bias. In some specifications bribes enter log-transformed and lagged values of bribes are used.
time_window: survey year (contemporaneous); lagged values used in mechanism tests

description: Money spent for the purchase of machinery and equipment, log transformed. It is the dependent variable in the baseline investment-bribe regression (Equation 1).

A dummy variable that takes the value of 1 if access to finance is a major or a very severe obstacle for a firm. It is interacted with bribes to test Mechanism 1, and the interaction is instrumented with the financial constraint dummy interacted with the instrument for bribes.
scale: dummy (1 = major or very severe obstacle)

description: The total monetary value of a firm's direct exports, log transformed, used as a proxy for firm efficiency. The authors use direct rather than indirect exports because direct exporting capability is a better proxy for efficiency, and they use the monetary value rather than exports as a percentage of sales to avoid a spurious correlation through the common denominator.

A dummy variable that takes the value of 1 if a firm has an internationally recognized quality certification such as ISO and HACCP. Obtaining such certificates requires maintaining consistent quality for an extended period and they cannot generally be obtained through bribery because they are not issued by local officials, so they indicate a longer-term orientation.

The percentage of temporary employees (employees with fixed-term contracts) over total employees. The authors assume that, other things being equal, a greater share of employees with temporary contracts is associated with a short-term firm orientation.

Integrationt is a dummy variable that indicates the time periods after the integration. It takes the value of 1 for periods after the Bottler was fully acquired by the concentrate producer and 0 before.
NonCSDs is a dummy variable that indicates whether the SKU is a NonCSD product. It takes the value of 1 for noncarbonated soft drinks and 0 for carbonated soft drinks.

A dummy variable that takes the value of 1 if SKU s experiences at least one stockout at DC i in period t, and is 0 otherwise. A stockout occurs when a DC cannot deliver an entire order to a given retail outlet; the weekly data were aggregated to the four-week period level.

Inventory (in days of sales) of SKU s carried by DC i in period t. Inventory data are available only at the period level, each period containing four weeks, and the variable is measured at the beginning of each period in some specifications.
time_window: period t (four weeks); beginning of the period in later specifications

description: The ratio between actual and forecasted sales, also called the AF ratio. It reflects the bias in sales forecasts; an average AF ratio of 1.01 means DCs forecast about 99 percent of actual sales.
The standard deviation in weekly AF ratios; it reflects the noise in sales forecasts.

variable_name: Simple promotion, promotion and transfer, and simple transfer dummies
description: Dummy variables code internal entry into the job into three categories: simple promotions (not accompanied by transfers), simple transfers (not accompanied by promotions), and combined promotions and transfers (both promotion and transfer occur during the same year). Entering a job by external hiring is the excluded category in the analyses, verified against the hire date provided by the firm. Promotions are identified by a change in rank from one year to the next, and transfers are moves across divisions, departments, or groups, restricted to transitions accompanied by fewer than 10 percent of the source unit's workers and fewer than 10 percent of the destination unit's workers.

Based on a 1-5 scale that assesses whether workers hit their performance targets for the year: 1 = 'Objectives significantly exceeded,' 3 = 'Objectives met,' and 5 = 'Objectives not met.' Around 9 percent of ratings are a 1, 56 percent are a 2, 34 percent are a 3, 2 percent are a 4, and .03 percent are a 5. The scale was reversed so that higher values indicate better performance.
time_window: annual evaluation; most recent evaluation in each job year

description: Assesses a worker's skills relative to the requirements of the job on a 1-5 scale, with 10 percent of workers being awarded a 1 (the highest rating), 50 percent receiving a 2, 37 percent receiving a 3, 2 percent receiving a 4, and .05 percent receiving a 5. The scale was reversed so that higher values indicate better performance.
time_window: annual evaluation; most recent evaluation in each job year

description: A forced ranking used to determine compensation and other personnel decisions and intended to reflect both performance and overall value to the organization; groups of managers rated many workers in the same rank to develop these rankings. The ranking splits workers into the top 10 percent, the next 20 percent, the next 60 percent (in 2009, this segment was itself split into a higher 40 percent and a lower 20 percent), and the bottom 10 percent. It was converted into a 6-point scale on which the 60-percent category corresponded to a 4 and the divided category in 2009 represented a 3 and a 5; the scale was reversed so that higher values indicate better performance.
time_window: annual evaluation; most recent evaluation in each job year

description: Calculated using workers' ages; workers were assumed to have been working since age 18 if they had no degree, with 4 years added to this age for a Bachelor's degree, 2 years for a Master's, and 4 for a Ph.D. In the very few cases in which this resulted in negative experience, it was reset to zero.

variable_name: Highest Bachelor's, Highest Master's, Highest Ph.D.
description: Dummy variables for the highest degree that a worker possessed (Bachelor's, Master's or Ph.D.), created from the academic degrees recorded in the original dataset. Education data were missing for around 3,300 of the 15,000 workers originally in the data, and workers who lacked education data were dropped from the analysis.
The logarithm of salary, one of the two components of employee pay. The logarithm was used because the pay components are highly skewed.

The logarithm of the annual bonus, which was based on both individual and firm performance and represented 38 percent of pay on average, rising as high as 98 percent. When individuals received a zero bonus, a bonus of one dollar was substituted in order to calculate a log value.

The logarithm of total compensation, analysed alongside the salary and bonus components separately. The authors note that the number of days in the year since the worker was hired and whether he or she was terminated during the year were controlled for because workers at the firm less than a year would likely receive a lower bonus.

Promotions across ranks are identified by a change in rank from one year to the next, and almost always occurred once a year as part of the annual personnel process. Promotion is modelled as an event in Cox event history models in which the time an individual is in a specific job is a unique case during which the worker remains at risk of promotion, with exits and transfers treated as competing risks and censored. Observations not at risk of promotion, in the top two ranks or in the final year of the data, were dropped.

Exits coded by the firm as 'Croesus Initiated'; from 2006 onward all exits were coded as 'Employee Initiated,' 'Croesus Initiated,' or 'Neutral', so the exit analyses were restricted to years after 2005 and the 9 neutral exits were omitted. Of 10,952 person-years analyzed, 1,135 ended in involuntary exit. The exit analyses used performance data from the year prior to termination because workers did not receive performance rankings in the year of their termination, and included dummies for division but not department.

Exits coded by the firm as 'Employee Initiated'; the exit analyses were restricted to years after 2005 because of problems with the firm's coding in prior years. Of 10,952 person-years analyzed, 1,118 ended in voluntary exit. The authors reran the analyses dropping the roughly 25 percent of voluntary exits that occurred because of dissatisfaction with career development or promotion opportunities, as these may reflect workers being counselled to leave, and found the same results.

The number of Democratic managers over the total number of Republican and Democratic managers, calculated by firm-year. Independents and third-party registered managers were ignored in the numerator and denominator. For 2022 managers were classified according to their current registration, and for prior years partisanship was assumed stable unless L2 reported a change in voter registration or that a manager voted in the other party's primary, in which case the party assignment was switched. Firm-years for which fewer than five managers could be identified were dropped.

The inflation-adjusted log of reported base pay for the subset of Glassdoor pay reports that reported their pay hourly. Tips and bonuses are excluded. Only hourly workers are included in the main analyses, and pay reports for occupations in which more than 80 percent of Glassdoor reports were salaried were dropped.

Hourly, monthly, and salaried pay reports were combined, all converted to annual-equivalent pay (assuming hourly workers worked 40 hours per week), and weighted by Occupational Employment and Wage Statistics national occupation-industry shares to approximate the overall U.S. earnings distribution. Unconditional quantile regression was then estimated at the 5th to 95th percentiles in decile increments, with bootstrapped standard errors.
scale: percentile of the annual-equivalent earnings distribution (5th-95th)

description: Workers' gender as reported by Glassdoor users, interacted with manager partisanship and all controls to test whether the Democratic pay premium is larger for women. Glassdoor asked users to indicate their gender upon signing up until 2020, so this model drops subsequent years.

An indicator variable coded 1 for blue-collar workers, defined as 2-digit SOC codes 47 to 53 inclusive, which includes manufacturing, transportation, construction, and maintenance/repair occupations; all other occupations were coded as service/administrative. The indicator was interacted with manager partisanship and all controls.

A binary variable for whether a pay report is at exactly $15 per hour, regressed on manager partisanship with firm-level controls and occupation-industry-metro area-year fixed effects. The authors also compared, separately for Democratic- and Republican-run firms, the share of pay reports falling within each dollar bin, subtracting the Republican value from the Democratic value.

A measure coded 1 if the state in which a worker was employed had increased its minimum wage by more than 50 cents the previous year, interacted with Share of managers Democratic and the control variables. Because some metro areas cross state boundaries, state fixed effects were substituted for metro area fixed effects in this model.

Managers were differentiated by location and position. Headquarters metro area was identified by a scale giving equal weight to the average pay of salaried workers, the share of total Glassdoor pay reports made by senior managers, and the average seniority of managers identified via LinkedIn, assigning as headquarters the metro area with the highest score. Revelio's position seniority scale, built from job titles, age, and employment history, was dichotomized at the median to separate senior managers. Human resource and operations managers were identified by cross-walking Revelio's occupational recode into Census occupations.

variable_name: Same party / Different party / No party
description: A three-category variable describing the relative partisanship of manager and employee in the experiment: Same party means both identify with the same political party, Different party means they identify with different political parties, and No party means the employee's résumé does not reveal partisanship. Partisanship of the hypothetical employee was randomized through volunteering at a partisan-coded (Young Democrats, Young Republicans) or nonpartisan campus organization, and each respondent evaluated ten résumés, four partisan and six nonpartisan.

An indicator variable coded 1 if the manager assigned the hypothetical employee to the high-wage position, the senior associate position paid $16 per hour, rather than the junior associate position paid $13 per hour.

Dependent variable equal to one if firm i chooses location j and zero otherwise. Each transaction is modeled as a choice among the 136 economic areas that received at least one entrant between 1985 and 1994, out of the 171 BEA economic areas (35 were never chosen).

Dummy equal to one if the economic area produced at least one patent in the focal industry and time period and zero otherwise. Patent stocks were calculated with three-, five- and seven-year windows preceding the focal year; the three-year window is used in the reported models.
time_window: three-year window preceding the focal year

description: Dummies indicating whether the economic area had at least one academic patent in the focal industry and period, refined into a low dummy (nonzero but below the industry average) and a high dummy (above the average); zero academic patents is the omitted base category.
time_window: three-year window preceding the focal year

description: Dummies indicating whether the economic area had at least one industry patent in the focal industry and period, refined into a low dummy (nonzero but below the industry average) and a high dummy (above the average); zero industry patents is the omitted base category.
time_window: three-year window preceding the focal year

description: Dummies indicating whether the economic area had at least one government patent in the focal industry and period, refined into a low dummy (nonzero but below the industry average) and a high dummy (above the average); zero government patents is the omitted base category.
time_window: three-year window preceding the focal year

description: Firm R&D intensity, measured as R&D spending scaled by sales, taken from Worldscope. Each firm's R&D intensity for a given year is compared to that year's average R&D intensity of all U.S. firms in the same four-digit industry, drawn from Compustat. Firms above the industry median are leaders and firms at or below the median are laggards.

Indicator that equals one when both the focal founder and one of the Inniskillin founders reported the presence of a friendship tie prior to founding. Founders were shown an alphabetized roster of all 111 wineries that ever operated commercially within Ontario and asked to identify the wineries at which someone on their founding team had at least one prefounding professional friend; 28 founders reported a professional friend at Inniskillin and 17 of those ties were reciprocated by an Inniskillin founder.

The average real price of the ice wines listed by Vintages for each producer in each year. The price charged for each 375 ml bottle is discounted to its 2002 equivalent using the Canadian consumer price index; wineries submit bids to the Vintages program including the price they expect to charge, and minor price adjustments may be negotiated.

Driving distance from the focal winery to Inniskillin, determined with Google Maps and recorded in hundreds of kilometers. The average driving distance between any two Niagara wineries is just 26 kilometers and the maximum distance is 56 kilometers.
An indicator equal to one if the chairperson of the securities company for which the focal analyst works in the focal year had any SDY experience, and zero otherwise.

The absolute forecast error of each earnings forecast made by securities analyst i in report r, issued in year t, for firm j's earnings in future fiscal year f is computed. The measure is the negative of the difference between this absolute error and the average absolute forecast error across all analysts covering firm j in year f, divided by that average. Higher values indicate greater accuracy.
time_window: report issuance year t, forecasting fiscal years t, t+1, and t+2

description: The number of site visits conducted by the focal securities analyst to the focal covered listed firm during the focal year. Ln(1 + Site_Visits) is the natural logarithm of one plus this count.

An indicator equal to one for visiting analysts who attended a focal site visit and zero for nonvisiting analysts who did not visit the same firm during the period from six months before to one month after the focal site visit. It is used in the difference-in-differences analysis of the effect of site visits on forecast accuracy.
time_window: six months before to one month after the focal site visit

description: A dummy variable indicating whether any profile-interview article published about the focal chairperson in a given year contained any of ten keywords semantically related to stronger work ethics in the face of adversity, generated using WANTWORDS and searched in WiseSearch.

A variable that takes a value of one if startup i engages in at least one public activity with external repositories on GitHub during the period observed, and zero otherwise. External repositories are those created and controlled by other organizations, which the focal organization can only alter by requesting changes to the organization that created the code or by forking and then altering the code.

The dependent variable is an indicator that becomes one starting from the quarter t when startup i, belonging to observation group g, raises a first financing round. The analysis focuses on a startup's first round as a fundamental funding milestone, and the analyses are conducted at the quarter level.

A measure of whether a startup will have launched a product by quarter t, estimated with the same difference-in-differences specification used for funding. Products are taken from Product Hunt, and because Product Hunt only started in 2014 the sample is restricted to startups founded after 2011.

An indicator for whether the combination of a startup's industry group keywords at the startup's founding year is relatively new, defined as less than three years having passed since a keyword combination first appeared on Crunchbase.

A measure that counts the number of startups active in a given year-quarter with the same industry group keywords as the focal one. The market is considered competitive if the number of startups possessing the same technology keyword combination is greater than the 90th percentile.

An indicator of whether a startup engaged with an internal repository, which it directly controls. Internal repositories are defined as those that originate from and are held by the focal firm, which created them and can determine what happens to the original source code.

Measured with Kirton's (1976) adaption–innovation inventory; the Italian version of the scale is composed of 33 items that participants rate from 1 (very hard) to 4 (very easy). High values indicate innovators while low values indicate adaptors, and absolute scores are used. Collected in a separate mini-data wave prior to the treatment.
scale: theoretical values range from 33 to 132; observed range 45 to 95
time_window: Time 1′ (before Time 2, prior to the treatment)

description: Burt's (1992) constraint measure, where higher values indicate fewer bridging relations across structural holes. It is calculated on the valued version of the information-exchange networks at each time point, which captures weaker, nascent relationships created after the intervention, and its natural logarithm is used in the analyses following Burt (1992, 2004). The main models use the post-treatment measures at Times 3 and 4.
time_window: Times 3 and 4 (post-treatment); also measured at Times 1 and 2 (pre-treatment)

description: Supervisors rated their subordinates' innovative performance using the innovation dimension of the performance scale developed by Welbourne, Johnson, and Erez (1998); the scale was translated into Italian and back-translated. The measure is the average of all the items of the scale's innovation dimension, and ratings were demeaned at the supervisor level to account for supervisor-level heterogeneity. The main models use the post-treatment measures at Times 3 and 4.

A binary variable that took the value 1 if an employee participated in the treatment and 0 otherwise. Employees were assigned to treatment versus control using a disproportionate stratified random assignment at the department level; 44 employees took part in the treatment.
time_window: one day of executive education during the observation period

description: Indicates whether a hospital acquisition occurred in 2006 in the physician's or dyad's three-digit zip code. The authors use the term acquisition rather than M&A because among the 59 events identified, 56 were acquisitions and only three were mergers; studying acquisitions at the level of the three-digit zip code addresses the potential endogeneity of physician and patient sorting based on acquisitions.

Coded 1 if a dyad had at least six shared patients by the end of the study period (2007) but had no shared patients during the first period of the study, and 0 if the dyad did not share any patients during the observation period. For each tie that formed in 2007, three unformed dyads were sampled from the same three-digit zip code area, with sampling probabilities weighted by the number of shared contacts each unrealized dyad had at the start of the period and sampling weights adjusted for unrealized ties' probability of inclusion.

A binary variable coded 1 for the continuation of a relationship that existed at the beginning of the study and 0 for its dissolution at the end of the observation period. Estimated with logistic regressions over all active dyads in 2005.

A continuous measure of the number of patients a dyad shared in a given year, used to capture both the persistence and intensity of relationships. Estimated with quasi-maximum likelihood (QML) Poisson models.

variable_name: gender (all women, all men, mixed gender)
description: Physician gender is recorded in the prescription database and measured categorically. In physician-level analyses the variable indicates whether a physician is a woman or a man; in dyadic analyses gender is categorized as all-women, all-men, or mixed-gender.

Constructed as the sum of patients an individual physician shares with all other prescribers in their network in 2007. For physicians who shared patients in 2005 but not in 2007, the authors performed zero imputation. The variable captures a physician's total volume of network-based resources.

Adopted from Rajkumar et al.'s (2022) methodology. The printed formula is garbled; per the text, Mij is the number of shared connections and Ci and Cj are the total number of direct connections of physicians i and j. The authors use the term tie embeddedness to distinguish it from traditional measures of tie strength that reflect relational intensity, such as frequency, duration, or emotional closeness.

Count of the total number of ties that persisted with same-gender contacts between 2005 and 2007. The authors depart from Vissa and Bhagavatula (2012) by not normalizing network dynamic variables by original network size, because physicians in this archival sample can add more contacts than their initial network size and network sizes are not strictly controlled.

Number of same-gender relationships initiated in 2007. Included simultaneously with the maintenance measures in models of total shared patients to capture the absolute changes in physicians' networks resulting from network dynamics of formation and maintenance.
Count of the total number of ties that persisted with different-gender contacts between 2005 and 2007.
Number of different-gender relationships initiated in 2007.

Calculated for each individual-year as the sum of squared shares of all inventions in each applied patent class up to each year t. Patent classes are defined at the two-digit level of the IPC, and the main category is used for patents spanning more than one category. The variable can range from close to 0 to 1, with higher values indicating a greater level of specialization, and it is not lagged in the main analyses.
time_window: cumulative up to each year t

variable_name: Specialization at the time of managerial promotion
description: Captured as the specialization measured one year prior to the year of managerial promotion, for all subsequent job spells. This measure represents the portfolio of experience acquired while working as a scientist, prior to entering management.
time_window: one year prior to the year of managerial promotion

description: Coded as 1 if the individual experienced any upward change in rank in the subsequent year and 0 otherwise. Promotions during moves between firms as well as within firms are included. Tested in the subsample of job spells within the scientific ranks, excluding observations with the highest scientific rank.

variable_name: Transition to the first managerial job
description: Coded as 1 if the individual moved into a managerial job in the subsequent year, and it is the first managerial job they took; 0 otherwise. Individual-year observations that follow a transition into management are not used for this analysis.

Coded as 1 if the individual experienced any upward change in rank in the subsequent year and 0 otherwise, estimated within the subsample of observations that have already attained managerial status, with observations at the highest rank (rank of 11) removed.

Continuous measure of the concentration of destination jobs that people are promoted into out of the focal source job, calculated with an entropy calculation with the opposite sign to entropy as it reflects a lack of diversity in destination roles. The formula is given as the sum over destination jobs of (m_ij/m_i) ln (m_ij/m_i), where m_i is the total number of promotions out of source job i in all years, m_ij is the total number of promotions into destination job j from source job i in all years, and n is the number of unique destination jobs that source job i feeds into. The measure is time-invariant, based on all promotions during the period, and is standardized (z-scored) by subtracting the sample mean and dividing by the sample standard deviation.

Measured from job descriptions in BigCo's job catalog. Common stop words were removed and words transformed into their standardized, stemmed form; the distribution of each word across different job descriptions was calculated using an entropy calculation; word-level entropy scores were averaged across all words appearing in a job's description. A job with narrow task content is described with words that appear in few other job descriptions. The variable is standardized so that a one unit increase translates to a one standard deviation increase in within-sample task content breadth.
Measured as the average logged number of people within each of the 20 functions across years.

Calculated on a yearly basis as the entropy of the distribution of employees within each job title across the roughly 50 business units. A high value means a job is widely distributed among a large number of business units, while a low value means a job is narrowly distributed among a small number of business units. The measure is standardized.
Measured as the diversity of roles that people entering the focal source job are promoted from, using an entropy measure.

For a given promotion out of source job i into destination job j, the proportion of all promotions out of source job i during the entire observation period that ended up in destination job j. Typicality of 1.0 means that all promotions from source job i went to destination job j; typicality of 0.2 means that moves from i to j account for only 20% of promotions from source job i.

Dependent variable in the discrete-time event history analysis, taking the value of 0 when an employee remains in the job and 1 if they are promoted out of it; all other forms of mobility (exit out of the firm, lateral mobility, or demotion) are treated as censored observations. The outcome is measured at time t + 1 with all independent variables measured at time t.

For each communicating dyad, the improbability that i and j would communicate, built from matrices giving the cumulative proportion of e-mail that members of group x exchange with members of group y for business unit, job function, office, and salary band, combined in a Cobb-Douglas form subtracted from one with exponents weighting the four boundaries. At the individual level, Improbi is the e-mail-volume-weighted average of this dyadic improbability across all of actor i's communication partners. It assumes its greatest value when a dyad's group membership profile makes its members least likely to communicate; the measure is bounded between 0 and 1.

Burt's structural constraint, an inverse measure of the presence of structural holes in one's network, calculated for each individual with the igraph package in R. Constraint scores were subtracted from their global maximum to invert the distribution and yield a direct measure of structural holes. The measure increases when an individual has many direct contacts and when those contacts are disconnected from one another.

One minus a Herfindahl concentration index calculated across the monthly set of positions held during the prior 77 months, measured separately for business unit, job function and subfunction, and office location. For office location, the index uses the proportion of the 77-month observation period in which the employee was assigned to each of the 289 U.S. offices.
time_window: 77 months prior to the e-mail observation window (2000-2006)

description: A continuous measure of the Euclidean distance between the individual's own career sequence and the medoid of the cluster to which he or she was assigned in a sequence analysis of the job functions occupied in each month of the 77 months co-terminating with the e-mail data. People with large Misfit scores are relatively far from any cluster. Because the distribution has a lower bound of zero, models were estimated on the natural logarithm of Misfit.
time_window: 77 months co-terminating with the e-mail data

description: A binary indicator for the presence (1) or absence (0) of communication between i and j during the three-month e-mail observation window in the fourth quarter of 2006. Only dyads with Improbij above the 75th percentile were included in the analysis, so every dyad was, by construction, separated by significant organizational distance and was at risk of bridging.

variable_name: Length of prior co-employment in the same function
description: The number of months prior to the terminal period in which i and j were both assigned to the same job function (or, separately, subfunction, office location, or business unit). The distribution is truncated at zero and highly skewed, so models were estimated using the natural logarithm of one plus the variable.
time_window: Months prior to the terminal period of the 77-month career record

description: A count of the number of unique individuals who communicated with both i and j in the full sample. The distribution is truncated at zero and highly skewed (nearly two-thirds of dyads had none), so hypothesis 2 was tested on the natural logarithm of one plus Common third parties.

In the two-stage models with the propensity score estimator, hypothesis 3 was tested using a dichotomous covariate defined to be one for any individual with Misfit greater than zero and zero otherwise. The 15-month sequence analysis yielded a highly skewed distribution in which 89 percent of the sample had a Misfit value of zero, mostly because they experienced no mobility.
time_window: 15 months spanning the two panels of e-mail network data

description: The same two brokerage measures used in the primary analysis (Improbi, the e-mail-volume-weighted average improbability of the actor's communication profile, and Structural holes, the inverted structural constraint) were recomputed on the second cross-section of e-mail network data. They serve as the outcomes in the inverse probability of treatment weighted models of the effect of atypical mobility.

The dependent variable is the hazard of mutiny for a particular regiment in a particular time period, with periods of observation measured in days and regiments as the units of analysis. A mutiny is a discrete event that occurs over time and is studied as a hazard that each regiment experiences over time; regiments exit the risk set once they mutiny or are right-censored at the end of the observation window. The authors recorded 142 mutinies out of 208 regiments at different times and places.
time_window: daily spells over a 303-day observation window

variable_name: days since a religious festival (festival clock)
description: A clock set to 0 on the day of a religious festival and incremented by 1 with each passing day, resetting to zero when the next festival occurs. Data on festivals were gathered from past Hindu (Saka, lunisolar) and Islamic (Hijri, lunar) calendars connected to the Gregorian calendar of 1857, and only festivals involving public display of faith, a procession or a gathering, and large numbers of people were included; exclusively private observances and Ekadashis were excluded.

variable_name: log distance from place of recruitment
description: Locations of regiments came from the event history data and places of recruitment mainly from Cardew (1903); names were translated into latitude and longitude, and where a regiment was recruited from a couple of nearby towns or villages the average longitude/latitude was taken. Distances were computed with the spherical distance formula, and the log of distance was used on the logic that the effectiveness of ties of communication and kinship decreases with the log of spatial distance.

A dummy variable set to 1 if a regiment was located within 25 miles of a Christian mission and 0 otherwise; the 25-mile radius takes into account the distance a healthy soldier could walk in a day. Data on missions as of 1857 came from Neill (1984), and the authors consider missions but not stand-alone churches. Among the regiments, 100 out of 208 were located near a Christian mission.
scale: 1 = within 25 miles of a Christian mission, 0 = otherwise

description: The size rank of the station on an ordinal scale ranging from 1 to 3, entered in the models as an inverted variable [4 - (size rank)] so that coefficients are easier to interpret. A larger value indicates greater strength of British presence.

A Simpson diversity index computed from the reported shares of total county population that are white (non-Hispanic), black (non-Hispanic), Hispanic, and Asian. The index is calculated as one minus the sum of the squared shares of population for each racial group, which measures racial concentration.

The Gini index captures the extent of income inequality in each county and is derived from census data. It integrates information about the number of households with incomes falling within different ranges into a single variable that captures dispersion across the entire income distribution. It equals zero when every household receives the same share of total income and increases to one in a hypothetical world in which a single household earns all available income.

The effectiveness of the TOT-UNICEF campaigns run in each county, measured as the amount of money collected. Funds raised in all community campaigns whose organizers' addresses fall in the focal county are summed, the annual totals are adjusted with the CPI deflator to account for inflation, and the total real funds variable is log-transformed to address the pronounced skew in campaign performance across counties.
time_window: annual total for each census year

description: For each TOT-UNICEF campaign the data record the promoting organization type (i.e., school, church, or club). The SUR analysis uses this variable to estimate three separate equations for campaigns organized by schools, clubs, and churches, holding that the institutional model for campaigns does not vary significantly across promoters.
level: campaign, aggregated to county-year by promoter type

description: Count of the physician's patients who were prescribed benzodiazepines for durations clearly exceeding guidelines, operationalized as more than 120 days in a given year, and who did not exhibit prescription-fill patterns consistent with misuse or abuse. Counting overprescribed patients minimized the concern that the measure captures sporadic mistakes.

Number of the physician's patients whose prescription-fill patterns were consistent with misuse or abuse in the calendar year. Patients were considered consistent with misuse or abuse when they obtained benzodiazepines from more than three physicians or when they had three or more overlapping refills, defined as filling two or more benzodiazepine prescriptions that overlapped by 25 percent of the days prescribed. Prescription episodes with fewer than five days' supply were excluded, and patients had to obtain more than a 120-day supply in the calendar year.

Dummy variable set to 1 if the physician has no connections and 0 if the physician has any connection to other physicians. The authors state that this operationalization conceptualizes isolation as a state that is distinct in character from being connected to the network.

The total number of ties a physician has to other physicians. A tie is inferred when two physicians shared six or more non-benzodiazepine patients in a calendar year, based on Barnett et al. (2011); networks were constructed for each year from patient sharing.

Local transitivity, defined as the proportion of transitive triplets; it captures the likelihood that any two colleagues with whom a physician formed a tie are also connected to each other. The local clustering coefficient is 0 if none of the alters are connected and 1 if all pairs of alters are connected, and it was imputed to be 0 for isolates and physicians with only one tie.

Dichotomous variable equal to 1 if the respondent had at least one friend in the internship organization prior to starting the internship and 0 otherwise. In the pre-internship survey respondents listed all the individuals they knew in the organization, where knowing someone was defined as someone they could recognize by sight and by name. They then reported the frequency of interaction, duration and closeness for each person and categorized each listed person as friend, relative, acquaintance, mentor, recruiter, internship supervisor, internship colleague, or alumnus; this categorization determined which interns had friends in the firm.

Dichotomous variable equal to 1 if the intern received a full-time postgraduate job offer from the internship employer and 0 otherwise. The offer data were collected from the post-internship survey; interns who had not yet received notification made a note of this, and the author contacted them the following spring and recorded their offer status. The offer outcome reported on the survey or ascertained during the follow-up was the same as that recorded by the career management centers.

Variable indicating whether the intern completed an internship in the same state as the university he or she was attending. Model 6 also includes an interaction term between this same-state variable and the number of friends the intern has in the organization.

Dichotomous variable equal to 1 if the respondent had at least one friend in the internship organization and 0 otherwise, taken from a single survey completed after the internship. To aid network recall, the author gathered the names of employees of each internship organization from the Martindale Hubble Directory, created rosters of employees for each organization, and supplied the relevant roster to each respondent before the survey; respondents categorized each person they knew.
time_window: prior to and during the internship

description: Dichotomous indicator of whether the law intern received a full-time postgraduate job offer from the internship employer, collected after the internship and verified against career management center records.

variable_name: missed one payment or more in breach of contract
description: Dummy-coded outcome measure that equals 1 if the borrower missed one payment or more in breach of contract during the life of the loan. The paper focuses on this measure in depth while making reference to the two- and three-payment outcomes in passing.
time_window: during the life of the loan

description: Dummy variable equal to 1 if the loan officer originating the loan had either consistent relational style, spirit of the law or letter of the law. SL and LL styles are regarded as consistent and distinct relational styles; mixed loan officers are not individually consistent.
Dummy variable equal to 1 if the former and subsequent loan officers have the same relational style, e.g., LLt → LLt+1 or SLt → SLt+1. It is contingent on a loan officer change.

Dummy variable denoting moving from a within-actor individually inconsistent style to an individually consistent style (Mt → SLt+1 or Mt → LLt+1). The original loan officer employed an inconsistent relational style whereas the subsequent one employed a consistent one—either letter or spirit of the law.
Variable coding cases when a client was transferred to a different loan officer (changed officer); dummy equal to 1 if there was a change in loan officer between time t and t+1.

variable_name: spirit of the law (SL), letter of the law (LL), mixed (M)
description: Three dummy variables classifying loan officers according to their relational styles. SL and LL styles are regarded as consistent and distinct; mixed loan officers blend elements of both. Three regional managers independently coded each loan officer as either SL, LL, or mixed using Table 1; discrepancies between individually consistent styles and mixed were treated as mixed. Interrater reliability was just below 80%.

The dependent variable is the day share of annual patent applications for firms and for individual assignees, computed as the ratio of the number of successful patents applied on a given day to the total number of successful patents over the sample period. Day shares are regressed on dummies for the last k days of the month and for days m to n of the month. The analysis uses granted patents from 1976 to 2009.

Dummy variables for the last k working days of the month, where k is 1, 3, or 5, are used as the main independent variable in regressions of complexity, work quality, and heterogeneity by firm size and technology cycle time. The dummy equals 1 for applications filed in the last k working days of a month. Coefficients and standard errors are scaled by 1,000.

Complexity is measured with six observed variables likely to be correlated with the complexity of an application: the number of claims, the number of drawings, the number of drawing sheets, the number of drawings per drawing sheet, the citation count within five years from the application date, and the probability of renewal at 3.5 years after grant. More claims and drawings are likely to take longer to complete and often result in higher fees for attorneys. Log number of claims is also used as a control in the conditional work-quality tests.

Work quality is measured using eight work-process-based measures and three work-outcome-based measures. The work-process measures are application incomplete notice, missing inventor oath or statement, additional application filing fees, new or additional drawing filed, information disclosure statement filed after the initial filing date, nonfinal rejection, request for extension of time granted, and restriction/election requirement; a factor analysis identified a single factor from these eight. The work-outcome measures are examiner-added citation share, application approval, and log review duration.
scale: binary for work-process measures and approval; continuous for examiner-added citation share and log review duration

description: Firm size is measured as the number of patents (or applications) belonging to firm j that were applied in year t, logged. It is used in the clustering regressions and in interactions with the month-end dummy.

Technology cycle time is defined as the mean time gap between a patent application and its backward citations, and has been used in the literature to represent the speed of technological changes in a field. Shorter cycle time indicates faster technological change. It is used in regressions with the month-end dummy and in interactions with the month-end dummy.

variable_name: Month-end deadline period (last k working days dummy) and corporate versus individual assignee contrast
description: The deadline penalty is operationalized through the calendar month-end: dummy variables for the last 1, 3 or 5 working days of the month mark the period when agents facing periodic deadlines are assumed to face a penalty for incomplete tasks. Corporate assignees, assumed to face periodic deadlines, are contrasted with individual inventors, who are not, and surveys and interviews of attorneys and inventors support the month-end deadline interpretation. In the calibration exercise the intensity of the penalty is proxied by a model parameter fitted to the observed last-day share.

Dichotomous variable for the respondent's gender, assigned based on the students' admissions office records and coded 1 for women and 0 for men. It is used as the main explanatory variable in the salary offer models.

Source of the salary offer as reported on the survey. Respondents chose among 16 options naming the primary source of each job offer; these were collapsed into four categories: Internship, Formal job source, Informal job source, and Other (the omitted category). The internship category refers to offers received from an employer where an internship first occurred, and the variable is coded 1 when the internship occurs at the organization from which the full-time offer originates, i.e., where employers had a chance to observe the candidate prior to making a full-time job offer.

The dependent variable is the initial salary offer received by a candidate, meaning the salary the candidate would be paid if employment commenced. Salary is used rather than total compensation because initial salary establishes a baseline for salary growth and because total compensation is affected by sign-on bonuses. On the survey, respondents listed up to four offers; the median number of offers received is 1 and the mean is 1.7.

Self-reported number of working hours a retail manager spends in a typical day on her department's selling tasks and on its servicing tasks. To measure relative attention the authors take the ratio between the hours spent on selling and servicing tasks; because this ratio is not symmetric around one, they use the logarithm of the ratio in the regressions, with zero denoting an even allocation of attention.
time_window: a typical day at the time of the survey (January 2018)

description: A scale measuring the intensity of the time and effort that a retail manager, working with her superiors, subordinates, and other departments, devotes to selling tasks and to servicing tasks. As with working hours, the log value of the ratio between the two task categories is used as the measure of attention allocation.

Expertise is measured by the number of years of work experience and training the retailer manager has in selling tasks and in servicing tasks. The log value of the ratio between the two tasks is used as relative expertise in the analysis.

An eight-item scale measuring the degree to which respondents are under time pressure at work, combining work-, personal-, and family-related items, with a Cronbach's alpha of 0.838. The items are reported as scales and the mean value of the eight items is used in the analysis. The authors treat time stress as a moderator of managerial attention and as a global assessment of a person's time stress rather than a domain-specific one.

Working hours are the self-reported daily time spent by the sales manager on the beer or soft drink product categories. To measure relative attention the authors first take the ratio between the hours spent on beer and soft drinks and then use its log value in the regressions, with beer always in the numerator.

Effort allocation measures the percentage of time and effort expended by the sales manager on selling beer or soft drinks. The ratio between the two product categories measures relative attention and its log value is used in the analysis.

Expertise measures the number of years of work experience a manager has in selling beer or soft drinks. As a proxy for relative expertise the authors use the log value of the ratio between the two products; the log-transformed ratio has a range of -3.689 to 3.296 with median and mean of 0 and -0.045.

The eight-item scale used in the Chilean questionnaire is identical to the one used in the Japanese context and has a Cronbach's alpha of 0.823. As in the Japanese data the mean of the items is used and time stress is treated as a moderator of managerial attention.

Monthly sales volume in hectoliters of beer and of soft drinks generated by each sales manager; achievement in sales volume comprises 80% of a manager's performance pay and the two main product lines cover 94% of total volume, so sales volume is used as a proxy for attention. The dependent variable is the log value of the ratio between the sales volumes of beer and soft drinks, with beer in the numerator.

A dummy equal to one when month t falls in the high season and zero otherwise; the main definition of the high season runs from September to March. High-seasonality months create significant time stress because of spiked market demand and hectic operational and marketing activities while the sales force capacity is kept largely constant, and the authors use them as a time-varying measure of time stress.

In the longitudinal analysis the authors keep years of work experience in each product category, beer and soft drinks, as the measure of expertise and use the log value of the ratio between the two product categories as relative expertise.

Participants first completed the schema elicitation task, asked to select four words associated in their minds with 'leader' from a menu of eight words in each of six distinct subsets. An algorithm then selected, in real time, an opposing argument generated by a Reference Sample participant who was cognitively similar to or different from the focal participant. Latent cognitive similarity was assessed based on the Jaccard Index of participants' schema elicitation task responses—the proportion of associated concepts that overlapped between the focal participant and the argument source; in the similarity condition the algorithm selected a source whose responses overlapped significantly with those of the participant, and in the dissimilarity condition one whose responses had little overlap.

variable_name: observable versus obscured latent cognition condition
description: Participants in the obscured condition only saw the opposing argument with no information provided about the source of the argument. Participants in the observable condition were shown a number (the Jaccard Index) representing the degree of overlap between their own responses to the schema elicitation task and those of the person whose opposing argument they were viewing, and were told that the number was either above or below the mean level of overlap between the focal participant and all participants in the Reference Sample.

variable_name: whether a participant changed her mind about the binary choice associated with an SJT
description: After viewing the opposing argument, participants were shown the SJT a second time and could revisit their decision. A change in mind was classified as movement across the midpoint of the 100-point slider scale, which ranged from −50 (the strongest possible position in favor of option 1) to 50 (the strongest possible position in favor of option 2), between the first and second time a person was presented with the SJT; for example, a participant was coded as having changed her mind if her initial response was −12 and her subsequent response was 9.
scale: binary (changed mind vs. did not change mind)
time_window: between the first and second presentation of the SJT

variable_name: magnitude of opinion change in the direction of the opposing argument
description: The degree to which a person's response shifted in the direction of the opposing view—whether they made a categorical shift in their opinion. By this measure, a person who shifted from −40 to −10 (moving from strong to lukewarm support for option 1) was assessed as being more strongly influenced than someone who shifted from −40 to −38 (moving only slightly toward the opposing view) or from −40 to −43 (moving further away from the opposing view).
scale: shift on a 100-point slider scale from −50 to 50
time_window: between the first and second presentation of the SJT

description: The equal- or value-weighted average of the profit weights κij that the owners of firm i place in year t on the profits of the n−1 other firms in the economy. Pairwise κij are constructed from institutional and blockholding ownership data. Observations where κit exceeds one are excluded because they indicate incorrect or missing ownership data.
Natural logarithm of one plus inflation-adjusted R&D expenditures divided by total assets. Missing R&D values are replaced with zeros, and a dummy indicates if R&D is zero.

Citation-weighted number of patents issued to firm i in year t. The measure sums patents, weighting each patent by its forward citations relative to the mean number of citations to patents granted in the same year.

Total stock market value of patents generated by firm i in year t. It sums the estimated stock market reactions ξj over the three-day announcement window following the issuance of each patent j granted to firm i in year t, as constructed by Kogan et al. (2017).

Pool of technology spillovers for firm i in year t, constructed from pairwise technological proximity TECHij and the weighted stock of R&D of other firms. TECHij is the uncentered correlation of firms' patent shares across technology classes (Jaffe proximity) or the Mahalanobis proximity that allows spillovers across classes.

Pool of product market spillovers for firm i in year t, constructed from pairwise product market proximity HPij, which is the cosine similarity of word frequencies in the Business Description section of firms' 10-K statements (Hoberg and Phillips 2016).

Ratio of existing ties to the maximum number of possible ties between alters in the banker's acquirer network, multiplied by 100. The acquirer relationship set includes all colleagues evaluated by the focal banker in the cross-evaluation exercise. All ties between alters were considered irrespective of the direction of the task-related information flow. The natural logarithm of the variable was used in the estimations to correct for skewness.
time_window: cross-evaluations collected in the second half of October 2001

description: Ratio of existing ties to the maximum number of possible ties between alters in the banker's provider role, multiplied by 100. The provider relationship set includes all colleagues who evaluated the focal banker. All ties between alters were considered irrespective of the direction of the task-related information flow. The natural logarithm of the variable was used in the estimations.
time_window: cross-evaluations collected in the second half of October 2001

description: The z-score of the dollar value of the annual bonus received by the banker for performance in the 2001 calendar year, provided by the bank for confidentiality reasons. Because the distribution is strongly skewed, the natural logarithm of the z-scores was used in the analysis, taken after rescaling the values to eliminate negative numbers.

The corporate title of the employee in 2001. The sample comprises the associate director, director, executive director, and managing director ranks, in this hierarchical order, represented by three dummy variables with the lowest rank (associate director) as the omitted category.

For each driver before the start of each race, the authors computed pairwise distances between that driver's points and those of his competitors. Using NASCAR's points schedule they defined the 'striking distance' as the difference between the points accruing to the driver who finishes last and the maximum number of points any driver can collect, and then tallied the number of lower-ranked drivers in striking distance of the focal driver. Contestant j is theoretically able to surpass i if i places last and j receives the maximum number of points.
time_window: measured before the start of each race, using points accumulated through race t-1

description: Computed by reordering the terms yielding the difference in points, this measure captures the count of higher-ranked drivers whom the focal driver could surpass if he received the maximum number of points and they finished last. It measures the opportunity of the focal driver to surpass rivals ranked higher in the points distribution.
time_window: measured before the start of each race, using points accumulated through race t-1

description: The authors assigned a 1 to a driver's entry in the event vector if that driver did not finish the race because of an accident, and 0 otherwise. This outcome is one of many destination states; NASCAR's publications identify a driver as having finished the race ('running') and clarify reasons other than an accident for not finishing, usually related to equipment failure. The rate of crashing is treated as a proxy for the unobservable tendency of a competitor to take risks.
scale: binary (1 = did not finish because of an accident, 0 otherwise)

description: The authors collected the ranks of each driver in the Winston Cup series points distribution at the start of the prior race and at the end of the prior race and identified the number of drivers who underwent a transition in rank. The measure counts the number of nonzero differences in starting and finishing ranks across drivers seeking to qualify in the prior race. To capture the number of rank changes occurring in race 1, each driver was assigned the rank of 1 at the start of the opening race.
