Guttman scale built from respondents' ratings (poor, fair, good, excellent) of eight services. A county scores as having quality service on an item if 50 percent or more of its respondents rate it good or excellent. The county scale score ranges from 0 to 8.
A panel of 11 judges ranked the participating organizations, mixed with dummy organizations, in order of goal specificity. The average of the judges' rankings was used.

OR/MS leaders listed the criteria by which superiors evaluated them. Judges classified each criterion as output, performance or efficiency by plurality. The percentage of output criteria per respondent was computed and organizations were ranked on it.
Same procedure: the share of listed evaluation criteria classified as performance criteria, ranked across organizations.
Same procedure: the share of listed evaluation criteria classified as efficiency criteria, ranked across organizations.

Modified version of Mohr's scale. Unit heads indicated the extent to which the nature of the research work in their unit required its members to work closely with one another as opposed to working individually.

Modified version of Georgopoulos and Mann's scale. Staff researchers rated whether the unit's research program was coherent and whether its research planning was well conceived; responses were averaged into a composite index.

Items from Pelz and Andrews on whether the unit was innovative in generating new knowledge or methods, productive in adding knowledge or methods, and contributed to scientific or technical development. Unit heads and external evaluators were weighted equally and responses averaged into a composite index.
Number of journal articles the unit published over the past three years, from organizational records, converted to lognormal scores.

variable_name: composite index of employee voice mechanisms
description: Hospitals reported whether registered nurses were subject to eight practices: formal grievance procedure, suggestion system, employee-management meetings, counseling service, ombudsman, nonmanagement task forces, question and answer program, and survey feedback. The index sums the number of mechanisms employed.
Each hospital administrator supplied the rate of voluntary turnover for its registered nurses for the previous 12-month period.

Nurses estimated how often they would be effective in resolving eight work-related problems (supervision, tasks, co-workers, pay, promotions), from 10 to 100 percent of the time in 10-percent steps; the eight items form a composite.

A ten-statement measure of how effectively management responded to and used employee voice, plus one-item measures of the effectiveness of voice mechanisms and the utility of efforts to change dissatisfying situations, on agree-disagree scales.
Minimum of the stated pay range for tellers, and midpoint of the stated pay range, each entered in a separate equation.

Six variables capture benefit level and flexibility: benefit percentage (share of payroll devoted to benefits), benefit flexibility (one item), paid days off, retirement plan, medical coverage and medical cost. Interrater correlation for flexibility ratings was .77.
The logarithm of the number of applications for full-time teller positions a bank received within the most recently completed fiscal year.
The arcsine of the percentage of employment offers made to tellers that were accepted during the year, assessed by asking the average number of offers made per teller position filled.
The logarithm of the average number of days a teller position remained open before it was filled during the most recently completed fiscal year.

variable_name: Number of evolved jobs and of opportunistic hires per department
description: Raters who had reviewed the reclassification or waiver request rated how far the job was tailored around the person's skills or interests on a 1 to 5 scale. Cases rated 4 or 5 were coded 1 as idiosyncratic jobs and all others 0. Counts of evolved jobs and opportunistic hires per department were used as separate dependent variables.
scale: count; rated 1 to 5, coded 1 for ratings of 4 or 5

description: Questionnaire item on the degree of uncertainty in total resources. Respondents (the department head and a second senior member) rated their department twice on a 1 to 7 item, first for 1979-1980 and then for the degree of change over the study period; the analysis uses the change variable and the mean of two informants' ratings when both responded.

Questionnaire item on how much ambiguity there is in the mission of the department or unit. Respondents (the department head and a second senior member) rated their department twice on a 1 to 7 item, first for 1979-1980 and then for the degree of change over the study period; the analysis uses the change variable and the mean of two informants' ratings when both responded.

Questionnaire item on how varied and unpredictable the sources of support are. Respondents (the department head and a second senior member) rated their department twice on a 1 to 7 item, first for 1979-1980 and then for the degree of change over the study period; the analysis uses the change variable and the mean of two informants' ratings when both responded.

Questionnaire item on how varied and unpredictable the problems the unit faces are. Respondents (the department head and a second senior member) rated their department twice on a 1 to 7 item, first for 1979-1980 and then for the degree of change over the study period; the analysis uses the change variable and the mean of two informants' ratings when both responded.

Questionnaire item on the degree of financial flexibility, meaning access to resources. Respondents (the department head and a second senior member) rated their department twice on a 1 to 7 item, first for 1979-1980 and then for the degree of change over the study period; the analysis uses the change variable and the mean of two informants' ratings when both responded.
Unit size at the end of the study subtracted from the size at the beginning of the study, from central personnel records.

Formalization was a feature of the studied organization rather than a coded variable: all departments operated under the same procedural guidelines, with about 250 job titles tied to compensation categories, posted jobs with written descriptions and requirements, and documented reclassification and selection procedures.

variable_name: superior environmental uncertainty; superior task uncertainty
description: Two instruments completed by the IS manager's immediate superior: Brownell's adaptation of Duncan's eight-item environmental uncertainty instrument, in which each item has two seven-point scales (criticality to decision making and extent of change over time) that are multiplied, and a nine-item task uncertainty instrument adapted from Withey, Daft and Cooper on seven-point scales. The final score of each instrument is the average of its item scores.

variable_name: IS manager environmental uncertainty; IS manager task uncertainty
description: The same two instruments, environmental uncertainty and task uncertainty, completed by IS managers about the uncertainty they face as manager of the IS function; item averages form the score.

variable_name: number of months the IS manager has worked with the organization; difficulty of evaluating the IS manager's performance
description: Two measures of senior management dependency used in the structural model: months of tenure of the IS manager, and a component from the IS manager's questionnaire reflecting how difficult it is to evaluate the manager's performance because of the nature of the job.

variable_name: percentage of revenues allocated to the IS manager
description: Single item asking the superior for the percentage of the organization's total gross revenues allocated to the IS manager as his or her responsibility, used as a proxy for delegation of decision rights.

variable_name: percentage of IS funds devoted to IS planning
description: Single item asking the IS manager for the percentage of total IS funds under his or her control devoted to IS planning, used as a proxy for the amount of planning.

variable_name: superior controlled versus IS manager controlled planning process
description: Six-item instrument completed by the IS manager on whether the IS planning process was superior controlled or IS manager controlled. The final score used three interval-level items after two items had loadings contrary to prediction and one dichotomous item was dropped.

variable_name: superior focused versus IS manager focused IS plan
description: Six-item instrument completed by the superior on whether the plan reflected senior management's goals or the IS manager's goals. The final score is based on five items after the first item loaded contrary to prediction; reliability was high (Cronbach alpha 0.77).

variable_name: dependence of the IS manager's compensation on achieving IS plan goals
description: Single item asking the superior about the extent to which the IS manager's compensation depended upon achieving the goals and objectives in the IS plan, a proxy for the bonding, monitoring and governance usefulness of the plan.

variable_name: difficulty or cost of ensuring the IS manager acts in accordance with organizational goals
description: Single item asking the superior about the difficulty or cost of ensuring the IS manager acted in accordance with the overall goals and objectives of the organization, a proxy for the level of agency costs.

Each bankrupt firm was paired with a matched survivor chosen for similarity in size and product/markets five years before failure, using three judges. The dependent variable in the logit analysis was survival (0) versus bankruptcy (1).
Data were gathered for the years t-5 through t-1, where t is the year of bankruptcy. Change periods were coded as dummies in the acceleration test.

variable_name: return on assets (relative to matched survivors)
description: Return on assets (ROA) of the bankrupt firm, taken relative to its matched survivor in the cross-lagged correlation analysis and as annual change in the acceleration regression. The text does not state the data source or formula of ROA.
time_window: years t-5 through t-1 before bankruptcy

description: The number of officers (vice presidents and above) of the firm provides the measure of top management team size.
time_window: years t-5 through t-1 before bankruptcy

description: Total number of board members who were not officers of the firm.
time_window: years t-5 through t-1 before bankruptcy

variable_name: percentage of team in core functions
description: Percentage of the team whose dominant functional track was in core functions: marketing/sales, operations/production, research and development. Dominant track is the one in which the person spent more career time than any other; some people are coded as no dominant functional track.
time_window: years t-5 through t-1 before bankruptcy

variable_name: average cash compensation per person excluding CEO
description: Average inflation-adjusted cash compensation for officers and directors except the CEO, based on total cash compensation paid to all officers and outside directors. Inflation adjustment uses the Consumer Price Index.
time_window: years t-5 through t-1 before bankruptcy

description: Mean number of years in the firm for all officers.
time_window: years t-5 through t-1 before bankruptcy

description: Variance of member tenures in the firm, divided by the mean tenure in the firm.
time_window: years t-5 through t-1 before bankruptcy

description: Ratio of the CEO's cash compensation to the average compensation of other team members, as defined for team compensation.
time_window: years t-5 through t-1 before bankruptcy

description: TMT composition was measured by seven team attributes: number of officers, number of outside board members, percentage of the team in core functions, average cash compensation excluding the CEO, mean tenure, tenure heterogeneity and CEO pay ratio. Yearly means, logit models and 5-year slopes of each variable were compared between bankrupts and survivors.

Percentage of the system produced in house, between 0 (fully outsourced) and 1 (all in-house production). It is calculated as the average across the individual components for that system, with each component weighted equally. Parts from wholly owned subsidiaries are treated as in house; parts from partially owned suppliers are treated as outsourced.

Average of the first Consumer Reports quality rating for the system in the introduction year and in the following year, as available; when only one rating is available, only one is used. Ratings range from 1 to 5, with 5 as the highest rating.
time_window: first two years of the product life cycle after a major model change

description: Long-Term Performance minus Short-Term Performance. Long-Term Performance is the average of the Consumer Reports ratings in the third and fourth years after the major model change, as available.
time_window: first four years after a major model change

description: Dummy equal to 1 if company headquarters are located in Japan. The authors use it because Japanese manufacturers were new entrants into the luxury segment.
Dummy equal to 1 if there are preexisting in-house sunk costs or plant investment for the system.
Dummy equal to 1 if the system is transmission, electrical, or brakes, based on the availability during the sample period of globally available innovative suppliers.
Dummy equal to 1 if the component was designed to be used for more than one vehicle model.

In the selection analysis, a binary indicator that the firm will obtain SA8000 certification in the future, using only precertification years. In the effects analysis, a binary indicator that the firm was SA8000 certified in year t; in the difference-in-differences it equals one only in 2008 for firms certified between 2005 and 2007.

The simple average wage of each establishment: the deflated total annual wage divided by the number of employees. Wages are deflated by annual provincial consumer price indices. Variables are scaled to 100% in 1998 and winsorized at the 99.99th percentile.
Dummy coded 1 if the average wage is at least 25% higher than the minimum wage of the county where the firm is located, using the statutory county minimum wage in each year.

Estimated average wage of production workers in the industrial survey, using the fitted regression model from the 2005 Private Sector Survey of China relating production worker wages to average staff wages, adjusted for annual changes in average wages.

Total value of industrial products produced or services provided by the enterprise for export, in 1,000 Yuan, deflated by sector-specific price indices. A second variable is export share of sales, defined as 100 times export sales divided by total sales.
Total value of industrial products produced or services provided by the enterprise for domestic sales, in 1,000 Yuan, deflated by sector-specific price indices.
Count of employees in the enterprise (persons).
